reviewText:
I don't know.

As big as the font is on the label it must be important. Im not much into natural  ingredients in cosmetics (I know this now because Wikipedia told me so)Im not into cosmeticsIm not into natural. I want a product that works, that moisturizes, that applies easily, is long-lasting under harsh northeastern winter weather conditions, doesnt smell like I left my cash at a full-service massage parlor and doesnt cost so much I couldn't afford to squander my money as previously noted.

This one is a fail on all accounts. I rate it mediocre merely because it isn't any less effective than most competitive products.

This is the largest size body lotion I have seen from Crabtree and Evelyn, and the best value. The jojoba has a nice scent, it smells clean and fresh. I put it on after my morning shower, the softness and smoothness stays with me, just what I need to get me through the winter months! Thank you for making this new size.

According to my wife, this is a great lotion!  It isn't watery and cheap like some lotions; it smells like soap and is rich, works well, and seriously does hydrate the skin.  She's glad we have it.  (Confession: I've used it a few times too, and I like it!)

The thickness, absorbency and quality of this lotion is really nice.  I find the bottle design to be understated and classic and pleasing.  I would not normally purchase because it does have parabens - multiple types.  I do try to buy paraben and other chemical free as much as possible.  I do think there is a difference is absorbency and moisturizing benefits though when you go chemical free.  It's a great moisturizer for those who could care less about all natural.

This is only lightly moisturizing and the scent reminds me of an antique shop; old and musty but not totally in a bad way. The fragrance is from my grandmother's time in the early 1900's.

The moisturizer sinks in almost immediately and leaves smooth lightly softened skin behind. If the scent wasn't so nostalgic, I'd like this as a summer lotion because it is non-greasy and has no stickiness to it.
summary: This is more like a summer body lotion with an antique scent

reviewText: This is pure heaven. I love this product. It is a great moisturizer and my skin just drinks it up. I put it on after the shower and feel ready to conquer the world. This is a much better buy than at the stores. I personally like the slight soapy smell. It makes me feel clean. Do your self a favor and get this wonderful bargain. Your skin will love you for it.

This generous 500 cc container has a sturdy pump and is filled to the top with product. This body lotion is silky and feels great on the skin. It reduces dry itch and doesn't slough off. It is a really good deal for the price.

Unfortunately, it has a really peculiar fragrance. When I asked my husband to smell this he laughed and said " Lifebuoy soap! 1965!" . The fragrance mix is exactly like classic bar soap. And it really lingers. This would be a 5 star product with another scent or unscented. Unfortunately the fragrance is so strong and odd that I would never buy this. It is too bad because absent the perfume, this is an excellent product.
summary: Very nice moisturizer but the scent is "bar soap from 1965". A real deal breaker

reviewText:
This works best as a hand lotion. It goes on cleanly and absorbs quickly with no greasy feeling, making it great for work or other situations where you need to be able to hand paper, your computer, etc. immediately after application. It's mostly just surface moisturization, though; definitely not a 'deep repair' kind of lotion for skin in dire straights. It has to be reapplied regularly.

The scent is somewhere between your standard 'clean linen' and 'powder' scents. It's pretty noticeable, and I can't see any men that I know willingly using it. If you're sensitive to scents at all, you won't like it either. I am not particularly sensitive to scents, but this one just didn't work for me. It had that slightly off tang of very synthetic or low-quality scents. Not so much that I couldn't use it, but enough that I won't be getting it again.

All in all, not a bad product, but not impressive or right for me.

My first impression of the Crabtree & Evelyn Relaxing Body Lotion is that it had a strange but good smell - I wasn't expecting it. After a minute or two, I did actually find it relaxing, but maybe too strong at first. After it drys the smell is quite soothing. The lotion itself isn't too greasy but  didn't moisturize my legs quite as much as I had hoped, especially for the $28 price tag. It's winter, so I've got major dry skin. After a little while, I have to either suck it up or apply more.  The presentation of the lotion, bottle and label, is great. Pump works well, and hasn't had any clumping/difficulty at all and I've been using this on my legs for weeks. I'm not too happy with the ingredients (lots of parabens) in the lotion, so probably won't be purchasing this when this bottle empties. Really can't get over how soothing the smell is though!

I am baffled by the 'love the smell' reviews.  I agree this is nice enough cream, but I find the smell unpleasantly redolent of cheap perfume.  I am unclear what about this product distinguishes it in quality worth the asking price from a much less expensive product when the latter can be had in an inoffensive scentless version.  In addition, I am unable to consider the benefits and safety of its enormous ingredient list as the white writing on light turquoise background is virtually unreadable.

It was a non-issue when this full size product of C &E body lotion was offered. The hotel chain I stay at offers samples of this in this line's shampoo, conditioner, soap, and lotion. I liked it so much that I head over to their store in Chicago to stock up periodically.
The fact is this is a fresh smelling lotion that is not too florid but imparts a sort of serene sensation after bathing. It goes on with ease and leaves my skin soft and pliant and feeling really fresh. I have extreme dry skin in the winter months, but this works great whenever because it isn't greasy and doesn't clog pores.
I use a lot of Crabtree & Evelyn products because they are high quality and they work well. I have never experienced any negative experience when using this brand or this product.
summary: Reminds Me Of The Lake On A Spring Morning

reviewText:
All things considered, this was a disappointment.

The smell, which is somewhat astringent and chemical, lingers.  Even if I liked the scent itself better, I prefer fragrances that soften over time, rather than.....stay there.  I am aware that what people find pleasant, scent-wise, and how long they like a scent to linger, are highly individual things.  That said, I would definitely not recommend this lotion to people who don't like strong, rather chemical fragrances. This one is cloying enough to give the user a headache.

I also don't think that this is a high-quality lotion.  It doesn't absorb well, and it really doesn't do much to soften or soothe dry skin.

Neutragena, Eucerin, Nivea, Burts Bees....all make products that are better moisturizers and have less strident smells.
summary: Scent is chemical, and lingering. And this moisturizer does not absorb well, and so does not actually moisturize effectively.

reviewText:
I too first received this as a hotel amenity. I know frangrance choices are very personal, but for me this is one of the best scents ever!  I'm not sure how to describe it--maybe beachy/ocean-y?  If that conjures up images of stinky fish, then just think clean, clean, clean.  Definitely NOT floral or any girly type of fragrance.  I always put this on before bed and it somehow really is relaxing, as described.  It is NOT greasy and has average moisturizing properties.

My only complaint is this scent doesn't come in a body spray.  There is a shower gel, shampoo, conditioner, hand treatments, foot treatments, etc, but no body spray.  I even wrote to the company, but they have no plans to produce one.  If they did, this would be the only fragrance I would wear.  Love it!

This setting powder worked really well, locking my makeup in for the entire day so I didn't have to reapply anything even once between the morning and evening. And as an extra bonus, it mattified my tinted moisturizer so my skin looked fresh but not shiny at all. Highly recommended.

From my wife: this setting powder made me look like a geisha. Instead of being translucent as promised, it turns my face white. Making it look dry and over done. I was hoping for a more matte look. However, it does seem to make my blush have longer staying power, even after a workout. The label on the packaging looks like a label printed from my computer. The quality of this product is questionable at best.

At first I was apprehensive when I saw how white this was... it looks clown-makeup white. Reminds me of corn starch. But it does go on completely transparent. I applied it over BB cream, and while it did give a matte finish, it made my skin look too dry and dull.

It's a high-quality product... it just didn't suit me.

I have very sensitive skin that is prone to acne and this did not cause any aggravation. This is my first setting powder, so I do not have any other experience to compare it to, but it worked as intended. I am a novice when it comes to the application of makeup, but had no hard time using this product. It lasted the entire day.
summary: I have very sensitive skin that is prone to acne ...

reviewText: I am very familiar with setting powder. For years I have been buying Watts Beauty Natural Loose Mineral Powder - Translucent Finishing - Setting Powder Mineral Veil - Eco Friendly Refill Bag - Huge 20g. It is the only thing that will work but sometimes the company gets the colors mixed up. Meaning, sometimes they place the veil powder in with the setting powder so the colors are never the same. I had to write them to get the correct shade. Since then I have not had any issues. I use setting powder because I have the fairest skin there is. I can never find anything at the drugstores or stores that carry the light shade I need. My routine, I wash my face with soap. I then use an astringent on it. I then use an oil free serum. Then I place a thin light oil free foundation on. I let it sit for a few minutes then apply the setting powder. After, I wait another few minutes and finish with a light pressed powder. I then leave the house with the pressed powder and use it as needed through the night but am usually told my face is flawless. It took me a long time to figure out what steps to take and what products. For the price, this is a much better value. The other one I use comes in a bag and you have to have your own container and powder puff. I like that this is all together and also cheaper. The other one cost more and you only get of the amount. I used this for a week to make sure I loved it, I do! I already use the parent company Loreal so I will be buying this one from now on. This is perfect for some many things but really great for fair skin and keeping your face from shinning. It gives it a matte look which I love! It also looks natural, as if you have nothing on. I am glad I found this. I will be making the switch.
summary: If you are familiar with setting powders, give this a try!

reviewText:
Well, this was a gem of a find! It's translucent, and I don't get any weird ghostly camera flash back when I wear it. It's soft, silky, and applies with the puff, or my powder brush, flawlessly.
It's very similar to a few other powders on the market, (tarte, MUFE, are two I have), that have a similar texture and finish, but this is very cost effective for the amount.
It doesn't change the shade of my foundation, no stark or overly powered areas.
Really loving this setting powder!
summary: See my skin, not my shine!

reviewText: I wasn't sure what to expect with the Vichy Dermafinish Setting Powder, but now that I've tried it, I'd like to know where it has been my whole life.  The powder goes on smoothly and evenly, thanks to the powder puff that is included.  I have noticed a real difference in the overall tone of my skin, and the best part is that this setting powder is lightweight.  My foundation seems to last a little longer throughout the day.  Since I hate to reapply powder over and over again, this is the perfect solution.  All in all, I've been impressed with Vichy products.  They do not irritate my skin and do not have a lot of unnecessary fragrance.  This is an excellent product.
summary: I'd like to know where it has been my whole life

reviewText:
This powder leaves a silky, flawless, slightly dewy finish to my skin. I don't use Vichy's foundation (the only foundation that looks right on me is MAC Studio Sculpt, unfortunately) but on top of other foundation or primer, the Dermafinish powder creates a beautiful effect. It goes on easily, stays put, and, given that it's translucent, should look good on any skin tone. Even though I have very sensitive skin that makes it impossible to use a lot of powders, I had no negative reaction to Dermafinish.

Overall, this is a fantastic finishing powder that keeps makeup in place while lending a smoothing, brightening effect to my face. Definitely recommended.

This setting powder is straightforward.  It's used after foundation and blush/bronzer to keep the makeup last long and to keep urban pollutants/smog and dirt/dust from getting absorbed. I've been using it in the winter and expect that it'd work even better during the hot and humid months.  As it is, it's kept my foundation looking good and meant less need for touchups throughout the day.  So far, it hasn't caused any reactions or skin irritation.
summary: Helps keep foundation and makeup in place

reviewText: I love setting powder, and am new to white setting powder.  Thus, I was hoping to love this product, and happily, I do!  White setting powder does make one's skin look a shade or two lighter than the underlying foundation, but I like that effect very much.  The powder takes the shine off, and keeps it off for hours.  This product meets and exceeds every hope I had for it.  Highly recommend.

Excellent results  - use on top of foundation.  Eliminates emergence of oil and shine, leaving a  nice even matte finish for hours.  When worn all day, it seems that a mid-day or early afternoon touchup is in order.  Translucent and does not seem to affect the foundation shade. Nice silky feel.

Allergy tested.  Paraben free.  Made in France.  Puff is enclosed.

Lately, I have been using many Vichy products.  This brand is manufactured by Loreal.  They are known to use Vichy spring water (from France) in their cosmetic products.  This time, I decided to go for setting powder (make up line of products rather than skin care which I used in the past).  My skin is combination oily.  Mid-day I start noticing my skin getting oily and shiny.  Often times, I must use oil absorbing paper or foundation powder if I want to keep my skin from shining.  Since I tied many Vichy products already, I wanted to see if this product will help with oil control and if product will provide good coverage for the entire day.  Another important factor for the product is not to keep my skin too dry so it does not "crack" during cold winter weather in Chicago (where I live).

I was surprised to learn that this product is made out of 100% talc.  I looked up FDAs definition of talc and this is what it says:  "Talc is a naturally occurring mineral, mined from the earth, composed of magnesium, silicon, oxygen, and hydrogen. Chemically, talc is a hydrous magnesium silicate with a chemical formula of Mg3Si4O10(OH)2.

Talc has many uses in cosmetics and other personal care products; in food, such as rice and chewing gum; and in the manufacture of tablets. For example, it may be used to absorb moisture, to prevent caking, to make facial makeup opaque, or to improve the feel of a product.

Health experts have maintained over the years that products containing talc are safe when used as directed, and recent scientific reviews of available data have supported this position. The Food and Drug Administration has determined that talc is Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS) for use as an anti-caking agent in foods. It is also permitted as an anti-caking agent in vanilla powder. FDA has listed talc as a color additive that may be used in coloring drug products and as a component of colors for use in drugs and cosmetics. - See more at: http://www.cosmeticsinfo.org/talc-information#sthash.qQ7ik6lm.dpuf"

So it is worth mentioning that this is safe product to use and will not have adverse effect on the skin and human body.  I like the fact that product comes with small puff which is used to distribute talk on the face once foundation is applied.  I love that talk helped even out the foundation color.  In spite of its while color, it did not change the essential color of the foundation, so no need to worry that your foundation shade will change. My skin was clean and oil free all day.  Skin has even texture.  And in the evening when I come home, it is easy to take off with the facial cleanser.  It does not leave heavy residue on the skin. After work, I often exercise, so another advantage of this product is that it will not "smudge" during exercise.  All in all, this is great product.  If I have to choose between applying primer on the skin and then foundation, or applying foundation first and then covering and smoothing it out with setting powder, I would go for the second option.  If for not other reason, then for the fact that it will not clog skin.
summary: Finishing powder for your foundation that will leave your skin tone color even for the entire day

reviewText: This Vichy 3 in 1 micellar solution is similar to others on the market. It does a good job of cleaning the face of makeup and daily grime. It does have a slight scent to it yet it is not overwhelming. I would get this product again.

reviewText: this is really great stuff. It does a great job cleaning my face. It is gentle and does a fantastic job removing makeup. Unfortunately the bottle was leaking when it was delivered. Only about 1/2 was still in the bottle. The cap was partially broke and will not stay on the bottle.

I like this cleansing water. Its gentle on my skin. Is not very scented and leaves my skin soft. It is not good for taking off heavy foundation or mascara so youll need regular

I use other Vichy products and like the brand.

This is refreshing!  It is a liquid water-like cleanser with a pleasant scent with a hint of rose.  I used a cotton pad to clean my face and it felt clean and soft after using this cleanser.  And it is so refreshing.  It wakes you up a bit.  You just put a little on a cotton ball and it cleans your make-up or facial oils.

I look forward to using it more and reporting back on the effect on my skin.  So far, am pleased with the product.

This is water with little bits of oil. It won't get very stubborn pieces of makeup or things that are waterproof or especially heavy, but with a little cotton or towel will get most of it. Left skin feeling much better than a harsh makeup remover. Great for traveling if you don't know what the water situation will be. reviewText:
Vichy Pureté Thermale 3-in-1 Micellar water is formulated to cleanse, remove makeup and calm skin irritation in one easy step that just requires pouring it on a cotton pad or cotton ball and wiping the eye area and face. No rinsing is required. I like that this product contains no soap, colorants, oil or alcohol, but I do wish it was free of chemical fragrance too (though at least the scent is light).

This is the best Micellar water I've tried for removing my face makeup (though it's not great for my eyes). I don't wear heavy makeup but do wear mascara, concealer, foundation and powdered bronzer, contour makeup and/or blush. My cotton pad is covered with makeup after wiping my face, and I've used my Clarisonic after and don't see residual makeup on the brush.

I still usually prefer to also use my regular cleanser, but this Micellar water does the trick when I'm tired at night as I just wipe my face it and let it air dry while I brush my teeth (and just follow with my serum and cream). My skin is dry and sensitive, and it feels clean and comfortable even without rinsing and doesn't feel dry or irritated from the Micellar water. It does feel just a bit tacky without rinsing, but that feeling goes away as soon as I apply my regular serum and cream.

I like this Micellar water for my face, but it doesn't work well very for removing my Lancme mascara (which is not waterproof). It stings my eyes and gently wiping doesn't get rid of enough of my mascara. I get much better results using Lancme Bifacil eye makeup remover and it has never irritated my eyes. So I use the Vichy Micellar water for my face makeup and the Lancme for my eye makeup. I think the Vichy Micellar water is a good product, but I'm taking one star off because it's not good for removing my mascara. 4 stars.

8/31/2017: My commute and work days have been really long lately, and the weather has been so hot. I come home beat and one of the first things I do is wipe my face with this Vichy Micellar Water. While it's not perfect, I've grown to love its convenience and how it's refreshing and removes so much makeup and grime without drying my skin out, I'm upgrading my rating from 4 to 5 stars.
summary: Good Product For Removing My Face Makeup Without Irritating My Sensitive Skin, But Not As Good For Taking Off My Mascara

reviewText:
I've been using micellar water for some time now to clean my face at the end of the day.  That's why I was happy to test out this Vichy product, since it's a brand I haven't used before.  I can say that the small bottle is pretty.  Prettier than the bottle my Garnier micellar water comes in.  So this wins in presentation.

Unfortunately, that's the only category this Vichy micellar water wins in my estimation.  The Garnier brand leaves my face feeling much cleaner and smoother than the Vichy, while the Vichy feels a bit soapy when wet on my face, takes longer to dry, and leaves my face feeling much drier than the Garnier does.  The Garnier has no oil, alcohol, or fragrance.  The Vichy has hexylene glycol, panthenol and parfum.  The Garnier comes in a 13.5 ounce bottle and costs about a dollar or more less than the 3.38 ounce bottle of Vichy.  Both Garnier and Vichy remove the small amount of make-up I use with no problem so there's a tie there.

So, no thanks.  I won't be buying this Vichy micellar water again when this bottle is empty.  My sister who is visiting me also tried it a few times and said it left her face feeling sticky and not refreshed.  If a product does not perform well and costs much more than a competing brand, it's obvious which one I will continue to use in the future.
summary: Pretty bottle, but what's inside is not my favorite micellar water.

reviewText:
I first got this as part of a set, but I had to buy this cleanser. A little bit on a cotton pad leaves my skin feeling clean, soft, and wonderful. Even with my dry sensitive skin there is no irritation, no feeling of tightness, no drying.

After using it my skin feels so soft. it's also great for travel since I can clean my skin quickly with a cotton pad. After years of searching I've found the cleanser that works for my skin and my life style.

reviewText: I've used micellar water for the past year, and I switch brands. This by Vichy is my least favorite. It takes off make-up OK, but it feels like it leaves a film behind on my skin. Also the shape/size of the bottle makes it hard to dispense. It was hard to squeeze, so I shook it onto a pad, but then it goes all over the place. There are better brands of micellar water at half the cost.
summary: It's OK, but there are better ones out there

reviewText: I love this stuff! I don't wear a ton of makeup but I swim almost every day and use sunscreen. Until now, I actually had trouble getting the sunscreen off my face.  It would clog my pores. When I got this, the sunscreen just melted off and it left me with clean, soft and fresh skin. I'm trying to take care of my skin and not abuse it like I always did. I use this with my Clarisonic and my skin is perfect! Love it

I have been using this with Opi Expert Touch Pads, which are just very thin cotton paper like pads. You could use cotton balls or anything like this to apply it with. It looks and feels just like water The ingredients list a fragrance but I cannot smell it at all. I wet a pad and use it to clean my face with, and it cleanses well. I usually use multiple little pads but that's normal for me with any makeup remover. It does remove makeup well, and it takes my hard to remove mascara off. It does not burn my eyes at all and it seems very gentle. After use, I notice that my skin feels like it does when I first wake up- a bit naturally oily. I thought it might be makeup residue so I've tried it when I have absolutely no make up on, and it feels the same. I think it is the glycerin in the product. My skin is dry though, so it has worked ok for me. To me the only downside is that it can come out too fast when I am not careful, causing waste. Occasionally too, not always, but sometimes, it can leave the skin around my t-zone feeling a bit sticky. That area of my skin is naturally oilier, so I would think that people with oily skin might want to try to get a sample of this product if possible before investing in it. It seems wonderful on my skin when it is dry and in need of moisture though.
summary: Removes makeup without stripping, but doesn't feel as natural when dry where skin is oily, can leave it sticky

reviewText: Cleans my face so well! Leaves my skin feeling soft and clean. Great for sensitive skin, did not break out at all. So convenient to have a three-in-one cleanser!  I love having a one step cleanser especially at night when all I want to do is go to bed!

My wife tried this recently:This micellar water revolution is something else, and Vichys 3-in-1 cleansing water is up there with the best. Its crazy how easy the most stubborn makeup glides off the skin and onto the cotton ball.  No more rubbing to remove eye makeup, no more lost eyelashes!  I didn't notice a fragrance with this product, so if you're sensitive to aromas, youll tolerate this product well.  Excellent product  if you're in the market for a makeup remover/cleanser, you should really give this a try!

Not only is the bottle elegant looking, but the product inside is quite simply, a delight.
It usually takes two or three cotton rounds to remove all of my makeup.
Using micellar water is quick and easy. Saturate a cotton round or ball and wipe away the grime.
This particular brand doesn't leave any sticky residue behind. It has a very light scent that is refreshingly pleasant. Gentle yet effective.

Before getting this I had used a liquid cleanser that would sometimes get in my eyes and burn. This doesn't irritate at all. I pour a little on a cotton pad, and it does a great job getting off my mascara and the grime that has accumulated on my face. Quite often I'm too tired and lazy to wash my face at night. This product is so easy to use that I am cleansing nightly. It's quite refreshing and has a very mild, pleasant scent.
summary: Refreshing with a mild, pleasant scent.

reviewText:
Excellent micellar water cleaner. It smells nicely, and it does clean my face well. It does not irritate my skin. Before I used La Roche-Posay micellar water, and did not like it very much because it left my face sticky with residue. Not so much with Vichy - my face feels clean after use, not sticky at all. When I wash my face afterward, there is no residue that needs to be washed off as it was the case with La Roche-Posay water.
The water gets rid of oiliness on my face, but does not prevent it from returning. If it was, it would have been 10 stars.
summary: leaves skin very clean with no irritation

reviewText:
Skin cremes I thought I had tried them all, it seems. Not all, a friend recommended Avene,after I expressed admiration for her glowing smooth skin. Some of the smoothness is, I know, due to injections, but not all. She had tried the Avene moisturizer at the recommendation of her dermatologist. She Uses it particularly in the winter when her skin becomes more dry. She paid a lot more for her Creme, than I did. I found it on Amazon, and was very pleased at the price.

This is more of a daily facial cream which I use morning and night. I cleanse my face with Cetaphil, and then I add a serum and top it off with Avene moisturizer. I only need some mineral powder, blush and mascara, and my day is set.

This moisturizer really makes my skin feel full and hydrated. It is not greasy, and absorbs any oil for a shine-free finish. The formula gives me a supple feel and a matt finish. I have never had sensitive skin, but as I grow older it has changed in consistency. It tends to dry more quickly, and, of course, more lines appear. Based on mybfriend's remarks and from what I have read, Avene has been well tested, is not greasy at all. You only need a small amount on your face and neck, and I use what us left on my hands. This skin care product is made in France, and there are several other components to the skin care line you can try. I am using only this face moisturizer, but may try the other products. I am completely satisfied with this moisturizer.

Recommended. prisrob 01- 06 -15

First, this product is definitely unisex and IMO actually skews masculine more than feminine. The ambergris and woods notes give this a fairly dark and only mildly sweet base, and the rose scent is quite subdued and "green". The overall effect is of a pleasantly floral barbershop type scent, which for me was just perfect. An inexpensive woods / rose mix that is not overly sweet or fake smelling is a great thing, and at this reasonable price point, it is even better. Cabaret by Gres is the closest competitor (in the rose / woods alleged feminine that guys can wear) and Cabaret has a far sweeter and more synthetic smelling rose to it, though Cabaret also is the more complex scent and has better silage and longevity (and is even cheaper!).

Longevity was decent, about 4-6 hours of noticeable proximity effect (about 2-3 feet of projection) and then becomes a skin scent for another 2-4 hours. Silage was moderate, not a room clearing force field. Compared to many other "mall bath and body store" scents, this is pretty impressive. L'Occitan for instance is famous for not inexpensive scents that last an hour or so and then vanish utterly. In comparison, this C&E frag comes close to giving you what the big fragrance companies offer and at a fraction of their price.

What's not to like? Some men do not want to smell like any flowers, ever. This is not for them. Many men and some women do not like powdery smells. This is a little bit powdery, kind of a resinous grassy note mixed in with the powder, and is not overwrought at all. Still, if you loathe powder even in small doses, you may want to try before you buy.

Perfume is very personal. I prefer scents that are earthy, clean, hints of citrus.  This scent comes out very strong and very rose scented.  I don't like it straight out of the bottle, but I do like it.  My grandmother used rose scented soaps, and this smells like her hands, and I miss her, so I  both love and dislike the initial scent.  The lasting aura is softer, vanilla and rose and ambergris (which reminds me of a Bob's Burgers episode). Perfume is personal, and how a perfume smells on you is personal.  If you enjoy the smell of roses, this might be a real hit with you.  This is not really my scent, but I find myself wearing it regularly because it really does remind me of the soap in my grandmother's home, and I miss her. Scent can take you places, remind you of things, set the tone.  Pick something that is distinctly you.
summary: I both love and dislike this scent, perfume is so personal.

reviewText:
I wanted to love this. The description sounded just like something Id like and i hoped that the toilette parfum would be light enough to wear to work and not offend anyone. Plus I have used other products from Crabtree and Evelyn and been pleased. Alas, it was not to be. I have a sensitive nose, overly sensitive probably. But this was all kinds of no. No with a capital NUH uh. The was to lavender as banana popsicles are to bananas. I adore a good fresh lavender but this was not a clear astringent lavender, it was a chemical maelstrom of lavender. It has a heavy alcohol top note, which is to be expected with a toilette water but it hung on much longer than I wanted, but the powdery middle note was just odd and it lasted much too long in that middle range of too strong to be two hours old. Then the bottom note is too much Grandmas hankie drawer for me, though it was more in the muted range I expected.

My advice if you want to try it because you like that old fashioned type of scent is to apply it properly- spray into the air and walk through it, never apply directly to the skin. Or try using it as a light room spray or closet spray. I don't want to preach here but gone are the days of women wearing heavy scents into work and getting away with it. So many of us are crammed into more reconditioned air and we all need to be sensitive to the noses of our coworkers. No one wants to be remembered as that strongly stinky person in the office. Your scent should be special to you and to anyone who is close enough to share it in your personal space.

I always stocked up on micellar water products when I went to France - they've used it & loved it for years.  It was supposedly invented for Parisian women because the water in Paris is so "hard".  The water is hard there, I can vouch for that & that is why the pharmacy was always one of my first stops when arriving in Paris.  Hard water makes it difficult to remove all your makeup & tends to dry out the skin.  Also, micellar water is wonderful for cleaning your skin even if you are not wearing makeup.

This is really good micellar water.  It barely has a scent & does not irritate my skin or around my eyes.  I use this water on a cotton pad to remove eye makeup and foundation.  I even use it to cleanse my skin when I do not wear makeup.  Just squeeze the water on to a disposable cotton pad, hold over your eye for about 15 seconds, then gently wipe away the makeup.  You will probably need more than one pad to clean your face.  I like "Swisspers" brand cotton rounds - you can buy them on Amazon or at Costco, etc.

This stuff is not magic, it's science & it's been around for a long time.  The micelle surfactant molecule is suspended in liquid/water and kind of grabs on to the dirt/oils/makeup on your face & doesn't allow it to stick on your face.  (That is my simple, non-scientist explanation.)  There is no irritation - even around eyes.  And the skin actually feels clean without rinsing with tap water - really!  When you use it, it seems like you are just using regular tap water except it actually dissolves/grabs the goo/makeup/dirt off your face.

Quickly and easily removes makeup with no oily residue. Apply to a cotton ball or makeup remover pad and after a few swipes, your hard to remove eye makeup disappears. No burning eyes. It's very much just like water!

Honestly I don't feel totally clean if I just use this cleansing water. I have started washing my face and then using this afterward to be sure I got all the makeup and dirt off. There is no greasy or sticky feeling after you use it. It doesn't bother my eyes at all. My skin feels moisturized and clean. This water does get off dirt and makeup even after I cleanse with cleanser and water.

I used just this water at night for a few days and got a small breakout. After switching to cleansing first and then using the water, the breakout cleared up. I have combination, acne-prone skin.
summary: Honestly I don't feel totally clean if I just use ...

reviewText: I've tried a different Vichy facial cleanser in the past, but this one is far superior.  It doesn't have an overwhelming scent, goes on easily, and wipes practically all of my make-up off on the first go around with a tissue, What I really like about this Vichy product is that I don't have to use water as a finishing touch so that I can just cleanse my face and then, if needed, re-apply new makeup.  Good product.

Vichy's Micellar Cleansing Water is fantastic! The absence of alcohol in Vichy's Micellar Cleansing Water means the product is gentler on skin and ideal for those with sensitive skin!. The product is perfect for cleansing, toning, or removing makeup. I have used it to remove heavy makeup, including thick fiber mascara, and it does a fantastic job. My skin always feels soft and refreshed after using Vichy's Micellar Cleansing Water and it doesn't leave an oily residue. I like that it comes in a smaller bottle with a sturdy lid, perfect for taking on trips.Garnier SkinActive Micellar Cleansing Water All-in-1 Cleanser & Waterproof Makeup Remover, 13.5 floz The price is comparable to Garnier SkinActive Micellar Cleansing Water All-in-1 Cleanser & Waterproof Makeup Remover - though Garnier smells a little nicer (this is subjective). I would definitely recommend this product.

reviewText: I was a little nervous at first about using this after reading the reviews, but this product is absolutely awesome. It is a very mild micellar water that isn't even slightly irritating to my sensitive eyes. (I use a regular eye makeup remover on my eyes.) The beauty of this product is that you can use it for any cleanups after you finish cleansing to take off random bits of eye makeup that may have been left behind. I also use it on a large cotton pad and clean my whole face with it - mainly to get all my face products off. I have some pretty pricey cleansers, and it's great to get all my makeup off with this micellar water first. The other great thing, when I use this alone (days when I don't have makeup on and just want to quickly cleanse), it doesn't leave my skin feeling dry and tight. I have normal to dry skin, and this works really well for me.
summary: Excellent, non-drying and not irritating  - great product

reviewText:
Vichy products are generally the best I've ever tried.  And I've tried them all from higher end to drug store.  Maybe I'm too picky and I expect too much from the promises.

This does exactly what it says.  It cleanses and removes and tones. I use Estee Lauder Double Wear Mascara which doesn't smudge in the rainiest of weather and it's a bear to get off. This water wipes it clean without rubbing and with one stripe.  I do use flat cotton squares instead of cotton balls but it's awesome

I have become such a fan of micellar water products in the last few years, because they're a convenient way to cleanse and tone my face at the same time. I don't typically rely on this product as an everyday cleanser, but it is very helpful on occasion, especially for taking off stubborn eye makeup. Mascara in particular is no match for this brand, since one or two swipes with a cotton pad seems to do the trick. It's worth mentioning that the back of the bottle claims that it's safe for eyes, but that didn't hold true for me. I opened one eye accidentally for one second while applying this and it immediately stung. This is definitely not eye-friendly or at least it isn't for me.

With that being said, it is very friendly to sensitive skin. This is also alcohol free, so I didn't feel any drying effect that would typically occur with some of the other toners that I've used in the past. The only thing is that this product did leave my skin with a tacky feeling immediately afterwards. I didn't wash it off to see if the feeling would disappear. It took about a half hour, but the sticky, tackiness did eventually fade. I also didn't need to apply additional moisturizer or anything, thereafter. A huge plus is that this paraben free, which always gets a star in my book. The fragrance is one of my favorite aspects, because it reminds me a lot of rose water, which I love.  All in all, it's a decent product for convenient facial washing and toner. I do like how well it removes my makeup. I just have to remember to keep my eyes shut extremely tight during use.
summary: A Convenient Way to Cleanse and Remove Makeup at the Same Time

reviewText:
I have sensitive skin with occasional eczema outbreaks when my skin comes into contact with harsh cosmetics. Then follow that up by a quality retinol product followed up by a quality anti-aging moisturizer and eye cream. While the product definitely has its place in the skin care routine it's far from being the only thing needed (unless you happen to be quite young with genetics to die for).

reviewText:
From the female side of the family. I've tried this fragrance and it's not for me -- but at the same time, it is entirely what it claims to be, and that is why I give it 5 stars. There's nothing like a perfume or "eau de toilet" (as this is), to divide the reviews. Some love it -- "my go-to fragrance! 5 stars." Some hate it and give it 1. The thing is, perfume is about the most personal thing you can choose.

Crabtree and Evelyn is a renowned brand, the product comes in an attractive glass bottle with a good quality nozzle, and it delivers exactly what it promises. So if you're wondering if the fragrance is for you, take a look at the ingredients. Do you like sweet rose scent? This is full of it. How about vanilla and citrus? They are strong notes. Then there's patchouli -- it's here. Bergamot is another ingredient: it's what gives the perfume to Earl Gray tea. Then there's ambergris, not necessarily something you can smell, but a rare and expensive oil produced by sperm whales, and a classic ingredient in perfumes (fitting for one named for the whaling town of Nantucket).

Overall, the fragrance smells to me of vanilla and rose. It reminds me of the scent of traditional talcum powder. As I say, it's not my favorite -- but then, it is exactly what Nantucket Briar Eau de Toilet claims to be. You decide!
summary: If You Like Rose, Vanilla, Citrus and Patchouli, You'll Love Nantucket Briar
