reviewText:
I decided to try this as I was curious about the claim on the front of the box "new re-plumping texture, daily sensitive skin anti-agine fill-in care, anti-wrinkle, firmness, even skin tone, broad spectrum SPF 25". Wow that promises a lot.

I was curious how they got this approved through the FDA and what the active ingredients were to achieve those results. The FDA did indeed approve this as a drug, the drug facts on the side of the box show the active ingredients are three sunscreens (avobenzone 3%, octisalate 5%, and octocrylene 7%). It lists the product's uses as a sunscreen and to use it before going in the sun. This is a paraben-free product.

The other side of the box states "for deep wrinkles, loss of firmness and uneven skin tone". These are said to be accomplished by the ingredients Vitamin C, Mannose to "fade out irregularities by by optimizing the interaction of light with the skin on application" and Hyaluronic Acid to "smooth the skin immediately". It also has Madecassocide and Neurosensine. This side panel says to use morning and night (the drug side of the box says to use it before going into the sun).

It's fragrance is light. The applicator is pointed with a tiny hole to allow minute amounts to be squeezed out of the tube at a time. I applied it thinly. It went on smoothly almost like gliding. I found it not thick or suffocating feeling on the skin.

As to the SPF for daily wear I need something higher than 25 as I live in bright sunny Houston and get sunburned with less than SPF 46 on while driving my car and dashing from the car to stores. I am skeptical about all the claims made for this but remain open minded. Since the SPF is lower than I need and the price is high I rate this 4 stars = I Like It. I use EltaMD SPF 46 clear every morning and I use a beige face powder with SPF 50 for touch ups during the day to prevent sunburn.

I ordered this cream for both myself and my wife to use. We have not tried or even heard of this brand before. Honestly, these higher-end skin care creams seem almost indistinguishable from each other. French or similar European origin, dermatologists endorsement, slick marketing, pharma-esque packaging, premium pricing, and on. There is nothing wrong with this I suppose, and competition is good for us consumers.

Our initial impression is good. The combination of a broad spectrum SPF25 sunscreen with a Vitamin C/Hyaluronic Acid moisturizing cream makes this product stand out a bit. It seems appealing as a good all-around daily use product and since it covers a few different bases one could almost consider it somewhat of a value in that sense.

The cream is rather light and rubs in easily. I can definitely feel it's moisturizing effect. It has a barely perceptible scent to it which is not at all offensive. I have rather sensitive skin and have not as of yet had any adverse reactions. We will continue using and expand on our impressions.

Worth the money! Totally recommend and will stick with this dryer forever!! Hair will stay healthy and if you want the salon results a professional dryer is really a necessity!!

If I had never owned a chi and had been using a Remington or something than I probably would have loved this - it does seem to be of good quality but didn't come close to my chi - the chi dryer dries my hair much faster leaves it smoother and shinier

This is far and away the best blow dryer I've ever used- nothing I've ever bought, commercially comes close.
The best tools do the job and get the best results...
My hair has never looked better- if you're going to use a blow dryer
on your hair-this is the one to purchase.
summary: Babyliss Pro BABNT6610 Portofino 660 2000-Watt Nano Titanium Ionic blowdryer

reviewText: great power to blow out smoothy shinny hair.  not heavy and it has a beautiful sleek design.  you can feel its power in your hands

high quality product, of course, it is Babyliss. I knew when I was looking to purchase a new hair dryer I was going to stick with the Babyliss brand, because I am in love with the flat iron. This product has lived up to my expectations, will continue to use Babyliss styling products on my precious hair!
summary: wish it had more temperature settings, but overall a great product!

reviewText: I found this BaByliss drier easy to handle, except for the fact that I couldn't figure out how to use the various heat settings with which the dryer is equipped.  There are two rows of small, easy to push,buttons and I thought that by pushing them, there would be a difference is temperature settings or speed, or both.  I guess I have't figured it out yet, but I will.  And, it definitely made my hair look shiny.

Honestly, I have no idea what this is supposed to do for my face in the long run. I take care of the problem areas of my skin with other products so even if it did some small thing, I'd never know. What I do know is the superfine mist feels awesome when my skin is overheated or tired during the day which will be a lot during the summer. The mist is cool and slightly moisturizing without any daily long-term effects like greasiness or astringency. I've been using it a couple of weeks and had no breakouts which means it passed a major product test for me. In winter I would probably call this more of a luxury than a necessary beauty product but as we go into summer and the hot, damaged skin season, it seems more like something good to have on hand as a treat.
summary: Delicate, cooling mist feels great on overheated skin

reviewText:
I love this mist. It feels lovely going on. It is refreshing. I feel that it is quite hydrating. I recently got rosacea after using medication. It is has been quite irritated and uncomfortable. Using this periodically throughout the day gave me the same effect as a moisturizer but without the irritation of applying it. Even putting cream on can be uncomfortable but this is always soothing.

It looks lovely over make-up. It gives a diffused, dewy look. But this is also where it falls short. The spray is a perfect delicate mist, except for a couple of big drops. So if you apply over makeup or a moisturizer, there will be a runny spot that smears. I've had mixed luck just touching up the spot but I wish I could get that dewy soft look without it.

The bottle is huge enough that you can use it generously. And you will want to because it is so lovely.

I don't see any benefits provided by this spray. The stars I'm giving are for the great design of the bottle. I wish I had a bottle like this for all my sprays, it's right between being a mist and a spray so it layers on your skin nicely. But I've used this on myself repeatedly now and see no benefits or any kind of difference on my skin. I don't recommend it, seems like a gimmicky waste of money.
summary: The stars I'm giving are for the great design of the bottle

reviewText:
I don't really get it. I've been using this product for a few weeks, and I've not noticed any benefit. My skin doesn't feel or look different. I can see where a mist would feel refreshing after working out, or during the summer. I think it's important to moisturize right after washing my face with clean water, to help retain the moisture. It's also my understanding that, under most circumstances, minerals and other nutrients work from the inside out, not sprayed on top just to evaporate.

I'm not sure what I was expecting with this spray. As mentioned, this will probably be refreshing on a hot day. But I'm just not seeing any other benefit.
summary: Didn't really do anything for my skin, but could be refreshing on a hot day. Not something I'll restock.

reviewText:
I'm not sure what this product is supposed to be.  I will say what I like about it.  I love that I can mist my face and arms while having a hot flash.  I have found no difference in the appearance or feel of my skin.  On a hot summer day, it is a cool refreshing mist.

Directions for Use:  apply to skin in a fine mist.  Wait for a few moments and gently pat dry.  A daily care product to be used at anytime during they day or evening.

It doesn't say where to apply it...face? body?  Is it a quick sponge bath, to refresh or a face product?  Better instructions are a must.
summary: Refreshing mist on a hot day.

reviewText: I have a condition called keratosis pilaris on my legs and my face. I have tried many products to help with this. Some work and some do not. I have been using this for about a week and I am pretty pleased with the results. First of all, parts of my face are extremely dry, while other parts are somewhat oily. I find that this spray works well for my combination skin. It feels moisturized, but not greasy. I wash my face with a charcoal soap, then spray this on and allow it to dry naturally and apply my makeup as usual. I also use it when I need a refresher midday and before bed. I love it!

My wife won't put any chemicals or weird things on her skin. She sticks primarily to pure oil products that don't contain things such as alcohol or preservatives. She has tried Vichy a number of times after bathing and found it pleasant, but she feels inconclusive on its benefits. It is always difficult to determine whether certain products are really having a positive effect. This would include things such as skin care products, vitamins and food supplements. It can only be judged on a subjective level which is prone to all kinds of variables. Unless something has immediately caused a bad reaction or problem; tough to tell.
It seems that there is nothing bad in the Vichy, which is why she agreed to try it. So far she says its nice.

To be honest, it feels like I'm spraying myself with a mist of water, and I don't see any difference between this spa water and regular water.  I'm not really sure what it is supposed to do, but I do feel a bit silly misting myself with water and don't feel like it's has any real beneficial properties.
summary: Seems like a fine mist of regular water, no noticeable effects

reviewText:
Testing this as a free product from the Amazon Vine program.

This is a very nice and easy to use product that has become part of the daily routine.
Fine mist spray that moisturizes withour ever feeling greasy, or like you're wearing a mudpack.
So easy to spray and go, let it sit for a minute and gently dry.
Time will tell on the results, but my skin feels great.
The research backing up this product seems credible after an internet search.

I am familiar with Vichy products and have always had a positive experience with products from this brand.  I wasn't sure what to expect from a can of expensive water.  The bar was low for this.

Unfortunately, I had a skin reaction to a food allergy and my skin was dry, irritated, and a bumpy, broken out mess.  Having previously dealt with this condition, I know that it takes about 2 weeks to completely heal.  The Vichy Mineralizing Thermal Spray Water arrived on day 2 of my reaction.  Ive used it daily for the past 5-days and the bumps/irritation has almost completely disappeared.  The skin that Ive used it on is no longer itchy or dry.  I have no new bumps or dermatitis.

Im sold on this product.

Although I prefer to use sunscreen only when Im going to be jogging, working in the yard or visiting a theme park, Ive been using this for about a week for both moisturizing and sun-blocking purposes.  All in all, it works well for both of those needs.  Like many sunscreen lotions, theres a distinctbut in this case faintscent, likely due to the sun-blocking chemicals necessary to attain a given SPF level.  Once applied, the scent fades quickly.  The lotion is on the thick side, more like a skin cream.
summary: Works well as moisturizer and as sunscreen

reviewText: I've been looking for a daytime moisturizer with an SPF of higher than the usual 15, because my skin burns easily and I want to avoid (or delay!) discoloring age spots. I've tried a few moisturizers with higher SPF, but they've all been too heavy and caused skin problems. This lotion is a broad spectrum SPF 25, but not much heavier than the Olay Total Effects Featherweight Moisturizer SPF 15 I've been using lately. At night, I use Neutrogena Healthy Skin Anti-Wrinkle Night Cream, but in the winter it dries out my skin, so a good daytime moisturizer is crucial. I think this combination will work well for me.

I am disappointed in Vichy's facial lotion with SPF 25 as it is greasy and thick. It sits heavy on the skin and literally feels heavy on the skin. It has a too strong fragrance that does not dissipate, I keep breathing it in and the fragrance gave me a headache. I am going to stick with Elta MD UV Daily Clear SPF 46 (or 40) as it is a light daily facial SPF face lotion that I can use under makeup and it has no fragrance (and despite it feeling light and non-greasy it does work great to prevent sunburn).
summary: Greasy & Too Strong Fragrance (Gave Me a Headache)

reviewText: I received one bottle of Vichy Aqualia Thermal Sunscreen 24 HR Hydrating Fortifying Lotion, 1.6 FL. OZ.  It is Broad Spectrum SPF 25 Normal Skin.  It is suitable for sensitive skin and is allergy tested.  It is oil free, and does have a lightweight texture.  It feels light on your skin, spreads easily and absorbs quickly.  The scent reminds me of the beach.  UVA/UVB protection.
summary: Just What You Want In A Sunscreen

reviewText:
While I liked the SPF25 of this moisturizer, I didn't like the way if seemed to sit on the surface of my skin.  This gave my face a whitish cast and it "pilled" when I tried to rub it in.  That means when I tried to rub this product in, it would actually rub off instead leaving what looks like the residue left over when you use an old fashioned eraser all over my skin.  This residue had to be brushed off which, in turn, tended to create even more residue.  This also left residue and white streaks all around my neck by the end of the day.  I would not purchase this product again.

Update: I ran out of my regular sunscreen and, in a pinch, had to make this one work.  I found that when this product is used alone, as in clean, dry, naked skin without any serums, primers, anti-wrinkle cream, make-up, etc, that it didn't pill and it was much easier to rub in.  Being able to rub it in well also eliminated the whitish cast that it previously left on my skin.

So, if you are at an age where you can get by with just a moisturizer, then this sun screen would be worth a try because, as sun screens go, it's pretty moisturizing.  However, if you need to layer products to address other skin issues then this isn't the sun screen for you.  Maybe someday they will make a moisturizing sun screen like this that does "play well with other products" or that is a multi-tasker, eliminating the need to slather on so many products.  Until then,  this is better suited to younger skin.  And, if you need to use acne products you younger folks might run into the same pilling issues when you try and layer the two.

I've  since been using up my bottle on my hands.  Does a good job.  My hands definitely look better and feel softer and the high SPF is helping to prevent future age spots.
summary: What a mess, needs to be used alone

reviewText:
I wanted to find a good hydrating lotion that was good also to protect against skin damage. SPF is needed nowadays. I have sensitive skin, looking at the product it says its good for sensitive skin, even "soothes" it. Allergy tested.

First off it smelled, like old lady which I hate. I have people who love to kiss and hug on me, and the last thing they want to think of is "granny" getting past that, it felt oily on my skin, burned a little, made my eyes sting and I did not even get close to them! my sensitive skin broke out into redness and i instantly washed it off. It had to be the fragrance in it and the tocopheryl acetate which is so well known to cause an immune response( rash, redness burning)  in people with allergies/sensitive skin.

when will companies realize that stinky lotions are out? and harmful ingredients?

Excellent lotion/sunscreen.  Very moisturizing but doesn't sit on your skin making it feel greasy.  It absorbs relatively quickly and most importantly for me for my sensitive skin, it doesn't cause me to turn red or break out as with much cheaper creams.

I confess that I love the Vichy line. The products work well with my sensitive skin, and you don't need to apply a ton of product for it to be effective.
This is one that takes a bit of getting used to. At first I applied too much. I have found that the best application method is to put a bit in your palm, lightly rub palms together and smooth over your face, all very quickly.
It seemed to give me a fresh 'brightened' look that I really like.

Usually scented skin products irritate or even burn my skin, but this did not.

Hydrates nicely. The container is a bit cheaply built (plastic), but the lotion works pretty well.

Yes, it's hydrating. Yes, it has SPF.

I prefer L'Oreal's La Roche Posay products over the Vichy one, but this one is great too!

This is a light, oil-free lotion sunscreen. It comes in a pump dispenser so you can dispense a precise pea-sized amount.  It absorbs really quickly and doesn't leave too much of an greasy feel, although I don't think this will be suitable for my oily skin once summer arrives again.

There is a moderate to heavy fragrance. It is quite pleasant and doesn't smell like sunscreen, but I wish companies would leave fragrances out of their face products.

This is almost exactly what I love in my facial lotions. I use glymed spf 30. The scent on this is that of regular body lotion, I am not fond of scents on my facial lotion. I do love that there is SPF 25, I see an esthetician for peels and they have always told me that you should use spf. I have had no problems with it leaving white on my face. Sometime the glymed cream needs to be rubbed in more than regular lotion due to spf. This made my skin feel a tad oily and that is something else I didn't care for. All in all, it's okay, it's not great. I would keep using this but doubtful it would replace my glymed.

Goes on light and doesn't feel greasy. My skin does feel less dry after using this for a week.  Claims to have SPF 25, which is a bonus. The scent can be a little overpowering but does fade away but if you are very sensitive to strong scents, you might be bothered by the scent.
summary: Goes on light and doesn't feel greasy. My skin ...

reviewText:
My wife likes the Vichy Aqualia Thermal Hydrating lotion - which is actually a sunscreen and a moisturizer according to her.

She likes that it is a moisturizer and a sunscreen 2-in-1 product but wished that it was a lighter texture. She is however, more concern with any reactions to her skin as she has mild eczema and this lotion does not seem to have any adverse reaction.

Good product for people with sensitive skin.
summary: Nice 2-in-1 product i.e. sunscreen and moistuizer, good for people with sensitve skin

reviewText: This is a very nice sunscreen/moisturizer. There isn't a strong sunscreen smell and it feels nice on my skin. A little bit goes a long way with this one. If you use too much of it at once it can take longer to absorb into your skin. It definitely does a good job of moisturizing and protecting my skin.

Okay as a sunscreen but not a great moisturizer. It does have a "lightweight lotion" texture as the description says, but it didn't absorb easily so it felt heavy on my skin. Also it's not good for use on eye area; if I sweat a little or my eyes water, it gets into my eyes and burns.

This is a nice quality product with a very intense smell that I immediately had to wash off as I was applying my makeup over it. The smell is meant to be, I am sure, quite pretty. However, everyone knows that you don't always love the perfumes that others are wearing. So, when I cosmetics company adds a scent that is so strong, and it is meant to be applied right under your nose -- this is just a huge mistake. I had to give it one star, because the smell actually made me feel like I was choking. However, I would truly not recommend this to any friend of mine, because so many of us suffer from allergies. In the past when I've purchased a face cream that I don't really care for, I have at least been able to repurpose it as a hand cream. Not in this case, because the perfume is so offensively strong. Absolutely not recommended..
summary: I had to immediately remove it! Beware: Dreadful smell!!

reviewText: Marvelous moisturizer! Works beautifully to keep face moist without any greasiness. I use more moisturizers in the fall and winter months and this lotion is doing a fabulous job of preventing those dry patches. Has not caused any breakouts that come with some of the lesser quality moisturizers that I have tried.
summary: Works beautifully to keep face moist without any greasiness

reviewText: as expected, I love this scent, and this brand for hand lotion.. it works.. keeps my hands moisturized..

This Crabtree & Evelyn product lives up to the brand's high standard, with premium scent and feel commensurate with the high price. It's packaged attractively as well, in a metallic-feeling tube with a high-quality screw top within a cardboard outer box attractive enough to give as a gift. The product inside the tube is white and rich-feeling, adding a lot of moisture without an oily feeling; a little dab goes a long way. Its scent is sharply citron/citrus without much of an afternote, smelling nice when it goes on but fading fairly quickly as it should. When applied thinly, the product disappears into the skin in seconds, leaving it feeling soft and pleasant for several hours afterward it's a really nice cream for hands or faces. Do note that it's so rich-feeling because it's based on macadamia nut oil, which might be an allergy problem (I actually checked it with a friend with a nut allergy and found the product didn't provoke a reaction from momentary contact, but it's probably best to be cautious). Apart from that, it's highly recommended.

I love the Crabtree & Evelyn hand cream. I typically am a lotion and hand sanitizer user. While lotion is great, sometimes once it is on my hands, there is not a noticeable, lasting difference beyond maybe a few hours or so where my hands feel softer. The Crabtree & Evelyn ultra moisturizing hand therapy, by contrast, has that lasting effect. It goes on and does not feel greasy or weird. My hands actually did feel softer for the entire day and over time. I felt like this cream was perfect for combating the effects of the current weather on my skin - cold and dry. Also, it smells fresh and natural, which was another thing I quite liked.
summary: Makes A Noticeable And Lasting Difference

reviewText: This hand lotion was great, it smelled fabulous and left my hands feeling moisturized. During the winter, my hands get terribly dry and cracked and this lotion seemed to do a good job bringing them back to normal.
summary: Moisturizes well and smells great too!

reviewText: While I really liked the scent of this Crabtree & Evelyn hand cream, I did not particularly enjoy that it did not absorb quickly into my hands and, in fact, I had to use tissue in order to turn the handle in my bathroom.  It did, however, make my hands feel soft and moisturized so I guess that's a trade-off for its non-absorbency.

My thoughts about what makes this product really unique...

I love that this very creamy lotion is infused with macadamia oil.  It also has honey and lemon infused in it, too.  When I first used it...I thought that it might be just a bit too emollient but it isn't.  It seemed to be absorbed into my skin immediately with no oily feel or residue.  I also love that this product says it will also condition nails and cuticles.

My thoughts about the target audience for this product...

I think that anyone who has dry hands will appreciate this product.  It left my hands smoother and less dry.  The scent was subtle, too.  The tube is rather pretty, too.  I don't mind allowing it to sit on my kitchen windowsill.

My thoughts about ways to use this product...

I think that this product is mostly intended for hands but using it on arms and elbows would not be a bad idea.  I make sure to really massage it into my nails and cuticles.

Finally...what the potential buyer might enjoy about this product...

I think that potential buyers will like the feel, the mild scent and the smoothing benefits of using this product.

I'm a lotion addict - I'm always looking for the 'next best thing' when it comes to keeping my hands soft and smelling nice especially in this bitter cold and dry winter weather. While I have my old stand-by favorites I'm always trying new ones and looking for something better.  This one! This was love at first try! It's thick and rich and does a wonderful job of moisturizing my dry hands, it absorbs fairly quickly and doesn't feel greasy and keeps my hands feeling soft for a long time.  I'm absolutely in love with the scent - it's a slightly lemony/woodsy scent, it's not very strong or over-powering but it does linger and I find myself smelling my hands allll day long and it brings a smile to my face. Even my husband likes it and commented on how soft it made his rough dry hands, and he likes the scent as well. I will absolutely be getting more of this when this tube is gone which at the rate I'm using it will be all too soon.
summary: My new favorite - Crabtree & Evelyn Ultra-Moisturizing Hand Therapy (Citron Honey & Coriander scent)

reviewText: This Crabtree & Evelyn hand cream is a very high quality product. It's a luxurious and rich hand cream that's very effective at adding moisture to my dry hands. This is a thick cream and only a small amount is needed with each application. My hands absorb this cream quickly and immediately feel noticeably softer after each use without feeling greasy or sticky. This cream feels similar to L'Occitane dry skin hand cream and seems of equal quality to me. The Crabtree & Evelyn cream does have a moderately strong scent (as does L'Occitane), so for those who don't like fragrance this may not be the best choice. I'm not a huge fragrance fan, but I find the scent interesting and pleasant. This cream contains a long list of ingredients, but I mostly smell a fragrant blend of lemon and herbs. I don't find the scent overwhelming, though any stronger and it would be too much for my taste. For those with nut allergy, macadamia nut oil is the second ingredient listed. The tube and outer packaging are pretty for gifting, and this cream is made in the USA. I really enjoy this Crabtree & Evelyn cream. It's an effective luxury hand cream that I'm likely to purchase in the future and highly recommend, except to those people who prefer unscented creams.
summary: Effective Luxury Hand Cream With A Moderately Strong But Pleasant Fragrance

reviewText: This hand cream is emollient without making your hands greasy.  It has a nice refreshing citrus scent to it.  I am going to take it to work and use it there for an nice pick me up during the day.  This leaves my hands super soft...I love it!
Love this stuff! After just one use my skin looks less shockingly pale. Only negative to me is that I don't love the smell.

I do like this and use it every other day.  I use the mousse every 3rd or 4th day and use this in between.  I took off one star because after a couple of coats it does look a bit orange.  One coat is ok.
Works well. Great smell! Doesn't smell like a fake tanner but rather more refreshing.
summary: Great smell! Doesn't smell like a fake tanner but ...

reviewText: I really like this stuff, you get quite a good amount. Got it as a sample from sephora but it worked so well i really wanted to buy it in the full size. gives you a nice glow for day to day or in winter. it does have a smell but its not a deal breaker for me!
I have repurchased this so many times. I refuse to go in the sun so it's perfect. The color is natural and the scent is not too strong.
I have used this daily moisturizer for years now. It gives my fair skin a a natural glow and doesn't have that weird self tanning smell.

January isn't the best time to review a sunblock product, but what I can say about Jack Black Sun Guard right now is that it is scent-free and feels good on the skin. Based on putting my hands in the water as a test, it is water-resistant. It isn't greasy, but it feels rich and does moisturize the skin. I will come back to this review when the weather is warmer and report on its sun-blocking properties.

*** UPDATE: Now that the weather is warm, I have used this product on several occasions, including sitting outside for hours at a parade, and found that it works well as a sunblock.

Jack Black Sun Guard SPF 45 Oil-Free goes on smooth with very minimal tacky sunscreen feel left behind.  It is oil free and formulated not to run into the eyes.  The directions state to reapply after 80 minutes.  That is a good amount of time for most outdoor activities.  This is a nice product and one that I would definitely get again. Well worth having on hand to slow down those solar rays from aging the skin.
Feels good on my face. It's not thick and disappears quickly without any residue. I am a fan of the jack black product line. Recommend

Active Ingredients: Zinc Oxide 8%, Octinoxate 7.5%, Octisalate 3%, Inactive Ingredients: Plantago Lanceolata (Plantago) Leaf Extract*, Leontopodium Alinum (Edelweiss) Extract Water*, Calendula Officinalis (Calendula) Flower Extract*, Cyclomethicone, Ethyl Hexyl Isononanoate, Ascorbyl Palmitate (Vitamin C), Sodium Chloride, Phenoxyethanol, Butylene Glycol, Iodopropynyl Butylcarbamate Dimethicone/PEG-10/15 crosspolymer, Lauryl PEG-9 Polydimethylsiloxyethyl Dimethicone, Cyclopentasiloxane, Dimethicone/Vinyl Dimethicone Crosspolymer. *Certified Organic .

I make my own sunscreen as well as I purchase sunscreen for times when I do not have time to make any since I need to surf. For that reason, when I purchase a sunscreen mix, I need the same formula as I use when I make my own organic sunscreen mix since it only requires few ingredients but for more protection like my nose, I bump the zinc. Zinc is what you see surfers put on their nose for protection. The more zinc, the more protection but it means a mix that is more like a mud since zinc is a powder that I purchase and add to VCO. For a small investment, sunscreens may offer me the possibility of avoiding sun burn, pain, cancer, medical bills, pain killers, etc. that come with exposure to the sun. For that reason, choosing a formula with the least amount of ingredients but high zinc oxide is the best solution. A good sunscreen formula should not have more than a handful of ingredients, certified organic at least 95% and FREE OF; fragrances, biologically harmful chemicals like Avobenzone, Oxybenzone, or UV Chemical absorbers, paraben, phthalates, PABA and 1,4 dioxane and alcohol. What goes on the skin is the same as being consumed through the skin. Chemicals, alcohol and fragrances are no protection for the skin.

Alcohol, Perfume & More Chemicals... No wonder there is no image of the back labelling or any image of the ingredients anywhere not even on Sun Burn's Website. This is sold at Macy's and Nordstrom. The fact is that when you pay as much as eighty for 160z, you're mostly paying for a lot of fancy packaging and marketing, including the cost of the supermodel spokeswoman in the Magazine ads. It gets worse when a cosmetics company is pushing different potions for day and night, for the face, eyes, lips, neck, body and feet. That really adds upwhich is exactly what that company is counting on.

I really like this Sun Screen because it is so light on the skin, that it is easy to forget you have it on.  Unfortunately, being winter it's hard to test this fully, but I did put it on for cross country skiing and love that it did not have a heavy oily feel. It goes on clean and for the sunny, snow reflecting day I spent skiing, it seemed to work fine.

I am looking forward to testing it at the pool this summer, but if it is as water resistant as it claims...this self confessed SunScreenaphobe may have found his new solution.

We spend a lot of time outside exposed to the sun.  I wear contacts and usually sunscreen runs in my eyes and burns like the devil.  Jack Black Sun Guard Sunscreen SPF 45 spreads on nicely and doesn't burn my eyes.  It wears very nicely as the day goes on.  It feels more like a daily moisturizer than a sunscreen.
it will be my new go to sunscreen.

I am a fan of the Jack Black products and use them daily. This sunscreen is indicative of how exceptional their products are. The creme easily rubs into the skin leaving no greasy residue. Especially impressive is that when doing physical activities (cycling in my case) the sunscreen does not run or sting the eyes. THis is a superior product and recommended without reservations

Light weight and non-greasy. It worked wonderfully, and I love using it on my face every morning. It appears to last all day as well.

Great product and I'd highly recommend it.

This sunscreen is non-greasy, unscented, and easy to apply. Its the perfect consistency; not too thick and not too watery. Its described as very water resistant and thats the truth. Its almost waterproof and getting it off your hands after applying it takes some doing. Ive worn it swimming and cycling and its held up excellent. Its expensive for a sunscreen but a little goes a long way. However, due to the price I mainly use it on my face and use cheaper stuff on my body. The bottom line is that it does everything its supposed to do and it does it very well.

You would think that a product like this would be best tested in the depths of the long hot summer. However, I recently had a business trip to Vermont and had to spend hours on the windy, sun drenched slopes at Sugarbush. While my face was cold, I didn't get wind or sun burn despite the conditions. While it was sunny, the wind blew wet snow from the trees on my face and the sunscreen didn't get washed away. I think that really helped.

An SPF rating of 45 is low by some standards (I have seen numbers MUCH higher) but having a product that both moisturizes and protects you skin is worth more than one that just filters out the sun. I am pretty sure it made a difference because my friend on the same assignment didn't use anything on his face and he came back with bright red, tender skin. Also, I missed a spot on my ear lobe and it was a little red at the end of the day. Not the most scientific test, I admit. Also, I didn't compare another product side by side (how I prefer to try these things) but there is no denying that this product did what it says it will do.

Truth told - I like Jack Black products and use a lot of them. This is one that will get a lot more use this summer and I'll update this if the brutal beating sun changes anything. Until then, this is a recommended product.
summary: Tested it on the slopes at Sugarbush, VT

reviewText: I like the light, non- greasy feeling when I put this on.  I have used it for 5 rounds of Golf under the hot LA sun and it protected me and I did not get a sun burn.

This SPF 45 sunscreen stood up to a sweaty, longer-than-planned 4-hour hike through the sunny Arizona desert mountains.  Before the hike, I slathered it on all exposed areas, and set out for my two-hour hike.  Oops, I need to learn to read maps better.

The lotion was fairly heavy going on, but I gave it a few minutes to sink into my skin before I went hiking.  Sweat didn't seem to bother it in the least, although it did bother me - I was hot and tired.  I had no sunburn redness on my skin by the time I made it home.

The next day, I took a several-mile walk but on sidewalks instead desert trails.  I used the sunscreen but forgot to put it on my exposed ears, and by the time I got home, my ears, and only my ears, were quite red.  I've used the sunscreen several times since then, and am quite happy with it.

It protects against both UVA and UVB rays, but I think that is pretty standard now.  What impressed me most was its staying power, its excellent protection, and the lack of any overpowering fragrance.

Jack Black Sun Guard Sunscreen SPF 45 Oil Free And Water Resistant is one of the highest recommended sunscreens from our Dermatologist. For anyone who has experienced skin cancer like some of our family members, finding a good sunscreen is extremely important. Paying twenty dollars or more for a 4 ounce tube of a great protective suncreen may seem expensive, but it is not in comparison to hundreds of dollars spent to the dermatologist appointments to treat sun damage.

Our dermatologist said the only sunscreens that offer total skin protection from the damaging rays of the sun will contain one of 2 ingredients- either Zinc Oxide or Titanium Dioxide. This Jack Black contains 8% Zinc Oxide and will give you total protection. You also need both UVA and UVB protection, and this sunscreen gives you both, so again you are totally protected.

Finding a sunscreen that gives you the total dermatologist protection is only half of what makes a great sunscreen. The other half is that it is not greasy or oily and will not run into your eyes and burn them when you are sweating or swimming outdoors. This Jack Black Sun Guard Sunscreen is not only non greasy and non oily, but it is super light weight, not containing any oils or parabens.  It's dermatology tested and has a very light scent, that won't overwhelm you or clash with your deodorant or fragrances. This 5 Star Sunscreen gives you total protection, won't run or drip into your eyes, goes on super light with a light fragrance- it's everything you would want from a totally protective dermatologist recommended sunscreen.
summary: Light Weight, Light Scent, Strong Protection

reviewText:
Here in Alaska, when the long days of light are here, you really need a safe, non irritating, effective sun protection that will last all day and into the night.

This is a well formulated, non greasy skin protection that is superior to other sunscreen protections.  It has a great creamy texture and applies evenly. This is a wonderful sun-block that provides wonderful protection against burning, 'blotching' and blistering from the sun's rays. No more pain after sun exposure!.

The container is well designed for portable and effective protection from the sun's harmful rays both UVA and UVB,  Allows easy, non-wasteful application.

Like it very much!!!
summary: Protects you very well-great for the Land of The Midnight Sun!

reviewText: I have two other sunscreens with zinc oxide:  a daily protection sunscreen made by Eucerin with an SPF of 30 and a Neutrogena one made for sensitive skin with an SPF of 50.  Of the three, my skin seems to absorb this one the best but it still left a bit of a white visible cast on my face after thoroughly rubbing in it.  My dermatologist wants me to stick with sunscreens that use zinc and/or titanium dioxide due to concerns that sunscreens with oxobenzone (a common ingredient in may sunscreens) actually promote the growth of skin cancers even though they prevent sunburns, so I keep trying different alternatives in the hopes of finding one that goes on as smoothly as the ones I'm no longer supposed to use.  I wouldn't say that this product is ideal in that regard, and perhaps my desire isn't reasonable because I understand that the way the zinc and titanium dioxide sunblocks work is that they actually provide a physical barrier to the sun's harmful rays.  Maybe that whitish cast on the screen is unavoidable.
summary: Not quite as chalky as other sunscreens with zinc oxide

reviewText: It's difficult to get fired up about sunscreen, but Jack Black's oil-free SPF 45 Sun Guard has kindled a few flames.  First, it works well as a general facial moisturizer--something I wouldn't typically attribute to a sunscreen--so thumbs up there.  Second, the product smells amazingly "chemical free" for sunscreen, particularly one with such a high SPF, so there's another feather in the cap.  Third, it doesn't run into the eyes like many another sunscreen out there, so it doesn't sting when the face gets wet or sweaty, making it a Triple Crown candidate in the sunscreen race.  It's typically on when I go running and hasn't let me down.  Good stuff.

We tried this sunscreen for the first time on a beach vacation in Central America. The sun was bright, we were on the beach for many hours every day and this sun screen really did it's job! It contains 8% zinc Oxide and I think that is why it does take a hefty amount of rubbing in to get the sun screen to disappear. I had to have my kids check to see if my face was white as a ghost! However, we used another sunscreen on the vacation as well (alba botanica).Alba Kids Sunblock SPF 45, 4 Ounce Both the Jack Black and the Alba have no parabens, no fragrances and no oils. However, I found that we needed to apply the Alba more often, especially after dips in the ocean. The Jack Black seemed to work better where this was concerned. This is a great little product and I plan on it being my go to sunscreen for pool season this summer.
summary: Excellent broad spectrum protection without Parabens, oils or fragrances

reviewText: I have used other Jack Black products so I am already a fan and the sun screen is another quality product. It fulfills my two main requirements which is that it protects from sun burn (which it does) and it does not leave an oily coat on your skin (which it also does). So this is an easy recommend. Hope this helps a little in making your decision.

I have sensitive skin and don't use any of the cheap sunscreens out there. I often use Neutrogena since it's a top brand that is dermatologist recommended. I'm beginning to see more options for us sensitive folk, and this is my first time trying Jack Black. Never heard of it 'til now, and I can't help but think of Jack Black the actor. I wonder if he lathers this on...

Hooray for oil-free options! This is essentially what I expected it would be - easy to apply but not too runny, doesn't irritate my skin, and doesn't leave my skin feeling greasy or oily. Most importantly, it protects me from getting burned! Also, an SPF of 45 is great as I prefer to use a minimum of SPF 30. My only gripe is the price for a small, 4-ounce bottle. It's a bit too much.

This is a really nice sun screen. I live in Colorado where the higher altitude means you need sunscreen if you indulge in winter sports. It goes on smoothly and leaves no greasy residue. It protects well in the winter sun. Can't wait to try it in the summer.

As you probably know, sun tan lotion can range in price from modest to very expensive.  I've usually found that the higher priced products are better (higher quality ingredients, etc.).  Unless, of course, you are buying your lotion at a resort, in which case everything is expensive!

Ive used this product before, during summer vacations etc. and it works very well.  I tend to burn easy, so a weeklong stint in Disney World in July meant lots of sun screen.

So, why Jack Black suntan lotion?  It definitely is high priced, at over $20 for a 4 ounce tube.  There are other products with similar ingredients for much less per ounce.  So on a strictly ingredient by ingredient, ounce for ounce basis, I would say you can get the same results elsewhere for less.

However, and it is a big however - the product goes a long way compared to some others.  It seems to have a higher percentage of zinc oxide and its other active ingredients in it than one might find in another brand.  It also has some inactive ingredients which are actually quite beneficial, as opposed to just being fillers.  Ive listed all the ingredients below.

This lotion also excels at being water resistant.  Ive used other lotions which come off easily in water, or wear fast when you perspire.  This one seems to stay on longer/better and I need fewer reapplications.  That alone can lower the cost per use.
 Also, It is really not oily at all.  You rub it in, and pretty much after that it is not noticeable as greasy or slippery on your skin.
Active Ingredients: Zinc Oxide 8%, Octinoxate 7.5%, Octisalate 3%, Inactive Ingredients: Plantago Lanceolata (Plantago) Leaf Extract*, Leontopodium Alinum (Edelweiss) Extract Water*, Calendula Officinalis (Calendula) Flower Extract*, Cyclomethicone, Ethyl Hexyl Isononanoate, Ascorbyl Palmitate (Vitamin C), Sodium Chloride, Phenoxyethanol, Butylene Glycol, Iodopropynyl Butylcarbamate Dimethicone/PEG-10/15 crosspolymer, Lauryl PEG-9 Polydimethylsiloxyethyl Dimethicone, Cyclopentasiloxane, Dimethicone/Vinyl Dimethicone Crosspolymer. *Certified Organic

I am not saying this is the only sunscreen out there, but it is a good one.  If you burn easily or just want good all around UV protection, this is a good product.  Again, there are less expensive alternatives, and based on your needs and the amount of time you spend in the sun and water, those might work fine for you.  If you need superior sun protection with exceptional water resistance, give this a try!
summary: Let The Sun Shine In! (But Not The UV)

reviewText:
We were warned about talc (a mineral) in our after bath powders so corn starch was the recommendation. Jack Black (spoiler, I'm a huge fan of their products) has offered a corn starch based power with a light lavender scent and I really like it. It's great for moisture absorption after bath and the "friction free" description seems to be accurate (ahem, it goes in your undies).

The scent is not over powering (I like that) and the container is easy to use - shaking out a handful is a snap. The only negative is that. like many Jack Black products, it has a premium price. Other than that, I like it and will buy it again.
summary: I like the scent, good moisture absorption qualities, friction-free works well on the naughty bits

reviewText: My wife loves this one .. very fine powder
This is expensive, but just use a small amount and it lasts. I use powder daily and my wife always complains about it. With this I use way less, and it just lasts better than your average powder.
Works well but very expensive Johnson's baby cornstarch one one third one quarter of the price works just as good
summary: Works well but very expensive Johnson's baby cornstarch one one ...

reviewText: Love it!

Super smooth and effective powder! There is a light citrus scent and the powder is extremely fine. A little goes far. I stay dry and no chafing. I have tried several others, like Gold bond etc, but JB Dry Down is much better and is non-talc, starch based. JBDD is a keeper!
summary: Jack Black powder is a winner!

reviewText: great
works very well!

Meh, it's alright as long as you realize it's basically just a fancy menthol cream. I'm prone to Amazon impulse buys and if you're reading this, you've probably done it too. I was taken in by the excellent advertising and I'm generally a fan of the high quality Jack Black line.  This one however, is just a pharmacy aisle cooling cream with "natural cures" of dubious effectiveness. I was underwhelmed and quickly went back to my $3 tube of Aspercreme.

Just so you know what's in it:

Menthol - The active ingredient and probably the only thing in this cream that does anything. Creates a cooling sensation as it evaporates which can be pleasant. However, a $2 cream at walgreens could do the same thing.

Dragon's blood - Actually an excellent dye and varnish, but a s***ty cure-all. It's a folk remedy with various and conflicting claims to all sorts of illnesses, none of which hold up to scientific scrutiny

Methylsulfonylmethane(MSM) - The oral agent for MSM shows some promise for the chronic treatment of arthritis and the topical form for rosacea and other inflammatory derm conditions. A real pharmacologic agent to be sure, but no data to any short term benefit to muscle pain/spasm.

Arnica - A herbal anti-inflammatory that has been used for centuries. Studies show possible long term benefit, but any short term topical effect would extremely dubious. A single dose of ibuprofen would seriously outperform it's anti-inflammatory properties even in the best of conditions.

Willowherb - A useful herb for many reasons - an ornamental, a sweetener, maybe even a food supplement provitamin. Just won't do jack s*** for your muscle pain.
summary: I was taken in by the excellent advertising and I'm generally a fan of the high ...

reviewText: This is a really soothing product when you have over done a bit in the gym or out on the roads riding your bike.  It's cooling and you can feel it working almost instantly.
great

It works...  Another great jack black product!  I'd been using this for over a year before I realized it had arnica as an ingredient.  I've used arnica gel and arnica pellets to reduce swelling, or avoid bruising after a fall or bump, but this adds instant pain relif and a wonderful herbal scent.  Yes, the first whif will clear your sinus's, which is an added benefit for me, but the scent doesn't last or transfer to clothing like ordinary menthol rubs.  Great for mornings when sinu congestion stiffens your neck.  My friend uses it on arthritic hands, and I've used it for pain in my back and shoulders.  It's soothing and the relief is nearly immediate, amazing.  I originally bought this after trying the shower gel.  I use it every day and it's a pleasure.  Refreshing and along with the hot water acts to soothe and clear morning stuffiness.
summary: Fabulous balm.  Another great Jack Black potion!

reviewText: This is a cooling, creamy balm that you apply to your joints and muscle aches. Dragon Ice feels cooling and mildly sinks in without smelling like a linament bomb. There are a variety of ingredients and the recommendation to apply it a few times over the day. I am good with that. For light duty muscle strains or joint aches in my legs, Dragon Ice is doing the trick. . . and the name is cool too! :-)

I don't think I would buy this, considering the level of performance (average) for the price (high). I'm fair/olive skinned and this made me look a little too yellow/orange. Aside from the nice fragrance, there was nothing special about this tanner. It isn't the worst, but it's not worth 5-stars or $50+.

I have naturally fair skin. I spend time in the sun and develop somewhat of a tan but my base is definitely fair. This product gave my skin a tone that was definitely more orange than bronze. With self tanners you have to be extremely diligent during application or you'll end up with streaks. I got a few streaks from this product but nothing major. My biggest issue is the resulting color. Maybe deeper skin tones would have better luck with this product. Sadly I can't recommend it for fair skin tones.
Not terribly difficult to put on, and it comes up with a decent tan. The fade is kind of choppy, but for a few days, my legs looked great! I'd definitely put this on my short list for next summer.
summary: Makes for a nice leg tan

reviewText:
My absolute favorite thing about this self-tanner is that it doesn't smell at all like your traditional self-tanner. It smells like a vanilla scented lotion.

It wasn't sticky at all and it went on very smooth. There is a little added color to help you see where it has been applied, but that color dissipates once you rub it in, so you'll still need to pay attention to where it has been applied.

As with all self-tanners, I've found that you do need to be careful when aplying this on knees or elbows. Apply scarcely or make sure that these dry areas are very well moisturized before applying the tanner, otherwise you run the risk of noticeable patches.

I felt like the color was nice and fairly natural. You do need to pay attention when applying in order to avoid streaks. I applied it using the Luxe tanning mitt, which was very soft and helped provide a smoother appearance  (but you still have to be thorough when applying otherwise you might miss a spot).

You cannot shower for 3 hours after applying the product, so you'll want to take that into consideration when deciding when to apply. I found that since the scent was nice, it wasn't a problem to apply the tanner and then go out about my day (although I would recommend waiting a few minutes before getting dressed).

If you're going the sunless tanner route, I think this is a good one.

I am done with the sunless tanning lotions, I think. I have tried a few different brands and none of them seem to be able to give me a look that I am satisfied with..

This product requires some careful application to avoid overlapping too much. Overlap too much and you'll end up with spots that are darker than others and it won't look right. It IS basically a stain product for the skin, so I shouldn't be surprised that it acts like a staining product does for wood. It isn't a bad product, but it just isn't for me.
summary: Another sunless tanning lotion that I am not satisfied with...

reviewText: This is a nice tanner but is definitely dark. You'll want the associated mitt, as it will stain palms and not come off. It was a little too dark for my pale skin, even after using the lighter version of this lotion.
summary: Nice, easy to use, but pretty dark.

reviewText:
I have used other Xen Tan products and I had much better results..  This is a two person review though hence the four stars.. My skin is usually medium color and now that summer is behind us my tan has faded and its fair.. When I applied it was hard to get the streaks out but with the glove I had it did happen.. My legs did have color, but with my skin tone it was more of a orange tan.. Not horrible but not a desired look..

I gave to my sister in law to try and she LOVED it ! She has a dark skin tone though and as a brunette and a base tan from the summer still the color looked really good.. So I would say this is a great weekly self tanner if you don't have a fair skin tone.. The glove is a life saver with these types of products, I would highly suggest purchasing as well

I had a better time with this than some other products. Foremost, the smell is fantastic! Secondly, if you purchase the mitt and apply this product with that, you'll get an even, smooth appearance. I started very lightly (because I am relatively fair). And then I used it slightly more aggressively. I was really pleased with the results. Therefore, I think you just need to try a variety of products (if you are fair), sometimes within the same brand. I had luck with this one ... you may also!

This is great for fair skin. This is easy to apply. A little goes a long way. You can use a sponge or a buffer to apply the lotion on.  I use a little . Just enough to get a little color in my skin. The scent is not overpowering. But it does not irratate my sinuses.

I have tried several XEN-Tan products over the last few months and this is one of the better self-tanners.
It goes on well if you purchase the XEN tan mitt. Otherwise your hands will be deeply stained.
The lotion has a nice, pleasant scent - similar to a suntan lotion rather than a chemical self-tanner smell.
The downside for me is that this takes a long time to really dry - directions suggest four hours and it does take pretty much that entire time before you will feel safe putting on any clothing that you don't want ruined.
The end result is ok but given the price and inconvenient wait time during application, I will use this on my face but otherwise it will not be my go-to self-tanner.

I like being tan but I avoid the sun religiously.

The mitt is really the key to getting this product on properly.  This went on evenly, more so than I have ever seen a tanning product of any sort.  It just looks amazing. However, ten seconds later, you realize you have to stay still for an hour and not put anything on for over four hours.  I have a moving disorder called ADD.  LOL.  If I stop moving, I see things I have to do.  If I try to stop moving, well, I cant.

I have failed completely to use this product properly or to get the benefits from the product, but it is entirely my own fault.

This is quite easy to apply.  One can get a mitt separately, but it goes on nicely and smoothly with one's hands.  Just wash your hands afterwards.  This is good for maintaining a healthy looking tan through the winter months.  This also has a more pleasant scent than many tanning lotions.  Definitely recommended.
summary: Good for maintaining tan through the winter months coming up

reviewText: I wanted to love this self tanner.  It goes on well with uniform color and no streaks. It comes with a mitt to apply it and I think thats what made to color so even. Its easy and fairly quick to put on and it has a pleasant scent.  Basically, it was good all around until I saw the final product. I think my complexion is just not made for self tanners. Ive never found one that doesnt look orange on me.  That being said, if you don't normally look orange, this might be a great self tanner for you.

My daughter likes to change colors. Usually it's her hair but sometimes she likes to change her skin color from its normal Northern European ghostly hue.  She says this went on easily and did not streak and it smells nice (it does - I checked).  She was happy with the results although the color did not look totally natural to me.  She was going to a convention as a superhero and I guess less than natural colors are perfect for that venue.
summary: Nice smell, no streaking not quite natural color

reviewText: This is a tough product to review because it worked pretty well for me but not well for my wife. I have lightish olive skin, my wife is fair with some freckles. We both tried it. My results were pretty good, leaving me with a pretty natural looking color. My wife, on the other hand, was not as lucky. Her color did not look so natural, and more orangey. Not pumpkin like, but not natural. It smells pretty good and skin does not feel dry. I used the tanning mitt and it left no streaks. My wife used it, and also, no streaks. One of the other problems was that everything darkens, so if you are hoping to blend freckles, dark spots, etc., it's not really going to happen. At this price, I would expect a lot more, and while it worked for me, it's not something I would buy.

This Xen-Tan weekly ultra dark self tanner is a high end product that produces visible quick results and has a really pleasant light vanilla scent. This tanner turns my pale skin really dark- I haven't had any sun in so long I was slightly shocked as to how dark it turned my skin. Although I'm pale, I have an olive skin tone and this tanner produces a good olive tone when applied to my skin. I don't get any hint of orange, and the color is a really rich and dark brown color. I also use a medium color Xen-Tan tanner that I really love and prefer to this one as it's a more natural look for me, and I get a more even application when I use it. This darker color shows more imperfections (though people who use tanner a lot won't have the same issue). This Xen-Tan lotion promises a dark tan, and it definitely delivers and turns my skin very dark, it lasts all week and it smells great too. It's pricey, but the tube is large and will last me months as I use it for my arms, legs and feet mostly rather than my whole body. It's a very high quality tanner that I recommend if you seek a dark rich color.
summary: High End Tanner That Smells Great and Delivers A Dark Rich "Tan"

reviewText:
I've been loyal to my St Tropez self-tan for some time, but was intrigued by XEN-TAN's line on Amazon.  I recently tried XEN-TAN's face tanner in the Mousse Intense Weekly Tan (Medium) and found the results quite natural, the scent very pleasant and not too tacky when applied to face.
This tanner, however, is geared towards body (and can also be applied to face) and comes in a "ultra dark" lotion for deeper tan results.  I was hesitant to apply more than a test area at first, having read some reviews that this particular product's results went a tad orange in tone.

Initial impressions - the scent is really lovely, reminds me of summer with the vanilla scent that isn't too overbearing, termed "Scent Secure".  It's a good thing when your self-tanner doesn't smell like typical self-tanner.  I felt the lotion was thick dispensing from the tube, but blended in without much effort.  There wasn't a major amount of tackiness post application -- many lotions I have tried from other brands tended to sit on top of skin and feel uncomfortable, especially in the hotter months.  Being that it's October, this assessment may be a little biased since the room temperature of the application is a little colder and not humid.

Touted on the packaging as paraben free and containing shea butter & green tea extract, there's an added perk of moisturizing the skin -- often self-tanners can leave skin dried out.  Once I've given the XEN-TAN Dark Lotion a couple more uses, I will update further on my observations.

This thick lotion works well to provide nice, instant color, but there are some things I don't really like about it.

It sort of smears on and you have to work it in really good to get it to apply evenly and blend.

The scent is not bad. It has a suntan lotion sort of smell - kind of like coconut or cocoa butter. No weird tanner smell.

You absolutely want and need to use a mit to apply this. It stains your palms instantly and no matter how well you wash your hands afterwards,  they will be stained for quite awhile... through several showers and loads of dishes etc.

It seems to take a long time for it to really set in and dry on your skin. The skin feels tacky or sticky for a few hours actually. So plan on walking around naked or wearing just a robe, or at the very least old clothes that you won't mind getting ruined. Until it totally sets in and dries on your skin, it will rub off a little and stain your clothes.

I use just enough to be able to cover my skin and work it in. You want to start out with as little as possible and then build it up as needed. The color is nice after the first application. Not too dark at all, but enough to tell a nice difference. If you start out too heavy, you will regret it because this stuff looks like poo real fast. Squeezing it out in your hand to use it, it looks like poo in your hand. So just start out with as little as possible. Remember it doesn't totally rub in and dry for awhile too, so you will be sticky walking poo if you use too much too soon.

The day after I apply it, it looks great. Seems to develop a little overnight and looks like a nice natural deep tan. If you use it too often though, I'm sure it will have very unnatural looking results.

All in all, the results are very good and I really like that it has no odd smell like most other tanners do. I do think a mit should be included since it is necessary to use. If nothing else, they could at least include a cheap pair of latex or plastic gloves to start you off with, like boxes of hair dye come with. Especially for the price, I just think they could include this. You can find cheap generic ones here on amazon though, so check those out before you spend on a branded one.

I was expecting a dark color on the first application.  This lotion doesn't quite work out that way.  I followed the directions, wetted the mitt down first, and rubbed lotion into my legs.  The mitt helps even out the cream with nothing on my hands.  This lotion has a nice aroma to it.  I had just showered and was probably still moist.  The lotion dries rather quickly and leaves no streaks if applied right.  A few hours later I saw a slight darker skin tone from that in the morning, an even darker hue the next day after a second application..  That was the DHA working.  The tropical scent still lingered, but it wasn't as strong as earlier. If I want to go even darker, I could apply more lotion.  This may be expensive lotion, but the results look natural.  Keeping skin moisturized prevents streaking and staining, but make sure you don't forget the feet!  On my first try, I didn't rub this on my feet and arches and an obvious difference was noticeable. .

I liked this tanner. It smells amazing, first of all. Second of all, it is very easy to apply. I received a sample of the tanner with an application mitt and that is the way to go. I showered, exfoliated and then applied the tanner. I made sure to go sparingly on my elbows, knees and ankles. I am slightly tan already from a summer spent mostly outdoors and this helped to even out my color and to deepen the tan I already had. I would definitely recommend this self tanner.

My wife tried this and was very pleased with the results of the finished product. She let my daughter help, who was fascinated by the process itself, and they had a good time applying. We don't like to sit in the sun or go to tanning places because of the rays and skin cancer(my grandfather died a horrible death from it so it always scared me). It did not give her a real dark tan more of a medium tan which she liked very much. The only thing she said that was negative was how long it took to apply and go through the process.

She looks great and she is happy so I am happy. Would use again!

Looking tan is not something I usually am concerned with, but there are occasions when I would prefer my legs not look so pasty white. I am impressed with the longevity of this product. After applying it to my legs the color wore well for almost a week. The result is not at all orange and it appeared very natural. And, although it is labeled "dark" I thought the color was more a medium tone.

I did use this product line's application mitt and that helped achieve an even tone, although those users more experienced with self-tanners probably will not need the help.  .

This lotion provides a natural color for me, without the orange hue. It is a process to apply, and it is best if you use the mitt, so that you don't have orange stained hands when you are finished. I was able to get an even coating with the mitt, and it worked well for me. I used this on my legs, and I was happy with the results. However, the price is really high on this. I usually use Suave Professionals Visible Glow Self-Tanning Body Lotion, Fair to Medium 7.5 oz, and the results of this lotion are really good, for a fraction of the price of the Xen-Tan. This lotion lasted a couple days, but then I had to apply it again, which was a process. If you don't mind spending the time to apply this, and then avoid any clothing that it might wear off on, for 3 hours after you apply it, then give it a try. I prefer to apply a lotion, let it dry, and then get dressed in anything I please, which is what the Suave lotion does.
summary: Works well, but is a process to apply.

reviewText:
Xen-Tan is a pricey tanner but it has several qualities that makes it better than your average drugstore tanner.

One, the smell. There is no off-putting self-tanner scent here at all. Sometimes Ill use a self-tanner and it smells okay but later as it activating, it will start to get that scent but not this one. Even later, still no tanner stink.

Two, it has less of an orange tone. One of the first thing you will notice about the Xen-tan products is that the color is more of a cool toned brown which gives less of that self-tanner orange color.

Three, the wear time and how it wears is great. With most drugstore tanners, I have to completely scrub down to bare skin weekly and completely redo my tanner so I don't get an uneven tan. This tan seems like it lasts and lasts. It also just faded instead of that awful patchy wear that I get from most tanners.

My recommendation is to apply with the Xen-tan tanning mitt which gives a flawless coverage.
summary: Wear Time is Good, Color is Good

reviewText:
I had never used a product like this before.
I suspect that it takes a fair amount of time to learn how to use it effectively and well.  I did get better results after I used it a couple of times (and got pretty un-wonderful results).  But I don't think that, in the end, it's worth the fuss and expense.

Others with more patience and more skill might well reach a different conclusion.
summary: Not easy for a neophyte to get good results with this. More experienced users might have a very different experience.

reviewText:
I have used another product from this same brand and loved it.  So I can say that brand has consistency.  My tanning lotion came with complimentary mitt which made application very easy.  There are so many advantages about this product: it has a pleasant scent, it absorbs quickly, it does not stain and is not streaky and it lasts for almost a week.

Personally I am not big on tanning, but there are times when I teach yoga workshops when I like to add a little color to my arms and chest so I do not look too pale.  Color looks natural, so no need to worry about looking "orange".

This product is a good quick fix to getting some color in your skin and it is healthier than going to the tanning bad (do not go to the tanning bad if you can help it, you are begging to get cancer).
summary: Perfect tanner for a short term fix

reviewText:
This self-tanner is an improvement on the old orange and streaky sunless tanners. Somehow it still does not look natural. I would never advise using it on my face that would just be too chancy.
It definitely works better than spray self-tanners and again the available mitt helps in application to achieve close to a natural looking tan.

One has to be careful in applying it around knees and elbows and especially any scar tissue it will turn many shades darker  so for those areas you need a lighter touch. If you follow directions and let it dry it will not stain clothes or bed linens.

It has taken me awhile to decide what I really think about this product.  I've tried self-tanning products in the past, and been unhappy with them, but I thought maybe this more expensive one is better.  And it is better, to an extent.

It goes on nicely, without streaking or spotchiness that I've found with other products.  That is a definite plus.  It is easy to apply smoothly.  There is a mitt available separately for applying the lotion, but I prefer using my hands, feel that I have better control that way.  I just have to remember to wash my hands well after doing that, and that is part of the instructions.

I tried this multiple times on my lily-white, never-see-the-light-of-day body parts.  While the "tan" was smooth, it was not as dark as I expected.  And for my skin tone, light, but tending to yellowish rather than pinkish, the effect was too yellow looking to please me.  I didn't get the dreaded fake tan orange effect, but I wasn't crazy about the color either.  It seemed to last about 3 days on my skin before fading too much.  At that point, it is still there, but not much of it so it needs a touch-up.  I do spend a lot of time in the water, and that may affect its staying power.  Still not splotchy though, which is good.

What this does well is blend in with current tan.  My body parts that I do expose to sun are somewhat tanned, but I have strap marks from my swimsuit.  Using this on those marks makes my skin more even-toned so my fish belly white does not blind anyone when I wear something that exposes those strap areas.

While prices can frequently change, this product was marked at over 50 dollars at the time I chose it, and I think that is too high for the results achieved.

When I first used this, I used with the mitt and found it messy and lotion did transfer to clothes if I were not careful enough.

Since then I have started to use it for tan highlights on my face, neck, arms and legs, applied lightly by hand.  I now love it!

It imparts a beautiful gently glow.
summary: Use but not as directed for this girl...

reviewText:
The Stila Smudge Sticks are one of my favorite eye liners.  They come in lots of great colors.  I've been wanting to try (but haven't been brave enough yet!) a couple of their brighter colors like the Purple Tang or the Deep Fuchsia but so far have only purchased the Damsel, Stingray, Metallic Umber, and Alpine -- some purchased from Amazon and some from a brick-and-mortar store (Ulta).

The liner is easy to use and really does last better than most other liners that I've used.  I'd doubted that the fact of it being waterproof would really help it to last on my eyes.  I was afraid that the "waterproof-iness" of it would only be affected by things like actual water--tears and rain and such--but that the liner would still disappear over the course of the day due to skin oils and the oils in my eye cream.  But, most days, my liner still looks the same in the evening as it does in the morning--and I can't say that about most roll-up stick liners that I've used.  On days that I know that I'll be in the hot outdoors for extended periods, I'll add a bit of eye primer first to help keep both my liner and my eye shadow from disappearing.  But it's usually not necessary for this liner.

The pigment stick twists up as you use it and need more.  So far, out of the many Stila liner pens I've purchased, I've only encountered one recalcitrant pen that didn't want to twist up more liner.  I held the pen with the open liner "tip down" and flicked it with my finger a few times mid-way on the pen, while twisting the pen to extrude more liner.  It finally started working again.

Of the four colors that I've purchased so far, my very favorite is the Metallic Umber, with Damsel being a close second.  They're my go-to, everyday liners.  The umber isn't overly dark and it's also just barely metallic.  Since I have pale blonde hair, I feel that the Damsel is a better choice for me as a dark liner than the Stingray, although I have used the glossy black Stingray for some evenings when I wanted more drama.  I bought the pearly Alpine to use on my waterline but I don't use it all that often.
summary: Easy-to-use waterproof eye liner really stays on and comes in great colors

reviewText:
I have the color "canary," which I bought (elsewhere) because it was on sale.  I guess there is not much of a market for yellow eyeliner.  But I like unusual eyeliner colors (not such a fan of black) and I didn't have a yellow in my collection.

I'm very happy with this product's performance.  This is a pretty bright, opaque yellow (not metallic or anything; the color chooser on the right hand side of the Amazon page is not particularly reflective of the color, for what it's worth).  I wear it over eyeshadow; today I have it on top of orange and it really lightens up my eyes.  It goes on smoothly and doesn't pull at my eyelid when I apply it.  The tip doesn't break.  It actually shows up.  I did not try to smudge it or create a smoky look (if you can even do that with yellow) but just wore a line of it on my upper lids.  It lasts all day (I am wearing primer in addition to my shadow, but I do have quite oily eyelids) and I can get it off with eye makeup remover, oil based cleanser, or even micellar water.  This has not irritated my eyes, which is nice since I wear contact lenses and have sensitive eyes.

There is one thing I don't like.  This is a twist-up product, as far as I can tell, and I am having trouble advancing the product in the tube.  I will play with it some more to see if I can fix this.  But really, it should work automatically.  On the one hand, I am glad not to be able to push too much up at once and break it off, but on the other hand, it's not much use if you can only use it a few times.  Assuming I can figure out the twist-up part, I would definitely buy this in other colors.
summary: great performance, but a bit hard to advance the product in the tube

reviewText:
As compared to Cool Water, (the role model for most male fresh aquatics) I found Eternity Aqua (hereafter EA) to be more interesting and less artificially pungent. EA begins with a great cucumber lotus accord that smells pretty unique, but sadly these notes are gone in less than 15 minutes. One is left with the all too common aquatic drydown of calone and cedar, with hints of lavender. Still, the calone (artificial melon) notes are underplayed here versus Cool Water or Nautica Voyage, and so this fragrance was less unpleasant for the intermediate term. (Both Voyage and Cool Water make me want to wash them off after about an hour or so, but EA was less annoying by far.)

Biggest problem with EA is longevity and projection. The longevity issue is a common one with male aquatics, and EA is very representative of that deficiency. The whole show is over in less than four hours, and the fragrance is close to being a skin scent in less than two hours. This is basically a cologne lifespan at an EDT price, but this longevity issue is pretty much par the course for this school of fragrances. If you want a long lasting aquatic, try Bulgari's "Aqua", but that is a darker more complex scent that is not as "fresh" as EA or its comparable short lifespan brethren.

The projection is also quite weak, which makes this good for the workplace, bad for clubs and other social settings where one might want to be smelled. Both Cool Water and Voyage project better, so if you want to reach out and touch someone's scent receptors from more than an arm's length away, EA is not the best choice.

This to me is between three and four stars. The sweeter opening and somewhat less artificial drydown are pluses compared to other fresh aquatics, and I like the cucumber and lotus notes, but they are all too brief. The fragrance as a whole could last longer, and the quickly departing top notes only add to the disappointment. If you like aquatics and want something a bit less strident, this is a good choice. I'm rounding up to four stars because I'm a sucker for cucumber smells.

Of course, I would also suggest not wearing aquatics at all. These are mainly weak, dull, and simple scents. I suggest trying something with more oomph and interest, like Dior Homme, Aramis 900, or Polo, but then of course you won't smell like every other male aged 16-30 out there. Whether that is a good or bad thing, I will leave up to you to decide!
summary: Slightly Different from Most Aquatics, Though Still Typical in Some Ways

reviewText: I've been a fan of Cool Water By Davidoff For Men. Eau De Toilette Spray 4.2 Ounces. When I don't have Coolwater handy, a good alternative has been Perry Ellis 360 Red By Perry Ellis For Men. Eau De Toilette Spray 3.4 Ounces, which smells very similar. First impressions of Eternity: + Nice masculine smell + Compact bottle that I can take through airport security when traveling As I went through my days, my next impressions: - One place I tend to spray is the middle of my chest. But Eternity doesn't seem to last as long as Coolwater or Red. When I get home from work after a long day and go change my shirt, I no longer smell any of the cologne, whereas I can still smell the other two in my clothing. I personally like that having that lasting smell. - When spraying, a lot of cologne comes out. So be careful and spray easy! - Can't believe this is nearly 3-times the prices of a similar size bottle of Coolwater or Red. Maybe because it's new and over time the price will drop. OVERALL: I like the smell. My wife likes the smell. But for the money I'll stick with the other two, which seem to last longer.
