The only thing I didn't like was the instructions to apply the product to both lips and eyes using the metal tip on the tube. Ewww. Why drag germs from your mouth to your eye area? I dispense some product onto clean fingers, and go from there.

This cream has only been in use for about a week, but wow does it ever feel amazing when applied to the eye area. I know that it's for eyes and lips, but so far I've only been using it on my eye area. When applied it gives a wonderful cooling sensation. I just turned 40 (or 29 + 11 years of experience as I like to say) and am starting to see tiny fine lines around my eyes and decided it was time to step up the anti-aging routine. So far, this cream has lived up to its promise. The puffiness is gone with minutes, the tiny lines filled out, and I look like I've a better night's sleep than I actually had.  The directions say to use one side of the metal tip to apply the cream to your eyes and the other to apply the cream to your lips. but that seems a bit on the uck side, so I use my ring finger instead to apply.

I've used Vichy products before (their oily skin/acne line is AMAZING) and have consistent, wonderful results. Their products are pricey, but the trade-off is that they work sooner, do a better job, and are so much more gentle on my skin than many less expensive products (and a good number of pricier ones as well).
summary: Helps to keep the years at bay

reviewText: Really nice lotion/cream for the fine wrinkles around your eyes and lips. It's hard to tell if these things work, but it certainly feels nice.

Do I hate that I paid $10 for toothpaste? Absolutely. Do I love that my mouth tastes like an Italian cookie or sambuca when I brush my teeth? Yup, $10 worth. I will shamelessly continue to throw my money at this product.
Tastes amazing. Makes my teeth really white. Reminds me of earl gray tea. It does freshen the breath really well. I keep an extra one in my car for touch ups after lunch and coffee breaks.

I love black licorice but I wasn't sure I was going to love it in a toothpaste. Turns out, I DO!
Doesn't taste like candy but more of natural licorice flavor. I don't taste much of the mint but that's fine by me. My husband HATES black licorice but he doesn't complain that I smell like it at all!
Love it.
One taste and I was hooked.  The licorice is subtle but lovely.  I look forward to brushing my teeth with this at night - it's like a little bit of dessert.
Great toothpaste. If you like licorice, this is something you've got to try. Say goodbye to boring mint toothpaste forever!

The ultimate test for any facial cleanser I use is - will it remove my waterproof eye makeup fairly easily and without too much rubbing? Unfortunately, this water facial cleanser did not pass that particular test. I applied on a cotton pad as directed and tried to wipe off my waterproof eye makeup.  It took three minutes of too-vigorous rubbing to get it to completely come off.

However, if you don't have waterproof makeup then this gentle cleanser might be for you. My skin did not react negatively to it after a couple weeks of use.  There is no smell, no dye. It feels and looks ...like water.

Even with just regular makeup, however, I felt that I need a more substantial cleanser than "water" because my skin still felt dirty. I would use another regular cleanser after this and indeed picked up quite a bit of makeup on my washcloth.
summary: Did not take off waterproof makeup easily

reviewText: I love using micellar water to clean my face. This has made a big difference for my complexion. I've tried quite a few different brands. I'm happy to report that this Vichy product barely has any fragrance, which is not the norm in my experience with Vichy. Just put a little micellar water on a cotton pad and swipe it over your face to remove makeup/grime. No rinsing required. It really refreshes your complexion. Recommended.
summary: Micellar Water Is A Game Changer

reviewText:
Unlike other reviewers, I did not find this so great. I had to use a decent amount on a cotton ball to get my eyeliner completely off and it took a little rubbing. Therefore, I think the bottle won't last as long as I would wish, considering the cost.
Also, I felt as if I needed to wash or rinse my face since I didn't want any residue from the product left on during the night.

My experience with this brand has always been excellent, so I was surprised.

I just gone done taking the day off my face with this product.  It is wonderful.  I washed my face before using it and I still was able to see dirt on my cotton ball when I did a second pass.  Very nice packaging and fast delivery.
summary: It is wonderful. I washed my face before using it and ...

reviewText: This is a mild Facial Cleanser that goes on gentle with a water like flow, my girl friend uses it to remove make-up before bed each night, no scrubbing or rinsing after using. Enriched with zinc, contains Vichy mineralizing thermal water it leaves your face feeling and looking fresh and healthy without any dryness. A little over 8 ounces is a generous supply for the price.
summary: Fresh feeling cleanness after cleansing your face, removes Make-up too.

reviewText:
I have never used a product like this that doesn't get rinsed off.  I usually have problems with products on my face burning my skin so my choices are very limited.  I applied this and I waited for the usual burn but it never came. What did happen was that I put this all over my face upon waking up and my cotton pad was very dirty afterward, I can't believe all that dirt was on my face. It does a really good job at cleansing the skin.

What I like about this cleanser is that it has a light scent and it is crystal clear, like water.

I have used two other Micellar Water Cleansers--Simple Cleansing Water, Micellar - 6.7 oz and Garnier SkinActive Micellar Cleansing Water All-in-1 Cleanser & Makeup Remover, 13.5 Fluid Ounce. I like both and used them in the afternoon before I walked so my make-up would not sweat into my eyes. Both did not take off my mascara completely so I looked like a chunky redhead raccoon. I tried this yesterday and my make-up and the mascara completely came off. The scent is faint and the texture truly feels like water. I had no irritation so my rosacea did not flare up. This is priced about $10 more than the Simple bottle but it works better. You use VERY little and instead of a cotton ball, I recommend cotton squares you can get cheaply at a dollar store. The mascara pulls onto the cotton ball and the squares don't

My face feels clean without being completely dried out, my skin feels invigorated and soft.  This doesn't have an over the top scent or leave any sort of lingering odor after use.  I like it, and see this as a product that I will likely order more of when I run out of it.
summary: I like it, and see this as a product that ...

reviewText: I am very surprised to really like this product!  When I ordered it, I was skeptical, thinking.. it's an expensive bottle of water... I don't quite get it.  But this has proven itself to be a great item.  A quick wipe of this takes oil off my face without drying it out.  It effectively moves basic daily makeup, finds remnants of lipstick that aren't even very visible, and leaves my face feeling clean and pleasant.  It is great for a quick wipe to remove the oils around my eyes from wearing glasses mid-day that can start to sting my eyes by the evening.  It will take off eye makeup if left to soak for a short time with the cotton pad, but for heavy eye makeup, I think for ease and complete removal, I would still use eye makeup remover and then go over it with this product to clean off THOSE oils.  This product is gentle on the eyes, has no taste on the lips when used for lipstick, has no odor at all - I honestly can't believe this works.. but it does, much more effectively than just water on a cotton pad (I tested that just to make sure I hadn't realized all these years I could accomplish this with just a cotton pad of water... I couldn't).  I am very likely to continue to purchase this product when it runs out, and have surprised myself by using it nightly before bed even when I haven't used makeup - I've never been one for a nightly regimen, but this is so quick and easy and I really like how my skin is feeling with cumulative use.  I definitely recommend this item and am glad it crossed my path, because I doubt I would have ever explored it for the cost.
summary: Am surprised to really like this and have been using as a daily regimen - I don't know why this works, but it does!

reviewText: I've been using Garnier's micellar water, and I have to say that Vichy Normaderm's is just as good if not better - I noticed that it removed my eye makeup quicker (eyeliner, eyeshadow, mascara) and without as much 'pressure'. I didn't notice any scent or residue, it leaves my face feeling clean and moist, and it's great for those times when I don't want to wash with normal soap and water. I just use cotton pads to wipe off the makeup and it really makes my face feel clean.

This is a nice, light facial cleanser. While my face routine is pretty much set (I use other products for my acne-prone skin), I use this micellar water to remove my eye makeup. I don't normally wear waterproof cosmetics, so this whisks everything off pretty easily. I did try it one time when I was wearing waterproof mascara, and have to say it wasn't as effective. I had to follow up with something stronger and creamier.

This product has a light fragrance and is basically water, so be careful when using, as it flows out pretty fast. Overall, it's nice.

UPDATE: Began to burn my eyes after a few uses. They stung so much. I will never use this Vichy or recommend because of the burning. I don't understand why it hurt so bad after a few uses.

ORIGINAL REVIEW (Four Stars): The Vichy Normaderm 3-in-1 Micellar Water Facial Cleanser is good, but I felt like my skin still had cosmetic residue on it after I used this product with a cotton pad. I had an unstoppable urge to wash my face with water & regular cleanser after using this, which I did. My skin felt much cleaner after that.

The cleanser also spilled into the sink because it pours oddly, so just make sure to put your cotton pad over the hole before upturning the bottle. This is great stuff for removing my (not-waterproof) mascara, but I will probably follow up with my regular cleanser.

I like this to take off makeup, but won't recommend to fully remove dirt and cosmetics all over your face.

This is a nice product for those of us with sensitive skin.  I small amount on a cotton pad gently removes makeup and dirt.  It does take a bit more to remove eyeliner and mascara, though.  But at no time did it flare my skin issues.  As well, the scent is nice and light.  I also like that I don't have to wash afterwards - I didn't feel that there was any residue - it all went onto the cotton pad.

This is obviously marketed for female users, but it works as a refreshing cleaning agent for us guys too.  It does have a little scent to it, but that's not overpowering, and it fades fairly fast.  I especially recommendit for us aged guys, loke in your 80's like me.
summary: It works for guys too...especially we aged ones

reviewText:
This facial cleanser (has a toner-like consistency, use on a cotton round) has no scent that I can detect. If there is fragrance it is so light as to be undetectable by me. It is pleasant on the skin and leaves my face clean and soft. While it did take my foundation makeup off,  it was less than successful with my eye makeup. I needed to use an oil based product to get my mascara off.

While I could use something more robust for summer, this is perfect for the winter skin care season. It is not drying and cleans without harshness. Easy to use, leak resistant container.
summary: Excellent gentle cleanser especially for fragile, winter skin. Just ok for eye makeup removal.

reviewText:
I've used this product as a stand-alone cleanser and as a follow up to my regular cleanser when I feel like my skin needs a little extra oil/sweat removal.  I'm surprised at how much makeup and dirt this removes, even after I've already washed my face. Yet it feels very gentle on my combination skin.  I've had no problems with breakouts from using this and no irritation or redness.  My complexion looks great.

I've read that Micellar water cleansers are a good solution for situations when you aren't able to fully wash your face: travel, camping, gym bag.  This  stand alone product definitely performs. My skin feels clean and refreshed, but not dry.

This is a beautiful lip and cheek stain that lasts all day on cheeks and needs to be reapplied once or twice during the day.  It is moisturizing, and natural-looking.  It has no scent.  I purchased Forever Red, which is a beautiful color, it's just not red.  It's very sheer salmon-coral on my skin and lips.  It's flattering, but it's not what I was hoping for in a color called "Red".  Even when layered and layered, this never gets to red.  It becomes deeper coral-orange...closer to Tomato Red...but still orange. If I'd had to guess which stain this was, I would have said Forever Peach! But it's clearly labeled Forever Red, so I guess it's just my pH that makes it so orangey. At least it turns to a color that's flattering on my warm olive skin.  If it turned pink or purplish I'd have to send it back.  I will definitely use Forever Red, and still search for the perfect red lip & cheek stain.
This turns my lips the brightest ugly pink. I threw the box away otherwise Id return it.

This is one of my absolute favorites for both lips and cheeks. I apply it once and it will stay on my cheeks all day, giving a very natural and youthful color. Same thing with lips, though you may need to reapply in the afternoon depending on what you eat and drink. It does have great staying power, and wears naturally. Often when I'm traveling I'll bring this instead of a separate blush and lipstick, and I'll often wear it for both even when I have my whole collection to choose from. Perfect for a no-makeup makeup look.
summary: It does have great staying power

reviewText: I don't think I'll be buying again

This is the best lipstick ever!!  I have ordered two and used the entire tubes. Perfect soft color, no feathering, feels comfortable and hydrating. I have a tube of this in my pocket at work at all times!!  Expensive but totally worth it!

I love this stuff so much. Gives your lips that freshly-bitten flush color and keeps me from picking at them. I use it every day multiple times a day. Smells lovely too. You can dab it on for a more natural look or layer it on for a stronger color.
summary: Been through three tubes of this stuff.

reviewText: Love it
Love the natural look

I've been using this stain by Jane Iredale for about 2 years. One tube lasts for a long time! I've tried both the Forever Pink and Forever Red. For reference, I'm very fair with freckles. Forever Pink is just a hint of color, perfect when I want to go with the no-makeup look. Forever Red is more noticeable and great when I want more of a pop of color. I've never used it on my cheeks, only my lips. Goes on smoothly and has a nice texture.

Product is good but the lip container needs improvement. Top won't stay on so I won't buy again. it really bothers me that you pay this kind of money and it does not work right, There is BARELY any color. I won't buy this shade again.
Feels good when applied but it doesn't have any staying power.  It gives you only a little color.
This is pricey, but creates a soft sheer pink.  Good stuff.

Love this kind of product.... And I'm a fan of Jane Iredale products. This is similar to the Dior self adjusting lipstick though priced about 10 bucks less and with better application . So easy to use in both cheeks and lips
Love all of Jane Iredale products.

Love this stuff. I received a sample of the peach color and I don't wear much peach but I liked it enough to try the pink. The color is light pink, almost like a soft pink-rose. If I put a thin coat on then it's lighter and if I want slightly more pigment I use 2 coats. Feels great on my lips. I apply every few hours. This is  not a thick lipstick and it's not a gloss. It's a sheer color that can deepen and slightly change after you put it on. Good for those who like lighter pinks. Goes very well with JI blush in: Cotton Candy and Awake - both of which I wear with this lipstick. Going to get the red next. Another win!
summary: This will always be in my purse!

reviewText:
I think I don't understand this product.  Or perhaps it just doesn't work with my body chemistry.  Either way, it didn't work for me.  I have this in forever pink and it just doesn't add a noticeable enough pop of color to my lips or my cheeks.  It's way, way too subtle for my taste and I don't have particularly dark skin or lips.  (I have light/medium skin with a neutral tone.)  I also don't particularly care for the balm-like texture on my cheeks.  It's fine on my lips but on my facial skin I prefer the more liquid-y stains.  For a stain product I much prefer the tints from Benefit such as Cha Cha Tint and Lollitint.  I own both of those and find the results to be much, much better.  With those tints I find that the color payoff is more pronounced, yet still has a natural-isn look.

Not a fan.
Thought it would have been a real pink but it isn't on my lips. hmmmmmm
Nice for a little color but it doesn't last as long as I'd like. It is a stain and not lipstick so it's nice for a little lip color when I want to look healthy and natural (for a short time!)
summary: Nice for a little color but it doesn't last as ...

reviewText: its good

I absolutely love this lipstick/lipgloss! it's strange ... it looks very, very light in color and goes on very smooth. Once it is on it becomes a pink color that looks very natural. It's amazing! Definitely fully recommend it.

Exquisite moisture -- like a glorified lip balm with a light fruit scent (though it must be natural because I do not see a fragrance additive). Unfortunately it didn't change my lip color nor would it really qualify as a stain. Still, it will be a nice treat for the frigid months!
summary: Luxurious lip balm with no color pay off

reviewText: I love the original color. I received this color via a sample and then purchased more. I like it on the cheeks but not the lips. The original color looks more natural. This one looks weird!
summary: Original color, yes! This color, maybe not!

reviewText: Great natural look.
Didn't like the color but since I ordered it I used it until it began to come apart from its tube base.
summary: Didn't like the color but since I ordered it I used ...

reviewText:
I've tried quite a few lip and cheek combination products lately, and usually I find that they look good on the cheeks OR the lips, but not both. This is the first product that really works for both, I think.

It's a light pink but it shows up on my cheeks (it's pretty pale). You can get away with using a little or a lot, and you won't look like a clown if you use a lot. (I was almost late to work one day experimenting with a similar product last week, when I had to wash my face and start over again, so this is an important consideration!) It's a faint color on my lips, and not too much of a shine, but good for a sort of "enhanced" natural look.

As a cheek color, it's fairly long-lasting. As a lip color, you'll have to reapply it after meals. It's not the most moisturizing lip color I've ever tried, but it's not the worst, either. I'd put it somewhere in between, which is actually quite good for a combination product.

It's not a stain, though, and I don't really feel much in the way of plumping effects. What I like are the color and the convenience of having a product that actually works on both lips and cheeks.
summary: actually works on both lips and cheeks

reviewText: My husband asked for this for his birthday. He loves all things Lacoste. It really does smell grear. He gets tons of compliments

PROS: My husband has sinus and allergy issues so he rarely wears scents. Fortunately, this didn't bother him. It had a light clean scent.

CONS: Neither of us was blown away by this cologne. I didn't find it either offensive or attractive. It has a generic smell that didn't impress.

3 - 3.5 STARS: It's simply okay. I don't think this is going to become my husband's signature fragrance.

My husband says that
Lacostes Eau de Lacoste is a light, crisp, clean scent. It manages to do this and still retain a masculine feel.
It reminds me of something fresh and sporty, the feel of summertime?  Something easily worn to work every day..
A great alternative to those heavy and spicy colognes you would want to save for evening wear.
He would recommend it for anytime you want to stand out, without a overbearing scent.
summary: Something easily worn to work every day

reviewText: I have many different brands of colognes, and among them, white musk scent was always my favorite. Like any other human sense related products, colognes are very personal because of ones preferences, but I found new favorite. I am not a big fan of strong scent or cologne and this one is not punchy. This white polo scent is very familiar and famous, yet not too strong at first, but it lasts longer than others I have tried. The scent is somewhat gentle for me, and I like it that way with longer lasting endurance. Imitations often have similar scent at a low price, but only last an hour or so. This one is from Amazon and for sure an authentic Lacoste, and the pure scent lasts pretty much all day and night freshly.

I originally snapped this up for my husband, as I was fond of the listed notes, the grapefruit in particular is a favorite. But our teenager is in a phase of wanting to smell nice so I let him have first dibs and I have to say that I'm glad I let him have it. While I like it and my teen does, I don't think my husband would care for it as much.

You definitely get the tuberose notes and this fragrance which gives it a really warm overall feel. It's very bright and clean at first but as the grapefruit burns off I find it's a bit sensual and I'd even dare say it's almost unisex. I tried it on myself and though I wouldn't wear it, I found it was a flattering scent even on me. (Ladies if you love sneaking a spritz of your guys' scent this is a great one).

If you like Ralph Lauren's Romance or Jean Paul Gautier Le Male I would definitely check out Lacoste Ea de Lacosta. I think this is a terrific choice for men in their late 20's and into the late 30's, it's very grown-up and established feeling but not so mature that it feels like a dad cologne.
summary: I love this and have a couple of similar faves to help you decide if you want to try it...

reviewText: Normally, a 3.4 ounce tube of Ahava Mineral Hand Cream runs about $16, at full retail. But being far richer, Ahava's Dermud intensive skin care line tends to cost more. So a 5.1 ounce tube of Dermud Intensive Hand Cream at this price, with free shipping, to boot, is a very good deal. Highly recommended for people with chronically dry hands.

I love Ahava products so when I saw this hand cream I thought I would try it. I normally buy the one that has the word "water" on the side and I love it. This one has the word "mud" on the side and I thought it would be similar. It is not unfortunately. The smell is different and I don't hate it but I just don't like it very much. Also this one is slightly greasy on the hands. It doesn't stay greasy but you have to keep rubbing it in.  I believe it does help your hands so I'm keeping it but in the future I'll go back to the one with "water" written on the label. Quite honestly I'm not even sure what the difference is between the two in terms of how they are formulated, but I know for sure I like the "water" version a hundred times better.
summary: I love Ahava products so when I saw this hand cream ...

reviewText: I have had dry feet for years and nothing seemed to help. This product made things better after just 2 applications. After a week, my feet, including my heels feel smooth and soft. Amazingly good product.
Love it.  It does a great job of moisturizing my hands. If it weren't so expensive I would use it on my entire body.
Remarkable product. Goes on smoothly. Absorbs quickly. No greasy feeling. Pleasant scent.
Really nice amount of moisture without being greasy.  My boyfriend loves it.

AHAVA Mud really works well on my extremely dry skin. I apply hand lotion frequently throughout the day and almost always after washing my hands. Just a small squirt of Mud is required to moisturize my dry skin. It goes on smoothly and is completely absorbed very quickly without any greasy residue. There is no discernible scent, and this is a very pleasant product to use.
summary: Effective Moisturizer and Pleasant to Use

reviewText:
The perfume is so strong in this lotion, I could smell it before I even opened the box.  Plus there is a foil seal on the tube which was sealed as it should be.  I tried using this for two days now & just can't stand it.  It is giving me a headache, add to that, my hands still feel dry.  I get a really thick "hard butter" at my local farmers market that is fabulous.  This stuff by AHAVA has nothing on that little farmers hand treatments, also the stuff I normally use contains organic essential oils which have never given me a headache.  Because of the perfume, I tried using this on my feet where I have some pretty bad calluses.  I can tolerate much better when it's on my feet.  It seems to be helping soften the calluses but I'm going to try the previously mentioned hard butter as I expect I'll have better results.
Overall this is not a product I would recommend to anyone, nor would I purchase it.
summary: Overpowering Perfumes & Not As Good As Local Hand Cream Supplier

reviewText: I have pretty dry hands.  I often find I get paper cuts from cardboard!  So I'm game to try any new hand cream in the hopes that something will help.  I was pretty excited to try this mud intensive hand cream.  Having tried MANY creams I would rate this one average. I feel you can get similar moisture with store bought hand creams like Aveeno for a dramatically decreased price.  It has a rather strong scent and I did notice that it left a smooth, waxy sheen on my skin.  But I wash my hands a lot for work and my sign of a good cream is that is gives me a good protective coat that penetrates my skin.  Sadly after after the first wash most of it had come off even after letting it soak prior to washing for 30 min.  A good hand cream for dry hand for me will still retain some moisture even after the third hand wash.  I don't think there is anything wrong with this hand cream just that it doesn't fulfill my requirements of hand moisture.  It isn't bad but for the price I expected something more spectacular.
summary: It isn't bad but for the price I expected something more spectacular

reviewText: I like this. It isn't greasy. No overt smell and it works. I needed a light cream and this is what it is. I got this as an amazon vine voice, but I am about to buy again

My husband is diabetic and has to watch the condition of his feet.  Due to weather, he ends up with chapping and worse, especially during the winter months.  He has been using this foot cream for a few weeks and is really impressed with how much softer it makes his feet to the touch.  It doesn't take much and he is fairly certain this tube will last him the season.  If so, we will certainly be buying this again in the future.
summary: Helps keep feet soft to the touch

reviewText: This foot cream worked so well I could not believe it at all. It was not greasy, nor chalky. Rather, it was smooth and very soothing. I was surprised that it had little discernible odor. It simply went on smooth, soothed, and was a pleasure to deal with. It helped my feet become happy feet.

I have to be honest  that I have not used this on my hands.  I'm extremely sensitive and generally don't like the feeling of lotion against my skin.  For my hands, I use a very light lotion from First Aid Beauty.  My elbows on the other hand need something a bit more substantial.  So, I have been using this on my elbows.  It definitely heals the cracks that are commonly found there when it is very dry and I have not had an allergic reaction to it.  Just a very tiny bit goes a long way and I have been overall happy with the results.  It dries quickly and does not stick to my shirt sleeves if they go past my elbows.

When I saw "Mud" in the name, I thought of the mud I saw at the local mud bath spa.  Really, I thought this was like a mud mask for my hands that I would leave on then wash off.  At the very least, I imagined it would look the color of mud.  Far from it.  This thick, tinted cream that wafts floral scents from an arm's length away does not even hint of mud.  But it must be the mud that's working.  It's been a long time since my hands felt this young and smelled this good.  I can't believe the price, but if ever luxury was worth the money, I've found it here.
summary: if ever luxury was worth the money, I've found it here.

reviewText:
This is my second Ahava hand cream product to try, and while I did not like the first one, I was pleasantly surprised by this one. I may have thought to give it 5 stars but the price and the scent.

The price is out of my reach at just over $28 (at time of this review) for under 4 ounces. I do firmly believe that we should not expect everyone to sell their products for so cheap they can't stay in business or make a profit, but this is still pricey. And yes, I believe you do get what you pay for, but when I ask myself would I purchase this for almost $29, it would not fit in my personal budget.

The cream is thick and a sand-brown color.

The scent is not cloyingly sweet, which I did like, and has a bit of spice scent to it, but it also has an underlying scent that I don't care for and can't quite put my finger on. I'm glad it's not flowery grandmotherly sweet or powdery scented, but wish the spice scent came through even more. It's almost plasticy? Or?

What deserves a high rating is how SUPER SOFT my hands feel. It does take a little bit to rub it into the skin and let it absorb, but my hands feel so amazingly soft.  I'm keeping this by me when I'm writing or editing so when my hands become dry, I'll have it close. I'd definitely use this for travel--it's small enough and concentrated enough to take with me. If not for the price, I would love to rub this into my entire body, and on my feet after giving myself a pedicure, but at this price I'll use it for my hands only so it lasts.

The ingredients list sounds interesting, but honestly it's difficult for me to make a determination on how those things work at a cellular level on our skins. For a hand cream, since we wash our hands frequently (everyone should be!), most of it washes away (unlike, say, a face cream or body cream), so you have the hope that for this price some of the product does its "thing" on more than the top layer of your hand's skin before it's washed away.

I recommend if you are looking for a really great emollient hand cream that makes your hands super silky soft and price is not a consideration for you in your personal budget.

When I first got this, I set it on my bedside table until I was ready to use it. When I went to bed that night, there was a super strong smell and I couldn't figure out where it was coming from. It was coming from this container of hand cream, which hadn't even been opened yet. I had to move the tube into my closet just so I could sleep. When I finally unsealed the tube and used some, which I was a bit hesitant to do because of the smell, I was completely nauseated by the amount of fragrance coming off of it. I am very sensitive to smells but even if I wasn't, I feel like this would still be way too strongly scented. As for the moisturizing capabilities, I only had this on my hands very briefly before having to wash it off because of the smell. In that short period of time, I wasn't terribly impressed. Add to my other complaints the fact that this costs $28. I will stick with my $9 bottle of Curel for 13 ounces.

This is very strong smelling. If you don't like that, their mineral hand lotion works very well. I use both. This one goes under my gardening gloves and is re-applied after doing things that cause my hands to feel chapped - water play or projects, etc. It sooths my hands and seems to heal them better than other products.
summary: Works fabulously well, but smells very strongly

reviewText: This is my second AHAVA hand moisturizer. Like my first one, this one also has a beautiful and soothing smell to it. The texture is soft and has a  non-greasy feel to it. It's very moisturizing. I apply a thin layer of it on my dry hands overnight and wake up with very supple skin. I love it!

I have dry skin, especially in the winter time in the northeast. Per a Sephora's salesperson's recommendation (yes, I know it's odd), I've been a fan of Goldbond for years because of its ungreasy feel and effectiveness. However, in the winter, it takes layers of it to get the job done. The first time I used this AHAVA cream, I immediately fell in love with it. It not only does not feel greasy but also super moisturizing. Best of all, the smell is so subtle and soothing. A little goes a long way. The skin feels moisturized all the way to the next day before the shower.  I highly recommend it to anyone who needs a quick fix for dry skin.

Very thick, this foot cream works well to soften your feet. I used it mainly overnight and wore thin cotton socks. It is thick, so you must be careful if going barefoot or getting into a wet tub. It does not have much of a smell, that I can tell.

The price is currently $26.50. There are other very good products out there that will soften your feet, including plain petroleum jelly, so I cannot honestly say I think it is worth the price. But, it is a good product, so if you don't mind spending an arm and a leg for your feet, then here's a foot cream for you.

It softened my skin dramatically. I don't quite have leather foot, but I do like to go barefoot when possible and that includes outside. So I have tough skin. This worked well. I wishy smells smells all right, is creamy and hydrating without being too oily - but it has t had triclosan in it. Something the EU has or is taking off the market because it isn't safe to use. So, yeah. I won't be using this again.
summary: but I do like to go barefoot when possible and that includes outside

reviewText: This cream is thick and goes on the skin very smoothly with a hint of oiliness.  It has a very pleasant but subtle scent. Besides using it for my feet, I also use it for my hands overnight.

So far I am liking this product. I put it on at night after my shower and let it soak into my feet all night while I sleep. I noticed a difference just after a couple of nights. My feet feel softer and smoother. I wouldn't want to put this on during the day and walk around all day with it on my feet, but it is a great night treatment.

In general I'd say that bagbalm does work better in terms of repairing the skin but this is a nice alternative. Sort of an unusual smell but it does its best work when applied overnight anyhow. Soothes the skin and does a little repair. You get a good amount for the price.

I really love this foot cream. I'm a fan of Ahava products in general and the Dermud line is great for intensive hydration. This is a thick cream, as is the hand cream in the same line, and for me it works best to use the products at night. They make for a really great deep moisturizing treatment. After several nights use, my feet are considerably softer. I will say that it's not my favorite scent, but because I'm using it at night, it doesn't really matter.

Putting aside the practicality of using this product, when used, I found the product worked exceedingly well.

In my case, my feet are in bad shape from very hard years in the military and then what can be best described as extreme law enforcement.  My right foot also continues to suffer the effects of full blown frostbite from a winter survival course.  These prior conditions result in dry and cracked feet, sometimes painful.  Therefore, I was particularly interested in this product and its application.  Application is as you would expect for a mud type product.  The scent is not an issue and better than what you could reasonably expect.  I really have to put time aside to use the product however.  I first use a pumice stone after cleaning my feet.  After drying my feet, I apply the mud cream.  I let the cream dry for about 10 minutes and then wash it off.

The first application showed immediate, though not miraculous, improvements.  Results from repeated use after nine days impressed me.  My dry skin is nearly no longer an issue.  Period.  The bottom of my right heal, which typically developed layers of dead skin and formed one large callous pad, is nearly gone.  I find myself no longer dreading showing my feet in public.

Bottom line, even at the high cost, I highly recommend this product if needed.

First off this stuff smells awesome! It is a very thick paste that I like to put on and let it soak into my foot, takes about 15 minutes or so to dry. reviewText:
Ahava Dermud Intensive Foot Cream is part of the company's Dermud line, whose products contain Dead Sea Mud. This foot cream also contains, among other ingredients, shea butter and aloe vera to soften skin, coconut and jojoba oils to lock in moisture, provitamin B5 and vitamin E, and Ahava's proprietary Osmoter, which is evaporated mineral-rich Dead Sea water that is supposed to draw water and nutrients from the lower layers of skin to the outer layers. Unsurprisingly, minerals are major active ingredients in this product. The cream is thicker in consistency than a lotion but not as thick as a cream in a pot. It smells medicinal mixed with floral.

The cream absorbs relatively quickly when applied, but you need to rub it in. Ahava recommends that you "apply generously to clean feet morning and night, paying special attention to soles and heels." I did this for a week and found it difficult to tell if the cream was beneficial to my skin. The cream leaves a smooth coating on the skin, like silicone. But no silicone that I recognize is listed in the ingredients. Setting that mystery aside, the skin feel smooth but not supple. I could not feel my skin through the smooth coating. After washing to remove any retexturizer, it did seem like my feet were more supple and moisturized than before. But dead or peeling skin was not affected. This is not an exfoliating moisturizer.

The mystery of the retexturizer: I was sure that the Dermud Intensive Foot Cream contained silicone -and a lot of it- until I looked at the ingredients list. This is the most aggressively retexturizing moisturizing cream that I've ever used. One application produces a smooth, even slick, skin surface. It is so pronounced that the soles of my feet are still slippery on tile floor in the morning after applying the cream the night before. This is a little dangerous. My toes also slip and slide against each other a day after applying the cream. This could be a desirable effect for some people, though I don't appreciate it. I don't recommend wearing shoes with slick insoles while using this cream.

More evidence of a retexturizer is the impairment of perspiration. When my legs perspire, my feet are bone dry in addition to being unnaturally smooth. Normally, my feet would perspire more than my legs. It's weird to run my hand down my leg, when it is a little damp, and hit bone dry foot. Again, this could be a desirable effect for some people -those whose feet perspire excessively. But it certainly feels and acts like silicone. Air penetrates silicone, while perspiration and oils do not. Whatever it is, the slickness makes it a poor choice of ingredient for a foot cream. But I'm not a fan of silicone in skin care products in general, so others may not find these odd effects objectionable.

Maybe the foot cream just has an excessive amount of glycerin in it. That is not the only ingredient mystery. Triclosan is an antimicrobial agent that has been restricted  by the European Union and will soon be banned in consumer hygiene products in Minnesota. In addition to disrupting the balance of bacteria on skin and creating resistance, the concern is the effect of triclosan on bacteria in wastewater. The tube of Dermud Intensive Foot Cream that I received does not list ingredients. But the list of ingredients on the box on Amazon's product page includes triclosan. The list of ingredients on Ahava's web site does not.

That list contains methylisothiazolinone, another antimicrobial that is cytotoxic and neurotoxic. Perhaps Ahava is replacing triclosan with methylisothiazolinone in anticipation of further restrictions on the chemical. This begs the question of why Ahava feels the need to put antimicrobial agents in its products. As a preservative? To retard odor-causing bacteria? No thanks. Methylisothiazolinone is also an irritating chemical and common allergen. Along with the fragrance ingredients alpha isomethyl ionone and benzyl salicylate, it makes this product unsuitable for sensitive skin. Although it did not bother me at first, the cream is irritating to my skin after a week's use.

To be clear, there a two ingredients listed on the old boxes that are not on Ahava's web site: triclosan and 2-Methyl-2H-Isothiazolin-3-One. There is one ingredient listed on Ahava's web site that is not on the box: Methylisothiazolinone. Which ingredient list represents the product you receive is anyone's guess. Ahava's customer service has been unresponsive to inquiries on this topic.

Ingredient list from Ahava's web site: Aqua (Mineral Spring Water), Glycerin, Butyrospermum Parkii (Shea Butter), Ceteareth-20 & Cetearyl Alcohol, Simmondsia Chinensis (Jojoba) Seed Oil, Ethylhexyl Palmitate, Sodium Lactate, Propanediol (Corn derived Glycol), Cocos Nucifera (Coconut) Oil, Decyl Oleate, Glyceryl Stearate, Aloe Barbadensis Leaf Extract & Aqua (Water) & Propylene Glycol, Peg-40 Stearate, Stearyl Alcohol, Lactic Acid, Maris Aqua(Dead Sea Water), Xanthan Gum, Panthenol (Pro Vitamin B5), Zinc Oxide, Parfum (Fragrance), Silt (Dead Sea Mud), Allantoin, Tocopheryl (Vitamin E) Acetate, Iodopropynyl Butylcarbamate & PEG-4 Laurate & PEG-4 Dilaurate & PEG-4, Hippophae Rhamnoides (Oblipicha) Fruit Oil, Lavandula Angustifolia (Lavender) Oil, Methylisothiazolinone, Tocopherol (Vitamin E), Hexyl Cinnamal, Linalool, Alpha Isomethyl Ionone, Benzyl Salicylate, Hydroxyisohexyl 3-Cyclohexene Carboxaldehyde, Geraniol, Coumarin, Benzyl Benzoate, Cinnamyl Alcohol, Limonene.
summary: A Decent Moisturizer -with Some Drawbacks and Mysterious Ingredients

reviewText:
I have had many Ahava products over the years.  This is the first mud one for my feet.  My wife and other relatives enjoyed the mud masks for the face.  The Ahava regular foot and hand creams are great.  This kicks it up a few notches because of the mud.  The smell is great.  The feeling on your cracked, dry barking dogs feels great - even for us manly guys.  I also used it for my son who has terrible dry skin and eczema behind his knees.  He didn't like the smell that much, but loved the feeling of the lotion.

Unless you plan on traveling to the Dead Sea in Israel, this is a great thing to use.

I always have some sort of foot care cream tucked into my home mani-pedi supplies. I have used various brands over the years and they all work a bit. Some are just smooth and creamy, some gritty and fragranced. I have very dry skin, and like to go barefoot in the house, so I have to make sure to attend to foot care, so I don't end up with callouses and split skin.

My first step is to use PROFOOT Pedi-Rock Flexible Callus Foot File, which is soft and large and easy to hold and use in may positions. This keeps the worst of the thick skin from forming. But my feet were still dry, despite daily attention with lotion. Then I had the opportunity to try the AHAVA Dead Sea Mud Dermud Intensive Foot Cream. I rarely give products five stars, but this deserves every single one of them.

After using this product a single time, I was pleased with the results. I then used it agin, a couple of days later, and was even more pleased. This is a non greasy, not heavily scented product that does exactly what it promises, it moisturizes a problem area and helps to keep feet smooth. I have no doubt that using it through the winter will not only leave my feet the better for it, but my hands, too.

I have been using this for about 5 days straight and I have really noticed a difference in the dry skin on my feet.  The mud goes on thick, as you would expect, with just a slight scent.  It dries fairly fast so you can put socks on or start walking without too much delay.  It really seems to penetrate into the soles of the foot leaving the foot smoother and more moisturized for 24 hours or so.  I am really going to enjoy this thru the winter when everything gets dried out by the heater.
summary: Moisturizing and smoothing mud cream for feet

reviewText:
Having tried multitudes of lotions, potions, creams, etc. to soften rough skin on feet, I have grown to accept what I thought might be the best out there.  None in the past was better than a few, and others fell far short of expectations.

For myself and a member of our home, who has very dry feet (both soles and calluses), we hoped this would be the one and it is.

'Mud' sounded intimidating and we thought that this might be why the others never truly performed as well as we would like.

First off...this is far from 'mud'.  It is a wonderful cream in a sustainable tube application.  White in color, light in fragrance, it absorbed well and pleasant.

After one day...excellent.  Two days...still excellent...and so on and so on.

YAY!
summary: First AHAVA product and am beyond impressed....truly the best and NO PARABENS to boot!

reviewText: After reading the ingredient label I've decided to avoid this product. Triclosan is an unnecessary ingredient that is being proven to have harmful effects on the body. Minnesota has already banned this ingredient (beginning in 2017)
Expensive but really good stuff. Just the thing for a really good foot massage right after a shower. Great on elbows, too!
summary: Expensive but really good stuff. Just the thing for a really good ...

reviewText: After trying this a few times, it really doesn't stand out as an excellent cream.  It has a strong scent which I really don't like.  It sort of make my hands greasy and when I went to use a pen after I used it, it just slipped out of my hands.  I did use it on my elbows that are dry and it did  an ok job but for the price, I really expected more.  I use Aveeno faithfully and I still feel nothing matches up to that.  The scent of this cream really does linger and it smells cheap.  As for moisturizing the skin, it's just ok and that's just my opinion.  It feels kinda heavy on my skin especially my hands.  It's just too expensive to be so-so.  I will continue to use my Aveeno.

This "mud" (lotion, really) is thick and creamy without feeling at all greasy. It leaves my skin with a powdery finish. I've been keeping it in my drawer at work and while at first it didn't seem to do much, my skin feels and looks softer than it has all summer after about seven days of use. Love it so far. Recommended.

reviewText: This hand cream works amazingly well - it goes on smooth, absorbs fairly quickly, and leaves your hands fairly hydrated (a bit shiny too, but I can forgive that). My primary complaint is that it has a STRONG, relatively unpleasant smell that reminds me of cheap Suave lotion. My son actually walked into the room, wrinkled his nose, looked at the package and said "why would you want to smell like mud?" But it doesn't smell like mud to me; it's more of a chemical-lotion smell. And it does fade a bit, thank goodness. Still, I'd recommend only applying it when you're not going to be around other people for 20 minutes or so.
summary: great hand cream, but has a strong, unpleasant smell (a bit like cheap Suave lotion)

reviewText:
I've always liked Ahava products and this hand cream is another winner in my opinion. Not only does this cream make hands feel smooth for the moment, but it actually seems to help heal dried and cracked skin. In my case, I have to wash my hands a lot due to working on various projects around the house. This cream not only helps soften skin, but it helps protect my hands for a couple of washings before needing re-application. It does this without making my fingers greasy or slimy like some cheaper brands can.

On top of that, the smell is mild, and a little goes a long ways for me - I can use about half or less of the amount of other less expensive creams.

Check it out - you'll never want to go back to your old stuff.

Feels luxurious and seems to moisturize on contact.
Nice and thick, not runny.
Not greasy.
Unusual, but pleasing, kind of herbal scent.
I also like the packaging: it's user-friendly and looks like it will be easy to use to the end.
summary: Great product. Excellent quality and performance.

reviewText:
My first error was applying this as generously as I would a traditional handcreme.  In that case it was a little "greasy." However, I did have the feeling the result was my fault, so I tried this again the next day. This time, I applied a conservative (I mean, VERY conservative) amount and then added a little more and a little more until I feel thoroughly moisturized. The overall effect (once I took my time and got to know the product) was outstanding. Super soft, super hydrated hands. Likewise, the fragrance is subtle (and not floral or fruity) and pleasant.

My advice would be to go slow with this product. And, let's face it, less product with greater effect means the overall tube is going to last longer. (And, I suspect that I may never be able to use this entire container!) With this in mind, the high sticker-price quickly becomes entirely justifiable.

AHAVA is a phenomenal brand that I have trusted for years. Invest your trust in this much loved brand also!
summary: A Small Learning Curve, But Truly Outstanding!

reviewText: I like everything about this hand cream. I was very pleased at the reasonable price point - it's actually less than I've been paying for it's European counterpart. Also, don't be turned off by the "mud" reference - it's not muddy. Excellent creamy formula. Very rich but not greasy.

This completely healed my hands and my nails are so long and beautiful now.
I no longer need cuticle cream. Does it all. .
I am asking for this and the foot cream for Christmas.

Excellent Non-Greasy Hydration

This Ahava moisturizer was easily absorbed by my skin and I only had to use a very small amount.  However, I didn't particularly like the scent, although I didn't find it objectionable.  Others may not be as sensitive to fragrance as I am and that's the reason for the four stars.

This would be five stars if it were more fiscally friendly.
I love the quality, texture, and almost no discernible scent.
Super silky texture which left my skin feeling velvety.

This moisturizer smells fresh and does not clog my acne prone skin (which gets dry in patches during the cold months). It's paraben free and approved for sensitive skin. Boasts Vitamin E and Aloe Vera as ingredients and that it will keep skin looking young, which is something I am looking for being in my 30s now!

reviewText: Ugh...the minute I opened this I got a strong whiff of fragrance. What is it with these manufacturers that they add potentially irritating scent to their products. I do not want to smell like my face cream. Nor do I want to risk breakouts. The cream seemed to go on well but so do others and at the price point it is not a good value. Lightweight moisturizer with very little scent. It absorbs quickly. I can hardly tell that I have put it on after just a few seconds. Smells nice, moisturizing, goes on light.
Great product for daily use.
Highly recommended.

A light cream that I apply daily right after I have cleansed my skin. My skin retains its moisture, and my skin is very smooth. reviewText:
This is a pretty good facial moisturizer! It has Vitamin E And Aloe.
I use it about twice a day and it leaves my skin feeling soft, smooth and most of all not oily.
The tube is not big so use about a dime sized amount and remember a little goes a long way.

reviewText:
I am a needlework designer who works with her hands in various fibers throughout the day.  The results is very dry skin on my hands.  I also have a tendency to develop hang nails that in-grow and my dermatologist has told me the way to avoid both is to keep my hands moisturized.  I have been using a very expensive shea moisturizer but decided to try the AHAVA cream to see how it worked.  I was surprised to discover that it works almost as good as a hand cream that cost more than five times as much.  As I have to continually re-apply the cream after I wash my hands (and I do that many times a day, especially when I am taking care of my toddler grandson), this amounts to a great amount of savings.  With this product and others, I find I do have to wash it off when I am actually working with fibers (so I don't get the oils on them and discolor them).  There are some products that works okay with fibers but they usually have lanolin in them and I can't use them.

My plan is to use this product throughout the day and to apply the shea product for overnight.  That way I get the value of both in the best way.

reviewText: I have used the AHAVA "Water" formula, and liked it a good deal. This is even better. While both absorb nicely, and neither is greasy, I find that AHAVA Essential Day Moisturizer has less of a scent (both have pleasant scents) and it is less likely to transfer when my hands get wet or damp. This product is excellent on my dry/peeling cuticles.

reviewText: Wow! At first I thought, this is crazy! It seemed really expensive. And then I used it....and again, WOW!!! This AHAVA moisturizer is pretty awesome! I had radiation to my left side, and I burned pretty bad (their words... and mine). So, I don't mind spending the money on a quality moisturizer if it really works, but this seemed like a lot, even for me. Well, it turns out you don't need to use that much, and it leaves my skin feeling GREAT! No real fragrance, very subtle. I can, and do, use it every day. My skin feels soft and no irritations!
