I found daily use and also as needed of Oribe light moisturizing cream and Oribe gold lust oil is more efficient for me, I live in low humidity Colorado. I don't think I would buy it again since other Oribe products are much better for my hair type in my climate.

I use this on fine hair.  I'm not a fan of beachy waves, so normally I'd never consider this.  But in fact it can give smooth volume as well.  I spray it lightly into dry hair, aiming it towards the roots, but not like a root lift spray.  I spray from the ends of the hair, through layers, holding them out with my fingers.  I then smooth the top layer.  I get loads of volume, without waxiness or heaviness.  Love this.
This stuff really gives hair a lift for that sexy, tousled look. I section my hair and just spray a little on the roots...too much and you could end up looking like you're entering a pageant

I have alot of fine but heavy hair. It's pretty hair, but flat and straight, a style which does not do me any favors.  Stylists are always amazed at the lack of body my hair presents regardless of styling technique.  Some have even taken on the mission to create volume/body as a personal challenge - to no avail.

I began looking for a good dry shampoo as I heard its use would create some volume and texture in ones hair.  After experimenting with various brands,  closely following each ones' respective instructions, I found those claims to be true, however, the dry shampoo product, regardless of brand, always left my brown hair with a matte, grayish white haze.  While searching the internet for yet additional dry shampoo candidates, I happened onto this Oribe product.  It's kind of expensive,(full size can $40) but it lives up to its promises by adding texture and volume to my flat hair without leaving telltale residue.  You can apply a lot for "big" hair or just a bit for a little "oomph".  I LOVE IT!!

I use this spray all of the time now and wholeheartedly recommend it for anyone suffering similar hair challenges to mine.

The Oribe Dry Texture Spray is amazing.  It gives fine hair whether dirty or clean tons of volume. I love the smell and although expensive a bottle last me several months.  I would recommend this product for anyone who needs some volume help.

It is no better or no worse than any dry shampoo on the market.  It is easy to use.  I don't find it gives my fine hair any added volume or lift.  It does smell nice, but I doubt if I would buy it again.  Too pricey.

I bought this after seeing it in a magazine used by a celebrity hairstylist.  He was using it on a hairstyle I had recently received so I thought I would give it a try.  I purchased it to make my hair look "messy" and full of piecy volume.  It not only did that, but I now use it as a second day dry shampoo and it is wonderful!  It not only smells heavenly, but really absorbs the oil and odor of my hair and gives mega lift at the roots.  I just spray a little on the roots, rub my fingers around my head and viola-fresh hair full of volume.  I know this was an expensive purchase but it is the best I have found so far and I will continue to purchase this product.  I just bought the Apres Beach Spray as well and can't wait to try that.
summary: Best product for volume and dry shampoo

reviewText: The Babyliss Pro had great reviews. That is why I spent the little extra money to purchase this. Some one from the company must have written the reviews, because this is no where near worth the money. It is hard to get the curlers in your hair, once in, the curls do don't last at all. You have to purchase extra clamps too. Buy something cheaper. Don't waste your money on this product! Think twice!
Does the job very well!

My daughter has very fine hair and this product helps her achieve the curls she wants in conjunction with the dryer I bought her. She is very happy with the product . She is 12 and it does nto burn her hair. We do not plug it in, we just put the setting lotion, wait ten minutes then put her under the dryer I bought on here for 20 minutes and the most beautiful curls are created.
summary: My daughter has very fine hair and this product helps her achieve the curls ...

reviewText: Great set of hot rollers.
I love the rollers, I was a little nervous because of the cost but am truly happy the way my hair stays attached to the roller and the curl lasts well.

I love BaByliss products and am glad I got this set instead of another I was looking at.  Rollers get very warm yet they have a protective padding around them. The size is perfect for me when I want larger, relaxed curls with volume. The unit heats quickly and I let them stay in while putting my makeup on. If I want my hair curlier I use smaller sections. When I want more waves I use a little more hair in them. It's been a long time since I've used hot rollers because I've had an a-line bob for awhile which is now growing out. This gives me flexibility in the style. I also wear hair extensions and these work great on the extensions without damaging them.

I remember my mom hot rolling her hair when I was a kid with ancient rollers from Conair that are circa late 70's. They still work but they are absolutely a fire hazard. But I still remember the pins that hold them in and pinch your scalp and the scorching heat that burned my skull as the curlers set. These are a little bit of a step above.

I have another set of hot rollers which are a little more like my mom's old Conair ones-they're also Babyliss which is kind of Conair 21st century. Those are the same style-the ceramic without the velvet coating. They slip out of my thick but fine hair easily and don't heat up as much as I need them to. These are kind of a little bit of a marriage between my new age ones and my mom's older ones. They have the new clips *the clamshell kind* and the old school pins based on your preference. They are large, 1.5 inch rollers which are not enough to get tight curls. If your hair is any length shorter than shoulders, these are only going to give you bounce, not curl. They're only designed to give big waves even in the longest of tresses.

I find that these heat up quick but not instantly. The velvet coating makes them touchable quickly so you can handle them without burning your hands immediately. I find that if I tease the section before I put the hair in the curls and volume last a lot longer. However-these are not all day curls for me, at least in my hair. The body and the soft waves last a decent while, depending on the amount of product and fluff I put into it. It's an easy "set and forget" type of do that's easy to put in while you're eating breakfast, putting on makeup, walking the dog (yup, expect some looks, but it's ok). It's important to mention that hair needs to be dry while using these. Also I found that the metal clips are less likely to leave funny looking dents in your hair although they are more painful to wear. Overall, a quick way to set your hair!
summary: Nostalgic like old school Conair, revived!

reviewText: These rollers make my longish fine hair look great with body that lasts way longer than anything else I have tried, and I have tried it all....AND the fact you leave them in 5 to 10 minutes max is a huge plus, hardly anytime to put in and take out, spray and leave!  I bought the travel ones and sent up to my parents, I will review those once I get there.  I didn't even want to be without them for the week I will be there, but I know they will never fit in the carry on, so just shipped the travel ones up there.

This is great for travel and fits snug in my suitcase.  This doesn't heat up to scorching hot but a more then warm.  If I need a tighter curl, I use Kendra Thermal Styling Spray.  If I want more body, then I just use a root lifter ( right now I'm trying out Pureology ) and Kendi Oil from the Bamboo line on the ends.  I have long straight hair and use the regular hot rollers to hold all my hair but needed something for travel and as we all know, a full set of hot rollers is way too bulky and take up too much room in a suitcase.  This is perfect.

Love these hot roller.  I wanted some for traveling and these will do the job.  The whole thing is nice and compact while the hot rollers are nice and get hot quick.  I love the fact that it comes with both butterfly and metal clips.  I love the metal clips and they fit inside the rollers which again is perfect for traveling.  I use protective gloves to use hot rollers and that really helps since they do get pretty hot.  I love, love these.  Very glad I purchased them.

thankfully I could return these -  I have hot rolled my hair for 20 + years - these are the worst rollers I have ever used - I bought them because of the size - I wanted some larger ones for a softer look with mostly body - the problem with them is that they  take a long time to heat up and they don't get hot enough to reach the outer layer of the hair and they also take forever to cool down which the cooling is what sets the curl . I have a set of Remington rollers which I love- they have clips that are heated as well that goes over the outer layer of the hair so that your whole head of hair is soft and shiny - unfortunately they don't have them in jumbo but I was able to go to their website and purchase an extra set of the large replacement  rollers so that I can use all large instead of medium/ large so if you are looking for a primary set of rollers I would suggest going with Remington hair setter or the curruso steam rollers which I also love
summary: dont come close to being as good as remington

reviewText: Love the size of these rollers.

After seeing how good Amy Adams' hair looked in American Hustle, I decided to give hot rollers another try. This set is on the expensive end of the spectrum, but it's great. Four of the rollers are jumbo and the other four are almost as big, which made my thick, curly hair quick to set. The appliance heats up quickly, and I needed to keep the rollers in my hair for only a few minutes. I'm happy with the result.

not my favorite, I was looking for something other than a straightener to curl my hair, and my hairstylist recommended trying hair rollers. Being that I love Babyliss hair tools, it was my first stop. I really debated getting rollers, but decided to take the plunge because of my stylist. I used them once, to do my hair for a friends wedding. Maybe I need to do more research on how to properly use rollers, but my hair did not hold the curls, even with hair spray. I was a little disappointed, and worst, my hair was not the best in those wedding pictures! Wish I would have bought a curling iron instead, since I know how to use it.
summary: not impressed for this BaByliss produce

reviewText: After reading the good reviews I decided to give these a try. I let them warm up for 10-15 minutes and the rollers felt barely warm. I tried a second time, leaving them on for half an hour and they still didn't feel hot. I tried one just to test it and the curl fell out immediately. They're very nice looking and come with clips, perhaps mine was a dud.

This palette has great colors in it, and is the perfect marriage between neutrals and color.  The neutrals colors have just a touch of green and/or gray in them which give them a unique twist.  They stay on best over an eye primer.  Without one, they do fade fast.

The texture is not chalky or buttery, but somewhere in between.  I love the whole thing- the palette itself is a beautiful light sage green and all of the colors look beautiful in there, as well as on the eyes.  I am cool toned medium/light skinned, but I can see these colors going well on warm toned people too.

Well worth the money if you like neutrals and greens, especially.

The liner in this set is also beautiful.  It is a black liner with gold bronze shimmer in it and it looks stunning with the colors.  The liner stays in place very well and is definitely water resistant if not waterproof as it claims.

I have a lot of palettes, but this one is definitely a combination of unique colors.  The pigmentation is excellent and the durability is also excellent over eye shadow primer.  Also looks good on older eyes- does not emphasize crepe look on eyes.  Blends well too.

This is one of my all time favorite palettes. Kitten is one of the best selling shades which is also one of my favorites along with bubbly, which is a beautiful champagne color. It also has a really pretty transitional shade called bliss. This a very versatile palette. You can go from a very neutral daytime look to a deeper smoky eye for night time. And for those fun days you can have a pop of blue. The pigmentation of these shadows is awesome. Definitely worth purchasing

Stila's famous In The Light Palette is everything you would expect! Nice pigmentation, excellent blendability and wears until you take it off. A quality product. For reference, I have dry to combination skin and am in my forties with hooded lids.
Very nice everyday palette, with creamy, highly pigmented shadows. I'm very happy with it.

Snatch this up before it's gone!  Stila is discontinuing this gorgeous palette.  I have a makeup problem and palettes are my weakness.  I have been limiting myself to what I see as the "best of the best" and this acquisition did not disappoint.

The textures of the shadows are beautiful, pigmented and creamy, and the color range is on point.

- Bare is the perfect cream matte highlight for the  brow bone.
- Kitten is the perfect shade for the inner corner.  It is a shimmery, pinky cream color.  I also like it on the lid, particularly when paired with Bubbly on the outer 2/3 and Sunset in the crease.
- Bliss is a mid-tone brown with pink undertones.  It great transition color and also a good lid color for an all matte look, when pared with sandstone.
- Sunset is a rose-gold.  I love Sunset either on the lid or in the crease.
- Sandstone is a matte brown.  This shade is perfect for deepening the crease or for use as a liner.
- Bubbly is a beautiful gold that is not too orange.
- Gilded Gold is similar to Sunset and Bliss.  It is darker than bliss and also has gold glitter, whereas Bliss is matte.  It is more matte than Sunset, which is a shimmer.  I think it plays well with a lot of the shadows and works well as a crease shade either on its own or used with sandstone for a deeper look (but not as deep as sandstone by itself)
- Night Sky is a cool steel grey with a touch of blue.  You can do a cool smokey eye with this color on the lid and ebony in the crease.  Kitten is the perfect highlight.
- Ebony is an almost black.

Also included is a Smudge Stick eyeliner in damsel.  It is a great, deep brown that is almost black but not quite....  This smudge stick is very creamy and soft so don't press too hard when you apply it.  Before it sets, you can smudge it but once this liner dries it will not budge.

The packaging is cardboard and a nice color.  The packaging includes a nice-sized mirror and the magnetic closure is strong enough to keep the palette closed.  I think this would be good for travel, as the size is great to fit into most makeup bags.  Only negative is that some of the pans were crooked, but that is pretty minor.
summary: Snatch this up before it's gone!  Stila is discontinuing this gorgeous palette.

reviewText: I only like the two golds. The other colors are blah. Too pricy.

Eyeshadow, I think looks best on younger eyes. However, when I have a special event or evening I apply eyeshadow. And, the eyeshadow I use is Stila. This product is always well made, you can rely upon this brand.

The In the Light Eye Shadow Palette is a collection of Stila's eye shadows in neutral shades that look best on me. The palette also includes a Smudge Stick Waterproof Eye Liner in Damsel, a matte chocolate brown, and an 8-page look book with detailed how-to tips and tricks. The look book is fabulous. If you want cat eyes or smoky eyes this booklet is for you. It also gives tips on applying the eyeshadow for an everyday look.

The shades come in a nice packet with 10 different colors. Bare (matte ivory), Kitten, Bliss (matte beige pink), Sunset (shimmery canyon pink), Sandstone (matte light coco), Bubbly (shimmery pale gold), Gilded Gold (golden brown with shimmer), Luster (dark aubergine with gold shimmer), Night Sky (blue with shimmer), Ebony (matte black). I prefer the matte beige pink or Bliss. I have blue eyes, and this brings out the blue very well.

These shadows do not run or smudge. They go on easily and feel very light. They have great staying power, and I do not have to re-apply in the evening. Stila is a product we can rely on.

Recommended. prisrob 10-20-14
This pallete is nice and the colors are beautiful. They blend like a dream and I enjoy the eyeliner that's included.
summary: This pallete is nice and the colors are beautiful

reviewText: Stunning palette. Has shimmers and mattes. I absolutely love it for every day use.
OK
I love this palette!  The colors are pigmented and so buttery. You can create tons of different looks with this guy.

I am using my husbands account. I bought this pallette a few weeks ago and haven't used it much. I like that it's a matte pallette but just haven't got into it much yet. I love the dark orangy shade (forgot the name of it) but I am just not really sure what to do with it yet. I haven't give it a lot of thought though considering I am a makeup junkie and I have toooooo much to choose from. I think to that there is to many neutral shades. I have used the black shade more than any (so far) for eyeliner. Maybe I will get into it later and see what I can do with it. I am not sure if it's worth the price of it or not. I guess I'll decide that later.

I love the palette so much! The colors are beautiful neutrals/earth tones. They are very creamy in texture. Soft, easy to apply and blend beautifully. They are very pigmented. I prefer this over my Urban Decay Naked Basics palette. This has more colors and is ALL matte. My favorite color is the fire color which is a beautiful rust color. The black color makes for a great eyeliner and is very dark black. The looks you can create with this are endless!
My husband likes it
Smells exactly like Liz Claiborne Curve but pricier...

The smell of this men's fragrance is no legend, it's intoxicating. I received it for Christmas in plenty of time, with no hiccups, for my husband. He had smelled the fragrance in one of our magazine issues and said he'd liked it. I'm wary of buying ANY fragrance without first testing to see if it will smell the same on the skin. If I was to surprise him, I had to take the risk. It was worth it. My husband wears it all the time now. He has expensive tastes in men's cologne, and this one nailed it out of the ballpark for me! He said it was his favorite of his Christmas gifts....now that's saying something! It was worth every dime.

It stays on! It is smooth and not clumpy. It goes on well. I love the brush. It is very precise and fine. One of my favorite mascaras now.
I have to say that because it is so waterproof, it only comes off with a quality eye make up remover.
This mascara is difficult to apply and remove
summary: Not as black as I wanted.

reviewText: This is a nice, black mascara that does a good job of making my eyelashes look longer. The brush, or applicator, doesn't have many bristles to it and I find myself going over my lashes several times to make sure I get them all evenly. It does go on well though when I get all my lashes. They look black and even in length. The mascara is waterproof and I've never found it to run or smudge at all. I use cold cream to clean it off at night and it comes off fairly easily. If you're looking for a waterproof mascara, this is a good one.

This is awesome mascara! It does everything it claims to do. It doesn't flake, even wearing it overnight.  There are no clumps and the wand separates and defines the lashes to make them look fuller and longer.

I curled my lashes then tried multiple coats and didn't see dramatic intensity or depth. I have blonde lashes but they're long and full so it shouldn't take a lot to get glammed up. My lashes did stay separated and not clumped like it promises. But I really didn't notice any difference between this brand and drug store mascara. No smudging though which was nice.
summary: My lashes did stay separated and not clumped like it promises

reviewText: Wife said it was ok.  Went on easy and stayed on.  Other then that she was just ok with everything about it.  It did look good on her and I did comment but it just wasn't her cup of tea. The mascara lasted the whole day and she didn't have to reapply it which made her happy.  She has other mascara that does the same thing and she gets pretty much the same results.  If you are looking for something good, this is definitely it.  It works as it says it does and does it well, it just doesnt stand out against the crowd.
summary: Does what it says it will do and does it well.

reviewText: My girlfriend was not happy with the performance of this mascara. The mascara goes on goopy and sticky, causing her eyelashes to stick together and requiring them to be combed out. She thinks that the purpose of it being goopy is to create a fuller look, but she does not want a fuller look at the expense of having tarantula lashes.

I have dry eyes and appreciated that this mascara does not irritate them.  It was easy to apply and I liked the shape of the brush as I could easily reach the outer and inner lashes.  It also didn't smudge.  I needed a couple coats of it and still wasn't quite getting the fullness I wanted so I applied another waterproof mascara over it that was less expensive.

For $25,, it would be optimal to apply one coat and get full coverage which is why I deducted a star.  I am able to use relatively inexpensive hypoallergenic waterproof mascaras with no problems and would not purchase this due to the cost as well as not getting the volume I wanted.
summary: Good for Sensitive Eyes and There May Be Less Expensive Options

reviewText:
I have sensitive eyes. And a lot of mascara's get in my eye, make them tear up and then smudge!  Yuck.  This mascara really surprised me and I'm glad I tried it.

What do I like about this product:
1)  This mascara applies easily.  It can also be layered to thicken the lashes but I just prefer a little darkening to give my eyes a little extra pop.
2)  It really is water proof and did not smudge!  (Okay, I got a little teary eyed and none of it came off!)
3)  It doesn't feel heavy or pasty like most other mascaras.  (This may not be the case if you layer a lot- I do not.)
4)  With make up remover it came off relatively easy.
5)  It did not irritate my eyes
Overall impression:
While I am not a huge mascara user this one fit all the issues that I typically have problems with.  It did take a little bit of experimenting to get the coverage I liked but once that was done I found it an easy and great addition to my makeup regime when I want to add extra splash.  I think the big plus was that it did not irritate my eyes.  I get a lot of eye allergies and have very dry eye.  Since it was water proof and did not get in my eyes, this is this first one I could tolerate for hours.  The only real issue might be the price tag for some people hesitant to give it a try.
summary: 4 1/2 stars  I have eye allergies and very dry eye.  This is the first mascara I could tolerate for hours.

reviewText: It's a nice mascara. The brush is oddly shaped but surprisingly convenient and fits the shape of lashes well in a direct swipe. The mascara itself leaves them not clumped and soft, and pretty well defined. I'd say it's nice both for everyday use and on a night out. The waterproofing seems to work pretty well, and though I sometimes rub my eyes, it doesn't come off. For a full tube at $25, it might be a little pricey, but seems worth it.

For the price point I was really expecting something amazing, and while it's good, this mascara doesn't quite fit that bill. While it doesn't clump or irritate (and is definitely VERY waterproof), the applicator is average at best. It also doesn't make lashes look fuller or longer; basically it just gives them color. It does what it says it should do, and nothing more, so again, for the price point it's just okay.

I love this mascara.

It's super easy to apply and doesn't clump.  My lashes look both thicker and darker.  I've also had no eye irritation.

The want is comfortable as well.

No smudging, no raccoon eyes, and I find that I don't need to reapply it during the day.  Once in the morning and that's it.

Very pleased with this!

LaRoche-Posay is a brand I love for skincare, and was excited to find out they have cosmetics! I have very sensitive eyes, with mascara being the worst offender. Through trial and error, I can usually find a non-waterproof mascara to use, but finding a waterproof one that I can tolerate is like finding the Holy Grail. And EVERY time I do find one, it is discontinued! I'm currently using Palladio Aqua Force Waterproof Defining Mascara, Black but I hate it. It does nothing for my lashes, but it's better than nothing if it's raining out or I know I might cry. I first tried this LaRoche-Posay before I took a shower. I didn't bother to curl my lashes. HOLY COW! It went on like a dream, and the more I applied, the bigger and more dramatic my lashes got. It even curled them (although not as dramatically as an eyelash curler). And they were smooth and silky looking, not clumpy or with bits hanging here and there. I then took a shower, making sure the water got right in my face. I was so shocked to see that my lashes looked exactly the same afterwards! Other waterproof mascaras I've tried didn't run when wet, but my lashes would uncurl, look mangled and "chunky." This mascara left them perfect. I did have a hard time removing it, however. I can only use non-oily removers due to my acne-prone skin, so I'm sure that's why. But I had to bring out the big guns and do a lot of scrubbing. I tried the mascara for real the next day. I experienced a slight irritation (burning) in my eyeballs after a number of hours. Sometimes when that happens, if I use a product a few more times, the burning stops. It doesn't really make sense to me, but that's what occurs, and did in this case. I now have an amazing waterproof mascara! I would use it exclusively if it was easier to get off with my normal removers.

Wife's review- I have straight, short lashes, and none of the many mascaras I've ever used make them look long or full, including this one. However, it truly stays put all day long. It doesn't run, looks exactly the same when I take it off at night as it did when I first applied it in the morning. Extremely waterproof. Doesn't budge when I wash my face. I have to use makeup remover to get it off. I will probably buy it again when I run out.

Ive used this mascara for a few days, and I like it a lot. I like to wear makeup, but Im a fan of a natural effect rather than the vamp look. And this mascara helps me to achieve the look I like in my eyes. The brush applies the mascara smoothly and it does not dries up giving my lashes a fake look, which other mascaras do even when new. This La Roche-Posay mascara gives my lashes a natural enhance look, while separating the lashes in a nice way.

However, it smudges without tiny black flakes all over. I don't mind to have a little mascara stain under my eyes at the end of the day, but the flaking I cant handle, because I wear contact lenses. So, this is a mascara that I would order again in the future and recommend to others, in spite of the smudging, because the benefits of the lack of irritation and the natural appearance.
summary: A good mascara for sensitive eyes

reviewText:
I can't begin to tally how much money I have spent on mascara, though I am sure if I did my hubby would have a litter of kittens AND puppies. Tubes upon tubes from drugstore brands like Covergirl and Physician's Formula to mid-line brands like Pacifica and Eyeko to uber expensive brands like Armani and Dior. Stila used to make a mascara that was my HG, but they discontinued it and broke my heart because none of their other formulas are as good. I've been mixing and matching brands since then, like pairing Maybelline Soft as the first coat and Full with Tarte's Lights, Camera, Lashes as the second to get long, full, thick lashes though still not as perfect as they were with Stila's mascara. I am always game to try a new mascara in the hopes that it will be like the Stila Stay All Day Mascara I loved.

It's a week in and I am beyond THRILLED with this mascara. So far, this has come the absolute closest to what the Stila formula was like. It doesn't dry out my lashes, it doesn't irritate my eyes, my lashes look like I'm wearing falsies, and best of all IT SAYS PUT. When applying it goes on cleanly without clumping or sticking your lashes together. I didn't even need to use a lash comb or curler. Two coats lasted me all day with zero flaking or smudging even when I was in a dusty big box hardware store and rubbed both my eyes pretty hard. I pulled a tissue out of my purse to clean up under my eyes because I was positive I now looked like a raccoon, but nothing was there. I checked my eyes when I got back into the car, and again, nothing. The mascara stayed put. There wasn't any irritation or crunch to my lashes - they felt like they were bare even though I knew they had mascara on them. That night it took a bit of effort to remove with makeup remover as face soap and water didn't take all of it off.

The price of this mascara is a bit cringe-worthy, but La Roche-Posay isn't exactly a cheap brand. I love their skincare, especially the line for acne as it cleared my skin without causing drying or flaking like prescription meds did. If La Roche-Posay is branching out into a full makeup line, I can't wait to see what they come out with next. Maybe if they produce other items they will lower the price a little. My Stila mascara was $18 a tube, and Tarte is usually $19-$21 a tube, though paying that much still isn't something I like to do. There are cheaper drugstore brands that work pretty well, but even the waterproof ones tend to migrate and end up under my eyes. Mascara tends to be one of those things where you get what you pay for. I'd rather buy one tube for $25 and know that I will use it day after day after day (until I hit the three month toss deadline) instead of multiple cheap mascaras that I end up using only a handful of times because it just doesn't live up to its marketing hype. This mascara is worth the price tag because I know I will use it exclusively until I need to purchase a new tube.
summary: If La Roche-Posay comes out with a full line of makeup, sign me up.

reviewText: Living in a high humid area and because I wear contacts, I consistently fight with my mascara either with raccoon eyes, irritation or clumping. Le Roche-Posay's Waterproof Mascara met my expectations and beyond. It is applied easily without clumping and gives a natural look. I experienced no irritation, no raccoon eyes, and it made my lashes look amazing. I am in love! Its a little pricier than my normal brand, but there is so many wins with this that I really do not care.

This is my first time to use La Roche-Posey mascara brand.  I chose black color because I love my eyelashes to be pronounced.  Sometimes just wearing mascara and a little bit of eyeliner can give my eyes the pop.  With some brands of mascara I experienced allergy in the past but luckily my eye did not complain about this brand.  I put the mascara on in the morning and it lasts fine without any irritation while I am in the office.  Mascara does not smudge and eyelashes do not look clumped together.  All in all, mascara gives nice, clean look to the eyes.  This mascara is waterproof.  It is easy to remove with the make up removed (I use Shiseido make up remover at the moment and have no issues taking mascara off).

I swear by a BB cream that this company makes. It's expensive, but worth it. I appreciate that this mascara is said to be good for sensitive eyes, but don't think it's worth the high price compared to Maybelline Great Lash mascara at about 1/4 the price. The latter is a favorite of many makeup artists and only require one coat. This mascara requires at least 2 coats to get fuller-looking lashes and the tube won't last long.

This mascara goes on light for a more natural look.  However, it  did cause slight irritation - mainly itchiness.  It didn't irritate me as much as other mascaras, but I did experience itchiness the day I used it and the day after.  Since my eyes are so sensitive, my low rating was also based on the following short comings

- It doesn't apply smoothly.  It goes on with small clumps as if the mascara was dried out.
- It smears.  By the end of the day I had dark circles under my eyes from the mascara smearing.

I wouldn't recommend this product even if your eyes aren't really sensitive.  The smearing is a nuisance and the little clumps when applying are a pain to remove.
summary: Doesn't Apply Well, Smears, and Causes Slight Irritation to My Sensitive Eyes

reviewText:
As described this mascara does not cause any irritation which is perfect for eyes that are sensitive to certain makeup ingredients.  It is fragrance and Paraben free which is a preservative used in most cosmetics.  It is waterproof but easy to remove  when it comes to washing your face.  Does not leave the "raccoon eyes" having you to put extra effort to remove the residue left behind.

However what disappointed me was it did not add volume or length to my lashes.  It darken them but that is about it.  They did not appear visibly denser even after multiple coats.
summary: Non-irritating but does not add volume or density

reviewText:
This is the best my eyelashes have looked in years!  Almost like I'm wearing false eyelashes, in fact.

I'm in my low 50's and have been wearing Laura Mercier mascara and Julep Length Matters mascara.  The Laura Mercier costs the same as La Roche-Posay, and of course, you can't know until you try it, but it makes my eyes water.  I've never experiences sensitivity to mascara until I tried the Laura Mercier - at a cost of $25 for the tube.

The Julep mascara is good, but not waterproof.  And it can't compare to the La Roche-Posay mascara!

I started by using a eyelash curler to my clean, mascara free eyelashes.  I then applied the La Roche-Posay mascara.  The brush is great - it's like mascara brushes used to be: thick and full.  Every eyelash received mascara by using this brush.  I'm seriously impressed!

I don't normally wear waterproof mascara, because it's such a hassle to take it off at the end of the day, but this mascara makes my eyelashes look so good, I'm going to start wearing it exclusively.

My eyelashes are full but not clumped together.  They are all separate.  And they look long, which is a very nice surprise.  Consider me a new customer.
summary: This Mascara Makes a HUGE Difference in My Eyelashes - Without Irritation!

reviewText: Excellent sunscreen. I rarely reapply more than once a day, and as of yet, it still seems to help a great deal. It's light weight and doesn't leave a greasy residue. The only sticking point is the price, because for the same type of product there are many other sunscreens available that are cheaper.
summary: Excellent sunscreen. I rarely reapply more than once a ...

reviewText:
Capital Soleil, a new line of products from Vichy, combines the attributes of a serious, broad spectrum sunscreen with that of advanced skin care. These products are intended to be used year-round (not just at the beach) and are appropriate for adults, and children over six months, with normal or sensitive skin. This particular lotion goes on quickly and smoothly and dries without stickiness. It provides excellent UVA/UVB protection while leaving the skin soft and moisturized.

I remember my parents drinking bottled Vichy water, a highly mineralized bubbly water from the hot springs in Vichy, France. The minerals in the water were supposed to be good for the digestion, especially after a heavy meal. At the site of the hot springs in France were thermal spas where people would go for therapeutic treatments. Today, Vichy Laboratories uses the same naturally formed mineral waters in their line of skin care products. The claim is that the waters contain 15 minerals and antioxidants that refresh and soothe skin, strengthening its natural defenses and increasing its ability to repair.

To me, the best part of this product is that you can wear sun screen without any of the telltale negative aspects: strong coconut or other beach-appropriate aroma, or shiny, sticky, heavy-coated feel. You apply this lotion, and you are the only one who knows it is a sunscreen.

This is some great high end sunscreen.  Totally non greasy and very effective at blocking out the sun.  Used it all day at the park yesterday and was totally clear of any burn.  What's really nice about Vichy Capital is that it applies and feels more like a skin lotion then your regular sunscreen.  It also has no real scent and my skin felt soft and moisterized while wearing it.  Havent' had a chance to use it in a water situation yet but otherwise highly recommended.
summary: Almost more like a skin cream then suntan lotion....but it also protects from the sun 100%.

reviewText:
High-number protection sunscreen is a necessity here, pretty much all year round.  We thus go through a lot of it, and have several varieties.

This is a welcome addition to our sunscreen shelf, and much more pleasant to use than the Neutrogena sunscreen that I have been using.  It is not greasy or unbearably pungent.  And it does good things to the summer/gardening roughened skin on my arms, and is thus better as a skin lotion than the Neutrogena sunscreen.
summary: Softens weather-roughened skin as it protects it.

reviewText:
I love this sunscreen. 60spf may be a little overkill, but I burn easy. It is extremely smooth and almost melts into your skin, very easy to spread. It feels light and airy.  It goes much further than other brands. I often have allergic reactions to sunscreens if it is over spf 20, but I don't get a rash from Vichy. That's probably the main reason I will continue to use this one. It also doesn't feel or look greasy, which is another pro. Smell isn't too strong. Oh, and I usually apply every 60-90 minutes, though they do suggest reapplying every 40min.

I don't like the price, but I can't argue that this isn't worth it.
This is good to use daily and it has help my sister's skin. She loves it and uses it daily

I really like this sunscreen. It feels very lightweight yet very water resistant. (I know it is because it is very hard to wash it off of my hand even with soap!)  I use it on my face every day and never have a problem with any breakout or irritation. I also like that it doesn't feel like there is a layer of grease on my face. It doesn't make my made-up face "shiny" like some sunscreen does. I really like it.

I love this sunscreen. It's very light, not sticky or greasy at all. It also does not have a strong scent so it's appropriate for everyday use. I know some might think the high SPF is overkill but the reality is that must of us do not apply enough sunscreen or reapply it often enough so the extra high SPF level will at least give some level of protection. This is on the pricier side for sunscreen but it's worth it for such a well-formulated, pleasant to use product.

Vichy's sunscreen is a light and pleasant sunscreen.  It looks and feels just like any other sunscreen, an off-white creamy lotion, but the Vichy does not have a strong odor and absorbs quickly, without a greasy residue.  The slight fragrance that the Vichy does have smells pleasant, and is barely noticeable.  In fact the Vichy reminds me more of a facial moisturizer with SPF 15 sunscreen that a straight-up SPF 60 sunscreen.  With that said, I won't be slathering the Vichy on my face daily, since it is not intended to be a daily moisturizer.  Rather I've been using it on my forearms and neck when I'm working in the yard, or spending a lot of time outdoors.  It's kept me protected for hours, and I haven't noticed any skin issues or irritation when using the Vichy.

All in all... a pleasant alternative to typical smelly and sticky sunscreens.

This is a great but somewhat spendy sunscreen.  The SPF is sixty and it stays on in water for forty minutes.  It works well in both adults and children and for those with sensitive skin as it is oil free, fragrance free and allergy tested.  This sunscreen goes on easily and feel very pleasant on the skin.  Other than the price I am delighted with this sunscreen.

Living in a sunny state, I wear sunscreen daily.  As the manufacturer advises this isn't for your face, I only use this elsewhere. Because I wear it daily,  I prefer sunscreens like this that don't smell like coconut or other beach scents. This sunscreen goes on smooth and absorbs quickly. I expect this tube will last a while, as a little goes a long way.

It doesn't leave me oily and is a great daily wear and great for the beach as well.  It's higher priced, but for a 60spf and the many nice features make it worth it.

I have white skin that easily burns. I experienced no difficulties after a day in the sun with this applied, however. I did notice that the lotion caused some redness on my face when I tried it out on a day that I was to spend inside. The manufacturer, though, clearly states that this particular product is not meant for facial use (they have other products for that), so that's fine - just for the rest of my body. The product has no strong scent and does not feel greasy or sticky. It is water-resistant, but I followed the recommendation to reapply it after going in the water. I'd like to see a 3.4oz version so that I can pack it in a carry-on bag without TSA taking it from me at the security checkpoint.
summary: Don't forget to put it in checked baggage rather than carry-on

reviewText:
Terrific sunscreen! High SPF (60,) water-resistant for up to 40 minutes, light texture, good for kids and well adults. I especially like that it absorbs quickly and has no fragrance. I can use on my face in place of moisturizer, and apply makeup right away. And I also don't smell like a pina colada.

Not inexpensive, but worth the money.

Most sunscreen with high SPF--something we fair-skinned people need--create an uncomfortable coating on the skin.  Vichy doesn't.  The cost is high, but will make outdoor activities much more pleasant.

I hate putting sunscreen on my face because it feels greasy, and looks shiny. Not the Vichy Capital Soleil. It spreads easily, absorbs into my skin quickly, and leaves a matte finish that feels soft without feeling greasy. This lotion is fragrance free, but not totally unscented. It has a very slight scent that is barely noticeable, and not disagreeable. I've used it several times, and have had no reaction at all. No redness, flaking, itching, burning, or rash. Capital Soleil 60 is now my go to for facial sunscreen lotion.

Here on Maui sunscreen is a fact of life year round.  Over the years I have tried every brand and formula imaginable with varying degrees of success.  Vichy is by far the best.  Applies like a lotion and vanishes into your skin, yet still provides superior protection.  Does not clog pores or annoy with terrible fragrance.  It also nourishes your skin with valuable nutrients, something more common products do not do.  This is a very important benefit for the long term health of your skin.  Vichy Capital Soleil is high end and second to none.  I'm happy to give it my highest Hawaiian tropical sun endorsement.

This stuff is WAY overpriced.  I bought this locally at Nordstrom.  It's a very nice product but at $10/ounce, this would cost you $40 for the same amount you'd get with Layrite super hold or Suavecito high hold.  The scent is nothing to mention either.  I do like the very solid glass container and will use it for some homebrew stuff indeed.

amazing. I received a free sample and was thinking I would trash it, but one morning I had little hairs sticking up and deciding to try it. I loved it, and purchased the full size the following week. It works on all hair types- straight, and thick- tightly curled. Your hair is not going anywhere throughout  the day with this. I love it since I get a little shine too. It smells nice and light- nothing offensive.
summary: Amazing, great, firm hold all day

reviewText:
My husband has been trying various pomades, creams and gels for years since his favorite brand got discontinued. We did finally find one that works well for him, but I thought he might like trying this one.

Baxter's has a lot of great products, but their pomades leave him flat. As in completely flat hair. He's been using pomades for years, so knowing how to use a pomade properly isn't the issue. He's used a few water pomades successfully. This was not one of them. He came home from work complaining with a piece of hair hanging in his face. This is not easily re-combable which is a must with any pomade he uses- this one needs a bit of water to comb back through.

This does work for me in small amounts to sleek my hair back in a nice neat bun or ponytail, but for the tiny amount that I use, this one jar will last forever. It does wash out well and smells good. It's a gorgeous jar. I do love Baxter's glass jar packaging compared to the tins we usually buy.
summary: Pretty color, nice scent, hold too soft for thick hair

reviewText:
This has a firm, gel-like quality in the hand. The blue color doesn't show up in your hair after you smear it in.

Bests: It's got good firm hold without making the hair crunchy or brittle. I have a nice wave in front and this helps me accentuate it and still be touchable or greasy.

Downside: It works best with shorter hair on me; if my hair gets longer, it doesn't work as well, with my hair ending up at odd angles and needing further brushing and combing.

Good stuff for just after a haircut, but not as good if I let my hair go for a while.

I thought this was just an okay product. It wasn't anything special and definitely not worth the listed price. It's a gel product and gives a soft hold. My sons have wavy hair that need some type of hair product in it to keep it from getting very messy throughout the day. I've been putting this in their hair and it gives a soft, pliable hold. It's not a strong hold and doesn't really hold their hair in place but it gives a controlled body. I think the hairstyle that you apply it too would really depend on whether you liked the product or not. I was expecting a product that would really hold their hair in place but it didn't. I also tried the Baxter of California Hard Cream Pomade, 2 oz. and the consistencies of the two products are different but we got the same results from both.

Over the years, I've used pomades to control cowlicks on family members' heads as well as to give my own hair a controlled, messy look. It has been my experience that water soluble pomades can't provide more than a medium hold, fine for putting down cowlicks long enough for pictures, but not strong enough to sustain a more controlled "do." Therefore, I was dubious of this product's claim to be both hard holding and water soluble, but it proved to be both. I've found Baxter of California Hard Water Pomade can hold my hair for hours and even stands up in strong wind. What's great is that it doesn't take multiple washings or too hot of water, it simply rinses out.
summary: No Mess, Water Soluble, Hard Holding

reviewText:
I'd never used pomade before (only gel), so the first attempt wasn't too smooth (pardon the pun). It's really thick, and as I tried to work it into my hair, it was like trying to get wax in. I added some water, which helped, but future applications required serious emulsification and wetter hair. Regardless, the end look was greasier than I'd hoped for, and that wasn't to my liking. Then again, I have a friend who is a regular pomade user and he has a slicked back look to his hair, so perhaps my needs run contrary to the product's purpose.

A week or so later, with shorter hair and a better understanding, I tried it again. This time it worked better. As advertised, it held my hair in place with no sticky or stiff feeling. While not as convenient as gel which merely involves a squirt and instant application, this Baxters pomade does what its supposed to do. Ill be using it until its gone, but due to the need to emulsify and mix with water to get a good consistency, I doubt Ill replace it.

I like the way this holds hair for the duration of the day even when applied sparingly, as long as my hair is damp.  It didn't work the way I wanted when I applied it on dry hair, but great when my hair was just damp.
summary: Love the hold when used very lightly on damp hair

reviewText:
There's really not much to write except that Baxter's Hard Water Pomade is very stiff and holds my hair in place for hours.  The only other pomade I've used is Crew and by comparison, Crew is more of a creamy consistency.  Baxter is much harder and makes my hair shine.  I would imagine it's great for specific cuts such as mohawks and other spiky hairdos but for my more conservative style, it's probably not the best, nor does it make my hair especially manageable.  However, it does indeed hold very well and I use very little at a time, so it's economical.

Good stuff.
summary: Makes my hair stand on end; stiff and shiny stuff.

reviewText:
The Baxter of California Hard Water Pomade works quite well. It's easy to apply evenly and holds well. I've only been using this for a few days, but I love it so far. It gives a natural-looking finish, but holds the hair pretty well. Given the cold weather we've been having this winter, I've been wearing winter hats on a daily basis, and it's easy to get everything sorted out and looking good again. So, this pomade seems pretty resilient. It goes on easy and cleans off easily as well.

Overall, this seems like a very good product.

My son has very curly hair and the hair around his face likes to form tight tendrils which he doesn't care for.  We use this on damp hair, smooth it back into the ponytail and it stays under control.  It also keeps the ponytail from frizzing and adds shine.  I also like it for my short wavy hair.  It keeps it in place and adds texture and shine.

It is tricky to get hair to behave and still be soft, but this pomade pulls it off well.  It goes on like a thick gel, and is shiny or matte if you apply it when your hair is wet or dry, respectively.  I have found that using a little gives my hair some motion and sheen, while applying more (but still not much) allows me to go full dapper and clean cut.  It works very well and surprisingly does not make my hair feel crunchy.  My only critique is that as the magic wears off over the day and the hair is tussled out of place, it leaves the texture looking on the greasy and clumpy side.  However, it is easy to wash out with warm water and start over if needed.

This Baxter of California pomade is real easy to use, and it only takes a tiny bit to get the hold you'd expect it to provide. Also, it leaves a natural, healthy look to your style, instead of being stiff and obvious. Love it!

So I've been using American Crew and a couple other brands like bed head and  g2b (blech) for awhile on and off (depends on my hair style). I have fine hair but it's pretty full and gets some really random waves and cowlicks so styling is always kind of a pain.
I'm really liking this stuff. If you put it on dry you're hair retains a dry look and doesn't get as waxy looking as some other pomades. Personally I don't think it even feels as waxy as some others I've tried.

Put it on wet and it kinda looks like you've got gel in your hair and like gel you can always run your fingers through once it's dried to get a fluffy, styled look.

But the best part is washing it out. I can't stand going to bed with Gel in my hair so if I'm putting off a shower till morning, I've always at least stuck my head under the tub faucet before I hit the sack. Problem with most pomades and gels is it won't wash out all the way so I have to use a little shampoo. This stuff seems to wash out completely, a few minutes under the faucet with some warm water and my hair feels like there was never any product in it to begin with.

The hold is pretty strong too, I can get my short hair to lay back flat with a double helping (about 2 dime sized blobs).

It smells nice, looks kinda cool with the blue tint, I don't know what else to say.
It's definitely worth trying it out to see if you like it.
I'm thinking I'll keep buying this brand now that I've used it.

So yeah, I recommend giving it a shot. Personally I really like it.

Before I start, I'll point out that my hair is thick and difficult to manage.  Even if its cut short, gels don't tend to hold it all day.  I was looking for a solution that would help me tame the wyld beast.  Currently I use Schwarzkopf's Got2B Glued, essentially Elmer's Glue for the hair.

So a little about Baxters. The name is for Bxter Finley, who invested Super Shape in 1965 and, with that success, went into all kinds of products for men: toner, creams, soaps and shaving creams.

My first experience with this Pomade was not positive. It didn't turn my hair orange, or make it stick straight out.  Instead, it simply vanished.  I put it on, rubbed it in and that was it.  No hold that I could tell, no shine, just simple disappearance.  The second time, I used more and saw some shine (or thought I did).  The third time, I mixed it with my normal gel (Got2be...) and that did the trick.  I had the hold and the shine came out.  In short, it looked good.

Its possible that different hair types will have different reactions or results. Simply, your mileage may vary.

But for my own hair, I'll use this as a supplement to my regular hair regimen, finding that it doesn't do much for me on its own.
summary: Review: Baxter of CA Slick Pomade

reviewText: A little of this product goes a long way.  It has more shine than the other pomade.  Scent, what there is, is very unobtrusive.  A jar of this will last a good while for those with longer hair.

I simply loathe the scent of almost every single hair styling product on the market. If it's for women, it's sickly sweet. If it's for men, it has this "men's sports cologne" kind of thing (hint to men: most women hate that scent!). If it's "unscented" it still stinks. Hair styling products nowadays smell like strong clothes detergents (and vice versa). I happen to love scent and good perfume, but the products I'm referring to all smell too much, and are just too loud. You'd think everyone in America had stuffy noses; why else would all these products smell so strongly?

I like extra shine and bit of hold for my hair and noticed that some had said this product smelled nice, so I tried it. It does, in fact, smell nice. It's a subtle (yes!) citrus smell. Though clearly not "all natural" by any means (and Baxter's doesn't claim to be), it does, in fact, smell pretty darned natural. It's a lovely scent that stays close to the body (or hair) and doesn't stink up the whole room. Folks who've been trapped in a small space with someone with too much product on will know what I'm talking about here. Unless you're plugged up, a morning elevator full of freshly washed hair can be an olfactory nightmare.

Unfortunately, I can't rave about the styling properties of this pomade as much as it's nice scent. It's simply okay. Now, don't tell me that it didn't work well 'cause (surprise surprise) I'm not a man. We've all got the same hair, don't we? This is a perfectly fine product for someone with very short thick hair who wants to add shine and that pomaded look. It does not keep hair in place unless one uses so much that it feels greasy. It's a bit too stiff for fine hair. Even in hot weather, the stuff doesn't "melt" easily. To use properly, one does need to put a bit in one's palm and warm it up. Then, put your fingers through your hair. If your hair is indeed fine, you might pull some of it out. Not advisable for those with thinning hair!

So, perfectly a-okay nice smelling pomade. Too many words here for such a middling product.

I was never one to use hair products until a few years ago when I got my hair cut by an obnoxious fellow who couldn't resist making rude comments about my thick and often unruly waves that, when left to grow, turn into unrulier curls. "This is the way that people used to wear their hair in the `60s," the twerp observed,  punctuating his comments with a little giggle. Once, after cutting my hair so it would "lay," as he called it, he managed to sell me on a tube of gel that turned out to be sticky, hard, and, frankly, kind of gross.

I switched barbers to avoid this twerp, and my next stylist recommended pomade. I quickly became a convert. Pomade is waxy rather than sticky, and can be applied to your hair without drying into a hard, plasticized mess that makes it obvious that you're using a hair product. Pomade leaves a slight sheen and your hair can be maneuvered into whatever style you like.

Baxter of California's Slick Pomade comes in a nice sized (2 ounce) jar that will probably last me a couple of years. It promises to give a "Medium Hold" with a "Shine Finish." It looked and felt fine on my hair, and I recommend it.

Another product for men that I decided to try out. I'm always looking for good hair stuff because my hair gets out of control in the summer with all the humidity. This is a little bit greasyish but I find that if I just use the smallest amount on the ends of my hair, it isn't sticky and keeps my hair from getting frizzy and wild. A little goes a long way so the price is pretty good. I would recommend this, just don't overdue it.

Similar to my experience with several other Baxter of California products, this one seems overpriced and fairly mediocre compared to its competitors.  The product itself works, it provides a soft hold similar to other Pomades.  The product feels like Vaseline, but is not greasy in the hair.  It holds well, though humidity seems to make it stop working fast.  It washes away quickly and easily in water, so even a dunk in the pool will make the product stop working; other pomades I have used stay effective until it is washed out, so you can restyle your hair after getting wet and you are good to go without adding more product.

It is a fairly small 2 ounce jar, but it doesnt take much product for each use.  Sadly, it takes about the same as the other brands of Pomade, which are in larger jars and cost a little less; 2x more product for 10% less price = better deal.

As with other Baxter of California products I have tried, this one seems overpriced and middle of the road.  There are better options out there for a lower price.
summary: Overpriced but does what it is supposed to

reviewText:
Both this version and the water pomade remind me of my son's Butch Wax when he was a kid. A sticky waxy product that you put in his hair to hold his flat top straight up. They appear to have that micro glitter in them or something that makes them sort of silvery. If I had time, I'd work the Slick pomade through my hair bit by bit, I think it would work great for definition and curl. But I don't, I use it for the front of my hair that tends to get very frizzy. It works for that and works to hold some lift in the front section without the use of hairspray. Be forewarned that they assume you know how to use this product as it comes with zero instructions or suggestions. The ingredients are on a little folded label stuck to the bottom and so if you're not an experienced pomade user, look it up on the internet.

Oh, just did a Google search - this is for MEN!! lol - I got it on the Vine program and didn't realize that since it didn't say "for men" anywhere on it. They do talk about it on a youtube video as being waxy and sticky but not leaving your hair feeling that way, and I have to agree. Guess I'll give this to one of my guy friends. Too funny! I did like the scent which was a faint citrus smell. I still may keep it to style the front of my hair and keep the frizzies down, plus I'm planning on cutting my shoulder length hair off, so...

The Soft Water Pomade - is less sticky, but not by much, but it does allow me to mix it with water in my  hands and smooth it throughout my hair. I still can't believe this is for guys...I mean women have pomades. Perhaps it's traditionally a guy thing. (pomades for your pompadour!)

This is the second Baxter Pomade I have tried. (I have also used the Soft Water Pomade)  Both smell pleasant and keep my long, thick curly hair from frizzing.  This gives a bit more shine than the soft-water pomade, but it is a natural-looking shine.  It is not oily or stiff, nor is it a "wet-look" shine. It is thick and a little goes a long way.  My last jar lasted a couple of months.

I deduct one star for the glass jar, as I use this in the shower and would prefer not to worry about breaking it. But no complaints about the product.

Since the company that made the pomade my husband used to use stopped making it, we've been trying to find the perfect pomade.

He's got straight, very thick hair that he keeps in an old fashioned cut that needs thinning regularly to keep it from standing straight up. He prefers having it sleeked back for his job, think 1960s family sitcom for style and it's pretty close. He likes pomades and creams because they can be combed through during the day to touch up.

This has a nice scent, and great texture. It does add a nice bit of retro shine with a classic pomade look and feel. Where it falls down, literally, is when it's nearly time for my husband to get his hair cut. It doesn't have enough hold to keep it styled when his hair is just a bit too long and thick. It doesn't have enough hold to pomp his hair either.

I think if you have medium thick hair with a texture a bit on the fine side, this would be perfect. With thicker, heavier hair, it doesn't hold a pomp, and won't keep hair slicked back without using so much you started resembling an 80s movie greaser looking for an oil change.

On my hair, which is waist length and very straight, it's perfect for sleek looks. A small amount adds a wet shine and keeps flyaways under control.

I do like it, but because of the limitations, we are still seeking that perfect pomade.

I liked this product and I am a woman with a medium length do with lots of layers. I was looking for a product that wasn't sticky or stinky and this one is great. I also want a product that doesn't leave my hair looking greasy. You get all that with this product. The only thing it lacks is hold power and you get that in the sticker ones. Overall I am pleased and I love the smell, it is light and lemony :}

Let me begin by saying that I have really short hair. I wanted a product that I could use to give it some body and shape it into place. Though my hair stayed put when I used this product, it felt greasy to me all day. Because of that, I don't think I'll use it again.

Creamy and smooth, doesn't leave a lot of buildup, and has almost no scent.  I wish the hold were just a little bit stronger, it kills frizz but won't hold your style for a full day.  It comes in a classy glass jar.
Excellent product that meets my hair needs
I'll keep buying this until they stop making it or I go bald. Love it. Matte finish. Soft hold. Adds a little body.

reviewerName: Leah Maines, best-selling, award-winning author, actor, and editor
reviewText: This is an excellent product.  This product give very good control, and adds shine, but it doesn't feel stiff to the touch.  It has a pleasing scent too.

This product was ok - not the best or worst I've tried.  I have thick, wavy hair that usually needs heavy-duty products to keep it in line.  This tamed the frizz but I wouldn't say it gave my hair any shape or hold.  I did apply it kind of lightly though.  Hope this helps!

If you are rocking a slicked down style this is a great pomade.  It gives my short hair shine and keeps it looking styled all day.  That said, if you are doing a style that has more of a high-but-natural look like a tall pompadour this pomade may be too heavy for the look.  Depending on how thick your hair is, this cream can have the tendency to weigh your hair down deflating your pomp.  Not good.  As always, it's about using the right tool for the job - this cream pomade will work brilliantly if your wearing your hair like Blaine on Glee, but will tank if you try to use it for a style like Kurt.  Sorry for the Glee reference, but those were the first two people who came to mind with the right hairstyles.
summary: Nice pomade - a little heavy though

reviewText: This is the second Baxter product I've used and I know this is a very high quality product as the ingredients are different from other similar products, and it works much better than others I've used. I have very frizzy hair and find it hard to discover products which I actually like and work with my hair; but this cream pomade is definitely one I can use that works. I'm sold on the Baxter name now. Great product, would recommend.
summary: Top quality product delivers...I love it! Great for frizzy hair!

reviewText: I love this stuff. I wish it weren't so dang spendy though because I have to use three finger dips to get enough on my palm to evenly distribute in my hair. I tried to be more sparing with it but found that it wasn't working. At the current rate I'm going, one of these jars will last me just under a month and I'm just not into myself enough to spend so much on a single product on a monthly basis. If the price were more reasonable I would consider it, but I guess I'll call this a short love affair with a great, but expensive, product.

Baxter's Cream Pomade is a nice, clean hair product that incorporates well on your strands and keeps things looking soft and natural through the course of a day.  I have short-medium mens hair and I prefer to keep my style looking clean-cut, masculine and unfussy and this product manages to keep things in line by providing some added volume and a subtle, moisturized finish.

The compact 2 ounce jar is handy when traveling and since a small dab is all I need I expect it to last at least 3 months with near daily use. The cream gets kudos for those who like to keep things low maintenance as it easily applies to your hair, washes out with no hassle and has no perfumed scent worth mention.

It's got a nice, creamy texture that feels good in the hand and in the hair. The hold is actually surprisingly strong and yet touchable and pliable. My hair looks relaxed and stylish, never messy, and doesn't feel like it has stuff in it. This is a great pomade when working with your hair's natural waves and style, and probably not so good if you want to spike your tresses or whatever, but that's not my style anyway. I would gladly buy this again and again for the style it gives me. Highly recommended for those going for an old-fashioned, traditional, gentlemanly style.
summary: My favorite Baxter product so far!

reviewText:
I have been using this for a month now and I love it! I have short fly away hair and this pomade has just enough hold to keep my aid in place during the day without making my hair look greasy or like it has a lot of product in it. The smell is also wonderful! My wife, who also has short hair, has been using it as well and she loves it and how the smell is there, but not overpowering like many of the products out there.

This is a great pomade and wonderful for some light hold styling!

I've tried many products to control my hair and many are just terrible... either too greasy, too shiny, too thick or too much fragrance or some combination of these. I had the opportunity to try this Baxter of California Cream Pomade and this may be one hair product that I'll actually use again. It's a very lightweight cream with a consistency similar to a hand cream. Previously I had been using MenScience Hair Styling Pomade (2 oz.) and it is very hard in the container... nearly like hardened wax. It's somewhat of a chore to use it because you literally have to scoop out a dab of it and let it warm up in your hands before you can put it into your hair. This pomade is very creamy and infinitely easier to scoop out and apply than the MenScience Pomade. Although the Baxter of California Pomade is not fragrance free, the amount of fragrance is very minimal and barely discernible. It's a lightweight holding power that lets my curls curl and at the same time leaves my hair soft. It may not provide enough hold for some hair types but for my hair, it works great.
summary: Light holding power that leaves my hair soft to touch and not greasy at all

reviewText:
Whoa! I just got done using this and blowing out my shoulder length fine dry frizzy hair and it is like new hair. I used the tiniest dab I could and spread it evenly through my damp hair, then blew it out like always and wow! I never knew my hair could look this good. My hair has shine like never before. It holds a soft wave. Every drop of frizz is gone and that's a miracle because I have very damaged dry sun baked hair. My hair is now perfection.

I can't even feel this on my hands after rubbing it on them to style my hair. It has zero scent. I used a dab half the size of a pea, so this should last for a year. The only con to this is that it didn't come in a box and has no ingredient list. I like to know what chemicals I'm using on my hair and skin. But the results are better with this than anything I've yet to use and that's quite a statement coming from an absolute product junkie.

What really impresses me the most about this is the way my hair doesn't get greasy from it.  I went for two days without washing my hair after I used this and my hair never felt greasy or weighted down.  The only way I could tell something was in it was the way it stayed smooth and shiny and controlled.

This is a gentle hold that smooths and shines. It's for men but women can use it too. It won't replace a super hold gel. But this is perfection for my needs.

I've got short wavy hair and the Cream Pomade works really well to keep it from frizzing and it adds just a bit of shine.  I don't use much, and rub in my hands with a little water before I apply to slightly damp hair and work through the ends.  It gives my hair a little texture and separation.  I usually work with it until I get the style I want, and then add a bit of hairspray for extra hold.  I love the light scent and the way it makes my hair feel.  Just a little is all I need...so glad I tried it!
summary: I know these pomades are designed for men, but I like them too!

reviewText:
The Baxter of California Cream Pomade is a good pomade that isn't too heavy or greasy. A dab or about a dime's worth, mixed with a few droplets of water is enough for me to style my hair for the today. I didn't need a strong hold, just some cream pomade to give my hair some life and definition. I normally do a side swipe and the hair on my sides back.

I like the glass jar that it comes in.

My hair does not flake out.

Washing it out after a couple days is easy.

Cream pomade is less sticky, tacky, and heavy. I'm digging Baxter's cream pomade.

Recommended.

This pomade is just about tailor made for days when I just need some help with flyaways but really don't want anything else. Running from the gym to work in cold dry winter leaves my hair static-y and out of control. A small amount of this product smoothed through my hair helps me regain calm. There is minimal scent and none once on my hair. There is no shine but most days I don't want that anyway. The cream formula warms easily in my hands and smooths over my hair with a touch. It doe not leave my hair sticky or tacky.

We'll see how much summer use I get from this but right now I carry this with me everywhere I go. I compare it to Bumble and Bumble Semisumo which I normally use; for the price this is a better value. Great job, Baxter!
summary: When I want a light touch

reviewText: My previous pomade by Baxter of California didn't go as well as this one did. I guess I just needed a different level of hold, so the cream pomade is the one for me it seems. PROS: Holds my short-ish hair well and all day. It's a good hold and looks natural. The scent is very light. A little goes a long way. CONS: It's a small jar All in all, this is a very nice pomade. I'll buy this again as the other product I buy is Bumble and Bumble Sumo Tech, 1.5-Ounce Jar, which is $35 for 1.5oz and for me, this works just as good.

My roommate and I really try to take care of our hair, me for my natural curls and him for his... unusual style of uplifting volumes of waves that can only be described as "epic."  While I do not, typically, use gels or pomades as they can never tame my hair (no joke,  it has a mind of it's own) I figured I'd give the Baxter cream a try with my roommate for a month and see the results... the results being, "meh, it's OK."

My hair rebelled almost immediately as, within the hour, my curls went right back to where they were, flipping me off for my obstinance.  My roommate, however, had better results albeit not enough to warrant future acquisitions.  My roommate explained how, while his hair had a nice hold for the first hour, it quickly reverted to it's natural state shortly after he left for work and required a slight reapplication later on.  This happened throughout the course of the week as he tried and over to get it right while I went back to my usual regimen of simple combing my hair.

After a week of testing we sat down and compared notes.  My roommate noted that he has stronger stuff that costs less than what Baxter was asking, making staying with his old regimen the obvious choice while I contemplated a buzz cut.

All in all the Baxter pomade is lackluster, especially for the price when there are more effective solutions out there for less.

I'm a male with shortish hair. I use a very little bit of this pomade to give my hair volume without getting "crusty," i.e., the kind of hardened finish a gel delivers. This pomade has a very slight but pleasant scent and is easy to use. The hold is soft, so I'm not sure how this would work with long hair. For most guys, though, this pomade works well.

I didn't give this pomade five stars solely on price. It's kind of expensive compared to other pomades. It is salon-quality stuff, though, so whether this pomade is worth the price depends on how much hair-styling is worth to you.

I have used three different Baxter Pomades and they are all really good. This one was good too but for my fine hair I like their pomade for hard water better, it has a little more hold. This formula is a little light for my hair but still a very good product. Leaves your hair soft, wavy and shiny with the fly-a- ways tamed down. Not at all greasy looking or heavy. You only need a very small amount, I comb it through my wet hair and shape it and let dry naturally. No strong fragrance just a very light subtle citrus scent that goes away shortly after applying. Great stuff

I have used Jack Black Hair Gel for the last 5 years.  When I had a chance to use the Baxter Pomade I figured why not give it a try.
First off it took me a few tries to figure out how much my hair needed (turns out much less than I would have thought).  Also, it was a bit harder to work into my hair compared to gel.  It seems that where you first put it in the cream wants to stay there you have to really work it in.  However I do feel that it is easier to style my hair with the pomadae.  The one drawback is that my hair feels greasy using the pomade compared to the gel.  However my hair always feels crunchy using gel so I prefer the greasy feeling of pomade.  I think i will be ditching my gel for the pomade.
I really like this product.

I had originally written a glowing review about this product a while back. I have used this product for a very, very long time. However I just opened my last bottle. An this is not the original version. This is liquid, has a rancid smell to it. Either it isn't the original product or l'Occitane has cheapen their product (i.e. 4 Reines pearlescent cream and the shower gel) that it does not pay to pay this price for the lack of quality.
summary: not what it used to be by a long shot.

reviewText:
One would think that with a name like "ultra rich", it would be thick; however, this is not the case with this lotion. It's very thin and watery. While it does do a good job absorbing into the skin, it's very expensive and I cannot say that it is any better than Aveeno.

I do use the L'Occitane Shea Butter hand cream and it is a great product. For body lotion, you can stick to a regular pharmacy brand.

This lotion lives up to the brand. It's very good. It goes in nice and isn't greasy. The fragrance is really good, too. I'd buy this again and would recommend it to anyone who wants a great lotion from a reliable brand.
Good as are all their products.

L'Occitane describes this lotion as "rich in shea butter" and that it "contributes to nourish and protect dry skin" as well as helping "to soothe skin, particularly after sun exposure or waxing." It has a scent that is hard to define, but it reminds me of a baby oil lotion that I used to have - in that it smells powdery. It may say that it has 15% shea butter, but it doesn't feel that it is very rich lotion at all. It does soak into my skin fast, which I appreciate in the summer time. I don't think this would be a very good lotion to use in the winter, especially if you live in climates that have low humidity but cold winters. I didn't notice that this was a particularly soothing lotion after I had a sunburn and lotioned the next day, but on the other hand it didn't sting or cause further skin irritation. I've used this product almost daily for over 4 weeks, and I have about 1/4 of the bottle left.  In my opinion, there are better lotion options on the market for less money.
summary: Okay for summertime use, perhaps not for wintertime use

reviewText: This is a nice enough body lotion, but I'm not sure it really counts as "ultra rich."  The formulation is actually quite thin- much thinner than I would expect from a super-hydrating lotion.  As for moisturizing properties, I found this did fine in warmer weather, but it's not enough to handle my dry skin the depth of winter.  I'd say this is a good mid-weight lotion, but doesn't hold up to more extreme needs.  The scent is quite light, and I think most people will find it inoffensive.  To me it basically smells like generic lotion.  It's not bad, but it's kind of a shame.  L'occitane has so many beautiful scents, I would love it if this was scented with their lavender.  In any case, this is a good lotion for warmer temperatures, but it's not as moisturizing as a thick body butter.

I'm a big fan of L'Occitane products - I use their soaps and shampoos and my wife uses various beauty products.  The L'Occitane Shea Butter body lotion is one of their longstanding products.  It contains 15% shea butter.  The lotion goes on smooth and soaks in without leaving skin feeling overly greasy.  Of course I suppose there are different skin types, skin conditions and tolerances for externally applied cosmetic products, so your experience may be different.  For me, it is very effective and I love the scent and quality of this and all other L'Occitane products.
