This lotion is a product I've purchased from the local L'Occitane store and I wasn't aware that Amazon carried it until recently.  One thing I will caution you about is that I once purchased this lotion in a local store (not a L'Occitane boutique) and the lotion had a rancid, sickening smell.  I think the shea butter or whatever the other ingredients are has a definitive shelf life.  The product I received from Amazon was fresh and wasn't off-color.

Overall - I would highly recommend this body lotion.  It says body lotion but certainly doubles as a hand cream.  That's primarily what I use it for since I have dry hands.

L'OCCITANE HAS A WELL DESERVED REPUTATION FOR WONDERFUL SKIN CARE PRODUCTS.

THIS IS A LOVELY HAND AND BODY LOTION THAT APPLIES EASILY AND SOAKS IN READILY.  NON GREASY, IT DOESN'T LEAVE YOUR HANDS OUT OF COMMISSION-(YOU CAN EVEN TOUCH YOUR MOUSE!)

ALMOST IMMEDIATELY IMPROVED DRY SKIN ON THE FOREARMS. WELL TOLERATED WITH NO SENSITIVITY.  NO ANNOYING SCENT.

WITH ALL NEW SKIN CARE PRODUCTS, PATCH TESTING IS USUALLY RECOMMENDED: BEFORE ZEALOUS APPLICATION, APPLY A SMALL AMOUNT TO AN AREA YOU CAN MONITER (SUCH AS THE UNDER BELLY OF THE FOREARM). IF NO ITCHING OR REDNESS, IT IS NOT LIKELY THAT AN ALLERGY HAS OCCURRED.  YOU MIGHT THEN WANT TO TRY MORE LIBERAL USE AND GREATER DISTRIBUTION.  BUT, WHEN IN DOUBT, ALWAYS STOP USE AND CONSULT A PHYSICIAN.

OVERALL, I THINK YOU'LL BE PLEASED WITH THIS VERY SPECIAL HAND LOTION, IT'S GREAT!

Our work has soap in the bathroom that is really drying.  I love having this lotion at my desk to use after washing my hands.  It works so well that sometimes I feel like it's not even necessary everytime I wash my hands, which used to be the case.  I've used the L'Occitane Shea Butter products before and I would definitely purchase them again!

I've been using the L'OCITANE SHEA BUTTER BODY LOTION on my hands and feet just before bedtime for the past month and I am impressed with how it softens my skin, making it appear healthy and smooth.

The cuticles around my fingers are excessively dry and cracked, I usually get hang-nails easily and I have to clip them with cuticle cutters, and I get the same on a couple of my toes (not so much the cuticles but the front of the toes) and using the L'OCCITANE every night and those issues have been minimized greatly.

I still have some dry spots on my right thumb and some on my middle finger of the right hand, but otherwise my hands look and feel healthy. Likewise, my feet are in much better shape and I can go much longer in-between using the Ped-Egg on the dry calluses than before I was using the lotion.

I knocked off one-star because the lotion is somewhat greasy after you put it on, but it does dry pretty fast, and there is a floral type scent that reminds me of the "Rose Milk" lotion or Nivea type lotions, so it lingers for a while, but it isn't overpowering.

Because it is a fairly heavy-type lotion, I don't want to use it on my body because I tend to break out. Otherwise the L'OCCITANE SHEA BUTTER BODY LOTION is pretty good and worth it.
summary: Slightly *Greasy* Until It Dries & Has *Flowery* Scent

reviewText: This lotion feels so good. It goes on rich and smooth and leaves your skin non greasy. It smells so good and leaves your skin feeling like butter. The scent is really 'm ice and not over powering. Great product and will do wonders on extra dry skin.

This lotion has lots of shea butter and is very moisturizing. However, it leaves the skin feeling soft and smooth, not greasy. I'm very picky about lots that me feel greasy.

The scent is light and not overpowering, which is nice. I highly recommend this one!

I first bought this lotion about ten years ago, and even though I usually love L'Occitane products, remember not being impressed enough with it to try it again.  Since it was offered as part of the Vine program last month, though, I decided to give it another try -- but am still not that impressed with it.

Although the name of this is "Ultra Rich," I've found that it's not nearly as moisturizing as other lotions I've used the last few years.  Since I live in San Diego -- where the climate is desert-like and dry -- I prefer lotions that are more like body butters in their thickness.  If you live somewhere more humid, you might like the lighter feel of this, however.

That being said, though, it also has a tacky feel to it that I don't like; it takes awhile to sink in, and doesn't leave my skin feeling soft to the touch.

Overall, it's fine if you like a lighter lotion, but, in my mind, the 15% shea butter in this doesn't justify the cost of this, and there are better, more moisturizing shea butter lotions out there (such as some of the Ahava, Body Shop, Shea Moisture, and African Skin Solutions lotions) for a lower cost.
summary: Name is misleading -- it's not that rich and is a bit tacky

reviewText:
I've used L'Occitane Verbena lotion and shower gel for many years. I love the scent and the hydration.

I don't know why I've never tried this Shea Butter Ultra Rich Lotion before - it's great! The scent is subtle but very nice and it really hydrates your skin. Shea Butter is really good for your skin. This lotion seems even more moisturizing then the Verbena.

It is pricey, but I find a little goes a long way. Recommended.

This is the perfect blend for me.  It's not too greasy or sticky and a little goes a long way.  I put it on once a day, before bedtime and no more cracked knuckles for me.  I know this is targeted for women, but it works great for men, too.  And no worries about smelling like a flower after you put it on.  Although I received this through the Vine program, I've also purchased this product for my wife, who also loves it.

Living in a humid climate has not stopped my skin from being dry so I slather body lotion on after every shower. I have been using Trader Joe's store brand enriched lotion for years.  The opportunity to try this luxury lotion was too great to pass up.  The creamy consistency is easy to distribute over the body.  It has a delightful aroma that does not compete with perfume and the aroma dissipates.  My skin is soft and not greasy, I can get dressed shortly after applying the lotion because it absorbs nicely.  For a body lotion user this is a definite buy!

I'm a older Women, and not impressed with this body Butter.
I was expecting a thicker richer type of Shea Butter for this price.

I do Not  find it goes in my skin like the Bliss body butter does,which also leaves my skin softer,
and my hands look younger with the bliss. (its also expensive but worth it)

L'Occitane shea butter does not feel thick to me, its more thin, and my body/hands do not
feel hydrated. Or I'm just use to a thicker body butter.!

The smell is pleasant and does not interfere with my perfume.
The pump has to be used with my left hand to pump, which Is uncomfortable , or the bottle stands on
my dressing room counter backwards!

I could only give this lotion 3 stars..
It's Ok..

This is a lighter lotion, but it seems to do the trick pretty well.  Doesn't clog your back up and all that.  I'm not crazy about the smell though, it smells like sunblock.  I'm assuming that's the shea butter, but its not my favorite lotion smell.
summary: Light, but it moisturizes... but the smell............... :P

reviewText: Long lasting and not oily..as usual smells wonderful.  I loooove this brand, as it was not oily or left with any residual feel.  Only a little goes a long way.  I use this for both my hands and face,

This very light body lotion has an ultra-light, clean scent that will not compete with your cologne. It leaves behind no greasy feel, and it is quickly absorbed into the skin. It is perfect for use in the warmer months of the year, when a heavy-duty cream is not necessary. It helps smooth work-weary hands and feet. The pump bottle makes it easy to use and readily available.
summary: Very Light L'Occitane Shea Butter Lotion

reviewText: I'll admit that I am no sort of lotion snob. I tend to buy the pretty generic stuff in large bottles for everyday use. While I am willing to spend a little more for top of the line mositurizing/healing cream (like Eucerin Redness Relief Soothing Night Crme, 1.7 Ounce or Eucerin Intensive Repair Extra-Enriched Hand Creme, 2.7 Ounce Tube) for times when my hands are extremely dry and cracked, I realy can't see the point in spending a lot of money for a [relatively] small bottle of body lotion for everyday use. This stuff may be as creamy and smooth as you can get, and it does have a pleasing aroma, but I still find it cost prohibitive. I was happy to use my sample bottle, but this isn't a product that I would be willing to spend money on on a regular basis. For the cost of this bottle, I can get two bottles of the generic stuff that are three times the size and that will last six times as long. The math just doesn't add up.
summary: Feels good and  smells good, but why is it so expensive?

reviewText:
I have used L'Occitane's 20% Shea butter for my hands.  They are constantly dry since I have to wash my hands at least 20 times a day.  It has been a life saver.  Before using the cream I was constantly getting paper cuts and my fingers could get rough.
So I was excited to try the body lotion.  It is a lot thinner but it also does a great job of coating my skin even after I wash it, it still stays on.  The lotion has a smooth, milky texture that glides wonderfully on the skin.  The only thing I don't like it that is has a rather strong smell that is little chemically.  If you are highly sensitive or allergic you may find it too fragrant and find yourself sneezing.
I really enjoy using this product, it is good for dry skin and retains moisture better than most lotions.
summary: milky with a smooth texture it leaves coats my skin well even after washing

reviewText: L'Occitane has a great reputation and I've used their products in some high-end hotels.  I had high hopes for the Shea Butter Ultra Rich Body Lotion.  By go-to brands are Kiehl's Creme de Corps (excellent and expensive) or Lubriderm Advanced Therapy (excellent and cheap). Compared to both of those, L'Occitane fell short.  It's comparatively thin and after a few hours the alligator skin on my legs emerged, requiring a new application.  I was also not a fan of the jasmine and ylang ylang scent. I would never have guessed that was the scent without reading Amazon's description.  I would not describe the scent as floral in any way...just stinky!

This sunscreen is oil free and skin is not hydrating after application. Skin looks like nothing was applied after washing. This is not a bad thing at all, but I expected something more rich. This this lotion will be great for oily skin.
The ingredients are great, and it absorbs quick, also make up application was good.
The package is not fancy, looks a bit cheap.

I've been using this for about two weeks now and overall think its a good product.  As moisturizers go it's a good one and I really like the fact that it doesn't smell and goes on really smoothly without any greasy or tacky residue.  The SPF is a bit low for me for everyday use and I do consider that a flaw. The packaging is nice and the container is pretty robust.  Overall a really good product.
summary: Good moisturizer, alas not a fountain of youth

reviewText:
This face cream delivered as promised--my face wasn't dry all day and it didn't feel like I was wearing an oily face mask.

One of the things about face cream that my significant other hates is that it usually smells like your granny's creamed-up face. This cream doesn't have a distinctive smell, so rejection is averted. Despite the face that it says it's oil free, it does have a heavy feel to it as you're putting it on, not that watery feel from some other oil-free creams (which I prefer). I don't usually react to skin products, and I didn't react to this one either.

Because I usually use some kind of hydrating cream anyway, it was hard to tell if this cream was any better or worse. I didn't have people commenting on how haggard I looked all of a sudden, so that has to mean it's working as well as the others ... right?

One of the main reasons why I wanted to try this cream was because it promised to give my face an extra boost with its added vitamins. In the salon I've had cream with vitamin C added into it forming a sort of cake onto my face that rolled off like dead skin by the end of the day; this cream avoids all that grossness and simply melts into your face. It has protected me from the Texas sun the few times that I've ventured out in to the 100 degrees and stayed in it for more than five minutes. I don't suffer from facial redness or puffiness, so I can't comment on those qualities.

All in all, I can recommend this one as a good purchase.

I chose this product specifically with a two week beach vacation in mind, knowing I would be getting a lot of sun and salt water, both of which are very drying.

I've been using it for over a week now and I've found that even if I apply it directly after a shower, my face feels VERY dry within an hour or so.  It looks sort of greasy going on and doesn't give me the "glow" that some other moisturizers give.  It's a relatively thin consistency, which might be good if you're someone with oily skin or who doesn't appreciate creamy moisturizers.  But I've had to supplement this with another moisturizer just to keep my skin hydrated.

I expected this to be far more hydrating than my typical moisturizers since it specifically says "super hydrating".  I am underwhelmed by the performance.  The two things I do like about it are that it doesn't have a strong scent (VERY important to me) and it has sunscreen included (also very important to me when choosing a moisturizer).  I'll go back to my other moisturizers and keep this in my travel bag.  There are better choices out there.

Super Hydrating is right.  My skin feels so soft after using this and not at all greasy.  In fact my makeup goes on BETTER on top of this than it did over the moisturizer I was using.  And you don't even need a primer!  There is no scent and the texture is wonderful.  I wish the SPF was just a little higher, but for everyday this is exactly what I've been searching for. Highly recommend.

I did find this moisturizer to be very moisturizing.  However, I like my moisturizer to do more work.  It hydrates and blocks the sun, but I like a face cream that has some retinol or highlighiting properties.  Cream is of medium consistency and little on odor.  It goes on very smooth.  For moisturizing I recommend it.

It's funny, so many cheaper brands of facial lotion fail because they try to do so much. They try to be the deepest moisturizer ever, or get rid of wrinkles, or for some unknown reason think it's a good idea to heavily perfume their lotion so we'll feel luxurious or something.

What I love about this straightforward and simple face cream is that it does exactly what it says and nothing more. It moisturizes my combination skin perfectly, not too heavy, not too light, and the sun protective factor works great. I can't smell it at all, which is perfect.

On most days, I spent about 1 to 2 hours out in the sunshine gardening. If I forget to use sunscreen, I definitely feel some soreness on my face and neck. So having sunscreen included in my normal daily facial moisturizer is great.

I was also really impressed that the pump dispenser dispenses an accurate amount to cover my face. When I first used it, I snickered at how little it gave me and I pumped out three globs of it and started covering my face. I quickly realized that this facial lotion goes farther than most brands do, so one pump was actually perfect for my face, and I'll use a second pump for my ears, neck, and back of my neck. Given how little you need to use for effective coverage, this actually seems like a pretty good deal as well as being an effective product.
summary: Unobtrusive facial moisturizer with effective sunscreen

reviewText: This is a very pleasant product with no residual greasiness and somewhat reasonable SPF coverage. I like the bottle, the texture and the way it makes my skin feel soft and rejuvenated. The price is somewhat steep at $40 and that is the only negative quality. Makes for a great gift.

My family has a tendency to develop deep, deep crow's feet, and it's something I've been battling against for awhile.  I live in Seattle, where the sun isn't a huge problem, but I still try to do a daily regime of moisturizer / sunscreen near my eyes every day.

I tried out this "Hampton Sun Super Hydrating Face Cream" and was pleased with the result. It has no scent or color, which is perfect. It goes on smooth and absorbs into the skin without residue or stickiness, which is also perfect. The applicator is easy; just one pump gives you the correct amount. It's a small bottle but a little goes a long way with this type of product.

The only drawback is the low SPF.  I usually use a 30 or higher, even up to 70 if I can get it. 15 is good enough for daily usage I suppose but isn't really a sun blocker. On the rare sunny days in Seattle, or if I got on a trip somewhere, I definitely need something stronger.

If you're looking for a nice moisturizer with sun screen that doesn't have much of that 'SPF' scent, this is a good one. Not too sure about the 'super hydrating', but the first time I tried it, I was amazed at how quickly it was absorbed and that it hasn't felt greasy at all, nor has my skin felt dry while wearing it. It provides decent coverage on that front, and a little does go a long way. SPF 15 isn't the strongest sun protection out there, but it can add up if you're using other make-up that provides additional protection.

I'm a ProActiv user, yes even in middle age, and I'm always skeptical of beauty creams. When I was younger I tried all kinds of expensive creams and just ended up wasting my money. I tried this particular product through the Amazon Vine Program have to say I like it. I have very oily skin, but contradiction to my oily skin, the North Carolina climate makes it so dry, so in an effort to moisturize without adding to the oil problem, my make-up tends to cake up and my pores are enlarged. Unless I paid lots of money, I could not find ONE cream that resolved oily skin, didn't dry out my skin and one that had SPF protection. I've tried this cream for about two weeks now and I can say that it's not oily, it moisturizes and it has sun protection all in one. I put it on under my make-up and it lasts, at the very least, eight hours and it doesn't enlarge my pores. I'd say this product was a keeper for this middle aged woman, but I'm having a problem with the $40 price tag. However, if you're one of those people who are used to spending $100+ on your face creams, this might be a refreshing alternative.

With no discernible fragrance and zinc oxide used for the SPF factor rather than chemicals, this Hampton Sun might be worth a try if you've had a reaction to other, less expensive anti-aging creams.

I do have a tendency towards allergic reactions, but have had very good luck with Neutrogena product line since I was a teen, and they're typically my go-to for my very basic beauty regimen. However, I'm always willing to try new things, and with still an occasional acne breakout happening on my now-wrinkled 50-year-old face, I figured maybe switching to a different moisturizer might make a difference.

I've been using the Hampton Sun for 40 days, with no noticeable difference in skin texture, tone, or wrinkled-ness (yep, technical term there!). It is easy to apply, feels very nice going on, and disappears well into the skin (I was worried about this with the zinc). I still got the occasional pimple while using this, so either the moisturizer I was using wasn't causing it, or I haven't given this one enough time to get rid of whatever effects the Neutrogena had on my skin. I'm leaning towards thinking it's just my skin and I'm stuck with a few zits every so often.

I'll continue to use the Hampton Sun and if the pimple situation changes, I'll revise my review accordingly. Otherwise, unless you have had allergic reactions to other face creams that contain chemical sunscreens or fragrance, I don't see an advantage to this product over much cheaper options available at your local drug store.
summary: Good for reaction-prone skin, others can stick with cheaper options

reviewText:
This is not a misting spray. It is a serum type of bottle that squeezes out the perfect amount of moisturizer for one application.  The design of the bottle is clean and easy to use.

 This was your eyes are soaked to the skin very quickly.  It is smooth and yummy.  I am able to put my foundation on immediately after applying this moisturizer.  I really wish you could test moisturizers to see if the SPF is legit....I hope it is.  Living in Florida you need a good SPF lotion daily.

This one is light,  not heavy. I detect no smell, but I also didn't huff it to find out.  This one is a bit pricey compared to others.  The active ingredients are zinc oxide and. Octinoxate...not sure what the latter one is.  Must apply 30 minutes before sun exposure.

I wear this face cream everyday as I am always outside gardening, doing yard work, or taking care of my flowers. Even though I have a car, I walk wherever I go, so I need something to protect my skin from the aging effects of the sun. This is great as it protects from both UVA and UVB rays, which is something many people forget to look for. There's more to sun protection than just the SPF.

This face cream is light and easy to put on in the morning. I reapply mid-afternoon, just in case, and I wear something a little stronger if I'm going to the beach, but this does work, and it feels great on my skin. My skin is so soft.

Also, even though this is advertised as fragrance free, it does have a nice light scent, almost like a faint whiff of almonds.
summary: Very light for everyday wear in the sun

reviewText:
This delicate, unscented cream goes on smoothly and a little goes a long way so it's economical to use.  I find that it does a good job of moisturizing without being heavy or greasy and my face feels softer after I use it.  It's absorbed quickly, leaving no sticky residue.  I've worn it both alone and under makeup and for me it works well either way.  If I apply it 5 minutes or so before I put on my BB cream, it doesn't interfere with it at all.

I really like the pump applicator; it's very convenient to use and dispenses just the right amount of the cream while at the same time keeping the contents safe from oxidation and airborne contaminants.

If you spend a good deal of time in the sun, you might prefer something with a higher SPF but for me and others like me who get only slight sun exposure, this offers decent protection.
summary: Good general purpose moisturizer with SPF 15

reviewText:
I love this Hampton Sun SPF 15 Super Hydrating Face Cream as a daily moisturizer. I don't mind the low SPF of 15 since I'm usually at home during the day. When I'm going to be out in the sunshine I can use something with a higher SPF number.

It feels so light, not heavy or greasy and works well under makeup. It does help to cut down on redness and has really made my skin feel so soft. You don't need to use a lot so there's no need to "lather" it on like I've had to do with some skin care products. There's hardly any scent to this product and I appreciate that.

Well worth the price.

Overall, I liked this moisturizer. It was non-greasy, very lightweight and I forgot I was wearing any once I spread it on my face. The label says it's "Super Hydrating" but it didn't feel so at first - only hours later did I feel a baby smoothness to my skin.

It's a little pricey for such a small bottle but since a little goes a long way, it's not too bad.

My main concern, however, is that the SPF is very low (only 15) so I prefer to use this only as a daily moisturizer if I'm just going to work and back, and don't plan to be outside much except for my lunch hour. I wouldn't use it if I planned to spend a lot of time outdoors. Sadly, that also rules out taking it along on a trip - which is a shame, since it's the perfect size for traveling.

Ironically, the brand is called "Hampton Sun" but a SPF15 wouldn't be enough for the sun in the Hamptons!
summary: Lightweight Odorless Moisturizer with Low SPF

reviewText:
I have somewhat sensitive skin and find many moisturizers to be irritating. I was pleased to discover that this product moisturizes effectively without the bothersome irritation. I also appreciate the fact that the lotion has almost no odor.

As for the mythical age reducing/anti-aging component: moisturized skin tends to look younger and this product is a very effective moisturizer. I have only been using the cream for a week or so, so can't really speak to this component too well. If at any point I notice that the clock has stopped (or reversed!) I will update this review. (From years of experience; don't hold your breath.) Also, for heavens sake, use a more effective SPF with this moisturizer because 15 certainly isn't enough!

I do like the companies environmentally friendly approach to packaging, so the 3.5 stars I give the product (1 star off for SPF, .5 star off for price point) is rounded up to 4!

Recommended for those needing an irritation free moisturizer, who don't mind the price point.
summary: Good for sensative skin but watch the SPF

reviewText: Cleared up my face

Brush arrived broken...had to spend 5 mins trying to reassemble the middle piece from the outer piece. I finally got it and used it twice and seems fine. Annoying though cause I bought clarisonic brand and paid the extra money. Had nothing to do with shipping..it obviously wasn't put together to start with
Wonderful product and quality.
love this machine , need more new heads tho .
love the pricing of the 2 cleaning heads, the packing came a little torn up and looked used. but the brushes looked and work great

I usually order these for double the price off another website and was really happy to find them on Amazon. Also really liking the acne sensitive version as it's much softer and feels more gentle on my skin. Very happy!

The brushes I received do not fit into my Clarisonic. I don't think there is much more to say.

Not Recommended. prisrob 06-04-13

This brush head is perfect for acne prone skin as the brittles are very dense so it prevents any irritation from occurring on acne prone skin.

My previous sensitive skin brush seemed to dig into the skin too much, so I prefer this brush head.

I love my clarisonic and take very good care of the brushes. I remove them every time I use them and allow them to dry overnight. I use my clarisonic once a week and my skin stays very soft and smooth. This product does not reduce pore size, but it does keep my pores so clean that they are invisible. The directions say these brushes are gentle enough to use daily but I haven't needed to use my clarisonic that often.

I purchased these heads to replace the one I had. After just a few uses, the brush is showing some wear, it still works but I can see the bristles are slightly bent. My other brushes lasted much longer.
summary: Works well, but are showing some wear

reviewText:
This review is from: Clarisonic Replacement Brush Head Twin Pack for Acne Cleansing (Misc.)
Ordered the DEEP PORE CLEANSING BRUSHES and some one threw the wrong brushes into the box. Well accidents happen. Amazon said this 'product is not from them' and caused me loads of grief and aggravation in trying to rectify their error. Calls, letters and a trip to the post office.........not what I expected from you guys. I bought tons of stuff and wonder why your customer service was non existent now?
I think you owe me.
Buyer beware --- is it Amazon or a sub contractor? Big difference in how you are treated.
I wasn't sure I needed new brushes until I replaced mine. If you use your system everyday I recommend you change them every 6 months or less.
I like this even better than the sensitive skin brush. Very gentle and really cleans pores well. Causes no problems with my roscea either.

Having had the machine since mid-2011, it's something I use about once a week. I've needed to spend some time cleaning out the dead skin cells (i have the older machine) and I have had to replace the band in the groove with a standard rubber band (used to have a different band, but it popped off long ago). Otherwise, it's lasted much longer than I would've suspected.

The suction isn't too bad, but on the highest setting, will leave pale skin somewhat pink. It does leave the skin looking better, and I would purchase this product myself.
summary: Still going strong a few years later..

reviewText:
This machine really does work to make your skin look brighter, smoother, and evens out tone.  I was on the verge of switching my moisturizing routine because my skin was looking dull.  After trying this machine, I realized I didn't need to switch.  It's very easy to use.  Make sure you watch the instructional video first.  There are two heads, a small round one and a larger oblong one.  The smaller head is for areas you want to treat more delicately.  It comes with filters, which you must change out after each use.  I plan on using this only a few times per year but I think the instructions say that you can use this a couple times per week.  Personally, I wouldn't use it any more often than once per week.

When I do a treatment, I wash my face first (I use Olay Daily Facials), dry my face, then use the machine.  After a treatment, my skin does look a little reddish and irritated.  The process isn't really painful but there is a bit of mild discomfort.  I apply my nighttime moisturizer (Olay Total Effects Night Firming Cream) and go to bed.  In the morning, my skin looks much brighter and clearer than before.

It comes in a nice box with instructional book, a DVD, two heads, two packages of filters, and wall electric plug.  I'd like to note that while running, it does make a bit of noise, so I wouldn't try to use it if someone is trying to sleep nearby.

I really liked the feeling this device provided while I was using it.  It felt like my skin was getting very clean, but, unfortunately, after I was finished the surface of my skin was covered with tiny vein fissures.  I used it on the lowest setting and did not use it aggressively, but my skin looked almost like it had been burned afterward!  I put chamomile on my face and it calmed down by the next morning with just a hint of redness, but it scared me when I thought it might be permanent!

I love the idea of this unit and if you have hearty skin I think it could be a great benefit in keeping your skin clean and bright so I gave it three stars, but if you have Rosacea like me you might want to steer clear of any kind of device like this that aggressively stimulates the skin's surface.

Cheers,
Claire

PS - It always makes my day to know that people find these reviews helpful. If you'd also like to ask a question or leave a comment I usually respond the same day, so if you have a question or comment (even if it's just to say, Hi!") feel free to post it below.
summary: Do not use if you have Rosacea!

reviewText:
I'm not getting any younger. In fact, I'm pushing 35. Guys typically don't use these types of products, but my concern is looking good, not impressing others. So, I decided to check out this product. Plus, my wife could try it too.

First, I'd recommend watching the DVD. It's really helpful since this isn't a "plug and play" type of product. The machine comes with three tips designed for different parts of the face and neck area. Make sure to put the tip on correctly.

Once you're ready, it's best to have a clean face. Then, you go over the skin with the tips using levels of suction that you feel work best for you. Level 1 seems to work the best all around. The DVD explains how to hold your skin and use the wand.

The company recommends using sunblock for a couple days after treatment and let me second this! You don't want to look older due to sun damage while trying to look younger.

Overall, I've had decent results with this product. It doesn't work miracles, but I've noticed my skin does appear tighter and healthier. Some fine lines and scars appear to be lighter. I also use Retin A, so it could be a combination.

I can't say this machine works miracles and it's very expensive. But, if you want to cut down on blemishes and fine lines, it could be worth your money. I haven't had any issues with suction or other problems, so I can't comment there.

Bottom line: it's pretty good if you have the money, but don't expect miracles.
summary: Good product, but don't expect miracles

reviewText: I have used this product quite a few times over the past few months.  I was excited to receive this product and was looking forward to the results it promised.  The first few times I used the product, it was amazing and I was very happy with it.  After these first few uses, however, it began to lose suction.  Overall, I was not impressed by this product, especially for the price.  I would assume that there are other products on the market that are of the same quality but for far less money.  I would suggest researching other products before considering this one.

I asked my wife for feedback after she has been using it for couple of months. She had a big smile on her face and says: I LOVE IT. I think that sums it up. She feels the product is totally justified in cost, and has excellent quality. It came with a training DVD which she watched.

In the beginning, it takes a bit to get used to it, but then on, it's really simple to use. She feels the product has really brought about a firmness, tenacity, and a lovely smooth and healthy feeling to her face and neck. She as a woman, feels empowered by this product. Many times at night I have seen her lovingly using this product.

She has really not faced any problems as being said by some other customers. Maybe the company has upped its game on Quality Control.

I recommend this product with reservations.  Although I did see improvement in my skin, I have concerns about both the performance and design of this system

The product is packaged in an attractive teal box.  The system itself is encased in rather cheap looking plastic and contains a separate power cord, three diamond heads and some filters. There is an adequate dvd that should be viewed prior to use. It is easy enough to set up although the heads are hard to remove.

First you decide which area of the face or body you are going to treat. You then choose which tip to use: normal for body and less sensitve areas, fine for face and sensitve areas or precision for delicate and hard to reach areas such as around the lips and nose. A small disposable filter is placed between the device and the head. Choose the level of suction--I never used anything greater than the first level.  Holding the skin taut, you then glide the head across the area two or three times. The skin is sucked into the vacuum where the diamond tip exfoliates.

I have mildly sensitive skin and found this device a bit rough. Although the DVD states that pinkness is to be expected and will disappear after a short time, I found mine lasted into the next day. I decided to use the device only once a week as opposed to the recommended two to three times a week sugested. My device also did not go over my skins as smoothly as demonstrated in the instruxtional dvd. Based on my reaction to the more gentle tips, I did not use around my eyes.  I did see results.  After the first treatment, my skin was velvety soft. After seven weeks of one use per week, I did notice some slight refinement overall. This year, I developed a small but annoying  line over my lips. It is like a light smoker's line (although I've never smoked), It probably annoys me more than it should. It has diminshed but not disappeared.

I would avoid this machine if you have very sensitve skin or adjust your usage as I did. This may delay the results. Overall softness was the most noticeable benefit although there were other small improvements. I would have preferred a retractable, longer power cord. The tips should be replaced after ten uses and the filters must also be replaced. So factor in the associated costs. (You can get the parts on amazon.)I did not experience the suction loss others complained about. I wish the tips were easier to remove and were marked in different colors.

This is a pricey machine. It does afford one convenience and privacy and is less expensive than repeated spa visits. It is easy to use and I did enjoy some positive results, most noticeably, increased softness. If you have delicate or very sensitive skin I would not risk it. With those caveats in mind, I would recommend it.

I ordered this because I thought it would help with the little tiny wrinkles I have around my eyes and forehead. I don't use it nearly as much as I'm supposed to, but I have noticed a difference in the smoothness of my skin. I think the little wrinkles are completely gone. Other people have noticed the difference in my face as well. I keep being told that I look healthier. Now I haven't done anything else different except to use this machine, so I know this is what they are talking about. I haven't had any of the other complaints that people have posted on their reviews about losing suction or bands breaking, so far so good. I will update if any of that happens. As of right now, I am pretty happy with this little device, I look healthier, and feel better about myself already.
summary: I'm pretty pleased with this product so far

reviewText:
I have a few wrinkles on my forehead that I would really love to see reduced without surgical intervention.  I have had microdermabrasion done at a spa before and enjoyed the results, so I thought this might be a less costly option.  It is less costly than repeated spa treatments, but it is also far less effective.

After using the machine for a couple of months, I can say that I have noticed some reduction, but not nearly as much as I had hoped.  I feel my expectations were fairly realistic considering what I know about my skin as well as my experience with the procedure, and I certainly wasn't looking for a miracle.  Perhaps it would be more useful to someone with only fine lines and not anything significant enough to be called a wrinkle.
summary: Not bad, but not great either

reviewText:
I've been using this once a week for a couple of months now. I found the instructional DVD very helpful, so I would definitely recommend watching that first for everyone as it shows you proper form when using the device.

I have combination skin, meaning I tend to break out, but I also tend to get dry patches from the drying acne products I use. As such, I'm finding this microdermabrasion device very useful at keeping the dry skin under control and also helping to prevent outbreaks. So it's 'two birds with one stone' in that regard. I tend to use it at a level 3 on my face and a level 4 anywhere else. It also eliminates those dry winter patches in just a couple sessions, which is great.

On the bad side, I question the quality of this device somewhat. Most of the reviews on Amazon complain of the system losing suction. I haven't had that problem yet, but I ran into another. One day after using it I noticed scratches on my face, they looked like cat scratches.  I hadn't noticed a scratching when using it because of the strong suction. I examined the device and looked at one of the interchangeable diamond tips and it had plastic sticking out at the seams from the mold when the thing was made. I smoothed it out with a nail file and didn't have a problem again, but I had those scratches on my face for a week! I would definitely make sure to examine the diamond tips when I buy replacements for it. Otherwise I like it, which is why I took off one star.
summary: Works good, quality is somewhat questionable

reviewText:
First, I need to warn potential buyers that if you have rosacea, do not use this machine on your face. I have rosacea and even on the lowest setting, the Nu Brilliance machine made my skin furious. No biggie - we rosacea sufferers know that dermabrasion may not be for us and this machine is definitely too harsh for our sensitive skin.

With that said, I used the machine on my less sensitive bits (forehead, back of my hands, arms, legs) and it is amazing. The diamond tip seems like a silly addition (is diamond really better than any other material?) but it works. My skin looks healthier, fresher and younger after only a few weeks of use. I have had absolutely no problems, no loss of suction, no loose pieces. The machine is sleek, super easy to use and feels very well put together.

All in all, I would recommend this for any home microdermabrasion seeker.
summary: Excellent home microdermabrasion kit for the price

reviewText: My skin is really sensitive.  It breaks out with most lotions and cleansers.  It doesn't like to be fussed with I've found out so as much as it kills me I often let it go on its own with the occasional help from a cleanser in the hotter months.  I've always wanted to try one of these machines but I worried that my face would have a meltdown.  Luckily for me the Nu Brilliance works beautifully and didn't cause any issues after use with my face!!  I've noticed that pores appear smaller and fine lines are not quite as defined.  I definitely love this machine and am glad I have it!

I was very impressed with everything about this microderm system. From the ease of use to the incredibly detailed instructional DVD, this machine surpassed my expectations. The results I got from this product were immediate. I could tell a difference in my skin as soon as I finished my first treatment.

I have been using this for the last month and have had positive results. I have sensitive skin and use this 2-3 times weekly and have noticed that my skin feels smoother but I cannot see a difference when I look in the mirror. However, I have clear skin and have discontinued my normal exfoliation procedures in favor of this Nu Brillance system.

The system provides three different tips and varying speeds for your skin. As recommended, I started with the gentle tip on the lowest speed and have worked my way to higher speeds. I use the gentle tips on my cheeks and the coarse tip on my jaw line and neck. I will continue to use this system to keep my skin feeling smooth and suple.

Whenever I test teeth whiteners or wrinkle creams, I use them in certain areas only. Then I can tell if they cause enough improvement to cover the costs etc.

Well, with this Nu Brilliance Microdermabrasion Skin Care System, I only used it on the left side of my face, every single time. I used it as directed in the included video, which I watched twice. I also watched a few youtube videos on this system and professional performing MDA on patients.

Ultimately, I would say this decreased my sun spots (freckles from too much sun tanning all my life) by a decent amount, and it removed the 'baby fuzz' on my 44 year old cheeks. Otherwise, I'd say it did absolutely nothing else. My skin is not tighter. My pores do not seem at all different. My skin feels and looks almost exactly the same in every way. Of course, if I had done my entire face, both sides, there is a possibility that I would see a difference, but how much? Enough to cover the cost of this machine? I don't think so. If I buy and use a wrinkle cream and have to get all the way up to the mirror, spend five minutes debating IF there is a difference, then I'm thinking it better be a very reasonably priced cream that at least smells nice etc. The Nu Brilliance didn't do much and I've used it faithfully in an effort to bring an honest review to folks that may not have money to throw away.

I hope this helps. Personally, I would not buy this machine again.

Sheri Gill - Writer, Mom, Mage
summary: I used this on only one side of my face for weeks. An honest review.

reviewText:
I'm pretty disappointed by this machine. A real microdermabrasion treatment is when crystals are blasted across the skin's surface, picking up dead surface skin cells along the way. The crystals and dead skin cells are quickly sucked up through a different tube in the same wand and go to a disposal bag.

This machine has a little metal crystal-cake inside the wand. The suction pulls your skin into the want tip and rubs it against the little cake-thing, which basically scratches a layer of skins cells off and vacuums that off onto a little cotton pad just below it. I'm not so sure this is good for your skin - I could be wrong, but it's WAY more abrasive on your skin than a real microderm treatment at a spa (and I have about three sessions a year and I exfoliate daily at home). It seems to me that the suction helps plump up your skin because of the way it sucks up your skin into the wand.

I'm not willing to do this to my skin any longer. I don't recommend the machine.
summary: Not like a real microderm treatment

reviewText:
I've been using Nu Brilliance for approximately 3 months now about 1-2 times per week.  I have had absolutely no issues with any mechanical failures or loss of suction.  It performs exactly as promised each time I use it.

First impressions:  It's a very sleek design:  both machine and packaging.  Simple controls.  Nothing complicated.  I was a little annoyed at the push to watch the DVD, but it's not bad and it really does help you understand the right way to use this.  I did find that it took about 2-3 times before I had perfected my method.

My method:  I've found the small tip works best for my entire face.  I get better suction and results that way.  The larger tip didn't work as well on this area (maybe just the shape of my face) but it's perfect for my upper chest and arms.  I don't think it really takes much longer to use just the small tip.  Also, I find that I am comfortable with it set on the 2nd level.  It causes slight burning and makes my skin red for a couple of hours (which is normal and what you want it to do).

Results so far:  It's pretty much instantly smoothing which feels great and my skin is less dry - it absorbs moisturizer really well.  I definitely notice my cheeks feel much tighter and firmer and my overall color is better - I've got a nice pink tone.  I was at a dinner party recently and was given a photo from it and I was surprised at how tight and "glowing" my face looked (and very pleased as well).

Several years ago I had tried microdermabrasion at my dermatologists office.  She advised it would help with the acne scars I have on my chin and forehead combined with the use of a Retinoid cream.  I think I did 3 sessions of it but chose not to continue it because of the enormous expense of it.  The NuBrilliance feels nearly identical to what I remember of the professional treatments.

I haven't used it long enough to claim any miracles, but it is a fantastic exfoliater and it definitely makes my skin look better and tighter and smoother.  At the price offered it seems that it would pay for itself very quickly.
summary: Easy to use, great results, no quality issues

reviewText:
I was a little nervous about using this on my face, so I prepared myself by watching the instructional DVD twice and reading all of the enclosed material. The DVD is very reassuring, and very misleading. They make it sound like you just need a little practice at the lowest setting and all will be well. Not true.

Right out of the box, my unit functioned poorly with the fine tip attached. I started trying to use it on my forehead just like on the DVD. They must have turned the unit off for those DVD demonstrations. You cannot slide the tip smoothly across your face like that. If you have adequate suction, as soon as you start to move across your skin, the tip pops off your face. With my unit, suction was sporadic and mostly nonexistent with the fine tip attached.

I switched to the precision tip, which gave me more reliable suction, but I still couldn't use it as instructed, because it HURTS. I was not pressing hard, but it was like pushing sandpaper tightly against your face and then dragging it across the skin. I don't have particularly sensitive skin, but this was so harsh that I decided to check some reviews before possibly damaging my skin. I'm glad I did. I won't be using this unit on my face again. One reviewer mentioned that people have been injured by this product, and she herself was under a doctor's care to heal the damage it did to her skin.

On the DVD they say your face will have some redness for about 30 minutes after a treatment. Once again, untrue. Many hours after use, there were still red patches on my face, and my forehead and nose had a burning sensation.

I thought maybe I could at least get some benefit from the machine by using it on the dry and calloused places on my feet. For that I used the coarse tip and a higher suction level. It was a complete waste of time. The only place you can get suction is on the bottoms of your feet. No edges or contours, because you have to the the entire tip flat against your skin to get suction. I have big calluses on the outer edges of my big toes, and there was no way I could get the tip flat enough to get any suction in that area.

I cannot recommend this product, and I suggest you read a large number of reviews carefully before making your purchase decision. I'll stick with more gentle forms of exfoliation, and accept my fate of being old and ugly.

I was very excited to have the opportunity to use and review this machine through the Vine program. I have not found any flaw with the product as other reviewers have mentioned. I it nicely packaged and all attachments have gone on smoothly.  My face is sensitive and using the low setting I had zero redness, when I moved up to setting 3 I experienced a slight redness for less than five minutes.  The no mess aspect of microdermabrasion is fantastic, I remember the days of sand like particles flying around my eyes and up my nose.  My skin feels great and I notice my mouth and eye area are looking smoother.  I predict with regular use the fine lines will continue to fade a bit more. Honestly, this is as good as going to a facialist for treatments and I like to be in control of my skincare.  No appointment needed!
UPDATE- I have used the product twice a week and I do see a great improvement in my skin.  Smooth with nice texture, the fine lines are less obvious to me and I am my greatest critic.

I have never had microdermabrasion, so I wasn't quite sure what to expect. Microdermabrasion is for aging or damaged skin. It isn't for acne. It helps get rid of those fine lines and facial scarring. This machine basically vibrates a small metal plate (reminds me of a metal nail file) against your skin as it suctions. (The vibration is caused by the suction.) You rub it over the problem areas and it renews your face. I did not notice much difference in my fine lines. Admittedly, I don't have many. It did make my face feel fresh and awake after. It seems to increase the circulation to my face and give me a more youthful appearance in that way. The tips for this machine have to be replaced every 10 uses. NuBrilliance Precision Diamond Tip 11 count You can order replacements through Amazon. It comes with 3 tips for various uses. Each tip needs to be replaced after 10 sessions. Each filter needs to be replaced every 2-3 sessions. So, know that there will be a small upkeep cost in this machine. It works really well. I have not had problems with it loosing its suction or had any difficulties with the machine itself. It also comes in a very pretty box, if you were thinking about purchasing this as a gift.

Really loved the product and I bought it even though I saw several reviews that said the suction stopped working properly. Mistake-The suction function stopped working on the lower settings almost immediately (2nd or  3rd use) and after 3 weeks the suction stopped working all together. I loved the results I got during the brief use, but unfortunately had to return it.
summary: Loved it but stopped working after 3 uses

reviewText:
I got this same machine out of a large well known mail order catalog.  I've had mine for two years and it has worked perfectly.  I use a new tip after every five uses, and I always do my arms and hands when I do my face.  I found I can't use high suction without redness which lasts over twenty four hours on my face so now I use it on the lowest suction.  The redness still lasts over two hours.  I have very mild rosacea.

I use only the fine tips.  It doesn't do anything for wrinkles but it smooths the surface skin beautifully.  It keeps blackheads and whiteheads almost non existant on my slightly oily skin.  I don't need to wear any foundation at all thanks to this as my skin looks better without it.

I sometimes use Peter Thomas Roth skin peel pads before I use this if I want an extra smoothing.  It takes at least five uses before you start to see lasting improvements.

I don't recommend using this more often than every week.  It is a very harsh thing to do to your skin, scraping off the top two layers as it does.  Your skin needs at least a week to regenerate.  I also do not advise using anything at all on your skin for twenty four hours after you use this as you have removed the outer acid mantle and anything you put on your skin will sink to the deeper layers.  Ladies, those are chemicals in all those creams and moisturizers, and your skin can't keep them out of your body after the acid mantle is removed.  This is just my opinion on this.  I don't want chemicals sinking into my skin when it is raw.

I had a dry scaley patch of skin between my eyebrows and after three treatments with this it's gone.  The tips get dull very fast.  They are nice and sharp at first and do the job perfectly but when you are using them after they are dull it's more painful and harsh on your skin.  Only five uses and I'm ready for a new one.  I haven't had any problems with loss of suction.

I think most women will be pleased with this.  It definitely makes your skin softer and smoother with weekly use.  Always use sunscreen when you are using this.
summary: I've had it for two years, not one problem

reviewText: Antica Farmacista Bath and shower Wash has a nice light citrus smell.  It didn't seem to lather up much but did leave a light moisturizing after feel. The one big negative and reason for not giving this another star is because of the pump bottle.  This has to be one of the worst pump handled bottles made.  It would only dispense a small amount and it is not fun to have to keep going back for more gel.  For the price and pump bottle, I can only give this a moderate recommendation.  The market is flooded with bath and shower washes and unless you are a big fan of the product I see no reason to change.

Overall I find this body wash to be about what I expected. It's a satisfying treat but nothing to make it a new absolute favorite. The wash itself is fine; it lathers and cleans like any wash I'm used to. The scent (grapefruit variety) is nice: gender-neutral, not too fruity or sweet, and more complex than what you'd usually pick up at the drugstore. It's not a particular favorite, but should have broad appeal. I really don't notice it once I'm out of the shower, though.

The bottle is attractive, and gives the impression of something you'd find in a nice hotel. The pump isn't especially convenient, though. I need about five pumps to produce enough lather for a whole wash; each pump is small so I don't feel it's a large amount, just an inconvenient process. You'll also be bent over if you don't have a shower ledge at a comfortable height. It needs to be resting on something since you'll need one hand to hold a sponge and another to work the pump top. All that to say, the packaging seems luxe, but I don't actually like it better than an average squeeze bottle.

This might be a good choice if you want something that looks extra fancy, or happen to know you LOVE one of the scents. Otherwise, it's nice but not remarkable.

The shower gel wash leaves your skin soft and the smell is very pleasant. My husband really liked it but it is way too expensive to use on a regular basis.

The container is the worst one I have ever used. The container is square and very awkward to use. The pump is impossible to use as it stays down when you pump. I you need to pump more then you have to lift it to depress it again.

I cannot recommend this product (even if the soap smells good) as it is very hard to use and way to expensive.

I am a huge fan of the body washes and soaps that have citrus in them.  My skin reacts really nicely to them and I get a nice clean feel without my skin getting overly dried.

This is a really nice bottle of body wash.  I like the light grapefruit scent, which I really only smell right when I'm using it.  No scent is left on my skin once it is washed off.

I've only got two things that I really want to point out with this one.  I generally spend about 1/2 the price of the current twenty-five dollars for my body washes/shower soaps.  So at $25, this seems a bit high.  Also, the consistency of this soap is a little thin.  I'm used to thicker soaps that lather really well.  This does lather, and it does a good job, but it is lighter.
summary: Light, Clean Grapefruit Scented Bath Wash

reviewText: My wife and I are totally enjoying the spa like feeling that we get after using the Antica Farmacista bath and shower gel.  It's got a light and luxurious grapefruit scent that is very invigorating.  In addition, it lathers and rinses perfectly leaving your skin nicely moisturized due to it's fine botanical blend.  What's more, the light scent does not interfere with my wife's preferred perfume or my cologne.  The simple, but very elegant bottle in which it comes, also displays beautifully in our bathroom too.  I highly recommend this product.

This shower wash has a really nice fragrance. The grapefruit gives it a nice, fresh scent. The gel lathers up nicely and rinses cleanly. I did find the pump to be frustrating to use. It only dispenses a very small amount (just a drop) every time you press down on it. It presses down smoothly but is very slow to go back up all the way. It takes a while to dispense enough and thats really frustrating if Im in a hurry.

And Im not sure why this wash is so darn expensive. Yeah, sure it smells nice, but there is nothing special about it.  I think that $25 for a 10 ounce bottle of shower gel is way too much. The only reason I got it is because I was able to get a review sample for free. Otherwise, I would never spend that much for a shower gel.

I got this for my wife to try out. I thought it would be great to get a better wash than we usually use. The body wash works like most other washes and does a good job of getting you clean. The only real difference is the scent which is a little stronger and lasts longer. Overall I think this product would be great for a gift for someone but not for everyday use as it is quite expensive.

At the time if this review this wash was going for $25 for 10.5 oz. I usually buy all natural and organic products so I do sometimes see washes that run $10-15 for this size (although I try to buy on sale.) I admit that I agreed to review this product because I was curious about what made this shower wash so special that they could charge so much. I all don't know.

The ingredient list - missing from Amazon's page at the time of this review - includes two sulfates, petroleum by products, and a ton of chemicals in the 21 ingredients listed. Of those the are only a couple I know for sure I would count as natural: water, honey extract, silk amino acids, sesame seed oil. Nothing special here at all that I can see.

The fragrance is fine. Lightly grapefruit. Texture is standard as well. Washes fine.

All this to say that I can't see a single reason why this would be more than $6-8 at any store. I'd rate the wash as average. But with the very high price this moves into the two star realm. I don't recommend it. If you don't mind the chemicals you can buy 3 or 4 large body washes for the money.

Grapefruit Bath & Shower Wash

I like this shower gel.  It smells good (of course that is an opinion), citrus clean, lathers really well & feels gentle on my skin. The scent is fairly unisex; not flowery or heavy musky/manly.  It is a really pleasant experience to use.  Is it worth the extra expense?  Maybe but I'm not sure I would pay the current cost for another bottle ($25).  The ingredients are not that unusual for a shower gel.  On the other hand, the scent is really quite good & not cheap smelling & it does leave my skin feeling soft & very lightly scented.  Or if you just want to treat yourself/someone else; I do like having splurge bath products for days I want to pamper myself.  If you have room in your budget, it's a good product.

Zinc Oxide is a physical sunscreen rather than a chemical one, blocks both UVA (320-400 nm) and UVB (280-320 nm) rays of ultraviolet light. Chemical sunscreens are less effective and carry unnecessary health risks. ZO is insoluble in water, used in many industries, in ointments, creams and lotions. Non-irritating, non-allergenic and non-comedogenic, used by athletes as a bandage to prevent soft tissue damage during workouts. ZO must be NON NANO / UNCOATED UPS -2 ZO which has a mean particle size greater than 30nm, when applied to the skin do not get absorbed into the body, do not enter the bloodstream, and are not a threat to human health.

SPF is a measure of how much longer someone will be protected from UVB rays than someone wearing no cream. If the sun reddens unprotected skin in ten minutes, for example, a person wearing SPF15 can be exposed to the sun without reddening for 15 times longer - 150 minutes. While UVB rays are behind the redness of sunburn, UVA rays damage the skin's DNA at a deeper layer. Both radiation types can cause skin cancer. The EU recommendation is for sunscreens to offer a UVA protection factor that is a third of their SPF.

Active Ingredients: Octinoxate 3.0%, Titanium Dioxide 3.0%, Zinc Oxide 9.0%.
Inactive Ingredients: Alumina, Butylene Glycol, Citric Acid, Cyclopentasiloxane, Dimethicone, Dimethicone/PEG-10/15 Crosspolymer, Ergothioneine, HDI/Trimethylol Hexyllactone Crosspolymer, Iodopropynyl Butylcarbamate, Iron Oxides, Lauryl PEG-9 Polymethylsiloxyethyl Dimethicone, Lecithin, Methicone, Micrococcus Lysate, Octyldodecyl Neopentanoate, Phenoxyethanol, Plankton Extract, Purified Water, Silica, Sodium Chloride, Sodium Hydroxide, Triethoxycaprylylsilane.

This is a brand that on their Website it is claimed ""A micronized physical sunscreen, with the cosmetic benefit of a skin-perfecting sheer tint for the face""... Dumping all those chemicals along with some ZO does not make it a physical sunscreen. This mix is worse than a roof tar. I got to this product since one of the top reviewers for a phony diet publication has written a five star review on this mix. It is amazing to see what some producers get to charge for damaging chemicals in the name of marketing.

reviewText:
First off, I love the color.  I don't have anything like this and I used it immediately upon receiving it (it was June's High Shine Club selection for me).

I did have to use 3-4 coats to really get it to be opaque, but light colors are often like that for me.  I think I am going to try it in the future over an opaque white polish; it should look great that way.  It was a good texture when wet (not too thin or too thick) and was easy to apply and I like the brush.  The finish on my nails is super smooth.

However, I did get chips on a couple of fingernails within 24 hours.  I had tried to be careful, and my nails aren't that long, so this was a little disappointing.  I touched up with new polish in the chipped areas and it's hard to tell I did any touch up unless you get really close.  So, I think my manicure will still last for a few days, though I expect to have to do more touch-ups now.  (I did peel a whole bunch of oranges and the polish didn't get messed up, so that was nice.)

I used a Seche Vite quick-dry topcoat with this.  I do have an Essie topcoat and I may try that next time to see if staying within one brand results in increased performance.  Overall, however, I'm pretty happy with this.

I actually came across this sort of accidentally. See, I was removing some dark red nail polish from my fingernails, and it left behind this really awesome pinkish hue. No, I did not use a base coat, and yes, I do realize the pinkish hue was a stain. But this got me thinking...I would pay for this look. I had no idea if I could replicate it, and it was a little uneven so I thought, "Wouldn't it be great if there was a nail polish that could give me the same effect?!" Turns out, there is. It's Essie's Pink Glove Service. I ordered it a couple days ago, received it today, and put it on. My nails are adorable. They look so natural and feminine! I would recommend this to anyone looking for a classic, elegant look for their natural nails. :)
summary: Love it, love it, and love it.

reviewText: I received a sample of this product from an esthetician in the skin products & cosmetic department of a medi-spa where I was checking out product lines. About 1 week after I received the sample I applied it to clean, healthy untreated skin and within 5 hours I had developed huge red streaks & tiny little blisters along my throat and jawline in exactly the same pattern as my fingers had applied the cream! A few days later, it started to peel..very tender and painful for several days and still shows discoloration along my jawline! After looking at the number of chemicals in this product, there is no telling which of them may have caused this reaction. From now on I will stick to my tried and true Perricone products which are created by a top dermatologist & researcher and skip these chemically-wannabes! Never again will I trust any of Strivectin's products!
summary: CAUTION! LOT'S OF CHEMICALS IN THIS STUFF! I Broke Out in a Red Streaky Blistery Rash!

reviewText: I think it is working! My jawline is firmer and my double chin is going away. Skin feels tighter and looks better. I have tried other drug store brands but you can feel the difference in the product as soon as you touch it. I should add that I am in my mid 40's but everyone thinks I am in my early 30's.

I had high hopes for this product due to the reviews I had read and from the product description. Sadly I will never be able to see any effects as I developed a rash that has gradually worsened over the last 2 to 3 days. Within an hour or two of applying it for the first time my neck and chest went pale pink, this went darker and spots also started to appear. I stopped using it and have been taking benadryl but so far it isn't going away, although I am sure it will in due course. A very expensive mistake!!

I had planned on buying other StriVectin products but it would seem they aren't suited for me.

I am 44 years old and have never had an allergic reaction to a skincare product or make-up in the past.

The StriVectin-TL Tightening Face Serum is a good serum at moisturizing faces, but does not immediately erase lines as it touts.  The serum definitely helped with the dryness I get on my face - as I age, my skin is slowly going from combination skin to more normal/dry and I find myself having to apply lotion twice a day to alleviate any dryness and flaking.  The StriVectin really helped keep my skin moisturized throughout the day, but even after a month of using the product, I haven't noticed any noticeable change in the number of wrinkles or any type of tightening effect on my face.

The serum itself is similar to a lotion.  The lotion goes on smoothly, absorbs quickly, and has a soft, pleasant scent.  It did not cause any type of skin irritation, and when used in conjunction with a facial moisturizer did help with the dryness.  It cannot be used as a standalone - without a good facial moisturizer, the moisturizing effect doesn't last very long.  Overall, this isn't a bad supplement to my daily facial routine, but it's also easily omitted since not much difference was noticed.  While it's good to try once, I'm not convinced I would buy this in the future as there as other serums that work just as well at a fraction of the cost.
summary: Helps with Moisturizing my Skin, But No Major Dramatic Change in Skin

reviewText: Per the wife: I love this face serum. It goes on like a light lotion rather than a serum. It immediately absorbs into the skin and is easy to use under sunscreen, moisturizer, etc. It does not break out my skin and makes the skin look firmer and tighter. I am very happy with this and would definitely buy it again.

This face serum works great.  I use it for my smile wrinkles next to my eyes.  It works by  increasing  the water content in your superficial layers of your  skin,  improving the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles.  It moisturizes your skin and makes it look healthy.  It sort of puffs up your skin and then the wrinkles are less pronounced.

This was my first time trying a StriVectin product. The TL Tightening Face Serum is a white lotion that is in a pump dispenser. It has a mild, pleasant scent. It is very pricey, & I have never used a tightening serum that costs this much, so I'm not able to compare it to similar professional brands. I like the scent, it is not flowery (which I sometimes have irritation with), & the lotion dissolved quickly.  As with any new cosmetic product, I started with a very small amount to make sure no irritation occurs.  I did not have any problems/ irritation using this. After applying, I do feel a tightening effect, however it is not a cure all for wrinkles & my sagging skin. I'm not sure if my expectations were too high based on the cost of the product, but for me, it was not a "fountain of youth".  Some of the things I really liked about this product: 1) paraben free 2) did not cause irritation 3) pleasant scent.

reviewerName: the old lady who lived in a shoe
reviewText: I can feel and see a difference just as soon as I put the product on my face. My face feels smoother and I see diminished wrinkles. I am a 61 year old grandmother and do not have very many wrinkles on my face. I am using the Strivectin for neck tightening too. After application, you can apply your normal daily lotions and serums. In time, the product says it will contour my face. I have no idea if that will actually happen. Just seeing less wrinkles and ones that are not as deep, I am sold. I will be using this day and night.
Product feels nice on skin and has a nice lemony scent. Hard to tell if it really tightened as much as it claims, but skin does look moisturized. Didnt experience any negative side effects.

StiVectin products, in my experience, are some of the best, and I trust them.  They are made in the USA.  This one, though, wasn't the best for me.  This might be a good one to get a sample of before buying because it is very expensive.
It's a white lotion in a pump dispenser.  I use 1-2 pumps per application so there are many applications in a bottle.  It smells a bit of citrus but it is a fairly natural, subtle scent.  It goes on and absorbs immediately.
It does seem to tighten my skin some.  I would not say that it brings back "natural youthful contours" but that might be partially because my face is a lot more fat than when it was youthful.  I tried it on my hands, and that's where I could REALLY tell it was tightening!  It does tighten my skin and it makes me look better rested.  So that's good, but, it STINGS.  It doesn't cause redness, but it makes my face sting and itch- especially my cheeks!  That's where I need it the most.
It doesn't make my face red though.  It feels like it does, but it leaves my skintone as it normally is.

This has been my experience with this product, and it's been nothing but good. In fact, just yesterday someone told me my skin looks really healthy. Thank you.

reviewText: What exactly is this product for?, seems to be the question predominating most of the reviews. The confusion has resulted in lots of bashing. Is it deserved? The ingredients are mostly geared to lightly hydrate and refresh the skin. They  include glycerin, aloe,and cucumber extract which all do feel refreshing on the skin and have healing properties. Glycerin, which is the second ingredient listed after water, attracts moisture from the air and an open bottle of pure glycerin will attract enough moisture out of the air to dilute the solution to 80% glycerin and 20% water. The results shouldn't be expected to feel like an arctic breeze wafting over your skin. But it does lightly cool and refresh as it's ingredients would suggest and are intended to do.  About 5 ingredients down the list is listed Mica. Mica is a mineral that has reflective properties, included to produce the "shimmer" properties of the product. The product has a pearl tint that it transfers to you skin as well. The result can be flattering and delicate. I would guess that this spray is best suited to younger, smooth, unblemished skin where it highlights those qualities. On sun damaged or less youthful skin, it highlights the irregularities and has, perhaps, the opposite effect that a user probably was looking to achieve. What I find baffling is why the box has printed prominently, "Smart, serious sunbathing", since the formula seems to contain nothing to protect the skin from UV radiation which would make it "smart" since UV ray damage is the primary cause of premature skin damage and aging.  The ingredients would suggest this product would best serve younger women with fair completions who want to hydrate their skin during normal activities and who prefer a pale highlighted appearance. Perhaps the chemists and the marketing people weren't invited to the same meeting. If you're looking for a hydrating and refreshing toner a much better choice might be Dermalogica's Multi-active toner sold on Amazon for $25 for 8.4 oz. For "Smart, serious sunbathing" definitely buy something with an broad spectrum SPF rating of perhaps 30. For a "shimmer", there are products that have a more even and consistent effect if you are looking for reflected highlights, or consider a bottle of pure glycerine at $7 for 16 oz. on Amazon. It is still one of the best stand alone skin products and is included in a multitude of creams and lotions. I gave it only two stars primarily because the marketing seems to imply something that might give a user a false sense of security even if it does enhance and refresh that particular user's appearance. It might be ideal for your complexion, but understand its ingredients  and use it accordingly.
summary: It shimmers and cools.......but likely is not for you. Here's why.....

reviewText:
As a makeup artist, I have worked with all kinds of concealers.  I have seen some of the best and some of the worst.

This concealer comes in a pen which turns up from the bottom.  There is a little window on the pen which allows you to see the exact product that is inside (including color) and you can see when the product is coming up toward the top.  This is worth mentioning because so many of these twist pens are easy to twist up too much because it takes a LOT of twists to get the product up.  If you twist too much, the pressure continues and you waste a lot of product.

APPLICATOR
The applicator is a flocked sponge type finish.  That allows the product to come up through a bunch of small holes and disperse nicely across the pad.

HOW TO APPLY
The best way to apply this concealer is to dab on the inner corner lightly (MAKE SURE TO MOISTURIZE WELL BEFORE USING THIS) and then gently tap the product with your finger and make it spread across the under eye area, getting less intense as it moves toward the outer corner.

COLOR
The color I tested out was Medium.  For reference, my skin tone is MAC NW25, Bare Escentuals Medium Beige, and Too Faced BB cream in Nude Glow.  I found the medium to be a touch too light in tone for my skin, but I could still use it if I set it with medium mineralize skin finish from MAC.  On lighter skin tones it worked nicely (as in NC15) as it is.

COVERAGE
As for coverage- it is light to medium in coverage.  If you are covering very dark circles, this might not work as well for you.

SETTLING INTO LINES
This is one of the few concealers that does not settle into the creases making you look ancient.  I tried this on a variety of people from aging dry skin eye area down to late teens with oiler skin.  It worked very well, especially on the dry aging areas.  That is very hard to find concealer for as it tends to age quickly as it settles into the creases.  It did not stay on as well for oilier areas.

FINAL COMMENTS
If purchased in the correct color, this concealer is expensive, but it does work especially well if you want the concealer to be undetectable on dry or aging skin.  I did not find any adverse reactions for anyone that I tried it on (myself included) and it did seem to last fairly well all day.

It is a contender for my top list of concealers, with Graftobian being at the top.
summary: Like a Second Skin If In Correct Color

reviewText: This is a wonderful product that does cover dark circles, but if you're under the age of say, 28, or if you have sun-lines around your eyes, it tends to cake, like most undereye concealers. The applicator takes a bit of gertting used to, but once you get the hang of it it works very nicely, applying an even amount of concealer if you use a light touch. I'm not sure i'd pay the price for this item, but it works just fine.

reviewText:
I have more eye puffiness than I do undereye circles, but this concealer is supposed to address puffiness, too, and who doesn't have at least some dark circles?  I tried this in the most popular color, medium, although I usually use a much lighter foundation (and I continued to do so over the top of this product).  The concealer went on rather clumsily (I'll get to that in a minute), but was easily distributed with a fingertip.  I swiped the foundation on over the top with a sponge.  I did feel any darkness was completely covered and stayed that way throughout the 17 hours I had the concealer on.

What I liked: Even though the concealer is darker than my normal foundation, the foundation (Clinique Even Better) covered it nicely; concealer and other make-up don't always work and play well together, but this one did.  The concealer stayed put through the day, and didn't seem to settle in lines or float to the surface and cake as some brands do.  I felt that it did the job of concealing although I haven't seen any change in puffiness (and mine may be more than any topical could handle, frankly).

What I didn't like:  I do think the concealer is moisturizing, which many will like.  For me, that's a bit of a problem, though, as the moist concealer sort of shines under the very matte foundation, and I think the shininess actually calls more attention to the area than dark circles would.  The applicator is one of those "twist to click, pushes product up through a sponge tip" types that takes a while to get product to you, then seems to deliver a lot all at once; Even with the sponge tip and despite illustrations showing someone swiping the concealer stick across their face, I think you are better off applying with a fingertip or separate sponge.
