Perfect for nighttime.  I am 49 years old with combination skin and this is working well for me.  My skin is much softer and seems "plumper" which is just my skin being moisturized.  I love it so far.
summary: Very little goes a long way - works very well on combination skin

reviewText:
I've been using AHAVA Extreme Night Treatment for about a week. The first time I applied it, I used 2 or 3 drops which was too much, Now I use  a little more than one drop. I'm applying it to my face, neck & decolletage

This product is a moisturizing oil that advertises to improve wrinkle depth, moisturize, firm the skin & improve the skin's texture.
In the week I've used it, it has moisturized & improved the look of my skin.  I haven't noticed much improvement in wrinkle depth.
 I like its flowery, rose fragrance, but it is strong & might be too strong for some.
I'm also using AHAVA Extreme Eye Cream which I've found to be very effective.

Check out Amazon's product photos to read the list of ingredients.
summary: Moisturizers my skin without leaving an oily feeling ... I like the fragrance but it might be too strong for some

reviewText:
This is a deeply nourishing serum, and my dry, parched skin literally drank this it in. There's a long and wonderful list of botanical ingredients along with minerals that soothe and heal the skin. I have used Ahava's  bath and body products but this is my first facial product and I love it! I have very dry (both water & oil) mature skin. My skin is a challenge for most product lines! After applying this "extreme" serum my skin glows with new vitality as well as feels moist without a greasy residue. I regularly exfoliate (and use Retin -A) and I feel that these steps really do help product penetration and give the most optimal result. I know rather quickly whether a product will work for me, and this one absolutely DOES from the first application. But I'm a realist, and know that it takes time to see results peak since it takes 30 days for the cells of the skin to turn over. If my first impressions are as good as they are now my skin will be looking much better as time goes on.

This serum is very hydrating without oily ingredients. It feels very much like a hyaluronic acid serum, it leaves the skin feeling smooth and soft without feeling like a cream. It's designed to be used at night but I plan on also using it during the day to see how it feels on my skin. So far I'm impressed and love that I only need a very small amount to cover my face so this bottle will last a good long time.

Honestly, I prefer higher end products due to the fact that I sat down one day and did the math and realized that they cost the same (over time) as cheaper products. In other words, if I use a product that costs $25 a month (less expensive products are not as concentrated, I use them up much faster) then that would cost the same as a luxury product that lasts 3 months per bottle ( @ $75 each). I hope that makes sense! Anyhow, I am a new fan of Ahava and recommend this serum, particularly for dehydrated and/or mature skin. Check the ingredient list if you are allergic to botanicals or algae, you might have a problem with this product if you have these sensitivities.

I have written a load of reviews about Ahava products and almost all have been 5 star. I was first introduced to Ahava on a trip to Israel about 6 years ago. When we visited the Dead Sea and then Massada, I went into the gift shop at Massada and saw some creams made by Ahava. Always looking for new skin care items, I read the boxes and saw all the benefits of the Dead Sea minerals and bought several of them. I have been hooked since. I think I have or have had, every one of their products. This night serum was new to me. It goes on smoothly, has a very light fragrance and my skin feels amazing when I wake up in the morning. Everyone over the age of 40 has to try Ahava products. My skin (at age 61) looks better and feels better than it did when I was in my mid-30's. There are definite benefits and results are quickly realized. You will love Ahava, the way I do. And this night serum is perfect as an introduction to the entire line.
summary: Another fantastic Ahava product. Love, love, love!

reviewText: I love Ahava products and this is no exception. I tested this out during the day. I washed my face and let it dry. Then I applied this to my face concentrating on area with fine lines. It feels like silk. It went on so easily and didn't pull around the eye area. After about an hour I noticed my fine lines were almost invisible. This seems to do what it says. My skin is very moisturizer now. I think using this before bed will be great. I can wake up with fresher, moisture filled skin.

I am a huge fan of Ahava. It works well without irritating my sensitive skin. I have been using this for several years and really like it. I am not normally the kind of person who spends big bucks on cosmetics, but I make an exception for Ahava. I was convinced once I tried a free sample.

I love the light scent like a flower but not overpowering at all.  The serum is very rich and it doesn't irritate my eyes like some other brands do.  I love Ahava products and have used over 6 items.  The effects are gradual but you will see skin with more shine after just a few days of continue use.
summary: I love the light scent like a flower but not overpowering ...

reviewText: I will be honest and say have only used a few nights. Wanted to try since it says only 2 drops per night and this is a good sized bottle..and expensive!  I've found that my face texture feels awesome.  Yes, maybe it is as one person says, that it contains something that coats it.  I just turned 65 and I'm preserving what I can..that takes keeping some moisture in my skin..this seems to be doing it.  It's too early to tell about wrinkle banishment, mine probably here to stay.  I do use the AHAVA mud mask and like it also.

A little dab will do ya.  This is oily stuff, filled with the extract of every plant known to mankind.  I kid you not.  That ingredient list is too long for anyone without cut and paste capability to re-post here.  It's written in micro-type and fills up most of one side of the box, but what the  makers apparently believe in is the power of the elements, so I will share that below:

micro elements (ppm):
strontium - 670
boron - 120
lithium - 40
manganese - 10
barium - 9

major elements (mg/L):
magnesium - 92,000
calcium - 35,000
bromine - 14,000
sodium - 2,700
potassium - 2,100

Out of all those ingredients, something was bound to work. I greased my face with AHAVA at bedtime.  It made my skin all tingly.  I was afraid I was reacting to something, but the feeling went away.  The next morning, my skin felt full of moisture and the fine wrinkles looked less visible.  I didn't use moisturizer and I don't need to.  Despite the oily base, I haven't broken out.

There are very few products that I would say help my wrinkles for more than the few minutes they take to dry.  This is one of them.  I am adding it to my arsenal of anti-aging products.
summary: my skin felt full of moisture and the fine wrinkles looked less visible

reviewText:
AHAVA products are a well known line in the area of beauty supplies. I have several products, and am very pleased with them.

Recently I was looking for a new night time skin product. I found AHAVA to have the essential qualities that I want. One of the ingredients in AHAVA nighttime skin product is sea minerals. Sea minerals are beneficial due to the high levels of magnesium, sodium, and bromide found in the salts. Sea Minerals may help improve and detoxify the skin, they say it also works to slow signs of aging as it targets fine lines and deep wrinkles. I have not found that my wrinkles are gone nor are ey lessened, but the overall feel and look of my skin has improved. I apply it nightly to freshly washed skin, I apply it to my face and then my hands. Smooth, rich feeling to both.

Recommended. prisrob 09-13-16
love it

LOVE LOVE LOVE this product!!! Takes very little to do an awesome job of moisurizing and smoothing fine lines. Skin absorbs it easily and goes great under makeup or alone at night. I've switched my entire skin care routine to AHAVA products because of this and the Osmoter. The mud masks and lotions work just as well. I use this not only at night but also a couple drops in the AM under makeup. Don't need to use half a dozen products any more to keep skin smooth and moisturized.

I like this because it has a nice light floral scent. I'm sure it could still smell awful if someone tried to take a bath in it, as people occasionally do with perfume, but it's nice so long as you're reasonable and doesn't smell so strong that I think it'd bother many people.

The bottle's pretty too of course, but that's it's at a pretty standard level of prettiness as far as perfume bottles go.
summary: I like this because it has a nice light floral scent

reviewText:
Rating and reviewing perfumes and colognes has got to be one of the more challenging endeavors. How to describe a scent. How it smells worn. How it lasts. Who will it appeal to. Who will it not appeal to.
This is a more of a heavy sent.
Flowery with some fruit. semi complex. Flowery with a musky finish.
Could be overpowering. Makes a statement. Too much will definitely be a bad thing for sure. . Use sparingly and you will be good during the summer.

Delightful, warm and juicy, and feminine are the adjectives that come to mind when describing this perfume. Eau Sensuelle comes in a gorgeous bottle that remind you of enticing layers of chiffon and spring turning to summer days. This fragrance was launched in 2009 after Rochas was acquired by P&G in 2003.

The top notes are fruity - blood orange, mango and bergamot. Middle notes -  Jasmine, Orris Root, Orange Blossom. Base notes - Dried Fruits, Musk and Pink Pepper. The blood orange and mango notes lends it a bitter and almost too fruity fragrance in the opening notes and then you start to smell the orange blossom. It almost smells like Juicy Fruit gum, almost. But then the flowery middle notes take over. The jasmine is fainter but the dry down is slightly musky and slightly spicy. The dry down works for me the most and therefore makes it a more complex fragrance than the cheap drug-store variety. It lasts 3-4 hours on me and the sillage is moderate making it suitable for work.

I will add it to my spring summer collection of fruity-flowery fragrances like D&Gs Light Blue, Burberry Brit, DKNY Be Delicious and my cheap go-to Shi by Alfred Sung. This is another lighter, fruitier and fresher sort of fragrance to add to this collection, but since it's new and light it will probably be gone by end of summer this year.
summary: Fruity beginning, musky dry down, a light and juicy fragrance for summer.

reviewText:
In my opinion, the base o fthis perfume smells citrus and white flowers while there is a distinct note of fruit balanced by what seems to smell of jasmine.  I do note there is a light "pwedery" scent to it, but not overpowering.  Under average office conditions, the scent lasted about 4 1/2 hours.  I did not find it overpwoering in the workplace and consider it great for that application.  No associated headaches or sinus reactions.  I received a few compliments on the scent.  One person however simply did not like it and called it "fruity."

If at all possible, I recommend first smelling the scent locally and testing it.
summary: Well made and subtle enough for work

reviewText: I got this for my fianc, as she has always been partial to citrus-based scents. This one is pleasant and also has notes of powder and herb, but as other reviewers have said, the fruit scent is a little overstated. A little spray goes a long way. The scent is potent and long-lasting. Nice for a springtime scent, used lightly, in my opinion.

I like citrus fragrances & I like white flowers so this should be a scent I adore.  I like it fine but the mango & dried fruits make it a bit too fruity for me.  This is not over-the-top fruit, the jasmine & neroli keep it in check but I'm really OVER the frooty tooty scents.  This one is not fake and cloying but just not my taste anymore.  If you like fruit scents but not too sweet, you may like this one.

This starts out with blood orange; a nice fresh & not-too-sweet blood orange but then the mango comes on a little stronger.  It's not too sweet, it has a bit of pepper note but I just don't care for it; the mango ruins this for me.  Luckily, bergamot & jasmine save the day, bringing a lemony, fresh flower note.  This is not the lush jasmine of Arabian scents but a fresh/light jasmine.  Underneath it all but not too heavy, is the musk & powdery note of orris.  It is not a dirty musk but more of a white musk.

The sillage is not huge & it lasts about 3 hours on my skin.  It is a well made and inoffensive/generic fragrance.  Much better than many other fragrances of this type. I prefer the Rochas fragrance "Tocade" - it's more serious & adult. Or if you like a more light/fresh Eau de Rochas, the "Fraiche" flanker version has no sweet fruits.

A bit of trivia:  Rochas is now owned by Procter & Gamble (2003).
summary: Fruity Flanker to the Original Eau de Rochas

reviewText:
I can remove everything on my face with one cotton round + a bit of this water. The little cotton round is filthy by the end. At first I didn't use a cotton round. I would put some of this in my hands and massage it onto my face. I thought it would be a waste to put it on something--that the something would absorb all the product. Rather, the waste was splashing this on my face.

It says you don't have to wash it off your skin, and sometimes I don't. Sometimes I just splash my face once or twice after with some warm water.

It's a nice fast way to remove foundation, brow product, eye shadow + mascara ... Great when I'm tired before bed!
Love this stuff. It's much better than the Garnier one with the pink top (that one burns my eyes)...but I don't know if I can justify spending 3 times as much money on La Roche-Posay.
summary: Great, but expensive for what you get

reviewText: The best Micellar cleanser out there!! This is such an amazing deal for the price and the amount of product you get!

Mrs. Boilermate reports this cleanser does a satisfactory job of cleaning, her face feels more refreshed when she's done, and the skin feels a bit tighter. Since she doesn't wear makeup, makeup removal capabilities could not be evaluated. In her opinion, it doesn't work enough better to justify spending what they're asking for it.

I also tried it, and it does clean well, but doesn't provide any real added benefit for me.

I do not wear a lot of make-up, but do apply sunscreen on my face every morning. My face is generally smooth, but will still get clogged pores and break out if I don't clean it properly (not a fancy regime, just a product removal regime, followed by a night time lotion).

La Roche-Posay Micellar Cleaner seemed to be removing my scant makeup, but on day 3 I noticed a zit in my T-zone area. Not good.

I'm back to using Neutrogena Ultra Light Cleansing Oil.

(for another baseline, the make-up removing clothes, no matter what brand, do not completely clean my face either and I tend to get a zit after about 4-5 days of cloth use).
summary: Did not Remove Sunscreen Layer Effectively, Which Resulted in Clogged Pores.

reviewText:
I've been curious about micellar water for a while now, so I was excited to get the chance to try it out. I typically wear non-waterproof eye makeup, but for testing purposes, I wore Stila's waterproof smudge stick eyeliner with Benefit's waterproof Badgal mascara. That combination doesn't budge come hell or high water.

The instructions say to apply the cleanser to cotton wool and apply, no rubbing necessary. Well... not exactly, at least not with my mega waterproof makeup. I used a cotton pad, and it took several swipes to remove most of the eyeliner. The first swipe did start to break it up, but it definitely required some rubbing. Unfortunately it hardly touched my mascara, and I wasn't about to rub hard or long enough to get all of that off. The skin around my eyes is rather delicate and doesn't react well to lots of rubbing. So I ended up washing the rest off in the shower with an oil-based cleanser.

The verdict for waterproof eye makeup: not amazing.

However, this micellar water did remove my usual, non-waterproof makeup quite easily. It just took a couple of passes to remove my eyeliner, and it picked up a good amount of dirt and oil across the rest of my face (I usually wear very light face makeup: just powder and blush). I did notice, however, that this made the skin around my lips tingly. I didn't put it directly on my lips (though it says it can be used to remove lipstick; I'll have to try with some of my heavier, stain-prone lipsticks in the future), but rather the skin above my upper lip and on my chin stung a little bit as the cleanser dried. It wasn't really painful and didn't seem to cause any lasting irritation, but it wasn't super comfortable

I have dry skin that's prone to flaking in the winter, and while this micellar water didn't dry my skin out, it also didn't leave it moisturized (which admittedly isn't its purpose). It felt very neutral, which is actually a good thing if you have combination skin. I feel like I'll find a lot more use for it in the summer, when my skin starts to produce more oil. For winter, I'll probably stick to my creams and oils to remove most of my makeup and use this as a spot cleanser for stubborn eyeliner.

Lest this review sound overly negative, I actually do like this product. It does the job well for non-waterproof makeup, and it left my skin feeling refreshed. It's not the product for my skin during winter, but it's a great cleanser.

Very very light fragrance, barely detectable.  I believe this type of water is somehow injected with a touch of oil so it does a super job of removing makeup and cleansing pores.  Very gently.  My skin feels soft and clean after usage.  I use with a warm washcloth.  I really like this product.

The Micellar Water Cleanser works as makeup remover, cleanser and toner. It's gentle and unscented.  Apply it with cotton, don't rinse it off, just let it dry on the skin.  It left my skin feeling clean but not "tight" or overly dry.  You can put eye cream, moisturizer and SPF after using the micellar water.

I alternate using this and my usual cleanser,  essence and serum regime.  The micellar water is quick, convenient, and it feels effective with just one step.

This product is wonderful! It removes makeup and oil, but doesn't leave your skin dry, like soap or harsh astringents. In addition, a little goes a surprisingly long--I can clean my entire face with two, moistened, cotton pads. The texture is like a softened, very slightly soapy water. It feels gentle, but cleans deep. Overall fantastic.
summary: Great product for your skin care arsenal!

reviewText: I love this Micellar cleanser! It is the only thing that has ever made my very dry skin feel good in the morning. Mornings are tough for me. I don't get enough sleep and I drink wine at bedtime. I have terrible coffee breath. This cleanser is refreshing and has just the faintest of scents. I can't decide if it's citrus or roses because the scent is almost not there, but I love it. My dry yucky morning face looks and feels better without having to fool around with soap, water, or moisturizer. My skin is more clear because until now I have skipped washing my face at all in the morning in fear of drying it out even more. Amazing product.

reviewText: I have been using Simple's Micellar cleansing wipes since they came out and this is an even better cleanser.  I am mystified as to exactly how this product works, but it does a wonderful job of taking off every spot of makeup with one swipe.  I have dry, sensitive skin and this left my face feeling clean and fresh.  I normally wash my face after using the Simple wipes but I found that this cleaned everything by itself with no need to really wash with cleanser.  I tend to over wash my skin which isn't great since it is so dry and this leaves it clean and a bit moisturized compared to using cleanser.

The cap was broken in transit but luckily the contents did not spill.  This product is made in France and it shows.  The English directions are rather poor.  I just use a cotton ball to soak up some of this cleanser and rub it on my face to remove any build-up.  There is no sticky residue or drying from toners and my face feels fresh and hydrated.  So, I recommend this product.

I wasn't sure what to expect when I was offered this bottle of micellar water. I have oily skin and I feel like it needs to be refreshed several times a day, but that's not always easy to do. Baby wipes don't cut it because they leave my face feeling greasier than not. Likewise, specialty facial wipes make me feel like they are depositing stuff on my face rather than removing it.

While the solution in the bottle looks like kids bubbles, this is actually a really great product. With just one cotton ball and a squirt of the micellar water, I am able to clean my whole face, and without feeling like I'm leaving any residue behind. I expected that, in order for it to really clean, this product would have to be astringent, but it isn't at all. It feels light, like water, but it's definitely doing more than just plain old H2O.

This product looks and feels just like water; it has a slight scent, but it's negligible. But the cleaning power isn't. I can keep this in my purse or desk at work and pull it out any time. This is also the perfect product for long road trips and overnights away from home, when I don't usually lug around all the products I use on a day-to-day basis.

reviewText: This is a nice cleanser. It's very minimally fragranced, and smells fresh. It very effectively removes makeup. I love it.

reviewText:
This product has a slightly floral fragrance. The directions say to apply with a cotton wool pad. If you have very heavy makeup this will probably not remove it all. If your skin is sensitive to cleansers and soap this might be worth the price; however my skin felt much cleaner and makeup seemed easier to remove with soap and water.

For those who are very adamant about their products being sealed  this had no safety/plastic seals, it just simply opens and you can apply it.
The price seems extremely high for those who can use soap and water unless you really enjoy fancy water and want to pay the price.

I was skeptical about using a Micellar water cleanser. I first tried the Garnier brand, with excellent results. However, the La Roche-Posay brand is one that I trust with sunscreens and other products I've used. It seems odd to wipe your face with a cotton pad with Micellar water and not rinse my face. But I'm telling you that my face is cleaner than ever and I have a glowing clear complex too. Plus, it makes "washing" your face faster to do when you just want to go to bed. I highly recommend this product. It's for all skin types; mine is combination type.

This product is somewhat efficient.  However, it does take (me) multiple passes and cotton balls compared to using Neutrogena wipes.  The scent is very mild and fruity.  This particular Micellar water, made in France by La Roche-Posay, is formulated for sensitive skin. It is described as safe for cleaning the face, the eyes, and lips. I had no trouble using it on my eyelids, but use care to not get it in your eyes.

Pros: Gentle 3-in-1 product does not require water. Cons: Does not remove mascara very well. Stock up on cotton balls! Ive been curious about Micellar Water for quite some time. I did some research and was surprised to discover that it has been around for more than 100 years. It was originally developed as a waterless way to clean the skin when the available water supply was inadequate or unhealthy. Micelles are tiny molecules of oil that are suspended in soft water. The oil micelles are attracted to the oil and dirt on the skin and when applied with a cotton ball, micellar water is supposed to effectively clean, tone, and moisturize and does not require rinsing off. This particular micellar water, made in France by La Roche-Posay, is supposed to be formulated for sensitive skin. It is described as safe for cleaning the face, the eyes, and lips. I had no trouble using it on my eyelids, but it was somewhat unpleasant in my eyes. It does not contain alcohol, parabens, soap, or colorants. It does however contain Hexylene Glycol, Glycerin, Poloxamer 184, Disodium Cocoamphodiacetate, Disodium EDTA, Citric Acid, Dihydrocholeth-30, Polyaminopropyl Biguanide, and fragrance. The fragrance is mild and florally-fruity, with a faint whiff of possibly witch hazel. Ive been using it for a little over a week. Compared to Neutrogena Makeup Remover Cleansing Towelettes , a cotton ball soaked with micellar water does a fair to mediocre job of removing makeup, gel eyeliner, and mascara. It cleans, but requires multiple cotton ball passes to get all the stuff off. After cleaning, the skin temporarily feels oily. The first night I used it, I rinsed half my face with water, just to see the difference. The water rinsed side was still oily, just not as much. The next morning both sides of my face were moisturized and smooth, but there was still mascara residue around my eyes. After a few days, I returned to using the Neutrogena Towelettes to remove my eye makeup and washing my face with a mild cleanser and water. Afterwards I wiped my face with the micellar water and a cotton ball. Used as an after cleaning toner, it did an excellent job of removing any residual cleanser and my skin felt refreshed, moisturized, and ready for whatever night cream I planned to use. I can see the benefits of using this product where the water supply is limited or unsafe, or as a fast refresher on the go. For travel, I still prefer to use the pre-moistened towelettes, which do not leak and clean the skin better.
summary: A Revival of an Old French Standby

reviewText: I use a cotton ball to apply to my face, neck and upper chest after washing it. It feels very clean and fresh with no residue. I used some in my facial steamer as well. Feels nice on the skin. It's a large bottle, so I put some in a spray bottle to take with me as well so I could mist my face while traveling.

Micellar water is an effective makeup remover.  It is gentle and left my skin feeling good. No tightness or stinging. After using it I applied moisturizer and went to bed. It took 3 cotton round pads to remove both eye and face makeup completely.  For me the cons of the product are: it is liquid-inconvenient for travel and I cannot use my facial cleaning tool with it. The pros of the product are: value for the price-one bottle will last a long time and it bundles multiple skin care steps into one. No more NOT removing makeup, no matter how tired. This amazing liquid and a cotton pad assures you can treat your skin well even on your worst day. It feels well going on,  your skin feels great when finished without irritation or redness. This definitely replaces the makeup remover cloths kept in the nightstand routine with the lovely raccoon-y eyes in the morning. I'm guilty of it too, as well as the "I'll do it later" but fall asleep instead. Give your skin and your pillowcases a fighting chance. They'll BOTH thank you!

Finally available in the USA.  I always stocked up on micellar water products when I went to France - they've used it & loved it for years.  It was supposedly invented for Parisian women because the water in Paris is so "hard".  The water is hard there, I can vouch for that & that is why the pharmacy was always one of my first stops when arriving in Paris.  Hard water makes it difficult to remove all your makeup & tends to dry out the skin.

This is really good micellar water.  I use this water on a cotton pad to remove eye makeup and foundation.  I even use it to clean my skin when I do not wear makeup.  Just squeeze the water on to a disposable cotton pad, hold over your eye for about 15 seconds, then gently wipe away the makeup.  You will probably need more than one pad to clean your face.  I like  "Swisspers" brand cotton rounds - you can buy them on Amazon or at Costco, etc.

This stuff is not magic, it's science & it's been around for a long time.  The micelle surfactant molecule is suspended in liquid/water and kind of grabs on to the dirt/oils/makeup on your face & doesn't allow it to stick on your face.  (That is my simple, non-scientist explanation.)  There is no irritation - even around eyes.  And the skin actually feels clean without rinsing with tap water - really!  When you use it, it seems like you are just using regular tap water except it actually dissolves/grabs the goo/makeup/dirt off your face.

reviewText:
I have a sensitive combination skin type. So my assessment is based on how the mask worked for the two separate qualities of my skin.

1) As far as sensitivity, the mask didn't have any adverse effect on my skin. I guess there was advantage to the masks organic content. There were no chemicals in this product that usually irritate my skin.
2) The mask REALLY dries your skin. Some areas of my face are oily, and after using the mask, they felt fine. However, the majority of my skin is of dry to normal quality, and my face mostly felt dried up by the mask. I didn't experience any hydration or reduction of blemishes.

After use for about a week, my husband and I have loved Juice Beauty Blemish Clearing Mask. It feels good on the face, and we both really liked how the mask doesn't dry out the face but stays moist. We will likely be purchasing more when we run out.

reviewText:

Overall I would recommend this product.  It seems to do a good job of controlling oil/breakouts without over-drying  your skin.  I need to use it a bit longer before I decide if it is a 5 star product, but if I continue to like it I will most likely increase my rating to 5 stars.

- Reduced the oiliness of my skin

reviewText:
I am in my mid-40s, yet I still have blemish flare-ups from time-to-time.  Right around the time I obtain this mask, I was experiencing a particularly bad outbreak (probably related to a new supplement that I had tried).

This mask by Juice is a thick, clay-style mask.  It is so thick, in fact, that I had trouble squeezing it out the tiny whole in the tube; a slightly wider open would've made for easier application.  The instructions say to apply a "generous layer" to the face and to leave on for up to 10 minutes.  This is not a peel-off type mask; if you leave it on the full 10 minutes, it will begin to dry on the face, but it needs to be rinsed very thoroughly with water to remove (it's quite easy to miss patches).

Overall, I liked this product.  I liked the thick consistency (despite the slight difficulty squeezing out of the tube), and the pleasant, fresh scent.  I felt that the mask left my face feeling clean and oil-free yet without feeling tight or dry.  However, I'm not certain about the "blemish clearing" claims.  The first time I tried it, my face did seem to clear, but that may of also been because I stopped taking the supplement that had acne listed as a side effect.  The second time I tried it, I actually wound up with a blemish on my chin shortly thereafter--again, this might have been a coincidence.

In the end, I think that this is a nice mask to help control oil and leave the skin feeling smooth, but keep in mind that 1) it may or may not help with acne, and 2) you don't get very much for your money (after just two uses, my own tube is significantly depleted).
summary: Nice quality clay-type mask which may help with oil control

reviewText:

reviewerName: Leah Maines, best-selling, award-winning author, actor, and editor
reviewText:
I will first say that this product is intended to be used as part of a Blemish Clearing regime by Juice Beauty. The instructions recommend using their Blemish Clearing Cleanser, followed by their Green Apple Blemish Clearing Peel before the application of this mask (twice weekly). I used my own facial cleanser and peel (Liz Earl's Cleanse & Polish and Sonia Dakar's Flash Facial).

The texture of this mask was smooth and pasty, with a white color. In the past, I have been off-put by the smell of some Juicy Beauty products (mainly their moisturizer). I was pleasantly surprised that this mask hardly had any scent at all--- which made using it much more enjoyable. The application of the mask was very easy and not the least bit messy. I have used a lot of clay masks (including mixing the clay with water myself) and it can be a big hassle that leaves residue everywhere and takes a lot of time. This mask stayed put and came off in a snap without a lot of extra effort. Wearing the mask was very comfortable (and only took 10 minutes). It gave a "wooshing and tingling" sensation that you usually experience with a bentonite clay mask. I have pretty sensitive skin--- and masks like this can sometimes leave my skin a little irritated. This mask actually made my skin feel very soothed. After washing the mask off, I noticed that my skin felt very fresh and moisturized. It felt a little tight in my t-zone--- but this was quickly resolved with a little serum. Juice Beauty recommends following the mask up with their Blemish Clearing Serum (I used Caudalie's Radiance Serum).

Overall, I was pleased with This Blemish Clearing Mask. I can see this easily being worked into someone's beauty routine if they have combination skin (like myself) or oily skin. It isn't over drying, and it is a very quick and easy way to reap the benefits of a clay mask without all of the work. An added bonus is the fact the company uses a lot of organic ingredients in their products. I'd like to point out that not all of the ingredients listed in this mask were organic ones--- but the majority of them were. If you are looking for a simple environmental-friendly mask-- this comes well-recommended.

This is very thick, goopy mask but it's easy to remove.  It can be rather drying so I will only use it a couple times a month - probably on targeted areas - to help combat breakouts. I just put a little dab on the offending spot before bed and in the morning the redness and swelling are gone.

I'm 31 and still get the annoying random zit every couple of weeks. I think it's more common than people think, getting acne well past your teenage years. That doesn't mean it's not a pain to deal with, especially when most products don't really work. So far, I really like this blemish mask. There's no horrid smell, and it's not thick and goopy. reviewText: Adult acne is not attractive or expected at age 79!  I haven't been one to have facials or use masks, but I leaped at this one because of the natural ingredients.  It's a pleasant experience, and after two masks, I see clearer skin, not only in the acne area, but all over my skin.  Skin tone seems to have become more even, and although I can't claim to look twenty years younger, my skin has a fresher tone, as well.  I'm impressed with the product.  I like the hand cream, too, and am checking the website for other products that might give me a brighter look!

I was impressed with the ingredients in this mask.  Most of them, I recognized as being beneficial and I didn't spot questionable ingredients in the list.

I'm over 60 so my skin is dryer and thinner than it once was.  When I was young, I never had problems with acne or excess oil.
The past few years, I've had more skin issues than I ever did in my youth.  I've been developing cysts so I need to do a better job of deep cleansing even though my skin is not oily.  Many masks are too drying for mature skin and some contain ingredients I don't really want to apply.

Although this product is a little pricey, I expect it to last through quite a few applications.  I found the product a little difficult to squeeze out of the tube and a small amount goes a long way when applied.
I immediately noticed a cooling sensation and checked the ingredient list again to see if it contained menthol or some form of mint.
A small amount was needed and I was pleased that it was much easier to remove than many masks I've used in the past.

I was also impressed by how my skin felt after I'd thoroughly removed the mask.  Most masks that contain clay dry my skin much more than this one did.  My skin felt clean, calm and soothed.  I'm convinced that all of the beneficial ingredients in this mask are good for any skin type and likely to help me keep my skin cleaner, calmer and not strip what little moisture I still have.

There are many recipes to make your own masks and other topical products that might be less expensive, but they also require having ingredients on hand and making a fresh batch each time you want to use them.  Most of us don't have the time or dedication to whip up a new batch on a weekly basis, so finding a product with great ingredients that works well and has a decent shelf life is great.
I feel that this is one of those products and my skin felt much better for having used it.  I'm hoping that continued use will keep my pores cleaner, my skin calmer and put an end to the problem of cysts developing.

reviewText:
REVIEW OF:  JUICE BEAUTY STEM CELLULAR REPAIR BOOSTER

This Booster serum is very easy to use. Although it is somewhat more expensive than other alternatives, the good news is that you need only  a very a tiny "pea-size" drop to achieve benefit.  So, in the long run, this might actually be a very cost-effective solution.

The first thing that I noticed was improvement in the way that the skin on my face looked  and felt: It was better almost right away.

With regular use, I began to appreciate  that the overall appearance of the skin was more radiant,  vibrant,  and youthful.  Those lines around the mouth, furrows between the eyebrows,  on the neck, etc. are not nearly as visible.  The skin has that glowing quality again!

It's hard for a layman to quantify or qualify "elasticity" ( that great quality of skin that declines as we age).  Suffice it to say that  the face just looks less sallow and more "plumped out"- (not fat , mind you, just less peaked and aged).

There is clearly less depth to those dreaded wrinkle `craters'.

USE:

Prime the pump the first time you use it to dispense the serum. A small, thin strand of serum  comes out-that's fine, it does not require that you use very much.

As with most facial products, just make sure to apply this product  to your cleansed skin.  It's probably a good idea to "patch test" on the under-belly of your forearm before putting this on your face to ascertain that you have no sensitivity or allergy to this serum.

The Juice Beauty line of skin care products are touted as an "organic solution"  that helps your skin to withstand the extreme dryness of winter and indoor heating and fend of the damage caused by oxidation and free-radicals. This damage unfortunately is a consequence of the things your skin fights against everyday-chiefly ultraviolet radiation (sunlight) and air & water pollution.  I read with interest a reviewer's comments that the skin damage produced by exposure to ionizing radiation to the face (as is used during cancer treatment)  has been markedly improved by use of this serum.

WHAT IS IT?

I would encourage the reader to go to the informative site that tells you more about this very different  line of skin care products called JUICE BEAUTY.

The components of their skin care line are discussed.  Chiefly, they use a blend of fruit stem cells infused into a Vitamin C, Resveratrol- rich grape seed formula.  In short, this line of organic products uses natural and organically found chemical ingredients that are found in the fruit stem cells of apples, grapes, and lemons.  This line makes use of resveratrol- a naturally occurring helpful chemical commonly found in grape seeds.

These skin care products are made with naturally occurring chemicals found in fruit and are never made with  petroleum by-products, "parabens,or propylene or butylene glycol, sodium lauryl sulfates,  pesticides, phthalates. No artificial or synthetic dyes or fragrances are present in this product line."

I was glad to read that these products are never tested on animals.

 REVIEW OF THE BENEFITS:

 -  Increases cellular turnover and powerful antioxidant action with Vitamin C, E & B5.

 -  Increases skin luminosity with Vitamin C.

 -  Fights free radical skin damage and firms skin with a proprietary blend of apple, grape, & lemon.

-  fruit stem cells infused into organic resveratrol-rich grape seed.
  Improves elasticity and plumps skin with hyaluronic acid.*

*A WORD ABOUT HYALURONIC ACID:

 Hyaluronic Acid(or hyaluronate or HA) is an anionic, non sulfated glycosaminoglycan distributed widely in mammalian bodies, chiefly throughout connective (tissue that supports, connects, or separates the different types of tissues and organs of the body), epithelial (skin, lining cells) and neural tissues (nervous system).

Previously, HA was injected into the skin using a sharp hypodermic needle- a process that caused bleeding and was reportedly quite painful.

Formulation of HA into a skin care serum allows one to derive the benefits of HA in a non-painful, easy to use daily regimen.

Current research with HA focuses on its use in skin regeneration and repair.

EWG Skin Deep Cosmetics Database rates the Juice Beauty  products quite favorably-among the best ratings out there. That site allows you to easily get the safety evaluation of your cosmetic products.

Overall, I am quite pleased with this skin care line developed by Juice Beauty and look forward to their expansion of the product line with better products that are backed by good research.
summary: HELP YOUR SKIN LOOK AND FEEL BETTER WITH NATURALLY OCCURRING FRUIT INGREDIENTS.GREAT EWG COSMETICS DATABASE RATING

reviewText:
Juice Beauty Stem Cellular Repair Booster Serum, 1 fl oz.

The description of the product is this serum reduces the appearance of wrinkles. Proprietary means they do not have to disclose the secret ingredient, whatever that might be.  The serum contains a proprietary blend of Fruit Stem Cells which help firm your skin and reduce the appearance of wrinkles. The benefits include increase in cellular turnover. Well, that all sounds wonderful and you really hope it does what it says.  My experience with this product is:
I really liked the texture and feel of this serum.
I liked the pump bottle, as I have used some serums that have an eye dropper and you have to squeeze the top to get the liquid in the dropper then squeeze the serum onto your hand and smooth into your skin.
The smell was not overpowering as some of the other Juice Beauty products I have used.  The age defying solutions kit smelled like lemon pledge.  This serum had a lovely light fragrance that wasn't over powering at all.
I want to use a product that contains organic ingredients and does not test on animals.  Those are important features in a beauty product for me.  This product makes the claim to use organic ingredients and not test on animals.
I used this product for about three weeks.  I used it twice a day.  It is supposed to improve cellular turnover.
I am in my mid 50s and Im always looking for a miracle.  However, this was not what I was hoping for.  I have used many, many products over the years.  All kinds of moisturizers, serums, vitamin A and C serums, and I have to sadly say that I noticed no improvement in skin texture or reduction in wrinkles.  Nothing, nada, zilch.  I sure was hoping that this would be different but unfortunately there is no such thing as a fountain of youth in any product other than minor surgery, or Botox or juviderm.
That is the bottom line.  I saw absolutely no difference in my skin what so ever.  So, for the price, I think you could use just about any less expensive moisturizer or serum and receive the same results.  As to overall experience, I liked the feel and texture, but not enough to spend the amount of money they want for something that did nothing a regular moisturizer is already doing.
summary: Not the miracle I was hoping for!

reviewText:
My 70 yr old mother's been using a different brand with peptides for the past 8 years.  It's done a great job in keeping her looking a decade younger.  Recently, she's started to get fine lines, and want something more powerful.

After three weeks of use, there is a significant reduction in her fine lines, and no adverse reactions to her sensitive skin.

For those who care about ingredients, everything checks out as safe on Skin Deep, and there are no Benzoates, which is a benzene based preservative many "natural" companies have started using after parabens became unpopular.

Keep in mind that she is a sun avoider,  so any repairs from the serum is not reversed with UV rays.
summary: Effective and safe for sensitive skin

reviewText:
This review is a neutral point of view thus far.  I can't say anything bad nor anything extremely good about this product.  I have applied it acording to instructions after washing my face and before I add any moisturizer ( I do not wear makeup).  My skin is super sensitive and has not broken out nor reacted badly, but I also don't see any significant improvement.  I must add that I do not have sun damaged skin.  Maybe treating such wrinkles with this serum is more noticable?

Also, one is supposed to use both the serum and cream for optimal results.  I only received he serum and therefore can't comment on the results when both products are used.

I will post updates if I notice any significant changes.
summary: Not sure about this for me

reviewText: I received this product from on the vine and can't say I've noticed a huge difference yet and do plan on updating this review since I have only been using this product for a little over 2 weeks. However, I do really like the consistency of this product as opposed to most serums. Most serums I've tried are applied by a dropper and a wetter consistency. This serum is not runny but still goes on smooth and one pump goes a long way. I also really love the fact that it's organic and all natural. I apply this in the morning and It only takes a minute or two to dry before applying make up. I also use it after I wash my face at night and after I apply it, I feel like my skin is actually tightening.  It does make my face feel good and I do think that my face looks well hydrated when I put this on as opposed to not using it. However, unless I see some major results by the time this container is gone, I can't really say I can justify spending the high asking price on this product unless there was some kind of money back guarantee.

reviewText:
After a few weeks of using this serum in the morning and evening, I have noticed a softening of lines around my eyes and forehead.  I would not say the effect is remarkable at this point, but it is apparent.  The use so far seems to indicate that continued use will lead to further softening of lines and healthier appearing skin. I have not experienced any side effects, and I would categorize my skin and eyes as being sensitive.

I think for consumers the question is whether the potential for a noticeable benefit is worth the additional cost of this product over a traditional moisturizer.
summary: This Serum Seems to Have a Positive Benefit to Facial Skin

reviewText:
Following extremely positive experiences with other Juicy Beauty products, my wife was eager to try the JUICE BEAUTY STEM CELLULAR REPAIR BOOSTER SERUM.  The serums results, however, did not live up to her expectations and were not comparable to other high-end skin booster serums.

WHAT IT IS:

- A thin/light gel, applied twice daily, that claims to boost and enhance skin tone and texture.

- The serum is composed of quality, organic ingredients such as grape seed oil, lemon juice, apple juice, white grape juice, aloe leaf juice, jojoba oil, sunflower oil, borage seed oil and hyaluronic acid.  The product is enriched with vitamins C, E and B5.

HOW IT PERFORMED:

- The serum itself IS thin with a silky, supple texture.  It applies easily and initially feels pleasing to the skin.  It is neither sticky nor oily and has no scent.

- Following application, there was a noticeable lack of absorption  the serum seems to rest on top of the skin rather than penetrating into the skin.  This was important because the lack of absorption limited the hydrating, smoothing and firming effects of the serum, especially when compared to another serum frequently used (Lancomes Advanced Genefique).

A WORD ABOUT PACKAGING:

- This product contains 1 fluid ounce of serum, but the bottle appears big enough to hold much more.  At first sight, it is easy to assume you are being offered more product at a lower price  check the volume.

I've tried many, many skin serums, and facial products of this type, and I have found the Juice Beauty Stem Cellular Repair Booster Serum, is not really much different than the other "high end" products I've tried.

I haven't really noticed a difference in my facial skin at all, or my neck. I'd really like to find something that would rejuvenate my skin because, although I'm only 50, i feel like my skin has aged more than it should at this point - thus I try the really good products, hoping for a miracle! I realize none of these products have promised miracles, but I haven't noticed any noticeable repair either!

I would say the texture of this product is rather sticky and tacky once rubbed into your skin. It's a gel serum, and not a cream or lotion, so I suppose it's to be expected, but it made my face feel "pulled" - like I needed lotion on top.

The product package does say it's been clinically validated for AGE DELAY, AND BLEMISH CLEARING. So to be fair, perhaps this is for a bit young appearing skin. And, I don't have any blemishes, so I can't speak to that.  I do like that it's anti-oxidant rich, and made without GMOs, any artificial dyes or scents, parabens, etc...

It does have some artificial ingredients, but nothing harmful. They are things like Ocetyl Palimate - which five products like Juice Serum "slip". What that does is helps make this a great primer under any make-up you might use. I just use a bit of concealer around my eye area, and this was perfect under the concealer .. as long as I didn't wait too long to put on the concealer.

I wouldn't use this product on a regular basis considering the price. However I would buy it for our daughter's as a gift, if they used it on their much younger skin!
summary: Mostly organic ingredients in this product...

reviewText:
Juice Beauty has created a skin lotion with juices from a variety of fruits.  I have used it for a couple of weeks with mixed results:

PROS:

1) Easy to apply and soaks into skin rapidly with no sticky residue.

2) Dry spots on my skin have vanished, leaving smooth, soft skin in their places.

CONS:

1) This lotion made me break out in oilier areas of my face such as around the nose and chin.  Directions say to stop using the product if a reaction occurs, so Ive had to leave it off for several days.

After a full week, Ill try this lotion again to be certain whether it is the cause of my acne-like eruptions or not.  I will amend this review if the breakout does not reoccur.

2)  The product contains one ounce of liquid.  For me, this should last about 6 weeks before a reorder is necessary.  With my results so far, the price seems excessive.

THREE STARS!

I got this product for my wife and her review is as follows. I'm in my early thirties, but my two kids are sucking the pretty out of me, so I thought I would try adding some kind of anti-aging product to my skin care regime. I have been using this serum daily, sometimes twice daily, for the last  couple of weeks. It feels just like a moisturizer or something going on, but perhaps lighter. At such a high price, I can't imagine putting this all over your neck and "decolete" everyday but I guess if you have wrinkles there, it might be worth it. I can feel it doing something to my skin after I apply it- just a slight warmth on my skin that goes away quickly. I follow this serum with some moisturizer of a different brand.

I can't say that I'm noticing any results as of yet and at $75 an ounce I was hoping for more. My skin might look a little more "luminous" and maybe it feels a little better, but I still look like I need a nap most of the time (which I do). Maybe some of the little wrinkles are looking less deep. I'll continue using it as perhaps the improvements are yet to come and if that happens I will update my review accordingly.

I definitely like the idea of organic and natural ingredients in a product like this, so I think this is certainly a better choice than a chemical laden facial cream. And it is mostly likely just as effective as a less natural product. I am skeptical of the anti-aging products, so I'll be pleasantly surprised if it actually does something good for my skin. So far, it sure isn't doing any harm, but I'm not looking much more luminous or young.

It seems that everyone who is reviewing this likes it; and while I agree that it's a pleasant serum, I just don't see a difference in my "just turning 33 and getting the start of wrinkles" skin. Perhaps I have not used it long enough; only for about a week and a half; but for the raving reviews and the cost of the item I am amazed that other than people who have skin allergies.... no one has taken issue with the extreme cost for what you get.  It goes on smooth and feels nice, I had to use two pumps to get coverage on my dry (but easy to get oily) skin.  But it wasn't enough on it's own, I definitely had to follow up with a light moisturizer or else my skin felt stretched.

But my basic problem with this is that I simply CANNOT see a difference, at all.  I like it. I would maybe spend 20.00 for it, to use it as a base for my foundation.  But for the price tag and the promises... it just doesn't hold up.  I am going to continue using the entire bottle and update this review in the future... but for the time being I just can't recommend this overpriced bottle of serum with no return; especially in this economy where every dollar counts.  I definitely would not recommend this one for the time being!

**********
After over a month and a half of using, I still see no visible difference. I still love it, but no way would I spend the money on something that doesn't show improvement.
summary: Very expensive for a nice bottle of moisturizer; don't see a difference in my skin.

reviewText:

reviewText:
After four days of using this product as recommended, twice a day, my face is itching and I'm experiencing mild burning.

I have very dry so I was looking forward to the hydrating power of the Juice Beauty serum. This product has initially worsened my skin condition. My face feels slightly chapped as if it were windburned.

Despite the fact that this company boasts of the organic ingredients, which are rich in antioxidants, there are other things in this serum that have the potential to irritate a person's skin. It appears that one of them is having a negative affect on me:

Here is a full list of ingredients:
Organic Juices Of Pyrus Malus (Organic Apple Juice)*, Vitis Vinifera (Organic White Grape Juice)*, Citrus Medica Limonum (Organic Lemon Juice)*, Aloe Barbadensis (Organic Aloe Leaf Juice)*, Vegetable Glycerin, Organic Plant Oils Of Helianthus Annus (Organic Sunflower Seed Oil)*, Simmondsia Chinensis (Organic Jojoba Seed)*, Butyrospermum Parkii (Organic Shea Butter)*, Octyl Palmitate, Caprylic/capric Triglyceride, Glyceryl Stearate, Magnesium Ascorbyl Phosphate (Vitamin C), Stearic Acid, Cetearyl Alcohol, Malus Sylvestris (Apple Buds), Vitis Vinifera (Grape Buds) & Citrus Limonum (Lemon Bark), Organic Essential Fatty Acids Of Oenothera Biennis (Organic Evening Primrose Oil)*, Linum Usitatissimum (Organic Linseed Oil)*, Borago Officinalis (Organic Borage Seed Oil)*, Xanthan Gum, Panthenol (Vitamin B5), Allantoin, Sodium Hyaluronate (Hyaluronic Acid), Tocopherol (Vitamin E), Sodium Benzoate, Potassium Sorbate, Ethylhexylglycerin, Citrus Reticulata (Mandarin), Litsea Cubeba (May Chang) And Cinnamomum Camphora (Ho Wood) Pure Essential Oils

Some are raving about the positive results they are having with this product. Perhaps I'm experiencing sensitivity to one or more of the ingredients. Whatever the case, I'm unable to recommend this serum based on my personal experience.

If you do intend to purchase this serum be sure to look over all of the ingredients first to check for allergens or other possibly irritants. Also, be prepared to moisturize after each application--especially if your skin is the least bit dry.
summary: This product irritated my skin. Check out the entire ingredient list before purchasing

reviewText:
I'm picky about the chemicals in my food, so why not the chemicals that I put on my skin? Juice Beauty is an organic skin product line that will change your standards for beauty. I sometimes worry that organic skin products won't work as good as chemicals, but I worry that chemicals aren't good for my health. So what do you do? Get Juice Beauty! I have tried other Juice products and I am received a sample of this a few weeks ago through a beauty subscription, so I've been using the Stem Cellular Repair Booster Serum all-told for nearly a month and I can absolutely see a difference in my skin, from texture to tone.

For reference, I am in my mid-thirties, I have rosacea/sensitive skin, I am caucasian with fair skin. I have to be super careful about the things that I use on my skin or else I can set off a serious rosacea flair up, particularly hyaluronic acid (which this serum has) but the Juice Beauty serum somehow lets me get a dose of hyaluronic acid without the redness.

I am often skeptical of "age defying" makeup and serums because my dermatologist always tells me that there are really only a few proven treatments that work. Besides retinols, hyaluronic acid is one of those chemicals that dermatologists are unsure about. But whatever does it, I swear my skin looks plumper and firmer and it feels softer.

The packaging is also nice because it comes in a pump (love pumps!) that dispenses just the right amount of product with no waste and keeps everything clean and sanitary. This is definitely a new essential in my beauty routine.
summary: A new essential for your beauty routine.

reviewText: I have enjoyed using this serum on my skin for the past week.  My skin feels smoother and softer,  while my foundation seems to look more flawless.  Looking forward to seeing more results over time.  This is an organic product with no parabens.  The pump bottle distributes a little serum at at time, so you don't waste the product.

My first impression of this serum is positive. I have used a competitor's serum similar in price but it is not packed with natural ingredients like this Juice product. The product goes on smoothly and is not oily. I apply the serum to my clean, dry face and allow a couple of minutes for it to dry before applying the Juice moisturizer. I have been using this product on half of my face and another moisturizer on the other half and I do believe the half getting the Juice products is silkier feeling.  My pores appear smaller on the Juice side. The item box clearly says to be careful with this product of you have rosacea or another sensitive skin condition. I have combination skin and have had reactions to chemicals in the past. This product presented no problem for me. UPDATE: The serum has passed the test!  Fine lines are disappearing and the quality of skin is improving.  I am glad I finally put a product through this informal test.  In the past I have always said nothing makes a difference from drug store brands to high end department brands and all in between.  When looking at my own face and comparing one side to the other I can tell Juice is doing a great job for me.

I'm so torn on this product.  On one hand, it sinks right into my skin with no greasy or lotion-y after feel.  My powder glides right on top of it without sticking or caking or changing the color or getting too thick.  It has made a difference on my fine lines (I'm still young enough I don't have the biggies yet).  It is in a pump container (no sticking my fingers in a pot!). It is organic to top it all off.
So what's the downside?  The price.  It is only 1oz of product (though the huge pump would lead you to believe there is a ton more in there).  If I had a much larger disposable income, I would absolutely use this under my makeup everyday.  I hate that I love it...

reviewText:
I'm really pink by nature, not freckly but fair enough that I've got to use a product with at least 30 SPF. This is the first time I've used something other than a zinc oxide sunscreen and I like it.

This clear sunscreen has low viscosity so it spreads very easily and quickly. It also dries quickly and I have the impression of not having it on. There are other clear sunscreens and I've heard people say they feel weightless as compared to the sunscreens we're more accustomed to using.

An example of another clear sunscreen is the Neutrogena Clear Face. It uses the same active ingredients as this Vichy Ideal Capital Soleil brand, so the difference is in the inactive ingredients. As this is the only clear sunscreen I've tried, I cannot compare based on experience but I do like that this one has only a slight fragrance.

I'm out and about a lot, and no matter how much I dislike putting it on, it's inevitable - I need to put sunscreen on my face.  The Vichy Captial Soleil is quite possibly the best facial sunscreen I've used to date.  The sunscreen works very well - when I put it on and was out for the afternoon in the warm California sun, I didn't get sunburnt on my cheeks and while I was sweating the sunscreen stayed in place and didn't bleed into my eyes rendering me tearful.

The sunscreen goes on very smoothly.  Unlike other sunscreens I've used, this sunscreen is very liquidy, which helps when putting it on your face.  It goes on evenly, dries quickly, and is matte in texture once dry.  It also feels very light on the face - in fact, I could hardly tell I was wearing sunscreen at all - and doesn't make my face look greasy at all.  I didn't have any issues with breakouts, and liked how the sunscreen didn't have an overpowering chemical scent.  The scent is very subtle, and once on my face I couldn't smell it at all.  I am also able to wear makeup with this sunscreen as a base, and I haven't had issues with the makeup running or smudging.

Overall, this is a really great facial sunscreen.  I started putting it on daily with good results, and haven't had any issues with burns.  I would definitely buy this sunscreen once I finish this bottle.
summary: Goes on Evenly, Dries Matte, Protects Well from Sunburn

reviewText: This is good to use daily and it has help my sister's skin. She loves it and uses it daily

I garden and I wear a sunscreen when I am outside.  This product worked really well for keeping my skin from suffering from over-exposure.  My only concern is that it is fairly pricey.  I can buy a really nice sunscreen for a fraction of the cost of this one and I didn't see much more by way of what this product could do for me.
summary: Nice but on the pricey side

reviewText:
I have been using this outside on my face and hands, even though it is winter.  Winter has sun.  It would also reflect on snow, if we had any.  We don't actually have any.

This went on cleanly, and lightly.  I am surprised that it even works because it is so light.  But we have been doing some yard work on our sunny early fall like weekends.  It is light and blends in very easily.  I don't smell anything except for the slightest chemical smell.

I am not sure what I think about SPF 50.  In all of my reading, I have seen that 35 SPF is all that is necessary.  What is important is that there be UVA and UVB protection. This one has that.

Earlier this year, when I was finally diagnosed with Ulcerative Colitis, my Gastroenterologist told me that having UC makes me more susceptible to skin cancer and that I should stay out of the sun, and if I do have to go out to wear a good sunscreen. This Vichy Ideal Capital SPF 50 Ultra Light Sunscreen is about as good as it gets.

I have extremely sensitive skin and I have a had time finding skin products that I can use due to them making my skin break out in either a rash or  acne. I'm 52-years-old. I shouldn't have acne. So, I'm always up for trying new things in hopes that I find something that works well without causing irritation to my skin. While writing this review, I discovered that they have some that is SPF 60 dry finish as well. I think next I will try that one. So far this doesn't irritate my skin at all. Of course, everyone is different so it's best to try it yourself. I will be trying the SPF 60 dry finish next.
summary: Great for sensitive skin. Nice way to protect your skin from the sun.

reviewText: Slightly oily (why I rated it 4 stars), but it is light. Needed to wait a bit before applying my foundation (to assure it was absorbed in). Works well, love that it is an SPF50 for my face. Lasted hours while I was outside (used this on a cruise where the sun was brutal). This bottle will last a long time as a little goes a long way.
summary: Great sunblock - a little greasy, but does the job

reviewText:
My go to sunscreen for many years has been the La Roche Posay Anthelios.  My main reason qualifiers for a really nice sunscreen are: absorbs easily into skin, no greasy feeling on the skin once applied, no overpowering scent, effective at preventing sunburn and doesn't irritate around the eyes.

I was pleased to see Vichy Ideal Capital Soleil scores high marks across the board on my checklist.  The packaging is simple, when you open the cap, the applicator dispenses a well metered amount of the thin sunscreen.  The consistency is like milk, and this helps for the product to absorb smoothly and quickly into the skin.  Within moments, I feel the sunscreen has covered and yet there is no heaviness or stickiness.  Many other sunscreens leave a film or layer and all you want is to wash your face off once out of the sun -- not with the Vichy Ideal Capital Soleil sunscreen.  The addition of Vitamin E and white grape extract are in there for additional protection of the surface layers of the skin, according to the side panel of the sunscreen's carton.

The sunscreen is noted as fragrance-free, I can detect a slight scent which is barely there.  Since it was not formulated with fragrance, there's no floral or cloying aroma which some sunscreens contain.  The sunscreen carries an SPF 50, with protection from UVA and UVB, important for avoiding signs of aging.  The sunscreen is also water resistant for 40 minutes for enjoying a dip at the pool or beach.  All in all, this sunscreen delivers and keeps you safe under the sun.
summary: absorbs easily into skin, no greasy feeling on the skin once applied, no overpowering scent, effective at preventing sunburn

reviewText:
I recently tried Vichy Capital Soleil SPF 45 Silkscreen Dry-Finish Lotion, 5 fl. oz which has dry finish to it and is for both face and body, well comparing this one, Vichy Idal Capital Soleil SPF 50 Ultra Light which 1.7 oz that is 50 spf that is marketed in a smaller container for the face...
While both are water resistant for 40 minutes this on is packaged with a smaller spout/tip on its plastic bottle, aimed at being stored with your cosmetics so it is easily applied in your daily routine. It also is quickly absorbed, has a pleasant light scent, does NOT leave in visible residue on your face, is ideal for applying with cosmetics....... however I personally do not think it is a great value for what you get!
I would rather buy the 5oz squeeze tube and use the dry touch formula with the spf of 45 as you get over 3X the amount of product for the same price!  If $$ is not a factor in your house then by all mens get the one designed for face only, you won't be disappointed but for my household I will get the bigger Vichy sunscreen, it works just as well IMO with cosmetic application.
summary: I currently use the Vichy Capital Soleil SPF 45 Silkscreen Dry-Finish Lotion, 5 fl. oz formula and compared this to that one

reviewText: This is super light and absorbs well. I applied this after I washed my face and used a hydrating serum, let that sink in well before applying the sunscreen - remember, summer may be over but your face, neck, and hands are still getting damaged every day that you don't wear sunscreen. After shaking as directed I put a tiny pool of this loose formula into the palm of my hand (about a dime size amount). Starting with my forehead, I was able to smooth this over my entire face. It stung a bit, but I have that experience with nearly all sunscreens I use. The uncomfortable sensation was over nearly as soon as it started. Initially it left my face a bit shiny, but as it absorbed into my skin the shiny appearance lessened, but was not completely gone. Through the day it occasionally itched a little, but that too was very transient. After a few hours you just totally forget you have it on. My skin just feels smooth. The only issue I found with this product is that it has a very beachy scent - a common sunblock scent. Initially didn't like the scent, but that did dissipate. Also, it's not terribly moisturizing, so I make sure to use a hydrating serum or regular moisturizer under this product. Very nice product.

I was honestly surprised by how much I loved this sun screen. The bottle has a tip that's designed to squirt out just the right amount for your face. Additional the sun screen itself is more liquid than any of the others I've tried in the past with such a high spf. It goes on my face easily and dries in seconds, so quickly in fact that the remainder I just wipe around my hands and there's no need to even rinse after. My skin absolutely loved it and as soon as it dried I felt like I was wearing nothing at all. The only complaint is the price point. a 1.7 oz bottle is tiny but costs quite a lot.

This is thin, and runs a bit when putting it on.  It goes on and at first, to me, it feels greasy, but that goes away very quickly, in just a few minutes after it is rubbed in.  Then it is totally invisible.  I waited about 20 minutes and sprayed an area that I had 1/2 a section covered with this sunscreen, and 1/2 that was untreated.  The water beaded up and ran off the treated area, vrs some beading and sheeting on the untreated.  The water resistance of this sunscreen was evident.
I don't smell any fragrance in it, but it has a mineral, natural smell.  It has very effective ingredients.  It's a fairly small bottle at 1.7 ounces.  I can see where it really appeals to some, but there are other sunscreens I think are a better value for my needs.  If you can afford it though, it is a good sunscreen that a few minutes after it is applied, disappears completely, and leaves skin soft and natural looking, but it does its job.
I would prefer that the cap be sealed with plastic.  Mine came in a box, but it wasn't sealed other than the flaps being closed, and there was no inner sealing of the product.
summary: A bit runny, but it goes on and disappears- it works well but leaves skin soft and natural

reviewText:
Vichy Ideal Soleil is definitely the best face sunscreen I've ever used.  Vichy is a European manufacturer known for its advanced skin care products. I believe this excellent sunscreen is an essential for everyone who wants to minimize damage from sun exposure.

Ideal Soleil is very fluid. I like the applicator which allows for just the right amount of sunscreen to be dispensed. Unlike some facial sunscreens that turn my skin white, Ideal Soleil works into my skin invisibly; it's practically undetectable. The sunscreen has an agreeable scent, too. What I value most is the benefit of a moisturizer that does a great job blocking out harmful sun rays including UV.

Yes, Ideal Soleil is priced higher than most ordinary, run-of-the-mill sunscreens but I think it's well worth it.  The applicator means there's no waste; and since the product is applied only to the face a relatively small amount goes a long way.  More than anything else, using Ideal Soleil means that outdoor activities are more enjoyable. I don't have to worry anymore about the sun's ill effects on my skin's health and appearance. That's a very good thing.

I highly recommend Ideal Soleil to everyone.
summary: The best face sunscreen I've ever used

reviewText: I had already fallen in love the Crabtree & Evelyn's Citron Honey & Coriander scent from using their ultra-moisturizing hand therapy (which is also fantastic!).  This lotion has the same wonderful scent but in a formula that is thinner and easier to massage into your body wherever you need it, it's great for soothing the dry winter itch that I get on my legs every year.  It absorbs fairly quickly without feeling greasy, and does a really good job of moisturizing.  This is definitely something I will be getting more of when it's gone. While the scent does seem a bit strong at first it does fade quite a bit after a while, but it does linger for a long time so if you are overly sensitive to scents and perfumes than Crabtree & Evelyn's products are probably not the best choice for you.
summary: Crabtree & Evelyn Citron Honey & Coriander Skin Quenching Body Lotion

reviewText: The lotion is everything I have come to expect from Crabtree and Evelyn. My skin stays soft and moisturized. It goes on nice and is absorbed quick with no oily residue. The only thing that bothered me about this one is the scent, my husband says it reminds him of bug spray. I really like Crabtree and Evelyn products--I consider them a more elegant version of Bath and Body Works.  However, this scent wasn't for me. Citrusy, yes, but with an undercurrent of something I find unpleasant. However, my teenage daughter LOVED the smell.

The lotion itself is nice!  Absorbs easily, is non-greasy, and moisturizes well.

my mom went to a conference recently and has brought home C&E lotion samples before but this one smells AMAZING! i love it. i don't think i'd purchase it because of the price but it smells great and does not leave my hands oily. i'll wait until she brings home more samples!

This is one of my favorites from oribe this is a light spray provides good texture and a light hold .I started with the small size and worked my way to the full size,there are many videos to show you how to use this.

I absolutely love this Hair product! II read alot of reviews before making the decision  to purchase this and I am sure glad I did. reviewText: I use this gel on my facial machine and Im glad I bought the larger tube however it would have earned 5 stars if I could have gotten a discount or sale as its very pricey for what you get.
It was good for me to try for my trinity facial toner.  You can get the same result from a less expensive product from your local drug store.  Aloe Vera has the same consistency.

I was so excited to receive this product for review, before accepting the offer I did a bit of research and read the reviews already out there on the PMD.  I have some acne scarring from problems during my two pregnancies and thought this just might be the answer.

I have used the Personal Microderm System for 3 weeks now, once per week.  If you receive this product do NOT use it without watching the product demo, this is extremely important, without watching the demo you could seriously hurt damage your skin.

The first day I used the product I was EXTREMELY careful, yet ended up with red streaks down my cheeks which ended up scabbing and some brilliant red circles on my cheekbones....I needed to attend a meeting that evening and quite a few people commented wondering what on earth happened to me.  At this point I was pretty leery since I wanted to help my skin not harm it.  It took almost a week, but my face healed up and I bravely gave myself a second treatment, it worked perfectly.  I think the trick is to be certain you only go over each section of skin only one time and be sure not to hold in one spot for any length of time.  After my third week I feel that my skin is much smoother and softer, I did notice the softness immediately.

The downside is that I can't seen to get the hang of using it on my hands, but it's a personal problem and in my opinion it is not a fault of the system.

There are two creams that are suggested for use with the PMD and I think it's a good idea to use them as well.  I really like the PMD and do recommend it, just use a gentle hand.

For the few minutes it takes to use the PMD, and the results it has given me I think it is very well worth every penny.  At $179.00 it really is a bargain if you compare the price to getting the same results at a Dr. office.

* I received the PMD system in exchange for review from the Fringe Network, I used this product as directed for three weeks and this is my honest opinion of the product.

I started using this product with the practice attachment for about a month, and I waited a full week between uses each and every single time. I didn't see any really difference, but I liked it well enough to keep going. After about a month I went up to the next attachment which I believe is called ultra sensitive.

The first few weeks were okay. And then about a week ago I noticed that I have dark lines and discoloration on my face. Now, I initially wondered if the complaints of this might be due to stripping a tan or something. But no... the lines caused by this device on my skin are dark.

Now, when I say I watched the videos, I don't just mean the one that comes with the device. I do mean *all* of the videos. The bad reviews, the everything. And I went it planning not to use the more abrasive attachments, and not to attempt using it too often.

Maybe... maybe for some people using it every 2 weeks could solve the problem. Maybe staying on the practice head (which doesn't do anything at all, really) could be worth it. But for the price?  And the risk of having dark lines and discoloration across your face? It's really not worth it in my opinion.

I didn't pay the full price suggest here. I found it on sale at Nordstrom. And even at $60 less it still seems like a huge risk to take with your face especially if you have sensitive skin.

I did honestly like it after the first use of the ultra sensitive disc. But discoloration with the most sensitive option is absurd.
summary: I watched the video and I waited
