This mascara has a deep, black finish that applied smoothly to my lashes. I didn't notice any significant clumping, but it did seem to take a lot longer than normal to dry on my lashes. It washed off with soap and water without trouble. I was less happy with how it smudged under my eyes, and that it took two coats to equal one coat of my usual Benefit They're Real! mascara. The brush is really annoying, too. I'm not sure how the ball at the end is supposed to help anything, but it sure makes the wand harder to get in and out of the tube. A couple of times I ended up flicking mascara on my clothes trying to get it out. That's a first for me since I started wearing mascara in the '80s!

It's worth noting that this tube holds a lot less mascara than other brands, too. It's 0.22 fl.oz., where Cover Girl is twice that. Event the Benefit mascara is 0.3 fl.oz. So while the price seems competitive, it's actually not very - especially since I have to use twice as much to get the same lashes I get with Benefit. I'll pass on this one.

The butter London Iconoclast mascara tube made a good first impression but as soon as I applied the formula to one eye, I had a terrible reaction. This was quite surprising since it has less of a sent than other mascaras, but for some reason, my eye itched and watered so badly I had to immediately wash off the mascara. The wand was very very flexible and the unusual brush design with a bristled ball tip will either be loved or hated. I like the design, I just cannot tolerate the actual cosmetic which is very unfortunate.

Went on nice, not thick and clumpy like many other mascaras.  But the best thing about this mascara is the brush, particularly the ball on the end.  It really makes separating the lashes on the outside of your eye easier and it is so easy to apply on the lower lashes.
summary: I LOVE the special ball tip on the end!

reviewText: I don't really like it.  The brush is divided into two parts.  The main section and the tip which is rounded or bulb-like.  The rounded tip on the end gets in my way and it didn't really carry enough mascara to do my bottom lashes.  The mascara made my lashes clump together which is the main reason why I don't like it.  So instead of 100 lashes to flutter, I had 30 stuck together.  I may give it another try, but my first impression is not good.  However sometimes a mascara is more liquid at first and then settles down and then it doesn't clump.  But I still don't like that round ball at the end.  I had to go back over my lashes with my Cover Girl mascara to try to separate the lashes which didn't work well since they were already clumped.
summary: I don't like the brush's special tip

reviewText: I normally use mascara that costs under $10. In fact, for most of my life the pink-tubed Maybelline, highly recommended by makeup artists, was my favorite. I had never used a brush like this. I liked the little bulb at the end and that it went on without clumping. However, I had trouble getting the wad back into the tube. It bent on my first attempt. It did straighten upon additional applications. The mascara wet on well, but the only thing I like better than my much cheaper brands is that the mascara is drier and so did not smear. It was about the same dryness as after a week of using my other stuff. Basically this was a nice every day mascara. It did not plump or lengthen my lashes as much as L'oréal Paris Super-volumized, Super-extended, Superstar Lashes Mascara (L'Oreal Paris Voluminous Superstar Black 622 Mascara)
summary: Nice for every day use but too expensive

reviewText: Butter London is a great brand of beauty products. I've been using their nail polish and lip gloss for years and always get complimented as a result. Now I tried this volumizing mascara, ad I'm very impressed. I'm not normally a fan of oddly shaped mascara brushes but this one definitely gets the job of reaching the corner lashes done. This mascara doesn't clump or melt in hot weather. It doesn't give me raccoon eyes by he end of the day either.

WOW is all I have to say about this mascara!

It's tough for me to find one that meets my criteria for mascara, actually I don't know that I have before this one in fact.  My criteria is that it a) doesn't melt off my face as soon as applying, I want it ON my lashes, not below my eyeballs.  b) doesn't make my eyes itch (my eyes are sensitive) c) makes my eyelashes look good.  While I realize that isn't a huge list it's really hard to find one that meets all three.  If it doesn't make my eyes itch, then it seems to melt off.  If it doesn't melt off, it makes my eyes itch or they just don't do anything and so forth.

The bonus to Butter London's Iconoclast is that the brush is really amazing.  It's a normal plastic brush for most of the wand but the end tip is a ball that lets you get in there to grasp the tiny lashes that can be troublesome to nab.

Personally I don't think there's mega volume but I think that it does build up decently.

There was a bit of fallout BUT it wasn't until about 12 hours in of my wearing on a 100 degree day when photographing a wedding.  That's really impressive considering how many times I put my eyes up to a camera through the day.

If you're looking for a solid mascara that gets the job done and won't make your eyes itchy, stop looking and buy!

Love this butter London Iconoclast Mega Volume mascara. The issue I've always had with mascara is that I can feel it on my lashes. This is so lightweight that I can't tell it's there and I love that. The wand is a little strange and takes some getting used to but the mascara is lovely. The price is a little higher for the amount that you get compared to other brands I usually purchase (Too Faced, Tarte).
My wife this mascara enough to use to regularly and would consider buying it again in the future. She believes it works better than many less expensive products.

I like literally everything from Butter London. It's what most of my nail products and makeup is.  But I hadn't tried this Mega Volume mascara before.

It is Mega.  It doesn't sting or flake into my eyes (I'm looking at you Urban Decay).  If I curl my lashes first, this is amazing. The applicator is sort of weird but it gets at the inner corners really well.  It is quite noticeable in the volume it packs, so when I put this on I didn't put any mascara on my lower lashes. I felt like that would be too much.

The only downside is you really have to take this off with remover and work at it a bit.  I went swimming with this on and came out major raccoon eyes. Yes, that would happen. But much more than usual.  I had makeup remover pads with me, and it took awhile to be able to not have black mascara all the way down my cheeks.
summary: Neat applicator, big volume, does Adele use this?

reviewText:
This is a great mascara if you buy your mascara from a department store as I do.
What I love about it-
* The brush is fantastic.  There is a little ball on the end which really gets into the corners of your eyes and makes it so much easier to get a light coat on the bottom of your lashes.
* The price is literally the same as I pay for mine at Belk.
* The product comes off seamlessly with a makeup wipe.  Mine usually takes 1/2 a wipe to get it off cleanly.
The only drawback with this mascara was that it took 4 coats to do the job that mine does in 3.  Overall a great product.
summary: Great brush for hard to hit side lashes and bottom lashes.

reviewText:
The first thing you'll notice when you apply is that it doesn't feel like the brush is "grabbing" your lashes. there isn't a lot of load or deposit, which is baffling me as to why they named it Mega Volume.

It's naturally separating and defining, but the volume only comes when you add additional swipes of the spherical ball tip. This means more "work" for you, building up layers of thickness.

If you want to "Swipe and go" out the front door with a quick flick of the brush, you're going to get a more natural look. If you're expecting volume, add a little more time to your makeup routine.
summary: Not a "swipe and go" mascara -- takes more "work" to get "Mega Volume" via multiple applications

reviewText:
Butter London is a very well known brand. I have tried their blush and nail colors and have been very pleased. The mascara is an interesting product. The traditional wand has a ball on the end, it does make applying the mascara easier, and does not clump. The mascara is jet black, and for my aging lashes did define and separate my lashes. I can't really see that it lengthens my lashes, but because my lashes are thinner than they used to be, it does provide some volume.

The directions are explicit and easy to follow. Apply to lashes using the center part of the mascara wand. Pull the bristles through the lashes in a zig-zag motion to coat each lash. Use the tip of the wand to lengthen and define. The mascara does apply very evenly, and I liked the application. For my use the mascara did not smudge, and I used it during a 90 degree day and went out to complete some errands. My face was moist and no signs of smudging. I think this was an excellent test. I tend to tear easily and that is the greatest test for mascaras, it did not run nor smear.

My use of mascara is usually limited for night time events, and I will certainly use this again. The one issue I have is that you have to exert force to get the ball end if the wand in and out of the mascara. A small issue, but an irritating one.

Recommended. prisrob 07-26-16
summary: No Clumping Of Lashes, Separates and Seems To Lengthen Lashes

reviewText: This gives a very black lengthening of the lashes. My lashes appear separated and long. The tip of the applicator helps get the outside corner lashes very long. Once the mascara dries it is stiff and makes it difficult to add more mascara to the lashes without clumping, so work quickly. I have fine, short lashes and this makes them look really nice and long, but it is definitely not a thickening bushy lash some people want. I also don't have any problems with it bothering my eyes.

Disappointing.  I have normal lashes - not long, but not too short.  Like all people, I want thicker, longer lashes.  This product just doesn't deliver well for me.  First, the weird shape of the wand makes it almost impossible to apply to all lashes - in fact, not even sure what the "ball" shape on the end is for because it seems useless.  Second, I don't like the mascara gel - goes on really thin and smudges easily - takes FOREVER to dry so it makes it easy to mess up application from the beginning or for it to smudge before drying.  I tried to put several layers on to make thicker, longer lashes but I just simply couldn't get it to cooperate. I just don't think I will purchase this in the future.

If you like a spherical tip to mascara wand, this could be the mascara you would want.  It does take some getting used to, but I think it is safer when first applying to lashes.  However, after working with the mascara, I did not find it really was significantly better than other mascaras I have tried and used throughout the years.  I did not put a primer on first; I wanted to see if it adhered to lashes, and it did without primer.

It did not provide better overall volume and I was disappointed.  I applied it initially and reapplied it twice more.  I did not not notice a significant difference.  I washed it off easily and tried it again, using a different technique of zig-zagging on first application and then working the tips of the lashes.  That worked somewhat better but not appreciably.  At this price point, I think that there are better mascara products out there with heavier coverage and no clumping.  This did not clump but it did smudge later after second application. On the plus side, my lashes did not itch, and this is a good one to use safely.
summary: Safe Non-Clump Mascara But Minimal Volume

reviewText: Butter London has some amazing Nail Polishes and is a great brand so I was curious to try their Mascara. In short, this was just an average mascara and is way over-priced. You can find better ones at the drugstore. The Wand was a little annoying to work for me and though I wiped the product on tissue before applying it, it has major clumping issues. It does make lashes appear long but the clumping just turned me off.
summary: Butter London has some amazing Nail Polishes and is a great brand so I ...

reviewText: I was SO excited to try this because I love, love, love brushes with a spherical tip. I fell in love with this style of brush years ago with Givenchy Phenomen'Eyes Mascara 1 Phenomen'Black 0.24 oz but didn't really love the formulation of the mascara liquid, so I've been experimenting with other mascaras ever since. Spherical tips don't seem to be very common (And I can understand why because it was a little weird at first and I probably wouldn't have picked it up and experimented with it without the coaxing of a makeup artist who raved about it.) so I was curious to see how this would perform since I've already had great experience with other makeup products from butter LONDON. So far I'm in love. The brush was a little wet and overloaded with product when I first opened the mascara so I wiped it on a lint-free cloth, as I've done with another mascara and it fixed the problem. After completely cleaning the brush of the existing product, dipping it back in and starting over I got just the perfect amount of mascara. I LOVE that sweeping this on my lashes gives them volume and length without being spidery or clumping. And the ball tip is perfect for getting the small lashes in the inner and outer corners of my eyes as well as going back over anything to make sure every stray millimeter of lash is covered. I also think it wears well. I don't notice it flaking or smudging off on my face even though it's quite humid and hot here in Chicago right now and I also commonly wear eye makeup to my hour-long workouts where I am sweating profusely. It also removes pretty easily with my Sephora brand makeup remover and a cotton round, which is nice because some mascaras can cling on so tight I find myself losing lashes when removing it. I'm a fan.
summary: I'm a sucker for a mascara with a spherical brush head, and this one delivers

reviewText: I was pleasantly surprised by this mascara. I have tried tons of mascaras over the years from Dior to drugstore, and have recently stuck with Maybelline New York Volume' Express The Rocket Waterproof Mascara, Very Black, 0.3 Fluid Ounce because it holds my curl indefinitely, gives me great volume, doesn't smudge or flake, and costs $6. I wasn't expecting this butter LONDON mascara to rival the Maybelline, but it does. The picture is immediately after application (two coats). I didn't bother with an end of the night pic because it stayed looking exactly the same after 12 hours of wear. It held my curl and didn't smudge or flake at all! In fact it performed almost exactly like The Rocket mascara. I haven't liked ball-tip wands in the past, but this one was great at helping to separate my lower lashes and getting the inner corner. I honestly don't have a single complaint about this mascara. It gives volume and length, as advertised, and won't move all day. This isn't a waterproof mascara, but it's close. I had to use an oil based eye makeup remover to take it off. I don't mind that at all though since this holds my curl like a waterproof mascara and doesn't smudge. The only reason I probably won't be switching to this mascara is the price. It's 3X as much as the Maybelline and they give me the same effect. Still, this is by far the best high end mascara I've ever used.
summary: The best high end mascara I've ever used.

reviewText:
I've been buying Butter London nail polishes for a few years and have always loved them, and have been happy to see that they've branched into creating makeup now, too.  This mascara creates a nice, dark, glossy color, and I really like the volume it gives.

The unusual brush shape takes some getting used to if, like me, you're used to a more conventional mascara wand.  After using this for a few days, though, I got the hang of it.  It's a bit tricky to use on your bottom lashes, but still coats those well.

While this is billed as a volumizing mascara, it also does add some length, without weighing down your lashes.  My current favorite mascara is Buxom Lash, and this is comparable in terms of giving a natural look to your eyes that is not too dramatic for daytime wear.

The formula also hasn't irritated my eyes, which water quite a bit because of allergies, and doesn't bleed when they've become teary.

Overall, I really like this!
summary: The unusual brush takes some getting used to, but then it stays in place all day, even with allergy-prone eyes

reviewText: This is a really nice high quality black mascara.  The first thing you notice is the non conventional shape of the brush at the end and you are either going to love it or hate it.  It really goes makes application easier but this may vary on the shape and thickness of your lashes.  This mascara goes on smooth and doesn't clump up and it dries quite quickly.  It comes off easy as well.  The bottle is a bit smaller volume wise than most mascaras.
Nice mascara, does a great job with volume but you have to be a little careful with it getting to spiky. I would not recommend more than two coats. But it's a nice long lasting formula
Product goes on well but skin appears greasy/oily after application.

This CC has light coverage, amazing anti-aging skin benefits with good clean organic ingredients like oils, reservatrol, hyaluronic acid, anti-oxidants etc. Shade "warm glow" is for light-med skin w yellow undertone. Gives very pretty slightly tanned healthy complexion. Evens out texture in skin but doesnt create texture, it is invisible. Finish looks like skin, it is smooth and slightly glowy but not at all oily. It doesnt accentuate lines, pores or peach fuzz. You don't have to set it. I sometimes use loose mineral foundation on top for extra coverage. Sunscreen is mineral only, non-nano. It doesnt have any chemical UV absorbers. Now they added more shades, i think there are 5.  My second tube, highly recommend.

Haven't used it but I used the one I bought from Juice Beauty.com. I like it as it blends well into my Asian skin. However, I want it to give more coverage as my skin has freckles and discoloured pots.
summary: I like it as it blends well into my Asian skin

reviewText: It's okay. It doesn't offer any coverage to speak of, which seems weird considering how thick and goopy it is.
summary: It's okay. It doesn't offer any coverage to speak ...

reviewText: Great for travel and sports. Has coverage for evening out skin tone without being a makeup that is going to noticeably smear off on your clothes or hat as you sweat. Recommended by the Environmental Working Group for non-toxic ingredients and good spf coverage.

I've never used a CC cream before, so I wasn't sure what to expect.  I think I like it, but it's not going to be an everyday thing for me.  The shade is good for my skin tone (I had "Natural Glow") but it doesn't offer a lot of coverage.  It can't really be used on its own unless you are having a very good skin day.  This CC cream provides a little bit of a shimmer or sheen, not the same as the oily skin I get in my T-zone, but a nice all-around glow.  However, if you are going to be using concealer to cover up blemishes, for example, the concealer will not have the same finish as the CC cream and may mar the finish a little bit (hence the "good skin day").

I love that it is SPF 30 and that it's a mineral sunscreen (I have allergies to some chemical sunscreens).  I would say the consistency is thicker than liquid foundation and that it's a little difficult to spread.  I don't care for the smell all that much, but for me, it faded fairly quickly.  (I can't think of anything the odor reminds me of to offer a comparison.)

Here are the ingredients (from the company website) since I didn't see them on the product page; note that many of the ingredients are certified organic (those marked by an asterisk).

Active Ingredient: Zinc Oxide 20%

Inactive Ingredients: Juice Beauty proprietary blend of fruit stem cells: apple buds, grape buds & lemon bark. Organic juices of apple*, white grape*, aloe leaf*, organic coconut oil*, caprylic/capric triglyceride, sorbitan stearate, castor seed oil, polyglyceryl-10 laurate, magnesium sulfate, organic sunflower seed oil*, organic jojoba seed oil*, Vitamin E, Vitamin C, sodium hyaluronate (vegetable hyaluronic acid), apple buds, grape buds & lemon bark, iron oxides, phenethyl alcohol, ethylhexylglycerin, mandarin & petitgrain pure essential oils.
So the ingredients are wonderful.  I am thrilled that the company not only uses hyaluronate of non-animal origin, but that it actually tells you the source!

In the end, if you are already a CC cream user and are looking for a product that has lots of natural and/or organic ingredients and a reasonably high SPF level, this would be a great choice.  I think I'll be using it most often when my skin is in a clearer phase so I don't have to worry about the effects of concealer.
summary: love the SPF; best for days when your skin is already looking good

reviewText: I just found this CC cream. It is organic and no bad chemicals. It does 12 functions. I got the warm glow color. Matches my skin perfectly. It's not heavy, but it evens out skin tone and gives an awesome glow. Those fine lines around my mouth and on my forehead are barely visible now. It seems like my skin gets better after I wash it off. I put it on over a light moisturizer and its perfect.

I'm very pleased with the Lacoste Femme Gift set. The fragrance is perfect for summer and reminds me of another favorite summer scent I had called Cool Water. It lasts quite a while and yet it isn't overpowering at all. The fragrance really is quite pleasant and the lotion felt so refreshing. The bottle is also quite pretty and the price is fairly good for such a gift set.

This eau de parfum has a very light fragrance. It is reminiscent of flowery cotton, but it is so light that after a couple hours when I held my wrist up to my friend to ask if she could smell it she could not. This is wonderful for those who are sensitive and hate those elevator chocker scents.

It comes in a handsome spray bottle. The lotion that comes in the package also has this light scent but the lotion itself is very runny. I would use it for the scent to rub on my skin, but as for it to be used as an effective lotion for skin softening/ body lotion for example it would have to have a creamier/thicker base.
The box makes a nice gift set and for those who like light fragrances this would be a good choice.

I have used this quite a few times as a top coat believe it or not.  I really find that it improves the lasting power of my nail polish.  It takes longer to chip and is nice and shiny.  I have used this over various brands, including OPI, Butter London, and Zoya.  Generally OPI performs the best for me, but I find that this extends the wear even of Butter London polishes which tend to chip quickly on me.  I like this!
summary: I use this as a top coat and love it!

reviewText:
Great product even if it is a bit overpriced for what your are actually getting.  The packaging states that it should be applied daily.  I find that to be excessive.  I apply as my base coat and then as a top coat.  This is a great top coat because it does harden your natural nails.  I was also very happy to see that it does not yellow.  The peeling at the edges began around the fifth day which is quite good for this type of product.

What I liked about the product and would warrant a higher cost then your basic hardener is the fact that there are not any chemicals; or so the packaging states!

Highly recommend if you are in the market for a good base coat and nail hardener that does not yellow or chip within a day or two.  I still find that it's price point is a bit excessive but will allow it because of the ingredients.

For what this is, Londontown's nail hardener is overpriced.  First of all, the packaging says may be used as a base coat.  For me, that didn't quite work because, having heavily ridged nails, this polish did NOT apply smoothly, and did not allow me to leave my nail with complete coverage of polish over my nails.  So that meant I had to apply another brand of base coat over that in order to be able to finish my manicure.

As far as hardening properties, can't say this did much of anything.  Some of my nail are fairly pliable, and even with this hardener they basically stayed the same after application.

Can't say I can recommend Londontown nail hardener and base coat, and especially not at THIS price.
It seems to be working really well. It is a bit pricey but have been keeping my nails from breaking. So it is a WIN

My nails are somewhat brittle and peel easily, so it was a relief to put some nail hardener on them.  The Londontown kur Nail Hardener is a quality brand but the price is really high. Luckily, it seems to need only one or two coats to work, so one bottle should last awhile.

Excellent product. I applied 2 coats without any polish so I could see how long the shine lasts.  Well, it's been 4 days and my nails are as glossy as the day I applied this base coat.  It also hasn't chipped or worn off the edges like the other top coat I use, which I re-apply every day.  This is definitely a time saver since I only have to apply it once a week.  My nails have also not chipped or broken since I started using this product which is quite a feat this time of year with all the baking, cleaning and decorating that goes on.

 I'm interested in trying this brands top coat.  If it performs as well as the base coat, my home mani's will last a lot longer.
summary: Best base coat I've tried in a long time

reviewText:
This is a high quality, durable, base coat for your nails.  It goes on smooth and dries quickly.  The odor is a bit strong, as all acrylic nail polishes are, but the smell fades in reasonable time.  3 days after I have applied this to my dry, clean, nails, I have no chipping.  The shine is great.  This is good for a base coat that is all you want on your nails - for that freshly manicured look; or for base under and over a color.  It's worth the money because it doesn't peel after a few days.

I recommend it.
summary: Doesn't Peel After A Few Days

reviewText:
This is a very promising product! Of course, time will tell, but so far -- I do love the results!

As soon as the weather starts turning cold and the indoor heat gets turned on at home and at work, my nails start chipping and seem to snag on almost everything I touch. I gave myself a manicure and used only this product on my nails. It seems to have given them a little more "stability," and the snaggle-tooth edges have not reappeared! It dries quickly, and I have reapplied it with good results. I put a little extra on the edges of my nails and a little under the free edge.

If you are looking for something to give your nails a light shine and improve their strength, I don't think you can do any better than Londontown. I hate overspending on cosmetic items, but sometimes, you really do get what you pay for. Therefore, recommended!
summary: Say goodbye to snaggle-tooth nail edges!

reviewText:
Kur Nail Hardener and Base Coat from Londontown is as good as one would expect from a premium nail product. It flows easily onto the nail and seems to be thicker than my other, less expensive base coats. It's almost as thick as a gel polish. Because it's thick, it does a good job of filling in small ridges or pits in my nails and creates an ultra smooth surface for my colored nail polish to go on. My nail polish flows over this like butter and looks great.

It also seems to do a good job protecting my nails from staining when using a dark red nail polish.

It's very shiny and even though it's a base coat, I did apply it over pale pink polish as a top coat and it seems to work fine. I didn't try it over my red toenail polish, though, because I didn't want to stain this base coat, as can sometimes happen when applying over dark colors and dipping the brush into the bottle repeatedly.

You could definitely wear this alone as a clear polish because it's so smooth, thick and shiny.

As far as it being a hardener, I really can't tell a difference. Maybe that only happens over time?

Kur is a very good product and superior to most base coats I've used and I would rate it 5 stars except I can't help but feel that $18 is really high. I know there are other premium brands that cost even more but I would never consider buying any of those. I definitely will consider buying kur when this runs out, but I'll be grumpy if I can't find it on sale.
summary: As a base coat, it really is superior

reviewText: Polish went on nicely and dries quickly, leaving a soft shine finish. Nails feel stronger and harder to break or snag. I like how this nail hardener makes makes my nail look and feel. I have a horrible time with nails breaking. My nails do not  bend so easily with this product on them. Using this polish on a regular basis is going to help them grow longer and stronger.

I just had tips removed and the salon ruined my nails by filing the nails down to where even with gel polish 3 nails ripped the first day.  Boy, was I happy to receive this product.  I used it as a top coat and what a great result.  My nails have stopped breaking and now I just have to be patient and wait for my healthy nails to grow. The only issue I have with the product is the price.
Highly recommend!

It looks good as a clear coat, but it is not stopping my fingernails from breaking at the tips.  I have only applied it two times so far in a couple of weeks, so perhaps as I give it more coats it will work better.  For the price, I don't believe this Londontown hardener is doing what I expected.  It does have a nice, smooth appearance when applied.
summary: Ok as a base coat, but the hardener effect is negligible

reviewText:
I've been using this for over a week now and my nails have not broken or split once, and by now they would have broken a couple of times at least without this.

I admit to not being a regular user of polish and base coats but whenever I do I get some improvement in how my nails look and this is no different. I especially love how this is free of carcinogenic chemicals such as toluene.  I never want to put chemicals on my skin or nails, hence few manicures aside from basic grooming.  But I feel as if this poses no chance for harm, and it looks nice on its own as a glossy clear coat.

Aside from the inexplicably high price this is a very nice base coat.

On it's own, this is a nice nail strengthener, it's shiny, dries quickly and wears evenly so that on day three I didn't really notice that the tips had worn off. My nails didn't peel while this was on, and actually seemed pretty strong after removal.
However, I rarely wear clear so I mainly used this a base coat, and I have to say that it was impressive. Even with other polish brands on top, this held them on my nails and kept them chip free for days longer than my usual base.
It's high quality hardener and while the price point is a little high, I would say it's worth it because it works.
The only negative, for me, is that the brush (while easy enough to maneuver) is of the thin type that I'm not particularly fond of. I've been spoiled with wide curved brushes in many recent polishes, and prefer that.
I would happily reorder this, and I'll be picking up some other Londontown polishes as well!

I used this as an extra top coat and I noticed it is better top coat than the salon top coat.  The ends of my nails, the color did not fray and flake off as quickly.  Easy to apply, typical for most top coat.  Not cheap,but there is a noticeable difference in keeping the color on longer. Time saver for me, who does not have enough time for weekly manicures.
summary: Expensive, but time saver at the end of the day

reviewText:
I do not love this anymore than my current base and top coat that is normally about the same price as this but you can find great deals sometimes on here and on Ebay. I feel like for $18 it better do miracles for my nails. My 2 yr old loves to get her nails painted and I always use a base coat so that it doesn't start to make her nails brittle and chip or yellow.

Like I said, it works, but it's way to expensive. You can find something just as good for cheaper.

My nails always break--probably because I spend so much time on a computer--so I am always the lookout for a high-quality nail hardener. Finally, I have found one that doubles as a topcoat and base-coat. For best results, stroke on every night to keep the effect going, and to give your nails shine. The price, for me, is worth it: not as costly as, say, Chanel, but more than my usual polishes OPI and Essie and quite a bit more than Cover Girl, Sally Hansen and Revlon. The extra $10-15 is a good investment, the brush is good, and the smell is faint and not offensive.

"kur" by Londontown works well, particularly for someone who does a lot of housework/has hands in water, etc. but still wants their nails to stay nice. It is a very good base coat and does help the polish hold up.

Simply by virtue of using a basecoat alone, you can help the condition of your fingernails, since some nail polish ingredients can dry out nails.

I don't read anything in the ingredient list that is really going to lend itself to conditioning the nail, or at least those ingredients are fairly far down the ingredient list. Not that I think kur is not helpful, but I think it's value is as a quality basecoat, not a conditioner. I would suggest periodic treatment with a nail moisturizer, or even good old olive oil, to help condition nails and the surrounding area.

The product odor is no worse than your typical nail polish product. It does dry evenly and is very long lasting, and the overlying polish absolutely holds up a little better than with store brand base coat.

I like this Londondown kur nail hardener.  The bottle design is like a cross between an Essie bottle and a Butter London bottle.  However, despite the grand marketing claims, I don't much in the designation of "nail hardener." Its medicinal properties to "heal" nails is probably slim to none.

It is longlasting and fast-drying as a base coat and top coat.  On those factors, it doesn't notably outperform current category killer Seche Vite, but seems to be aiming at a different section of the market (i.e. higher-end, like Butter London).  But I give it 4 stars because it performs well and is 5-free (its formula omits harmful dibutyl phthalate (DBP), toluene, and formaldehyde, formaldehyde resin and camphor).  Seche Vite is currently not (contains Toluene).
summary: 5-free, and works well as a base coat and top coat

reviewText: Stings the eyes, but does remove makeup well.  I like the scent (mildly flowery).

First off, if you've never used a micellar water/solution before , I strongly recommend giving them a shot. Micellar waters are a soap free non-rinse cleansing solution that gently and effectively removes makeup, dirt, and other debris on the skin by using micelle molecules that, when applied to the skin, encapsulates debris within the molecules which removes it from the skin without stripping and irritating even the most sensitive skin. It's all very scientific. There's a slew of information that you can find on micelle molecules and how they work.

Micellar solutions can be used in a number of ways ( i.e. a makeup remover, toner, cleanser) and working them into your skin care routine can really save you a lot of time.

After using a whole bottle of the pink version (which is for normal and sensitive skin) I decided to try this green version out (for oily and combination skin) when I needed to reorder because within the last year my skin has become excessively more oily in my T-zone and chin, yet exceptionally dry everywhere else. I really wanted to see what, if any, difference there was between the two.

Since I still had a few applications worth in the pink bottle I decided to do a side by side comparison for a few days by using the pink version on one side of my face and using the green on the other. I typically use my micellar solution to remove my makeup and prep my skin for washing and cleansing with either my Murad Time Release Acne and Ant-Aging cleanser, or my Caudalie foaming cleanser. If I'm feeling particularly too lazy/tired, or if I'm not wearing any makeup I'll use it on its own.

Both perform the same at successfully removing makeup and dirt, however I found that I had to use more of the pink solution than the green to achieve my desired results. Both are similarly gentle and refreshing and remove eye makeup without struggle or irritation, but again it seemed like the green removed more more quickly than the pink. The pink does tingle more than the green. If you use these solutions you know what I'm talking about. For those of you that don't, I say "tingle" because it's the only word I can think of to describe the sensation. It is not a burning, menthol, or medicated type of tingling. It's not uncomfortable or irritating by any means and is more strongly felt in more sensitive areas or areas that are more clogged than others. Also, it stops pretty quickly and is not felt once the solution has evaporated. I'm assuming that this tingle sensation is in part linked to the encapsulation of debris by the molecules before evaporation. If you've ever eaten Pop Rocks, imagine a gentler, much less extreme version of that sensation on your skin.

In my side by side comparison I noticed that the side on which I used the green solution stayed grease-free longer than that of the pink. The green side also feels less taught after drying than the pink. Although, I hadn't noticed any tightness in feeling with the pink version before trying the green and comparing, so the difference is slight yet enough to notice.

The pink version is clear, however the green is light blue in color. The ingredients are significantly different. I won't list them all here but I will point out that the pink version has cucumber extract whereas the green has ginkgo biloba extract instead. The green seems to have more ingredients than the pink and is NOT fragrance free like the pink one...BUT despite the fact the pink does not have any ADDED fragrance, it does have a smell. The pink version definitely smells stronger than the fragrance of the green. Oddly enough, the green smells like cucumber and rose. The fragrance of the green version is so slight it's almost unnoticeable upon application which causes me to believe it is included to either counteract any scent caused by an ingredient the pink version does not have, or for those who don't like the way the pink one smells. The pink has a slight tinge of chemical smell but primarily (and this is just what it smells like to me and the best way I can describe it) it smells like dirt. Yep. Dirt. Literal earth. Almost the way dirt smells after it rains. It's not horrible or overly offensive to me personally, it's just much stronger.

If you're trying to choose between the two, the added fragrance and the smell of each might be a big determining factor.

Another pro for the green is that I paid almost $10 less for the bigger bottle (500 ml) than I ended up paying for the smaller (250 ml) bottle of the pink. I realize this is relative and depends on sellers, availability, and location (the 250ml pink bottle was purchased at $34 before shipping from over sea's).

Do I like one more than the other? Not really, although, I think the green version suits my personal skin needs better than the other at this point in time. They both are exceptional at what they do. Micellar solutions have become an integral part of my beauty regiment. These bottles last quite awhile and have removed my need to buy cleansing wipes and other makeup removers, which tend to break me out eventually.

I hope this review was helpful to those trying to decide which product is right for you. Everyone's skin and needs are different and to say "this ones better" or "that ones better" as a blanket statement doesn't really help anyone make an informed choice, IMO.
summary: Green version or Pink version? What's the difference?

I've been using this as my daily SPF product for face and I've been very happy with it.

Because it is a mineral sunscreen and it is not tinted, it may leave a bit of a white sheen/layer on your face.  This is not a problem with this particular product but rather a feature of pretty much every non-tinted product in this category (if you need a tint, there are products available from CoTZ and Coola that should suit your needs).

The texture is a bit more lotion-like than some of the other mineral sunscreens I've used lately. I really like the way it dries, almost powdery -- and it's very good as a base for liquid foundation.  I feel like it's giving me good sun protection.  I don't spend a lot of time outside but I haven't noticed any tanning.

Here are the ingredients since I didn't see them on the product page:

-Titanium Dioxide 1.5%.
-Zinc Oxide 17%.

Dimethicone, Dimethicone Crosspolymer, Caprylic/Capric Triglyceride, Glyceryl Isostearate, Polyhydroxystearic Acid, Silica, Butyloctyl Salicylate, Polysilicone-15, Dimethicone/Vinyl Dimethicone Crosspolymer, Iron Oxides, PEG/PPG-18/18 Dimethicone, Triethoxycaprylylsilane, Tetrahexyldecyl Ascorbate, Green Tea Extract, Cranberry Fruit Extract, Pomegranate Extract.

This does contain some silicones if you are watching out for those.  I'm happy to see the vitamin C (ascorbate) and plant extracts, which will have a lot of antioxidants to add an additional layer of protection against sun damage. reviewText:
First off, I love the color.  I don't have anything like this and I used it immediately upon receiving it (it was June's High Shine Club selection for me).

I did have to use 3-4 coats to really get it to be opaque, but light colors are often like that for me.  I think I am going to try it in the future over an opaque white polish; it should look great that way.  It was a good texture when wet (not too thin or too thick) and was easy to apply and I like the brush.  The finish on my nails is super smooth.

However, I did get chips on a couple of fingernails within 24 hours.  I had tried to be careful, and my nails aren't that long, so this was a little disappointing.  I touched up with new polish in the chipped areas and it's hard to tell I did any touch up unless you get really close.  So, I think my manicure will still last for a few days, though I expect to have to do more touch-ups now.  (I did peel a whole bunch of oranges and the polish didn't get messed up, so that was nice.)

I used a Seche Vite quick-dry topcoat with this.  I do have an Essie topcoat and I may try that next time to see if staying within one brand results in increased performance.  Overall, however, I'm pretty happy with this.

I actually came across this sort of accidentally. See, I was removing some dark red nail polish from my fingernails, and it left behind this really awesome pinkish hue. No, I did not use a base coat, and yes, I do realize the pinkish hue was a stain. But this got me thinking...I would pay for this look. I had no idea if I could replicate it, and it was a little uneven so I thought, "Wouldn't it be great if there was a nail polish that could give me the same effect?!" Turns out, there is. It's Essie's Pink Glove Service. I ordered it a couple days ago, received it today, and put it on. My nails are adorable. They look so natural and feminine! I would recommend this to anyone looking for a classic, elegant look for their natural nails. :)
summary: Love it, love it, and love it.

reviewText: I was never really into the expensive nail polishes like Essie. However, one day I fell in love with a color my friend was wearing. It was DJ Play that Song. So I asked her if I could borrow it. The polish went on very smooth {I always were a bottom coat}. I only had to put 2 coats on to achieve the desired color. I loved it!! I am a faithful fan of Essie now, with DJ Play that Song as my most favorite polish color. It is a slight neon purple color, however not to bold. I have it on my toes now and receive tons of compliments.
I love this color (and many of Essie's colors), but the polish gets so many bubbles as it dries that it's unusable.

Usually, my nail polish chips in 1 day... this one is long lasting, but I find that I need to shake it often (almost between each nail) or it gets clumpy, and then it dries with a dull finish.  Nothing that a little attention to detail and a clear coat can't fix.  I'm really impressed with the long lasting wear which is what bumped it up from a 3 to a 4.
summary: Long Lasting but has a dull finish

But it's held up so far with a top coat.  Definitely in my top 5 favorite polishes out of the 50-something I have.

On a side note, the polish arrived very fast, a day before the shipment stated.  The polish was properly wrapped in bubble wrap and then put into paper packaging that was encased with bubble wrap as well.

reviewText: As usual Essie has another hit!  Great color for a mani/pedi for summer.  Looks great on most skin tones  Shipped quickly too.

DJ Play That Song is a semi-neon purple color with red undertones. I say semi because it's not a blazing neon. It can be worn to work. It looks just like it is pictured in the bottle - pinkish purple. I tried to take pics after applying but my camera wouldn't capture the real color. I tried in sun/shade/indoors/lights.. but didn't work. The color is really pretty to naked eye.

Saturday Disco Fever is a bright pure orange color. This is not a very blazing neon, so I am able to wear it to work. It looks fabulous in sunlight as well as indoors. I felt that this color is more suitable for evenings and parties in Summer. I was a little apprehensive at first because I personally don't like Yellow/Orange shades. But this color worked for me. It is more red-toned than yellow-toned. This dark Orange looks good on nails too.

The formula on both the polishes is great. Two coats are enough for perfect opaque polish. They dry quickly but dry matty-ish. So top coat is a must for me. I applied a base coat (OPI Base Coat), 2 coats of polish and a top coat (OPI Top Coat). They lasted more than a week on me which is rare :-).
summary: Essie DJ Play That Song and Saturday Disco Fever

reviewText: Love this fun color. I get tired of only pink and red shades. This was a great way to mix it up without the color being too young looking for this 30-something woman! :)
Just put this color on my hands and feet Luv it !!! I would recommend this color to all my friends

reviewText: What a fun and unique bright pink. This color is thinner then the darker Essie colors making it a lot smoother and easier to paint. It's not as neon as I thought it would be, however, it's still a bright and fun color. If you want true neon, I would recommend China Glaze Pink Voltage instead.

First off I love the color of this polish in the bottle.  However, as is noted it is translucent---so I bought the Essie Blanc--which is recommended as a first coat.  It still took about five coats for the polish to look ok---not fantastic just ok.  I am not expecting this manicure to last long as it required so many coats to look acceptable.  I will have to try it without the white undercoat maybe it will look ok but I doubt it.  I would not buy this color again.
The formula is a little thin, but its a beautiful color for summer. I use it over a white polish ( like I do with most ESSIE brights) and it looks beautiful.

This is actually my first time purchasing an Essie polish and I couldn't be happier with it! Great, non-streaky formula, applies evenly and gives your natural nails a perfect, even base color. Great for a basic french mani or layered under more bold colors to help them pop. The finish was nice and shiny even without a topcoat and I got about 8 days out of it with minor tip wear. Definitely a perfect sheer pink. Will absolutely be purchasing more polishes from Essie in the very near future!

L'Occitane is one of my wife's favorite skin care brands, and is always high quality, so I jumped at the chance to review this.  The first thing that I noticed is that one pump gets a LOT of foam... enough for a full face washing.  Even though this is a relatively small bottle, it is going to last a WHILE, so it's not as expensive as I initially thought.  It's still pricey though, however I think it's well worth it.

The scent is a very faint herbal scent that works well for either a man or a woman.  It cleaned my face very well without overdrying it.

Highly recommended.

For those of you who, like me, have sensitive skin, you may have a bit of a problem with this.  You see, it stings a bit when you use it.  The stinging sensation goes away when you massage it in, but it's a perceptible sting every time.

It seems to cleanse well.  The product is a soft, lightly scented foam and the scent did not get my allergies flaring.

However, I'm finding that I would prefer to use a product that cleans as well, but is better for sensitive skin.  If the sting was accompanied by some sort of amazing result, I would continue with it.  But for now, I'm going to return to a product that doesn't sting when I use it.

An effective cleanser for those who do not suffer from sensitive skin!

I wash my face every day, twice a day. Once in the morning and once at night. The three important things that any cleanser I use has to have is 1) to not irritate my skin 2) To get off my makeup easily and c) to not leave my skin dry.

L'Occitane Immortelle Precious Cleansing Foam does not irritate my skin, it has a flowery smell and it does go on gently and foamy. It does not leave my skin dry. It also does not clean off my make up. I always have to follow up with a different cleanser to get that done. I do not wear heavy makeup, I do not wear waterproof make up and it still does not clean my face enough. If I was to pay this much for a cleanser, it darn better clean at least a regular mascara off!! It would not even take off my lipstick!

I would never get this product again, it smells terrific but that is just not enough for incentive.
summary: Fancy name for a mediocre cleanser.

reviewText: Always a great face wash. My mom and I both use it and when we run out our skin starts breaking out. Definite NEED

I've been using this cleanser in the shower for the past few weeks.  Since I typically shower after exercise, I have to contend with sweat and oils, and this does a good job of removing both.  (It does not remove waterproof makeup, however.)  I find this to be a gentle cleanser and easy to rinse off (without leaving any residue).  Although it does have a slight (artificial) fragrance, the fragrance doesn't linger for too long.

Here are the ingredients since it is difficult to read them in the zoomed-in product image:

Water**, Disodium Laureth Sulfosuccinate**, Glycerin**, Disodium Cocoyl Glutamate**, Decyl Glucoside**, PEG-6 Caprylic/Capric Glycerides**, Cocamidopropyl Betaine**, Gentiana Lutea Root Extract**, Helichrysum Italicum Extract**, Anthemis Nobilis Flower Extract**, Citrus Unshiu Peel Extract**, Parsley Extract**, Strawberry Fruit Juice**, Grapefruit Fruit Extract**, Raspberry Fruit Extract**, Sodium Cocoyl Glutamate**, Butylene Glycol, Glyceryl Laurate**, Citric Acid**, Fragrance, Sodium Benzoate, Sodium Chloride**, Ethylhexylglycerin, PPG-26,Buteth-26, PEG-40 Hydrogenated Castor Oil**, Potassium Sorbate, Hexyl Cinnamal. (**Natural Origin Ingredients)

This is free of parabens and artificial dyes and it also doesn't contain any sulfates.  You still get a reasonable lather, and I'm sure the foaming pump is helping with that.  I like all the fruit extracts; those are going to contain antioxidants that should help a bit with free radical damage (but don't forget to use a good sunscreen, as well).

If you are looking for a cleanser that is gentle and sulfate free, this is definitely one to check out.  However, if you are going to be wanting to remove makeup with your cleanser, this is probably not for you.
summary: very gentle; does not remove waterproof makeup (but does get rid of sweat and oil)

reviewText:
Really nice product.  Pleasant, gentle foaming action and excellent-but-gentle cleansing.  Great for a quick clean before bed/makeup removal.  If price was lower I would highly recommend.  It seems to exfoliate and leave my skin surface very smooth. Current price point seems excessive for value/related to the L'Occitane brand name?

Initially I found this scent pleasant-- after some time I now find the scent almost moldy or mildew-ish/ an unpleasant smell.  I am not sure if this is due to deterioration of the product, or if I originally just talked myself into liking the scent because of my love of L'Occitane perfumes!!  Either way, the smell is likely to be unpleasant for some users, and it may be wise to use your bottle very quickly.
summary: Effective facial cleanser, icky scent (possibly deteriorated product?)

reviewText: The foam is wonderful and leaves face feeling fresh and clean. As usual with L'Occitane products, the smell is delicious.
summary: The foam is wonderful and leaves face feeling fresh and clean

reviewText: Gentle, cleans off makeup, doesn't seem to strip my skin, and smells nice.

I love this product.

Pros:
+ Does not irritate my sensitive skin (even when sunburnt).
+ Gently cleans oil and grime from my face yet it does not feel stripped of all moisture.
+ Foams just enough but not too much during actual face washing
+ The product rinses off cleanly and does not leave slimy residue
+ There is a scent but it is not overpowering or overly strong.
+ Foaming pump feels like I'm being more economical with the product
+ Refills are available for this product.
+ The bottle is refillable and reusable.
+ The foaming pump produces a consistent foam and does not squirt liquid near the end of each push like cheaper foam-pumps

Cons:
- A bit pricey but something I would splurge on.

Highly recommended.

I've been using this facial cleanser for several weeks now and am pleased with the results.  It has a light floral scent that dissapates almost immediately.  I've not had any breakouts or greasy spots or dry spots since I started using it.

At first, I was concerned that it would not get my face clean.  Like many new products, this is a diluted cleanser and comes out as a very light foam. It rinses away quickly and leaves your face clean but not feeling tight like other cleansers.  This took some getting used to for me.  There are times my face gets oily, especially in the summer or when I've used a lot of product in my hair and I really wasn't certain this watered down feeling foam would cut through the oil.  However, I was pleasently suprised at the clean fresh feeling on my face.
summary: Very light foam but it cleans

reviewText: Wow, a little golf ball size of foam really works on whole face and neck.  Really removes the oiliness and does not leave the face dry.  I love it.

I love this company's products.  I buy at least 15-20 different products a year, and I was excited to use this cleansing foam.
The smell is delicious!  I absolutely love using it, and actually looked forward to coming home from work and washing my face and neck.
Cleaning power is so-so.  To take off my mascara, I need to follow-up with make-up remover.  Of course, this product does not claim to remove make-up, so I did not remove any stars for it.
Price is high.  I understand it's L'Occitane, but $30 is very high, even for this company.  Bottle size is generous, but still, pricing needs to be in low $20's in my opinion for the value of the product.
summary: L'Occitane cleansing foam is oh so good!

reviewText:
I love and cherish my L'Occitane Shea Butter Hand Cream, so I just had to try this product out. First off, unfortunately this will not be something you can travel with easily; it is too large at 5.1 fl oz for flight travel, and the cap is not leak-proof.

The Review

First off, I have to say that I have weirdly sensitive skin. I can only wash my face once a day (at night), because if I wash twice a day, my skin gets super dry and really irritated. This happens no matter the cleanser I'm using. I did try to go to twice a day with this cleanser, and the same thing happened. The scent on this is so hard to define, it was lightly scented floral. Not overwhelming at all (I have a pretty sensitive nose).

Let's take a look at the claims on the packaging, which states that "effectiveness tested on 26 women over 4 weeks":

Skin is perfectly clean: 100%
Skin's balance is maintained: 100%
Skin seems smoother: 92%

Now never mind the extremely small test group, the first claim is kind of a given. Skin is clean? After using a cleansing foam? Say what?! Cheekiness aside, this product did clean my face fine, including days where I wore makeup and days where I didn't.

Next claim that the skin's balance is maintained. Well, as I said, I tried using this twice a day on my sensitive skin, and had irritation and dryness. But I realize that my skin is not like most people's skin! If I remember correctly, I had 2 "horns" (what I call huge pimple eruptions) during the 4 week use - but that is about par for me.

Last claim that skin seems smoother. I literally noticed no difference in the smoothness of my face.

After 4 weeks of once a day use (besides 5 days where I used it twice a day), the bottle is just under 1/2 gone.

The Verdict

For $28 for a 5.1fl oz bottle, I would not splurge on this product. Besides the fact that I think foaming washes are wasteful, before I was using this, I was using Simple Moisturizing Facial Wash, which is currently $5.97 on amazon for 5 fl oz. It works just as effectively as the L'Occitane, at less than 1/4 of the price. No, it doesn't have any scent, but I think I can deal.

If you're the type to splurge, have at this! If you're not, check out the Simple product line.
summary: Dubious claims for a high priced item; better inexpensive options on the market

reviewText:
I have used floral water in the past and never really cared for it. I just don't like cleaning my face with pure liquid. I do really enjoy this foam version of a floral water cleanser. The foam and the pump make this cleanser quick and easy to use. Like all foams, this cleanser washes off of your face relatively quickly. It leave my face feeling clean and slightly tight, but not dry.

I prefer to use a deep exfoliating cleanser for my bedtime cleansing ritual. However, I have been using this cleansing foam on my face in the morning in the shower and on "lazy" nights when I am too tired for a more in-depth facial cleansing. It makes me have clean skin before bed with little effort.

Maybe it is because I have used floral water before, but I don't mind the scent. It has the same flowery scent as the other floral waters I have used. The scent does linger a little on your skin after you use it (although not as strong). I have had my Husband tell me that I smell good after using it.

It does kind of annoy me that it says on the bottle that they tested it on 26 Women over 4 weeks. That's ridiculous. Anyone who has ever done any research, studies or surveys can tell you that a sample size of 26 is not enough to give you accurate results. I honestly hope that no one buys it based off of this "research". I have not noticed any long term effects.

I do like this and will continue to use it. However, I feel that the price is way too high. I know that rose water is expensive and L'Occitane is a French company and therefore expensive. Still, I would not buy it at the current price.
summary: I love this for a quick "lazy clean"

reviewText: The foam has a nice texture to it and does a very good job of cleaning. It is light and foamy and gives your skin a fresh feel. I don't consider this a makeup remover so don't have those expectations as some previous reviewers have noted. It's a bit expensive so is it that much better than a cleanser that is, say, half the price? Not really so it price is a concern I'd say go with the lower price. This has a bit of a fragrance which I could do without but as far as the cleansing aspect this does a fine job.

I love using this face wash. It feels so soft going on my skin. Foams up great - and the smell is wonderful! It is a truly luxurious experience.
I have sensitive skin and have not had any breakouts from using this product. I highly recommend this cleansing foam as a way to treat yourself to a refreshing way to finish a long day!

Love washing my face with this! This was my first experience with a cleansing foam and I love it!  So light and airy I was concerned it wasn't actually working.  So one night I used a cleansing cloth after rinsing off the foam and didn't find any residual grime or makeup.  The cleansing foam really works!  The only necessary follow-up is an eye make-up remover as this stuff stings if you get it near your eyes.

Yes this cleanser is expensive, but the bottle is translucent so I can see there is still lots left after weeks of use.  When this bottle eventually runs outs, I plan to purchase another.
summary: Look forward to washing my face each night!

reviewText: I wish I could give it more stars. This cleansing foam feels so good. I have sensitive skin and photosensitivity, and this time of the year with sun issues, many products can irritate my face. This cleanser does not. It feels so nice, each night, gently washing with this. There is just a light scent, which is very nice, clean, and not long-lasting. My face feels great afterwards. No stiffness or drying. Just soft, clean, and natural. I highly recommend this.

I am a fan of several L'Occitane products, but this is not my favorite. Two years ago I had extremely bad eczema (from allergies) surrounding my eyes. I eliminated everything and used physician-recommended remedies, but the troubling eczema persisted until I used L'Occitane Immortelle Eye Cream, which cleared the eczema completely in less than 10 days. I tell this story to show that there really seems to be healing power in the Immortelle flower extract that makes up this portion of the company's line. At that time, and since then, I have tried many L'Occitane products, with varying results. I had tried this face cleanser in a small trial size and was somewhat underwhelmed. It is "weak" as a makeup remover. It is incapable of removing the Clinique eye makeup I wear daily (not waterproof!), so I always have to follow it with my usual face wash, which removes the mascara and eyeliner very easily and completely. I would not willingly use two products - seems like a waste. It never harmed my sensitive skin, but never seemed to help either, and it leaves my facial skin very tight, which my usual cleanser does not. I have placed this 5 ounce bottle in my shower, which seems more appropriate of a use to me, since I shower in the morning when my face is makeup-free. I will not be replacing this cleanser; at this price, it should have some distinct advantages, which it does not - not for me at least. And one final comment on the smell that some are saying is chemical: I think that you are smelling the Immortelle flower extract, which L'Occitane does not try to mask. All the Immortelle products have this smell, for obvious reasons.
summary: Immortelle has advantages, but cleanser is weak

reviewText:
I have been using the products from this brand for some time, and I have used the  eye cream in the past with great results. What I love about this cleansing foam is that the pump dispenser dispenses easily, it dispenses the exact amount that I need to wash my face and no more and no less, it dispenses the liquid in a foam so it rinses easily away and cleanses evenly without getting too much or too little on some places of my face, and it is a highly effective cleanser that strikes just the right balance between cleansing and moisturizing.

I usually use the lush brand of facial cleansers, but I find them a little difficult to use because you need to take a pea sized bit out of the tub, mix it with water, and then spread over your face and hope that you don't get a clump stuck near your hairline or on a dry part of your cheek.

While I have tried other brands of facial cleanser in the past, I have found that most cleansers strip my skin and leave it feeling itchy, or worse, leave a residue that makes me break out. I was surprised to find that this cleansing foam was 100% on par with the quality and results I usually get from using the lush brand, yet it was so much more pleasant and easy to use.

I would definitely recommend this cleansing foam, and now that I have tried it, I foresee myself using it regularly and purchasing it once this testing sample runs out.

I've used a lot of facial cleansers and this one is definitely the lightest I've ever used.  It goes on almost as a misty foam and I could barely feel it on my skin. Yet when finished, it definitely cleansed and removed makeup, etc. I'm a bit more used to thicker gels with microcleansers so this was quite a change.

Interestingly for me, the packaging with the fancy gold label and French name made this appear to be more like a high end perfume - it almost felt gimmicky. So I had to really convince myself that this was actually cleaning. But the end result was that my skin didn't feel like it had heavy cleaners on it and it felt a lot less 'stiff' (I didn't feel the need to run for the moisturizer after the shower).

The Precious Cleansing Foam by L'Occitane is a wonderful face wash.  I've always been skeptical with trying new facial products as I've dealt with acne even as as adult.  This was a very gentle face wash.  The foam is very light and airy.  It is gentle yet removes all makeup from the face.  It is leaves the skin feeling refreshed and super clean without any residue from the wash.  It also has a very pleasant "nature" fragrance which is not too overpowering yet you can subtly notice it.  Very refreshing and leaves skin feeling super clean, yet it is gentle enough to use daily!  Great product!

This hydrating foundation product from La Roche-Posay is as high-quality as their brand would lead you to expect, and while it's expensive it might be worth the price. It feels creamy but not greasy and applies easily  and a little goes a long way. Nice consistent shade and a long life once applied, with no heavy feel on the skin, make it a good choice, even despite the pricing.

I love Roche-Posay products. This new foundation is great. Easy to apply, blends in easily, non-greasy. My skin looked moist (not matted) and overall happy with the product. I am disappointed in the color however, seemed a little darker than what I normally would wear (despite the color showing in the ad). Please keep that in mind when ordering this. I really don't think I can use it anymore because of the color.
summary: Nice product, wrong color for my skin (too dark)

reviewText:
My wife doesn't usually wear foundation as we live in the humid south. However, the La Roche-Posay Toleriane Teint Hydrating Liquid Foundation goes on light and feels soothing and cooling to the skin. This is not a heavy foundation, but a light cover up that helps even out skin tones. My wife loves how natural it looks and feels.

A small amount blends nicely without feeling as though it's clogging up pores and it stands up to warmer sub-tropic temps and humidity without melting off her face. She primarily uses it as a spot foundation especially on dry patches. The foundation feels nourishing and does not irritate her skin. Overall, this is a quality foundation that feels good and stands up to Florida conditions.

~ Kort
summary: Light Foundation That Evens Out Skin Tones

reviewText: The La Roche-Posay teint hydrating liquid did not irritate my skin and was easy to blend.  It blended with brush, beauty blender, and fingers easily.  I liked the smooth feel of the foundation on my face during application.  I found that it did not really feel dry after application and felt like I had a heavy moisturizer on my face that did not absorb well.  To counter this feeling I applied powder and found that I had to do that in order to feel comfortable and also to keep the foundation from creasing in my nose and from separating on my face.  I prefer liquid foundation to include an SPF even though I wear an SPF under a foundation.  I liked that after blending that my skin looked sun-kissed.  I felt that this was more like a tan colored foundation the medium beige.  I needed a lot of this foundation in order to blend it properly.  I would order a lighter color even for summer.
summary: ... hydrating liquid did not irritate my skin and was easy to blend

reviewText: This product was hard to review because of the color.  It wasn't so much that it was too dark for my tone, but very orange.  I'm not sure what type of skin you would have to be able to use this.  The formula felt nice, but it was just too orange for my skin.

As other reviewers are saying the Honey Beige shade is darker and more reddish than shown on the Amazon page. Used very sparingly, my girlfriend is able to blend this so it didn't look quite so dark on her skin. She likes that it's fragrance-free and didn't cause any irritation. Because she had to use so little, coverage wasn't that great but it still looked pretty good. It's expensive, so not really sure if we'll be buying this again. If we do it will be in a much lighter shade. We recommend you evaluate these in person to get the right shade for your skin.

**** 4 STARS - CONDITIONAL RECOMMENDATION ****

My wife thinks that this an ok product but not good enough to replace the product that she has been using for years. She will finish the tube and if her opinion changes by then I will update this review

I was worried when I received the bottle that the color would be too dark - based on the outside of the bottle.  But once applied, it went on nicely and the tone was right for my skin (no watermark line at the chin).  A little goes a long way and it didn't feel oily or thick once applied.  I typically use loose powder with my foundation and the powder adhered nicely to it, giving that matte finish I seek.  Of note is that it was very yellow on my skin - not a golden yellow but a sallow yellow.  I had to add powder to knock back the yellow.

This foundation is suitable for normal, sensitive as well as dry skin types.
It matches my skin tone and suits me well.
Instructions say to apply foundation with fingertips in a circular motion from the center of face outward.
It provides good coverage. The skin feels smooth and creamy after application.
This liquid foundation hydrates the skin.
It did not create any reaction to my sensitive skin after applying.

I definitely agree with the other reviews; get a shade or two lighter than you think you need. The color is significantly darker than it appears online.

However the formula itself is a dream. When a face makeup categorizes itself as being for normal to dry I usually find it to be too oily for my combination skin. Not so with Toleriane Teint! Its the perfect glow without being greasy. I love it for those days when you want a no-makeup, makeup look. I loved the sheer coverage and it didn't make my somewhat sensitive skin breakout.
summary: Gives a beautiful glow- but buy lighter than you think you need!

reviewText:
The Honey Beige is a bit too dark for my skin, but in the summer it's not as noticeable. I will not downgrade this product because of that. The liquid comes out evenly and applies easily, evening out my skin's tone.  It's non irritating and non-fragranced.  This product reminds me of DermaBlend and how it reacts to my skin.

The skin looks fresh for several hours after application when indoors.

So when this arrived I thought "OH NO! there is no way this will match my skin" because the bottle was much lighter and more pink.  However the product inside doesn't look anything like the color of the bottle.  So you really need to sample this before buying.

I was super lucky in that this actually DID match my skin.  I have been using it for about a month now and I really like it.  I normally wear a Lancome liquid foundation and I have found that this one is a bit thicker and seems to stay on a bit longer.

My only other qualm with this makeup is that the way the bottle is designed - a tiny squeeze and you have enough foundation for 3 days.  I wish they would rethink the bottle a bit.  I do like that it's a squeeze bottle, however I wish the opening were a bit smaller so that I could get the exact amount I want out of it.

I would purchase this again.
summary: Color inside doesn't match the bottle - but it's a good makeup

reviewText:
This La Roche-Posay Toleriane Teint in "Golden Beige" is darker in tint than I expected.  It dispenses and applies easily, but there's a strong alcohol smell and it feels tight and drying if you have dry skin.  It's definitely not hydrating as advertised and like other reviewers have mentioned, it feels chalky.  The primary ingredient, after water, is silcone (dimethicone), which I don't think is ideal since it can feel heavy.  Also, there's no SPF.

I found the coverage kinda of grainy, too.  I like that this is made in France, but I don't see any other reason to get this when there are other mid-market and drugstore options that are better.
summary: drying on skin and alcohol-like smell

reviewText: I love this easy to apply formula that is very buildable.  It is more moisturizing that a lot of brands, so if you have dry, easily irritated skin like me, you are going to love this foundation. I have found that I don't need additional creams while using this.  I use a sunscreen and then a light primer with silicone and this just glides on.  It does not transfer easily nor does it wear weird.  It does not fall into your creases but seems to float on top.  Yes, it is a bit pricier than a lot of foundations but a little goes a long way and a tube can last me 2-3 months easily.

Product would be best for those with white skin and peach undertones.
Light beige is more muddy looking than the picture suggests.
I honestly would not recommend this brand for persons of color. If that is not you, it is a five star product.

I have dry skin, so my biggest anticipation with this foundation was its claim of hydration. I applied it without my usual facial lotion, and my skin never felt tight as often happens without lotion, and it remained smooth all day, so that right there is a win for me.

The shade is much lighter than what Ive been wearing lately, but once blended in it looks very natural, covers well, and even hides some of my darker and redder spots better than my darker powder foundations have been. I was also able to actually see my blush better without having to apply multiple layers. It seems to remove easily with makeup remover or a good old face wash, but doesnt smear on cloth or people.

Not sure how long this small and definitely premium-cost container will last, especially as I haven't yet gotten the hang of squirting just enough so Im probably using more foundation than needed. And then theres excess creeping out, but that may be worth it to some people. All in all, I thought this was a good, premium foundation.

I do like this product and it goes on easily, but be careful to putting too much on at once. At least for me, it didn't blend well, but I've got terribly dry skin at times and I need some moisture down on the skin before attempting to apply any makeup at all. That said, this applies beautifully to say my hand or lower arm that isn't quite as dry.
summary: A little dab will do it.

reviewText: I have used a couple of La Roche-Posay products and everytime I am impressed by the quality. This Hydrating Watercream Foundation with Hyaluronic Acid for Normal to Dry Skin really does even out and illuminates my skin. It provides hydration without making my skin feel too heavy. It went on easily and stayed put all day. Happy to have found another great make up brand and product.
summary: It went on easily and stayed put all day

reviewText:
I ordered this thinking it was going to be a good match to my complexion.  I have warmer skin with yellow tones and I have used Loreals honey beige true match foundation, which matches really well.  This honey beige is really dark and more peachy than honey. It did not match well with my complexion at all.

It was also rather thin and did not cover very well. I couldn't really use it to see how long it lasted because my face looked horrendous with on (as it was too dark) so I cant comment on its staying power.  A plus was that it was fragrance free, as promised.
summary: Honey Beige - Darker than I expected

reviewText:
Medium coverage formula. Made for sensitive, intolerant, allergy-prone skin. One ounce lasts a really long time. I have gotten away from brushless direct application foundation and enjoyed using this product at home. Instructions are to use after applying a facial moisturizer, SPF, and concealer, while i use the foundation then the concealer.

l'oral-answers/the-question-of-animal-testing: La Roche-Posay/L'Oral themselves do not test on animals anywhere in the world, nor does it delegate the task to others.  L'Oreal does sell  products to China, which may or may not test any given product on animals.
summary: Ivory Color Foundation with Hyaluronic Acid for Normal to Dry Skin, 1 Fl. Oz.by La Roche-Posay Toleriane Teint

reviewText: My wife thinks the foundation is pretty nice, but the honey beige was too dark. She thought that honey would be a lighter beige but actually it's darker than beige and almost a light brown. It does seem to cover and lay well on the face, but since the color was wrong she didn't do more than try it.
summary: Honey beige is darker than we thought

reviewText: I received the "Golden Beige" color. This is darker than my normal skin tone, so it makes me look like I've gotten a slight tan. The foundation is fairly thick but goes on smoothly. The opening is on the bottom, so it comes out easily, though you may end up using more than necessary. I'm not crazy about it but it doesn't irritate my skin. I plan to mix it with a lighter shade so that it approximates my skin tone more.
The color is nice but not crazy about this
summary: The color is nice but not crazy about this

reviewerName: Gina Pera, Adult ADHD Expert and Author
reviewText:
If you have relatively flawless skin and seek mild cover without SPF protection, this product might be for you.  It goes on easily, has no detectable fragrance, and doesn't seem to pool in wrinkles.

For me, with my "aging" and "somewhat blotchy" skin, it did very little.

This Toleriane Teint Hydrating watercream foundation by La Roche-Posay was a disappointment.  The honey beige color is very very dark.  I was expecting something much lighter.  I would call it closer to brown than beige.  It's much too dark for my coloring.  The foundation is easy enough to apply and goes on smoothly but it has a slight chemical smell that I found very off putting - sort of like a burning plastic odor.  My advice is to find somewhere you can test the colors in person against your skin tone before purchasing otherwise you may be disappointed with your choice.
summary: honey beige is very dark and it has a funny chemical smell.
