reviewText:
First off, I love the color.  I don't have anything like this and I used it immediately upon receiving it (it was June's High Shine Club selection for me).

I did have to use 3-4 coats to really get it to be opaque, but light colors are often like that for me.  I think I am going to try it in the future over an opaque white polish; it should look great that way.  It was a good texture when wet (not too thin or too thick) and was easy to apply and I like the brush.  The finish on my nails is super smooth.

However, I did get chips on a couple of fingernails within 24 hours.  I had tried to be careful, and my nails aren't that long, so this was a little disappointing.  I touched up with new polish in the chipped areas and it's hard to tell I did any touch up unless you get really close.  So, I think my manicure will still last for a few days, though I expect to have to do more touch-ups now.  (I did peel a whole bunch of oranges and the polish didn't get messed up, so that was nice.)

I used a Seche Vite quick-dry topcoat with this.  I do have an Essie topcoat and I may try that next time to see if staying within one brand results in increased performance.  Overall, however, I'm pretty happy with this.
I was looking a finish like this for a long time. It's just what I want!!! Little bit pink and transparent.

I actually came across this sort of accidentally. See, I was removing some dark red nail polish from my fingernails, and it left behind this really awesome pinkish hue. No, I did not use a base coat, and yes, I do realize the pinkish hue was a stain. But this got me thinking...I would pay for this look. I had no idea if I could replicate it, and it was a little uneven so I thought, "Wouldn't it be great if there was a nail polish that could give me the same effect?!" Turns out, there is. It's Essie's Pink Glove Service. I ordered it a couple days ago, received it today, and put it on. My nails are adorable. They look so natural and feminine! I would recommend this to anyone looking for a classic, elegant look for their natural nails. :)
summary: Love it, love it, and love it.

I have it on my toes now and receive tons of compliments.

Usually, my nail polish chips in 1 day... this one is long lasting, but I find that I need to shake it often (almost between each nail) or it gets clumpy, and then it dries with a dull finish.  Nothing that a little attention to detail and a clear coat can't fix.  I'm really impressed with the long lasting wear which is what bumped it up from a 3 to a 4.

reviewText: As usual Essie has another hit!  Great color for a mani/pedi for summer.  Looks great on most skin tones  Shipped quickly too.

I tried in sun/shade/indoors/lights.. but didn't work. The color is really pretty to naked eye.

Saturday Disco Fever is a bright pure orange color. This is not a very blazing neon, so I am able to wear it to work. It looks fabulous in sunlight as well as indoors. I felt that this color is more suitable for evenings and parties in Summer. I was a little apprehensive at first because I personally don't like Yellow/Orange shades. But this color worked for me. It is more red-toned than yellow-toned. This dark Orange looks good on nails too.

The formula on both the polishes is great. Two coats are enough for perfect opaque polish. They dry quickly but dry matty-ish. So top coat is a must for me. I applied a base coat (OPI Base Coat), 2 coats of polish and a top coat (OPI Top Coat). They lasted more than a week on me which is rare :-).

This serum has a nice feel to it.  It isn't runny which I like, to me it is more like a cream.  The scent isn't overpowering either.  I will update in a couple of months on how it does for my skin, so far I like the results of it and have been using it for a couple of weeks.

I have been using this product faithfully twice a day for a few weeks. My skin quality has improved greatly. My forehead looked almost scaly after I applied foundation but after using this product it has smoothed out noticeably.  Fine lines and brightness is also improved. The product goes on smoothly and does not leave an oily or heavy feel. I use this on clean skin and follow it with sunscreen and moisturizer in the morning, I then apply foundation. This serum is a sheer layer and does not leave skin feeling greasy. At night I again apply the serum and follow it with an oil in dry areas and a night time moisturizer. I have had no breakouts or reactions since beginning to use this product. Even though I am well beyond the age of acne I get an occasional breakout but not since using this serum.

I've had good results with this product line. However, this serum is not working for me...yet. I like the unscented serum. I applied a few drops on my face where saggy jowls are starting to appear. This product is supposed to give back bounce for your skin. I've been trying it off and on, I can't tell any difference. I'll update if there are any changes in my results.

Pros: - the texture is silky, and it goes on smoothly and easily while not feeling "wet" or gross - while not its intended purpose, it feels very moisturizing - I've been using it about a month, once a day, and am only about a quarter of the way through the bottle. It's long-lasting - La Roche-Posay as a brand has been recommended by my derm and their products tend to work really well; I think this is no exception - my skin feels soft and comfortable after using it, even when my skin felt extremely dry prior to applying the serum Cons: - I just don't care for the fragrance. It's mostly a "clean" smell but also slightly... medicinal? It's not strong enough that I'd stop using the serum, but I also question why serum needs any fragrance added in the first place when everyone's moisturizers already have fragrance added. For the sake of completion, my daily routine for the past month has been: Simple Refreshing Facial Wash Gel,Elizavecca Hell Pore Clean Up AHA Fruit Toner, this serum, Guerisson 9 Complex Cream, and finally Etude House Sunprise Mild Watery Light Sunscreen This routine has been working really well for me even though the weather has been cold and dry. Certainly I think this serum helps my skin feel soft and balanced despite the weather.

Long before they were available in the United States, I would stock up on LaRoche Posey on every visit to France, and beg anyone coming from Europe to bring items on my shopping list.
Now that they are readily available here, I'm happy that the formulations are just as effective as the European ones.
This is a wonderful serum. It lays the foundation for the rest of your skin care, and I use it with and without a moisturizer over it. It's that good. I'm in my late 50s, and the little criss cross lines under my eyes are softened.
summary: Helps Other Facial Products Work Better

reviewText:
I really love how this makes my facial skin feel.  The serum is silky and feels wonderful when I put it on.

The problem I have is that the scent is extremely strong.  It's very perfumy and it makes me uncomfortable to have it on my face.  The scent lasts and lasts, too.  It doesn't go away.  I've tried putting the serum on and waiting and waiting for the scent to dissipate, but it doesn't.  I have to wash it off.  Too bad it's so highly scented because it really does make my face feel wonderful.

This is a moderate portion of skin serum designed to have anti-aging attributes. Since I am 52, I assume I am in a target demographic for it. My skin is normal to dry, very fair, suffers from some sagging, thinning, and fine lines especially around the eyes. I can't speak to how it will work for those who have a skin type which differs from mine.

In terms of effects, I've been using this after showering in the evening as well as in the morning. It does  appear to help lesson fine lines/wrinkles to some extent by plumping the skin around the area. It leaves skin soft, smooth, and somewhat silky to the touch. It does not help with deeper lines or wrinkles such as creasing on the sides of the mouth or with larger forehead wrinkles (though it does lesson them to some extent, especially within a half hour or so of application). It's a good moisturizer/serum, but it's not a miracle worker.

The cream comes in a pump which offers conservative amounts with each push. This is a good point as one pump is enough for your face and a second for your neck. I assume this will last for quite some time at the rate I'm using it. That being said, the price is on the high side and I'm not sure if the effects are actually worth it. My main feeling about this was that, while it's a solid performer, there are similar products which do the same thing at a lower price point. Also, I found that it didn't do much for areas which have very thin skin and seemed to make the darkness under my eyes more noticeable (perhaps by contrast?). It seems to work more on underlying tissues than on the upper layer of skin which would explain why it does less for the very thin skin under my eyes.

This is a white cream with a slightly medicinal scent, but it is not overbearing in any way and does not linger. It absorbs quickly into the skin and does not leave it greasy in feel nor does it transfer any residue to your glasses. My skin isn't especially sensitive, but I will say that I didn't have any sort of negative reaction to it.

I've only used this for about a month so I can't speak to how it'd work with longer term use. However, if I experience appreciably better results over time (as I go through the remainder of the bottle), I will update this review.
summary: leaves skin with a silky feel and eliminates fine lines

reviewText: I love La Roche Posay as a brand. I think their products are top-notch!  That being said, I'm not really sure what to make of this product. Since I use prescription Retin-A on my face, I decided to use this serum on my neck. It feels nice going on, absorbs quickly, doesn't leave me oily, or produce any irritation. I think it's nice as a moisturizer, but I don't see much in the way of firming or other visible changes.

Great slightly medicine-y smelling product.  Goes on smooth like a gel, and isn't sticky, but definitely hydrating and smoothing at the same time.  Makes the fine lines on your face soften and also makes everything feel smoother in general.  A little goes a long way as well and definitely makes your face feel firm but soft.  I really enjoy it except for the smell.

I've only been using this for a couple of weeks, so will update my review as I use this more since skincare products generally take awhile to show any difference.  In the short time I've been using it, though, I've come to really like it.

Since it's a serum, it feels light going on, but also hydrates surprisingly well.  It sinks in after just about a minute, so you can add any other products on top of it after that.

I wish that this had more anti-aging ingredients in it and haven't noticed any plumping effect, but it works well as a moisturizer in the dry winter weather.

Also, Paula Begoun (whose ratings I usually check when considering purchasing any new skincare items) notes on her website that the
Substiane line products all contain "something called Pro-xylane,a made-up term representing a group of ingredients in the formula. This patented trade name was coined by L'Oreal, who happens to own La Roche-Posay. You would think that if this blend of ingredients was so special, then other L'Oreal-owned companies would use it, too, but they don't. This ends up being a good emollient base, but there is no research showing it has special benefit for skin. It certainly isn't a must-have."

Based on that information, I will continue to use this as a moisturizer, but will continue to use my regular antioxidants, too.
summary: Works well to hydrate the skin

reviewText:
La Roche Posay is noted for their quality skin products. Substiane Visible Density and Volume is designed to help restore skin's elasticity, bounce and sagginess. As skin ages it becomes thinner. This product claims to plump up the volume and restore a more youthful feel. The product contains two ingredients that work together; Pro-Xylane for density and LR2412 which bolsters the Pro-Xylane.

Though this product can be used alone, mature skin will likely want to use it in tandem with other anti-aging products. Personally I wish they would have combined this with an anti-wrinkle product to keep things simple. But they didn't.

You only need a small amount of this - a dab according to their website, to smooth over the skin. I like the hygienic bottle. The product has a slight plastic smell to me but it's very faint. It feels good going on and my skin appears slightly smoother on application. I will see how the results are over time.

Another home run from La Roche-Posay. After using this for almost a month, I can testify to the amazing effect it has had on my skin. I have found the small lines around my eyes have all but disappeared and my 60 year old skin is plumper and fuller and way softer to the touch. I do think $65 is a high price for a small amount of serum which is not coming directly from a physician's prescription. But, after having used this now for a while I think it is an amazing serum and a must have for anyone's aging skin. Skip the doctor's office and spas and try this first. You will be amazed at the results.
summary: Pricey but well worth it. Skip the spas and do it yourself at home

reviewText: I've hit that age when my skin is starting to lose elasticity and I'm getting some lines around my eyes and on my neck that just won't go away (yeah, this happens. I know. But I'm going to fight it!). This came recommended to me by a skin aesthetician friend and I really like it. Have used it for a couple of weeks and feel like it's doing some good for my skin. If nothing else, my skin feels smooth and isn't irritated by it (I have sensitive skin).

In spite of the fact that I am several decades beyond adolescence, moisturizers have always clogged my pores and made my skin break out--even though my skin is dry now and could use a little moistening help. This is the first moisturizing product I've tried that doesn't make my skin break out, and it leaves my face feeling pleasantly "moist" (or not its usual dry) all day. I'm not a good judge of how different my skin looks, but I'm sold on the product because of how wonderful it makes my skin feel. Also--when I have tried products called serums before they've been sticky and didn't absorb well. Not so with this one. It's creamy, sinks right into my skin and is pleasantly almost without a scent.

If your skin is dry and prone to fine wrinkles, this may work for you. My skin, even in middle age, is oily and more prone to creases. This type of serum doesn't really work for me. It feels a bit too thick for daytime wear. I think it gave me a zit, besides, although hard to say for sure. Of course, not every product is for every skin type. Just my opinion.

This really has a nice feel to it. It says you can wear it alone or under moisturizer. I have done both, or worn it under sunscreen. I am not too fond of the scent, but it is not strong and almost immediately I stop noticing it.

My skin is very sensitive and it turns red at the least provocation. This has not caused any reaction at all. I am not doing a clinical study, so I don't know if its claims of adding volume are legitimate, but I do like the way my face feels after using this. I will but more once I finish this bottle.

UPDATE: It took me three months of once or twice-a-day to finish the bottle. I like it enough that I am buying more.

La Roche has several lines of skin care products.  Which one you choose depends on what you want to do.  I have tried several of their products, and have liked every one of them.  I wish this was not $65 as I would love to get more Substaine Visible Density and Volume in the future.  It really works!  This product is designed to fight sagging. They recommend using morning and night, but I am using it once a day to make it last longer.  It still made a difference in my skin in a week. One pump is enough to cover my neck and face. It made the most difference in my neck under my chin.  I was also told over the holidays that there is a "glow" to my skin by people that had not seen me in a while.  This may be due the combination of products I am currently using, and not just this one, but it is at least helping the situation with visible results.  I definitely recommend and will be buying more as my budget allows.
summary: Another winning product from la Roche Posay

reviewText: This Substiane is now my go-to day and night cream for right after washing. I find it works best for me when my face is still just slightly damp, and one pump will provide full coverage all over my face, including over my eyes, with the extra bit of moisture from post-wash (feels like it holds in/ seals in the water on my face). This Substiane cream is very impressive. I'm usually not one to buy expensive cosmetics, and just tend to use simple, neutral lotions because I have very sensitive skin. This Substiane has caused me zero reaction, and even though it has a very light (pleasant) fragrance, it dissipates fairly rapidly, so that I'm not having to smell it for hours. The moisturizing effect is instantaneous, but lasts me pretty much all day, and even my typically driest areas around my mouth, under eyes and in the middle of my forehead seem continually soft and hydrated. Considering how well/ long this moisturizes, I had none of the expected feeling of heaviness or greasy residue when I initially applied this either- it just vanished into my skin as my face fully dried from my wash, and just felt like fresh skin- no tautness, no plastic-y barbie face feeling. This is one of the best, if not the best facial cream I have ever used.
summary: Non-irritating and Fresh Feeling, Moisturizes All Day. May Be the Best Face Cream I've Ever Used

reviewText: I like that this serum really tightens the skin on my face. You don't need a lot to see results right away. This serum has no fragrance, so it won't interfere with perfume or anything else. I have sensitive skin, and would normally break out if I put anything on my face, but this didn't make me break out at all. I love this serum, but I wish it came in a bigger bottle. Although you don't need a lot, it is still something you would need to replace once it runs out.

I wasn't totally clear on exactly what this product was supposed to do.  The wording on the bottle is rather cryptic, replenishing corrective intensive.

Once I tried this product, it became clearer what it was supposed to do.  My face looked plumper, for lack of a better word.  Normally the word plump is not associated with a positive thing.  As I have gotten older, my face has become a bit more gaunt.  I think that is a natural outcome of aging.  This product seemed make my face fuller so my face looked younger.

I also liked the fact that this product had no scent.

It is easy to use, all you need to do is to apply it day and night, before you put on moisturized.

If you are looking for something to make your face look better, you may just like this product.

La-Roche Posay Substiane Serum feels good on my face and neck. I'm in my 50's and have sensitive skin that gets really dry. I use one or two pre measured pumps of Substiane Serum on my face and neck (avoiding my eye area) and apply my regular face cream over this serum a couple minutes later- which leaves my skin feeling nice and comfortable all day (or night). This serum has a richness I enjoy as it feels soothing to my dry skin, yet it doesn't feel greasy or sticky to me. It smooths and hydrates my skin and seems to make some fine lines appear a bit less noticeable. This serum has a firming feel I look for in products as my skin has lost elasticity with age. Substiane Serum is a white, creamy serum that's rich and thick, but applies smoothly and my skin absorbs it well. I like that this serum has no parabens (a controversial preservative). It does have noticeable fragrance, though it dissipates quickly and doesn't aggravate my allergies or irritate my skin. Overall, I really like  Substiane Serum as it has a rich texture that feels hydrating, firming and soothing to my sensitive dry skin.
summary: Rich But Non Greasy Serum That Does A Nice Job Making My Sensitive Dry Skin Feel Smoother, Firmer And More Hydrated

reviewText:
I used this cream just once so far, it is very light and creamy.  I felt my skin tighten after application, and little goes a long way.  The cream has no fragrance.  My face feels soft 6 hours later and I was out in the wind walking my dogs.
I will update within a week.
summary: Very light and creamy, there is no fragrance, and my soft feels soft 6 hours later even after being out in the wind...love that.

reviewText:
I've been a long time fan of Agave Healing Oil (I love using it on my hair after I've done a weekly deep conditioning mask to further lock in moisture and add shine), but I've never tried any of their other hair care products so I was excited to try the shampoo and conditioner because I have another tried and true line (Davines Oi) I use regularly because it just works for my thick, coarse, wavy, color treated hair  This set is especially great because specialty hair care products can be expensive and it sucks to buy full-sized shampoo and conditioner only to determine you don't like the results, scent or something else.  The shampoo and conditioner are essentially travel-size (though on the larger side of travel size), while the Healing Oil is the smaller of their two full-size offerings.

Trying this shampoo and conditioner I really like them.  The shampoo does a good job of removing the styling products I use in my hair, without stripping my hair of moisture and making it feel like straw.  The conditioner also does a good job of putting moisture into hair without weighing it down or over-conditioning.  The scent is also soft and pleasant without being overpowering.  I still think the Davines Oi line gets my hair a tad softer and makes it feel a bit healthier, but this is still a really great choice.  I could see it being perfect for someone who has hair that is not as dry or color treated as mine.  I could also see this being a really nice gift for someone who likes nice hair care products.

Would recommend.
summary: Nice set to see if Agave's products are for you

reviewText: I got these, and carted them off to the gym to try them post-workout.  They were certainly good enough; my hair is definitely shinier.  But, because it takes a lot of product to shampoo and condition thicker hair, the trial sizes won't go far.  I won't be able to eke more than a second shampoo and conditioner application out of them.  I've found that I generally need more than that to do a sound assessment of shampoo:  allergies and sensitivities often don't show up--or recede--until I have used the product for more than ten days.  That's obviously not an option here.  Would I go out and buy the full-sized products just to be able to test the shampoo (etc) adequately?  Maybe, when the product is inexpensive.  This isn't.
summary: Good enough: my hair IS shinier. But: Those with thick hair probably won't get more than 2 shampoos from trial size product.

reviewText:
The word "moisturizer" seems a bit misleading here. While I absolutely love Juice Beauty (I use their face-wash, eye creme, moisturizer, everything!), this is a rare miss (for me). It is WAY too thick and awkward. I am hyper-vigilant about applying sunscreen before a run or a bike-ride. I've used more brands than I can even catalog. Nonetheless, this would come somewhere around the lower-middle of the list for its messiness, difficulty of application, and odor. Likewise, the bottle is pretty small. So, if you are like me and apply this to your arms, legs, and face, you may find yourself being a little disappointed at how quickly the tube "disappears."

The organic/natural angle had me hopeful. We have been very focused on organic/natural health and beauty products for the last two years. But, this one did not quite make the grade.

Still a Juice Beauty fan though!

The best part about this product is that you don't have to worry about it for a long length of time-it lasts for around 80 minutes per application. I was hoping it would have a more lotion like feel to it but it was rather harsh. My wife and I did not care for the smell of it-which is a big issue for me because that is the first thing I test with any of these new products is the smell-the stronger the smell the better that I like it. Also the price was high for the amount that you were given.

Not a terrible product but nothing to write home about.
summary: Did not care for the smell...

reviewText:
There are some ups and downs with this product but ultimately it's not a Sunscreen that I would buy.

PLUSES
 Organic, which I love
 Lasts 80 minutes
 Is water resistant!

SUMMARY
Despite the fact that it's winter there are days, especially at higher elevations, where there is bright sun.  I really wanted this to be a sunscreen that my family could use that would prevent sun burn, and which would reduce wind burn.

What I found was a not-so liquid product that felt heavy, like zinc sunblocks, but which didn't sooth or go on easily.  It felt like it was abrading my skin.

After I put it on my skin felt raw. I don't know if it's a reaction to one of the ingredients --I have quite a few allergies and super sensitive skin-- or a reaction to the non-flowing, non-liquid and slightly gritty nature of it.

If you have younger, less delicate skin it might be worth a try, but I don't recommend it to older gals or those which super sensitive skin.

As background, I am a fair skinned middle aged woman.  I always use sunscreen on my face and neck; and during the summer I also use it on my arms, hands and legs. Whenever I see my dermatologist, he says how "youthful" the skin on my face looks, which is nice, but all I can think is that if anyone wants to know how old I am, all they have to do is look at my hands.  Keeping sunscreen on your hands year round can help prevent those nasty age spots and discoloration -- if only I had known.  This Juice Beauty SPF 30 Sport Moisturizer will do the job for you.  I liked the fact that it was thick, but was less thrilled that it felt dry going on.  The active ingredient in this sunscreen is zinc oxide, which is a great sunblock, but also explained the dry feeling.  I feel that it has good staying power and won't wear off too quickly, but if you are looking for a moisturizing sunscreen, this isn't for you.
summary: Good coverage, long wearing, dry feel

reviewText:
It's nice to have a moisturizing lotion that can be used by both my husband and me. It felt a little thick going on but it absorbed well. The scent is very light and is gender neutral. It didn't have that chemical smell that most other sunblocks have and it did not irritate my eyes as others have done. Neither of us had any sunburn during the time we spent getting our vegetable garden winterized, which was a good 60 minutes or more in the sun.

It does its job well and I would consider getting it again for limited time use in the sun.
summary: Sunblock worked well without causing irritation to my eyes

reviewText:
This mineral sunscreen works really well. It's creamy, thick and has a pleasant citric scent that dissipates quickly. The natural, 20% zinc oxide formula is gentle on sensitive skin and suitable for the whole family. It appears to work better than other natural sunscreen that I have tried in terms of performance and consistency. It is also water resistant.

This sunscreen is tinted in light beige and could possibly stain light color clothing during application. It has good moisturizing effect since it keeps my skin from drying out. All in all, it works very well as a moisturizing sunscreen. It is a little pricey but the natural formula is gentle on the skin and yet effective as a sunscreen.

Rubs in easily and provides safe protection for the entire family. We had no tanning or burning while using juice. I especially like that it is all organically sourced. It's nice to know what is going into my products. The container will last for about six adult full body applications. The price is really comparable to similar products. The active ingredient is simply twenty percent zinc oxide.

First off, when I requested this from Vine I thought it was a facial moisturizer, which is not its intended purpose. I have tried it on the face for when I'm feeling winter-dry flaky skin and it does work well, but the product is very thick and you'd have to wait some time for it all to sink in before applying makeup. As a night cream? Again might work, but the scent is so strong I wouldn't be able to apply it and stick my head right into a pillow and smelling it all night. Yes, the scent does dissipate, but not immediately.

As a body moisturizer? I liked it a lot, despite the thickness of the cream (apply lightly and then add more if you like). It does help with the winter-dry flakiness, and right after applying I could pour water on my skin and it repelled it - a good thing for those out in the great outdoors. As for the sunscreen aspects? It's November in Seattle and we've not much sunshine these days, so I can't test it or comment on that aspect of the product at this time.

All in all a good moisturizer, except for the strong scent. I am sensitive to perfumes and aftershaves and other strongly scented things, so that is a deal-breaker for me and thus the lower rating. Your mileage may vary.
summary: A good product, but the scent is too strong for my tastes

reviewText:
As someone who has had two surgeries for malignant melanoma, know the importance of sun protection. For years, went in the sun as a kid without any, and some thirty odd years later paid the price big time.  That said, if you are light complected and go out in the sun for any period of time, 30 SPF is probably the MINIMUM level of protection you should be applying.

Really like the fragrance and texture of the product.  Have very reactive skin lately, and applied without any irritation whatsoever.  For the price you get a good amount, and would strongly recommend this for all those people who have shied away from using sun protection in the past.  Am one of those people too because I have never liked the chalkiness of your typical sunblock.  This cream is a welcome change from all that, and recommend it for all who like to frolic under the sun.

Facial sunscreen and I have a bad relationship---chemical sunscreens make me itchy, blotchy, break out, you name it! I love that this sunscreen didn't do that, and it also didn't grease my face up. Since it's a physical sunscreen it will flash back on photos, so expect a washed out whitey blankness if you are doing photography in lower lighting.

No stinky fragrance, it feels more like skincare than sunscreen. I will buy this!
summary: If you are sensitive to chemical sunscreen try this

reviewText:
I do not like when I put on sunscreen and its streaking white across my face, nestling into every curve, into my hairline, my ears.

Juice Beauty SPF goes on clear and stays clear. BETTER YET this stuff smells amazing. Fruity and light. It is chemical free, containing all organic ingredients.

I have sensitive skin and this did not make me burn, break out or itch.

This is a rich moisturizer with sun screen. The scent is lovely, like lemon peel. I am very fair and need sun protection at all times, year around. Unfortunately this product contains tocopherol (Vitamin E) which causes me to have severe dermatitis when used on my face.  I can however, use it on my hands, legs and feet. I love the feel of it and the scent. Unlike so many sunscreens, it is not greasy and absorbs well.

I think the thing I like most about this moisturizer is the very genuine scent. It smells like genuine essential oils, not some artificially concocted perfume from a lab. This is a generous tube. I am looking forward to using it on vacation but I am not sure it will last that long....it is hard for me to use other products that lack this great fragrance!
summary: Nice, rich moisturizer with a terrific scent

reviewText:
I'm reviewing the sunscreen in November, so I haven't been able to try it under the strong summer sun.  It has a slight citrus scent and is quite thick.  Part moisturizer and part sunscreen, I've noticed that it leaves my dry skin looking a little greasy although it just feels dewy.  While the product might not be as comfortable during the humid days of summer in NYC, it feels like a sunscreen for outdoor sports in the fall and winter seasons.

As a mineral based sunscreen with 20% zinc oxide,  Juice's Beauty SPF 30 offers good coverage.  It's tinted but blends in easily.
summary: Mineral based and part moisturizer, might be better suited for fall, winter and spring sports rather than summer

reviewText:
Pros: has a great texture and consistency
Goes on easily
Absorbs quickly
Feels good on skin
Doesn't irritate my sensitive skin
Cons: smell is somewhat strong and like parsley out of container, but dissipates quickly

I don't consider this moisturizer really.  It's sunscreen.  It's 30SPF, which is great, and it is water resistant for 80 minutes, which is also great, and I love it as a sunscreen.  As a moisturizer, it's greasy at first, and it's light beige but is a bit hard to rub in, and it is very strongly scented with lemon and something that smells like a petroleum product, though I don't see that in the ingredients.  It's not pleasant to smell, IMO.  I can't really pinpoint where the fragrance note that I don't like is coming from though.  Luckily after a few minutes, that smell gets a bit better, and a softer lemon scent predominates.

It is not causing pilling under makeup.  I've tried 2 kinds of CoverGirl, one kind of Revlon, and Japonesque, creams and liquids over it, with no pilling at all with the creams or liquids.

The ingredients all look good and healthy for skin - though some might be sensitive to the Vitamin C, it seems a low enough concentrate it is not making my skin red.  Really high concentrations of of Vitamin C, over 20% make me red as a beet, and I have no redness at all with this product.

I prefer other moisturizers by far.  As a sunscreen though, I like it and think it's fine, though I don't like the smell initially.
summary: No piling under makeup, harsh initial fragrance, greasy at first, but does absorbs nicely

reviewText: This is a great moisturizer! I have some dry spots on my face, and some spots a little oily. This worked well with both areas. It went on smooth and felt great all day. I love that it has SPF in it, as I burn easily and need the extra coverage. Overall, highly satisfied!

As I write this in November in the Midwest, I can't really speak to the sunscreen performance of this Juice Beauty SPF 30 Sport Sunscreen.  I'll take the manufacturer at their word that it will perform as an SPF 30 protectant.

Claims, including reviewers ravings, of wonderful organic fundamentals notwithstanding . . . the product derives it sun screening protection from good old zinc oxide (20%), just like nearly all the other sunscreen creams, lotions, and sprays.  The organic/mineral/natural marketing milieu regards only the carrier crme which likely does have beneficial moisturizing and rejuvenating properties.  The tube indicates that this is "Certified Organic".

How do I like it?  As I said, I assume it does provide SPF 30 protection.  The 3.75 oz tube is a convenient take along size which I prefer to the harder to carrier jumbo tubes and bottles offered elsewhere.  Directions advise to shake before using.  Do that.

The crme is skin toned (Caucasian anyway).  Helps prevent that white look, but can also stain white clothing. Odor is interesting.  Not that familiar coconut tropical odor you get poolside on the cruise ship (which I like, by the way).  This is more an earthy scent with a hint of citrus.  Not disagreeable, but very different from the herd.

I don't care for the texture of the residue after application.  It feels like a powder which was suspended in grease. It hangs around -- not powdery, not greasy . . . or maybe it's both.  Either way, it's annoying and seems to not want to go away.  On the upside, it does indeed seem to moisturize and nourish the skin.  And it does not wash off easily.

In summary, an effective zinc oxide sunscreen that is different from the pack.  Organic ingredients.  Earthy scent.  Annoying texture.  Moisturizes effectively.

The moisturizing aspect of this lotion is highly effective and it has a somewhat strong but pleasant smell. The ingredient list is healthy and all natural. It's a simple 20% zinc-oxide formula so it's safe for me and my children. However, being a mineral sunscreen it's more difficult to spread than the more commonly available sunscreens and it doesn't completely blend in. That's the downside to natural sunscreens, they're all like that but I've used several of them and this one is much better than most. It's also expensive but a little goes a long way. However, due to the price I mainly use it on my face and use cheaper stuff on my body. It's also highly water resistant and it's held up well while swimming and cycling in hot, wet Florida. The bottom line is that it does everything it's supposed to do and it does it well but know what you're getting into when you buy this type of sunscreen.
summary: good choice for a natural sunscreen

reviewText:
This is a really nice moisturizer/sunscreen. When I first got it and opened it, my first thought was that it was going to be too dark for my light skin. Fortunately, it absorbed into my skin and wasn't too dark at all. The scent is a very light, mild scent that isn't too overpowering which works well for me and my sensitivity to strong scents.

I have very sensitive skin that breaks out at the slightest provocation. Most moisturizers and sunscreens will make my face break out terribly. So far, this has not caused a breakout in my skin. I am very light complected so I need all the protection I can get when out in the sun, and this product gives me that without irritating my skin or making it feel greasy.
summary: Very good product. I would buy it again.

reviewText: I recently tried and liked Juice Beauty Blemish Clearing Mask, 2 fl. oz. so I was very curious to try this product. First, it is worth noting that this is sunscreen, not just lotion that happens to have SPF in it. I say this because the name initially threw me off since it is called moisturizer and not sunscreen. But from reading the packing and applying it is definitely sunscreen. I say this because I regularly buy both and while lotion with SPF is my go-to on a day to day basis it's usually not waterproof enough or applied in a large enough quantity to provide adequate protection if you're wearing a bathing suit. First, I'll start with what I like about the product. I like that it is waterproof for 80 minutes. I also like that it is natural. That said, I'm not sure this product is meant for my needs. First, it has a very pungent smell. Admittedly, I tend to be sensitive to smells so if you are not, you may find yourself less bothered by the scent. But I had my boyfriend, who is less sensitive to smells than I am, try it and he too found the smell strong and unpleasant. It reminded me a lot of household cleaner, which I wasn't expecting since the other Juice Beauty product I've used has no scent at all. It also seems to sting my sensitive skin a bit. I wasn't expecting that because again, I've really liked the other Juice Beauty product I tried. It's also quite thick. I got this with the intention of using it on my face, but it feels too heavy. It also gives no indication of whether it is appropriate for acne prone skin so I'm a bit nervous it could clog my pores. Because of that, it seems more appropriate for my body, though functionally I have an easier time applying sunscreen with a spray. Based on my experience, this just isn't the sunscreen for me. While it's not natural, I've been much happier with Neutrogena Clear Face Break Out Free Liquid Lotion Sunscreen SPF 55 - 3 oz (Pack of 2).
summary: Don't care for the smell, texture, or feel on my skin

reviewText:
I work outside a lot, use sun screen daily, and with living in Southern CA, I am always on the lookout for sunscreen that is more natural instead of chemicals. I like the zinc sunscreens, but I do not like how they make your skin look chalky and are hard to wash off. Especially for day to day use, going to meetings with a chalky face, is not the professional look I am going for. This sunscreen is great because it has zinc, but it also has oils that helps it spreads smoothly, so you do not get that chalky buildup.

So why the one star? Well, I am not sure that everyone else got the same sun screen that I did.... it smells awful! It smells like if you ripped open a smelly leaf, rubbed it in kerosene, then added some lemon zest. It gave me a headache after 2 mins, made my sister sneeze uncontrollably after one sniff, and I could not get any of my co-workers to try it after one whiff. The only good part, is that it washed off easily, no residue, no smell. Makes me wonder about it's waterproof ability -- the other sunscreen I use is the scentless Blue Lizard which is great for swimming -- it's so waterproof that you can see the water bead up off your skin once you apply it. Which also makes it impossible to scrub off. Alas, you can't have it all!!
summary: I can't get past the smell

reviewText: I have loyally used Juice Beauty since 2008. Every productmoisturizer, cleanser, toner, mask, serum, lip moisturizer, etc.has left my skin feeling and looking exceptional. Their SPF 30 Sport Moisturizer is no different. After applying the moisturizer, my skin feels smooth and protected. Many of the JB moisturizers I have used in the past, especially those with sun protection, including this sport moisturizer, are thick in texture and leave almost a white finish on my face, which is not a product everyone person can wear, as everyone has a different tone of skin. However, with some gentle reinforcement onto your face, the white tint will minimize. (I understand some individuals do not favor the thick, white finish, but I have made it work for me). I also appreciate that once applied to my skin, I feel satisfied that is does not easily rub off onto clothes (through changing sessions). Lastly, when I simply do not feel like wearing makeup, I use moisturizer solo, which always blends nicely onto my skin. I spend a lot of time outside, and thus far, I have not suffered from extreme sun damage thanks to this and other SPF Juice Beauty products. Compared to other Juice Beauty products, $16 is not a bad price at all. Knowing that my skin is protected makes this product valuable to me. I highly recommend it, and I will continue to purchase this moisturizer as well as other JB products!
I recently bought this item. Well I'm certainly not disappointed. It's thick and creamy, smells very nice and most importantly super-hydrating.  Really superb for the winter months.
Love this line, gives me great moisture without being heavy or greasy.
AAA+++
Fabulous line of products!!!! Great for people like me with rosacea, very calming and soothing!!! Packaged well and prompt!!!!!!
summary: Great for people like me with rosacea

reviewText: Thus is great!
summary: Having been using this for a while. It leaves myskin most but nit oily or dry. Very pleasant smell.  Love it!

reviewText: The items may be great for others but these products left my face extremely dry with scars on my face.  I now have to see a dermatologist to help clear.
Have to use more than the serum ( 2 pumps instead of 1 pump). Hope this product is the real deal. Doesn't have the Orange scent that this product is known for. Hum?
I love how this makes my mature skin feels - silky and smooth.  Image has great skin products at a very affordable price.  Highly recommend!

Light blue colored not greasy, cooling, not thick, more like half and half thickness. Has smell of light fragrance. I am not sure what ingredients are in the lotion. I applied it on my skin after skin felt dry after warm shower in Winter of January 2016. My skin was less dry and feels like clean coat of oil was applied on my skin with moisture absorbed into skin to cool down the dryness that I felt and tightness went away. After 15 minutes when moisture is absorbed into skin or evaporated and thin oil is left on skin it provided protection from further skin drying. It prevented my usual chapped skin, cracks, and redness.

reviewText: When I first applied this, it felt wonderful.  My skin felt moisturized and dewy soft.  By the next morning, I had whiteheads all over my forehead.  It was hideous.  This might work for others, but my face didn't like it.

This treatment has the consistency of a thick moisturizer. It goes on smooth and clear and then absorbs into the skin, so do not think that this is like a mask. I generally have fairly dry skin, especially in the colder months, and I have had good luck with this product keeping my skin moisturized. I use it almost every night instead of the few times a week that are recommended. The cream has a fairly strong perfumey smell, though, and I would prefer for the scent to be less powerful.

Makes my skin super soft.
Highly recommended!
I love the fact that this can be used as a mask and as a night cream. I use it both ways and it's wonderful. Oh, and the jar, which is a hefty 2.54 oz, lasts me around three months!
I very like this! It makes me feel comfortable when I use this!

I liked the way this feels on my skin- light and soft, yet it does a great job of moisturizing. I tested this while back home on the East Coast during very cold weather, when my face quickly became dry and felt like fine sandpaper, and the Aqualia made a huge difference. Having the hyaluronic acid in the cream is much more convenient that using HA by itself, too. I used is as a night cream, not as a mask.

The consistency is smooth and light, and I did not notice a scent. The cream has a light blue color and the jar is a deep blue. I did not notice any adverse reactions and my skin did not feel greasy or oily. I've tested another product that cost several times what this product does, but it was heavy and left my skin oily even in the morning after a night's sleep. Aqualia was just perfect for me.

At $28, it is not inexpensive but I think it is worth it. A little goes a long way, so a jar will last quite a while. 5 stars
summary: Light and soft feel on your skin, but is wonderful moisturizer

reviewText:
This Vichy Aqualia Thermal night Spa treatment is almost like a gel, or a cross between a gel and a cream. It feels cool when I first apply it, probably because it has a fairly high water content. That's a good thing, because it keeps my face and neck moisturized for the better part of the night or day. Even though it's a night treatment I like to put it on my face in the morning because it isn't greasy and it absorbs within a few minutes, especially if I message it into my skin. The first few times I used it, before bedtime, I think I used too much because most of it just sat on my face and didn't get absorbed and eventually ended up on the pillowcase. Using a little less seems to work better. It makes my skin feel moisturized and lessens the appearance of small wrinkles.

This product has a light, pleasant fragrance which I would describe as floral. Because it feels so cool to the touch initially, I think it will be refreshing in the summertime when the weather is hot.
summary: I use it for daytime too

reviewText:
Another wonderful skin care product from Vichy.  Vichy is product line manufactured by Loreal.  They are well known for using thermal water form Vichy springs in their skin care line.  This product is intended for night time application on the skin and it is marketed as "overnight mask".  main ingredients of this product are: thermal water, squalane and citric acid.  For anyone not familiar with Squalane here is a brief description of the ingredient:

Squalane and Squalene are oily substances that are common components of other oils. Both Squalane and Squalene are natural components of human sebum, a mixture of lipids produced by glands in the skin. In cosmetics and personal care products, Squalane and Squalene are used in the formulation of a wide variety of products including bath oils, hair products, eye makeup, makeup foundations, lipstick, suntan and sunscreen products, body powders, nail products and in cleansing, moisturizing, and skin care products. Sqalane is sourced from shark liver; non-animal source also comes from olive oil. Another commercial non-animal source is phytosqualane, a compound derived from a farnesene in a sugar-cane sucrose fermentation over genetically modified Sacccharomyces cerevisiae yeast strains. Farnesene is dimerised to isosqualane and then hydrogenated to squalane.

What is also important to mention is that this product has light blue color and it is incredibly easy to apply on the skin.  It is not greasy, it absorbs well and have sublime fragrance.  For anyone with sensitive skin, it may be important to mention that this product contains fragrance.  Size of the product is generous - 2.5 oz. and this big jar will last for up to 6 months if used up to 3 times a week as recommended by the product instructions on the back of the packaging.  Grocery stress and retailers like Walgreens carry this product in their aisles.  As far as price goes, it Is affordable skin care for anyone's budget.

I have received my product via Amazon, so I am not sure if it is the case with the packaging in the retail stores.  Cobalt blue packaging of this product had product descriptions that were in Cyrillic.  In their letters it says that this is new Innovative product , paraben free.  Just packaging itself, was like a piece of novelty that I found very amusing.
summary: Night time skin care spa ritual

reviewText:
I picked this up for my wife, who loves trying out any new beauty product. She has used Vichy before, and is reasonably fond of the brand--not her favorite, but good enough. She was surprised how much she loved this night spa, and gave it full five stars. It goes on easy, as a blue cream so you can be sure you get full coverage. She likes the light scent as well, and said it felt good to put on her face after a long day at work.

She feels refreshed and invigorated the next morning, and is very happy with this night spa. Enough to buy it again!
This cream is as smooth and a effective as one can hope. With creams it's always hard to gauge improvement, but I do feel that my skin is more supple and looks like it has a healthier shine.
summary: but I do feel that my skin is more supple and looks like it has a healthier shine

reviewText:
What is the very best about this Vichy aqualia thermal night spa lotion is the texture, it's a gel lotion and is really a cooling, light feeling, yet cushiony cloud of comfort.
It doesn't irritate my skin at all, and after applying seems to create a lovely barrier.
In the morning after rinsing my skin feels soft, smooth and very well hydrated without any irritation or break outs.
I really like the scent, it's clean without any hints of floral or chemical.
This is a night spa experience that I will be repurchasing.

Love the texture of this gel cream.  It's cool, absorbs quickly and leaves my face feeling dewy and not greasy.  Plus my face still feels soft and dewy when I wake up the next morning.  As far as I'm concerned, it doesn't get any better than that.

The instructions say 1-3 nights a week for this product, but I have used it nightly.  I love it.  It is blue (which made me wonder if it would soak in) but it does, it is almost like a gel, very soft and hydrating!  It soaks in almost instantly after a shower.  It does NOT feel greasy or heavy-it is extremely light and moisturizing.

I add moisturizer in the morning when I wash my face, but do not use this product.  Since I wash my face, I don't find it to be any more "supple" than without using the product overnight, but I like it just the same.  I didn't notice any difference with my face/neck-but like the feel of the product and its moisturizing factors it does not hinder me from buying it again!

It has a light clean scent (not much of one), another words the scent is barely there.

I love this stuff! I just wish it was cruelty free...  Anyway, I had the wonderful opportunity to try this night spa cream/gel and really enjoy it. The instructions say to put on a thick layer and rub in - depends on your definition of "thick" - I use a little more than the amount I would use of my standard facial moisturizer, sort of like you made a mistake and put too much on. I rubbed gently into my skin and go to sleep. I wake up with such smooth soft skin it is amazing. I have dry skin that tends to react to everything - the only reaction I had to this product was, ah so soft. It visibly improved moisture and overall appearance of my skin. And one side note, I have used it in the morning as a super moisturizer too after using my cleansing brush and it moisturizes beautifully, so you don't have to restrict yourself to night use only.

I have used Vichy in the past and have all been pretty good. I liked this as a moisturizer the best. You can use it as a mask as well but I feel like just the moisturizer is good and this way I get more use out of this. Overall, you don't need much to feel the difference. It isn't greasy or oily to put on.

I feel the effects don't last too long though, hence one star off. The next morning, my skin hasn't changed too much but I do feel a little bit of a difference. It is not drastic enough yet to notice a change. The other thing is I noticed that in the ingredients, they used blue 1 in this, probably to get that blue color but some of the ingredients I really did not think would be necessary.

The ingredients are: Aqua/water, glycerin, dimethicone, caprylic/capric triglyceride, squalane, ammonium polyacryldimethyltauramide/ ammonium polyacryloyldimethyltaurte, CI 42090/blue 1, CI 42053/green 3, dimethiconol, sodium hyaluronate, phenoxyethanol, poloxamer 338, disodium edta, caprylyl glycol, citric acid, biosaccharide gum-1, xanthan gum, parfum/fragrance code FIL: B159170/2

I would like it if there were a few less ingredients and more natural.

Otherwise, it does a good job of moisturizing the skin.
summary: Supple skin - wish there were less ingredients

reviewText:
this is a product that is really liked in our household... it has a wonderful texture and consistency, great smell... not greasy...

it applies well - not much is needed at all - very economical! one jar will last a year! it goes far due to its rich, creamy mixture...

a bonus is that in the morning, the skin still feels smooth (i can vouch for this)

my wife says that this product makes her skin feel great - she loves this product!

I have to say, I got a few, little squiggly stretch marks anyway when using this cream--but I'm not one that believes in creams completely preventing stretch marks. I was very swollen at the very end of pregnancy (preeclampsia) and am pretty sure that is the reason I got stretch marks. I didn't get them with my first child, and moisturized religiously (not with this cream, though).

I didn't really like the bust serum much--it was truly a serum and less hydrating than the belly cream. Again, I didn't feel like it did anything. The belly cream smells really nice and is very emollient feeling, but sinks right in. although I'm not pregnant anymore, I'm still using it as an all over body lotion. It's great.

All in all, I really like the belly cream and would recommend it, but definitely don't think there's anything topical that is a completely foolproof method to prevent stretch marks. I have used a lot of these types of products and would prefer this Mustela cream over bio-oil any day :)
summary: Nice belly cream, but would skip the bust serum.

reviewText: 3.5 stars - I used it on my 2nd pregnancy hoping to reduce the effects of stretch marks. It helps with the itching on my skin as it stretches, however, I don't think it had much effect on the stretch marks at all. I found the scent to be too strong for me. I was really sensitive to scents earlier on in my pregnancy and this lotion used to make me nauseous. It got better as I became less sensitive to the smell in the third trimester. I would have preferred all pregnancy products to be unscented. Also had a problem with the tube design. The cap always caused the lotion splatter when opened.
summary: Moisturizing but no help for stretch marks

reviewText: A really good firming moisturizer. This keeps my skin hydrated and more pliable. This would reduce the likelihood of stretch marks but at the end of the day so would any other hydrator. This product feel good and went on nicely. It dried fast and kept my skin soft until the next shower so for that alone I recommend it. It's also free of harmful chemicals.

Whether or not one gets stretch marks during pregnancy is most likely genetics, but it doesn't hurt to apply cream every day to help prevent them - and Mustela is the only brand that my ob/gyn recommends. I like that it's light and easy to apply, and the small bottle goes a long way. That said, I still did get a few stretch marks - not too bad, all about a week before my due date. (Sounds like I"m not too unusual. The packaging says that 96% of women did not get marks after using this cream, but in small print it clarifies that there were only 26 women involved in their trial.)

But now, the bust serum: this is amazing! It's a true serum, slightly clear and liquidy. It seems to tighten even as I'm putting it on. Is it a placebo effect? Who knows? It feels good! Are my breasts still stretched out? Oh, sure, breastfeeding does a number on them. But they feel good, and at least THEY have no stretch marks!
summary: Great set and would make a perfect present for a mom-to-bed

reviewText: Wife's review- I'm 7 months pregnant with baby #2, been using this since I started to show (about 4 months). I've only been using it once daily, after showering. I'm bigger than with my first pregnancy & so far, no stretch marks. So it's doing what it's supposed to. However, with my first pregnancy, I used Palmer's cocoa butter for stretch marks and also did not have stretch marks. I'm about to run out of the Mustela, and when I do, I'll go back to the Palmer's- simply because it's over $20 less. I'm not sure the bust cream is doing anything at this point, but it is a nice moisturizer and smells good.

The clinical data looks impressive at first, but they are consumer *perception* claims, and let's face it, we all know that stretch marks and skin elasticity are highly genetic. Nevertheless, the cream and serum are developed in France under EU cosmetic regulations which are more stringent than the US. Thus, these formulas are EVEN free of paraben replacements like phenoxyethanol or caprylyl glycol, which is highly commendable. The stretch mark cream is the winning formula in this kit. The Bust Serum is really just a temporary tightener (it has lots of film formers which help give a sensation of tightening and hold) but feels really nice and is great for postpartum without implications to breastfeeding.

reviewText:
Both lotions smell very nice, not over powering and won't compete with your perfume if you wear one. I chose this because my skin is super sensitive and I figured if it's safe for a pregnant woman, it's safe for any woman, right? Plus, if it will plump up your breasts, why not your face? If it'll remove stretch marks, why not crows feet?

For the bust cream:
I can't say that I've noticed the differences advertised (no "plumping") and in checking the ingredients, this scores pretty low on the toxicity scale, which is nice. It's not greasy, feels great when you put it on and I do believe that moisturizer is going to help you feel better and helps keep your skin young looking.

Bust Firming Serum:

AQUA /WATER/ EAU, PEG-6, BUTYLENE GLYCOL, DEXTRIN, 1,2-HEXANEDIOL, DIPHENYLSILOXY PHENYL TRIMETHICONE, ACRYLATES/C10-30 ALKYL ACRYLATE CROSSPOLYMER, PEG-40 HYDROGENATED CASTOR OIL, GLYCERYL CAPRYLATE, HYDROLYZED SOY PROTEIN, DIMETHICONE/PHENYL VINYL DIMETHICONE CROSSPOLYMER, PARFUM (FRAGRANCE), XANTHAN GUM, HELIANTHUS ANNUUS (SUNFLOWER) SEED OIL, SODIUM HYDROXIDE, GLUCOSE, SOPHORA JAPONICA FRUIT EXTRACT, CENTELLA ASIATICA EXTRACT, SORBITOL, HYDROLYZED AVOCADO PROTEIN, MALTODEXTRIN, PENTYLENE GLYCOL, CITRIC ACID, LUPINUS ALBUS SEED EXTRACT, CI 47005 (YELLOW 10), CI 16035 (RED 40), TOCOPHEROL

This again is a nice smelling, non-greasy moisturizer. Will it prevent stretch marks? Well, stretch marks are genetic so I would be interested in learning about a lotion, potion or cream that could actually do that! But again, using moisture on skin that is stretching quickly will make it feel better and certainly can help with the awful itchiness that can start when the belly really starts to pop out there. So I would be cautious in believing this will fend off stretch marks - science just doesn't support that. But it's a nice lotion.
