AQUA/WATER/EAU, DI-C12-13 ALKYL MALATE, ETHYLHEXYL COCOATE, CETEARYL ALCOHOL, DICAPRYLYL CARBONATE, HYDROLYZED SOY PROTEIN, BUTYLENE GLYCOL, CERA ALBA/BEESWAX/CIRE DABEILLE, LAURETH-23, GALACTOARABINAN, BUTYROSPERMUM PARKII (SHEA) BUTTER, GLYCERYL STEARATE, 1,2-HEXANEDIOL, CETYL ALCOHOL, CETEARYL GLUCOSIDE, GLYCERYL CAPRYLATE, PARFUM (FRAGRANCE), XANTHAN GUM, CETYL PALMITATE, COCOGLYCERIDES, SCLEROTIUM GUM, ZINC GLUCONATE, PENTYLENE GLYCOL, HELIANTHUS ANNUUS (SUNFLOWER) SEED OIL, SOPHORA JAPONICA FRUIT EXTRACT, HYDROLYZED AVOCADO PROTEIN, MALTODEXTRIN, CITRIC ACID, LUPINUS ALBUS SEED EXTRACT, TOCOPHEROL.
summary: Don't have to be pregnant to use

reviewText:
Mustela makes a big thing about their products being natural and hypoallergenic. Since I have sensitive skin, I always try a dab of any cream on the inside of my arm (where the skin is thin) and wait for a few hours. It only took a few seconds to realize that the Stretch Marks Prevention cream was problematic for me! It made my skin red and irritated, even on the back of my hand where I rubbed the leftover portion when more came out of the tube than I expected. I immediately washed my skin but it stayed red for a while and felt like it was burning.

So what is in this prevention cream? MustelaUSA says "AQUA/WATER/EAU, DI-C12-13 ALKYL MALATE, ETHYLHEXYL COCOATE, CETEARYL ALCOHOL, DICAPRYLYL CARBONATE, HYDROLYZED SOY PROTEIN, BUTYLENE GLYCOL, CERA ALBA/BEESWAX/CIRE DABEILLE, LAURETH-23, GALACTOARABINAN, BUTYROSPERMUM PARKII (SHEA) BUTTER, GLYCERYL STEARATE, 1,2-HEXANEDIOL, CETYL ALCOHOL, CETEARYL GLUCOSIDE, GLYCERYL CAPRYLATE, PARFUM (FRAGRANCE), XANTHAN GUM, CETYL PALMITATE, COCOGLYCERIDES, SCLEROTIUM GUM, ZINC GLUCONATE, PENTYLENE GLYCOL, HELIANTHUS ANNUUS (SUNFLOWER) SEED OIL, SOPHORA JAPONICA FRUIT EXTRACT, HYDROLYZED AVOCADO PROTEIN, MALTODEXTRIN, CITRIC ACID, LUPINUS ALBUS SEED EXTRACT, TOCOPHEROL." (I apologize for the caps but I pasted this from their site.)

None of these are among my usual allergens but many of them I have not heard of.  I have had problems with some fragrances and a few fruit products. Fragrance can be anything so it is hard to judge but it is noticeable as soon as you open the tube. In EWG's Skin Deep Database, fragrance is the ingredient that keeps this product from getting a high rating, along with Laureth-23, which they say can cause irritation and organ system toxicity, and zinc gluconate, which can bioaccumulate and also has organ system toxicity.

The Mustela website claims good results based on a "Clinical trial conducted on 26 pregnant women who used this product throughout their pregnancy."  But personally I cannot recommend it. I did not dare to try the second product in the package after the bad experience with the first one. It also contains fragrance.

This set is made in France.
summary: The Stretch Marks Cream Made my Skin Burn.

reviewText:
The Mustela Belly and Bust Pregnancy set is great for a pregnant woman. I used the Palmers Cocoa Butter for my first pregnancy and didn't get any stretch marks on my stomach area. I didn't think to use it on my hips and upper thighs and ended up with some stretch marks there. My second pregnancy I used just regular lotion and ended up with stretch marks on my stomach. I can't say pregnancy lotions prevented my stretch marks. It could be a difference in where I gained weight each pregnancy, my age during each pregnancy, or other factors. So for my current pregnancy I was happy to be using a lotion specially for pregnant women.

The belly cream is medium thickness. In the winter I use a body lotion for very dry skin, which is thick. In the summer my skin allows me to use a regular lotion that is much thinner. The Mustela cream feels right in between those lotions consistency. It absorbs into the skin with some gently rubbing and dries pretty quickly. I try to use it at least twice a day. It has a light floral scent. Nothing obnoxious which is good for a sensitive pregnancy nose.

The bust serum is a pale peach color and has the consistency of most face serums I've used. I breast feed both my kids so my breasts are in need of firming up. Prior to my first pregnancy I read somewhere that sagging breasts actual are a result of improper bra support prior to birth. So it recommended a good bra and not going braless. I'm past that point, so I've been using the serum. It too has a light floral scent. It absorbs quickly. I have not really noticed a difference in firmness, but I'm going to keep using it.
summary: Great for a pregnant belly & bust

reviewText: I used this cream to help relieve some of the over stretched skin after pregnancy.  I got this too late to prevent any stretch marks, but I think it has definitely helped my skin retain some of the elasticity that I lost.  Drinking lots of water also helps, but skin doesn't do it on it's own....the lotion definitely helped me get my body back!
summary: Lotion helped me get by body back!

reviewText:
The Belly and Bust Pregnancy Skincare Set comes with offers 2 specially formulated products, Stretch Marks Prevention Cream (5.07 oz) and Bust Firming Serum (4.22 oz).

I love that the Stretch Marks Prevention Cream doesn't have a funny odor. It actually has a pleasant smell. If you apply more that the directed amount you are left with a residue, but if you apply a thin layer like the directions state you should use then it goes on smoothly without staining clothes or any residue. It also works well as an overall body lotion to moisturize your skin, anywhere other than your belly. I haven't noticed any stretch marks.

I really enjoy the pump on the Bust Firming Serum more than the squeeze tubes of Mustela's other products. This serum has no smell and I like the orange color. It feels like it's working from the tightness the serum leaves on my skin. A small amount goes a long way and it doesn't feel sticky. It feels quite smooth. It's reassuring to know that Mustela identifies that breasts need a different Cream than your stomach.

The cream is very light and is has a nice smell...

I can tell it's meant to moisturizer the skin and keep it from cracking... if this is used early on I can definitely see it reducing the chances of having stretch marks!

It's cool going on and not greasy...

Remember it's stretch mark prevention... not stretch mark removal...

 Avocado peptides: a patented active ingredient that promotes suppleness, eases tightness and brings elasticity to the skin.

 Arabinogalactan: patented active ingredient that activates elastin fibers and promotes collagen to prevent the formation of stretch marks.

Beeswax and shea butter: hydrates and nourishes the skin. Bust firming serum: a non-sticky, quickly absorbing serum formulated to help firm skin and tone tissue for a restructuring effect: light, delicate floral fragrance with notes of rose, bergamot and plum.

 Centella asiatica: boosts firmness and tones tissues for intense firming action.

This products incorporates a lot of great ingredients and I recommend it.

Stretch marks are mostly genetic so a cream or lotion will probably not totally prevent them, rather they can perhaps help ease their appearance when skin is properly hydrated and moisturized. I am lucky enough not to have any stretch marks from previous pregnancies but have saggy skin from my recent pregnancy a few months ago. These two creams are easily absorbed by my skin and i like using them after showers to lock in moisture and hopefully firm up those areas.
summary: really good moisturizer that works for me, for stretch marks per se i am unsure..

reviewText:
My wife has not used this on her "bust and belly" because she has flawless skin and has remained impervious to the affects of pregnancy...

We have been using this for the kids' skin.  The lotions are really great and absorb quickly.  The scent is also very pleasant.  Similar to other Mustela products, it's light and clean.
summary: Not Just For Bust and Belly...

reviewText:
My oldest daughter is pregnant and started getting stretch marks, so she wanted to try this to stop any more from developing. After having six kids, I wanted to see if the breast firming gel would work for me as gravity has done a number on my figure.

My daughter absolutely loves the stretch mark product. It goes on easy, no gross residue, and has a pleasant scent. It also stopped the development of additional stretch marks in their tracks and she seems to have experienced a lightening of the few she did develop before using this in addition to not developing any others.

To be totally honest the breast firming product, which is kind of like a gel (but with no residue) didn't do much for me but it seems to act as a very good moisturizer and also has a very pleasant scent. Perhaps if I had used this product in the set throughout all of my pregnancies I would have had better luck. As it is, I saw little to no improvement in the bust area and my daughter also came into my bathroom to use it daily and she couldn't tell a difference really either (although that may be because she doesn't need help in that area).

Overall, even if the breast product isn't a hit the stretch mark cream definitely is and is worth the price of the set itself. I've tried stretch mark creams during my pregnancies that cost much more but did much less than this product has done for my daughter. Definitely recommend if you're worried about keeping your skin in the best shape possible during pregnancy and postpartum. One of the few stretch mark creams out there that really works.
summary: Awesome Stretch Mark Cream But Breast Product Could Use Improvement

reviewText: So, I have been using this for about a week (26 weeks preggo) and I can't really tell if it's doing anything with the stretch marks, but it is helping with my irritated skin.  Since the skin is stretching, it is SUPER dry and itchy ALL THE TIME! I have started using this anytime it starts to feel itchy (so like 3-4 times a day) on my belly and chest.  It is very moisturizing and really makes the skin feel nice. It also has a subtle, but nice scent to it.  It immediately stops the itchy/dry feeling and lasts about 6 hours or so before I start to get itchy again and need to reapply.  Overall, it's good lotion, I feel like only time will tell for the stretch marks, but as for the moisturizing part, it's AWESOME!

The bust cream is particularly absurd. I bought it for my wife. The bust cream is a silicone-like, clear cream, with a slight scent that dries clear. There's a big difference between a slightly tight feel on your skin and actually firming breasts. You need several pumps (each pump is not much cream) to have enough to cover your breasts. The stretch mark cream is a thin, white cream with a stronger scent. There's nothing remotely medical about these cosmetic lotions.

I really like the Mustela brand for their Stelatopia unscented moisturizing lotion, and we've used a ton of their milky bath oil when bathing our child, but these lotions are being marketed with pseudo scientific nonsense. The firming agents are a joke, with trace quantities of avocado that have no medical action.

It's a shame when a brand builds trust with one product, just to erode it with false claims on another.

A few minutes ago, as I was preparing to sit down to write this review, my husband admitted to me that he was curious about these products and had used the breast firming cream on the loose skin under his chin.  He's impressed!  I've been using it as well - mostly in the areas of my décolletage  and we have both noticed the firming up of that skin.  It's a cool gel that goes on with little fragrance.  I use a single pump on my neck and collar area and work it in until it has fully absorbed.  You can even feel a tightening sensation.  I would recommend the "breast serum" very highly to anyone who is interested in toning up those tender skin areas under the chin.  It would also benefit those who have recently lost weight and have a little bit of extra skin to contend with every day.  I give this half of the review 5+ stars.

The Stretch Mark Prevention cream is very nice too - but I don't know how revolutionary it is.  It has a stronger fragrance than the bust cream and goes on smoothly with fast absorption.  It doesn't make your hands feel greasy.  The fragrance is a bit much when used on the top part of the body - it's easier to take if you keep in the belly, saddle and upper thigh area.  It contains agents that help promote your skin to manufacture collagen and encourages elasticity.  It also has shea butter in it to moisturize the skin.  A regular routine using high quality ingredients like these should help reduce or eliminate stretch marks.  I would give this product 4 stars on its own.

Overall, this is a great set that would make a wonderful gift to a newly expectant mother.
summary: The Bust Firming Cream works wonders for skin of all ages.  The Stretch Mark Prevention cream is very high quality.

reviewText: I used Mustela Pregnancy belly (previously called double action strecth mark cream) with my two previous pregnancies, and had no stretch marks due to pregnancy. Now that I am pregnant with my third child I have used this new version daily, and continue to have no stretch marks. This may be genetic...but I continue to use this product hoping it is helping! When not pregnant I have stretch marks on my hips and insides of my legs. I've been using the stretch mark cream on those areas this pregnancy as well and have noticed that they are diminishing in appearance and are less noticable. I've also noticed that my skin is SO soft where I have used the products. My skin also feels less itchy from the stretching skin. This is the first time I have used the bust serum and I'm a fan. I use it on my bust area, chest, and up to my neck area. It goes on smoothly and does not have a scent. These are both a must have for every pregnancy!

The lovely thing about this breast ointment is how cleanly it dries.  It also has a soft, smooth, silicone like texture that is pleasant, and it has no particular scent.  It does add a bit of comfort, but seems to do little else.

I can only rate it three stars because I found the size of the product absurd given how quickly it dries and how much you need to use.  It's a little larger than an Avon hand lotion and it has a pump (which I like).  If you have breasts of any size you will need to use about 5 pumps to cover your breasts and massage up to your neck according to the instructions.  Unless you have small breasts, you'll plow through a tube of this quickly.

The body lotion doesn't dry as quickly and is a little easier to work with.
summary: silicone like texture that is pleasant

reviewText: I have had two babies and do not have a single stretch mark to show for it. (Thank goodness) I have no idea if it was from using the MUSTELA skincare products or not, but I like them so much that I would definitely not take a chance on having stretch marks. The lotion is very creamy and smell is soft and almost like a product that you would use on a baby. The bust firming serum is a gel and I used that more on my neck than I did on my breast. The cost of this lotion initially seems a little high, but if it the end result is smooth tummy, it is worth every penny.

Mustela has been making skincare for babies and their mommies since 1950, and are committed to using natural products that are safe. Most of the ingredients they use are plant based.

This kit comes with 2 products:  one 150 ml squeeze tube of Stretch Mark Prevention Cream, and one 75 ml squeeze tube of bust firming serum.  They are both in easy to apply bottles with pop style tops.
They both have a strong fragrance that I find to be pleasant and feminine.  Quite luxurious after a hot bath.

The Stretch Marks Prevention cream is created to help prevent stretch marks during pregnancy and is made from 3 principle ingredients: Galactorabinan, Avocado Peptides, and Shea butter.  The Bust firming serum is made with  3 key ingredients which are centella asiatica, elastoregulator, and avocado peptides.  The ingredients are created by Mustela Labs, and again, are plant based, natural, and safe. There are other ingredients in both products, like water and binding properties, but the key ingredients for skin softening are as listed above.

Hypoallergenic, safe for breast feeding mothers, and created with the environment in mind, I think this set makes a great baby shower gift.  The sooner a mother to be can begin applying the stretch mark prevention cream, the better.  (Of course, lots of people get stretch marks during growth spurts, so this cream can be used for anybody, you don't have to be expecting).

The instructions on the box recommend starting the cream by the 8th month of pregnancy.

Just based on the ingredients, the reputation and longevity of the company, and the wonderful fragrance of the products, I like this set.  It would be ideal as part of a bridal shower gift basket.

As far as results, the Mustela company had clinical studies that are quite favorable.  In their studies, 26 expectant mothers used the stretch mark prevention cream and 96% of them developed no stretch marks.  Those are positive results!
summary: Lovely Fragrance - Clinical Studies Were Performed - Safe Products From Reputable Company

reviewText:
I'm an off label user; I took this set for a refill of the stretch mark cream. I use it on scars and my growth stretch marks ( grew 6" in one year at 15). It minimizes them and keeps them from getting irritated. The bust serum was new to me. I tried it out and it has a slight pulling effect. I also tried it on my dcolletage and my neck and it does seem to minimize crepe and wattle. Don't get old ladies. :)

I like these products a lot. They have a safety tab and are minimally scented. I am fond of a Mustela in general as a product line. This set is a very good value.
summary: Cream is great on existing stretch marks and scars. Bust serum gives a gentle toning/tightening.

reviewText:
This is a pleasently scented lightweight lotion for the prevention of newstretch marks and to help reduce the look of existing ones. As a new mom I'm using it for the latter purpose. The cream itself is moisturizing without stickiness or oiliness but it does take awhile to soak in and leave that nice matte feeling. I've been applying it to my stretch marks and while I feel it will be awhile before I know how well it works to fade them it is deeply moisturizing so I can definately see this going a long way towards preventing them.

The breast firming serum is the reason I'm giving this set as a whole four stars rather than five. It's thick and not nearly as pleasent to apply as the cream. It takes so long to soak in that I can only use it when I'm pretty sure I won't be nursing the baby soon. Even then I have to keep on an old shirt after I use it since I'm not comfortable getting it on the inside of my nursing bras. That said, I does seem to have a firming effect. For now I'll be saving it until my little one is older and I don't have to worry so much about timing the application of it.
summary: wonderful cream paired with an ok serum

reviewText: goes on non greasy. Does not have a heavy smell to it. Makes my skin feel very soft and supple. Definitely something I would continue to use.  Like it a lot

Loving this stuff so far! It's about the only thing that helps with the itchy skin and I have super sensitive skin and it hasn't been a problem. Liking it so much that I want their products for the baby too!
summary: It's about the only thing that helps with the itchy skin and I have super sensitive skin and it hasn't been a problem

reviewText: My wife and daughter have been needing a new hair dryer for awhile (the one that just died was a joke gift I picked up years ago which featured the cast of "Twilight" on the casing?!?!). The FHI Technique Nano is small, but powerful, and comes with all of the doo-dads that they seem to like, diffusers and whatnot.

This is a well made, typically functioning blow dryer. It has plenty of power and plenty of heat. It also has a blue "cool shot" button which toggles the heat on and off. If you find you are not getting much heat, it is probably because it is toggled off by the blue button; just press that button once and the heat will come back on. This can get very hot, hot enough to burn you if you hold it very close to your skin, so be careful. The intake filter has a removable cover which can be removed for cleaning if necessary. It also has a removable concentrator and diffuser. Be sure to line up the tabs before pushing them on and then twist them into place. The power cord is pretty long and very thick and tough. The blower is nicely balanced and feels very comfortable in the hand. This is an excellent choice in blow dryers.

I'm in a constant internal battle. I dislike blow drying my hair but I love the way my hair looks after a blow out. The FHI Brands Technique Nano Weight Pro 1850 makes the chore of drying my hair a lot more enjoyable. First, it's significantly lighter in weight than my old hair dryer. It's temperature is consistent and it dries my hair much more quickly.

It has three heat settings and low and high speeds with easy to push switches. It also has a cool shot button. It comes with a diffuser attachment and an attachment for directing heat right to the brush. The cord is strong and includes a velcro band for securing the cord during storage. It also comes with a storage bag.

I've been happy with the performance of the FHI Brands Technique Nano Weight Pro. It takes less time to dry my hair and my hair appears less staticky.

This is by far the best hairdryer I've ever owned. It dries my hair very quickly, (I have straight, fine hair), it's not too heavy, powerful, easy to handle, and most importantly - anti-static! Especially during the winter months, this is a real issue for me, and now, no more flyaway hair! It also has a long heavy duty 9' swivel power cord - which is extremely helpful. And it also includes a travel/storage bag, a nice bonus!

The heat and fan speed switches are very comfortable and easy on the hand and wrist. One huge NOTE: the "Cool shot" Blue Button, is an on-off switch! Unlike my previous hair dryers, where you only get a cool shot of air as long as you are holding the cold button, the Nano Pro stays cold until you click the button again, turning off the cold air function. This is actually a very nice feature of the Nano Pro-Tech ceramic hair dryer, if you realize hiw it is designed. I initially thought it was a malfunction when the next time I used it, there was only cold air blowing out. I thought I had burned it up after the first use, and I had not - I only had to push the blue button in to disengage the cool shot feature. I overlooked the directions in the enclose pamphlet and made a quick phone call to the manufacturer, and it was resolved immediately, wants she told me the blue button was an on-off switch, or an engage and disengage future. It went back to warm/hot instantly as selected. Again, another really great feature if you use cold air to set styles. Much easier on the thumbs; you just have to know it's an on-off switch!

Our daughter has coarse curly hair and the diffuser attachment is fantastic for setting and styling her hair. Really very suitable for all hair types. Love it!  (reviewed by my wife)
summary: The Best - Powerful, Prof. Anti-static Hair Styler/Dryer

reviewText:
Misleading title, this is 1500 watts not 1850 like you would assume by the title & the  fact that nowhere in the description does it list the wattage!
Definitely what I would consider a "Pro" grade dryer other than the 9' cord. I've had $20 dryers that worked better (I can dry my hair faster with my cheapo ConAir that I've had for years.) Also the attention to detail is lacking. The attachments don't fit the dryer well at all (they are too small to even go onto the dryer, maybe you can rig it up with duct tape if there is one that you would want to have on it 100% of the time. For this price it was definitely a let down....IMO
*Save your money, this is NOT the Droid...errrr "dryer" you are looking for......

I have very long (to the top of my butt) straight hair that I want to keep healthy, so I needed a hair dryer that would keep me from going outside with wet hair, yet also not damage my hair.  Granted it takes a while, but this hair dryer is perfect thanks to the cool setting that stays cool.  It has always been frustrating to buy a hair dryer with a so-called cool setting to only find out that it gets warm.  When on cool this stays cool!  I love it!  Granted it takes a lot longer to dry ones hair using a cool setting, but personally I think it's more than worth it. The attachments are very easy to use & switch out.  Just make sure you line up the little marks on the attachment with the marks on the hair dryer & you are good to go!  It even includes a little Velcro wrap to keep the cord tidy.  It's such a simple thing, but so useful.  A simple non padded travel/storage bag is included.  Overall I'm more than satisfied.

This FHI Heat Technique hair dryer does a fantastic job on drying my curly hair and not causing a lot of frizz

It offers 3 heat settings and a high and low air setting.  It comes with a concentrator attachment along with a diffuser. The diffuser has a nice sized cup to it so you can gently lay a lot of hair in there at once.

It is very light weight and feels nice in my hand.  The cord is really long and seems more durable than other dryers.

I would recommend this dryer to curly haired girls (and guys!)

This review is for the FHI Brands Technique Nano Weight Pro 1850 Tech Hair Dryer:

Firstly, it is a 1500 watt dryer. Seeing that it had "1850" in the title, I thought it was an 1850 watt... nope. I always thought that they put the number of watts in the title, so this threw me off. Which leads me to my next point... drying time.

Since it's 1500 watts, it took me much longer to dry my hair. I have medium length, thick hair. For the past few years, I've been using my trusty Conair Pro Hairdryer I purchased at Costco. It's an 1850 watt hair dryer, & I think paid less than $20 for it. I don't think I've ever paid more than $25-$30 for a hairdryer, so in reviewing this, I'm comparing it to what I'm currently using, & dryers I've purchased in the past.  This one claims
"reduces drying time up to 50%". That was not the case for me, & it actually took me longer! Drying time: 3/5  Not specifying wattage in the description (I couldn't find it), & the fact that I thought the "1850" in the title was misleading: 0/5.

Weight: This is listed as lightweight. Yes, it is lighter than the Conair & some of the others I've used, although not the lightest one out there. Being Lightweight: 4/5

Cord: The cord is 9 feet long, does not retract, bulky. For your average home user, the cord is ridiculously long. Where this would be beneficial is for stylists in salon, or for the home user that does not have a plug close to where it's going to be used. Cord: 3/5 (for a home user), 5/5 for stylists- I think the cord would be sturdy for a stylist due to the thickness & that long length is needed.

Quietness: This is listed as "feather light, quiet & powerful". I did not find it to be "quiet".  It was not as loud as some that I've used, but definately should not be described as quiet. "Quieter than some" may be the best way to describe it. Quiet?: 3/5

Design: This dryer has 3 heat settings & a high/low. The buttons push left to right which makes it a little clumsy when you're used to having the buttons move up & down. Not necessarily a bad design, just something to get used to if you've been using one that has the different configuration of buttons.  The "low" setting is basically useless. Very slow & if I were to try to dry my hair on that setting, it would probably take me hours. The back has a vent cover that removes easily to clean. That is a nice feature. It comes with 2 attachments & a travel bag that is nice. Do people travel with their hairdryers anymore?  Probably not, but it's nice if you want to store it away. Overall design: 3/5

Final thoughts: In regards to claims that this hair dryer "Produces flawless shine", "reduces frizz" & "Eliminates static"- Unfortunately, I did not find any difference in the shine, static or frizz of my hair after using this. It did the same as my other dryer, with just more added drying time, which I think is due to the difference in wattage between this one & my older one. So, overall, I rate it a solid 3 stars. I think it may be best for a professional stylist based on it's features & at it's current price point. I hope you found this review helpful. Happy Shopping! :)

I have a condition that causes chronic pain, mostly in the morning and at night, making it hard for me to move stiff shoulders and arms. I also have very long hair that usually takes forever to dry. As a result I haven't used a blow dryer in years. Then this came. Not only is it light enough that my arms aren't so sore afterwards but it cut my drying time by quite a bit making it feasible to use a blow dryer again. This blow dryer impressed me so much I'll be looking at other products from this brand. It's really the perfect hairdryer for those with pain/mobility issues.
summary: Perfect for Those With Pain/Mobility Issues

reviewText:
This is a wonderfully lightweight hair dryer that works well and dries my hair quickly. The warm setting is plenty for my needs even with long, thick hair. The high setting does dry my hair even faster but is uncomfortably hot. My favorite thing about this dryer is how nice and light it is. It's so lightweight that it almost feels like a toy. Even with half an hour of continuous use drying the hair of several of the kids my hand didn't feel tired.

The reason I'm giving it four stars rather than five is because of the cool button and the cord. The cool button is very easy to press and once pressed it keeps the dryer on cool. The button is situated right where I want to grip the handle so I have to adopt a somewhat awkward grip in order to keep from pressing the button. The cord is the other reason. It's a heavyweight matte finish cord which is very long. I can see this being an advantage in a professional salon but at home the cord becomes combersome and makes this otherwise very lightweight dryer heavier than it needs to be since you're having to hold up several feet of cord while using it.

I must say that while this is a pretty good dryer, it's not as good as my simple Conair dryer. Both are similar size and both include the diffuser thing and the more narrow "finger curl" tip, but the Conair is about half the price of this FHI dryer. After using this one three times, I have to call nonsense on the claim that this FHI dryer is faster than other hair dryers.... It takes the same 15 minutes to dry my hair with both this unit and my Conair. Charging extra for speed means I expect....well...more speed. (I have thick hair that reaches the small of my back)

My primary issue with this dryer is the fact that the accessory parts do not fit on the dryer! The diffuser goes on, but is almost impossible to remove because it's too tight. The finger curl narrow attachment simply will not go on - it's too small for the end of the dryer. You can't force it or twist it and there are no actual instructions to show that it might got differently than the diffuser does. So I have a pricey dryer that is less functional than my simple Conair. This one does have a very long cord and that's quite handy except that to put it away, I have to wrap the cord around the dryer or stuff it in the included storage baggie. Ummm....no. My old Conair has a retractable cord so I am not risking a break or crimp in the power cord every time I finish using it. Bottom line.... I'm tossing this FHI dryer in the guest bath cabinet for the occasional visitor rather than using it myself.
summary: No faster than a Conair, attachments do NOT fit! No retractable cord means it's a pain to put away in a small space

reviewText: This hairdryer comes with attachments that either focus the air into one area or diffuse it into a large area.  I use the diffuser because it seems to help my hair be less frizzy.  It comes with its own bag where you can keep the attachments or travel with the hairdryer.  The hairdryer has several settings for heat and intensity.  RECOMMENDED.

For 18 years I used a Solano blower dryer I bought in 1980 for who knows how much money and I loved it. It finally died and the next Solano lasted about 1 year so enough for that.  I've tried others but for the last roughly 6 years I've been using the Conair (coppery orange color) that they came out with that used an AC motor rather than the typical DC motor. I love it because it pushes a lot of air and while not "quiet" in any sense, has a more pleasing sound than most.

This one seems OK to me. I personally find the 9 foot cord to get in the way but all pro dryers have them and one expects that.

So while this seems like a nice compact, lightweight dryer (like most pro ones - we always assume the real pro ones will be big and heavy but my hair guy tells me this is almost never so as they don't feel like holding  the big heavy ones all day), but I prefer the sound of my $35-ish Conair.
summary: Nice dryer, works fine, but like my AC-motor Conair a bit better

reviewText: Am I the only one who finds the idea of a "travel" shave brush a tad ridiculous? A normal shave brush takes up, what, like three cubic inches? This brush has a hollow handle to conceal the brush head in, compacting it all the way down to a size of (wait for it) TWO cubic inches! Wow! Now I have so much more room in my travel bag, I'm going to grab my extra floss! If you're the kind of person who wants to travel with a spare *cheap* brush they don't mind losing, well, this thing costs FIFTY dollars, how much did you spend on your *good* shaving brush? Now don't get me wrong, this brush works well. It lathers really nicely, though its bristles are just a bit soft imho, but it is a good, very functional brush. But FIFTY dollars? FIFTY? One of the other reviewers said of this product, "Although this brush is expensive, you are getting what you pay for." How? All it does is apply shaving cream to your face, and don't tell me its cause its badger hair, badger brushes do NOT have to be all  that expensive. Sure, the hollow aluminum handle is nicely crafted but its also HOLLOW ALUMINUM. They use aluminum to make SODA CANS, for pete's sake! There's no way this thing should cost what it does. Again, a good brush, but the pricing is ridiculous. Even as a pure luxury item, there is way cooler stuff to spend your money on. In short, who is this for?

A nice little brush that didn't skimp on quality. Badger hair is a prerequisite for safety blade shaving and you shouldn't have to leave your brush home when you travel. Baxter of California makes it easy to pack your badger with an aluminum case and smaller than usual brush head that does the job amazingly well. Just be sure to dry the head before enclosing it in its aluminum case to avoid damage. This is a great brush and would make a nice gift as well.

My wife got this brush for me on the Vine program. I have been using a badger hair brush for years, but would not take it anywhere we go overnight. (Not that I go anywhere that much since becoming disabled, but I digress) I am accustomed to using a quality badger hair brush that has the "silver tip" hairs. These are the preferred hairs to use from the coat of a badger for a brush. This brush does not have the silver tip hairs. Badger hair brushes have the unique ability to not clump together very much when wet. I found that this brush clumped up more than my my daily shaver brush. Never the less it is still far superior to a boars hair brush, which are terrible as far as having clumps of stuck together hairs. The actual brush part itself is rather small, but adequate enough to hold enough lather to cover your face. I found that it built a nice lather in my shaving soap cup, which is filled with "Colonel Conks" lime scented glycerin soap. The handle of this brush is fairly long as shaving brushes go, and it provided a nice "feel" when lathering up my face. After finishing my shave I noticed several hairs had come loose from the brush, which if this continues after a few shaves will only grow worse. I'm thinking that this is just part of the break-in stage though. Time will tell, but Vine requires timely reviews, so I'm giving this review now, and will make any changes if I feel they are necessary after I've use it a bit more. The brush does not come with a stand of any kind, though you could stand it with the brush up, but brushes should ALWAYS be hung brush down to dry, as  the longer it stays wet down near the base the more likely it is to break down the glue that holds them in place, and the more likely the hairs themselves will become damaged due to soap buildup and possible mildew from dampness. A good shaving brush will last for years and years if cared for properly, but will deteriorate quickly if not. The stand I have for my daily shaving brush does work with this brush, I just think the company ought to include a cheap plastic stand which only cost about one or two dollars, on which to hang the brush to dry. This brush is fine for what it's designed for. packaging up and carrying in your shaving kit. Just make sure it's completely dry before closing it up and storing it in the kit. I think it's a nice brush, and  as I said earlier, better than a boars hair brush, and I would recommend it for a travel brush. A good quality badger hair brush can cost well over $100.00 and some more than $200.00. This isn't a bad product, but it's not the best. I do like it and will use it some more when I go out somewhere.
summary: Baxter of California Aluminum Travel Shave Brush

reviewText: I really like this brush.  Firstly, it comes in an attractive little box.  Then, actually need to put it together.  Its aluminum casing is very light but seems to take a bit of a beating since I have dropped it a few times with no damage at all.  The brush itself is soft enough to not irritate my face but rough enough to pick up the beard.  I don't know if this brush is better than others since this is my first, but if there is one better, I cant see how.

I regularly travel for work and have been able to streamline my traveling routine down to a near-scientific process to lessen the hassle of modern day airline travel. So when given the chance to try out the Baxter of California Aluminum Travel Shave Brush I jumped on board straight away.

--------------------
Use:
This little brush has a fantastic self-contained design that makes storing and thus porting the brush inside a travel bag very easy. The brush arrived in a cardboard tube already collapsed in storage configuration. Assembling the brush is as easy as unscrewing the collar, and then using the same piece to screw the brush onto the base. Once assembled the brush is quite a bit taller than my Merkur badger hair brush that I have been using for years. However, that isn't a detraction and the longer handle is actually quite nice.

--------------------
Construction:
The entire brush is made from machined aluminum and has an attractive black anodized finish making it look sleek and modern. The brush is well built, feels quite sturdy although very light, and secures together perfectly in both configurations. No complaints here at all. The badger hair is, however, quite a bit softer than my Merkur brush. That isn't a major issue unless you use certain shaving formulas. For example with my cream based everyday shaving cream (Proraso) this brush works perfectly. However, with Colonel Conk's Shave Soap which is a hard (think bar of soap) shaving soap and not cream based this brush will take a lot of elbow grease to break the soap down into a usable lather.

--------------------
What I like about this badger hair brush:
(+) Perfect for travel. The brush stores inside the handle thus protecting the badger hair and preventing undue wear and tear.
(+) Attractive design and finish. The black anodized aluminum is very modern and sleek.
(+) Brush works well with my shaving cream.

--------------------
What I don't like about this badger hair brush:
(-) The badger hair on this brush may be too soft to work with certain shaving soaps.

--------------------
Conclusion:
Consider your own shaving habits and products before purchasing. If you use a cream based shaving formula then this brush might work just fine for you. However, fans of hard shaving soaps will find this brush lacking.

This is the best travel brush we have found yet.  The design is genius - it's a little tube with a screw-on ring for a lid. Unscrew the ring, take the brush inside out, then turn the brush& put through the ring and screw back together & you have a perfectly stable travel brush, no joints or parts to come loose and wiggle around while you are shaving.  The open design of the lid allows the brush to dry fairly well even when it is put away, although of course the open design means that it will leak a little water.  Just wrap it in a washcloth or put it in a baggie when it is in your suitcase and it will be fine.  The brush itself is of good quality - it is badger hair, hasn't lost any bristles yet, and is solid metal.  It could be a little heavier, but I guess lighter is better for travel.  My husband travels a lot and says this is the best travel brush he owns.

This shaving brush looks very nice. It consists of three threaded metal pieces and is quite compact. It also came with an insert explaining quite well best practices of shaving with soap and brush. Unfortunately, the actual qualities of the brush are not that great.

1. It smells like a wild animal that has not washed for a while. Other manufacturers of brushes (e.g. Rooney) indicate that the brush is sterilized. Unfortunately, I could not find any indication of this on the product packaging or the brush itself. The stench is quite strong. I conducted several experiments trying to remove this smell, and none of them eliminated it completely. DISCLAIMER: trying to do the following actions with your brush may damage the product. First, I washed the brush hair with soap. This did not help. Then I poured boiling water on it. This did not help either. Then I dipped it in 91% Isopropil Alcohol. This did help a bit. After about a week of brushing the smell is still there, but not as strong.

I stopped by at a local "The Art Of Shaving" store that sells high end shaving brushes, where a salesperson confirmed that even high end brushes (priced at about $250+) can be smelly.

2. The bristles of the badger hair are quite prickly. My favorite Rooney (I paid about $100 for it about 8 years ago) is so smooth and silky, that maybe I got spoiled. If this is the case, I suggest splurging enough to buy a "silver tip" brush: the quality of shaving experience will be much higher.

reviewText: I really liked Londontown Lakur Nail Polish in the Trolley Away shade. It's a nice purple color. I felt that the pigmentation was high quality. I used a base coat by Julep. After that dried, I applied two thin coats of Trolley away. I put a clear top coat on to protect the color. This polish lasted me about a week. I am pretty rough on my nails, so a week to me, is a good amount of time.
summary: Works Well With A Base Coat And A Top Coat

reviewText: I quite pleased with this polish. It goes on smooth and creamy. The color is beautiful and very vivid for a pastel. I really like how it looks on my toes!

Wife loves this color.  She's already gotten compliments on it.  She said the cracking is in line with most other brands she has tried.  She did mention it is also more expensive for similar quality polishes (hence minus a star).

Pretty color. Goes on smooth and looks great. I didn't put any base or top coat, if I had the polish might have lasted longer. As it was, it didn't last any longer than less expensive polishes. Overall, good polish but too pricey. (Currently $16 USD)
summary: Pretty color. Goes on smooth and looks great

reviewText: I expected a lot from Londontown Lakur Nail Polish and I am happy to report that it delivered on all fronts! While you still need the top coat for the full effect, this lavender polish goes on thick with as little as one coat and stays on for much longer than cheaper brands. It took a week for this to start cracking, which says a lot, as the majority of my time is spent typing and working with my fingers. We didn't have a choice of color and I must say, I don't think I would have chosen pastel purple for my nails, but you know what? It doesn't look half bad! The color is a little darker than your traditional pastel purple, making this look great for literally all sorts of events. It dried quickly enough-- not as fast as polishes advertised as 'quick drying', but still, my nails weren't out of commission for very long. Overall, I'm very pleased with Londontown's Lakur Nail Polish and will be keeping an eye out for it in other colors.

It's nail polish, don't over think it.  Goes on thick and easy.  One coat is good, two coats is great.  Don't rush painting it on.  Take your time to get a great professional look.  Dries about as slow as professional, but good things come to those that wait.  Takes a beating and holds its ground.  My wife works a lot with her hands at her job and she only obtained a small chip days after applying.  Yes, that price tag might scare you a bit, but if you want a really good product, you have to be willing to spend more than you normally would.

I have no complaints with this nail polish - it is a really pretty, eye-catching color.  It lasts pretty much as long as I am used to nail polishes lasting - none are going to last forever, but it's perfectly adequate for what it is.

This is a nice polish! The color shown on the screen is what I received (which is not always the case with online purchases). The polish is free of the nasty stuff you don't want to have on your fingers. The polish also goes on easily, and stays well through every day usage. I would buy this brand for sure!

I am not a nail polish expert or particularly picky, but Londontown's nail polish did the job well! It is a pretty lavender color and went on as well as my other nail polishes. It also seems to be holding up well so far. I read that Londontown doesn't test on animals, so that is a big pro to me. However, I probably wouldn't order it again because of the price ($16 as of now).

I generally buy OPI, which has a similar price point, and this is a similar product.  It goes on thick and nice, and lasts a long time.  Honestly, what sets this apart is the bottle shape.  I hate the round OPI bottles.  They are so painful to store.  I know that sounds dumb, but I like to have a lot of different colors, and this takes 3/4 of the space just because the bottle isn't round.  I am sold!
summary: Love the rectangle bottle! Great product! Similar to OPI

reviewText: Loving this new color and brand.  Soft and not matted  and without white tone that I don't like.  Lasts for about a week before chipping, normal time line.

I am usually skeptical about higher priced beauty products. I like many of them, but I have also been burned by paying a lot for things that end up being quite similar to their drug-store-level counterparts. I do my own nails because I work around the house and use my hands a lot. Manicures get chipped in a few days for me. I do like some polishes more than others because of their durability. I have been stuck on pearly white Sally Hansen for a looooong time, but they stopped making it. :( I usually choose light colors because you can't see chips as well as you can with dark. I love dark reds, but there is too much maintenance. I was worried about this lilac color because first, it is a different sort of color and I worried that it would look weird on me. And second, would any tiny chip really show.

I put on the first light coat (I don't usually do heavy coats because I am impatient! ha ha!! I inevitably reach for the remote or something and smudge wet polish!) I was worried because it seemed pretty sheer for the first coat. I usually need 2-3 coats based on how much I put on with each swipe. On the second coat, I was happily surprised that it covered pretty opaquely. This was nicer polish than I first assumed! I did touch up 2 or three nails with a third coat where I put it on too thinly. They looked really good! I was also happily surprised at how much I liked this color. It is noticeable, but not too teenager-y or funky. I like those, but they are just not appropriate for work. I save the glitter for new years eve and vacations! This was pretty and feminine, but still not boring.

The biggest surprise was how well it wears. I put this on and went about my normal day. Paperwork, typing, washing dishes (I don't wear gloves or anything like that), cleaning my bathroom, even decorating our christmas tree and untangling those evil lights!! THEN I took the photo the next morning. I figured if it looked scratched up or chipped, I would report it fairly. But it didn't. And I was kind of expecting it too. I would totally buy this brand in more colors.

edit: I forgot to add one little thing: If you buy a color you like, make note of the name. Strangely, my bottle does not have the color name on the bottle at all, it was only on the box the bottle came in (which I threw away.) It is just a blank bottle.

update: Actually, three IS a name on the bottle...it is just really tiny and was hard to see. (I added another photo...I needed to see it using my camera, my eyes couldn't read it alone!) Also, I have to add that I LOVE this polish. I am actually on this page again to buy some more colors. It lasts really well for me, even with no topcoat (I usually don't have time for that) and with USING my hands. I don't wash dishes with gloves, and I have been baking all week for christmas and this stuff has held up like a champ. LOVE it.

update again (1/10): I loved the purple so much, I also bought this item in the Early Grey. I liked the performance of the lilac (Trolley Away) so much that I wanted more colors!!! The grey is very nice too...it kind of reminds me of car primer or a battleship (ha ha!) but it is shiny! I never thought I would like grey nail polish, but it really performs like a neutral. It looks great with black! and it seems to resist chipping on me very very well. I am trying not to buy more colors so soon...I would like to buy them all!

This is definitely not as quick-dry as some of the OPI polishes I've used in the past, but it layers on very thick and gives a great finished look that more resembles having had your nails professionally done than anything else I've used at home. Two coats was perfect, without either the recommended base or top coats. It definitely made my nails stronger, and it lasted a solid week before beginning to chip at all (which is saying something, as I am rough on my nails!). Even at a week and a half, it's only just started to chip at the edges.

Trolley Away is a lighter color than I usually go for, but I found that it grew on my quickly once I tried it. It's a beautiful neutral, and would be an amazing color for spring. Light but clean, it's not really pastel and can almost serve the same way you'd use a neutral "griege" type color, with a hint of extra feminine flare.

I will be looking to order more from this company, and simply keeping in mind that I can't do any dash-and-go jobs when applying it!
summary: Not Quick Dry, But Lovely and Durable

reviewText: When I first got it, I was a little surprised about the color and didn't think it would look good, once I put it on I did like it. I think it compliments my skin :) I only one coat without a base. After I washed dishes later on that night I noticed that my right hand (I'm right handed) the polish was chipped. I wouldn't expect for a polish that costs this much to need several coats, but I guess I will try it again. After looking to see the price, I noticed that there are other "steps" available from this line. I have never paid more than $5 for a nail polish that I put on myself. I am going to try using a base coat and top coat to see if that gives it more staying power. If it does, i may up the stars.
summary: Nice Color but Cracked Out On Me

reviewText:
PROS: I liked the color. It dried quickly. I especially liked that the second coat dried quickly. I was happy to note the next day that I didn't have a waffle imprint from my sheets on my nails. I didn't find it any smellier or less smelly than other polishes.

CONS: A second coat will definitely be needed. Otherwise, the color is very uneven.

Like any nail polish, it started chipping on the second day I had it on. But it should be noted that I didn't use a top coat. I just used the nail color.

I'd been wanting to try this Londontown polish since reading about it in _Allure_ magazine, and I really do love it!  I'm a nail polish junkie, and have been increasingly seeking out brands like Butter London that steer away from those nasty chemicals that are in traditional polish.

I'm also pretty hard on my nails and seem to get chips right away, but this actually lasted two full days on me (which is pretty impressive for me!) before the tips started chipping.

With just one coat of this color, you still get nice, dense coverage, and two coats gives you even more.  If you look at the photos I uploaded, the one on the right is with one coat, and the one on the left is with two; you can tell that one coat still gives pretty opaque coverage.

The Trolley Away color is also really fun.  It's a cross between lilac and lavender, and adds a fun and yet neutral pop of color to an outfit.  I'll definitely be buying more shades from Londontown.
summary: Lasts really well, and the Trolley Away color is really fun!

reviewText:
I haven't been putting on nail polish recently, but the Londontown polish doesn't have the usual toxic chemicals.  It's formaldehyde-free, camphor-free, resin-free, vegan, and cruelty free.  The polish has a milder scent.

The color is a little darker than it the photograph shows, with a little bit more of blue, but it looks like lilac.  It was easy to apply and after two coats, it looked nice and even.
summary: Free of toxins, pretty lilac color

reviewText: Great soft lilac color that reminds me of Necco wafers and Easter eggs.  It gives great coverage with two coats.  It's a natural polish so it's free of scary chemicals.  For this reason, it smells really nice - slightly floral - but takes quite a while to harden.  I really like it.

I do not normally wear such light colors, its all black and reds for me. BUT something about the pigment, and the quality of this product enticed me. I love it on my nails, it goes on easy...and freaking stays on! a solid week went by and NO chipping at all! I did put two coats, but that is pretty normal. The pigment, the color on this is amazing, its indescribable. It made my hands glow like I dipped them in flowers.

I am a licensed cosmetologist (licensed to do hair, skin, or nails) but this brand is new to me. I'm quite familiar with the popular brands, OPI, Essie, and Creative, to name a few. This Londontown brand is even pricier than the professional salon quality brands, so I have high expectations.

I was sent this polish in Trolley Away ( a nice, pastel lavender color) to review but was not sent the base coat or top coat to try it with as recommended on the Lakur box. So I used my own favorites (CND's base coat 'Sticky' and CND's top coat 'Super Shiny') which I've been using for 10 years.

Here are my basic impressions:
- The polish applied very well
- The color was good enough even after one coat, even though I always do two coats of color
- It dried to the touch quickly, however it seemed to hold that soft stage for a good while (I was out of dry drops so I didn't use those and am comparing air dry time with other polishes)
- The polish has not chipped as quickly as other brands I like, but it seems more impressionable to dents and marks than other polishes

I am interested in trying more of the Londontown Lakur color line. I think this is overall very good polish. Not perfect, but good.
summary: Strengths and weaknesses, according to this cosmetologist

reviewText: I use all kinds of polish, mainly OPPI when I have the monkey.  This is a lovely shade and does not chip very easily and I clean the house with no gloves.  The color is one I would tend to use in Spring but I cam wait till then.  The color is just beautiful.
summary: Very nice shades and lasts with no chipping

reviewText: This is a high-quality product. The color, Trolley Away, is a very pretty lilac. I've always liked Londontown nail products and this is no exception. While the Trolley Away isn't outrageous, for me I'll probably go with a more natural color next time just because I prefer the natural look.
summary: High-quality Londontown nail product, this one in Trolley Away, which looks like lillac to me.

reviewText: My daughter and I love the color of this nail polish. It goes on with just one coat and is a bright lilac color. It's also toxic free!
Very pretty lilac nail color. Went on smooth, in my picture just one coat! On top, I used Seche quick dry top coat.
summary: Cute lilac with one coat coverage

reviewText: The nail polish is high quality, and a very pretty colour, but is intended as part of a three-step manicure. Since I do not have the nail hardener, or the sealer, I cannot vouch for the effectiveness of the process. However, considering the price of the items, this is quite an expensive trio. One may as well go to a salon.

My signature scent is Creed Green Irish Tweed, but unfortunately, I can't afford to keep myself covered in it all the time.  LOL.  Anyway, Mont Blanc has lent his name to this (new to me, but launched in 2001) fragrance, Presence.  It shows its age a little, but the classic oriental spiciness gives it a timeless quality.  I'm also a big fan of the top notes which include ginger, cinnamon, bergamot and cardamom.  Could easily be a unisex fragrance.  The packaging and bottle is understated yet classy.
summary: Not a new fragrance, but still relevant

reviewText: This has a light, pleasant scent that is perfect for applying right out of the shower, and the scent lasts for quite a while. My son really likes the scent and the large bottle size makes it a good value for the price.
summary: Nice manly smell, but not too heavy

reviewText:
This is a more day time fresh out of the shower scent in my opinion. It reminds me of a scent from either the 70's or 80's that i remember smelling as a kid. Its very patient and strong smelling. I'm not exactly sure which note is the standout that i small the most but it has a powdery smell. It could be the cardamom which naturally is very strong.

I found the notes online and they are:
Top Notes:
Ginger, Bergamot, Cardamom, Cinnamon
Heart Notes:
Sage, Apple, Heliotrope
Base Notes:
Sandalwood, Teak, Amber, Tonka, Musk

This cologne lasts almost all day and again its more of a light gentle scent not a strong woodsy or spicy manly scent. It kind of reminds me of something Calvin Klein would put out where it can be a unisex scent. That's just my opinion.

You may want to go to a store and try the tester on this one first because when i first sprayed it on it was ok but then as the day went on it started giving me a slight headache because of one of the notes became the dominant one. I find myself liking it but then not liking it. Its strange or maybe i'm strange. lol. The shape of the bottle is to me like a long cut in half circle wedge. Its a large bottle too so it will last you long especially that this is more patient stuff.
Great cologne. Long lasting. Smells great, like a quality cologne. Clean, fresh, classy, and masculine.

Testing this as a free product from the Amazon Vine program.
I like this scent, it's quite a timeless masculine scent with plenty of woody overtones a little oriental spice and some musk but not overpowering.
Fragrances are so subjective so it's difficult to recommend this for everyone, but from the point of view of everyday wear it seems to last well through the day and into the early evening, something some more expensive or well known fragrances do not.
Presence was launched in 2001 so it's been around a while, top notes are ginger, cinnamon, bergamot and cardamom; middle notes are apple, sage and heliotrope; base notes are teak wood, sandalwood, tonka bean, amber and white musk.
Nice mix of a fresh modern scent combined with some classic tones that lasts.
A little pricey for EDT (Mine as tested is a 2.5oz bottle)as the listing at $55 is for a 1.7oz or 50ml , and this price range is usually 3.4oz or 100ml
summary: Classic meets modern in a masculine fragrance.

reviewText:
Best men's Eau de Toilette out there.  I've been using this for over a year now and I always get compliments.  The smell is manly yet not overpowering and it stays with me most of the day.  The ladies always notice it and tell me they like the fact that there are no feminine traces in the scent.  I like that!

I highly recommend.  Was so glad to get a bottle from Vine since I was running low!!

Try it guys.  It's got that fresh manly scent you remember from the barbershop with modern overtones that make it truly unique!
Love the time and was recommended by my Dermotologist

I had never used a tinted sunscreen before and I'm not sure what I expected, but it certainly worked well for it's primary function and I actually did look a little tanner with smoother skin after application. As a guy, I'm guessing this might be analogous to wearing some light makeup, which is not something I would have ever thought to do, but it was alright I guess. Only warning is that if you're wearing white clothing and it touches your face, it can stain it.
summary: I had never used a tinted sunscreen before and I'm ...

reviewText: Loved this product! Easy application and looks great. Good coverage. Use daily on face.
vs Cotz or TiZo3 (similar silicone-based, tinted, physical SPF products), this one never sets and feels sticky all day.

This Mineral Tinted Crme is not only a pleasure to use but it is a very important product.  First of all,  it looks gorgeous on my skin.  It provides lovely coverage and my skin looks fresh, not "mask-y" like so many foundations and creams.  It looks like I don't even have anything on yet it covers my brown spot!  Secondly, having had a precancerous lesion on my face a few years ago I swear by all products that provide good quality sunscreen.  So what more we want than a fabulous beauty product and sun protection?!!
summary: This cream provides gorgeous coverage AND superior sunscreen.  Yippee!

reviewText:
I purchased their cooling lotion and while it works very well, I have to agree with others that it was a bit runny and had too much of a scent.

I took the advice and tried this.  It is less runny and it smells much better.

After using it for just a few days, I can actually notice a difference on those difficult spots like elbows, knees and feet.

I will surely keep using this.  As for the cooling lotion, I will still use that too.  I have very dry skin and when the itch sets in, the cooling lotion really does the trick.
The lotion is great, makes you feel very soft
I've got very dry skin, this helps a lot.

This product really does provide epic moisture; it's a very rich, thick cream. I put it on after I shower and there is no need for more lotion the next morning before getting dressed- this stuff stays. It has a luscious fresh lemon scent, rather like lemon custard ice cream. If you have really dry skin this will be great for it.

I did find it a little too thick; it can take some time to get it to spread out and rub in. It doesn't leave a sticky or greasy feeling, though, once you get it rubbed in. The only weird thing about it is when I'd wash my hands after using it, it feels like there is a barrier there that needs to be removed and it takes a bit of soap to get that weird feeling to go away. Oddly, this only happened on my hands; the rest of the skin on my body felt fine when I showered, no feeling like there was a film there. Perhaps it just has time to sink in better (24 hours versus maybe an hour before washing my hands).

Jack Black, it seems, makes a product for just about every square inch of skin on a human being. I use their products (most bought with my own money but - truth in advertising - this one came via the Vine program). I have always had very dry skin and have experimented with just about every brand of lotion on the market to get relief. With the recent change in the weather from hot, hot, hot to cool, cool, COLD I have been taking hotter and hotter showers. This ill advised practice leaves the skin on the back of my legs and arms itchy and dry. So dry, in fact, that I often wake up scratching the back of my calves with my big toe (TMI???) I have tried a lot of things from cheap creams to expensive lotions and they have not done much to alleviate the problem. When this product came up on the Vine queue, I saw it said "body" hydrator so I guessed it was for more than the skin on your face and decided to give it a shot. I was right!

I have been using it for over two weeks but after just 3 days, the skin on the back of my arms and legs is SIGNIFICANTLY less itchy. Plus, those dry, rough patches at the elbow (admit it, you have them too) is softer and less itchy as well.

There has not been an overall softening of the dry patches but they have definitely improved to the point that I can get through a night without scratching. I have to say, I didn't expect that since, as I said earlier, I have tried many other products with limited success. While it's only been about 10 days of use, I see a real personal benefit to the use of this product.

Oh - I also use it on my dry hands and it's working very well. Plus, I really like it's non-greasy quality - I think that's especially important for hands.

One more point - When I put it on for the first time my wife asked if I was using a cologne (not something I regularly do), so there is a definite scent to the product. I personally like it - fresh without being over powering. SInce we all have different opinions about scents, yours may differ.

Summery - one star for the great pump dispenser. One star for the scent and non-greasy way it leaves the skin. Three stars for the success I'm having getting my dry skin under control.

Recommended for anyone with dry skin.
summary: Another solid product from Jack Black - great for my "Winter" dry skin

reviewText:
I don't generally use moisturizing products except in the dead of winter when I can't tolerate my dry, chapped skin any longer. My girlfriend encouraged me to try one of the Jack Black products assuming (correctly) that I would like the smell better than the typical "Grandmother" scented lotions like Nivea or Ponds that usually seem to be in our house.

The Jack Black Epic Moisture Extra Rich Body Hydrator is a high quality, concentrated lotion that soaks in quickly and completely and doesn't leave any greasy residue that you have to wipe off your hands or body after applying. It's only fall at the moment so my skin isn't too dry yet, but I've been applying the lotion every few days to my elbows, knees, and hands and I must say those areas feel nice and smooth and soft. My girl commented on my softer than usual hands and was most appreciative for the effort.

I generally wouldn't spend this much on a personal care product, but I can see the bottle lasting me a very long time because it does go a long way. I think I'll be grateful this winter having a higher quality moisturizer with a fragrance I actually like, rather than having to tolerate the usual Grandma smelling stuff - so maybe this year I'll actually start using the stuff before my hands are so chapped that they start to bleed!

**** RECOMMENDED! - 4 STAR ****
summary: Great product, but a bit overpriced.

reviewText: This lotion is both light and dense - it really soaks into my skin and softens quickly.  The scent is light and pleasant and doesn't get in the way of any other scent I choose to use.  I use it on my legs which tend to be pretty dry and they have been looking much smoother so that I'm not embarrassed to go bare-legged.  All in all, a terrific product!
summary: I use it on my legs which tend to be pretty dry and they have been looking much smoother so ...

reviewText: I currently use Jack Black Cool Moisture Body Lotion and I had a chance to try the Extra Rich Body Hydrator.  First of all I like the Extra Rich scent better than the Cool Moisture.  It also seems like the Extra Rich moisturizer has way more exotic ingredients than the Jack Black Cool Moisutizer.  Price wise they are the same but Extra Rich is 4 oz smaller.  I have very dry skin as I live in Vegas and I also use tanning beds on a regular basis.  The Extra Rich goes on easy absorbs right into my skin and leaves them feeling moist the entire day.

My first impression when I felt this lotion was that it's too watery but once I rubbed it into my arms and legs , my skin just soaked it in. My skin felt so soft and not at all greasy like I expected. The scent is a very fresh citrusy scent that is not overwhelming. It very common for scented products to give me a migraine but this one didn't. My husband also uses this lotion and he doesn't have any complaints, which is a good thing because he is a man of few words unless he dislikes something. We both have normal to oily, sensitive skin and neither one of us had any breakouts or issues with this lotion. The fact that this is paraben free, alcohol free and made with organic ingredients are huge pluses! I recommend this to both men and women who like a citrus scented lotion that will make their skin feel incredible.
summary: Unisex scent and ultra soft skin

reviewText: First of all, I use many different Jack Black shaving products so I was excited to get to try something different through the Vine program.  In my experience, even though Jack Black is pricier than most, it's been worth the extra money.  In this case, I can't say that.  The lotion is ok, but even when applied as directed on slightly wet skin, it just doesn't seem to stay with you throughout the day as advertised.  I guess smell is a personal thing, but I really don't like the smell of this particular lotion... again, personal preference.  Regardless, even if I liked the aroma, it seems way overpriced compared to some of the other skin products I've tried.  If I could split the rating I would give it 3 stars for quality and one for value.  Sorry Jack Black.  I remain a big fan, but I can't recommend this one.

I am an addict of Jack Blacks lip balm, so I was excited to try out their body hydrator (or lotion).  The bottle is an attractive deep blue color, and is made of plastic.  The pump works well and releases a solid amount of lotion per squeeze.

The lotion is on the high level of moisturizing ability.  I have very soft hands that don't require lotion, so this lotion felt greasy to me.  However, my wife has very dry skin and said the lotion was perfect for her.  So Id recommend this lotion for people that have very dry skin, as its powerful.  It reminded me of the strong hand relief lotion that Aveda makes.

The odor was nice, but nothing special.  Coming from Jack Black, I expected a nice masculine smell.  Instead, it had a lemon ting to it.  I couldn't smell anything other than lemon in it.

Overall, this would be ideal for someone that has very dry skin.
summary: Powerful lotion for very dry skin.

reviewText:
This is a an excellent, rich body lotion, even for very dry skin or rough areas like elbows and knees.

You only need a little bit and it hydrates the skin so well. It is a little thick, like a cream or body butter, but there is no residue left on the skin and no greasy feel. It makes your skin soft, smooth and moisturized. It is a little bit of a splurge to buy, but it is so worth it. Since you do not need to use a lot at a time, the bottle will last quite a while. The performance and quality make the cost totally reasonable. The scent is fresh and natural, possibly a tad spicy/natural. It does not linger though and will not interfere with cologne or aftershave scents.

There is a matching body wash for this, called Epic Moisture Clean Cream Body Wash. I just picked that up at Sephora. It is nice to use matching products.

We buy a lot of Jack Black products and they are all great. Since they are heavily concentrated, all of the products last a long time. The Hand Healer is excellent for very dry, rough, and cracked hands - especially if you have "construction" hands with calluses etc., from doing construction types of work. The Face Buff scrub is the best men's scrub we have come across and we have tried tons of them. My husband and son have both been hooked on the scrub for years now. We also buy the lip balm, glycolic cleanser, and Bump Fix for razor bumps and ingrown hairs.

This is a brand we have come to rely on over the years. High quality products that work very well

Jack Black products are pretty good, this body moisturizer is another. I like the pump style rather than the pop top in other brands. its a decent size bottle so it should last a while as a little goes a ling way. Because of the price (reason for 4 stars) I don't think i'll be using it for everyday after shower moisturizer. I'll be using it in the winter time when I find my skin needing extra care as well as in the summer. Its very rich like it says and soaks into your skin real fast. It does not leave any greasy feeling just soft hydrated feel.

some of the important points that this moisturizer has is:
Alcohol-Free
Colorant-Free
Paraben-Free
Certified Organic Ingredients
Vegan
Suitable for All Skin Types
Cruelty-Free
Safe for Sensitive Skin
Dermatologist Tested

I personally like that it has all these things. I try to purchase skin care that is similar to those points. Its the same as you are what you eat. Your skin absorbs bad chemicals too so we have to be careful. Overall this a great super moisturizer but for me, i'll only be using it for those special times where i need an extra boost because its just too expensive for everyday use.
summary: excellent super hydrating moisturizer but a bit pricey for everyday use

reviewText:
This is my first time with 'gourmet' branded and quality lotion.. usually its cocoa butter for me.

So I was a little surprised @ the price, but I must say the over all smell, packaging, and feel/saturation of the Lotion was all good. The lotion is thick, like very thick which was surprising.. and my friend said to look @ what its made from and compare to other lotions (??)...

The ph of my skin/sweat is high I think (so someone told me) so often times @ massages or etc my skin turns the oils or lotions into a musty smell I cant stand. Dr said its normal, n alot of people have this but don't know (yhink - ear rings thst turn color when xyz metsl is used..) So fsr so good with this tho. No issues.
Will have to see how my skin is in deep winter and im all dry tho.
summary: and feel/saturation of the Lotion was all good. The lotion is thick

reviewText:
This is indeed a very effective lotion.  it's thick and creamy and, although have fairly inflamed skin at present, this cream did a nice job of calming it.  Personally LOVE the smell of this so it's no issue that it lingers.  Others who are more fragrance averse might find it intrusive.

As much as I like this moisturizer, the price for 12 ounces is probably a deal breaker for most.

can tell a definite difference in the skin from this moisturizer.

The Jack Black Epic Moisture Extra Rich Body Hydrator goes on smoothly and feels extremely refreshing, without much of a fragrance. I wanted it because it contains shea butter, but I also had to look up a couple of the other ingredients. I found that Argan oil, which comes from the kernels of the argan tree, known as 'liquid gold' in Morocco, is a lightweight oil that can be used as a daily moisturizer for skin, hair, and nails. Capuacu butter is similar to cocoa butter, rich and creamy. The Jack Black Epic Moisture Extra Rich Body Hydrator is extra rich, but is NOT extra creamy. It is also not extra fragrant.

The hydrator just seemed to sink into my skin. They also do feel more moist. I'm enjoying using it, particularly on hands and arms. I've been washing my hands very often recently because I work with small children at church and tend to pick up whatever virus is going around. My hands were really beginning to look abused. This hydrator began helping from the first application. It's going to get some heavy use this Fall and Winter.
summary: Great hydrator that just seems to sink into my skin, making it feel moist. I'm using it particularly on hands and arms.

reviewText:
If you like moisturizers that contain Shea Butter, you will most likely love this Jack Black product.

Let's start with the bottle, which is a pretty dark blue plastic. The pump on the bottle has a good sized top, and the lotion flows easily from the very first pump. So, good packaging.

The lotion itself is lightweight, and does not have a heavy or greasy feel.  It has a fairly thin consistency, and starts out white in color. As you smooth it over the skin, it turns to a clear emulsion which sinks right in. The moisture lasts for hours, and leaves a nice sheen on the skin.

Besides Shea Butter, the product contains coffee seed oil  and organic green tea, which the manufacturer says are "antioxidants to help firm skin for improved tone and texture." It also contains Meadowfoam, Olive Fruit, and Argan Oil. It does NOT contain parabens, and is vegan.

The scent is clean and light, fades quickly, and is suitable for men or women. You can either apply the lotion after showering or bathing after drying off, OR, you can apply it to slightly moist skin, and wait for it to "dry down". (Applying it to damp skin is supposed to give "maximum moisturization". (I apply it to dry skin.)

While not inexpensive, the bottle is a generous 12 fl. oz., which should last for a decent amount of time, since it spreads so easily, and because you don't need much to cover large areas. (Example: pump out an amount that is just slightly larger than a quarter, and you have enough to moisturize both arms and hands.)

With winter on the way, this is a moisturizer I'll use often.

I will admit I am slightly turned off by the price of this lotion. $35 for any lotion which does not add years to my skin seems a bit steep, but that is all in the eyes of the beholder.
 The lotion does have a light, pleasant, and non-flowery fragrance, which fades very quickly. I would say that within a hour, I could no longer notice the fragrance.
The lotion has a decent consistency. It is not as thick as most body creams but is not watery either. I was pleasantly surprised, when I applied it to my legs that it actually stuck around for several hours. When applying it, I thought that due to the lightweight consistency it would dry up on my skin quickly, but this was not the case. The moisture lasts for around 8 hours and did a decent job hydrating my dry skin.
 Overall, a nice product which delivers good results without having an overwhelming scent.

I loved this hydrating lotion. smooth and creamy, it has a lemony, slightly astringent scent that is bracing and invigorating.
