This cleansing cream from La Roche-Posay is:
- Thicker than usual gel cleansers
- Has some fine particulates that act as exfoliants
- Has something in it that kind of gives your face a little shine. This might be what they are referring to as the "brightening"
- Feels pretty neutral on your skin overall

Good product choice!

La Roche-Posay knows skin.
For years, when friends were coming back from Europe, I would beg them to tuck some LaRoche Posay products in their suitcase for me. I couldn't be happier, now that the company has many of their wonderful products available here in the United States.
This deep cleansing brightening cream is suitable for most skin types. It is non drying and non irritating, and offers mild exfoliation. There are a lot of products on the market that tend to overestimate themselves, this is not one of them. Squeeze a bit of the opalescent cream onto your hand or better yet, your Clarisonic device, and add enough water to bring up a milky foam.
Don't expect a lot of oversudsing. Like most European products, they don't have an overabundance of useless  lather that is the result of questionable chemicals.
The scent is somewhere between a botanical and a floral, but it is so light that many people won't notice a sense at all. After rinsing, skin is soft and ready for your moisturizer.

This is a very effective cleansing foam that really perks up your complexion. I like to use it to start my morning shower, then rinse it off as I wash my hair, giving me a full wake up for the day, and it's gentle enough that I've had no issues.
summary: I like to use it to start my morning shower

reviewText:
I started using their sunscreen years ago and have been very happy with it. Since then, I have sampled two of their other products and have been pleased with those, as well. This cleanser was a real surprise in that a very small amount created a lot of creamy suds, yet, when I washed it off there was no residue and my skin felt incredibly clean.
The exfoliating quality seemed very non-abrasive and gentle.
I have no idea if it will actually improve the look of my skin with prolonged use, as they claim, but I like it a lot after only short term use.

UPDATE: I have been using this for a while now and my face has never felt this clean. It truly feels as if whatever I accumulated during the day is completely washed off. Another really excellent product.

I'm a guy and when I first tried this (squeezed it out of the tube) I thought 'yuck' as it felt like a lotion and not like a cleanser at all. But I rubbed my hands together as directed and sure enough it turned into a nice foamy lather that seems to clean well (I have slightly oily skin and many cleansers just don't feel as though they're really getting the job done). I was surprised at the amount of lather (I'll use less from here on out) and what a nice smell it had, in that it has a really mild scent that disappears almost immediately.

I was also surprised at just how 'strong' it was. When I rinse it off my skin feels as though every tiny bit of oil is gone and I remain surprised at just how little an amount you need to squeeze out to get a bunch of lather.

So I like it. Do I like it $25 for a 4 oz tube enough. I don't think so, but on sale I'd probably buy it. And to be fair, I might anyway, as a very small amount foams up to be far more (and works well) than I expected, so I keep reducing the amount I need to use, which means this may last longer than I thought. I'm hoping that the $25 is an intro price and that it goes down because as I get used to it I don't want to give it up.
summary: Great for a guy: amazingly strong with tiny amount and smells fine

reviewText: An excellent cleanser, which leaves my skin feeling clean, slightly dry, but not unacceptably dry. You don't need to use much, which is fortunate because this is a pricey cleanser. I doubt it stays on the skin long enough to do anything about dark spots.

This cleanser is soft, easy on the skin, and lathers well.

My skin is already fairly clear. This cleanser keeps that way and keeps is healthy and soft.

Recommended.

This is great on my sensitive skin.  It's got a nice clean feel.  It lathers/rinses well and leaves my skin smooth without drying it out.  It's got a pleasant scent that is not over powering, and smells clean.  Overall, I really like it!
This stuff is great.  A very little goes a LONG way so don't waste it.  Professional products like this, you only need a very little bit.  Will purcase again.
summary: This stuff is great. A very little goes a LONG way so ...

reviewText:
Normally I break out when products requiring repeated use contain alcohol.

This one does---albeit very low on the totem pole of ingredients---but nevertheless did not cause a rash.

It doesn't do very much for the way my eyes look, but my skin feels good.

Having said that, I would not purchase anything this expensive ever again. I ordered it only thanks to the Amazon Vine program, since it did not cost me anything, and when this jar is gone, that will be that.

This eye cream is great, especially for those with sensitive eyes.

Virtually every other eye cream I've tried makes my eyes tear and I can't use them. This L'Occitane cream does not. It's lightweight but still does a great job of moisturizing and keeping down the wrinkles.

I'm also sensitive to fragrance in cosmetics. Divine Eyes has a very light and pleasant herbal scent that I notice when I first pump it out, but it's undetectable on the face.

It has a pump to get it out of the bottle. Usually pumps aren't my favorites because they are "one size fits all." However I found that it was very easy to control the amount of lotion I got from the bottle.

This lotion has everything going for it: effective, nice scent, easy to use & great for sensitive eyes.
summary: Effective Cream for Everyone, but Especially for Sensitive Eyes

reviewText:
Because I frequently travel on red-eye flights for work I am no stranger to baggy eyes and uneven skin tone around the eye area while trying to get through the course of a day. I've experimented with plenty of eye cream options over the years but L'Occitane's 'Immortelle' product really stands out for the great, lasting results provided. The moisturizing effects last for a good portion of the day and the skin toning finish provides a nice refreshed look to your overall complexion.

Application is via a pump spray and the gel absorbs quickly and consistently into the skin and gives off a very slight, pleasant fragrance that lingers for a short spell before drifting off into the ether. While the product may seem pricey for the half-ounce of gel a small dollop is really all you need for each eye area and should last for a few months even with near daily use.

Good quality with great results.

I'm not big with facial creams, but the #1 quality of a good cream/gel is that it not be greasy at all. I hate the residue of something greasy. This eye cream passes that test well -- it immediately absorbs into my eye. I try to remember to use it nightly, but I am far from perfect with that. I feel like I have less puffiness and darkness around my eyes in the morning, but it's so hard to tell. I like it, though. It'd get it again.

First, the packaging is great. Since this stuff is super precious, I appreciate the precision pump that puts out just the right amount. I'm pretty sparing, so I can usually get both eyes with one squirt. I am always concerned about getting every last drop of product out, so I'll have to see how that goes once the pump fails to provide.

Another great thing is that this doesn't have some of the crazy, scary ingredients that other similar products have and there is minimal fragrance. I'm hypersensitive to smells, so this makes the difference between usable and not.

I've been using this for a while now and while I can't really see any big difference in wrinkles/fine lines, I love the high level of moisture it provides without ever being heavy or looking greasy. Even days that I skip it, my sensitive eye skin feels soft and moisturized. With that said, I'm not entirely sure that it is worth the incredibly high price tag, but that's a decision I'll have to make at the end of the jar...I would definitely repurchase if I can find a decent sale though.
summary: the packaging is great. Since this stuff is super precious

reviewText:
I'll start by saying that it's nearly impossible to determine the efficacy of eye creams over a short period of time. The ability to judge the reduction in wrinkles or skin tone takes more than one month nth or one container of a product.  So take this and any reviews comments with carful consideration before making your purchase.

I used this product virtually every morning for the last 30 days. Over all I have been very pleased with the results and have always liked and had good results with L'Occitane products.

As others have mentioned the packaging is top shelf befitting a product in this price tier. However the white text on gold box make it very difficult to read. So that may be reason they include some Braile text on the package as well.

The glass bottle features a pump dispenser that delivers just the right amount of cream with about half a pump. A full pump gives you enough for both eyes. The bottle holds only half an ounce but based on how much you need each day I would estimate that you'll get about 90 days worth from the bottle  it's a good thing since this cream is at the very pointy end of the price curve for such creams.

The product is labeled as "Ultimate Youth Eye Cream". I am not sure if that means it's the ultimate cream for young people or for those seeking youthful eyes. The box claims that 74% of users report the product intensely nourishes the eye area. It also claims to reduce wrinkles and dark circles. After using the product for just thirty days I have a hard time verifying those claims. What I can say is that the product didn't create any issues for my skin. No break outs, no dry skin, no problems at all.  What I will say is that I didn't notice any change to my dark circles.  My skin did feel nice but not really any different since switching from my last eye cream. Overall I think it's most important to use something rather than nothing. So far I've enjoyed using tis cream and if price isn't a concern for you than I don't have any issues recommending this to you. My only negative comment would be that it doesn't feature any sunscreen. That's propbably as important to maintaining your skin as anything else. Other than that I have enjoyed this so far  but the fact that it doesn't seem to be effective on my dark circles means I probably won't repurchase.
summary: Top quality eye cream that works as well as others.

reviewText:
It's just ok. I haven't noticed any difference after weeks of using it.  It hasn't firmed my skin up, but it does seem better moisturized.

It's a thin consistency and I'm used to a thicker cream. It looks like it will last a long time, something welcome in an item this expensive. After a while, it gets in my eyes and stings. I cut back on how much I used, but it often finds it way into my eyes.

I'll keep trying it for a few more weeks, but for me, this eye cream didn't work to decrease fine lines or improve any appearance in my eyes. I'll keep using it for a few more weeks and if anything positive changes, I'll update this review.
summary: 3 weeks of using and it's not for me

reviewText:
For the cost, you need either a well-lined pocketbook or a very discriminating buyer. I will say that the packaging and presentation is top-notch.

Now, does the product actually work? Hard to say, at this point, but I think it might have better results on eyes that are more in need of help. My wife isn't sure about it yet but I have a hard time seeing what's there that needs help. Will update if we have anything further to add after longer use.

Mrs. Boilermate says:
This is really easy to use. The bottle has a small pump which easily dispenses just the right amount to dot around one eye.
The lotion blends in easily, with no greasy residue.

I tried using this around just one eye for a couple of weeks.  No miracle occurred. Mr. Boilermate could not tell the difference. I thought it did make a difference to some lines around my eye, but they are still there.

(Mr. Boilermate tells me he does not see any crows feet  but I don't think he would tell me even if he did.)

I will keep using this, but would not buy it for the cost.

This actually does work. It is not by any means a miracle cream where your eyes will automatically be perfect but it actually does help. I noticed a nice tingly feeling when I put the cream on and it has reduced dark circles drastically. I went without it for a few days and noticed the dark circles more. It did not take them away completely but it really did help with them.

The bottle itself is a nice design as the pump gives you exactly what you need for both eyes. Not a lot is needed to achieve the result.

It also does not have a bad smell to it. It's a pleasant aroma and nothing too perfume-y.

My one gripe with this is the price. It's a lot to shell out for the cream. There's also a lot of ingredients in it including different oils and then names I cannot pronounce. I know some of it is needed to preserve the cream but wish it was a little less chemicals in it.
summary: Drastically reduce dark cirlces just really expensive

reviewText:
My wife was very pleased with L'Occitane's 'Immortelle Divine Eyes'.  From packaging to scent to efficacy she was happy on all accounts.

Pricing: Its definitely expensive, but most such products are.

Packaging: The bottle looks nice on her dresser, with a pleasant shape and color.  More importantly, the pump in the bottle works well, and distributes the appropriate amount with each press (not too much, not too little).

Fragrance: The fragrance is pleasant but very subtle, which is good for a product you'll be putting on before sleeping.  There should be no worries about it keeping you up.

Efficacy: Most importantly, the product worked.  My wife noticed that dark circles and fine lines were diminished after several days of use.

Given that the product not only does it says it will, but is also nicely packaged and presented, it definitely earns five stars.

I love this eye cream.  It has a nice, soft feel, a pleasant fragrance, and above all, it really seems to work!  I have noticed the beginning of the fine lines I'm getting around my eyes starting to fade after using this stuff for a number of weeks.

I didn't have any reaction or anything like that.  It worked well no matter what brand of eye makeup I decided to wear that day.  Overall, I cannot say enough good things about it.  I would highly recommend it!

This was tested by a woman in her 60's every day for two weeks and she saw no visible difference to any dark spots under the eyes and no reduction in puffiness. It was also tested on a woman in her mid 30's and she saw no visible improvements either. It's a pretty bottle, although rather small, and it smells nice and moisturizes well, but for the price tag I expect to see some visible improvements but we were disappointed, I can't recommend.
summary: It's a pretty bottle, although rather small

reviewText:
I have been using L'Occitane Imortelle Divine Eyes as instructed (morning & evening applications) for just under 3 weeks.

I really, really wanted the L'Occitane to lessen the dark circles under my eyes & reduce the fine lines around my eyes, but the cream did not.  In fact, I don't see any noticeable difference whatsoever.

On the positive side, the cream does not irritate the eye & is creamy (thick).  It does not dry out my skin.

Perhaps this eye cream works for a younger (under 50) person.  For me, it did not.
summary: No Change in Fine Lines or Dark Circles after about 3 Weeks of Use

reviewText:
I've been using this product for just over two weeks now and have noticed a slight improvement to my skin texture around my eyes and eyebrows. I'm a furrower - you know, one of those folks who is always scrunching their eyebrows together. Mostly this is because I work on a computer all day and this is my concentration reaction. I'm on the younger side for this product, but I've already noticed some of those lines forming and several of my girlfriends are already doing the whole Botox thing. Not being one to use tons of products, or go to the extreme for beauty, I was happy to try out this product.

Advantages:
- Hardly any smell! I love that this doesn't add yet another layer of fragrance or smell to my normal routine of body and hair products.
- I use this after a shower with slightly damp skin, and one pump does my entire face, so I can see this lasting a good bit.
- Small packaging and profile allows this to easily travel with you - no need to buy another expensive bottle just to travel with.
- Layers great with other face products, like an SPF moisturizer or BB cream.
- I have super sensitive skin, very prone to break outs from random things, but this product has yet to give me any skin issues. No bumps, redness, drying, or peeling. Just really awesome moisture.

Disadvantages:
- I've noticed that if I use this at night (the instructions say to use day and night, but I use only after a shower), the following morning I will have a little oil build up on my skin.
- I did notice a slight tingle when I put this product on, again - I have super sensitive skin. It was not alarming to me, but was noticeable. I didn't have any redness or bumps, however.

Overall, I really enjoy this product. At the price point, I find it hard to want to purchase for myself and will probably leave this to the Christmas or birthday list. The fine lines beside my eyes and brow lines appear more plump and less noticeable, so I would definitely say this product works.

Almost two weeks in and L'Occitane's Immortelle Divine Eyes is starting to make a difference.  Judging before and after with such products has always been difficult for me, but the fact that two weeks in I can tell a difference is a positive attribute for this gel.

Application itself is fairly simple and keep in mind that it doesn't take much.  Rubbing it between your fingers before applying, pat it into the skin around your eye, then smooth it out.  It has a very low/mild scent that isn't very noticeable.  I didn't experience any irritation immediately after applying it or into the day/night.

Overall, the skin seems and looks more smooth, less puffy and more of an even tone.  While the price is high, the end result is certainly worth it.  It's very seldom for me to find a product that doesn't bother me when used around the eyes, so I was pleasantly surprised and will continue to use more of it in the future.
summary: Good results, no irritation, little/no scent

reviewText:
This is the lightest, silkiest eye cream I've ever tried, but don't mistake lightness for ineffectiveness.  The tiniest amount of this cream spreads out and penetrates deeply into the skin around my eyes (I also put a dab of it around my lips.)  I'm in my 50's so I don't have the time to use skincare products that don't work.  If it wasn't effective I would toss it (regardless of how much it cost) and move on to something that worked, leaving a scathing review in my wake.  But this is just... luscious.  That's the word that comes to mind each time I use it.  It's absolutely luscious.  When I use it before bed, in the morning my eyelids are still soft without a hint of crepe-iness (if you don't know about crepe-y eyelids yet, thank your lucky stars and use this product - maybe you can avoid for a few extra years.)

It may not be the cheapest product, but the tiniest dot of this cream does both of my midlife eyes so it lasts forever.  Besides, trust me, your eyelids are worth it - it thought I was using good products when I was younger, but if I could go back in time one of the things I would do differently is to spend more money on my eye cream!

Nobody likes walking around with dark circles and bags under their eyes, but we all know it happens. Stress, no sleep and AGE all happen. I was excited to try this L'Occitane Immortelle Divine Eyes cream.

It is very expensive, whether it works or not! I'm not personally the type who would pay this for the amount you get, but I know some people would. With that said, this cream really does make a difference both under your eyes where the bags form AND on your eyelids where the dark circles start showing up.

A little dab goes a long way, which is why when you push down on the bottle you only get a little squirt. After using this cream for 7 days my bags were all but gone. I noticed other reviewers who were concerned about the chemicals in this product. I say you can have bags or chance the chemicals. It's kind of a given that these products are not all-natural. This cream does work though and I highly recommend it!

Maybe not a miracle in a bottle but pretty darn impressive. My wife has been using this for a little while now and I can actually notice changes around her eyes. She looks even more beautiful than usual. Some of the smile lines around her eyes really seem to have gone or decreased. She says that applying the cream actually has sort of a "luxurious" feel. Goes on very smoothly and you really only need the tiniest of daps.
summary: She looks even more beautiful than usual

reviewText: This eye cream has really made a difference on the puffiness under my eyes.  I have to say I am kinda surprised that I already notice a difference after a week and a half.  I put it on each night before I go to bed before my nighttime moisturizer.  My eyes are much less puffy and the dark spots less noticeable.  The bottle has a convenient pump on the top so I can put a little on my ring and middle finger to apply under the eye.  There is no smell and the cream absorbs quickly.  If you are looking for something that makes a difference quickly, you found it.
summary: Reduces puffiness around the eye quickly!

reviewText:
Frankly, after reading some of the reviews and shelling out $110 for this L'Occitane Immortelle Divine Cream, I expected it to be wonderful and that I'd absolutely love it.

That wasn't my experience, though.  For starters, the HEAVILY perfumed scent was very unappealing to me with my first use.  I don't insist on only unscented facial creams and usually expect at least some underlying scent in most beauty products that I buy.  However, this is by no means an "underlying" scent with the Immortelle Divine Cream.  Instead, the strong perfume hits you as soon as you remove the lid.  Fortunately, the heavy scent doesn't seem to last more than a few minutes after applying it to my face.  Or at least I didn't notice the strong smell after a few minutes.  My skin can sometimes react negatively to heavily fragranced skincare products, but I experienced no breakouts with the Immortelle Divine Cream.

As far as the anti-aging benefits, I haven't noticed any difference in three months of use.  In fairness, I always use high quality facial creams and serums, so it's unlikely to register the same improvement in a situation like that as opposed to someone who uses few, if any, high-end beauty products.  My skin texture neither improved nor worsened, although I did notice that my skin wasn't quite as dewy or glowing with this cream as it is with some other night creams.

What I DO like about it?  It seems to last a bit longer than similarly sized jars of other creams.  I think this is because a smaller amount seems to go further when smoothing onto your face.  It has a bit of an oily texture going on, so my face would be a greasy mess if I used the amount I'd normally use.  The result is that a little 1.7 oz jar is lasting longer than usual.  This would be great if it happened to be a night cream that I loved.

This L'Occitane Immortelle Divine Cream works best used only as a night cream.  For several hours, my skin is left with a greasiness from it that doesn't work with any daytime makeup application.  It's fine for daytime when I'm going without makeup, but most days I apply at least a light dusting of bareMinerals powder.  The powder just thickly gums up on my skin when I tried to apply it over this cream, even if I wait for a half hour or so.  And liquid foundation just sort of disappears and doesn't adhere to my skin.

I'm always concerned about high-end beauty products possibly being counterfeit and I specifically avoid buying them if they're far below the normal purchase price or have slight differences in packaging.  My little jar arrived in original box with all of the safety seals, including the pretty embossed gold foil inner seal.  The expiration date on mine wasn't great -- due to expire 2-3 months after my date of receipt.  I'd actually intended to send it back for a refund after I noticed that, but time got away from me and by the time I went to do it, it was after Amazon's 30-day return policy.

Bottom line, this cream does as well as any of my other favorite night creams in the $50-80 range.  If you don't mind the strong perfume scent or paying extra for a cream that doesn't seem to do anything special, you might be happy with it.
summary: VERY strongly perfumed and doesn't seem to work any better than less expensive night creams

reviewText: Product works!  It's fantastic.  Sad because I can't take the smell.  Unfortunately, I can't get past it (that bad), so I won't be buying it again.  If you don't mind the smell, it's one of the best anti-aging products I've ever used
summary: It's fantastic. Sad because I can't take the smell

reviewText: During a recent trip to Florida, I told my sister about the L'Occitane Divine Eye serum I have been using and loving for several weeks. To my delight, she pulled out a nearly half full jar of L'Occitane Immortelle Divine Cream, 1.7 oz for me to use while I was visiting. Having sensitive skin, I never know what will spark a reaction, but this was fortunately not an issue with this cream because the only reactions I encountered were favorable. First of all, it does have a slight scent but I do not find it objectionable. It's very creamy and emollient, so a little goes a long way and it leaves no oily residue on my face. I can't tell you how many times over the week I was told that my skin is soft after someone touched my face. I returned home with the jar, thanks to my sister's generosity, and I'll consider purchasing another jar when this one is emptied.
summary: Smooth and creamy with a minimal scent

reviewText: This creme smelled like a mixture of honey and old lady and not in a good way. The tiny spoon that helps you scoop the product out is just that -tiny. I don't like the kind of creams that you must dip in due to the risk of bacteria. I don't care how expensive this creme is or what celebrity utilizes it. I enjoyed faces creams from Benefit, Ponds, and others that smelled better. 4 weeks into applying this creme and I didn't see a difference.

This is a wonderful cream. It isn't a miracle in a little glass bottle, but it makes my skin soft, and it feels very soothing when I apply it. It works wonders as a moisturizer. It has reduced some fine lines, and there is a slight fullness to my skin that wasn't present before. I generally have sensitive skin, but this cream caused no problems for me. If anything, it's helped clear up some problem areas. Also, a very small amount goes a very long way. When you consider how much use you get out of it (mine is going on 3 months, still over half full) the price point isn't quite as ridiculous, especially considering how good of a cream it actually is. Definitely recommended.

I'm reluctant to pay for department-store and brand-name lotions and potions, because the extra expense is usually for luscious packaging, while the contents are more or less the same as the drugstore versions. But I must say, this facial cream was a luxe treat like I'd never experienced before. It's as if the a formula were hand-crafted for me alone -- a lovely citrusy scent, applying smoothly, and leaving my skin soft and velvety. I also adore the tiny spoon for scooping out the product, which prevents bacteria on one's fingers from contaminating the cream.

I have combination skin, and this cream slides on, sinks in, and refreshes my skin for hours. I do use mineral blush and powder afterwards, or it might be too glossy on my face. Still if I were a fairy-tale princess and went to the apothecary in the woods for a magic potion, I could not be more pleased.

Love the silky, non-sticky texture of this product and that less than a pea-size dab absorbs quickly leaving my skin soft and hydrated without breaking out my sensitive, combination skin.  The fresh, marigold-like scent is pleasant and doesn't linger on your face.  The cream comes with a little spoon which I like because I don't waste any of the product under my fingernails.

While this face cream is outside my typical skincare budget, I've been impressed with how my complexion has improved after several weeks of use.  I plan to purchase once my sample runs out.

I've been on a tear lately with expensive skin creams. I found a product in the Sisley line I adore, so I figured I must be missing a lot. Well, after going through a LOT of samples, I can honestly say that there are as many good creams and treatments in the cheaper, even drug store lines, as in the creams that retail for $200, $300, and up (yes, they really exist.)

L'Occitane has always been one of my favorite body care lines - I adore their fragrances, and their lotions are long lasting and super silky. The Immortelle Divine Cream is my first encounter with a L'Occitane facial product, and I must say, it's a nice acquaintance.

If your skin is super dry year round, count this cream on the short list of holy grail items. It WILL hydrate your face! Very nice, silky cream, no oily residue. I like the little spatula you get to keep the container contaminant-free (this is standard with more expensive skin care lines that come in a jar.) If your complexion is like mine, combination skin, the Immortelle cream might be overkill in the hot weather. I really do not need super heavy hydration when it's 90 degrees in the shade.

I got this cream when it was still pleasant out, and I was pleased with the result. The onset of summer heat, though, has caused me to pack away the cream until the cool days of fall return.

But I will be using it again, for sure. I know it seems pricey, but compared to the super expensive creams I've tried, the size is actually quite nice. Maybe not the bargain of the century, but remember, this IS for your skin. If it works, and it doesn't break the bank, it's totally worth it. I'd definitely recommend it.

This is probably the best smelling skin cream I've ever used.  And it feels really good on my skin.  I have scent sensitivities and often either the perfumes or the ingredients in skin creams make them hard for me to wear.  But the scent of this cream is quite agreeable.  It also feels lovely on my face.

I only wish it weren't so expensive.

L'Occitane's "Immortelle Divine Cream" comes packed in a stylish golden jar with 1.7 ounces of product. Initially I did a double take at its price versus quantity but after using this twice daily for a month I estimate that I've used less than 10% of the cream and can totally envision the contents of this pot lasting for a year. All in all, a reasonable price when stretched out for the duration.

The cream itself has a mostly neutral odor with delicate floral notes (likely the Immortelle and Myrtle essential oils) that I personally find to be quite pleasant. The product comes with a small caviar spoon to dig out a small dab - and 2 doses is all you need to cover the entirety of your face. Absorption happens quickly and initially adds a noticeable moisturized sheen that recedes to a more natural, flushed look within 15 minutes. Your skin won't feel greasy, but rather moisturized and conditioned to the touch. The product is non-comedogenic and I can attest that no breakouts or irritations have occurred. I particularly like the overnight results that the cream provides - a healthy radiance and vibrant, tightened tone all around.

Lovely product with good lasting results and elegantly packaged making it a nice gift item to boot.
summary: A little goes a long way

reviewText:
Full disclosure, as you can see by the green "Amazon Vine" badge next to my review, I received this product for free in order to try it out and let people know what I think about it.

The cream itself is not too thick - it has a kind of 'whipped' texture and it's a little bit greasy/oily for a day cream. I use it as a night cream instead, because otherwise it feels like my makeup is being applied on top of an oil slick. The scent is very minimal, which was a pleasant surprise given L'Occitane's usual strong scents.

I think this cream would be great for drier skin, but if you have more oily skin you should find a less oily day cream, or use this as a night cream.

Confusingly, this pot of face cream comes with what appears to be a very tiny shovel. I guess it's not cool to just stick your fingers in the jar and then apply this stuff to your face? I tried using it, but it just seems silly. You're going to then wipe it onto your fingers, hands or face anyway, so why bother with the extra piece?
summary: Pricey, a bit on the oily side for a day cream

reviewText:
L'Occitane Immortelle Divine Cream, 1.7 Ounce
Category: Skin Care

This product is the things built from the things we dream about. This is the ultimate divine cream. Noticed difference in my skin after one short week. Thank you L'Occitane for such a winning product.

L'OCCITANE IMMORTELLE DIVINE FACE CREAM

L'Occitane has a well deserved reputation for wonderful skin care products-and this is a superior face lotion.

Visually, the presentation and packaging are esthetically very pleasing to the eye. This would make a really nice present!

This face cream has a very rich, creamy texture and a fresh light scent. The scent is neither cloying nor overpowering and does not interfere with your cologne or perfume. Its price point may be a little higher than many usual face creams, but I find I use a lot less, adhering to those 5 small point application techniques:  One dot respectively on the forehead, nose, right and left cheeks, and chin. I have used a light dot around the sensitive eye area with no adverse consequences.

Using it this way, one jar lasts about 3.5 months.

L'OCCITANE IMMORTELLE DIVINE FACE CREAM goes on easily and  spreads well.  The scent is reminiscent of a light floral/citrus/pear combination. The texture of the cream is rich and nourishing and is readily absorbed, without any excessive greasiness. The pillowcase never has any greasy residue on it as can happen with other night creams. I find that this face cream is well tolerated as no redness, blotchiness, nor rashes have ever developed after months of use.  Additionally, this face cream does not appear to be comedogenic (pimple causing) at all. That often happens when a face cream is too greasy, not well absorbed and just 'sits' on top of your skin, trapping in the bacteria (Propionibacterium acnes)  that can cause pimple development.

Trap in moisture in your skin by lightly cleansing the face with clear water prior to application of the cream. This habit can be especially helpful after a shower.

L'Occitane Immortelle Divine Face Cream can be used well with most skin care regimens.

With all new skin care products, Patch Testing is usually recommended: before zealous application, apply a small amount to an area you can monitor (such as the under belly of the forearm).  If no itching or redness develops, it is not likely that an allergy has occurred. you might then want to try more liberal use and greater distribution. But, when in doubt, always stop use and consult a physician.

This super face cream works very nicely as a night cream.

It's just a really fine face cream. Highly recommended!

UPDATE:

After many weeks of use, the face seems brighter and more alert. Any dark circles under the eyes have visibly diminished and there is no puffiness around the eyes. Others have favorably commented (are you doing something different? getting more sleep or exercise?) -so it's not just my impression.

The facial skin appears visibly improved with regular use of this face cream. No discoloration or other blemish have ever occurred while using this cream.

L'Occitane Immortelle Divine Face Cream has been used nightly for a few months and it is well tolerated.  Its best use seems to be as an all-around moisturizing night cream (no sun block) that helps to even your tone and coloration. There has been no diminution of age-related skin 'dark spots'

No change in my original opinion after months of use. I still like it a lot.
summary: HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!  GENTLE, RICH SUPER FACE CREAM. A LITTLE GOES A LONG WAY!

reviewText:
I simply can not get past the heavy furniture polish smell of this cream. I've been using it for about a month and see no difference in my skin, aside from the fact that it's much greasier after application.

I'm 43 with dry but fairly healthy skin and only started using a dedicated face cream this year (previously used olive or other oils, supplemented with the occasional eye cream my mom would give me, maybe as a hint?). My regular cream is Kiehl's Ultra, which made a noticeable difference in my skin within a week. I seldom wear makeup other than mascara, so I expect a face cream to do most of the heavy lifting for my appearance, and I'm doing nothing to change the effect or appearance of cream once it's on my skin.

I switched to this to road test it and was very excited to try such a fancy "miracle cream." Unfortunately, the heavy lemon pledge scent was impossible to ignore, and the greasy feel and look turned me off even more.

The best thing I can say about this cream is that a little goes a long way--a month of twice-daily use barely put a dent in it. I'd estimate that it easily goes 2-3x as far as the Keihl's. If I had liked it, it would have definitely helped rationalize the additional expense (ounce for ounce, this is 4-6x as expensive as my usual, depending on the size jar).

But I didn't like it. Besides the heavy scent, the cream is very greasy and was slow to absorb, even into my dry skin. I didn't like the shiny, greasy appearance on my face, and it did nothing to improve my fine lines to make overcoming the odor and feel worthwhile. In fact, the greasy look seemed to accentuate them, especially around my eyes. Maybe it takes longer than a month to have any effect, but I'm not willing to keep suffering it to find out.

It didn't irritate out my skin, which does tend to be sensitive, and I liked that it did not include sunscreen (usually the irritating culprit).

Because it's so expensive, I'll keep it around and try it again in the winter and see if it's less offensive in cold, dry weather. But for summer use, I kind of hate it, but I'm giving it 2 stars because it goes so far and doesn't irritate my skin.

This is an exceptional moisturizer.  It sinks into my skin easily, and it smells wonderful.  The smell is a sort of fresh-light floral, much like the matching facial wash.  When I have this moisturizer on it feels like my skin is protected by a soft blanket from all of the hazards of the world.  This is a fairly intensive moisturizer, and is meant primarily for nighttime use.  I would find it too heavy for the morning.  A little bit goes a long way- it's pricey, but the jar will last for quite some time.  This is wonderful moisturizer- expensive, but really does live up to the hype.
Gave this to my wife, who keeps trying to find a good face cream that doesn't irritate her skin. Granted - everything does, and she doesn't even use soap. Sad to say - this one didn't pass the test.

At 42, I'm a bit younger than the target market for this product, but I love skincare products and L'Occitane, and so eagerly picked this up as part of the Vine program.  I've been using it now for about a month (I wanted to give it time to work), and am impressed with how lovely this makes my skin.

When you first open the box it comes in, be sure to check the corner of the box for the small application spatula that is tucked away in a fold of the corner.  The spatula makes for a more hygienic application since you don't have to dip your fingers into the jar and risk the possibility of introducing bacteria into the cream.  (Of course, Paula Begoun mentions that skin creams and lotions should really be in tubes so that the product ingredients don't oxygenate and lose their potency; the spatula doesn't help avoid that issue, but at least it makes things more sanitary.)

Because this cream is thick and because I use a lotion with SPF during the day, I've only been using this at night.  I spread it on over my Retin-A, and it helps keep my skin supple and moist.  I don't think that it has made my fine lines any less noticeable, but it helps alleviate the dryness and peeling that my Retin-A sometimes leaves in its wake.

I have sensitive, oily skin, and appreciate that this is also non-comodogenic, so it won't clog pores or cause pimples.

It's a lovely luxury product that makes your skin feel silky smooth!
summary: Very rich cream that softens the skin

reviewText: I ordered this through Vine for my wife.  She loves the way it makes her skin look and feel, and also the fact that it takes only a tiny amount for full application.  It is expensive, but it looks like I've started something and will reorder when it's time.

Okay, so I'll start with the good. This is probably the finest, most effective, and most luxurious feeling facial cream I have ever used in my entire life. After cleansing, I smoothed the cream onto my face and was shocked at how quickly my skin took on a dewey, youthful appearance. I have a nine-month-old baby, and so some nights are more full of sleep than others. Using this cream gave me the look of having had a full nights sleep, even when I definitely had not done so. It seemed to reflect light away from dark spots, and it filled in some of the wrinkles I've developed in the last year from pregnancy and just having a little one.

Unfortunately, all of these wonderful traits are counteracted in some part by the fact that the scent is so powerful that it makes me sneeze, immediately, regularly, and for hours until the scent finally fades. I realize that the scent is just the natural plant scent, however, it is way too strong for me. I've tested it on five different occasions, and every time I went from having no desire to sneeze, to sneezing for four hours straight until I felt as though I was suffering badly from allergies or coming down with a cold.

I've taken to diluting the cream by using it on a wet face, so I use less cream and have less of the scent sticking to me. It makes the cream somewhat less effective at moisturizing, but since there is less of the scent, it also minimizes the terrible allergy I seem to have to that scent.

Overall, I would highly recommend this cream, unless you are sensitive to fragrances and need an unscented product.
summary: Incredibly effective antiaging cream, but the scent is far too strong and makes me sneeze

reviewText: The moisturizer has a smooth texture that is not too oily. It is not actively scented but still has a 'cream' smell. I'm not sure it's possible to make any cream that has absolutely no scent. The big question is whether or not this is an anti-aging cream. I doubt it. It's a fine moisturizer but to be honest, for the price, I don't think it lives up to the billing. If you don't mind spending the money then there's not reason not to buy it, but just don't expect any miracles.

I'm coming back to comment on this cream after using it on and off for some time.  It's currently Nov. 28, 2015.

I'm updating the Star Rating to 5.  The reason is that I have not, in all my years, found anything that works as well as this product.  The best indicator that I can give you is that my husband always comments positively on my complexion after I've used the the Immortelle Divine for two days.  And I'm old.

It makes my skin smoother, softer, and brighter.  I'm a fan, even though I have to save up to make a purchase.

=============
I have sensitive skin and allergies and had NO problems using the L'Occitane Divine Cream.  I didn't have any breakout nor allergic reaction either on my face nor neck.

What I liked about this cream was how light it was.  For comparison purposes I used L'Oreal night creme on half my face-- for three and half weeks-- and the Immortelle covered beautifully and smoothly and felt much, much lighter than the heavy L'Oreal.

What you might want to know is about the scent. It's not floral, and in fact, I'm not sure there is one, except for the natural odor of the ingredients.  The scent is so unusual that I'd not even try to describe it.  Maybe like lanolin?  I noticed other reviewers described the scent as chemical but it didn't make me think of chemicals.

As I mentioned I used the Immortelle Cream on half my face and neck for almost 4 weeks and my cheap-by-comparison L'Oreal night creme on the other half. To be honest I didn't notice a superior performance during this time span. Both lotions seemed to improve the look of my fine lines and neither made a dent in the heavier lines I now have forming between my brows.

SUMMARY
I really like the L'Occitane Immortelle Divine Cream. If it was in my budget I would buy it for use during the summer months. It's a wonderful light lotion that feels good and does seem to diminish my fine lines without leaving me with that heavy feeling.

If you have the funds you should try it and see if it will work better for you.

I have tried all kinds of face creams in all price ranges and I did not believe it was possible to surprise me at this point. However, Creme Divine by L'Occitane is an absolutely outstanding product that is unlike anything I have ever seen. I have been using it for about 3 weeks and my skin already looks as fresh and young as it hasn't looked in 15 years! I am absolutely amazed that a facial care product can deliver such visible and phenomenal results.

The cream has a very enjoyable, tender, citrusy scent, and the packaging is beautiful. The only problem I have with the product that my husband now loves it, too, and uses it every day. The cream is pricey but I feel compelled to keep buying it because there is simply no other product on the market that I'm aware of that has this outstanding transformational effect on my skin. It moisturizes, rejuvenates, and makes the skin look fresh and blooming.

This luscious cream is wonderfully scented with a floral smell. It is thick and creamy and spreads well, although I did think it was a tad greasy for my taste. I live in Switzerland and my skin was very dry during the winter so this cream was perfect for me, now that it has gotten warmer I think it's too much for me. It leaves my skin soft, glowy and smelling fabulous. I don't think it has done much to reverse signs of aging because I'm not even 40 yet but my skin softness and dryness was improved noticeably through the winter. I gave it a 4 star because the jar sucks big time, you have to use a spoon to get the product out and if it's tucked in the upper rim, good luck scrapping that out. For the price they could have design a better jar, lol

Elemis is a fairly new line of skin products. I have used their moisturizer and cleanser, and I liked the way my skin felt after use. You need to be careful with oils, they can at times cause breakouts if they are too heavy. I use this oil on my lines and wrinkles, and I have a few. I could tell the quality of this facial oil is high. I like using it on my problem spots on my neck, chest, and hands. I can feel the difference in my skin and there's no residue.

This oil leaves my mature skin soft and ready for makeup and moisturizer. I use 3-4 drops of the oil in the morning and in the evening. My skin looks and feels softer.  I have some skin dryness, and the oil has been effective.  This oil penetrates deeply, leaving my skin feeling silky and visibly more full and supple but not greasy. Sometimes I use it all over my face but in the warmer months I will use it on my lines and wrinkles.

Recommended. prisrob 08-14-17

As an 84 year old man, this works very nicely on my skin.  The scent is not too strong.  It leaves my face feeling fresh and rejuvenated.  The price is a bit prohibitive though, especially for those on social security incomes.  Otherwise, I can recommend it highly.
summary: Expensive but effective for this old geezer

reviewText:
This expensive little glass bottle with glass dropper is targeted towards 'mature skin'.  I have been feeling older lately but in all honestly I am 36 years old.  I do not know if I am the target and if I will see any difference.

I use the oil every night right before bed and love how it smells.  It is a light fragrance and feels so smooth.  The directions do not actually state if this should be used in the morning, evening, under make-up etc.  This leave me baffled but I still use it at night because it does leave a sheen and bit of oiliness.  The three recommended drops for the face and neck seems to be just too little to accurately massage as it directs.  I end up using about 5 drops for my whole face and neck.  My skin does feel smooth but I do not know if I see any discernable difference in my nasolabial folds.  This is the area that has begun to bother me as of late.  My skin does feel oilier so I do not see myself using the pro-definition oil and applying moisturizer.  I would apply it by itself.

The product is expensive at 79 dollars for the little bottle but if it proves to work then I wouldn't see any reason not to continue the regimen.  So this is my conondrum... does it really work for me at this age?  Do I have mature skin?  I have been getting more and more brown patches but then again I freckle and am very fair skinned.  Only time will tell if it has helped the my non-existent wrinkles;  I am more concerned with my frown lines, folds and loosening jowels.  I would like to mention that I have not had any break-outs but my pores do get clogged as they normally do.
summary: Smells divine, feels silky but expensive.

reviewText:
I suppose when the product says "for mature skin", they aren't meaning my 30-something face, but eh, what's the harm? If anything, it'll be more gentle on my rosacea-prone, hormonal acne-prone, sometimes even eczema/psoriasis-prone skin and that's certainly not a bad thing in my book.

I've been experimenting on numerous facial products just to find that perfect combination for my skin. My current cleanser is Obagi Gentle Rejuvenation Soothing Cleanser, and I've been enjoying the smooth application and how clean, but how moisturized my skin feels afterwards.

In the mornings, following my cleansing routine, I was using the Vichy Idalia Antioxidant Serum, which did an OK job. Nothing bad, but not something I need to rush out and purchase before I run out of product. And before that, I was using L'Oral Paris Age Perfect Cell Renewal Rosy Tone Moisturizer, which worked just as fine as the Vichy Serum at a more reasonable price.

After plucking Elemis-Pro from the Vine, I replaced my Vichy moisturizer with this facial oil. I do adore the bottle shape and the dropper is fun - though it's incredibly challenging to get only 4 drops, and I don't feel like I get good coverage on my skin using only 4 drops (I end up wasting so much on my hands). However, the results after a week of using it are really nice - my skin has remained clear of blemishes and redness, and it continues to feel smooth. I haven't noticed any improvement on droopy jowls or facial lines, but then I am in my 30's and don't have a lot of those yet.

But let's briefly talk about cost. Right now on Amazon, this is $79 for 0.5 fl.oz. That's a LOT of money for such a small bottle - even using only 3-4 drops per use!

My recommendation is to use this maybe weekly or biweekly in addition to your daily moisturizer. I'm going to try that myself, to stretch out the use of this product and see if it's enough to make me want to plunk down $79 for a replacement bottle in the future.
summary: From a woman in her 30's - works great, a little too pricey for replacing your daily moisturizer

reviewText: Great smell. It is an oil so it is greasy but absorbs quickly. Dropper top is nice giving you the control to get only the 3-4 drops recommended. I've learned from experience that if I use too much there is a good chance I will break out. You will see results over time but not overnight. I use before bed only so a bottle lasts a long time.
summary: Expensive but a bottle lasts a long time if used as recommended

reviewText:
Nice looking bottle and ingredients, but unfortunately caused severe acne break-out for my wife.

This appears to be a good quality product.  Of course, it is an oil, and it has a nice feel to it; however, my wife had a pretty intense eruption of acne, nodular, with use of only a slight amount, one time.  My wife is not particularly sensitive to anything.

One would have to weigh their decision on use carefully.

I really like the way this makes my skin feel- soft and supple, without being greasy. I use it under my makeup and it has no negative impact on the longevity of my makeup wear. All in all I am pretty happy with this product!

I'm almost 60 years old, so I shouldn't have to worry about acne anymore.  Unfortunately, a few hours after using this oil, my entire face erupted in acne.  I tried it a few more times, just to make sure it wasn't a fluke.  It wasn't; each time, I got more acne than the time before.  Oh, this oil made my skin feel soft without an oily feeling, but I'm too old to have my face covered in acne.  I won't be using this anymore.

As one of the other reviewers noted, since this oil is made in the EU instead of the United States, you can trust the ingredients to a much greater extent. The EU operates on the "precautionary principle," meaning companies bear the burden of proof to show ingredients are not harmful. America essentially follows the opposite course. Ingredients have to be shown as harmful to be removed. Another issue is that in America, many ingredients are considered 'trade secrets' that do not have to be disclosed... the most common being 'fragrance,' which can disguise a whole raft of poisons. Our system is based formulaic methodologies of cost-benefit analyses and quantitative risk assessments ostensibly offered to provide more 'sensible' and 'rational' solutions. In actuality, the system is motivated by a desire to accommodate industrial and producer interests not our health.

That said, the Elemis oil is evidence that you don't have to rely on cancer-causing or toxic products to smooth out your wrinkles and restore essential oils to your skin. This product works fine. No added smells, so on that front it is very mild. As a practical guy, the bottle seems to me to be a bit over-kill. I'd prefer a reduced price with the oils stored in a plain little brown bottle (to protect from the sun) and just a screw off cap. Turn the bottle upside down briefly on a finger tip and you get a full dose without having to mess around with a dropper. However, I presume they have done the market research to know people are more attracted to this bottle shape.
summary: Excellent Quality Oils, Selected for Restorative Properties

reviewText: This is a lovely facial oil. I adore European skin care products because the EU has banned over 1100 ingredients in skin care (the US is sadly lacking with only a handful of ingredients banned) and I trust the European products more than the American ones. This is full of a myriad of oils, all known for their healing and moisturizing properties. Only a couple drops are needed and they glide on and absorb quickly. I have sensitive skin and didn't have any issues with this product. It helped me feel better about my 48-year old face which has recently started looking a little dull. Love this product. It smells wonderful too.

This oil smells really nice. However it didn't absorb very well into the skin and left my face feeling oily until I washed it off. I wore it under makeup and that was a huge mistake as it make my foundation look smudged and greasy. Probably best for dry to very dry skin. Also I have sensitive skin and it wasn't too happy about this oil, had a little bit of redness after I put it on.

The product appears to be very streamline and CORDLESS but that is completely inaccurate.  Although, NOT AMAZONS fault!!!  I placed an order and received a corded product which is not what I was looking for.  Amazon graciously re-ordered it for me and low and behold the same corded product arrived.

I then went onto the Silk';n web site and saw the corded and portable / rechargeable photo's as well.  I waited over the weekend until the manufactures office was open and they no longer make the cordless / rechargeable model.  So,  needless to say I am ordering another make and model.  Who wants to be lassoed to an electrical outlet!!!

Honestly, I didn't get it. I mean, I guess this product just isn't for me. I barely have time to breathe let alone sit there with a thing on every single zit (not that I have that many). So, I guess I really didn't have the time to use it properly, so the 3 stars is mostly for inconvenience.

I ordered the Silk 'n Blue Acne Solution Device with my fourteen-year-old granddaughter in mind. She is sufferng, like so many young teens, from periodic outbreaks of acne. She and I sat down and opened the box. Inside were the acne device, a cord, a charging device, and a small booklet of instructions in English and a couple of other languages. Both she and I read the instructions. Just inside the front cover is a page of Quick Start Instructions which we both read. The first thing they said to do was plug the charger into the wall and place the device on the charger for 6 to 8 hours. I wouldn't call that a quick start. But we followed the instructions and then went out shopping and had lunch. After we ate, we found a couple of cute summer outfits. That worked to my grand-daughter's advantage. When we got back, she went in and washed her face with plain old soap and water. There was plenty of time for her skin to dry. The charging time was still not up. She and I waited some more. The lesson here is don't expect to be able to use this thing as soon as you open the package. Plan ahead.  We didn't.

The 6-hour wait was over and we pressed the on/off switch. A green light flickered to life and finally stayed on. Ready for action. My granddaughter's blemishes were concentrated on her forehead and chin, so those were the areas she concentrated on with the Blue. The LED light was on and she held the Blue against the skin on her forehead for a little over 3 minutes. She found the head of the device was getting pretty warm. She moved the head of the Blue to another place on her forehead every 3 to 4 minutes. She thought the heat was getting pretty warm. She applied the Blue to about 8 areas on her  forehead and 3 areas on her chin. It took about 40 minutes to get around to all the areas that had blemishes. She was through for the evening. The Blue was returned to the charger so it would be ready the next morning. After the Blue had been on the charger for another 6 hours, I removed it as I had read in the comments not to leave it on after it was fully charged.

The directions said to use the Blue twice a day for 6- to 8-weeks to start and to repeat the treatments twice a week for maintenance. The maintenance schedule seems reasonable but getting there seems to be a real hike to me. Lucky for my granddaughter, it's summer vacation but to keep up that starting schedule during the rest of the year would be difficult.

She managed pretty well through almost 4 weeks of treatments but she was definitely flagging in her enthusiasm. The treatments, lasting at least an half-hour each, twice a day, were taking up an awful lot of time, time she would have preferred doing other things. Fortunately, she was showing some fairly decent results with her skin. Maintenance arrived just in time, or I think she may have given up.

Her skin has been fairly clear now for a couple of weeks and she has been doing the maintenance schedule. I hope she can keep up once school starts again. We discussed the ratings for this device and she felt the amount to time necessary, especially at the beginning, was a real problem. She liked the results aside from the rare new blemish. I thought the time spent charging and getting the Blue off the charger so it didn't overcharge was a pain. All in all, we decided that 3 stars were just about right. The results were pretty good but it took an awful lot of effort to get there.

I got this to review through the Amazon Vine program.  I have had some trouble with breakouts around my chin and bottom of face, I think mostly because a new hair product I was using.  Anyway, I stopped using the hair product and thought maybe using the Silk'n Blue would help clear up this breakout.  I also breakout a lot during my monthly cycle and was hoping this would help with that as well.

In short I used it for a few weeks and didn't really notice much difference either way.

This is a nice sleek device, it lasts a week or so on one charge and comes with a nice stand.  The blue LEDs turn on when the device is close to your face (you do have to power it on and then bring it close to your face for the lights to turn on).  It's an interesting idea and similar to the Tanda (which I had previously used and had similar results with..that is to say not much change in skin quality).

The main downfall to this device is that is incredibly time consuming to use.  Silk'n recommends treating the area for 2 minutes, 2 times a day for 6-8 weeks to see results.  Since I am reviewing this for Vine I only have 30 days to try it.  In reality though I only used it for a couple weeks once a day.  With the 2 minute per area treatment time it was taking me about 30 minutes to treat my face (just chin area and forehead).  It was just way too time consuming.

Additionally the area where you are holding it on your face gets pretty hot.  Maybe this will be nice in the winter, but in the summer it just makes your whole body sweat.  It's pretty uncomfortable and my skin was red and poofy when I was done with a treatment.  I did the treatments at night and the poofiness and redness was gone by morning so it wasn't a huge deal..but my skin felt a bit raw.

I also had a bit of trouble getting the light to come on.  I would turn it on and then wait a few seconds and put it up to my face, the light wouldn't come on.  So I would turn it off and turn it back on and try again.  It did this every time I used it, so it always took a few minutes to get it running.

In the end I noticed absolutely no change in skin quality.  If you have really severe acne this might work better but for my occasional breakouts it didn't seem to be all that effective.  I personally don't have to time to keep using this giving the lack of benefit I was seeing with it.

Pros:
- Sleek looking and easy to hold
- Only have to charge weekly
- Nice stand and charger
- Didn't make my skin worse

Cons:
- Made my skin very hot, in the summer this made me uncomfortable and sweaty
- Left my skin red and poofy and sensitive right after use (this went away by the next morning)
- Took forever to treat a small area
- Didn't notice any change in skin quality
summary: Very time consuming to use and no discernible change in skin quality

reviewText: Works well, but l don't know it its worth the effort for someone with a lot of acne.  The footprint is small so going over a large area is very time consuming.  I used the device in conjunction with clean & clear persa-gel right before my period and while it did not prevent all acne from appearing, there was a noticeable difference to months past. I'll keep using it.

If you have a bad case of acne or possible other skin conditions, this might be a solution. My daughter and son have started breaking out so they tried it. The use has to be patient and methodical during application, and as kids, they just aren't but they gave it a shot. There was some improvment with my daughters sking, but not with my son's.  Granted, they are only 3 weeks into the 6-8 week period of seeing results, but I doubt it is a program they can stick to. Which makes the blue light treatment worthless for them. Others may benefit though.

~ Kort
summary: Not Sure It Is Worth It

reviewText: Both my husband and I have been using this Silk'n Blue Acne Solution Device for a while now and seen significant results. I have a couple problem areas but my acne problem is on the minor side still I have seen significant improvement his problem is bigger he has some problem areas with repeat breakouts on the regular and it has been very helpful for him his troubled areas are much more clear/clean. It is a bit time consuming but worth it, it does not get very hot, I am please we have it as he definitely needed it especially since it gets in there kills bacteria many his pimples never really pop but are deep into his skin. We are very pleased.

I have always had problems with acne. I have tried prescription acne creams, products on television, in the stores, and even received treatment from doctors. Yet, nothing ever really seemed to work. It worked for a little while but then it seemed that the acne would adapt to the products or treatments and stop working. I can not count the many times I cried myself to sleep due to the acne. Which if it was just a simple pimple or blackhead that is one thing but as I have gotten older, my acne seems to have grown to sometimes the size of a nickel/quarter and not just on my forehead but all over my face and on my chest and back. One of the biggest issues is that the acne forms but with no head to it and hot compresses don't seem to help that much.

So I picked this up to try it. Wow, after using it 4 times already I noticed a big improvement. I had one that was like the size of a quarter and already it is about penny size or less. I am happy. The heat does get hot but not hot enough to burn. I did notice after the first time that I had a couple of small bumps appear due to the heat and the drying effect from this device. I am looking forward to see if this device really does help keep future breakouts from happening and give me clearer skin. Either way, this device is worth the money for happiness.

Silk n Blue Acne Solution Device is an amazing product that works ! My son has terrible acne on his face,he used silkn blue on one side of his face to see if it works after a few days his face looked clean and clear. It was really unbelievable!! Now he has to use it on the other side. You use it by holding it on the affected area for a few minutes then move to the next spot . It works really well and I would highly recommend it !!! It is a great product !!!

The Silk'n Blue Acne Solution Device is one of many products in a crowded market of skin and acne products.  After a short time with item, it does seem safe and easy to use.  It can be time consuming and results appear to be positive.  Of course, only long term usage can really determine the overall effectiveness.

The instructions are easy to follow and using the device is simple to operate.  I will say that it takes time to cover the entire face (if needed), so that is something to keep in mind.  Covering limited affected areas is a little easier, but still time consuming.  It also seems a bit flimsy, so I would be concerned about its lifespan.

I personally have notice some improvement over the short term.  I'd be interested to see how it goes over the recommended 6-8 weeks.  I found it best to use in evening when more time was available, but it is supposed to be used twice daily.  It gets warm, but nothing too terribly uncomfortable.  I think it's worth adding this to your skincare treatment.  I still think other products might be necessary, but there has been some effectiveness after using the Silk'n Blue.
summary: Effective, with only a few downsides

reviewText:
This is a relatively simple device and kit. What you're getting is an upright charging stand and the blue-light device itself which is slightly thicker and approximately similar in size to a standard electric toothbrush without the brush head. Once the device is charged up (takes about 6 hours on the initial charge) the device is ready to go. To use, you simply turn it on and press the top surface against your skin.  At this point the blue light is activated and will gradually heat up (the manual says it can go up to 106F but it never feels too hot or unpleasant) as you keep the device pressed against your skin for 3-4 minutes.

Does the device work? At this point, having used it for around a week it's difficult to accurately gauge as the instructions recommend twice daily use on your skin and best results will take place after 3-7 weeks of continuous use. I will say that I did have a couple of early stage breakout spots that I treated for around 4 days and so far they have not progressed to a full stage breakout. I continue to treat the problem area daily and so far the results are holding up nicely.

The device has a nice sleek to it and is simple to setup and use. The surface area could be a bit larger as it is triangular in shape with each side about 1" long and so it will take around 30 minutes to cover the entirety of your face. Watching a TV show or reading through a book/magazine does make the time go by but you will certainly need a degree of patience in order to take full advantage of this product.
summary: Good results with early stage breakouts

reviewText:
So far so good. I've found the Silk'n Blue to be a really great alternative to both prescription and OTC medications for my skin problems. What I especially like with regard to that is that I don't have to worry about side effects and adverse reactions with medications, as well as allergic reactions - such as contact dermatitis all the way to anaphylactic reactions. I've even had paradoxical reactions and in one case with a pretty common medicine had Stevens Johnson Syndrome - which no one would ever want!

I feel very comfortable that I'm not going to have any of these reactions with the Silk'n Blue - I haven't had any problems with it so far, and I'm finding my skin slowly clearing. My husband suggested I treat one area and leave another - so I can visibly compare the difference. This was a great idea, so I decided that was how I would go about comparing how well the Silk'n Blue is working for me. (I will post pictures IF they're not too embarrassing!)

I like the warmth of the Silk'n Blue on my skin. It's a very gentle, soothing warmth, I've never felt any burning. The time investment isn't much more than applying medications, and I feel that I'm doing something both safe for my skin, and good for my skin. There's no smell as there often is with medications for the skin.

As I said, I'm slowly beginning to see positive results with the Silk'n Blue on my skin. I would recommend this to anyone suffering from hormonal acne (or any other type of acne).
summary: Great alternative to Rx or OTC skin medications!

reviewText:
This is not my first experience with light therapy.  There are red and green options for other types of skin treatments.  However blue light therapy is used to treat moderate acne problems, the blue light kills the acne bacteria while it helps tighten pores and decrease skin's oiliness.  Continued use will help less acne breakouts and reduce the inflammation of your skin.

Dermatologists and salon's use light therapy to help problem skin and sessions can run anywhere from $45-60.  It would be more cost effective to do them yourself at home.  It is time consuming, but you can easily do it while watching TV or reading a book.  Noticeable results are expected to be seen in 1 to 3 months with continuous use.  Even after your skin has cleared up, you must continue a routine maintenance treatments or your breakout problems will come back.  This has held true to my green light therapy for dark spots.
summary: Light Therapy Has Been Proven To Work

reviewText:

How do I measure the 3-minute time span? With a stopwatch? Do I need to keep watching the bathroom clock while using this? No I have better things to do.

reviewText:
Let's face it - no one likes zits! Almost everyone gets the occasional zit and lots of people (especially teens) get them on a regular basis. Some people are unlucky enough to have severe cystic acne but no matter what variety, no one likes them. Prior to the availability of home blue-light therapy units like this one from Silk'n, most home treatments involved salicylic acid or some form of peroxide applied to the face. Anything stronger required expensive visits to a doctor and often medications taken internally.

Light therapy has been used by doctors for various skin conditions for quite some time with good results. Blue light therapy in particular is very good for acne because it kills the bacteria that's at the root of every zit. The blue LEDs in this device operate at a wavelength of 415 nanometers. Additionally, this unit has heat which is also good for killing bacteria and speeding healing.

This unit is rechargeable and features an array of 24 blue LEDs on the head. Treatment is administered by placing the head of the unit directly on the affected area for 3-4 minutes twice daily for a period of 6-8 weeks and then once weekly thereafter as a maintenance routine.

You will notice that the LED head gets very warm - up to 106 degrees. This is a part of the treatment and it is not uncomfortable to me or anyone in my family but for people who have extremely sensitive skin, it may feel uncomfortably hot.

One unique thing about this unit from Silk'n is that the LED array is surrounded by a metal collar which prevents scattering of the light from around the sides of the head. I have a different light therapy device that does not have this and I have to keep my eyes closed during treatment on certain areas because the light from that unit is very bright to my eyes. This unit directs the light on the area being treated with almost no light leakage.

The unit is light weight and comfortable to hold. It comes with a charging stand that is keyed so it's very secure in the stand, even when bumped. It takes about 8 hours to completely charge. The battery is non-replaceable and when it will no longer hold a charge, the unit has reached it's lifespan and must be replaced.

After fully charging, to use the device you press the power button on the front and then wait until the green indicator light stops blinking and glows continuously. Place the head against the affected area and leave it in place for 3-4 minutes. The blue LEDs will not light up until it is placed against the skin. I like this because the light never shines in my eyes.

Move the unit from affected area to affected area, treating for 3-4 minutes per area.

While I like many of the features on this unit, there are some that are lacking in my opinion and should be included in later versions of this device. First, the head is quite small and thus can only treat a very small area at a time. This is fine for occasional break-outs in small areas but it would take as long as an hour twice daily to treat most of the face. There are units available with much larger heads that will probably work better for people with problem areas covering a large part of the face.

Second, there is no timer. I'm very surprised that no timer was included! When you are treating multiple areas of the face twice a day for 6-8 weeks, it can get very tedious. Watching TV or reading while treating is almost essential but it's a distraction to try and time each section. The other similarly priced unit I have has a timer. Hopefully, Silk'n will add this to future models because it's ridiculous, IMO, not to have a timer.

Still, the build is solid and I think the added heat speeds healing of break-outs. It's working very well for my almost 13 year old son who is just beginning to get a zit here and there so I think it's a good device for people with mild to moderate breakouts on small areas of the face. For acne that covers large areas of the face, I would look for a unit with a larger treatment head and a timer.
summary: A good approach to mild/moderate acne and break-outs

reviewText:
There is nothing that will make a teen wail "My life is OVER!"  faster than a case of acne and I think it really can do a lot to damage a Child's self-esteem.  It makes me sad to see adults with terrible acne scarring that could have been avoided. As far as I can determine eating things like greasy food or chocolate causing acne is a myth.

First I should remind you this device is not for scarring, wrinkles, dark spots, rosacea, cystic acne or anything else except inflammatory acne. Of course don't use on moles, cold sores etc. If you're on a prescription consult your dermatologist. If you have dark skin start using the "blue' more slowly.  They think that maybe darker skin types are more sensitive to the infrared heat in the device, and maybe they should get used to the device more gradually. They don't say so but I would think this would be a reason to avoid using on tattoos.

You should have some kind of timing device (an hour-glass egg timer works well) to tell you when to move the device to another area. Wouldn't it be nice if they could put a time reminder on it like they do electric toothbrushes? But the most important thing you will need is patience and determination.  You have to hold the device on each area for three or four minutes twice a day.  You won't believe how long three minutes really is. If you're listening to music it's about the length of one song (unless it's "stairway to heaven" of course)

Be sure to completely charge the unit the first time before you use it.  Be sure your skin is completely clean and dry before you start. They say it will take from three to seven weeks for the "Blue" to work but I think there is a visible improvement in as little as a week.  After the acne clears you will need to continue weekly for prevention of outbreaks.
