Additionally, this makes my face look extremely shiny! it's not matte in any way, even w foundation over it. Powder works, but I don't normally use powder.  If this didn't have the sunscreen ingredients in it, I would happily use it as a moisturizing and protective night cream (and just avoid my eye area). However, it's not working for me in the daytime, unfortunately.

Update: I used this on cold days (not for working out), and it works a lot better, without causing the problems I described above.
summary: Moisturizing and Light, but Not as Good for Workouts or Hot Days

reviewText: Love it!

In pursuit of truth, my wife is reviewing this product.  Nothing seems to work on my own leathery face, I'm leaving it to her to describe it.

The Obagi360 isn't the first retinol product we've used.  Usually, when applying you can feel it going to work, a slightly burny, tingling feeling.  Within a couple of days, you begin to notice the effect. Its a little tighter, a little lighter.  Within a few weeks, your skin looks healthy, happy and younger.
The only difference I notices with this Retinol was that the burning/tingling effect was pretty unnoticeable. I didn't think it was working until, a couple days later...  In short, the cream does everything I'd hoped without some of the side effects I've experienced in the past.  Nice job, Obagi Medical!
summary: Review: Obagi360 Retinol cream.  Exec Summary: Solid retinol solution, doesn't seem very strong.

reviewText:
Obagi was one of the brands recommended by my dermatologist which is why I considered this Retinol treatment over others. The packaging does recommend avoiding the use of this product if you are pregnant or nursing. It is a fairly small container, but it does not take very much product since you're essentially spot treating areas rather than applying it to your entire face.

I've used it around my outer eyes. While I don't currently have any deep lines or wrinkles, since I've entered my thirties I've started noticing an increase in fine lines. I feel like this product has been helpful for that.  Unfortunately, you have to continue using these types of products or the wrinkles will eventually return (unfortunately, that's just the nature of aging).
I have been using retinol for years but just started on this brand.  I noticed that it does seem to tighten the fine lines and smooth out my face, I like it and I will continue using.
Love this product. Been using this for years

I have been using this product now for two months. My forehead wrinkles are much less noticeable as well as the wrinkles around my eyes.  I had to start off with very little the first two weeks as it was a little harsh for my skin. I received a .05 and that was much gentler and now I can use the 1.0 as my skin is used to this product.

I apply at night only, and am very pleased with the results. This is a product that I can see myself buying in the future and continuing to use as I really like what I am seeing in the mirror.

I received this in addition to the Obagi360 System, (3 Count) which I have been using for several weeks. The system actually comes with a .5 Retinol and that along with the other products have worked well for my skin which normally can be very sensitive. After a few weeks of using the above system, I switched out the .5 for this 1.0 retinol not expecting much of a difference, but I was wrong. Within a day there was visible irritation in several areas on my face. I thought it might be a fluke and kept using it for another day, but it got worse (severe redness). I discontinued use of all products for a week and went back to my regular routine and my skin cleared back up. I then began using the .5 again and experienced no issues, so without going back to to the 1.0 I can only assume that the increased strength is too much for my skin. Overall the product line seems good, but be cautious if you have sensitive skin.
summary: Retinol 1.0 too much for my sensitive skin

reviewText: This retinol is non-greasy and has actually made a bit of a difference in my complexion.  It did not cause any breakouts (something that lots of skin products saddle me with), and I did not get any irritation (apparently redness and peeling can be common with retinol products).  It is easy to apply, and a tiny bit goes a very long way. There is no scent to this, which is nice.

The skin on my face is super sensitive at the best of times, and given that it's winter my face is super-super sensitive and so after one application I knew that I would have to wait until later spring, when there is more humidity and my skin could produce enough oil to protect itself, to try this Retinol creme on the fine lines I now have.  My face became blotchy and irritated and I didn't use a lot.

SO HOW TO TEST?  Looking around I decided that the back of my hands would be perfect as they look terribly old.  Hot water, sun, gardening, etc. has made my old mom hands look very wrinkly and 'decorated' with some sun/age spots.  So good subject.  I chose one hand, the left, so I could compare and contrast.

Dark spots -- This Obagi Retinol creme has lightened all of the dark spots on the hand I used it on, save one, the oldest.  I can barely see the other dark spots now,  and I'm pleased with those results.  I'll continue with the remaining spot.  Perhaps being the oldest, it's going to take the most time and effort.

APPLICATION -- I use very very little of this creme.  For one thing, it is difficult to get out of the tube.  But I'm okay with that. This is an expensive product so I don't want to use more than I need to.  What I use is several pinhead size dots on the back of my hand.  I then rub it in.  The Retinol leaves my hand feeling soft and I've experienced no irritation.

*One of the things you absolutely need to do is wear sunscreen.  Even in the winter I've been using sunscreen on that hand as Retinol makes skin photo-sensitive.

WRINKLES -- This is where I've been pleasantly surprised and kind of amazed.  The skin on the back of my hand looks and acts younger.  It has less of a papery, dry and thin old-lady look and it definitely is showing fewer lines and wrinkles.  Even when I flex my skin in an effort to make wrinkles.

SUMMARY
I tested this on one hand so I could clearly see if there were changes.  The test hands now look different.  The one that has had the Retinol creme looks younger and all but one of the brown spots is almost impossible to see.  Can't wait to bring the other hand and my face up to speed.  From what I have seen, this product works.

I had my doubts that this product would do anything that noticeble for my skin as I am getting to an age where the smoothness is gone and in its place I have larger pores, uneven texture and uneven coloring (plus problem areas). The bags are starting and the smile crinkles are there when I don't smile. I resigned myself to reality and aging. I have used many good quality expensive creams and gels that feel good but don't seem to make any significant change.

BUT I started using the Retinol 0.5 alongside the Obagi Professional-C Peptide Complex about 5-6 weeks ago. And while I don't have before and after (I wish I did now) I can't get over the noticeable difference. I follow the directions and try to use the sparing amounts recommended. I was concerned the first week of use because immediately after application my skin really flushed and then I got areas on my check and around the eyes that started peeling (a thin layer). I stuck it out and now I have neither issue. I must say, my skin hasn't looked this smooth and even-toned in AGES.

I had my concerns as this is a skincare product normally sold under a dermatologist's care and observation. I really didn't have any problems and I am sold on the Obagi line. With these results, I feel good to say that I believe the product I received is legit. The cream's not especially unique in appearance and fragrance-- a normal moisturizer type texture that I take care to spread out with 2-3 pumps of eraser-sized dollops. I'm very happy and plan to continue.
summary: Thrilled with my skin after 5-6 weeks of use

reviewText: I was pleased to find that this didn't irritate my skin; my skin is sensitive and prone to allergic reactions. I did not experience any redness or peeling while using the product. The retinol has a pleasant texture and is lightly scented. I was surprised by how small the tube was but a little goes a long way with this product. It absorbs well and does not leave any unpleasant residue. My skin did appear more even after regular use of this product and others from the Obaji360 line but it's difficult to tell what I can attribute to just the retinol or if it was using the whole system.

Good for the face, makes skin smoother.

Hard to tell if it actually works, but definitely no skin reaction yet.
summary: Seems to Work, No Adverse Reaction

reviewText: I use Obagi products (along with Ahava) as part of my go-to beauty regime. I love being able to purchase retinol products without having to get it at a dermatoligist's office or by prescription. I use this retinol every night before I go to sleep (after thoroughly cleansing my face) and I can attest that after using this for upwards of a month now, I see a major change in the skin under my eyes. Having been prone to bags and dark circles since I was a teenager (yea, I know I started young), I am seeing smoother looking skin (not as puffy) and the circles have faded and my skin looks glowing. Obagi products are not cheap, but in this case, you definitely get what you pay for.
summary: Another great Obagi product for my 60 something year old skin!

reviewText: I recently finished using Oil of Olay's retinol serum and I decided to start using Obagi's product form their 360 line.  Like other products form this line, this one is also loaded with too many chemicals and too little natural ingredients.  Retinol is a form of vitamin A and it gradually refines skin texture while effectively minimizing the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles. Some people are sensitive to retinol and can experience acne breakout.  Obagis Retinol features retinol entrapment technology which makes it effective yet minimally irritating. Ingredients: water (aqua), caprylic/capric triglyceride, glyceryl stearate, cyclopentasiloxane, butylene glycol, stearic acid, butyrospermum parkii (shea) butter, polysorbate 60, stearyl alcohol, glycerin, retinol, polysorbate 20, dimethicone, carthamus tinctorius (safflower oil) - safflower oil contains lubricant properties that prompt the skin to retain water and moisture. The oil consists primarily of linoleic acid, an omega-6 that is packed with essential vitamins. Safflower oil prevents dryness and roughness and removes dirt and oil. Its content makes safflower oil a key treatment for issues including eczema, psoriasis and acne. Its hydrating properties lend skin a healthy glow, promote elasticity and reduce the appearance of wrinkles.  But then again, if this ingredient so to precious and healing why is it that company uses the least amount of the product in the formula and upfronts the product with artificial stuff?
summary: Vitamin A with safflower oils and shea butter

reviewText: The tube is extremely hard to get anything out of. I have used this product for a week and my skin is very flaky and dry after using. I will be sticking with my usual product and throwing this in the trash.

Effects are comparable to Retin-A albeit in a bit more subdued and subtle manner. If you're coming to this product after a long spell of not using Retin-A you will experience some dryness and peeling but that is the byproduct of the formula doing it's job. Your 'new' skin will also be a bit tender and sensitive, initially, so if you're out in the sun next day you'll want to use a good facial sunscreen to protect your skin and minimize redness. The product comes in a small plastic white tube that contains 1 ounce of lotion. A small pearl is all you need to cover your face for overnight treatment so even with nightly use you should be able to get a good 2-3 months out of this.

I started to notice a difference in two weeks. I have sensitive fair skin and there was some peeling from about the third day to the sixth day. After that it was fine. I didn't break out, experience any discomfort, or rash.

The Obagi is unscented, which, for someone like me who really dislikes heavy chemical or floral fragrances, is a real plus.

A little goes a long way, only use about a pearl sized drop.

I've never used prescription Retinol, but for me this worked well

The difference between Obagi360 Retinol and the Retinol that a dermatologist prescribes is strength. Obagi360 Retinol is much more mild. The area skin treated with prescription strength Retinol responds by first drying up and then flaking off, at least that was my experience. The skin left behind, that which was uncovered, was new, pinkish, and the area was smooth or smoother than it was. This cream from Obagi360 Retinol doesnt work as quickly to produce results, but it does produce results. I can see a difference after morning and evening applications, daily, to the fine lines on the outside of my eyes. The lines are easily half as noticeable and Ive only used a third of the tube. I am hopeful that the lines get more erased the more that I use the tube, but I know that the cream will only work to a certain point. For now, I like what Im seeing and am rating it four stars. If longer use results in more improvement, Ill love this stuff and up my rating to five stars. Bottom line is yes, it helps ward off encroaching lines.

To be honest, I really didn't think this would work but I've been using it a while and I can tell a difference. I have some tiny wrinkles around my mouth that are real obvious when I laugh and since I've been using this, I notice they are slowly getting less obvious. I'm really pleased with this stuff!

I like this Obagi Retinol..I do notice a difference, and I have used other over the counter Retinol before.
Not sure Im using this right, cause I first put on my obagi liquid C serum first, then use the Obagi Retinol.
I Wait in between each application, then put on moisturizer.
Im older, and I can notice my smile lines, and forehead look smoother.

When you take the top off, you push down on the ball top that is there, and out comes enough for one application.
This tube should last for a long time. Although I do think its pricey!
summary: I notice a difference, and also use C seruim with this.

reviewText: I'm happy with this Obagi360 Retinol1.0 product. It is not as strong as my prescription .025 Retin-A of course, but as an all around night cream with non-prescription levels of retinol, this is excellent, and good for maintenance if you are not using Retin-A or only sporadically using it as I am. This Retinol 1.0 does not have the drying and flaking effect of the prescription level product, but just leaves my skin feeling very healthy and balanced, as if I was not wearing a cream at all. This has nearly no scent, and a little goes a long way. I generally use this only around my "problem" areas more prone to wrinkles, around the eye and lip areas (which I never do with my Retin-A), and this does not cause me any reaction, but actually feels soothing. Over a week or so, I do notice the need to exfoliate, and the areas I apply this Retinol 1.0 seem to be fresher looking afterwards. Overall, this is a very effective and high quality night cream, and the addition of the Retinol seems to provide a nice boost for maintaining healthy looking skin.
summary: Effective Night Cream, Makes Skin Feel Balanced & Look Fresher

reviewText: I really like this product but have to give it 4 stars instead of 5 due to the price point and the fact that it isn't as effective as a Retin-A product. With that being said, if you're like me and have very sensitive skin Retin-A can be very irritating whereas, because this product isn't as strong, it is less likely to irritate skin and I didn't have a problem with it irritating mine. You can actually feel it working, and people who have used retinol products in the past will be familiar with the feeling so you know it's doing its job. With that being said, don't expect miracles. It does fight fine likes and wrinkles and gives skin a more youthful appearance but you have to keep using it. It's not a face lift in a bottle. If you're realistic with your expectations and prefer a retinol product to Retin-A you'll like this product.

The Obagi360 Retinol comes in a tube with a pump dispenser that regulates that amount released.  A pea-sized portion is enough and the cream goes on smoothly.  I have sensitive skin and had no problems or sensitivity.  It causes less drying than my RoC retinol creams.  I haven't been using it long enough to see whether it really will remove fine lines and wrinkles, but it seems very good so far.
summary: Non prescription retinol from a high quality source

reviewText: Nice quality skin care. It goes on smoothly and feels good on the skin. For a non-prescription retinol product it works very well. I have had no issues with breakouts etc

This one was hard to decide on how many stars to give.  On the one hand I love the Retinol cream  ~~ I'd never actually used any before and am truly amazed that I can tell dramatic results between my eyes and forehead.  It works quickly, smooths on easily and is not greasy at all, has a pleasant smell and isn't crazy expensive.  But the packaging on this stinks!!  First I could NOT get the cream to come up out of the tube ~~ then when I squeezed to hard to try and get it to come up the top popped off and the retinol cream went everywhere!  Crazy waste, not good package.  You can have the best product on the market and if 1/2 of it is going to get wasted you can bet I won't purchase it again.  Need some improvement for the standard of product this is, IMO.
summary: This one was hard to decide on how many stars to give

reviewText: Is it real or an imitation.  I got this on a free trial and my wife was thrilled.  She'd used Retinol products with great results.  Before I went and checked reviews and found several reviewers thinking this is a "pretend-to-be-real" product, my wife was wondering the same.  My wife swears by Obagi but seriously questions this one.  Given the price point, I don't think she will be replacing this when it is gone.  Several other Obagi products seem to be getting reformulated and one by one she is moving away from them.  It would be interesting to know if these are REAL Obagi products which have been reformulated or if they are imitations across the line from other online suppliers.
summary: Not sure if it is real Obagi

reviewerName: the old lady who lived in a shoe
reviewText: Okay, so you know how some cosmetic treatments are coming in this little tube with a press top that lets a small amount out of the tube? This product has that feature. At first I was concerned that a bunch would squirt out, but nope, just the right amount. I placed a small amount on my face and didn't experience any issues. It is recommended to use at night and does the magic while you sleep. It absorbs quickly and completely and is designed to remove fine lines and wrinkles. Remove away my love. Take them all away. Make me look like I am young again. You better believe I will be using all of this product.

This just feels wonderful.  I haven't been using Retinol on my face just because of general not paying attention.  I have been using a Vitamin C serum booster.  I know that is supposed to be before moisturizer but just haven't been bothering. I know better than that.  I am 54 years old and know that my skin feels great because I have been using good cleansers and moisturizers consistently for almost 40 years.  Now was not a time to get careless.

My skin just soaks this up.  After just a few uses the skin around my eyes feels as soft as ever.

My wife and daughter love Ogagi products: This product is fantastic.  According to Obagis website, the 360 line of Obagi was geared for the 20- or 30-somethings who are trying to maintain youthful-looking skin.  I wasn't sure if this product would be strong enough for my late-40s skin, but it was, and it worked.  It is a potent retinol that brought a younger-looking skin to the surface.  When I first used it - for the first week, it stung and my skin peeled a little, but that is exactly what it should do if its a worthwhile retinol.  I noticed a difference in my skin within the first week and it keeps getting better.  Its lightweight and has a similar scent as the other Obagi products (slightly floral, slightly medicinal).  Best over-the-counter retinol Ive ever used!

As I have gotten older (late 40s now), I have become more interested in using retinol-based products to keep my skin looking healthy and to minimize the appearance of some of the growing lines and wrinkles.  This product seemed to be in the retinol range that was about right for me, so I was interested in trying it, and I have been using it nightly for about three weeks now--perhaps not yet enough time to see major changes, but I wanted to provide at least a preliminary review.

The good news is that I have not experienced any skin problems related to this product.  I know that retinol can cause breakouts, and I was concerned about this, especially given that I can be prone to acne, but I have not had this issue at all, so I was pleased.  In terms of improvement in my skin's appearance, I haven't noticed anything major.  It does seem like on the mornings after I use the product, my skin has a slightly more "tight" appearance--i.e., drier, less oily than usual.  But otherwise, I will need to continue l using the product for long to see whether I experience more significant benefits.

The major downside to this product is the packaging.  It comes in a small squeeze tube with a pull-off cap. To dispense the produce, you must squeeze the tube, and there is a TINY hole at the top which releases the product.  This process is VERY difficult, and it has only become harder as I have used the product.  This past past week, when I was squeezing the tube, the entire top popped off, and the product splattered all over.  (Note:  this has happened to other reviewers as well.)  The tube wasn't very fully to begin with, so it is disappointing to lose product in this manner.  Plus, the top will NOT pop back on, so now I have to reach into the exposed tube itself to use the product, which isn't particularly sanitary.

Based on my knowledge so far, I would be hesitant to recommend this product.  However, I will keep using it and will report back if I see improved results.
summary: Some usage difficulties due to poor package design and few noticeable results

reviewText:
I read all the reviews and was a bit concerned about breakouts, but so far I guess I've been lucky.  I've been blessed with "good" skin but have begun noticing some deeper lines around my mouth and between my eyebrows so that's where I'm focusing right now.  I do think I see some slight improvement which makes me very happy. I'm not looking for miracles, just improvement.  Yes, it's pricey but no prescription needed, and the tube should last me quite a while.

I wish it was fragrance free because I'm quite sensitive to smells, but thankfully the scent dissipates after a short while.  It definitely appears to be the actual product and not fake as some reviewers have mentioned.  Honestly, I don't know how the tube could be emptied and refilled anyway.  Yes, there are quite a few chemicals in this, and I am careful not to overload my skin with artificial ingredients, but I'll continue to use this if I see results.

UPDATE  03/04/17:
Well, I cannot use this.  After applying nightly for probably two weeks (per directions), suddenly I broke out in burning, red, dry skin where I applied it between my eyebrows.  Researched retinol and discovered mostly recommended to apply every few days to build up for sensitive skin.  Redness has not subsided after 4 days.  And because it makes the skin hyper-sensitive to sunlight, this will definitely not be staying in my house.

This does what it's supposed to do. I've been using this about two weeks. I'm definitely noticing fewer lines around my eyes and mouth, and the difference on my forehead is striking.

However - in the past I've had trouble with retinol products because of my very sensitive skin. I have eczema and retinol can cause that to flare up. But with this being a lighter strength, I thought I'd try it anyway.  The first few days I applied as directed, also being very careful to make sure I moisturized well on my more eczema-prone areas. After four days, I stopped using the retinol around my mouth and eyes as these areas where the skin is already thin were starting to redden.  After a few days, the redness went away, so I tried again, but only applying it every other day. This seems to work well so far, I'm still seeing reduction in thin lines but the redness has not returned after a week.

So my verdict is, if you've tried retinol in the past and had trouble, this might work for you.  Take it slow and watch your face closely for changes, both the good and bad ones, and be prepared to adjust your routine. I'm very pleased with how it's working.
summary: Better for my sensitive skin than other retinol, but still have to be careful

reviewText:
I have terribly sensitive skin.  I'd hoped that the very low amount of retinol in this cream would mean that it would be ok for me (when I was younger I could tolerate this level of retinol) -- but my skin still had a reaction to it, and I had to discontinue using it.  Oh well.  It did initially feel gentler than most retinol creams, though.

I am able to at least use up the remainder of it on some small surgical scars elsewhere on my skin, though (just not on my face or the delicate dcollet area of the chest).  It does help with that...it was my dermatologist's idea.  I hadn't realized before he suggested it that retinol helped with improving the appearance of scars.  I guess it makes sense that it could improve the texture and appearance of scars, since it helps with wrinkles...so that may be a good suggestion for those who couldn't tolerate it on their face, but have an almost-full tube of this left!
summary: Too harsh for face, but helped with scars

reviewText: I've been using this for 2 weeks, and it does seem to making my skin a bit more elastic and softer. However, I do feel that it's causing my skin to be oilier. As a result, I've been having increased acne break out when I was clear before starting this product. I'll continue to use this product for another week or so, but if the acne persists, I'll have to stop it. So for now I'm a bit ambivalent to the results of this cream.
summary: I've been using this for 2 weeks, and it ...

reviewText: If you have very sensitive skin you might want to stay away from this product. I use other retinol products without any problems but this one really made my face break out. I'm sure it works fine for other people, but for me, I'll have to pass on this brand.
summary: Made my face break out. Not for sensitive skin.

reviewText: Not exactly what I expected but it is nice

Its okay. My wife uses it and she tells me she doesn't notice any enhancements to her skin. Its a good skin cream but there's no changes in skin texture, wrinkles or freckles. Its real expensive and if it wasn't for getting this through Vine we would never buy this. I've read some of the other reviews that suspect this stuff is a fake. We won't say that but the effects that are on its enclosures don't really tell the correct story. With all of the good ones out there this formula lacks credence.

This is my first experience with Retinol. I am 56 years old and fair skinned. I used the Obagi 360 Retinol 0.5 for several nights and used the Obagi Hydrate in the mornings. You just need a very small amount of both.
I used the suggested pea size amount and I did not experience any facial irritation. I think that my skin does appear a little bit smoother, but the real difference I feel is in the fine lines at the outer corners of my eyes.
I am very pleased with this product.

While retinol is highly effective at  reducing the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles, it can also be harsh and irritating. Not so this product. It is a lightly fragranced white cream that applies easily. I noticed a slight tingle upon application but no burning or redness. I applied to half my forehead. The application area felt dry but didn't peel or flake. Initially I did not notice any difference but after about a week and  a half, the skin seems more slightly more refined. I had no issues with the container. The product dispensed easily. The time release formula does appear to be more gentle than other retinol products but it takes time to see noticeable results. I do wish it were fragrance free though.

It's hard to measure how well a product like this works, unless you only use it on half your face (which I did not do).  However, I feel a tingling sensation when I apply it to my skin, which gives me the feeling it is working.  Also, it does seem like my skin around my eyes (which tends to show age the most) is a little more smooth since I've starting using this product a few weeks ago.  I also use other skin care products and a regime, so I cannot say 100% it's a result of this product, or it isn't something my mind wants to see, so does.  I really like that there is a little pump that seems to dispense just the right amount.  I see from previous reviews it used to just be a squeeze tube that tended to burst, so I am glad I got one of these improved packages.  I'll update if I see any more results, but for now, it seems to be working well.
summary: Tingling feelings suggests it's working; pump dispenses right amount

reviewText:
Very nice product.  Expensive but then of course retinol is expensive so that's just part of it.
Several reviewers have commented that the packaging appears to have been tampered with but the one I received did not appear that way.
It is very difficult to dispense the first use out of the tube.  I mean you really have to push hard for the product to come out of the tube. Perhaps that might have been causing some of the issues.
I have received the results with the skin that I would expect to receive.  Pinkish coloring, some flaking and then evening out.
You can't go wrong with Obagi products.

This just didn't seem effective to me. I should have purchased the stronger strength but my mistake. Anyway I am not new to Retinol but I decided to give this a try and with most Retinols I have always had a slight burning sensation at first and with obagi I had nothing at all. I haven't had this long but long enough to know this isn't gonna cut it for me. I am back to using the Image brand at night .I have been using image Retinol for a few years and still get the slight burning sensation which is what I expect with good retinol. I do like other products from obagi and wouldnt say I wouldn't try the stronger strength  but as far as I can tell from this it's basically a weak moisturizing cream. I hate to leave negative reviews but this did nothing for me. Also the tube is a pain ,it's not easy to squeeze out at all. I wouldn't recommend this to anyone with Athritis in hands. Still may consider the stronger one.

I have used more products than most people... high end products and prescriptions. This retinol is very effective. My skin looked younger and had a beautiful flush to it in one week. It peeled but only mildly...nothing that would prevent one from going out in public. I used this cream in conjunction with a prescription bleach cream to remove discoloration I have and it WORKS!!! I highly recommend using this with a hydroquinone. Great also for acne scars. I haven't even finished the first bottle and already purchased a second. Great price for the product as well. Has a hydrating feel which is nice and does not have an odor. MUST wear sunblock whole using this at all times.

I have used this product in one form or another for over 35 years....it is the best there is.  Be patient at first when you start to experience a slight peel, which will soon pass....nothing keeps skin so good and pores so small and collagen so plump...in fact..ALL Obagi products just cannot be beat.  Do not expect wonderful smells and luxury containers....it is just the real  deal !
summary: it is the best there is

reviewText: I like it but it is very hard to squeeze out.
Great product!!! Won't clog pores.  Won't irritate skin.
2nd bottle. Please apply in the evening.

This is a fairly thick, cream conditioner and it has worked very well for me. The ends of my hair tend to get dry and I've been using this conditioner with each wash. I've noticed a big difference in how much less dry my ends are. It goes on easily and the scent is mild and pleasant. It takes slightly more rinsing than other conditioners I've used, but perhaps that's part of why it works so well. It was easy to squeeze out of the tube when it was full, but it gets a little harder as the product is used up. The 6.8 ounce size lasted a good amount of time since I used some just on the bottom third of my hair each time. I would go through it quite quickly if I used it more. Overall, it makes my hair look healthy and I'm happy with this product.

As I get older my hair has lost some bounce and smoothness and has become more brittle and difficult to manage. I have used and have been willing to use almost anything that would help the condition of the ends of my hair. This ORIBE INTENSE CONDITIONER has worked great for me. I started using it after every shampoo, but find that I only need to use it about every other time now. The smell is luxurious, with a slight spice and freshness to it. It only takes a small amount to the ends of my hair and then I worked it back towards the scalp. It is the quality product that I expected from ORIBE.  Granted, its so expensive, but this tube should last me a good while.

I really liked this conditioner overall although not as much as my  normal deep conditioner that I get at Costco. My hair was easy to comb through (and it's usually very full of tangles) and felt soft. I live in a dry climate so conditioner is a must. I got this product for free and after seeing the price of it on Amazon (at review time $49), I'll tell you I probably wouldn't buy it due to the cost since my normal conditioner is under $20 for a big bottle and does a slightly better job. If you have heavily dry or damaged hair, you might have a better experience and find the product value better. If this were around $20, I would say it would be a great value. Maybe I'm just too frugal...it's a great product.
summary: Great product but a bit too pricey for my blood

reviewText: I can't stop raving about this...in fact I've been trying to ration it because it's a bit on the pricey side...but it's worth it!  I wish there were more per container because I'm tempted to use it daily, but it seems to work just right if I apply it 2x a week and the instructions suggest as much.  My hair no longer feels "crispy" and retains moisture longer. Where this really shines is that I need to use less hair product to -style- my hair after I apply the Oribe intense conditioner.  The fragrance is pleasing but not overwhelming, and the cream applies perfectly easily, with a nice clean rinse.  The container doesn't retain its shape very well so I do wonder if it would do better in a bottle with a pump but it's an insignificant concern.  Really, I love this stuff but will have to stock up if there's ever a sale!
summary: A little goes a long way!

reviewText: This conditioner is priced as a luxury hair care product.  The packaging is certainly lovely and the conditioner is effective in creating softness and shine.  The conditioner works well enough but to be honest, I did not find any significant differences from the salon-quality conditioners I regularly use (Brocato/Redken/Matrix/Joico).  The conditioner worked well and certainly looked and felt luxurious.  Performance wise- it was about the same as the salon quality conditioners I regularly use.

The old Brylcreem ad, a little dab'll do ya, fits this product well. Just a small amount of this thick silky conditioner will get the job done well. I'm always amazed how the textures of before and after application differ. But not only does the hair become lighter and finer in feel, but the look becomes healthier and shiner. The medium sized tube has a modern sleek look, is a deep metallic hunter green shine to it; and is light weight, easily handled, and the cap flips easy to apply desired amount. There is a very slight perfume hint of aroma afterwards as well. I'm been using it for quite some time and haven't even gone through half the tube.
summary: The Old Brylcreem Ad, A Little Dab'll Do Ya, Fits This Product To A 'T'/Easy To Use/Great Results/Lasting Use.

reviewText: I had never used ORIBE products previously, but knew the name and wanted to try it out.  It is a very thick conditioner, and a little goes a long way.  It smells absolutely amazing, with the scent probably being my favorite part of it.  It rinses out easily, leaving my hair soft and shiny, but not greasy or weighed down.  I'm not sure how fifty dollar conditioner is supposed to work, as this is my first foray into this price-point, but I would imagine it should do all the things a drugstore brand does, plus make you feel like you are doing something luxurious.  ORIBE's Intense Conditioner easily checks all those boxes, and has luxury in spades.
summary: Smells amazing, conditions just as well

reviewText: I have color treated hair which needs some extra help to look good, by which I mean that I have to use rich conditioners and I am not one of those lucky few who can go with just shampoo alone. This conditioner has a very thick consistency, and reminds me lot of L'Oreal Total Repair 5 Damage Erasing Balm, by how it affects my hair. This ORIBE Intense Conditioner has a very nice pleasant smell, it reminds me of men's perfume; I do like it, and I think it would work very well for mens hair. I do not mean that it is very strongly a men's scent, or that women can not use it--I like it. The rich consistency of this ORIBE Intense Conditioner hydrates my hair well and makes my hair less fuzzy. I didn't see any difference by holding it for 10 minutes in my hair or just by applying and rinsing after just one minute. It works well for me and I am very glad I tried it.

I have long, fine, color-treated hair and am always looking for a conditioner that will leave my hair soft and manageable without weighing it down or making it look oily. So far I am impressed with this product. A little goes a long way and you can definitely feel it coating your hair when you apply it. It's thicker than regular conditioners, but not as thick as some other deep conditioners that I've used previously. I was able to comb my hair after towel-drying without any additional products and I blew my hair out. The top of my hair feels nicely conditioned, but the bottom is still more dry then I would prefer. It did not weigh my hair down. I would not call this produce "intense" but it's a nice conditioner and smells great.

This leaves my hair feeling really soft and silky for several days after use (and following a few washings). Hair is straight and fine and it might weigh it down a little bit but it's worth the softness. I love this product.

I've been happy with Oribe products and this is another winner. I have straight color processed hair. It tends to get oily, but the ends do get dry from blow drying, etc. The Oribe Intense Conditioner package says to leave it on your hair as long as you want and can be used daily. The conditioner smells great and you feel like you're in a spa with the fancy packaging. I left it on my hair for a few minutes after shampooing and it felt good on my hair. When I dried my hair it seems to give some extra body, but I thought my hair would be smoother with this product. Don't get me wrong, it's a great conditioner, but I didn't get the more polished look I was hoping for.

Daily use of a blow dryer and hot iron can leave my color treated hair feeling dry, so I use a conditioner every time I shampoo.  Although I have a lot of hair, the individual texture is fine and this Oribe Intense conditioner provides moisture without weighing my hair down.  My hair is shoulder length and about  Tbs. is all I need to use.  I apply the conditioner from the mid-shaft down and leave it on for 3-5 minutes before rinsing.  This product has a clean, fresh fragrance and leaves my hair soft and tangle-free, with plenty of volume.

Im used to paying salon prices for a quality conditioner, but I have to admit that the price on this product (currently $49 for 6.8 oz.) gave me sticker shock.  This conditioner works well for my hair type but Id find the price prohibitive.
summary: Leaves my hair soft and easy to manage with lots of volume

reviewText:
I've used Oribe products before, so was  happy to review this.  The conditioner is very nice.  Leaves hair soft, hydrated.  Was recommended to me originally from my hair stylist.  All Oribe products I've tried have been excellent.  Pricy -- but very good.  With most  you can use a little amount.  For the conditioner, massage into clean hair, wait a few minutes, rinse.

I have long hair that has been straightened; very thick and dry.  The de-tangling primer is great - and the Royal blow out is really nice (for some reason my hair dries faster when I use that).  The Glaze is very very nice also.  and shampoos.  Note: there are different types for different types of hair.

I have fine thin hair, although a lot of it. This conditioner is addictive.  It's light weight but incredibly moisturizing and helps we fight down that pesky frizz too.  I love the smell and texture of it.  Not's not heavy either, leaves little to no residue.  Highly recommend.

I'm giving this a neutral rating because it may work great for others...just not for me. It weighs hair down and ends up heavy, impossible to style and frankly in need of a re-wash asap. My hair is on the finer side and I suspect this would work better for those who have very course hair. Normally I really like this brand but this is the exception to the rule; leaves hair heavy, limp and unmanageable.
summary: leaves hair heavy, limp and unmanageable

reviewText:
The review addresses the packaging, delivery system, the results, and the price (for what the consumer receives).

Foremost, the packaging strives to impress the consumer. The cardboard box, while entirely unnecessary, insinuates that this is a luxury item and requires additional protection (hence a box for a plastic bottle of conditioner). The (relatively small) tube is ombre and thus trendy in appearance. Likewise, the flourish on the bottle's cap is slightly reminiscent of a Versace product. All told, there is an extraordinary effort to separate this conditioner from similar conditioners. This may speak to one who must have "unique" or "extraordinary" household staples.

Practically speaking, the delivery system has pluses and minuses. The squeeze tube allows the consumer to more easily complete the tube with less frustration. However, the squeeze tube crushes fairly easily. So, if one is buying this for the overall aesthetic, that's quickly made irrelevant. Likewise, the aperture of the tube is rather small in circumference. For me, this was surprisingly frustrating. I have long hair (about mid-back), thick, wavy, silky hair. A "dime-size" bit of conditioner is not going to provide the proper treatment. So, I just kept squeezing, and squeezing as the smallest amount of conditioner slowly, painfully emerged. Erg. And, for me, this container would be gone in about two weeks (of every-other-day use).

The product itself distributed with ease. And it made my hair feel even softer and even silkier instantly. I had high hopes of the a blinding shine! I let my hair air-dry and gently began to comb it. It was slightly more tangled than usual and required just a bit more work than usual. Nonetheless, the overall results were quite lovely. Shiny (not blinding, but nice), bouncy, silky ... but I honestly achieve those exact results with my favorite mid-range conditioners. Now, it does have a uber perfume-y fragrance, so that might be what distinguishes this from one's standard salon-conditioner? (But this is also a caution to those who have sensitivities and allergies -- the fragrance is pretty big and a bit "old-school perfume" in nature).

Overall, the results were lovely. Shiny, bouncy hair. Nonetheless, many mid-range conditioners produce these exact results. This seems to be more of a "visual statement" than anything else. So, I would simply caution consumers that while the container looks "pretty," the contents produce  relatively predictable results.
summary: Shiny Bouncy Hair from a Small Tube at a Premium Price ...

reviewText: This is really thick and hydrating. It leaves my hair feeling super soft and silky after using it.
summary: Leaves my hair super soft and hydrated

reviewText: Excellent product.  Hair is much softer

This makes my lashes very long.  I would like them to be thicker, but the length is great.

I don't get any smudging or flaking when I use this mascara.  None at all.  It's easy to apply to my lashes and the wand, while a little short, works great.  Also, there's no clumping!

I do find that it's a little harder to remove than the mascara I usually use.

I like this mascara a lot but I don't think it's going to replace the one I normally use, as I like fuller, thicker lashes than this one gives me.
summary: VINCENT LONGO Volume Plus Mascara, Black

reviewText:
I have been using Lancome Definicils mascara since it came on the market in 1991.  It's great mascara and I like the brush.  I've tried other mascaras and always go back to Lancome.

This is a very close second to my beloved Lancome.  Nice brush, goes on smoothly, doesn't clump, doesn't flake and looks nice.

Definitely feels like a high quality product.

------------

I've been using this for months, and love it.  It may replace lancome as my favorite

I tested this a couple of different days against a couple of competing products by putting Vincent Longo on one eye, and a competitor on the other, then going for a full day without removing it, during which time I slept, kept house, worked, shopped and worked out.
The first was Covergirl Bombshell, in black, which has 2 different parts to the application.  Vincent Longo was easier to put on, but after application of both products, I could not tell the difference.  I had a couple of small smears with each that were both easy to remove.  After my normal short nap, I noticed I'd lost some of the Vincent Longo- that eye had a bit of racoon-ness to it, but most of the product was still on.  I went about the rest of my day.  At days' end, the Vincent Longo was 3/5 of the way completely gone, so it was easy to remove.  The Covergirl Bombshell was holding strong, but it takes a bit of effort to get off with a makeup removing cloth.
The next day, I put Vincent Longo up against Lancome's Hypnose Doll Lashes.  The Lancome looked MUCH better.  It holds the benchmark to me of really long, full eyelashes.  Once again, after a short nap - this time with no foundation on - I'd lost a lot of the Vincent Longo.  By 7pm, when I left to work out, I had to apply MORE because most of it was gone, and I looked a bit funny with only one eye looking 'done.'

I'd say, if you want a nice looking mascara that is VERY easy to take off, and you are willing to reapply it often, this might work for you.
If it is really volume you are after, you can save some money buying the Covergirl Bombshell and doing a bit of minute or two of extra work to get it on and off.  If you want a higher end mascara, there's still lots of better stuff out there.

To me, good ol' $4 pink tube Great Lash has all-around better staying power than this product.
summary: Looks nice, but not as good as Covergirl Bombshell

reviewText:
I'm not one that likes the heavily lined and lashed look so many are doing, and was a little fearful about what I'd look like using this product. As it is, I only apply eyeliner and mascara to my upper lid and lashes. Another fear is that I wear glasses and having a smudge on my lens drives me nuts. Would this cause a problem?

You can put this on as light or as heavy as you want. Just add more strokes for a darker, thicker look. I suppose the more strokes you use, the longer your lashes will be from the fiber build up. Is that really any different than other mascara?  I don't know as I've never used many strokes in the past.

There is absolutely no clumping or flaking and it goes on a great deal smoother than the less expensive stuff I've always used. So I was immediately impressed. When touching the lashes, you definitely feel the fiber that makes them look longer and thicker.

One thing that really stands out is that it stays put. It doesn't say it's waterproof, but there has been no smearing or running from tears when reading a book or when in the rain. Unlike the other product I've used, this mascara does not end up smeared on my lower lid as the day goes on, and I don't believe any smudges on my glasses are a result of using this.  It's not at all difficult to remove when you are ready.

Would I have purchased this at a price so much higher than what I've paid for others? Probably not. I don't believe I've ever spent more than $9 for mascara.  I do like the look, how well it stays on and the fact that it goes on smoother than anything else I've used.  So while I can say that I like it, I'm not sure if I'd be willing to pay $25.

Amended 8/12/14:  I've had the chance to try out another brand of mascara that also promotes longer, thicker lashes by the addition of fibers to your eyelashes.  I do have to say that this mascara does a better job and goes on much smoother.

I liked the color. My lashes looked longer and thicker. Unlike some mascaras, it didn't make my lashes hard. Washing it off was relatively easy and I didn't lose any lashes in the process.

4 STARS: Though my lashes looked great, it was nothing extraordinary. At this price point, I would hope to be blown away by the results.

I loved this mascara! It's creamy, rich,  did not clump, and  did not my eyes itch. There is a very, very  light fragrance. I only wish the brush was fuller with more bristles; I have thin, short eyelashes that need all the help they can get.
summary: Love the mascara but wish the brush was fuller

reviewText: While I love Vincent Longo's Water Canvas foundation, I don't care much for his mascara. I have long lashes, but they are getting a little sparse in my late 40's. I don't see any added volume over my usual mascara, Borghese Superiore State-of-the-Art Waterproof Macara, Black, 0.3 Ounce. There are silk fibers that add some volume, but they also look a little funky if they end up near the end of your lashes. So far, I've not noticed any clumping or flaking, but neither does the Borghese for less money. My lashes also feel softer with the Borghese mascara. This is removable with soap & water.
summary: Not much different from others I've used

reviewText:
Being born blonde is both a blessing and a curse.  A blessing because you have the most fabulous hair color and a curse because you have wispy, pale eyelashes.  I've been searching for the perfect mascara that would transform my lashes from wispy to wonderful.  I've tried them all - Lancome, Cover Girl, Rimmel, MAC, Dior.  My extensive and exhausting market search has lead me to two products:  Younique's 3D Fiber Lashes and Vincent Longo Volume Plus.  The former is actually two products (a gel mascara and fiber lashes) and works ah-maz-ing-ly.  The latter delivers almost (but not quite) the same results but with one less step.

I liked this mascara.  I really did.  It's a good color (even for a pale blonde), goes on easily, and washes off with relative ease.  I would buy this mascara again - if they lowered the price.  At $25 though, I would choose Younique's 3D Fiber Lashes of Longo.  If I am going to shell out the lash cash, I want to see BIG results.

Here's a link to the other product:  is [...]
summary: I'm ready for my close-up, Mr. DeMille

reviewText:
I've used all kinds of mascara, everything from Wet'N'Wild to Covergirl to Loreal, etc., and I think the Vincent Longo mascara isn't any better than the Wet'N"Wild brand. I didn't like the way it felt, and I didn't think it looked any different.

I will be sticking with my Loreal Volumizing mascara instead.

I was excited to try this mascara, but I wasn't too thrilled with the product. The application of the mascara was great: it went on smooth and initially looked very nice, but it started to clump almost immediately! I spent literally fifteen minutes trying to fix the clumpy mess that resulted. I also notice that this mascara was very flaky: flakes were falling all over my face, causing me to have to re-do part of my makeup. On the plus side: the applicator is a great size (not too big, not too small), it has a pleasant smell, and the packaging is pretty. Personally, I'll stick to my $7 Covergirl mascara any day before I would purchase this product again.

I liked this.  I didn't love it.  If I pay $25.00 for a mascara, you better believe I would love it. I usually buy Boots mascara at the local Target.

I have sparse, skimpy eyelashes.  I have problems with allergic reactions so it was with a great deal of trepidation that I tried this.  I used it for a week at work (I work in school).  The weather fluctuated between cold (36 F) to warm (75 F).  It rained and it was windy and sunny.

It didn't cause any reactions.  The volume was there and the color was consistent.  Removal at night was a breeze.

The reason it didn't get 5 stars was because around 3:00 p.m. I would catch a look in a mirror and I had raccoon eyes.  The wind and rain made me look like I had two black eyes.

Aiding me in this review is my lovely assistant, my Significant Other, who tried the product on her lovely blue eyes and reported: It goes on very easily, even with the first application which is not always the case . It stays on well and doesn't flake off during the day. I like the packaging too - it's a good size for a purse or pocket. It is the first higher end mascara that I have tried that is actually worth the price.

My opinion is that it looks Wowza!, but I may be biased here.

On the plus side: this mascara goes on neatly, doesn't clump and has good staying power.  It's also fairly easy to remove.
However: it doesn't seem to thicken or lengthen my lashes at all.  There is nothing dramatic about this mascara.  I wouldn't consider switching to this from any drugstore brand.

This has been a really nice mascara, the greatest thing about it being the lack of clumps.  The tube feels a smidge small, but it and the wand are excellently designed.  Excess mascara is pulled from the wand as it's pulled from the tube, leaving you just the right amount to dress up your eyes without ugly clumps.  Lack of clumping and an excellent wand give wonderfully separated lashes.

Layers well (but additional layers aren't really necessary).

Wears long!  Lasts to end of day.

However, I did have to deduct one star for both price (too high) and because of occasional flaking (still rare, but more common than with many other mascaras, and flakes are quite painful in the eye!).  Also, since this (Excellent) formula is somewhat dryer than other mascaras, I wonder about the shelf life of the mascara?

I would buy again, but only on sale.

Vincent Longo's mascara is very nice.  It goes on smooth as silk and stays on all day.  At the end of the day, it comes off fairly easy, which I like.  I didn't clump, a big plus.  But the price!  I use a bargain brand - Maybelline Full 'N Soft Mascara, and I love it because my results are the same for $5 stick vs $25 one.

The first time I used this, I loved it. I was just using a fast swipe as I ran out the door and was really digging the brush. Smooth and natural looking without being naked of mascara. I like to go between natural and drag queen usually, not way overdone and noticeable but not just one coat. I usually like two, with a good wiggle at the base of the lashes for good separation. I hate clumps and flaking. Unfortunately, on the 2nd application I wasn't as happy. I waited maybe 30 seconds before my 2nd coat and it turned into a clumpy, what the heck just happened mess. I don't ever do a dry second coat, it doesn't look natural to me. So this was very aggravating.  I had to remove one eye completely and start over. I feel like maybe once I get ahold of how the formula works this is a nice mascara. But there should have to be a learning curve for a mascara of this price. I actually still prefer the covergirl flamed out mascara over this.

I've been using this mascara for a few weeks now and I think it's "nice".  It goes on smoothly and has staying power but cleans off quite easily when you want it to.  I liked that it didn't clump when I was applying it and seemed to build some length without looking too funky.

I usually use one of the standard makeup brands that cost around $8 so I was hoping to be more impressed.  I haven't used it long enough to know if it's actually better for my lashes than any of the others, but they did seem to remain more supple after applying it.  I'll withhold final judgement for a later time but I don't think I'd pay the $25 price that they're asking right now.

This is a very high quality eye cream best used for aging skin. It is meant to be used in conjunction with other facial beauty product and not as a stand alone treatment.

This eye cream is a thickish white cream that glides on smoothly on to the under eye area. There is a slight, unobjectionable fragrance that dissipates quickly.

A single pump is enough to produce enough product for both under eyes. Just a little of this product goes a long way.

In addition to the moisturizing component, there is a subtle puffing reaction to this cream that smooths out the area and reduces the look of fine lines and uneven texture of the skin. I did not find this to be a permanent solution, however. The crepey texture returned when I discontinued the use of this product. Whether this eye cream will have more long lasting results remains to be seen.

I actually like this eye cream better than the matching facial moisturizer.  This eye cream is quite light to the touch (whereas the whole face moisturizer is quite heavy).  It doesn't sting my eye area, which some eye creams do.  The cream is unscented and comes in a pump bottle.  The bottle is tall and thin, like a roll-on perfume shape.  I'm not someone who is wholly convinced that I need a separate eye cream.  I don't notice much difference in my eye area between eye cream and a regular face moisturizer.  For that reason, I'm not sure I'd purchase this.  That said, if you are someone who definitely wants a separate eye cream, this is a nice one.

I have difficulty finding the best eye cream on the market that will have all the right ingredients to fight the signs of aging and at the same time not irritate my eyes.  Last time I used Image skin care for eye area and had to resort to using it only at night before sleep because my eyes would get irritated and I would cry constantly.  During the day, my eye were red and irritated not to mention that my make up was completely ruined.

This product comes in a very convenient packaging.  Eye cream is stored in a slim pencil like container.  It is a rich cream that has many healing ingredients that will fight wrinkles and discoloration around the eyes: water (aqua), methyl glucose sesquistearate (emolient and sufactant), octyldodecyl myristate (fatty acid), caprylic/capric triglyceride (a mixed  A mixed triester derived from coconut oil and glycerin that serves as emolient emollient, dispersing agent and solvent), glycerin, saccharide isomerate (water-binding agent and emollient that contains natural carbohydrates found in the stratum corneum of human skin), methyl glucose sesquistearate (which  functions as a skin-softening agent and emollient), lactobacillus ferment (a genus of bacteria that is heralded for its use as a probiotic - Good bacteria that feeds on sugar and starch, generating lactic acid. This process not only preserves, but creates B-vitamins, probiotics, Omega-3 fatty acids, beneficial enzymesmaking food more nutrient-dense than in its unfermented state).

All in all safe and effective cream with plenty emollients that will keep skin moisturized at all times.
summary: Rich eye cream that will protect and moisturize

reviewText:
I think the words "Ultra-Rich" in the title of this eye cream are a bit rich (dumb pun intended). I find this eye cream, although rich and thick-feeling when dispensed, sinks in quickly when applied, and leaves barely a trace. This is great for someone like me--who is 32 with oily skin, and very slight crow's feet creeping in--I would rather not have an "Ultra-Rich" eye cream. When I think "Ultra-Rich", I think something similar to Kiehl's Creamy Avocado Eye Treatment (which I swear never completely sinks in). So, I personally believe the title to be slightly misleading.

With that said, I am really enjoying this eye cream and will be sad when I run out. I LOVE the vacuum pump packaging--so hygienic. I also love how quickly the cream sinks in, and how I can apply concealer straight away without worrying about creasing. However, I don't think this eye cream is special enough to pay over a hundred dollars for another tube. It didn't make big, marked improvement over time. I have been using it every day for over a month.

Perhaps I view this eye cream in a critical light simply because it is a medical grade brand. I typically hold medical grade brands to a higher standard. They often perform better because of better ingredients and higher concentrations of effective ingredients. But for a medical grade skincare brand, I simply do not think it's worth the price. Now, if it were $50....I would definitely buy another tube ;) I do prefer it over Bobbi Brown Hydrating Eye Cream (my old reliable), but Bobbi Brown is half the cost for the same amount of product. If I catch a good sale, I will buy another tube ;) I like it enough to use it daily since receiving it (and I am not one to use something for the sake of "using it up").
summary: I'd Buy it Over and Over Again--if it were Half the Price

reviewText:
I took this eye cream to the beach, and was really happy with how it performed.  It's rich, but was absorbed quickly.  I used it at night only, because I'm tired of day creams dissolving my eye makeup.  After using a pump or two around my eyes at night, I noticed that the skin around my eyes looked thicker in the morning, my makeup went on smoother, and I didn't need as much concealer.  Win!

Yes, I received this for free, but I will buy more.  It's good stuff!

The wife has tried this, she really likes it, helps hide those lines, however compared to her lower priced moisturizer, she doesn't really notice much difference. She really likes the Obagi products, but she would most not likely buy this again due to the high price.

I gave this a two week trial before this review to give it a genuine test.  It is ultra rich for sure, and felt good around my eyes. Didn't sting if it got into my eyes when I slept on my pillow.

The package is larger than many eye creams.  It had no obnoxious fragrance.

It felt good. Here's what I found: it seemed to work better on the eye puffiness above my eye, rather than helping the circles under my eye.  I can't imagine buying two different products for such areas in close proximity.  The Clinique salesperson insisted I needed two, one for under eye and one for lid, and at over $50 that as just nuts. I don't have that kind of time or money.

I used this on both.  But the results, as I said, were more effective on puffiness.  I noticed too that if I put it on in the morning, it didn't give me any trouble (pilling or such) when I put on primer and foundation. It also didn't conflict with my shadow primer.  So many primers!

I would give this five stars if I had seen benefits on my under eye area, which aren't genetic but related to exhaustion.
summary: Good product, but not a cure-all

reviewText:
Gentle & hydrating, this moisturizer is creamy (not at all oily) and absorbs quickly & it really does improve the appearance of the fine lines around my eyes.
Rather than being in a tube, this eye cream comes in a pump.  One pump dispenses a little more than I need for both eyes.  I use the excess above my lips to help minimize the lines that come with age.
I am able to apply makeup soon after applying the cream and don't have any problems with  eye shadow 'creasing' on my lid.
 This eye cream helps with the fine lines around my eyes & gives my eyes a more youthful look.
(I'm a senior citizen)
summary: Creamy but not oily, Very Hydrating, Gentle & Absorbs Quickly. Gives my eyes a more youthful look. Pump Dispenser.

reviewText: I have used Obagi products in the past and was very happy with them. This eye cream really does help reduce fine lines around the eyes.  I was also surprised that it smoothed out the area below my eyes which have lost fullness as I age.  That area doesn't appear as sunken in now.  The pump provides an easy way to get out just the right amount for application.  I wish more products incorporated a system like this.  Yes, these products are expensive but until recently, they could only be purchased at a doctor's office.  I did have eyelid surgery twenty years ago and use a more expensive cream around my eyes to keep that area in good shape.

Works very well at diminishing fine lines and moderate deep wrinkles.  Also does a good job of hydrating crepe eyelids.  As far as dark circles and bags go, this cream comes up short.  So, based on your eye issues, this cream will either be the greatest or a complete waste of money.
summary: Great for wrinkles but not for bags and dark circles

reviewText: My dermatologist recommends the Obagi line of skin care products, and I have used (and loved) their toner for years.  So I was happy to have the opportunity to review the Rejuvenation eye cream.  It is a wonderful moisturizer, feeling cool and comfortable when you apply it--I'm not sure if mint is one of the ingredients, but it had a cool refreshing feel to it as if it contained mint.  While I'm not sure it had a significant effect on the appearance of the wrinkles around my eyes, it felt so good I didn't care.  :)
summary: Cool and refreshing moisturizer for eyes

reviewText: I have used many, many high end eye creams and the "OBAGI" creams and lotions are my favorite brand. It contains 0.5 oz and is on the expensive side for the amount that you are getting, but it has a pump dispenser that gives you the exact amount that you need for both eyes. It lasts much longer than other lotions that have more product for the money. It goes on very smooth and does not have a scent. My skin is very sensitive, especially around my eyes and "OBAGI" never irritates my skin. I personally like the small tube size which is perfect for traveling through airports without the heavy weight and size of many other creams.  I look for a product that goes on smooth and keep my skin soften.  Short of Botox or surgery I have not found a miracle cream, but it absorbs into the skin quickly and doesn't accentuate the lines around my eyes by make-up settling in the creases. The lotion feels very creamy out of the bottle, but I have no problems applying make-up right afterwards because of how quickly it absorbs into the skin. I also use it at night after washing my face and it does not take away from that clean, fresh feel like some greasy creams do.  I like it and think that it is worth a try.
summary: I like it, but the price should REALLY be a lot lower

reviewText:
This is a nice eye cream that does a good job hydrating the skin under your eyes.  You can feel it working - a soft little tingle and a slightly cool sensation tell you that it's doing something.  The dispenser actually dispenses a bit too much - and it's hard to get a smaller amount dispensed - the pump is a little stiff and seems to dispense the same amount, regardless.

What gets dispensed is more than enough to cover my under eye area.  I use the leftovers around the outside of my mouth, the other area on me that has a host of those tiny little lines that are mostly just begging to be filled and moisturized.  The product does not have a discernable fragrance and is appropriate for use by men and women alike.  In terms of effectiveness, it does help to plump up those areas that have a little crepe or fine lines.  I've used it every day for a little over a week and I would say that the results are fairly typical for this product type.
summary: A nice moisturizer that helps lessen the crepe effect around the eyes.

reviewText:
The second time I tried this product, my eyes started stinging, and my left eye dried out as well.  I had to wash my eyelids to stop the stinging.  I will not be using the product again. If you do use it, be careful not to get any in your eyes.  Not recommended.

Will update this review after my wife tries it for a bit longer, as she has not had any stinging in her eyes.

02/02/2017.  After 3 days of use by my wife. she now says that she's having a mild stinging sensation.  I encouraged her to discontinue use of the product.

1. Given the expense of this product, you want to use as little as possible for every application. However, the pump on the tube facilitates getting more than you need.

2. It's going to take many weeks if not months to find out if this product has any effect whatever. If this were a cheap eye cream, I'd recommend taking the risk. But given the expense of this product . . .
summary: Given the expense of this product . . .

reviewText:
I think it would be very difficult, as a layperson, to confirm or deny the claims of this eye cream in regards to its cellular effects on the skin.  It's an expensive cream and there's a definite tendency for most humans to bias towards "this works" if we spend on it, so I'm just going to go by what I can see with my own eyes.

I did a test with this eye cream over and against plain old vaseline.  I used each one for two weeks, and checked the results each morning both with and without makeup.

I have pretty bad allergies, so my eye area has been getting red and irritated.  My dermatologist recommended that I moisturize the area heavily, and he basically said - "use whatever you want as long as it doesn't further irritate the skin and keeps it moist."  I ordered this cream shortly after.

On the pro side, it's easy to get the right amount with one pump.  It has pretty good coverage and it absorbs fairly quickly, but not so fast that it feels drying.  It doesn't feel sticky or heavy.  It didn't have any negative interactions with my allergies either.  When I applied makeup over it, I noticed fewer lines (due to the moisture in the skin) and the dark circles around my eyes were easier to cover.  When I didn't apply makeup I felt that over all my skin around the eye area looked less irritated and sunken.  It is unscented, which I appreciate.

In terms of negatives - this stuff is so expensive.  It's not very much product, and it recommends twice a day application for best results, so you are going to run out of it FAST.  I can't imagine having the budget to buy this every 3 months.  It also expires quickly, but if you use it as directed you won't even need to worry about that.

When I compared it to the results of Vaseline by itself, it came out ahead for application - using Vaseline around your eyes (at night only) is sticky, and if you wipe your face you can smear it around onto your pillow.  Vaseline doesn't exacerbate most allergies either, so it's a tie there.  The place Vaseline wins out is the LENGTH of time you stay moisturized.  You only need to apply it once, at night, to get the same basic visual effect that you get with Obagi.

Over all I'd say this is not worth the investment.  If you want a good eye cream, there are plenty of products that claim to do the same sort of thing and probably have about the same level of effectiveness.  This product is okay, but it didn't wow me in any way.
summary: A decent moisturizer, but small size and high price make it impractical

reviewText: This eye cream seems about average in performance to me, with the same level of hydration as (for example) Peter Thomas Roth Mega Rich Intensive Anti-Aging Cellular Eye Crme, 0.76 Ounce, but for three times the price for 1/3 less product. On the plus side, it doesn't irritate my skin at all. It hydrates pretty well, sinks in quickly, and doesn't leave my skin feeling at all greasy or sticky. Fine lines caused by dryness fade with this like they do with any decent eye cream, but I don't notice any impact on regular age creases. I usually use Algenist Genius Ultimate Anti-Aging Eye Cream, 0.5 Ounce, but was excited to try this cream because the positive reviews I've heard of Obaji products. Given the hype and price, I'm pretty disappointed and will go back to the Algenist or Peter Thomas Roth products. (Or if I'm feeling like I can afford a premium product, I'll buy La Mer's eye cream instead, which is the best I've every used but very expensive).

It is very moisturizing for the thin skin around the eyes and it does not cause any irritation for the skin or the eye. I am not sure if it actually improves any wrinkles, unless the wrinkles are simply a result of dryness. Other than that, it does keep my under eye skin supple and moist. With that said, it is very pricey. I don't know if I'd pay such a premium for a little eye cream that doesn't last me that long and doesn't really do any magic to erase my wrinkles. I could put the same amount of money into Botox and get a better result.
summary: Good as an eye moisturizer but very pricey

reviewText: My skin is prone to reacting badly to perfumes and lotions, so about half the stuff I try causes breakouts. This product did not! It goes on smoothly, has almost no scent, and does not have a greasy look afterwards. Easily absorbed, doesn't irritate--good product!

Absolutely amazing product.  I've long used the Hourglass primer, but this is great on my dry cheeks and undereyes.  No greasy feel, but just very soothing somehow.  It does minimize the look of pores and fine lines.  And it does not have the heavy occlusive texture of some silicone primers.  I have sensitive combo skin and I've had no irritation or breakouts from this.  It's my new favourite product.  It's also helped my foundation and blush stay put for an entire workday in high humidity

This Jouer Anti-Aging Moisture Primer has gone to my Top 5 Beauty Must-Haves after only a week of using it.  I love how this product absorbs into my skin and makes my skin feel smooth, soft and appears to diminish the fine lines around my eyes.  When I apply my foundation it is much easier and lasts all day long.  I loved the price point and felt like this product delivered more then I expected!
summary: Thrilled with the price and results

reviewText:
I didn't really care for this primer. It did provide some coverage and helped my makeup stay on with the help of setting powder. However, it my makeup started fading/rubbing off just three hours in. This primer also made me look paler. I also felt it was unusually thick, almost like a foundation.

That said, it does what it's supposed to. It just wasn't my favorite.

For the past several years, primers have moved from being the season's novelty act into a staple for many women, particularly those who are beginning to or already have wrinkle or dark spot issues. It performs the same function as primer paint does on a wall: it provides a smooth, clear surface upon which makeup can perform its charms.

Or it should. Some primers are heavy or come in colors that really aren't as neutral as the manufacturers say. Primer isn't a once-size-fits-all product.

Jouer, a line that's relatively new to me but which has some impressive products, touts its primer as being beneficial for its moisturizing and anti-aging benefits. Both these claims are new to me when it comes to a primer. I can say that Jouer does get at least half of it right.

This is probably one of the most moisturizing primers I've used. It lacks the texture of Smashbox's Photo Finish, which is probaby the gold standard in the primer department. That's because Jouer doesn't have silicone in it, the substance which makes foundation and other products 'glide' on the surface of primer and which prevents makeup from settling in and accentuating fine lines.

Even so, the Jouer primer doesn't noticeably increase the appearance of wrinkles; on the other hand, it doesn't camouflage them nearly as well as Smashbox or other primer. You might think that's because Jouer is less expensive, but that's not the case. Smashbox is actually less expensive.

Having only used this for a short time, I couldn't swear to its anti-aging benefits. I do see where, for the right kind of skin, this would be a great primer. My skin works better with evil silicone (let's not even get into parabens, of which Jouer is mercifully free.)

I recommend giving Jouer a whirl if your prime isn't giving you the moisturizing effect you want. You could definitely do worse (but then, it'd probably cost you a lot less!)

Ok I think this does help a little bit.

It definitely gives a slight glow, I think the peptides kindof fill in wrinkles and evens out the skin, though I'm not sure about long-term benefits or if it will eliminate wrinkles.

It feels nice & refreshing going on. It's not greasy but not very moisturizing either.

It has a mild lotion scent to it, not strong, but not totally odor free (a little bit like grandma LOL).

I definitely like that it has no added fragrance, no silicone, and is mostly chemical free. It's primary ingredient is shea butter. And, even though it's advertised as primer, you can use it without makeup (it's color-free, absorbs instantly) or even use it as a night cream. It's kindof expensive for a night cream, but as a primer with all these benefits I think the price is reasonable (currently $38).

Hope this helps - thanks!
summary: Not perfect but it does help

reviewText:
First of all, I did not break out in hives - that's the most important part, in my opinion. :)

You won't need a lot of this to cover your face. A little goes a long way. It feels very light and smooth, not greasy. It has a light fragrance, even though it's supposed to be fragrance free. I love how easily it smoothed onto my skin, and after rubbing them in and smoothing out with my finger tips, it actually makes my skin look a little sparkly... not in the sense that it looks metallic, but that there seems to be a natural sheen it brings out of my skin.

It doesn't, however, seem to smooth away any of my wrinkles... so I am not sure about the anti-aging part, and it doesn't really make it easier to put on my make up, which is why I gave it three stars instead of five. I remember years ago trying a sample primer from Olay - I wish I remember the exact model of the primer, but that worked like magic.
