reviewText: This is easy to use, glides on and covers blemishes beautifully. I was impressed by how it blended with my skin, even as it was covering and blending with a different shade of skin on arms v. legs.  I didn't think it would be so good, but this is definitely not at all like the cheap concealer you can buy in a drugstore. Really good product.
summary: Did a great job covering blemishes and blending beautifully with skin -- Very pleased!

style.Color:: 40W Medium: For medium skin with warm undertones

reviewText: This is a very good foundation stick to cover up tattoos or blemishes.  Goes on very smooth. Stays on well.  The stick of foundation comes in a large lip stick container.  Foundation stick itself is almost 3/4 across.  Does what the product description says.  Goes on smooth, stays on nicely until you remove it at the end of the day.  Nice cover up.

style.Color:: 40W Medium: For medium skin with warm undertones

reviewText: I recently had the chance to try out a few Dermablend products, and this is one of my favorites.  While I don't have tattoos or large marks to cover up, I do have veins and bruises that I wanted to hide when I wear skirts and dresses this summer.  This does a fantastic job of doing so.  I still will use my Sally Hansen leg products for daily summer use, but this is great to use underneath for darker veins and marks.

style.Color:: 40W Medium: For medium skin with warm undertones

reviewText: This foundation stick is really convenient and easy to use. Just a few swipes across your face, blend and you have full coverage. Even though it is just a stick it still feels pretty heavy once it's applied. I was hoping for a quick on the go foundation and this one feels a bit heavy for just running out of the house with. The color blended really well with my skin tone and I'll continue to use. But with the heaviness of this I don't know if my skin could take wearing it every day so it might be a special occasion foundation
summary: This foundation stick is really convenient and easy to use

style.Color:: 35C Caramel: For medium skin with very cool undertones

reviewText:
I ordered this to cover blemishes and redness on my face. It works perfectly for that. Always dab, don't rub because rubbing will only apply a thin coat that doesn't cover well. If I can't get enough on there, I will rub some on and then dab it with my hard concealer brush.

I like to use a darker color then my foundation, when attempting to hide redness, so this color works well for that. I follow everything up with Dermablend finishing powder. It stays on all day and provides great coverage. It is a nice, creamy formula. Dermablend is a high quality company and so far I have been impressed with their products.

style.Color:: 70W Golden: For tan to deep skin with warm undertones and a hint of bronze

reviewText:
This is amazing! I had a wedding to attended and some serious suntan lines to conceal. This was a perfect product to even my shoulder lines  and conceal the various tan splotches from a burn that peeled. I high recommend to anyone looking for body concealer.

Make sure you set this with a clear powder. It holds up well to long days!!
summary: This is amazing! I had a wedding to attended and some ...

style.Color:: 30N Sand: For light skin with a neutral undertones

reviewText: I'm a little torn here. My rating is probably closer to 3.5 stars. This does provide coverage, but the finish did not look as smooth as some of my other long wear foundations and it does feel heavy. I was able to make it work by using a mineral powder foundation on top and then a regular setting powder over that, but since I don't have a ton of things to cover, this won't be my go-to foundation most day. If you do need serious coverage, I could see this working well.
summary: Great coverage, but not as smooth as I would like on it's own.

style.Color:: 70W Golden: For tan to deep skin with warm undertones and a hint of bronze

reviewText: I noticed other reviewers commented that their stick was hard or clumpy.  Mine was not.  It glides on like lipstick.  Problem is, it doesn't provide full coverage for my scar.
summary: It glides on like lipstick. Problem is

style.Color:: 40W Medium: For medium skin with warm undertones

reviewerName: Gina Pera, Adult ADHD Expert and Author
reviewText:
Even though this shade is a little too dark for my face, it still covers quite well and durably a couple of red spots on my cheek and nose.

Well blended, it camouflages a scar on my chest and, when I've been clearing brush in the yard, the red dings on my forearms.

I like this type of applicator. Great for traveling and takes up very little space.

style.Color:: 30N Sand: For light skin with a neutral undertones

reviewText:
I got this for use as a concealer, assuming that since it was meant for concealing tattoos or imperfections or scars that it would do a good job on undereye circles. Maybe its formulation isn't good for that area of the face, but I didn't find this to be helpful as an under eye concealer. It was thicker than most concealers, which I expected, but I thought a little would go a long way.

I didn't want to downgrade the product because I used it for an unintended purpose but wanted to reflect that it didn't conceal dark circles on tender skin very well.
summary: assuming that since it was meant for concealing tattoos or imperfections or scars that it would do a good job on undereye circles

style.Color:: 35W Tan: For medium skin with warm undertones

reviewText: This works really well to cover tattoos. Yiu can layer it for heavier coverage. It actually stays on and doesn't come off when I sweat.

style.Color:: 50C Honey: For tan skin with cool undertones

reviewText:
Well, I can't say that I'm overly impressed with the coverage or the blending.
I used this on a burn scar on my leg. The scar is over 20 years old. The first pic is the scar. The second pic is the application and the third is were I blended the product on it's own while the last photo I dusted mineral powder over it.

Either way it is pretty sheer and I can't help but think that advertising this product to cover tattoo's is misleading.

style.Color:: 35C Caramel: For medium skin with very cool undertones

reviewText: Bought to cover bruises and spider veins from an injury on my leg. I picked what I thought would be my color online, but it's impossible to truly tell, and the color is darker than expected. I would recommend matching this in person in a store somewhere before ordering online. I put on two coats and it faded my bruises but didn't completely disappear. I needed to build up a few more coats to achieve complete coverage, but then the coverup was obvious because it didn't match my skin tone. So I settled on just fading the areas I was trying to cover. I like that it comes in stick form and is easy to use. I didn't know I would need setting powder and tried my regular facial powder, but it didn't work well. So I'm trying to avoid rubbing off the coverage until I can order the Dermablend powder.

style.Color:: 40W Medium: For medium skin with warm undertones

reviewText:
This didn't work at all.  Whether it was for a spot or a tattoo, it came out clumpy from the tube, and following directions still wouldn't work as it should or cover anything well at all.

Definitely not up to the quality we've come to expect from Dermablend.

style.Color:: 30C Beige: For light skin with very cool undertones

reviewText: I really like the stick version of this foundation for really high coverage. This works so well to cover imperfections on my face. I also decided to try it to cover my tattoos, to see how it worked. It completely covered a white tattoo on my wrist so that it was totally invisible. The large black tattoo on my foot was a little more difficult. I was able to build the coverage so it was completely covered, and set it with powder, but it did look a little thick over the area. At a glance, it looked like there was nothing there, but if you focused on the area it was obvious something was going on.
summary: I really like the stick version of this foundation for really high ...

style.Color:: 50C Honey: For tan skin with cool undertones

reviewText:
Firstly,  not the fault of the product but the color honey didn't match my skin at all,  so I won't remove points for that.  I will say that to use this product you will have to match your skin color perfectly or it will stand out like a red flag.  It would be nice if ordering online  to be able to order sample colors before investing 20 something plus.

I got this product  because at my age I have spider veins on my legs that I would like to conceal.
 The texture of the product is nice,  blends easily,  and has some moisture but isn't greasy.
Coverage:  It hides my spider veins well straight from the stick,  but when blended I'd say it's about 70% coverage.

My biggest complaint is that it accentuates my crepey skin,...but I suppose any makeup on an older person would do so.
 If you are older and that doesn't bother you,  it's a good product to over some coverage  IF you can find a perfect color match. It might fit the bill for younger skin if the color match is spot on.
summary: About 70% coverage for spider veins when blended.  Accentuates older skin

style.Color:: 65W Bronze: For tan skin with warm undertones and a hint of bronze

reviewText:
Dermablend has a great product lineup with some great camouflage blends. From heavy to lighter coverage they all feature some amount of SPF protection.
I really like the quality and feel of it. It leaves skin feeling smooth and is not greasy nor sticky. The texture is silky which is a nice surprise.
The coverage is excellent and a little goes a long way. Even applied to hands and neck this works well on most areas.
It has good water and sweat resistance and stays on well. A quick scrub with a good skin cleanser and water washes it off. You do have to put some effort into it.
Great foundation and camo. Professional strength is right.
I find the stick applicator to be very convenient and easy to travel with.

style.Color:: 70W Golden: For tan to deep skin with warm undertones and a hint of bronze

reviewText:
I'm going to buy this in my shade. I received this product for free through Amazon Vine. I knew the shade I got would be too dark for my complexion, but I really wanted to try it. I'm SO glad I did. It reminds me of the Max Factor Pan-Stik I used back in the aughts, except not as oily. To make it "long lasting" you must use a setting powder. The directions say apply the setting powder, let it set for 2 minutes, then dust off the excess. I did this and it did not budge. I typically use a setting spray, not a powder. But I will make an exception for this foundation. It's FULL coverage, and once it's set with powder, it's not budging. I LOVE THAT.

I love trying new foundations. I probably have about 20 different foundations right now. I've tried liquids, powders, cremes, aerosols...high end foundations I've special ordered from France, to low end drugstore brands.

Right now I'm on a quest to replace my favorite foundation that was discontinued about 5 years ago. The original Este Lauder Maximum Cover Camouflage Makeup. I stocked up before they stopped making it, so I've casually searched for a replacement since then. Este Lauder made a "Doublewear" replacement version of my fav, it's not as good, and it has very few shade options. I'm almost out of my old stock, so I've recently gotten more serious in my efforts to find a replacement.

My optimal foundation would be highly pigmented, full coverage, long wearing, waterproof, and transfer resistant. It can not feel like an oily/silicone mask. Plus, if it's oily or silicone based, it's just going to slip off---therefore not transfer resistant.

This foundation is what I've been searching for. It's not as lightweight as my previous favorite, but it's full coverage (without feeling like a mask) and it stays in place once it's set! So, yeah, I definitely recommend this is you're looking for something that fits the same prerequisites.
summary: FULL coverage. Stays in place once it's set.

style.Color:: 30N Sand: For light skin with a neutral undertones

reviewText:
I am new to using the Dermablend brand, but I have found that I really like it.  This is an ideal product if you are looking for full coverage.  I have some dark under eye circles and this make up did the trick.  I did not find the product irritating at all and really like the way this is packaged.  The stick is easy to use and a convenient size.
I do recommend using your finger to apply because it is easier to control the amount of product, if you just use the stick to apply directly under eye it is a little heavy.  I have used some powder to set it. The product blends easily and stays put all day.
I have not tried this to cover tattoos or bruises, but I'm sure that this could provide good coverage for those uses.
summary: This is an ideal product if you are looking for full coverage

style.Color:: 50C Honey: For tan skin with cool undertones

reviewText: I have light olive skin, when I first rolled it on, it looked a tad too orangey for my skin tone. When I smoothed it on and it looked good and I could barely see it.  I really like that the stick is wide and thick, so you can you use it on big areas. It was easy to adjust the height and it goes down easily. I bruise easily, so I rubbed this over the smaller one, smoothed it, and I could barely see it. I also tried it on the bigger one, I had to use a lot more.
summary: A tad darker than I normally use, but worked for me.

style.Color:: 35W Tan: For medium skin with warm undertones

reviewText: This is an excellent product.  I have age spots on my face, and I have tried several products to cover them.  None of the products I have tried previously have been satisfactory.  I am very happy with the coverage  Dermablend Quick-Fix Body Full Coverage Foundation Stick provides.  I am amazed at how well this product covers and I am happy to not have the spots showing.  This stick is easy to apply, and I highly recommend it.

style.Color:: 30N Sand: For light skin with a neutral undertones

reviewText:
I ordered this product to cover dark circles under my eyes and little irregularities on my face. While I am not thrilled with the texture of this product (kind of thick & heavy) ) it does a good job for that. There is a faint scent that fades pretty quickly, which is great. The color I received matches the one in the advertisement well, and works for me & looks as natural as this stuff can look.  It's a bit more pricy than others I have bought, but a small amount goes a very long way.

Overall this is a good, useful product. Does what it says it will do, minimal scent, easy to carry, and lasts a long time. Recommended.

style.Color:: 20W Almond: For fair skin with warm undertones

reviewText:
This Quick-Fix Body Full Coverage Foundation Stick from Dermablend is pigmented enough to cover scars, birthmarks and tattoos, as well as various other skin challenges.

First off, you really need to go to a store in person to find the right color for your skin. Dermablend makes a wide range of shades and the color must be spot on to get flawless, undetectable coverage. After you find the right color, you can order it online forever but the right color is crucial. There are many stores that carry the Dermablend line. I go to Ulta and Macy's carries Dermablend, too.

This is like a very fat lipstick and you can apply it in several ways. You can just glide it on or you can use your fingertips to apply ti or you can use a make-up brush. Different methods work better for different skin challenges so take the time to practice.

Do yourself a favor and use a setting powder. It makes all the difference in appearance and in durability. This will last all day without smudging or rubbing off on your clothes if you use a setting powder.

This make-up is buildable, meaning you can apply progressive, thin layers to achieve the level of coverage you need. Again, practice applying it until you figure out what works perfectly for you. You'll be rewarded with great coverage that lasts all day.
summary: Great coverage that lasts all day

style.Color:: 35W Tan: For medium skin with warm undertones

reviewText: I have a scar where I had a cyst drained. If I wear a low neck blouse or open vee type of shirt it can be seen a little so I thought I would try this. It covers it fairly well, not completely unless I want a dark spot there, but enough to where it's not as noticeable. I am now trying some castor oil on it and using my massager to try and make it shrink some. I'll let you know if that actually works. Since I've had it for 2 years, I'm not too hopeful. I'll be happy just to have it dimmed down somewhat and this stuff does do that. It goes on smoothly and blends in well if you get the right shade for your skin.

style.Color:: 35C Caramel: For medium skin with very cool undertones

reviewText:
It works well, it even covers tattoos. It's not greasy and it's specifically designed for acne prone skin.
Once it sets, it lasts the whole day without getting smudged, and it doesn't stain your clothes.
It's waterproof, i.e. sweat resistant, but it wouldn't survive a whole day at the pool of course.
It works best for covering "flat" imperfections like tattoos or varicose veins. It's not so good at covering bumps like acne or choppy scars.
If you're not sure which shade to get, just go to a big department store like Macy's. They'll help you pick out the shade and they'll give you tips on how to apply it.

style.Color:: 30C Beige: For light skin with very cool undertones

reviewText: It might cover light imperfections but this did nothing to cover a tatoo on my arm that I got when I was a teenager that I've been wanting to hide ever since moving to Florida, where long sleeves aren't an option in the summer months. It's rather greasy so it's hard to get it "built up" enough to cover it properly. I can see this being an okay general concealer and I love their other products but this definitely didn't do anything to cover my tatoo.
summary: Too Greasy and Didn't Cover My Tatoo

style.Color:: 20W Almond: For fair skin with warm undertones

reviewText:
Some of the features are as follows:-
1) This coating suits my skin shade and type well.
2) It hides the occasinal pimples or acne scars that I get.
3) It is thick and blends to the skin evenly.
4) I feel that it would last for a long time.

style.Color:: 35W Tan: For medium skin with warm undertones

reviewText: After having heard about Dermablend for many years, I was eager to try this product. I was disappointed. It does cover marks, but only if you use a huge amount. But if you do, you have this big weird patch of highly textured skin under a blob of makeup. Very obvious! Rubbing it in so that it blends with the skin only gives medium coverage. I don't know what all the hype is about. It's just a regular stick concealer, in my opinion.

style.Color:: 35C Caramel: For medium skin with very cool undertones

reviewText: This full coverage foundation stick by Dermablend is a great product for covering redness or skin imperfections. It is very important to get the correct color because that's what makes it blend in perfectly. My wife used this for redness on her chest and it worked great. It glides on smoothly and the coverage was excellent. For redder areas like birthmarks, it requires more of a layering process but the coverage is still above average. It lasts up to 12 hours and doesn't need to be reapplied it during the day. If Dermablend Foundation Stick is used first, followed with your foundation powder the result good. I would recommend this product.

style.Color:: 35W Tan: For medium skin with warm undertones

reviewText: Good coverage-blends well

style.Color:: 30C Beige: For light skin with very cool undertones

reviewText: This stuff works so well! It's thick so you're getting some serious coverage when you apply it. It's basically a stick foundation but in a size that works well for using it anywhere, not just the face. It will help hide spots on the skin, cover red areas and even lessen how much a scar stands out. I've even put this on over a sun burn and it covered the bright red skin. It blends easily with your hands, so you can even keep it in your bag for touch ups throughout the day without the need for brushes of sponges. Works awesome!

style.Color:: 35C Caramel: For medium skin with very cool undertones

reviewText: This is excellent at concealing.  I decided to use this on a beauty mark before a trip down to the swimming pool.  This blended well and concealed my beauty mark Perfectly and lasted hours even though I was in and out of the pool and hot and sweaty all day.

style.Color:: 70W Golden: For tan to deep skin with warm undertones and a hint of bronze

reviewText: This is by far the best foundation I have ever used. The coverage is something that you get from a high end foundation and I can honestly compare the coverage to Kat Von D's Tattoo Coverage Foundation. A few swipes with a large brush and you have the best coverage. It blends with your other makeup for a flawless finish that lasts through what you put it through. I sweat a lot with it being summer and this stuff doesn't clog my pores but stays in place and gives me full coverage all day. I love this foundation and will continue to use it. It works so great but doesn't cost as much as the other stuff which is great. Love it so much.

style.Color:: 30C Beige: For light skin with very cool undertones

reviewText: I used this one on my neck. I have issues with red dotting on my skin specially when it gets hot. So tried this one out. No setting time. Does not come off on to my clothes. Covers the area beautifully.  Wide like a blush stick and goes up like lip stick. Over all this is one i would use all the  time.

style.Color:: 70W Golden: For tan to deep skin with warm undertones and a hint of bronze

reviewText: Great coverage. I use it to conceal age spots and blemishes. It works great. It is easy to blend and covers well, without using the suggested setting powder since I don't have it. Anyhow, it gets the job done.

style.Color:: 65W Bronze: For tan skin with warm undertones and a hint of bronze

reviewText: This product would be pretty good... if the color looked anything like it does online. I am using a calibrated monitor on a MBPr and also compared it to color on pc. The actual product is both darker and orangier than what it seems like it should be. Even holding the actual shade up to the box it has much more orange to it, and no real bronze. We thought this would be great for a darker skinned latina with a nice rich tan... but alas no good. It might work well for people with spray tans though. It was easy to apply and seemed consistency wise to work well. Hard to keep going with how it worked when the color looked terrible on everybody we tried it on.
summary: Bronze is perfect compliment to spray tan

style.Color:: 30N Sand: For light skin with a neutral undertones

reviewText:
I wanted this to cover some fine line scars on the back of one hand and some discolorations on my face from sun damage.  I had tried every concealer I could find in both powder and stick format and nothing really worked.

This did work, but with a bit of a learning curve.  I either didn't use enough or used too much the first few times.  I did not use the setting powder as I didn't have any, but the concealer stayed in place all day.

I had never used Dermablend before, but had heard of it for years.  I wish I had tried it a long time ago, but I am glad to have it now.  Also works well under the eyes and on dark age spots on hands and face and forearms.

I really like it
summary: Works well to cover fine line scars on hand and on age spots on face

style.Color:: 35W Tan: For medium skin with warm undertones

reviewText: This quick fix stick offers satisfactory coverage where I need it. It obliterates red, puffy scars and matches up to tan lines.

style.Color:: 20W Almond: For fair skin with warm undertones

reviewText: I have several tattoos and sometimes I have an event where I do not want to show them off, so I use Dermablend to cover them up. This is a very thick makeup , so it really covers and blends very well. I would have preferred a lighter color, because I am very fair, but this color works when blended and covered with a powder. Perfect for special occasions when I want to look more "elegant". It also is great for covering up moles and freckles.

style.Color:: 35C Caramel: For medium skin with very cool undertones

reviewText:
This DermaBlend stick is designed for quick cover ups.  If you have to hide a tat for a job interview or you just need to make a zit invisible the stick seems to work.  I have some age related spots developing near my hair line.  Im basically fine with them but if Im dressing up for an evening on the town Id prefer to have them hidden.

The stick come in a tube like a lipstick.  It blends well and you can dab it right on the skin and then use your finger to smooth it out.  I  have sensitive skin and have noticed no ill effects.  I might also mentions, even at my ripe old age I still get occasional breakouts of rosacea on and around my nose.  This has worked wonders in hiding the Rudolph nose.

style.Color:: 30N Sand: For light skin with a neutral undertones

reviewText:
This lipstick size foundation works very well to cover flaws before applying liquid make-up.  Depending on your size I think it would take a long time to cover a body with this small tube.

Tap the foundation on then blend it lightly. Let it dry and apply make-up. Setting powder helps. The foundation last all day. Dermablend has a make-up remover which works great.

Dont leave the foundation stick in your car or a hot area. It seems to have a low melting point and you're likely to come back to find all of your foundation lumped in the lid.

style.Color:: 30N Sand: For light skin with a neutral undertones

reviewText: While I like the Dermablend Quick Fix Body Coverage I like the Dermablend Leg and Body Makeup Liquid Foundation more. Both products do a good job of coverage but the Quick Fix stick feels dry and doesn't go on as easy. I will stick with the Body Makeup.
summary: While I like the Dermablend Quick Fix Body Coverage I like the ...

style.Color:: 65W Bronze: For tan skin with warm undertones and a hint of bronze

reviewText: I got this in bronze figuring it would go well for my tan time of year. It's a lot darker than I thought it would be and more of an orange-y tone. I tried it to cover a tattoo - if you put it on and don't try to blend, it covers. But the moment you blend it at all, you can easily see the tattoo through it. I found it difficult to blend and it would need to be reapplied a lot. I didn't like this dermablend stick at all.

style.Color:: 50C Honey: For tan skin with cool undertones

reviewText: Pretty good cover up. I have an old black tattoo in a bad spot and this does cover it pretty well. I have to really putty it on thick, but it does work. It might be a little thick for the face, but it does cover up pretty well, it's a beginner 30 year old tattoo, very black, if it can cover that, then it can cover a modern colorful tattoo. I took off a star because of the weird fact that the honey color looks like my skin till I put it on and it was darker. but I recommend it for tattoo cover up.
summary: Honey is a little darker than it looks in the stick

style.Color:: 30C Beige: For light skin with very cool undertones

reviewText: Excellent coverage, easy to apply and long lasting. Doesn't prompt any skin reaction on a sensitive skinned person.

style.Color:: 50C Honey: For tan skin with cool undertones

reviewText:
This "Honey" color looks lighter than it goes on.  It has a very warm yellowish color.  It covers better than the liquid makeup, but it still doesn't cover areas with a lot of black ink well.  It covered red and blue very well.  Also, I noticed for my husband's arm tattoo that we really needed 2-3 different colors because part of his tattoo extends to his lighter inner arm and up past his t-shirt sleeve line, so the tattoo itself is on 3 different shades of skin.  My makeup stick broke in no time flat, even without swiveling it up in the tube.  I stuck it back in there to use though.

The setting powder really helps with this.  It makes it look much more natural once it is on and it helps keep it from rubbing off onto clothes and it adds a bit of coverage itself.  I found that putting on the stick, then the setting powder, then going back over the black ink with the stick, tapping, then more setting powder, was the best coverage I could get.

This is very heavy, and it stays put.  It does take a lot for one application on a larger area though, so for everyday use this could get very expensive.  It's creamy and it goes on smoothly, but it is heavy and I feel it.  I don't like it on my face.  I feel like my skin can't breathe at all.
summary: Combined with the setting powder it is the best coverage for a tattoo I've seen, but covering black ink is still iffy

style.Color:: 50C Honey: For tan skin with cool undertones

reviewText: This product did an excellent job covering up a scar from a curling iron mishap! When I wear short sleeves, it really does bother me, and this concentrated stick applicator really gave a nice layer of natural color to make it disappear.

style.Color:: 35C Caramel: For medium skin with very cool undertones

reviewText: I'm very happy that I tried this Dermablend Quick Fix Body Full Coverage Stick! I had a small but very specific need. I recently had a scrape biopsy of a questionable lesion on my chest (benign and normal, thankfully!). This has left a 1/2" bright-pink spot of brand-new skin which is very obvious when I wear a V or scoop neckline. Daily sunscreen still doesn't cover this unsightly, sensitive spot. But the dermablend does cover it 100%. It stays on all day with zero smearing. It also shields it from any sun damage, which could permanently discolor the new skin. Since I had great luck with it, I tried it on other discolored areas of my body, and it worked equally well. I am so satisfied with this product! It washes right off when I shower. I've always known about dermablend, but now I have become a devoted customer.

style.Color:: 30N Sand: For light skin with a neutral undertones

reviewText:
Color..Sand. Derailment full coverage makeup.

Beautiful coverage.  Color matched perfectly.  Easy to apply and when it sets up with time, waterproof, smug proof and best of all covers bruises,tattoos ... any imperfections that you want to disappear ..... gone!!!!

Highly recommend!

style.Color:: 35W Tan: For medium skin with warm undertones

reviewerName: the old lady who lived in a shoe
reviewText: I used this  stick on my wisdom spots on one hand. I put two applications to cover the spots but I would probably need to tap on a few more times to truly cover the spots. It doesn't take a whole lot of the product to cover an area like the top of your hand, but you do need to build on it to see the best results. I can tell that my hands do not match any longer since one has lots of wisdom spots and the other no longer does.
summary: great coverage anywhere you need it on your body.

style.Color:: 30N Sand: For light skin with a neutral undertones

reviewText: I loved this makeup. I'm only using it on my face but adds great color and is very attractive. Wow!

style.Color:: 20W Almond: For fair skin with warm undertones

reviewText: I do like this body stick, because it does an excellent job covering dark circles under my eyes, and it does a great job covering a small scar I have on my knee, but my daughter used it to cover a small tattoo on her wrist, and it didn't do the job. It goes on kind of thick, but it wears off during the course of the day, so if you have small scars on your face or body, I would say this is a great product, but for using to cover tattoos, it might not do the job you are expecting it to.

style.Color:: 35C Caramel: For medium skin with very cool undertones

reviewText:
This stick cover tattoo very well and lasts in normal conditions. I didn't test it during heavy exercise etc.
If you find matching color you're golden.
I'm not happy with ingredients, mineral oil and talc are the 2 first. I don't have any bad reaction but advanced skincare industry don't use them, especially for face. I wouldn't use it as a foundation on my face (the look was too heavy too).

style.Color:: 20W Almond: For fair skin with warm undertones

reviewText: This is a wonderful product that covers tattoos and any other birthmark you might have. It stays on until you take it off. Great in hot weather and water resistant
summary: This is a wonderful product that covers tattoos and any other birthmark you ...

style.Color:: 50C Honey: For tan skin with cool undertones

reviewText: Fantastic results using to cover a tattoo and a couple of skin spots (age type spots or moles).  Once a day seems to be enough in areas where there is no rubbing or excessive sweating.  If you're not really looking for it, you won't know it's there.  There are other products available for facial use, but this will even work there.  I didn't use the setting powder, but the box instructions indicate that use of the setting powder will provide coverage lasting up to 16 hours.  There are a whole gaggle of shades available -- shop for yours.  Made in USA.  A L'Oral product.

style.Color:: 65W Bronze: For tan skin with warm undertones and a hint of bronze

reviewText:
This makeup stick is helpful to apply on sun-damaged arms that can look unattractive and leave a woman feeling self conscious. With summer here, it's important sometimes to pull a pretty short-sleeved blouse from the closet and wear it instead of hiding under the fabric of long sleeves in hot weather. Only a small amount of the product needs to be applied at once, and it needs to be rubbed in carefully. Once it is smoothed on, it doesn't look artificial or splotchy.

Although it is not meant for the face, it works well as a contouring kind of blush stick.

style.Color:: 30N Sand: For light skin with a neutral undertones

reviewText:
This quick fix goes on smoothly. I tried it on my sister's skin, whom is of mixed race, and it blended perfectly... after rubbing it in. It was like using a highlighter, that's how smooth it was going on the skin.

This product is of great quality and does what it says it's supposed to do. I covered blemishes and pimples on my sis and she looked great.

style.Color:: 40W Medium: For medium skin with warm undertones

reviewText:
No complaints at all.
I have a couple of patches of Vitiligo and this does an excellent job of covering them up.  I haven't tried the setting powder yet but it seems to have plenty of staying power on its own.

style.Color:: 30N Sand: For light skin with a neutral undertones

reviewText: This cover stick is ideal for the facial scarring I sustained many years ago in a fall (and for which I should have had plastic surgery, but for being young and poor).  It stays on and conceals all day.  At least on the chin, where I need it, I don't notice once it's on.  The instructions advise following with their powder but I don't.
summary: Does a good job of covering a scar

style.Color:: 20W Almond: For fair skin with warm undertones

reviewText: I wanted to try this for some spider veins on my legs. Some are light, some are a bit darker. This worked relatively well to cover them. However, the almond (the lightest color available) is kind of an odd shade to blend in with my skin tone. It blends better when I have a tan. Otherwise, it just takes a bit more effort to apply it and blend it. It works well on some small sunspots too. The key, I think, is to really use a light hand when applying and add a little bit more until you reach the desired coverage, then blend, blend, blend! This stays put and doesn't wear off readily. If they offered more shades, I think that would be great.
summary: Some effort required, but works pretty well.

style.Color:: 35C Caramel: For medium skin with very cool undertones

reviewText: I've used this product for years

This does a nice job minimizing the occasional dark circles under my eyes. It blends and absorbs easily and is gentle on my sensitive skin. There is no greasy feeling and it stays in place all day. It has a flexible applicator that makes it easy to get the cream under my eyes, but I haven't been able to use it to blend it in all the way and still resort to finishing it off using my fingers.

I don't see much in the way of anti-aging as there are still fine lines in my skin. To be fair, I didn't expect any anti-aging miracles as I'm well beyond the "early signs of aging" and into the "visible signs" category. Rather, I was looking for a good, lightweight cream concealer to brighten up my eyes, and this does the job nicely.
summary: Lightweight concealer brightened up my eyes

reviewText:
My wife has been using this for a while and noticed a softness that she said was not there before. I don't know about the anti-aging part working that much but she says that she notices a difference and that is all that matters to me. Was not irritating to the skin which has happened with some of these products.

Will use again in the future!

I use this after aby serums and eye cream. It is more of a cosmetic than an anti aging product. It works very nicely. I was afraid it would be too iridescent and leave the eye area too shiny, but that did not happen. It makes skin tone and dark circles look more even toned and helps to hide these imperfections. The skin looks tighter and smooth. I actually apply it even a little lower than the eye area and a little more out towards the side side of my face because I have hyperpigmentation from sun exposure. This really helps to hide it and it doesn't look like you have any makeup or anything on your skin. Your skin just looks better. So smooth and more perfected. I really like this one. Similar products that I have tried were too shiny/iridescent but this one is perfect. It really makes it look like you did contouring and used cosmetics to change the look of your skin, but it doesn't actually deposit any color on your skin, so it doesn't look like make up is on you at all.
summary: males skin look tighter and smooth

reviewText: As usual, my wife is the "tester" of these cosmetics. She reports: "the circles around my eyes are not too dark, so my concern was fine lines, and even before ordering I realized that this is a pigment cream and that I would use it as a day cream not at night.  The shiny pigment is very distinctive and very reflective, and makes skin look more smooth and fresh. This is how it affects how fine lines look and brightens up the skin around the eyes. You can achieve a similar effect with different shimmery powders as you apply make up, but this cream you can wear alone; and I love the flex tip for cream application (see picture). The only thing for me was that the cream washes off too easily. Since we live in a hot, humid climate, and I play tennis and sweat a lot, creams in general melt off my face easily. In one sense it washes off easily, but on the other hand, its not sweat resistant enough. The cream doesn't have any smell and it also did not cause any allergic reaction. The color is pale pink/nude, with a shimmery effect. I plan to keep using it. This is a eye contour idealizer, not a preventive cream, but gives instant help to look more relaxed :) "

I've been using this for the past 10 days or so and I really haven't noticed much of a difference. My skin feels a little softer but that is about all. I'll continue using the product since I have it. I'll post again if I notice any improvement.

This is a light tinted eye cream (my skin is ivory/porcelain and it matches perfectly) and intended to reduce dark circles. I got it to try for its moisturizing and smoothing properties. For me, it works very well as a light concealer. It's smooth and creamy, and a little goes a long way. I can't really attest to its ability to cover dark circles--from reading the reviews so far it looks like it is somewhat effective. I am supposing that is in regards to how 'dark' the circles are and how much they require coverage. At any rate, as a moisturizing eye cream and light concealer, this works very nicely.

This product is made in France and come with a very neat pliant plastic attached applicator. The cream is fair flesh tinted and does moisturize very well. It is marked "allergy tested" and for "sensitive skin." Regrettably in my view it does not bear any indication that it has NOT been tested on animals so I must, therefore, assume that it is NOT a cruelty-free product.
summary: Under-eye moisturizer not cruelty free labeled

reviewText:
The first thing you will notice when using this is the unique applicator - a long, soft, silicone 'tongue' with a hole through the middle from which the product comes out. The product is a pinkish cream that tints a little and covers up bags and dark circles lightly (note: doesn't cure or fix them - just reduces appearance). It has a pearly texture.

For me, the problem is large bags under the eyes. Admittedly, I didn't notice much of a difference when comparing use on one eye only - both eyes looked the same to me.  Perhaps this is something that works better when not under close scrutiny in a mirror - e.g., outdoors or from farther away.
summary: Interesting applicator but didn't notice much of a difference - subtle?

reviewText: This product was too thin to do it's job.  My under eyes didn't look any less puffy.  I put it on one eye ,waited, compared  and you couldn't really tell I put anything on.  I did have high hope for this product but I just don't think it is very effective. On a positive note I have sensative skin and this product did not irritate it.
summary: This product was too thin to do it's job. ...

reviewText: The Idealia Eye Cream is part concealer and part eye cream.  It has a silicone applicator that doesn't work that well for me - I prefer to squeeze out a small amount and apply that to my skin directly - but that's a comment on the packaging than the product.  The Idealia Eye Cream has a slight pearliness to reduce dark circles, this works well for me.  The tint does make this cream more a daytime eye cream than as an evening eye cream.  It's too early for me to see if the product is able to address fine lines.
summary: Tinted eye cream that helps with dark circles

reviewText:
This reminds me of my beloved Caudalie Premier Cru for eyes, but at about 1/3 of the price.  It's first and foremost an eye cream for daytime.  It has a slight amount of color and pearliness to help mute dark circles under the eyes.  I love it.  It's definitely giving me the brightness I need in the morning without wearing actual makeup.  It's like a tinted moisturizer, but for your eyes.  Once it dries, it looks very natural.

The applicator is a little weird and takes getting used to, but once you practice with it a bit, you realize it's great.

At first I thought this was a cream to reduce dark circles and bags. I read further, so I realized it was more of a cover up. However, I find it doesn't really work well. Maybe for someone younger with less circles or bags, but for me I couldn't even tell much of a difference before or after.

The eye cream is supposed to blur the under eye and reflect light so it doesn't look as dark. For me it really didn't do anything. I put it under one eye and saw a little difference, but I'd go with a regular concealer in the future.

On the other hand it scentless and didn't irritate under my eye.
summary: Didn't see much of a difference

reviewText: The best eye cream so far. My wife loves this. Not cheap, but well worth the money for the quality of product . Highly recommend.
summary: The best eye cream so far

reviewText:
First you should understand this is not a cure for dark circles. I would say it is more like a concealer although it does have caffeine, to treat poor circulation, and moisturizers. You apply it with the silicone applicator and it gives a smooth, no-sticky finish to your under-eye. It dries quickly to a satin finish. It has reflective micro-mother of pearl pigments. Im not too sure about the anti-ageing part. It is  paraben-free. I'm not sure a good moisturizer and a concealer wouldn't do the trick at a much lower price.

Vichy is an LOral brand, made in France.

It's a little too transparent to do a really good job covering very dark circles, but if you have a minimum of dark shadows under your eyes, this product will likely work well. I like the applicator, and the product goes on smooth, not sticky, and you don't have to pull on the skin below your eye to get it to spread evenly.
summary: It's a little too transparent to do a really good job covering very dark circles

reviewText: I've been using this for about 3 days. It is light and creamy and absorbs quickly. It has light reflecting pigments that make the dark circles appear lighter, but it hasn't actually changed them. It doesn't help with the fine lines around my eyes.

Nothing ages a person as much as sun damaged skin. Living in the southeast where the sun is blazing almost every day of the year, both accelerated aging and skin melanomas are a constant worry and so I always wear sunscreen  when I leave the house. There are 17 sunscreen ingredients approved for use by the FDA. Fifteen of those are clear chemicals that absorb UV light. Incredibly, 9 of those chemicals are known endocrine disruptors meaning that they interfere with hormonal functions in the body as they are readily absorbed into the skin and find their way into the bloodstream. Plus, the effectiveness of those chemicals can wear off or be used up as much as 90% in just an hour of exposure so need to be reapplied. Only 2 of those 17 ingredients are minerals that sit on top of the skin, one of those being zinc oxide which is why I will only use a product that only uses zinc oxide as this one does, for both effectiveness and not having the possible downsides. Zinc oxide used to be a thick paste that was obvious and unattractive. Not so at all in this TIZO sunscreen. It has a slight skin tone tint to it that for me at least having olive colored skin blended easily and dries almost clear. It dries to a matte finish with no greasiness. It seems to be effective and has no unpleasant characteristics in my use, so it's become the only product I use. Highly recommended.
summary: Of 17 ingredients approved as sunscreens, 9 are known hormone disruptors! Zinc oxide however is safe and effective.

reviewText: Not the color cover I was looking for, the color is to light !

I am currently using this when I go hiking.  the bottle is small and lightweight, and the sunscreen works great when you are at higher elevations where you tan more easily.  I often have problems with getting a burn on the back of my neck or on my knees and this product worked great for that.  It didn't seem to sweat off easily either.

Its perfect for that, but this item is definitely not family size.  this is a single serving kind of bottle.

Clearly, the TiZo people went through some great testing and product formulation to make this sunscreen.  It worked awesomely on my skin.  But, there is a price for this.

I think its far better than the "average fare" you would pick up at your corner store endcap.

This is a nice sunscreen with just the right amount of tint to hide minor imperfections.  It doesn't irritate my sensitive skin, and it absorbs smoothly and evenly.  Very easy to add to my morning routine and helps keep my skin protected from sun damage
summary: Great sunscreen, with just the right amount of tint

reviewText: TIZO Ultra Zinc Tinted Sunscreen is broad spectrum, SPF 40, and water resistant. To me these are all important components of a sunscreen. I've used a few different zinc sunscreens over the last few years and most of them are heavy making them hard to rub in to your skin. Leaving your face and body where you applied the sunscreen looking whiter. The TIZO tinted sunscreen rubs/blends in much easier than I have experienced with other sunscreens. Since it is tinted, it doesn't leave the white residue on your skin. It does leave you feeling like you have something on your skin. I would say most similar to the feeling of wearing a makeup foundation. It definitely feels like by the end of the day you need to wash it off like you would your makeup. The bottle is big enough to last awhile if you are only using it daily on your face. If you do use this as a sunscreen for your body it will of course not last as long.
summary: Blends in easier than most zinc sunscreens

reviewText: Used this during our beach vacation, it works, no sunburns! I'm darker than the tinted sunscreen but it blended in nicely. Would definitely buy this again!

This is the first tinted sunscreen I've ever used and I must say I love it!

The coloring is the shade of nude instead of white as I am accustomed to for sunscreen. The consistency is like lotion. It applies well and absorbs quickly and doesn't make my skin look off in color in the least bit.

I feel comfortable wearing this on my face and it hasn't stung my eyes. It doesn't leave my skin looking greasy or feeling oily. My skin doesn't break out after this is worn.

It works extremely well when following the instruction of reapplying at least every two hours and lasting 40 minutes in the water.

It doesn't really have a smell to it so if you are sensitive to fragrances this is a good choice.

The price is a bit high for the 3.5-ounce tube you get. This may work well for someone with a higher budget for skincare products but it's just a bit too much for mine. I certainly recommend it though.

TiZO  makes it easy to figure out the use for the product on the package it states this is for protection. In other words this is not a daily facial morning moisturizer. This is a sunscreen that you put on when you know you were going to be in the sun and need protection. This is not greasy and it absorbs well. It has a matte finish. It does not feel greasy. It is labeled for body and face (both). It is a light tent. I have very fair skin and this is fine for me. The SPF is 40. This is a high-quality product. Rating 5 stars = love it.

This is an excellent sunscreen. I've only been using it on my face which is highly sensitive to the sun due to hyperpigmentation. Very few sunscreen products actually work to protect those areas and keep them from getting super dark.  This is probably my favorite one so far. It works impeccably well, doesn't sweat off immediately or run off in a white or tan mess, my face feels cool and dry while using it and it doesn't clog my pores. The area above my lip is typically the most sensitive and it actually tends to feel hot and sweat a lot and is the hardest area to keep from getting darker. I can tell that this works better than other priducts i have tried because i don't find mt upper lip sweating before the rest of my face and i do not see it getting noticeably darker than the rest of the dark spot areas. I would pay whatever I have to, to get this protection and keep me from getting more and darker hyperpigmentation areas. About 80% of my forehead is a big brown splotch, above my lip like a mustache (so attractive lol) the center of my chin has it light enough that I know it's there but other people won't realize it, and then high up on my cheekbones I have a large patch on both sides of my face. So, yea, I go through a ton of sunscreen and am always looking for the best because it is nearly impossible to keep them from getting darker unless you just never go outside. I'm at the beach a lot, so I definitely need stuff that works. This was my first time trying this brand and I love it, so I will buy more. I'm writing this review from Hilton Head South Carolina , on the beach, actually,  and am very impressed with how well it has worked in the blazing full sun. Figured it was a good time to express my thoughts on it since I was sitting here thinking how my lip is not burning and I do not have streaks etc sweating off my face. Good stuff!
This is one of the best sunscreen face creams I have ever tried. Its SPF 40 rating is perfect protection for long sun exposer without skin damage. It is also a great moisturizer.

This goes on super smooth and blends well especially for a zinc sunscreen.  I wear a sunscreen on my face daily and this is definitely one of my favorites.  I have had some zinc ones in the past that you can't really get the white sheen to blend in completely, and when it is worn daily on my face, that's not a great thing!  I really like this one, no scent, no residue...just good sunscreen.

I was a little leary to try this as the price is prohibitive and quite frankly "tinted" anything is almost always a surefire way of saying that a product is going to make your face look like a mask several shades lighter than actual skin tone. I was actually surprised that in this case the tinting is very mild and most likely in place to conceal the levels of zinc, which is white and chalky, in this product as it does blend in with my skin tone and does not look muddy or fake. Overall I am pleased with it's sun-blocking tendencies and yes I did have to wash my face in the evening because it does not appear to wear off throughout the day like other sunblocks do. As other reviewers pointed out it also tends to be a bit drying but I found that I can successfully fend that off by applying my moisturizer before putting this on.

Do I consider this a good sunblock for face? Yes, I do but to be honest the price is prohibitive and yes, Zinc is one of the best sunblocks out there. I know this because for years when I worked outdoors I used Destin, the diaper cream on my face to great effect in protecting my face (yes, I looked like a Kabuki performer but I was protecting my face from 10 hours of sunlight so looks were not so important.) So I guess my issue is how do I go from paying 3 bucks on a tube of diaper cream that offers the same face-saving protection as this $40 sunscreen? My budget is the determining factor.
summary: Great sunscreen but others work just as well for much less

reviewText: Very light, easy to apply, feels more like a lotion than sunscreen. Was a bit nervous about the tint to the sunscreen, but it applies evenly and blends in well with the skin.

Having sun damage, especially when you are aging needs really strong protection. Unfortunately, the best sunscreens contain the active ingredient Titanium Dioxide or Zinc Oxide-they give you the highest protection, but leave your skin a chalky white. I have always worn hats all my life as my fair skin never liked the sun, but my other family members did not and now must wear both a good sunscreen and a hat.

It is worth every cent you spend on a good sunscreen that is recommended by a dermatologist, and our dermatologist recommended this TIZO brand. We were told if you don't see the active ingredient of Zinc Oxide or Titanium Dioxide, keep looking. This Tizo Age Defying Fusion has Zinc Oxide and gives a high protection against the sun's rays, as I burn very easily and I didn't burn at all wearing this in one afternoon. What I like best about this TIZO, is that it is tinted and doesn't leave you looking chalky white. Great protection from the sun's damaging rays and not going on your skin chalky white, makes this a 5 STAR Sunscreen.
summary: Great Protection & Tinted, So You Don't Look Chalky

reviewText: I've been using this on my face since I don't see the point in using a tinted sunscreen on the body. Works well. I live in high altitude desert and the sun all year round can burn you when you are out doors for any length of time. This is a SPF 40 broad spectrum, water resistant (up to 40 minutes) zinc based sunscreen. The cost is high, but if you like it a tinted sunscreen worth it--the sunscreen spreads evenly and disguises some of your fainter flaws!
summary: Works well in high altitude desert

reviewerName: Gina Pera, Adult ADHD Expert and Author
reviewText:
A family member just had a melanoma growth removed, so that has renewed my commitment to using sunscreen.  (That and vanity. The left side of my face features "sunspots" from driving the car.)

I like the fact that it is tinted, so I don't have that "freshly embalmed" look common to the non-tinted sunscreens.

As far as I can tell, this product was formerly called TiZo Pure Mineral Protection, and the Environmental Working Group gave it a score of 1, meaning "low hazard." As much as we want to protect children from the sun, we also have to think about the chemicals we're putting on developing bodies. You can see what EWG has to say about the various ingredients at EWG dot Org.  Search for "TiZo Pure Mineral Protection, Ultra Sensitive Skin, SPF 35."

In a recent issue of Consumer Reports, sunscreens are rated. According to the accompanying article, CR testing found that many of the "mineral" sunscreens (zinc, etc.) weren't as effective as the "chemical" sunscreens in blocking UV rays.

So, much remains up in the air about the safety and effectiveness of these sunscreens.

I like this product because it wears nicely and it seems to be "safe" insofar as EWG's ratings of ingredients' go.  Is it as effective in blocking the sun's rays as some other products? I have no idea.
summary: Wears nicely; seems to do the job!

reviewText: Very nice sunscreen, goes on smooth, not too heavy, but very expensive at $41.99. Cotz is 1/2 the price, e.g., and there are other, equally good sunscreens at half the price or less. So, yes, this is a good product but I consider it overpriced.

Even though I have used some good products, I am on a neverending quest to find an even better sunscreen. In California, applying sunscreen is a year-round thing, and although my skin is not exactly fair, I still am  obsessive about making sure no one leaves the house without a protective layer.

I had not heard of TIZO before trying it, and now that I've got my own tube, I still can't find much information other than the ingredients and the fact that it's manufactured in the USA by a company called Fallen who used to sell a similar product line under the name Cotz. It looks as though their strategy has been to market this product through doctor's offices, but in most ways it's a pretty average sun protection product.

Buying cruelty-free is important to me, and Cotz appears to have been cruelty-free so I'm guessing that TIZO is as well. Did I mention that their website is mostly fluff? TIZO is also not included on any of the cruelty-free websites, and none of the Fallen products past or present appear on the EWG sunscreen list. The product label lists about 20 inactive ingredients with multi-syllabic names, and I haven't yet gotten around to checking each one for safety in the EWG database.

The sunscreen is allegedly tinted, but it is the least-tinted tinted sunscreen ever. It applies easily, which isn't always the case with mineral sunscreens. My skin is not sensitive and I don't usually have problems with sunscreens. This one is no exception.

With so many great and effective sunscreens on the market, this will not be a product I'll be buying again. It's not bad, but it doesn't stand out in any way.

I am a huge fan of COTZ for faces in the natural tint--I think it is made by the same company--both are located in the same Pennsylvania town. It holds up to a very sweaty face in extreme humidity--when I go to shower, I use a baby wipe to remove it, and the baby wipe is heavily tinted, so it must be staying on. However, in the darker, cooler months, the tinted version can be too dark and too matte looking, and the lighter untinted version is kind of white. This is a good compromise. It doesn't seem to be as sweat resistant--only rated 40 minutes, vs 80, and it leaves my skin looking dewy, rather than matte. The tint is very slight, and because it's all zinc, vs. part titanium dioxide, it's not at all opaque. My skin just looks like well-moisturized skin, with no whitish cast. I have medium-toned German-American skin, for reference, with a neutral undertone and reddish cheeks. I just touch up the red places with L"Oreal Lumi Cushion foundation, I look totally natural in daylight. Good stuff!
summary: Great for a natural look on older skins

reviewText:
I am quite fair skinned and have used sunscreens for years.  What I like best about TIZO is the tint, it is not that whitish color smearing on my face only to be reapplied often.  TZIO is thick, maybe due to the Zinc Oxide, which isn't great but it's tolerable.  The price, which is over $40, I believe could stop sunscreen users.  TIZO has an SPF 40 and many high end cosmetics with an SPF 25 are more costly.

Thinking of the damage the sun can do to one's skin: cancer, aging and more, $40 is a small price.  Many patients regret they didn't use sunscreens. So, despite the fact that you have to re-apply every two hours or sooner if swimming or sweating, it will be beneficial.  It's worth a try.

I went to the beach for vacation and used a hypoallergenic, sensitive skin child's sunscreen...it worked well, I did tan a little but I broke out.  This sunscreen is heavier but had better protection.  I did not break out...loved that!  I did not tan at all as it has zinc oxide in it, and is not greasy.  Do not be alarmed when you notice it goes on with a skin tone color then goes clear. It stings if you get it in your eyes.
summary: Awesome sunscreen protecion....I did not break out or tan

reviewText:
This sunscreen is tinted (as in flesh-colored).  It only contains zinc oxide, no other sunscreen ingredients.  When applied it adsorbs quickly and doesn't leave any residual color or sticky feeling.  Attached photos are the sunscreen prior to application and following briefly rubbing it in.

We have not had an opportunity to test whether it is sweat-resistant or would sting your eyes.  Besides that, it is a good sunscreen and provided protection during several hours of swimming.

The SPF 40 this is a good level for my sensitive skin. It is 20% zinc, so it doesn't soak in right away but the medium tint kept it from looking like a Kabuki mask. I tried rubbing it in parts of my body with different tones and it blended in just fine on both the tan areas and the lighter. Still people with darker skin may find it too light. It was like a mass market medium foundation color. I don't notice any scent and it does not bother my sensitive skin. I have been using EltaMD SKINCARE UV Daily Broad-Spectrum SPF 40 TINTED, 1.7 oz sold to me by my dermatologist. I like this much better. The EltaMD rubs in quicker, but it leaves my face shiny. I also saw a study checking how effective different brands are and the EltaMd was toward the bottom of the chart. It says SPF40 but it really wasn't. I don't know how this would test in a scientific study, but I would buy this before the EltaMD, even with the push from my dermo to buy the stuff they sell.
This is the best sunblock I have ever used - and as a person who lacks pigment  that is quite a statement from me!  It does not burn your eyes, so  terrific I have used it on our grandchildren.
summary: This is the best sunblock I have ever used - and as a ...

reviewText:
The salon I get my haircuts at uses ORIBE (and my hair looks wonderful afterwards), but I never tried this brand at home. I purchased all sample shampoo and conditioner available because I wanted to see if the results would be that great using ORIBE products at home. With conditioners I'll usually know from the first try if I like them (if they can smooth and hydrate my hair enough); with shampoo I need a little more use to see how the scalp reacts, but I can tell from the first try if they're too stripping or not cleansing enough.

The shampoo did a decent job at cleaning my hair and scalp, with a lush but not too thick foam; I did need to lather twice to get a good clean. But it's expected that a shampoo targeted for colored hair is not the most cleansing possible (to preserve color).
The conditioner was OK, but didn't managed to moisturize enough my thin frizzy hair.
The `Beautiful Color` shampoo and conditioner gave more texture/grip, making my hair looking matte and being more tangled than usual. The hair was soft, but the results were not better than drugstore hair products. My hair was also limp, with no volume.
The scent was nice, almost citrusy, similar to any other Oribe product; what I did liked is that it doesn't linger in the hair (I don't want to smell like my hair products).
summary: OK haircare products, but nothing too impressive

reviewText:
I love the product and good on color treated hair.  I have mostly grey hair so coloring tend's to dry out and  this shampoo

reviewText: I have fine/thin hair and Love this. It takes a very little amount and doesn't  make my hair limp. It is a bit costly but we'll worth it.

I originally bought this line of shampoo, conditioner, and masque from my hair colorist, figuring it was polite to try it out at least once before going back to my usual drugstore brands. I realized after awhile that using Oribe products were making a huge difference in how long my salon-red hair stayed vibrant and glossy; can't go back to the cheap stuff now!

This shampoo seems pricey for the size, but in actuality it's not---it dispenses as a thick cream and a small amount (a grape-sized dollop?) is all you need. You must emulsify it in your hands (rubbing together) and then apply it to very wet hair. It does not "foam up" as detergent-type shampoos do, which could mislead you into thinking you need to use more. With just the small amount, my hair gets cleans without stripping out all the red color. The matching Oribe conditioner and the weekly masque are perfect complements.

For those of us who routinely (every 6 weeks at least for me) go to a colorist to get our hair done professionally, it's silly not to use the right products to protect that color investment between salon visits. I was always suspicious that high-end hair products were a waste of money, after using Oribe I'm now a believer!
summary: Definitely worth the investment if you're a "salon redhead"

reviewText:
I've used a couple of hair removal creams in the past. One for legs, another for face. I have never used a chemical depilatory in the bikini area before. bliss "Fuzz' Off Bikini is not for use on your face, head, breast, perianal or genital areas. Don't use on moles, irritated skin, sunburned skin, scars etc.

If you hover your cursor over Amazon's product photos you can read the ingredients, warnings & instructions for using this cream so I won't repeat them, but will remind you to follow the timing instructions. It's important not to leave this cream on longer than 10 minutes.

I don't have sensitive skin & didn't have any problems. bliss 'Fuzz' Off Bikini worked for me.

I was skeptical of this bikini hair remover, I have only used Nair before but trust the Bliss name.  I have to say - this is so much better than shaving.  It is very easy to use, and lasts longer than shaving.  I use this in the shower, and have to say it works very well.  There was also no irritation afterwards, though I did put some moisturizing body oil on the area after my shower to cut down on dryness or itching and that worked well.  I would buy this again.
summary: Works well and lasts much longer than shaving.

reviewText:
I have dry and sensitive skin.  I tested this in apprehension, but no need for fear!  No itching, no redness, no rash, no irritation!

Also, no hair!  Well, mostly.  I'm a brunette and this product did leave little dark dots of hair roots.  They're barely visible but worth noting in case you are looking for something to completely erase all evidence of all hair.
summary: No itching, no redness, no rash, no irritation!

reviewText:
"Fuzz off" is a hair-removing cream that comes in a two-ounce tube and can be spread out over the skin directly from the tube by turning the applicator around to ON/OFF.  The tip is soft and bends to the skin. There is no messy hands if done right. This cream works like Nair but doesn't have that obnoxious smell, although there is a slight smell more like moisturizing lotion or sunscreen.  This cream is meant to smoothen the skin in the areas that have already been shaved by leaving the cream on the targeted skin for five minutes, and no more than ten minutes.  This stuff is not meant for the face (there is another Bliss formula for that); it truly is just meant for the bikini area.

The ingredients are (taken from the Bliss website since it's not mentioned here) Water, Urea, Mineral Oil, Calcium Thioglycolate, Cetearyl Alcohol, Calcium Hydroxide, Potassium Hydroxide, Ceteareth-20, Bentonite, Fragrance, Butyrospermum Parkii (Shea Butter), Glyceryl Rosinate, Titanium Dioxide, Disodium EDTA, Silica, Olea Europaea (Olive) Oil Unsaponifiables, Cocos Nucifera (Coconut) Oil, Theobroma Cacao (Cocoa) Seed Butter, Simethicone, Aloe Barbadensis Leaf Juice, Theobroma Grandiflorum Seed Butter, Mauritia Flexuosa, Tocopheryl Acetate.

The tube is easily thrown into a hygiene bag.  Users must make sure the applicator is in the OFF position after use, because otherwise the cream shoots out at the next use.  My one concern is the high price.
summary: Best used after a close shave

reviewText:
Wife uses this to get the stubborn hairs that she misses after shaving or in areas that cause to much irritation.  This is not meant for removing large swaths in your deforestation ritual. So you will need your preferred method of removal or partial removal first.

This is great for getting those annoying hairs that seem to defy the blade or trimmer.  So unless you are waxed completely or have gone through laser hair removal, you will have some fuzz here and there.

It is not noxious like Nair.  It's not painful like a wax.  The only complaint is it's a little pricey for 2 ounces.  But if you like to have that total smooth look or smooth in some areas and you need help, this is a wonderful think to have.

Update - be careful not to leave it on too long because it will cause irritation.
Finally, something that really works!!!

Wow, that smells good!  The nice smell of this should not be overlooked.  I have never used a hair removal cream that worked AND smelled good.

This was really easy.  It has a built in applicator.  I had to smooth out a couple of places but it went on almost perfectly.  I wiped it off at 4 minutes and all the hair came off easily and painlessly.  I have to say this beats the hell out of a wax job.  You can get hurt from those!

I am becoming a fan of Bliss products.  They may not do everything they saycellulite anyone?but they smell good and are made with quality ingredients.  And there is a little boldness in claiming to take away cellulite.  The directions say to put that cream on your thighs and do 10 deep squats.  LOL. I like the Bliss style, anyway.

The cream comes in a tube with a wide silicone applicator, and it can be locked so it will not spill and a cap to cover the applicator. The applicator helps to apply the cream all over without ever touching it with your hands. I needed about 7 minutes for it to work, and I did not get virtually any red spots on the skin, and those were gone within minutes. Don't forget a watch to time the application!

I typically use the Nair Shower off version of this type of product so I was excited to use Bliss's version and see how they compared.  Where the Nair typically leaves spots that needed to be touched up, the Bliss version left none.  Which I am still quite amazed about to be honest.  I kept thinking that there would be but once everything was cleaned up there wasn't a single touchup left!!  While this product is quite pricey it does seem to go a long way, which is good.

While this product didn't seem to leave the razor burn rash I get with EVERYTHING quite as badly, it still did a bit so I followed this up with my favorite Bliss product: ingrown hair eliminating pads.  Highly recommend for those that have the same issue.

Overall I'm pleased with this product!  It's not going to be as effective as waxing but it was convenient, easy to use and MUCH less painful (NO pain actually) than waxing.

I always use Nads "wax." When I say "always," I mean ever since the product hit the market. I tried depilatories as a teen, but the noxious odor and the spotty results had me seeking other solutions. So, when I ordered this, I did have that old fear. Nonetheless, I am happy to report that this product is genuinely outstanding!

Foremost, there is that signature odor, but it is not nearly as strong as some others. Secondly, the "spatula" type applicator makes dispersing the product fairly easy. HOWEVER, I tried multiple times to evenly distribute the product and it always ended up a little stripy. So, when I was completely done, I use a finger to smooth the product (and then quickly washed). I followed the directions and used a washcloth to remove the product (I waited six minutes instead of the five indicated ... do not go over ten). It wiped off 100% clean. Not 80, not 90, not 96 ... I mean 100%. What?!

Moreover, I have extremely sensitive skin. And, while I was fine with the patch test, I was nervous about a larger usage. I experienced zero redness. No negative reaction whatsoever.

To be honest, this probably will not replace waxing for me --  the results do not last long enough. However, when I am in a rush, this will be an excellent second-place.

Highly recommended!

I normally use either Laura Geller or Physicians Formula blushes. I'm fair and cool-toned, with dry skin. Truly, you only need to touch the blush with your brush lightly to have enough color for fair skin. Swiping your brush across will put too much on the brush. They may be more pricey than drugstore brands, but you use so little it'll be a long time before you "hit pan". I'm not sure if this would show up on dark skin though. It doesn't look cakey and stays on all day. It's the perfect pink for cools and neutrals. The compact is high quality, too, and looks like it won't break like cheaper blushes; it has a firm "click" when closing it.
summary: Perfect blush and worth the (slightly) high price

reviewText:
I adore this blush, it looks beautiful on my skin. It's highly pigmented yet applies very smoothly. The trick is to gradually build up color (it's much easier to apply more than to try to remove too much) with THIN layers or alternate layers with a thin coat of translucent powder. I don't apply powder to my cheeks since this part of my face is normally too dehydrated yet this powder blush gives a very smooth application....even over my "sticky" tinted sunblock. One light layer of this blush on my pale skin is plenty for day wear. 2 or more layers works better for me for evening. This color (in my own case) DOES have a deep enough pink color for nighttime makeup. It looks gorgeous with either deep or pale pink lipstick. I do feel though, that the Petal Pink may be a bit too pale to show up on darker skin, depending upon how deep your skin is. The photos in the product description are not only a good guide for how this color will appear on different skin tones, they are exactly accurate as far as color is concerned and what this blush realistically looks like on the skin.

This blush is neither matte (my preference) nor shimmery (my nightmare). It''s somewhere in between. It does as promised in not drawing attention to my large pores and less than perfect skin. I have been looking for a blush exactly like this that is not so matte it looks like I've been dipped in flour (not a good thing with very dry skin) and applies very smoothly (even color rather than "clumped" in some areas). I cannot use any metallic, shimmery blush at all simply because it looks awful on my mature skin. Besides, I'm looking for a natural looking hint of color rather than cheeks that scream "BLUSH!". This Julep blush is the best I have used so far. The color is concentrated, yet it applies with a sheer, natural look that can be built upon if needed for more subdued lighting situations. On my skin it wears very well and lasts with one application. I also love that the color stays true, and doesn't oxidize (go orange) on my skin, and looks great in either indoor (artificial) or outdoor lighting. I do plan on trying out more products from this line....I'm that impressed! Highly recommended!

I was a little alarmed when I saw how very, very pink this blush looked in the package. Because, wow...is it pink. However, I sallied forth, using a blush brush to lightly apply the product to my face. The color, once applied, is a subtle, almost translucent shade. At the same time, the color saturation is very good. I know that is a bit contradictory, but it is true, nonetheless. How to explain? You can see the color that has been applied, but the illusion of skin is there. It doesn't apply like a crayon, where the color is completely opaque. This blush looks natural.

As to the pore minimization, I can't really speak to that. I don't have particularly large pores in any area in which I would be applying blush.

I work 12 hour days, and I reapplied the blush about 8 hours in. I think that is a very reasonable amount of time for a makeup product to last.

Bottom line - The blush is a great shade. Love the natural way it looks when applied. Long lasting. Great packaging. I like it.

This is my first Julep product, and I am super impressed with this amazing blush called petal pink.  I wear a minimum amount of liquid makeup and add a blush for extra color, as I'm very pale.  My go-to brand for many years is usually L'Oral, but Julep is going to be a close favorite.  The brush application over my cheekbones was fast with beautiful results, better than my other brand.  I only needed ONE quick swipe and the amount of color produced was just right.....that has never happened before!  The color looks very natural especially on my many decades old, face.  So the age-defying premise is really a moot point for me, but I must say that "your happy look" is right on.
summary: Amazing color with just one swipe on the cheeks!

reviewText:
I expected a darker color (based on the photo) but mine was way too pinkish. It comes in a nice case with mirror (no brush). When I used my own brush, it was very powdery (which I dislike as it goes everywhere). The color  looked sort of OK when on but did not last the day (had to re-apply).

Based on the price ($24) I would not buy it. There are a lot of other brands that are much more cheaper (or even more costly) that would perform better.

reviewText:
It's very light and unlike my Neutragena blush, it doesn't last. I hate to say that, because the eye shadow of theirs I have is wonderful. that's really all there is to say. That being said, it does not last like my Neutragena blush, it has to be reapplied a couple of times during the day. I've upgraded to 3 stars, that being said, I would not purchase it.

This seems like nice blush. It's very bright. You can see in the photo that it is brighter and darker than the color on the package. The package shows a more mellow and warm pink; however, the actual product is darker and cooler. The packaging is beautiful, but I try not to be swayed by packaging because you don't leave the house with the package on your face but the cosmetics inside.
