The question you have to ask yourself is is this lipstick better then other lipstick.  Is it worth the 20 dollars to try to use it.  So far that answer has been yes.  First off the color is spot on and looks exactly like what you see.  It looks nice and it actually does work the way it is supposed to.  Is it perfect, no, but then again nothing is.  That being said, sometimes things are not worth the little extra you pay, sometimes they are.  In this case I do believe they are.
summary: Good color, good lasting power, good all around lipstick.

reviewText: From my daughter: Shade 03 is the perfect color for people like me who don't know much about makeup or fashion. It is a soft, peachy-pink that should look good on a lot of different skin tones. It has just a little bit of shimmer in it. A little goes a long way. I tried looking the product up on EWG.org, but couldn't find anything. I have extremely sensitive skin, so I will be updating this if I find it causes any problems.

I really like this blush by Japonesque.  The color is a beautiful shade of pink, the case is artistic and sturdy.  The blush should be applied sparingly with a gentle hand.  Happy with my purchase from Ulta!

This Japonesque lipstick is excellent! My lips really look stunning, it makes them pop. Shade 07 is actually a little darker than I usually get, but I'm glad I got it because it looks good. Wore to work for the past two days and it hasn't smeared or gotten on my teeth with blotting. My husband also appreciated that he didn't look like he was wearing lipstick after giving me a quick kiss.

Favorite thing about this lipstick is that it makes my lips look fuller. It works a little like a moisturizer too, but I still applied some to my lips before applying the lipstick. It goes on super smooth and comes off easily. I also only applied it once, in the morning and then again after lunch to freshen it up. I probably didn't need to even do that, it still looked great.

I was skeptical about this lipstick because of the price- but it is definitely worth the cost. It lasts through a work day, is moist and doesn't make my lips feel dried out. LOVE this lipstick!

This lipstick formula is full coverage.  The colour applies evenly and smoothly.

I have chronic dry lips and vaseline every night before bed and this lipstick does not feel like it dries my lips out.  There is a bit of colour staining on the lips as expected with full-colour and full-coverage lipsticks, but it can be easily removed with regular makeup remover.

Overall I do like the smooth formula.

Nice, smooth, non-glossy but not too matte.  Longevity, wear is good and an improvement over my usual longer-wearing lipstick from Stila.  Shade 07 is definitely not my shade.  I gave dark blonde hair and very pale but pink/ruddy skin.  This is just too dark, as a lipstick. In the tube it looks almost like Black Honey from Clinique but as an opaque, matte it just doesn't work for me. I blotted it a bit and it was wearable but still very goth looking against my skin.  I will definitely try a different shade.  07 also accentuates any yellow in your teeth (mine are average white, and I do drink tea, but 07 made me reconsider smiling which is never a good thing!)
summary: Nice formula, 07 too goth dark for my shade of pale

reviewText: I have just one word for the Japonesque lisptick and that is WOW! It is a beautiful color (07) although I had no idea exactly what color it would be. The lipstick goes on smooth and makes my lips feel very soft. It lasts a long time and feels great. Luckily this color (07) is the Pantone Color of the Year for 2015-Marsala. So I will be fashion forward in 2015 with this color lipstick.
summary: Pantone Color of the Year Marsala!

reviewText: I wasn't super impressed with this product. The curve of the lipstick itself is unique, but I didn't find that to be an asset in application. The packaging is cheap-looking for such a high-end product. The color I received, Shade 07, is more brown than I anticipated and is just okay. The color also wears off easily after eating/drinking. I will not purchase another one of these lipsticks.

I always try new lipsticks with a bit of hesitation - most of them promise to last and almost none of them do, at least for me. Japonesque is a new to me make-up brand, and this is the first time I've tried their lipsticks - in Shade 07.
It's a pretty wine color shade that goes well with my fair skin and dark hair. The case is very nice, a sturdy dark plastic that shows the color at the bottom and the top (helps to take away the guess of 'what color is this' if you have a busy make-up bag/case/drawer).
One thing I noticed right away is that the lipstick itself is 'curved' at the tip, or indented so it fits over your lip. This is very helpful to get that cleaner lip line when applying the lip stick, though it'll be interesting to see how that wears down with use. It's a nice touch.
The lipstick itself is very creamy when you apply it on and goes on very smoothly. There's no obvious scent or taste to it, and my lips don't feel dry or tacky as the day wears on. The lipstick does a good job of staying ON the lips without any bleed (especially good with such a dark color).
Japonesque Pro Performance lipstick does a really good job of lasting through the day and normal wear, which impressed me. There is a bit of color transfer to the lips due to the pigment of the lipstick, and again, it doesn't dry them out (guess it does live up to the moisturizing aspect). The performance and the fact that this lipstick is so creamy makes me want to try out more colors, as does the price. The current price of $20 is NOT bad for a high end performance lipstick at all.
Not too sure about the 'volumized lips' bit, though. Sometimes I feel a tingle, similar to what I get from the Buxom lips gloss, but not often. Don't know if they have a similar plumping agent in this lipstick or what...
summary: wonderful moisturizing lipstick with staying power

reviewText: This lipstick goes on pretty smoothly. The color stayed on pretty long. As far as the shade that I received, #07, even though I'm a natural brunette with olive color skin, I felt that this shade was a bit too dark and overpowering for me. I think a slightly lighter shade would look nicer and a little more natural. As far as the price, I'm not sure if it's worth it. In the past I have purchased lipsticks for a quarter of the price, and I felt that they worked just as good as this one. That's the only reason why I'm giving this product four stars instead of five.
summary: GOES ON SMOOTHLY BUT NOT SURE ABOUT PRICE

reviewText:
I visited my parents over the holidays; they live in Knoxville, Tennessee.  Dad is eighty and Mom is seventy-seven.  Mom doesn't leave her house without wearing a ton of makeup.  I figured if anyone knew about lipstick, she would.

  I requested the JAPONESQUE Pro Performance Lipstick, Shade 07, from the Amazon Vine Program.  Usually, Mom wears various shades of pinks and reds.  The JAPONESQUE Shade 07 looked great on her.  Surprisingly, it did make her lips appear fuller.  I was skeptical until I saw her wearing the lipstick.

  She said the lipstick went on easily and came off easily.  It does have moisturizers.  Mom said her lips felt good wearing the lipstick as though it was lip balm.  Most importantly, she has worn it for several days in a row and hasn't experienced any type of allergic reaction.  Mom is like me; if a product will cause allergic reactions, she will be the one to experience them.

  Mom definitely plans to keep wearing the lipstick until it is gone.  It came in a box that is perfect for gift giving.  The lipstick tube looked very elegant, stylish, and attractive.  I highly recommend the JAPONESQUE Pro Performance Lipstick because of its easy application and long-lasting attractiveness.  Also, it does make lips look fuller.

  I don't know if the lipstick made my Mom's lips appear sexier.  (JAPONESQUE claims that it will.)  You will have to ask the old men sitting on the benches at West Town Mall--the ones who kept staring at her as we strolled past them.
summary: JAPONESQUE Pro Performance Lipstick is an Easy-to-Apply, Long-Lasting Lipstick that Looks Great on My 77-Year-Old Mom!

reviewText:
As a lipstick addict, with dozens of lipsticks, I feel as if I know what I want in one.  This one is moist and dewy yet has amazing longevity on my lips and lasts even through a meal.  It imparts a slight stain of color which stays on for hours.  Usually when a lipstick is this long lasting it has a slightly dry feel on the lips and is one I avoid for that reason.  This feels moist and smooths out my lips instead of drying them, so I feel it is worth the high price for this since it accomplishes longevity while staying moist.

This is similar to Yves St Laurent lipsticks with the same extremely high pigmentation and staying power.  It is actually superior to that brand because of the non drying formula.  This covers up all pigmentation on my lips with a semi matte appearance.

There isn't a lot of glossiness with this which can be good or bad depending on what you prefer.  The pigment is saturated.  I have dark lips that this completely covers and that also is something I love about this. The tube/case itself is nice but not special.  And this color is a beautiful deep reddish mauve color which works well on my skin, even though I am pale.  I feel that $20 is a high price for a lipstick so it needs to be special, and this deserves the high price.  The assortment of colors is also perfect.  I now want to get shades 1, 3, 5 and 11.  All the shades look gorgeous.
Beautiful color, nice pigment, natural color peachy/tan not shiny or sparkly.

This is a very pretty little compact containing a lovely shade of "velvet touch blush." The color, number 03, is a soft peach-pink tone that looks lovely on one's cheeks. Velvet touch blush is a very fine powder blush applied with a brush which you need to supply. It is a sheer blush that does not overwhelm. You can apply one layer, or more, if you like. I actually like the effect of just one layer of blush as it is very subtle. No ridiculous pink spots on your cheeks.

It lasts well on the cheeks and doesn't get on your hands if you touch your face. My skin is super sensitive to make up and I have had no problem using this blush, something I can't say about every blush I have tried.

The blush comes in a two-inch square compact with an attractive enamel type pink design on the top. Inside, the lid has a small mirror to help you see when you apply the blush. The compact is small enough to fit in almost any size purse. You might want to note that although the brand of this blush is Japonesque, it is made in Italy, not in Japan.

I am very happy I got this particular blush and would recommend it to my friends. It has earned a permanent spot on my make up tray.
summary: JAPONESQUE Velvet Touch Blush, Shade 03 is a lovely color of peach-pink blush and a new favorite of mine

reviewText: Japonesque Velvet Touch Blush gives a nice, sheer blush that doesn't fade. If you're ordering online, Shade 03 is actually pinker and less peachy than it looks in photos, but maybe that's my monitor. It doesn't come with an applicator, but is in a beautiful case with a mirror. I like the sheerness of it, it looks very natural if you select the right shade.
summary: Japonesque Velvet Touch Blush gives a nice, sheer blush that doesn't fade

reviewText:
This blush is a very intense color, so you can use very little. The compact has no brush, so you'll need to supply your own, which is fine since you need a larger brush to apply lightly.

The compact is small, about 2 inches square. It is sturdier than most drugstore compacts, so it might travel okay in a purse. But when I opened the box it came in, there was powder all over the inside of the box and on the compact, so it doesn't seem to be a tight fitting lid. I'm leaving it in my makeup box at home.

The color (03) is far darker than shown on the screen and leans toward a coral shade, which isn't exactly the right color for me. But if it's your color, this could be a good compact for you.

My wife received this blush.  Here are her thoughts:

I would consider the quality of this blush akin to MAC or Bare Minerals.  It goes on very well (one or two strokes is all you need). The color saturation is very good which means the color really shows, and it appears silky and radiant on the skin.  What I like best about this blush is that it combines the "sheer radiance" powder look of Bare Minerals with that of a blush in one product.  If you look really closely there are little gold flecks that give you a glow.  The color is more of a peachy-pink which looks good on most skin tones (fair-medium).

It last very well!  I went shopping and after pulling clothes on and off over my head several times and the blush stayed pretty well.  Many times, I find that blush wears off by the end of the day.

The packaging is lovely, the compact is rather small (approx 2 in. x 2 in and 1/4 in deep) and comes with a mirror (sadly, no applicator).

I deducted one star because the color on the side of the box in more pinky (like Shade 01), than reflective of this color (shade 03).  If you are judging the color by the color on the box, you might be disappointed.

Overall, I would consider buying this blush again.

I confess that my blush usually comes from the grocery store. As I get older -- which means both that I have to work a little harder to like how I look when I go out the door and that I have more financial resources -- I have been trying higher-end makeup products and discovering that there are actually reasons to prefer some of them.

This one is a keeper. It seems to work with my skin better than grocery-store blush... it's more on my skin and wants to stay there instead of the other that is happy to fly away. (And I have an oily complexion, FWIW.) I am extremely happy with the way this goes on, the way it stays on, and the way it looks (and feels!).

I think that part of the think is that it's sort of lighter weight than the blush I'm used to, so there's better color for less product on my skin. Also, as mentioned in the product info, this means that you can build up the color more effectively than the relatively clumsy products I'm used to. This ends up feeling more like naked skin to me when I wear it, because it is so lightweight.

I don't think budget-strapped me in my 20's and 30's made the wrong choice, but I'm really happy to discover this blush and will be buying it again.
summary: Excellent silky and light powder blush

reviewText: Very nice blush in a "lightish" rosy color.  The blush was well-packed, and out of the boxes (sort of generic-looking) comes a nice, metal case with a pretty design, in the color of this blush shade #3.  It is easy to open, and the blush is fine and well-pressed. In other words it is not loose at all.  I already have a shade of coral in an expensive brand, and this differs in that it is a subtle blush.  Of course you can build up the color, and for this price it is a lovely deal.  I would compare it to generic brands at the beauty supply.  Not too difficult to get color transfer, but not a gawdy mess either.  I still prefer cover girl, because of the shimmer, but really this does not crumble like that one either.  I used a large blush brush, and I put a bit on my cheekbones, and a bit on my nose tip and chin, and I have a shimmer powder that I put over that.  Just a bit so my wrinkles do not get too pronounced.  Recommended!
summary: Very nice blush in a "lightish" rosy color

reviewText:
I have aging skin that tends toward being oily. I'm naturally dark skinned and even darker since I am outdoors a great deal. This blush from Japonesque, Shade 03, is a lovely peachy pink color that looks wonderful with my dark coloring.

The thing I really like is that it is quite sheer. One application across my cheekbones gives me a hint of color without looking like I am "made up". It looks very natural. If I want a more pronounced glow, I can apply more and build up the color. This is perfect for aging skin because less is more for most of us. Plus, there is less chance of accidentally getting too carried away and going out with a clown look. ;-)

This is a powder blush but it isn't chalky. It goes on smoothly and seems to stay put for a number of hours.

There is no applicator included but I like that. I have a natural bristle blush brush that I prefer so I always toss those silly little applicators that normally come with powder blushes.

The blush comes in a small, square compact that is so pretty. Japonesque has designed them to look like Japanese laquerware with a beautiful, free-form swirl of colors on the top. They have also thoughtfully included a mirror on the inside of the compact for touch-ups on the go.

The Japonesque line is priced higher than I generally spend on cosmetics but because this blush is so delightfully sheer and the color so nice on me, I will probably purchase it when I run out.

I picked this up in Shade 03 as part of Amazon's Vine program, and have worn it every day this week.  The color is a really pretty peachy-pink that reminds me a bit of NARS' famous Orgasm blush, but without as much sheen to it and with a bit more peach.

I also recently tried a Japonesque eyeshadow quad, which was a bust for me since the texture was very chalky and the color barely showed up on me. This blush, though, is much nicer.  It applies evenly, and lasts on my oily skin (over primer and then foundation) a good five hours, which is about what most blushes last on me.

In terms of color, I'm pretty fair (I wear MAC foundation in NW20 or Bare Minerals in Fairly Light), and this showed up as a nice rosy blush.  Because peachy-pink colors like this work well on many skin tones, I think it would be great even if you had darker skin.

The compact itself is also so pretty!  The case has a lovely design on it, and it feels nice and sturdy.  I don't carry blush around with me in my purse, but if you do, this case should hold up well.

Overall, it's a nice product, and I'll definitely be trying more of their blush shades.
summary: Nice quality blush, and Shade 03 is nice for fair skintones

reviewText: Soft velvety powder color perfect for light to medium skin tones!  This compact will fit easily into your purse and stays closed so you don't have to worry about making a mess! Goes on easily with your blush brush and stays on all day.  Never clumps or looks fake.  I'm loving this color, and this product!

Nice quality case with great coloring, look, and feel. The color itself is a little bit on the orangey side of the blush spectrum. I wasn't sure how this sort of color would look, since i've never ventured toward that direction, but it gives off a nice glow. The blush also has tiny bit of sparkler in it, which is always a step in the right direction. I would buy this as a gift for a friend or family member, the presentation is beautiful.

reviewerName: make me a vine reviewer again please
reviewText: First of all I love the case for the blush. Quite lovely. The blush powder is fine with a tiny bit of sparkle. I was hesitant about the color since my skin color is light with a little blush from sunburn occasionally. Shade 03 is pink with a touch of peach and is absolutely lovely. The quality is excellent and I would like to see more products from Japonesque. I am really pleased with this blush.

Japonesque Velvet Touch Blush Shade 3 is peachy pink with a little bit of shimmer. The color builds as you apply more layers. Too much pigment can make the older generation look like clown make-up was used. With Japonesque Blush, one or two 'layers' is enough & doesn't look clownish. Younger women can apply it heavier & still look great. It stayed on all day for me (about 6 hours).

The mirrored compact measures 2 1/4" square. The compact is a little bit hard for me to open...which can be a good thing, because the blush won't get over everything in my purse or make-up bag. But, I always end up getting my finger or thumb in the blush when I open the compact. I'm practicing other 'opening techniques' to prevent this problem.

Mirrored Compact
byob = bring your own brush. (make-up brush not included)
summary: Shade 3 is peachy pink with a slight shimmer...for me, it looked good most of the day (at least 6 hours)

reviewText:
This blush comes in a tiny yet pretty compact with mirror but no applicator. The color of the rouge that they call "shade 03 teinte" is what I would call coral or salmon with a pink and orange hue. I really love the "marbled pink enamel colored" case that it comes in.

I found this very easy to apply and even after applying translucent powder over the blush, I could still see the color on my cheeks.  The blush is silky and stays on all day.  There's not much in this compact at 6.5 grams (0.229 ounces) so it will last me about two months. Overall, I like this makeup.
summary: Silky coral-colored blush that goes on easily and lasts all day

reviewText: I thought this blush might be a bit to pink for me, but it is really perfect.  I have medium skin tone and brown eyes and hair.  This blush compact arrived in a small box that calls this a radiant powder cheek color, and when you look at the first ingredient it is talc.  I also noticed it is made in Italy but distributed through CA.  The compact itself is beautiful, not cheap at all with a very pretty pattern on it.  The mirror is great and the size is perfect for your purse.

I got this for my wife to use and she said it is very easy to use. It comes in s nice little compact with a mirror on the back of the lid. She also said that it is a nice color(shade3) and that it stays on throughout the day like it should. It is a very well made blush and she liked it

reviewerName: Meryl K. Evans, Digital Marketing Pro
reviewText:
The photo -- a cross between pink, salmon and red -- captures the color accurately on both of my monitors). Even though the photo reflects the color, the description could be more specific as I wasn't sure what it'd look like before seeing it. Shade 03 doesn't say much!

It doesn't take too much to apply the right amount. My skin color is fair and it works. I don't have skin issues, so I can't speak to whether it would work for those who have sensitive skin.

While the artistic cover looks lovely, I'd rather have a bland cover and spend less than have a fancy one that may drive up the cost. The compact size should be a good fit for small purses. However, because it doesn't come with a brush -- which is just as well because those little brushes are useless -- you'd have to add one. The color didn't last all day for me despite my spending the entire day indoors.

If you have unanswered questions, please comment so I help you decide whether this is for you.
summary: Nice color that works for many occasions

reviewText: Shade 03's application is very lightweight, just like their other products. It's a cute, peachy shade and has a hint of shimmer to create a real glow. The case is very sturdy and takes work to open making it ideal for traveling in your purse throughout the day.

This blush glides on pretty smoothly. The pigmentation provides a nice peach color for my cheeks. I thought that this blush blended really well too. I thought this blush was long lasting in wear. I would definitely recommend this if you wear blush, the color is subtle and not at all overwhelming or garish.

I usually do not use the more expensive brands of makeup such as Lancome or Clinique.  I often buy Cover Girl or Maybelline and even Wet'n'Wild.  I received this blush through the Vine program so I thought I would give it a try.  I also tried this manufacturer's foundation which I gave 5 stars to.  This blush is very vibrant.  You only need a light brushing of it over your cheek bones and it shows up very well.  It has a bright pink pigment.  Often with the less expensive brands you have to use quite a bit for it to show up but that is really not the case with this brand.  I am not crazy about the bright pink but would probably like the same brand with a peach or tan color.  If you are looking for a moderately priced makeup that is bright and bold then you will like this brand.

The Japonesque Velvet Touch Blush is a very good blush that my wife found to be significantly better than the cheaper blushes she has been using for years.  It goes on very easily and leaves a  beautiful color that can be blended with others.  The color lasts all day which cannot be said of the cheaper brands

*** Positive Points: ***

- Easy to apply without the caking or powder fly off that my wife gets from the cheaper eye shadows
- Lasts all day
- Has a slight degree of sheen once applied
- Comes in a very attractive case that has a built in mirror
- Made in Italy (in case anyone wants to know)

*** Negative Points: ***

- Relatively expensive
- Does not come with  a brush
summary: Expensive But Is Easily Applied and Lasts All Day

reviewText: This blush is a pretty pink/peach shade. It has a light sheen to it, but not glittery. It doesn't take much to add a little glow to my complexion, just be careful not to apply too much. The case it comes in is really pretty too. I wish the description would give more information on the shade instead of No. 3. Because picture and actual product are different. Recommended.

I don't like when I have to be careful not to look like a clown after applying blushes. This one is not ad pigmented as others. I neet to use several layers for color to show up.
Shade 3 is very pretty, pinky peach, which looks very natural on my NW25 complexion. I swatched it on my hand and the color disappears rather fast and it's not as pigmented. For example I use my favorite Lancome blushes also as a eyeshadow and on lips and I can clearly see color, not with Japonesque blush. Also the first ingredient is talc which make the texture velvety but a bit powdery and this is why it doesn;t stick to the skin so well.

Packaging is very cute.

This good quality powder blush comes in a colorful square compact. Shade 03 is a soft peach with a touch of shimmer. It blends easily and the color builds. Most people will need more than one swipe. That being said, it does provide a natural glow. It doesn't have that cakey feel some powders do.  Lightweight, it should flatter most complexions. It does fade a bit so the color  needs to be be refreshed during the day. I was a bit concerned about the shimmer but not to fear. It adds vibrancy, not shine. I have somewhat sensitive skin and suffered no negative reactions. This blush works nicely on bare skin, with primer, foundation and over cream blush. The product is made in Italy.  Overall a very nice velvety smooth blush with buildable color that contributes to a flattering, natural look appropriate for all ages.

Pros: No clumping. No flaking. Definitely thickens lashes as advertised. Maybe it's my imagination but it seemed to double the lash length. It holds up very nicely over 10 hours.

Cons: The application brush is an odd size and could use some more brisles. It's not waterproof
summary: I like it ... the price is right ... will buy it again.

reviewText:
Whenever I try a new mascara, I apply it to only one eye and then apply the mascara I had been using to the other eye and compare. I do this because all mascaras enhance the lashes to a certain extent and it's easy to be dazzled without another mascara to compare it to. So, up for comparison is this Japonesque "lash loading mascara" and my number 1 favorite mascara so far: Loreal Miss Manga. Both mascaras are about the same size Japonesque is 0.3oz and Miss Manga is 0.27oz. Japanesque is manufactured in the UK and Miss Manga is manufactured in the USA.

Well, after applying one to each eye, there's a huge difference in performance and Miss Manga is by far the winner. Lash thickness appears the same, but Miss Manga makes lashes look a solid 50% longer. I'll also say that the Japonesque brush is horrible and I had to pick two clumps off my lashes. By the end of the day I had blacks black smudge under the eye wearing the Japonesque. I would describe the performance of Japonesque as "below average", like something that would be alright if I had bought it at a dollar store. But it's not a dollar, it's $20 which is just criminal!

I have never been able to wear make up for more than 3 hours without rubbing it all off. I put on the nuertogena eye shadow and this mascara and did not feel itchy or crazy and looked great for 6 hours. it is so cool to be able to wear make up. absolutely recommend!!!

Lash Loading? Talk about a hefty claim that seriously does not hold up. This mascara is more like "smear" loading. I usually use a volume mascara since my lashes are so light and thin. When a product promises :

High definition volumizing mascara. Inspired by the runway and behind-the-scenes tricks, JAPONESQUE Lash Loading mascara creates incredible lash drama and a super-charged false lash effect"

It better come through especially when its twice as much as the mascara I usually use (covergirl). First when I took the brush out, huge glob of mascara was at the brush end I had to quickly plunge it back in a few times to get rid of it, or risk it being all over my face. First coat was weak, second coat was the same. It gave no volume, it loaded no lashes, every time I brushed it on a bit would "dink" right onto my eyelid cause the formula is so runny. I was using make up remover left and right. In the end I probably used 4 coats and it was like using one. I would not ever buy this again.

I am a faithful user of estee lauder mascara, simply because I have allergic reactions to a lot of cheaper make-up.  I was excited to try a second brand that is sold on Amazon.  I did not have an allergic reaction to this, but I also didn't love it.  It doesn't go on very thick, and application was trunky.  The shape of the brush was weird.  I had to turn it side ways and keep shifting until I got the thickness I liked.  Instead of two or three quick swipes per eye, I probably did over 10.  I applied for almost 5 minutes, and didn't love the result.
summary: Not my favorite mascara.  Sticking with Estee Lauder.

reviewText: This mascara is good, but the brush makes it tricky to work with, particularly because the bristles are spaced so widely apart. The result is very well-defined lashes, without any clumping issues, but not necessarily the volumizing effect I was hoping for. I found that this works better when layering the product underneath a more volumizing mascara. But for $20 per tube, that shouldn't really be necessary.

This is a nice duo of shades that comes in an elegant case. There is a silvery pinkish mauve and a mauvish-purple with silver glitter in this duo. Some other duos come with one matte shade but this is the one Japonesque offered me to try. If you're looking for softer mauve-pink and purple shades, this may very well work for you.

The shadows are soft and there is fall out. Since they're glitter based velvet touch shades, there is a little more fallout that say matte shades. They need a primer to keep them on or they will fall out too quick, Urban Decay primer potion is my favorite.

I needed a duo for my purse for touch ups but the case though beautiful and sturdy, is a little too thick to carry in a smaller purse, wish it was a little thinner.

These velvet touch shades are softer and better than drug store brands but not as super-pigmented as the luxury brands in the same price range like MAC or Urban Decay. Especially Urban Decay shades are buttery soft and highly pigmented, and you can get a palette with many more shades for a similar price. MAC 4 shade special palettes are usually the same price as this Japonesque duo so I was expecting a little more.

However, it's all about shades and these 2 shades are harder to get as a duo in some collections and if it works for you it is a nice product.
summary: Very soft and lustrous but not as pigmented as some other luxury brands.

reviewText: Gorgeous colors, a soft shadow that goes on nice and light; not too dark which is what I was worried about with this color palette.  It is a little pricey however no more so than what you would get at the make-up counter at your local department store.  The compact is very pretty and stylish.  It's very nice.  I recommend.

Favorite!  I'll say it again...favorite!  Ok...it's not perfect because it's a rather soft shadow with some fall-out.  But the color is just what I was after, and one that is difficult to find.  The case is artistic and sturdy, and I'm delighted I found this at my local Ulta.
summary: LOVE The Color Combination!  A Favorite!

reviewText:
I have never tried a Japonesque foundation, so when a friend recommend it i decided to give it a go. I had never had perfect results with other brands and it was always touch and go trying to find that perfect match.

The Japonesque Velvet Touch Foundation is an absolutely beautiful Foundation. It's soft and fluffy and extremely light like air to apply. They recommend using their foundation brush, however you can use a standard foundation brush (i got mine at the dollar store), or even make-up sponge applicators.

I am using the Shade # 05. I am not Asian, but actually multi-racial and this color blends perfectly with my light brown skin town. and covers completely and evenly. It's so light you'll forget you're wearing it no matter the weather be it hot and humid or cold and raining.  I would absolutely recommend this make-up it's truly amazing!
summary: 10 out of 10 This Foundation is Wonderful!

reviewText: From my daughter: This foundation is amazing. My skin is so sensitive and almost everything irritates it. I can't even feel this on my skin. It blends in so perfectly and evenly. It doesn't sit in the lines or pores. I love the texture and the feeling of it when it goes on. I have given up on almost all beauty products over the years and have just been using Leven Rose Jojoba oil on my face, mascara and lipgloss, but I am happy to have found this product to use for special outings. It has a faint scent to it that I could do without. I will update if I have any reaction to this product.

This product is extremely light when worn, and easy to apply.
I don't have the specific Japonesque brushes but it seems to work fine with a regular foundation brush.
It's very much like a lightly whipped mousse foundation and feels very soft on the skin, even in layers.
My daughter who was a makeup consultant for Clinique thought it was a tad expensive compared to other products out there, but also added that due to the consistency and size it would probably last better than a liquid type foundation.
Available in a variety of skin tone shades, although as this was a free product through the Amazon Vine program I had no say in what color shade was sent.
summary: It little pricey, but very nice product

reviewText: I do not leave home without mascara and I have olive skin, so I'm always looking for a good new black mascara.  Japonesque Lash Loading mascara has some very good points.  The black is a deep flat black. I can pull it off with olive skin and I bet if you have porcelain toned skin this would look amazing.  It does really cover your lashes - the mascara itself is a good texture.  The flaw for me was the brush.  It's fabulous, reminds me of the Definicils brush which is my all-time favorite.  But it is a bit too long.  I do have small eyes and a small face, so this might not be a problem for you, but that extra millimeter of length made for a slower application lest it become sloppy.  One other note.  This is not waterproof - which is an issue for me because I workout (and shower) during the day.  So I'm using thsi as my Saturday night mascara.  When I have the time - and won't be working out - this is a great dark black look.
summary: so I'm always looking for a good new black mascara

reviewText:
PROS: This won't clump!

CONS: It won't clump because the formula is basically black water!

The big brush has been well covered in other reviews, but sometimes big brushes can be great. The problem here is that the brush is that spiral kind with tight, fake hair-- think a giant sized version of the $1 e.l.f. mascara. I personally like bristle wands because of how they grab the lashes, but the newer plastic kind has it place. This one finds a weird, unhappy medium.

I miss L'Oreal Featherlash, as I think light formulas can be fabulous for avoiding clumps. This isn't just lightweight, it's literally the consistency of water. Even with careful application, this flicked little black dots under my eyes and onto my eyelids every time. This stuff doesn't seem to love lashes, but they LOVE the skin around them!

If this was a $5 mascara, I'd recommend it to people who wanted more of a tint and maybe the illusion of length (its "lash loading" but didn't make my lashes look any thicker, but didn't do a bad job making them look longer) but isn't worried about thickness. Even using multiple applications between the lashes drying just seemed to "trace over" the lashes, but never built thickness.

At $20, it's absolutely ridiculous that it has the problems it has. Right now I'm using a Makeup Forever mascara and a $5 Revlon "Grow Luscious Plumping" mascara I picked up on a whim, and both prove you can do MUCH better than this in every price point.
summary: "Oh black water, keep on rolling..." (down my face)

reviewText: This is a very thick mascara. With a long lash brush, it really makes your lashes stand out. The mascara goes on thick, and stays on all day. A little thick for my liking, but works for me. I've never tried this brand, so I didn't expect such a thick product. It is Lash Loading!!

I was curious to see how this mascara compared with my favorite mascara (Younique Moodstruck 3D Fiber Lashes).
I read what some of the other reviews said and a couple said that that brush was too big and awkward.
That wasn't the case for me; in fact, that's one of the things I liked about the mascara:  the brush.
Many mascaras, when you pull out the brush, are filled with heavy clumps and you almost have to scrape the brush in order to use it cleanly.
Japonesque's mascara brush came out cleanly and without clumps.
I tried the mascara over a seven-day period; on the first day, I noticed flakes.  On another day, I rubbed one of my eyes and the mascara smudged all over and I looked like a raccoon.
It took three applications before it actually made my lashes look volumized and thick.
The box didn't indicate if it was waterproof or not; I used water to wash the mascara off, so it's not waterproof.  I prefer waterproof mascara.
So, while the brush was nice and clean to use, I didn't like the flakes or the way it smudged.
I'm not sure how long the tube will last if it takes three applications to make eyes truly volumized.
This mascara was good --  but not great.  I wouldn't purchase the Japonesque Lash Loading Mascara.

Like several other reviewers, I noticed the light application with this mascara described by the manufacturers as "lash loading."  I actually like the light application since it makes layering mascara (I've always heard that mascara is supposed to be applied that way) really easy.  I've never found a mascara that didn't clump into things that look like tarantula legs around my eyes.  It would seem that all of my previous mascaras weren't designed for layering.

I applied three light coats of Japonesque Lash Loading Mascara.  No tarantula leg eyelashes!  So I added a few more coats to see if clumping would occur.  It wasn't until coat 8 that my lashes began to clump.  That's a pretty good series of mascara layering!

I also had the opportunity to cry (it was that sort of day) while wearing this mascara.  It smeared but did not run right away.  Fortunately, there wasn't a lot of crying so I didn't test whether this will hold up to a sob.  I imagine it would not.  And it does remove easily with salt and water.
summary: Love this for layering coats of mascara!

reviewText: Ok, first and only complaint not certain why this is $20.00-that being said it works well I have short/boring eyelashes and this does make them seem fuller longer and a tad sexier. It goes on smoothly no clumping and smudging. All in all it works well/looks good I would use it again for certain but not at this price!

I don't like this mascara at all! It took a really long time to dry, I kept blinking little dots onto the area under my eyebrows, and it didn't make my lashes look any bigger. Then somehow it ran down over the course of the day into psycho-looking raccoon rings under my eyes. A mentally ill man oogled me at the Trader Joe's and that was the highlight of my experience with this mascara.
summary: I don't like this mascara at all

reviewText:
There are two things that stand out about this product: its size, and the corresponding difficulty of avoiding clumps.  As far as the actual pigment goes, it's a nice clean black with no hint of brownish or grayish tones.  However, the humongous applicator means that you are 100% more likely - or at least *I* am, I'm not the most graceful thing - to apply mascara to your eyelid and around the lash area instead of right onto your lashes.  I usually don't do this with the mascara that I use regularly, Physicians Formula.  And I thought the Physician's Formula applicator was huge!  I've uploaded a photo so that you can see the pretty dramatic difference between a normal large size applicator and this one.  You may notice how the Japonesque applicator has no transitional area at the base, just goes from wand to *poof* huge brush.  I definitely notice this when applying.  Probably wouldn't if the brush was a bit smaller.

Because of the size of the applicator, big giant chunks of mascara come off of it during any given application.  These of course either clump your lashes together (I made extensive use of my lash comb) or else fall off in plops on your cheeks or down on your outfit.  I'm not a fan.
summary: Giant applicator and resulting clumps make this a mascara to avoid

reviewText:
I'm mostly a skincare girl rather than a makeup girl.  However, I was not blessed with curled lashes and need mascara to hold my lashes up.  I have sensitive eyes and have tried almost every mascara on the market from drugstore brands to professional theatre brands.  So far, this mascara does not clump, the texture is smooth and it really fluffs up my thin lashes.  The formula dries quickly enough to hold the curl in my lashes.  So far there has not been any noticeable flaking, but this tube is brand new. I will report back in a week and then another week after taht to see how the formula dries in the tube and when it starts getting dried and flaky.

So far this is a very nice mascara.

I love the Japonesque brand, and have quite a few items. However, this velvet touch shadow in 06 didn't live up to the usual high quality I'm used to from the brand. Perhaps it was just the colors, but the pigment payoff was very low. It took a lot of work to get enough color on my lid to show up, (and I'm very pale), over primer. The consistency and texture was nice, smooth, not powdery and indeed velvety. But, I wouldn't pay the premium price for an eyeshadow that has such a lack of pigmentation. The wear time was on par with my other shadows, about 8 hours, but it was so light to begin with that it was more of a wash of color all day. The shimmer was very nice without dating or aging my look. 06 does make for a pretty neutral, and the case is beautiful. I just don't think that the pigment was there.
I might try another duo, because I do like the texture, but will be wary.

This is a great eyeshadow duo - the two shades of purple (with highlights of shimmer, and a bit of pink) go on easily with a brush and when blended together, look really beautiful. The eyeshadow transfers well from brush to eyelid without a lot of dusting transfer (so it doesn't immediately fall off the brush and shower your face with eyeshadow as you apply it) and it really blends together seamlessly to give your eyes a flawlessly blended look. It's a subtle shimmer and doesn't have any harsh lines at all between the colors they just go together so well!

I do wish that these had names, rather than just shade 6 - so for reference because of computer screens' color can differentiate, if these were made out of Crayola crayons, the lighter shade would be Lavender with Pink Carnation highlights and the darker shade would be Violet, but with highlights of Fuchsia and Silver. Together they look lovely! Plus, the case is quite lovely and includes a mirror.
summary: These Shades Compliment Each Other Perfectly!

reviewText:
I have the color 06 Velvet Touch with is a set of purples.  I love the colors, and I love the wearability of them (they last through the day).  I love the buttery blendable powder texture.  I love that the package is petite but the pan is wide enough to really dip a good brush in.  Purples are very forgiving, flattery colors against all skin and hair colors.  Very universal.  These have a bit of a shimmer (but not a glitter) to them, and they apply to a more neutral finish than they appear in the pan.  I really love these and will be taking a look at this brand in the future.  I especially love that there is no "fall out" from your brush with this formula, so you have control over where you apply color.  (Note, there is no included brush, which, in my opinion, is a positive.  It makes the package more sleek, and I prefer to use a good brush instead of pre-packaged ones.)

Two points of concern based on the current listing worth pointint out.  One, I don't think the image is very true-to-color.  These purples are warmer than the image implies.  Also, the listing seems to emphasize the mineral content of these, and it should probably be noted that the first ingredient is talc.

Overall, I would definitely recommend this shadow.
summary: Image color not exact, but product quality excellent.

reviewText: Nice eye colors. The colors are like the pictures. Not too dark or too light. They go on smoothly and make my eyes shine. The box these colors sit in is nice and sturdy. So if I dropped it it would not break. However it should have come with an applicator to apply the makeup.

Shade 06 is a violet/plum deeper shade with a light mauve or light lavender pale shade.

It is more heavily pigmented that typical drug store shades, but I have been spoiled by my Urban Decay Naked 2 palette, which contains eye shadow that has a consistency and pigmentation that is about as perfect as it gets!  The Japonesque shadow is not as good as the Urban Decay...but it is nice.

I think either a primer or (in my case) a lighter shade of cream eye shadow underneath is essential for shadow like this.  Put on alone, it will tend to fall off your lid, and you won't get the full benefit of it or its full color.

The case is very nice -- sturdy, elegant, well made.  It is not going to break when you're halfway done with the shadow...my pet peeve!  Overall, this is a very nice shadow, just falls a bit short of Urban Decay or MAC as far as the texture and pigmentation consistency.  But a little still goes a long way, so the darker color specifically will last a long time.
summary: Nice shadow; better than drugstore brands

reviewText:
I am a diehard user of Bare Minerals, Benefit, and Urban Decay. I rarely wander since I am allergic to just about everything (which is my lame problem and no fault of any cosmetic company). So, I had a little worry when I tried this (especially on my eyes) ... but, WOW, it was just gorgeous (and with no negative reaction at all)!

The pigment is really lovely and stays put better when you use a primer (but most make-up does). And the size of the case is PERFECT! It easily fits in my little Marc Jacobs "camera case" bag. (AND, the inside of the top lid is a full mirror!!!! PERFECT!) Also, I think this pairing of hues (#06) is outstanding!!

I am so enamored by Japonesque! I'm now adding them to my short-list of overall great products/great products for sensitive skin!

I have the Shade 06--purple-- shadow duo and I love how the two colors blend together. Neither purple is too bright, even though they have a bit of shimmer to them.  (Which is fine since I'm rather conservative when it comes to makeup).

The shadow duo comes in an attractive case with a small mirror.  You'll need to have your own applicator.  I found this eyeshadow to be easy to apply and blend.  It doesn't cake or crease, but it barely makes it through to the afternoon after applying it in the morning.

This gets five stars for the smooth, creamy application! Very nice shadow formula.

Three stars for the color, so I've split the difference and left four stars.

The purple is a vivid purple, not a greyed or smokey underhue. There is considerable shimmer, and if your eye area is the least bit rough or crinkled you aren't going to want this. Even with primer this formula made my eye area look my age.

I do love the quality and feel, it's right up there with Urban Decay
summary: Read if you have rough lids and for color guidance

reviewText:
I must admit I was a little surprised at how small the compact was when it arrived, but I really don't know much about Japonesque as a brand except I've seen the stores in Europe. Obviously it's one of the higher end ones (considering the price), and the packaging is very impressive - the case is very pretty and sturdy, this is something you can throw in your purse or travel bag and not have to worry about breaking (unless it gets really crushed). There's also a handy mirror inside of the case even though it's small. Obviously, there's no applicator wand with the shadow.
Now, on to the shadow itself - I received Shade 06, which is a pretty mauve/purple duo. I'll admit that I used a primer before putting on the eyeshadow, which I always do. That might have helped a little. The eyeshadow itself isn't too bad, it went on easily with both finger and brush, didn't feel harsh to the eyes and while it broke up a little with application, I will say that I didn't have any fall out while applying it (which was very nice).
However, the colors aren't as concentrated as other brands I use (which tend to be high end brands such as Urban Decay, Make Up For Ever, etc.). That might be why they say 'ethereal veil of color or layer and build for dramatic impact'. It's not BAD, but just know if you want the full impact of the shade you're definitely going to have do that 'build' to get to it.
So, you get a nice matched color combo in a very handy, pretty case that shouldn't break on you without some effort, and it's a decent make up (not the greatest, but if you like an eyeshadow that you can work with, something maybe that can start out subtle and then build up), then this would be worth a try.
summary: pigmentation could be better, but decent

reviewText:
Initially I thought that this would not be useful because it is solid black, which can look way too hard on those of us with over-50 eyes.  But since one can draw a VERY fine line with the pencil, this counteracts the fact that the liner is solid black. It allows one to line upper and lower lids very subtlely.

What I don't know is whether the fine point will stay fine; if it becomes blunt, that is that because I dan see no way that one couid sharpen the pencil....or refill it.
summary: Good liner.....at least while it is new, and the point is sharp

reviewText: This is a really nice eye liner pencil. The color is perfect for me, black and the point of the liner is very fine. I think this will be one of my favorite pencils. The liner goes on easily and is water resistant. Just smudge it with your fingers or a brush to get a smokey look. I highly recommend this eyeliner.

Great eyeliner, smooth even application that lasts all day. It also blends easily and I'm very pleased with how well it defines my eyes. Also, as someone who is sensitive to make ups - this is non-irritating.
summary: Great eyeliner, smooth even application that lasts all day

reviewText:
This liner glides on smoothly and defines my inner and out eyelids very well.  Usually I have to use a cigarette lighter to melt eye pencils so that they go on smoothly.  I did not have to do that with this one. It also washes off well with soap and water but resists coming off with just water. I scrub around the eyes twice with soap and water using my fingers as I do when getting off all make-up.  It would be nice if I could just dial the pencil when the tip gets worn but I don't mind that I have to use a sharpener with this pencil.  Overall, I love it,

I would consider purchasing this pencil liner if I ever run out of Shade 01 which appears black to me although I wish they would have just labeled it a color I could understand instead of with Shade numbers.
summary: Pencil liner glides on smoothly, lasts all day, and washes off easily with soap and water

reviewText:
When used with a foundation brush and stippler (or skunk brush), Japonesque gives a flawless, airbrushed look that is so desirable right now.  The foundation is very smooth and light - much creamier than most whipped brands. The consistency is between a liquid and a powder - one huge reason to apply this with a foundation brush and not fingers or a sponge. You'll want the brush to glide it on smoothly rather than mash it bluntly into the skin with a finger for best results.

After applying with a foundation brush, the coverage is excellent and smooth. The stippling/skunk brush, when lightly dabbed, then further smooths the makeup to bring out the powder portion and give that airbrushed feel. Stippling also easily removes any demarcation lines or application misses. It's a look you can't get with the $10 drug store foundations.

The feel is light and doesn't coat or cake (you won't have cracks with this foundation when you smile).  Shade 05 is a medium darkness - a light tanned Caucasian, for example.

I've loved the Japonseque line ever since I found it a couple years ago at Ulta. Great brand, although a little pricey, but good quality and will last you a long time.

Unfortunately this shade (#5) is a little too dark for me, but I shared it with a friend of mine that goes tanning a lot and it was perfect for her. She has a light olive complexion and it blended very well on her skin and didn't streak. Next time, I'll stick to the lighter shades.

As a base, it goes on creamy and you don't have to use a whole lot to get good coverage. It is smooth and has a pleasant fragrance to it, unlike a lot of cream foundations. The velvety cream has staying power and covers an multitude of imperfections. It comes in a sturdy bottle with a tiny little foundation scoop that makes it easy to get out. Neither my friend or I experienced any sort of break out or rash due to this product and after application, we totally forgot we'd put it on. If used properly, it won't rub off on clothes or phones throughout the day.
This foundation feels nice going on and has a sheer look to it while giving some coverage.  My face is naturally pale, so I should look for a lighter shade than #05.

This foundation spreads easily and evenly. Once applied it looks very natural.  I like the butter-like consistency of Japonesque very much. I usually use Estee Lauder Double Wear make up which is a liquid; this is my first expertience with this consistency make up, and so far it's been positive one.  The scent is very nice too.  Shade 5 matched my skin perfectly.

There is a small spatula enclosed in the box, which is a nice touch.  Unfortunately the black jar has transferred color to the spatula in places, so the spatula looks dirty now.  Maybe the company can reconsider packaging or materials to prevent this from happening.

I'm a long time Lancme Dual Finish user and have used it in matte bisque II for years. I've tried liquid foundation here and there and don't care for it at all. I like to even out my skin tone but I like to look like I'm not really wearing makeup. I guess I've been stuck in a foundation rut, but I didn't realize it until I tried Japonesque. The texture literally feels soft like suede or velvet and like it's barely wet. I tested shade 05, and looking at it I thought it might be too dark but not at all. In fact, it made me realize my Lancome shade is too light and makes me look washed out. I'm used to applying the Lancome with a damp sponge and didn't have the foundation brush recommended for the Japonesque. But anxious to try it, I washed my face, used my Dr. Weil serum and Lancome face cream, eye cream and eye concealer. My jar of Japonesque didn't come with a spatula (if it did I didn't notice it) so I dabbed some on each cheek with my fingertips and used my regular sponge to work it into an even application over my whole face, including over my eye concealer. The results are awesome! Natural yet more radiant than what I've been using and my skin feels so soft and slightly moist but not greasy. This product doesn't accentuate age lines like some foundations can do, like the dry bare mineral ones. It left no streaks or obvious foundation appearance. I later bought the recommended Stippling brush, and it works great applying Japonesque, leaving an airbrushed but natural look. This product is made in Italy, luxurious and the same price range as Lancme. A jar has lasted me quite a long time while trading off with my Lancme dual finish (which usually lasts a month or so). So happy I tried this product and definitely recommend it.
summary: Bella! Love This Velvety Smooth Foundation Made In Italy

reviewText:
The Japonesque Velvet Touch is a mousse style foundation that leaves an air-brushed, matte finish on application.

A foundation brush is required for an easy and even application. Since the foundation is light and airy, a non-greasy moisturizer prior to application provides a perfect base. By itself, as long as you are close to your shade, it blends in for a nice , natural look for daily use. Since the product finishes matte, it also makes a great foundation to build on.

Japonesque has eight shades for this product but there is no accurate color chart available (even on the website) to make an informed decision. For shade #5 of 8, it seems to be on the lighter side. I would have expected the shade to be slightly darker.

There is a slight odor on application that dissipates after application.

The product works as advertised but at 36 dollars a bottle is at the high end of this product range.

Recommended.
summary: Easy To Apply Product Provides Light To Medium Coverage

reviewText:
I couldn't tell from the pictures which shade would be more suitable for me. I am light complected with pink undertones. I received shade 05 and it is a bit too dark for me. It's a medium shade with yellow undertones. I let my mom use it since it is closer to her skin tone and she likes it. The makeup is really thick and a little bit goes a long way. It comes with a little spatula to scoop it out. The directions say to use a foundation brush to apply it. It's also a good candidate for a beauty blender or some other kind of sponge. I find that using fingers does not work well, it is too hard to get smooth even coverage.

The makeup is good and provides buildable coverage. It's a bit heavy for my taste, but that is personal preference. The quality is definitely there.

Japonesque comes in a sleek, black, elegant looking jar.
I think its not so much a skin enhancer as a skin smoother and a flaw cover-upper

It has a silky and smooth, ultra fine, slightly powdery texture and slides on and immediately disappears into the skin.

It is heavier than BB cream and is less translucent, but much lighter and more weightless than typical foundation; even whipped foundation.

It covers and perfects better than any product Ive tried.

The instructions advise using a foundation brush to buff and blur the product into the skin and then to sheer out with a stipping brush. I don't have either so I used my fingers. The downside is that scooping out contents with a finger doesnt work well, especially if you have long nails.

Others may object to the slightly paint-like scent but its faint.

My skin hasn't looked this flawless in years.

I am not big on foundation, and I don't usually wear a lot of makeup. Japonesque Velvet Touch Foundation (shade 05) was a near perfect match for my skintone and texture from the beginning.  This foundation goes on smoothly, blends easily and you don't feel like you are wearing makeup at all.  Almost always I brush a translucent powder over any foundation that I wear. I didn't need to do t is with the Japoneseque Velvet Touch foundation.

The look is flawless and it stayed all day even under conditions such as under tv studio lighting which can be really harsh.  I would definitely recommend it.

What a beautiful foundation! It's lovely & very natural on the skin. It's important to use a brush with foundation like this in order to get even coverage ( a stipple brush would be best), otherwise it can look streaky when applied with fingers. Less product is needed this way and it will last longer than liquid foundation. My skin is a bit dry this time of year so I did a good exfoliation and moisturized my face and neck before application. I also love how it looks with a primer applied (I use Miracle Blur) when I'm going out. It looks smooth and is virtually undetectable, somewhere between light and medium coverage, yet is build-able if needed. #05 is perfect for my skin tone.... a paler medium color complexion with a slight yellow undertone. There is a fragrance, but it seems to dissipate immediately upon applying to the skin. The scent reminds me of ylang ylang, it's a bit sweet smelling rather than floral. I'm glad that the scent fades quickly since I don't care for fragrance in my foundation. This mousse style foundation gives a pretty airbrushed matte look and has the feeling of a high priced (department store) foundation. This foundation would be ideal for Normal to Oily/Combination skin, may be a bit too "dry" for dehydrated skin unless compensated with a very good moisturizer and/or exfoliation. Highly recommended!

Update: dang - tip broke right off while lining eye and now need to find something to sharpen it. Disappointed that it already broke off with only a few uses.
------
I wanted to try this eye pencil because I rarely use eyeliner -- I'm not good at it, and at my age (57) if one isn't careful, defining the eye can look harsh.

I've had great results with this product as long as I'm extremely careful how I apply it, and how much I apply. What makes it so easy to do this is how efficiently and easily the pencil glides over my eyelid. Anyone over 50 knows how weird the eyelid can become, so having a pencil that easily glides is important. No pulling at all--this pencil creates a smooth and "even line." Personally, I like just a hint of liner, so I carefully make very close "dashes" along my upper eyelid close as I can to my lashes, and then gently pat to smooth. This created the best look and I couldn't easily tell I'd used eyeliner -- which works best for me to have that subtle look. I did also try this on my lower eyelashes - but taking it only about halfway and then patting it to "smudge" -- do this carefully and the look is one where your eye is defined without the harshness.

If you are younger and can line your eyes all smoky and sexy - then you'll most probably love this pencil for the easy with which it glides.

I'd like it in another color than black - just to experiment.

I'm so happy with this product! I was a bit apprehensive because in the past when I've used eyeliner pencils, they've gone on with difficulty; either it's too sharp and hurts my eyelid or it's not sharp enough and it barely shows up. I've also experienced the pencil breaking during sharpening. I am happy to report that that is NOT the case with this pencil. It goes on extremely easily and doesn't hurt my eyelid or pull my skin in any way. Even when I sharpen it to a fine point, it still feels more like an eyeliner gel pencil during application, which made me very happy. It lasts all day and doesn't smudge, however it comes off easily when I wash my face before bed.
summary: Goes on easily and lasts all day

reviewText: I loved the Japonesque eyeliner. It goes on smoothely, both for upper, lower, and waterline/tightlining purposes. Shade 01 is a bold, rich color -- it goes on evenly, and stays on all day. It sharpens nicely in a standard eyeliner sharpener, and looks gorgeous. Since I got it, I've been reaching for it over more expensive eyeliners: it goes beautifully with both warm (copper, bronze, brown) and cooler (greys, blacks, pearls) eyeshadows.
summary: Smooth, even application for all-day wear

reviewText: I ordered this for my wife, who is a bit of a makeup snob.  She really likes this, especially for its nice lines and all day staying power.  She does feel it "travels" a bit much, which is her only complaint.
summary: Nice lines, long lasting, and almost perfect.

reviewText:
I don't wear makeup often because I have very sensitive skin. This one is said to be gentle so I decided to try it. I did not have an allergic reaction so that much is positive.

The coloring rod is fairly soft and goes on smoothly. It's much too dark for my fair skin so I smeared it to a gray shade. Unfortunately I really need a brown shade because my hair is light brown with red undertones.

One of the product illustrations in the listing shows the ingredient list. Most of the ingredients seem safe for the skin. I was curious about cyclopentasiloxane, which seems to be in the silicone family and can evaporate, so it may eventually dry out. In the Skin Deep Database I found that it has some degree of toxicity so don't put this in your mouth. Overall this product appears to be safer than the average cosmetic product.

I'd like to see this in a light reddish brown. It goes on easily, at least while it is new.

This eyeliner is creamy and goes on smoothly. I was pleasantly surprised at how thin a line I could draw and how easily it applied. Some pencils are so darn tough to get on that the line ends up being too thick for my liking and your lids are nearly torn during the process. You won't have any problems with this liner.  It really is perfection in a stick in my opinion. I softened the look by smudging with my finger.

Will continue to use and look for additional colors.

This eyeliner is pretty good. It's kind of like a very thin and soft black crayon. It goes on dark and smudges easily. It isn't waterproof though, so it somehow disappeared off my face before the day was over.
summary: This eyeliner is pretty good. It's kind of like a very thin ...

reviewText:
JAPONESQUE Eye Defining Pencil is a beautiful creamy smooth eye liner that goes on with great precision and allows you to get a thin line or do eye designs with great accuracy. It lasts all day (and night if you don't wash it off really well).  It's extremely waterproof won't smudge unless you don't allow it a minute to dry once applying.

Overall this is one of the best eye liners i've tried i'd highly recommend.

I much prefer eye-lining pencils over all the powders and "paint on" varieties that have come out in recent years.  Call me old fashioned.  If you're like me, and have owned a few dozen different brands over the decades, then you'll understand the frustration of finding a great liner, only to have the wood shaft of the pencil splinter when you sharpen it.  Cheap wood - the bane of pencils of all varieties.

When I opened the cap on this liner I was delighted to see a very tight grained light colored wood.  I itched to sharpen it right away.  I used a basic sharpener and can't tell you the happiness I felt to shave the thinnest curls of wood off the pencil.  This is made possible by the tight grain of the premium wood they encased this lovely liner inside - not by an extraordinary blade.

And the liner?  Shade 01 is the deepest pitch black I've seen in a very long time.  The pigment is super saturated so your lines are consistent from beginning to end.  It goes on very smoothly and it resists smudging and moisture for hours.  It comes off when you take it off. With sharpening you can create a super fine tip for the thinnest lines, or you can use it the way it comes for a medium width line.  The color is even and lasts all day without problem.

I'm addicted and buying the other color too.  I love it.

Added Jan 24, 2015:

So I bought color #2 not really knowing what color to expect.  I wasn't sure from the pictures if it was brown or a shade of grey.  It is definitely not brown.  It's a dark grey or a lighter black than #1.  The quality is just as good and the grain is just as tight on the wood.  #2 is a better shade for my fair complexion.  I continue to be impressed by the long-wearing quality of this eyeliner.
summary: REVISED:  High quality eyeliner that lasts all day.  #1 is super black, #2 is a more subdued black or dark grey.

reviewText: First, I am not a regular foundation user, but I did get the foundation brush recommended to try this out.  From 5 feet away, my skin looks nice; however, at close range, it is obvious that this foundation has picked out every pore and wrinkle.  Color 05 is a light beige, and matched my pale skin well...though I prefer a bit more pink as oppose to a pure beige.  Many hours after application, touching my face still leaves brown streaks on other surfaces (clothes, kleenex, etc.), so this foundation does NOT "set."  The texture is fine, and I don't notice any skin tightness (of course this may just be the lack of actual drying to the touch).  I may use this again, perhaps if I go out at night, but I don't think it would stand scrutiny in sunlight.
summary: Tub foundation; you need a real foundation brush to use

reviewText:
This foundation is not as creamy as I would expect, and does not go on as easily, smoothly as the foundation I use now and have used for several years. The color, however, is spot-on and once you get the mask on, the effect is very nice. Your skin does not look painted on, which is a huge plus.

Recommend you use some soft lotion [preferably oil-based] before applying this foundation. It makes for a much easier application.

I am always looking for high quality make up especially foundation and mascara. I have very sensitive skin and suffer from rosacea so it seems most make up either irritates/ dries my skin or exacerbates the rosacea. I am very pleased to say that Japonesque is very friendly to sensitive skin. I am fair skinned and shade 05 was a perfect match for me. The foundation is very light and even though it advises to use a brush to apply, I found that applying with my fingers worked just as well.

I highly recommend this foundation!!!

JAPONESQUE Velvet Touch Foundation, Shade 05 is light and easy to apply. My skin did not have adverse reactions. For $36 for a 5 oz jar is a bit pricey, and I find Maybelline Mousse Foundation just as light and a lot less expensive.

I gave up makeup a few year ago when B&B creams were introduced.  I love the lighter feel of a B&B cream over the stiffness of most foundations.  That is why, at first, I was skeptical to try this product.  I have never used Japonesque before and now I am really glad I did.

This product looks very thick but when applied with a brush and moisturizer it goes on like its name, velvet.  It covered my skin much better than my current B&B cream and didn't have the tightness or thickness of most other foundations.  I really love the way it feels and the way it covers up the redness in my skin.  And, like a B&B cream it can be layered where you may need additional coverage.

The price seems high at 36.00, however keep in mind you use very little of the foundation and the product should last you at least 4-6 months.

Overall a great foundation, I would definitely recommend.

Nice matt finish,  easy to apply and close up, you cannot tell you have foundation on.  Not messy to use, and last the whole day at work. Can use with blusher.  I am pretty amazed how well the blended into my skin color.
summary: Very good quality foundation, good blend.

reviewText:
I am quite light-skinned and when I was asked to try Shade 05, I thought it might be too dark.  I am more than pleasantly surprised that it blended with my skin tones.  Since you can build up the coverage, there is flexibility with this foundation, which I find unusual and of high quality.

 I have had the cosmetic on for over 12 hours, and my face remains fresh looking, I do not have to touch it up or apply an extra coat or a separate powder product.  I am very pleased to be introduced to this cream foundation.  I usually use liquid but this formula is easy to apply and a welcome change from other products.

Japonesque Velvet Touch Foundation is a velvet-like smooth, and soft foundation. It goes on lightly and feels nice and smooth. It is not heavy or greasy. It is a nice thin coverage to make a matte one color tone to the face. It is nice and dry. It's hard to describe, it's not wet and creamy but is velvety as the name states. It does not clog up or gather on the skin, it glides on and makes a nice foundation.

I have sensitive skin with rosacea and had no problems using this foundation.

I am more than pleased and will make the switch from my usual brand, Bobbi Brown. I rate this 5 stars = I Love It.
summary: Velvet-Like and Dry Foundation That Is non-Greasy and Fine For My Sensitive Skin

reviewText:
Wife likes this a lot... it's slightly darker than her normal foundation shade.  But, it gave her a warmer glow, if you will, which is perfect on those gloomy fall days here in NYS.

It lives up to its claim of velvet touch.  I like the way it looks on her.  I'm too dumb with these things to know if this is priced well or not.

One of my favourite brands for practical professional makeup tools is Japonesque, so when I heard that they were going to have a colour makeup line I was quite excited.

This lip lacquer did not disappoint. The colour is fresh, application smooth and it keeps my lips moist.  The price, as always, is reasonable.

My only complaint is that there isn't a zooming colour chart to refer to when purchasing online.
summary: Reasonably-priced, high quality lip lacquer from a professional brand.

reviewText: I really like this product and thought that I wouldn't.  It seems like it would be greasy.  You just have to be sure and blot your lips always or you will leave marksd on glassware.

This lip lacquer is not anything like your typical lip gloss.
It is richer and more pigmented than a gloss and the application is more precise and smooth with the included brush.
As for the texture, it goes on easily and dries to a soft, matte finish but not one that is too drying like many other long wearing lip products.
What impressed me the most is the intensity of the color. I usually wear a similar shade lipstick under my gloss since most glosses fade so quickly. Not this one. This is the first lip gloss that I have used that can stand alone as far as color longevity.
While it is not as intense as a traditional long wearing lipstick, the color does last and is perfect for a natural look that is still polished.
The 04 shade is a nice, soft pink that I imagine would work well for most skin complexions. FYI - The online photo of this shade appears to have a bit of brown in it but it does not.
While I normally think luxury lip glosses are not worth the premium price, this is not your average lip gloss and is worth consideration.

I was intrigued to try out this lip lacquer. It looked like lip gloss and I dislike the feel of lip gloss on my lips since it is so sticky and my hair gets in it and sticks to my lips - a mess.

I applied this lip lacquer to my lips and it felt like regular lipstick. I like the shade and the notion that it is applied with a brush which allows for greater precision. Recommended!
summary: Not that tacky, sticky lip gloss of yesteryear - more like lipstick that is applied with a brush

reviewText: The finish is matte, which I like, and the color is vibrant. Best of all, it lasts throughout my eight hour workday. However, I find application a bit chalky. It's not sticky, but it's not what I expected from a matte finish product. I like it but I'm not too sure about the application because while it does dry quickly, until it dries to the matte finish, it has an odd texture.

I thought this would be a typical lip gloss, but was delighted that it has a very beautiful matte finish.  The brush application makes it very accurate for a nice smooth line.  It made my lips look fuller, too.  It has a very light, quickly fading vanilla/sugary scent which is very pleasing.  It's long lasting and this color - shade 04 - is a beautiful natural pink that is very flattering to my light complexion.  I had not heard of this brand before trying this lip lacquer (I generally use lancome) but I like this so much, I want to try their other cosmetics.
summary: Gorgeous matte finish, beautiful, natural color

reviewText:
I found this lip color very close to what it looks like on the picture -- a nice soft hue.

The feel of it was a bit discouraging -- too chalky and clumpy for my liking. However, the color stayed on for most of the day, which was helpful.

It's a decent product but overpriced (currently $20 on amazon). I think there are better lip conditioners and glosses out there that last longer and that go on much smoother (I like Sephora's line, personally).
summary: ... this lip color very close to what it looks like on the picture -- a nice soft hue

reviewText:
I don't normally go for liquid lipstick and I absolutely hate gloss, but this product really surprised me.

It goes on beautifully.  The coverage is exceptional.  It comes with a brush applicator, rather than one of those doe foot things  I don't like those.  The product is neither gloppy nor sticky.  It feels really comfortable on; it moves and stretches with my lips without drying.  It lasts a pretty long time.  I went until lunch time without needing a touch up.  And its one step  theres no separate balm or clear coat necessary.

My only gripe is that I wish it came in a larger range of colors.  With only eight shades to choose from, the color range is a little limited. Theyre all strictly roses, pinks, and traditional reds, too.  There isn't one single edgy color.  But then again, this is my first experience with the brand, so for all I know edgy just isn't their thing.  I got Shade 4, which is a bright, bubblegum pink that did not flatter me at all.

All in all, my experience was positive enough that Im willing to certainly try another shade in this product (Shade 8, perhaps, would be more my style?) and am open to their other products as well.
summary: Great lipstick but a very limited range of colors.

reviewText:
This Japonesque lip lacquer is a very nice product. The lip lacquer feels substantial and goes on easily with a brush, not a applicator nub. The lip lacquer seems to stay on the lips for about the same time as regular lipstick.

The problem with Japonesque is that the color (shade 04) doesn't match the online color chart. With shade 04, because of the color chart, I expected brownish pink. Instead shade 04 is bubble gum pink- no brown at all. Shade 04  would work better for those who prefer pink makeup.
summary: Nice Product that has a Substantial Feel. Shade 04 is Bubble Gum Pink & Doesn't Match Color Chart Shown

reviewText:
