I like this lipstick it was a good color and went on easy, but I wasn't impressed with the consistency. It went on very tacky and I was expecting a high gloss but it was kind of matte. The paint-brush like stick made it a little harder to paint my lips - since I'm used to Lip Lacquer having the snub tip applicator.

Overall, it was a good Lip Lacquer - but it didn't blow me away.
summary: Pretty shade, not a great consistency

reviewText:
I first balked at the cost of this product but was fortunate to be able to try it.  Normally we never spend this amount on what i socmmonly known as lip gloss.  We were pleasantly surprised.

The lacquer itself is much thicker and deeply colored than anything we have tried before.  The viscosity allows for precise application and the brush is likely the best I have ever used.  The product provides a matte finish as opposed to shiny gloss and does not harden when dried.  Somehow, it seems to remain moist while not coming off easily.  There is very litle smeel associated with the product- best described as slightly sweet.  In our use (3 girls tested the product), we all agreed the prodcut stayed applied for hours and did not lose intensity of color.

NOTE ON COLOR SWATCHES IN PRODUCT INFORMATION:  As a photographer, it is important for me to point out that it is very difficult to match exact shades of the product you are looking for through a computer monitor.  The vast majority of computer monitors do not display colors accurately, particualrly different shades of the same color unless your monitor is capable and color calibrated.  Even then, unless the manufacturer created a white balanced and color balanced image and exported it perfectly, there will still be a variance.  In short, you may want to visit a local store that has the hardcopy color swatches.

Very Nice lipgloss. The applicator brush is easy to use and allows you to line and fill easily. The lipgloss has a nice sheen, feels very comfortable to wear and isn't sticky or tacky feeling. It's not a lip stain so don't expect all day coverage, however, it does last a long time for lipgloss.

The color is very opaque in my opinion. It's more like a blend of a lipstick with a high sheen than just the sheer lipgloss.

This particular shade (4), is very pink. I would call it carnation pink.
summary: Very Nice lipgloss. The applicator brush is easy to use ...

reviewText: This is different from anything else I have ever tried.  Expected it to be a gloss but it is more opaque and matte than a gloss.  The color is more intense and has much higher coverage than a gloss.  It is moist but not greasy or sticky.  The color stays on quite well for hours.  The packaging feels high quality.  The gloss has a faint nougat sweet kind of scent.  I like this,  and would reconsider repurchasing, but would be afraid to purchase online because the color swatches do not match reality.  Based on the swatches I would have expected no 4 to be a very warm clay pink.  It is actually a very cool  dark peony kind of pink.  Not sure whether the color shift applies equally to all the swatches shown, but my experience with No 4 would make ordering online a little precarious.
summary: Very nice but colors do not match the online swatches, making reordering online precarious

reviewText: The colors in this palette are relatively true to the tones reflected in the photographs, and they do last all day with a bit of primer (I use Too Faced primer). However, I'm a bit disappointed with the fall-off quality. When I load my brushes, I feel like more of this brand falls off the brush during application and on to my face/into the air. I typically do my eye make-up first to fight this issue, but I think it is worth noting that the Japonesque brand seems to be a bit worse about this than Urban Decay and Too-Faced. It's actually more like a Smashbox competitor for me...mostly good, but not 100%.
summary: A bit of fall-off but good color representation

reviewText:
This shadow palette is the first product I've tried by Japonesque, and I'm not that impressed with it.  I love makeup and consider myself a makeup junkie, and my favorite eyeshadows are usually those by MAC and Urban Decay.  The texture and color payoff of these Japonesque shades are not up to par with those other brands, especially given the cost of the Japonesque shadows.

It's hard to tell from the photo, but the 02 shade set is a lovely mix of taupe and purple-y browns, and the colors make my green eyes pop. (For color reference, I'm pretty fair and wear MAC foundation in NW20 or Bare Minerals in Fairly Light; I have green eyes and auburn-brown hair.)  The upper right color is similar to MAC's Woodwinked, and the bottom left color is this gorgeous purple-y brown that is very unique.  However, they have a very chalky texture and are hard to apply; even with my Urban Decay primer underneath, I had a hard time getting these to show up, and had to add multiple layers.

The case on this is also so pretty.  You can barely see it in the photo, but the upper lid is a unique design that adds a richness to the feel of this. The entire inside of the lid is also a mirror, which makes this perfect for travel or on-the-go touch-ups.

Overall, I feel like this is a mediocre product, and am honestly surprised by how much it costs.  For the same price, you'd be better off building a custom palette at MAC or Inglot, or buying one of Urban Decay's smaller palettes.
summary: Shade 02 set is fantastic for green eyes, but not a lot of color payoff

reviewText:
I apply eye shadow with a soft brush, and this stuff was so hard just to get on the brush, I'd hardly call it velvet. The colors are nice, I just don't find the texture of this compact easy to apply at all. The shadow is hard and chalky. Maybe it is best applied another way. It's hard to say when no applicator is included. For the price, you'd think they could swing that.
Overall I've liked Japonesque products, but not this one.
I don't expect to buy their powder-based products anymore.

My wife has brown hair and olive complexion and she loves this shade (#2). There are four shades of brown - nice and natural earth-tone colors. If you have olive or dark skin complexion, this will be perfect for you. Still usable if you have light skin, though.

I like the darker brown personally since it's ideal for evenings and it's a bit mysterious too. My wife plans to use the shadow in the fall and winter season, but likely just sparingly in spring and summer.

The only thing missing... a brush to apply. It would be nice if one were included.
summary: Perfect for olive and dark skin complexion

reviewText:
As a preface, I am a huge makeup collector and I have eyeshadow from many companies.  I can appreciate different textures and pigmentation.  My favorite eyeshadows are from Urban Decay, Lorac, Tarte, Bare Minerals Ready, Smashbox (Photo Op only), Too Faced, etc.  Sorry to say, but this palette was a miss for me - especially considering the price of $34.  This is Elf quality makeup.  If you are used to high quality, easy to blend, creamy eyeshadows you WILL not like this.  At $34, I couldn't help but remember that my beloved Too Faced Natural Eyes palette was $36 - $2 more for 9 shadows (as opposed to 4) and all are far superior in quality.

On the positive side, the packaging is beautiful and sturdy with a nice mirror.  The size is great for travel and the colors look very nice.  I love warm neutrals.  Unfortunately, however, the quality of these shadows is sub-par.  The two top shadows have virtually no pigment and leave a virtually undetectable wash of shimmer on the eye.  The bottom left shadow is a bit better, but is still kind of dry.  The matte brown is the most pigmented of the bunch but is stiff and dry and hard to blend.
summary: the packaging is beautiful and sturdy with a nice mirror

reviewText:
Let's start with a little honesty. I'm no beauty guru. In fact, I'm a stay at home mom of three, which means that if I'm lucky, I put makeup on once a week. But I still LOVE makeup! So, while I'm no expert, I DO own more than my fair share of beauty products, even though I use them quite sparingly.
This JAPONESQUE eye shadow palette is simply stunning. I actually audibly gasped when I pulled it out of the box. It's GORGEOUS. The box is a show piece, and three of the four shadows are beautifully shimmery. At first I was a little disappointed because when applying the shadow it didn't seem to have much hue to it and appeared to be far less bright than I thought they'd be. However, after a full ten hours of wear, they the colors looked EXACTLY the same as when I applied them! I was really impressed with the longevity of the colors. So, to be honest, that's a pretty good trade-off, as I have no need to look like I'm going clubbing, but I DO want my eyeshadow to stay put all day long.
One draw back, which I know is common to higher end eye shadow, it does not come with an applicator, so make sure you have one or a makeup brush handy if you purchase this. But who doesn't, right?! Overall a great, beautiful, and durable product that I would certainly purchase in the future!

This shadow palette comes in a very attractive case, with four shades of browns.  The colors are mostly from talc and are firmly in their dividers.  There is no applicator brush with this, though.  One can use one's finger (but that causes the color to get hardened by skin oils) or use a separate brush to apply the shadow over the lid.  The good thing is that this talc-based color does not crease easily in the skin.  The shades are very complimentary.  This is a nice collection of browns for younger women.

This has the most gorgeous case--a shiny lacquer finish with vivid abstract splotches on it. The colors are lovely neutrals, reminiscent of my former favorite Dior shadow palette, but, alas, like my former favorite, three of them are too shimmery for my aging eyelids. Supposedly one is metallic and two are pearls, but it is hard to tell the difference. The matte brown is lovely, with a great payoff, but not the staying power of my Bobbi Brown mattes. The shiny shades are way too shiny for anything other than the very inner corner and brow bone, despite being lovely neutral colors. Even smoothing with my finger, which sometimes helps, doesn't help. I can wear Trish McEvoy Glazes without any problem, but these are too shiny.

sigh The case is so gorgeous....
summary: Gorgeous case, probably great shadows for younger eyes, but....

reviewText: The colors are great for me, it goes on smooth, it gives just a little sparkle which is a nice look as long as it isn't heavy. It is not a shadow that will last all day though. I found that it rubs off easily or just wears off during the day so it would need to be touched up at some point during the day. It also leaves a crease after a while which in all fairness most eye shadows do. I have had a hard time finding a shadow that will not crease at some point during the day.

This is my first time using a product from Japonesque. I really love the concept that they create unique shade for so many different skin tones. The shadow colors for Shade 02 consist of a deep matt brown I use as the definition shade and then the three other colors provide slightly different hues of light shimmer. The overall look is a very lovely subtle shadow. I have worn it out for more subdued evenings out. I like a more dramatic look for evening out on the town. But both daytime and casual evening it's a perfect match.
I was a little surprised that there is no applicator. I used my own brush at home but for travel it's one extra accessory to bring.
I do love the big mirror in the pretty case.
I will likely try more Japonesque products. I especially like the emphasis on a more natural look.

This is the first Japonesque beauty product I have tried and I am very pleased. I have dark hair and dark brown eyes and dark skin and the Shade 02 is perfect for me.

There are four eye powder eye shadow colors in the compact. There is a warm, cocoa brown color that has a matte finish. The other 3 shadows are metallic and include a light gold color, a coppery bronze color and a medium brown. The shades are subtle enough that with my coloring, they are suitable for daytime wear.

The powder is silky and glides on effortlessly for me with no dragging. There is no applicator included but I always throw them away anyway. I apply my eyeshadow with the tip of my little finger.

I haven't had any problem with this shadow settling into the crease of my eyelid like some shadows do.

The compact is beautifully designed to resemble Japanese black lacquer with purple, light blue and green, free-form splashes of color on the top. It's square and also has a mirror inside for checking your makeup on the go.

My only issue with this product is the price. It's more than I would likely pay for eye shadow but that's just me. However, if I found it on sale, I would definitely buy this shadow set when I use this up.

I recently made the switch from Maybelline Matte Mousse foundation to NARS Radiant Cream foundation. I've really been on the fence about this change because I love how NARS feels, but I hate how shiny it makes my face.

The Japonesque finishing powder was just what I needed!

It matted down my face substantially so it doesn't look like I'm sweating profusely.

Make sure you learn how to use it, first, because it can make you look dead if you don't.

I've just started realizing that I've reached the age where a little makeup can do wonders for perking up my pale complexion and covering some freckles that have morphed into *gasp* age spots.

I've always gone the natural face way so I had no idea what finishing powder was.  The first thing I did was to just apply it to my freshly washed and moisturized face.  And looked like a corpse.  I couldn't imagine that was a "look" that most people are going for.  So I did a little research and found that typically finishing powder is applied on top of foundation.  So I washed and moisturized again, then applied some Bare Minerals foundation, which I haven't been loving as much lately because it seemed to give me a wrinkled paper look that wasn't flattering (or desired).  Since I'm an artist by trade, I decided to use the Japonesque as I would highlight a painting or drawing. Very nice.  But not WOW.  So, again with the washing and moisturizer.  This time I used some creamy foundation from Maybelline.  Then touched up the shiny spots with the Japonesque and WOW!!  My skin looked like a porcelain doll's, beautiful, even and lovely. Love it, love it, love it.

It comes in a cute but expensive looking case that stays shut in my bag or drawer. and includes an application sponge.  But I think it goes on better with a big, fluffy brush.  The texture of the powder is very silky and light and it makes my skin feel smooth like velvet, even with liquid foundation which tends to make even my dry skin look and feel a little greasy.  It also covers up spots very well and evens out the skin beautifully with a matte effect.  It looks really light in the package but it didn't change the shade of my makeup, it just made it all come together and look, well, finished.  It's translucent so it just blends in with whatever I am wearing and makes my skin look luminous.

I was worried at first because the power is white, and was afraid if this was going to make me look like a ghost. Fortunately it goes on light or, at least, I put it on lightly and it is enough for me to have a smooth coverage without changing the color of my face. I would advise against using too much. It feels light and comfortable on my combination skin, and the case is quite pretty.

This is a very sophisticated case with a very sophisticated product. My face tends to be on the greasy side, so I always aim to have some kind of finishing powder that seals my face and keeps it from looking brilliant right away. This one works very well so far, with no color whatsoever you can apply it on top of any make up you normally wear or simply without any other makeup underneath. It works wonders for hitting the gym with no other make-up on. You will look fresh as long as you don't sweat it off. The mirror is the perfect size and makes me wish other face powders came in a case like this one. Definitely a brand I'd purchase from.

This is a great product for erasing the shine on your face. If you want to get rid of an oily buildup, definitely this product. It's great to use over a liquid coverup, if you desire.

Katiebabs
summary: Pleasing Powder to Erase the Oil (B Grade)

reviewText: The powder is very light, I don't even feel like I'm wearing any make-up.  It blends beautifully and helps diminish some fine lines and darker pigmented skin (like my freckles).  I love the fashionable case and the fact that when you close it, it stays closed until you click the latch to open it back up.  That's very important to me as carry it in my purse and it's a bundle of loose items.

Very nice finishing powder after applying foundation. It is very fine powder and has a silky matte translucent shine when applied, very lovely results and doesn't change the appearance of the foundation, it just helps to reduce the shine and make it look beautifully nature and even. The applicator included is not real useful, you should have a nice large powder brush to apply this for best results.
summary: Very lovely powder for finishing your foundation

reviewText:
The JAPONESQUE Velvet Touch Finishing Powder is light and silky and gives my face a polished, matte finish. The powder is very fine and delicate and doesn't settle into the small lines under my eyes - a problem I have with the mineral powder I had been using.

This powder is best applied sparingly and with a light touch. I have a pale complexion and didn't need to use a lot - too much gave me a washed out look. It took a few attempts to find just the right amount to use, but once I did, I was able to achieves a translucent look. I use a big fluffy brush rather than the sponge applicator which comes with the compact. The sponge tends to apply the powder a little too heavily for me, however it works well for touch-ups on oily areas later in the day.

The powder comes in a very pretty compact case with a large mirror. The case closes tightly which at first was annoying, but later I appreciated that it stays firmly closed when carried in my purse or bag.
summary: Light, silky powder and a translucent finish

reviewText:
This powder performs the main job I expect when it comes to a face powder: it produces a more matte finish in oily areas of the face and helps to set foundation. However, while the description speaks of "blurring imperfections" and "silky color," I don't really find that it provides much coverage. Or at least, I can't use enough to get coverage without looking chalky, though it's fine if used with a light hand. For this reason, I really prefer using a powder brush instead of the included flat sponge, which I also felt removed too much foundation. Since this powder has a tendency to look too pale on me (my foundation color is usually "light") I'd have reservations about recommending it for deeper skin tones unless you know from experience how translucent powder works for you.

The case is excellent - attractive, sturdy and with a nice-sized mirror - though perhaps a bit difficult to open.

I have tended to prefer loose powder personally. However, when I use this side-by-side with my own favorite shade of loose mineral powder I cannot tell any difference in the results. It hasn't won my brand loyalty, but it's a decent pick.
summary: provides a nice matte finish when used with a light touch

reviewText: My girlfriend wanted to start using a finishing powder so she tried this one out.  The compact is nice because it comes with a mirror, and unlike other finishing powders that she's tried, this one is a compressed powder.  Even when using a small amount, she felt that it washed out her skin tone and left behind a pale color even though it's supposed to be invisible.  She's also tried Bare Essentials mineral veil as well and prefers that to this JAPONESQUE product.
summary: Leaves a pale finish even in small amounts

reviewText:
I have light skin, large pores, and a shiny face.  I look so amazingly matte, small pored and perfect when I use this!  I really like it. It is so lightweight on the face, non pore clogging, the powder is really light colored and I thought I might have a bright white face, but it just sort of mattes the face without adding a lot of weight or color.

I love it.  I look fabulous.  I have used the sponge enclosed and a brush.  Both provide a great result.

I am switching from benefit cosmetics to this velvet touch finishing powder.  I love the result.

I wasn't sure what to expect with this but I was concerned because the powder is so light and I am olive skinned. I don't often wear foundation but as I age, my skin isn't as even as it used to be. So I've been applying this as a way to even things out. It is silky smooth and leaves a faint lighter tone. You don't need much and my skin feels really soft all day.

It's nice and comes with a mirror and a powder pad for application.
summary: Silky Smooth, Leaves a Faint Light Tone

reviewText:
Powder is the usual finishing touch after foundation to matte down the infamous 'T-zone' of forehead and nose that most of us have. Japonesque Finishing Powder is translucent, meaning that it works for probably all but the darkest complexions. (I'm a twin to Snow White, so it's rare a powder is ever too light for me.)

As for the powder itself, I'm in love! The finish truly is silky; the powder is whisper light and imparts a very, very subtle glow. That means that your T-zone oiliness is tamped down, but the skin doesn't look DEAD. It looks radiant, alive - matte and beautiful. (The compact comes with an applicator, but I'm a brush girl myself.)

Working with this powder is a sensual delight! It's so silky and fine that it feels like a beauty treatment just putting it on. The luxurious case is just an added bonus and will do your handbag proud.
summary: I'm in love! Probably THE perfect powder!

reviewText:
I rated Japonesque Velvet Touch Finishing Powder 4 stars because it is a nice finishing powder. At first I thought the color would be to light and cast a white effect but all you need a tiny bit applied to a large powder brush ( i use Eco Brand) instead of using the sponge applicator it came with.

I originally thought this was an Asian product from Japan but it is actually made in Italy. The case is beautiful and well made. The mirror is a perfect size to carry with you and reapply makeup,  if needed.

Overall, I did not notice an illuminating effect like my other finishing powder which I like but it does give a nice matte finish that helps eliminate shiny foreheads and T-zone area. This did not make me break out and is best used applied lightly on oily parts.

The compact on this powder has a pretty design, a good-sized mirror (you can see your whole face), and a soft sponge for application.

This powder itself has a light, smooth, airy feel. Actually, a velvety feel, so it's aptly named. It's purpose is to set makeup and give skin a matte finish, and it delivers those results as promised. The "mattifying" lasts for several hours, probably longer if your skin is very dry.

The shade is sort of an egg-shell white, which the manufacturers say is universal. This is true, to some extent, but I'd caution those who use it to APPLY WITH A LIGHT HAND. I mention this because if you apply it heavily, you get a "lightening" effect. In other words, you'll see white on your face. This is not to say the product has any glitter or pearl. It does not. Still, use too much, and you'll notice that white look.

Four stars instead of five because of the color, which is a little tricky to apply (at first) without getting a too-pale look.

Finishing powder is meant to be used on top of foundation, not on your bare skin. My wife was a little skeptical of the advertisement of the product as having no tint or color. It claims to be universal, for all skin tones, but it's white by itself. So the foundation must provide your natural skin color beneath the finishing powder. She was very pleased with the product, how it softens or gives a "matte" look to the blush she uses. It blends in very well and gives a fresh look to the makeup. It doesn't hide imperfections, but keeps your skin from looking glossy. It feels very light on the skin, not like a "mask". It worked well under the humid conditions in Hawaii, and for her medium tan, caucasian complexion. Overall its a high quality powder and she was completely satisfied.
summary: Works as promised, for medium tan, caucasian skin tone

reviewText:
I've used every brand of concealer around-from the expensive stuff to the drug store stuff. This is one the best. I had never heard of his brand before nor tried any of their products. I didn't know what to expect. First, color is fab and the texture is like silk. It went on smoothly with a brush, finger or sponge. Second, it stayed put all day, and a little went a long way. The compact was a nice touch, too. Rarely do concealers come packaged this way and the packaging is chic.

The only drawback is the price. I got mine for free, but if I had to pay, I may have hesitated a bit. $30 is a lot for concealer, but this does work well. When I run out, I may just bite the bullet and pay up. It is the best I have used so far.
summary: Elegant, beautiful product that gives great coverage.

reviewText:
I've used Japonesque tools before (palettes, brushes) but never makeup so this was a first for me. Usually there are 2 types of concealer-concealer for circles and concealer for blemishes. This is the kind for blemishes, even if it's in a palette and not a tube. It's very soft and I could see using a brush, although I use my fingers. (I've used Laura Mercier before and this reminded me of her concealer for blemishes.)
I'm  fair with pink undertones and shade 2 went on yellow-BUT blended in totally. 5 minutes after applying it I couldn't tell I was wearing (undereye) concealer-it just looked like I was even-toned. Becuase I have dry skin and was using it in winter the 'velvet' finish didn't help me, it just accentuated my dry skin, and that's why i'm giving it 4 stars out of 5. (I'd give it 41/2 if I could). It also never made me breakout and didn't feel heavy at all. And it didn't migrate all day.
If you have yellow undertones and are looking for a blemish concealer, this is great. I really need a heavier concealer for circles but I'm keeping this handy for my chin breakouts. Also this has a really pretty cover that looks great on your dresser (or bathroom sink).
summary: Creamy and Covering w a Velvet Finish

reviewText: Nice little compact, can fit just about anywhere, your purse, your pocket. Very smooth, like velvet, goes on just a little or heavier if necessary. Does not cake and is good for dry skin though not greasy. I apply it with my finger tips for just a little coverage, but you can use a makeup brush for better coverage. A little pricey for such a small amount. However, I like it!

I have very fair skin, so I thought this might be too dark, but it blended well. The coverage is amazing! I usually don't bother with concealers because they don't cover what I want covered, and they show under my regular makeup.

This works greats for all kinds of marks, and it feels like there is nothing on my skin. I'm very pleasantly surprised by how well this works.

So far I love it. Great coverage without looking cakey. It doesn't have a super matte finish, just perfect for natural looking. I use it in my t zone and under eyes and it doesn't sits in the lines and pores. it does have soft focus finish. Great for touch ups (I use fingers, blends fast and beautiful).
Shade 2 is perfect for my NW 20-25 complexion, it brightens me up. It has yellow undertone and it is lighter that in the package.

Very nice creamy concealer for fuller coverage.  I really liked the thick formula on this product, it can be blended out very thinly or it can be built up for fuller coverage.  I like to dab a bit on my fingers and warm it up and then work it in with a brush.  I really liked the slightly peach tone, as it will cover up the darker circles better.  Very nice.

This reminded me a lot of Laura Mercier's concealer that I like quite a bit.  This had very nice and elegant packaging.

I look forward to trying other products from this line.

This is a full coverage concealer with a matte finish. It is very creamy and easy to apply with a makeup sponge, wet or dry. Shade 2 matches my light asian skin tone perfectly or if it's a bit off, I can mix in other concealers to get the perfect color. It seems to stay on throughout the day, with primer, foundation, and finish. It doesn't feel cakey or look cakey at all. The only gripe I have about it is that it does contain paraben, so if you are wary of these chemicals, it does contain parabens, thus the one star taken off. It is a great concealer otherwise.

I received this concealer in Shade 02.  I have a very light olive complexion (Greek heritage) and have had problems finding a shade that would work for me.  This was perfect for my green undertones.  I have considerable broken capillaries on one side my nose that developed when I was pregnant with my first child.  I like to conceal these but most concealers rub off in just a few minutes.  While this one is not waterproof, it stayed on very well for most of the day.  I had to reapply twice but compared to other concealers that is hardly at all.

I am very pleased with the color, the coverage, and the staying power of this concealer and will certainly buy more and other products in this line.

I don't wear a lot of makeup or tend to spend money on it, so my usual concealer is an inexpensive store brand.  I was always happy with it, but I much prefer the Japonesque concealer now that I've tried it.

The concealer is very smooth and creamy and comes in a cute little case. Being a natural redhead, my skin is quite fair but the 02 shade works well for me.  I had to purchase a small brush to use with the concealer, but the brush makes the application easy and effective.  I've used it for small spots as well as to even my skin tones over larger areas, and it works well for both. I don't use foundation, but after applying the concealer I use powder and the finished effect is very even and holds up well over the course of the day.

At first glance this seems to be a promising product but unfortunately in spite of the really cool packaging it fails to deliver. The case of this concealer is fabulous,  the color scheme is pretty and it comes with a handy mirror. The concealer glides on smoothly and has a velvety feel, as far as coverage it did cover/conceal very well. I used it under my eye and to cover a few blemishes. The section under my eye got streaky midday, and the tint on top of my blemishes sort of changed to a yellow tint. I have admit that when I put it on maybe the light I had didn't show the color difference right off the bat. But the product creasing is a huge no-no even with the right shade. As much as I loved the packaging I'm not impressed with the concealer itself.

While I like the texture of this concealer, I'm just not impressed overall. I run on the neutral side of fair-light thanks to blue, pink and yellow undertones and unfortunately, like many concealers this was way too yellow hued for me (I got Shade 02). It looked very obvious even after lots of blending. I also found that it did not conceal redness (I have a doozy of a zit right now and have cheek redness) well which is my primary need when it comes to concealer.

I do love this case though! It's elegant, just the right size and has a mirror which is great for touch-ups. So while I didn't fall in love with this concealer I was impressed enough with the brand that I would consider checking out their other products such as the Velvet Touch Blush or their many brushes.
summary: Too yellow for me, but the texture is lovely.

reviewText: I love this adorable little compact. It's a cute size and small enough to be convenient to put in your purse. Right now I don't have a concealer brush to use with it, so I used my finger. Just use a very light tough, and almost a light tapping to spread it around. And go light, not heavy. It left a soft look and blended well into my skin. I didn't even have to use a foundation. I just applied to a few red and bumpy areas on my face. But it leaves such a smooth finish, I almost would like to put it all over my face. But I didn't . It blended well. This can be for people who do not like using foundation or makeup in general, but just like to cover some little imperfections, but you could also use this after putting on foundation or before putting on powder to cover any areas where you need a little extra coverage. The small size and pretty colored compact would make this a nice stocking stuffer. What would be cool is if the company started putting a little brush right inside. But until I get one, my finger worked just fine. Just tap and blend lightly - no rubbing it on.  That really just ends up rubbing it off.

Super nice product.  Goes on with a velvet feel to it and covers nicely.  #2 is just a tad dark for my complexion so I am going to order #1.  My skin is very fair so I am passing this along to my significant other to use on his sunspots.

I have purchased many concealers over the years and so far, I like this one the best.  This is my first purchase of a Japonesque product and if this is an indication of the quality, I will be ordering more items.  A definite recommend.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
Update, I ordered #1 and it is perfect for my complexion.  This covers well and feels velvety and creamy.  Really pleased.  My sister tried it too and is ordering some for herself.

JAPONESQUE Velvet Touch Concealer comes in a small (approx 1.5 x 1.5 inch), attractive case with a mirror inside its cover.  There is not much product included for the price.  I thought the concealer blended in well and did a good job covering pimples.  However, I did not think that it worked as well hiding my dark spots.  Overall, I did not find it to work any better on my skin problems than less expensive concealers.  Therefore, I would not recommend.
summary: Did not work well on my dark spots

reviewText: I have pail skin and freckles.  This shade is a good one for me.  It works well to hide the dark circles under my eyes.  It goes on smooth and even, and blends nicely on smaller, trouble areas.  It is not heavy at all, which is nice.  It comes off cleanly when washed and doesn't leave any residue on the skin. I did have a bit of a hard time getting good full coverage on my whole face.  Overall, it's great for darker spots, but I didn't care for it for full face application.
summary: Great for trouble spots, not really a full face concealer for me

reviewText: JAPONESQUE Velvet Touch Concealer, Shade 02 is a good concealer. For $20 for a small compact is a more expensive than 5-10 dollar concealers that do the same thing. No adverse skin issues, yet more than I'd pay for a concealer that is just as good as other, less expensive brands.

Long  awaited product.  Superior coverage, blends like magic.  Even after many hours of wear it did not break down, no product caking in small wrinkles.
Very pleased with this concealer, a little goes a long way, complete coverage for deep dark coloration under eyes.
Will also be checking out the other offerings of this brand "Japonesque".
Highly recommend this concealer.

This is one of the better concealers I've used. It has good coverage for blemishes and areas of discoloration and uneven skin tone. The "flexible" texture is one of my favorite aspects of good concealers. They don't dry out blemishes and cause flaking of the skin, which then causes the makeup to come off as well. Instead it stays somewhat soft, but then the matte finish keeps it from looking shiny. So it's a nice combination. The finish covers and blends the concealer into foundation makeup, but then the "flexible" texture keeps skin from drying out.

While the price is higher than a typical drug store makeup, I find it also covers better and lasts on the skin longer. It's a very tiny compact of makeup, so don't let the product photo make confuse you into thinking this is large like the size of a pressed powder compact. This little case is the size of a 50 cent piece, so it will fit inside even the smallest of handbags. The shade 02 was perfect for my skin tone. I have fair skin, but it's still one shade darker than the typical ivory or porcelain skin shade. So 02 was perfect for me. Very nice!
summary: Doesn't dry out skin/blemishes and also has a matte finish, so it blends right into foundation makeup

reviewText:
The Japonesque Velvet Touch Concealer is a cream concealer in a pot for relatively full coverage. Instead of a plain pot, it comes in a small compact of shiny black plastic with decorative strokes of purple, pink and white on the top, 1 3/8 inches square and about 1/2 inch deep (4.3 x 1.3 cm). There is a small mirror inside the lid. There are only 1.5 grams (0.052 oz.) of concealer in the compact. I have the 02 shade, which is a little light for my light olive skin. It works well on some areas of my face, but the 03 shade would be better on others. The tone is relatively cool, not warm, and perhaps a little peachy.

I normally use Mac's Studio Finish Concealer, so I compared the Velvet Touch Concealer to that. The Velvet Touch has a very smooth and creamy consistency. It is thick enough to stay in place but not as thick as the Mac concealer. I use a sponge-tipped applicator to get the Mac concealer just on the spot I want it; if I want to cover a large area, I use a brush. The sponge-tipped applicator was not as successful with the Velvet Touch Concealer, but a brush worked very well. The Velvet Touch glides on exceptionally smoothly, and it blends easily using the tip of the brush. I was very pleased with how easily this concealer covered blemishes and blended seamlessly. The Mac concealer blends nicely also, but it requires more work.

As the Velvet Touch Concealer worked so well on blemishes, I had high hopes for it covering hyperpigmentation. This didn't work as well. The Velvet Touch is not heavy enough to cover dark spots or patches. It goes on smoothly and easily with a brush, much more easily than Mac Studio Finish Concealer, but it doesn't cover as well. Dabbing it on with a sponge tip or trying to build it up didn't help much. Dark areas show through. I am very happy with its coverage of blemishes, though. The velvety matte texture is a perfect match for my skin, and it blends nearly flawlessly with a few flicks of the brush. Even without foundation, it is just about undetectable.

As there is increasing concern about the safety of ingredients in cosmetic products, I should mention that this concealer contains propylparaben, a preservative and endocrine disruptor. For the benefit of those with allergies or other concerns, this is the full list of ingredients: isodecyl, neopentanoate, polytheylene, C12-15 alkyl benzoate, isocetyl stearate, ethylhexyl pamitate, mica, silica, vp/eicosene copolymer, synthetic fluorphlogopite, orzanol, tocopheryl, acetate, lecithin, tocopherol, ascorbyl palmitate, glyceryl stearate, glyceryl oleate, citric acid, propylparaben. May contain: CI 77492, CI 77491, CI 77499 (iron oxides), CI 77891 (titanium dioxide). The "may contain" ingredients are pigments.
summary: Impressive Texture. Great Coverage for Blemishes. Less So for Hyperpigmentation.

reviewText: Goes on smoothly.  It covers blemishes, freckles, and age spots quite well.  It blends easily and cannot be seen once foundation is applied.  It is a very small package of concealer.  This is great as it fits in the purse but, because I think it is not in line with the price, I took a star away.
summary: It blend easily and cannot be seen once foundation is applied

reviewText:
If you order Shade 02, when it arrives you may be tempted to think there was a terrible error at the factory because it looks really orange in the bottle.  Rest assured that it does not look orange on your face.

Although it goes on fairly sheer, there is a peach tint to it so if peachy shades look good on you, Shade 02 might be a good color for you.  The color is sheer but the shimmery bits are not and they show up the most.

I've worn this two different ways.  I have mixed a little bit in with the tinted moisturizer I use as foundation.  In the mirror at home I didn't notice much difference but under the fluorescent lights of the office, my face looked noticeably glowing and shimmery -- perhaps more shimmery than I prefer for work but not so much that anyone commented on it.  I also have just put it on the cheekbones as suggested on the Amazon catalog page.  I noticed that much less at work and almost could not tell in my bathroom mirror.  It will take some playing around with this to get the right level of luminosity without being too shimmery.

Update:  The more I have used this, the more I like it so I raised this by a star.  I now use it exclusively mixed in with my tinted moisturizer. With practice I have gotten the balance just right so I have a glow but don't look too shiny.  The other day one of my co-workers commented that I had a glow about me -- and I fessed up that it was due to this product more than anything.
summary: Don't be fooled by the bottle -- it's not as orange as it looks

reviewText:
Not sure why it matters what color this illuminator is in the bottle--Liquid Light looks no different than any other illuminator I've ever used. Illuminator is generally a translucent product, Actually, I think it's great that Japonesque offers slightly different shades for a more exacting tone. If it looks orange when you put it on, you're using too much--this isn't tinted moisturizer or foundation!

That said, if you're familiar with illuminator, you won't be put off by the color. Comparing with others that I've used, what I like best about Liquid Light is just that--it's really the lightest illuminator I've ever tried. It absorbs immediately and feels great--it leaves a subtly smooth, satiny texture to your skin, and doesn't 'sit' there or look filmy at all. It's high on the reflecting particles, which I'm not too fond of, but if you're looking for an illuminator that is part-shimmer, this is it.

One way or another, it does certainly brighten your complexion. Looks great at a short distance as it really does capture light, so I think this would be great photo-makeup as well. It all depends on what you're looking for--but if these elements fits your taste, you'll be quite happy with this product.

Wow, the shine and radiance! It's good to highlight features. Very easy to apply and easy to wash off.
Long lasting and beautiful.

I have a light/peachy complexion and after reading some of the other reviews I was worried about how it would look. I think it looks good. And since it is so orange coming out and lightly sparkly I had my biggest critic, my mother, look at it in natural light and indoors to be sure it looked good and she said it did as well.

I don't honestly know how to use something like this as a highlighter. I imagine I could look it up online, but I won't bother. It's gives a great and brightening all over coverage.
summary: Good Overall Coverage - Not Overly Orange or Sparkly

reviewText:
I was very surprised at the color when I received the Kaponsque Liquid Light Shade 02 in the mail. this product has more orange undertones than any lightening/brightening product I own. I tried this on with bare skin and I immeditly washed it off. My face looked orange no doubt about it. I applied my foumdation, Naked Skin by Urben Decay in shade 3 and then applied a half a pump on the top of my hands and dabed ontop of my cheekbones with a foundation brush. This looked much better but still wasn't entirely impressed with the color on my skin. It left small sparked on my skin which I did not like. Though it was a brighter orange color it did lighten up some once spread onto my skin but I felt it made me look like I had a bad spray tan on my cheeks.

The packaging was very nice, the pump worked well.  However this did not work well with me skin and perhaps someone with a more darker skin tone my appreciated this more.

I actually really like this one.  As one of the other reviewers said, it's oompa loompa orange in the bottle but it goes one more like a bronzer.  I have fair skin with pink undertones and it gives me a nice sunkissed look.

It's a little glittery and I only use half a pump so that I don't look like an oopma loompa.  I thought it was supposed to be a foundation, but it appears to be more of a bronzer.  I applied to my cheeks, nose and chin  but not all over my face as I was fearful that would look like a fake tan.

The only thing I would change would be the glitteriness.  I would prefer less glitter.  Not none, just less.
summary: Nice sunkissed look on fair skin

reviewText:
JAPONESQUE Liquid Light, Shade 02 is LIGHT!  It is light in every way. Straight out of the box, it looks a lot darker than it does when applied. The product is light and absolutely non greasy. When applied, there is no heavy make up feeling, like that of some foundations. Which leads me to say, that this product says that it may be used as a foundation or as a bit of color to highlight. I have tried it both ways. When applied this does not cover any flaws, because of the lightness of the product, I myself prefer to use it as a very minimal splash of color on my cheeks over a BB cream that I use. The color is barely there, but it feels to me as if it just brightens up my face a bit. So, if you are looking for a dramatic look, this is not the product for you. If you are going for a bright, natural look, you should certainly give it a try!

Edited to add that this is a cruelty free product!

This highlighter is labeled Luminescent. It certainly is that - meaning it is shiny and sparkly. I expected glowing, not almost fluorescent.
I guess I am old school and feel that shininess on my face looks like it needs a bit of powder - back in the day when a shiny nose was expected to be alleviated.
This make up, makes your cheeks shiny. The colour is nice but quite frankly it makes me look like I've been sweating. Perhaps in a nightclub setting with special lighting it would be attractive, but in normal conditions it just does not look right in my opinion.

Oh dear.  This really does come out looking metallic orange.  It does not look natural at all.  Nor does it blend in well with fair-toned skin.

The product is packaged nicely in a good-looking .84 ounce (25mL) pump bottle.  My pump didn't work, despite pumping down on it several times, so I used the pump tube to apply the cream.  The cream rubs in nicely and has a nice moisturizing affect on the skin. This I like, but the sparkles in this cream really do sparkle in sunlight, which I just don't care for.

This may be better suited for a teen or 20-something-year-old, or perhaps for a late night party, but for everyday office attire for an older woman, no.
summary: Metallic orange sparkles on cheeks look clownish

reviewText:
I love a sparkly face, ever since I discovered glitter as a child I will continue to wear make-up that dresses me up in illumination!

Japonesque luminescent highlighter is divine, lightweight, easy to apply and you will not end up looking like a 7 year old that just found a stash of glue and glitter and went nuts.

I applied my primer as usual, and combined my regular liquid foundation with a tiny squirt of this. It really does highlight without being whorish.

I also used it just on my eyelids with some mascara and it brightened up my eyes.

To be  honest, I thought this was foundation, but it is a blush.  Also, the color is not the same as the picture...it has peach tones which should not go with my skin tone but amazingly it does. It blends beautifully, and you must blend it in or it looks cheap.  There is a shimmer to it, quite pretty.  The is no fragrance which I prefer.

So to wind up this review.  It wasn't what I thought it was or the color but I love it anyway.
summary: I Love It...Light, creamy and blends beautifully with a shimmer

reviewText:
I saw this and wanted to try it.  It definitely sounded interesting enough, adding an extra dimension and all per the description.  Anyway, it comes out of the pump bottle orange with sparkly flecks which almost look like glitter. It goes on smooth and doesn't look orange at all after applying. By catching the light, I can see why it would create a shimmering incandescence, etc. like the description says.  Therefore, it does stand to reason that it does add to your glow and appear natural as it doesn't go on heavy and doesn't look like you are actually wearing anything.  I actually like the natural looking part. I added a bronzer on top and looks fine.  Just remember to lightly blend over cheekbones only to add that extra dimension look.

Overall - I think it's light enough to look natural, but does have an effect.  I like it and will continue to wear it under my bronzer.  Just add blush then if you prefer or as I'm discovering, for the casual look - without blush looks even more natural.  But, either way - it appears to look great.  Marilyn
summary: Light enough to still look natural!

reviewText:
I have some bad news.  This product will not change your life.

The descriptions says that, not only does it dress your skin in an illuminating veil of radiance, but that it creates a beautiful shimmering incandescence that light skin from within.'

I was hoping to be transformed into a shimmering incandescent version of myself.  That hasn't happened, though perhaps when I've used it for longer, I can look forward to these life-changing properties.

I'm a minimal makeup kind of girl, so  used it on top of my BB cream, which is all the foundation I use.  I applied Japonesque to accents the contours of my cheekbones.  And, while the color looks a little strange when pumped into your hand, it blends nicely.  I added a touch of blush on top of the Japonesque to add more color.  The effect was pleasing and very subtle, which is always my goal.  I don't have any urge to look like I've used a ton of makeup.

It comes in an elegant-looking little pump bottle with a small footprint.  It pumps a reasonable amount of product.  It doesn't tip over easily.

So I like it.  I'll have to get back to you about lighting my skin from within.  I may need to stick a light bulb in my mouth for that, but then I'd look like Uncle Fester.
summary: Warning!  Japonesque Will Not Change Your Life.

reviewText:
Hello.  My name is Leah and I'm a Cosmetics Addict.  I can't see a new cosmetics line without buying something from it.  When I saw this Liquid Illuminator by Japonesque, I said, "Get in my cart!  Momma needs a pretty fix!"

After ordering it, I searched Amazon and the Japonesque website for manufacturing information, but nowhere on the Japonesque website or on Amazon does it say where the products are made.  As a bonafide China Phobe, I was extremely nervous that this product was made in China.

So you can imagine my delight when I received the box and saw on the outside the words Made in Italy.  Huzzah!  My new beauty fix won't melt my face like battery acid!

Then I opened the box... And saw that the Liquid Light was neon orange.  I am talking Willie Wonka and the Chocolate Factory OOMPA LOOMPA orange.  I was tempted to package it back up and return it to Amazon for a refund, but in the name of fair, impartial scientific research I knew I had to at least try my new OOMPA LOOMPA Lotion.

The first squirt came out super orangey and flecked with iridescent flakes.  Talk about taking a turn for the tragic worse!  Not only was I going to look like a character from a ridiculous children's movie, but the iridescent flakes were going to highlight my 45-year-old wrinkles.

This product taught me a valuable lesson: you're never too old to believe in miracles!

Not only did the liquid light lotion go on smoothly, but it blended into my very pale skin without leaving an orange residue.  The glittery flakes blended in as well, leaving a slight sparkle.  This lotion leaves my pale skin looking like I've just spent today at the beach. It gives me a fresh-faced, sunkissed look!

Negative:
- The lotion blends enough that wearing it under foundation is pointless.  You won't even be able to tell you're wearing it
at all.

Positive:
+ This lotion is light enough and leaves just the right amount of flush/bronzer on your face to make it perfect for wearing instead of foundation, like to the beach or when you want a sans makeup day!
summary: OOMPA Loompa fears banished with first use!

reviewText: Japonesque Liquid Light, Shade 02 is a super-odd color when you pump it onto your finger, but goes on translucent with a bit of radiance. It was okay, didn't love it. I was hoping for a more dramatic, no- other- make- up- needed kind of application. It was, however, a smooth, nice feeling lotion-type make up. Non-greasy and non-staining.

From the directions on the packaging this product is more of a bronzer, highlighter, blush sort of thing.

After you have your foundation on put a little bit over your cheek bones or any where you need to bring light to your face.

Powder and finish as usual.

The cream is like foundation consistency. It has a sparkle shimmer to it. After applied you can see the shimmer a little, but it is not as if you just rubbed glitter on your face.

It is subtle and very pretty. Wore it on a morning I was particularly tired and everyone thought I looked refreshed and awake...I know when I started the day I felt neither.

Before ordering this product I was unfamiliar with the Japonesque brand. I'm pretty minimalist when it comes to makeup (my go-to is tinted moisturizer and loose powder). Per the product description, "This innovative light-reflecting liquid glides on to refresh the skin and enhance the complexion's natural glow -- creating a beautiful shimmering incandescence." I was excited about a product that would enhance my natural skin tone without caking on a bunch of heavy makeup. Unfortunately this product fell short of my expectations.

My single largest gripe is the color: this product can be best described as an orange-inspired metallic bronze. Considering the purpose of the product, I thought perhaps the orange hue would fade into my skin tone when applied (which is classified as medium with orange undertones). Sadly, it doesn't. I applied it to one side of my face and the orange hue completely took over and never really blended in.

All in all it just wasn't for me. Perhaps someone with a deeper skin tone with more orange undertones could appreciate this shade more than I did.

I have pretty sensitive skin, so I wasn't sure about this stuff. I used it after showering in the morning and it did seem to make my face a bit greasy. I have realativily normal skin, with very minimal grease/acne issues. It slightly irritated my skin, making it a bit pink for the first few days, but once I got used to it (after 3 days or so) it was fine. I do like the light scent of this. Overall, I don't really feel like this is anything special or unique.

This gel applies very soft and rubs in easily, leaving no oiliness, residue, or scent. A small amount goes a long way, and it makes it easier to apply foundation makeup. It leaves your skin feeling very soft and evens out your complexion. Compared to other cream based primers, you don't even feel this on your skin, while a cream primer feels heavier. Helps give a great soft look when makeup is applied. My wife didn't experience any negative skin reaction from this. This is one of the best primers she has tried. Excellent product.

My wife has been using the primer for the past week now when she puts on her makeup for work. She mentioned that it makes it a bit easier to apply her makeup as it goes on smoothly after this product has been applied.

She also mentioned that she has had no issues with the product throughout her day. I had assumed maybe given it's a face product and her job involves her running about (teacher) that it wouldn't last but she assures me it does. In all she thinks it's a great product and probably will get another one once she eventually gets through it all. She says that may be awhile though as it tends to not take too much of the substance for her to get a good application.

Japonesque Velvet Touch Primer feels light on your skin and very comfortable. Foundation went on smoothly over the primer and I did not notice my skin being more oily afterwards- the primer has a dry feel to it. It is clear, with no glitter/sparkle or tint. I think this is comparable to other quality primers in both function and price. At present, it is $32 for .84 fl oz- pricey, but a little does go a long way.

Impression: good primer that works, but not better than other primers in the same price range or some primers that is less costly. (e.l.f has a nice primer that costs a whole lot less than this)

Japonesque  Velvet Touch Primer, I found this primer to be a one of the better primers around. Very little of the product is needed and goes on like a silk glove.  I find that a primer has to live up as a base for makeup, an under lining to prepare your face for the star.
Japonesque Velvet Touch Primer does exactly that.  Not heavy, silken feeling, and the one thing I look for is staying power.  I do not wear makeup everyday, Doctor visits, The Mall, I normally wear a light moisturizer so when I do apply the works, it's important to me to have a line of products that does not look heavy,and  after a few hours have not folded into the fine lines on my face.
This product wears and wears.  No caking of makeup, A superior primer. This is my second product from their line.  As my first was their concealer, and I am very pleased with the coverage of that  concealer.  When my foundation is finished I will be looking into this line for other products.
Their  pricing would be in line with  most all of the others. The amount of product is generous and economical as very little of their products are needed to a complete coverage.
Highly recommend

This is absolutely excellent primer.  It is actually perfectly named.  It takes hardly any at all to smooth over my face before I put on foundation and it makes all the difference between the foundation lasting either 6 hours or until I sweat, whichever comes first, or until I remove the makeup with soap and water and washcloth.  My skin, which gets blotchy and breaks out at the slightest insult, has been more clear and less winter-dry-and-flaky since I started using it. I also love that there is a BOTTLE full of the stuff, instead of a thin straw worth of product that is artistically twirled inside a bigger empty bottle, like some of the other products I've used.

It does feel smooth and glides easily over the skin, I wouldn't say that makeup stays on longer with it. It doesn't help with wrinkles but does seem to minimize pores somewhat. You only need to use a small amount over your face.

This review is split into two aspects. One pertains to the packaging/shipping and the other to the product itself.

The packaging/shipping:
When this arrived, I removed it from the box and it slid right through my hands. I quickly realized that about 1/4 of the product had leaked in the box. At first, I thought the bottle or pump had cracked. Then, I noticed that the top was nearly entirely unscrewed. If there were a seal or clear tape to secure this area, this may not continue to be a problem in the future. As is, I lost about $8.00 worth of product. (It had turned into a weird gelatin like substance in the box.)

The product:
I have used a variety of primers in the past. My worst experience was with Bare Minerals. Their primer literally "balled up" or "rolled up" as I applied it. I took it back to the Bare Minerals store and the woman told me that it happens frequently with primers. Hmm. This primer, on the other hand, is phenomenal! It has a very light smell (so it should not be an issue for those with sensitivities/allergies), it goes on smoothly and with ease, and it truly does create a smooth canvas for your makeup. I have tried both Bare Minerals matte foundation (powder) and Buxom with it. In both cases, the results were almost an air-brushed appearance. Wow! Super nice!

I have extremely sensitive skin. I had zero negative reaction to this. Impressive!

The size:
I have paid considerably more for about half the size of this bottle. I would say that this is a deal!

Hopefully, Japonesque can tweak their packaging just a bit (to avoid loss of product). If so, this would be a five-star product (and have my devotion FOREVER!)

This primer has a very nice velvety feel.  And, compared to similar quality primers, the price point is just about right.  However, it may just be my skin type, but this one felt and looked a bit greasier than other primers I have used.  My makeup seemed to take on a bit of a shine.  But it is a good quality product and your makeup looks smooth and lasts longer just like a good primer should do
summary: This primer has a very nice velvety feel

reviewText:
I was hoping this primer would help hide 2 tiny scars I have near my eye. This did nothing to fill them in. Make-up/base does a better job in filling in the scars.
I did apply this with my fingertips and even after washing my hands with soap my fingers still had the bubbles of water on them and my skin - face and hands felt smooth.
What really bothered me was that it seemed to draw my face and the tightness made me look tired.
This just didn't seem to work and was an extra layer of something on my skin.

I am NOT a makeup junkie.  I'm careening towards fifty and don't have the average 17 year old's makeup skills.  On an average day I wear eyeliner and drugstore foundation or powder.  When offered this sample product to review I was interested to see if it could provide a quick solution to a bit better appearance at work (I tend to have dark circles and somewhat red skin).

This primer feels lovely when applied -- it is velvety and not oily.  In my experience it does improve the look of my skin and the lasting power of my makeup.  Not sure how I feel about covering my face with silicon polymers :), but I really like the look and feel of this primer. Loses a star due to the crazy price point-- makeup junkies won't flinch at the price, but the average person will.  In short, this is a very nice quality product- reminds me of past experiences with the Clinique line.

Size of product is generous and the dispenser is very nice, smooth operating and dispensing just enough/avoiding waste.  If you want to make primer a part of your routine this product is a good choice.

As I get older, I have realized that primer is an absolute necessity. It fills in fine wrinkles and provides a matte canvas for foundation.

I have used DHC Velvet Skin Coat and more recently Clarins Flash Beauty Balm.  I swear by my Beauty Balm but it retails for $45. At $33, this is a less expensive alternative. It does pretty good. It is on par the DHC primer for both price and usability. The Japonesque's size is big for the price.

Japonesque is a colorless fluid that goes on silky and evenly, and leaves your face notably smoother, velvety and more even. Nearly zero fragrance, which I prefer. Compared to other brands, I'd say it's a bit thinner or watery going on, but this seems to help it spread more evenly and feel weightless and not at all greasy. I've tried several other brands, but so far the Japonesque seems to be the best find so far. Definitely worth a try.

My fianc immediately tried this item as soon as i gave it to her. Here is her review:
The feel and texture of this primer was so smooth and glided evenly on my skin. Even with my dry skin, it showed no dry patches at all! It was like starting on a smooth, clean palette! After applying my foundation, it almost had an airbrushed finish. I would recommend this to anyone and everyone! Definitely worth the price.

Apply before foundation to smooth & prime complexion. A weightless gel with the affect that my makeup looked newly applied hours later and my skin is softer and firmer. I have a fair complexion, 50 year old skin and I had no side affects.
summary: made in Italy and a new to me product.

reviewText:
I don't use a lot of make-up so I just have the basics.  I had not thought of "primer" as a necessity.
Boy was I wrong! This works sort of like the gesso primer on a canvas. It fills and smooth's all the tiny lines and imperfections and foundation goes on like silk.  The primer is a clear gel and it only takes a tiny bit and leaves a matte finish. It dries almost immediately.

Ingredients: cyclopentasiloxane, dimethicone crosspolymer,dimethicone/vinyltrimethysiloxysilicate crosspolymer, silica, nylon-12 and a dozen other things I had never heard of. Works well, though.

This gel primer went on really smooth like laying down a velvety carpet on your face. Non greasy and so very light. I am impressed with the fact that it made my skin tone exceptionally even before I applied my make up foundation. A promised my make-up went on for a flawless brushed look. I can easily wear this without make up on days I do not feel like getting "all dressed up" and still look good. It comes in an attractive  25ml/.84oz clear glass bottle with black plastic cap with rubber pump.  I highly recommend it

I am new to the Japonesque line of products - this is only the second one that I have tried. But like the first, a lip lacquer, I am impressed with the Velvet Touch Primer.
The name does say it all - this primer goes on like velvet without leaving behind a heavy or greasy film.
It provided a nice base for my makeup and helped even my drug store foundation look better and last longer than usual.
Other primers sometimes leave behind a sticky feeling but this one does not so I can see this working well for even the oiliest of skin types.
The price point is high compared to drug store products but on par with department store cosmetic counters and is definitely worth considering if you are looking for a quality primer.

I'm honestly not sure that this company really even knows what a primer is supposed to be...

It doesn't look or feel like one.  It feels and looks like skin cream.  It does go on smooth, but it doesn't help to mask pores and things like that like a primer usually does.  (I typically use Bare Escentuals or Smashbox or Too Faced for primers).

The part I REALLY hate is that it's white!  And glittery!  It LIGHTENS my skin tone!  It shouldn't be changing my skin tone at all, it should be either clear or flesh tone.  The absolute worst part is the glitter.  I don't know if they wanted to give your skin a more "radiant" look or something, but I look as if I'm trying to wear makeup meant for a teenager.  I really don't want to look like a stripper with glitter all over my face.

I wouldn't recommend or purchase this product.  It is NOT what a primer is supposed to do.  My absolute favorite is Smashbox's pore-refining primer.  It is excellent.

I generally order my cosmetics and primer from Korea. The BB creams, highlighters and primers by Korean companies have worked really well for my very pale and listless complexion.

Japonesque Radiance Primer is certainly radiant. It has a bright almost metallic finish. The effect is fine under makeup. It does give a brightening effect. It is smoothing and makes a nice base for makeup.

The only downfall- and it's a big one- is that it is also glittery. The finish would be great if not for the tiny flecks of glitter. It makes me look like an emo vampire. I'm just too darn sparkly.

If however, you happen to be a sparkly vampire, this would suit you perfectly.

Japonesque is known for its line of high quality make up tools like brushes.  With this new line of foundation and colors, I see they are approaching this market very carefully.  This primer is easy to apply, seems to be mineral based.  It says on very nicely and doesn't clog the pores.  It allows the skin to breath while doesn't get oil up too easily and the colors stay on long and nice.  It is not irritating.  The primer comes in several different shades.  it's a decent size.  apply sparingly.  it lasts all day. Also easy removal with any makeup removal cleanser.  Highly recommended.
summary: ... for its line of high quality make up tools like brushes. With this new line of foundation and ...

reviewText:
The performance very much varies person to person. For my roommate it worked perfectly. It diffused the look of fine lines and imperfections. It was fantastic.

For me out was nearly Halloween makeup if I wanted to go as a sparkly vampire. It was almost like I was wearing glittery.

For another friend it made her look much younger, and like she'd just come back from the gym all sweaty.

Results seem very individual, but when it works, it's amazing.

I really was looking forward to trying this primer. I have never used any before and really do not like the heavy look many brands of makeup give.
I tried it without foundation, with and just using a blush over it.
My charming daughter said that I looked like the character Data on Startrek when I had it on without anything else, even with just blush it really left my skin with an unnatural shine - yes it did look like Data's make up. When I tried it under a foundation - it made no difference in my appearance, except that it was just more make up on my face.
I was really disappointed in this product.

This is an excellent primer. My skin literally glows, I'm so excited that I was able to try. I've been using it for the past two weeks and I can see a major difference between this primer and my previous primer. I put a light coating of primer all over my face before using my foundation. It lasts all day long and doesn't feel greasy. I don't always go all out all over my face, and this works brilliantly to illuminate/highlight too.

Great price for the size of bottle you get, this will last me quite awhile. One pump goes a long way! The pump is a major plus too. I forgot how much I love using a pump- it lets out the right amount, I don't ever accidentally squeeze out too much. No chance of it getting sloppy in my make up bag.

Love this stuff and the natural glow it gives me all day long!!

I have never worn primer before and after trying this product, I will probably never wear it again.  It wasn't that this product was so bad...it's just that I didn't notice any difference in my appearance.  Here are some pros and cons:
Pros
1.  It went on smoothly.
2.  It felt nice on my skin.
3.  A little goes a long way!
4.  No scent...which is great for sensitive skin.
5.  The pump jar is nice.

Cons
1.  It's an expensive bottle for no evident change in my appearance!
2.  It doesn't cover up blemishes.
3.  It's sparkly!  Not many women I know want to have sparkles on their face.

All in all, I don't think I will be buying it.  It just seems unnecessary and is just one more layer of make-up.
summary: This Primer May Fit Your Needs, But Not Mine!

reviewText:
I was a bit put off at first by this primer. I've used other products to even my skin tone without using foundation. This is so white and twinkly that  you absolutely have to put foundation over it.

That said, under foundation it looks amazing The glitter effect fades and it just brightens the skin tone. My makeup looks fresh all day, which is a big deal for me since I usually have a bad case of shiny face by lunchtime. The pump dispenser is nice, and a tiny bit goes a long way. There's no discernible smell and the texture is smooth without being too thick.
summary: Makes my foundation look amazing and stay fresh all day

reviewText:
This item was given to me for my review.
Originally, I did not like the Japonesque Radiance Primer. I felt it was too thick and made little sense to use. However, I read some of the other reviews and tried it with my skin cream. I use Vanicream http://www.amazon.com/Vanicream-Lite-Lotion-8-Ounce/dp/B000TCWX68/ref=sr_1_13?ie=UTF8&qid=1415724154&sr=8-13&keywords=vanicream, and I mention it specifically because it has no additional fragrances and works well with my extremely sensitive skin. I don't know what would happen if one mixed this primer with a moisturizer that has fragrance. Just saying. Anyway, I applied moisturizer first, let it sink in, then applied the primer and moisturizer mixed together over the top. I liked it very much that way. It gave my cheeks that glow, even after I applied my dry foundation. This would be excellent for someone who does not wear makeup, but would like to give their face a fresher look. I know as we age, our skin can get a ash-like coloring, so this is a nice solution...or if we are just looking tired, and as a wife and mother, that is relatively often. It works with or without foundation. So, yes, I am glad that I took the time to find out if I was using it correctly or if there was a better way to make it work for me. It is a shame that products do not come with suggestions like in the reviews, but perhaps the company will rethink their packaging. Giving customers options means the product has a better chance of being successful.
summary: Turned out to be a useful product after all

reviewText:
This actually works.  It doesn't look like there is anything on your skin but it creates a pallet for your best makeup to go on smooth.  I was shocked.  I expected that it might cover some of the redness or be colored in some way. It's not.  It's clear.  But it seems to fill in some of the fine lines and make a clean fresh pallet for my foundation.  It has no odor and didn't stick to my fingers either.

Love the outcome!
My wife says this gives you a "dewey glowy look".  Whatever that means.  It's like a pearl color and gives you a shimmer under your foundation.  She wouldn't recommend it for everyday use.
summary: Decent for when you want to look jazzed up

reviewText:
A little bit of this goes a long way!
This does not feel like your typical primer.
I think this particular "primer" does best with lighter skin since it is light in color and has a silvery shimmer.

I found that mixing a small amount with my moisturizer gives my face a nice glow without lightening my skin or over-doing the shimmer factor.  The shimmering elements(mica) in this are very fine/tiny so they are not like glitter chunks.  I think it really gives a nice look for night-time events and used sparingly can be worn in the day...unless you want to be very shinny & shimmery.

I was extremely tired the last few days and have applied this primer in the morning for a day look.  I found that it really did help!  I only used a small amount like usual but it gave me a little lift for my very tired out skin and eyes.  I was pleasantly surprised when I looked in the mirror and expected to look tired like I felt....but I didn't.  The light glow of the primer and some good concealer did the trick.

I like that this does Not have a strong scent and has not made me breakout so far. It is a nice sized, pump jar as well.  I am wondering if over time this will clog my pores with all of the tiny pieces of mica in it, we'll see.
summary: A Little goes a Long way-not a typical primer.

reviewText:
First impression, it's white.  That terrified me a bit, but it goes on clear.  It just looks SO white in the bottle.

It doesn't feel like primer.  It's more like a highlighter and it's glittery,but the flecks don't seem huge.  I only use about a half a pump when I use it, but I think if you use more you might feel like you are going out to a night club.  It seems good enough for day use...I didn't find it too glittery.  It did a decent job of filling in the fine lines around my eyes.

Update: I've started mixing it with my BB cream and it gives a nice dewy look.
summary: Don't let the white scare you, doesn't make you look like a clown.

reviewText: I was excited that I got the opportunity to try out this Japonesque face primer.  First off, my skin is a light olive tone, so this primer does not come across as "glittery" as other reviewers with fair skin mentioned.  It is more of a luminous, pearly look on the skin.  Definitely has pink undertones in the cream.  I would not wear this alone on my skin, as it looks too iridescent, but rather with foundation over it.  I think it leaves a nice canvas for my foundation, but I don't like it as much as my Smashbox.  You do get quite a large bottle (.84 fl oz.) for the price; it seems that it would last a long time.

This primer in part lives up to the product description. It is weightless and silky. Very easy to apply you'll find that a little goes a long way. A half pump would be plenty.

Looking at it through the clear glass bottle it reminds me of my favorite white iridescent nail polish, literally.

On my skin it brings an much more shine than I care for along with tiny sparkles. It makes me look like a glittery ghost because my skin is very fair to begin with. This product washes me out completely except for the shimmery shine.

That said, I'm hesitant to give it a two star rating. My reasoning for this is that this primer goes on smoothly and requires very little for coverage. My skin is a bit on the dry side but this didn't affect the application process. Plus there is absolutely no scent. That's a huge plus for me. Not only am a sensitive to smells, I have allergies to many fragrances.

Speaking of ingredients for those who are interested here is the list:
Aqua/Water, Butylene Glycol, Polyacrylamide, C13-14 Isoparaffin, Laureth-7, Tin Oxcide, Phenoxyenthanol, Sodium Dehydroacetate, Methylparaben. May Contain: CI 77891, Titanium Dioxide, Mica.

Many of my friends are photographers who double as makeup artists. I have a feeling that this primer might do magic when used by someone who actually knows what they are doing. I also think that for photo shoots it might yield radiant results.
summary: Could yield radiant results with just the right skin tone if you don't mind glitter
