All the other pricy serums I've used have had more of a pump-type dispenser which makes it harder to spill or waste product. Applying it to my skin was also tricky because 2-3 drops didn't seem to go very far. Adding it to moisturizer does seem to make it easier to apply to the entire face. However it does make me wonder if it will make this booster lose its effectiveness and potency because many of the topical prescription products I've used for my face have specified applying it to a clean face and letting it absorb fully before adding lotion. When applied without the lotion it feels lightweight and absorbs quickly. Even though it is an oil you are applying so little to your skin that it doesn't feel greasy. The scent isn't overly pleasant but thankfully is also not noxious and seemed to dissipate quickly enough. I then followed up as directed with my serum. Generally I find these things take a couple months to fully see the effects so I plan to report back after I've had more experience with this product to see whether it does seem to be boosting my skincare routine and how long the bottle lasts. (Yes, it's pricy but similar products I've used that have only required 2-3 drops have lasted me for months.) To date though I do think it works with what I'm already using to make my skin feel soft and supple.
summary: I like how it makes my skin feel so far

reviewText: The first day I used this, my husband remarked that I looked pretty. The second day, my mom told me I looked "absolutely gorgeous." Not compliments I get all the time, so I'm giving the credit to this stuff. It's a light oil with a gentle lemony scent. Easy to apply, though the dropper thingy is a little strange. On the bright side, since the top comes off, no product will be wasted. Price is high, but it's a quality product.

I have always had oily skin, but I have been losing moisture with age. While I am still not entirely convinced that this is worth the high cost, it does really boost your moisturizer. I like to add it to my current products for just a small increase in moisture.  A little goes a long way but it is dependent on your individual skin type.
My only complaint is the packaging.  So many cosmetic companies use packaging that is very difficult to get the product out towards the end or its hard to use and you waste it.  This falls into the messy category.  When you spend a lot of money on a product it is incredibly frustrating to spill it.  The dropper is hard to get the right amount, especially if you only want to add a small amount.  You will definitely have soft skin though!
summary: I like to add it to my current products for just ...

reviewText:
This is one of those beauty products that I'd categorize as "nice to have but not essential".

StriVectin doesn't make any outrageous anti-aging claims regarding this oil; it's supposed to supplement your current regimen by "boosting" the moisturizing effects of whatever products you're using. Basically it's a combination of oils (along with the company's patented NIA-114 formula) and you add 2 or 3 drops to your moisturizer, or apply the oil by itself.

Despite the shocking age that appears on my driver's license, I don't have dry skin so this product really didn't work for me. My skin is `Normal' with a tendency to get a little oily in the t-zone (though that's not an issue in the colder weather). Despite adding only the teeniest drop I can manage into my night cream, this just makes my skin look and feel greasy. It never seems to actually absorb into my skin, and I don't care for that "oil slick" look and feel. Some other things to consider:

*Slight perfume fragrance
*Contains a form of Niacin (may cause skin to "flush")
*Oily, acne-prone skins should use with caution

Would I recommend this product? That depends on your beauty budget and your skin type. If your skin is very dry and your current moisturizer doesn't offer adequate hydration, then this may work for you. Personally I consider it a little pricey and I've used similar products that were less expensive and worked just as well.

*The small "instruction" leaflet included with the product is inadequate. You have to comb thru the tiniest print imaginable (and over 12 languages!) to find two sentences about this product. Like most people, I'm concerned about the products I apply to my skin, and I'd appreciate more information.
summary: Added moisture for dry skin but may be too oily for other skin types

reviewText:
This high quality oil is intended to be applied to the face in conjunction with another beauty product.such as Retin-A at night or a moisturizer in the morning. General guidance recommends that the lightest formulation be applied first, so a thin serum goes on the face first, then an oil, then a gel, then the thickest preparation such as a cream or lotion.

I use Atralin (a prescription based RetinA gel) over this oil and the results so far have been very good.

I have already been applying Argan oil to my face under other preparations for several years, and I find that the two products, when applied together, enhance each other. This oil is intended to work the same way.

This StriVectin Booster oil is a mixture of various oils and liquid based moisturizers. It penetrates that face quickly and leaves the skin silky and moisturized, not oily.

Although applying it by itself cant hurt, it is quite expensive and works to its best advantage when combined with a second preparation.

Update:  I like the way this feels on my face, the way it moisturizes, nourishes & illuminates my skin. I ran out a few months ago, and  finally decided to purchase more.

I have normal skin, with  fine wrinkles that come with age. I've been using StriVectinLABS Booster Oil for about a week now. You're instructed to use 2 to 3 drops twice a day after cleansing your skin. Then follow through with your normal skin care routine. The Booster Oil is very moisturizing. It is so moisturizing that I continually forget to apply my moisturizer.

The Booster Oil seems to be a little bit thinner than argan oil. I like its light lemony scent. In my experience, the Booster Oil takes a couple minutes to absorb. Maybe this is because my skin isn't dry. I use a magnifying mirror & always check before and after I apply the Booster Oil. My skin really does look more luminous after I apply the oil and my fine wrinkles aren't as noticeable.

The dropper lid has a pump on top. Instead of squeezing a bulb, you push on the pump to fill the dropper.

All in all, I'm pleased with the Booster Oil, and will update my review as I continue to use the product.

This Booster Oil is based on the NIA-114 technology. You can learn more about this ingredient/technology by doing an internet search.

I received the wrong insert in the package. I hope StriVectinLABS corrects this error.
summary: Moisturizing...light, lemony scent...a little goes a long way...feels similar to argan oil

reviewText:
I was pleasantly surprised by this oil.  We've all heard the hype from skin care products: "younger looking skin", "turns back time, "renewed glow." Well this product comes as close as anything I've used.  Although I'm 62, my skin can be dry one day and oily the next.  I've used Clinique and Origin products for many years because everything else irritated my skin and left it red and broken out, so I was leery, but since I got it as a Vine choice I thought I'd give it a try.  Right away I wanted to knock it down a star for having the wrong information on the paper insert and for the dropper.  The insert is for a different product.  Hopefully they will correct that.  Be careful of the dropper as it drips and you can waste a lot of expensive oil quickly.  However, once I started using it and got the hang of the dropper (put your finger under it as you take it out of the bottle) I backed off on marking it down.  For a few minutes, it felt a little greasy, but then it was absorbed and just felt nice.  I love the scent.  It smells at bit like a spice, but I can't quite place it.  The oil is soothing, not irritating and after a week of use my skin feels SILKY.  I really like the way my skin looks when I use it under my makeup, but using it at night is a pleasure too.  The scent is lovely and refreshing after a long day.
This oil is not cheap, but it will last (if you don't let it drip all over) since you only need a couple drops.  You can mix it with your regular moisturizer to make it go farther if you want.  If you don't have very dry skin, you may only want to use it once a day.
I am overlooking the two negatives and giving 5 stars for the silky feel and the softness of my skin which is what it is all about anyway.

UPDATE:  I'm in love with this product.  It lasts a long time (just use a couple drops) and it makes my skin feel so good.  I can tell that fines lines have been reduced and my skin is softer.

From my wife, who has tested and used this product:

The serum goes on very smoothly. It doesn't feel like you need extra moisturizer with it although it recommends you put your favorite moisturizer over the top. It has a nice, light smell, and I've experienced no stinging or itching like I have with other serums. It makes your skin feel instantly smooth. I look forward to seeing some of the longer-term effects soon. the brand is a trusted one, and this is a good edition to its line.

StriVectinLABS High Performance Booster Oil, 0.5 fl. oz.

Category: Skin Care

Wonderful high quality skin care! This skin gem is packed in a compact size bottle thats extremely attractive which also makes it easy to slip into your purse for a fast refreshing application during the day. The product is nourishing and goes on easily without leaving a oily feel. The scent is light and refreshing with a hint of lemon. Terrific product!

It is really hard to review this product so quickly but I have to review it within 30 days per Vine program rules.  What I can tell you now it has the consistency of a thin, clear oil.  You don't need much and it goes on smoothly.  I only wear it in the day if I am not going anywhere or at night.  I use it around my mouth on my smile lines and forehead. I will do an update after some more time to give feedback as to whether it is helping to fill my smile lines and forehead ridges.  UPDATE: I do feel this product has helped improve the look of my skin so I have upped this to five stars. July 26, 2015.

I've used a number of moisturizers in my time, but I have to be honest and say very few have come with a price tag anywhere near this item. So to say the least, this product had a ways to go to receive a favorable review from me as I've always found my $10 bottles of moisturizer to be more than enough for my needs.

That being said, this performance booster oil (notice the word moisturizer isn't included, they do not want to be compared to simple moisturizers) has been very impressive so far. The best way I can describe it is the difference between a $50 pair of shoes and a $200 pair of shoes. While the $50 pair of shoes will get the job done, you won't feel the same level of luxury and comfort as you do with the $200 pair of shoes. This booster oil is the $200 pair of shoes. The oil goes on extremely easy, and my skin has been feeling much more soft and smooth than it did after using the $10 bottles of moisturizer. Its a difference you really can't understand until you try it as I never knew my skin could feel so soft.

I'm docking it one star because the price is still a bit out of whack. Somewhere around the $50 pricepoint would be a bit more reasonable and would lead to more repeat buyers.
summary: High Performance Mousturizer at a Somewhat Reasonable Price

reviewText:
Ive been using this for about a week.  Sometimes, I applied a few drops directly on my freshly washed face, and sometimes I mixed a drop with my regular moisturizer. In both instances my face felt soft and hydrated, not just for an hour, but all day!

Curious as to what this was, I did a little research. Besides reconfirming my decision not to follow a science-y path, I also learned that NIA-114 was invented by two biochemists. These scientists, while searching for a cure for skin cancer, discovered that NIA-114 repairs, and rejuvenates skin.

Some of the top ingredients include: Helianthus annus (sunflower seed oil); Sesamum Indicum (Sesame Seed Oil); and Carthamus Tinctorius (Safflower Seed Oil). There are other oils and a fragrance too. I don't understand all the science behind how the water soluble Niacin added to fat-soluble Lipophilic equals Niacinamide blab bla bla bla. But I do know that it feels great, and helps my skin look better.

Recommended.

During the winter months my usually normal skin tends to dry out, plus the older I get the more moisturizing I need. Many of the products I've used to "brighten" my skin and minimize fine lines have the side effect of drying out my skin and causing it to get flaky and itchy, so I was happy to add the StriVectinLABS High Performance Booster Oil to my daily routine. After only a short period of time, I find it is already working well. Adding the oil gives my skin a soft, almost radiant, glow.

The product is packaged in a small bottle with a dropper that is used to apply the serum. It can be a little messy to use as there is no real control over the drops - it's best to get them to your face quickly so they don't spill. There is a pump on top, but that only seems to make the drops come out faster. The oil has a light fragrance - it's not bad but I can't place what it smells like - and after a half hour or so the scent disappears.

Two or three drops was enough to lightly cover my entire face. A small amount of the serum goes a long way. On top of that I added my regular moisturizer with sunscreen for daytime, and one with skin brighteners in the evening. When first applied it does feel a little greasy, but within a few minutes it was absorbed into my skin.

One annoyance, which in no way affects my rating of the product, but seems to be occuring with more and more packaging: The print on the bottle and on the leaflet in the box was so tiny I needed a magnifying glass to read it. When I finally did find the instructions it was only a few lines, and not much information. A little searching online told me what I needed to know to use the product correctly, but it would have been nice to have it in the box as that is the first place most people look for direction.
summary: Gives my skin a soft, almost radiant, glow

reviewText: An ok product that doesn't really stand out. Frankly, I actually didn't like the feel of it on my face. It just felt oily. My face has never had dry skin issue, so perhaps this product isn't for me. Hard to say if I recommend it. At the price, there are many other similar products that are cheaper.
summary: I actually didn't like the feel of it on my face

reviewText:
I have dry middled skin and I now have to use a moisturizer day and night.  I used a Stri-Vectin product some years ago, which I think was an eye de-puffer, but I don't remember.  I know they have a good reputation, and they're somewhat expensive ($62 for this product!).

In the course of the last few years I've gotten very picky about what I eat and put on my body, and more focused on natural products and fewer chemical.  I hesitate to slather my face in a product that doesn't tell you all the ingredients.  Much like "natural flavors" in food can mean MSG, I want to know what NIA-114 in this product contains.  I like that it contains vitamins A, B, C, D, and E, but it's the unknown ingredients I don't like.

It moisturized my skin the way most oils too, leaving me slightly greasy in a good way.  But I wouldn't buy this product based on the mysterious NIA-114.
summary: Moisturizes and provides vitamins, but has unexplained ingredients

reviewText:
My wife has used this as a part of her morning and evening routine, and despite this being the first week of using the heat in our home, complete with all of the associated dry air, it's a welcome refreshing.  She uses this in addition to her usual serum, and the results, while not amazing, are quite nice.  In the short term the main benefits are the moisturizing, and we're not expecting much more immediately.

Sadly this all comes at a price, which can quickly add up.
summary: A great moisturizer, at a price

reviewText: UPDATED REVIEW 12/7/14 I SAID below that I hadn't noticed any difference in the lines between my eyes. WELL, that has changed. The lines are Definitely reduced. I'm shocked and amazed... and have fallen in love. HIGHLY RECOMMEND you try this. ========================= Now that I'm older I've discovered that I can indeed have dry skin. That after decades of battling oil, I now have to worry about chapped skin and skin that is badly in need of hydration. One of the problems I have in finding solutions is that I have very sensitive skin (with lots of allergies) and I have skin that can still have a breakout problem if I use something excessively greasy. So I was interested in trying out this 'booster oil'. One thing I liked was the ingredients. Nothing that I could find that you couldn't buy in the EU with it's higher requirements. The next thing I discovered was that this booster oil didn't cause any allergic reaction. I tried it on the inside of my elbow and wrist first, then on my neck and finally on my face. All good. I am using the booster oil by itself and in conjunction with the two creams I use: L'Oreal Paris RevitaLift (cheap) and L'Occitane Immortelle Divine Cream (expensive). RESULTS I've hit the lines between my brows with the booster oil by itself, and later with a combination of the booster oil and creams... and I've noticed no difference. If this changes, I'll report. I've used the booster oil to supplement my creams and... I be gosh darned if it hasn't improved the look of my skin. I haven't noticed changes to the micro-creases I have, but my skin looks smoother --both in the less irritated sense, and in the more uniform complexion sense. SUMMARY One thing I've noticed is that prices can change radically after the first rounds of reviews come out, so I won't comment on price; it could change. I like this booster oil. It actually doesn't take much to enhance the effectiveness of other creams/cremes, and it didn't irritate my skin. I know other people have said that it absorbs right in. That's not been my experience. It's an oil, it acts like it. But it's not greasy and if you don't overdo it, you won't shine for long. I did experience an improvement in the tone of my complexion.

This has a pleasant scent. It is not too floral, and it does not have the strong alcohol-esque odor properties that is a turn off for me and can be found in many scents. It's a nice, somewhat sophisticated, and not typical for a "masculine" scent, so it may be appropriate for unisex.

Others have noted that this does not last long. I suppose this is true, but I could smell it for many hours. I am sensitive though, so this is probably different for different people.

I'm no connoisseur, but from what I can tell, this is was a good price for a product with this quality. I'd compare it with other varieties in the same price range at a department store.

The packaging is nice, too. I don't care, but some may!

Plus: My wife likes it.
This smells amazing. It is the perfect blend of spices without smelling overwhelming. I love this fragrance.
like this smell
Got this for hubbys birthday, he loves it and it smells amazing.

I knew about makeup setting spray, but I figured it was like hairspray, and I don't like hairspray, so I was very hesitant to try it - I thought my face would turn into a MASK! Not so! This spray lightly "sets" your makeup in a very natural way! Just follow the directions - you'll like the results.
summary: but I figured it was like hairspray, and I don't like hairspray

reviewText:
Like hairspray for the face, this product promises to protect and preserve make up under all conditions. While the heartbreak of makeup fade does not keep me up at night, I have experienced it. I don't usually have much opportunity to retouch and reapply and it is annoying to look washed out. The product is an aerosol spray which is applied by misting over the face at a distance of eight to ten inches. Make sure your eyes and mouth are tightly shut and that your makeup, especially mascara, is completely dry before applying. It has a light scent that fades quickly. I sprayed it on full makeup, that is primer, foundation, eye liner, shadow, mascara, lipstick and blush. My face felt wet and it took a few minutes to dry. No dewiness or shine was added and it looked rather matte. Although there was some fade at the end of the workday, it was not  extreme. My skin tends to veer from normal to dry in colder weather and it did feel a  bit parched after using this. It could be I was not accustomed to it but the spray  contains alcohol.

The twenty nine dollar question is whether I would use it again. And the answer is maybe. It did work but I am not crazy about it being aerosol. I have tried other setting sprays that I prefer. One that stands up well to heat and humidity is  Urban Decay All Nighter. I wore it at a summer wedding in the south and it was great. They also have a hydrating version for dry skin.  Makeup Forever Mist and Fix smells marvelous and left my skin feeling comfortable but not looking greasy or shiny. Extremely light, it contains no alcohol. Skindavia has a version, Makeup Finishing Spray, that is paraben free, cruelty free and hypoallergenic. It is designed to work in all temperatures, from the hot and humid to the super chilly.  If you have a busy schedule and don't want your makeup leaving before you do, Japonesque setting spray is certainly an option to be considered. It does work but is perhaps more comfortable for those with normal to oily skin.

For me this is ok make up setting spray. First of all it contains alcohol so probably will be a bit drying. It's the 3rd ingredient, after water and nitrogen.
This is first aerosol make up spray I'm using and I though the mist will be more fine, instead it sprays in big spurts, make the whole face wet (with visible white patches, but they are disappear fast and do not ruing the make up).
This spray doesn't make up appear dewy, it's just a regular look, very slightly matte.
There is scent to it, but rather pleasant and it doesn't linger.

I prefer Make Up For Ever Mist and fix spray or Mac setting spray. They are more hydrating and don't contain alcohol. MUFE spray still spray more product (very dewy look), and Mac has a fine spay mist.

This comes in a spray bottle that contains about 3 OZ. It has a very mild scent that fades out fairly quickly but not completely. When sprayed on the face it leaves a sticky feeling that does not go away. It is difficult to spray the face without getting this in your hair especially when your eyes must be tightly closed for protection. The expectation for this product was much higher than its actual performance. The very high cost should have resulted in a lack of stickiness and a more pleasant scent.
Love this I'm sold on it

Worked well on my friends face. No reaction to it and she felt it worked well. She likes to try all kinds of makeup to explore the different results that best suits her. It needed to be put on occasionally, but she was pleased with the results.
summary: She likes to try all kinds of makeup to explore the different results that best suits her

reviewText: Each time I use this Japonesque Makeup Setting Spray I like it more and more.  After all my makeup is applied and on I put a headband on to hold my hair out of the way I hold the can about 8 inches from my face, close my eyes really tight and spray lightly all over my face.  I keep my eyes closed for a about a minute.  I use a tissue to blot lightly to take the excess off.  It leaves my face looking so much better and yes, like it has been airbrushed with an expensive unit.  The best part of this:  I cannot be without this product and so very happy to have it.

If you can get past the fact that this is an aerosol and not a spritz spray then I'd say its very comparable to Urban Decay's All Nighter makeup setting spray.  It felt odd using an aerosol at first but it certainly held up in the makeup department; no smudged mascara/ shadow all day!

TIP- Do not spray directly onto face ( I could never get it evenly distributed doing it this way).  Rather spray the air a few inches above and in front of your face and "step into" the spray.  This ensures an even coat of setting spray all over the face.

Pricey but recommended.

I tried this with my MAC makeup and also with some other cheaper stuff (a mix of revlon and max factor) it does make a difference when you're wearing the cheaper stuff. I didn't notice a difference with my MAC.

This is not expensive if used correctly even everyday. It's a 3 oz liquid for $29, I'm not sure why people think they'd get a huge bottle for that price.

I'm not a fan of the alcohol in it.

My wife enjoys perfecting her makeup, whether it be trial and error, Youtube clips, blogs, etc... she's picked up a few tricks.  The one she recommends to many of her friends is to use primer and a setting spray.  She tried out this spray, and she's happy with the results.  The spray does it's job, and when the day is done, it removes with her face wash.  Sadly, it's not perfect, as the aerosol feels a bit heavy compared to some of the pump sprays she prefers.  It's also a bit tacky to the touch,
summary: Good results, but the aerosol feels a bit heavy

reviewText:
Works great! I put this on with full make up: concealer, foundation, blush, eye shadow, liners, lipstick and powder. I applied it at 3:00 pm on a warm, but muggy afternoon.  At 9;00 pm, I took it off with cleansing cream and it looked just like it did at 3:00, except the lipstick.
I did have to get a piece of paper and fan my face to dry the product, but it didn't sting my eyes or burn my skin.
I usually use NYX Matte Finish, which has a pump spray.  I like the way this product works better.  The mist is more fine and it last longer.

To be fair, the only make-up I use is mascara and lipstick.  That said, my lipstick did not set and was easily came off on my husband's lips and my mascara ran.  Also, for a few minutes after I sprayed the solution on my face, it made my face sticky.  That cleared up totally after a half hour or so.
My guess is that this would better serve people who use foundation.  But I don't know for sure.
summary: Specify What Kind Of Make-Up This Sets For Better Ratings...

reviewText:
This is a good product for what it is. I don't normally use a setting spray for street (everyday) makeup but it does hold your look very well. The spray isn't sticky, dries quickly, and isn't irritating to the skin. It held my eye makeup even better than I expected. I didn't have eyeshadow in the creases like I normally do after 8 hours of wear. And the scent was pleasant and faded quickly.

I think the bottle itself could use a little redesign though. I think it sprays too wide. It got into my hair and on my shirt just from a quick spray directed at the middle of my face. I think it would benefit from a slightly smaller spread.

Other than that, it works very well. I will keep it to use for special occasion makeup and when I do stage makeup.

This is like hairspray for your face.  It's the best way to describe it. It holds everything in place in a similiar fashion but it's not sticky like hairspray.  It's just an all over spritz that makes your face feel set.  My makeup doesn't come off on my glasses, fingers or shirt when I use this item.  It just holds everything on your face in a nice form and fashion.
summary: Who knew I needed this so bad

reviewText:
Japonesque makeup setting spray absorbs quickly and prolongs the application of your makeup. It is transparent and doesn't dry skin.  The product prevents fading and transfer, providing a freshly applied look.

This product is intended to be used after applying makeup with eyes tightly closed.  The product should be sprayed evenly over the face.

You might think something like this would smell bad but it is a light scent which isn't overpowering or unpleasant.

The product goes on kind of wet and takes some time to dry on.  It does not seem to induce a shine and it doesn't detract from the makeup application.

In terms of longevity or the product standing up to its claims, this product does seem to work for those long term events, special occasions or situations where you will want to keep your freshly applied makeup looking good for a prolonged period of time.

The product was tested in a low humidity (SoCal, 8% RH) environment in November as well as a colder environment (Boston, light snow) and a high humidity environment (Central FL, 80% RH).  The temperature and humidity extremes didn't seem to affect the product's effectiveness.

Overall - this is an effective product that I would purchase again.

Long before Evian water was in every grocery store in the USA, it was only available as a spray just like this Japonesque makeup setting spray.
Criminally expensive and first only in luxury stores, Evian water spray was touted as a refreshing and/or setting spray.

This product is NOT sticky. After many uses, it was never anything but velvety soft.

After putting on my makeup, one very quick spritz is all it takes.

If you use it like hairspray, you are wasting the product. By using it incorrectly you might get some stickiness...instead of a setting mist, you are creating a mask.
Used correctly, it perfectly sets makeup bith a barely noticeable fresh, clean scent.

A one or two second burst at 10 inches from your face will cover the entire face evenly.
Considering that, this is not an expensive product as the per use cost is minimal.
summary: Great product, low per use cost

reviewText: Not exactly sure how this works, but it does!  I have been using this for a couple of days straight and my makeup actually stays on throughout the day.  What I love most is that my mascara doesn't come off below my lashes anymore!  I don't even notice it is there, it doesn't make your face feel tight or like it has a film on it.  My only complaint is that when you spray it on there are a few spots that have large white drops of the liquid on it.  I dab those with my finger and they go away but i am not sure how it would look to dry like that if you missed it.  There is very little smell and it really doesn't take much of it to hold all day.  If I was going to a party or event I would probably use more of it, but for every day, I can see this bottle lasting for quite awhile, which is nice considering the price.

The Japonesque makeup setting spray was something my wife was eager to try. She does not usually have an issue with her makeup coming off after a few hours but she can never get it to last the entire workday, especially when the weather is humid.  The spray is really easy to use...simply spray it on after you have applied your makeup.  The trick is to get it on with your eyes closed  but a little practice is all it takes.  It does have a mild scent and feels a little sticky at first but after that initial application it starts to feel better. Once applied my wife did say her makeup seemed to last a bit longer so it works as expected.  We did not have a chance to try it in humid weather (since summer is over) but I would imagine that is when this really comes in handy.  The downside to this spray is that it is really expensive especially for the quantity you get.  Also it has alcohol so it will eventually dry out your skin. This product would be great if it were cheaper or in a larger quantity but as is it's only for special occasions not daily use.
summary: Great For Special Occasions But Too Expensive For Daily Use

reviewText: Setting spray is good after make up is applied to keep it looking good through the day. Kind of like shellac to a hardwood floor. It's not glossy but a very fine spray that keeps the make up in place. Surprising enough this Japonesque spray works great.
summary: Setting spray is good after make up is applied to keep it looking ...

reviewText: I was originally introduced to makeup setting spray when I was having my makeup done by a professional for an event. She used Urban Decay's All Nighter and made me enough of a believer to go out and buy it for myself.  For everyday makeup application I don't use it because I am acne prone and try to use as few products on my face as possible, but for special events it is fantastic and really does increase the longevity of my makeup.  (Which I appreciate because I have very dry skin and even with primer for both my skin and eyelids, makeup never seems to last as long on me as other people.)  Unfortunately I don't like this product as much.  It does seem to feel similar on my skin once applied but the biggest difference to me is in the kind of mist.  With the All Nighter the mist is very fine and seems to just lightly coat my skin.  With this, unless I hold this quite far away from my face it seems like a very strong mist.  (And if I hold it further away from my face, it's harder to control it from going in my hair.  I don't hate this and it's possible I might be fine with it had I not tried the Urban Decay version first, but I personally prefer that version.  This is especially true since both seem similarly priced.  I do though wish with both products they were more transparent about whether it is okay for acne prone skin.
summary: Not my favorite makeup setting spray

reviewText:
When I opened the box for this I thought "Really? They could jack up my face and run a new one under it for that price". The bottle is a little bigger than my thumb.

I suggest you do a "test-patch" on your inner elbow before you put this on your face. You can read the ingredients by enlarging the thumbnail photos on the left of the product page. You won't be able to read them on the actual box without a powerful magnifying glass.

When they say "oil" that's what it is, about the consistency of mineral oil. It has a very subtle citrusy scent.

After cleaning my face I only use a couple of drops to cover my face. (If you use too much you will be a greasy mess and it will take some time to absorb.) Over that I use a vitamin "C" serum then, after a little time for that to absorb, I apply a moisturizer. It leaves my face warm and a little pink for about five minutes.

The results? First I have to tell you I'm leery of any cosmetic that makes extravagant claims so I wasn't expecting much.  I am pleasantly surprised. After just a week my skin looks much better. The fine lines at the corners of my eyes are less and a line on my forehead is less obvious. Is it the oil or is it because it helps the "C" serum to absorb better?  I don't know but whatever it is it seems to work. Is it worth the cost? I'm still debating that.

I like the idea of a booster for your favorite moisturizer.  It's a bit expensive but a little does go a long way.  I use it once a day, with my night moisturizer.  That's the one that does the heavy lifting.  It has been a few days and I haven't experienced anything unpleasant.  Quite the opposite.  I find it to be smooth and fragrance neutral - it doesn't over power my night cream.  I can't say I've noticed a huge difference.  Maybe more balanced in my complexion - more thoroughly hydrated.

I have been using it for about three days. I am not noticing a real difference in reducing my wrinkles (probably because I don't have that many ... just laugh lines), but my skin is softer. It feels good and the smell is not medicinal. It is rather lemony and to be honest, it is refreshing.

I don't use a lot of it and I do put it directly on my skin and I just rub it in. It goes a long way and I put it on before I put my moisturizer on and two hours later, my skin is still feeling soft.

The only reason why I am giving it a four star rating is that the price is a bit prohibitive. $71 is a lot of money to spend on anything and I will treasure this bottle for a long time since I cannot justify spending this kind of money for something this nice. If I was able to afford it, I would buy it and give it to my friends as it is such a lovely product. Whether it works permanently remains to be seen, but I do like this.

As someone who has struggled since childhood with incredibly sensitive skin that is prone to breakouts, I'm wary when it comes to trying out new products.  At the same time, I'm always on a quest to find something - anything, really - that will benefit my skin, and help me with issues like hydration, decreasing hyperpigmentation from acne scarring, smooth out the texture and tone, and won't leave me with new blemishes.

When I first began using this product, I followed the directions and applied the exact amount recommended, twice a day.  I immediately noticed that my skin felt smoother and softer, but after a couple of days, I did start getting some breakouts.  I discontinued using the product for a couple more days until things cleared up, and then I decided to give it one last try.  I've been using it twice a day ever since without any problems whatsoever, so those initial breakouts were (thankfully) an aberration; in fact, given the results that I've seen this then, those breakouts may not even have been caused by this product, at all.  I say that because, while this isn't part of the treatment's claims, ever since I began using this regularly, my breakouts have decreased to almost nothing, and the little ones that I may get clear up much faster than they formerly did.

In terms of how the product goes on the skin, just two or three drops at a time really is all one needs, because a little goes a long way: it spreads out beautifully and immediately sinks into the skin.  It doesn't make the face feel greasy, but you can feel - and even see, to an extent - that there is a moisturizing product on the skin.  The directions state that it can be applied directly to the face, or mixed into one's moisturizer or other face products.  I've tried both methods; in terms of the latter option, I've mixed it in with a little bit of serum and some oils that I use (jojoba, hazelnut, and sometimes tamanu).  It works great by itself, and I don't have any problems applying makeup products on top of it -- it gives the skin a nice dewy finish, but not one that's super shiny or anything like that.  When mixed with the other products, I do feel like it helps them be more effective, in terms of increased softness and moisturization.

It's good that so little is needed per application, as the bottle is teeny tiny.  That said, I've been using 2-3 drops twice a day for about 3.5 weeks (cumulatively), and I still have around a quarter of the bottle left.  So it won't last you a super-long time, but given that it's only .5 oz., it is lasting longer than I initially expected it would. (Side note: given how little product there is, all things considered, the cost is an issue, and I mention that a bit farther down in this review.)

The aroma is lemony, in nature.  It's strong enough to notice, but as the product sinks in, that fragrance dissipates until it's gone entirely.

As for the claims:

It's supposed to improve the appearance of dark marks and hyperpigmentation.  I'd say that that's true.  Now, it won't completely rid you of all sun spots, acne scars, etc., but what I've found is that it does soften and blur the darker bits of hyperpigmentation a bit, and those that weren't as intense in color have faded greatly while some have even gone away.  So, all things considered, this is the only product that I've ever used where I can actually see it making a difference with some of my acne scars, and I started noticing that about 1.5 - 2 weeks after I began using this treatment.  In short, it's not miraculous, but it does make a difference, in varying degrees.

It's also supposed to reduce the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles.  Pretty much the only real line I have is a horizontal one that's about 1.5 inches long and is about an inch below my hairline on the right side of my forehead.  After almost a month of using this product, that line isn't as noticeable.  It's still there, of course, but it's not as defined and deep as it was a month ago.

It also claims to improve skin tone, texture, and firmness.  I've already mentioned how this makes my skin noticeably softer, and that started right after the very first application, as did the effect of toning down some of the redness on my cheeks.  It's also helped to get rid of rough patches that had previously been stubborn and really difficult to try to get rid of, even using exfoliators and scrubs.  As for firmness, that's harder to judge.  I haven't noticed anything in that regard, as of yet, but I suspect that with continued usage, I likely will.

It's also supposed to decrease natural moisture loss, and I can say that my skin had been really dry before I started using this, but now, my face both looks and feels more moisturized.

Finally, it claims to fortify the skin to defend against sun and age damage.  That kind of defense is obviously difficult -if not impossible - to quantify.  All I can say is that, with how this treatment has benefited me thus far, I wouldn't be at all surprise that after the passage of more time, I start to notice that there's something to this claim, as well.

The one and only downside to this product is the price.  As I mentioned above, this is the only product that I've ever used that has noticeably helped my skin without creating still more problems.  Unfortunately, after I finish the last quarter of the bottle, I'm going to have to go without because for me, at the moment, this is prohibitively expensive.  You get what you pay for, of course, and I can't say that  it's not worth the cost, it's just not something that can fit within my budget, which is greatly disappointing.

To sum up, this is a treatment that produces great results, delivers on its claims, and hasn't hurt my ultra-sensitive skin in the slightest.  If this is something you can afford, I highly, highly recommend this product.
summary: Has Given Noticeable Results Without Irritating Sensitive Skin

reviewText:
I'm giving this 3 stars, a neutral rating, because I really can't figure out what this stuff is good for.  I was expecting some documentation inside the package that I could peruse, to answer questions I have, such as "what does it do?" and "is it edible?" but there is no documentation inside the box aside from what is printed on the very small bottle.  Somewhere I noted that it warns not to use it in your eyes.  I did look up the patents listed.  As far as I can tell, it purports to repair damaged skin.

I have a rare medical condition, thought to be an auto-immune disorder, that causes skin problems on a part of my body where elasticity is of prime importance.  I've dealt with this for years, and have tried all kinds of ointments both prescribed and over-the-counter including Clobetasol, Protopic and Elidel as well as virtually every moisturizing cream you can think of, including for example "Chamois Butt'r".  As far as I can tell this product is designed to literally tighten skin, and although I did try it on various parts of my body, it is probably exactly the wrong thing for my specific condition.

It reminds me a bit of liquid bandage, or a very weak glue.
summary: Maybe useful if you want to tighten your skin

reviewText: I went to use this product and removed the plastic when it dropped on my tile floor.  The bottle is actually thin glass covered by plastic.  I was able to salvage some sans pieced of glass and found that it made my skin a bit sensitive.  The directions say you are supposed to use a couple of drops mixed in with your moisturizer, but I don't see the benefit in taking this extra step.  Why not make a product that already has it in it?  The serum itself goes on very very oily and is fairly strong.  It has a pleasant light citrus smell.  I had to remove it after about a hour or so because it was so oily and seem pretty potent.  While my skin did stay sensitive for about a day or so, I did not experience any exfoliation effects.  So far, not terribly impressed.  But, perhaps someone who was able to use the whole bottle might have a different experience.

Instead of applying this by itself, I mix it with a serum on my palms before applying.  It thins the serum, and makes both products easier to spread on the skin.

It does make my skin burn some days, so I would consider this worth using a couple of times a week.  It does help even skin tone, so I recommend it for occasional use.

The benefits of Niacin for your skin are well documented so I was very excited to try this product. I'm so happy with it! I think my skin looks and feels great lately after using this regularly and I haven't ever had a product where I noticed such a difference. It didn't cause any adverse reactions or breakouts despite it being an oil.

I almost always apply it by mixing it in with a moisturizer and this works very well. This product is very expensive but you only need 2-3 drops each use so I think it may last quite awhile. I love this so much I want to buy their other products despite the cost.

Nia 24 Treatment Catalyst, 0.5 oz. seems to help make my skin softer. You do not need a lot. Been using for about 5 days and can notice how softer my face feels. It is a bit pricey at $72 via Amazon Prime shipping. It has a slight scent, yet not overwhelming. One of the few products where I actually saw results. Wish the bottle were bigger.

I deducted one star from this product because of the cost. I have been using it for a week and have been happy with the results. I know you are supposed to mix this in with a product that you are using but I was most impressed with using it on a few areas of my arm that had dry patches. I actually just put a few drops on my hand and rubbed it directly into the area. It absorbed right in and instantly made the area feel better. I think over a longer period of time, it will make a big difference in the appearance of the skin. My face moisturizer also seemed to absorb better while using this product. I'm happy with it and would purchase it again if is was a little more affordable.

So far I have been very pleased with this facial product. It is a very light serum, almost silicone-like and only takes a tiny bit for the face. I do notice it leaves my skin with a nice, soft, moisturized glow. The NIA24 Treatment Catalyst also has a lovely scent. I am using it in conjunction with my usual moisturizing routine, applying it before using either day or night cream. It will take time to see if there is any long-range impact, but my experience with items like this is that continued use can only improve the skin. I have combination skin; basically t-zone and somewhat sensitive. I have not had any problems with irritation or breakout.

My wife mentioned that she noticed she's seen a difference in her pore size since using this product with a lotion she used consistently beforehand. She mentioned how with this product it seems to work a lot better than it did previously. Her base lotion was the most affected by it as she mixes it in each use prior to applying it.

She mentioned how it's hard to mix in with lotion because of the consistency of the droplets of the catalyst but the eyedropper helped. She said she likes the product a lot but may not be able to justify the price given the results despite the nice moderate effects.

Ive been using this skin care product for almost three weeks, and Im sorry to report that I do not see any changes in my skin so far.  I think it may be that it takes several months to show its benefits.

While I do not see improvements to date, I do not see any unpleasant side effects either.  I use it on a clean face and neck where it soaks in fairly quickly.  After it dries, I put on my normal Vitamin C serum.

Ive been using the Vitamin C serum for three months, and I have found it to be effective over time.  My skin glows without noticeable blemishes, so it may be that Id already accomplished most of what can be expected from this serum before I began using this pro-niacin preparatory serum.

Ive found that a little (just a single drop) is sufficient for about half my face, so I expect this bottle to last several months.  I did not received a full bottle for testing because the lid had not be properly screwed on at the factory, and oil was all over the interior of the packaging.

Nia 24 Treatment Catalyst is fairly expensive, so, having no improvement to report so far, I don't imagine Ill purchase more of this product.

THREE STARS!
summary: No Noticeable Improvement, but No Unpleasant Side Effects Either

reviewText: I have been using this every other day for two weeks. Now, it's a little difficult for me to tell if anything is truly happening here. I layered this with Ole Henriksen Truth Serum Collagen Booster and later with GLAMGLOW Thirstymud. With both products, my skin broke-out. I have never had any issue with blemishes, so one blemish on my chin and three on my decollete is highly, highly irregular. The off-days, I used prescription Atralin (a very strong retinoid), so that took care of the blemishes. I have used all products except for this Nia product for years and have never had a negative reaction. So, last night, I wore JUST this product to bed ... and woke-up with a blemish on my nose (again, this is HIGHLY, highly unusual). So, it would appear, for me, this is not the best choice for my skin. And, that I saw no difference in my skin was also discouraging (however, I do see a dermatologist twice a year for fillers and peals as well as using prescription retinoids since I was in my twenties ... so, I'm not sure what I expected). The fragrance is appealing, the bottle is VERY petite, the delivery system is clean/smart (and should eliminate contaminants from entering the bottle) ... but, it just didn't work for me. Nonetheless, to may work for you. Give it a try.

I am on a constant quest to find good products for my face.  I am fair skinned and unfortunately, I spent my youth baking in the sun. Can we say baby oil and iodine?  I am paying the price now.

I was curious about this product promising to help repair sun damage.  I am happy to report that after only a few days' use, my face looks brighter and my pesky age spots are less visible.

Why I love this product:

* It works! At least it works for me.  My skin will never look like that of a 20 year old, but it does look better.

* Only a few drops are needed.  I was initially surprised at the small size of the bottle, but it should last a while since I only need a little bit each time.  Unlike some other reviewers, I had no problem just using 2-3 drops to cover my face.

* The delicious smell.  It smells faintly of limes.  I have tried so many facial products that have strong artificial smells and that turns me off.  This product smells refreshingly different.

* The nice texture.  I thought it glided smoothly onto my face and didn't think it was sticky as some other reviewers have reported.

* I feel pampered.  I remember seeing the Nia 24 products in my dermatologist's office.  I feel like I'm getting a mini-spa, dermatologic treatment in my own home.

If you are looking for something to help your skin recover from sun damage, this might just be for you!
summary: The smell alone would make me want to buy this!

reviewText:
When I told my husband that I received a free bottle of this $71 product, he said, "What if you like it?" At that point, a week ago, I was highly skeptical,  and replied I doubted it would be an issue.

I'm in my fifties, and frankly, there's been no "miracle beauty cure" that I've thought has done a thing for my skin. Getting enough sleep, eating a good diet, protecting my skin from the sun,and washing my face with high quality mostly natural products has been my strategy. I was blessed with a good complexion and tight pores.

I think it would be bizarre to be my age and have no visible signs of aging. To want for that seems ridiculous, in my estimation. But, of course, I want to look my best, as we all do. My skin is fairly dry, has some age spots and lines, and the skin has become less taut. So, with great skepticism, I tried this. I've used neem oil in the past, as it's been used in India for a long, long time. I prefer oil to moisturizer, as I dislike the feeling of product sitting on one's face. Neem and coconut oil both are excellent moisturizers, but they both left my skin too greasy.

Much to my surprise, this Nia 24 really made my skin look and feel great upon the first application. It can be used alone or with another product. I used it alone first; three drops were plenty for my entire face. My skin felt moisturized without any greasiness and stayed that way through the day. I didn't make my skin red or tingly, as some others report. In addition, I was quite pleased that this product has a nice natural smell of citrus. A few minutes after application, I no longer noticed the smell, which is unusual these days with most skin care products. Very nice indeed!

As the week progressed, my skin really did look more healthy. I kept asking myself, "Is it because you know this is pricey?" Considering my extreme skepticism about any beauty products, I think the answer is no. I like how my skin feels and looks, and the sheerness of this product. As for the age spots, I have not noticed a difference, but if I do, I'll come back and give this five stars. Honestly, the only reason I'm not giving it five stars is that I can't really believe that $71 is a reasonable price. I know there are more expensive products out there, but there are also less, and I'm guessing someone is making a tidy profit. Of course, that's what companies do, but at this price, it's just a luxury that most people would have to think more than twice about. Sure, it's less than a shot of Botox, but that's not a great thing to compare it to. Still, I can't say anything else bad about this product other than the price is too high for this shopper. If it were less, I would definitely purchase it, though. I love the way my skin feels!

I used the product with some under-eye product and this worked really nicely.
summary: My skin is happy with it

reviewText:
I'm outdoors for a good part of each day so sun damaged skin is always a cause for concern and I'm always on the lookout for good preventative and restorative products to keep my outer layer nice and healthy. Nia 24's Treatment Catalyst is an effective product to add to your skincare regimen particularly if sun damage is a concern. The Pro-Niacin formulation helps to fortify skin and will improve the appearance of hyperpigmentation and sun spotting. It also does work maintaining general skin health and appearance by preventing moisture loss and boosting tone and overall firmness.

Keep in ind that as a treatment catalyst this is not a 'one and done' product. For best results this should be the second step in your routine. Ideally, the first step = cleanse/exfoliate; second step = Nia 24 Treatment Catalyst; third step (a combo of 1 or all) = serum application/sunscreen/moisturizer.

I've been using this for several days as instructed by the directions on the side of the box, but I can't really tell any difference.  Maybe there is a very slight difference in some minor creases around my eyes but even those I'm not completely certain.  2 to 3 drops is not enough to even lightly cover an entire face and it takes me about 5 drops.  I sometime feel a slight warming afterwards but not always. After application, I usually apply a light layer of organic rose seed oil as my main moisturizer.  The Nia24 smells like a combination of citrus and flowers - not wonderful but not bad either.

I'm really not certain as to what to expect from this product.  Some people say they have had wonderful results by greatly reduced facial lines and wrinkles, but I haven't seen that happen yet.  I don't really have any "wrinkles", even though I'm in my late 50's.  But I do have some slight crinkles and lines around my eyes and a couple at the corners of my mouth that I would love to see reduced, but they're still there just like always.

Personally, from my experience, I wouldn't spend the money to buy this unless I was certain it would do what it says it will do.  I'm giving it 3 stars and I'm being very generous.  I will continue to use this product and if I notice a significant change in improvement in my crinkles I will raise the star level and update this review to reflect that change.

I don't mind paying for quality, but I am highly cost conscious.  So if I am going to pay many times more for a skincare product than a similar drugstore product, I want to feel confident that it is worth it.  As a 46 year old woman, keeping my skin as youthful looking as possible has become a high priority for me, and something I am willing to put some investment into--as long as my return on investment is worth it.  The Nia 24 skin care line definitely comes with a hefty price tag, so I did a little research to determine whether I was paying for hype and status or actual quality.

A quick internet search showed that the Nia 24 line is well-respected in the dermatological community and is generally sold only in physicians' offices.  It is a premium product that comes with a premium price tag.  It was started by a husband and wife team.  Both have PhDs in pharmacology and their life work for years has been researching the effect of niacin on human health.  They have published many papers on it in well-respected journals.  Based on everything they have learned through their many years of research, they started their own skincare line, Nia 24, in 2006.  It has been well-received by highly respected dermatologists.  Since then, including niacin in skin-care products has become more widespread in general, largely based upon the research findings of the Drs. Jacobsen, founders of Nia 24.  So buying their product is kinda like having Dr. Freud as your psychotherapist.

The main benefits of niacin in skincare products are thickening the skin (as skin ages it thins), reducing skin pigmentation, protecting the skin, increasing cell turnover, and having a beneficial effect on DNA metabolism, theoretically even reducing the chance of skin cancer.  All of these are well documented and either scientifically proven or proven to have a strong connection.  One of the drawbacks of niacin is that it can induce skin redness and flushing, including a slightly burning or tingling sensation.  Nia24 contains pro-niacin, a patented formula that greatly reduces the flushing issue in pretty much all people except the most highly sensitive.  This flush, should it occur, is not a cause for concern and will lessen with repeated usage.  I, myself, noticed no issues whatsoever.

The first Nia 24 product I tried was the Intensive Retinol Repair.  Long story short, I liked it and was surprised at how my skin just soaked it up, moreso than my usual retinol creams.  The Nia 24 Treatment Catalyst is designed to be used with any skin product, increasing its absorption and effectiveness.  You can put a few drops on your face before applying your other product, or mix a few drops in with your product.  I chose to put it on my face first.  It is slightly oily, having a light, pleasant essential oil kind of scent, and has a consistency that reminds me of a silicone hair product.  I would not recommend using it under makeup.  One of the benefits is that I used noticeably less Intensive Retinol Repair after I had applied the Treatment Catalyst.  So in that way it will really pay for itself, just a few drops allowing me to use significantly less of another expensive product, and helping that product to work even better to boot.

Since I started using the two products almost at the same time, I really can't say if the Retinol Intensive Repair works better with the Treatment Catalyst.  But since it is from such a highly regarded company and will actually save me money in the long run, I will be including it in my beauty regime going forward.  I am fortunate in that I have few wrinkles, but I will say that the light wrinkles around my eyes do seem to have disappeared pretty much entirely, even when looking at my eyes in my magnified makeup mirror.  I noticed that after only a few uses.

I received a small bottle of Nia 24 Treatment Catalyst, 0.5 oz in exchange for my review.  I had seen the price set at $71.00 and I thought for that amount of money it better work.  I have used it for about a week and a half.  That is hardly enough time to tell if a new product works.  However, after the first use, I woke up the next morning and had blemishes on my face. They were on my nose and around my nose and a small blemish on my chin.  I thought well, it's a new product sometimes breakouts happen and I will just use it once at night and see how it goes.  The first use was with the Nia 24 Treatment by itself.  I used three drops and had a hard time getting it smoothed over my skin.  This did not seem to be an adequate amount to provide full coverage on my face. The next morning I mixed three drops with my moisturizer and used it that way for three days.  I used it every morning and night, but every morning I woke up, looked in the mirror and had two to three new blemishes.  By the end of the few days I used the product, my face looked like I was going through puberty.  I am in my fifties.  How embarrassing.  I had these awful blemishes on my nose, cheek and chin.  Mainly however, the breakouts were on my nose.  So after the first few uses of morning and evening, I thought I will not put any on my nose and see if this really is the cause of my breakouts.  My nose remained clear after a couple of days, but I still had breakouts on my cheeks and chin.  I then switched to just using it at night.  Finally, the last night I used it and woke up again in the morning with more blemishes, I said that's it.  I have had enough.  My skin is still recovering from all of the breakouts over the past week and a half.  Unfortunately, I did not notice any change in my skin as to less lines, softness, and smoothness.  I don't really have a problem with skin products causing breakouts.  I use a lot of different products.  With this product, my face would continue to break out even in the middle of the afternoon.  I would go to the restroom and there would be another blemish on my nose. I believe my skin was just too sensitive for this product.  I also believe that even if I had noticed any improvement, I would not be paying $71.00 for a skin product.  I find that amount to be a bit lavish for someone like me who works for a living and has to live on a tight budget.  Overall, I cannot recommend this product.  It may work for others, but my skin could not take any more.
summary: I had terrible breakouts from this product.

reviewText: This is a very expensive product as you only get half of an ounce for $70.  It does work well at helping damaged skin and only a few drops are needed as you combine this with other skin care products.  I was lucky enough to get a free sample but probably would not buy this myself but go to my dermatologist for a prescription/treatment that would be at least partially covered by a prescription plan.  An eye dropper is included to deliver the drops of this precious serum

I was excited to try Nia 24 since I had heard such great things about niacin. The bottle is very small but you only need a small amount. I like the applicator; it is a slightly curved dropper so you get just the right amount.

I used it for more than a week and I am still not seeing much change. I use it every night after washing my face and before moisturizer. One thing I noticed is that my face turns slightly red wherever I put the niacin. It goes away when I put moisturizer on. I thought it was supposed to open up your skin to make the moisturizer more effective but I have not yet seen that. In fact, it seems to do the reverse. I feel like the serum seals my face and the moisturizer can't penetrate. I wind up with flaky skin on my cheekbones, which I never had before. I'm going to continue using it for another week but if there is no change, I may discontinue usage. Maybe niacin just doesn't work for me.
summary: Nicely designed package; but not seeing much change

reviewText: I USE THIS PRODUCT IN THE DAY TIME AFTER MY TREATMENT, MOISTURIZING, AND C+E CREAM.  IT SEEMS TO BE WORKING WELL.

I got a small sample tube of this cream with a beauty box I subscribe to. Before that tube was gone I was here on Amazon buying the full size. I have sensitive skin and it's always on the dry side. I was going through a very bad spell that lasted for days after having used a mask that was way too irritating. My skin was actually sore. While using the sample, my skin irritation vanished completely. So I thought afterward that maybe it was a little heavy, but I've been using and loving it ever since.

It is very pricey, but the price here was actually much lower than on the web site associated with the beauty box I got my sample in - definitely great prices on this brand here on Amazon. You only need a tiny pea-size amount to moisturize your whole face, so the tube lasts foever. The consistency is like a thick gel cream that spreads easily over your entire face. It's super moisturizing and the moisturized feeling lasts me all day. Now this cream would likely be too heavy for people who have oilier skin, and I may have to back off a tiny bit in the hottest part of the summer, but otherwise, this is my go to moisturizer. I absolutely love this stuff!
summary: The best moisturizer I've ever used on my dry skin!

reviewText: Moisturizing but not greasy/heavy which is great in a warm climate.

This curler is made of high quality material at a reasonable price.  Since it is used near the eyes, it has to be made of good material. The nice feature of this curler is it uses chamomile moisturizing pads, each of them suppose to last 3 months.  The package comes with 3 pads.  Maybe because this product is very new, I can't find any replacement pads being sold on Amazon.com.  I guess they will show up before these pads are used up.

The design and construction allow easy application and produce desirable results.  I recommend it!

I normally use an eye lash curler by Revlon (not expensive).  I have just kept using it, because it is simple to just buy new refills and keep using the same one.  I curl my eye lashes a LOT.  I mean probably 4 or 5 times each eye before I'm satisfied.  I have medium length lashes, but they are blond and very fine.  It's difficult to get mascara on them without clumping or weighing them down.

When I first tried the Georgie Beauty curler, I was disappointed, because it doesn't open very wide. This makes you take an extra couple of seconds to get your eye lashes in place correctly.  I was going to rate this curler a 4 because of this.  However, they curl my lashes so much better than my previous curler!!  They LOOK very similar, but these curl better. I don't know that it is because of the pad or not, but something works better.  I now curl each eye 2 or 3 times instead of 4/5 times. One time would probably be fine, but I will have to let go of my thought process that I HAVE to do it more than once.  I'm extremely happy that I can cut off a little time in the mornings.  Every little bit helps!
summary: Works much better than my previous curler

reviewText:
I have been using a Shiseido eyelash curler for many years and have had no problem replacing the pads which are readily available.  I wipe the pad down after using and I don't use the curler after applying mascara, so it is still perfectly operational and looks good after a very long time.  The eyelash curler by Georgie Beauty resembles the Shiseido and numerous varieties but it has something special in the USDA-certified organic blue chamomile enhancement to the pads.  It is sold with the enclosed pad and an additional two replacements.  I've been unable to locate the pads for purchase at this time, but being that the tool is now sold at major higher end department stores, I'm sure they will be available in the near future.

This curler works no better than the Shiseido or any other I've used.  I am not impressed by a pad with chamomile because I don't think it will last longer than the initial use for a person such as myself who cleans the tools they use on their eyes.  Yes, it is nice to include a couple of replacement pads, but to me, they are no better than others and since the curler costs about as much as my previous tool, I still prefer my long time friend eyelash curler.

Lash curler? Sure. Ultimate? Eh. I can't see what would set this lash curler above the rest. Oh, don't get me wrong it's definitely better than the cheap one I got out of desperation once at a cheap chain store for a few bucks. That lash curler was truly worthless. However, I've used a variety of other lash curlers from the beauty store over the years and most of them work just as well as this one.

Comparing this one to my Emite lash curler that came recently in an Ipsy bag, I actually think the Emite one curled a bit better and also felt less wobbly because the handles are wider. That said, this Georgie curler was almost just as good and cost a few dollars less. It does come in a nice box for packaging and they include a few extra cushions--which are nice as they can get worn out or fall off after much use.

All that said, there is nothing "ultimate" about this lash curler, I'd say it's quite average and does it's job fine but it is not THE ultimate lash curler,no.
summary: Works fine, "Ultimate" is a stretch, and compared to the Emite curler...

reviewText: The eyelash curler does it job and I am happy to see that it has removable cushions so that you can change out the portion that actually touches the eyelash.  For eye safety, that makes a lot of sense.  However, I am not able to find replacements for the cushions for sale.  I would hate to think that I would have to buy a whole new curler in less than a year.  Hopefully, the manufacturer will make the replacements available soon.
summary: Does curl well but can't find the replacement parts

reviewText: This curler performs much like the old fashioned curler it's modeled after.  I can't really tell a discernible difference when using the moisturizing pads on this device.  It curls exactly as well as the old models, with much the same results.  It's good if you need a curler.
summary: This curler performs much like the old fashioned curler it's modeled after

reviewText: Initially I thought, how can an eyelash curler be better than another. Okay, so it doesn't pinch, that's nice. But the boost for the eyelashes, c'mon. Well for two weeks I used my old curler - with a new pad and I used the Georgie beauty curler on the other. Initially I couldn't tell a difference in curl or what have you, but in two weeks I could tell that the Georgie eyelash was fuller and silkier. Weird, I know, but it happened. So if that's important to you, you should have this curler.
summary: I thought it was silly at first

reviewText: I didn't notice anything special about this eyelash curler.  The curler pads are pretty, and the tool itself is sturdy, but it still pinched my eyelid.  And it seems like it takes more work to get my eyelashes to curl than my usual Shiseido lash curler.

This curler works great and I like the fact that it is infused with organic chamomile. My lashes certainly need conditioning with all the mascara I wear and remove daily. Hope that it helps to keep the lashes in shape, it sounds like a great idea!  I do wear contact lenses and the chamomile doesn't bother me at all, it was one of the things that I was wondering about at first, but had no problem. The curler also comes with 2 extra refill pads which is nice.
summary: Condition and curl your lashes in one step, what a great idea!

reviewText:
The Georgie is built exactly the same as other lash curlers, works exactly the same way and still yields the same results as my old Maybelline curler. The only differences I can see are the chamomille-infused gel pads that are supposed to condition the lashes and the price tag. Do gel pads really work? I have no idea. My lashes look no different than with the other curler. And, big question, where do I get replacement gel pads?

So, the Georgie is a lash curler and it works but it is more expensive than a curler that is equally effective.

3.5 stars for price and lack of a known source for replacement pads.
summary: It works, it curls, it costs too much

reviewText: I have used many different lash curlers over the years, so I decided to give this new one a try. I thought it was just "okay." It was serviceable, but there is nothing special about it that I would recommend over any of the others I have used for years.

I haven't used one of these in years but lately I've found myself in the market for a lash curler. I've taken to wearing night masks since I sleep in the day, but unfortunately not all of them have a space allowance for eyelashes, which leads to unruly lashes. This doesn't sound awful until one such unruly lash decides that it wants to take up residence in your eyelid. Not fun.

As far as the basic design goes, this is a pretty good curler. It's easy to use and while I do wish that it was wrapped with plastic (as opposed to rattling around inside the box), I have no complaints about the design or its use. If you've used one of these before then you'll know how to use this. The pads are nice and soft and despite accidentally yanking on my eyelashes at one point (in an attempt to get it properly positioned), it's slightly difficult to really do any damage with this. As promised, I didn't feel any pinching or crimping while using this.

My only hesitancy would be with the chamomile pads. I don't know if this would take a long time to see the conditioning claims, but I haven't seen any difference yet.

So is this better than some of the cheaper alternatives out there? To be honest, I don't know. I haven't used any other curlers in years and the ones that I'd used prior to that were on the cheaper side. I don't see where this has any new bells and whistles but I also have to admit that I had a nicer experience with this than I did in the past.
summary: Works nice, not sure about the chamomile conditioning claims

reviewText: I have a Maybelline Expert Eyes Eyelash Curler which has flat inserts and which I paid less than $8 for. This curler's inserts are more concave allowing me to get a greater curl. However, I do not feel the silicone insert infused with organic blue chamomile is going to make much of a difference on my lashes. Nevertheless, only time will tell. This curler comes with two extra inserts. The package recommends replacing the inserts after three months of use. The silicone inserts are infused with chamomilla recutita (chamomile) flower extract which is USDA-certified organic blue chamomile. This product is made in China. I will update my review if I have any positive or negative results. I do like this beauty product and it does curl my eyelashes well, but I probably would not pay the current price of $18 just for a tad more curl and the promise of conditioned lashes.
summary: Curls slightly better than my Maybelline curler

reviewText: This is a pretty good curler. I like that the pads are soft and the whole thing is made from metal. Maybe not as sturdy as some of the more expensive ones I've seen but it will certainly last a long time!
summary: This is a pretty good curler

reviewText:
This is just another regular eyelash curler to me.  Besides the word "chamomile", there is no difference in the feel or curling effect from the average regular eyelash curlers with the plain old white replacement pads.  The pads on the Georgie Lash Curler are made of silicone and infused with organic blue chamomile that are suppose to naturally condition your lashes.  However, if you are going to coat your lashes afterwards with mascara...what's the purpose?

I one thing I not like right away was I could not fit my entire length of my eyelashes and had to do both eyes in two sections.  The curler is very small in width.  I measured it corner to corner and it is 1 and 1/4 inches long.

I guess for the asking price I expect something a bit more more than "high-end" than the average curler with different pads.
summary: Fancy Name for An Average Curler

reviewText:
It's an eyelash curler. It works the way you would expect any eyelash curler to work.  The pad on the bottom half is teal, and made of a squishy gel-like material that is soft, but it's really no different than any other eyelash curler I have tried.  Eyelash curlers only pinch when they are used incorrectly.
It does come with two extra pads, which will be great as long as I don't lose them before I need them!)

I don't curl my eyelashes daily, but when I do, Ive used a Shu Umera eyelash curler for more than a decade now. (Ive never worn fake eyelashes, so this was tested solely on natural lashes.)

This Georgie beauty model is very comparable, if a little less well-made. (Feels kind of chintzy and breakable in my hand.) The big difference here is supposed to be the conditioning pads, which I did find softer than the rubber pads on the Shu Umera (which Ive replaced a few times in the curlers lifetime), which is likely gentler on lashes  less likely to pull them out  but it also made the curl less distinct because they don't hold as tightly.

The Georgie recommends curling the same way Ive always done it: hold once close to the lashes, release and then curl again closer to the ends. The results are decent and the product easy to clean, but one thing that didn't seem to work as well as with the Shu, probably due to the composition of the pads, is the old trick of briefly heating the eyelash curler with a hair dryer for a longer lasting curl.

This does come with two sets of replacement pads, which is nice, as the instructions advocate replacement every three months. Of course that leaves one to wonder where youll find replacements, as they're not (at least not yet) carried on Amazon, and my local beauty supply store doesnt carry this product line.

Otherwise, this is a decent curler, though Im not sure the conditioning adds much beyond gentleness.

Oh and, just FYI, always curl your lashes BEFORE applying mascara, not after, which is probably the best thing you can do to protect your lashes.  I will say that while I regularly wear very little makeup, one of the most noticeable differences I can make to my face at my age (40), is curling my lashes and then putting on mascara. It really does make a large, noticeable difference. Not something I take the time to do every day, but testing this product reminded me of.
summary: Decent, Gentle Curler, Skeptical of "Conditioning" Claims

reviewText: This is a great eyelash curler! Soft and cushy, and doesn't pull. East grip handle makes it quick to look glamorous!

I've never been great about taking care of my skin, but now that I'm aging (late 50s), I am trying to be better. One troubling area is my neck.

I was a little afraid of trying this product because I've had some allergic reactions in the last year or so after trying some cosmetic products. Fortunately, this one did NOT cause any allergic reactions.
