It can deliver up to a pulse per second. It turns off automatically after about 30 seconds, which can be annoying as that isn't always long enough to find the next spot and get it to activate.

Some difficulties are getting it exactly on the right spot each time as the tip is rather large, and getting it to activate - it doesn't always seem to sense that it is on the skin. Lifting and re-applying or pressing a little harder into the skin can help with that. This unit is recommended for daily use; for larger treatment areas many pulses may be required.

This unit provides a 1440nm laser pulse of 3 J/cm2 (low) or 4 L/cm2 (high). This is very similar to the output used in a 2006 study by Weiss et al to treat wrinkles and scars and showed improvement in 94% of patients after a series of 3 treatments 4 weeks apart. They also used a 1440nm laser in the range of 3 to 7 J/cm2, but with a broader beam requiring fewer pulses.

This laser provides non-ablative treatment through neocollagenesis by heating a small column of skin; it is considered a less intense treatment allowing more frequent use with no "down time" or painful recovery. It is more mild and has less dramatic results than some of the more powerful (and painful) laser treatments, but is perfect for frequent home use.

Stick with it for at least a week because it is much easier to use (and tolerate) after some experience. Missing days is no big deal either; it is more of the cumulative effect that is important. I love this device and highly recommend it for anyone who is motivated to improve their appearance!
summary: Much more convenient than the doctor's office!

reviewText:
The Iluminage Skin Smoothing Laser had helped reduce the appearance of my fine wrinkles. Most of my wrinkles are still on the smaller size around my eyes. This laser only works on the eye and mouth area. I wish it worked on foreheads because those are my most prominent wrinkles. This laser is FDA approved which is one of the main reasons I am fine using it. The instruction manual is very informative, read it before using this laser.

This came very nicely packaged. You receive the laser, stand, charger, USB cord, and travel bag. The laser does have a safety feature so kids don't mess with this. You have to hold the power button for 3 seconds before it will turn on. Since I don't think that would distract my toddler from thinking this was a toy, I store this in the box. I could use the travel bag, but the box holds it so tightly in place I prefer storing it there. The base is very sturdy and when the laser is sitting in it, it is a little heavy. There is a pretty strong magnet that hold the laser in place with thee base. You can feel the pull and hear the click connection. Which is another reason I think my son would think the magnetic feature is a fun toy.

Hold the power button and the laser turns on after a few seconds. It makes a beeping greeting sound and spells hello across the small screen. When on, it will say low which means it's on the low setting.  Press the power button again for the high setting. The Ponds Institute (the maker of this device) and I both recommend trying the low setting first. They also recommend testing the device on your forearm first. You want to check to make sure the laser isn't cracked or damage before you begin. And after multiple uses you may need to clean the laser with some rubbing alcohol. It's also recommended that you use this in the evening during your week day beauty ritual. That is in hopes that the redness will be gone or lessened by morning. You should use two fingers from the hand not holding the device to pull your skin tight as you use the laser on the wrinkle area. You are supposed to move the laser over slightly so there is a small overlap of where you just used it. That is so you cover the whole area. The top of the laser is round and that circle area will light up white when the laser is flap against your skin. It turns blue when you press the button and the laser is in use. It will beep when done. It is over very quickly. Everyone has a different pain tolerance, but I felt like it was a small pin prick. It is a little shocking at first. I imagine especially if you have a lot of wrinkles and are using the laser 40 times in one area alone. The laser has sort of plumped up my skin helping to minimize my wrinkles. I have fine wrinkles and sensitive skin so I use this about every other or every third day. I don't wear much makeup. Mostly just concealer on a daily basis which is why I'm concerned about the appearance of my skin.

In the attached pictures is a photo of the laser and base in the packaging. The picture of my forearm is after I used the laser on it. The photo was taken about an hour and a half after I used the laser. You can see I did a poor job of overlapping the laser. The top half was with the laser on high, the bottom with the laser on low.
summary: ... Smoothing Laser had helped reduce the appearance of my fine wrinkles. Most of my wrinkles are still on ...

reviewText:
I was apprehensive and a little nervous before receiving this skin smoothing laser. I did a lot of research and most of the reviews I read said it was very painful. I've used an epilator on my face for years and that can be painful, so I wondered if this could actually hurt worse. The laser arrived in a heavy box (the laser and base are heavy), with a cord, a USB cable and very nice bag to put it all in.

Before first trying it I read through the whole instruction manual (written by an English speaking person) to make sure I knew what to do. I was still nervous to try it, but I tried it on my forearm first like is recommended in the manual. To power on the device you need to press the power button 3 seconds (if you only press a second you'll get an error tone; I know because I got a couple of them at first). The laser pulse starts out at low (to set it to high you push the power button). So, it was set to low and I finally got up the nerve to place the lens of the laser on my forearm; I saw a blue light that meant it had delivered the pulse. Huh? I didn't even feel it. It counts the number of pulses on the device so I knew it had worked. So I tried it on high on my forearm; that I could feel but it was nothing like using an epilator or even a tweezer. After that I got brave and tried it on my face (make sure your face is clean and dry). I only used the low setting the first time and I didn't do many pulses, only about 10 on each side of my mouth (40 in each zone is recommended and there's 4 separate zones; 2 on the side of the mouth and 2 around the eyes). I could feel it on the low setting, but nothing compared to tearing my hair out by the roots via an epilator. I didn't see any reddening in the area afterward, but I did put on some skin serum (I have since seen some reddening of the skin).

There is a separate instruction sheet showing a website to a Skin Clinic to track your results. They included a USB cable to do this, so I plugged it in and my computer installed the software and then nothing. So I went to the URL and got this message: "Welcome to the iluminage Skin Clinic Thank you for your patience as we work to bring you a new, improved treatment experience. Stay tuned!" A device this expensive that comes with a USB cable only for the purpose of connecting to the skin clinic website and it's not working. :-( (Three weeks later I checked again and it's still not working)

I read that there was a study of women between 35 and 55 and the majority of them could see a difference after using this; sometimes in only two weeks but possibly not until 8 or 12 weeks. When I read that I thought yikes! I'm almost 65 so I wonder if this will really help me; I guess only time will tell.

It's a few days later and I have used this 5 times so far on my face and then took a break on the weekend, which is recommended. The most annoying part is that you have to get the laser *perfect* before it will emit a pulse; I think that may be why some people don't think it works. The second night I tried this it kept going off after 30 seconds because I wasn't placing the laser correctly. That night it took me over 1/2 an hour to finally get 40 pulses on each side. I'm getting better because last night only took 10 minutes. The second night I started putting the laser on "high" and I honestly can't tell much difference between the "low" and "high". (When I'm posting this about 3 weeks later I can now do 40 pulses on each side in a couple minutes). I know some people have written that it really hurts, but honestly to me even on "high" it doesn't hurt near what an epilator does. Everybody's pain threshold is different and I have a high pain threshold (I was told by a Dr. after a tonsillectomy at age 21 that I was the only adult patient he'd ever had who didn't complain about the pain afterward). Plus I've had debilitating headaches from a neck injury for close to 40 years now, so unfortunately pain is something I've had to deal with.

Does it work? That remains to be seen. I had planned on posting before and after photos, but between the time I started this review three weeks ago (I save it in notepad) and posting it, my Mom passed away. ;-( So I will be postponing the photos because if anything I think I may have added more wrinkles and need to start again from scratch.

I received the iluminage Skin Smoothing Laser for my honest review. I have wanted to look into what is advertised in my city as laser light treatments.  I have reached the age where this is something I think could benefit me.  So with much delight I ordered the iluminage Skin Smoothing Laser hoping for younger looking skin.  Per the description of the iluminage Skin Smoothing Laser it states The skin smoothing laser delivers pulses of laser light below the surface of the skin, where wrinkles form. This technology is known to trigger the body's natural response to generate new collagen fibers. Skin's support structure is reinforced from within-significantly reducing wrinkles. Safe enough to use at home, yet as effective as professional lasers for the treatment of facial wrinkles, such as wrinkles around the eyes and mouth.  I was very excited to try this and read the instruction manual at least six to seven times cover to cover. I had no experience with laser treatments and I wanted to be very safe and sure about using it.  I charged it immediately as the instruction manual stated there would not be a full charge on the laser.  With great anticipation, I used it the next night firmly aware that there may be slight stinging and redness.  I first tried it on my forearm as stated in the instructions.  I had two red welts on my forearm for a full 24 hours.  This did not deter me in any way.  I used the laser, and yes it stings.  I compare it to many, many bee stings.  After a full four zone use (this is the recommendation in the manual) and 40 pulses per zone, my face was intensely red and my skin had welts all over.  The stinging persisted for 25 to 30 minutes.  It was very painful.  I had to take some ibuprofen for the pain.  The next morning I still had redness on both checks.  I used it again that evening, same thing happened, intense stinging and redness and pain.  I took ibuprofen again.  The third night I was getting ready to use the laser and my husband said, I wouldnt use that as your face looks quite puffy!  Now, I have been married for nearly 30 years and I have never heard those words out of my husbands mouth.  Your face looks puffy!  So, I decided, per the manual instructions, that I should skip a night as I have never had any type of laser treatment done and apparently my skin was quite sensitive.  However, this still did not deter me from my quest for younger looking skin.  I have regularly used this laser treatment almost every night for three weeks.  I even took a before picture before I started.  I took an after picture last night and compared the two.  Unfortunately, I see no difference whatsoever.  I specifically wanted to try this laser treatment for my smoker lines on my lips.  I have not smoked in years, but I still have the lines to prove that I did once smoke.  Also, I am beginning to see lines around my nose area and into my forehead at the top of the nose between the eyebrows.  However, the forehead is not a zone and the instruction manual says not to use this laser on any other area but the four zones.  They are underneath the eye and around the cheeks, around the mouth and chin.  I wanted this to work so badly that I proceeded to use it every night with the stinging and pain and yes it does sting and it is painful.  I spent every night I used it with burning and redness.  I did find if I used a moisturizer right after, the redness did not last but the stinging did.  As the nights went by, I did have fewer welts on my face and the redness did not last as long, but I still had intense stinging after use for at least 15 to 20 minutes every night.  So, after three weeks of conscientious use, I see no improvement in the appearance of lines, wrinkles, or skin tone.  I will however, continue to use it hoping that eventually I will see some improvement.  If not, I will stop as I cannot even begin to imagine continuing to use this laser treatment every night, experiencing pain, and no results.  I am hoping to gradually see less lines and wrinkles.  Can I recommend this product?  Not at this point in time.  I will attempt to update if I do experience the results I am truly looking for.
summary: My skin has not changed in anyway after three weeks!

reviewText:
I was interested to try the iluminage Skin Smoothing Laser to see if it would help the appearance of lines around my eyes and mouth.  I've had some "crow's feet" for a while not, but am just starting to notice a couple of "smile lines."  I'm 41 and have very fair skin.  I can handle mild discomfort, so thought to myself, "Why not?"

First, the pain was more intense than I expected, especially around the mouth area.  I tried using a pain relieving cream several minutes before using the laser treatment, but it didn't make it much more pleasant.  In addition, my skin stayed red for quite a long time after each use.  I used the laser at night and expected the redness to fade by morning, but it didn't (good thing I often work from home).  Someone with less fair or les sensitive skin may not have the same problem with redness.  I think I could get used to the discomfort, but I can't use something every night that causes noticeable redness well into the next day.  Most makeup makes my skin break out, so covering up the redness with foundation isn't an option.  Since I couldn't continue using the device, I unfortunately can't comment on the long term effectiveness.

I think before purchasing this item you need to be aware of how it will affect you.  I would suggest trying a laser treatment at a spa so you know what to expect and how your skin will respond.  If it goes well, you'd save money with this device in the long run.  If you don't like the laser treatment or have any side effects, you know not to spend your money on this one.

I tried my best to ignore the pain but I just could not get past two rounds of treatment, even at the lowest setting. Not that it was excruciating but it was just so unpleasant that I did not feel it was worth it. Plus my face was red for hours. Thus, I do not know if it works at all. If you are used to laser treatments at the doctor's office then you will probably be fine. If you're like me - someone who has never had any laser treatments before using this device - then I would say consider your pain threshold very carefully before paying for this product. The manual states that regular use will result in diminished sensation of pain but unfortunately I could not continue.

Otherwise, I found it very easy to use. There are sound and display indicators which lets you know the setting, how many pulses you've done, assessment reminders, and whether the laser pulse was properly delivered. In addition, once you reach the maximum amount of pulses per treatment, the entire thing will shut down for four hours to prevent excessive use.

I also found the design to be aesthetically pleasing, an elegant device on my bathroom counter.
summary: Could not get past the pain

reviewText:
Works. Is it painful, well ... sorta. The reality of this particular skin treatment is that it does cause pain when you use it. The good news is that it does work to help create better looking skin. I used it for about 2 weeks on some wrinkles on my face and they definitely improved.  The device is super easy to use and charge, and the set up is really nice. The stand is great, it has a great firm hold on the "wand" and it looks nice in the bathroom.

The bad news is that it hurts. I think the better way to describe it is between a sting and a sharp burn. But it isn't overwhelming and you can certainly handle it. Now if you are super sensitive to pain and are not really into clearing some skin issues up, then you will not be motivated to do it. But if you are motivated and want results, then you will be bale to easily handle the sting and you will be happy with what results.

Also, be aware that this is not the equivalent of a face lift. This seems to work best on smaller areas.
summary: Works and if you are motivated, then you will get satisfactory results.

reviewText:
The first word that comes to mind when I think of this gadget is OUCH.  Oh, and OUCH, and OUCHEY OUCH.  I guess I just don't dislike my wrinkles enough to endure this, even on the lowest setting, especially around the eyes.  The description of it feeling like a rubber band plinking your face is putting it mildly.  It's just too uncomfortable for me, and as I said, perhaps I just don't hate my wrinkles enough quite yet.

I know people who use it with no problem.  I tried it on a friend who told me it was only mildly irritating to her.  I had another friend say she would do it if she felt her wrinkles were enough of a problem, which she does not.  I had another friend who wouldn't let me near her with it.  I think it all depends on how badly you want your wrinkles minimized and how high your pain tolerance is.  My friend who said it didn't bother her at all has been using it and said she has noticed her skin is smoother.  So, is it a gadget that works?  It seems it might be.  But, I couldn't tolerate it long enough to see any results at all. For me, not a worthy purchase, but for those who can tolerate the pain, it's fine and worth the effort and cost.

What I would suggest is perhaps going to a spa and having one treatment to see what it feels like for yourself.  If you can tolerate it, then purchasing your own would be worth it.  As I said, my daring friend said she noticed a difference, so I'd say it works, if you can get past the discomfort.
summary: Great, if you can get past the discomfort

reviewerName: Keleigh Crigler Hadley, author of Revenge Inc.
reviewText: They say, "No Pain, No Gain." This product works BUT, it comes at a price.

I've been on the hunt for a good curling iron. I tried everything, nothing was working to my satisfaction or holding a curl longer than an hour or two. I got this randomly wondering what all the hype was about and I LOVE IT. I got a haircut my stylist called "a lob", a bit shorter in the back coming down a little longer by the face. I've been dying for cute beach waves but I'm a hair idiot and lazy in the beauty department on top of it. This was super easy to use and fast. The first time I used it I didn't use any product and it stayed till the following day. It fell over time into the perfect beach wave. I use it on the slower setting so I can make sure it won't take off without me being ready.

I usually scoff at the high priced beauty tools, they all get hot right? Apparently I was wrong. I'm a convert. I also found it almost forty five dollars cheaper with some coupon codes through Kohls. Buy this.

Okay so at first I was hesitant about this. A lot of money for a curling iron right?! The first few times I used it I was sure I was going to end up sending it back. Well, after some practice I LOVE THIS THING! I have shoulder length hair and I can do my whole head in 9 minutes! The curls stay all day and it doesn't damage my hair! I leave the ends out for a beachy look, and my hair seriously looks GREAT! Keeping this for sure! If you are like me and want glam hair but am not particularly skilled in that area, this is your tool (with a bit of practice)

Absolutely love this! If you are on the fence about this, let me help push you over...This is amazing. I have long, very thick hair; I will style my hair with this, use my boar bristle brush to soften the curls and then I have gorgeous waves/curls for DAYS. I use some dry shampoo as needed(washing hair daily is a nono) and even after days the curls fall into nice waves and give great body to my hair. It cuts down the time curling SOOO MUCH! My hair hits mid-back when not curled and would take me 35-45min to curl it before I had this, now its done in 15mins max. To the reviewers saying their hair burned..you can adjust the temp on it..also, use heat protecting spray. This is an awesome weapon for your hair arsenal. I attached a photo of the back of my hair 3 days after I first styled. The trick is wash your hair at night, then use a thermal active setting spray to both protect hair and hold curls, I finish with Loreal elnett hair spray and do a gentle sweep with my boar bristle brush. It seems like a lot of steps, but it leaves me with days of great hair.

Scared the ^%^%% out of me!!
Have used before.
Then, one day it kept curling and wouldn't stop the rolling mechanism!!! It hit my scalp, was SCORCHING HOT, and scared me to death!  What if it hadn't stopped???
I unplugged as fast as I could!!
I'm too scared to use again :((
I missed the return date by TWO days :(((

I love this curler.  I have no idea how to curl my hair but I can do it with this.  I watched many u tube videos which helped.  My hair is one length so my curls only last a day but I still love this thing. Great gift idea too.  Update :  After using this for a while now, I'm even more in love with this.  I have gotten so many compliments on my hair.  One thing that made a huge difference are the oribe products I started using.  The dry texturizing spray is to die for and the mousse is amazing.  These things really help with my curls.  I can't live without this iron now.
MY STYLIST JUST DID MY HAIR WITH IT AND I LOOK AMAZING, NOW I JUST HAVE TO LEARN TO DO IT
summary: ... JUST DID MY HAIR WITH IT AND I LOOK AMAZING, NOW I JUST HAVE TO LEARN TO DO

reviewText:
You make the best shadows.

Golds aren't always my best color, but this has such lovely mattes and that rose gold..so pretty.

When swatched on my arm without primer, these still look amazing, but when doing makeup, I do always use eyeshadow with primer, so take that into consideration.

Overall, the colors are a nice balance of light/dark and half are shimmery, half are matte. On my super pale skin, the colors swatch and show up pretty true to what they look like in the pan. They go on smoothly and evenly and blend well without ever getting muddy. If you've ever used LORAC shadows before, these are on par with their typical quality. If you haven't, think Urban Decay or Wet'n'Wild (yes, I am aware that is the super cheap brand, but their shadows are top notch if you aren't in the know).

Since I don't go out of my way to buy gold tones, I can't really compare this to similar palettes, but if a pop of golden shimmer is what you need, this is a lovely option.

This palette is another entrant onto the neutrals scene and the second Lorac Unzipped palette.  Like, the original, Unzipped Gold features 10 full sized shadows.  This time, the shades are in the gold and brown family and the palette is overall extremely warm toned.  3 are true mattes, 1 shade is a satin matte, 1 is a matte with some glitter and 5 are shimmers.  Like other Lorac shadows I have tried, the shades generally are really pigmented but the shadows are soft, so if you don't tap your brush, you will get fallout on your cheeks.  This palette comes with a nice sized sample of the Lorac eyeshadow primer.  It will last a while and it is high quality - one of my favorites.  I actually am using the full size at the moment.

The quality of this palette is not QUITE as good as the original Unzipped palette (or Lorac Pro).  I found that the shades in the bottom row are creamier and smoother than the shades in the top row.  The quality of the shadows in the original palette was more even.  The original has no finicky shades, whereas this palette has 1 shade that has chunky glitter - Uninhibited.  I found that it performed similarly to Trick in the Urban Decay Naked 3 - chunky with fall out.  It doesn't swatch consistently.  I haven't tried applying it to my eyes with a damp brush yet, but that may help.  I wore it yesterday and even after tapping my brush, I still had some fallout.  I posted pictures of the swatched shades.  All shades were swatched on my forearm with no primer.  The first picture is the top row of shadows, the second picture is the bottom row.

Overall, I think the palette is good, but I can see that it won't really be a favorite.  It is missing a mid-tone shimmery brown.  The shimmers are all very gold and are not quite right for the outer third of the eyelid.  None of the four brown shades are shimmers.  I would have liked a mid-tone shimmer to add more dimension to eye looks.  There are better neutral palettes out there.  This one is good, but I think the Too Faced Chocolate Bar, Lorac Pro (Original), Too Faced Natural Eye, and Urban Decay Naked 1 are all better curated palettes.  In contrast, Unzipped (original) is the best pink-toned/rose gold palette that I have come across (superior to Urban Decay Naked 3).
summary: Good neutral palette but not THE best.

reviewText:
The Lorac Unzipped Gold palette is a nice addition to your palette collection if you already own some palettes in other more matte finishes. This one works well for summer and fall as it adds many more Gold shades that work well with a nice summer tan.

It contains 10 shadows and a mini Behind the Scenes primer.
Top Row:
 Undressed (matte)  a light skin tone base matte shade
 Uninhibited (Shimmer)  a light peachy rose pale gold shade, best worn with a wet brush
 Unpredictable (shimmer)  a peachy coral gold shade, with a bronze effect also best applied wet
 Undeniable (matte)  a medium brown matte shade with warm undertones
 Unedited (matte)  a dark brown matte shade for crease, this shade is not as pigmented and needs a primer to stick
Bottom Row:
 Unlocked (shimmer)  very pale frosted gold shade, great for highlights
 Unlimited (shimmer)  light yellow gold shimmer shade
 Unleashed (shimmer)  bronze coppery-gold shimmer shade, best applied wet
 Unwind (matte)  a medium taupe or coffee brown matte shade
 Unafraid (shimmer)  deep brown shade with a slight pearl effect for lining or dramatic effect

I would not advise using these shades without the primer as the fallout is pretty high on the more gold shades. The shades are buttery and highly pigmented but not more buttery that some MAC shades from the new Brownluxe or Copperluxe palette. I would say the fallout is just as much as many Urban Decay shades from the Naked Palette so you know that you have to apply primer to make these shadows last. However, these shadows are slightly less glittery than some Urban Decay shades. I think this palette from Lorac is more suited for some fairer skin tones than the Naked palette if you're looking particularly for gold shades.

Overall, this is a nice addition to a collection but if you're looking for a first palette Id go with the Lorac Pro Original or even Urban Decay Naked.
summary: Works well as an additional palette, some beautiful gold shades. Best with primer.

reviewText:
I have a lot of eyeshadow pallets, but none of them really offer a true gold option. Most were too pink on the rose-gold side, and pink does not work for my skin tone. Seeing as you tubers and beauty bloggers are touting the beauty cry, "go for the gold this summer!", I was in a search for options that were friendlier to my face.
Enter Lorac Unzipped Gold. This is truly the midas touch of eyeshadow for me right now. It's neutral enough for my pink edged tone, and none give me the albino rabbit eye look that I've unwittingly worn on my fair face.
The texture is blendable, smooth and even. I didn't get any chalky finishes, or patchy applications. All 10 were soft, but fall out was minimal for me. I love the deep brown tones that work and blend perfectly with the pale yellow hued golds.
To note, when they say shimmer, because of the nature of golds in general, these look to be a little more on the metallic side when applied. But, I personally love it. I have to admit I reach for this palette most often right now. It's easy to do a simple eye for work, and then add more oomph when I get home, or go out.
These can be applied wet for more drama, though I don't typically use them that way. But, I haven't had any changes in texture on the powders I've gotten damp.
I've always worn them over primer, and the lorac primer is excellent. I get all day wear, which for me is a full 8 hours with zero fade.
The price seems steep, but it's a little less than other going palettes, and well worth it from the size and quality. The mirror is also generously sized and usable. I am not disappointed and will be checking out Lorac for more options!

Although mineral foundations have their appeal, I have usually opted for cream or liquid foundations. They offer a greater variety of colors, provide greater coverage and last longer. In cold weather my skin tends to get dry and few powders offer sufficient moisture.  However when the warmer weather comes around, I like to go with something lighter. This foundation by Scott Vincent Borba is unique both in formulation and application. The compact contains a cream, one side of which is tan pigment and the other is white. Among other fairly standard ingredients like mica, zinc stearate and silica it also contains vitamins A, C and E, antioxidants including cherry root extracts, camu camu, arnica, hyaluronic acid and diamond powder. It is SPF 29. The compact rotates, allowing you to ground the solid into a powder which is then applied with the included "foundation/micro-exfoliation tool.

As with any powder there is a bit of a mess and some fall off. However, it did apply easily and left my skin feeling velvety, smooth and pleasingly moist. It felt light on. I would describe the appearance as diffuse rather than opaque. It definitely softened the appearance of  minor flaws and pores although it did not eliminate them. I used it on both bare skin as well as with primer and there was no significant difference. It did seem to last a full workday and I did not have to reapply. I am on the lighter end of the fair/light spectrum and found the color just a tad too dark for my complexion although it will be fine once I get a little sun. The accompanying brush is quite lovely. The brushes are soft and secure. I do think that terming it a "micro exfoliation tool" is a bit of a gimmick. Technically a tissue or a washcloth can serve as a micro exfoliation tool. The angled bristles make it ideal for applying contour as well as the foundation. It felt nice in my hands and was a good size and weight. I do like the SPF value however if you spend much time outdoors I would not skip regular sun screen.

This set also came with a foundation treatment mask which can be used prior to application of the foundation. The product is made in the United States. The package warns one to avoid contact with eyes or broken or damaged skin.

Overall I liked this foundation and love the brush. It is not drying and imparts a soft, natural look. I think it would work well for woman combating the early signs of aging. I was pleasantly surprised by both the look and feel. It is perfect for those with normal to oily skin. I think people with dry skin might benefit from it also if they use both moisturizer and primer. It is very gentle and soothing, an ideal alternative to liquids and creams.
summary: Skin That Looks Good and Feels Good

reviewText:
Ive used both the Mary Kay and Bare Minerals version of this powdered foundation.  This is different in two ways.  The first is that you twist the compact to grate the foundation to provide you with the powder, versus turning the container over and giving it a shake to get powder to a place you can where you can pick it up.  The other is that instead of one solid color, part of it is white and its up to you to mix together completely or not.  I really like that aspect as our faces aren't naturally one color, so putting on a foundation with more than one color that isn't perfectly mixed actually looks less like you're wearing something while covering up minor imperfections.

This does a great job with covering up fine lines and discolorations, and gives my complexion a smoother look without my normal reddened blotchiness.  I haven't needed to reapply as the day goes on.

The brush is a short bristle compared to others Ive used for this type of foundation product, although its incredibly soft and narrow.  That does allow for more refined placement if you're going lighter or darker in a specific area.  I cant begin to understand how/why its described as something that exfoliates, though.  I expect your washcloth would do a better job for that.
summary: Two colors can give you a more natural look

reviewText:
I have been using mineral make-up for many years now, and I am really pleased with the results from this Scott-Vincent Borba product. The "01 Fair/Light" color matched my skin tone perfectly. The ability to use less or more of the white powder should enable this make-up to accommodate the skin tone of most women. and yield a pretty close match. Like all powder-based mineral make-up, the coverage is not as full as what you would get from a liquid or cream foundation. However, for daytime use, this make-up has the perfect amount of coverage, not too heavy and not too light. I was also able to go a full 10 hour day without having to re-apply or even touch-up this makeup.

While the cost of this make-up greatly exceeds the local drugstore brands and offerings, it has many pluses which most women will appreciate. The SPF factor of 29, the anti-wrinkle properties, and that fantastic brush, just to name a few. Since I do not wear make-up everyday, I can afford to spend a bit more on a quality product since it will last me longer, and probably will end up costing about the same as the drugstore brands if I used them daily. Well, that is my justification, anyway. Let's just say this is fantastic mineral makeup which leaves your face smooth and silky, and maybe, you, too, will decide that you are worth the best.

I love makeup. I wear it every day, and am always trying new products. I even subscribe to a number of monthly "beauty boxes."  Was eager to try this foundation!

To use, you simply give the (tiny! mirrorless!) compact a twist and it "shaves" some foundation off for you. One side gives you the color, the other side gives you white. You then swirl them together, and apply.

I have pretty fair skin, and found that this was a tad too light for my complexion. I recommend this shade (01) only to those who are the lightest of the light.  It went on easily, but looked the same as any other mineral powder, in that it *accentuated* every pore and fine line on my face. I then tried it on my teenage daughter, who has perfectly smooth skin and it looked a lot better. This is basically what I've found with other mineral foundations--they work the best the better your skin is to begin with.

Now on to the brush--it is very small, with short, densely packed (not fluffy) bristles.  They are super-soft, so I have no idea how they are supposed to "micro-exfoliate" your skin. Doesn't make a bit of sense. It applies the foundation really well.  You can also use it with liquid foundation.

As a bonus, you get a tiny tablet that is supposed to be a facial mask, with bizarre instructions on how to use. Couldn't figure out what to do with it, nor do I even know what is in it.

Overall, I don't recommend this foundation in particular.  There are so many similar products on the market, that I don't see the need to spend nearly $80 on this one.

Scott-Vincent Borba's Anti-Fatigue Skin Care/SPF 29 Mineral Foundation is an interesting innovation.  The packaging, as far as I know, is unique.  And the accompanying 'foundation tool' is the best makeup brush I've ever encountered.  Frankly for the price, they should both be stellar.  And they come close.

The compact allows the user to twist, grind, and mix a fresh batch of mineral foundation each time.  The resultant mix (which looks more like a powder than a cream), is both light and moist.  And there's some user control over the shade achieved.

It's then applied with the truly luxurious brush.  The texture of the brush is extremely soft and flexible, yet it holds the powdery mix and delivers it exactly as desired.

The foundation is light in feel, long wearing, and according to my spouse, brighter than my usual Lancome.  It doesn't do much for my wrinkles and other imperfections, but works well over my usual cover-up.

It's first rate and the brush is fantastic; I like both.  It's fun to try and works well.  Potential buyers may want to try an internet price check.
summary: First rate mineral foundation, fantastic brush, but pricey....

reviewText:
I don't wear a lot of makeup and when I do, I prefer to keep it light and natural looking. I've been using Bare Minerals for a couple of years but haven't even been happy with that for a while. I don't even know if I can tell you how thrilled I am with this Scott-Vincent Borba product. I only hope I can find it for less when I run out.

The "brush" can't even be called a brush - it's like a pouf of velvet on a stick. It's ruined me because all my other brushes feel like horsehair now. It's just the right texture for applying the powder which is slightly moist - it doesn't absorb the makeup or lose it in the bristles, just holds it on the ends.

I have fairly light skin so I needed to mix nearly all of the white in with the beige powder to get the right color but I did end up with what I think was a perfect match. Coverage was much better than Bare Minerals, slightly less than liquid foundation. I didn't notice any anti-aging effects or impact on the appearance of my tiny wrinkles but I have a small scar that I usually see through other makeup that almost vanished and this powder did a particularly good job of evening out some of my blotchy red spots. It blended easier than any makeup I've ever used and thanks to the fabulous brush, it was no problem to ensure there was no dreaded foundation line around my face and neck. I ended up with a dewy finish - there was no powdery residue, just a bit of soft color that looked very natural.

Very good coverage lasted through the morning, I needed some touchups by lunchtime and the powder had worn off by early evening but I'd still consider that fairly good performance for a powder foundation like this. What was left washed off easily with my regular cleanser. I have sensitive skin and this didn't give me any problems at all - I didn't have any acne breakouts either.

Since I don't wear it much, it's not often that I find a makeup that I'd pay a serious amount of money for but I'd do it for this.

$78 for a foundation and brush?  Crazy, right?  Well, maybe not so crazy.  When I opened the brush, I thought, "What, this tiny thing?  It's going to take forever to put my foundation on."  But the foundation went on really quickly, almost as quickly as my big puffy brush I usually use with loose powder.  I buy high-quality brushes as a rule, but I love this brush even more than my normal one and will be using it from now on.

I am surprised that this foundation is described as a cream, as it looks and applies like a powder.  I tried it on bare skin, on half my face.  My teenaged daughter immediately pointed to that side of my face and said, "That side looks better.  And younger."  I was surprised at the younger comment.  Then she asked if that was the side that has the makeup on.  It is that light, that you can hardly tell that you are wearing it other than that you look better.  I put some on her and she loved it too.  She has extremely sensitive skin and so far has had no issues.  I agreed to let her wear it--on special occasions.  Hey, age has its privileges, like indulging in top-of-the-line makeup.

Like portable loose powder makeups, you open the compact to reveal a thin second cover with holes in it.  However, you don't twist it, put the lid back on, shake it and remove the lid to get to the powder, as with other compacts I have owned.  You merely twist it, and similar to a clicking lip gloss applicator, a small amount of powder is deposited on top.  Kinda cool.  One side is light and the other is dark.  The first time I applied it I swirled it all together and was surprised when it turned out a little too light, even for my fair skin.  It is very easy to custom blend right there in the container, getting the proper amount of light and dark to customize to your skin tone.  Whatever is left over (light or dark) is perfect for highlighting or contouring.  This sounds complicated but it really is not and takes only a fraction of a second of thought and no talent.

I was surprised at just how much I like this powder and will continue to buy it.  Hopefully by the time I run out, Amazon will sell the powder separately from the brush

My wife absolutely loved trying this product! Although I don't know how these things price at the store my wife does. When she saw it she said "high end product" and immediately grabbed it and her and my daughter went to the bathroom to test this product. She said it applied to her skin near perfectly-had a very soft touch and lasted all day long for her. She made a point of mentioning the brush which was real nice and not cheap like some of these products are.  The compact itself rotates which is a good thing I was told.

Would recommend!

Okay, I'll begin by saying that I actually like this product a lot, but I will add that I have been a fan of mineral makeup for about 8 years now.

The Scott-Vincent compact is sleek and I love the turn dial on this that allows you to grind and mix a fresh batch each time. I also can control the color a little better, I can tap out some of the white and that gives me a little darker color which is perfect as I need a shade between light and medium just to deal with the naturally dark eye circles I was cursed with. It says that it is a cream but it really is powdery, but stays. I'm a fan of mineral make up because yes, it does make your skin look smoother, does not have the heavy and drying feeling of wet foundations. And of course it it SPF 29 (but quite frankly all mineral makeups offer a degree of SPF protection.)

Tho' I have to admit, what really sets this product apart is the exfoliating application brush! What an amazing and beautifully made little brush, this feels like Heaven on my skin. I could just stroke this on my face all day and its like this amazing little message. When I went to Youtube to check out videos on the product (I was hoping to find out about using the mask, I will get to that next.) I found an HSN advert and was a bit dismayed to see the foundation retail for $24.00 dollars (with free shipping) of course halfway thru the video Scott-Vincent intros the Brush and it retailed separately for $25.00 (still not thrilled that Amazon retails this set at $78.00 when HSN sold them for $49.00 - but hey that's why we browse and compare, right?) But I will say that, YES! I would be perfectly happy to pay $25.00 for this Brush alone, it is quite simply the BEST makeup brush I have ever seen/used in my life and it cleans up beautifully. LOVE this Brush.

Now on to the weird part.

Along with the compact and brush came a mask. This is frankly the oddest gimmick I have as yet to encounter with foundation. The instructions included read as follows: "To prep skin for even quicker skincare benefits, apply mask prior to first use. 1.) Brush white skin care side of foundation treatment on face. 2. Place moistened mask onto face for 5 minutes to enhance nutrient absorption into epidermis. 3. Use both sides of foundation treatment going forward.

Ummm - okay. This is why I went to Youtube and I did not find a video offering instruction on this part of the "application". So I winged it by following the above directions. It was odd at best, Since it is only really a one-time use deal there is not a whole lot of purpose for it. Second, maybe if I lived somewhere with some humidity it might not have been a big deal. But I am in Wyoming which is an arid desert state, my skin dried quickly and felt very dry and tight so I washed my face and tried again with my usual three step routine: 1. wash face. 2. apply moisurizer and 3. apply foundation. This was much more satisfactory.

While I might not agree entirely with the price and one of its extras, I do enjoy the foundation and I LOVE this Brush!
summary: Great Product but the Brush is where the real magic is at!

reviewText:
Have you started to get ready the morning after a late night and faced bruise-like under-eye circles. In order to avoid scaring people, you reach for the concealer. But perhaps you used a liquid concealer and found that you had to build up layers, work around fine lines, and still go back with a swab to correct your work and try to get a convincingly refreshed look. Or you've gone with a powder and spent far too long dabbing away at the circles, stuck between dark shadows and a powdery look?

This Concealer Kit has a thick, silky cream with natural-looking full coverage. Compared with liquids and powders, it provides better coverage with much less effort. It's light, though, so once you've made your corrections, you won't feel it.

The special sponge applicator has a handle, so it's comfortable and gives greater precision. The sponge on the handle has a teardrop shape that allows accurate application in small spaces.

Apply it in the morning and expect to touch it up for evening.
summary: EXcellent Coverage and a Natural Look

reviewText:
Method of application is key in how effective this concealer will be for you. The fantastic teardrop applicator is your friend - use it! The instructions say to put some concealer on your wrist first and use that as a palette for applying to your face but I do not like that method as it wastes product. I use the product straight from the jar.

I used the "medium" concealer which is the best option for me out of the 3 colors possible. The product is thick and stays on all day. It does cover blemishes if applied correctly. With the applicator, I dab and blot the concealer on my skin and then blend gently. A little goes a long way.  I don't use foundation just powder to set it.

I do wish that it came in more shades.
summary: Thick and stays on all day

reviewText: I didn't expect this product to be so awesome. Under eye concealers often make me look weird, even if they are the right color and match my skin. They can be cakey and hard to apply evenly. Enter the wonderful Scott-Vincent Borba brush that comes with this creamy concealer.  The brush is amazing and the cone shape enables you to really get in the corner of your eye and smooth the concealer in a way that looks natural. It is great for uneven pigmentation also and the brush gives a light touch.  The concealer itself is a great consistency, goes on well, blends into skin and makes me look so much more awake. I love this product and use it every day...even before I run.
summary: This is a super duper light concealer that everyone should own

reviewText:
This is an effective concealer.

In truth, have not experienced any of the extremely dramatic improvements that people
report.  Everyone detects imperfections in their skin, so a response to any skin care
product is going to be very individualized, and highly personal-right?

The ingredients are fairly "natural" and include shea butter, apricot,  cocoa and many
minerals.

To avoid any drying effect, moisturizer is applied on the cleansed skin first, then the
concealer.

Overall, I like this product. Although it comes with an applicator,  the "tap-tap-tap"
gently with your fingertip approach seems to work better.  More control that way and
also use far less than the applicator-full.  This method allows a nice and subtle lighter
application of the make-up.

PROS:

- No irritation. Does not upset sensitive skin

- Easy to apply

- medium color works well

- long-lasting

- no heavy scent

--no heavy "caking"

CONS:

-the major one is expense. $65 is very high for such a small amount.

At this point, still prefer Clinique Line Smoothing Concealer Light for Women.  Price $22
vs. $65 and results are good. Applicator has a light spongy-ness to it which allows fine
control.

RATING:

5: overall product

3: high cost

NET: 4.5, (not a choice) so 4 here.
summary: NICE PRODUCT. GOOD THINGS DO COME IN SMALL PACKAGES.

reviewText: Nice product.  Lighter than I was expecting for medium.  I am pretty fair and this worked pretty well without looking like wrong shade.  Probably would have worked better for dark circles if had correct lighter shade, but I did like the more sheer cover of this that didn't look like I was wearing googles.  Brush is nice as well.

As a mother of an infant I have permanent dark circles under my eyes. When I had the opportunity to try this concealer I jumped at the chance. Unfortunately, it is too light/sheer to cover my dark circles. It works well for highlighting and covering red blemishes. The tool is phenomenal and works great even with my cheap concealer that does a better job covering dark circles. Lastly, if you are trying to avoid them this product is not paraben free.
summary: You can still see my dark circles

reviewText:
I decided to try out this Anti-Fatigue Concealer Kit because Ive reached a place in life where I still have quite good facial skin for a 70+ year old with the exception of the eye bags.  Seems that in the last few years the bags have turned into steamer trunks.  I tried other products but end up looking like an owl  especially in photographs where the product seems to glow.

Ill admit that the Scott-Vincent Borba line is a bit spendy for my budget but in the end you get what you pay for.  In this case I can truthfully say that my eye bags are hardly noticeable and I look considerably better (and younger).  The trick seems to be the applicator which allows you to blend the product professionally at home.  I never get that cake-like gunk that I get with other brands.

I found the product is long lasting and has not upset my sensitive skin whatsoever.  To me this is a blessing.  I confess that this is probably not a product Id wear every day but for those special events where I want to look my best this concealer for the eyes is the answer to an old ladys plea.
summary: My eye bags had turned into steamer trunks and this product really did help - a lot.

reviewText: I liked this concealer but not as well as the one I was currently using. This one is extremely sheer which is good on most areas especially on age 50 plus skin and it does not look heavy or leave your more wrinkled areas more noticeable. I always mist with witch hazel then use my sunscreen moisturizer with a drop of Moroccan oil and then concealer before using a highlighter. This has a nice moist consistancy on it's own and goes on very silky with the excellent applicator which I really liked. The medium is lighter then most other mediums I have used, almost too light for me but not bad, I would have liked it a touch darker and I am somewhat fair to med..The reason I like my Benefit brand Boing medium concealer better, it covers way better if you have scars to cover, this one was too sheer for those areas and did not cover as well. Benefit Boing also covers dark circles much better then this product. For half the cost I will stay with Benefit brand but this was a close second just not as good for my particular needs.
summary: Good but not my favorite for dark circles and scars

reviewText: No study has shown conclusively that parabens cause cancer, or that they are harmful in any way, but studies have concluded that parabens can act similarly to estrogen, and estrogenic activity in the body has been associated with certain forms of breast cancer. Some may say that it's an over reaction, but in a family with members that have a genetic predisposition to breast cancer and / or have fought breast cancer, parabens are avoided. It is entirely my mistake that I ordered Scott-Vincent Borba Anti-Fatigue Concealer Kit; I missed that it contains methylparaben. Therefore, it wouldn't be fair to give Scott-Vincent Borba Anti-Fatigue Concealer Kit a negative rating because of I'm paranoid. If you have no qualms about parabens, this looks like a product worth trying. If you too have paraben paranoia, I can suggest NARS Radiant Creamy Concealer, Vanilla (more colors than Vanilla are available).
summary: Don't Judge From This Review, I Couldn't Use It

reviewText:
I admit that I don't tend to spend a lot of money on my makeup. So I was wondering - at $65 is this concealer worth it? And I can honestly say, yes it is.

I loved everything about this concealer. It's creamy with just the right consistency - not too thick or thin. It feels very light on my skin. The applicator is perfect. Instead of having to use my fingers to apply concealer, this tool makes it easy to apply without tugging at the skin around my eyes.

I've always had dark circles under my eyes and this concealer does a great job hiding those circles and it lasts all day.

I have fair sensitive skin and tend to go with a lighter shade of concealer, but I have this concealer in the medium shade and it's the perfect color.

$65 is a lot of money, but you don't need to use a lot of this makeup and it will last a long time. Definitely well worth it.

The best thing about this set is the tool.  That's why this product is a 5 star rating.  It really makes the cost worthwhile.  Using your finger to put on under eye cover up can put undue pressure on your under eye are.  This tool is lightweight and angled to give the best coverage.  The make up itself lasts above average amount of time. You get a lot of it in the jar, but it doesn't always last the whole day.  You may need a touch up. I've tried a lot of under eye concealers, and I've found that a need for touch up to always be the case which is why I said above average. I usually have fair skin but my face has tanned a lot this summer so medium is a good compromise.  I will need lighter in the winter.  When deciding color for under your eyes, you can go a bit darker than the skin tone on your face (but not too much darker). I'm not sure about the anti wrinkle part, but I think it's working.  I use a Lancome product during the day and another at night under my eyes so it's difficult to compare the anti wrinkle aspect. However, I do think my under eyes are a bit lighter so I don't have as dark of circles since starting this product.  I think this product has a lot to offer, and recommend it.
summary: Triple the benefit - coverage, tool, and under eye protection

reviewText:
I usually have problems finding the right coverage with concealers. Often they are either too thick and cakey or too thin a consistency that kind of just vanishes throughout the day.  This CC cream has just the right medium consistency that is just thick enough to stay, yet thin enough to be easy to apply and blend.  I received the medium shade and it is perfect for the summertime when I have a bit more colour to my face.

The best part about this CC cream is that it comes with an almond-spaced brush.  This brush is the perfect size to apply and blend. The sharp point helps move the product right to the corner of the eyes.
summary: Good, long lasting coverage. Excellent sponge-brush applicator

reviewText:
This product is slightly darker than most of the 01 foundations and concealers I own, especially the ones I tend to use in winter.  I am usually a bit darker in the summer, and I suspect this color will work just fine then.

It goes on well, and seems to wear well.  It blends well.  It removes well.  It's a good concealer.  It has a nice consistency.

I would give it five stars if it were slightly lighter.
summary: 01 was a little dark for me

reviewText: An excellent concealer, this goes on smoothly and stays on well.  I only had to reapply it after getting a little sweaty.  It has a very light scent to it, barely noticeable really.  It doesn't feel heavy and after a few minutes I didn't even feel it there any more.  I have red cheeks from rosacea and this covered it very nicely.  I am quite pleased and would recommend it!

The texture is smooth and lightweight. Very easy to apply onto the skin, and it dries up and sets quickly once applied. It doesn't crease up in the lines. It also looks very natural and blendable. The only issue for me personally is that it is not pigmented enough to offer enough coverage for dark circles under eye.
summary: Natural looking but not enough coverage

reviewText: I was excited to try a CC cream but am always disappointed by concealers since my skin is very light.  I was extremely pleased at how this product concealed my dark rings under my eyes and how well it blended.  It would have been fine applied with fingers but I used a concealer brush to make sure it was extra blended.  It didn't feel heavy and I didn't even notice the extra layer on my face throughout the day.  I will definitely use this product for blemishes and dark circles under my eyes again!!!!

Gave this to my wife to try out as she has fair skin and has a difficult time finding things that match.  It turned out pretty good for her and the color did a good job of blending with her skin color.  She said it was pretty nice and that it went on as expected.  It lasted for a while and it did cover the dark circles under her eyes.  Regardless, this is a good product and she would use it again.

The first thing I do after washing my face is to apply a moisturizer because my skin is on the dry side. I haven't used a concealer in a while, but there have been times that I have wished that I had one on hand. I was quite pleased to have the opportunity to try the Scott-Vincent Borba Anti-Fatigue Invisible Corrective Concealer Anti-Wrinkle CC Cream.

My first impression on seeing the packaging was, wow! It looked like it contained a jar the size of my Bare Minerals Foundation. That seemed like a lot of product. I soon realized that I was mistaken as the jar takes up only about .75% of the box. The box is made with interior walls that hold the smaller jar in place. It disappoints me when I buy a package that seems to hold a good amount, and find that in fact, there is mostly air or excess packaging. I don't see the point of having the much larger package. The jar is attractive, but the lid is nearly as big as the jar itself, which I also think leads the purchaser to "see" a larger amount than is actually provided. This is intentional and very common, no matter what we are purchasing. A lot of time and effort is put forth to make us feel we are getting more than we actually get. The jar is pleasing to look at however, and the lid fits snugly. I keep my cosmetics in a small basket and I have no concern about the lid coming off when this is tossed in with the rest.

The product itself is good in my opinion. When I first touched it, it did feel a little clay like, and was not the soft creamy texture I expected. I used the handle tip of a small brush to take a small amount of the product out of the jar, and placed it on the back of my hand, because I prefer to apply and blend make up with my fingers. When applied, the Scott-Vincent Borba Anti-Fatigue Invisible Corrective Concealer Anti-Wrinkle CC Cream is much softer and lighter than I expected it to be. I use a dusting of foundation over it and it works great. Now, I don't have very dark circles under my eyes, but it is a little darker there than I would like. It also covered a small blemish that popped up recently. Bottom line is that I do like this product, and for me, it does a nice job. I am very pleased. My eye area does look brighter when I use this.

Very soft and a little goes a long way.  Applies smoothly and evenly on the skin, no heavy blotches especially around the lower lip of the eye.  I didn't have to reapply another layer to even out the coolor.  So easy to use and helped with minimising those bags under the eyes, until you caught up with your sleep.  My complexion is semi olive tone and this worked, but the next shade up works the best.  Held up for full work day, no humidity Under cold weather conditions.
summary: One application and the job is done..nice and light.

reviewText:
It is just OK, it covers blemishes well for me using a cosmetic brush but it is much too stiff and hard for under the eye. You are not to pull or tug at the eye area because of the delicate skin there but if you use this that is what I would have to do. It is very stiff and doesn't play nice in the eye area. It is not exactly for fair skin either. Under my eyes my skin is really light and I can see this standing out with the little I did apply, for the rest of my face it was fine though. I can't understand why they would make it so thick and so stiff like this if it is to be for the eyes?
I would not recommend this product for the eye area but for blemishes it is fine.

You get a fairly ample container of concealer. I found that it is not greasy but then again not all that 'spreadable'. It covered spots okay, but I mostly use concealer under my eyes and I had problems getting it to blend easily in those areas. I was disappointed. High expectations due to the price of the product. A bit on the pricey side. I had to add a little lotion when I had put the cream on under my eye area to finally get it to blend.
All and all - not seeing anything special about this product.
summary: A little disappointed - good for spots, not so much for under eye area.

reviewText:
I used this product as an under eye concealer and eyelid primer.

First, let me cite the PROS:  this CC Cream is a nice color that brightens the skin.  It conceals dark circles under the eye really well.  There is a fragrance, but it's not unpleasant.  The product lasts all day.  As a primer, it keeps shadow and liner looking beautiful all day.

Now for the CONS:  the product should come with an applicator.  The pot is too small and deep to get your finger into if you have long nails.  Fortunately, I already had a brush I could use which was a good thing since I was so excited to try the product.  The CC Cream doesn't glide on smoothly and seems to accentuate wrinkles.

Considering the price, I'll probably stick with my regular concealer.

As a corrective concealer this product does work.  However the consistency of the product was too thick.  I have European Caucasian skin and I am at the half century mark.  I thought this would be a good product for me.  However, I think the product is old and lost some of its moisture.  I also have been told not to stretch my skin too much as it will cause wrinkles.  Applying this product, well, I had to really rub and stretch and pull my skin, a lot.  I was like clay or old glue.  I have used thick concealers before and they always have an oil or something to make them apply easily.

Another problem I had was the packaging.  Women my age are the primary target for this product.  However, I couldn't read the packaging.  This product is made in the USA so why not omit the French and put the information on the package & jar in English with larger lettering?

I got this product free for a honest review, but I don't see paying $35 for a jar of clay.  I really didn't see any "Anti-Wrinkle" qualities in this product.  Yes, it does get rid of dark circles, but that is more because it was soooo thick.  I didn't hate it, but I didn't like it either.

The Scott-Vincent Borba Anti-Fatigue Invisible Corrective Concealer Anti-Wrinkle CC Cream performed much better than I could have imagined. It went on easily (I used a foam applicator). It has more of a powdery instead of a creamy texture and a little goes a long way! I was very impressed with how it concealed and didn't look like I used a trowel to cover up my dark circles the way some of the others do. I was pleased with how well it concealed my dark circles throughout the day. It also works on blemishes, dark spots and redness - just dab a little on under your makeup and they're gone! My imperfections are gone and without the dark circles, I feel like I look younger. I also don't notice the wrinkles as much. It is gentle on the skin and didn't irritate.

I'm very impressed with the quality, coverage and the tiny amount that is needed when using the Scott-Vincent Borba Anti-Fatigue Invisible Corrective Concealer Anti-Wrinkle CC Cream. This container will last a long time and is definitely one I will be replacing when I run out.
summary: Conceals well and I didn't need to use much at all!

reviewText:
I was very interested to try this thirty-five-dollar concealer as I've been searching for one that met my needs. I'm disappointed by this one, unfortunately, although I had wanted to like it.

This is a generous pot of concealer, it will last a long time for the average user. The texture of the product is what got me, in that it does not apply well to under eye areas--despite the claim that this product is great for under eye areas and reduces winkles in said areas. I tried this concealer out in a variety of ways, using fingers to apply as well as a concealing brush. Note that the product suggests using a brush to dole out the product onto the back of your wrist, then from there to apply with the brush to your face.

I will say, I was pleased with how this product covered blemishes, quite well, when using a concealer brush. As for the undereye area? Which is big for me, as I'm a fair skinned lady of Swedish descent who has dark circles to cover, this product did not meet my expectations. It was hard and too dry to apply easily to the under-eye area well. Worse, I'd apply then move onto my foundation (which is quality product, Vincent Longo's Water Canvas Foundation) and this concealer would then gum up under my eyes. It didn't "play well with others" so to speak. When looking close up in the mirror, this product was OBVIOUS and easily seen on the eye. It didn't crease, but it "gunked up" on top of my skin and that I just cannot stand.

Also, it has a warm, yellowish tone, which is great if you're Asian but for a fair skinned Swede (with pink skin tones, not warm) it was just awful. This is what I can't understand about the beauty industry: every "fair" skinned product is made for warm skinned people. Meanwhile, there is a world of cool toned, Scandinavian skinned people out there needing COOL TONED products that the beauty industry is completely ignoring.

The texture was a miss as well, this product was just hard to apply well in that it is a hard creamy yet chalky consistency, like what you might find in a concealer stick that you twist to use. You can scoop it up on a brush, but as soon as it hits skin and air it starts drying and becomes difficult to smooth, I felt like I was smudging it onto my skin and this is not a pleasant thing when you're messing with delicate, under-eye skin. I really hate the texture of this concealer, overall.

However, I must say it did do well in covering up small red blemishes when applied with a small concealer brush. Unfortunately for them, but fortunately for ME, I do not get small red blemishes very often. So this product is very unhelpful overall, in my opinion. They would do well to 1) make a shade for cool toned fair skin and 2) create a product that is easily applied, this thick cream isn't cutting it and does not work--especially considering the claims they make for this product being good for the under-eye area as well as good for hiding tired, wrinkled eyes.
summary: OK for blemishes, not a good concealer overall, NOT for fairskinnned

reviewText:
I have mixed feelings on this concealer. My first impression was that it had the consistency of CLAY! Definitely NOT pliable or creamy at all!

I had intended on using my concealer brush but ended up tapping the top of the concealer repeatedly and surprisingly after only about 5 taps, there was a sufficient amount to tap and pat to blend under my eye (one eye) . After tapping it repeatedly I tried to blend it abit for a better finished result. (*It does NOT blend easily at all) but all in all it only took about a minute or 2 to do one undereye area and it is a very dry finish but that is what makes it stay in place and not cake into wrinkles like the more liquid concealers that glide on so easily.

Don't get me wrong, at first I was  sure I did not like it when it went on so oddly compared to other concealers I've used in the past (and I am in my 50's so I've tried a LOT!
After putting it on I applied a mineral foundation that this works very well with, I don't think it would be so great with a liquid foundation but it seems that it was made for a mineral one as Scott-Vincent Borba also sells a mineral foundation.

So I was pleasantly surprised that it does diminish my fine under eye lines as it does not settle and weep into them as the day wears on. The coverage is decent, I've never found one that eliminated them entirely and this does as good a job as most 've used in the past, as far as the dark circles go.

All in all if you are older like me this is worth a go IF you are  using a mineral foundation and want a concealer that stays put and doesn't melt into the wrinkle creases making them look worse! I got the light 01 fair/light shade, I wish I had gotten the next darker shade as I read that it had a bit more yellow in it and I have that hue in my skin and it might have looked even better.
summary: At first I thought I was going to HATE it but I am pleasantly surprised

reviewText:
I have used concealer ever since High School and that was many years ago.  I have dark circles under my eyes that are simply genetic.  My brother has them too and we don't know why we have them since neither of our parents or grandparents had dark circles under their eyes.  But, nonetheless, if I don't wear a concealer I really don't want to be seen by anyone since I look like a panda bear without it.

I love this concealer, if it wasn't so expensive I would use it all the time.  I have used all sorts of different brands of concealer sticks and creams over the years and all seem to work o.k. but none as well as the Scott-Vincent Borba concealer.  The main difference is this concealer lasts a long time before those tiny creases start to show in the inside corners of my eyes.  All the other concealers showed the creases in practically no time and I am always smoothing them out. And I really like that the S-V B stays very smooth.  Also, the color blended in perfectly with my complexion which is medium pale.  I was very pleased to see only the slightest hint of the dark circles lurking below my eyes.  They are nicely hidden and for all practical purposes, non-existent while I wear the concealer.  I like that a lot.  I just wish I could afford this stuff  - I would buy a case of it.....A LIFETIME SUPPLY would make me very happy.

For those of you who have slightly dark circles or just temporary circles......I'm happy for you.  But for those poor souls who managed to get doled a serious set of permanent dark under-eye circles, this stuff is awesome!  I dread the day use my last dab of it.
summary: This is the Best Concealer I've Ever Used

reviewText:
I am really happy with this concealer.  I found the fair/light shade perfect for my very fair freckled skin.  The concealer does not come with an applicator, is quite thick and creamy, and (in my opinion) smells really nice.

To apply the concealer, I used a smallish makeup brush and then blended it with my finger.  This works really well for small areas, like the dreaded pimple, and larger areas like under the eye or my poor nose, which is always slightly red thanks to too many sunburns as a kid.  The concealer blends easily and looks very natural.  It's pricey, but a little goes a long way so the product should last a good long while.

Thick, creamy and covers without using very much. I don't want to feel as if there is a lot of product on my face; so, having a little go a long way is not only good for thrift but for how it actually feels.

The coverage is excellent for little discolorations, scars, or simply after not sleeping enough.

The color seemed like a true light to me, but not a super light.

No scent that I could discern. Another plus.

The product is on the thick side and not easy to apply, but the color was correct, I had fair.
It conceals well, dries fast, was great at covering pimples and the mustache area.
The tone was even after it was applied.
You only need a little bit.
It blends well with foundation and powder. I started with a clean face.

Recommended
summary: Not easy to apply, but worth the effort

reviewText:
I have an immense collection of fragrances, with a particular interest in sporty scents such as Lacoste Essential and Nautica Voyage, and I've been very pleased with Burberry Brit Splash for the past week or so.  It's a nice, watery, summer, fresh smell that doesn't scream frat boy or Axe cheap.  It's a fine blend of scents that also doesn't overpower anyone within nasal range as many fragrances, such as anything by Ed Hardy or Axe, wreak of cheap ingredients and overpowering musk that can only be described as machismo.

I am very satisfied with how Burberry Brit Splash smelled on me and the pleasant reactions of those around me and will continue to wear it on the appropriate occasions.

If you're looking for a light, clean scent, Burberry is definitely a must try. The bottle is very easy to look at, nice design with the spray atomizer easy to use. Just a small amount lasts for hours.  It has a woodsy, vanilla, clean scent (to me) but I'm sure it will smell a bit different on anyone as it works with your own body.  My son wore it to work and had many, many people tell him how good he smelled.  Not his normal scent but one he would definitely purchase in the future.

Got this for my husband who is really picky about his fragrance. He loves Polo Blue by Ralph Lauren for Men, Eau De Toilette Natural Spray and is really unwilling to try anything else. With his birthday coming up I figured I'd get him something that he can change up and it was a hit. He loves the light not overpowering scent and so do I. It's great for both day and night. If the man in your life like the stronger stuff then you might want to get something different. This is definitely not your Axe deodorant spray but for a real man's man.
summary: It's great for both day and night

reviewText:
It is always difficult to review colognes and aftershaves as scent is a very subjective thing, and trying to describe it with words is like trying to describe a color.  What I can say about this Burberry Brit Splash is it has a very pleasant, light scent that is not overpowering like so many fragrances people often wear these days.  I agree with another reviewer who referred to it as clean-smelling, but this is not the kind of scent you might find on bath soap or deodorant.  It is much more refined than that. This one is intimate and intended to be smelled by someone nearby.  It is the ideal scent for a man to wear while out on the town with his favorite lady and for more romantic moments.  My wife seemed to really like the scent after I sprayed some on.

There was no price listed for this product at the time I received it for review, so I cannot comment about cost and value.  What I can say is the bottle I received was quite generous in size (almost 14 ounces), much larger than I expected, and should last a very long time.  It has an atomizer on the top of he bottle, which allows for very light application.  The bottle is attractive and looks just fine sitting on the edge of my sink.
summary: light, pleasant, intimate scent that is not overpowering

reviewText: The Burberry Brit Splash provides a very nice scent.  I like the smell of the splash and my wife loves the splash.  She generally only likes certain men's cologne products, like CK One, but she really likes the Burberry.  It actually caught me by surprise as she kept taking about how much she likes how it smells.  The Burberry would make a great gift as it comes in nice box and the bottle is nice as well.  I don't like the spray cap and find it hard to take off at times.  Outside of the spray cap the bottle looks good and presents itself well.  I would buy the Burberry again, and I'm sure my wife will make me buy it over other products.  I would even consider giving it as a gift to my dad.

I love the way this smells on my husband!  It does have a fresh clean scent that's perfect for daytime wear, but there's also an undertone of something almost musky about it.  It's actually pretty sensual, but maybe it's because it's my man wearing it.  Burberry is all about the classics and this fragrance delivers that on all levels.

At the time of writing this review, there was no volume or size information available on the page.  For reference, this is a review for the 100 ml (3.3 fl oz) bottle.  The packaging is well designed and the bottle is very attractive (better in person).  This would make a great gift.
summary: This is a light, fresh, and enticing scent that makes my man smell really good.

reviewText:
I put this on and then, like a creeper, stood by my wife really close, leaned in a bunch of times, gave her a bunch of kisses and then when I got no response I actually asked her how I smelled. She said she noticed a soapy, clean scent but thought it was a new deodorant. Not exactly what I was going for with this cologne.

My opinion is that this scent is clean and fresh. It's light and pleasant. It's not overpowering. It's also not very distinctive.

I received this in exchange for my honest review.  In order to assess the value of a review for your own personal buying decision, I think it's important to understand the preferences of the reviewer.  I adore scent.  I favor somewhat pungent natural fragrances with strong notes of rose, cumin, amber, but also some soliflores.  My own personal fragrances tend to come from places like Andy Tauer (Une Rose Chypree), LeLabo (Rose31) and Annick Goutal (Rose Absolue, Eau de Charlotte).  Formy husband I like Serge Lutens Chergui.  So, if you do not share my tastes, what I have to say about Burberry Brit will not be relevant to you.

I found this to be a  generic modern chemical ozonic  rather sweet fragrance, not very easily distinguishable from many that you can sample at Sephora.  To my nose it has more in common with the scent of dryer sheets than the kind of fragrance I am drawn to.  Very little silage, but it is quite long lasting on the skin.  Fragrance is a very personal thing.  For me personally it is not a match.  Neither on me nor my husband.  Your mileage may vary, as they say.
