It is by no means a heavy makeup, but does enough to give the skin a healthy look while staying matte.  It does not hide pores (nothing does!), but I think I can say it minimizes them, blurring their edges,  while other foundations I have tried actually made them look bigger, who wants that?!  The medium color is by no means dark, and I would imagine most people would use that unless you have very pale skin.  I have no noticed any shimmer in it either.

Applying with a good brush is a must, and although it is a bit costly, if it saves me experimenting with other lines, then I am happy to continue using it.  I think it is also important that they DO NOT TEST ON ANIMALS.  The SPF of 29 is also good to have.
summary: Blends great, minimizes pores, stays matte...my go to foundation now!

reviewText: I was a little worried that the medium color would be too dark but it suits my skin coloring just perfectly.  To use this product you flip open the case and then turn the dial which grinds off a combination of the makeup which you then apply with a brush.  What I like  about this product is that although it goes on as a powder it doesn't leave my skin looking like it's been dusted with powder.  The product provides a good amount of lightweight coverage that doesn't leave my skin with that product heavy look or that weighed down feel that you sometimes get with a cream foundation.  I found it to be a little messy though if you twist the dial too much and grind up too much of the product at once, so start with a slight twist on the dial first so you don't grind up too much at once.  I really like this product and it will definitely become a permanent addition to my makeup bag.

I have fair skin, so I am always worried about colors being too dark, but this was a pretty good match.  I like the built in SPF protection.  I felt like the product stayed on my skin nicely, and I did not need to reapply.  I also did not feel like I was wearing a ton of make up, which is important to me.  All in all a great product.
summary: but this was a pretty good match

reviewText: This is the most unique foundation I have ever used. I would say that with one application, coverage is light to medium but it is build-able to full coverage and if done with a good primer underneath, it will not look caked on.  At first, I could not figure out how to use it until I realized that you have to turn the dial to freshly "grate" your minerals. Swirl and mix the 2 components together with your brush and your fresh foundation is ready to beautify your face. I like how it makes me skin feel fresh and clean all day, never greasy. It really does last all day long and I have not felt the need to touch up in the evening.
summary: Medium coverage that is buildable to full

reviewText: I just could not get this make up to work well for me.  The design and idea of what it promises is awesome, but I just didn't notice a difference at all to my skin.  The color was lighter than my olive skintone so I definitely used my mineral based powder over the top of it.  It didn't really cover the blemishes and dark spots, so really, it didn't help my beauty regiment at all.  Another negative is that I had two pimples pop up while using it...and have had a pimple in probably 10 years, and this was the only different in my daily routine.  I was really hoping for something great to happen with this powder and I loved that it has SPF 29 on it, but it just didn't work that well for me.
summary: Not much coverage and I actually got pimples from it!

reviewText: I wasn't sure how this makeup foundation would look on my face. Especially since there's a darker side & a lighter side that you twist to grind up and then mix together before applying to your face. My present foundation just seems to disappear into my pores and it doesn't even look like I have makeup on. So......I was pleasantly surprised that this foundation too looks absolutely natural. I love it!

Not sure Scott-Vincent Borba is worth the hype.  Results for me are similar but better in a much less expensive product.
I prefer not to mix powders before applying.

Maybe my expectations were too high, but I figured that at $250 an ounce this stuff was going to be amazing.  My compact came with a small facial towel and the recommendation to dust my face with just the white powder and then apply the moistened towel for 5 minutes.  I did this as directed and didn't notice any immediate results.

I have now been using the powder for over a week and I will say Im not impressed.  I normally use a loose mineral powder that runs me $65 an ounce and I love the look and coverage it gives.  For me the Scott-Vincent Borba Mineral Foundation didn't improve the look of my skin immediately and besides offering SPF protection I really cant say that this product is worth the cost.  That being said Ill continue to use it until its gone and update my review if I have anything to add.

Perhaps it's a 5 star product, but I am deducting a star for the packaging defect. My compact is missing the grinder, which I'm sure would be helpful. When I opened the compact, the metal dish of makeup flopped out along with a large spring. After looking at it and comparing it to the pics on Amazon, I could see there was no way to grind the powder.

I opted to use my buki brush that I use with Bare Minerals to swirl lightly over the powders. I was able to get great even coverage this way. The product does a nice job covering pores, goes on with a nice matte finish and has a nice soft feel. I would agree with the 8 hour rating.

It is lighter than other medium shades. I would say it's a bit lighter than Bare Minerals fairly medium. It is good for pink and neutral undertones. Yellow and olive undertones would probably not go well with this medium shade.

Well, I felt stupid but then again, maybe someone else did this -- I couldn't figure out how to use the thing! It said grind....huh? It was only after studying the thing a minute or so that I saw the dial. Duh! I think this is lighter than typical medium shades which worked great for me because I was disappointed at first that it was medium because medium is usually too dark for me. This medium is not. It does make my face feel soft and gives a nice matte finish. Other reviewers said you can buy this elsewhere though for less and it comes with a brush other places. If that is the case then find that place and buy it there. You do need a make-up brush. It is a must.
summary: An applicator Brush is a must

reviewText:
Overall, I was really impressed with this foundation. I'm a bit of a foundation junkie, and have gone through my fair share trying to find the perfect one. I'm not sure this is perfect, but it is pretty darn close.

Things I liked:

*For people that use loose mineral makeup, it's always annoying to make sure that the powder doesn't go everywhere, especially if you carry it around with your for touch ups. This product solves the problem by shaving off the product (skincare and foundation), so you can get the amount you need, use it, and not sorry about it making a giant mess. I love it!

*Excellent coverage. While this is not camouflage level, it really does provide excellent coverage without feeling heavy or looking mask-like.

*Mineral makeup has the tendency to make dry skin look flaky and unattractive. I don't know if it's the makeup or the added skincare in this formulation, but it makes my dry skin look great. No flakies!

*Long-lasting! This lasts pretty much an entire day without a need for touch ups, which I find very impressive. I do tend to add a smidgen more midday, but it's probably not necessary for more people.

*No animal testing!!!

Things I don't like:

*Color is lighter than described. This actually worked out for me, as I tend to have light skin and not medium, but I do think it runs light and people need to be careful to order the right color.

*Price! This is crazy expensive for a small amount of foundation. This would definitely be more of a special occasion foundation for me if I decide to purchase. It's just too expensive for everyday use.

---
Overall, I really like this foundation. If it were a bit cheaper, I think this would be my everyday foundation.

It's hard to purchase makeup online.  I had to base color selection for this on other brands I've used in the past that suit my blonde, blue-eyed complexion.  That's anything in the beige/light tan line.  Looking at the Amazon description pictures, medium looked perfect for my complexion color.  What I received is too light, and the packaging makes it impossible to grind different proportions of light/dark ingredients.  It's also impossible to tell when this product is running low because the grinder top is permanently affixed.  I have included what both colors look like when mixed, and it is much lighter than any of the Amazon description pictures, and much too light on my face without being noticeable.

To date Amazon only sells two colors of Scott-Vincent Borba foundation, so I started snooping around online to see if this was available in darker shades.  Yes, it is, but the real surprise is that it is sold much cheaper elsewhere and includes a perfecting brush.  I can't afford to make such costly mistakes.  This is a nice foundation, but it would be nice if all colors were included, as well as accurate blended pictures.
summary: Making A Wrong Color Choice Is An Expensive Mistake

reviewText:
While at first I found the idea of grinding my own makeup each time I used it to be an unnecessary gimmick  I quickly learned to love the smooth flawless finish this makeup gives me.  It looks like I have amazing, natural un-madeup skin when I'm wearing this.

I first tried applying this with a sponge, which caused the sponge to absorb most of the makeup as it is very damp and full of moisture, and not much was left to smooth on my skin.  A foundation brush is a must with this makeup and you can blend and smooth out this makeup into either a very thin coating, or apply it thickly for more coverage.  This is highly blendable and can build up in multiple coats as it dries to give you the exact coverage you want.

The medium shade is perfect for my medium to fair, warm skin color.  I do not find the shade to be one that requires an exact match since this does allow some of my own skin shade to show through, although I put on a fairly thin application.

The grinding of the makeup to mix with the cream can be a little messy but not bad.  Then you swirl the brush through the foundation to mix it up and this does seem to make the  makeup more natural looking.  Also my skin seems to love the treatment aspect of this and I noticed when I washed this off at night that my skin had a healthy glow.  I do love this makeup but not the price.  Also I love the SPF 29.  It's great makeup.

I tend to be in between the shades of light and medium usually, so I opted to try the darker of the 2 shades, as my last mineral foundation that I bought was on the pale side and everyone noticed (Not in a good way!) and commented that my face looked ashen. As I definitely wasn't going for the zombie look this time, as I am new to this brand, I figured if I had to guesstimate I was going to go darker than lighter......darn, Darn, DARN!

Although this medium  shade compact was not as dark as it appears in the picture because after you mix it up it is about 1/2 that shade as the other powder it whitish. However for my skintone it didn't look good as I have a lot of yellow in it and this did not  "self correct" and blend in like some other foundations I have used did.

When I put it on very lightly it is not so noticeable but then I don't get any coverage for my freckles and blotchy patches.
 In hindsight I should have tried the lighter shade , At least by the pictures here on Amazon it appears to have a bit more yellow/warmer tones in it and it may have been just the one that would have been right for me....hope this review helps someone else choose their correct shade. Wish I got the lighter /warmer toned one!

As for the application/ grinding mixing aspect...this was more messy than my bare minerals foundation as the mixing procedure with my brush caused much more to spill out the sides than when I normally load my brush with the bare minerals foundation. But that wouldn't deter me from using this if I had the right shade for my skin. It has no noticeable scent and I had no irritation from using it and I have VERY sensitive skin!
summary: Most importantly, choosing the correct shade if you're in between shades, have a yellowish undertone freckles or melasma

reviewText: This is the first time that I've every tried mineral makeup but I found it very easy to apply and it also looks great on your skin.  I love the fact that you can adjust the color to match your skin zone. It doesn't come with  an applicator though, so if your'e like me and new to mineral makeup you'll have to purchase one before you can use it. I also think that it's a little more pricey than it should be.

I already spend a good amount on makeup because I am white with lots of natural blush with a tinge of European yellow to my skin.  With the rave reviews I had really high hopes for this brand. I was SO disappointed.  The color was super light, it didn't do a good job covering the extra natural blush my face has; it was hard to get it to conceal anything. It was light and airy, which is nice.  But honestly? For this price, go and get yourself COLOR matched at a Lancome counter.  I already use their Dual Finish mineral in Matte Ecru II... and I put each makeup on half of my face. The CHEAPER Lancome totally outdid the other... with my Kabuki brush, I got a nice, light and airy finish with that and it actually MATCHED my face and smoothed out the imperfections.

Now, that being said, if you happen to get this and it matches you perfectly, then great!  It's a nice makeup, and applied it looks very similar to the very high quality Lancome.  But then you have to deal with the "fresh grind" mess. And it's a mess.  I was super annoyed by it sending powder everywhere; and then you have the added step of having to blend it before applying it. I think it's just a fad and people may be "oohed" by it, but it's really just an added step and a pain!

One last thing; there is a little disc in a separate little bag. Don't toss.. it's your face mask!  I didn't know what to do with it, but I moistened it thinking I would rub it on my skin but it unfolded (albeit a bit painfully) to a large mask that fit my face perfectly.  It really refreshed my skin and made it feel lovely and tingly.  But it's one time use only; so that's not so hot.

So my suggestion? If you like this, go for Lancome instead and get color matched; their dual finish is super similar in how it looks on and skips the annoying grinding step.  And I do believe it was actually cheaper as well!!  I use their liquid under sometimes as well, with a touch of the powder on top for when I want more coverage; otherwise I just use the mineral to make me look like I have awesome skin without any makeup on!
summary: Go get color matched at a Lancome counter instead - grinder makes a mess, color matching impossible!

reviewText: this comes with a white tablet that they call a mask that they ask you to use before using the product. to use this product open the lid, and it is like a dial turner go back and forth till you have a brown and white mixture. I used my angled brush that i own to apply. I like that it does no emphasizes the lines in my face. it actually makes me look good without being too heavy.

I have a lot of allergies, but this did not set them off at all. Easy to apply and not visible to the naked eye. We'll see how well it works after I have been using it for a few weeks, but so far I am pleased.
summary: Easy to apply and not visible to the naked eye

reviewText:
I tried first this BB cream through the Amazon sample program, as I was having concerns about the shade selection. La Roche-Posay usually has great formulated and performing product, so I was expecting to like it.
With a thick mousse consistency, this BB cream applies easily and leaves a perfected looking skin, very soft and comfortable; for my combination skin I almost don't have to set it with powder. The finish is indeed matte and the pores are blurred.
I'm a yellow toned light-medium complexion (MAC NC20, maybe NC25 in the summer) and the light /medium shade in the BB Blur is a little too dark for me. Since it's a BB cream, the color kind of adapts to my skin, but the coverage is light to medium, so it still looks off if it's not a match.
The SPF 20 is low, and since it's a BB cream (you can't apply too much product) I would suggest layering it over other higher SPF products.

Note: If you get the sample, is a tiny 1ml packet. I'm still using the credit for a La Roche-Posay sunscreen, so it was basically still free.
summary: Great BB cream if the shades suit you

reviewText: Best foundation out there, not oily, doesn't make my skin irritated or look oily. Last all day.
Returned it. Did not like how it went on or blended. Bare Minerals primer is better for me.
summary: Did not like how it went on or blended

reviewText: Very nice !

Best mattifier I have found. Goes on like silk. Your skin is instantly transformed. For those who said it's heave etc, u are using too much! U only need a drop for your whole face. Can use alone or under foundation. Really absorbs oil.

I have recently started using this BB cream and I really like it.  It makes my skin look much better  very even and smooth, plus it feels incredibly light and silky going on. Most impressively, it really blends away your pores somehow.  It only comes in two shades  Fair/Light and Light/Medium.  I bought the Light/Medium although I am pretty fair and it blends in perfectly.

The only drawback is that it does not seem to absorb any oil despite the description and needs to be set with powder.  In fact, Effaclar is La Roche-Posays acne line but this is not at all drying.

This is definitely the best option if you are looking to minimize the appearance of pores (and who isnt?).
summary: Awesome for Minimizing Appearance of Pores

reviewText: Works nice as a foundation. The color is much lighter than I expected so I recommend ordering a shade darker than you normally would.

This is a fantastic bb cream and IMO is great as a foundation for mature skin. (I purchased mine for $13.99 from eBay, includes shipping).

Mine is the light/medium and provides a smooth, beautiful look. I have found my holy grail!  And even though it's a mousse, it's not super airy so you really can use a small amt so you're not paying for air.

A rare miss from La Roche-Posay. It has a fluffy, souffle like texture, and it blended on my skin nicely, providing a good amount of coverage. However, as the day progressed my skin began to feel like an oil slick. The product also seemed accentuated my pores and fine lines as the day went on. I have oily, acne prone skin, so this might work better for someone with drier skin.

I wanted to love this! I did, I truly did. Felt great, skin looks amazing but it did not stay put! I took a nap on the couch with this on and it got everywhere! SO sad. Sent it back. Search continues . . . sigh.
summary: I wanted to love this! I did

reviewText: Feels silky but looked like pancake makeup on me; also extremely light in color (I'm very fair, but this was white-ish).  Love the Effaclar line, but this one was a total bust.
summary: Feels silky but looked like pancake makeup on me

reviewText: This is the second la Roche-Posay product I've tried and I'm becoming a fan.  This product goes on smooth with a minimum smell to interfere with any perfume you might be wearing,  The only problem is that this particular color has too much yellow tint for my complexion.  I'll probably use it for face contouring and/or on my neck...maybe even on my shoulders if I'll be sending lots of time outdoors...
If you like the no make-up look, this is the perfect foundation for you!  A tiny drop in the palm of my hand covers my whole face.  Especially nice to keep shiny nose at bay.  Highly recommend this!
summary: If you like the no make-up look

reviewText: Another winner from La Roche Posay! Absolutely love this! They had something similar a few years back that I found in Paris but could never find here once I ran out. The good news, this is even better and it truly 'blurs' in so well with your skin that you need the tiniest amount, seriously. Squeeze too much out and you'll have more than you need. Love that it hasn't made my skin breakout yet either when most makeups (even acne safe ones) usually do! I'm pretty fair, Irish skin with a little redness and the lighter of the colors works fine. Just a little more rubbing with my fingers to 'blur' in

La Roche Posay Effaclar BB Blur seems to even out my red splotches and blemishes without a thick coated look. Since my skin is dry I find it necessary to moisturize before applying the product and doing so is not a problem. Without some kind of coverage, my neck and throat look bad. I can put a tiny amount of the BB Blur there early in the morning and my neck still looks good that night.

Much of the makeup I use makes my face itch. This product did not. It has a light feel and it goes on evenly. With SPF 20, it protects skin from sun damage.
summary: An Advanced Way to Cover Skin Blemishes

reviewText: I'm not a big make up person so rarely use this sort of product, mostly because I don't want to look as if I'm wearing makeup. I really like this product, specifically because it blends in so well and feels invisible. It covers spots and uneven skin tone really well. I am very fair skinned and this product is perfect for me. Not sure how well it would work on darker complexions. I would buy this product.
summary: Goes on smoothly and hides blemishes, disappearing into skin. Not a heavy, visible makeup.

reviewText: I received the fair/light shade of this Effaclar BB Blur.  I have never used this brand much less heard of it.  I have used many BB and CC creams, but this BB Blur excels all the other products by far.  It goes on smooth and creamy.  The coverage is wonderful and it looks very natural.  The color for me was perfect as I am fair skinned and I particularly liked the way it covers but doesn't look heavy.  I also didn't have any problems with breakouts like I sometimes do whenever I use a new foundation.  I have been using Almay Smart Shade and liked it pretty well, but this BB Blur outperforms it by a mile.  I guess, if I can afford this slightly more expensive BB foundation, I will definitely try to keep this one.  I was very impressed with the look, texture, and coverage of this product.  I was pleasantly surprised by this product and would recommend it to my friends.
summary: Love it! Plan on continuing to use it.

reviewText:
La Roche-Posay Effaclar BB Blur is a great product. The only La Roche-Posay I have used in the past was sunscreen and I was pleased with its performance. So when I was offered the opportunity to try this product, I was very interested.

The color I received was fair/light which was a great match for my skin tones. The cream was on the thick side rather than thin. But I found that it spread very easily over my skin. Only a small amount was needed to cover my face. I had no problems with the cream settling in any lines on my face as a few others have said. I liked the matte finish which I found lasted very well. All in all, I was pleased with the way this cream looked on my skin.
summary: La Roche-Posay Effaclar BB  Blur was a success on my skin and I liked it

reviewText:
I have tried multiple liquid foundations and as far as BB creams I have tried Maybelline and Garnier. This La Roche-Posay wins hands down. OMG I have never had a foundation as good as this stuff. The texture is weird, it is a mousse and doesn't look super smooth when you put it on your hand to apply but I can't get over the way this feels when you apply it to your face. It feels so smooth and silky soft on your face. There is no greasy feeling or wet feeling, it is so weird from the second you smooth it on your face there it feels like you already applied foundation and powder at the same time and no effort at all to blend it in. I hate to use the word weird because it is above awesome!! One sweep with your finger or make up applicator and it's instantly blended. Not only does it feel good but it provides excellent coverage it looks as if your face is airbrushed flawless. I received this in the fair/light and it works perfect for me. The color is great it isn't too light and is really natural looking.

 I'm not one to splurge on myself, I have 3 daughters and they always come first. I feel guilty spending $10 for make-up but I will probably be asking for this for Christmas or birthday or splurging and buying it because it is that GOOD!!! BETTER THAN GOOD!!! BEST I HAVE EVER HAD AS FAR AS MAKE UP GOES. I can say 100% I highly recommend this product.

This product is positioned as a "BB cream"--which I think may be the cosmetic industry's new term for "foundation," which sounds like something your granny might wear. In fact, this cream is 20 SPF sunscreen that not only protects your skin from harmful rays, but blurs the appearance of big pores, covers zit,and absorbs excess oil. I love it. My skin is quite fair and luckily, the "light/medium" shade works well.

Not cheap, but worth it and I love not having to apply sunscreen first and follow with foundation. Who has the time?

The texture of the cream mousse made it hard for the product to spread evenly on my skin- which is combination. It was almost too thick and dry, but it might work better on oilier complexions. The coverage overall wasn't great, and didn't really blur the look of my pores either. While it wasn't a great BB cream for me, I did find that it works surprisingly well as a primer.
summary: but it might work better on oilier complexions

reviewText:
I have been using a similar product from Origins and have also use Boscia brand.  This wins hands down.  Unlike the other two brands the La Roche keeps the shiny afternoon skin at bay.

Very smooth, feels light, not like I'm wearing a mask, covers extremely well, no scent and the color is perfect for my skin tone.

I've definitely found my new covering cream!  Definitely recommend and the price is right too!

This cream as a high surface area coverage ratio. So you need to use a fairly small amount to get a natural looking finish. My wife doesn't have oily skin and found the cream easy to apply and effective.

Oh my god, I love this product!
I am of Indian origin, I have the fair product, and it is too light for me. BUT--
This product goes on light as air, and when on, is softer than my own skin.
I'd almost say that this product gives you a pretty "glow".
No, it's not shiny, it's matte. I mean a healthy glow. Very natural looking, though.
You know all those lovely actresses in Korean dramas? They must use this product to make their skin look so good.
I've tried a few other BB creams (including Korean BB creams) and this one is the best I've tried to date.
It's expensive, but worth it. A little goes a long way. I'm going to get the other shade because I like it so much. I just hope it's not too yellow for me.
Five stars all the way!
summary: Light as air, makes your skin look soft, natural and amazing

reviewText:
I received the light/medium BB Blur by La Roche-Posay.  The color is a bit too dark for my skin tone which is more of a light/Ivory with yellow undertones.  That being said, I gave it to my daughter to use who 1) has T-Zone oily skin.  She gets break outs on her forehead and chin and is always looking for a product that won't contribute to her oily areas.  2) She has a slightly more olive tone than me, but not by much and she said that she could work with the light/medium but wants to try the light.  As for the coverage?  The product itself goes on beautifully. It feels almost silky but not oily.  It is excellent for all day coverage.  My daughter loved the way she could canceal her blemishes without any caking and without any added oil.  Just remember to powder lightly and set with a spray and you're good to go for hours!

We are going to try the light color and post an updated review after using for a longer period of time.  As of now, the product covers blemishes and sets beautifully.

Recommend!
summary: The product itself goes on beautifully. It feels almost silky but not oily

reviewText: I love this cream.  I use it for makeup.  I love the feel, the look.  It can be worn with or without powder finish.  This works for me.
summary: La Roche-Posay Effaclar BB Blur, Medium

reviewText: This gives a cover that really does 'blur' on the skin. The texture is somewhere between a very soft and smooth sand, and silicon. It lays on your skin  instead of staining it. If you use any other cosmetic products, I think this should go above and not below. I have olive, slightly tanned skin and this gives a nice blurred highlight to my skin and then, over time, seems to fade back a bit. There is no scent and a very little goes a very long way. You do not need much. I think there is just a bit more pigment in this product than the norm for BB creams. Overall a good product.
summary: Silky texture, blur is an accurate description

reviewText: The color is much darker than I would expect for a "fair/light."  The coverage is good, but the cosmetic sinks into lines.  I'd recommend this for someone without any wrinkles and pale but not truly fair skin.  I didn't like the way it felt on my skin, though I didn't have any adverse effects.  It is fine if you are wrinkle free, but I'd recommend other products if you are 30+.

The name really pushes the fact that this covers up pores and blemishes.  I put it on half of my face to test the differences.  While it was nice, I found very little difference in pores.  That being said, I really did like the fact that it lasted all day with no shine!  It goes on smooth and has a neutral smell.
summary: While it was nice, I found very little difference in pores

reviewText: I really like this BB Blur foundation. It's super light and creamy, but truly does dry matte just as it claims.  It covers well, although not as well as a true foundation (but it doesn't claim to either).  It's smooth enough that I can wear it without powder and still not feel oily - and I have very oily skin.  I have fair-medium skin and this color worked well for me. I think I could probably get away with the next level of color, too, but overall was very pleased with this. It feels like I'm not even wearing makeup. Love it!
summary: I really like this BB Blur foundation

reviewText:
I've been using this for a few days now, and really like it!  It really does blur out small lines and discolorations on your skin, and feels nice and light.

I always check Paula Begoun's Beautypedia website, and they said this about it:  "Effaclar BB Blur goes on too sheer to cover more noticeable imperfections (i.e. deeply pigmented blemishes or dark spots), but its sheer to light coverage evens out the complexion in a natural-looking way. More to the point, the blurring effect really does help soften the appearance of pores and even fine lines to a minor degree. As for the claim that it keeps skin matte all daythat won't hold up if you have very oily skin, but you will at least get temporary shine control and this won't make your skin oilier."

I wear MAC foundation in NW20, and this was light enough for me.  It would be nice if it came in more color choices.

The silicone in this also makes it glide on like silk, and it lasts all day for me, even though I have oily skin in my T-zones.  It is also fragrance-free.

Before ordering this, though, I hadn't realized that La Roche-Posay does animal testing, and that would keep me from ordering this again.
summary: A nice, lightweight BB cream that does help to blur lines

reviewText: This is one of the best blemish concealers I've tried so far.  It is easy to feather in with the skin surrounding the blemish without accidentally "uncovering" the concealed area.  The tube is pretty small, but it only takes a teeny tiny bit to be effective.  This is an in-between shade on the yellow & red spectrum, so it works with a wide variety of light complexions.

I wish I had tried this La Roche Posay BB cream when it was really sunny in my area as it goes on easily and doesn't have any scent which would interfere with my perfume.  Although my skin is not prone to blemishes,  I'm glad to have this BB cream even though winter is approaching with less daylight and thus my skin isn't as shiny as it is in the summer..  What I found to be a real plus is the packaging of this cream as it comes is a lightweight plastic tube which makes it easy to put in my purse for subsequent applications during the day without worrying about any spills.

This was my first time trying the product and something from this line.  Its not for me, and it may be perfect for someone else.  Two reasons its too light, I wear a Cover Girl 05 light color and this is lighter than that. It takes maybe five minutes until it completely absorbs in it my skin, while its sitting on top of my skin it cracks and looks like a mask, when absorbed its ok, nothing special.  I have 50+ New England fair and rosy, somewhat sensitive skin.
summary: and it may be perfect for someone else

reviewText:
The color I received was light/medium but the color is definatly a medium and anyone that has fair skin this would be too dark. I have a light complextion myself and felt it may have been a little too dark for my skin-tone.  I thought it did a good job with makinging my pores dissapear and gave my skin a nice matte look. I topped this off with my makeup forever pressed powder and felt like I had a nice medium coverage.

I blended this product onto my skin with my dampened beauty blender and felt like it went on well. Overall I liked the product but feel this color didn't quite match my skin tone.
summary: Nice coverage but light/medium too dark for my skin

reviewText:
I am always on the lookout for a new BB foundation creme.

La Roche-Posay Effaclar (seriously that name though) caught my eye. Oil absorbing, matte finish, SPF. I chose the light/medium because the fair light seemed TOO light.

I have fair skin, but pink undertones. The light/medium was too yellow undertone for me, it fits a more light olive toned skin. BUT my girlfriend loves it! Its perfect for her skin, and she loves the way it feels, and looks after hours of wear. I get to see it up close and it really does even out her skin, cover any blemishes and is matte all day.

Finally a product gets it, that "fair" doesn't mean "bloodless". Not since the old Cover Girl liquid makeup from back in the 80s have I found a product that creates a perfect blend between brown pigments and pink pigments in all that cream color to look like my northern European skin tone. That was my first impression upon trying the BB Blur. My second one was, wow, you only need a tiny bit of this stuff in any one area because it floats rather than coats. Several practices later, I can achieve a healthy look that doesn't accentuate creases yet imparts a shimmery radiant glow - especially from more than a foot away. Up close in the mirror, I can see it if I'm not wearing other products on my face. And I can feel it because I never used to wear makeup, so anything that goes on my face I can feel and it vaguely annoys me. Lipstick? Don't get me started. But I must say, this is one of the lightest and least offensive of the products I've tried and I'm very pleased that the color tone is a natural and slightly healthier looking shade for me. I had others check to see if they could find demarcation lines but they couldn't, so the product lives up to its name - Blur!

This is much more thick and covering than your typical BB cream, it is more like a CC cream based on a few of those I have tried.

It looks good from about 2 feet away, but up close it really settled into fine lines and looked like I had a full face of make up on.

I really like the texture, whipped cream more than liquid and it went on smoothly.  It definitely has yellow as its base undertone, so if you are rose complected like me it will look a bit odd, BUT it is good for under eye discoloration since yellow counteracts the purplish circles that show up with exhaustion.

If you are yellow toned and looking for full coverage, this is a good choice. If you are looking for a lighter BB cream, look elsewhere.
summary: Too thick for a BB cream IMHO

reviewText: This is probably the best BB cream I've ever tried. First the tone matches my pale skin perfectly and blends in in such a way that people generally can't tell I'm wearing anything special. I have good skin on my cheeks, but a more problematic T-zone so the ability to blend means I can use this only where I really need it. My forehead which is prone to some redness and small bumps now looks completely completely clear, and my nose which is prone to large pores and oiliness stays smooth and matte all day. Best of all, when I paired this product with the La Roche-Posay New Pigment Serum, 1.01 Fluid Ounce, the SPF 20 in it revealed the sensitivity caused by the serum so I'm able to have clear-looking skin while treating my dark spots underneath. Very very happy with this whole line.

This is only my second BB cream I have tried. Since it got such great reviews on beauty blogs and is relatively reasonably priced versus other higher end BB creams, I thought I would try it. It has a great light, dare I say fluffy texture, which may sound odd but it goes on like a dream. It conceals nicely and has a nice mat finish.

However, I give it 4 stars because it touts itself as absorbing oil for all day matte skin. In this area, it did no better than any other foundation I have tried, BB or not. When it goes on it feels very powdery and smooth, but after a few hours my nose, which is my problem oily area, was greasy and needed a blot. Still, it gave me a no makeup look which I really love.

Also, I generally get medium toned foundations, or whatever a particular brand considers it's true medium. This is VERY orangy for a medium. Another reason I give it 4 stars. It works fine on my nose, but on my chin to neck it was very obvious. So since I do like the texture a lot, I ordered the light to use both. It only comes in two shades, so I suspect that this might be something lots of women will need to do.

The finish on this is amazing.  I love the blurring effect and it's not greasy or shiny.  It feels good on my skin.  But the shade is kabuki, yo.  I'm a very pale woman with very little melanin, but I had to order the medium tone.  This particular shade will be good for only the whitest of whiteys.

Took me a while to realize that a TINY bit goes a long way with this BB cream. It's different, and not as matte as I wanted it to be, but I love La Roache products, and I think this looks better than it feels going on the face. It also smells really really bad, like plastic or something odd.
summary: but I love La Roache products

reviewText:
I bought a sample of this, but I tried this product before and most La Roche-Posay sunscreens I tried are great products.
The Anthelion AOX Daily Antioxidant Serum is a very lightweight but hydrating product. Like most SPF 50 products it leaves a slight shine to the face, but once I got my make-up on, all look great. The finish is silicon like to the touch. It wears very well under make-up during the day.
summary: Great serum sunscreen for daily use!

reviewText: Love
the bottle started oxidizing. it was gross
Excelente very Nice!

This sun screen feels great on my skin. I don't notice any real smell after applying it. My skin reacts to certain chemicals and I react to certain smells.  I have had no problems with this product.

I suffer from dry skin especially in the winter so this not only protects me from the sun but it makes my dry skin feel better which is a big plus. I have worn this while doing yard work and raking fall leaves and it has worked very well.

I have other sun screen products.  This seems to be the best when it comes to making my skin feel moisturized. I would use it even if I did not need a sun screen to make my skin feel better.

I have extremely sensitive skin, and I discovered both this brand and this product via my dermatologist.  I LOVE this sunscreen. Gentle, scent-free, goes in silky smooth, absorbed almost immediately, and offers a high level of protection. The drawbacks are that the bottle is small and it is very expensive. Consequently, I will slap on something cheaper when I work out, go to the beach, or work in the yard, and I save this for using under makeup before work or a social engagement.

I thought from the "serum" in the name that this would be one of those anti-aging serums I have been anxious to try but in practice it seems to be more sun screen than anti-aging product.  However, reducing sun damage *is* anti-aging so it does have that long-term effect.

It is more chemical sun screen than physical barrier sun screen.  It goes on very sheer and light feeling so you could use it under makeup every day.  I think it is a good sun screen, it just wasn't exactly what I was expecting.

It feels greasy, made my face shiny and caused my skin to break out.
It also had that unpleasant 'sunscreen smell' when I applied it (though the smell does fade).
It seemed effective as a sunscreen, has a very high SPF - but I would not recommend it for folks like myself with sensitive or oily skin.
Also, it's not good for use on eye area; if I sweat a little or my eyes water, it gets into my eyes and burns. Really painful.

I've bought other La Roche-Posay items in the past and have always really liked them, so I was eager to try out this new product. I was expecting it to be heavier than it is, but it really does feel like a serum on your skin, which is amazing considering that it has such a high SPF of 50. It doesn't leave a white cast to the skin at all, and it plays nicely with moisturizer and foundation over it. When buying beauty products, I usually check Paula Begoun's Beautypedia site to see if the claims that the product makes are valid ones, and Beautypedia had this to say about this product: "So why doesn't this earn our highest rating? While this "serum" contains a notable amount of vitamin E (tocopherol), it's disappointing that the other antioxidants are included in such minute concentrations, especially given that this is advertised as a "high-potent antioxidant complex." We wish La-Roche-Posay would have included more, but we'll take any we can get since the research is clear that combining antioxidants with sunscreen gives skin a significant environmental boost and helps to further offset the damaging effects of UV light. [ . . . ] As far as the claim that you'll see improvement in the appearance of dark spots goes, don't get your hopes up there. This formula lacks the skin-lightening ingredients needed to do that, but at least the sun protection will help prevent sun-damaged induced dark spots from getting worse." Overall, this is a nice sunscreen, but I may stick with my Eltamd UV Clear SPF 46, 48-Gram 1.7 oz. since the ingredients in the Elta MD (especially the niacinamide) are better for getting rid of dark spots.
summary: A nice, light serum that works well under foundation/make-up

reviewText: This serum has a nice subtle scent and a little bit can cover the entire area.  It rubs on smooth and soaks into the skin well without leaving it looking shiny or greasy.  I have very sensitive skin and this serum did not seem to bother me at all.  It did little for the darker spots on my skin, however, I did notice it improving the lines I have around my eyes and mouth.  It made them not quite as deep and defined.  Overall, pretty good for lines, not so much for dark spots.
More like sunscreen than serum.  Smells good and absorbs well.  But it didn't feel like serum.

I like this serum to protect from the suns damaging rays. Its very light, odorless, and absorbs easily. I put it on after my moisturizer and my skin doesnt feel clogged up or slathered in products. It works well as a sunscreen on my face and neck. It says it reducing fine lines and signs of aging. I don't see evidence of that on my skin, but as a sunscreen Im sure its preventing them from getting worse. It also claims to reduce dark spots. I have a couple and it is making them slightly lighter in color. Overall Im happy with this product and Ill continue to use it.

I like how it feels and that it absorbs fast.  My skin feels smoother after using it. It is not greasy. I cant see any visible differences overall.  The box lists for Drug Facts five active ingredients, and their purpose all say they are for Sunscreen.  It seems to be a glorified facial sunscreen.  I dislike putting sunscreen lotion on my face, I would prefer this instead but at this price, I would hesitate.

I have not used a serum before so I had to learn about it first.  Wikipedia (Nov 2015) defines serum as a buzzword for lotion in the cosmetic market.  A few cosmetic sites say there is no formal definition, but cosmetic serums are rapidly absorbed and highly potent.  They are the cousins of lotions and moisturizers. They typically focus on one of these areas: dry skin, aging, dark spots.  My concern because it does absorb into your skin so fast is with the ingredients of which I am not qualified to speak to and will watch for others opinions on this.

When sun rises at 6am and sets at 6pm, you only have to reapply your sunscreen 6 times a day to prevent sun burns. In the Northwest after rainy season begins, it's much shorter. Weather her Pacific Northwest can have cloudy day and yet you can get full face sunburn, because, sun's uv rays passes through clouds. I know because, I get the best tan when I am riding bicycle on a cloudy day not thinking about sunscreen. That's when I get sunburns when I forget about it because I can't see the sun all day long. Instruction says apply after clean rinsed face, apply 15 minutes before going outside. It is not sweat proof. Not for children under 6 months. Ingredient smells just like any other 50 SPF sunscreen. Less chalky when pumped out of the bottle. Smell isn't as strong. It's not greasy either. It says do not use on broken or damaged skin. Apply on top of moisturized skin, like rinsed, washed, and after moisturizer. Also keep the bottle inside paper container because the bottle cannot be exposed to inside vehicle heat nor direct sun exposure. Heat and sun will depreciate the active ingredients. Take good care of your skin. You only have one face for entire life.
summary: Once every two hours to save your face, literally from aging

reviewText:
The good:

-doesn't feel greasy
-has a sunscreen* (50 spf) in it but isn't waterproof so use an actual sunscreen if swimming or perspiring heavily
-Antioxidant complex (Baicalin + Vitamin Cg + Vitamin E) to help protect skin from free radicals caused by UV rays
-causes no noticeable irritation on my sensitive skin so far
-goes on smoothly and makes a nice base for makeup

The concerns:

-contains *Oxybenzone, which is a sunscreen that blocks out UVA/UVB rays. However, not to mention the ecological impacts oxybenzone may have on the environment (read the other reviews to learn about that) l, it turns out that scientists aren't 100% positive oxybenzone is not linked to endocrine (hormonal) disorders in humans, cell imbalances and yes, even lead to skin cancer.  None of this is 100% proven yet, but there is enough concern that studies are still being done on it. The recommendation is to avoid sunscreens that include oxybenzone, retinyl palmitate (a type of vitamin A) and anything over 50 spf.
-the price is substantial. To those on a  budget (or just frugal) there are alternatives that will do as well and without the concerns of oxybenzone.

My apologies to the manufacturer for a less than positive review. I just can't recommend this product with the concerns I (and others) have about the ingredient oxybenzone. And I want people to know that it's not necessary to spend a chunk of your paycheck to have beautiful skin. Do some research on the concerns about oxybenzone to see some natural and lower cost options. This is just my humble opinion.

This seems kind of a misleading product. It talks about it being some kind of serum - made it seem really fancy but it is really just an expensive sunscreen. Looking at the ingredients, there are no antioxidants but plenty of sunscreen products in here. Well, I decided to give it a try anyway.

This came with the product already out of the box and the cap off. It seem to have came out of the packaging during transit. It took a few pumps and then the product came out. It is extremely thin and I did not care for the smell. It irritated my nostrils and I will not be using it again.
summary: Expensive sunscreen - not any special serum

reviewText:
It seems that many people are wisely paying increasing attention to skin care. There is a plethora of products from established companies to fill various needs.

Laroche-Posay has entered with a combination of two high-demand products: a 50 SPF sunscreen and antioxidant moisturizer.

This kind of product is, inevitably, very much a matter of personal preference. Skin types vary; allergic reactions may occur; scents and absorption may be experienced differently.

My experience is positive. The lotion was easily absorbed. There is no disagreeable result.

To the extent one relies on this product as a sunscreen, it's a very expensive selection. Sunscreens require frequent replenishment over time or outdoors, so the higher consumption of sunscreen compared with a sole-purpose antioxidant can be costly.

On the other hand, if one is not going to apply this as a sunscreen, it may be wise to compare it with other stem cell skin products.

Another issue that bears attention is the ingredient list. Oxybenzone is an active ingredient in this product. It is controversial in some quarters. Dermal application, particularly to the face, justifies some scrutiny. My suggestion is to conduct a quick web search, via WebMD or another authoritative curator, so that  you can make your own decision with confidence.
summary: Combined Sunscreen, Stem Cell Serum--High Quality, High Price

reviewText: Been using for a week. Skin is soft.  Love that it has SBF of 50.  I live in Florida and want ONE product with moisturizer and SBF combined.  There is no detectable scent with this product.  The packaging is clean and there's an easy to dispense top nozzle.  One pump is enough for  my entire face.  This will last a long long time.  My skin is soft, clean and has not broken out using this.

Even the sunscreen recommended for under make up by my cosmetic dermatologist is not as good as this product. The serum is light and has a primer like quality. When distributed on the back of my hand it did smell of suscreen BUT when I applied it to my facial skin I did not notice the sunscreen at all. Makeup went on after this serum and moisturizer and it was a smooth and non oily experience. Sunscreen is necessary year round for everyone, the dangerous rays manage to get through even on grey winter days. Great product. This comes in a glass pump bottle.
summary: A New Addition to My Beauty Routine

reviewText: It goes on easier than your typical sunscreen and is not heavy at all.. very light and silky feeling and blends in well.. not greasy!  Has a very faint smell (smells like sunscreen) that goes away quickly.  It smooths the skin like a face primer lotion would. Makeup goes on nicely after use of this product.  All thumbs up from me!
summary: Smoother skin in seconds with SPF protection...

reviewText:
A serum, in my opinion, is the most important part of a skincare regime.
You can have the best moisturizer, the best cleansers, toners, BB and CC products. You're wasting money without a good serum.

This is an amazing serum. It goes on light, yet has a UVA and UVB filtering sunscreen. No heavy feel, just weightless protection that is the foundation for anything else you apply. You can even wear it all by itself.
It might seem expensive, but a little goes a long way. It you need to make some hard skincare choices, splurge on this and for the other steps opt for quality lower priced products.

Expensive but it does a good job. The one thing that I like is that it does not have a scent to it or very light scent. Usually I like strong scented skin products but this one works lighter. My daughter and wife love it but the rest of us have also been using it too. Great when out in the sun and it is not real greasy either which some of these products are. Wife likes using it on her face when we are outside the boys like it on their hands-makes your skin feel soft and young again.

If the price was lower would be a staple in our house-will be watching for sales on Amazon.
summary: High price but does a great job!

reviewText:
My wife and daughter love this stuff.  They both use it regularly.  As they tell me, it goes on before they put on their makeup and works as an exellent sunblock.

I have used it myself, though admittedly I forget most of the time.  It goes on smooth and does not feel greasy or slippery.  I spend a lot of time driving or in the sun, and can notice a difference in my skin at the end of the day on the days I use it compared to the days I dont.  I usually don't wear sunblock, even though I know I should, becuase I cant tolerate that they all either feel greasy, or make your fell 'crusty' if you use the sprays.  This is a great option since it doesnt make me feel either.

If used sparingly it will last a long time, which is important since this seems to be the mose expensive sunblock ever made.  Ok, not THE most expensive, but they aren't afraid to charge for it.  Is it worth it?  I think so, but that is completely a personal call.
summary: Everyone in our house like this stuff.

reviewText:
Really nice serum.

Don't take the instructions to "Apply generously" too literally. You'll run out of this if you accidentally squeeze too hard a few times, which I did when I first used it.

This AOX serum applies on really smooth, has but the slightest-sunblock smell despite being broad spectrum SPF 50, and makes my skin feel nice.

Highly recommended, though I think it's overpriced. It'll be more economical to get separate serum and sunblock.
summary: Good but Might be better to get Anthelios and Serum separately.

reviewText: This is a good sunblock/skin protector.  My (only) reservations are these: one has to reapply this product more often than is convenient, and more often than one has to apply other (quite good) products that are competitors to the La Roche-Posay Serum.  Since, in addition, this product is quite a bit pricier than many of its competitors, unless I discover when this bottle has run out that my skin is transformed, I am unlikely to want to get a second bottle of it.
summary: Good sunblock/skin protector, but one that has too be re-applied (too) often.

reviewText:
The La Roche-Posay Anthelios 50 AOX is a non comedogenic, silicone-based sunscreen and antioxidant serum which uses tocopherol (vit-E) as its antioxidant base.

The serum spreads very well and a small amount will cover a large area - I could get a single pump to cover my entire face - albeit rather thinly. I'd guess that a 1 to 1.5 pumps is probably average. The serum goes on rather greasily and is not really pleasant feeling to apply. The greasy feel dissipated in a minute or so and left the skin feeling somewhat smoother (not as smooth as applying a moisturizer, but similar). With careful conservation, I'm guessing this single vial would probably last two or maybe even three months (assuming you are reapplying every two hours as directed while you're exposed to UV rays).

There is no true scent associated to the serum other than a sort of faint and generic chemically smell when first applied. It didn't bother me much and seemed to go away within a few minutes.

The serum also contains things like baicalensis root and cassia leaf extracts, both which are often used as antibac/antifungal and anti-inflammatory type medicines.

The Anthelios 50 AOX is a decent sunscreen that goes on rather greasy, dries smoothly and does not have a noticeable scent afterwards. The non comedogenic aspects are great, especially since many sunscreens seem so heavy and clogging. However, there's quite a few chemicals included as well as being silicone based, which isn't exactly eco-friendly. If you have sensitive skin, this serum has quite a few glycols in the ingredients, so you may want to test it out before using all over your face.
summary: An ok silicone based serum with good sunscreen benefits and no scent - goes on greasy, but dries smooth

reviewText:
AOX stands for Advanced Antioxidant Technology but no where in the active ingredients does it list any antioxidants, like Vitamin C.  As far as I can tell, this is just an expensive sunscreen because the active ingredients list sunscreen chemicals only.  I wanted the corrective AOX effects of the product but I think it is only protective not corrective so it will do nothing for the fine lines or wrinkles I have now.  I didn't realize this was only a sunscreen.  A serum is clear and this is a creamy fluid like a sunscreen with antioxidants added although like I said, I don't see any antioxidants listed in either the Active or Inactive ingredients.

On the plus side, when I use this cream, my face is very, very soft.

Amazon put a sticky label on the side of the box so I can't read one side of the box and the LA Roche-Posay website doesn't show the box in detail.

I typically dislike all sunscreen products. They smell terrible, most make my face break out, they feel greasy and because I work outside with horses almost every single day the layer of sticky sunscreen can draw extra dust & dirt to my face and neck. This La Roche Posay Anthelios is a little different than the usual stuff out there. It has that gross sunscreen smell - BUT it goes away very quickly after you apply this. I am pretty impressed with how fast the smell is gone. We're talking minutes. Well done.

The product itself looks and feels just like most of the other sunscreens out there on the market when you pump it into your hand. It's white and is a creamy type texture. Maybe a little silkier than the cheaper grocery store beach style stuff. This goes on like a moisturizer and a little bit (for me at least) goes a long way. I find that a ball about the size of four peas is just right to cover my face completely without leaving a greasy coating on my skin. It absorbs within a few minutes and my face and neck feel soft and smooth. My face can be a nightmare with any products, but I have not had a rash or irritation from this serum. Again - well done La Roche.

My one star deduction is quite simply the value factor. As much as I like this product, I can't understand how a woman like me can afford to use it daily. The suggested use on the bottle is reapplication every two hours while exposed to the sun and daily use otherwise. If you are a active outside every day for more than two hours at this price, there is no way I can afford two or three bottles of this a month! That's more than my cell phone bill. It's a great item, but a treat, like a trip to the spa.
summary: Absorbs very fast, scent vanish very fast, no skin irritation or break outs. Budget breaker for outdoor lifestyle

reviewText:
Because I've only been using it about two weeks, I can't comment on the long-term effectiveness of this serum-type cream.  However, I do notice a soothing, cooling effect under my eyes when applied and I believe I do see some puffiness reduced.  (The puffiness under my eyes after a long day is minimal at most but I figure it's good to know about a product that at least partially addresses what it purports to do.)

This is the first such product I have ever used so I cannot compare Baxter with similar products but I can say that I do like what it appears to do when applied in a thin coat under my lower eyelids.  It's very mild, no stinging -- just a slight soothing sensation and a smoothing of the skin in the area.  However, it is quite expensive and I haven't noticed any long-term effects so while I like the product, I'm not quite sure it's worth it.  If I notice that the reduction I'm seeing begins to last beyond 12 hours or so, I will update this review and upgrade to five stars.

No odors, goes on clear, and a little bit goes a long way.

I believe this product is a little misleading in its claim to minimize puffiness and dark circles. I have not seen that result when I used as directed (just a small drop) I did find that it soothed dry under eye skin so if your under eye problem is mostly due to that then this might be a little more helpful than it was for me.
summary: Didn't minimize my dark circles and puffiness

reviewText: I love this stuff. Definitely seems to be working. You just need a little bit to do the trick. It definitely helps with the crows feet and the under eye puffiness. I haven't used a ton of under eye products, but this has definitely been the most effective one. It's fairly expensive, but this should last me a few months at the rate I'm using it.

This stuff feels really good after you put it on.  Ive been using for a few days and my eyes do look "fresher" after I've used it.  I'm lucky enough to not have dark circles.  We'll see how it does with the tiny lines over time, but it does make my eyes feel really good in the morning and i often have that yucky tired eye feeling.  longer term use will tell more, but after a bit, I do like this.

This is only an "okay" under eye cream. Basically if you want to reduce puffiness under the eye, you want an anti-inflammatory. This is why most people advise to use a tube of hemorrhoid cream, as that's precisely what the active ingredient in those creams is for. The caffeine content of this cream is apparently doing the heavy lifting on that front.

So what does this product give you that a much cheaper tube of hemorrhoid cream wouldn't? Not much, I'm afraid. The rough part of using this cream is that is has a bit of a tingly / mentholated feeling, which isn't all that comfortable near your eye. I haven't had any issues, but I'm always terrified that if it goes into my eye I'll have a very bad time.

It's a small tube for sure with .75 ounces of cream packed into a compact tube. The cream is squeeze dispensed and comes out of a long and very fine plastic tip. Really though, just a small dab (think a small droplet or two) is needed to rub around your eye area so even with frequent use this tube should last a couple of months. Overall it's a quality product. It blends into the skin easily, doesn't leave a greasy residue, has a pleasant fragrance and actually does reduce eye puffiness.
summary: A little goes a long way

reviewText:
I really like this eye cream.  It dispenses easily and effectively through the needle nose applicator.  It has virtually no smell.  And it absorbs quicker than any other eye cream I have used.  After application I was left with a clean and healthy skin feeling under my eyes.  No oily residue but a moisturized look and feel.

I have used plenty of different eye creams, some costing much more that Baxter, and I will be coming back to this product.

In terms of effectiveness this Baxter under eye complex does work.  It takes a small quantity under your eyes to reduce the puffy circles that you would ordinarily get with fatigue.  It won't eliminate the puffiness or circles completely but it does tend to help.  The other benefit is that this is supposed to prevent wrinkles.  I am not too sure about this claim but your mileage may vary.  The one big downside to this is that it is very pricey.  You get less than 1 oz of for almost $30 bucks which seems a bit outrageous especially when other remedies (such as hemorrhoid cream) work equally well at reducing puffiness around the eyes.

It's always difficult to review items like this that take some time for maxim benefit to be seen. That being said, I have found this under eye cream to be helping some work puffiness, even after the first couple of uses.  I have used and enjoyed other Baxter of California products, and despite what another reviewer wrote, they do NOT testing animals.
summary: It's always difficult to review items like this that take some time for maxim benefit to ...

reviewText:
This under eye cream contains various emollients  to protect the skin from loss of moisture and reduce the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles when used regularly.  It also contains caffeine, which is intended to reduce puffiness.

It has a mild medicinal fragrance that is not unpleasant.  It is concentrated and just a tiny amount leaves a smooth protective barrier that lasts.

The plastic tube holds just 22.5 ml or 0.75 oz. and has a fine tip that conveniently dispenses a very small ribbon.

Ingredients:  Water (aqua), glycerin, cyclohexasiloxane, propylene glycol, cetyl alcohol, stearyl alcohol, squalane, stearic acid, palmitic acid, peg-100 stearate, cera alba / beeswax, glyceryl stearate, nylon-12, aluminum starch octenylsuccinate, PEG-20 stearate, phenoxyethanol, butylene glycol, methyl methacrylate crosspolymer, caprylyl glycol, panthenol, tocopheryl acetate, chlorphenesin, caffeine, sodium hyaluronate, calcium PCA, acrylonitrile/methyl methacrylate/vinylidene chloride copolymer, adenosine, sodium hydroxide, hydroxypalmitoyl sphinganine, Alteromonas ferment extract, Corallina officinalis extract.

I wanted to give this a few weeks before I reviewed  it. I placed this on my husband's pillow.  I felt it would be easier for me to see any differences in his face rather than mine since I see his so much more than my own.  I did. I noticed a brightening in his skin.  It looked fresher and the color seemed a bit more even.  My husband did not see it as much.  There were no changes in the crow's feet around his eyes though.

The pillowcase itself is very sleek and soft. I think he slept better with it and maybe that is why is skin looks fresher.
summary: Skin is fresher looking but no difference in wrinkles

reviewText:
I like the nice feel of this pillowcase but have not noticed a difference in my fine lines.

I am in my late 30's and have fine lines around my eyes. After using this pillowcase exclusively for a month I have not noticed any difference in my skin. I do not use any other type of wrinkle products so maybe if I layered products and used this pillow with something else it might work but does not seem to do anything on its own

Let's ignore the price for a moment: this is a very fine pillowcase. It's soft, it's attractive, it's comfortable. The color is neutral and perfect for my chocolate-cherry-hued bedroom. Will the pillowcase rejuvenate you? Since this fabric is touted as "patented," you might wonder about the science behind it. Though I searched a few different ways (Illuminage is a joint venture of cosmetic research company Syneron and Unilever Ventures; Cupron's patent pertains to its antibacterial/antimicrobial properties which is why you'll see the material used in socks) I could not find anything to substantiate the rejuvenation claim. A clinical study involving 57 participants suggested a statistically significant positive effect, but copper-infused fabric is not the same as copper peptides, which have been proven to affect the skin, and I personally was not convinced by the photos. Subtle differences only, could be lighting-related. Too, unless you sleep with your face buried in the pillow, any rejuvenating effect will be uneven, limited to the side that touched the fabric. And if you sleep on your back, you're not going to see an impact on your face at all. My own experience is that the side of my face that comes in contact with the pillowcase looks a lot less smooshed than it would with a regular pillowcase when I first jump out of bed. A half hour later, both sides look the same. I notice that Amazon sells a similar product at a much lower price, so if you're skeptical about the technology but still want to give it a try, there's this option: London Luxury "Skin Glow" Pillow Cover Cupron Copper Technology I like this pillowcase, I really do. And compared to the price of a peel, laser treatment, fillers, or facelift, it's a bargain. But you're also not going to get the same results as you'd get with one of those treatments.

With an aging baby boomer population, products like this are flooding the market.

And speaking as a baby boomer, I'm thrilled with this pillowcase!
It isn't any more expensive then a high-end pillowcase from Frette or Sferra, and it has the look of a bed throw pillow, and we all know those can be well over a hundred dollars if adorned with embellishments.

Add in that it feels fabulous on the skin, and the fact that it is 'rejuvenating' is just icing on the cake.
But does it work to help skin look it's best?
In my opinion, yes, I believe it has made a difference in the month that it's been my sleep companion. A subtle difference, to be sure, but considering all of the above, that's just fine with me.
summary: All Things Considered, a Excellent Value

reviewText:
I am trying to use the eye mask from the same company now. It is nice and silky but it falls off my face about 90% of nights. I think my eye are looks better now, but is it due to the magic of copper mask, my new diet, my meds or supplements I am taking, we will never know. Anyway, I just had to try the pillowcase just in case it does work, and the double blind placebo controlled studies say that copper infused pillowcases do work on reducing wrinkles. I figured - pillowcase cannot fall off my face, right? I sleep on my side with over half of the face buried in the pillow, so I should be golden, unless I forget to turn in my sleep, and then I will be golden on one side only, ouch.
Obviously, the pillowcase will not work if you sleep face up the whole night - there sill be no contact between pillowcase and your face.
The pillowcase comes rolled in a nice round box (should be good for gift giving). The instructions say to machine wash, but not use fabric softener in washer or dryer. It leaves me a bit confused - what about the dryer sheets?
The package says there were multiple double-blind placebo-controlled studies that show that the technology (copper infused fabric) works for wrinkle reduction. Interestingly, I could not find any specific links on their website, but I did find two articles on PubMed from 2012 and 2009 that did support the claim, at least for sleeping on copper oxide-containing pillowcases. The pillowcases in the studies had 1% and 0.4% copper oxide, respectively, there is no mention on how much copper oxide in the Cupron fabric here. The illuminage website says that Color and anti-aging technology proven to last over 100 washes. The technology sounds very exciting and it is something that is so easy to use. Sleep on it and that is it.
I also wanted to say kudos to the company to publishing the before and after photos of mature women with wrinkles - sometimes companies advertise anti wrinkle products and show a 25 year old, trying to convince us how good it works on her. Of course it does, she is 25, she does not have wrinkles.
The pillowcase is made of 249 count polyester, and it is rather soft and silky, but it feels exactly as sleeping on a poly pillowcase.

I honestly can't say if this pillow case is helping the skin on my face, the very fine copper fibers are too small to notice but the pillowcase has a silky feel thats not un- pleasant. A standard pillow fits perfectly.  Copper, an excellent conductor of heat, was thought to stimulate a warm flow of healing energy. Very little copper from copper peptide products penetrates the skin. Charged molecules, including copper and peptides, do not readily permeate the skin barrier so I question how you benefit much from this pillowcase.
summary: This is a nice silky pillowcase but don't expect miracles from it.

reviewText:
Wrinkles can sometimes be a problem as people grow older so it was with some interest that I saw this product, Iluminage Skin Rejuvenating Pillowcase with Copper Oxide, on Amazon.

The advertisement on Amazon tells us that: Pillowcase fibers are carefully embedded with copper infused technology, derived from the well-known essential mineral. Clinically proven to reduce the appearance of wrinkles for smoother, younger-looking skin in as little as 4 weeks.  OK, I have four weeks to determine if this pillowcase works to reduce wrinkles.  Ill come back and update my review then.

Before leaving this review, I have the freshly washed pillowcase here on my desk.  It measures 25 by 20.  It is colored a light copper brown and it does have a slight, not objectionable, metallic smell.

The cost of this pillowcase is high -- $60.  For that amount of money it ought to do what it promises.  Silk pillowcases are much, much cheaper and they do work well to pamper the face and neck.  That said, many five star reviews for this product attest to the fact that it does help to reduce wrinkles.  Well see!
summary: An expensive replacement for silk pillowcases.  I hope it works as advertised.

reviewText: I really like the iluminage Skin Pillow.  I have not noticed any difference in my skin but I have only been using it for a few weeks - I have noticed less hair breakage in the shower in the morning though - probably because my hair glides over the pillow.  The pillow itself is beautiful and really goes well with my existing decor and looks like an accent pillow propped on my bed.  I have not washed it yet - but it seems like it is good quality and will hold up.  I will update my review after a few months of use.

Is it a good pillowcase? yes, its super soft and lovely to sleep on ....except it smells like copper a bit and after awhile it felt rough. I have been sleeping on this for a week and I do not feel more refreshed, or wrinkle free, or rejuvinated. Maybe in time this will happen but I am impatient.
summary: its just a pillowcase with a hefty price

reviewText:
This is an interesting pillowcase with infused copper ions to help rejuvenate skin appearance during sleep. It is silky smooth and soft, and very well made. The envelope closure keeps my pillow inside and makes it neat and tidy. Having used it for some times now, I have to say it is really nice and cozy to sleep in. It does seem to make the wrinkles around the eye a little less prominent. Though I cant be sure if it is just my imagination or a placebo. Anyway, the biggest difference is that I no longer have creases on my face when I wake up. My old cotton pillowcase was a lot rougher which, unknowingly to me, probably was the cause of the creases.

All in all, I really like this pillowcase. Its silky smooth, comfortable and luxuriously looking. I can't say for sure but it does seem to help with my skin appearance somewhat. I hope the results would be more noticeable in 4 weeks per instructions. So far so good.

I love the feel of this!  Im not a fan of silk sheets and this is a wonderful blend that feels like silk with the softness of cotton.

I would pay this much if it reduced or lessened wrinkles. However, from my experience and examination I see no noticeable different. If this changes after the 4 weeks as stated in the instructions I will update the review.

It is  pleasant feeling pillow cover and there was no noticeable smell right out of the package.

An interesting concept.  I recall my grandfather who always wore a copper bracelet and swore by the benefits in combatting arthritis.

This pillowcase is a nicely finished, copper infused, 100% polyester item.  Very soft, and comes beautifully and novelly packaged in a cylindrical container.  Labeling indicates a 249 thread count and a dimension of 20" x 30" (mine is in Standard size).  Machine washable (NO fabric softener, NO ironing), and claims to retain effectiveness for 100 washings.  There is an initial odor out of the package, I recommend an initial washing before use (a good idea for all new textile products).  Made in China.  My experience? . . . .

A pleasure to sleep on.  Sleek and smooth.  The gentle contact alone should be plus for the face.  Judging, objectively, my own facial results after a week of use is hard.  I've never been a big mirror scrutinizer when awakening in the morning.  I suppose I can imagine some reduction in wrinkles (my 60+ face is not too bad to start with).  I certainly am sleeping well on this pillowcase, so the rest alone has a therapeutic benefit.  Theoretically, I really like the idea of the copper exposure.  Sorry if I appear to be waffling, but I want to offer a frank evaluation and, frankly, I'm not sure yet.

The price is not cheap.  But it's well made, a pleasure to sleep on, and a novel idea (the copper infusion) that I like and at this point I cannot disprove.
summary: Well made.  A pleasure to use.  Waiting to see if it works . . .

reviewText: I like this pillow case a lot. The open end tucks over the pillows so it stays in place. It's very soft. It has helped me reduce some lines. It's by far not a miracle, but it does help. My face seems to be staying the same. No deep wrinkling when I wake up. The only issue I have is the pillow seems to snag easily. I had a jagged finger nail I was not aware of until my finger snagged the pillowcase. So I just make sure my nails are always filed. I love the pillowcase
I give the pillow 3 stars for now because I'm not sure about the antiaging properties. I do wake up though with no creases on my face. That might be due to sleepery fabric though.
summary: I need to research more about copper etc

reviewText:
This is a great pillowcase. It fits my normal standard sized pillow perfectly and hasn't fallen apart from the washing machine so it seems to be holding up well. As for the claim about rejuvenation I'm not entirely sure yet since I haven't seen or felt any differently. It is very comfortable though as it is very soft and smooth.

It feels like a really nice pillowcase and I look forward to future results from my skin interacting with it.

This is a nice and soft pillow case.  It has a slight odor and you will want to wash it first.  I washed it in scent free detergent with cold water and some towels on delicate.  You cannot use fabric softener on this, so be careful using a dryer sheet with it.

It feels very soft, and it feels luxurious.  I've been using it for a few days, but I don't really have too many wrinkles.  It hasn't caused me to break out and hopefully makes me look younger over time.  It claims the action lasts the life of the product.  I like the feel of the pillow case and hope it keeps my skin feeling smooth.

While I haven't had or used this pillowcase long enough to experience any age-defying magic, I can tell you that the struggle and frustration to get the plastic wrap off of the container this pillow case came in definitely took a few years off my life.

It has a strong oder so it's something that I'd want to wash before using, but there's no specifications as to how this item should be wash. It notes that the pillow case is machine washable and to not use fabric softener, but I'm not familiar with this material so I'm not exactly sure what cycle and temperature it should be washed at. I'd be bummed if i washed out all the rejuvenating powers before getting to use it.
