I just wish there was a little more product for the buck but this did a great job that I probably will be buying more in the future.

If you are thinking about buying it I would definately give it a try!

My better-half used this. I really appreciate the light scent and I love the way it tousled his very thick hair. He just recently had it thinned and layered by a stylist and this Jack Black cream  just gave it the very finished, very sexy look that I adore. And, of course, his report was, "This stuff is pretty nice." That's high praise.

We will be purchasing this once the tube (which is a very generous size) is complete.

I have thick, straight, short hair, but I like to have a little fullness to it, without it blowing away or going flat.  I usually use a hair gel, which works great when I want it to be stiff and spiky.  This Jack Black texture cream gives me the hold I want without the stiffness.  Now I can enjoy a natural and sleek look, which is great for when I want a conservative look.  My hair also holds its shape through out the day.  I know I'll be using this texture creme for my daily grooming routine on a regular basis.
I'm a big fan of Jack Black, and this product was not a disappointment. A great, subtle, masculine smell.  It has a light hold that isn't greasy or hard.  A good product!

Good on short hair.  I have previously used Jack Black Hair Gel and it sometimes was a bit clumpy.  I don't have that problem with the texture cream.  My hair is pretty short and I comb it right after I get out of the shower.  The finish texture keeps my hair in place for a few hours and by that time my hair will stay on its own (I keep the front pushed slightly up and without product it would look like I have bangs).  The cream is easy to wipe off and not sticky with a somewhat pleasant scent.  I was using Baxeter of California pomaide before the Jack Black and I can now say that the Jack Black Finish Texture will be my go to hair product.
summary: Not sure it would work as well on long hair as it does on my short hair.

reviewText:
This is a nice, easy cream.

Pros:
-"Sleek finish" is a good description. It's not greasy, but it does give you a healthy luster. I like it.
-Hold is just medium. I found this to have a little bit weak hold for my taste, but I tend to prefer a strong clay pomade, so given that this is labeled a "flexible hold" I think it's about right Zero crunchiness.
-Pleasant smell. The "olive & rosemary" works out to a neutral, not-too-chemical scent.

Cons:
-None, so long as you're looking for medium hold and not something stronger.

This is one product that "does what it says on the tin". Recommended.

This is a very impressive texture cream..The first thing I noticed was that it didn't leave any sticky feeling residue on my hands after application.  Then, after my hair dried, I noticed how soft and manageable it was.  There was no crunchy feeling but yet no fly away hair either.  Just a thumbnail size dollop was just right so the tube should last awhile.

The man of the house uses this texturizer, but because my hair is short, I use it occasionally too.  It's perfect for hair that is on the dry side, as the natural oils and botanical extract ingredients restore moisture and leave a smoother look without feeling greasy or weighted down.  The term texturizer always confuses me--some brands labeled that way give a tousled piecey look, but Jack Black Sleek Finish doesn't.  Instead, this lightweight cream does exactly what its name implies--tones hair down just a notch.  To me it's more of a hairdressing conditioner that helps tame frizziness.  This may not apply to men, but I've noticed it takes much longer to dry my layered bob-length hair when using this product--that's okay because the trade-off is better behaved hair and some added body.

I have oily, baby fine hair with no body and most of these types of products weigh the hair down and make it feel oily about half-way through the day. I have tried American Crew Molding Clay and a Dove for Men paste and while both are nice products I have the same issue.

When I was given a chance to try this for free as a Vine reviewer I didn't have high expectations, but I liked the fact that it's described as having strong hold and a matte finish, which is what I wanted... And it works better than the others have. I doesn't add any additional shine and it holds pretty well. And, a big factor for me, is that it has a pleasant smell that goes away quickly, and enough so that as I sit here typing this I can't quire recall how to describe it.
summary: Description is true: Matte finish, strong, hold, and a minimal, pleasant smell

reviewText: While this seems quite expensive, it performs well providing a strong hold with a matte finish (dry look) and adding some texture and weight to your hair. It's similar to and compares favorably to American Crew: Classic Fiber, 3 oz but less greasy feeling, more clean feeling, with a bit less hold. This has a bit of a basil type scent that isn't really noticeable at all once on your hair.

I have thick curly hair and most product just makes my hair flat and curly. This however (much to my surprise) didn't. I only used just a little bigger than the size of a pea. Used my hands real fast to soften it up and then applied it all over, restyling my dry hair. It kept my hair in place, only slightly curly and didn't flatten it.

Its not greasy or sticky after it dries. I even mowed the lawn and sweated up a bit and the clay still kept my hair in place. It also doesn't look like i have anything in my hair, its matte so there's no glops of shiny stuff.

It is a bit expensive but you only need a little bit so it will last a long time and the fact that it worked on my thick curly hair is worth the price.
summary: Did the trick on my thick curly hair

reviewText: I received both the Jack Black wax pomade and this product.  While I really like the wax, the clay pomade is probably my all time favorite.  I get a fantastic hold without a greasy, unnatural look by using just a little bit of this applied to damp hair.  No greasy residue, no shiny giveaway, just a great look that holds all day.  I highly recommend this.
summary: Just a little dab'l do ya

reviewText:
I really love this stuff...
I did not need much at all, and I got the same effect as using my bed head wax... Very light not sticky... I love that when I used my dry towel it came right off of my hands, it smells awesome. It might be expensive, but it seems like it's going to go really far and last me awhile. I don't really have anything bad to say about it.

My usual pomade is Baxter of California Clay Pomade, which promises the same "matte finish" and "strong/firm" hold as this pomade, so I can do a direct comparison. In the end? The two are fairly equal, although they have their own strengths.

Where the Baxter is better:
-The Baxter pomade has a firmer hold. If the Jack Black is 4/5, the Baxter is a 5/5. With the Baxter I can walk through strong winds and my hair doesn't even feel the breeze. With the Jack Black my hair certainly moves, but it tends to stay in place, so that at the end of a day I look pretty close to where I started. Both products have very good hold, but the Baxter is the winner.
-Probably thanks to the firmer hold, I prefer the end result of the Baxter. It really sets my hair the way I want
-To my eye the Baxter even looks a little less greasy than the Jack Black- the Baxter is the better "matte finish". If I were to rate them on matte finish, I'd say the Baxter is a 4/5 (still looks like you've got a wet product in your hair, not a true "matte"), while the Jack Black is a 3/5. Neither is greasy, but the Jack Black looks a little more wet than the Baxter.

Where Jack Black is better:
-Easier to spread. The Baxter feels like it's raw clay in your hands, and can easily leave small clumps if you're not careful. The Jack Black spreads much more easily, so if you're running out the door you can apply it more quickly with less danger of clumps.

While it might look like I stacked the deck in favor of the Baxter, the ease at which the Jack Black spreads really is a killer. The Baxter pomade really goes on like modeling clay, it benefits from a little extra dip of water on your hands and a little time to warm up. If you're in a rush, you can end up with globs of raw clay in your hair. The Jack Black is much more creamy, so it goes on quickly with much less risk. Personally I'm okay with the extra work of the Baxter, but so long as you don't mind the wetness of the Black and you can deal with its good-but-not-perfect hold, the Jack Black is the better pomade for a quick application. So each of these pomades has their own application, meaning the discerning gentleman has his choice.

A couple other quick comparisons:

VS Jack Black Gel Pomade: The gel works like the "Dapper Dan" in the movie "Oh Brother, Where Art Thou?". The gel has much lower hold, and a slicked-back appearance. These products are for two entirely different hair styles.
VS Jack Black Wax Pomade. The wax pomade is a very generic pomade. Average hold, average shine. If you don't need a cement-like hold, and you don't mind a little shine, the wax might be perfect for you.

I have thinning hair, and in recent years, have moved away from wet or gel-based styling products (they don't make thinning hair look good).  Now I typically use grooming creams, fibers, or clays. This Jack Black clay is a great product because it provides medium definition without adding any slickness.

It will make your hair look good without looking like there is an abundance of styling product in it. In comparison to American Crew fiber, this clay is easier to pull from the canister.  It spreads smoothly, and has virtually no scent.

This a nice pomade that holds my hubby's uncontrollable hair quite well. I have very fine thin hair and I tried it and I also like it. It does have pretty good hold without making your hair feel stiff and hard. It does give a matte finish. I have a problem with very strong fragrances and will not let my hubby wear anything too strong as it makes me sick. This pomade has a very light scent that is tolerable. We both like it and use it. It's easy to apply and work through the hair, and after styling, you can't really tell you have product in your hair, which I like a lot. We will definitely buy it again.
summary: Great product for thick or thin hair.

reviewText: Great for piecing and finger styling. Has holding power without making hair hard or crunchy. It doesn't look like there's any product in your hair when you use it, as your hair stays rather dry and matte... whereas hair gel would add a sheen or shiny look, in comparison. Overall good stuff, especially with certain types of styling. If you do a lot of strategic placing, this is the type of product you'd like.
summary: great for piecing and finger styling

reviewText: Really good product for hold and a neat appearance. I grew up in a time when pomades were out of fashion, but I like the look and thanks to shows like Mad Men for making it stylish again. Works well on dry and slightly damp hair but did not perform as well with a blow dryer. This is best for men with shorter hair. Quality product.

I had heard good things about the Jack Black brand so we wanted to try out some of their hair products. We have been trying out three different kinds of hair pomades (clay, wax, and gel), we didn't care for any of them but this one was the worst.

Both my young boys have slightly wavy hair so I have to put something in their hair to keep it in place while they are at school all day. We use mousse, hair gel, etc. Weve been using different Jack Black pomades for the last few days. The Clay Pomade was the worst for us. I couldn't get it to mix with their hair. It left white clumps all in their hair. I mixed it in my hands first to get it warm and even mix it with water but it won't really warm or mix. I literally had to go back through their hair and pull chunks of white clay out.

We won't be using this one again.
summary: Chunks of White Left in Hair

reviewText:
I picked this up for my husband, but I've also been using it, too!

My husband has a short, cropped style, and this is great for adding texture.  He usually uses Jonathan Dirt and does prefer the Dirt over this since Dirt gives a bit more piecey-ness to his hair, but he does like this, too.

It washes out cleanly, and adds a matte texture to the hair with little to no shine.

I've been using it to piece out the ends of my short bob.  While I like the look, however, it doesn't hold my hair in place for that long.  (I realize, of course, that I'm not the target audience for this product, so my review of four stars is based on my husband's review of it.  :-) )
summary: Greats nice matte texture to your hair

reviewText: This hair gel does what it promises in that it won't make hair crunchy. However, it also fails to hold a style to any significant degree. We gave it a good-faith effort for about a month with my son's hair and decided that it simply doesn't work to maintain his pretty simple styling either. Not much else really needs to be mentioned in a review of this unfortunately.
summary: Doesn't Work: Not Crunchy, But Won't Hold Either

reviewText:
My husband often uses a hair gel to keep his hair in place and  to keep it looking neat. His hair isn't very long, just enough to get messed up. He is always willing to try different hair products and thought this might be a good one. He was mostly disappointed with this one, mainly because it didn't do a good job of holding his hair. The scent was kind of citrusy and a little strong, but that would have been okay because it disappates rather quickly. I thought it smelled pretty good. But in order to get this gel to hold his hair he had to use a lot, enough that it gunked up his hair and made it feel dirty. So we really can't recommend this one.

The company apparently made another gel prior to this that people liked. It sounds like they should have stuck with the old formula. All too often companies try to improve on a popular product and change some of the very things that made it popular for ingredients that don't perform as well.

Works ok but does leave your hair feeling a little crunchy and stiff.  You can also notice a sticky feeling as well after use.  It states you will have neither but you have both.  It does work as a gel though.  The smell is fruity smelling and I really liked it.

The most important thing about my hair gel products is does it hold throughout the day. And that is a yes for this product. I like to change the style of my hair regularly and have straight hair so that is usually not a problem. I tried it a few times changing styles and it held up good. Also like the scent of these Jack Black products (just started trying them out). The only thing is the price is too high-unless you are getting a bigger bottle the price should be lower.

Did a good job for me and would use in the future.

I have hopelessly fine long hair; life occasionally requires me to wrestle it into an undo. Within minutes of the finished products, hair begins to escape. I tried this as a holding gel and was pleased that it held the flyaways but didn't give me helmet head. I really like the scent that admittedly is not feminine. The combination of grapefruit, sage and ginger really worked for me.

My husband has curly hair which is difficult to tame and somewhat thinner than it was I. His younger years. I convinced him to try a little and he liked it a lot. He's not a hair product kind of guy but recognized the brand. We are both using it now and are both satisfied.
summary: Effective hold for him and her. We both like the scent.

reviewText:
My husband actually laughed when he used this gel. He couldn't figure out what it was for, since it apparently didn't do a thing. His hair after application was like he had just washed it with baby shampoo: super soft and with zero control.

If you are looking for a hair gel, keep looking. This isn't worth the tube it's packaged in.
summary: No hold, so what's the point?

reviewText: This product smells great, a mix of grapefruit and ginger, both of which I like.  While the label claims that the gel is "Firm Hold," I would, to some degree, beg to differ.  The hold is pretty good IF you "do" your hair with the gel, style it and then leave it alone.  Also, don't go out into a strong wind because you might have to re-style your hair, which will break the gel's hold somewhat, causing stray hairs to drop onto your forehead.  Bear in mind that I have fine, short hair.  I prefer Jack Black's Wax Pomade over this product because it gives me a stronger hold.  The hair gel might work for you and your hair, but unfortunately wasn't the best for me.  It will likely be something I use on weekend evenings after I've done some yard work, showered and then wish to have my hair styled for a few hours on an evening in watching TV, reading, etc.  I don't trust its hold in the elements.
summary: Somewhat firm as long as you don't meddle with your hair after styling it.  Smells great.

reviewText:
I just tried this after getting a trim this afternoon.
I glanced at a few of the reviews that compare this formulation to a previous version of this product. Since I am not in any position to make comparisons I like this product and think it does a very good job infusing my hair with both body as well as extra volume.
To avoid excessive stiffness I applied this product to the roots of my freshly washed and dried hair that remained damp. After that I combed it through my hair and used my hair dryer at the lowest setting to quickly complete the drying process. While doing this I fluffed my hair directing the dryer's nozzle at the roots.
Considering I just had my hair done it looks like it has volume and the illusion of length. I use a lot of product because I have very fine and silky hair. Additionally, I test a lot of hair products. I liked this product because used sparringly it isn't excessively sticky and doesn't appear to have a drying effect. There is a little stiffness in the root area but expected this because of the way I applied the product.
This is made for a man, but because it is not strongly scented and what smell there is seems to disipate quickly I see no reason why a woman can't use this as well.
This is a little pricey based on the size, but used sparringly it should last for awhile.

I have never tried the original gel, so this review is based solely on the performance of this product for me.

I used this to help bring out the waves of my shoulder-length hair, and it did ok, but not as well as other products. One of my favorite products is Paul Mitchell's Sculpting gel, and this one is not as good as that. I felt like this product was somewhat sticky, and my hair was drying in crunchy delineated locks. (I used about a nickel-sized glob.) It took a lot of working through with my fingers to break up the crunchy sections and get a natural look of waves.  I think that's kind of ironic because "without the crunch" is part of the ad copy. It is "reworkable" if I mist my hair and re-scrunch.  It does smell really good, so that's a plus.  Is it "body building"?  That seems like a bold claim. It was able to help my hair hold a good mess of waves, and my hair definitely looks like it has body, so maybe so.  I think on short hair you'd have to be very sparing with this  or you'll end up with a crunchy mess. Since the tube is quite small (for a hair gel), maybe that's a good thing.

No hold. I don't know what Jack Black is thinking with their "Max Hold" products, as they all seem to be more like "a little bit of hold", whereas their "strong hold" products are pretty sturdy.

I mean there's not much else to say. I used more than should be necessary, and I could barely tell I had anything in my hair. The level of hold is almost nonexistant. Even with very short hair and a large amount of product, this did absolutely nothing to hold my hair in place. It's about as much help as rubbing lotion into your hair- sure that'll weigh down the follicles a bit, but that's all you're getting.

But, there's nothing offensive about the product. It smells fine and it doesn't harm my hair. The finish is good. So I can't take all points off, but close to it.

Smells good and performs good. Give good holding power and a little sleek shine without being extremely stiff or crunchy. It washes out without leaving any residue in your hair and it doesn't turn into a white flaky mess while it's in your hair. You only need a little bit for good control so the tube will actually last awhile. Same great quality and scent as other Jack Black products.
summary: Nice hold, without excessive stiffness or crunch

reviewText: I have been using the Jack Black Gel for the past few years and was bummed when they changed the formula.  It it ain't broke don't fix it but I was pleasantly surprised that the new formula is just as good.  I have thick hair that I keep short and just need a about a dime size of gel to keep it in place for a work day (it loses its hold after about 8 hours).  Careful if you put too much in your hair will have good in it and will harden and make your hair sticky.  Only thing I noticed with new formula is that the gel has a bit more scent but once in the hair my wife has not mentioned that I smell different and the product is not as thick which in my mind is a good thing.

I received this product for free as part of the Vine program and per usual I glance at reviews to see what others thought of the same product before I submit my own review. I am a bit surprised to find that this hair gel has received so many negative reviews - overwhelmingly 1 or 2-star reviews (as of the writing of this review). That has not been my experience using this product for a few days, however, I do not have the history with Jack Black Hair Gel that some other reviewers do.

My "go-to" hair styling product for the last several years has been American Crew Forming Cream. That product strikes a good compromise between styling hold and control and avoids hard, stiff hair a.k.a. helmet head. It is, however, a bit pricey so I am always on the lookout for other products with similar performance at a cheaper price. I think Jack Black Building Hair Gel is that product even if the savings are marginal.

I've worn this product two days; both days work days where I keep my hair neat and tidy. The product has performed great! The gel is clear, definitely fruity smelling (no surprise there), and holds my hair while not giving me hard, stiff hair. The Jack Black definitely is stiffer than my American Crew forming cream but nothing like the cheap drugstore gel of my youth. Honestly any stiffer and you might as well buy a tub-o-gel (in neon blue) from the drugstore.

I found that styling my (short) hair was as easy as the forming cream I use. The Jack Black product held my hair throughout the day without issue. So for me this is definitely a product that I would purchase and use again.

I did deduct one star for the following reasons:
 Stiffness: Simply compared to the American Crew product I regularly use.
 Smell: I'm not a fan of the fruity smell of the product when first putting it on. It's not noticeable after a few minutes but definitely perceptible at first.
summary: Good Alternative to American Crew Forming Creams & Pomade

reviewText:
Not my kind of product. I have two issues with the formula:

High Shine: Really they mean "slicked back". This isn't intended to make your hair look voluminous and healthy, but greased down like in the movie "Oh Brother, Where Art Thou?", that kind of look. I wasn't expecting that.

Max Hold: This I just disagree with, unless that's as strong as this line goes. Using a generous amount given my hair is longer than usual, I applied the pomade and went about my day. My hair never seemed to have "max hold" and by the end of the day my hair was quite a bit messier than my usual clay pomade. Perhaps it's a good amount of hold for this type of product, but "max hold"? Doesn't seem that way.

So if you want a good amount of hold in slicked back hair, this would be a wonderful product for you. But it certainly wasn't what I was expecting.

This is very much like a traditional pomade in that it gives your hair a wet look and holds quite strongly. It's not quite as oily as a traditional pomade however, which is nice. It also has a nice mild after shave type scent which is hardly noticeable once applied.

If you don't want a shiny look, look for a different product as this one is for a shiny look.

That said, this seems too expensive!
summary: This is very much like a traditional pomade in that it gives your hair ...

reviewText:
This is a different look for me and I like it. It's a slicked back look and only takes a dab on a fingertip for me. I've got kind of a big head so the slicked back looks natural for me, plus it has that serious look that changes my behavior for the better by reminding me what I am based on what people tell me I am.

This is easy, easy to apply. Just mix on hands and then run through hair. Follow up by combing straight back. It lasts all day despite using so little product. Washes out easily.

Another good Jack Black product. I use all kinds of gel/lotions in my hair to create various looks depending what my moods are on that particular day. The most important thing is does it hold my hair in place and how long does it stay. And this product stays all day long and in the place that I want it to so that's a big thumbs up. Also like the smell that lasts all day long too. The only thing is I wish there was more for the price but it does a good job I can not argue with that.
summary: Hair Stays in Place all day long!

reviewText:
Slicked-back hair is in fashion once again.

This gel hair pomade has a sweet citrusy fragrance reminiscent of barbershop aftershave balm.

It is easy to comb through the hair, produces a high sheen, and does a good job holding the hair in place.

The plastic jar holds 2.75 oz.

Ingredients:  Water (Aqua), PEG-40 Hydrogenated Castor Oil, Steareth-20, Polyester-5, Propanediol, C12-15 Alkyl Benzoate, Glycerin, Phenyl Trimethicone, Hydrogenated Ethylhexyl Olivate, PPG-5-Ceteth-20, Jojoba Esters, PEG-12 Dimethicone, Citrus Grandis (Grapefruit) Peel Oil*, Lavandula Angustifolia (Lavender) Oil*, Macrocystis Pyrifera (Kelp) Extract*, Basilicum (Basil) Leaf Extract*, Ocimum Adansonia Digitata Seed Oil*, Moringa Oleifera Seed Oil*, Schinziophyton Rautanenii Kernel Oil*, Sclerocarya Birrea Seed Oil*, Camellia Sinensis Leaf Extract*, Melaleuca Alternifolia (Tea Tree) Leaf Oil, Salvia Lavandulaefolia (Sage) Leaf Oil, Panthenol, Hydrogenated Olive Oil Unsaponifiables, Ethylhexylglycerin, Cetrimonium Chloride, Phenoxyethanol, Chlorphenesin, Benzoic Acid, Sorbic Acid, Acetamide MEA, Tetrasodium EDTA, BHT, Benzyl Alcohol, Limonene, Linalool. *Certified Organic

Jack Black Gel Pomade is the greatest thing ever for slicked-back hair styles.  Yes, it's the greaser style, and if that's your thing, this is your product.  It's also certified organic.  It smells a bit like citrus to me.  Lime, to be exact.

You can also use this to get the perfect part in your hair.  There are lots of videos online that can show you how to do that.

This product is cruelty free, organic, and Dermatology tested.  If you need your hair to stay in place with high shine and max hold, this is your product.  The 2.75 ounce container will last for months.
summary: Good High End Product for Creating Slicked-Back Styles & Great Parts

reviewText:
Both my young boys have slightly wavy hair so I have to put something in their hair to keep it in place while they are at school all day. We use mousse, hair gel, etc. Weve been using different Jack Black pomades for the last few days.

We didn't care for any of the Pomades but the gel was probably the only one that we will probably use up. For us, the wax and clay ones were just too hard to use. The gel is more user friendly.

It states that it give a high shine and max hold. I think the hold is medium not high. By days end, their hair looks messy. The shine is not really a shine but more of their hair looking greasy.

We aren't big Jack Black Pomade fans.
summary: Medium Hold, Greasy Looking Not Shine

reviewText: This is a great pomade, especially if you style your hair using your fingers and not a comb or brush. It's very thick, my husband only has to use about a nickle size amount on his hair. It holds the style all day long but it doesn't make your hair hard. Very nice product and definitely recommended.

My husband used this first. Instead of using a little discretion, he took a fairly good amount of this (over a teaspoon) and his thinning hair looked slicked down and bordering on a helmet head look. Nothing moved....he could have been stuck smack dab in the middle of a tornado and that hair wouldn't have shifted one bit. I didn't want to touch it.
I used this this morning on my damp hair. It has very little scent and what is there quickly dissipates. I dabbed the tips of my fingers of one hand in the jar and removed a small amount. I rubbed it in my palms and just sort of ran it through my hair and then combed my hair. I was going for a slicked back look for the beach today. My hair stayed in place, but being very fine and silky it seemed to have more texture. While it looked shinier (my hair is a medium ash blonde), it didn't look greasy or gluey.
I actually like the way it looks and holds. My only advice is go easy when using this. It takes a very small amount to get results.
summary: A Little Goes A Long Way

reviewText: I can not say enough about Jack Black products.  I buy them for my husband as much as possible.  We had  not tried this one yet and my husband was anxious to try it.  I thought that it would be perfect for styling his hair.  I actually used just a teensy swipe of it to keep wispy hair strands back when I put my own hair into a loose bun.  So...it has a great sort of sticky consistency.  You really just use a tiny bit to get all of the control that a short men's style needs.  It has no discernible scent.  It does what it says it will do.  If you want control and shine...this is a great product.  Men who love "spiky" styles will love this one!

I personally don't like this either.. I use Suavecito and love it!

This is super high shine, and i mean HIGH shine.. its very very greasy and oily.. Its not the look im going for. the scent is fairly decent.
summary: I personally don't like this either

reviewText: Directions for use and a list of the ingredients can be uncovered  by peeling back the round label on the underside of this pot of Jack Black Gel Pomade.  I've tried this on dry hair and on slightly damp hair and must say that a little dab will do you in either application.  Having a very slight scent which dissipates after rubbing the small amount in the palms of the hands, it is easier on damp hair, but there is no reason to stop there since it provides a bit of a shine either way.  In my experience, a greasier look is achieved when a heftier amount of the pomade is used, but with the recommended dab, the hairs are nicely directed by the palms of the hands and a shine tops off a ruled head of hair.  Although marketed for men, there is no reason in the world that women cannot use this grooming product which sure beats Alberto VO5 that my parents used.  The list of ingredients is comforting and the company has impressive ethics.
summary: Little effort, a small dab and your hairs can be tamed

reviewText: I used baby Mustela products with my first child, so when I found myself pregnant with my second I figured I would try a Mustela mommy product! This stretch mark cream did not disappoint. I didn't have many stretch marks, but I used the cream to prevent them. I loves the thickness of the cream, not too thick, and the scent. I had no problems with the smell and actually enjoyed it very much. I used it daily until delivering my son and then continued using it on my body.
summary: This stretch mark cream did not disappoint. I didn't have many stretch marks

reviewText: I do not have stretch marks from my recent pregnancy but I love this cream as a moisturizer after showers. It is easily absorbed and works well for my dry skin. Stretch marks are genetic so caveat emptor.

reviewerName: Keleigh Crigler Hadley, author of Revenge Inc.
reviewText: My stretch marks are too old to disappear, (tears), but I use this cream on my cracked feet. It definitely keeps my feet soft and supple without being greasy. And being that your feet are conduits to your organs, I appreciate that this cream is non-toxic.

Ok, so if you are looking to help keep from getting stretch marks or even to reduce them, this cream will not help with those results. It is a nice cream. It goes on easy and non greasy. A few others mention a scent. I did not have any issues with the scent. Again, however, that was not why I was looking forward to this cream. Don't waste your money for no results.

Having a baby is real hard on a mothers body. I remember my OB/GYN telling me it takes 2 years for a mothers body to recover from childbirth.  So I ordered this Mustela stretch mark prevention cream for my daughter-in-law that was expecting. She just recently blessed us with our first grandson. He was a large baby, and she is a tiny, petite young woman. She told me she has some stretch marks but that she's putting this cream on everyday and it seems to help. She told me that she was using a different cream, but she thought the Mustela was better than her other product. Plus she's more appreciative of this cream since it's more natural and paraben free and won't hurt the baby while she's breastfeeding. Mother and baby products are so advanced since my childbirth days, and I'm so happy and grateful for that. Thanks Mustela!

I love that the Stretch Marks Prevention Cream doesn't have a funny odor. It actually has a pleasant smell. If you apply more that the directed amount you are left with a residue, but if you apply a thin layer like the directions state you should use then it goes on smoothly without staining clothes or any residue. It also works well as an overall body lotion to moisturize your skin, anywhere other than your belly. I haven't noticed any stretch marks.
summary: I love that the Stretch Marks Prevention Cream doesn't have a ...

reviewText: I ordered this cream because it says its compatible with breastfeeding. My baby is already here but I was using it after the baby to see if it would diminish stretch marks already there. This creams sounds amazing since in studies "96% of women did not develop stretch marks during their pregnancy". Although this is hypoallergenic, I don;t think this is compatible with breastfeeding! The scent is nice, but it is very strong and I don't use strongly scented lotions while I am breastfeeding because I don't want it to bother my newborn!

I gave the Mustela Stretch Marks Prevention Cream to my daughter in law to try as she is currently pregnant. She hasbeen using this cream for a few weeks and so far has been happy with results. She does  have stretch marks from previous pregnancies so did not expect this cream to get rid of those,  but wanted to minimize how quickly they started to show with this pregnancy. The cream has kept her skin very moisturized and soft. She uses about a quarter size amount daily and that provides enough coverage for her entire midsection, front and back areas. The cream goes on thin but provides great moisture. The scent is pleasing; it is soft but not overpowering. We are in the winter dry months and this cream has helped relieve any of the itching that comes from dry skin brought on by they dry air and skin stretching for baby. Does not feel tacky or sticky like other creams she has used in the past.

This Mustela stretch mark prevention cream is white in color and has the consistency of lotion.  It goes on easily, absorbed into my skin quickly, light weight and not greasy at all.  I feel like it made my skin feel really soft and smooth.  The big downfall for me was how strong the fragrance is.  I am super sensitive to smells.  I can't walk into the bath and body store in the mall without getting a headache.  I don't wear perfume or anything really heavily scented because it gives me a headache.  I can use scented products if the scent is light, subtle and fades fast.  I was disappointed that this stretch mark prevention cream has a heavy floral scent.  While the scent is good, it is heavy and lasting so I couldn't take the scent and eventually had to wash it off.  I also want to mention in my first trimester (and most of my second) I has horrible morning sickness and was incredibly sensitive to smells/fragrances (they made my nausea so much worse).  I had to use fragrance free everything or I would have a headache, the nausea would be intensified and I would be sick.  Just something to keep in mind if you are pregnant, really nauseous and sensitive to fragrance than this might not work for you.  If you have no issues with fragrance than this prevention cream will make your skin feel soft and smooth!  This cream is hypoallergenic, and free from parabens, phthalates, phenoxyethanol, bisphenols A and S, caffeine and alcohol.  Overall I thought the cream felt nice on my skin and made it feel soft but I can't comment on the stretch mark prevention because I was unable to use it consistently due to the fragrance. I would love to give this product another try if it was fragrance free and had no scent.
summary: Made my skin feel soft and smooth but be aware it has a very heavy floral scent

reviewText: I was excited to review the Mustela stretch mark cream as I always have high hopes for finding something new and different that will improve the elasticity of my skin.  My first impressions... The product comes in a squeeze tube with a clear flip cap which immediately broke when I tried opening it. Not a big deal but....  The cream itself comes out rather thin and is easy to spread around on your skin.  You will need to rub it in until the white texture disappears.  The cream definitely gives skin a different feeling from all the other products I have used and does not dry out. The effect is quite noticable.  The one disappointing aspect of the product has to be the scent and fragrance.  It lingers for hours upon hours and can be distracting.  If you are sensitive to smells or odors this will not be the product for you.  Overall, I certainly think this has a positive effect for my skin and will be using it during the night only due to the fragrance.
summary: Good product that increases elasticity but not a fan of the fragrance.

reviewText: My doctor said that nothing can prevent stretch marks and that it is genetics. "If your mother had stretchmarks or your fathers mother then you are more likely to have them and the elasticity of your skin"  With that being said I still gave it a try and I ended up having to wipe it off as it has a pretty strong floral smell. I did not find it to be similar to any other mustela product I have used and was left gagging.

I've never been pregnant but I have lateral hip stretch marks from growing 6" in a year in high school. They are easily irritated and prone to dermatitis. I also have a large thoracic scar from childhood heart surgery. This also is prone to be irritated by nearly anything.

This cream s a great balm and protectant for scars and stretch marks. It is a white cream that goes on clear. It is not sticky or greasy. It does not stain my clothes. It has significant reduced redness and localized dermatitis on my scar. I also like that this product has a safety strip to prevent tampering.

The fragrance is different than other Mustela products, like a light floral. It is pleasant and does not bother me or make itself known. Just FYI, this cream has uses beyond pregnancy concerns. I like it a lot.
summary: Good for scars and existing stretch marks.

reviewText: My teenage son loves this product. The 1st can I bought at the barber lasted him a year!!! That's amazing to me, so I don't mind spending more than your average cost of  a hair product bc it's totally worth it! He has very thick Italian hair with the pompadour cut/style. Use it on dry hair and make sure you lather/work it very well in your hands before applying. It holds his style all day long through school, gym and sports!! A regular men's Pomade just doesn't hold the hair back and keep it in place after an hour or so, especially if you go to the gym or do any kind of sports. My husband tried it in his hair, which btw is not thick at all and has started thinning a little bit, and he doesn't care for it. But that's not really the type of product he should be using for his hair type. Now if you have thick, coarse or a longer cut/style you'll love it!!! No other product has held up as well, and we've tried them all. It smells so fresh and clean too. I love the scent! Layrite cement is truly an unbeatable quality product!! Great seller, fast shipping, packaged securely. We will definitely be repurchasing here when it gets low. I've attached a few pictures of the old style can compared to the new one, which is also much better at keeping the product airtight when not in use. 100% Recommend!!!

This stuff is ok but not as good as the regular super hold pomade. It gives you that icky feeling by the end of the day. I also find that it does not wash out as easily as the pomade, especially not just with water. The shine is a little less and it is more matte feeling than the pomade but honestly not a huge difference. Same vanilla scent which is nice.

If you absolutely want low shine/matte, this stuff is ok. Otherwise I'd opt for the regular Layrite Super Hold Poomade
summary: Not as great as the standard Layrite pomade

reviewText: The pomade does the job it was intended for but the pomade seems to leave a slight white residue.

The fragrance on this conditioner was so incredibly strong that it literally made me gag. I was really looking forward to trying this, because it's a brand with a great reputation, and the texture was thick and looked highly moisturizing. However, I'm very sensitive to overly strong fragrances, and both the fragrance itself and the sheer overwhelming quality of it made it so I didn't even want to put this on my hair. I really wish companies would make it clearer if they are going to use this quantity of fragrance in their product. I use a wide variety of hair products in my very long hair, and many of them, indeed most of them, do have some level of fragrance, but this is way over the top.

My long hair tends to frizz, and my daughter's fine hair tends to tangle, so we use a lot of leave-in conditioners and detanglers. This is by far my favorite.

It's an effective detangler and moisturizer, and leaves hair soft and frizz free with not residue/product feeling on the hair. My hair looks and feels nice and clean, but without the usual frizz. Generally, with leave-ins, there's a bit of a tradeoff, and you pay for your detangles and low frizz with hair that fills just a bit tacky, and your hair will tend to need to be washed more. This was as close to freshly-rinsed hair as I've ever experienced. I'm very, very pleased.

I have medium textured, dark, long layered hair, that's fairly straight if I comb it out wet or wavy if I leave it to dry naturally, which I prefer. My waves look great and feel clean air-drying with this. My daughter has fine straight hair which can get really weighted down by other leave-ins, and this one left her fine, light hair looking clean and shiny.

The scent is pleasant and understated. The pump dispenses judiciously. Great all around.
summary: My very favorite leave-in. No frizz, and hair looks and feels clean and soft, zero residue.

reviewText: My daughter has long, naturally curly hair. She is really lucky because it is so pretty, but it has its drawbacks. It takes a long time to dry and gets tangled easily. She often looks for leave-in type products, but so many make her hair sticky or greasy. This is really nice. It smells really really good, too! She mostly just uses it on the ends where most of the damage occurs. She will be getting this again when she runs out.

I was happy to give this a try.

I have very long, naturally wavy hair.  In humidity, it can frizz.

The product is lightweight - it doesn't weigh my hair down and doesn't look greasy. (Note: I always worry about that with a leave in product, but this disappears wonderfully.)  You only need to use a bit, though because of my hair length, I do think I used a bit more than some other reviewers.

The scent is mild but pleasant.

Finally, and most importantly, it tamed the frizzies!

Will continue to use!

I really like that this leave-in conditioner can be used on dry hair.
During the winter months, when it's so dry inside, I apply this on the ends before bed.
I believe it makes a bit of a difference in the amount of breakage as I toss and turn.
Not crazy about the scent, but it isn't so overpowering that you can't sleep.

It can also be used as an after-shampoo leave in conditioner on wet hair.

Even the slightest hint of humidity causes my wife's hair to frizz out of control. When we have time off we go to the tropics where the extreme humidity takes her frizziness over the top. This arrived in time for a vacation to Yelapa, Mexico with about the highest humidity yet. She tried this the first morning and it worked far beyond her expectations. She had not the slightest trace of frizz yet her hair wasn't flat or oily and looked full and healthy. It styled easily. For myself I don't have her problem so I wasn't impressed for my own sake but she will be sure to always have this before we travel.

Okay so I've cut my hair down to a more manageable length and it has decided that it want's to go very "cotton ball" with this newfound cut.  My hair is thin but there is a ton of it - about half of it is strait and the other half is curly (no rhyme or reason as to which half at any given moment) the key is that my hair is dry.  Very very dry.  It's not quite to the "haystack" look yet - but I figure when I hit 40 I will probably attain that quality.

I have tried several different hair products to see what makes my hair as simple to do as possible while still looking okay.  Many of the leave in conditioners (which is what I am considering this) leave my hair looking like I rolled around in grease - or that I haven't washed my hair in a month.  I purchase a lot from Sephora so I tend to get a lot of samples from them and have tried many different conditioners, oils, moisturizers etc.

After using this a bit here is my take on it.  My hair is about 4-5 inches long and I don't need a full pump of this product the full pump would probably still be a bit too much back when my hair was shoulder length.  This isn't a bad thing - just letting you know that you don't need a lot of this at any given time to have a great effect. I have found that using this product leaves my hair much less dry feeling - it's bouncy and moisturized without being greasy.  The scent is also very nice - it's an attractive scent that is very light, nothing overpowering.  It is rare that I try a hair product and decide that I would actually buy it again.  I honestly plan on getting more of this when I run out.  It appears pricy at first but with the tiny amount that you need - it will outlast most of the other products by a long shot.
summary: I would definately buy this again

reviewText: This Obliphica Seaberry moisture cream really hydrates my hair without making it greasy.  You don't need to use a lot of this cream to hydrate our hair and it has a nice scent to it which isn't overpowering.  I usually put this on my hair when I get home from work so it works overnight to moisturize my hair.

Obliphica Professional Seaberry Moisture Cream has the texture of a lotion, bluish with a verysubtle fruity fragrance that fades quickly.

It really helps with tangles, as my hair is course and dry, I've found it softens the hair and adds silkiness. Having recently overprocessed my hair, this mosturizing cream really helped the brittleness and damage.

Using this leave-in conditioner has been a very pleasant experience and all I can do is rave about the product. I found no flaws in its use at all.
summary: Has Really Improved my Dry Over Processed Hair

reviewText: This is a leave-in conditioner is recommended for damaged, weakened hair.  My color treated and heat styled hair can be a bit on the damaged side so I thought I would test this out.  This conditioner is recommended for medium to coarse hair and i found I had to be careful not to add too much to my medium hair or it would get weighed down.  The scent on this was light and pleasant.  I found my hair seemed soft and more manageable.  Overall, a good product but probably best for thick to coarse hair.
summary: Leave in conditioner for thick to coarse hair

reviewText:
My hair is curly/wavy below shoulder-length and although I have a lot of it, the texture of the hair itself is thin so it is easily weighed-down and readily tangles. Leave-in conditioners often completely flatten my hair, but somehow this product hydrated the always dry ends, eliminated the frizz so the curls are soft and defined, and all while maintaining the volume.

I used a quarter size dollop (one full pump) on damp hair starting at the ends and sparingly working my way up stopping before reaching my scalp. The tangle issue makes combing wet hair somewhat slow but with this product it sped up the process. After styling my hair looked great.

The pump mechanism is easy to operate, turn counterclockwise to open the pump and clockwise to lock. The cream is somewhat thick but is easily dispensed and dispersed well in semi-wet hair. Also, the pump is relatively easy to control  depress slightly for a small amount, a bit more for half a pump, etc. This precision helps avoid wasted product.

The fragrance is hard to describe, not a simple herbal or citrus scent, but a more complex perfume. Granted this is subjective, but I find the fragrance very pleasant, but even if not a favorite it is not overpowering and becomes quite faint after an hour.  Overall the product works beautifully.

I love that this can be used in dry hair.  This is the 3rd Obliphica Seaberry product that I've tried and they have all be terrific.  They all smell very similar and it is a very clean, fresh, slightly fruity feminine scent.
My hair is super long, about hip length and the ends get so dry.  This goes right on and really smooths them so they don't feel like straw, instead, they feel soft and freshly washed, with soft shine and overall just very much healthier and improved.  It does not look oily or weigh hair down.
The pump bottle is easy to use and one pump should be enough for most people with shorter hair.  It takes me about 3 on my ends when my hair is dry, but if it is damp and I use it after a wash, I take 5.  Still, it is a very generous amount and looks like it will last awhile.

I notice it also makes my hair easier to brush- it has some detangling action whether it is used on damp or dry hair.
summary: Excellent restorative product for finer, long hair when ends get straw-like- improves, softens, shines, detangles - good stuff

reviewText: I did not know what to expect, especially when it said I could use on dry hair - but it's very light yet moisturizing.  It kills the dryness on my bleached hair but doesn't weigh it down - in looooooooveee.  smells good and has a lavender tint that is great for diminishing some brass.

I have long, fine hair. I tried this as a leave in conditioner and it was ok, a bit heavy, but it dried and was fine. As a conditioner, it's good, but not better than the one I already use, and it's much more expensive. I also think the scent is a bit loud, which is typical of some shampoos and conditioners. I took off one star for the combination of price and scent. If I were working in a formal office or seeing clients, e.g., I would not use this in the morning. I'd wash my hair the night before.
summary: Good conditioner, strong scent, high price.

reviewText:
I have waist length fine hair with moderate volume. This leave in works brilliantly for me, leaving my hair, soft, shiny and knot free. It seems to be able to calm flyaways without making my very fine hair look flat and greasy. For all my hair length, 2 pumps was plenty to get the effect that I want.

The scent is pleasant but mild enough to not be lingering or annoying. I'd buy it if it was scent free but the fragrance is not enough to irritate me.  I like the consistency as it goes on smoothly and does not lump or drag. Overall an excellent experience from a product I had never heard of before. Very pleased with this, hair looks great.
summary: Surprisingly wonderful results from this leave-in. My fine waist length hair is shiny, smooth and not weighted down

reviewText:
I had been waiting on the product just like this to come out! Other detanglers have been leaving my hair oily, greasy looking and weighed down. I have found what I needed! Plus the scent is awesome without being overpowering.

See, I have this thing where I like to put my hair in a knot on the top of my head all the time like a loose bun and it causes a lot of tangles. So when I take it down and try to style my hair all I have is a frizzy matted up mess. It only takes a little bit of this product in the palm of my hand. I do have long hair so I use I guess about the size of a quarter on my hair. I use it on the ends and I'm able to pick it out or run my fingers through my hair and get the style that I want without the knots, the pain, the frizzy flyways or losing 200 hairs in the process.

I guess I should tell you a few things about the product itself, besides the awesome scent, it is generously portion and comes in a pump bottle that is very easy to use. It doesn't leave residue on my hands after use. It doesn't take much (as I said before) to get the style results that you're looking for and it does not leave my hair looking like a Crisco trap. I love it and will look forward to continue using this on my unruly hair!

This stuff smells amazing!! And is VERY GOOD at Smoothing. Just a hint, My hair is bra-line length and 3 pumps is TOO much, 2 pumps is plenty and perfect for My thick hair. The SEABERRY SERUM smells Even Better!!!!
summary: This stuff smells amazing!! And is VERY GOOD at Smoothing

reviewText: made me breakout
Keeps my blonde/balayage highlights in great shape. Can't live without it.
dries the crap out of your hair
Great product, keeps my hair healthy and my gray in place!

I purchased this after having my hair dyed back to lightish blonde from medium brown. I had some pretty horrendous brass/yellow colors coming through so my stylist recommended a good quality purple shampoo. After the positive reviews, this is the one I purchased. After using for a couple of weeks it did very little against the brass. I would guess this is better for preventing brass from hard water (which I do not have) than removing brassy color that is already there. I did not find the odor obnoxious or unpleasant in any way. I did find this to be a drying shampoo as well - which I followed up with Pureology Hydrate Conditioner and a leave in conditioner. To get the more platinum brightness I wanted, I've been using the Pureology Perfect 4 Platinum shampoo/conditioner - much less drying and a pleasant coconutty smell.
summary: Expensive and Drying, Probably works with hard water

reviewText: Love it, very hydrating and lovely mild scent.
Love this product!  Brightens my highlights and natural colors beautifully. Love the smell. Use the Oribe spray detangler too.
Nothing I can say other than love, love, love!  Don't need much to make it work. Price might chase one away, but does last a long time and my blond is beautiful. Never brassy or dull.
Love it!  Lovely mild scent.  Great for fine hair
Ok but tiny

Really disappointed. Two hairdressers RAVED about Oribe, as if it was the best brand ever. I'm unimpressed. First of all, I bought it quickly, thinking I bought shampoo. It was bad enough as shampoo - i.e., I was disappointed that it didn't leave my hair soft and it really didn't brighten it. And, since I have super curly hair, I frequently use conditioner to wash my hair. When I realized this was conditioner, I was more than disappointed. Talk about drying out my hair!  What a waste of money.

The smell is ok, a bit too perfumey for me. I specifically purchased it for use with keratin treated hair. While this claims to be safe for keratin, the second time I used it I noticed that my hair was starting to get frizzy. I found this to be really upsetting as I'm only 6 weeks into a keratin treatment, and it's winter, and keratin usually lasts me easily 3 months through a steamy summer. I can't say for sure that this was the cause, as each keratin treatment and product is different, and I've had 3 different keratin products over the past 9 months. Frankly, even if this worked really well, the price is outrageously absurd and I've had better luck with drugstore purple shampoos and conditioners. No more Oribe for me.
made me breakout
I'm not a blonde but I tried this anyway and its an awesome conditioner by itself. Its super hydrating and leaves my hair silky soft.
Discovered in Europe and now buy in US.  Solves all our problems with cracking dry skin on feet. A little more expensive than other creams but worth it.
I like the consistency and fragrance but it doesn't do.a great job keeping my feet from developing rough skin. The Blue foot cream works better but is greasier.
Got introduced to this product while in Europe.  My husband has extremely dry feet and it has helped to keep them soft and skin not peeling.
summary: Keeps my husband's feet in great shape

reviewText:
This Vichy Aqualia Thermal Eye Balm is light blue translucent gel. It  has a lightweight viscosity and it feels like a wet, watery gel. However, even a few hours after application, I can feel a light moist ointment-like film (not sticky) under my eyes where I applied it, So I feel like it's moisturizing quality is lasting. It contains some caffeine, which is supposed to help counteract fatiguing looking eyes.

The balm is dispensed by the smooth action pump dispenser. It comes out in a small ribbon shape.

I am very pleasantly surprised by this teensy tiny itty bitty pump bottle of light blue gel for the areas surrounding the eyes.  The pump action is smooth,  the gel is light blue and very absorbant, it feels a tad cool when applied,  and most importantly,  has a rather benign fragrance that is not at all disturbing to me.  I doubt that I'll look younger even when this 1/2 ounce container of gel is depleted, but I really like it and am happy that the box contained a best by date.

I don't see or feel a difference. Although I like some things from this product line this is not one of them. It is so thin, water. I don't feel like I have any moisturizing from it. I ended up getting another product that is creamier.
great

This stuff is really adding some moisture back around my eyes, in the time I need it the most...winter!  It is a tiny little bottle of blue gel but it really doesn't take much to go around your eyes.  I usually use a half of pump each time.  I have been putting it on before I go to bed and have noticed that my lines are less noticeable and some of the bags under my eyes are going away.  This a winner in my book!
summary: Little dab is all you need

reviewText:
Finally starting to see some improvement in the dark circles under my eyes after using this product twice a day for almost a month.  The puffy bags under my eyes are also less noticeable.  They puffy bags are still there, mind you,  but they just don't stand out as much when I  look in the mirror.

The product itself is very soothing and feels like you are dabbing cool water underneath your eyes.  It melts into your skin without lots of rubbing or tapping and the cool sensation lasts for awhile after the product has been absorbed.  The product doesn't seem to work as well with the deeper wrinkles at the corner of my eyes so I will probably layer a thicker wrinkle cream there at bedtime.  For anyone not over 55, this product could be all you need.
summary: Seeing small improvement on a plus 55 year old pair of eyes

reviewText: This is one of the many serums that are probably great if you have dry skin that accentuates your wrinkles. If your skin isn't dry, there isn't as much benefit, imo. I don't have dry skin, just wrinkles, lol. This has a very smooth feeling, very touchable and silky and the scent is light and pleasant. I wouldn't spend $29 on it, tho, because it just doesn't have much benefit for skin like mine (not dry, but beginning to sag and wrinkle). Your mileage may vary.
summary: Best for dry skin, it seems

reviewText: I have to admit I was skeptical about the claims of this eye balm.  I have been using this just a few days and noticed results already.  The dark circles under my eyes are disappearing and my eyes look less tired.  Vichy Aqualia Thermal Eye Balm feels great when it goes on, and it definitely helps more than just using my regular moisturizer.
summary: Great Treatment For Tired Looking Eyes

reviewText: This eye balm gave minimal reduction in puffy lower eye lids and while it goes on smoothly, it didn't improve the skin around my eyes enough for me to recommend it to others.

This product contains mineral water from French volcanoes. That fact alone is a good enough reason to buy it. It is a wonderful conversation starter.

I liked the eye cream. It worked exactly as advertised. It feels smooth and luxurious on the fingers, and cool and soothing on the eyes. The blue color looks slightly radioactive. There are volcanoes involved. French ones.

Seriously, it is very nice.
summary: Soothing eye cream is a product of French volcanoes.

reviewText:
I've got all kinds of eye creams and gels and really like this. It hasn't completely transformed my appearance but after just a few days, I think I can see a subtle difference. I will add a comment to this review after I've used it awhile longer, as I suspect it could take 3-4 weeks. Meanwhile I really like the way the product feels. It comes in a small container with a dispenser that releases just a drop at a time, which is all you need. It's not greasy or oily. As promised, it's light and feels good on my skin.  As other reviewers said, it's cooling and soothing. The word "balm" is appropriate! I actually look forward to putting it on every day, and I'm not a real make-up kind of person.

Good one!

I'm not big on wearing a lot of creams and moisturizers, but this stuff goes on smooth and is hardly noticeable. I'm at the point where a little extra moisturizing around the eyes is a good idea. With Vichy Aqualia Thermal Eye Balm it glides on smoothly and is hardly noticeable. I can feel a slight tingly hint of moisture, but it is not greasy. The scent is very faint and fades almost immediately. This is great for a light smooth touch of moisture.

I have been using some new moisturizers recently, including eye creams. I think this its the best I have tried. First, it doesn't pretend it will make you look younger and make your wrinkles disappear. It does state that it well hydrate and reduce puffiness and dark circles. And it does do this. At least for dark circles as that is my issue. This is a gel that feels very  cool and moisturizers nicely. I use it at night and in the morning. It's fine for wearing under make up. It makes me look more refreshed and awake and not like a zombie as I sometimes do. I keep this in my refrigerator for an even cooler feeling. I think that helps as well.
There is no scent and no irritation.

As I age, I am using more skin products aimed directly at my eye area.

This is one of the better products I've tried. I use it in the morning, and it is very refreshing. I actually enjoy using it. The scent is pleasant and not too strong--unlike some of the other Vichy products.

The product also does a good job of making my eye area look younger and fresher. So far, this is my favorite Vichy product.

Very nice plumping gel.  One pump is all that is required for both eyes, so this small bottle will last a while.  There is no pain, no burn and no odor which makes for a great eye balm.  The primary mission of this balm is to renew the under eye zone.  With a bit of caffeine to plump and lots of emollients to smooth the lines, the balm goes on quickly and stays a bit "wet" to the touch for a while.  By wet I mean it is moist, not tacky and not uncomfortable.  The balm is a light blueish color but absorbs in entirely clear.  I think the blue tint actually goes to help brighten the skin under the eyes.  All in all a nice additional touch before regular makeup in the morning routine.
summary: Very nice, comforting eye balm that plumps and smooths lines.

reviewText:
I have been suffering from severe gastritis.  What does this have to do with eye cream you may ask?  As a result, I haven't been eating or sleeping well.  And my eyes show it.  I have dark circles under my eyes and the wrinkles seem to be more pronounced.  I was intrigued by this eye creams claim to awaken and brighten.

Why I like this product:

* It works!  My eyes look brighter and less tired. And this is just with using this eye balm and before I put on makeup.

* It moisturizes without being really heavy and greasy.

* It has no scent.  I have passed up countless skin creams because of their cloying, heavy and artificial scent.  I am happy to report that this cream has no scent.

* It glides on.  The little pump works easily and dispenses just the right amount of balm to put under your eyes.

If you are looking for a product that will help you look less tired and more awake, this may just be for you.
summary: A nice way to brighten your eyes

reviewText: I am always looking for high quality skin care products to take care of my somewhat tired and dry skin. Not having tried this brand before I didn't know what to expect, but I was pleasantly surprised by this eye gel and like it quite a lot. A small pump is all it takes and has a lasting moisturizing effect for me. I place a few dabs under each eye each morning and night. It is comfortable and cooling and lasts. It also seems to help my makeup go on better because my skin is more balanced and evenly moisturized. I also feel good that is paraben free. It contains caffeine as many other eye creams do, which I believe is supposed to drain and stimulate the cells to have a smoothing effect. I like this and plan to try other products form this line.

Day One (2 December 2015)
I have been noticing some puffiness around my eyes and darkening circles so I thought I would try a new eye product.  I will come back and update this review to share the results in a few weeks.  I do like the way this eye balm feels when I put it on and would probably give it five stars on that alone, like a light gel.  However, I am not fond of pump dispensers because, over time, I find that they will occasionally spurt out too much product and I prefer the control afforded with a tube or jar.

Again, I'll update this review with my results in a few weeks.  Or sooner, if there are results sooner.  Crossing my fingers!
summary: Lovely, Light Gel in a Pump

reviewText: This VICHY AQUALIA THERMAL EYE BALM definitely makes the bags under my eyes look better.  It's pleasant-smelling, cooling, and very gentle--unlike other products I've tried that had a strong all-day fragrance or left my face feeling sunburned.  The hydrating effect of this Vichy Aqualia is also longer-lasting than the effect of the other products I've tried.  I'm very, very happy with this product

Let me preface this review by admitting that I'm a middle-aged man of Greek descent. Therefore...I'm hairy. The primary reason I wanted this Tria Beauty Hair Removal Laser device was to remove the hair from the top of my feet and toes. I wear lots of sandals and flip flops during the summer and I can't stand hairy feet. In the past I have shaved them, and once I even had them waxed. After waxing the hair was thinner and less dense. That's where the Tria Laser comes in. I have used it several times in the past few weeks and there is a noticeable difference in the amount of hair on my feet. I am almost positive that after using it repeatedly for 3 months all my hair will be completely gone.

This is a bright pink device that I would be slightly (okay, extremely) embarrassed to show my friends or family. But nobody needs to see it. I like the results and that's all that really matters. I'm sure a professional laser treatment from a dermatologist or other specialist would be more effective, but for a home device this fits the bill nicely.

I have never used anything like this, but was pleased with how the laser hair removal product worked. It's quite expensive, but I guess compared to regular salon treatments, this could be a money saver. It's small - very compact - and easy to use.
summary: I have never used anything like this, but was pleased with how the laser ...

reviewText:
I have used it once and here is my feedback on first usage:
  * It is easy to use and convenient to hold
  * It takes a long time and set aside a good amount of time.  Ideally use it for facial hair and hand - I have not tried it for legs
  * You will feel sensation on your skin, if it is high - apply some ice and numb your skin before you use.
  * Does not cause any rash/allergy on skin

So far in my use on face - it completely got rid of the small hair.

Yet to see/experience the long term benefits on how it will really work in reducing hair growth - will update this review later.
summary: Effective, easy to use for small areas

reviewText:
Features:-
1) It uses professional laser technology and ensures removal of unwanted hair permanently.
2) It targets the pigment in one's hair and permanently disables the hair follicle's ability to regrow hair by a laser beam of light.
3) It is much cheaper and convenient that the laser treatment done from various well known clinics.
4) It is designed for smaller areas like underarms, upper lip, chin and facial hair etc.
5) It removes existing hair and minimises the future hair growth.

Cons:-
1) It is quite painful while using this product. It feels like sharp stinging every time.
2) It created spots and rashes on my skin as an after-effect.
3) The battery lasts for a shorter period and has to be recharged again.

This is the best at home device that actually works , IMO. I have gotten quite a few but this one has delivered results . I did my research before purchasing it and debated for fraxel co2 vs this device and i am glad i bought it . I finished the first treatment phase a few months ago and i definitely noticed my face plumped up during the resting phase . I barely have any wrikles - and i am 42 . What i've noticed so far : some tightening , hyperpigmentation is dramatically reduced and the pores look a lot better ( i also use the pmd pro device for microderm at home ). It helps with sun spots and small acne scars . The plumpness took place during the resting phase - i guess this is when the body produces more collagen . I am ready to start the second treatment and i have to say i am excited with the future results . I am a regular consumer , was not paid to review this item , i just wanted to share this for people like me looking for a good maintenance tool .

I paid $500 a session- a total of over $2000 for a series of laser treatments like this at my dermatologist's office. I purchased this when I saw how much I could save using this device. My first device ordered arrived with a defective battery but the major beauty retailer I ordered it from replaced the device right away without issues. My new device works really well. It works just as well as my treatments in the derm's office did. My skin is baby smooth, it is much clearer, and looks more even toned. I'm glowing. This is a great device for those in their 20s, 30s, 40s, 50s, but I am not going to say this device will take the place of if you believe you need a fact lift, PS, botox, or injections. If you are looking to maintain your appearance then this is for you. It's not a pleasant feeling on the face but I don't mine since I get good results. A good tip I learned when my derm did this treatment for me was to run my hand (palm side to face) beside the area I just treated to cool my face off a little during the treatment process.
summary: Get it. I love it. Yeees!!!

reviewText: I got this for my wife because lilac or purple is her favorite color - not because she might actually need it - I want to make that perfectly clear just in case she's reading this.  This is one of those items for which you are not going to get very definitive performance promises.  My wife says that it is easy to grip and use and you get simple feedback on when to move to another zone on your face.  She says it stings a bit but it it is tolerable.  Clearly visible results may take the full 12 weeks - and I'll report back later if things change - but I do see some improvement already.
summary: Easy to use treatment for facial skin

reviewText:
I need to first state that I've only been using this product for 16 days rather than the 30 that is recommended.  I also haven't used the Tria products that the manufacturer recommends, but have instead been using coconut oil, which I have been using for years on my skin.  That being said, I still feel able to review this product with accuracy.
I have not had any issue at all with the battery draining as others have, so for me, this is a non issue as the Laser charges and stays charged perfectly.
I was very surprised for the first few days as to how much the process "stung" my face.  It felt like tiny needles were penetrating my face while using it.  I almost didn't continue, but after about 5 days, the pain was gone while using.  My face never got burned or red or looked in any way unnatural.  It just felt uncomfortable for about 5 days of usage.
I truly believe that my wrinkles are much lighter.  I am fortunate to not have an overt amount of lines or wrinkles, but the frown lines around my lips and the laugh lines around my eyes are reduced.  Again, only using for 16 days showed improvement, so I can imagine that using it for the full recommended time will show even more improvement.
I am not going to purchase the recommended skin care line.  I LOVE my coconut oil and will always use that so I apologize for not being able to comment on this product using the recommended skin line.
I do believe that this laser does exactly what it claims to do.  It lessens and reduces the appearance of deep lines and wrinkles.  I find that it works very well and other than the initial discomfort on my sensitive skin, it has been a pleasure to use and I will continue using it.

Remember when they introduced home perms after years of having permanents the domain of licensed beauticians only? This laser is something like that. A game changer.  It may not be quite as fancy or include someone to hold your hand, do the work (such as it is), or give you advice (other than what is in the very complete instructions), but we now have control over all of our own basic skin care!

This little tool is not as powerful as the one in my doctor's office. She is in Beverly Hills and has a nurse/cosmetologist wielding the laser for her patients. As you can see, I've done this before and I believe that a little bit of this treatment done frequently at home may beat a more intense treatment less done frequently.

PS: I am having a bit of trouble getting Tria to accept my forehead. Maybe it's too bony. Lucky I have brains.  I still like it, and wouldn't downgrade it from a love affair in view of the money I'm going to save!

As someone who has used the doc's treatments as well as this hand-held device, my advice is not to let the warning in the brochure scare you. Companies must play it safe. Just start with the first (trial) step to assure yourself. I used it on my hands the first time as a test--at the lowest laser intensity.  Move up to the third level slowly as you come to know what to expect.  With the first treatment on your face you may see an immediate glow that wasn't there before, but my skin is very light so that may show up on me when it doesn't on other skin types.  I love this aspect of the treatment.  With a treatment every day, that glow becomes part of my daily routine.

OK, I'll say this, too. I'm saving a heck of a lot of money! Just like the home perms did back in the 50s.  If you're too young to remember this, that's OK.  At least you'll know that beauty miracles aren't all that new--just different with each decade. (-:
summary: Game-Changer Beauty Aid--Frugal and a Daily Glow

reviewText:
The Tria Beauty Age-Defying Laser is expensive. Or is it? I have relatives and friends who regularly get treatments including lasers, Botox, and collagen treatments from their Dermatologist at a cost of a minimum of $600 per visit.  So maybe this laser is not so expensive.

The laser has three settings. The first setting is for training so you can get used to the sensation the laser creates on your skin.  The second two higher settings are to be increased with time.  I tested it with level one on my clean forearm first.  While you are slowly drawing it across your skin, the laser lights up.  When removed from your skin, the light goes off.  There is a definite tingling sensation which when stopped feels a bit like your skin is burning and the sensation lasts a minute or two. Since it wasn't too uncomfortable, I started with the training level one on my forehead, chin, cheeks and the side of my eyes (not too close).  It takes some practice to smoothly draw the laser over your skin.  Make sure you clean your face before using the laser and completely dry before use.

I have only been using it for about a week and have not really seen any improvement and although after the treatment, my face does still feel a bit burned, but the sensation does go away.  My skin does redden slightly but returns to normal after about 5-10 minutes.

There is a detailed instruction booklet, which I would suggest reading in its entirety before use.  It is fairly simple to understand and use of the laser is also pretty simple.

The equipment itself seems very well designed and manufactured with style and elegance including the packaging.  If you spend a lot of money at the Dermatologist, this laser may be worth the investment, but I am certain the results will vary based on your skin condition and your sensitivity to the laser.
summary: If you regularly go to the Dermatologist for skin treatments, this laser may save money over the long term

reviewText:
Understand that this Tria Laser tool is a collagen stimulator, is not a drink from the fountain of youth, and you may fall in love with it because of what it actually does successfully do.  Results are not instantaneous, but require weeks of consistent treatment, so when people say it is all that and a bag of chips, what they see in the mirror is what they wish to see.  That being said, this tool appears to do what it claims to do, stimulate the collagen which plumps up slight wrinkles in facial skin over bone, and anything else is a byproduct of the attention the user is likely also giving to their skin while using the Tria.
