Try the Tria on your cleansed and dried off forearm to be sure you recognize the prickly sensation that will be felt on the face.  Use it on a cleansed and dried off face, avoiding the eyes, staying on areas that cover bone, following a four sectioned or zoned order.  I have found that as suggested in the Tria online video, I prefer to move the device vertically along my forehead area and horizontally along the remaining three zones.  I then use a facial serum and moisturizer to rehydrate the skin and I drink a glass of water to rehydrate my interior.  It is suggested to perform this ritual five out of seven nights a week prior to bed for twelve weeks, raising the stimulation from one to three as you can tolerate the prickling sensation.  Stimulation is increased with the levels as is the timing for eachieving zone.  My sensitive skin showed no adverse reaction at any stage, that is no redness, darkening or burning.  I also religiously apply sunscreen during the day and would do this if I did nothing else to my face.

This is a good tool and becomes easier to use over time because it becomes second nature to move the laser area along the face.  For the first few nights, I found that I had difficulty getting it to move smoothly and if it did not touch the skin, the laser stopped working.  Initially, that was frustrating, then I discovered that by assuring that my skin was completely dry after being cleansed and then carefully regulating the pressure with which I moved it across my face, the two minute treatment went by as quickly as the two minute cycle of my electric toothbrush.  Like my toothbrush, the Tria alerts me when a zone is completed at each increment.  Unlike the toothbrush, this turns itself off at the end of a treatment cycle.  I can lock the device and then unlock it by holding down the power button for a few seconds, a safety feature I appreciate.  My Tria arrived with no lotions or potions, just the device, charging cradle, USB cord for the cradel and plug for the USB cord.  Enclosed was a little purple folder containing the instruction manual.

This tool is not cheap and considering the battery is expected to last perhaps three years tops, it is not for everyone.  If you typically spend a substantial amount of money on skin care products, estheticians and spas, I won't advise against trying this.  As for me, the true test will be hearing what my Dermatologist says at my next biannual visit.  The Tria won't rid my skin of the effects of time, age and sun damage, but if it continues to help plump up those tiny wrinkles with my own collagen, I'm not complaining.

So far I like this item. I haven't used it long enough to notice a difference, but I am using it only on one side of my face so I can report back over the next few months.
It feels like little pin-pricks on your skin when using it. I used it at the lowest setting and it was definitely uncomfortable. I don't even want to try the second and third settings. I didn't have any redness or swelling afterwards.
After three weeks:
I had friends guess which side of my face I was using this on and they all guessed correctly. It is slowly minimizing my wrinkles on my cheeks (smile lines) and on my forehead. I am still not used to the pain associated with using this, it hurts to use. I'm not sure the results are worth the pain.

I love these new butter london 10x lacquers.  I actually find i have a longer wear time if i put on two coats and do not use any top coat at all.  I get 5 days which the longest wear time i have ever gotten in any finger nail polish.

I love london butter products!  I really like the 10x nail lacquer.  I put it on leave to dry over night.  put the top coat on in the morning and it last me several days.  this is a record for me.  Lots nail polishes last for maybe two days on me.  I love how may nails feel when I remove this polish.

This is an opaque light pink polish that isn't sheer.  It requires two coats. The first coat didn't go on very smoothly, I would have preferred a bigger brush, but the second coat evened it out.  I have another Butter London polish, a purple orchid shade, that went on much easier than this one.  However, it does last quite a while without chipping.  I don't think this formula is in any way superior to Essie polish though, and Essie is almost half the price.  The color is very pretty, perfect for spring and summer.  I wear it with a gold confetti topcoat, which helps the polish last nearly a full week without a chip.  When I do get a chip, I simply add another layer of the confetti polish, without removing the pink base coast underneath.  I didn't want a sheer look this time and this polish certainly delivered an opaque finish.  It's also quite shiny.  I used the Seche Vita topcoat, which not only dries the polish quickly, it helps it last longer.  I apply the clear topcoat every few days.which keeps the finish shiny and the chips to a minimum.  All in all, I'm giving this polish four stars because the first coat was rather spotty, although the second one delivered a flawless finish..

This polish is terrible. It's not the problem of the polish itself since I already owned several, there is a problem with the way it is stored. It's way too thick and too gloopy for a fresh Butter London nail polish. Butter London polishes are famous for being thin and easy to layer. Layering the second coat on top of the first one isn't an easy task for the polish I've got.
Very disappointed I can't send it back. Had to order a new one directly from the brand. Waste of money and time.
summary: Too thick, not like a fresh Butter London nail polish

reviewText: I was able to pick this up in two colors as part of the Vine program: Golden Glow and Matte Tan. This is the first time I've used a Lorac bronzer, and I really love them both! On the Lorac website, it mentions that Matte Tan is a good general bronzer if you're fair, and I definitely agree. I wear MAC foundation in NW20, and the Matte Tan leaves a nice, soft color that looks really natural. That being said, I think I love the Golden Glow color even more. It leaves a pretty sheen to the skin, with no sparkles or glitter, which I've encountered in other bronzers. My skin can sometimes be really dry so I was worried about using a powder bronzer, but it doesn't sink into dry spots. To apply it, I use an S-motion, starting on my temple, sweeping down below my cheekbone, and then sweeping down to my jawline. I then apply a bit to the bridge of my nose, where the sun would naturally hit. Although the compact comes with a little brush, I bought the EcoTools Domed Bronzer Brush, which had fabulous reviews both here and on Makeup Alley, and it works great. I highly recommend these bronzers!

I love Lorac products.  The powders are highly milled, and apply evenly.  If you love Lorac eye shadows, you will love this powder.  I am fair skinned, so this color is perfect for me.  You can build this up, so it will get darker.  There is a little shimmer, but you won't feel like you are putting on a glitter bomb.  These is a ton of product in here so this will last a long time.  The container is easy to open, and is sturdy.  I was surprised with how nice this powder was.  I definitely recommend this if you are light to a medium complexion.

A few years ago, I went on a long, long hunt for the perfect bronzer. I finally found it and it was a super inexpensive drugstore variety (Almay!). I've been obsessed with it since. I was excited to try this pricier bronzer, and while I really like it, I didn't really find it a replacement for my regular routine, but more of an add-on. My drugstore bronzer makes me basically a shade darker, but really, really natural looking. The LORAC Tantalizer gives me a golden shimmer.

Maybe I'm just too pale, but I really liked layering my regular bronzer with this one over the top. When I used this on its own, I just didn't feel dark enough; I felt shimmery. For me, this is a great layering option, especially for a night on the town!

This is a true bronze color, not too much red, making it suitable for dusting all over my face. I have light olive skin and with light application, it provides a hint of color with good translucency. There is a bit of shimmer, but not overly so. I've dusted this on my neck and decolletage with good results. Recommended.
summary: Good Color for My Olive Complexion

reviewText:
This is a large cake of bronzing powder. It surprised me how large the compact is, but as it's a body bronzer, that's what you want.

It is very shimmery and comes out a coppery bronze color. One star off for the fact it is slightly orange-y and very shimmery.

The compact has a unique opening. Rather than flip the top, you swivel the top to the side. Underneath, the same arrangement and there is a fan brush for applying it to shoulders, arms, legs, face.

If you want shimmery bronze for evenings out, this is fine--it will look better on tanned skin as it's so orange that a pale person will look a bit coppery.

I'm so impressed with this -- it's a great bronzer.

For reference, I'm fair skinned, and tan only slightly; golden glow turned out to be a good shade for me. It looks like it would be sparkly, but it's a lot more like a glow.

Pros:
1. The bronzer goes on easily and looks great
2. It is a generous size
3. The packaging is very clever, including a brush stored in the case and a mirror on the back.

Cons:
1. I wish the mirror was visible on the front side instead of on the back, but it's not that big of a deal.

I was sent this bronzer in Matte Tan and Golden Glow.  I like the Golden Glow a lot better because the color is darker and it shows up better on my skin.  I have a medium skin tone.  Also, this bronzer has a bit of shimmer, like my favorite bronzers do.  It gives the skin a healthy glow without looking like a disco ball.  I have been using this product for a few days, now, brushing it on my forehead, along the hairline area and under the cheekbones to breathe life back into my skin after applying foundation.  The powder is high quality and up to the high standards I have for Lorac products.

I have added a picture showing the color of this bronzer compared to my favorite bronzer, Too Faced Sun Bunny.  As you can see, the color shows up nicely, just like Sun Bunny.  Lorac Bronze Glow is the lighter color, Too Faced Sun Bunny is slightly darker.  Overall, this bronzer is good for women with light skin to medium skin.  I know that the bronzer  looks really shimmery in the swatch, but when you apply it with a brush, it looks a lot more natural.

As for packaging, the bronzer is too bulky.  The package is about double the thickness of the packaging used by other companies, e.g. Too Faced or Mac.  I wish the packaging were slimmer.  The bronzer comes with a brush that is good for contouring, but given the shimmer, this isn't really a bronzer you'd want to contour with.  I think it's a good brush for matte bronzers, but I prefer to use a fluffy brush for this one.  There is also a nice sized mirror at the bottom of the compact.  Just remove the sticker on the bottom to make the mirror usable.  I would have preferred the mirror to have been placed under the cover.

I have loved and used Lorac cosmetics before so I was absolutely thrilled when this bronzer as well as the matte bronzer appeared in my Q!  Let me tell you that I truly love both of them.  The matte is so natural but this one is, too...it's hard to explain the difference but it is sort of a glowy one...without glitter and too much shimmer.  I can't even decide which one I love better...I think I love them both!  I love the size of this product...it's just the right size...not too small to use.  I love that it is a total package...we were in NYC for the weekend and I didn't want to lose my tan...this product was perfect to keep my glow going!  The brush is right inside...it was one less tool that I needed to pack.  You can use this wet but I don't really want to...I like it dry!  It isn't drying...it's easy to use...and I love the look on my summer skin!

This bronzer has a silky feel and is pigmented, as I've come to expect from the Lorac brand. The powder is finely milled and does not feel dry to the touch.  The color is not too orange, but is quite light compared to other bronzers in my collection.  Also, while the bronzer is supposed to be matte, there is a slight sheen to it.  I'd call it more of a satin look rather than a true matte.  Personally I prefer the slight sheen because it looks more natural than a true matte. I have a medium skin tone and I am currently tan.  I am wearing Makeup Forever Mat Velvet + Foundation in #53 (perfect match) at the moment.  The bronzer doesn't really show up on my skin very well.  I can use it to slightly warm up my face, but it is not usable as a contour.

I have attached a picture of the bronzer swatched on the underside of my arm in comparison with two other bronzers in my collection.

Left: Too Faced Chocolate Soleil (Matte)
Middle: Lorac Tantalizer Baked Bronzer in Matte Tan
Right: Mac Refined Golden Bronzer (has some glitter particles)

As you can see,the bronzer is lighter than both of those.  Also you can pick up the slight sheen.  I didn't photograph it, but it is also significantly lighter than Too Faced Sun Bunny bronzer.  I will update this when I have a chance to compare to a few other popular bronzers.  I really can't comment on lasting power.  It doesn't really show up on my skin, beyond a slight warming effect.  That said, I got compliments on my nice tan when I wore it, so while I can't use it for contouring, the subtle effect is noticeable to others. :)

The packaging is very bulky.  The top is see through and it slides to the side to allow access to the bronzer.  Underneath, there is a compartment with a brush.  The brush is flat and good quality.  It is really good for applying the powder for contouring purposes.  I think you would still want a fluffy brush to blend if you are fair, but I think the brush is good for application.  In fact, I am taking it out of the compact to use with bronzers that are better suited to my skin tone for contouring.  There is a nice mirror at the bottom, although I don't love having to constantly flip between the bottom and the top to apply the bronzer while also using the mirror.  The packaging is also REALLY bulky.  Because of the brush compartment, it is very thick, so it isn't great for travel.  Also, I don't really love how both the top and brush compartment slide out.  I prefer more traditional compacts with the mirror inside the compact.
summary: Nice bronzer for ladies with fair or light skin.

reviewText: I've been stealing these from my husband and am loving them!  With 2 young kids, I don't have time to exfoliate as often as I should and never have time to sit still for long.  These exfoliating wipes are perfect for on the go where i can exfoliate in minutes.  Unlike other wipes that leave your skin red, burning or irritated, these are gentle yet effective. My skin feels smooth and tighter since i've been using these.

Anyway, I've enjoyed a lot of different CK colognes for men, and this is another fine cologne from the company.  My wife and daughters all give it two thumbs up.  Definitely worth giving.

reviewText:
I got this Calvin Klein Reveal Eau de Toilette spray for my 22 yr. old son who loves things like this. When he wore it, it has a very clean kind of spicy smell to it. It lasts a pretty long time too. He put it on at about 5pm, and I could still smell it when he came home late that night at about 12:30am.

He went to see his girlfriend, and he said that she really liked it, and she wanted him to wear that from now on. He said that while they were out, they ran into a couple of his friends, and got asked what kind of cologne he was wearing, and where he got it. So I would highly recommend this to younger guys, as well as older ones too.

Gosh, this is a very sexy, soft scent.  My husband is wearing it today and he loves it.  It smells so soft and sexy and clean.  It's not overpowering.  My husband gets a headache from strong, floral or sweet scents.  Every year, I go and try to find him a new scent and I always tell the person at the store, i'm looking for a soft, sorta powdery, clean scent.  This one I would have bought my husband if I smelled it in a store.  The bottle is very sleek looking too.  I actually wear my husbands colognes sometimes and for the past 2 hours i have it on and I love the way it smells on me. I think I'll wear it tomorrow to work.  It's a great scent.  All I can say is if you like a lighter, powdery, clean scent this is it.  There are no florals  and I don't smell any citrus or salt.

It is difficult to review a fragrance when my claims cant be measured or substantiated by anything solid. The only real claim that can be made is how it smells and how long it will smell like that for.

In this review I will be comparing it to my other Calvin Klein product Aqua.

I have been using the Aqua product for about 6 months and before that I used Polo Black for about 2 years.

Reveal is a lighter fragrance than both Aqua and Black, which I like, and along with that, it is not in the least overpowering.

In relation to the product description, stating that it has a captivating, salty, oriental scent with identity is something I can neither confirm nor deny. In addition, I am in no position to comment with any authority about the content if its top, mid or base notes. I imagine that like me, the average consumer would also only be able to talk in broad terms about the cumulative effects of the ingredients.

What I can say is this:

It smells great - light but not feminine.

It is packaged in a very attractive bottle which comes in a stylish box.

My wife really likes it.

The only negative is that it appears to lose its strength quite fast compared to Aqua and Black.

All in all, I recommend this as a good buy,
summary: Very nice fragrance with the quality you expect from Calvin Klein.

reviewText: Wow! This smells super nice on my husband and lasts all day!  He has even gotten compliments at work.  The scent is a woodsy/musky scent that is just light enough to catch your nose and make you breathe deeply.  He has about 3 other Calvin Klein colognes and this one is by far my favorite.  The bottle is understated but attractive.

reviewText:
smells nice but to me,it can almost be a unisex fragerance. its hard to describe and smells are subjective so hard to do a review.
I would say it has a bit of a sweet smell to it but still masculine but can also see a gal wearing this and pulling it off..

The Reveal is subtle, pleasing, and good for most occasions.

It's not overpowering that you can't wear to work or just going out.

Love the bold, wide design with precise curves.

Worth a look.

This is a nice scent, it has a citrus like scent.  Does not have the "chemical" smell some seems to have recently.  The scent is not overpowering (1 spray), but last a long time.  My wife and daughter both commented that they liked it the first day I tried it.  It has an efficient mister type sprayer, so you don't get squirted, but get a controlled and consistent spray each time you press the sprayer.  This bottle will last a long time, unless you overspray which I highly recommend you do not.

Years ago my cologne of choice was a Calvin Klein creation called CK One. That scent was light clean  and citrusy, the type that I still prefer though my current go to choices have been Issey Miyake L'eau D'issei and Fierce by Abercrombie and Fitch. (Mentioned to establish a baseline of personal preference.) Those both qualify for the suggested correct strength of a scent also, of being barely detectable until someone has leaned into your personal space. I was anxious to see what the people at Klein had released with this new Reveal. Love the container which has clean lines and suggests something simple but elegant inside. The first spray revealed a scent that had strong overtones, at least to my nose, of Vanilla beans and a hint of Almonds; both very pleasant. It takes a few minutes for any scent to mix with your individual body chemistry and skin oils and any initial alcohol to evaporate before it settles down to it's real character. Allowing that time left still very strong scent of vanilla and perhaps talcum powder, but very, very sweet. Almost overpoweringly so. In fact it caused me to react by repeated sneezing. Something I've never experienced with any product before. You want a scent to linger so it lasts throughout your day, but this scent was so strong I found myself with a headache and actually needed to wash it off!  Imagining, perhaps, something else in the environment had caused the reaction, I applied it again the next day, but the reaction was the same. The scent was so overpowering that I felt the need to apologize to anyone near me, and hoped I wasn't giving off the impression of those people we all know who seem to take a bath in their perfume or cologne. (My elderly third grade teacher comes to mind, though was forgiven after my parents explained that elderly folks sometimes have their sense of smell diminished so put on copious amounts of a scent until they can detect it!) To be clear, I like the scent and tones, but if the volume could be dialed back considerably. I even tried spraying it on my fingers to just then dab a bit on my neck, but it still has boom box volume. Sorry Calvin, you still have all my boxer and blue jean dollars, but until the scent is toned down in another incarnation, I can't use Reveal. I suggest, as with any scent, a person test it at your department store of choice or at a duty free shop between flights to see if the scent and powerful strength is to your liking. As with all things, scent and strength are relative to our individual taste and perception. But the screaming volume and cotton candy sweetness that lingers unfortunately make it unusable for me.
summary: A pleasant initial vanilla and almond scent, but overpoweringly sweet and strong!

reviewText:
"Sensual. Vibrant. Captivating." That's what the advertisement is selling, but I have to be honest, upon my first sniff I had to check and make sure it was indeed a men's fragrance. Perhaps it was the floral overtones that caught my attention, or the way it reminded me of cotton candy the longer I lingered over my husband's neck where he'd sprayed it, but this scent wasn't what I'd expected when I read the those three little words.

The scent is musky with a hint of spice, but sweet. I'd say it would be perfect for a tween, teen or twenty-something, but might be a little too soft for older gents. It's a youthful scent that while not off-putting; it's clean and fresh, isn't particularly sexy to my olfactories. Obviously scent is a subjective thing though, and while it may not be my cup of tea.

My husband initially liked the scent, but said over the course of a few hours of wearing it he began to find the scent off putting. He said it smelled like 'food' to him. I asked him to describe the 'food' in question and he said he couldn't. I asked him if he'd dribbled some food on his shirt.  Rolling his eyes he assured me it was the 'Reveal'.  We decided that for us - this scent was not good.

Fragrances work differently with each person's body chemistry to produce unique scents - that's why there are so many!  I give this 3 out of 5 stars (on the Amazon rating scale that's 'It's OK'...) based upon the experience my husband and I have had with this scent.  It's not bad, but it's definitely not for either of us. However by looking at other reviews I guess our experience puts us in the minority.  Take this into account before buying this product.

My advice regarding purchasing ANY scent  you've not yet tried: Go to a local department store that carries it to spray some on and wander around for a few hours first. I think that's the only true way to know if a fragrance is for you.

'Sweet. Clean. Unpredictable.'  These would be the three words I'd use to describe 'Reveal' after experiencing it first hand. Test drive before you buy. If you try it out, you'll have the best chance at enjoying it and not being disappointed... or hungry.
summary: Clashed with body chemistry creating unexpected result

Make no mistake, this mask is very good.  It revives parched hair and makes it soft, smooth and shiny.  I used it for years because it was part of the Wen kit I received every couple of months (ordered from the original infomercial).  However, I recently discovered Shea Moisture treatment masks and I'm happy to say the results were better than with this Wen treatment.  SM is sold in drugstores, Target, Walmart, Ulta and Sally Beauty Supply.  There are several formulas, one for every hair issue.  I use the Manuka Honey formula (only at Target and Ulta) or the 10 in 1 Renewal formula.  The honey formula is a bit more moisturizing but both formulas are excellent.  I use them with a heat cap for 45 minutes or so once a week or every two weeks, the same way I used this Wen treatment.  The result is gorgeous, healthy looking hair.  My hair is color treated and I use heated styling tools several times a week, so dryness is always an issue.  SM masks are really hydrating and they give me plenty of body and shine.  The best part is SM masks are about $10-$11 and the Wen treatment is 5 times as expensive.  If you want to waste your money, then by all means purchase the Wen treatment.  However, if you want the exact same outcome for a fraction of the price, then give SM a try.  I no longer receive the Wen kits because SM works just as well and there is a cowash for those who love the Wen cleanser.  I really missed the lather of shampoo so I switched to sulfate free SM years ago and I absolutely love it.  My hair looks just as shiny and healthy as when I was using Wen and my color looks wonderful too.  I won't go back to Wen but I did like it when I was using it.  However, it was just too expensive.  SM is reasonable, sulfate, silicone, paraben and cruelty free.  What more can you ask for?

Now that I have let my hair go gray (or in my case silver) I needed a deep treatment that I can use as often as once a week or as little as once a month. My hair is smooth, not oily. It does not have an overwhelming smell like most do and washes out easily. I'm using this once a month right now and very happy with the results.
summary: Great Hair treatment for gray hair

reviewText:

The fragrance reminds me of something I tried a few decades ago--It is "tangy", but not quite floral and not quite citrus.  Every time I use it, my brain focuses on trying to identify the fragrance.

With the slippery feel and the weird fragrance, the product does not give me a pleasant, uplifting experience.  I don't hate it--I don't love it.  It may suds nice, but I don't feel any great benefit from it.  It has not helped, nor hurt, my facial skin.
Good cleansing gel for basic daily use. I think that this is a good substitute for your current daily cleanser. It cleans effectively and feels nice afterwards.

I really like this cleansing gel. It cleans my face well, and leaves my skin feeling soft and smooth. With winter coming on with a bang, and the furnace running like crazy, I appreciate that it doesn't dry my skin. I'm not one for scented products, but the scent of this is nice and not very strong, and I don't mind it. I don't mind the price for this product, I only need a little bit to wash my whole face, and this bottle should last quite a while, so it's a better value than you would think.

I look forward to washing my face with this every day.  It gently removes makeup and oil without leaving my face feeling stripped.  It has a fresh scent that reminds me of Lily of the Valley.  It's fairly thick and the dispenser is easy to control, so the bottle should last for several weeks.  I have combination skin so this provides just the right amount of oil removal without leaving my skin feeling dry or causing my skin to break out.

I am TERRIBLE about facial care. Cleansers, creams, collagen and a thousand other non- C-words are just the type of the iceberg of things I am clueless about. Some of it (like makeup) are because I'm that balance between "Not Giving a Darn" and "I Prefer Sleep Thankyouverymuch"; others (such as facial cleansers), it's because I'm good old fashioned lazy.

So while I'm probably not the best person to judge this, based on a counter full of similar competing cleansers, I can at least give a beginner's opinion of the product. And that one is: it seems to do the job nicely, cleaning my skin, clearing up blemishes, yet having a clean, pleasant smell and washing out nicely.

The smell is particularly pleasant - light "ocean" or "fresh air" scented. I love that it's a scent without being too "in your face". Application was easy; the bottle delivers a small dime-sized amount which is more than enough to properly wash your face. The texture is smooth and dense, so it's probably better to lather in your hands before applying to the face. Regardless, it goes on smooth and clean. Rinsing is likewise easy; it doesn't slide off with one splash of water, but neither does it stay on like a mask.

I definitely enjoyed this product for the time I've used it. The only "problem" is that, given my history with washing my face, I don't know that the price (now unavailable, but I swore I saw $17) would be worth it. I tend to be that person who buys beauty products, uses them a couple of times, realizes what a pain in the rear they are and forget about them for 6 months before the cycle returns. I guess if you have very sensitive skin or are concerned with your skin because of makeup and such, then this would be a good investment.

Brought to you by:
*C.S. Light*

reviewText: Until reading about this product, I never gave a thought to the effects of hard water on my face. But now that I've used this product, I understand! What a difference. Most soaps and facial cleansers dry my face, especially my cheeks and forehead. This product leaves the skin feeling smooth and clean, with no noticeable dryness! A very small amount goes a long way, and when you add water it foams beautifully. My skin feels more clean and definitely less dry. reviewText:
This is a fresh smelling, clean rinsing, nice and foaming face wash. My skin felt clean, but not tight or dry. It didn't feel like it had a residue either. I paired it with the matching vichy purete thermale toner and it left my skin completely clean of make up.
It didn't irritate my eye area, and removed my eye makeup without difficulty.
This is a very nice staple cleanser.

I have very sensitive skin and am allergic to a lot of different cleansers.  This works really well because it is basically free of all chemicals.  It has a wonderful scent that is not too overpowering (which is good since it goes on my nose)/  I like that it has a light lather so you can clearly see where you have rubbed it in circles.  It rinses away quickly with only a few dunks under the shower spray and doesn't feel like it has left anything on my skin afterwards.  It's not a tightening cream or anything like that, so my face just feels normal after I have rinsed it.  Overall, it's nice to have a cleanser than just cleans and doesn't try to do anything else.  No moisturizing residue, dryness, or anything else, just clean.

This is a gentle cleanser from Vichy known for superior cosmetics. The cleanser has an extract of the moringa seed, typically found in the foothills of Himalayas, that is used to purify water. This probably diminishes the effects of hard water on skin.

So far, I had been using Nuetrogena's Healthy Skin Booster Cleanser which is cheaper than Vichy and has a pretty good effect on my skin. However, it also contains Sodium Laureth Sulphate that can be drying on the skin. The Vichy cleanser does not have that ingredient and has more of glycerin that helps soften the skin. It is a gentle and rich cleanser that helps eliminate the hardness in water and really remove the makeup from the skin.

I still need to go over the area around the eyes and my lips with another product as the waterproof mascara and eyeliner and 24 hour lip colors are harder to remove but Vichy manages to get most of the makeup off without drying out my face. It is great especially for the winter when I need to make sure I don't use drying products on my face.
summary: Moisturising and gentle cleanser, great for my skin especially in winter.

reviewText: I normally use Cetaphil Gentle Skin Cleanser but was really intrigued to see if this expensive gel cleanser was better, especially given its hard water claims. (We definitely have hard water here.) The gel is very thick, and has a light, but not overpowering, scent which I would describe as similar to other fresh air or ocean breeze varieties. Theres a slight tingle when you rub in the low-foam soap, but it doesnt leave your skin feeling tight or stripped, just soft and clean. I used it in the shower, just as I do the Cetaphil, for a daily morning wash. It rinsed cleanly and had some substance going on, allowing you to rub it around a bit, before it just washed away. Plus, a little goes a long way, which, given the cost, is good. Its a natural, paraben and silicone-free product, which is appreciated, and I did really like the way it made my skin feel very, very soft and not at all dry. All in all, this feels and works like what is: a high end cosmetic cleanser. Its very nice, and the only knock I can think to give it is on cost, which would make it hard for me, a beauty cheapskate, to buy again, but all-in-all I did find it better than my Cetaphil, and really liked how its made my skin feel after use.

reviewText:
This water and glycerin-based cleanser is truly for my sensitive skin, with no parabens, sulfates, or silicone.  It cleanses well and leaves a fresh feel to my skin.  Although I would categorize this as "non-drying," of course it's going to remove some of the surface oils that you're trying to wash away.  The pump bottle dispenses a thick, dime-size amount that's the right amount to cover my face.  Because the formula is so thick, I wet my hands first before dispensing so that it spreads more easily over my skin.

It's difficult to find a facial cleanser that doesn't contain silicone, a compound that I'm allergic to, and it's great that the Vichy face wash stays away from silicone, parabens, and sulfates, three cosmetic additives that can cause skin reactions.  Thank you, Vichy!

I suffer from redness caused by rosacea, and I am always looking for ways to minimize that redness. I like to use green-tinted primer to counter-act the redness and it usually works because it is simple color theory: green and red are opposite on the color wheel, so they neutralize each other. But that only works in theory. Some color correctors or primers can leave you looking muddy or green. Japonesque color correcting crayon is just subtle enough (think green tea) that is neutralizes red without making you look weird. In fact, it made my skin look like my skin, only way better.

I apply this once in the morning and as long as I am not super sweaty or touching my face, it lasts all day. I can apply tinted moisturizer or foundation over it without causing a weird texture or reversing the effects. I imagine it will work wonders for people who only never to cover a red spot, but for someone like me with lots of redness, it is a marvel.
summary: Perfect way to neutralize the red

reviewText:
When it comes to make-up, sometimes certain colors do a better job of creating certain effects or' correcting issues. Lilac can correct sallowness, orange can correct dark circles, and yes, green can correct redness. Hence the Japonesque green correcting crayon, which is a really nice-sized make-up 'crayon', a nice thick one which you twist at the end to make more of the creamy, soft, foundation-like 'base' to come up (instead of having to worry about sharpening it). It can be applied directly to your face, by your fingers, a brush or a blender, whichever you prefer, and a little does well to hide a blemish or a hint of redness beneath the eyes, whatever bit of redness you're trying to hide. It blended well with the foundation I put on over it (nothing too heavy).
Though to be fair, I have fair skin and this is a light green, so it might be why it works well on me.

Many years ago I had a green concealer stick that neutralized red places on my face.  I hadn't used one or even seen one for years, until I saw this Japonesque correcting crayon on Amazon.  Both of my college age daughters have times when their face breaks out and they want to cover the redness, so I ordered this stick for them.

First of all, it's big (4 inches long and .3 ounce of product) and will last a long time.  I like that it rolls up like a lipstick, and that it goes on smoothly.  It's a light green color, which is the "opposite" of red and neutralizes blemishes or reddish areas in skin. Just dab a tiny dot of the green on the problem area, blend and the spot disappears.  I used a bit just to get a feel for it, and it really does make redness disappear.  It doesn't leave your face looking green, though, and you can use foundation or powder over the top of it.

Both daughters were very happy with this correcting crayon, and now I suppose I have to buy a second one to prevent fighting.  It seems a little expensive at $22, but when you find a good quality product that works well it's worth it.
summary: Neutralizes redness in your skin - works perfectly!

reviewText:
When I opened the cap, the entire bullet came out with it. I was able to put it back in the crayon, but it smeared some as the product is very soft, so it doesn't look great anymore (and for the price, that's annoying). Normally, Japonesque is a trusted brand for me, so I'm not sure what happened here.

As for the color correcting, yeah, it works well with fingers or a brush to conceal redness, but it didn't work any better than my concealer alone. Also, it's expensive for what feels like cheap packaging. I'd reccomend trying a drugstore color corrector before buying this one.
summary: The entire bullet came out in the cap

reviewText:
This color correcting redness remover looks like green tea in a stick, and since the line is Japon/Japanesque, and since steeped green tea bags also help with redness (under the eyes), I can't imagine a better color. Of course green is typically the color of redness removers, of which I've used a few. However, the Japonesque one is superior to any I previously used.

For starters, it's moist and feels wet, which makes application a breeze. It's great for my nose contours, which tend to show redness, my eyes (ditto) and cheeks. It is smooth and feels good when I'm applying it. I notice it blends extremely well and does not show under my foundation. Another terrific tool in my makeup arsenal
summary: Green is the color of beautiful skin

reviewText: There was quite a learning curve with using this stick, I ended up giving up on it after a few days. I found that it did help with hyper pigmentation but it tends to melt too much and the product just gets spread around as I continue to apply makeup. It isn't as effective over the course of a full day as a mineral based color corrector product I usually use is. I think this would be fine to try, but I don't think anyone would have this as their go to product for color correction.
summary: Didn't work so well for me

reviewText: I have broken capillaries on one side of my nose that date back years ago to my first pregnancy.  I've even had surgical procedures to lessen the look of this but I still have considerable redness on my nose.  I wear concealers but was intrigued by the thought of a neutralizer type of product.  When I got it and it was green, I wondered how it could work - but it does!.  I use this and then put on my foundation and you can't see the redness at all.  It is a nice larger size and I think it will last quite a while.  I will certainly be buying this again in the future.
summary: Neutralized the look of the my red broken capillaries

reviewText:
The lavender shade of this concealing crayon is intended to neutralize yellow and brown spots. A green shade is what is used to cover red discolorations. The theory is that in order to conceal a discoloration, use the color located in the opposite position on the color wheel. The elements/hues that create a particular color are camouflaged when the opposite elements/hues are applied.

I have a couple of light brown spots on one side of my forehead -- small but I notice them. Following the manufacturer's instructions, I lightly drew a couple of lines over the area, and gently rubbed/buffed the concealer into the spots. Then I applied my usual foundation and the brown spots were very hard to see. The crayon went on smoothly and lightly. Blend well -- a little goes a long way.
This does help but not really any better than my normal concelaers which are a lot cheaper.

I ordered this color correcting crayon to help cover the spots on my face. It does correct the color somewhat but not make it disappear completely. It seem to work the best when using the crayon on the spots first and then applying a foundation and blending it in. Also, it hasn't caused any reactions on my sensitive skin so far. All in all, I think this product is okay. It's not 100% but does lighten the spots somewhat.

I'm pleasantly surprised by how well this color correcting crayon works. I have occasional breakouts and they are sometimes hard to conceal. This crayon is light green in color that neutralizes the redness from the breakouts very well. It goes on smoothly and has a nice texture that blends in with my skin very well. Though it does leave a somewhat green tint on my skin. I would just use a tinted moisturizer or a foundation to go on top of it. No irritations or reactions so far. All in all, it does a good job of mitigating the redness from the breakouts. Easy to use or carry. I'd highly recommend it.

This really does just look like a huge crayon.  So, when they say color correcting crayon, they've nailed it.  I was surprised that it already had a pinkish tint to it. I could see where that might not match everyone's tone.  I have a fairly dark spot on my right cheek probably from too much sun while riding a motorcycle.  If I apply foundation alone, it seems to make the spot even darker.  It is very nearly impossible to conceal 100% and I have never found a product that has been able to do that.  Therefore, when I saw this product, I really wanted to try it out.  I followed the instructions via drawing the stripes and then also blending it with my foundation as well.  I also tried it without blending in the foundation, that didn't work at all.  But, when used with the foundation blending, you can see from the pics, it did help lighten the dark spot quiet a bit.  Is it 100%? Nope.  But, again, this is a pretty severe spot.  I would say if anyone had only half of the amount of pigmentation discoloration of my spot, this product would more than likely work to cover it completely if used per the instructions.  Meaning - blending it with the foundation.  Overall, it did help lighten the spot, but wasn't able to cover it completely, therefore I'm giving it 4 stars. I will give 5 stars to the product that can cover it completely.  Marilyn
It does a good job if covering colored spots and it hasn't irritated my skin. It's also nicely designed to carry around without getting ruined. Definitely well done for keeping in a makeup bag.
summary: It does a good job if covering colored spots and it hasn't irritated ...

reviewText: It's ok. Not sure I'll get it again. Smells good, but feels a bit waxy.
Love Jane Iredale LipDrink Lip Balm.  Great to apply to your lips, especially with the  fall/winter seasons coming.  I highly recommend this product!
summary: Love Jane Iredale LipDrink Lip Balm

reviewText: I'm glad this wAs a free item. The color is awful and it does not soften the lips.

I bought this in the color "crush" after trying a sample of the " nude".  I really like the nude color better and the sample seems to have more of a scent.  Maybe it's just me but either way this is excellent lipstick.  My lips feel and look instantly hydrated.
summary: I really like the nude color better and the sample seems to ...

reviewText: This is a great product-- really protects my lips, with a dash of natural looking color and no waxy feeling. I don't leave home without it.

I like Burts Bees tinted lip balm (less $$$) but Jane Iredale "crush" balm has nicer texture and yummy smell so $$$ price is justified. Other brands have prettier hues though. I don't use conventional lipstick as it usually contains lead
summary: "crush" = intense color and no funny taste

reviewText: At long last, the best lip balm & tinted no less!) - love the name of lip drink - suits perfectly. Glides on, you can feel the moisture. Delighted. Wear it over lipstick and on its own. Bought Buff - nice nude color that matches my own. Love Jane Iredale products - such fabulous stuff!

If you've never tried Jane Iredale products you should give them a try. I've yet to try one of her cosmetics I haven't liked. This Lip Balm in buff color is really terrific and I am now use it at night to moisturize as well as during the day,

I like to use it during the day with a nude lip liner because it adds just the slightest color to my lips and makes them stand out yet not look overdone. For this reason it is nice if you just are going out for the day and want a natural look for your lips.  If however, you're looking for something that would really add more color you may want to try one of her other lip color  products. This one works more like a gloss.

Recommended. I'm obviously a big fan. My only critique is that it doesn't moisturize as well as I'd like; a simple chopstick almost works better but this obviously looks better.
summary: I really like Jane Iredale products - recommended with a nude lip liner

reviewText: I love this lip balm!  I received a sample size from a friend and after using it daily for a few weeks my lips were so soft and I swear they feel/look more plump.  I loved it so much I ordered the full size one.  It has a fresh lemon type of scent in the sheer one.  The only thing is the sheer color is white and it basically turns my lips white so i need to either put color over it or buy one of the tinted ones next time.
Love this! Light, pretty color and moisturizing. Always a reorder for me and I am very comfortable with the ingredients in Jane Iredale products.
Moisturizing and is really a pretty natural look
Excellent lip balm.

This is the best lipbalm EVER!!! I have been searching for an awesome lip balm and I have found it! It's nourishing and has a light lemony scent. My lips have improved tremendously since I started using this.  The name lives up to the product..your lips literally drink it up.  I bought the buff color and it's a nice neutral shade, highly recommend.  Price was reasonable and as always super fast shipping.
summary: LipDrink is an AWESOME lip balm for thirsty lips!

reviewText: Enjoy all JI cosmetics.
Great stuff. In this dry winter in Los Angeles it seems to be the only lip stuff they consistently works
summary: Great stuff. In this dry winter in Los Angeles ...

reviewText: i use this as a blush not much as a highliter
I like it ... a little gritty on my face but still nice and I have used it a few times.

The Gilded Honey adds highlight to the face but the color it imparts is the real difference.  The Gilded Honey adds a warm, light tan color to your cheeks or wherever you place it. So it creates a contrast to the pink blushes and gives the skin a gentle bronzing effect...very good pigment payoff but you don't have to worry about it over-browning your complexion...watch the highlighting as this product definitely provides it in just one sweep. I use it near my upper cheekbone up to my eyes and touch it on my eyelids.  It doesn't add more pink, it combats the pink tones of blush with a subtle layer of tan highlight.  Using a light touch you can swipe it on your nose, cupid's bow, chin, and forehead to add warmth and contour the face. I love it although I use it lightly and not low on the face...creates that all over shiny appearance if you overdo.  Cheekbones only for me most days.
Great product!

I got the small version of this highlighter in a Birchbox subscription a couple years ago and I used it every day for about a whole year. So this stuff is dense as HELL. You barely need any for it to show up, and it'll last you forever (for everyone complaining about the size).

When my little sample ran out, I tried about 5 other highlighters before caving and getting this one again. Nothing compares. I'll have to come back and add some photos cus this stuff makes me look like I was touched by Zeus.
summary: I'll have to come back and add some photos cus this stuff makes me look like I was touched by Zeus

reviewText: This is a gorgeous champagne highlighter. A lot of people say it is very similar to the Becca Champagne Pop highlighter. It probably is somewhat similar but it's not exactly the same color.

These are excellent wipes.  They are thick and durable almost like a very thin cloth.  The best part about using a quality wipe like this is that you will use less while cleaning baby.  These are the best for poopy diapers.

I had heard that baby wipes could be used as hand cleaners for removing paint. So I got this to try it out and sure enough, it is a great way to clean your hands, especially in the field. I don't mean to imply that these are harshthey are very mild which is why I use them over harsh cleansers made for artists.

There is a slight residue of moisturizer, but that is fine especially when your hands might be getting chapped. The scent is mild and doesn't intrude at all like I remember some wipes. They are listed as fragrance-free, but there is a slight scent which I can't quite identify. However, like I mentioned it is very mild. It might just be the smell of the moisturizer. After using these on my paint sullied hands, I have no doubt they will work great with your baby as well.
They don't smell like anything - like they're supposed to.  Seem nice and gentle.

These are described as lightly scented, but I find them to be very strongly scented. Perfumey, with a musty note. Not a pleasant scent.
The wipe itself is soft and decently sized, but due to the scent I won't be using these.

Thinner than expected and not entirely fragrance free. Took a lot of wipes to clean up a blow out today so perhaps they're too thin. But these wipes are very soothing and have the poorer amount of moisture.

Amazon generally offers quality items at great prices, but I have to factor in the cost when I review these items.  As of this writing, one relatively small bag of 70 wipes is selling for $8.  I do not find that to be a good value.

In terms of the product itself, it's heavily scented.  While the scent isn't terribly objectionable, I don't personally care for it.  On the positive side, these wipes are sturdy and work well for their intended purpose.

So they're decent wipes, but two things I don't like, the scent and the price.  Please note that while my wipes were heavily scented, the link that was provided for this review references unscented wipes.  I'd probably like those better, although I'd still feel that the price was excessive.

2.5 stars rounded up to 3 for the reasons discussed.
.
summary: Amazon generally offers quality items at great prices, but I have to factor in the ...

reviewText: My son has a sensitive bottom and these wipes are great. It is not exactly fragrance free, but the scent isn't bad. However, I do like the one-and-done type wipes and you definitely need more than one of these - I would not say they are "extra thick" as Mustela claims.
summary: Need More Than One to Get the Job Done!

reviewText:
This 70 pack of Mustela Dermo-Soothing Wipes are great wipes. I'm a mom of a baby who is still in diapers and who also has extremely sensitive skin. These wipes are Fragrance-Free, pretty soft and thick. They do not crumble apart when using and are sturdy and efficient in cleaning the diaper area.
A lot of baby wipes contain alcohol which tends to be extremely drying on a baby's skin. I appreciate the natural ingredients used in these baby wipes. Overall a great and effective product.
Nice alcohol-free soothing wipes for sensitive skin. I like the easy open and re-sealable dispenser  great wipes to keep on hand for quick and soothing clean-ups.

I had some Mustela products that I loved that had a woodsy/herbal scent. I understood they changed up their fragrance to the current formulation. All of the blue label Mustela products seem to have it.

These wipes were said to be fragrance free but I got the scented ones. The package is safety sealed and the wipes are nice; just moist enough and do not fall apart. However the fragrance is definitely a love it or hate it thing. I find it very strong and baby specific. It also lingers. If you have any of the newer Mustela products, it is the same scent. I don't love the fragrance but the wipes are just fine. However I would not use them on my ( or a baby's) face since the fragrance would drive me crazy. If these really were available in a non fragrance form I would buy them.
summary: Nice wipes but the scent is cloying

reviewText: I'm an adult with no babies. However, I have sensitive skin and like these wipes to freshen up my armpits and neck on a hot day.
summary: They work well for adults with sensitive skin

reviewText: Great product!
I believe it was fake. Left my scalp itchy and inflamed
Love the scent. It really works well with absorbing oil and also gives limp hair volume.
Amazing find. Keeps hair fuller and fresh. Saves an extra day of not washing and yet still have non greasy good hair day
summary: Amazing find. Keeps hair fuller and fresh

reviewText:
Big fan of Baxter products.  The pomade I use everyday so of course when offered this for free through vine it was a no brainer.  The deorderant is nice, but if you are a heavy sweater this product is not for you as the ingredients to fight that problem are not their, but to use it in conjuction with an unscented antiperspirant could be an option.  The moistenizer is nice and is made for people with normal skin, goes on smoothly and washes off without leaving an oily residue.

Overall a great gift for dad, husband, boyfriend, son, or yourself for the upcoming holidays.

This is an excellent kit. As with many Baxter products it's a bit expensive, but very good quality as well.

Included:

Deodorant. This is the scent I'd been looking for my while life. Gentle musk with a hint of citrus, maybe some notes of sandalwood. It's a very clean scent, just a hint masculine. I love it.

Clay Pomade. This stuff is the best. Wet your hands, warm it up like modeling clay, and rub it into wet hair. I've driven to my destination with the windows down and arrived in high winds, and you couldn't find a hair out of place. Amazing stuff. The only worry is that it doesn't always apply evenly, so grab a hand mirror and spot check in case there are any clumps.

Oil Free Moisturizer. Sometimes my knuckles crack, especially if I'm staying at a hotel or other place with hard water. This stuff does the trick every time. Extremely moisturizing, and smells good too.

Overall:

I love all the parts of this kit, and highly recommend them.

I have been using BoC products for a few years now.  I really like this pack.  The deodorant smells great.  I use it in conjunction with a nighttime product and the combo keeps me dry all day.  I have semi-oily skin and the lotion does leave my face looking a bit greasy by the end of the workday, but YMMV.  It moisturizes really well so I still tend to use it quite a bit.  I have several clay/wax/pomades and the included clay pomade has made it into my rotation.  I have fine hair and I have found this one is best applied to damp hair then I use the hair dryer to work it through my hair and give it some hold.
summary: Nice kit, all products work well

reviewText:
I have enjoyed using this product.  The kit contains Deodorant, Clay Pomade, and Oil Free Moisturizer.

The deodorant is 2.65 oz.  It is an alcohol free, sensitive skin formula.  The container is round.  I love the light smell of citrus and Herbal musk.  I have been using it a few days and am very happy with the results.

The clay Pomade has not been used yet.  It is in a glass jar holding 2 oz of product.  The top says the product is a firm hold with a matte finish.

I have used the Oil Free Moisturizer.  This is a hydrating lotion for men.  The lotion is for normal to oily skin.  The product is fragrance free.  The plant based hydration technology absords quickly to restore the skins moisture barrier,  leaving the skin feeling smooth and refreshed.  I have used the lotion of my normal skin a couple of times and it has left me skin feeling good.  There was no oily feeling after use, which I hate.

I did receive this item as a Vine Test item.  I would have given it 5 stars however the items showed up in a clear plastic baggie.  If the items are packaged as the picture shows in a nice box, it would make a very good mens gift and I would have given the product all 5 stars.

Great set of nice working products! The Clay Pomade was the product my husband questioned. He is used to a firm hold shiny product that puts his hair in a NON movable state. This was different, it has super hold but not shiny. It was more of a natural hold, without the "fake" hair look. The moisturizer is perfect! In fact I have found myself using it so many times! It is non greasy and fragrance free which is nice. I like that it moisturizers without the feel of needing to wash your face, some moisturizers leave such a shiny glow which I hate. Lastly, the deodorant is great. It has a light scent, fresh citrus scent that my husband said worked fine all day. Went on smooth and kept him fresh, exactly what you want!

I have long used the clay pomade and the skin moisturizer in this set, sharing them with my husband. The pomade has firm hold but no shine and is great at lifting find hair for volume without flakes. The moisturizer is completely fragrance free, works all day without any build up or pilling. It us the only skin care product my husband will use on his face. All three products are full sized.

The deodorant is secented with a citrus musk that in my opinion is gender neutral and very pleasant. I do not sweat profusely under my arms so this is ideal for me. There is no way my husband would ever use this as he works in a non air conditioned facility and relies upon heavy duty antiperspirants.  If I gave him this as a gift he'd throw the deodorant out. Fortunately we can share this and I really love the deodorant. In our house this set gets a complete work out. As long as that is the case for you, this is an excellent trio of products from one of my favorite companies.
summary: For us, a wonderfully useful kit. Make sure you understand it includes deodorant, not antiperspirant.

reviewText:
This is a nice 3 piece set of high end grooming essentials for men.  The stick style deodorant is made for sensitive skin and has a wonderful, masculine smell to it.  It's a full sized unit

There is also a boxed 4 ounce tube of oil free moisturizer.  The directions say to apply liberally to face and neck.  It's odorless, so I (a woman) am using it on my face and neck and it blends well.  It does not make my face shiny.  It's a keeper for me and I usually use Estee Lauder face cream, so that tells you what quality I am used to. I apply it liberally to my face and neck and its literally absorbed in minutes.

There is also a nice glass jar of Clay Pomade.  It's 2 fluid ounces of solid Pomade.  It's firm hold.  Nice stuff.  It has a matte finish, so it holds short hair in place, or you can create great parts with it, and there's no shine.

I like this set and my husband does too.  He especially loves the deodorant.
summary: A Good Set of 3 Products Marketed For Men

reviewText: This shower gel has a light, 'perfumey" fragrance. It lathers well and rinses clean. My wife said her skin felt soft and smooth afterwards. It did exactly what it was expected to do and did it well. But so do many other products on the market. I would say that this product's popularity would depend on the user's taste in fragrance.
Works great for shaving legs in the shower. What I love is that this oil isn't slimy at all. It rinses out very well but, it's moisturizes. Love!
summary: Works great for shaving legs in the shower

reviewText: A soft floral fragrance shower oil, that goes on smoothly,  and the result is hydrated looking skin.  I like that it is not super oily, more like a richly conditioned body wash.  The fragrance is soft and not over powering.  I like how it made my skin look and feel.
summary: I like that it is not super oily

reviewText: Non slippery in the shower and you feel soft after drying your skin.  Not as soft as SoftSoap but SoftSoap is very slippery when wet.  The fragrance seeps out of the bathroom and smells so good everywhere.

I love how this shower gel smells.  It also feels great in the shower.

It leaves my skin a little dry too so I have to make sure to use the NUXE oil.
summary: I love how this shower gel smells

reviewText: Fantastic fragrance, reminds me of neroli and gardenia with a hint of powder.  Makes lots of soft, creamy lather that leaves skin soft and smooth but not greasy. I only wish that the golden shimmer lingered on my skin instead of washing down the drain.  They do make a dry oil that has a golden shimmer which you apply to your skin post shower but I haven't tried that so I don't know if it has the same great smell.
summary: Taking showeres to the next level.

reviewText: This is a an decent shower oil with an OK scent. Nothing offensive here, but nothing particularly outstanding or compelling either. Maybe that's a good thing. We don't have a lot of experience wit shower oils and were surprised to see that it lathers like a soap. I think if you want a very moisturizing cleanser than this is worth a try perhaps,  but for us  it is decidedly middle of the road.

I'm not... particularly impressed with this shower oil, particularly for the price. Don't get me wrong; it's not a bad body wash. It cleans and does the job, but it's definitely not a product I'd pay upwards of $15 for.

It claims to leave your skin with a satin finish, and... well, my skin felt the way it does when I use most body washes: a little moisturized but not overly so. It definitely doesn't moisturize as well as the Olay body wash I usually use. The gel itself is golden and shimmery, but it doesn't leave any sort of shimmer on your skin. The scent is rather strong, but strangely enough it isn't as heavy when it's lathering up as it is in the tube. It's a pleasant enough fragrance, but it is on the stronger side, if you have a sensitive nose.

Is it good? Yeah, it's a nice body wash. Is it worth the cost? Not for me.

This is a product which has all of the trappings of luxury. It looks shimmery and golden. It feels smooth and silky. It's also fairly expensive for the quantity and it smells fairly nice (albeit a tad strong right out of the bottle - the scent mutes well as you shower). The problem is that, while it moisturizes decently, it doesn't lather well and it doesn't moisturize as well as a dedicated after shower lotion. It doesn't even feel like it's cleaning your body, though I'm guessing it is.

Using this product reminds me of something I learned in a documentary on ancient Rome quite some time ago. Gladiators cleaned themselves by slathering olive oil on their skin and then having it scraped off. This feels like one is cleaning in a similar fashion rather than using more traditional soap. This isn't a bad thing, it's just unusual, and one tube isn't going to last long relative to using soap. I'd say this is best used for specific applications (face, legs, etc.) rather than a full body use.
summary: lots of style, less so substance

reviewText:
I was initially not sure what to make of a "shower oil". After giving the NUXE Prodigieux shower oil a try, I have to admit that I'm pleasantly surprised with it.

The shower oil is a thick, amber colored gel embedded with golden shimmering flecks. It works up into a light lather and rinses off easily. It leaves me feeling clean, soft and moisturized. There are also no oily residue or look on the skin. The golden flecks rinse off and disappear completely, so I'm not sure what they are for or if they do anything to the skin.

My only gripe with this product is the strong scent. It isn't unpleasant but it is a little too much and tends to linger after shower. The residual scent is less obtrusive but it still lasts for hours. I don't mind the smell in the shower but would rather not have the smell stay with me for long.

Overall, I like that the shower oil leaves me feeling clean, soft and moisturized. However, I don't like the strong scent and its lingering effect.
summary: Great shower gel but strong scent

reviewText:
This is a pretty nice shower oil, but the scent is very strong. Reminds me of Ban de Solel suntan lotion, that we used when I was a kid.

It works okay, has a bit of shimmer but the scent is very strong.

I used this tonight with a loofa in the bath tonight and while it smells great, it doesn't really leave much of a shimmer like I had hoped it would.  I don't know if I thought I would look like I was painted with diamond cream (Arrested Development) but I hardly looked like an Emmy statuette.  It does make your skin nice and soft but so do other less expensive products.  Heck, buy some of that sparkly spray that sell at Halloween for your hair in bulk and add it to your body lotion.  Problem solved.

I love, love, love this shower gel! It's pearly softness transforms into a lovely feeling bath soap that gently cleans and moisturizes your skin and leaves a beautiful sheen behind after rinsing. Your skin will thank you for this, I promise! Worth every single penny and more! I give this 5 stars and a big thumbs up!
summary: Your Skin Will Love You For This!

reviewText:
My wife was a bit confused by this one--she wasn't quite sure what it is supposed to be. Shower Oil? That's not a cleanser, not a moisturizer ... and it's claims are vague to say the least. Still, she is always happy to try out a new beauty product!

She said it foamed up when she used it, which was unexpected. The scent is super strong; no subtlety here. She wasn't a fan of it, but that is always up to personal preference. It lathered up and rinsed off with little muss or fuss. She has used it a few times now, and says she doesn't notice much effect. Everyone's skin is different, she said, but this did nothing for her.

I wasn't sure what to expect from a shower "oil", but I must say I'm pleasantly surprised.

I use it in my shower poof and it lathers quite nicely. Two shots of soap into the poof as I shower is enough to get my entire body squeaky clean. By clean, I really do mean clean. I wasn't sure if my skin would feel oily or greasy after my shower, but in actuality it feels quite clean and gently moisturized. If anything, I would like it to be a tad more moisturizing, especially since it's an "oil", but I'd rather have it be too little than too much. I put lotion on after I shower anyway. I didn't notice much of a "golden shimmer", but my skin did look very nice after showering and lotion.

The scent is very subtle, which I appreciate as I don't like my bath product scents to overpower lotions and/or perfumes. I wouldn't say the scent itself is anything spectacular, kind of a floral, beachy, slightly spicy scent but what's nice it's versatile enough to go with most perfumes I wear.

All in all, I really like this shower oil. Recomnded.

This shower oil may sound a little strange. I have used some products marketed as such which just left a greasy residue on my skin. This is a little different because it emulsifies when it comes in contact with water and gets sort of creamy. After applying and adding I thought this was a nice moisturizing product that restored moisture to the skin's surface and left my skin with a soft glowing patina that looked far nicer than dry skin with a crocodile look that resembled one of my handbags.
This product has a nice scent which isn't too much and it left my skin feeling better after a day at the beach. I have used another product that works in similar fashion that is less expensive, yet this is also equally nice.
My only advice is that the shower got a little slippery when in use so a rubber bath mat might be needed.
This eyeliner is great, a very nice dark navy. Just what I needed.
summary: A great every day eyeliner. Great color

reviewText: I don't wear a lot of eye liner, just a bit at the outer edges, from center of eye out. This works for that purpose. I use the smudge tip from my other pencil since this doesn't have one. I don't find that it sets after 30 seconds like stated. By the end of the day, it's basically worn off. Not hard to clean, I don't end up having to rub the delicate skin under my eyes, so that is a plus. It is an ok pencil and doesn't irritate my eyes. I would use it again at a reasonable cost.
summary: Goes on smooth, easy to remove without pulling delicate eye skin.

reviewText: I like this pencil very much. It goes on super smoothly like a premium product should. Sometimes even the more expensive pencils can let you down, this one doesn't. It is nice and pigmented, and doesn't skip or jump when applying. I haven't really noticed it lasting longer than other premium pencils, but it does perform better than drugstore kinds. For the longest wear, I usually use a premium liquid (I like Urban Decay 24/7 and Kat Von D Tattoo liner) but they aren't pencils. Liquid doesn't smudge like a pencil can, so I do like to have pencils around. I do usually "set" the pencil with a similar color eyeshadow on top. It does seem to make them last a little longer for me.

Though 10 hours is NOT my experience for how long it stays, it does go on smoothly and works as well as my typical kohl.  It is a bit odd to need to sharpen what looks like plastic, as I'd typically expect some sort of advancing mechanism.  The pigment itself is quite soft, so sharpening is more challenging than I consider ideal.  Good color, easy application, doesn't last all day.  So, not bad but not perfect.

I am very impressed at how well this eyeliner glides. It's like a felt tip pen the way it smoothly writes. It was a bit too harsh looking for me without blending it. After some trial and error, I did learn that you have to smudge it pretty quickly before it dries/sets. It did seem to last a while, but by the end of the work day, it didn't look like I had just put it on. One of my eyes waters a lot during the day, so I do rub and blot my eyes frequently which could be the reason for it looking less fresh. My teenage daughter has claimed it as her own and really likes it.
This eyeliner goes on smoothly and stays put all day.  I would recommend.

When I opened the package of this eyeliner, I was confused. I was expecting a liquid-ish application, though it looked like a pencil. Technology is a wonderful thing, and never more evident than in the cosmetics industry!
This gel liner is genius. I prefer liquid liners over pencil, though most often I end up using a blend of both. But for precise application that stays, it's liquid for me, hands-down.
This eyeliner may have just bumped it.
It goes on glossy smooth, and exactly the shade of black I expect it to be--dark and opaque. I didn't have to go back over it repeatedly to get it solid, as happens sometimes with liquid. Also, if I made a mistake (which I did), it cleaned up quickly and completely without leaving a shadow. That's pretty awesome.
The applicator tip looks like a pencil, which is very nice. If you're quite deft of hand, you can still get nice thin lines. If you're not so careful or concerned about thin lines, this applicator is really made for moderate lining, with a medium application. It doesn't take much effort to get a nice, solid line.
If you're someone who has problems with your hands yet loves the look and ease of liquid eyeliners, I think this one will give you less frustration. I have issues with the agility of my hands, and with tremors, and this eyeliner is very forgiving. It's a novel concept, really, to have makeup easy to use for people who have disabilities with their hands.
My only reason for marking this eyeliner down one star is $16? That just seems crazy expensive for what is essentially still just a eye pencil. $10, maybe, most likely a solid $8. Price is the only real impediment to this eyeliner.

EDIT: After wearing it for several days, it is irritating to my eyes. It wasn't at first, though at this pint I'm certain that's what's caused my eyes eo become itchy and red. Bummer. Also, it's difficult to remove. Waterproof is right. Even with an emollient remover (Artiste), it takes a bit of pulling and scrubbing to get it off.
summary: Lovely, smooth, and forgiving if you have unsteady hands

reviewText:
This eyeliner has extremely smooth application and stay all day longevity.  It glides on with no resistance.  You must use eye makeup remover to get it off.  I made a mark on my hand as well as using it on my eyes, and two days later, after two showers and many handwashings, it is still faintly there.  Just don't slip when you apply it or else you'll have to remove everything and start over.

The blackest black is REALLY black, too dark for me but excellent for anyone looking for this color.  I really thought the colort would be okay; however, it's darker than my  mascara.  That's my mistake, though, not the product's.  I'm thinking of buying a different color since it doesn't smudge and goes on so easily.

-- Debbie Lee Wesselmann

I love, love the Gel Long-Lasting Waterproof Gel Eyeliner. This is by far the best eyeliner that I have ever used. It goes on really easily and smooth without gaps. It does not pull nor tug and the point size is perfect. While I doubt that I would have chosen Blackest Black as my first choice, it looks fantastic and lasts all day.  My next purchase will definitely be Rich Brown. It is not super easy to remove but it is so worth it.

I have been trying really hard to learn to use this pencil met gel product from Julep.  The blackest black color is wonderfully rich, yet the product just wobbled off at the end as I opened the cover. I thought perhaps it was an error, or it was damaged somehow. As I touched the piece that fell off, I noticed it is very soft, which is understandable since it is advertised as gel. As I touched the piece that fell off, I noticed it is very soft, which is understandable since it is advertised as a gel.  And I applied what was left exposed from the pencil to my lash line, and I found it looking very nice.  However, as carefully as I was trying to apply it, product would find itself under my lower lash line, and it would not remove. I tried make up remover towelettes which have very good emollients, yet after two towelettes I could not remove the black.

I was guessing that because a gel needs to dry well before setting,  I would be able to remove what was underneath my lower eyelashes.

I do have this problem with most eyeliners, landing under the eye. However, I prefer those which are removed easily.  I would like to find a longer-lasting product like this in the future that will be easier for me to use. Perhaps it is just me.
summary: Not working for me well at all. But definitely long-lasting, and rich.

reviewText: When I was on a book signing, I used Bobbi Brown eyeliner because it was the only one I could count on to not smear or wear off all day long. Well, finally, I have found another eyeliner which is equally as long lasting--Julep's. Also, because it doesn't come in a little pot, it is less apt to dry out. TOTALLY less apt to dry out! Here is the sharpener Julep suggests you buy to keep this waterproof mascara sharpened: Julep Gel Eye Glider Sharpener . I am not sure yet whether this is a good buy, but the eyeliner sure is! I have photographed it next to my tattoo, so you can see how very dark the darkest black is. I am loving it!

I purchased the blackest black liner and it's just what I needed. It lives in my purse and just a quick swipe gives me beautiful results as a dark and black line on my eyelids. It does not fade during the day, especially if applied over eye primer, but even without it works well and stays put all day. It's like drawing with a crayon only better as it's made of gel and so it's lightweight and has staying power and does not pull on the eyes. Something I hate about pencil and pen liners as they pull too much. Not this one.

It's great for the waterline too as the liquids can get inside the eye. However, applied on the waterline it can smudge a bit during the day and needs a cotton bud or tissue wipe occasionally so it does not spread under the eye. It works better than liquid in a hurry as it's faster and easier to produce a sharp line. For those who like really thin lines, it might still be better to go with liquid or a sharp pen type liner as this pencil produces slightly thicker lines, but they're really smooth. The color is consistent and pigmented, unlike some other liners. It also smudges less than Urban Decay liners for me.

The only negative is as it gets used it can get thicker and does not produce a crisp line as it does when it's pointy so I have to shave off the tip a bit to give the same result. I wish it was a self sharpening type as it does not sharpen well and tends to break sometimes. That is why I reduced a star. It's still a great product.

Update - Reducing another star as it's impossible to sharpen this pencil! After using it a few times the tip disappeared and the pencil does not sharpen with the 2-3  different sharpeners that I tried. Finally figured out that you have to press really hard to sharpen, but does not sharpen to the same type of point and makes a thicker smudged line. However, I bought another one as I do need to use pencil when I am in a hurry, I am now trying to find the perfect eyeliner pen. There are some nice ones available at Sephora.
summary: Smooth, pigmented, all day application. Hard to sharpen.

reviewText: Really a very sexy and attractive color.  Bold and alluring but not over-the-top.  Easy to apply and stays in place.  High quality product sure to get you noticed in a good way.  5 stars.
summary: Easy to apply and stays in place

reviewText:
It is no longer halloween and my glam band days are over, so I rely on my wife and daughter to give me their expert opinion on this. Both like the color -  a bit bold for their tastes but not overly showy. I light coat is good. It feels good on and is easy to apply with a smooth texture. It stays on the lips and actually helps moisturize and protect during the day. I'm not a big fan of the price, nor one of lipstick in general, but I have to say that my gals look good in it. I would say this color is best for dress up occasions even though it is a lipstick that is "healthy" to wear anytime. I like the natural ingredient list (most of them anyway like aloe and rosehips) and the fact that "10% of all retail sales go to the We See Beauty Foundation to fund women-led, worker-owned cooperative businesses in America." - Yes!
