Okay, I'll admit that I did try it while at home. To me it felt a bit thick, but I'm used to chapstick at most. It did go on easy, though I got a few laughs at my attempts apply it neatly. It felt good on my lips, didn't turn my teeth red, didn't have a smell or off taste. I don't recommend eating it though. I have to admit, I looked fabulous. :D

~ Kort
summary: MAKE - Strong enough for a man, but made for a woman.

reviewText: The color is vivid and highly pigmented. I love that this Maraschino Cherry shade is not orangy red, but more rose/pink. It is a moisturizing lipstick. Usually that means the oil that keeps your lips from drying also let the color fade and wear out much quicker. Not the case here, the color goes on creamy smooth and precise like matte lipstick. It doesn't smear. Primer is recommended but I wore it without and had dinner right after. At end of the night, the color is there and needed only a bit of touch up. I'm not familiar with the MAKE brand, but this lipstick will stay in my go to tray.

This is a bright, bold red that leans just a tad toward pink. Its molded angle makes application very easy. The texture is creamy, a perfect balance between, say, a Benefits stick and a MAC matte stick (Benefits goes on like a lotion, but it runs; MAC's matte colors are almost chalky). I put this on in the morning, had lunch, and only needed a light application after - no running or smearing. It's got enough moisturizer in it to keep my lips from burning at the end of the day, when I remove my makeup. Color stays sharp, which is difficult to come by, but absolutely essential, in a bright red. I did wear a liner with it, and it does perform better when I do. Odorless. Recommended.
summary: Bright Red Stays On, Doesn't Bleed

reviewText:
The MAKE Cosmetics Dual Phase Eye Makeup Remover may be pricey, but it works and works fantastically.  While I love using coconut oil to remove my makeup normally, coconut oil does feel incredibly greasy and doesn't always work well on some cosmetics, particularly those "Everlasting Lipsticks".  The MAKE makeup remover melts eye make up away without irritating my eyes and can easily lift off those stubborn lipsticks.  To use, simply shake the bottle, put some onto a small cotton ball, then wipe the makeup off.

After using this remover, I didn't have any ill side effects or skin breakouts.  The remover is gentle on the skin, doesn't have a strong scent, and works very well.  This is a remover I would purchase again.
summary: Removes Makesup, Particularly Everlasting Lipstick, Very well - No Breakouts, Gentle on Skin

reviewText:
This eye makeup remover is very effective at removing eye makeup, including those that are water proof.  It doesn't cause any irritation and is easy to wash off.  There are a few reasons I am not giving it 5 stars.

1) Pricey for what it is (mostly oil and water)
2) Application process is wasteful (pouring onto a pad causes excess product to be used)
3) Fluid separates quickly (again, oil and water)

For background I have always used a drop of baby oil on my finger tip to remove eye makeup, then I wipe it off with a bit of tissue and wash my face.  It's super cheap and works great.  I used the same technique with MAKE and it greatly reduced the waste of saturating a cotton round or tissue and since this product is so pricey, you'll want to come up with some way to conserve it.  Also, be quick wit the shake and use method for better results.  The benefit this product offers over my baby oil method, is that it doesn't seem to leave the same oily residue after wiping it off that baby oil does.

This MAKE eye makeup remover works fantastically well.

What I love about it is that it caused no eye or eye area irritation for me and I have very sensitive eyes and a ton of allergies and sensitivities.  The other thing I love about it is that you aren't left with an oily feeling.  I had no feeling that I needed to wash anything off.

The only downside is that a bottle doesn't seem like it lasts long.  My teen daughter and I having been use this sample for a week or so and out bottle looks like the picture.  So expect to buy every month.  (No down star because my daughter tends to overdo :)
summary: No Oily Feeling & Works So Well

reviewText: Great! Works perfectly at removing eye makeup without leaving a greasy residue at all. Other eye makeup removers I have used work well at removal, but left a greasy residue that made makeup application challenging the next day. This one did not do that at all. Nice product!
summary: Great! Works perfectly at removing eye makeup without leaving ...

reviewText: This is an effective and gentle make-up remover.  I gave it 4 stars because of the price and because it feels oily on application.  You have to shake the bottle well before application as the oil does separate quite quickly.
summary: An effective and gentle make-up remover...good for sensitive eyes/skin

reviewText: The MAKE Cosmetics Dual-Phase Eye MAKEup Remover is fairly pricey eye makeup remover. The size is smaller than I thought it'd be. But it is a nice, gentle formula that works really well. There is no harsh chemical smell and doesn't even irritate a small dry spot near my eye. It's definitely nicer than drug store brands. So, if it's worth a heftier price tag for you, this is a good product.
summary: But it is a nice, gentle formula that works really well

reviewText:
MAKE goes on smooth and easy. I swipe a cotton ball on each eye and, voila, my mascara and eye pencil disappears without any excess rubbing. So even though some of the other Amazon.com reviewers have had a different experience and found it to be ineffective in removing makeup, my experience has been positive. Perhaps, too, now that Ive gotten older, I don't wear as much makeup any longer, which makes the process nearly effortless.

In addition, even though the makeup remover is oil-based, my skin does not feel greasy, and actually after I use the product it feels smooth.  I like that MAKE is fragrance-free and infused with cucumber and chamomile, such a nice gentle-sounding association.

Though I would have eliminated one star for the hefty price, I did not. After a final analysis, I gave MAKE five-stars because the product is made New York/GoLocal, is not tested on animals, cruelty-free and, best of all, 10 percent of all retail sales go to We See Beauty Foundation to fund women-led, worker-owned cooperative businesses in America.  Nice to have such a beautiful business in the beauty business!
summary: MAKE, MAKEs a womans life a little easier

reviewText: Very light and non-greasy.  I use a primer under my mascara and it's almost impossible to take off with other eye makeup removers.  This product DOES remove the primer!  You have to be sure to shake the product well though.  Although I do like this product, I'm only giving it 4 stars because of the price.

Make Beauty, a company founded in NYC ( I cannot find out exactly what year) has made a gentle yet effective mascara and eye makeup remover, with its Dual-Phase Eye Makeup Remover. What's more, if you check out the box, you will see that this remover is also offered for use to remove lipstick. I tried it both ways and was very satisfied with how it performs. In the first place, as a lipstick remover, it was efficient, gentle and thorough. My lips felt as if I had had a beauty treatment afterwards. They were actually smoother.  Also, there was no lipstick bleeding into those tiny feathery lines which can surround your lips as you get older. It removed my lipstick very nicely and cleanly. So, plus points for that!
As far as performance as an eye makeup remover, I used this on mascara  which I bought specifically to test this Make product. My eyes have been quite sensitive for several months and I have been avoiding eye makeup. Lo and behold, it removed the mascara quick as a wink, with no ill aftereffects and no mess, either. My eye area looks perfectly clean and feels wonderful.
I checked the prices in the local drugstore and this Dual-Phase Eye Makeup Remover it a bit more pricey, but there are plenty of products up there with it which do not hold a candle to it. And yes, it has cucumber and chamomile-infused water in it, which make it gentle and easy on your lids. I like it a lot and would definitely buy it again!  Recommended.
summary: Top notch, gentle yet effective makeup remover by Make

reviewText: This is not my favorite eye makeup remover.  I needed twice as much just to remove simple mascara.  I like a remover that works quickly and effectively.  This one did not do it for me.

I have a multitude of problems with my eyes, including dry eye and blepharitis, so getting all my eye makeup off is important. I use waterproof mascara and a gel eyeliner, which can be hard to remove. This oil-and-water combo does a good job without causing any eye irritation. I followed the advice of other reviewers, and I swipe with my finger and then go over the area with a tissue instead of using cotton balls or q-tips, which absorb too much of the product. I'm happy with any product that I can use without too much rubbing or tugging on the sensitive eye area.
summary: Good makeup remover for sensitive eyes

reviewText: Takes off even stubborn mascara without rubbing. Doesn't leave a greasy film, worked great even with my contacts in. Light scent that dissipates.
summary: I'm happy that I discovered this brand!

reviewText: This skin illuminator was quite easy to apply and gave a glow to my cheeks as I used it after I applied my powder blush.  As I put it on in the morning and did not re-apply it, the illumination did fade in  the afternoon.  I plan to carry it in my purse so that I'll be able to keep the glow that it imparts during the holiday season.

This MAKE Cosmetics Skin Illuminator is a pretty good product. It brightens up my face after application. You do have to be fairly gentle when applying because it can remove your foundation fairly easily. The problem comes in with the "button" you have to push. Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't. Sometimes you get nothing, sometimes you get way too much and other times you get nothing. The make-up itself is great quality but the applicator could use some work.

Wish the applicator issues I'd say the price is too high for the product you get. There are better options on the market at more reasonable prices. Overall, I'd say spend your money on something that has a better applicator and good makeup.

I found this product to be just fine. I love the brush and product in one applicator idea but found it hard to control the product at first. The dot that comes out on the applicator just kind of globbed in one spot but a little practice with the built in applicator distributed the illuminator right where I wanted it. I used moisturizer to thin it out and I also used foundation on another area. Both worked but defeated the ease of the one step application. Used alone as intended a light touch works best. When I used this on myself I did not see a big difference perhaps because I was in bright bathroom light and critically looking for a difference. When I tried it on my daughter and then saw her in normal light across a room at a party she glowed.

The MAKE cosmetics skin Illuminator comes in a barrel shaped applicator.  You have to press the end of the barrel to get the product to come out on the brush.  Sometimes a small amount of product comes out and sometimes more than you might need comes out.  I'm not sure how to regulate that.  This product is supposed to be applied over your regular make up to highlight and illuminate your face, but wiping it on actually removed my foundation and so that didn't work for me.  I found that I had to carefully pat it on my face with my fingers to control the amount I applied and not smear off my regular make up.  I tried putting  it on just under my eye brow and that gave me a nice brightness to the eye brow area, but if I got it on the crease of my eye lid, it created a build up in the crease that was unattractive.  For the price, you can get a powder type product that doesn't remove your regular make up and is easier to control.

I'm going to go through this point by point because I really wanted to like this product but found it lacking in several areas.

First, the applicator. You push up on a "button" at the bottom to get the product onto the brush. Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't - as in you get nothing, or you get too much, or if you're lucky it's just right.''

Second, the color. It looks much darker than it is, and once applied it gives a *tiny* bit of shimmer if you use enough, but not much more than that. Additionally, when I put it on over my makeup, it basically 'washed' my makeup off. When I tried to put it on first and then put makeup over it (both options are suggested on the product's box, by the way), my makeup, which is very light in terms of coverage, hid what little "illumination" this product offered.

Third, I agree with the other reviewer who mentioned that it made their skin feel tight. It wasn't the most unpleasant sensation ever, but it also isn't the way I want my skin to feel after applying a product that is supposed to soothe it.
Adds a nice glow to your face,but it is a little price,y and only works for very light skin tones.

Have used three or four times since recieving it and don't really find it does much at all. It is a sheer product but it's thicker than I'd like adding more layers than I needed. I will note that when used without any makeup (going to the gym) was when I liked this product best. A little touch to brighten without looking made up

I tried this product a couple of times, each time I put it on over my makeup, but I have to say that it didn't illuminate my skin as expected, I honestly could not see the difference to my skin after applying it other than it added a different color to my skin. It was easy to apply (it looks like a pearly lotion) it comes out through the small brush after you press on the end of the applicator, and even though you're suppose to use the brush to distribute it, I also ended up using my fingers to smooth it into my skin. I noticed that the color actually looked a little bit lighter on my face once applied (I'm a brunette and I had the nor color).

Additionally, after applying it, my skin didn't feel any softer, if anything, it felt a little tight. I honestly don't think it's worth the price and I would not recommend it.

This is an interesting product. It's definitely a peachy pink color with tiny glints of light reflecting off the face, what some call sparkle. I put on only a little and it gives my face a nice glow. Too heavy and it looks clownish to me.

I was looking up some of the ingredients. Two of them are Nylon-12 Fluorescent Brightener 230 Salt and Polyvinylalcohol Crosspolymer. I found this description of those two product together: "patented luminescent ingredient that emits and diffuses visible light to dramatically reduce the appearance of skin imperfections. The 5 micron particles are undetectable by the naked eye and consist of a fluorescent core encapsulated with a crosslinked polyvinylalcohol (PVA)." The product also contains mica, a mineral, which is what I assume is causing the sparkle as light hits the mica and bounces off.
summary: Give my face a nice glow

reviewText:
This is a  light and subtle highlighter that dispenses product for easy application in a brush form.  Especially in the winter, skin gets dry and after application of foundation and make up it can use a little highlighting to bring back the glow.  I prefer subtle highlights and this product does not make your face look shiny but gives it a glow that looks really nice in photographs.  If I want more shimmer I can always use a bronzer.

 I have another product from NARS is that is also an illuminator  in compact form and this product complements it nicely. I can carry this in my purse for quick touchups.
summary: Adds that subtle glow to the face, great for dry winter skin.

reviewText: Apricot highlights with illuminations sounds all good.  Packaged in an easy-to-carry, easy-to-apply stick wherein the creamy contents ooze through a brush in just the right amount sounds better yet.  But, alas, the color of the product adds nothing save perhaps...maybe a  small amount of evenness to the skin surface coupled with a hint of luminosity.  I know these benefits with less subtlety and more satisfaction can be had in a somewhat less convenient delivery system for a lower price.

There are some things about this highlighter that are good- the brush to apply and a nice looking compact container. The colour nor is lighter than it looks on the site, so if you need a darker highlighter, this might not be for you.
You push down on the button on one end, which is difficult to do while holding it up to your face. It takes one or two pumps to have the liquid come out on the brush. However sometime two pumps and definitely 3 and it drips off. You also have to brush very thoroughly in order to have it look natural.
The price seems high for what you do get, especially compared to other brands and methods of applying highlighters.

I tried this product that came without directions. The ingredients are all fine, but I didn't notice much change to my facial makeup. I applied my customary makeup products and then brushed this under my eyebrows, on my cheekbones and chin. I noticed subtle illumination. The tube contains an applicator brush and a push button on its end. After pushing the end button, a cream flows out onto the applicator brush and then you can sweep it on places you want to highlight.
summary: Subtle New Illuminator - almost invisible on fair skin

reviewText:
Given the price of this product, I doubt that I would purchase it.
It does provide a bit of glow, but the color is so pale that it can't do double duty as blush.
The concept is nice and the product is easy to carry and use to apply.

As someone living on a budget, I can find many far less expensive products that provide both color and glow.
This one only provides one of those properties and is priced at nearly $35.
It does a good job of what it claims to provide, but is too expensive for what it is.

My wife has never used a skin illuminator before, but has heard of it.  It is suppose to give you a glow where light would naturally hit your face.  Being a novice at this, my wife found it easy to use.  She has carfully placed it right on her cheekbones and some of the her brow bone.  The product indeed give a subtle glow.  My wife admits that it maybe better for someone who has been using this type of make up.  It was easy and convenient pen type application with a brush of just the right size.  The product applied smoothly, and little goes a long way.  She likes how easy it is to take with you in its slim container.

I like the subtle color of this illuminator. The color is a very pale rose that is easily blended. The application brush is really more for getting the product onto your skin. I recommend blending with finger tips after that. I wouldn't say the effect is very noticeable or dramatic. It's more like a subtle hint of color.

We got this on a sample basis, with no choice as to color.  This is a bit darker than my wife would have bought, as her skin is fairly pale.  Still it did provide a nice "glow" and as she feathered out the application, the color became more of a match.  My wife thinks she will purchase the product (in the lighter shade) when this one runs out.  My wife did agree with one of the reviewers in that the product does not last all day, and a quick reapplication in the late afternoon is necessary.
summary: Adds a nice glow and seems good for sensitive skin.

reviewText:
I had trouble on my first attempt to apply this product.  The nozzle didn't seem to work, however after fooling with it for a few minutes I saw it needs to be snapped down to break the tabs securing it in place.  It was a rather messy adventure and I wound up spraying the product into my hands and rubbing it into my skin.  The result was a minor sun glow.
For my second attempt I brought this into the shower with me.  After showering, including exfoliating with a loofah, I towel dried my body and sprayed this from every imaginable angle.
This was the best way for me.  The nozzle still leaks a bit, however it does its job.
This dries within 5 minutes and leaves a fresh clean scent.
At this price I think the can needs improvement.  Perhaps some texture so its easier to grip, or even better a nozzle that functions cleanly and properly.  This is a fair skin light color.  For a deeper tan I'll stick with my L'oreal sublime.
summary: Nozzle needs improvement / Leaves a light glow and fresh scent

reviewText:
I am fair-complected, but definitely prefer the way I look when I have some color.  I used to enjoy tanning in the sun and indoor tanning beds.  Eventually, I paid the price, mainly age spots and even basal cell carcinoma.  So I tried to embrace the white look, but I just couldnt, especially in the summer when wearing shorts.  So now I get my color through sunless tanning products (and insist my daughter do the same thing).  I am not looking for a lot of color; I just don't want to be super white.

When I saw this Hampton Sun Sunless Tanning Mist available in the Amazon Vine program, I decided to give it a try.  It is pricey, costing significantly more than what I usually pay for sunless tanning products.  Each time I spray it, the mist goes everywhere, which is wasteful and slightly messy.  I did not notice other reviewers complaining of the same thing, so perhaps there is just a problem with the nozzle on my particular bottle.  The tan I developed from this product looks good; very natural looking.  The color is subtle, which is what I want.  However, some people may prefer more color.  Because of the cost, I will stick with more reasonably priced products (such as Jergens) instead.
summary: Like the results, but its expensive & the spray goes everywhere

reviewText: Hampton Sun lives up to the claims on the can--this mist is easy to apply (I even got my back), produces beautiful non-orangey color, and smells less like tanning stuff than other self tanners I've tried.  So nice to be able to get a safe but natural-looking tan!  I recommend this tanner!

It applies evenly, but maybe it's too subtle for me. To test this product out, I used it generously on one arm and one leg. I left it there for a couple of hours, I went in the sun, I went under lights and I really couldn't  tell the difference.

It is subtle. Very subtle. But the stuff smells wonderful. And goes on easily. I just didn't notice a big difference in my coloring. I'm very pale too. VERY pale. So this stuff had all kinds of things to work with. Not that impressed.

I use self-tanners in the summer and always have mixed results. Usually, no matter how careful I am and how much prep I take beforehand, I end up splotchy and more orange than brown. This one is different. The spray bottle makes it really easy to apply. All I had to do was rub my hands over it. Also, this tends to start out light and gradually built-much less likely to make a mistake this way.

I love it.

My arms are quite tan from gardening but my legs were still fairly pale so I wanted to use a product to give them some color without spending more time in the sun.

This product is easy to apply.  The spray goes on light and so even I wonder if I really need to rub it in to my skin to keep it from streaking.  And it doesn't take very long before it is dry enough to put clothes on.  But after two applications, my legs don't seem that much darker than before.  I am curious as to whether this has a cumulative effect so will keep applying it a couple times as week as suggested on the can.
summary: Easy to apply but not much color

reviewText:
This tanning mist is really great. I had some doubts when I first used it because of the spray/mist instead of a cream. The spray is much like sunscreen, and very easy to use. I noticed within a few hours the subtle changes to the tone of my skin. After using the mist for a few days, it did look like I had a real tan and not a fake on. I would definitely recommend this product to anyone who wants a tan but doesn't want to sit under the sun for hours to get it.

Katiebabs

I honestly dislike this product for two main reasons:

1. The spray goes everywhere, it's much too fine of a spray, so you truly can't use it inside. Using it outside means you have to have clothes on, which means you can't get the spray everywhere without getting it on your clothes. Frustrating.

2. I didn't see any significant results, possibly because I am using it outside and there isn't enough product getting on my skin, as I don't want it to get on my clothing. Would loved to have had this work, but sadly I'm very disappointed in it.
summary: Spray is too wide, and fine. Can't use it indoors as it will get on everything, outside has it's problems too. Disappointed

reviewText: Hampton Sun Sunless Tanning mist gives GREAT color. I'm naturally very pale, so I was afraid this tanning mist would make me too dark. It didn't. It gave my legs subtle color that definitely was more golden brown/tan than orange--which is a win in my book! But while I loved the color, the application process wasn't so smooth. I've only used cream sunless tanners in the past, so maybe some of my difficulty comes from being a spray tan newbie. In any case, I had a very difficult time actually spraying the mist onto my legs. It was like the nozzle didn't work quite right--I had to push very hard to get anything to come out, and it ended up going on in spurts--it was impossible to spray evenly. I used my hands to smooth it out, but, once the mist had "cured" for several hours, I saw that my legs were very streaky and blotchy. I followed the directions to the letter, applying to clean, dry skin, and not putting on clothes until my legs were completely dry, but I still had less than stellar results. (In fact, I stepped outside wearing running shorts, took one look at my legs, and went back into the house for jeans--I was embarrassed by the streaks on my legs, which definitely screamed "fake tan!") The next day, I applied more, this time focusing on the streaky/blotchy parts, and once that had set for several hours, my legs looked at least presentable. I'm going to keep trying, but I'll probably go back to the cream lotions once this can runs out.
summary: Nice tan, but hard to apply evenly

reviewText:
This is a pretty good sunless tanning mist.  It has a nicer fragrance than most, and it doesn't leave a greasy or icky residue behind like so many.  (Like Jergens, ugh!)  You do have to be careful how you spray, it takes an experienced hand.  Anyone new to sunless tanning mists... there will be a learning curve.  It darkens slowly, which I like, and seems to reach its full darkness after several hours.  It doesn't last as long as I was hoping.  But it does fade nicely, which I think is nice.

Overall I think it's more than decent.  A little bit goes a long way (which it should, given the price!).  I'm not necessarily sure it's worth the price tag, but if you're wanting a mist in a bottle, I think this one is pretty good.

I found this product easy to use and the color result was nice. Includes aloe vera and witch hazel that hydrates your skin. Drys quicker than lotion tanners (win-win!). I started using tanning products 15 years ago when I was to go to a wedding in the south and had a northern winter tan (ie fluorescent white) in a sleeveless summer dress. I was amazed how great these products work on your arms and legs and chest. I even tried it very very lightly on my face and used makeup to do the rest.

Some tips if using this for the first time:
*Select the lightest color to start and work your way to a darker color until you find the one right for you
*Apply lightly the first time and go heavier every couple days until you find the right amount for you
*Shower or bathe before you use, scrub your skin and rinse completely to prevents streaks
*Dry completely before using
*Apply ONLY in a cool room - it will take A LOT longer for the product to dry if you are warm or hot
*Use LESS around elbows, knees and ankles
*Wash hands IMMEDIATELY after applying or they will dry 3x darker than the rest of you for DAYS (been there done that!)
*Stand - stay unclothed until completely dry
*This Jergens product color goes on instantly AND will darken over the next several hours
*Use DAY 1 for natural-looking color - Use again DAY 2 if you want darker
*ENJOY!

Good to Know hints from the manufacturer:
*To break the safety seal on the clear spray nozzle, press down hard on the front of the sprayer until it clicks.
*For best results, depress the top front end of the spray button.
*To apply to face, spray product on hands and then apply evenly to face.
*Avoid contact with eye area.
*Does not contain sunscreen
*Before applying - do not use moisturizer as it will blotch the tan - wait 3 hours after applying

These all have worked well for me (Fair skin, Irish, light brown hair):
Clarins Intense Bronze Self-Tanning Tint 4.2 Oz.
Christian Dior Bronze Self Tanner Natural Glow for Body, 4.3 Ounce
St. Tropez Self Tan Bronzing Mousse, 8 fl. oz.
Clinique Self Sun Body Tinted Lotion Light / Medium 4.2 oz / 125 ml Light / Medium
Flash Bronzer Tinted Self Tanning Leg Gel with Pure Vitamin E , 4.2 oz
Estee Lauder Bronze Goddess Revelation Tinted Self-tanning Gelee Body 1 Oz (30 Ml)
Tanceuticals CC Self Tanning Body Lotion
Shiseido Brilliant Bronze Quick Self Tanning Gel (for Face and Body) Gel for Unisex, 4.2 Ounce
summary: The strong scent was a let down

reviewText: I had to use this tanning mist a couple of times to figure out the best way to use it, it is a little different from what I typically use, a foam from Jergins.  It does spray out a fine mist but it is a pretty wide area and the first time I used it I was in my small bathroom, it got on a few things so the next time I used it, I sprayed it on outside.  Like I said the mist is fine but it does say to use your hand to smooth it in, so you will still have to touch it.  It does have a nice smell going on, not your typical sunless tanning smell, although about 12 hours later I did start to smell that.  The "tanning" time to show color is SLOW...so don't think to do this and go somewhere and look tan.  I think it was about 12 hours also to full color time. The color was a nice tan color and it faded slowly also, which was good.  So with preparation, this would be a good tanning mist to use weekly.  It is a little pricey but it also doesn't take much to put it on your skin, overall I think it is a good product for a sunless tan.
summary: Slow to develop, slow to fade

reviewText: The product itself is OK and doesn't leave you orange for too long.  It doesn't have a nasty smell to it either. The container was difficult to open and I ended up breaking the lid off when trying to apply the product.  After fixing that, I quite liked the results from the spray.

This is my first encounter with Hampton Sun, and I have to say, I'm pretty impressed. The spray goes on nicely (once you get the hang of it), and the tan that develops is a nice color that actually LOOKS like a tan, not like orange Kool Aide. It has a pleasant, fresh smell, something I've never had the pleasure of with a tanning spray.

The only downside is the price. I got two legs out of this, and from the feel, there seems to be enough for one, maybe two more sessions. That's a pricey tan!
summary: Actually looks like the real thing

reviewText:
With all the press about skin damage and cancer (to say nothing of aging due to sun), lots of people are rethinking tanning in beds and the sun. Consequently, you have products like this that want to bronze you without the skin damage.

This spray is pretty good on that front. It goes on easy, has a very light smell that goes away with time, and doesnt feel like its very thick on the skin. If done correctly, it has a very nice look.

The key to an even, tanned look is to follow the directions! The biggest problems come from user mistakes. So, don't just think you can spray and go on the fly.

While these tanners aren't as good as the real thing or professional spray tans, you can get some benefit from this product. Its pretty good. Although the price is high, a little goes a long way.

This was my first experience with a spray-style self-tanning product.  I do use self-tanners in the summer, mainly to give some color to my bare legs.  However, I generally use inexpensive drugstore products, namely Jergens Natural Glow.  I was interested to see how an aerosol product would compare to what I had been using.

My first issue with the Hampton Sunless Tanning Mist was that the aerosol spray button was loose when I took off the cap.  In fact, I wound up having to hold it in place in order to use the product, which obviously made usage pretty difficult.  Even without that issue, I found the spray MUCH more difficult to use than the creams I have used in the past.  First, I couldn't control the amount of spray--it was way too easy to apply too much.  Plus, the spray was very thin, making dripping a problem.  Finally, I found it more difficult to ensure that I was applying the spray evenly given that it was clear (when I use the creams, I can see exactly where I am rubbing them in).

Once I finally was able to apply the product, I did my best to remain still and unclothed for about 15 minutes in order to allow it to dry evenly, which was rather inconvenient.  On a more positive note, however, I did not have any problems with streaking.  I used the Hampton Sunless Tanning Mist for three days in a row.  At best, I would describe the results as subtle.  I did give me a nice bit of a honey-colored shade. but someone looking for a deeper, richer tan is likely to be disappointed.  Of course, continued applications may result in a darker color, but the product directions (which were very hard to read due to the white text) suggest using the product only twice per week.

So in the end, although I thought this product provide a decent, soft tan shade, I was a bit frustrated with the difficulties of the spray applicator, and I will probably stick to cream-style self-tanners in the future.
summary: Produces nice (subtle) tan, but aerosol spray is difficult to use

reviewText:
This item was given to me for my review.
Long, long ago, I tried using a tanning lotion on my legs. The lotion gave me an orange/yellow look, with streaks, and the result was that I looked like my liver was failing. Not a good look on me. My hands were stained, as well, even though I washed them afterwards. So, I was not super hopeful about this Hampton Sun Sunless Tanning Mist. I mean, there is a reason people make jokes about these products. However, I found that this tanning mist is easy to use and gives me a good result. I exfoliated my skin, dried myself off, and sprayed the mist on in the shower, making sure to do one leg at a time then rub it in, so it was put on smoothly. The first time I used it, I only did my legs. The mist does have a smell, but it was not too bad and dissipated after it dried. The mist went on easily, even when the can was help upside down, and it went on evenly, so I did not have streaks or darker areas where my skin is rougher. I am considered fair skinned, but I get dark easily. The lotion turned a nice, light, barely there, but still noticeably there, bronze. The next time I used it, I used it on my upper body and my legs. I had no problems with the mist, and I did not have any rashes with it, even though my skin is a bit sensitive. The color was lighter, probably because I put it on lighter and only went with one thin layer. I did not turn orange or a sickly yellow. It is nice. My only complaint is that the directions are terribly hard to read on the metallic background, especially because the lettering is in a light colored, small font. Additionally, one of the directions seems to say that I need to "watch out around the hairline," but it does not detail what that means. Watch out how? Again, the manufacturer seems to believe that the user has experience with the product, or with the type of product. My experience is limited. I did make sure to blend the spray well, and that seemed to be okay. I am not sure what else I should do or may need to do when I apply more?
summary: Does not make me look like my liver is failing

reviewText: The Hampton Sun Sunless Tanning Mist does the job, but still leaves streaks like other sunless tanning products unless applied carefully and thinly. Be sure to follow the directions.  My favorite sunless tanners are ones that apply gradually so that there is no streaking and no orange color. Jergens is great and a decent price. This product does go on clear, but later you can see spots you've missed when it dries and sets. I have fair-to-medium skin in the summer and this gives me a bit more color in areas that don't otherwise see the sun. But I wouldn't use it to even out my tan. It does moisturize, but not as well as Jergens.
summary: but still leaves streaks like other sunless tanning products unless applied carefully and thinly

reviewText: This stuff works pretty good! I have lightly tan skin naturally and this provides very subtle but non-orange results. The things I didn't like: it comes out clear, the spray format wastes a lot of product, and it's expensive. If you don't mind these things though, it's very easy to use.
summary: This stuff works pretty good! I have lightly tan skin naturally and ...

reviewText: This is a pleasant enough moisturizer, but it is not any better than the higher end moisturizers you can buy at Target for half the price. I like the jar and the mirror on the lid, but that doesn't improve my skin, I'd rather the product worked better or cost less. It is pleasant to put on and has a botanical aroma which is pleasant, but for $35 it better perform really well and I would say that it performs ok. There are a lot of skin products out there and I have used  A LOT of them from La Mer to Olay and I would say that this jar is just not worth the money.
summary: It is ok, but not anything special

reviewText: The smell is good, not great. Also, it's very liquidy, so it's suitable for the summer season, definitely not the winter season in cold places.

I am on a constant quest to find a good night cream for my dry skin.  As I have gotten older, my skin has become drier.  The challenge has been to find a skin cream that moisturizes deeply without being greasy.  Well, I am happy to report that this skin cream does just that.

Why I love this product:

* The heavenly texture. It is described as gel, but it is really more of a cream.  I guess thats why the word balm is in the name.  It just glides onto my skin.

* It works.  My skin feels moisturized, yet not greasy.  Even in the winter, when my skin is especially dry, it works.

* The pretty pink color.  The balm is a light pink, and its quite pleasing to the eye.  This really has nothing to do with how well it works, but it is a pleasure to put on this balm.

* The light, pleasing scent.  I have been disappointed with so many skin creams because of their heavy, artificial scent.  I never considered myself all that sensitive to scents until I started trying some of the other creams.

* The detailed picture inside of the box that shows the best way to apply this cream.  Who knew there was an art to this?

If you are looking for a nice skin cream that works to moisturize, you will enjoy this product.

I haven't noticed any change in my wrinkles or tone in my skin, but it is a pleasant cream to use.  Another reviewer mentioned the mirror lid, but I didn't notice it until I read her review, and it's true.  However, I like to use a hot washcloth on my face before I put products on it, to get rid of any impurities, and I do that in the bathroom with a big mirror!  Anyway, the scent reminds me of roses, the cream is pink, and you just need a dab to cover your face, neck, and hands.  I figure, I want my hands to be wrinkle-free, too.  So far I haven't noticed any changes in my skin, but It is a pleasure to use this cream, because of all the properties that make it like it is.  My face is not dry now but I still see the age.  Does anything really help that?
great

Good smell and feel to this product. My wife said it leaves her with softer, smoother skin. Very absorbent, and not an irritant. Used wisely, could last a few months. Well regarded product and highly recommended!
summary: Good smell and feel to this product

reviewText: This is a fantastic recovery gel that goes on easy and doesn't feel greasy or sticky. There are a ton of skin products out there that claim to do the same thing as this, but none of them really seem to be able to live up to their claims like Vichy does. The scent is light and very pleasing, and doesn't irritate my sinuses like some products tend to do. Vichy is definitely a step above the rest, and the price of admission isn't all that bad either. One of the affluent ladies I regularly deal with has tried products costing more than triple what Vichy costs, but keeps coming back to Vichy because their products work better for her. I'm very impressed with the presentation, quality, and effectiveness of this recovery gel and wouldn't hesitate to recommend giving it a try.

Several things I didn't enjoy, very fragrant.  The lotion was very fragrant and also had an odd taste, yes taste, I could taste it even though it was only on my face.  And I do have a husband who also kisses me, he said it was perfumey and kind of a turn off.  The lotion also dried my skin out.  At first I thought, this lotion is new, I'll just give it time. I had already been using the serum for awhile, so I was surprised at how dry my skin got. By day five my skin was red and itchy and very visibly dry.  I gave it a few days off, and tried again, the same thing happened.  This is not a lotion for me.  I have mildly sensitive skin, oily in the T-zone, and dry everywhere else, my skin is neither mature or very young, it's in it's 30s.  I used as directed, with other Vichy products I had already been using.  This lotion was not for me.  Perhaps others will have more luck.
summary: I don't think this face cream works with my skin type.

reviewText:
The interesting thing about this product is that so many of its pros also wind up being cons.

For example: the texture of the cream is very light - some have called it almost gel-like, and I'd agree with that.  That lightness makes it easy to smooth on the face.  The downside to that: it's so light that it doesn't impart much moisture at all.  This would be great for someone who doesn't have particularly dry skin, but for those of us who need a big dose of moisture, this doesn't work for that.  For those who benefit from light moisturization, be prepared for how this product gives you that: in my experience, after it's smoothed on, it leaves a lightly tacky, even greasy feel to the skin.

The scent has gotten a lot of mentions in reviews, and there is a reason for that.  I thought it would be fine for me even though I'm very sensitive to strong aromas because "parfum/fragrance" is the last item on the ingredient list.  Initially, it seems to have a lovely, light rose scent.  However, that scent doesn't dissipate at all - it just sits there on your face, and for me, it became cloying and eventually overwhelming.  By the time I'd had it on for about a half hour, I'd begun to develop a headache and had to wash it off.  (Side note: it didn't come off easily at all with just water; this is the kind of product that requires some kind of cleanser to totally remove.)

The packaging is nice, in terms of the inside of the box having diagrams and instructions for application of the product, and the jar is quite pretty with a useful mirror serving as the top of the lid.  The downside here, though, is that this obviously requires you to dip your fingers into the product in order to then apply it to your face; as such, even with clean hands, eventually bacteria could start to be a concern, so I would have preferred if the cream had come in a pump-form.

The aspects of the product that don't have "cons" - it's paraben free, and even though my skin is highly sensitive, I didn't experience any irritation when I put this on my face.  (However, it is worth noting again that I could only tolerate having it on my skin for a half hour because of the fragrance.)

It's been so difficult - actually it's been impossible, thus far - for me to find a moisturizer/cream that won't irritate my sensitive skin and won't make my extreme sensitivity to fragrance come into play.  This product will likely work for people who don't have to deal with those things and don't require a product that delivers a lot of moisture.  For all of those like me who are on a quest for an effective, non-irritating, non-aggravating moisturizer, the search continues.
summary: Very Light Moisturization With A Fragrance That Proves Overwhelming

reviewText: from the mouth of my in-house tester: "... it has a wonderful texture, a pleasant, light fragrance... it goes on, stays on, and is NOT greasy! i have sensitive skin and have not had any problems with this product or the day cream, Vichy Aqualia Thermal Rich Cream, 1.7 fl. oz. (this product is definitely a night cream, which is much heavier)" one very nice touch is in the design of the packaging - more specifically, the actual jar... the lid is a MIRROR!!!! outstanding job by the designer and manufacturer - this would make for a very good travel product!

Vichy Idealia Skin Sleep Night Recovery is a lightweight lotion with a light, pleasant fragrance that will be a welcome addition to any bedtime skin care regimen.  One thing I really like about this product is that Vichy has cut down on what ends up in the landfill by condensing their packaging.  The instructions for use are printed on the inside of the box rather than on a leaflet that's tucked into the box.  The box comes apart easily so you can read the instructions, but isn't so flimsy that it comes apart in shipping.  The instructions, when followed, enhance the experience of using the product by guiding you through a light massage of your head and neck.  The product itself, leaves my skin feeling nice and dewy when I retire and I wake up with soft-feeling skin.
summary: Enjoyable Addition to Bedtime Skin Care Regimen

reviewText:
I have sensitive skin and a sensitive nose. I was not able to use this product because the smell irritates my sinuses. I was not expecting this because other reviewers had written that the scent was light and pleasant. Since my skin is sensitive, I tested this product on the skin of my arm, planning to leave it on overnight to watch for any irritation. Unfortunately, fumes rose into my nose immediately and I felt a headache coming so I rinsed my arm off. Then I went to bed, but had trouble going to sleep because I could still smell it and my sinuses felt very irritated.

This seemed odd because the smell seemed flowery, like roses, and should have been pleasant. I don't know why it bothered me so strongly. But I would not dare put this on my face!

On the plus side, the formula is paraben-free. And many people seem to like it. However, it also contains a list of chemicals, some of them questionable. Here's the list from the manufacturer's site: AQUA / WATER  GLYCERIN  ALCOHOL DENAT.  PRUNUS ARMENIACA KERNEL OIL / APRICOT KERNEL OIL  ISONONYL ISONONANOATE  POLYSORBATE 20  NIACINAMIDE  DIMETHICONE  PROPANEDIOL  ISOPROPYL LAUROYL SARCOSINATE  PEG-20 METHYL GLUCOSE SESQUISTEARATE  AMMONIUM POLYACRYLDIMETHYLTAURAMIDE / AMMONIUM POLYACRYLOYLDIMETHYL TAURATE  BHT  C13-14 ISOPARAFFIN  CI 17200 / RED 33  CI 15985 / YELLOW 6  TRIETHANOLAMINE  CAFFEINE  SODIUM HYALURONATE  PHENOXYETHANOL  ADENOSINE  TOCOPHERYL ACETATE  DISODIUM EDTA  DIPOTASSIUM GLYCYRRHIZATE  CAPRYLOYL SALICYLIC ACID  CAPRYLYL GLYCOL  LAURETH-7  HYDROXYPALMITOYL SPHINGANINE  XANTHAN GUM  POLYACRYLAMIDE  ACRYLONITRILE/METHYL METHACRYLATE/VINYLIDENE CHLORIDE COPOLYMER  PARFUM / FRAGRANCE  FIL 688810 10

BHT is Butylated hydroxytoluene, a controversial ingredient. It's generally derived from petroleum. The MSDS says "Hazardous in case of skin contact (irritant), of inhalation (lung irritant)." That applies to using it full-strength, which is not the case in this formula.  Other questionable ingredients include denatured alcohol and polyacrylamide.

I hope this is helpful to somebody.

Well, I like the texture and feel of this cream but it has a strong musky scent that I dislike.  In fact when I opened the jar my cat took one whiff and ran away!  It seems to be a decent moisturizer but no special effects I could see from the advertised ingredients-mineral water and caffeine.  Just a gimmick I think.
summary: Scent too strong but decent moisturizer

reviewText: I really love this stuff.  Its a fabulous night cream that drenches your skin in moisture while you sleep.  You wake up refreshed and invigorated and ready to take on the day.  It's a nice gel cream free of unpleasant odor.  I like it and recommend it.
summary: It's like treating your skin to a refreshing glass of water

reviewText:
It's a nice "every day wear" fragrance that won't leave your co-workers gagging for breath.
This fragrance is so light that within a few seconds of spraying it, I could hardly tell I was wearing any. I spritzed again on my wrist, and again, only a few (2-3) seconds later I could hardly tell it was there.

It has a very sweet fragrance that teminded me a tad of Mickarl Kors' Summer scent, but this is more flowery than Kors'.
  The bottle is very cool looking. The bottom half is real glass (as you would expect) with an acrylic top that matches.
  I am not familiar with Josie Natori at all. Never heard of the label before. Seems pretty good.
 .

What struck me most about the scent is how sweet smelling it is, almost overwhelmingly so. There are floral undertones, not fruity. But the scent reminds me of older ladies. On the plus side, the scent definitely lasts and doesn't smell cheap. My mom enjoyed it.

Josie By Josie Natori Eau de Parfum, 3.4 fl oz.  This is a product that I had the pleasure and honor of trying out and reviewing.  It is one of the best products I've had the opportunity to test and rate.  The scent is so lovely.  It is hard to describe.  But with my limited ability to capture it's beauty, I will say it is sexy, sophisticated, elegant.  It's not fruity or sweet. (If it is, that part of it is subtle.)

I only spray on a very small amount, because too much perfume can (and probably will be) a disaster, and most everybody will be offended.  So unless someone says "no perfume because someone has allergies or because someone doesn't like it", then I only spray a very minute amount - only enough for it to make you have a scent of cleanness and elegance, rather than having a smell of mustiness.
summary: Josie By Josie Natori Eau de Parfum, 3.4 fl oz

reviewText: I like Josie Eau do Parfum.  The scent is nice, though a tad too strong for me.  After spritzing a very small amount behind my ears and cleavage, then crossing my wrists over cleavage, rubbing wrists together, I approached my husband to get his opinion.  He did not care for it.  Well, he won't be wearing it anyway!  LOL  (He prefers a much lighter floral fragrance on me, such as L' Air du Temps.)  Josie's fragrance is made up of a jasmine (sampaguito - national flower of Philippines), Asian pear, bergamot (also found in my favorite Earl Grey tea), freesia, and orchid, plus the usual other ingredients that are there to stabilize and keep it fresh.  This is a perfume that seems to be more for evening wear, than morning and during the day.  It's been about 5 hours since I applied it, and I can still catch a whiff on my wrists.  Rather pleasant, I think...so I would say let it linger a while before going out.  It is referred to, as being a vibrant mix of being confident, sexy, and delivering a spirited energy.  I guess I'm just a little to quiet and mellow, so I'll wear it occasionally with caution.
summary: Josie is a nice scent, but use small amount.

reviewText:
Overall, I like this eau de parfum, but am definitely not in the "love it" category.

There are many scents happening at the same time, which may appeal to some, and to which others may be adverse. It is not a light fragrance, and that said, my 17 year old daughter doesn't like it. As difficult as it is to describe a fragrance in words, especially given that it's all totally subjective, I would say that this fragrance is probaly one of those that women will immediately like or dislike as it's not one of those "beat around the bush" scents that you need to contemplate. It's definitely got musk, citrus, floral and tea notes happening, and I would honestly say that it's not a strong feminine fragrance (but does have a sweet finish) and has "shades" of more masculine scents. Like I said, a lot of different scents happening all at once, and a little goes a long way.

I do like it, but don't know if I'd actually pick it up and buy it for myself, as I have other fragrances that I really adore, and to add the fact that it's not a very inexpensive perfume. The bottle itself is unique, but very heavy and bulky.
summary: I quite like it, but think there will be lovers and haters of this fragrance, not too many who can take it or leave it.

reviewText:
I have not had much luck recently with commercial fragrances, as they all tend to smell the same with my body chemistry, sort of chemical like and cheap.  Since I tend to gravitate toward woodsy or floral type scents, I thought maybe a fragrance that claims to have a more fruit based scent (Asian pear in this case) would be different.  I was wrong.

Josie smells fine in the bottle, but when I apply to myself, I first get a strong alcohol smell-like I had spilled rubbing alcohol in the room.  Then the alcohol smell goes away, and I am left with a scent that is hard to describe.  It is not Asian pear, nor is it citrus, but more of a can of tropical fruit salad smell.  This fades quickly and is followed by a floral scent, like freesia and hyacinth mixed with Ivory soap.  On my skin, it smells absolutely nothing like the matching body lotion did-which is a good thing.

Not a terrible scent, and it did not give me a headache like Reveal by Calvin Klein, but it is not for me.  It does smell better on my clothing, curtains, and as an air freshener than it does on me.  It does not even smell nice on my daughter, on whom the body lotion smells wonderful.  Guess I will have to stick with perfume oils.
When first sprayed, to me it is like fresh linen, floral and sweet, and a tiny bit of spice.  Then after an hour it changes character and becomes more subtle and has a powdery sensual fragrance.

When I ordered this conditioner, the product page didn't list the ingredients, so I was unhappy to discover that this has multiple silicones to achieve that smoother look. Although using silicones to this end is common practice, they can create build-up over time and weigh down hair, and, for those of us who are sensitive to it (yes, I took one for the team and tried this for several days), it can cause skin irritation and even eczema.  But does this Obliphica conditioner work as promised?  Pretty much.  It does contain keratin for hair repair.

I have blonde, wavy hair that verges on curly if I have the right cut and don't style it.  Perhaps because of the silicones in this conditioner, I am able to style my hair more straight than usual, and it has a nice gloss.  The Obliphica conditioner doesn't deliver the kind of silky magic that an argan oil conditioner will, but it still detangles and makes my hair feel nice.  If you have curly or wavy hair and want a straighter style, this conditioner works toward that end.  It did rob some body from my hair, but, when I'm going for a smoother look, that's not necessarily a bad thing.

This isn't the best conditioner I've tried, and it isn't the worst.

-- Debbie Lee Wesselmann
summary: It Smoothes and Weighs Down Waves and Curls

reviewText:
I really like the way this conditioner makes my hair feel. I have thick hair that's straight to wavy depending on the day and what it wants to do. Add the cold, dry air or humidity to the mix and I definitely require something that helps make my hair a little more silky and tamable. I've been using this Obliphica Seaberry conditioner and have been seeing great results. Since it's for course hair, I was worried that it would be too thick and weigh my hair down, but it is actually very lightweight. At the same time it works to soften my hair as a stronger conditioner would typically do.

The pump style bottle is really convenient in the shower, although for the price I wish the bottle were a little larger. The scent is a bit reminiscent to those small tubes of conditioner that come with at home hair dying kits. I actually kind of like it. Another thing to note is how easy it is to detangle my hair after conditioning with this product. I often battle to get tangles out with my wet hair, but this does a nice job at detangling, so it's easier to comb my hair through while wet.

UPDATE 11/2017: I just wanted to come back and reiterate how amazing this stuff is. Whenever I stop using it and move on to try another product, I immediately see the difference and what I'm missing. I then go back to it and my hair looks great, again!
summary: Does a Nice Job at Detangling and Softening My Hair

reviewText: It smells great, and it's a high quality conditioner. It's difficult to get out of the bottle though, and the price is prohibitive.

It was good, made my hair soft for days, thick formula, smelled nice. only complaint is that it only pumped out a little bit of product at a time and it was slow so I had to like pump it 10 times just  to get the amount of product I wanted. Other than that I would certainly recommend it for thicker hair.

Great clean smell. Easy to apply and it rinses out easily as well.  The pump vs. a tube is quite nice as well. Had my daughter use it as well and she likes the amount of condition it does for her hair.

Obliphica's seaberry conditioner is a wonderful conditioner.  First, it smells amazing.  It's a combination of fruity and floral and smell wonderful in the shower.  The scent is not overpowering and most of it rinses away, so thankfully would won't walk around smelling like flowers all day.

The conditioner is not the thickest.  Pantene's conditioners feel like they coat my hair better while sitting in the shower.  I feel like I need to use a lot more of the Obiphica to get the same "saturated-feeling" coverage.  The Obilphica rinses easily and leaves my hair free of tangles and stiffness.

After towel drying my hair, I always run a small amount of conditioner through it and then let my hair air dry.  It usually dries into a mass of loose curls and waves.  The Obiphica leaves my hair feeling very soft and smooth, better than Pantene, for sure.  It also leaves my hair smelling fresh and clean with little frizziness.

Two issuea I have with this conditioner are that the bottle is smaller than most conditioners and the pump applicator does not have much travel, so it takes a couple of pumps to get a decent amount out.  The price is high too, but I will leave the value judgement up to you.

FYI: I am a male with hair that rests just above my shoulders.  It is thick and wavy and is modestly greasy.

All in all... great conditioner.

(4/17/17 Update: I removed a star from my rating because as the bottle starts to empty it is practically impossible to get the last bit of conditioner out of the bottle.  The pump can't reach it and the bottle isn't flexible enough to squeeze it out.)
summary: Leaves my hair silky soft and smooth, but the bottle is small and the pump is annoying.

reviewText: This conditioner softened my hair and gave it a lot of shine.  It is thick and that helps it stay in your hair and condition.  The directions suggest leaving it in your hair for a few minutes to allow it to work.  It comes in a very pretty container as do all Obliphica products.  It may cost more than other conditioners, but I think it is a case of "you get what you pay for".

The Obliphica Professional Seaberry conditioner comes in a colorful bottle with a hand pump.  Using the pump, it emerges easily from the bottle.  It has a light color and pleasant scent.  The conditioner has to some extent smoothed out my curles, but has left my hair soft and clean.  I recommend it.

I've only used this a couple of times and can already tell the difference in my hair. It's not a tangled mess for one thing and it really shines for another. The best thing about this conditioner though is the smell. I can't describe it but it's the nicest smell I have ever smelled. You know the smell when you walk into an expensive salon...well, somehow they have bottled it here. I have been using cheap conditioners and when I go to comb my hair out it is still tangled somewhat but not with this one. Once my hair was blow dried, it felt smooth and silky which is amazing since I have very thick hair and it's always kind of wild looking otherwise. I really like that it has a pump as it makes it so much easier to use. I did let the conditioner set in my hair for about 30 minutes while I took a bath, so that might make a difference in how it does for your hair. Probably the longer the better.

A little over ten years ago my stylist convinced me that it was time to switch to an ionic blow dryer.  I was a little skeptical  I was already using a name brand dryer, how much difference could an ionic dryer make?  All it took was one use to convert this doubting Thomas into an ionic evangelist  my hair was smoother with less frizz and static electricity.  After continued use the condition of my hair actually improved; it was shinier and healthier looking.

Ive owned three Bio Ionic brand dryers; this Power Light is my fourth.  I have a lot of confidence in this brand, and I love this particular dryer  its really top of the line.  It has the usual features (variable heat and power settings, a cool shot button, 9ft cord) and comes with two nozzles.  At just slightly over one pound its noticeably lightweight for a full size dryer.  Its expensive, but its professional quality and it delivers  I can get a fast, smooth, frizz-free blow out without damaging my hair.

This may sound funny, but blow drying your hair is a skill, and like any other skill it takes practice.  If you're like my sister and you just point the dryer in the general direction of your hair and hope for the best, then don't expect any miracles from this (or any other) dryer.  But if you use good styling products made specifically for your hair type and invest in a good quality brush, then this dryer can make the difference between just getting your hair dry and having it look like you just came from the salon.  If its in your budget then I say go for it  its a fantastic blow dryer and I highly recommend it.

**Note:  The filter is easy to clean, and youll want to do so frequently.  A clogged filter can make the dryer overheat, and can even shorten the life of the dryer.
summary: A high end, salon quality dryer - worth the investment!

reviewText: The dryer works just fine, but I can't say there's a big difference in frizz on my end. I have very fine hair that tends to frizz easily. With this hair dryer, if there's any difference it's very minimal. I do like the verity of modes and that it's fairly lightweight, but I wouldn't spend the listed $200 on it.
summary: Nice hair dryer but not worth the money.

reviewText:
I previously received the Remington D3190A Damage Control Ceramic Hair Dryer, Ionic Dryer, Hair Dryer, Purple from Vine and have been using that (sparingly - mostly in the evenings so I don't go to bed with a wet head!) to dry my hair. But one big problem I've had with my Remington is that the Cool button is really close to where I naturally rest my hands when drying my hair, so I always inadvertently press the button while driving.

The Bio Ionic does not have this problem. Not only does it dry my hair faster (!!! Yes, my fluff-ball lion-mane dries faster with this puppy!), it is quieter (!!!) and the cool button has to be clicked down to cool, not just depressed slightly by a errant finger.

I really enjoy drying my hair with Bio Ionic. I tend to avoid drying, because my hair is colored, but when I do, I love how quickly the Bio Ionic works. It's fairly light-weight (as dryers go), though of course, with the attachments, it's cumbersome to manipulate around my head to dry my hair smooth (but this is inherent in most dryers, not just Bio Ionic). My hair is nice and smooth, especially when adding some oil (I use Organix Repairing Awapuhi Ginger Dry Styling Oil). And my drying time goes down substantially! Normally, it takes a full 30+ min to fully dry, but I start feeling results immediately instead of after 5 minutes of drying.

While the Remington still isn't bad, I definitely prefer the Bio Ionic. We'll see how many blow dries it has in it!

UPDATE 01/04/17: I have been using this to straighten my hair, and it's works AMAZING. I have NEVER owned a blow dryer that could blow-dry my hair as straight as this one can - even without the permanent straight treatment I got, I could get away with blow drying straight and walking out - no flat iron needed!

Brought to you by:
*C.S. Light*
summary: Replaces my Remington D3190A as my fav

reviewText: This is a great lightweight dryer that has the perfect amount of heat for my thick, coarse hair.  It dries so much faster than my old dryer, it's almost unbelievable.  It only takes me about 15 minutes to get the perfect blowout.  The ions really help eliminate the frizz, even in my somewhat wavy, frizz prone hair.  It's also super quiet and I really notice the difference.  I dry my hair most of the way using high heat and then finish with the medium setting.  The concentrator nozzle works great and helps me get very smooth locks.  I really appreciate the fact that this dryer is so much lighter than my old one.  My arm doesn't get fatigued at all when I use it.  This is my first Bio Ionic dryer and so far I'm really pleased with it.  It has all the features that I want coupled with the light weight and the fact that it's so quiet, which makes it a pleasure to use.  In the past, I've only purchased cheap dryers and have truly never been happy with their performance.  All of them were heavy and extremely noisy so this Bio Ionic dryer is a welcome change.  The old dryers never really controlled the frizz and my hair always felt really dry and damaged because it would take forever for my hair to dry.  This Bio Ionic dryer will save a lot of wear and tear on my hair because it dries it so fast.  It takes me less than half the time it used to.  I've had this dryer for about 2 months and am really pleased with my purchase.  It's definitely been worth every penny.  My hair is smooth with tons of volume and it now takes me almost no time at all to dry it, even though it's pretty thick and heavy.  I definitely recommend this dryer for anyone with my hair type.

Absolutely AMAZING!!!i had no idea a hair dryer could make my hair so smooth, healthy and shiny!! Those ions really make a difference and this dry beats every dryer I've tried the T3, Salono, Elchim, GHD, Chi etc. Works especially well with the Bio Ionic blue wave brush for the best blow out of your life! I could never blow out my hair like my stylist but now I can with this amazing dryer! I'm getting compliments because my hair is so so shiny!!! Thank you, Bio Ionic! im in heaven!! This seller is great too for the price and the quick shipping!!
This light is the same light my salon uses.  LOVE it.
Great quality and price. Like other reviewers stated, the cord can come out of the bottom where it is plugged in, but I just make sure to not move the lamp at all after plugging it in.
Authentic CND lamp and works well. I would recommend this seller. I've been using for 2 months with no issues.
summary: Authentic CND lamp with no issues

reviewText: I'm sooooo glad I bought this led light from cnd  it works very well on my cnd shellac polish would purchase over again

This is an excellent makeup remover (note: NOT A FACE WASH). I learned that quickly when I tried it as a wash and it did not work, then I read the label! I'm so use to using similar looking face washes it was just second nature to use it that way but this is strictly a makeup remover. Just use a little on a cotton pad and makeup comes right off, no rinsing necessary and it leaves your skin feeling soft and clean. This is a clear gel, no beads or color in it like I expected. It has a very light floral, slightly rose scent that quickly dissipates. Not sure I would give up my 7 dollar Neutrogena face wash for this, which works just as well and is way cheaper but if you just want a makeup remover, not a wash, this does do the job with ease.
Greg eat makeup remover. Works well on waterproof makeup as well. My only hang up with this product is that it's a bit messy. One pump of the remover is plenty.

This cleaner works well and has a very pleasant scent.  It was able to take makeup off that I had worn ten hours.  It also did not dry out my skin.

It was, however, emailed in a bubble envelope by Amazon, which caused the dispenser to crack.  None of the product was wasted, however I was not able to use the pump, unfortunately.
summary: None of the product was wasted, however I was not able to use the ...

reviewText:
The La Roche-Posay Makeup Remover Micellar Water Gel Cleanser is an effective makeup remover and is gentle on the skin.  The gel dispensed from the pump is soothing and did not irritate my skin.  Makeup, including mascara and eye liner, came off with gentle rubbing and did not require me to have to use a separate towel or tissue to scrub off the makeup.  While it says that you can simply wipe off the excess and dry off your face, I preferred to rinse off the excess product and dried my face after ensuring all the product and makeup was removed.  My skin did not break out after use, and my skin felt very clean afterwards.

The scent of the cleanser was very minimal and pleasant.  It did not leave my skin with any type of scent on it, nor did it leave my skin feeling overly dry or oily.  I used my regular moisturizer afterwards and the products didn't react with each other adversely.  Overall, if you're looking for a good cleanser that removed makeup effectively, this is a nice one to consider.
summary: Effectively Removes Makeup, Left Skin Feeling Fresh and Clean Without Feeling Overly Dry/Oily

reviewText:
This makeup remover works well.  The ingredients are as follows:
AQUA / WATER
BIS-PEG-18 METHYL ETHER DIMETHYL SILANE
CARBOMER
SODIUM HYALURONATE
SODIUM HYDROXIDE
POLOXAMER 184
DISODIUM EDTA
CAPRYLYL GLYCOL

PHENOXYETHANOL
PARFUM / FRAGRANCE

It is your basic remover, and I am not sure the price is justified.

It does clean well and leaves your face feeling clean and smooth.  I would say it is decent, but there are less expensive alternatives.

gentle yet very effective. removed all makeup including mascara with only two pumps on a cotton pad, however i always choose to double cleanse no matter how good the product. did not sting my eyes which is a big plus!
This is a good simple face cleaner.  Granted I am not removing makeup, but it does a good job and doesn't leave my skin dry, which is typical with other products

This is very pleasant to use.  It has a light fragrance and feels like a gel moisturizer going on.  You simply wet your face then apply one or two pumps.  I use a bamboo baby washcloth to then wipe the product off.  It takes all the makeup and grime off without any oily feel at all.  It doesn't burn my eyes whatsoever.  It's like a very wet gel.  It only takes 1-2 pumps to clean my face- and it does a very good job of gettin my mascara off.
It really makes me feel a bit spoiled.  I normally have used makeup remover wipes but this leaves my skin feeling even cleaner and smooth.  This is a product that I will continue to use.
summary: Very pleasant to use, cleans and freshens better than my cleansing wipes

reviewText: Very mild makeup remover. I have sensitive skin and eyes, so I appreciate something so mild that the detergent ingredient, Poloxamer can also go into contact lens solution (no tears.) There are also no parabens.  Put on a cotton pad and gently wipe eye area. Makeup is gone. If you simply wash your face as usual and then use this, you will usually find a lot of residue left in the eye area if you wear shadow and mascara. This takes it off. Nice pump, too.

If you are searching for a gentle and easy facial cleanser to remove make-up, this is a great choice.  This requires no rinsing. It doesn't have a strong scent which is a plus in my book. Just massage in and go on.  It feels like soap going on, but it rubs right in.  It seemed to do a good job removing make-up.  Overall, I am pleased with it.

I have very fine, thin, colored hair. Finding a conditioner that doesn't weigh my hair down is a constant struggle. Obliphica Professional Seaberry Fine to Medium conditioner is the product I've been looking for!! It smells amazing and has a lovely feel in the hand. It is not too thick or too watery, and works great on my hair. I use about a silver dollar sized dollop and run it through my hair.
This comes in a super handy pump bottle which makes getting it out with one hand super easy-no caps to unscrew.

I'll be ordering the shampoo as soon as my current bottle runs out.

This line is one of the new products on a TV major shopping channel and I always want to try new hair and beauty products.  First, I can see why it is labeled as being for fine to medium hair.  I have a lot of hair, but the individual hairs are pretty straight and fine and I have a hard time working this through my hair.  I end up using a lot more than the "normal" amount just to feel like I have at least the ned of my hair covered.  Someone with thick hair would have a really hard time.

And that leads me to a second criticism.  I really hate the pump on the bottle.  It gives only a little bit per pump and I have to pick up the bottle and pump it into my other hand.

On the plus side, it doesn't have a perfumey smell so I can use it without having scent issues.  The product works fairly well but I don't see anything that would make me choose it over a much less expensive conditioner.  For that reason I wouldn't get it again.
summary: I have to use a lot to work it through my fine hair.

reviewText: I've been using this for a couple of weeks and I really like it. I actually use it in lieu of shampoo. I scrub my scalp with it and pull it through my hair, then let it sit while I finish my shower. It rinses out cleanly and leaves my hair soft and clean.
I have chemically treated colored hair. The conditioner smells great but it is very watery. I prefer a creamier conditioner. It left my hair limp and lacking body.
summary: Didn't work well for my hair type.

reviewText:
This smells very nice, but it doesn't work that well as a conditioner. I left it in for 4-5 minutes and combed it through with a shower
comb. The first thing I really noticed besides the fact that it felt kinda "dry" was that my hair tended to tangle more and it was
difficult to comb through my hair.
I have baby fine hair that I pamper and I never dye it or use a hair dryer on it. It is in pretty good condition because of the way I treat
it.
After my hair dried, I noticed that there wasn't much shine and that I had more fly away hair than usual.

I would not recommend this conditioner

reviewText:
The first thing I noticed was that the bottle seemed to be poorly thought out since the short travel of the pump meant that if you have long hair like I do you are trying to get enough to do the job without sending the bottle off into space or the bottom of the shower.

Secondly the smell was wonderful, hard for me to describe but a strong fresh smell that I really liked.

The actual finished product of my hair was supple and silky but as a bit of a detangler (as most conditioners are) it was almost useless.

All things considered it was a nice product but I doubt I will buy it at the posted price vs the results

reviewText:
It's a good conditioner, it definitely made my hair softer and easier to manage.  I love the smell, and I love being able to run my hands through my hair and have my aging, color-treated, daily blow-dried hair feel SOFT. Even the next morning, before I wash my hair again, I can still feel the softness, it's long lasting.

My only quibble is with the packaging. This particular pump is short to the base, and does not dispense much product. And I found I needed a lot of product to get full coverage.  I found myself having to get 4-5 pumps to cover my shoulder length hair.  A pump that dispenses more would have been more useful. And the pump being so close to the base also seems to make it a little stiffer, it's not as easy to pump as other products I have.

But other than the pump, this is a nice conditioner. Recommended.
summary: Great conditioner with some packaging issues

reviewText: I love this conditioner has a hand pump, because I don't have to worry about dropping it and it spilling all over the floor. And it's more convenient for me to use it. The fragrance is light and smells awesome! I leave it on my hair about 3 minutes, rinse, and then comb through my hair. It's an excellent detangler and conditioner for my fine hair. It doesn't weigh my hair down at all. I only use a little bit after washing hair. My hair looks smooth and shiny after using Obliphica. I love it!

The Obliphica Professional Seaberry conditioner comes in a colorful bottle with a hand pump. Using the pump, it emerges easily from the bottle. It has a light color and pleasant scent. The conditioner has to some extent smoothed out my curles, but has left my hair soft and clean. I recommend it.

Rating this as a high just ok. I mean, it did work well on my thinner hair, left it smooth and manageable, as good as other conditioners I typically use. On the other hand, this is a relatively small bottle (10 ounces) at a high price. I usually by 32 ounce conditioners (typically Agave products) which per lower ounce cost, work much better. I also didn't care for the fragrance right out of the container (thought it was too strong smelling). After applying and rinsing it I found my hair smelt much nicer (and not as strong as immediately thought). I do like the impressive little container and the applicator plunger. Just think that for the cost per ounce you can do much better.
summary: Nice, light conditioner. A little on the costly side per ounce.

reviewText:
Ok - for starters I have to state that it's an unfair comparison to my current haircare regime but I LOVE the results.

Background On Me
#1 I'm a male
#2 I currently use Head And Shoulders 2 in 1
#3 I'm very particular about my hair - it has to look just right even when I'm walking my dog.
#4 I have never more than $10 on a shampoo or a conditioner
#5 I have never heard of this brand before

The Experience
#1 The item ships in and attractive and expensive looking bottle
#2 Love how it smells in the bottle. but thought this might be a bit flowery for my lumberjack exterior ;)
#3 Once applied, it smells different - like a lighter version
