#4 I have been using 2 squirts for my slightly long hair and feel confident 1 squirt will suffice once I get a haircut
$5 my hair feels FANTASTIC
#6 It has given a little volume to thinning patches up in the most northern regions of the outback

Overall Impression:
Delighted with the product. It definitely delivers a very satisfying experience from the small amount needed, to the aroma while washing and after, and it leaves your hair feeling and looking great, and a lot more manageable. At this point, I think I have probably run my hands through my hair about 20 times in the few hours since I washed it earlier today.

In Closing:
I cannot tell you if you are going to love it because I don't know what you currently use, but I can tell you if you are considering making a considerable upgrade from the cheaper end of the spectrum to this product, I do not foresee any regrets... period.
summary: LOVE THIS - my hair hasn't felt this soft in YEARS.

reviewText:
Not surprisingly, since this is for fine/medium hair, this is a very light, not very moisturizing conditioner that seems to be geared toward a healthy scalp.  For those with normal-dry hair, this would be a Very Bad Option for regular use down the hair shaft, and yet it seems (even for us) rather lovely at the root. Also, as occasional styling goals would call for a lighter hair texture, I think dryer hair could use this occasionally for specific goals; but beyond that or scalp only use, you should avoid this if your hair is dry.  If your hair is Oily/Fine, I think you could LOVE this, particularly if you have struggle for body or want to encourage a beachy effect.

Silicones.  Lots of silicones.  So, the immediate reaction for me is disappointment because this is NOT "CG."  (I have seen more silicones than this in some other products though.)

If you avoid silicones, this isn't your conditioner. But, let's talk about silicones, shall we?  They get a bad rap, but they aren't inherently bad ingredients. They can smooth the hair and help create the illusion your hair is healthier than it is while also providing some protection from the elements and from heat products.  The trouble with silicones is that unless they are specifically water soluable silicones, you'll need shampoos with detergents and sulfates to get rid of them.  Sulfates, again, aren't always evil, but they certainly CAN be (much more so than silicones), especially since some shampoos are formulated like dish soap.  This is one reason lots of people follow something called the "CG Method" ( Curly Girl Method, google it) when choosing our hair products.  It helps when you have fussy frizz-prone tempermental wavy hair like mine. We're trying to avoid those sulfates.  Silcone filled products (conditioners, stylers, etc) will build up without a thorough cleanse, and unfortunately, this product contains both Dimethicone and Amethicone,  in their non-water-soluable form.  Which means this lovely smelling conditioner is a No-Go for CG purists and a rare use product for modified CG girl like me.

When I ordered there was no ingredient list.  So here it is:
Water, Cetyl Alcohol, Isoproply Myrestate, Stearalkonium Chloride, Steryl Alcohol, Gycerin, Quaternium-18, Hippophae Rhamnoides (Sea uckthorn) Oil, Stearamidopropyl Dymathylamine, Dimethicone, Amodimethicone, Octoxynol 40, Isolaureth 6, Polyquaternium-10,  Fragrance, Lactose, Cellulose, Hydroxypropyl Methyceelulose, Tocopheral Acetate, Irone Oxides, Hyrolyzed Keratin, Simmondsia Chinensis (Jojoba) Seed Oil, Triticum Vulgare (wheat) Germ Oil, Citric Acid, Methylchloroisothiazolinone, Methylisothiazolinone.

This product also has a few ingredients that are cool and interesting because they are the sort of ingredients that some hair likes and some doesn't.  Hair varies, like skin varies.  Some hair likes protein, some doesn't.  Same with other ingredients. So, this has some of those: Quaternium-18, Polyquat-10, Glycerin, Cellulose, Hydrolized Keratin (which is a protein, which is usually good for those who use heat often or color their hair).  My hair loves protein and glycerin, so this isn't a bad ingredient list for me, except for the non-water-soluable silicones (since I don't use shampoo often).  A more moisturizing formula would have suited my hair better, but probably wouldn't have been ideal for the finer haired target.  (Glycerin pulls moisture, so your experience with it will depend not only on your hair but on the humidity of your environment, in a dry area you might find it a drying product, but in a humid environment it will pull the moisture toward your hair not away from it; how much you like having that moisture pulled into your hair would depend a lot on your hair texture and styling goals.)

Oils included are Sea Buckthorn Oil, which is a really cool oil, healing, anti-aging, soothing, and antibacterial.  It's fairly high on the ingredient list and I imagine would make this soothing for someone with an irritated scalp.  Jojoba oil is also included, which is another soothing oil thought to promote hair growth and unclogging hair follicles, so this seems like a wise choice for thin hair conditioner.  Neither of these oils are heavy and none of the deeply moisturizing oils are on this list (which makes this less of a fit for ME, but still makes it a good option for those with fine hair).  This ingredient list seems to aim for a healthy scalp, which seems excellent as a goal.  The instructions specify leaving this on for 3-4 minutes, and I find myself wondering if that is in part to allow these scalp benefits time to take effect.

One reviewer described this as heavy; I seriously question whether they even used this product.  I cannot overemphasize how Very Lightweight and LIGHTLY moisturizing this product is.  I'm three days post wash and my hair (which is dry) is starting to feel a little moisture hungry.  I'm really not the targeted hair type, so this DOES NOT mean anything negative toward the product.  But, this is LIGHT.  Light, light, light, light. You'll have to decide for yourself if that's Good or Bad for YOUR hair type, but I think you can safely disregard the reviewer who described this as heavy.  Even though I air-dried my hair, it really has that superlightweight feel of after a blow out. If you'll note the above discussion of oils, those are the only two, neither are heavy.

This conditioner isn't for thirty hair, but it is lightly conditioning.  It didn't leave my hair truly dry, but I suspect that used daily over time, it would. The lightweight seems a good option for those with oily/fine hair or for root use only.  This might also be good occasionally used for when you're styling in a way that needs weightless hair or for beachy looks.  For dry hair, skip it.  At least skip it for the length of your hair.  It's just not hydrating enough.  However, I really liked it on the roots, as it didn't weigh them down, yet provided some light benefits there.

I have sensitive skin and this was non-irritating to my scalp.

Smells girly and quite perfume-y.  Personally, I love the perfumed smell (asthma and all), but that will be a personal choice and as with all fragrance, there's always someone who will hate it.

I also appreciate that this is a "for fine hair" product that is not filled with salts, which are so drying but sometimes included to fake volume.  As far as I can tell, the only alcohols included are fatty alcohols, which should not concern you.  There is ONE that I see, and it is fairly high on the list.  But I have seen five or more on a list, so I can live with just one.

Made in Israel.  Not tested on animals.  Not vegan, though.  Contains Wheat, Iron, and Lactose.

It's a nice conditioner, and I may try another from this line, but mostly I'll stick with the three conditioners I love and rotate.  Joico Kpak, Nexxus Hydralight, and Nexxus Youth Renewal (though I'm sad they changed the fragrance of that last one)---of those three the Hydralight is the only one I would recommend for fine hair.  My main take away is that this a pretty nice ingredient list for a product with silicones, but I'm not willing to pay $26 for silicones instead of oils.  And this is best for hair that tends toward oily, not dry.  Also, it's obviously NOT a fit for people who are CG purists or who simply don't uses traditional shampoos.  But, if you aren't turned away by the price point and you have fine hair AND you don't mind shampooing, this would be something I say you try.
summary: Review for the label reader, Ingredient conscious.

reviewText: I neither like nor dislike the fragrance of this conditioner and cannot even describe what the aroma is like. Nevertheless, this conditions my fine hair nicely without weighing it down and left my locks soft. However, I am also very attracted to fragrance and this just doesn't have a strong enough nor an attractive enough scent to make me want to purchase this. Based on the other reviews it appears I'm in the minority in not being overwhelmed by its scent.
summary: This conditions my hair nicely but the fragrance does not attract me enough to make me want to purchase this

reviewText: Love

I bought this topcoat to seal the nail polish strips I started using recently. It kept my nails shiny and chip free. When I was ready to remove the polish, it practically fell off. It didn't even take 5 minutes.
summary: I bought this topcoat to seal the nail polish strips ...

reviewText: Product is a 10. Makes your hair baby soft. Love it

I used this kit yesterday and today my hair is smooth and soft and definitely a lot stronger.  I used 1/2 ounce of #1 with 3 ounces of water (you can use less if your hair is short or more if it's longer) and applied it to dry hair.  I left this on for a couple of hours and then applied #2 directly on top and left the mixture on for another couple of hours.  I then shampooed and applied a hydrating mask for about 45 minutes with heat.  I then rinsed for a full five minutes and then applied my regular styling products and let my hair air dry overnight.  This morning my hair is in great shape and it looks and feels very healthy, almost like virgin hair.  My hair is color treated and I also have highlights and although my colorist uses Olaplex fatihfully, it is also quite damaged from aggressive heat styling.  In addition, I've had a small amount of breakage recently so I needed this Olaplex treatment because it can stop breakage cold.  When I combed my hair yesterday after this two step treatment, I had absolutely zero breakage.  My hair is very smooth and the ends no longer look frazzled or frayed but now lay smooth and flat.  I will continue to use #1 and #2 regularly, which will only improve my hair's condition.  I recommend this kit for anyone with damaged hair.  But if your hair is not damaged, Olaplex will not make any difference.  I do recommend using a hydrating mask afterward because Olaplex can sometimes leave hair feeling dry.  You can also do an intensive protein treatment after Olaplex but before the mask.  This will restore even the most damaged hair to a healthier state.  Following this Olaplex stand alone treatment with protein and moisture is recommended on the company's website.  You can of course add #1 to color or  bleach but you'll want to bump up the strength of the developer because Olaplex slows processing time, especially for bleach.  I got this kit from my stylist and I would be leery of ordering it on Amazon, where fakes abound.  However, read the reviews thoroughly and if possible order it through Prime, that way you can return it if it doesn't look right.  The Olaplex labels are easily counterfeited so you need to make sure the bottles are sealed and that there is an instruction manual in the package.  There should also be a measuring device for the bottle of #1.  Hope you like it as much as I do.

I use these products in a stand alone treatment.  I mixed 1/2 ounce #1 with 3 ounces of water (per the website instructions) and applied this to shampooed, towel dried hair for about an hour.  I then applied #2 over it without rinsing and left the mixture on for several hours.  I then shampooed and used a deep conditioner for about 45 minutes with heat.  The deep conditioner I used does contain a small amount of rice protein, which is good for my hair (Shea Moisture Manuka Honey mask) but you can do an intensive protein treatment if your hair is really damaged and then follow that with a protein free mask (Shea Moisture Raw Shea Butter mask is protein free and excellent).  Olaplex does not address cosmetic issues like moisture and shine so it can sometimes leave hair dry, which is why I always follow an Olaplex treatment with a moisturizing mask, even if I don't do a protein treatment too.  Olaplex is by far the biggest hair breakthrough in many a decade.  It increases the number of disulfide bonds that are present in healthy hair and depleted in damaged hair.  Any chemical or mechanical service disrupts these bonds and Olaplex helps to repair this.  However, it is not a license for total abuse and it will not restore hair to a virgin state (although it may feel that way).  It is simply insurance.  When used as a stand alone treatment, Olaplex will restore hair to a healthier, stronger state.  But if the abuse continues, you will need to do a stand alone treatment regularly to offset this.  My hair is color treated and highlighted and I heat style regularly, so I would have to say that my hair is quite damaged.  I do a stand alone treatment once a month but use #2 weekly overnight and then shampoo and deep condition the next morning.  By doing these treatments in this way, my hair is much healthier looking and certainly much stronger.  I haven't stopped the coloring/bleaching or heat styling, but I know my hair can withstand this treatment much better than it could before.  Prior to doing a stand alone treatment schedule, I did have considerable breakage.  My colorist uses Olaplex so I've had many in-salon treatments, which did improve my hair's condition considerably.  However, the real breakthrough came when I started doing stand alone treatments at home.  This did more to help my hair become resilient than merely using #3 weekly.  Truthfully, using #3 didn't do much unless I used it immediately after getting #1 and #2 in the salon.  The week I used #3 after the salon treatment it did make a difference.  However, subsequent weekly treatments did much less and weren't as noticeable.  That's when I switched to using #2 weekly, which did make an improvement over #3.  However, the best thing I've done for my hair in a long time was to buy the traveling stylist kit and use #1 and #2 as stand alone treatments.  I'm not going to add #1 to the color when I touch up my roots because the salon color brand I use is very gentle and does almost no damage.  I'd rather save #1 and use it as a treatment afterward.  In sum, this kit is a godsend.  You can consult the Olaplex website for info on how to use it as a stand alone treatment.  If your hair is damaged, it will make huge difference as long as you follow it with protein (if necessary) and a hydrating mask.  The Olaplex site even refers to the protein and moisture steps so it's not just my recommendation but theirs as well.  If your hair is not damaged, Olaplex will not make a difference.  For me at least, it's been a savoir.  My hair is no longer breaking and I know I can grow it longer without worrying about more breakage.  However, I still use heat occasionally but much less frequently than before.  It was obvious that the heat that was causing the breakage because my colorist uses Olaplex religiously so I don't think the bleach was causing the problem.  I recommend Olapelx for anyone who has damaged hair and wants to strengthen it measurably.  It's not a cure-all but is insurance.  There are imitators but only one patented product.  Make sure you get the real deal.  I don't know whether Amazon sellers are legit or not and the same holds true of ebay.  Consult the seller ratings on both sites to make sure you're dealing with a decent seller.  I know that runwaybeautytrends on ebay sells the real deal because I've ordered from them numerous times and have always gotten the exact same product I get from my stylist.  I have no clue about Amazon sellers though.  It's a bit risky to order from Amazon and I have been duped once when I ordered perfumed lotion so I'm leery of name brand beauty products simply because there are so many disreputable sellers here.  However, I would read the reviews carefully.  The traveling stylist kit sells for $79 retail so any price considerably less than that probably means it's a fake.  If you don't know what the real kit looks like, it would be extremely easy to dupe.  The real thing comes with a special measuring device for #1 and has a complete instruction booklet inside.  All the bottles are labeled, "for professional use only" and are individually sealed.  If you decide to risk it, be sure you inspect the packaging carefully before you open it.  If there is any discrepancy, promptly return it and get your money back.
Best protection for your color treated hair hands down!
It is a great product !
amazing stuff you could ever buy for your hair. I use it with any color as well as home treatments. worth the investment to preserve the integrity snd life of your hair.
summary: amazing stuff you could ever buy for your hair

reviewText:
I have tried many different kinds of cleansing/skin care regime from my dermatologist and I always keep on coming back to Obaji.
I know they are on the pricier side, but the results are bar none. I use Obagi Nu-Derm's entire line so I can't say how each one would work individually...but as a whole my skin has never looked or felt smoother, clearer or even in my entire life. I can now leave the house with just applying sunscreen and mascara. Before I had uneven skin tone from acne and sun spots. I also have very sensitive skin and cannot tolerate Retinol A and many skin brightening products as they sting and burn terribly. This does not burn or sting at all and you only need to use a little as a small amount is enough to cover your entire face.
 I can't say enough good things about this Obagi skin care line.
But with all products, you have to use this over a period of time to see results. I saw noticeable differences after about 5 weeks of regular use. I hope this helps.
summary: A product that actually works! A++

reviewText:
Years ago I used the complete line of Obagi products through a physician's office and loved the results. However, the system is intense. If you use the prescription products your skin is likely to peel, get red etc. to reveal the smooth skin underneath. Eventually, I had a reaction to one of the products and discontinued the regime.

The Nu-Derm Blend is the over the counter version of Obagi's prescription skin lightning product. The RX version contains 4% hydroquinone. Hydroquinone is an aggressive treatment for sun damaged, pigmented skin but it may also damage skin tissue and is banned in some countries. So using the less aggressive FX product will take longer but may be best in the long run.

The FX product contains arbutin, exfoliants and antioxidants to help smooth the skin and reduce the appearance of dark spots, age spots, freckles and other hyper-pigmenation. Combined with a retinol product such as an over the counter 1% retinol or prescription strength it can be even more effective at renovating the skin.

I found the product to go on smoothly. It does have a chemical smell to it that is not the greatest. It will take time to see how effective it is at brightening my skin. But I like the rest of the products in the line and feel this is likely to be another winner. I plan to combine it with an OTC 1% retinol product.

Obagi Nu-Derm Blend Fx, 2 oz. is a skin cream that is meant to brighten skin as well as mositurize. I can state that it works very well for the latter. Your skin does feel nice and smooth and it has a pleasant fragrance. This is not a high power bleaching cream however. It is meant to gradually lighten skin as in age spots or maybe a patch that is uneven in color due to other reasons.

It does work as a brightening agent, but again, this is NOT a bleaching cream that you are gonna see major results quickly. You want to apply it regularly and do take care to see how it reacts to your skin. Be careful that your skin is not too sensitive for this product. The manufacturer advises that you check with your doctor to see if this is a safe product for you to use. I agree that should be done, but this cream is mild and I do not think there are going to be many who can not use it.

Obagi Nu-Derm Blend Fx, 2 oz. is recommended for a person who has a mild skin problem that a brightening cream would correct. This is a well made, high quality product.

My wife found this interesting but isn't sure if it really did anything from her. We understand that the arbitun is for brightening uneven skin tones including age spots. But that's not really a problem my wife has. She says it does make her skin feel fresh, but that she really doesn't notice a color difference. But again, she doesn't have the issues this product solves.
summary: An interesting product but not for you if you don't have uneven skin tones or age spots

reviewText: Have to have my Obagi!  Have been using the Obagi system for two years now--wish I had started much sooner.  Skin looks smoother, more radiant.
summary: Have to have my Obagi! Have been using the ...

reviewText: It does make skin smoother/brighter.  I've been using this at night for a while and my skin seems "fresher."  My skin isn't as dry and it seems to have helped reduce red spots (inflamed areas).  I have a lot of freckles, but haven't seen any reduction in their appearance with this product.  I didn't not seem to get sun burned any easier while using this product.

I had used Obagi in the past under the care of a dermatologist, but never a product quite like this.  I did get a brightening factor for sure after several weeks, however my skin was overly sensitive to it.  Even using it more sparsely than indicated, I often would get irritated skin, and so I discontinued use.  Even during the brief time, though, I did see a benefit regarding its use.  I should have spot checked it first, which was my error.  I seem to have built up an intolerance to it, though.

I do think it's quite overpriced, as many similar products sell for far less and are more available to the average consumer.  I would definitely shop around.
summary: but never a product quite like this. I did get a brightening factor for ...

reviewText: I will admit I have did not use this everyday consistently for weeks and weeks on end, however I did use it after any evening showers I took. I never put it on in the morning because I worried about sun exposure. It's thick but quickly absorbed into my skin. I always like how my skin looks the next day when using this in the evening. I have dark spots from old blemishes and some redness, and my skin tone always looks more even the next day, even clearer. It does have an odd scent I don't care for but it goes away quickly once the product has dried. I was leaving the office of a surgeon the other day and they sold the entire Obagi line.
summary: I always like how my skin looks the next day when using ...

reviewText: I love the brightening results of this cream, and really enjoy Obagi products in general. However, I feel this cream is too moisturizing for my oily, slightly acne prone skin. If I avoid certain areas where I'm prone to break out, I find it works well. But the problem is, some of the areas on my face (chin and cheeks) where I am prone to breakouts are also areas where I'd benefit from the brightening effects. So, if you are someone with normal to dry skin, this could be perfect for you. I usually temper this blender with benzoyl peroxide in my problem areas, and obviously a retinol (which the Obagi Nuderm system is designed to be used with anyway). I use a low strength retinoid, so if I bumped up the strength, I'd probably prefer the amount of moisture this Blend Fx delivers. All around, this is a great product and actually works at brightening the skin without hydroquinone. It will not work as quickly or dramatically as the blender with hydroquinone, but I was surprised how effective it is without that typically critical ingredient.

Obagi is a high quality well known brand that is also touted by alot of dermatologists I've visited over the years...

I've actually used some prescription RX in the past that my dermo gave me to smooth my skin - Hydroquinone.  This Obagi cream is intended along those lines in a milder form.  I do find the Obagi easy to apply and feels fine on my face - no irritation, etc.  This type of cream is not advisable with sun exposure...I typically use it before bed.  Results are good - not as effective as prescription Hydroquinone but I still see noticeable results of more even/clear skin and less irritating to my skin than Hydroquinone.

At current price of $90 this Obagi is not cheap...but an effective product from a well respected brand.  4-STAR rating by me in consideration of price/value.
summary: effective product from a well respected brand

reviewText: My skin tends to be quite dry in the winter. This product coats your skin as a white translucent cream initially, with almost as much thickness as an ointment, but then quickly is absorbed leaving my face soft and moisturized. There's no particular scent, and the cream is easy to spread thinly around my face.  After a week of use, I haven't noticed any irritation or redness. The cost is quite high but not out of the typical range for AHA-containing products, and the 2 ounce size will likely last at least a couple of months.
summary: Non-irritating, moisturizing, facial cream with AHA.

reviewText:
It unnerves me when a product comes with a medical warning. It DOUBLE unnerves me when this warning is not stated in the product description.

I knew about the sunburn warning going in. That one is stated upfront. Im not a sun worshipper and besides, this skin brightener and blending cream arrived in the dead of winter in the Northeast. So imagine my surprise when I flipped it over and found a very different warning label on it:

Contains sodium metabisulfite, a sulfite that may cause allergic-type reactions included anaphylactic symptoms and LIFE-THREATENING or less severe asthmatic episodes in certain susceptible people.

Really, Obagi?! Its not like asthma is a rare condition or anything. Shame on you for not giving this potentiality the spotlight it should be given. Rant over.

Since Im not asthmatic, I took my chances with the Nu-Derm Blend Fx for the sake of a fair review. Fortunately, I was fine, and I do feel like my skin is slightly brighter when I use this cream, slightly being the operative word. Do I think its upwards of one hundred bucks brighter? No way, not even close.
summary: NOT for Asthmatics and Substantially Overpriced

reviewText:
During the summer I'm on my motorcycle or in the pool.
Although I wear sunscreen products faithfully, between sun exposure and age, those pesky spots still pop up.
This goes on smoothly with less irritation than the prescription retinol I've used in the past.
As with any similar product, stay out of the sun when using it.
My skin is indeed brighter. It didn't seem to be the best with deeper lines, but after a month fine lines are less noticeable. Dark spots are somewhat lightened.
summary: Not a Miracle (nothing is) but Works Well

reviewText: I would have to agree with other reviewers, that while this product seems to work OK, it is not the best.  I did not notice a strong smell from it.  It goes on light and did seem to smooth out my skin tone, especially under my eyes.  However, I have other products that do much better and are much cheaper.  Overall, I usually like the Obagi line, but this product is just OK
summary: too expensive for an OK product

reviewText:
I had really high expectations for this product, as I have heard lots of raves for the Obagi skincare line.  I used this product twice a day, every day (per the instructions) for 4 weeks but have seen no improvement.  In fact, it made my skin drier.  I now have these dry patches on either side of my mouth which is beginning to clear up now that I've decided to stop using this product.  To be clear, it did not brighten my skin or in any way improve its appearance.  I have medium skin which is prone to hyperpigmentation.  I applied on areas with dark spots which did not lighten at all.

I have a feeling that for this product to be effective, it has to be used with the entire line.

A little goes a long way so apply carefully. The smell is unpleasant to me - what I would characterize as "yeasty" but it does go away after a few minutes.

One thing to note is that you must be religious about sunscreen.  I used sunscreen in the morning but forgot to put it on in the afternoon before my one-hour walk.  I noticed that my skin was red/sunburnt later that day.  And I don't usually burn.  This product does make your skin more sensitive to the sun so don't forget to protect it!

The Obagi Nu-Derm line is the one most recommended by dermatologists/plastic surgeons. I have gotten the whole set plus prescription retin-A, which is normally mixed with the Blend, and I can attest to the terrific results on my darker skin. Some people complain that using the line makes you too pale, but that has not been an issue for me.

This is a gentler product than your doctor's Blend, and I'm just as happy to avoid hydroquinone. I know hydroquinone has a respectable track record, but if I can fade darker spots and areas without it, I'd rather go that route.

A few people have commented on the fragrance. I love it myself. The product is not perfumed, but smells to me like potent chemicals, not horrible, not like hydrogen sulfide for example, but if you're not smelling anything, you may have a stale bottle.

I stopped using the line when I switched to laser treatments. I'm thinking it may be time to go back. It's hard to review this single product in isolation because it's designed to work with the set, including prescription retin-A, but Obagi remains the gold standard for facial skin care.

The smell of this blend is awful. It dissipates fairly quickly but really is unpleasant. I used the product twice a day on the back of one hand for two weeks and I have seen no difference. This is a smooth cream that is not greasy or oily but oh the smell!

I usually love Jane Iredale, but this blush is a disappointment.  I know the picture shows the tube, but it is REALLY small, 3" tall with only 2" of product inside.  I thought I had misordered and got lipstick at first.  The color is nice, goes on very nice, but SMELLS.  I think they made it smell like chocolate - yuck.  Seriously, when is the last time any woman put chocolate on her face? I buy Jane Iredale because of the superior quality, quantity and non allergic smells, etc.  This one failed on all three.  So, if you would like to smell like chocolate, buy this blush.
summary: Little, little tube with little product and big smell

reviewText:
The In Touch Cream Blush in color named "Candid" seems to be the closest in color to the Pure Pressed Blush named "Dubonnet".
The "Connection" color is excellent as well.
Best makeup ever!!

I've never used a cream blush and usually wear very little, if any, make-up.  I decided to give this product a try though and am happy with the results.  My first try, I ended up putting way too much on and it looked like I had gotten a sun burn.  The next try, I used a just a small dab and it worked much better, giving me a little color without making me look sun burnt.  I like that the application is easy.  I can't use powder based make up because they typically contain corn products and I'm allergic to corn, so breathing in the little corn dust in powders is not good for me.  I don't know if this product is comprised of corn, but since I can't breathe it in, I don't get sick from using it.

I did a little research on the Jane Iredale company and was happy to learn that they are cruelty free and don't allow their products to be sold in China.  Any company that sells make up or food products in China is required to either test their products on animals themselves or pay for a Chinese company to do the testing.  I wish more companies would take a stand against animal testing in this way.
summary: Easy to apply and not tested on animals

reviewText: Really like it but it comes off easily

This is the first time I am trying a powder based blush and I am impressed.

This is a very small quantity and it will last a long time, you can apply with your fingers, but I would suggest you to get a nice brush so that it can be easily and uniformly applied.

Just once a day is enough and it stays on, it is small and easy to carry in purse if you want apply it later
summary: Different to apply, but stays on and looks good

reviewText:
I have dry skin and I have always wanted to give cream blush a try. I made sure my skin was washed/dryed/prepped and once I applied this I found it to be smooth and creamy and have a nice smell. Also, not testing on animals makes me feel better about using it.

I used a blush brush to apply, but you could also use your fingers and then blend in. I find this to not be glossy and to have more of a matte look which is beautiful. The product size is quiet small, but I found that it didn't take much to bring color to my cheeks and I find that the size/price and for how long makeup "should"be used for is all in line.

Its an awesome color and the application was easy peesy! I am not new to cream blushes. I own a few from Mac to Nars but this one I liked a lot!
Its "cream to powder" which means its easy to apply, you simply glide it on your cheek or lips and blend it with your fingers. It "sets' like a powder but still gives you a glowy look. It stays put all day which isn't true to some of the high end blushes I use and it hasn't caused any irritation to my skin.
I think this color would suit all skin tones. I have a fair/brown skin tone and it looks good on me! I used it on my lip and it was just my natural color.
The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars was for the size and the price. for 0.14 oz I feel $28 is too much.
summary: A sweet subtle glow with a hint of color!

reviewText:
I loved the color on this. It fits perfectly any skin color and makes a smooth blend to match your skin. It has a nice long lasting citrus smell which I loved as well. It's small, fits almost anywhere, any purse, and make up bag. But, it's oily. Although it feels like it dries almost instantly, you can still have the oily sensation on your skin. Maybe if you use some kind of make up neutralizer powder after applying this, would be better.

I honestly liked it but the only concern I have was the oily result. Other than that, it's perfect!!
summary: I liked it but feels very oily on my skin

reviewText: My last blush was a compact powder that broke and crumbled in my make-up bag and I quickly tossed it out.  I had yet to purchase anything new, so this was the perfect item to receive for review. The amount within is not much, but a little goes a long way and the color and quality are worth it. I love that I can just swipe a little in my cheeks and blend in, it looks very natural, not streaky and there has been no skin irritation. The price may be high on this one, but I actually believe it is worth it, which coming from me is rare.  Overall I really like it and I'll add this to my buy list for when it runs out.

This cream blush is very small and easy to take in your makeup bag, it's not bigger than lipstick just a tad thicker. The application can't be any easier, dab some on your skin and blend, plus you can add more to make it more pronounced. It's not too pink nor red, it provides a hint of nice mauve color (I have fair olive color skin). It is neutral/cool based so can be worn by almost anybody. I applied it in the morning and touched up at lunch but I normally do that anyway.
summary: Neutral/Cool based shade that compliments fair/med skin tones

reviewerName: the old lady who lived in a shoe
reviewText: I have to say, I was surprised that the blush case was actually smaller than most lipstick cases, although it is also wider. We tend to think of those big tubes that we used to get cream blush in and this is no where near that size. The blush feels good on my lips, my cheeks and my eyes. This is one of those do it all type cosmetics and it has a sheen to it to give it a bit of a sparkle. It can be used under or over your regular blush or by itself. I use mineral cosmetics when I wear cosmetics and I prefer them to other cosmetics. I feel they are better for my skin and can be worn lightly or added too for more vivid colors.
summary: all purpose blush in a tube

reviewText: The cream to powder concept is interesting. I know "women of a certain age" are advised to ditch powder for rouge, but I never liked that shiny look. This is a nice in-between. It goes on smoothly, and within a few applications, you learn to use a light touch. I thought the Candid color might be too dark, but it's a good color for my fair skin with rose overtones. The only thing that surprised me was how small the tube was -- keep in mind that the product is only 0.14 oz.

Verdict? This product is great.
I was skeptical of this blush at first, thinking "cream to powder" meant it would go on like either foundation from a compact or lipstick, and then have to be rubbed in hard to distribute. I was so wrong. It goes on silky-silky soft and subtle (seriously--I tried it on my lips and it was far more silky than any lipstick I've ever tried, though it then settled to a gentle powder). And when it said to apply over blush for a more "dramatic" look, I had images of 1980s blush streaks, but nothing could be further from the truth. It goes on super-super subtle and soft. Yes, you *can* push hard to get it a bit darker, but you'd really have to work at it--by default it goes on as gently as a typical powder blush. And the color (Candid) is a subtle-subtle pinkish, so it will probably work with most skin tones as it's too gentle to clash :-P and easy to distribute (with just a fingertip) for a moment or two after applying. I tried it on my lips and it made almost no difference--took a tiny bit of the color out of them, but was hardly noticeable. It was super-subtle on my eyelids as well; I'll probably just use it as blush.

I was a bit surprised at the shape of the container. I think I must have been expecting something shaped like lipstick, because this was really short at just 2" (lipstick is usually 3-4"), and stubby/wide (1" diameter whereas lipstick is normally 1/2-3/4" wide). But that actually worked better for broad/smooth application vs. narrow streaks, so it makes sense.

Note: the jane iredale site has more pictures and details about colors if that would be helpful for you

This cream blush is nothing to brag about but I am using it.  Has to be applied often - more - as it melts into the skin quickly.  It is not drying, but maybe a little too creamy.  Not awful, but not great.
summary: Jane Iredale In Touch Cream Blush

reviewText: The color was not at all what I expected. It's VERY PINK, and not in a natural way. The color shown here looks very natural, a pachy-pink color and perfect for my fair peaches-n-cream skin color. Sadly to say, it is so pink that I cannot use it. I'll find someone to give it to. Not for me
summary: Not the color shown on the screen

reviewText:
Love the color!  Perfect for summer.... I prefer cream blush, I think it adds glow and not a powdered cake look that makes ladies looks older and over done.  I much prefer a natural glow :)  So dab this on the apples of your cheeks, along the top of your cheek bone and the top of your forehead along the hair line (where the sun would hit) and blend... then GLOW :)  Gorgeous... Beautiful....  Formula feels nice, creamy not sticky. No powder means no creasing nothing sitting on top of your skin.  Color is bright in the stick but not bright on... just natural.

My heritage is Scottish, Irish and English.... can you say fair skin, freckles and blue eyes.  very pink undertones to my skin.  So this clear soft pink is very much what my skin looks like when I have been in the sun for the afternoon.  Just kissed by the sunshine and healthy glow.  Lovely

Love the size and compact nature of the container.  No brushes, no applicators... Love that... less is more.  It is sophisticated and easy.

There is no sparkle in the color I bought (Clarity) which I prefer.  At times I use a illuminating foundation with adds enough "light" to my face.  If I want sparkle I can add that in other ways (great liner) or gloss on my lips...

Light, soft, natural glow is what you get with this lovely compact little cream blush. I imagine it is going to last me a while as I don't need a lot.

So just dab, blend and glow.

Like the product but 3 stars for the shoddy way it's put together. Like another reviewer, when I opened the top the entire blush popped out onto the floor. For the price they are charging I expect the product to be intact and a larger tube as well.

4 stars for color and texture
1 star for the shoddy tube
Natural looking blush that your husband will not only like but think that the blush of spring is now natural, but we won't tell him different!
summary: Natural looking blush that your husband will not only like but think that the blush of spring is now ...

reviewText: This is such a good product, healthful for your skin, looks natural and is not made with any harmful chemicals!
summary: This is such a good product, healthful for your skin

reviewText: I am satisfied with the quality and ease of application of the product.  The color is nowhere near what I expected but it's "okay".  I would not have purchased it had I seen the color represented more appropriately in the photo.  It is absolutely not a pink color.  It's a darker, bronzier look but using a little of it makes it tolerable.
summary: IT IS NOT THE PINK COLOR SHOWN!

reviewText: I really like Jane Iredale products but I feel like they are not very durable.  I really like the smell of this blush and the fact that it is not tested on animals.  The color looks really nice on my pale skin.  The reason that I give it a three is because it broke off in the top after only a short time of use.

From the wife: Nice and smooth texture. Initially, it seems heavy for a tinted moisturizer, but it spreads smoothly and gives a light coverage. It is moisturizing but I do have dry skin,  so I put my day moisturizer on first and put the tinted moisturizer over it.
The concealer provides great coverage for my dark under eye circle.  With the use of a concealer brush I was able to put it on smoothly.

The nice, compact packaging is efficient to take with you when you're traveling or keeping it in your purse.

I love the quality of this product, after using it several times I got to appreciate it more.  It gives a fresh look all day.  It feels light on the skin and it specially great now during the summer months.

If you are looking into higher end cosmetic, Vincent Longo is a trusted name and this tinted moisturizer lives up to that.
summary: Vincent Longo Ultra Light Tinted Moisturizer

reviewText:
I have to say that I was a bit disappointed by this product.  Usually, I like something that has more than one use for it, but this moisturizer was quite heavy and I felt like I was back in the 80s in high school when I used to wear a thick layer of base/foundation.  It's much more styled like and feels like makeup than a moisturizer, although I did like the actual moisturizing effect.

I thought the tint was extremely dark.  I'm a VERY pale person when it's not summer and in the summer time, I tan like a brown bear.  Even with my really dark tan, I found this cream to be extremely dark and noticeable on my skin.  My other concealers are much lighter and blend easier.  I didn't feel like I was simply wearing some moisturizer on my skin...it was like I was wearing foundation.  As the day wore on, I could see it in the pores of my skin, almost looking crackling.

Overall, it might be a good product for someone looking for a moisturizing base, but I haven't worn base since 1994...so this was extremely heavy for me.  Also, the price point is not something I would be willing to pay.  A nice try, but not something I'll get again.
summary: More like base/foundation than a moisturizer

reviewText: I decided to give this concealer a go, as I am an occasional user of the concealer from Origins (under $20). In comparison, the Vincent Longo applies to my skin more smoothly and more easily. The coverage is about the same, but the Longo feels like a higher quality product. They both wear off after several hours, but maybe only because I have oily skin.

I realize light can mean colour tint or light weight feeling. With makeup labeled light - this was a darker tint than I expected, but the meaning is a light feeling make up/tinted moisturizer. The cream is more of a makeup base than what I would label a tinted moisturizer.
Canvas is another part of the name that lends one to believe it might be heavier than what it is.

The concealer is heavy enough that it covers a birthmark on my face. The tinted moisturizer stays on my face as long as base make up normally does, as does the concealer.
The tube with its screw on lid-concealer holder can be a bit awkward to useunscrewing the top concealer container to get to the moisturizer and then having to wash hands before handling anything else, leaving your tube to sit on a counter.
The concealer has a tiny round mirror in the lid which is nice especially if you are using it at the beach for example. The one main downside, at this time for me is the high cost of this product. I have other products that preform the same functions as well at a fraction of the cost.

I love products that can serve multiple purposes. The idea of a tinted moisturizer with sun protected is appealing to an on-the-go girl like myself. Also, it was a great idea to include concealer and package it along with the tube. I had never owned a Vincent Longo product before, but knew they had a reputation for being good. In a nutshell, it is. The texture is like silk. It went on smooth and left a dewy finish. Alas, the latter is bit too dewy for the summer in the US South. I am going to save this until the Fall when the temps drop and my skin stops cranking out the oil. However, this would be a great option for those with dry to very dry skin. One thing, though, this product was darker than I expected but given how sheer it is, it was not a problem.
summary: Beautiful texture, glides on smoothly, but you may want to save this for Fall

reviewText: I have been a Lancme user for many years now. I have medium color skin (lots of freckles).  I was willing to try the Vincent Longo Ultra Light Canvas Tinted Moisturizer.  I really like the light feel, the color, the convenient tube with concealer,  the ease of application and most of all, no skin irritation.  I have posted pictures to show you the similarities between the two products!  To test this product, I actually did a side by side test of my own face and even I couldn't tell the difference.  In the picture, you will see this product shown next to a Lancme product - Bisque is the color. I truly enjoyed the product and am pleased to be able to continue using this!
summary: See side-by-side comparison to Lancome Bisque

reviewText:
This Vincent Longo tinted moisturizer is gorgeously lightweight and easy to apply.  However just like other tinted moisturizers, the product tends to fall into the deeper lines and creases in your face during the course of the day.  This is where the accompanying concealer shines.  It is perfectly colour matched to the tinted moisturizer and is of a thicker consistency.  It should be applied sparingly and gently to the areas where one needs coverage plus into the the deeper lines on your face.  The thicker consistency fills-in the lines as well as evens out discoloured areas and helps prevent too much tinted moisturizer from moving into your facial lines during the day.  The finish is smooth and flawless without looking caked-on.

I really like this dual-product approach.  I can mix a bit of concealer and a bit of moisturizer on the back of my hand and apply it all over my face for something with medium coverage or use both products separately and strategically.

Overall I am quite impressed with this product.  This #4 colour is similar to my MAC C3-C4 foundation colours.
summary: Strategic multi-use tinted moisturizer and concealer duo.  Equivalent to MAC C3-C4

reviewText: I am a fan of the Baxter products love their bar soap and their hair pomade.  However the grooming lotion did not do much for me.  I have medium length thick hair.  Would put on my hair when damp and it helped style it but did not hold for long.  As others have said it does  have a nice scent.
summary: A fan of Baxter of CA but will pass on this one.

reviewText:
I'm always on the lookout for a good grooming product and this Baxter of California Grooming Lotion is so good that I'm thinking about switching from the product I currently use - Redken Grooming Cream.

First, I will say that I have thick hair and that this product is extremely lightweight. If you have thin hair and need something with a bit more holding power this probably won't be a good product for you.

What I like about the Baxter:
(+) Lightweight. I live in the swampy Midwest and hate heavy hair products that frequently feel greasy and even start to mix with sweat (when working out). No such problem with the Baxter formula.

(+) Odor. Or more specifically the lack of a strong odor in this product. There are some citrus and eucalyptus notes but they're very subtle.

(+) Application. The grooming lotion is opaque but rubs in clear and disappears easily into hair without any white streaks.

(+) Hold. Apply with water onto damp hair for a sleek finish or apply a small amount to almost dry hair for a more natural looking finish. The hold is light but on my thick hair it's perfect.

Great product, a bit expensive but otherwise recommended!

I'm always looking for new products and new ways in which to do my hair.  Experimentation is my weakness.  I used this grooming lotion and was pleased with the results.  Maybe I shouldn't be so worried about my hair...But thank goodness for products like these.

Highly recommended.

This is an aromatic grooming lotion that leaves a soft, textured look.

Good if you don't feel like the sticky or heavier holds like pomade.

First Baxter product I am not a fan of.  For my hair it does NOTHING.  It goes in pleasantly and has a nice odor that lasts about as long as it will take you to get dressed.  My hair is fairly short and truthfully I don't get the purpose of the product as it does not hold my hair in place at all.  Maybe someone with longer hair would find a better use by ridding  themselves of curls, but as for me, the slight friz i do get this product is not worth the money.

This "grooming lotion" doesn't seem to do very much. It smells and feels pleasant when applied, with a very light barbershop scent that fades quickly, and vanishes into post-shower hair quickly. After that, it seems to work like a light conditioner, nothing more: the hair is maybe a little more controllable and a little heavier, but doesn't have any significant texture or hold at all. It's not much of a hair "product" as far as I can tell; more like a post-wash conditioner, which is pleasant but doesn't have enough of an effect to justify the price. I'd stick with Baxter's (or other brands') various pomades instead.
summary: Doesn't do much beyond light conditioning

reviewText: I tried this on both my wet and dry hair and while it has a slight smoothing quality on dry hair it does nothing at all on wet hair.  I have much better products although on a man's very short hair who only wants a hint of something in his hair this might be perfect.
summary: Does not work well for shoulder length hair

reviewText: I love this stuff. I use it in conjunction with another styling cream and it's worked really well. It's very light - the instructions say you can use this on its own, but I need a little more hold. Still, this has added just the little extra texture and hold to make the difference. I really like using this stuff and I'll be purchasing more of it going forward.
Not impressed. Didn't make my hair look or feel any fuller. Didn't keep it in place well. Non greasy, smells good, but didn't make my hair look any better than before I used it.

The best thing about this is the fragrance, which I can't identify, but seems like fruit or something in nature.  I t has a nice creamy texture, which you apply while your hair is still damp.  I do have fine hair, about 5 inches past my shoulders. When they say light hold, don't think it really has any, not for longer hair, anyway.  Other than the fragrance and ease in comb-out, I don't see any difference using this.

This is a very lightweight hair cream.  It has only a slight scent of peppermint or spice, it's a little antiseptic but in a clean and fresh - and not chemical - way.  I rub a small (1/2 inch) bit into my hands and then into my hair and it does a fine job holding my "style" all day.  No frizz, and my hair doesn't feel stiff or waxy.  However, I have pretty short, and manageably wavy hair.  This wouldn't work for something that needs a lot of hold.  Washes out clean, with no build-up.  I wish it wasn't so expensive.
summary: Sweet, light, and clean with decent hold

reviewText:
This seems like a decent base product, it softens hair and keeps frizz at bay. Keeping the hair in place? Not so much. My husband still needs to use a paste for that. However, a big plus is that on day two, he doesn't wake up with totally oily hair. Strange, but love that!

The fragrance is very subtle and fresh though, it reminds us of botanicals--real ones. Very nice scent, light and easy.

We might get this again solely for keeping his hair oil-free, not the giant greasy chrome-shine mess on day 2 that he's used to.

This is not only a great setting mist, it's also an awesome sunscreen.  I use it because the Florida sun is relentless and I need a good sunscreen every day. I hate the greasiness of most high SPF lotions and they don't work well under makeup when you have oily skin like I do.  So this spray SPF 50 mist is the perfect solution.  I have worn it when riding motorcycles and it's worked like a charm.  I've also used it during outdoor sporting events and I've never had even a hint of sunburn.  I use it daily to set my makeup and it's been a true champ at keeping my face fresh even as the heat and humidity climb.  I have used it for about 6 months in all kinds of situations and it's always worked perfectly.  When riding the bike, I keep it in my backpack and reapply every few hours.  I do the same thing at any outdoor event.  However, just one spritz is all I need for any regular day.  It can sting a little when it first goes on, which is not uncomfortable, so be sure to keep your eyes closed but it dries almost instantly.  It's far superior to any sunscreen lotion, especially if you have oily or combination skin.  I highly recommend it for all skin types and I have repeatedly purchased the large bottle at Sephora.  There's simply nothing better than this two in one product.

Caused me to break out when used. Kind of burns your eyes. I spray and walk with my eyes closed so the fumes don't get in my eyes when I open them. You definitely don't burn with this stuff. I wouldnt repurchase due to the price and breaking out.
summary: Caused me to break out when used. Kind of ...

reviewText: Leaves behind a bit of sticky feeling but helps keep make-up on beautiful
Good
This stuff is awesome! I disagree with other reviews that it felt heavy. I spent 3 days on the desert outside from noon to midnight and my makeup didn't budge and no sunburn! That's a winner!!!

I apply this about 1/2 hour before going out into the sun for an extended period of time over my makeup. Obviously with a face full of makeup, smearing sunscreen will ruin everything.  This product allows me to keep my makeup intact while protecting my skin. Because it is a sunscreen mist, be prepared to have a very fine, sheer white mist over your skin. Having used this product for over a year, my skin has not broken out. I like the rosemary scent very much - very refreshing. Be careful when applying that it doesn't get on your hair because it will make it greasy, just like regular sunscreen. One thing I do not like is that the product clumps inside the bottle around the opening. Make sure to shake well before use.
summary: Perfect if you have makeup on

reviewText: Top is very hard to handle. Color changed after 2 days, started to look dity.
Pretty nail polish, but the top is very hard too handle.
Favorite soft hold hair spray. Smells heavenly and just look at that bottle!

I didn't use to like hair spray but this product changed my opinion, now I cant get enough of this hair spray, smell great, I would say light hold but enough to keep the shape and volume I like, hair feels soft.
summary: Fantastic for light hold, leaves my hair shinny and soft

reviewText: This didn't work for my straight lifeless hair.

Gentlemen, if your stylist reaches for this stuff- RUN! It's left me with the most horrid smelling hair, like someone dumped a bottle of old lady perfume on me. It is way too strong and fragrant, very feminine too. It's lasted for days now even after I shampoo. Holy hell.
summary: Scent is awful, not for men

reviewText: its ok
Does not work.  But smells good.
Excellent dry shampoo, does not leave white cast, smells great without being too perfume-y.
I couldn't love this dry shampoo any more. It smells like coconut and love, and leaves zero dusty residue on my dark hair. Holy grail!

After trying tons of dry shampoos, I received a sample size of this in a Birchbox on month, and I was hooked! Some people don't like the smell, and I love it--so I'll try to explain what it smells like. It's faintly powdery/musky, and is only strong when first applied--after about five minutes, you really can't smell it, and neither can other people (I asked.) What I love about this dry shampoo is that a little goes a long way, it doesn't make your hair feel filmy (like you're covering up grease with powdery crap), and it really makes you feel ALMOST as fresh as if you'd washed your hair. A great pick me up, and if you're not ready to take the plunge because it's pricey, try getting an R+Co kit so you can try a smaller size along with other products, like their blow-out balm. Happy dry shampooing!
I love the scent.  If you use too much, your hair gets crunchy. A little goes a long way.
Greatest dry shampoo. I was a big fan of another brand - but have now totally switched over.

works great under make up. very thick so i mix with a littel moisturizer. makes sunscreen easier to spread but still get SPF and then also it is a great primer. put it on.. wait 10 minutes till not sticky them put on makeup.

I typically dislike facial sunscreens because they tend to feel oily and heavy. Im very pleased with this one though! Its light and my skin feels like it can breathe! Dont expect this to give you coverage like a foundation but, I appreciated the tint as I don't wear makeup when swimming or working out outside. Love that its a mineral block too!
Love this sunscreen.  Goes on smooth, adds just a hint of color, and provides excellent waterproof protection.  Easy to apply without feeling heavy and greasy.  Recommended.
summary: Goes on Smooth, Excellent Waterproof Protection

reviewText: My wife loves this stuff.  She uses it when we go to Disney so that she has protection from the sun, while giving her just enough color not to look much like a tourist.  Me on the other hand, I am white as a ghost so everyone knows I'm not from around there because I use non tinted sunscreen.  Haha.  Anyway, this product gives her a nice glow not a leathery looking tan.  Overall, I suggest you try it if you want the best of both worlds.
summary: My wife thinks its a great product!

reviewText: Very good sunscreen. Easy to put on . No battle with white streaks since the flesh colored tint helps it to blend in . As a sunscreen it worked just fine. Feels good, not greasy.

The wife and I tried this for a couple of weeks now when we are outdoor with the kids, it works well. I have a slightly darker skin color so I have to work this in a bit for me to not have a pale look. But once on its great knowing I have zinc sunscreen protection. No allergic reaction, we like it, but it's just a bit too expensive for such a small bottle.

We were wondering if this tinted sunscreen would be too tinted and show up on the skin; it doesn't at all!  It's good sunscreen - it's not oily and it doesn't smell bad.  Anyway, we're glad we have it and will for sure use it all!

Excellent tined sunscreen!  I have a medium to dark skin tone and was very happy with the tint on this sunscreen.  Helps to even out my complexion on those beach or pool days when I'm not going to be wearing makeup.  It applies easily and is lightweight.
summary: Lightweight tinted sunscreen!  Great for medium complexions.

reviewText: Now that I have tried mineral sunscreen there is no going back to the traditional formulas. This goes on smooth and leaves no residue or sunscreen smell. The only drawback is that the tint is only in one color. I have applied it alone and it is fine for a beach day where makeup color matching does not have to be perfect but for daily use I like a more exact color match. I mixed this with my foundation but had two issues first I cannot put enough into the mix to be sure that I am getting the necessary sun protection and second it changes the tint and consistency of the foundation I have finally found that works for my skin tone.  Additionally, it alters the color of my costly matched foundation which already has SPF. This tinted mineral foundation will be used for outdoor activities when I am forgoing my regular make up routine. It does not run into my eyes and goes on smoothly. I would love an array of tints to select one to match my skin tone.

I really like using B&B creams instead of  foundation and powder because I have older skin and I think they can look too heavy and are aging. I decided to give this a try and I am glad I did.

This is a great sunscreen and it feels so silky on my face. Most B&B creams leave my face too shiny but not this; it's got a matte finish which is really nice.

I appreciate that it's tinted but if you're expecting that tint to coverup facial imperfections like broken blood vessels you may be disappointed  - but it's not meant for that. Heavier foundation cream or coverup would be necessary if that's your goal.

Instead this just will give you a little glow and even the tone on your face and since I am fairly pale I appreciate that. The fact that it is such an effect sunscreen just makes it all the better.

Highly recommended. It is pricey, and the tube doesn't hold that much, especially if you're planning on using it daily on your face and neck. But it does work and it will leave your face feeling silky and moisturized without being shiny or greasy.
summary: One of my favorite tinted facial sunscreen moisterizers

reviewText: Beautiful silky feel to what is almost like a foundation, but not quite. It's a tinted broad spectrum sunscreen with an SPF of 40. It acts like a foundation or could be used as a primer or just instead of makeup foundation.  We tried it on two of us with different skin tones and it went on a little dark and then as we spread it around, it just blended in perfectly for both of us.  I like it very much.  That's just the easiest way ever to protect against the sun.
summary: Creamy mineral sunscreen with an SPF of 40 that behaves like a tinted cream foundation. Can be used under or instead of makeup.

reviewText: Too dark for my face. Sunscreen went on smoothly and absorbed well. Since it only comes in one color, I cannot recommend this product for fair skinned folks. The shade is a light to medium tan. Works well as a sunscreen. Felt good on the face. Just too dark for me to wear.
summary: Worked well, but shade was too dark for me

reviewText: Excellent sunscreen.  I like the light tint, it blends and doesn't show at all.  It lasts quite a long time.  What I like most is it doesn't irritate my eyes.  Any other type I use, if I apply near my eyes, it irritates me like hell.  This one is much less.  I have to say though, it's a small tube for a big price.
summary: Excellent sunscreen. I like the light tint

reviewText:
Wow. Discovered this through Amazon product recommendation. Goes on light. Feels very silky and gives off a matte finish. Does not leave a slick feeling like chemical suncreens. It does feel like silicone based make-up primers I've used from other brands.

The tint is nice and works well with my color (medium light). That said, the product is just barely tinted..and once smoothed on, it barely give off any color at all. It does not have as much coverage as a tinted moisturizer in my opinion. I definitely apply make up on top of it when going out. That said, if it's not a perfect match for your skin, it probably won't matter much.

I am a blonde but this tinted sunscreen still looks natural on my face. Since my dermatologist has found several pre-cancers spots on my face, I am very glad that it has an S{F of 40. It is expensive but there a very small hole where it is dispensed and I just use it on my face so it will last a long time. There is no sting when you apply it.

This feels AMAZING when applying! It's soft, smooth and glides right on. I love that it's SPF40 and does its job well. Especially around my nose area. I've even used it on my chest <it's quite expensive to use it there all the time>. I'm in my early 50's and this does not dry my face out, or make it oily. There is no scent <that I can detect. I've worn it alone and with my foundation. I'd LOVE for it to be in a darker tint so that I can wear it more often when I have a darker tan. This works well, without foundation, at the beginning of the season and at the very end, otherwise it's too light to wear alone.

Four stars due to the price. It's super expensive, otherwise it would have been five stars.
summary: Great for using alone with the slight tint. Wish they made it in different skin tones.

reviewText: I absolutely love this sunscreen. I actually use it as a foundation. It gives a beautiful matte finish but with a light flawless coverage that doesn't give you that overly made up look. It really gives you the mineral foundation look. The fact that it protects so well from the sun is obviously the main benefit and it's much needed here in Florida. Doesn't sweat off like so many other sunscreens and foundations. It is pricey but you get what you pay for. No dripping and the tint alllows you to apply it evenly. I'm pretty fair skinned and the 3 was a perfect match for me. Looks and feels amazing. I'll definitely reorder when I run out.

I only wish this were a little less expensive!  This goes on nicely and makes my skin feel smooth and matte, while moisturizing at the same time.  Awesome SPF 40 on this and water resistant.  The tint looks like it's for a darker skin tone, but when you put it on, it blends right into your skin tone, and I am very fair.  Makeup goes on very nicely afterwards.  I use a mineral powder and I feel like it made it less caky than it sometimes looks.

I've heard my dermatologist talk about this brand before (she recommended it for sensitive skin) but I was hesitant to try it and waste the money in case it didn't work for me- so I am glad I was able to get the chance to review it. I hope my review of this product will help you in making the right choice for yourself. After breaking out while using many other sunscreens, I use this with great results.  I'm a busy mom of two little ones and needed something that worked well with a little tint. This sunscreen which contains titanium dioxide (8%) and zinc oxide (3.8%) provides a bit of tint and color to my face. I have olive skin and it's the perfect match for me. You're supposed to put it on about 15 min before going out in the sun and reapply every two hours. Tizo is the only sunscreen that didn't cause little allergic reaction zits to pop up. I'm so happy to have found it, and the tint just adds a little color to your face. I love this stuff and it works so well.
summary: ... heard my dermatologist talk about this brand before (she recommended it for sensitive skin) but I was hesitant to ...

reviewText: Tizo my face
best tinted sunscreen on the market

I've tried a lot of mineral-based sunscreens before and most are either too heavy and greasy and/or leave that dreaded white cast. This is one of the few that does neither. It feels more like a foundation primer than a sunscreen. It glides on the skin, has a silk-like finish, and leaves no white cast. (Well, it is possible to get a whitish cast if you apply too much, but even then it isn't that bad.) I absolutely love this product. I just wish it came in a bigger container. 1 ounce won't last too long if anyone applies this as directed every day.

As a pale face ghost with super sensitive skin, I look constantly for a facial sunscreen that won't break me out or feel gummy under foundation.  The Tizo Non-tinted facial mineral Sunscreen Primer is a godsend!!!!!!!! It is probably one of the best facial sunscreens I have owned, including those I paid megabucks for at the dermatologist.
First it is free of chemical sunscreen filters, dyes, fragrances, oils and preservatives so my skin doesn't freak out.  It feels soft and absorbs quickly and dries matte so you can apply a tinted moisturizer or foundation over it. The only thing I wish were different about this is that it is only 40SPF. I prefer 70 SPF and higher for my face but I'll just have to be more careful about hats and parasols
This is the best sunscreen I have ever used.  I have literally no pigment and it keeps me from burning...does not sting eyes.  Perfect - expensive but well worth the money.
summary: This is the best sunscreen I have ever used

reviewText: Okay, this is very good sunscreen, it blends in nicely and easily. It doesn't feel greasy either. However, these are very expensive. We will continue using this and the tinted version we received from Tizo, but these are a bit to pricy for our daily sunscreen use. For now we use it when we know we will be out in the sun for longer periods of time but use our daily SPF moisturizer for daily use.

Every other day I go to an outdoor pool for water aerobics in the direct sun. I've had trouble finding a sunscreen that lasts for the entire 75 minute class. I think I've finally found one! The last one I tried lasted but it didn't offer the level of protection you need in the California Central Valley summer sun. Since using this (and during the longest heatwave on record) I have not been sunburned once. It comes off when I shower after class but not before. I can't recommend this highly enough. Imagine. A product that does what it claims to do. Will wonders ever cease?

While this sunscreen is effective, I cannot find a single attribute that differentiates it from any other sunscreen that is similarly or lower-priced. Its two active ingredients are Titanium Dioxide and Zinc Oxide, both of which can be found in almost all sunscreens. Like all sunscreens containing zinc oxide, the lotion is thick and white and hard to spread and has to be worked in so that white streaks won't show.

I was attracted to the terms "age defying fusion" (which sounds sort of scientific and implies that this lotion will protect better than any other of similar SPF) and "facial mineral sunscreen, non-tinted" (which I failed to interpret as ordinary white zinc.)

Bottom line: this sunscreen is no better and no worse than any other zinc-based sunscreen with a SPF of 40. It suffers from the same inconveniences and benefits from the same protection for the same length of time. It neither moisturizes nor offers any special ingredients that will extend your youthfulness or reverse the effects of the damages of aging. It is, simply put, a typical sunscreen.
summary: Nothing makes it different from any other zinc-based sunscreen.

reviewText: I really am impressed by this mineral sunscreen. It is unscented, a trait I really appreciate. It is a white cream that has a white cast for just a few seconds, but it disappears as soon as rub it into your skin. This also doesn't irritate my sensitive skin. It goes on smooth and wears well without makeup or under makeup. I can see myself buying it over and over.

I reallly like this sunscreen and this TIZO brand is one of my favorites. The only negative would be that it's a bit on the expensive side and there's not a lot in this container so be aware of that.

What makes this sunscreen so great is that it has such a great feel to it. It just glides on your face and makes it feel so silky and soft without feeling sticky.  My skin feels not only protected from the sun, but it feels moisterized as well. It's simply the best I've used.

If you're looking for a little color to go along with your sunscreen, I highly recommend the TIZO 3 Tinted Facial Mineral Sunscreen. That's my favorite but I use this one too.

Highly recommended, with the reservations expressed above.

TIZO 2 Non-Tinted Facial Mineral Sunscreen SPF 40 is a very good mineral sun screen and long lasting at the beach even if you go swimming several times. It stays smooth on the skin without oiliness or stickiness.

I recommend it!

I wear mineral sunscreen on my face daily. I've worn everything from professionally compounded mineral sunscreens to over-the-counter product.  Unfortunately, this TIZO 2 Non-Tinted Mineral Sunscreen caused problems for me than it solved.

PRO
1) It's a mineral-based sunscreen.

CONS
1) Once on my skin, the lotion felt oily and dry.  It stayed that way until removed with soap and water.(I have sensitive, *dry* skin, and it made my face feel oily to the touch.)
2) It feels cakey and oily when worn with face powder or makeup.
3) If you have oily skin or sensitive skin, it may not be the choice for you.
4) It seemed to take a lot of product to achieve full coverage of my face and neck.

Having worn mineral sunscreens ALL of my adult life, I just cannot recommend the formula of this product.
summary: Mineral Sunscreen Works But Has Some Issues

reviewText: Waterproof sunscreen that is good for your skin and you can wear everyday...it doesn't get any better than that!  I would not rely on TIZO 2 to protect me for a long day at the pool or beach but it is perfect for everyday wear which might include an outdoor family reunion or watching the kids on the soccer field.  It is only waterproof for a few hours so keep that in mind if your reunion includes a water balloon toss :-).  A little heavy going on but absorbs quickly and fully.  Looking forward to trying the tinted version.
summary: Looking forward to trying the tinted version!

reviewText: I had never heard of the TIZO brand before ordering a few of their products through the Vine program, but I really like all the ones I've tried -- including this one. According to the TIZO website, "TiZO 2 is a facial mineral sunscreen for lighter skin tones and those with very fair skin (Fitzpatrick I and II)." I have fair skin (I wear MAC foundation in NW20), and this doesn't leave a chalky or whitish cast to my skin. It also leaves a matte finish, and doesn't interfere with my makeup. It feels silky going on, and I can apply my foundation about five minutes after using it. For the last three years, I've been using EltaMD UV Clear Broad-Spectrum SPF 46, 1.7 oz as my daily facial sunscreen, and I like this TIZO one just as much
summary: Designed for fair skin -- and goes on without leaving a chalky cast

reviewText:
TIzO 2  SPF 40 facial mineral sunscreen non- tinted  when applied as thin as possible still made my face turn white due to the zinc oxide and titanium dioxide  which are the active ingredients for the sunscreen.  It does give a matte finish as marketed, it is not shiny. But it is more greasy on the surface of my skin than my usual. I am accustomed to using Elta MD SPF 46 **clear** whose active ingredient is zinc oxide in a **clear** formulation.

Because I live in Houston Texas with strong sun  and because we have so many bright sunny days all year round I need to wear a high SPF every day. I use the Elta MD clear SPF 46 as my daily moisturizer. I am always on the lookout for something that might be better but I am not going to be able to use this because it turns my face white and vecause it is heavier.

 I would recommend this only for when you are going to the beach or going to exercise outdoors if you think that SPF 40 is all that you will need.

I do not wear foundation makeup or powder so I did not test this product with putting multiple layers of other makeup products on top of this sunscreen.

Rating 3 stars = it's okay as a sunscreen for use when outdoors if you don't care that your face has a bright whitish cast.
summary: Not a Daily Wear Morning Skin Moisturizer

reviewText:
Being pale and protective of my skin, I do my best to look after it - I try to have some sort of sunscreen on, either in my make-up or beneath it. I've tried a lot of sunscreens for my face since they go well with make-up and prevent break-outs, sprays and creams, higher and lower end brands.
I LOVE TIZO.
I've never heard of it and tried the non-tinted mineral sunscreen, and love how it goes on so smooth (there's a powdery feel to it), there's no scent, there's no white 'gleam' or after-effect to it, no greasiness at all. It's almost like a primer, in fact. There's no reaction for my skin, it's great as is if I don't wear make-up and it doesn't affect my make-up on the days I wear it over the sunscreen.
It's not cheap, but a little goes a long way. I wish I'd heard of this before I'd bought another brand for the summer. I know what I'll be using from now on.
summary: I've found my sunscreen from now on....

reviewText: In these photos Obagi Nu-Derm zinc sunscreen lotion (z-cote formula) is on the left, and Tizo2 is on the right.  The difference is that Obagi has a more oily appearance, while Tizo2 is a matte finish.  The Obagi sunscreen tends to catch into and highlight skin lines, while Tizo2 disappears easier with some rubbing.  I just wish this were not so expensive, since it is a rather tiny bottle.  In that respect the Obagi product is a better value.  This one is nicer cosmetically.

I have had an ongoing battle with skin cancer for several years. It is rather stressful and unpleasant but it does make you remember the importance of sunscreen. From my understanding, a mineral sunscreen provides an actual block against the sun as opposed to chemical sunscreen. So I mostly wear zinc heavy sunscreens. Mineral sunscreens are notoriously annoying to use. They are thick. They are hard to rub in. They leave a white cast. They feel gross and heavy.
