While it was rather strange getting accustomed to a shampoo without lather, this shampoo gets my hair really clean without stripping. And it smells amazing.

I have long, layered hair, medium textured, and when I wash with just this shampoo and no conditioner, my hair actually feels and looks thicker. Honestly--my loose hair has more volume, and my ponytail actually feels thicker. But my hair feels utterly clean and uncoated, so it's mysterious to me.

On the downside, it is incredibly expensive. As someone with relatively low maintenance hair, I don't know if I can rationalize the price tag forever.

On the other hand, I wash my hair once a week, max, and my hair seems to stay clean looking and feeling longer with this cleanser than my regular drugstore products, so the economy of it might work out over time. Before this product, my hair would look pretty greasy leading up to shampoo day, and over the last several weeks, it's actually looked pretty dang good with longer spans between, even with running. If I were rich, no question, this would be my very favorite shampoo.

If I were using a lot of product and washing my hair daily, I couldn't rationalize the expense. Much of the value of this product for me is that I can extend the time between washings.

I do prefer at least a bit of leave-in conditioner because my hair is frizz-prone in humidity, but I could almost get away without it.
summary: Makes my hair look and feel thicker, look clean longer. (But so spendy.)

reviewText:
My hair is thick and in pretty good shape, but has a tendency to be a little dry.  I use this once a week and then use my regular shampoo and conditioner the other days.

It takes getting used to and I used too much the first couple of times trying to get a lather which of course, I didn't get.  The fragrance does not bother my allergies at all.

I like it and I like the way my hair smells and feels after using it.  I rarely blow my hair dry and if I don't use electric rollers or a curling iron to smooth out the dry ends, my ponytail looks like a broomstick.  When I use the ORIBE I do not have that problem so that's a major plus for me.
summary: Works well on senior color treated hair

reviewText:
I have thin, gray but color threated blond shoulder length wavy hair. Not good waves, just random ripples requiring the punishment of styling tools.
I was super skeptical of the price-but you definitely get what you pay for. I use shampoo and conditioner daily. Generally mid priced ($14.99), depending on what my pharmacy has on sale.
This creme is shampoo/conditioner in one and it's legit! One wash and my hair feels and smells amazing! The scent is nice and lasts all day, my kids snuggled a little longer because my hair smelled "so good!".
The only draw back is I can't use it daily. I have to wash daily due to oily hair and more than once a week and my hair seems weighed down and difficult to style. So I add it to my Sunday night routine.

This smells AMAZING! But I confess, I don't think it's worth the luxury brand price. My daughter and I both have very fine, long hair that needs moisture in the length. This worked great for her but I can't imagine using this more than once a week as it definitely leaves oils in the hair. With us fine types that can be too weighty and for her it just made her hair look and smell dirty faster.
summary: Great smell but just not for us.

reviewText: The creme feels unusual from cleaning hair since it does not foam. It takes quite large amount of it to work through the hair, probably because of that. It does make hair very soft and smooth and sleek, but also very limp. My hair is oily, and it seems like the product does not wash off all the oils from my hair. I started using it for second wash after washing my hair with my other shampoo first, it did make a difference, but not enough of a difference for me to justify buying another bottle after this one runs out.
summary: and it seems like the product does not wash off all the oils ...

reviewText:
This was my first time using a cleansing cream, so I was not sure what to expect. I do like it, but not on days where there is a lot of product in my hair needing to be washed out. In those instances I use a clarifying shampoo or regular shampoo first because this doesn't remove more than a little hairspray or mousse.

It is thick and not runny at all, like a heavy conditioner. It doesn't lather. It does rinse well and doesnt seem to buildup on my hair. It doesn't add any body or fullness, but it also doesn't weigh my hair down too much. It does seems to make my waves want to disappear though, so it is better for days when I want to wear my hair straight or if I'm just showering before bed and letting it air dry with no intentions of styling til morning. My hair does look healthy and shiny and feels a little softer.

The scent is nice. It is an herbal mint scent that doesn't seem to last on my hair much after its dry.

It gives that really light feel to hair, like when you just got a hair cut at the salon.

Overall I do like it, but wish it didn't take the life out of my curls/waves. Perhaps a different version if it would be better for that issue.

Light floral scent. Smells beautiful on the hair. The texture of it reminds me of the Wen product: once applied to washed hair, it feels like a rain coat is put on. As soon as water hits it, it almost feels like oil on my hair. However, after drying, my hair does not feel as soft and moisturized as with my Fekkai conditioner. It just doesn't have the same kind of effect...

I really love this product! I have medium fine processed hair that is naturally curly (waves not tight curls) and prone to frizz. We have a high mineral content in our water here, so I generally do one clarifying shampoo a week with a deep conditioning. I alternated adding this product into my routine. First I shampooed and then used this product as a final treatment. Next I shampooed, used this product and then used the conditioner as a final treatment. This product works miracle on my hair both weeks. My hair was softer, shinier and less frizzy. I think the week when I added the conditioner probably was the best my hair felt and looked. Normally I have to apply morrocan oil to my hair daily and sometimes twice a day, using this product pretty much took care of the need for that.

I also love the smell of this creme, it smells minty clean. It also smooths on nicely and you don't have to use too much, which at this price point is a good thing!

All in all I highly recommend this cleansing creme!

Oribe cleansing creme completely won me over.  This is the 3rd non foaming hair cleansing cream I have purchased.  All of them from salons and all of them very high quality.  This is the only one that really felt like it cleaned my hair and left it super soft.  I have shoulder length, very thick, course and frizzy hair.  It is also colored treated which lends itself to even more damage.  I have used this product 3 times already and love it more each time. I love it so much that I have banished my husband and son from using it.  The first two times I think I may have used too much because it is hard to tell how much you need to cover your hair.  I now use about the size of 2 quarters, which works well for my length and type of hair.  The first thing I noticed was how silky soft my hair felt when I rinsed it off.  This never happens and I usually have to glob on conditioner to get even close to that feeling.  I decided to use conditioner with the cleansing cream as my hair is damaged, but if you have thin hair or non processed hair you may be able to skip the conditioner. It has a pleasant fragrance but I do miss the Oribe signature 'hair care' product smell.  This Cleansing cream isn't cheap but now that I have used it, I just cant see going back to my salon shampoo anymore.  When your hair looks great, you feel great.
summary: Worth every penny for soft and silky hair.

reviewText:
Premium product at a premium price. I doubt I would purchase this for myself normally as I don't really have the budget for this luxurious of a hair cleanser. I do want to thank ORIBE and Amazon for the opportunity to review a sample. With the price aside I would like to say that I do love the product. It is absolutely a top shelf product.

The fruit and flower extracts, unique botanicals and other natural ingredients are a wonderful blend that amazes me how well it cleans and leaves your hair feeling. It is a great formula and I do enjoy using it. It tames my somewhat course hair and leaves it feeling soft and manageable without over doing it. I love the fragrance too. It says it is ideal for all hair types and I believe that. It works so well.

This is the most expensive hair cleanser (can you call it a shampoo, it is more a cream with no lather) that I have every used. I can see the reason for it. It is great. 5 stars.

Yes, this is an amazing hair cleaning and conditioning product that is elegantly packaged with simplicity, has a delicious aroma and is by far the most interesting formula I've used on my hair.  There is no sudsing, get that -- no lather, just massage the white cream into your scalp and locks, let it rest, then rinse.  The hair responds as it dries, the scalp feels wonderful from the mint, and you don't think about the cost. This is expensive, but like an old commercial for another line pronounced, "I'm worth it."
summary: Hair product is delicious on the hair and scalp

reviewText:
I have colored thick hair that is below shoulder length.  I used about 2 heaping tablespoons of this and washed my hair from the ends up.  This does not lather but it smells great.  As I rinsed my hair I noticed I did have my large comb in the shower.  I was able to run my fingers through my hair including the parts that get most tangled with minimal effort.  I have never been able to do that in my entire life.  (When I was little, my mom used to cut my hair because it would get so tangled).  I normally go a week between washings and I can tell I'll be able to go that long with this.  After one use, my hair feels healthier and more manageable.  It's easier to use the Wet Brush on it during the day and it has remained tangle free.

I deducted one star because of the price as at this point in my life, I would not consider spending $44 for shampoo.  If cost is not a factor for you, I definitely recommend this product if your hair is colored or long or thick.

Graying "old person" hair, susceptible to dryness and frizzing.  I usually condition liberally to get something resembling silky hair.  So how did this Oribe work out?  Super!!

Comes in an attractive mint green bottle with a pop-up applicator top.  It's plastic, but looks very nice.  The creme is a white viscous consistency, pleasant citrus scent with a hint of mint.  The scent lingers after drying and I love it - which is a surprising plus as I don't usually care for citrus type scent in a hair product.  Follow the instructions to apply (work in for a couple of minutes, follow with a conditioner).  The lack of lather was strange but the end result was great.  Clean, moisturized, no frizz, silky.  Love it!  Made in USA.  Pricey but a high end product that works.
summary: A really different experience -- I like it!

reviewText: I'm not usually a fan of expensive  bath items but this is one product that won me over.  We don't typically use sulfate free shampoos or conditioners in our household, so I thought this was worth a try.  It doesn't bubble and lather like traditional sulfate shampoo, so that took a little getting accustomed to.  The results were nothing short of fabulous.  After washing a few times with this in place of our regular foaming shampoo, hair was clean, soft, fresh smelling and best of all, highly manageable.  I was able to easily style my hair into a nice neat conservative style without using hair cream. My hair would be frizz city if I tried that with a run of the mill shampoo.  We also like that this product is cruelty-free and there are no harsh chemicals.  The fragrance is pretty pleasant as well.  It's an herbal/minty combo that smells very fresh and clean without being overbearing.  This works very well with our naturally styled hair and completely eliminates dry hair frizzies.  Like most shampoos/cleansers, the directions instruct to apply, rinse, repeat. You're supposed to leave it in for a minute or two during each application. I actually found it works very well when I apply it at the beginning of my shower, work it into my hair down to the scalp really well and just leave it in until I'm done showering. I rinse it out right before exiting the shower. That has done wonders with my hair and helps the product last longer as well.
summary: Soft, manageable easy to style hair

reviewText:
Update 5/29-
I color my hair. Sometimes my head feels hot when I do.
I wear my hair in a ponytail a lot, in the sun. Again, hot head & tight.
My scalp is tortured.
I've started pressing this into my scalp bc of the mint & my head is instantly refreshed.
Maybe it's in my head, (haha, get it?) but I feel this gets the blood going again & it smells so good.

Update 4/12-
For test purposes, I used the exact same products on my hair sans the Oribe.
I used my leave in conditioning spray, after my hair was towel dried, in place of the Oribe.

My hair was ok but not nearly as soft.
I must use a deep conditioner because of years of hair abuse but it weighs down my hair by day 3 if I don't wash.

The Oribe gave me deep conditioner quality softness with leave in conditioner weightlessness.
It's magically found a way to keep moisture & bounce and, it smells great.

Also, the bottle is really growing on me.
I feel pretty just using the jade green bottle.

Original review-
I know usually packaging is irrelevant but this arrives in a cardstock quality box.
He made me laugh when he saw the bottle & said it looked like cut jade.
It really is pretty, even for plastic.

Seems like it would be a great gift for the beauty fan in your life.
 It is packaged & priced as a luxury item & would make a beautiful impression ti make someone feel special.

So, does it work?

I followed the instructions & used it after shampoo but before my regular conditioner.
I use a paraben free thickening shampoo which leaves my hair very squeaky & easily knotty if I don't follow with good conditioner.

I usually use a leave in (Redken All Soft)
after I towel dry, to smooth out frizz.
 I skipped my leave in to see what this would do.

This was wonderful to immediately detangle after shampoo.
There is a light mint smell which felt clean & comforting.

My hair air dryed with smooth bouncy curls.
Soft & light.
The next day I spiraled my curls with a flat iron for definition, still run your fingers through soft & no frizz.

A week later, with working 14 hour days
 & a quick dry shampoo for days 4,5 & 6,
 my hair is still soft, not weighed down & has bounce with some "fluffing" at the roots.

So, yes, it works & for the amount needed,
I understand the value in the price.
This bottle should last quite a bit.

A preface: I have blonde, shoulder length, highlighted, fine hair that tangles VERY easily.

I was anxious to jump on board the cleansing conditioner / sulfate free / later free bandwagon after recommendations from my hair stylist, and also from my sister, who is always on top of all new and coming hair trends. It's hard for me to find a good product that doesn't weigh down my hair or leave it too greasy because it is so limp and fine.

So lets hop to it. Here is a list of what the product claims it does, with my feedback on the actual results.

Claim: Non-foaming formula gently removes dirt, oil, and. buildup without the use of surfactants or sulfates.
Result: I typically wash my hair every 3rd or 4th day, so there is DEFINITELY dirt, oil, and buildup from hair products in my hair. I use the ORIBE product by running it through my hair from roots to ends, and then spending a little bit more time massaging it into my scalp to make sure all of the grime is washed away. The product doesn't lather, which takes some time getting used to, because it didn't initially FEEL like it was really cleaning my hair because of how used to regular shampoo products I was. Anyway, I've been very pleasantly surprised at how clean and fresh this leaves my hair, with a really pleasing light scent. As for surfactants or sulfates, neither are listed in the ingredients. A+ for this category.

Claim: Leaves scalp balanced and soothed.
Result: I wouldn't say my scalp feels any different than from any other product I've used, with the exception of Nioxin. I used to use a Nioxin product that actually DOES leave behind a tingling soothing sensation after washing. Only a neutral C rating in this category.

Claim: Detangles, moisturizes, and smoothes without silicones.
Result: My hair is always SO KNOTTED after washing and conditioning, and even with the help of a Wet Brush and "It's a 10 Miracle Leave In plus Keratin" conditioning spray, I'm still pulling through tangles. Fast forward to using ORIBE. This is the ONLY product I used. NO conditioner, NO "It's a 10". And my hair brushed through with only the help of my Wet Brush. No silicones are listed in the ingredients. So all the praise hands, and an A+ rating in this category.

Claim: Strengthens and protects from damage.
Result: I must admit, I am guilty of all of the cardinal hair sins. Coloring, blow drying, heat styling, and tearing through tangles and knots. Also, I mostly wear my hair in a ponytail, which can be damaging to the hair shaft. Needless to say, my hair has not been in the best shape over the years. I have a lot of breakage. I am also 12 months post partum, and went through the lovely months of post partum hair loss. I lost A LOT of hair, which is now re-growing and giving me a ton of fly-aways. I can absolutely report that I am not noticing as much hair left behind in my hair brush, and my hair health really appears to have improved. I often stop to notice that my hair really does look shiny and healthy, and damage seems to have been smoothed over. I sometimes use a curling wand to add loose curls to my hair, and on days after I style my hair, I can often see frizzy hair left behind from the heat. Surprisingly, this has NOT been so while using the ORIBE product. Downside to this: my hair is a bit more limp than with the use of other products. B+ in this category.

Claim: Tames and controls frizz.
Result: Truth. This product absolutely tames and controls frizz. Is it at the detriment to volume? Yes. Atleast a little bit. I was able to run my fingers through my hair, but it did turn a little bit greasy the following day. It was also a little flatter in the days following my cleanse than I would typically prefer. C+ in this category.

Claim: Protects color from fading.
Result: I have not noticed any discernible difference in the brightness of my highlights from the use of this product. Has it been detrimental? No. But it has definitely not been any kind of miracle worker and has not decreased my need for cut/color appointments. C rating.

Overall, I'm a definite proponent of this product, but would recommend only using once a week at the price point for which it is listed. $44 is a LOT for a cleansing/shampooing product, atleast for me, and I don't think the benefits are so significant that this is a "must-use every time" product to achieve results. By using this once a week, and Clairol Shimmer Lights shampoo/conditioner once a week, I'm really happy with how my hair looks and feels.
summary: The Results Are In: Product Claims vs. My Experience Broken Down by Category

reviewText:
I have been using cleansing creams instead of shampoos for about a year now. This is a nice addition. It smells slightly citrus' slightly mint, barely floral. It did a nice job with my hair which ;ooks and feels great after using. It suggests you can use a little conditioner after and that is where ORIBE cleansing Creme for Moisture loses the star. I usually use New Wash (used to be Purely Perfect) and I like feeling that I don't need conditioner after, without being at all weighed down. I assume it is the difference of cleansing oils used.

But if you want a change, and you are not a fan of Wen, which I am not, this is a very credible addition to the NO POO line of hair products. Smells better than all of them.
summary: Nice addition to the NO POO line of hair products.

reviewText:
My wife used this as directed and is seeing probably 50% hair growth reduction after 4 applications using the medium level (there are 3 intensity levels).

Personally I'm indifferent but I know people don't like shaving because I don't enjoy shaving. For those wanting permanent reduction of hair growth, this is an effective tool. I believe the price is fair because one can spend a little less and get a lot less in such a product.

Here's why this is a good solution:
* It's faster than older and cheaper models, meaning the pulses are coming quickly - especially if glided over the legs and it senses stubble (use after shaving).
* Uses both light and radio waves, and bears the FDA certificate that it's clinically proven to work.
* The options to use three levels allow for testing before building to a higher intensity level.
* The actual area that's getting treated is larger than those of smaller and cheaper units. The metal bars on each end of the part that touches the skin being treated, when in contact with the skin produce pulses. The pulses on this unit cover more area than other units I've seen, hence less time and effort needed.

As I said, the results are plain to see after only 4 sessions and the effort was minimal. Also, there was no pain or irritation - per my wife.

In the past, I tried Veet Infini'Silk Light-Based IPL Hair Removal System For Home Use without success, so I didn't have much hope that the iluminage would work. I was wrong. Even from the first use, it took longer than normal for the hair to return. Each use (a week apart for 7 treatments) caused the hair to take longer to come back, until it didn't come back at all. Iluminage requires you to shave prior to the treatment, then use the system on the shaved areas. There are parts of my body (specifically, the inner, upper thighs) that always has stubble, even immediately after shaving. Using the iluminage on those areas "burns" the stubble, making the area smooth and hair free, which surprised me (since it supposedly needs complete hair removal for the system to work. This system works better on some areas than on others. While it did help reduce the facial hair, it didn't eliminate it completely from my chin. I'll keep using it on that area, then report back if repeated treatments help.

The iluminage Precise Touch hair remover is smaller than the iluminage touch that was previously introduced, but I am uncertain as to the differences since I have not seen the first model.  This one is small enough that it can be taken along for travel if necessary, say if you will be away from home for more than a week. I say this because it is suggested to use the hair removal tool once a week for seven weeks to achieve the best results for permanent hair loss.  Since it is not battery operated, all you need is an electric outlet and about twenty minutes if you want to use this on both legs.  Of course smaller body areas would take less time, but that gives an example of the time involved.  This is used after shaving and I have used it immediately after shaving to get at the root of the matter, that is the hair.  There was no real sensation and no smell of burning hair.  Wearing the provided small goggles adds a level of security, particularly if one is sensitive to strobe lights because this functions by small bursts of bright light which should not be looked at.  There are a lot of warnings for this product, like not using it over areas with tattoos, something that could be an issue.  I would recommend visiting the manufacturers website to view their video about using the product and hope that you do not find the seven times weekly to be as offputting as I did.  My first interpretation was to use it seven times for a week, but knew instinctively that would be too often.  I have not used this on the high setting but likely will progress to that temperature in time.  This is an interesting grooming tool that could benefit many and at the cost of around three hundred dollars right now, it could actually save money for those who have hair removed professionally.

In my family the women tend to be "blessed" with way too much unwanted hair.  I have never shaved, rather, Ihave always gone after the roots of the hairs to thin out regrowth.  I have also tried NoNo but found it to be useless for me in that this device truly DID burn off the hairbut did not reach below the skin surface which made for stubbles the next day.  So, back to the epilators.
This device intrigued me.  It promises permanent hair reduction (note that it does not promise that no hair will grow back).  The booklet is detailed and spells out the Do's and DON'Ts as well who should not use this device.  (If you have a pacemaker or other item implanted, do NOT use this device.
The other reviewer reported burned hair.  Maybe she missed the part where it says that hair must be removed first before using this device.  iluminage goes after the hair follicle, not the hair itself.
Protocol is once a week for 7 weeks, then touch-ups as needed.
It is way too early to review the EFFECTIVENESS of this device.  I will update this review i about 2-3 months since that will give me enough time to fully evaluate this device's effectiveness.

This is a hair removal device that burns away unwanted hair. It uses a combination of light pulses and radio waves to burn the hair without damaging the skin. That sounds like a pretty good idea, doesn't it? I tested the appliance, and it seems to work as advertised.

This test was done on a younger person. She has lots of healthy, thick hair. She complains of hair on her hands and knuckles, although to me it looked barely noticeable.

After a few false starts, we read the manual thoroughly and tried again, and the product worked as advertised. But, it seems, over time,  we became less enamored of the appliance. Shaving, waxing and epillating are all very effective hair removal strategies. This device adds another step on top of those procedures, that will make the results more permanent, so you can do less shaving, waxing and epillating in the future. So it's an investment you can make now to make your future grooming efforts less taxing.

Please be sure to read the instructions carefully. Do not look directly at the bright light. And one more warning -- my lovely teenager had written on her hand with a sharpie pen. When she used the device on the inked skin, it sent out big sparks. I suggest you do NOT use this device on skin with ink.

Weeks later, my teen has forgotten about this device. I asked her why she gave up on it, and she said the process was too slow, and she did not want to spend time every day working on hair removal. I would say that is her personal choice and some other people would have more patience and get better result.
summary: An interesting solution for unwanted hair

reviewText:
I have been using this for a few weeks now and it seems to be working.  It does a great job.  It has 3 settings - 3 being the highest and is a bit warm on the highest setting.  If you can stand the higher setting, it will do a better job of removing the hair.  It slowly does get rid of the hair and it doesn't seem to come back.  But, it does take a few weeks (6) to get most areas totally gone.  This is easy to use and flashes when it is actually working.  It comes with goggles (like you would use in a tanning bed) to protect your eyes from the very bright flashes.  You just keep moving it within an area and try to hit the same area 2 or 3 times.  This is a great product and so much cheaper than going to the hair removal salons and paying the salon prices.

This item works while being plugged in to an outlet, so no battery to charge or run down.  Works Great!  Marilyn

Iluminage Precise Touch Permanent Hair Remover seems to work, at least by thinning unwanted hair.  The device is easy to use.  First you shave the area you want the hair growth to slow from.  It should be noted that this product is not intended for facial hair removal on men.  It can be used on a male or female body, and certain areas of a woman's face, but not on a man's face.  So I am assuming it won't work on course hair.  The instructions do not say that, but I am putting two and two together here.

You use  the device  once a week for 6 weeks, which ends up being 7 treatments.  So again, shave the area you want hair growth to slow on.  Choose your setting preference  on the device.  Making sure the two silver RF bars  touch your skin, move slowly across the area of skin you are targeting. so the lights flash over the area you trying to rid of unwanted hair.  Just keep the device moving, do not stop.  You can glide over the area 2 or 3 times per treatment, but apparently no more.  Female facial treatments are a bit different, as the area you are trying to rid of hair is smaller.  So you are to use a stamping motion with the light, again 2 or 3 times for a treatment.

The device doesn't promise  100% hair removal, but 94% over the course of 6 weeks.  My husband is noticing a less hair growth on his back (yes,  his back), which is a good thing.  A very good thing.  Beach goers around the world will thank you next summer.

So from what I understand from research on this item, it is made to have 150,000 pulses, and then won't work anymore.  That's a lot of pulses.  Probably more than we will use in our lifetime.  The only reason I mention this is that it may not be good for someone trying to use it in a business, using it on lots of people.  But 150,000 is a lot of pulses. For the money, it's worth buying a new one if you burn this one out. FYI and food for thought.

We'll give this to my hairy daughter when she comes home from college for the holidays.  She's obsessed with hair on her arms, and already shaves them.  I'll make a follow up post to update readers on how this works for her.
summary: 7 Treatments in 6 Weeks & You'll Have Less Hair Growth

reviewText:
I have used this twice on my girlfriends armpits, one a week as noted in the directions. She has dark hair and fair skin. You can definitely tell something is happening when you get it going. A bright light emits in a flash. This kit comes with glasses to protect your eyes because it is very bright. There should also be a slight smell of burning hair that follows the flash. She said she felt a faint pinch-like sensation, but tolerable and she did not wince at it. After a few weeks to see how the results came, she said it some hair grew back, but thinner. So there were definitely results. According to the instruction booklet, a good shaving is necessary to do before you use this. And for those with red hair and pale skin, a waxing is recommended. So, although the package says it can do any hair and skin, each person much do the appropriate preparations before just going straight to this step.

In the time we were allowed to review this product, I can't say with 100% certainty that I can give a completely fair review as this is a time. But so far my girlfriend is pleased with the results so far and will continue using it.
summary: In the limited time I used this, there are slight results that will improve over time.

reviewText: I'm not much for skin care sets. I like to buy my products separately, since I always use one up one product before another, but this is a very nice product, and would make a nice gift for someone. The foaming wash is very refreshing, the cream has a nice light scent, and the peel left my face feeling fresh and clean. Not a product I would buy, but a very nice product.
summary: Left my skin feeling fresh and clean

reviewText: Bliss is the bomb. Truly, the foaming face wash is a staple in my bathroom. The energizing cream is also refreshing and fabulous. This set gave me my first opportunity to try the inquired-peel, and I really liked that as well. This is also a great value for the money. Awesome set.

I've always been very pleased with Bliss products, and this A-Bright Face kit is no exception.  Bliss products smell and feel great on my skin and have a really fresh feel.  First of all, the face wash is an excellent product for many skin types.  It rinses cleanly, is lightweight, and leaves a fresh scent.  Unlike some cleansers, there is no residue left after rinsing, and it could be used both morning and night.  The Triple Oxygen Day Cream is a great product, as well.  Lightweight and fresh, it goes on nicely under makeup. I wish that a night cream would have been included instead, but the Triple Oxygen Day Cream is still an excellent product and is a nice addition to my morning skin regimen.  Both the cleanser and the day cream are full size, so this is a good value.  However, I didn't have as much luck with the That's Incredi-peel.  I felt that it was too harsh for my skin, and I don't even have overly sensitive skin.  My face felt a little irritated, but this was quickly remedied by my night cream.  Also, there were 5 peels.  I used them every other night instead of the recommended daily application, and I think this was just as effective.  I feel like I could evaluate the peels more effectively if they had been paired with a night cream.  All in all, I'm pleased with the results and pleased with how my skin looks and feels.  If you have never tried Bliss products before, this is a good set to get you started.

Bliss A-Bright Face makes a very nice 3 Step at home facial set. The set comes with:
Fabulous Foaming Face Wash- you begin this first step by washing your face with this slightly foaming cleanser. I found this actually works better after washing with my favorite soap first. After removing all my makeup, this cleanser goes on a damp face and works best on an already clean skin, as it is a very mild cleanser.

That's Incredi-'Peel'!- After your skin is clean, you gently wipe this pad on your dry skin. You do not rinse this off, but simply cover with your night time moisturizer. Whatever moisturizer you normally wear to bed at night, you simply put on over this peel.

Triple Oxygen Energizing Vitamin C Day Cream- In the morning, you massage this day cream into your face and neck before you put on your make-up.

For a person with no skin issues, this is a great spa type skin care routine. If you have sun issues- sun sensitivity, have had sun damage or skin cancer, these products- specifically the Peel- most likely will increase your sun sensitivity causing burning or sunburns. The Face Wash and Day Cream don't have the sun sensitivity the Peel has.

My sister and I always test new skin products together, as I have pale- sun sensitive skin that freckles, and my sister has a light olive skin that the sun loves. My sister loves all three products, but I cannot use the Peel, as it gave me a slight burning sensation. There are also warnings not to use the Peel, if you use Accutane or Retinoids, or have Rosacea, Eczema or have open cuts on your skin. The Face Wash and Day Cream were great for both regular and sensitive skin, but if you have sun sensitivity, the Peel will make your skin burn due to it's sodium, oxygen and citrus acid ingredients. Since only 2 of the products work for all skin types, I'm giving it 3 1/2 STARS.
summary: Incredi-'Peel' Not Great For Sun Sensitive Skin

reviewText:
I was really excited to try the Incredi-peel, and I do really like what it seems to be doing for my skin, but 5 pads applications isn't even a full week's worth of product when you're supposed to use them once a day. The pads are very large, it seems like they could make them about half size and it would still easily work for my face, neck, and upper chest.

I love the scent of the moisturizer, and it feels very nice going on, but it left my cheekbone area feeling dry after a few hours. I live in the desert so I'm thinking this might be a perfect moisturizer for those who live in more humid conditions. The size of the container is much larger than the contents, which seems a little disingenuous and tacky.

The cleanser feels nice and smells so nice, but it failed at removing my mascara and eyeliner, which are not waterproof (Neutrogena Healthy Lengths). It left my skin feeling nice afterwards, but I don't really feel like it's effective.

Overall I think these are nice products made from high quality ingredients, but the results fail to live up to the cost.
summary: Wonderful smell, but not effective enough on my skin to justify the cost.

reviewText:
I think that bliss A-Bright Face is an affordable, useful and appreciative facial-at-home kit. The bliss line of beauty products are associated with blissspa, a well-known international chain of beauty and wellness spas. I believe this excellent product makes a great gift for the lady in your life.

The gift pack includes three items that are intended to be used in sequence. fabulous foaming face wash (6.7 fluid ounce) is used to clean the face and neck. that's incredi-peel! (5 pads) is intended to be used over night to gently remove the outer layer of skin. triple oxygen energizing vitamin C day cream (1.7 fluid ounce) is applied in the morning to nourish the face throughout the day.

I highly recommend bliss A-Bright Face facial-at-home kit to everyone.
summary: As affordable, useful and appreciative gift idea

reviewText: I usually don't do beauty sets. The last time I had one was over 20 years ago when I was back in high school. Usually, I just mix and match products from various lines because even though I have very oily skin, most sets have at least one product that is too harsh and drying for my skin. Therefore, I didn't have high expectations when I ordered this bliss set. However, I was pleasantly surprised. This is great. The star product here is the peel. Unlike similar ones I have tried, this didn't sting my face or irritate it. I saw a difference in my skin after the first use. The cleanser is gentle and removes all make-up and while I usually don't use any creams on my face except for sunscreen, sometimes the cooler weather does dry out my skin. This one is lightweight enough for my very oily skin without turning me into an oil slick. Over all, very well done! Would make a a great gift.
summary: Great beauty set for people who like steps

reviewText:
I was pretty underwhelmed by this set, although I wish I could rate the products individually. I've used cleansers, peels, and moisturizers from everyone from Cetaphil, Basis, and L'Oreal to La Mer, SK-II, and Algenist, so I'm going to compare these products against the best (and worst) of that bunch.

Cleanser: Disappointing. Not only does it not really foam, it also doesn't remove makeup very well. I could tell I still had residue on my face, but tested this with a cotton pad soaked in (Algenist) toner. Sure enough, it came away with makeup on it. It also doesn't foam enough to work well with my Clarisonic. Maybe I've been spoiled by Algenist's cleanser, but this cleanser is only good for a light morning cleanse. It's sure not going to get Benefit They're Real mascara off without a lot of serious rubbing (if at all).

Moisturizer: Fair. It has a light, orangesicle scent and color, and leaves a slight tingle on the skin. The container is MUCH bigger than it needs to be for the amount of product, so don't expect as much as the picture shows. The moisturizer absorbs quickly (especially if you spend the suggested 30 seconds rubbing it in, which sure seemed like marketing silliness to me), and doesn't leave me greasy. That said, it's far too light for my combination skin in arid conditions. I have to use a facial oil over top to make this even barely acceptable. On the plus side, it didn't break me out. But it also didn't have any dramatic brightening results, so I'd just call it "okay."

Peel: Pretty basic AHA peel pads. The size and thickness were nice, and there was enough product on one pad to use this on my neck and decollete in addition to my face. But this set only comes with five pads, and since you're supposed to use it daily, it's not really enough to do more than decide if you can tolerate them. These don't add much to the set other than give "deluxe sample" cachet. As far as peel pads go, I'll probably go back to Dr. Dennis Gross or Peter Thomas Roth, since I've been happy with their results and price point.

Overall, I find this to be an overpriced set of mediocre products. I should also note that mine arrived with the cleanser leaking all over the inside of the box. If you plan to give this as a gift, you might want to be prepared for a less-than-stellar presentation.
summary: Okay but overpriced for what it is

reviewText:
This is sort of an odd set to try, at least in my expectations.  To me, it should have night cream instead of day cream, if that makes sense.

So here goes: the facial wash smells lovely and has a great feel. Lathering but not too much, rinses clean very fast. Feels good with no tightness. I love this (and it coordinates with my bathroom!).

Next it says to try the "peels".  The box comes with five but it says to use one nightly or every other night. A week's worth is all?  I'm a cheapie: I'm a maybe once every three nights.  The peels themselves do sting much more than when I've had spa facials.  They sting alot. And I don't have sensitive skin. But there's a great deal of product on the pad so I was able to do my face, neck, and decolletege, even the tops of my hands.  When it dries it says to put on night cream.

But the included cream is a Vit C boosted DAY cream.  ??? Just kind of threw me off, I expected it to be night cream. So I used my own (Vichy) and it seemed fine.  The sizes of the cleanser and cream are full size; the peel, like I said, only contains 5.

Does my skin seem "A-Bright" today? It does! I'm sure it's just a psych thing, but it does feel smooth and even. My hyperpigmentation is still there but let's see after all the peels are used. I will update my review then!

This is a set of facial care products that are not only luxurious, but work well. They have a delightfully light, fresh scent - usually fragrance is a deal breaker for me - I'm annoyingly sensitive to perfumes, but these products don't cause my sinuses to so much as twitch.

The wash is gentle and wonderfully foamy and the moisturizer is very nice and seems to work as well as my favorite moisturizer, Eucerine Co-Q10 Cream. It's nice and thick and a little dab will do you. It goes a long way.

My favorite thing is the Incredi-Peel. I will be buying a larger pack of these. Only five come with this set but they're so big that you can cut them in half. (I store the other half in a zip-lock bag.) The peel is effective and gentle and feels great coming off.

This set makes me  - and my skin - feel pampered and healthy. it would make a great gift, too.
summary: Luxurious Skin Care in a Kit

reviewText: I am a fan of bliss products but I had never tried the items in this set before. The face wash smells great and exfoliates while not being too harsh. The peel wipes ( 5 included) treat age spots and rough areas. The day cream is lovely and not too heavy. It also has a wonderful scent that lingers pleasantly. In combination this is a terrific treat for winter skin. Highly recommended.
summary: Love the set...wash, peel and day cream all excellent

reviewText: All to often,  I find a skin care product that I really like but the fragrance prevents me from using what otherwise would be a perfect product.  I am happy to report that this trio from bliss is lightly scented and has truly been providing me A-Bright Face. The wash is gentle and foamy enough for me and the moisturizer is thick enough that a small dab will do and it feels great when gently massaged into the face.  I have used the Incredi-Peel in the past with good results, so that was the motivator for my getting this set.  At the suggestion of the sales person,  I cut the pads in half and place the second half in a snack size plastic bag for later use. This set is a terrific value and good opportunity to try bliss skin care.  If you haven't already,  try their hand creams for relief.
summary: Opportunity to try all 3 in ample sizes at a good value

reviewText: This is a fairly heavy candle in a glass container which is recommended to burn for up to two hours at a time. The candle emits a fairly mild odor which is unlike anything I have ever sniffed but it is not offensive. The primary purpose of the candle is to try to mellow down the scent coming out of the gas pipe that is our pet Dobie. Certain foods set off his gas producing machinery and the result is very unpleasant. This candle does help a bit.

This is a strange candle.. Other than its high price point ( at this time ) its instructions state not to light over two hours at a time... I am a candle burner.. I come home, relax, open a bottle of wine and light a candle or two.. Usually for more than two hours more like around four  .. So the idea that this candle should only be burnt for two hours was a little strange but its a high fragrance candle, and the fragrance will probably be overpowering or too strong if lit longer?

I followed the instructions and I guess the instructions are true.. After the timer went off my living room was nicely fragrant with a tea-e flower scent.. Lighting for three hours would be too much, although when I blew the candle out the smell slowly went away..  For the next couple nights I lit the candle again for two hours, and the same effect my living room smells great ..

So my final conclusion is this candle is as intended.. It smells great at the moment, and does fill the room up with a very fragrant unique scent that I would expect to find at a high end retailer or fancy decorated home..  The candle should last for 55 hours, that is almost a month of daily lighting if I want the ambiance this candle creates.  I gave it four stars to start, but realized its a pretty strong smelling candle and although priced high its most likely worth it to the market that can afford it .

There is a joy to a good candle that can make a room and a mood.  The right size flame, the right smell, the right flicker... when they come together some primal human need is met.  This is one of those candles.  It's a great size for a centerpiece or focal candle at 4"high and 3.25" across.  Not too big, not too small, just right.  The flame is very clean burning and the scent is just the perfect amount that you know it's there and it wafts in and out of your awareness but never overpowers the room.  The candle is contained in glass jar and the entire container glows when the candle is lit. The Ovando logo is on one side of the jar and can be displayed or concealed as is your preference.  Overall this is a great candle!

I like this self tanner product a lot because the ingredients are a lot better than other commercial tanners. It has a very nice, mild smell that doesn't linger. While it does foam up using the pump, I wouldn't really describe it as a mousse. I didn't have a tanning mitt to use so I just use my hands. It went on well and dried fast as promised.  It does tend to build up around areas they recommend you avoid such as the knees--of course.

Overall, I really recommend it. I'm happy with the color and coverage (I have an olive or yellow undertone). The color faded evenly over 5-6 days and there's plenty left for more use.
summary: Pleasant odor and provides good color

reviewText: Overall the application of the product went on very nicely. You do need to be sure that you have a tanning mitt. Vita Liberata has one that you can purchase right here on Amazon. Vita Liberata Tanning Mitt I just went to my local beauty store and picked one up for a very comparable price of $6.00 and it worked well. I have tried other self tanning mouses before and have had great luck and success with them and this is no different. The overall color was great on my light/medium skin tone. You need to be careful when you put this on, paying close attention to how you are applying it and making sure that you spend time really rubbing it into your skin. Go very light on your elbows and knees as well as along your ankles. I typically do those parts last using what little is left on the mitt. The color this gives is a nice natural brown color.

I absolutely love the finished look from using Vita Liberata's self tanning mousse!  I did buy Famous Dave's 2 sided taking mitt to apply my self tanners with.  I had been using Jergens tanning lotion, but I was darker with 1 use of this mousse than I was with 2 weeks using Jergens.  I like that the mousse is colored, so you can tell when it is rubbed in good.  I didn't have any problems with streaking, except I went too heavy on my toes and Achilles tendon area. My mistake, though.  My only complaint is the price for the small size of the bottle. Vita Liberata carries a lotion that is twice the size for about the same price. I don't feel I get as tan from it, though.  The color I get from this mousse is a nice golden brown. I love this, because I normally tan a reddish gold. The brown looks much nicer. Plus, the mousse dries very quickly.

So far, so good with this self-tanning. For those of us used to creamy white self-tanners that you rub in after a shower, this is different. You need to apply the product at least four hours before showering, after exfoliating, so using Vita Liberate requires planning. However, it dries quickly and--here's the big plus--you can see where you're rubbing it in. The directions tell you to use a "Self tanning mitt." I don't own one--I don't even know what one is--but I used thin latex gloves and got a good result. The mousse has no awful, chemical smell, but then again, I think that's a thing of the past with self-tanners. (I usually use Jergen's and it smell's good.)

I have fair skin and expected the "medium" shade to be too dark but it was a nice tan, and not too orange-y, like some self-tanners can be.

I would have given this product 5 stars rather than 4 were I able to use it right after showering. I find the logistics of using it a half day in advance of showering to be annoying.

I thought I'd be scarred for life by the self tanning experiences of my tween and teen years (90's to early 00's).  I have a distinct memory of a Bath & Body Works self-tanner turning me into a streaky orange mess.  Thankfully self-tanners have evolved A LOT since then with easier application and more natural results.

Prior to receiving this I'd tried (and liked) Vita Liberata's Fabulous Self Tanning Gradual Lotion but was more excited to try this variety because I like quicker results and find tinted mousses to be the most user friendly from an application perspective.

To apply this, you first cleanse and exfoliate your skin.  (I also like to shave my legs first.)  But you DON'T use any in-shower moisturizers or apply any lotions, creams or moisturizers after showering.  You towel dry your skin.  Then, you apply to your skin with a mit (not included) in long circular motions, going easy around the elbows, knees, hands and feet.  The foam is tinted which makes it easier to make sure you don't miss a spot.  (Though I still like help from someone else to get between my shoulders and to my mid-back and make sure I'm even all over where I can't see.)  You then need to wait 4-8 hours for your tan to develop, though the mousse dries pretty quickly lessening the chances it rubs off.  (Though whenever possible I still like to wear dark, loose fitting clothing and eschew undergarments whenever I can just to be safe.)

I will say that nailing self tanner is a combo of technique + formula and I've product-agnostic I've definitely gotten better at this the more I've gotten a feel for it.  That said, I do think this product is pretty great.  It glides on smoothly and evenly and without a strong odor.  It dries quickly as advertised and develops into a beautiful, natural glow that makes my permanently pasty skin beach ready.  As someone who is more pale I would prefer a lighter color for winter use (this particular line doesn't come in light/fair, though their phenomenal line does and their gradual line allows for a light glow as it is buildable), but I like this for the summer time.  I also find as long as I take good care of my skin while using this (minimizing the number of hot showers I take, limiting pool time and patting my skin dry vs. rubbing) I do get 5-7 days of wear out of one tan.

I'm a fan!
summary: Proof self-tanner has come a LONG way over the years

reviewText:
Okay, so.  No tan here.

Long story: For one, I did everything it said. I already had a slight base tan despite using sunscreen. I shaved first, exfoliated to death, and applied exactly as it said, in circular motions.  But then, down the bottle, it says, "Shower in 48 hours to reveal your beautiful tan". What? I have to wait 48 hours to shower? Ick?!?!?!?

So I waited two hours instead, making sure to get it off my hands as those looked pretty silly. I also went a little crazy when first applying, deciding to "self tan" my whitest of parts (namely what you don't see in a bikini). I thought it would be a treat to NOT have a snow white stomach.  It did nothing except accentuate stretch marks from three pregnancies. Really!  They looked MORE noticeable and they are old stretch marks.  Sigh.

I took my shower, dried off, and then applied my favorite moisturizer.  My skin did look good but I think it was all the other steps and not so much the self-tanner. Maybe in 48 hours I'll suddenly be tan?

It's a messy mousse too. Hard to control application.  And if, by chance, your hair is wet and drips on it, you get a watermark. Like a long tear. Which is how I felt after.

I know this is high end stuff, but I see no difference between this and Jergens or those store brands that are cheap.

Works well.  Probably the best feature is that it dries quickly.  So many of theses self-tanners have a terrible odor but this one does not, another plus.  Exfoliating prior to application is important, especially if your skin leans to the dry side.  Apply in  circular motions instead of up and down to avoid any lines.  It lasts about three days and then tends to have a blotchy look.  It was shipped in a bubble envelope and leaked all over so some product was wasted.  Since this is a bit pricey, waste is an issue.
summary: Probably the best feature is that it dries quickly

reviewText:
This is the first self-tanning product I used that dried very quickly and stays on for more than a day.  I am light-skinned and the tinted mousse was a natural looking color for my skin.  I have used a mitt before and find it makes the most sense.  If you work it in circular motions, the tanner spreads evenly and no streaking.  I usually toss out the mitt, however, and do not reuse it unless it is washed and dried thoroughly.

I've tried so many products that the price for this self-tanner did not seem out of line.
summary: Fast Drying, Long-Lasting and Good Color

reviewText: Brighten up your complexion for a special evening, or just to look tanned for a Summer party, in just a few minutes by smoothing on a few drops of this lotion, it darkens over few minutes, so don't apply too much at first. The color fades over seven days, too, so you're not suddenly too light.
summary: Brighten up your complexion for a special evening, or ...

reviewText:
Vita Liberata comes as a mousse.  It has a tint to it so you can see where you are applying it.  It does dry somewhat faster than spray or lotion type tanners, so be prepared to work quickly to avoid streaks.

It is low on fragrance, but what I did detect was not necessarily a pleasant smell.  Not terrible, but eh.

As far as color, it is natural looking but it is more of a pale brown with no hint of a golden tan, so be sure that is the color hue you are looking for.

Since it dies fast there is less chance of color transfer. I always feel like I cannot touch anything, sit anywhere, or get dressed for a long time after applying a tanner, but this dries fast so I was a little less concerned.  I did not notice any transfer on my shirt or elsewhere.

The color fades by day 4 or so and it mostly gone by day 6.

I am somewhat fair skinned but still found the color natural enough.  I just would have preferred a slight more realistic shade.

Overall, it works and does not smell.  It can be streaky if you take as much time applying it as you would a lotion tanner.  The color is what would make me not buy this again, it is too brown to be completely realistic.

This is a high quality product that gives you a nice tan without the drawbacks of possibly getting skin cancer through lengthy sun exposure. As I get older, I'm avoiding the sun a lot more, so this is a great alternative. It goes on smoothly, has no annoying chemical smell and dries fairly quickly. I'm not sure why it's called a "mousse" as I associate that with hair products, but it does come out as a foam. My only quibble is the price - it's quite pricey for the amount you get, but the Amazon price is still less expensive than Sephora. I would stock up on this when it's Prime Day or on sale.
summary: High Quality Tanning Product - A Good Alternative to Possibly Harmful Sun Exposure

reviewText:
A tanned skin is always a damaged skin, so if you want to have a great tan with the health hazards associated with sun exposure, self-tanners are an excellent option.

They call this a medium tanner, but it looks pretty dark to me.  You'll get a noticeable and largely natural tan immediately.  To be candid, I prefer the Vita Liberate Fabulous Self Tanning Gradual Lotion, which goes on clear, is less messy and more subtle.  But still, this is a very good product.  4 stars.

First I want to mention that as soon as  I removed the cap/lid, the container leaked and tanner dripped on my clothing.  I was able to get the stain out with lots of cold water and some soap.  Then I tightened the two sections so it wouldn't leak again and it's working now.

This tanner creates a foam.  You will find it easier to apply if you use a tanning mitt.

I am fair skinned and have been using sunless tanner products for several years.
I used a tanning mitt which helped me apply the tanner without leaving any streaks.
The tanner did not have a fragrance and dried quickly.
One application tinted my skin a light brown shade.
Most sunless tanners leave my skin with more of a golden glow which I prefer.
The tan began fading around day 6.

For best results, follow these instructions which were provided by Vita Liberata:
"-Ensure skin is clean and exfoliated.
-Always use a tan mitt and with two to three pumps at a time, apply with circular movements.
-Use sparingly on hands, feet, knees, and elbows.
-Do not moisturize or use moisturizing shower gel prior to application.
-Shower after four to eight hours, and if naturally pale, leave longer before showering."
summary: One application tinted my fair skin a light brown. It dried quickly and had no odor.

reviewText: I am fair-complected, but definitely prefer the way I look when I have some color.  I used to enjoy tanning in the sun and indoor tanning beds.  Eventually, I paid the price, mainly age spots and even basal cell carcinoma.  So now I get my color through sunless tanning products.  When I saw this Vita Liberata Fabulous Self Tanning Tinted Mousse - Medium in the Amazon Vine program, I decided to give it a try.  The product has several plusses.  First, the foam is easy to apply and dries very quickly.  Therefore, as the directions state, apply this tanning mousse with a mitt or gloves, or your palms will be tan as well.  Also, this product really does give a lot of color.  In fact, I often buy medium self tanning shades, but in this case, the medium color is quite dark on me and I would probably be better off using one of their products marketed for fair skin.  Another plus of Vita Liberata Fabulous Self Tanning Tinted Mousse is that it does not have a strong unpleasant smell like some of the other self tanning products I have used.  On the negative side, this tanning mousse is quite pricey, costing significantly more than what I usually pay for sunless tanning products.  For that reason, I deducted a star, but overall, I like this product and would recommend.

I am very impressed with Vita Liverata line of Tanning products. This one is a more traditional as it tans over several hours. The product is tinted and I have very pale skin, but I used the medium mousse. When I first started to rub it on I thought it might be a bit too dark/olive colored, but after letting it dry I really kind of like the immediate tint to the tanner. This Mousse is more of a foaming liquid. This can make it a bit more difficult to apply because it needs to be put on in small areas, blending all the way. I prefer this mousse to lotions. Lotions tend to be sticky and greasy for a long time and get sticky again when I get sweaty going outside in the summer. This dries quickly and completely.

Good looking tanner that dries fast.  It does not last as long as they claim though.  My wife has needed to reapply every 3 days almost on the dot.  It looks good and does not smell.  It is a quality self tanning product but just know you will have to reapply quite often which can become costly at $30 a can.
summary: Great Tanner - Have to reapply often

reviewText: This tanning mousse goes on evenly and really gives your skin a nice tan look.  I only use it on my legs but am sure it would go on just as easy for the rest of the body.  The tan lasts a few days.  I've tried a lot of self tanning products and this one ranks up there as one of the best.

This is a medium tint mousse and it is truly fabulous.  It is fast drying and doesn't have any strong chemical odors.  I've used it once and it gave me a natural looking tan.  I use self tanners to avoid prolong sun exposure and also to help even out my slightly suntanned skin and it does the job.  I wish the price point wasn't so high on this brand, but it is a fabulous self tanning product.
summary: Great medium color, natural looking self tanning mousse

reviewText:
Vita Liberata Fabulous Self Tanning Tinted Mousse IS fabulous!  Having tried a number of other products, there are characteristics that you focus on..notably how easy is it to apply, how fast does it dry, what does it smell like, and finally what kind of tan does it actually produce.  Vita Liberata is not the least expensive self tanner but it may be the best.  For this comparison, I love Fake Bake (price and final result), but find application more problematic.

Easy to apply?  There are creamy products, liquids, and mousses.  For all, I skip the special glove... I simply use disposable plastic gloves and put the product directly on my skin or on the glove itself.  Usually I stand in the tub to avoid getting the tanner somewhere more difficult to wash.  Liquids like Fake Bake are bit more messy than Vita Liberata mousse.  Vita Liberata is easy to control, and tt goes on easily and evenly with a disposable glove, just keep it moving and avoid "hot spots".

Both Fake Bake and Vita Liberata dry quickly, allowing you to put clothes on (or sit on the couch) with little transfer.  Fake Bake definitely has a tropical aroma at the beginning but it does calm down--Vita Liberata has almost no odor from beginning to end, something I really like.

With any of these products, you should leave them on for greater than 4 hours before washing them off.  DHA needs some time to react with the outer layer of your skin to produce the darkening effect.  Both Vita Liberata and Fake Bake have a tinting agent in them, so if you want to go outside right away you can.  After you take a shower, the tint comes off, but a pleasant tan like color remains.  It is surprising how easy this really is and the color against white skin is orange brown... maybe not totally natural on all skin types, but it certainly takes care of pasty white legs making shorts weather more pleasant for everyone (!).

This type of "tan" lasts about a week, but in that time you might be able to get a little sun on your legs. (These products and the tan they produce do not provide any protection against sunlight based radiation, so be careful if you are *really out in the sun*).

I love the tan that Vita Liberata Self Tanning Tinted Mousse produces!  Vita Liberata is essentially fragrance free, goes on super easy with almost zero mess, and allows you to put clothes on within 10 minutes due to quick drying and low residue.  After a shower, you will be amazed how tan you look!  Personally, I have a new favorite tanning mousse and think the price is worth it for a premium product hitting so many of the features I love with the final benefit of tan that rivals any tan I could get by staying out in the sun for hours.  Bravo!
summary: Very low fragrance! Great coverage and tan!

reviewText:
I love Vita Liberata, it's very similar to St Tropez mousse but without the smell.
I like self tanners with the tint for instant bronze color and you can see where it was applied.
I have no idea while they even advertise 2-3 week lasting period, as we shed skin everyday, but it last good 4 days.
Cons: price and size.
Pros: healthy skin with tan without UV damage. Worth investing!

I've been using this product over the summer in between applications of their other "instant tan" product (https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00865610O). This product goes on clear and turn your skin brown over a few hours. I like it because it hold the brown longer when you combine it with their instant-tan product. It is brown, not orangey like old style products. I don't find it streaky at all as long as I take my time a rub onto small sections of my legs. The ingredients are high quality made in the U.K. I have even used this on my face occassionally to add a little kiss of the sun glow when I go out for the evening. I use it about once ever 1-2 weeks throughout the summer and still have a lot left in the container (a little goes a long way). i LOVE this product!
summary: I LOVE this product! It works great and a little goes a long way.

reviewText:
This is the best self tanning lotion I've used.  While I'm not sure I would call it "odorless," it does have a lot less of a scent than most cosmetics -- even other cosmetics that are unscented.  It goes on very easily -- not so thick that it requires a lot of rubbing but not watery, either.

As to the tanning effect, I am extremely fair skinned.  One application is enough to give me just a hint of a tan the next day.  If I use this product a few days in a row, it definitely looks like I've been on a beach vacation.  I haven't used it more than than because I don't want people to look at me and immediately know that I'm using a self tanning lotion; I never get a dark tan because I generally use a lot of sunscreen and avoid sun exposure due to my tendency to burn.
summary: Nearly odorless, applies evenly, provides subtle tan if you don't overdo it

reviewText:
I got this for my mom who says she likes it well enough.

One thing she mentioned is that the color is not orange which is a definite plus.  (She tried another self-tanning lotion that turned her skin a bright orange and she couldn't scrub it off fast enough.  So I guess that self-tanning lotion was really an exfoliant.)  Also, the color works very quickly to develop so you have to add it slowly.

She also likes that it doesn't streak if you are careful to apply it very evenly and it dries fairly quickly.  She didn't use mitts or gloves; she recommends just washing your hands really thoroughly after you apply it.

Another positive is that it's barely scented so it doesn't clash with her perfume.

The only negative is price, which she says is high for this type of product.
summary: Mom likes it.  Doesn't stink, doesn't dry to an orange color.  A little expensive.

reviewText: Beautiful color but for the price I would get St. Tropez tanning mousse instead. The mouse is MUCH easier to spread and absorb into your skin quickly. And most importantly dries way faster.
summary: Go for a tanning mousse instead of this lotion

reviewText: This lotion is amazing! I'm usually banned by my husband from using self-tanners because they smell AWFUL. Like a mixture of chemicals and body odor. I am always on the hunt for one with no scent and thus far I have not been very successful. Which means I live with my very pasty complexion. But this one has almost no scent! I was blown away at the first application. I noticed a subtle difference even after one application. There were even some finger outlines on an area where I wasn't doing a thorough job of rubbing it in, which would never happen on the more subtle popular drug-store lotions I have tried. I can finally look sun-kissed without smelling terrible!

Vita Liberata comes as a lotion and mousse. This is the lotion.  I've tried both and find they perform about the same.  The mousse is a bit more streaky but also dries faster. Both versions have a tint so you can see where you are applying it. You have to work evenly to avoid streaks, and be prepared to touch up a little with your mitt (NOT included).

It is low on fragrance, but what I did detect was not necessarily a pleasant smell. Not terrible, but eh.

As far as color, it is natural looking but it is more of a pale brown with no hint of a golden tan, so be sure that is the color hue you are looking for.

It dries well.  I am always concerned about color transfer. I feel like I cannot touch anything, sit anywhere, or get dressed for a long time after applying a tanner.  This dries nicely but the mousse version dries very fast. I did not notice any transfer on my shirt or elsewhere.

The color fades by day 4 or so and it mostly gone by day 6.

I am somewhat fair skinned but still found the color natural enough. I just would have preferred a slight more realistic shade.

Overall, it works and does not smell. It is no more streaky than other lotion tanners and if you are careful you will get good results. The color is what would make me not buy this again, it is too brown to be completely realistic.

My skin is super pale, and I'm usually fine with looking like a fresh piece of cod, but every once in a while I like to bring my legs out of the shocking zone. This Vita Liberata Gradual Self Tanning Lotion is very nice for just that purpose - once I've done a good exfoliation.

There isn't that awful self-tanner smell, and the color develops slowly over the course of the day (or night) until my skin is slightly tinted with a bronzy tone, rather than an orange-brown tone. I don't choose to go very dark because it wouldn't be very convincing, but the little bit of color is a welcome break from my usual pallor and allows me to go stocking-free with skirts. This is more expensive, but in the end, I use less than a tube every season so I don't mind the price for a much more pleasing experience and end result.
summary: Good application and light bronzy color on my pale cod-colored legs

reviewText: This tanning cream is certainly a gradual one but that is what I favor over sudden streaks and orange hands.  The smell is familiar to other tanners such as Jergens.  It is also white in color which usually tanners are "tan" in color so in a way that makes it a little more difficult to see where you have missed applying it but other than that it is a good product and does what it claims.

Vita Liberata's self tanning gradual lotion is a great product. It has no smell when you first apply it. However, after about 3 or 4 hours, I can start to smell a little hint of self Tanner.  This doesn't bother me, because I have used Jergens tanning lotion, and it smells stronger from the beginning. Vita Liberata's lotion works much better than Jergens. The color is browned and deeper. Even though this lotion doesn't work as quickly as their mousse, it still comes out the nice golden brown color. It just takes more uses to be as dark as the mousse. It is also double the size for the same price!  The lotion goes on nicely and soaks into your skin.  I didn't think I would be fine with just this as a moisturizer (I have very dry skin), but it really has worked great.  I also use a taking mitt when applying this lotion. It dries too quickly when using over the whole body, so your hands would be colored on the palms and nail beds if you tried barred hands and then washing, I think. It might be okay if you were just doing your legs.  I really love the color, ease outdoor application, lack of too much smell, and size of the bottle.

I am fair-complected, but prefer the way I look when I have a bit of color. I used to enjoy tanning in the sun and indoor tanning beds. Eventually, I paid the price, mainly age spots and even basal cell carcinoma. So now I get my color through sunless tanning products. When I saw this Vita Liberata Fabulous Self Tanning Gradual Lotion in the Amazon Vine program, I decided to give it a try. I had previously tried Vita Liberata Fabulous Self Tanning Tinted Mousse  Medium, but found it was a little too dark for my skin.

Vita Liberata Fabulous Self Tanning Gradual Lotion is easy to apply and dries fairly quickly, and develops some color over 4-8 hours.  This works well with my light skin.  Reapply every few days to maintain color.  Should you want more color, simply apply more often.  In addition to adding color, this lotion also contains ingredients which moisturize your skin.  Another plus of this lotion that is does not have an unpleasant smell like some of the other self tanning products I have used. The only negative is that Vita Liberata products are a bit pricey, costing considerably more than what I usually pay for sunless tanning products. For that reason, I deducted a star, but overall, I like this gradual tanning lotion and would recommend.
summary: Works great on my light skin; a little pricey

reviewText: Probably the only thing that I didn't like about this tanning lotion was the price, other than that I found it very easy to apply with a nice natural sun kissed color.

This is one of the best self tanners I have ever used.  A little goes a long way and you need to apply it quickly.  I love that it dries so fast...I usually need to stand in front of a fan to get a self tanner to dry in order to be able to get dressed and not stain my clothes.  It also does not have the a
smelly self tanner smell.  It gives a nice tan which lasts for a few days.  This is now my go to self tanner!
summary: Vita Liberata Self Tannee...it IS fabulous!

reviewText:
After the mousse disaster, I'm not impressed with this. I tried this first. It wants you to leave it on a long time and then shower. It's applied the same as the mousse, and while it is a bit easier to apply than the mousse, it's all the same.  Exfoliate, scrub, apply with mitt, clean up mess, stand back naked and wait to tan.

I've tried three of their products and don't get why they are so high priced. I see nothing that knocks me out.  Lancome has a self-tanner that works better.

One positive is I didn't turn orange. I didn't turn anything.

Recently my five year old granddaughter looked at me and said, "Grandma, I think you have a farmer's tan".  Kids do say the darndest things, but she spoke the truth in this case.  I started using this product to help even out my tan, and I am very pleased with the results.  It does have a scent, but it is quite mild.  It is not cheap, but sometimes you have to pay a little more to get a great product.

I really really like this self tanner ~~ up to this point the only one that I felt like gave you a natural looking tan was St. Tropez, which is higher than this is.  It gives you a true natural looking gradual tan.  I'm naturally very pale, and while I do go to the tanning bed occasionally I like to maintain a light tan on my legs continuously.  This goes on wet and you have to rub it in a for a min. or two but you get a great tan, for me overnight.  I always put it on after I exfoliate before I go to bed.  The one thing to watch is that you have to be very careful around ankles and feet and hands ~~ apply very sparingly and make sure you rub it in really, really well.  If you don't it will be significantly darker on those spots.  And it's not easy to get it back off, lol.  Overall I'd recommend this to anyone who wants a true natural looking tan without the sun or tanning bed!
summary: Overall I'd recommend this to anyone who wants a true natural looking tan without the sun or tanning bed!

reviewText: I've tried many self-tanners, from the inexpensive Jergens brands to pricier offerings.  This self-tanner from Vita Liberata has been one of the best ones I have used.  The instructions are a little complicated, as not only are you supposed to apply to clean, dry skin, but also you are supposed to shower several hours after application to "stop" the tanning process.  I didn't do the latter.  I simply used this product like I use all self-tanners:  I took a shower, exfoliating my skin in the process, dried off, and then applied the self-tanner, being careful to avoid areas that tend to absorb excess lotion, such as knees.  By the end of the day, I was rewarded with an even, honey color.  There were a few places where I noticed a faint demarcation line, but I blame this on my own application, not the product.  Another advantage of this self-tanner is that it has a very mild scent that was pleasant yet faded quickly.  I had a natural tan, and I used this self-tanner to even out some of my tan lines; it worked well for that purpose.  Overall, I am very happy with this product and would definitely recommend it!
summary: Easy to use; produces warm, honey-colored tan

reviewText:
After years of looking for decent sunless tanners, I had really become excited years ago when I won a basket for Clarins which had the best sunless tanner in it that I had ever used.  Then time went on and I found Alba Botanica's moisturizing sunless tanner, which still is one of the best sunless tanners I have ever used, but sadly, I think it may have been discontinued, or perhaps they are reformulating.  I can not find it anymore.

When I had a chance to test out some sunless tanners from the Vita Liberata company, I was interested to see what kind of results I would have.  I have been pleasantly surprised.  This is a lot more expensive than Alba Botanica but it performs similarly, including moisturizing.

WHAT IS THIS TANNER LOTION LIKE?
First of all this is a white lotion which is not overly runny.  The cap twists off which means you have to put it somewhere when you are applying, and set it down in between squeezes.  The lotion itself has very little smell to it.

HOW DOES THIS APPLY?
I have to say here that I do not like mitts.  I think that they waste product and are only for one hand.  I developed a method ages ago that involves using silicone gloves such as the hair stylist gloves you buy at Sally Beauty Supply.  I put a rubberband on the tube and attach the gloves to it so that they are there to use multiple times.  It is important to use BOTH hands.  By appying with both hands quickly and one area at a time, legs have no streaks on them.  On the arms it is not a problem to use one hand.  Neck and other places are easier to use both hands if necessary.
