summary: So gentle it doesn't bother my eczema but it WORKS!

reviewText: I have combination sensitive skin that is prone to redness. I like to exfoliate a few times a week to rid my skin of dry bits and definitely prefer gentle exfoliation. This product didn't have much of a scent and no real grittiness both of which are a plus for me. I followed the instructions and used two pumps, then massaged the product in circles until what they called rolls formed. To be blunt it is rather gross, it feels similar to washing your face after a sunburn, however the yuck is not a deal breaker. My skin felt very clean, soft and tight post using it but it also felt irritated in areas. A good moisturizer helped calm the irritation but it did last over an hour. All in all I'm left with mixed feelings about the product, it does work and I did like the final results but the process is gross and I would have preferred zero irritation.

This is a pretty cool product! You use a couple pumps of the serum  and apply to the face. Little balls of dead skin start showing up and then you rinse. Afterwards, the skin is smooth and refreshed looking. Highly recommend!
summary: This is a pretty cool product

reviewText:
I was flabbergasted at how this product works. I'd just come home after weeks in a physical rehab facility. Since my movement was impaired, I depended on the staff for washing with the hospital-like products there. As a result, my face had dried out terribly.

When I came home, I had this product waiting for me. After washing my face with my usual face soap, I dried it and applied it. It  was very strange. I was so dry that what I considered an amount that should spread all over one cheek was practically absorbed on contact. I kept rubbing and little rolls of dry skin formed. My dress looked as if I'd been caught in a shower of some weird little white worms. I repeated this process all over my face and was amazed at how soft it felt and how well it absorbed the moisturizer that I applied afterwards. I've never had a product that produced such results so quickly. The dead skin literally rolled off and fresh new skin was exposed. My skin feels so soft I frequently touch my face just to make sure I'm not imagining things.

The product advertises itself as a skin "brightener." I'm not exactly sure what brightening is, but as far as cleansing, cleaning, renewing, and softening this is certainly the best and fastest I have ever seen.

EDIT: No reflection on the product and I have not changed my mind on any of the above BUT there was a problem with the delivery mechanism whereby the pump no longer pumped up any product. I ended up having to (literally) cut up the bottle (Not easy--trust me--it's very hard plastic) but I didn't want to waste what felt like about half the contents. I don't know how this is supposed to work (some sort of vacuum action or something?) but there wasn't a tube and pumping did nothing. I got everything out using kitchen tools and so on, but there should be a dependable delivery system to make sure that you get out every last drop.
summary: Prepare to be (pleasantly) amazed!--read later edit

reviewText: This is a good product for sensitive skin, which I have. I experienced no reactions. There is not a strong scent, which I appreciate. I don't know if in the long run this will lighten the few spots I have or not, but it definitely seems to exfoliate well and tighten pores. It's a rather small container for $30, but I don't need to use a lot, so I expect it will last at least six months, if not more. It seems as effective as Dermalogica Daily Microfoliant, but is less expensive.
summary: Good exfoliation and pore tightening for sensitive skin

reviewText:
I would say this is the weirdest exfoliate I've ever used. My face seemed clean, but those little ball things were kind of disgusting. Whatever happened to using a 'normal' mask or a soft face scrubbie with some decent soap?

$30 for 25 grams / 0.86 ounces is prohibitively expensive. Especially considering there are better exfoliates out there and a much better price point. Some of the best Korean face masks are only a third of the price.

This reminds me of the paraffin treatment that makes dead skin roll off your feet. I LOVE THIS PRODUCT!! My skin has never felt so smooth ever. My face drank up my nighttime lotion and oil. I will buy more of this. WOW product
summary: Made my nighttime lotion and oil just soak in LOVE THIS

reviewText: Kind of disappointed.  The other good reviews and product experience with Jack Black prompted the purchase.  But I am not impressed at all by the scent--almost like a cheap detergent smell.  It is light, at first, almost Davidoff White Water like smell.  But it fades away quickly and it takes quite a few sprays to get anything lasting.  It is Body Spray so I am not expecting the strength of a Eau De Toilette, but it fall short of my high exception of Jack Black products.  My first disappointment with Jack Black.
summary: Kind of disappointed. The other good reviews and product experience with ...

reviewText: great
Good light scent. Great for a quick spray or two when you get out of the shower. I pack this in my gym bag.
Perfect
Incredibly good body spray. It works as well as cologne and smells better than most new scents out there.
smells fresh and clean
Amazing spray, smells just like the soap

Out of all the skin care products I've ever tried, the Neovadiol line from Vichy is my favorite. I always use their wonderful oil and find that the Nuit Cream and this day cream work wonders on my skin. This is a thick, a little bit goes a long way, creamy moisturizer that works and keeps my skin smooth for hours and it also does well under make up. This is a good cream to hydrate skin and takes the focus out of fine wrinkles. I love the Neovadiol line-I can't say enough good about it for skin, especially for over 50 skin. This is just a wonderful product and I highly recommend the Vichy Neovadiol Oil-oh man, that stuff is wonderful for plumping and hydrating my skin. This in conjunction with the oil works makes skin smooth and soft all day.

Let me first gently say that selling anti-aging creams has become a very big business.  I think we all know why.

Creams, such as this, create temporary effects that are not permanent.  This will keep you buying the product for years which will become very profitable for the company.  That is the business model of almost every anti-aging cream.

If you are fine with that, then this product is probably a good one to use.  My wife used it and it did, temporarily, improve the appearance of her facial skin.  Not dramatically, but some improvement.  We won't keep getting it because of the expense, but you are certainly welcome to.  Enjoy!

It is hard to give a true review after only using a product like this for a few days but here are the current results after a few days use.

The Vichy cream is nicely packaged.  The jar comes in a square box to protect the jar.  The jar is 2 tall and 3 wide.  It was fully filled.  We have had some other brands in the past that make a large container but only fill the jar half way.  Very nice packaging by Vichy.

The cream goes on very smooth and appears to be moisturizing my skin nicely.  The cream is a very smooth filling moisturizer.

Per the packaging:  This cream is for post-menopausal aging. The cream is for fragile, thinning skin with extreme dryness. This is for normal to dry skin.

I will update as more time goes by.  At this time I am very happy with the feel and texture of this cream and I am very happy with the results so far.  I have had NO side effects.
summary: Nice Packaging, Nice Texture, Nice Moisturizer.

reviewText: A little of this seems to go a long way and it's tolerable as far as the balance of coverage versus absorption. Generous size, acceptable non-irritating fragrance and overall seems nice. The chemicals are not all that natural...I've been strongly leaning toward more organic and natural options rather than synthetics and toxic/harsh chemicals. Only time will tell if this actually has any real results but for now, there are no negatives.

My wife has used Vichy products for years. The Neovadiol has produced visible and tactile results in moisturizing her facial skin.

This product uses some aggressive ingredients such as dimenthicone. Dimenthicone arouses some suspicions on many sites yet scientific studies cited in Wikipedia indicate it's safe for skin when used in cosmetic products (such as this one). There's always the possibility that later studies will confirm suspicions; I have no certainty on this.

The Neovadiol moisturizer is sophisticated in terms of chemistry. Thankfully, my wife didn't experience any allergies or side effects. It is surprising how this truly moisturized her skin, almost too good to be true. For now it seems like a reliable product to me.
summary: Aggressive skin moisturizer with results almost too good to be true

reviewText: Feels not too greasy on my skin.  I would recommend it.

My skin is certainly not menopausal, but I wanted to give this lotion a try, as many products that I have tried have not helped my skin feel moisturized and well treated. I began using this lotion about five weeks ago, and although I realize five weeks is not that long of a window for me to make a solid assertion, I am impressed with the results I have observed so far. First, my faint face discoloration (one of my skin issues) is still present, but I have noticed a slight evenness improvement in the tone of my skin. These results may be minimal, but I am satisfied so far. Also, although this moisturizer is a day cream, I also use it at night, and I cannot get over how soft my skin feels after each use--which is a reason I do not mind that this cream does not include SPF. I love how lightweight the lotion feels after application, which was initially surprising because the cream feels thick upon touching it, but how it absorbs into my skin tells me this cream is gentle during application. The cream is not greasy and has no strong scent, but it does smell fresh and pleasant. Thus far, I really love this moisturizer. Previously, I was using an all-natural brand, which is what I prefer using, but unfortunately, despite its promising results, I had to switch to another brand. Since having the opportunity to test the Vichy line out, I am impressed. The price is worth the investment. The bottom line is that this lotion treats my skin fairly and leaves it feeling smooth.

I've been using this cream for almost a month now. The "Anti-Aging Need" in the description states for Post-Menopausal Aging. Since I've been post menopausal for over 20 years now I think I qualify. :-)  (Why do they show young women on ads for older women's products?)

Even though this jar only holds 1.69oz. it does last a long time because I only use a dab at a time and spread it around my face. It's a thick silky cream that is not at all sticky or greasy, absorbs into the skin, and has a pleasant mild scent (to me it could have more scent). I've probably used less than half the jar so far. I had another Vichy product that I really liked that was a lot more floral scented.

So, does it help plump the appearance of my wrinkles? Not that I can tell, at least not so far. Does it provide hydration? I'd say yes. Is it worth the price? To me, no, but I have never been one to wear much makeup or worry about wrinkles (I earned them, after all). I do like the feel of the cream on my face and I feel like I'm pampering myself when I use it.
summary: Only need to use a teeny amount

reviewText: As a post-menopausal lady, I was looking forward to trying this. It did not disappoint. It really adds new life to my dry skin, without making it feel greasy. It has a light fragrance, which is very pleasant, and absorbs quickly. I know it's a day cream, but I use it as an overnight cream and it works just as well.

While I haven't seen dramatic results from thus cream, it feels good and seems to be evening out my complexion. It also adds a slightly more luminous glow that's subtle but enhancing.
My skin definitely feels moisturized but not greasy.
summary: Good cream from a reliable company

reviewText:
I know I've said it before but I'm a huge fan of the Vichy brand.  For not much more than the drugstore brands and for about half the price of the boutique and luxe brands I've tried,  this brand delivers very good results.

I've been using the night cream in the Neovadiol line for awhile, so I was looking forward to giving the day cream a try.  I found the results similar to that of the LIFTACTIV line as far plumping, diminishing the look of wrinkles on my forehead and the deep vertical lines that run from the bottom of my nose to the outside corners of my mouth and giving my jawline and checks a lifted look.  This also helps with evening out skin tone but not enough for me to give up my Vichy ProEVEN dark spot corrector.  Just don't use to much, a few dots are all that's needed.  Using too much not only wastes product but can cause foundation or BB/CC cream to pill.
summary: Just a few dabs work wonders

reviewText: Overall this is a good moisturizing cream--goes on smoothly, absorbs quickly, doesn't leave an oily residue, and moisturizes the skin nicely. I was surprised to see the box says "post menopausal," since that's not anywhere in their pictures on Amazon, and I haven't yet hit that life milestone. But the cream worked just fine. My only not-quite-complaint is that the cream smells exactly like Bed Bath & Beyond. If you're used to all-natural products (I am), it does have a slight chemical tinge, but in general it will leave *you* smelling like BB&B for an hour or so. Not an unpleasant scent, just a bit odd to have on your face.
summary: says "post menopausal"; smells like Bed Bath & Beyond

reviewText:
Having been experiencing  serious post menopausal dryness on my face, I was really excited to try this moisturizer. I'm happy to report that it has pretty much lived up to my expectations. The cream itself is smooth and light, yet super moisturizing. It glides on easily and sinks right in, with no oily feeling,  just soft, fresh feeling radiant skin.  The moisturizing lasts all day too, so though expensive, you get your money's worth.

I really recommend this product, my only caveat being that I seem to break out with the occasional pimple, but nothing major and it's worth the intensive and long lasting moisturizing.

Vichy is a brand of long standing, and generally speaking, makes nice skincare products. If you're looking for a moisturizer that does what you need it to do, this would do the trick.

The brand claims that this has some kind of firming ability for skin sagging due to age and menopause, but either my skin's not that far gone, or I just don't see the result. It has a pleasant fragrance (to ME, because I like strongly fragranced products; if you don't, this won't be your cupppa), sinks easily and quickly into your dermis, and doesn't have a greasy feel.

I like glass jarred products, but many don't, concerned as they are that active ingredients in jars fall apart quickly, or become contaminated from sticking your fingers in them. I have a big supply of small plastic spatulas, so product spoilage isn't an issue for me.

I don't see any ingredients in this that have wowed me, but on the other hand, I haven't experienced any distress from Vichy's proprietary ingredients either. (My skin is pretty normal and pretty impervious; if you have sensitive skin, you might want to think twice.)

This is pricey for what it is, but I've spent more and gotten much less on other brands. It's a good moisturizer, but I'm not prepared to go along with the 'menopause' benefit claims. Need soft skin and money's not an issue? This will work for you.
summary: Pleasant moisturizer, but not so sure about the 'anti-menopause' skin claims

reviewText:
Vichy Neovadiol Replenishing Care Moisturizer is a special Daytime Moisturizer made for Women who are post menopause.  It's wonderfully creamy and thick and blends in really quickly. It doesn't feel sticky or gummy and is comfortable under foundation.

After moving to California from Washington State my skin had a hard time adjusting. The Vichy Replenishing care Moisturizer completely cured my dry ashy skin and it now looks soft and feels soft to the touch.

Although this is for post menopause I would highly recommend this for pre-menopause as well because of it's intense moisturizing power. This is a great product I would highly recommend.

This product has a very sharp scent kind of like a perm, and just the fumes sting my eyes without even applying it.
I might have been able to predict it if I had been paying attention as the application instructions particularly avoid the whole eye area. If you have any irritated areas it stings when you apply it.

(UPDATE 10-13-2017)- Been using this for a while now, and I am impressed even more than originally. This stuff is great and the price is right too, compared to other lines I mentioned below. I highly recommend this cream, again if you can tolerate the fragrance which I have gotten used to. ---------------------- I have been using and exploring skin care for quite some time now, so I have had a chance to use many different brands at a wide variety of price points. Let's see how Vichy Neovadiol Compensating Complex compares to the creams I have used. WHAT TYPES OF CREAMS HAVE I USED Some of the creams that I have used are as follows Lancome Absolue Lancome Renergie Multi Action Algenist Firm and Lift Algenist Genius Loreal Vitalift Yes to Blueberries L'Occitane SKII L'Oreal Genesis LaPrarie Clarins Christian Dior (variety of them) Chanel Shiseido The above list only reflects some of the brands I have had a chance to explore and test out. Keeping this in mind, I will compare this cream for effectiveness and what results it achieves. WHAT IS THIS CREAM LIKE? Vichy Neovadiol Compensating Complex is indicated to be for mature skin that is post menopausal. That means that the targets are for plumping skin, shrinking pores, radiance, making skin feel denser (thus more youthful), contours, and more of an even tone to skin. This cream does not have SPF in it which I am THRILLED about. If you want to use SPF, then you can put it on yourself. The jar is glass another feature that I like. It has a tight fitting cap with an inner seal which helps the cream from drying out. The color is a beautiful iridescent peach color glass and the cream inside is an icy peachy pink color. It is a bit thicker than the night version of this cream Vichy Neovadiol Replenishing Care Night Cream, 1.69 fl. oz.. HOW DOES THIS CREAM PERFORM? When applying this cream, it is extremely lightweight- not at all thick and sticky like you might expect. It goes on easily and absorbs VERY quickly into the skin. The best way to put it on is to dot about a lentil to pea sized dot on each quadrant of the face and then spread it into the skin. There is a very heavy scent to this, which I have to be honest at first with the night cream made me want to retch, but I quickly got used to it. Many people would probably find it pleasant, but at first it was hard to get used to. I have used this with the night cream at night so the combination of the action is to be considered. I find that the cream leaves my skin very plump, glowy, moisturized for 12 hours until I use the night cream, and there is absolutely no sticky residue. I find that it does seem to work best when I apply 99% Natural Hyaluronic Acid Serum 1 fl oz (29.6 ml) Liquid on BEFORE any moisturizer and after cleansing the skin. I use this with all skin care as it improves performance greatly. This skin care line will enable you to have a much better canvas to use makeup on for older women. I do makeup on older women quite often and one of the biggest problems is not using really good skin care first. This skin care (along with the night cream) will greatly improve the skin so that makeup application will be much nicer and less apt to look caked on. I would say that this is an excellent skin care line for mature skin if you can tolerate the fragrance. WHAT I LIKE ABOUT THIS CREAM Excellent price for what you get Glass jar A little goes a long way It is not sticky Absorbs quickly Differences begin quickly Does what it promises WHAT I DON'T LIKE ABOUT THIS CREAM Fragrance is a bit overbearing. THE BOTTOM LINE I have to say compared to the other lines of skin care that I have tried over the years on myself and on others whose skin I work on, this line of Neovadiol Compensating Complex is a serious contender for performance with good price range compared to high end. I would put it in the same ball park as some of Lancome, Algenist, Dior, SKII, and I find it even better than some Chanel, Shiseido, Clarins, and L'Oreal (although this company appears to have ties with L'Oreal). I really do not like the heavy scent, but I did get used to it. It does not make my eyes water, and it fades away quick enough to be able to use it. For the price vs performance, compared to other lines, I have to say this is a five star, although I am tempted to give it four stars due to the fragrance. If you or someone you know has mature skin this would be a great cream to try out to improve makeup application and skin appearance.
summary: How Does This Compare To Other Lines Of Skin Care For Mature Skin? - A Professional Makeup Artist's Perspective (UPDATE)

reviewText:
For the past few years I have been using skin care products with retinol and other anti-aging properties. They do brighten my skin and give it a younger appearance, but they can be very drying and cause my skin to look flaky.

The Vichy cream is the first moisturizer I've tried that has immediately given my skin a smooth, radiant look. (The dryness would return with a few hours with other moisturizers.) The cream is thick and rich, and a small amount goes a long way. It has a smooth, rich texture that feels nice when I apply it and is absorbed quickly.

I am not thrilled with the scentit's some kind floral and a little too sweet for me. I would prefer a more modern, clean, refreshing scent, but it did fade quickly and didn't linger, so not a problem for me.

I am always thrilled to find a high quality beauty product that is paraben free. And this is the only one I have run across that is formulated for POST menopausal women.  I also love the texture of the cream--silky. As to some of the other youth-i-fy-ing claims, I'm never that convinced with any product. It is certainly as good--and may over time be better--than many I've tried at a higher price.

I should mention that the packaging is nice. It has a subtle feminine aura punctuated with a little shine, a little luxury. I'm not sure, but I think that kind of thing could add to the placebo affect. If nothing more, it looks nice on my makeup counter when I forget to put it back in my makeup drawer.

Vichy is a LOral brand, along with over thirty others. The company has been around for about eighty years so they should know what they're doing by now.

The Neovadiol line is for mature skin and they seem to have finally found something that really works, at least for me.

The cream is silky smooth and I really couldn't detect a fragrance for more than a few minutes. It absorbs quickly and fills in tiny wrinkles.  I don't wear a foundation but it feels like something that would work well under makeup.

My skin is 70+ years old and fairly sensitive to products with lots of perfumes and some additives.  This Vichy did not irritate me at all.  That is a big plus.  It also did not feel at all greasy.  It went on smoothly and left the skin feeling silky - not slick.

I'm really lucky to have good skin thanks to genetics but there comes a time when thinning occurs, no matter what you do.  Like many of the products in the current anti-aging trend, it has a rather high price point so it's important that you're getting what you pay for.  I used the product on the backs of my hands (the real "tell" when it comes to aging skin) and notices smoothing and less creping.  Also, you only use the smallest dab at a time so the 50ml jar will last a long time.

The aroma is neither perfumed nor medicinal - just a fresh smell that won't interfere with your cologne.  All in all I'm pleased.

This is a beautifully presented set of essential oils for your hair and scalp. You get a nice box* that contains twelve tiny (0.12 oz) vials and an applicator.

You are meant to apply one vial to your hair every few days after a shampoo and towel dry. The solution has a lovely smell, botanical and a bit sharp, perhaps rosemary? Some essential oils known to promote hair health are rosemary, cedarwood and clary sage.

reviewText: I have found this PHYTO product to be very effective. I am not a new user of this product but have been very pleased with its results for some time. When I moved out of the metropolitan area where I had purchased this product in high end stores, I never thought I would be able to have regular access to it. I was very pleased to find Amazon now carrying this PHYTO product. There is no doubt in my mind as to its effectiveness but to get maximum results you need to do other things as well. You need to eat a hair healthy diet, reduce stress, and not over process your hair. When you do these things, the PHYTO Phytologist Exclusive Scalp & Hair Concentrate will multiply your good results and make your hair noticeably thicker looking and even arrest hair loss. I am a believer in this product.

An overwhelming number of hair products promise to deliver stronger, silkier hair. Among this me-too! array, PHYTO stands out for its unusual mix of ingredients and mostly for its delivery mechanism, which involves tiny glass vials and a dropper. (I cut the tip off the dropper because I couldn't figure out how to make it work otherwise and could find no directions anywhere...nothing like a scalp tonic to make you feel stupid!) The dropper lets you apply the liquid in the vials to your scalp. Again, not much information on strategy is available, so I freestyled it.

The fragrance is pleasant -- despite the ingredient list, it does not smell like chocolate -- and the product doesn't gunk up my hair. I can well believe that the concentrate is having a positive, albeit subtle effect on my scalp, and also that it might take a few dozen vials and many months before I can determine whether or not it's worth continuing to use.

The little vials are truly adorable and I am trying to figure out a creative destiny for them, as tossing them into the glass recyc would feel almost criminal. Keep in mind that with this product you're getting less than 1.5 ounces total, or about 7/10 teaspoon per application. There's a lot of waste involved, and thus, as fun as it is to play bathroom chemist, I am researching similar products with a less complicated delivery mechanism.

P.S. This tonic is not for the follicly-challenged. The day may come that researchers discover a way to grow back hair where none currently exists, but this is not that product.

reviewText: I have tried a lot of dark spot correctors,  both drugstore and luxe brands, and while my dark spots did fade initially every product eventually stopped working. reviewText: This spot corrector cream really does lighten sun spots and dark scars. I had previously used a different brand spot corrector, that was like a gel in consistency, and it worked great, but the problem was that the gel sat ontop of the skin and took forever to dry. This product is more like a cream in consistency and absorbs quickly. I'm currently using this cream on some red marks left behind by acne and also a red scar on my arm. The cream is definitely lightening both of them. I use the cream twice daily, once in the morning before I put on my face lotion or makeup, and then in the evening after I wash my face. My number one recommendation is just to be consistent and patient. It'll probably take a good 6 months to a year to fully fade a spot. The way I think of it, in a year from now this mark could be gone or it could still be? Which would you choose? Well, I'm going to try and make it go away!  To speed up results, I like to also use a 15% glycolic acid peel.

I like it but to see results you have to RELIGIOUSLY apply it twice a day followed by sunscreen when you are applying it in the daytime or it will be counterproductive!!  I use their Vichy Ideal Soleil 50 spf sunscreen or their Capital Soliel 45 spf Dry Finish  sunscreen (which is a waaay better value as you get 5 oz as opposed to the 1.7 ounces in the spf 50 one) over it. Either are great for sensitive skin (which I have)
Now back to this Dark Spot Corrector cream. It has a nice clean, light scent that dissipates in about 20 minutes. Is on the thin side for a cream and it absorbs quickly into your skin, (*it does NOT sting my sensitive skin at all)
I don't stop at the face but apply it right down to my decolletage area as I have as many dark spots there as on my face. To give this a fair try do be consistent and as long as you apply the sunscreen over it (and reapply the sunscreen as directed, if you are outside for quite awhile) you should definitely see results. With longer usage you will see more improvement and definitely STOP future damage and more dark spots from appearing. I took away a star as they really should sell it in a larger size (with a price break for a quantity purchase) for people wanting to do their entire face and neck area like me,  Mnfr....hint, HINT!!
I know I am not alone....
summary: Works very well IF you use it 2X daily & DON"T forget to use a good sunscreen and repeat the sunscreen as directed if outside!
