reviewText:
I like this moisturizer. It's lightweight, absorbs fast and smells nice. I thought the lightening agent would be retinol or one of the popular acids, mandelic, glycolic etc but it is actually derivative of salicylic acid- beta-lipohydroxy acid.
The LHA is more for acne- ''According to a 2007 study published in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology, LHA works in a similar fashion to salicylic acid. Specifically, LHA decreases the concentration of bacteria found within the pore. LHA has a lipophilic (fat-loving) nature and relatively slow penetration in the skin, which together make it an effective exfoliant, even at low concentrations. The LHA molecule has been found to separate transmembrane glycoproteins at the corneosome/corneocyte interface, cleanly detaching individual corneosomes from one another (European Journal of Dermatology, 2002). Studies have also shown that LHA appears to have antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, anti-fungal and anticomedogenic properties, combating acne and even dandruff.''

Because I already use pretty good skincare items to keep my melasma at bay, I use Vichy gel more of a acne control. Although I'm almost 40 I still have a problems with occasional pimples. This cream made a nice difference and I can honestly say that my skin is clearer. I use it everyday and I don't experience any dryness or redness.

The most effective and fast in getting rid of dark spots were Obagi tretinoin, hydroquinone and TCA acid. After I made my skin even I use night retinol cream at night, vitamin C serum during the day and once a week mandelic, lactic or light TCA peel. My skin looks pretty good. After the summer I saw 1 dark spot on my cheek and I just burn it out with TCA peel.
I use at least SPF30 everyday and during the summer I reapply sunscreen every time I'm going outside or every 1-2 hours if outside, wear hat most of the time.
I have to say that once someone develops melasma it will stay forever, you can only maintain the results. One day without protection in the sun can ruin months of treatments.

Melasma is different than sun spots (age spots, liver spots). Melasma is hormonal induced and sun spots are from sun exposure. Melasma looks like splash of the paint or shadow and sun spots are more even and superficial. Melasma can not be treated with IPL lasre (heat) and sun spots can. The best is go to a doctor and google a little bit.

I hope this will help a bit.

I've been using this for two weeks, primarily on the back of my hands.  I have sun spot damage from way too much time at the beach in my younger days.  I haven't noticed any improvement yet, however, you're supposed to keep using the cream for 8 weeks for results.  So, time will tell.  I tried using it on my face on an area where I also have sun damage, but I broke out with blemishes so I discontinued facial use.  I was surprised, because I don't have sensitive skin.  Also, it took me a while to figure out how to open the tube.  It opens like a tube of glue; remove the cap and prick the foil seal.  I guess I was supposed to know this.

I was initially irritated because the product offered no instruction on how to open the package. Be warned that you can't just take the bottle out of the box and expect it to work. You will need to screw down the applicator so it will punch open a hole.

Once that was accomplished I tried a small amount on my skin. I don't have lots of dark spots on my face, but I do have some on my hands that I would like to eliminate or at least fade. Fortunately, no skin reactions, but also no miracles yet. The changes are said to happen over a longer period of time. I will update as I continue to use.

I am supposed to use this twice a day. Not sure I'm going to do that because I really don't like the scent. Yuck. Way too overpowering for a skin cream. I'd prefer this product have no scent--or go with something much more subtle.

I really liked the way this moisturizer, because in my opinion that's what it is, was absorbed into my skin.  So far as making dark spots get lighter, I can't vouch for that inasmuch as it takes 8 weeks, according to the information on the box, for this to occur.  However, my skin did feel softer after just a few applications of this cream.  I'm not sure if the corrector cream contains any sunscreen but since I applied it after I applied serum, it doesn't make a lot of difference to me.  Just as an aside, I like the subtle fragrance of the product.
summary: Good Moisturizer, Not certakin abot spot removal

reviewText:
My first concern when trying any new product is whether or not it will make me break out. I am happy to report that it has not. This is a very light lotion, but it doesn't take much to cover my face. It moisturizers well but I do use another lotion on top at night. I think my skin looks  brighter but it is too soon to tell how well this will work as to fading spots and evening out skin tone, it takes several weeks to make a noticeable change. This can be worn under makeup.
Also,  when you first take the top off, use a pin to poke a hole in the tube. And squeeze lightly or too much will come out at once.
summary: brightens my skin, doesn't cause breakouts

reviewText:
This cream by Vichy is very light and easily absorbs into the skin. It's not a bleach but a gradual exfoliant, which takes about eight weeks to work. So I am reviewing it now, having used it for a few days and will update this again if this turns out not to be effective. But Vichy makes some excellent products so I have no doubt this will produce the promised results.

As an exfoliant, you might think this would be harsh on the skin but it isn't. It has a light, mild fragrance and is rather thin in consistency but distributes well, nonetheless. It feels very clean when applied and doubles as a moisturizer. It also made my skin feel soft and nourished without being oily or leaving a noticeable residue of product. While you're waiting on the exfoliation of dark spots, this doubles as a really nice moisturizer. So there's that.

You don't need a lot of product with each application (I'm doing once a day at night) so this should hold out for the eight weeks, at which time I will assess and decide whether or not to buy another tube (only one ounce). It's expensive but if it works, it would be worth it.
summary: A little goes a long way, good moisturizing

reviewText: Most of the time I use BB creams instead of foundation, but I just need minimal coverage. Am sure it makes a difference if you are after fuller covering on skin. Nevertheless, this is a light cream that does a great job on my skin. It provides a nice, light moisturization and just enough coverage for me. I really don't reapply it more than once a day, but I'm not out in the sun a lot and it's Autumn here, now, so I don't see a need to use as a sunscreen. I like the light scent. This is the third Vichy product I have tried, and I have to say I've been favorably impressed with all of them. I usually use Lancome, Estee Lauder or Tatcha, but I vary products. I think they work better if you don't stick with one brand for ages.
summary: Vichy Idealia BB Cream Does Nice Job

reviewText:
While I appreciate the magnificent ingredient that go into this product, I find that 1. Mixing moisturizing and cover just doesn't cut it for a 60-year-old with age spots.  There is a product Vichy makes which is a moisturizer for post-menopausal women.  2. While the SPF 25 is impressive, I tend to rub my face and end up with tears running down my cheeks, and the burning stops when I take my makeup off and rest my eyes a bit.

I know it sounds like I do not think this is a good product, but it unfortunately is wrong for me.  I would use it as a moisturizer at best, and take the shine off with Physician's brand mineral pressed powders.

Still, I gave it 4 stars because I believe if it has the good reputation it does in Europe, then there is something to it.  I'd like to try the other post-menopausal moisturizer under my mineral powder.

I believe this product has potential for younger women to take care of their skin so they do not let it become dry, wrinkled and sun-spotted too soon.

I think it is worth a try.  It goes on light and fresh, and a younger woman would likely get a glow.
summary: I know it sounds like I do not think this is a good product

reviewText:
This is the second BB creme I have tried.  I like the idea around these cremes, coverage with spf properties along with some skin brighteners.

The Vichy creme goes on very smoothly and importantly does not burn my sensitive skin at all.  The color (light) will work for many light skin tones from porcelain  to a neutral fair tone.  My skin has some cool undertones and it blended well.  This is moisturizing.  My face felt hydrated and soft.  These are the best features along with the spf.

What I did not like was hiw thus sat in my pores.  This did not minimize them and it sat in fine lines too, seeming to accentuate them.  This overs minimal coverage so I had to use a concealer for some uneven tones in my skin.  Overall a good moosturizer, but I needed to put make up over this product for even coverage and to reduce the appearance of fine lines.
summary: Good moisturizer but not great coverage

reviewText: I'm mid-30's with combo, sometimes very dry skin. I don't wear a lot of makeup, usually just mascara and BB cream. There are a lot of things I like about this BB cream. I love that it has sunscreen. Has a light feeling but also feels moisturizing. It goes on smoothly and melts into skin. Nice texture. Looks beautiful, though this seems light dependent. In certain harsh sunlight it seemed to exacerbate fine lines because of the mica in it. I also didn't like the fragrance which seemed floral to me. Lastly, I think this light color would be best in the dead of winter, for me it was a bit too light with the last hints of tan from summer time. Personally I prefer a mica free(for me this means shiny-free) BB cream but some might really like that quality. I've actually just started using it more as a highlighter with my regular BB cream underneath and that's working well.
summary: 3 1/2 stars: some great things, some downfalls

reviewText: As I said in a previous review, I'm new to Vichy products and so had no idea what to expect as far as quality goes. Idealia fell very flat for me. While the color was a great match and it goes on nicely, I was very disappointed with how it made my skin look and feel. I applied it after moisturizing and even with that, the product seemed to clump, delineating any dry skin areas and making them more noticeable, not less. Someone with oilier skin would probably love this product, and the sunscreen component is nice, but it's definitely not for me.

Vichy Idealia Medium BB Cream is a great beauty product.  It provides good coverage where you need it and leaves your skin feeling silky smooth.  It feels light, never heavy like some foundations and cover ups that can make your skin feel like you just covered your face with frosting.  Also it has SPF 25 to protect your skin in the sun.  It also contains anti-aging antioxidants. Love it.  Recommended it.

I generally have fair complexion except for late spring and summer when I get slightly tanned from working in my garden.  This is the perfect color light foundation for me for those "tanned" times.  Otherwise, it is a little dark.  I still have a bit of tan left over as we have had a fairly sunny fall, so it still looks pretty good on my skin tone at this time.  It provides a light coverage but I still have to use a concealer for any spots or dark circles.  It seems to even my skin tone out otherwise, which works for me.  I have a slight shininess to my skin after putting it on but I use a colorless power to blot that out.

I would not use this everyday because that doesn't fit with my lifestyle but it is great to have it for evenings out.
summary: Sheer coverage and a little darker than I expected in medium

reviewText:
Vichy claims that this BB Cream does 6 things. (1) Illuminates instantly, which it does. Skin appears to glow when even a thin layer of this cream is applied. That's partly due to the titanium dioxide and mica, but whatever the reason, this is the strongest quality of the cream. On the other hand, if you don't like an illuminated look, you'll definitely want to avoid it. (2) Hydrates. I think it does, but my skin is so dry that I moisturize a lot before applying. Probably the best test is at the end of the day at which point my skin still feels moist. (3) Visibly smooths fine lines. At the very least it doesn't emphasize fine lines, which some makeups do. (4) Pores look refined. I have small pores already, but I'd say this BB Cream minimizes them further. (5) Conceals dark spots. I get no concealing effect AT ALL. None. So, for me, it utterly fails on this claim. (6) UVA/UVB protection. This claim is absolutely true. The significant amounts of chemical sunscreens that give this an SPF 25 rating have prevented any suntan or sunburn every time I've worn it. Unfortunately, on the two occasions that I applied it near my eyes, the sunscreens ran into my eyes and stung for over an hour. So, I'd say this Vichy Idealia BB Cream delivers on 5 of its 6 claims.

Here's where the problems lie. (1) The color range is stunningly narrow. There are only two colors as far as I've been able to discover, the Light and the Medium. I tried both. Neither of them worked for me. So, I combine the two and get a reasonable shade for my light skin. (2) The cream has a fragrance. A lot of reviewers both here and on MakeupAlley say that they like the scent. I don't. But it isn't so strong that I can't stand it. Over a short time, it fades. (3) There is no coverage. I get a bit of skin "treatment" and a nice glow from this, but my dark undereye circles and few broken capillaries are not camouflaged. If the coverage were stronger, the too-light Light and the too-dark Medium shades would really be a problem. (4) There is no way I can use this anywhere near my eyes. The runny texture and the chemical sunscreens make this impossible to wear either on my upper lids or undereye area. The eye area is where I need foundation most, so I use a foundation like Dermablend cream or L'Oreal True Match around my eyes and use this BB Cream on my cheeks and jawline. So, instead of making my makeup routine quicker and easier, this adds a step.

Finally, I'm impressed that the formulation includes some really interesting ingredients. I am especially intrigued by the Saccharomyces/xylinum/black tea ferment.
summary: If you want illumination and have light to medium skin tone, this is a good BB Cream

reviewText: The medium color is quite dark, darker than I expected. The cream is light in texture, and I love the smell. It is very easy to apply. It does even out skin tone a little bit, but not much, I still have to use concealer. It does not seem to cause irritation as many other products do, I have sensitive skin with rosacea. It does not seem to help with oiliness, but it does not make it worse, either.

The consistency is a little thicker than I like for a face cover.  I am guessing that it is due to the SPF sun protection which is a good thing, but it means I have to thin the product to get the look I want.  It is also a little lighter than I was expecting for a medium -- being too light for my face with the remains of a summer tan.
summary: A little thicker and lighter in tone than I prefer

reviewText: It goes on easily. I like the squeeze tubes that are stored upside down for these sorts of things. It is very light coverage and I wouldn't say one application will last all day long. However, it isn't greasy like some other BB creams I've tried or chalky. I'd use this again as just a bit a pick me up to the skin.

The great thing about BB Creams is that for one product, its multi function. In Vichys case, the product claims to:
illuminates instantly - yes
hydrates - yes (but not heavy)
visibly smoothes fine lines - no
pores look refined - yes
conceals dark spots - no
UVA/UVB protection SPF 25

In order for my skin to look better and more concealed, I had to brush on face powder. Otherwise, the BB Cream didn't produce a noticeable difference. How does Vichys product compare to other brands Ive tried like Clinique and Mary Kay? For me, its the same.
summary: Works Just As Well As the Others

reviewText: Just as a little background:  I usually use Neutrogena tinted moisturizer/sunscreen in light/medium for everyday -- I don't work and just use the tinted moisturizer as foundation.  The Neutrogena costs about $20 for a tube these days, which I thought was a little high.  The Vichy Idealia BB Cream SPF 25-Light is something of a higher end product and costs a bit more.  I found that the Light was a shade of pink/porcelain and thinner than the Neutrogena, which is about the weight of a heavier cream.  Even though I am very fair, the Vichy Light was too pale for me and I ended up combining it with the Neutrogena so I wouldn't look completely washed out and I really didn't trust the SPF factor because the cream was so thin.  I think that for me, sticking with the Neutrogena light/medium is the way to go.  If you are in between shades, maybe using the Vichy BB Cream mixed with something else would work.

I have been using a competitors BB cream, and I have liked the results. These foundation-creams seem to lie on top of the skin, masking wrinkles. Ordinary foundations seem to accentuate the wrinkles by sinking into them.

This particular BB cream has a higher SPF, 25. That is good, because the suns rays can accelerate to wrinkle formation. The only problem is that this foundation must be kept away from the eyes, because it does irritate eyes and burn. This creates a problem for women like me, who apply foundation to the eyelids and under-eye area, in order to create a more uniform canvas with which to work.

This cream does seem to nourish the skin, making it softer. It blends easily, providing a light, glowing, healthy coverage. It seems to last much of the day, and it is comfortable to wear and non-drying.
summary: Nice Multi-Purpose Skin Treatment: Foundation, Moisturizer, Sunnscreen All in One!

reviewText: This is a nice, light-weight BB cream, though not my favorite (I prefer Kiehl's BB cream).  I can't speak to the sun protection capability since it's autumn, not summer here and we haven't spent oodles of time outside, but it does provide a light coverage & moisturize. One thing I did notice which I did NOT like was that it seems to darken my skin around my upper lip, which is weird. So, I took off a star for that.  I'm not overpowered by this product's performance, but it's adequate. The reason I prefer Kiehl's (which is very pricey) is because it does something indefinable to my skin which has elicited comments as to how nice my skin looks and I haven't had such comments while using this product.

Vichy Laboratories V Idealis BB Cream is marketed as one cream that has 6 benefits.  The benefits are instant illumination, hydration, smooth lines are smoothed, pores are refined, dark spots are concealed, and last but not least, UV sun protection.

This cream comes in a lovely rose colored squeeze tube and smells beautiful.  There is a fragrance to it.  The directions are only for sunscreen use.  Apply fifteen minutes before you go into the sun, etc. I use this cream as a light, lovely scented base.  I dab a bit of loose powder over it and go.  It does illuminate my skin and makes my face feel great.

The tube is only 1.3 ounces but a little dab goes a long way.  It's a nice, light base for my skin that also works as a sunscreen.  Win win!
summary: Light Base That is Used as a Sunscreen

reviewText: Vichy BB cream is light and stays on very nicely. This BB is also very moisturizing and the SPF rating of 25 is pretty high for a BB cream. This is probably better for lighter to medium skin tones, but it's very thin so it may not matter too much. If you're looking for a thicker cream with more concealing power though, you'll be disappointed. Try something else in that case.
summary: Light and thin and moisturizing. Good if you need minimal coverage

reviewText:
I like everything about this except the price, which is why I gave it four stars instead of five.

It has an SPF of 25.  It combines chemical sunscreens such as Homosalate and Octisalate with physical sunscreen, titanium dioxide.
The tube dispenses a very fine line of product so you can precisely control how much you use.
The product goes on very smoothly and feels very good and moisturizing on the skin.
Coverage is pretty decent for a BB cream.  I put some on the back of one hand and compared with the other.  The hand with the product felt moisturized and softened for several hours. Freckles were slightly covered.

This cream has sparkles in it that are very apparent in the sun but not in shade.  You may or may not be OK with that.  I'm not sure whether the sparkles have something to do with the sun protection or are intended to have a light dispersion/cosmetic effect.

The medium shade that I received is more toward the golden sand end of the spectrum than the pinky beige.  Works well for me personally.  I think of myself as more fair than medium but the medium shade of this cream was fine for me.
The scent is noticeable but pleasant, mildly rose-floral.  Not a problem for me and I am very sensitive about fragrances.
I really like this quite a lot.  Too bad it costs so much.
summary: Quite like everything about this except the price.

reviewText: I'm surprised how much I like this facial cream. I normally find face creams that contain sunscreens very heavy and thick. That is definitely not the case with this product. It is very light yet still hides skin imperfections beautifully, while actually smoothing the skin, rather than emphasize wrinkles. I also often have a problem with creams like this drying my face out once it's washed off -- again, not the case. This Vichy cream apparently contains a good moisturizer, as my face was not dry at all once the cream was washed away. I'm very pleased with this product and will definitely purchase in the future.

Hmm. It is my understanding that BB creams are supposed to be a replacement for foundation, sunscreen and moisturizer all-in-one.  This cream just says it's for sunscreen on the label.  It has little to no discernible tint.  So as a sunscreen it works fine.  It goes on nice and smooth and does provide light moisturizing.  I don't liked the scent, it is strong and musky.  Needs improvement.

Though I use beauty products, I really don't know too much about them. I go by ratings and price most the time. So I had no idea what a BB cream was until I looked it up. Essentially, a BB cream is a moisturizer with added skin care benefits. It's tinted as well, and says it conceals imperfections, but in my opinion, it's really not thick enough to hide much.

However, it feels good on the skin. It has a nice scent. If you're sensitive to fragrance, you may want to choose something else.

The added qualities include antioxidant Vitamin E,  which is an anti-aging formula, 100% mineral pigments and pearl pigments, fortifying and soothing Vichy Thermal Spa Water. It's paraben-free, non-acnegenic. non-comedogenic (these all sound like made-up words to me, but what do I know), allergy-tested and made for people with sensitive skin.

Honestly, I hate the cost of beauty products. I'm not sure I would pay the $29 price tag for this, but if you're willing, it is a nice product.

I am meticulous about applying sunscreen, even in the winter.  I like products that serve multiple purposes, like this one.

Why I like this product:

* It goes on smoothly.

* It has SPF of 25.  I find products with 15 SPF don't provide enough protection.  The sunscreen ingredients:  homosalate (6%), octisalate (5%), octocrylene (7%) and titanium dioxide (3.75%).

* It is tinted, so it makes my skin look smooth and polished.

A big negative for me though was the strong scent of this product.  It is strong and it is very artificial.  I found it quite unpleasant after a while, especially since its on my face and close to my nose.  I gave up using this product because of that.  It is funny how scent is so personal.  Other reviewers remarked on the very light scent.  I am not usually so sensitive to scents, but this scent was very unpleasant for me.
summary: Goes on smoothly but has a very strong scent

reviewText: Nice tinted BB cream; light and blends well. It has subtle coverage and left a semi matte finish on my skin which I love. I did not however care for the scent; why cosmetic companies put fragrance in their products is a mystery to me. I would recommend this product except for the price. I feel there are plenty of drug store alternatives for less.

This is pretty much as described--a light cream with "fair" pigment and sunscreen. It's pretty sheer, so the fact that there aren't a lot of colors to choose from isn't a problem. It isn't going to cover as much as real makeup, but it does offer some nice evening. It's not irritating (and I get easily irritated by skin products!)

The only issues are pretty minor. It does leave my skin rather shiny, so requires some powder to look finished. And, of course, it isn't remotely sweat-proof, so if I wind up unexpectedly exerting myself, it gets a bit messy. But any tinted make up is like that.

Overall, recommended. I will happily keep using it, and consider purchasing more.

I've tried many other BB creams and have a favorite that I use everyday.  Vichy is a new product for me.  This product doesn't measure up to others I've used.  Most BB creams blend into the skin providing moisture, sun protection and minimal coverage.  I found Vichy to be heavily pigmented and the medium shade is much darker than other products.  This product didn't blend in and looked blotchy and much too dark on my skin.  I would not recommend it.
summary: Many better BB creams are out there!

reviewText: I ordered the Micro Singlepass Straightening & Styling iron because I have a natural wave/curl to my hair. Which of course I dislike. I really need something that will straighten and calm down the frizzies when humid (which is all the time here in the Midwest). The straightening iron/wand worked beautifully and gave my hair a wonderful shine while straightening all the natural flips & waves. I haven't tried using the curling iron part yet, but I'm confident it will perform wonderfully too.

Included with this one inch straightening iron is a heat resistant pad to rest the device on while styling along, a clearly written User guide, and two hair clips. There are five temperature settings which range from low  260 degrees Fahrenheit to the highest settings 410 degrees. It is recommended that thin or damaged use the low setting. There is also a guide for how slow to move the iron through the sections, again dependent upon the thickness of the hair.

The power cord swivels where attached to the iron so nothing gets tangled up as the iron is turned. The guide for how much hair to straighten with one pass is visually provided  it should be no thicker than the iron plate and no wider than the same plate. Two clips are included to keep portions of hair out of the way while straightening lower sections. Start at the bottom and do the top last.

I followed the instructions for thin hair although my hair is more medium in quantity and thin in texture. It is curly but not intensely so and it usually will yield to a straightening iron on the occasions when I use one. I selected the lowest setting, which is still quite hot at 260 degrees.

This device is advertised as a one-pass iron and I was interested to see if it lived up to the claim. Again, following the User Guide it was suggested that I pass hair through the heated plates at two to three inches per second. So, counting the seconds off as I glided through I ended up with absolutely straight hair. It worked beautifully without issue.

My only quibble is that the controls are not intuitive but after using it once or twice the process becomes automatic. Press the power/temperature switch until the five tiny LED lights begin to cascade while the iron heats up.

When the lights glow steady double click the power/temperature button again until the lights flash then cycle through the temperatures. Let up on the button when the desired temperature is reached. The light will flash on that setting but wait for it to glow steady before using the iron. To turn off the iron press the power button and hold until all the lights go off.

The housing is smooth so hair cannot get caught in crevices or rough edges which is a problem Ive had with other flat irons. The ceramic plate size is small but it made it easier for me to position the iron but it did take a bit more time to complete the job.

The cord swivels where connected to the iron to prevent it getting wrapped around and tangled up. It is about eight and a half feet long which provides plenty of length no matter the location of the electrical outlet or whether using on yourself or styling someone elses hair. The electrical system adapts to worldwide voltage automatically which is a convenience if one travels internationally. There is also a built-in one hour shut-off.

Pleased with its performance.
summary: T3 Micro Single Pass Straightening and Styling Iron

reviewText:
I absolutely hate straightening my hair. I don't like doing anything with my hair and most of the time I just wash it and let it air dry because I hate spending time and energy on it. This straight iron may help change that. I waited until my hair was dry (the instructions say to use it on dry hair) and then followed the directions for fine hair. I was pleasantly surprised by how quickly this straightened my hair. This straightener also comes with clips to section your hair and a little felt pad to rest the hot tool on.
The reason I am giving this product 4 stars instead of 5 is that the heated part is only 4 inches long, instead of being spread along the entire length of the straightener, which would have straightened my hair even faster.

This is an okay straightener. It warms up pretty quickly, it goes smoothly thru my hair and is fairly light weight. It also comes with good directions and professional style hair clips to section off your hair while styling it.

That being said, it doesn't do as good a job as other straighteners that I've used (Bedhead and Chi are the two I use most frequently). I have fine hair that is curly and frizzes easily, so it isn't too much of a challenge to straighten normally. I wouldn't suggest this for hair that is really difficult to straighten as it just doesn't seem powerful enough for that.

This is a very nice straightening iron right from the get go. I have thick wavy hair, so I first used the lowest setting. The iron heated up really quick and the lowest setting did indeed straighten my wavy hair. I think to add curl I would need the higher setting. I like the quality of the iron it seems very well made, and looks sleek. It comes with a pad to rest it on to protect your counter top. It is expensive, so beware of that but so far it does seem worth the money. The iron works very well, looks nice and heats up so fast. I feel it is well worth the price, and in the end it straightens very well very quickly.

I love this straightener!  It does a very nice job and my hair stays smooth. I like that it has adjustable temperature settings and I found it to be very comfortable to hold. I am not sure why, but I tend to burn myself with some other straighteners but I didn't have that problem here.  I also found that my hair doesnt feel as hot.  All in all it is a great product

If you hate frizz and want nice smooth hair, this is for you.  Regardless of hair texture, you will find that this flat iron aka frizz buster will smooth your hair and leave it with a pleasant look and feel.

With this you get an instruction guide and 2 hair clips to section off your hair as  you straighten and/or style it.  You can adjust it from 260 F  - 410 F based on your needs.

The thicker your hair, the higher the settings you might want to use.  Be sure to straighten no more than the recommended amount per second.  You will be amazed at how lovely and smooth your hair will feel.

Excellent product.  I highly recommend this one.

The iron heats up to the highest setting in just one minute. I gather it would be even faster for lower settings. The white outside is all plastic and so is the golden part. The cord is longer than usual, and it is really nice, I didn't realize how restrictive 6 ft cord feels until I tried the T3. The cord also swivels easily so I do not have to worry that it will tangle, and I do not have to fight with tangled up cord. The ceramic area is very smooth and it works perfectly, but it is on the smaller size, about 1 inch by 4 inches, so it is great for shorter hair, but it would be too little for longer hair that needs a lot of work.

The iron looks very stylish. They include a heat proof mat, but it is quite small, and black, looks like it is made of dense felt. It looks OK on my very dark brown vanity, but it just not as pretty as the iron itself.

I checked out the warranty on the iron, and they say for the warranty the iron has to be purchased from an authorized retailer, and it has to have a silver sticker with the serial number. The problem is that the sticker is located on the box, not on the iron itself, so if you throw the box away you might be in trouble if something goes wrong. It also looks like in case of warranty claim you will have to send the iron to them first before they will evaluate it and decide if they replace it, and it should take 3 weeks. I am not comfortable with this kind of customer care for such an expensive luxury product.

This is an elegant hair straightener. I wasn't able to get it to curl or wave my hair, but that wasn't a problem for me.  Maybe with more practice.  I was able to get it to be stick straight and that's why I ordered this.
My hair is no more shiny with this straightener than with others, but I loved using it.  The hair clips are well padded and sturdy and hold my hair in place while I work on other areas.

I got this for my wife who has medium length hair that curls a lot more than she cares. She likes the resting pad, clips(2) and swivel cord (avoid tangling). As with many products, one pass is possible if you have thin hair, hair is not too curly and you go slow  which of course takes time. She did not notice any real time saving with this.

4 stars overall  it works, but only a portion of the wand is heated and the temperature controls are tricky to get at the desired level. She likes it and will continue to use it.

To start, I do love how well this works for making waves in my hair. I had a wave wand a few years ago and it never worked as well as this one does. This wand gets super hot, and it curls my better than my other wand ever did. It does come with a full size glove (not just a partial finger glove) for using while styling, and also a pad for sitting the styler on so you don't burn your counter top. The tip of the curling wand is a good size so you have plenty of room for your fingers so you don't burn yourself. It heats up quickly and the power cord has a swivel end, so you don't get tangled up when curling with it. This T3 Micro comes with just a single tapered barrel. There are additional straight barrels and clip barrels made for this T3 Micro and they are interchangeable with this wand, but before deciding on which to buy, you may also want to check the price of the T3 Whirl Trio, which comes with all three barrels. If you're wanting all the styling wand barrels, it may be more cost effective to buy the full set together in the T3 Trio. But if you're just wanting the T3 with the tapered barrel, then this one has you covered. It's an outstanding curling wand and I'm planning on ordering a clip barrel to go with it, to replace my curling iron.
summary: Loving the waves I can get with this, but check out the T3 Trio if you're planning on buying any additional barrels

reviewText: Makin' waves. My daughter asked me to grab this for her, she has beautiful hair, but it's straight as a pin. She uses a curling iron, but she wanted to give this wand a try because she wants waves, not curls. It took a couple tries, but she finally found the heat setting wanted and how to use the wand to get the waves she wants.

TLDR; Great for short hair little pricey

My partner and I recently donated our hair meaning we got at least 12" off; she had about 16" taken out and had it substantially thinned. Its now a couple inches past shoulder length. She absolutely loves this style wand now. When she had thick luxurious mid back length hair, (she's mostly mexican with some african american in there and would get "offers" on her hair consistently) she hated wand style curlers. Whether its this brand works that much better or her hair length, we can't be totally sure, but we do know the lighter and shorter hair makes the cone shape so much easier to deal with. No more fussing to keep hair on there and coming out with under curled hair.

I went to get her a different barrel for it and was a little shocked by the price. While we are big fans of how smooth and shiny the hair comes out and how great the curls look because of this product, both the overall price and the alternate barrel prices seem a little high. Make sure you use the glove! I thought I didn't need it, and as a result things got little hotter than I would have wanted. Also were pretty sure from using that if you have long, thick hair, you will have the same problems with this one that we have had with other ones and will end up very very very unhappy. Maybe they should start putting a little spindle on the end!??! Either way with short hair, were now fans!

This curling iron has a tapered barrel but the device is convertible so it can be switched out and other barrel sizes/styles are available for purchase separately adding to the functionality. This particular configuration is the one I was looking for  something that creates casual beachy waves rather than consistently sized obvious curls.

My hair is already curly and although I usually let it be what it is, there are occasions when I either use a flat iron or a curling wand in an attempt to create a more controlled style. And, although this is different from my old curling iron (no clip to hold hair in place) that was the point of using this style  loose and casual. There is no danger of ironing an unattractive ridge from the clip on the iron in my hair. It didn't take long to master the technique with this curling iron, and I got the natural look I wanted.

I started at the lowest setting (260 degrees Fahrenheit) with the assumption I could always increase the heat to one of the remaining four higher settings (300 to 410 degrees). The included User Guide illustrated the correct position to hold the iron  with my left hand holding the handle, reaching over my head with the end pointing down. With my right hand (wearing the glove) I wrapped my hair around the barrel and held it there a few seconds before moving on to another section.

The heat level should be adjusted depending upon the texture and thickness of the hair. Adjusting the temperature is not intuitive but operation of the power/selector button is clearly explained in the Guide. To avoid frustration read and follow the steps. After a couple of uses it becomes automatic. My hair is finely textured and medium thickness. Since it is already curly, it is reasonably responsive to curling. I wasn't fighting board straight hair which would require a different setting. The areas around my face that tend to frizz were tamed into shiny waves.

Besides the User Guide, included is a heat proof glove to ensure the hand wrapping the hair does not accidentally get burned by coming in contact with the barrel there is also a heat-proof mat to rest under the end of the iron. There are small built-in plastic feet which act as a stand to keep the iron, when at rest, above the counter top. There is also a heat-proof pad included which worked well on the counter under the heated end.

The power cord swivels where attached to the iron so nothing gets tangled up as the iron is turned. It is also nine feet long which allows ample length to hold the iron over the top of the head whether sitting or standing or where the outlet is located  also a necessity if doing the hair of another person. The electrical system adapts to worldwide voltage automatically which is a convenience if one travels internationally. There is also a built-in one hour shut-off.

The housing is well constructed and completely smooth without anything to catch or tangle in the hair, unlike some curling irons Ive used. For people who change their hair style frequently, the flexibility offered by use of the additional sizes of barrels is a plus. For my use, this style is perfect as is.
summary: T3 Micro Whirl Convertible Styling Wand

reviewText:
This product looks beautiful. It's sleek and modern, but you shouldn't buy it.  The barrel doesn't open, so you wrap your hair around it and it gets very hot.  So hot, that I burned myself using it, despite following directions.  I prefer styling wands that open where you curl your hair around the barrel.
Nothing holds your hair in place as you turn it and it keeps slipping.
This found its way into my trash bin after the first use.

T3 Whirl Convertible - my family put this through the paces.  Sadly as a grown man I am at the phase of my life with declining hair follicles - thus I no longer have my Fabio locks to actually use this styling wand (and I would have back in the day ;p.  Luckily my beautiful wife and 9 year old daughter both have fabulous long flowing hair so they have been able to put this T3 Whirl to the test.

First off let's address the elephant in the room - price.  This T3 Whirl current price is $185 - a perusal of current Amazon Best Selling ranking of "Curling Irons & Wands" shows the bulk of the best sellers in the $20-$30 range (see url directly below).  This T3 Whirl shows as  the 123rd best seller in this category as of today.  My family has generally used the $20-$30 curling irons (aka styling wands in the past).
http://www.amazon.com/Best-Sellers-Beauty-Hair-Curling-Irons-Wands/zgbs/beauty/11058251#1

So for the price what is better?  The general consensus from the ladies in my house is the T3 does produce quicker curls that are longer lasting...and since nobody ever seems to be ready to go on time there is a value to that.  In terms of usability - we found the T3 easy to learn - watching the online video tutorial is highly recommended (especially for those not adult age).  Once learned it is easy.  The ceramic barrel does get hot - hence wearing the included safety glove is mandatory and you'll be fine.

In terms of T3 interchangeable barrels - it wasn't so quick for me to find out what the usefulness of each barrel was (and at current price of $85 per extra interchangeable barrel this info is important).  The Amazon listing has a comparison chart currently listed for T3 whirl but the tapered barrel wasn't currently included in the info from what I could tell.  I did find the tapered barrel info under the T3 Whirl Trio Amazon product llsting - url directly below.
http://www.amazon.com/T3-Whirl-Trio-Interchangeable-Styling/dp/B00MUB9IXC/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1447078934&sr=8-1&keywords=T3+styling+wand

The description there related to Tapered Barrel says "1.25 - 0.75 inch Tapered Barrel Ideal for:"
 - Beachy waves
 - Textured waves & curls
 - Loose, tousled curls
 - Natural-looking waves

We didn't have the other barrels to try so we can't comment on how different the curls are.  Actually I don't even know what "beachy (beatchy?) waves" are unless they are the kind I surf on - but as I mentioned previously my wife & daughter are happy with the curl results they get from this T3 Whirl.

Another thing I noted in learning about this product is the alternate product offering on Amazon T3 Whirl Trio is basically this same product but with 3 barrels instead of 1 and currently priced at $230.  From what I see each extra barrel currently sells for $85.  So T3 Whirl Trio is a much better deal if you are the kind of person that really knows your "beatchy curls" vs your "mermaid waves" or even your "red carpet glamour waves".

So to summarize - in our experience this T3 whirl does produce better curls faster which is good since it costs more than the typical competition.  It's easy to learn how to use if you watch the online tutorial and wear the included glove to reduce burn risks.  At current price of $185 this is 6x pricier than typical curling irons on the market but that's worth it to some people for the better/quicker results.  If you are a curls expert and plan to add more wands get the Trio set and save yourself some money.  Overall I rate T3 Whirl 4-STARS in consideration of price/value.
summary: More expensive but does deliver faster/better curls...

reviewText:
Overall, I'm happy to add this wand to my styling tools, and I think it will be my go-to curling tool. For reference, my hair is shoulder blade length, not too thick, mostly straight with a little wave and some tendency to frizz. This produced lovely beachy waves, truly similar to what I see when I've let my hair dry in a bun at the beach, but smoother and shinier.

My only disappointment was the tendency for the waves to fall out quite a bit over the first couple of hours. Perhaps using a strong hairspray rather than a sea salt spray would hold more (though I think I'd like it less) as well as using maximum heat, though I felt setting 4 out of 5 should be adequate for my hair texture.

The shape of a curling wand really lends itself to a natural looking style and getting more of the length of my hair in contact with the barrel. Yes, you have to wrap your hair around and hold the tips in place, so there's more risk of a burn if you aren't careful. The glove protects well, though it made it harder me to deal with the hair, so I tend to take my chances without it. The technique is different than a curling iron, but I didn't find it too difficult to master.

For the money, you're getting a beautiful and high quality instrument. The ability to change out the barrel for other styles will be valuable to some, if it's worth paying for more; I'll stick to this one. I think the ceramic and tourmaline really contribute to shininess. I also like the ability to select a temperature. If you have never used a wand, I'd suggest starting with something lower cost to see if you like using this shape of wand. But if you're ready to invest in a great one, I have no cautions about this selection.

This wand heats up fast and gets really hot.  You can change the temperature (5 heat settings) which is a nice feature.  You can interchange the top "wand" portion with other wands of differing widths and curling barrels (these convertible pieces are purchased separately).  Attaching and detaching the wand is easy (you twist and pull) however you'll want to wait until the wand is cool before you do this (unless you are wearing a glove).  That is the one downside to convertible styling tools vs. having several stand-alone styling tools.  If you want to use a different curling styling tool, you'll have to switch the top and wait a minute for it to heat up (not the end of the world but when you're in a hurry - who wants to wait?).

Yes, the price is rather intimidating however if you've ever purchased professional grade hair styling tools then you know that they don't come cheap.  My current wand cost $160 (Enzo Milano) and did not have a temperature feature nor was it convertible.  I think this curling wand is better than the one I already own.

This tool creates beautiful curls.  It appears to be very well made.  The longevity of the product of course can only be assessed through time but on the surface, it appears to be very well made.  I like that it has an auto shut off in case I forget to turn it off in the morning.

The T3 Micro Whirl Convertible Styling Wand with Interchangeable Tapered Barrel gives you the option of switching out various sized and styles of wands to obtain different styles of curls, but comes with a tapered barrel that allows you to create loose curls/waves (you have to buy the others, and it can get expensive considering the price of this piece). The tapered barrel arrives separate from the base, and it did take a little effort to attach it. Once in, it is a solid curling iron, and you also receive a silicon pad to rest the curling iron on and a glove to protect your hand since you wrap the hair around the wand and have to hold it in place.
You adjust the heat to the desired setting (included instructions tell you how and recommendations for hair thickness/brittleness). You wrap an inch or so section of a time around the wand with it pointing downward - I didn't use the glove and didn't burn any fingers (did feel some heat though) and while doing the back of the hair is a bit tricky, must say it did turn out lovely and the boyfriend adores the results. Some curls are almost spiral, but on the whole (my hair is almost to the middle of the back, fine but lots of it) yes, it's a nice, loose, curly wave.
This is not a cheap curling iron but the results are impressive and its smaller size not to mention you can break it down means it'll be easier to take while traveling.
summary: love the results with this iron

reviewText: This is a beautiful styling wand. Even the box it comes in is beautiful. If your hair will work with the barrel that comes with the wand, then you are in luck. However, if you need a different barrel to make your hair curly, then you have to go out and buy it/them. Then it becomes a little pricey. In fact, the basic unit itself seems pricey to me. The unit come with a glove to protect your hand while you wind it around the barrel. Be sure to use it to avoid burns. It does get hot - almost too hot. There is no clip thing to hold your hair onto the wand, so your hair may slip off until you get the knack. Overall I am ok with this unit, but I doubt I will purchase any of the extra barrels because they are so pricey. Also the fact that the unit gets so hot is a minus for me. Hence, I only rate this at 3 stars.
summary: This is a beautiful styling wand

reviewText:
The curling iron is made of two parts that you are supposed to connect, and you can buy and connect different barrels. Unfortunately, mine broke when I was trying to connect the two pieces. The barrel part that goes inside cracked when I tried to lock it. Now there is a big crack along the part of the barrel that goes inside of the handle. It is all plastic in there, and apparently, it cracks way too easy. I called the company - they hung up after a few minutes of wait. I went online, and was able to write to them from there. It says I will receive a response within two business days, but they are still silent. To get warranty repair or replacement you need to have the serial number which is conveniently located on the outside of the box and nowhere else, so you can inadvertently throw it away and possibly be left without warranty. The website states that for warranty you have to have the silver sticker with the serial number still attached, they do not specify what is it supposed to be attached to, though. The website also states that if your product is going to be replaced under warranty, you should send it to them first (it does not say who will pay for it), and they will mail you another one withing three weeks.  I seriously dislike all this kinds of tricks.
Aside from being broken now, the iron looks very attractive. The cable is long and swivels easily so it will not be tangled up with use. To exchange barrels, you most definitely have to wait until the one you were using cools down, which probably means you are not going to use two different barrels to make the same hairdo.

This T3 MICRO TWIRL CONVERTIBLE CURLING IRON comes with a 1.25" straight barrel with clip that is suitable for creating glamor waves, tailored waves, or volume with curl in very long hair.  (The included barrel is totally unsuited for use with my short hair and bangs.)

The handle can be used with any of four other available barrels (currently priced at $85 each on Amazon).  For classic, full length, bouncy and defined curls, you need the 1" straight barrel with clip.  For bombshell, full-bodied, sexy-style waves, you need the 1.5" straight barrel.  For uniform spiral curls, or mermaid or defined waves, you need the 1" straight barrel.  For beachy, textured, natural-looking waves, you need the 1.25"-0.75" tapered barrel.  The barrels are easy to insert, and are locked in by a sliding ring at the top of the handle.  The barrel clicks when properly locked into place.  The locking ring has "padlock" markings that indicate whether the barrel is locked (for use) or unlocked (for removal and swapping of barrels).

WARNING:  This curling iron heats up really, really fast!  Being unfamiliar with curling irons, I burned my fingers by briefly touching the barrel (accidentally) before the LED lights stopped flashing to signal that the barrel was heated and ready for use.  Unfortunately for me, this Twirl Convertible model does NOT come with the heat-resistant protective glove that is included with some other models.  Because of the high temperatures achieved, this appliance should be kept under lock and key in households with children.

There are five temperature settings, ranging from 260 degrees F. (for damaged or chemically treated hair) to 410 degrees F. (for normal to thick hair).  It's easy to change the settings by double-clicking the power switch and then clicking to cycle through the LED lights indicating the temperature settings.  To turn the curling iron off, you hold down the power switch until the LED lights go out. (Oddly, the instructions do not say how to turn the appliance off.)

Using the curling iron requires holding the handle upside down over your head, and then wrapping a strand of hair around the barrel by holding the end of the strand with your other hand.  Some manual dexterity is definitely required!

The curling iron has a built-in stand--flat projections on the top of the handle and the tip of the barrel--that allows it to be placed on a level surface.  Also included is a pad that is probably intended to further protect any table or countertop when the curling iron is set down on the stand.  This is a good thing, because the stand is clumsy to use--the curling iron has to be placed "just so" for the stand to keep the hot barrel off the level surface. There is an auto shutoff feature that turns the curling iron off after one hour.

This is a beautiful curling iron, one that works fast and creates nice waves.  However, because the stand is clumsy and there is no protective heat-resistant glove included, I rate it at 4 stars ("I like it" on the official Amazon scale).
summary: Heats Really Fast; Included Barrel Is Suitable for Creating Relaxed Waves in Very Long Hair

reviewText:
This is quite a nice curling iron.  It seems to be well constructed and is an attractive appliance.  The colors are white with copper-ish colored trim.  I expect the copper color to definitely wear off with frequent use, but for starts it's the loveliest curling iron I've ever seen.  And I guess it should be for $185.00.  I have several curling irons and brushes stuffed under my bathroom sink right now and none of them compare to this one.  The clip that holds hair against the heated barrel is strong and the clip must be opened to release hair once it's been curled.  You will not be able to easily pull it out without losing some hair so be sure to open it again.

The various 5 heat settings are really nice to have and are very easy to set.  I don't like it very hot but my daughter has very tough hair and needs to use the highest heat setting.  The T3 Micro Twirl Convertible Curling Iron comes (I believe because it's not quite super clear) with a straight 1.25 barrel but you can purchase different sizes of barrels.

It heats up fast and they include a black pad to rest the hot barrel on when you lay it down on your bathroom countertop.  I think that was a very nice extra since it could possibly damage it if it was really hot.  The tip of the barrel does not heat up so you can hold it with your bare fingers if you need too.  Still be careful though, because you have less than an inch of "cool tip" to hold onto.  The cord is nice an long and should give you plenty of room to work especially if you only have one electrical outlet and have to share the counter space with someone.  And the cord swivels from the end so getting your cord all curled up shouldn't be a problem.  It also has a 1-hour automatic shut off (which I admit, I haven't tested yet).

It's got a nice weight too.  It might get your arm tired for a while until you get used to it.  The instructions are well written with good diagrams so even if you don't read English you can still understand it, but then I guess you won't understand this review lol. I expect this curling iron to last me for YEARS since it's so pricey.  Hopefully, I will never have to purchase another one.  I like this curling iron a LOT but am only giving it 4 stars for now.  I have to give something like this some time to see how it holds up and then I will come back and update this review.
summary: T3 Micro Twirl Convertible Curling Iron

reviewText:
This is quite a hair styling tool! I love the idea of a convertible tool with attachments. The large barrel that came with the curling iron was excellent for long beachy waves. It heats up very quickly, has a smooth clamp, and is very easy to maneuver. I also appreciate that it came with a hot pad for it to lay on. It is a big curling iron (even the base unit).

The only reason for one star off is the cost. I think it is overpriced at $185, especially since it doesn't not come with additional attachments.

This is one of the nicest beauty appliances I've ever seen. Even at luxury price points, many items are purely functional and one can't wait to stash them away in a drawer to eliminate visual clutter in a bathroom or dressing area. This little beauty of a beauty tool, however, you'll wanna leave out. It's just that nice looking, and shouldn't tools we use to enhance our appearance inspire that goal? Aside from its good looks, it's very ergonomically designed. It has a comfortable balance in the hand, the lever has a perfectly tuned resistance, and there's nothing your hair can catch on during use. This makes curling your hair a very slick and sleek operation. It's simply a pleasure to use.

According the manual, there are five additional barrels available to interchange with the convertible base . They are: a 1.25-75" tapered barrel, a 1" straight barrel, a 1.5" straight barrel, a 1" straight barrel with clip, and a 1.25" straight barrel with clip. That's quite a long list, and helps justify the lofty price point, especially if you like variety in your styling habits. I, however, don't curl my hair on a daily basis and that's why I removed one star from the review. I think there are less expensive and functional options available for folks who don't require an iron day after day.

This iron heats up impeccably fast. It reached its hottest setting in under 30 seconds! I have very thick hair, so I had to use very small portions of hair on each go. The result, however, were very soft, shiny and sleek curls like nothing I've ever previously experienced.

This is just a gorgeous, high quality curling iron that's just a pleasure to use. The price point is a bit steep for occasional users, but if you require a curling iron for everyday use, do not hesitate to purchase! This will prove a vast enhancement to your beauty regimine.

Sleek,  beautiful, and luxe. Lookwise, this is and impressive curling iron. Functionally, it heats up fast and evenly.  High temps allows for fast curling.  I have thick, naturally wavy, Asian hair.  Curls stay all day and the heats seals cuticles and leaves hair shiny.

I gave this curler 4 stars instead of 5 because even though I got this curler free to test and review, I think it's pricey for a curler. For way less, you can get a Hot Tools curler (same brand that my stylist uses) and get the same results.  But of course the Hot Tools curler won't be as sexy/pretty looking. I believe in spending more for a flat iron because the nice expensive ones actually makes a difference.  But I have found little difference between pro curling irons of various price points.

T3 is a great brand and I love their straightening iron so I was really excited to try their convertible Curling iron. It heats super fast and has 5 heat settings. The unique part about this iron that while this one comes with a 1.25" barrel, you can actually purchase a different size T3 barrel (sold separately) and use it with this. You simply click the barrel and twist to lock in place. You clamp a small section of hair, twist it around the iron and voila- you will have gorgeous, soft curls. The one con in my opinion is that the whole iron is mostly all white including the barrel and you may accidentally put your hand on the barrel thinking it is safe to touch like the handle. Other than that, this is a great iron and being convertible, you can get different looks with the same iron by purchasing the different size barrels.

What an impressive curling iron!!  At first I was shocked at the price for this iron.  Then after I studied how it was made and what options were available for it, I saw why it is priced like it is.  First of all this is certainly made to last and last and last.  This iron will hold up to commerial use but for the everyday user what you are going to get is a lot of versatility.  It allows interchangeable barrels which are for sale elsewhere on Amazon or on the internet.  Those barrels are as follows:

1) 1 inch clip barrel---for defined curls
2) 1 inch straight barrel--for undone waves (whatever that means??  LOL)
3) .75 inch tapered barrel---for tousled waves
4) 1.5 inch straight barrel---for loose waves

Already comes with a 1.25 inch clip barrel for polished curls.

Intelligent digital technology.  An internal microchip controls temperature fluctuation ensuring even, optimal heat.  This is a nice feature.  Prevents burning of hair, I would hope.
Also note the following:
Ceramic barrels, 5 heat settings (WOW!), Auto world voltage and 1 hour auto shut-off

When I pulled this item up on Amazon I saw that this review would be the first so I tried to give you a lot of information.
Mostly because this is a pricey curling iron when first viewed but I think that when you consider all of the issues that
I have tried to share with you I think you can see what it is more expensive that a "usual" curling iron.

There is nothing "usual" about this nice product.
Highly recommended
summary: Highly recommended---you'll probably leave this one to someone in your will  LOL

reviewText: okay this product is good in a sense that it heats of HOT and fast. it makes my hair looking shiny and my curls last FOREVER. butttttttt I can tell it damages my hair. and ALL day long my hair smells burnt. and I promise I do not have thin hair. I have very healthy thick hair and nothing can really damage theses locks. I use this iron on Important days because I know my curls will last but definitely not on a everyday bases because I can FEEL the damage

reviewText: This curling iron/wand is the absolute BEST!! It's nicely made, a pretty and professional hair tool that's much better for your hair than cheap ones.  The curls and waves it makes are perfect and they last for days which is not normal for my hair!! I love each barrel I have gotten for this iron! It's worth every penny!! It's the best curling iron/wand out there!! I'm beyond happy and this my favorite hair tool!!

Unfortunately, this item arrived defective.  My wife was able to try it and it gets plenty hot and does a good job of curling her hair.  The problem is that the curling attachment won't fully lock in to place, so she's reluctant to continue to use because she's afraid it will come apart and burn her.  Since I received this through the Vine program, I'm not able to return it.

The T3 Twirl Convertible Curling Iron is certainly one of the highest quality (and highest priced) irons available. It has a luxury look and feel that is commensurate with it's price.

The Twirl comes in a white printed cardboard box with a plastic tray inside that holds the handle and 1.25" Tourmaline + Ceramic clip barrel separately. PLEASE SAVE AT LEAST THE TOP OF THE BOX! There is a silver serial number sticker that you need for warranty purposes. T3 will only honor the warranty if you have this number.

We found it a bit tricky to assemble the clip barrel to the handle. There are no markings on the handle or barrel on how to line up the two pieces. You need to consult the instruction manual for exact directions and even that wasn't very clear. I suppose most people will just be using the included 1.25" clip barrel so it shouldn't be a big hassle after it's first installed, but if you plan on buying extra barrels you'll want to practice installing and removing them a few times until you get the hang of it. Once we figured out how to assemble the two pieces they fit together perfectly and we had none of the breakage problems a few other Amazon reviewers noted.

The 5 level temp control button is intuitive to set and the iron heats up and is ready to go in way under a minute. My girlfriend and sister both tried out this iron and really loved how pretty it looks, and how solid and high quality it felt.

My sister uses a regular Conair curling iron most days on her medium length thick hair and she immediately noticed how much more "powerful" the T3 felt. She said it seemed to take less time for each curl with the T3 over her Conair. According to the product description: the "Digital SinglePass technology maintains consistent, even heating along the plates, which is the secret to one-pass styling and long-lasting results without exposing hair to unnecessary heat." My sister did, however, find the T3 to be quite heavy to hold and maneuver, and the barrel clip is very strong so she needed to manually release it each time instead of just pulling the iron off her hair like she does with her Conair.

My girlfriend rarely uses a curling iron but was eager to try out the T3 because it looked so pretty. She found it a bit heavier than she was accustomed to, but thought it gave her nicely defined curls and didn't seem to make her long thick hair as frizzy as her Revlon iron does. According to the product description: "when heated, the unique T3 Tourmaline + Ceramic styling surface emits negative ions that seal the cuticle, eliminate frizz and deliver shiny, long-lasting results."

My sister and girlfriend both liked the long 9 ft cord and the cord swivel design on the T3. Both of them said the cords on their curling irons were twisted messes and hoped the swivel design would prevent this on the T3.

If the T3 Twirl Convertible Curling Iron is in your price range then you are certainly purchasing a premium quality styling accessory. For near daily users the quick heating, rock solid temperature control, and low frizz results will make this curling iron a worthwhile investment. For more casual users this iron might not be the most economical choice.

**** 4 STARS - HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! ****

From my 33 year old professional makeup artist family member: "I absolutely love this product. Super easy to use. Heats up quickly. Lightweight in comparison to my other curling iron and I love the stylish streamlined look with the white and gold color of this curling iron, the controls are easy to use. Gorgeous curls that last all day! This product does an excellent job producing flawless curls with lots of bounce."
summary: Lightweight; Quick Heating; Easy to Use

reviewText: I style my hair exclusively by curling since it's long, course, and quite crazy.  I have several different Hot Tools curling irons in different barrel sizes.  I received the T3 Micro Twirl Convertible Curling Iron with Interchangeable Clip Barrel (1.25 inch barrel) and was fascinated in the idea of having interchanging barrels (I wouldn't mind having one tool with several different barrels).  My husband had to connect it for me since I was having difficulties and didn't want to break it.  It heats up fast and you can control the range in temperature.  I set it to the second hottest range and works well for my thick course hair.  It comes with a protective hot pad for your counter but you have to be careful with your fingers since the tip still gets pretty hot.  This curling iron is quite amazing and haven't gone back to my Hot Tool irons since getting this one a few weeks ago.  If you want to get a great product and aren't concerned with the price then get this curling iron and it's accompanying pieces.  If you are looking for a budget curling iron then I recommend Hot Tools.

While this is a super nice curling iron, I had a few issues with it... first off, it's super expensive. I'm not sure the cost is justified... only time will tell with how well it holds up over time.  Secondly, the clip barrel they send is very large, 1.25 inch... and it barely gave my hair a curl; mostly just on the ends. I tried it on my daughter's hair and same thing... just the ends.  This was on the highest setting too. Super strange; usually I can get more curl out of my hair than that! My hair was super hot so I know it should have done more. I think this barrel would be good for giving your hair a bit of body and wave, but not really for long lengths of hair.

The second issue I was having is that it WON'T lock in properly. I followed the directions perfectly and it just wouldn't lock. Maybe this is why it wasn't curling great?  I see others are having similar issues... makes me feel a bit better, that I'm not just doing something wrong.  When a curling iron is 400 degrees, you want to make sure it locks securely!!!

So that's the negatives... what's positive: the design is awesome with the swiveling cord. I also like that you have to HOLD DOWN the power button... no accidentally turning it off while using it.  I like the LEDS that show when it's still heating up, and what level you are at, etc... and it heats up really quick... super nice!  The clip worked great even on my daughter's fine hair... and wasn't overkill on my thicker hair... still opened easily.  And the looks... it's really stunning. Quality seems good as well overall.

For a bit less price, and a fix on the weird locking thing, I would have given this a glowing 5 stars.  But after reading other reviews about their customer service, I'm worried this is going to be a waste of my tax dollars (yes, we Viners get taxed on these items, so they really aren't "free".)  I just can't give this better stars.
summary: Barrel will not lock in to my iron... and very pricey!

reviewText:
Up-Date 2-16.
My Granddaughter is a hair dresser. Since this is so large, I do like using this curling iron, I told her to give it a try.
She tried it on her long hair. She said, I can't believe how heavy the barrel is. Its very uncomfortable to use, and so heavy.

As far as being Professional, I do not think this would work well.  Since you have to keep changing hot barrels, and I found it a bit difficult to do,
 and If your doing a wedding party, this would not be the iron you would want to use, as It turns off automatically after about a hour!

When you put the barrel in-together, make sure you Unlock it, then Lock it once its in place.
To lock etc. is on the middle bronze part. It will have the lock and unlock sign.
Although very small to see I think.

I cannot find where it say's how many blue lights are telling you what the temp means? High or Low?
You have to double click to get it to move the heat higher or lower. The lights one mine are either 3 lite, or All 5, which is to Hot for
my thick weaved hair. .
Since its So hot, I'm assuming, I can't get mine down to a lower heat!
My older inexpensive electric curling iron lights up the degrees of heat its at, like a oven. This does Not.

The directions are on a large fold out nice paper. But is hard to read in some area's, cause its written So Small!

I like that the curling barrel is Ceramic..

I would not buy this curing iron for the reason I gave, and the price. Although it looks very nice!..

reviewText:
This is a really nice curling iron. It's so much sturdier in its build than the Conair irons you get at Walmart. The interchangeable locking heads are well implemented -- at least, the one that comes with this box (1.25") does; at $85 a head, I haven't tried any others yet. It feels well-balanced in my hand and I suspect I'll get use out of this for many years to come.

That said ... I was lucky enough to be able to get a review copy of this. I have to ask myself: if I were shopping for a curling iron, would this be worth the price? I guess it depends on volume of use. For someone like me, a curling iron is an occasional tool (I already have wavy hair).  I think it is for most women I know. I couldn't justify myself buying this under normal circumstances; as it is, the 1.25 head isn't the head I'd prefer, but I don't know that I will ever spring for the head I'd use most (the tousled waves wand). This almost feels more like a professional's tool -- someone who needs a workhorse to curl hair everyday.
summary: A beautiful styling tool, but maybe too much for the average woman

reviewText: Purchased this as a gift for a friend and I fell in love with the palette so much that I ended up buying a second one for myself. I've always heard great things about LORAC but I've never tried it myself. Really happy that I did. Can't wait to try their other palettes.
summary: ... a gift for a friend and I fell in love with the palette so much that I ended up ...

reviewText: Really disappointed in this palette - the colors do not pick up well on brushes nor is there good color payoff when applied. I returned it.
For the price this is incredible! Great for anyone starting their make up collection in need of a really nice blush and highlighter. the nude color is very orange and the gold is very sheer
summary: Great for anyone starting their make up collection in need ...

reviewText:
For the price this is a fantastic palette. The colors are creamy and pigmented and go on beautifully. The palette is slim and it has a mirror which makes it the perfect palette for my purse.

The shades are so versatile, any of them can be used for an eyeshadow as there are matte browns, a deep gold, a shimmery silver, a deep wine color and a pink. The matte browns can also be used for contouring. The pinks and browns can together mix or be used separately as a blush. The shimmery silvery white is great as a highlighter and the gold can also be used as a bronzer. So in one palette I have it all. I don't need to carry anything else, other than an eyeliner and a lip product in my purse.

All the shades are such that they complement all skin tones and can be used with many outfits.

For the colors and price, I recommend it for your every day purse palette.
summary: Versatile palette, nicely pigmented, and at a value price.

reviewText:
This was a total impulse buy for me, sometime last year.  It is a pretty good deal, especially for Lorac!  I am already highly familiar with Lorac shadows as I have been working my way through the Lorac Mega PRO 2 palette this year, but I like to rotate something new in on weekends for variety.  This is the latest palette I tried.

I don't do contouring (I am super pale and it doesn't look right on me) so I skipped the bronzer *as* bronzer, though I have used it some as a neutral shadow color.  As for the blush, what I like most about it is that the pigment is fairly light.  I have another Lorac blush palette and that other one is SO pigmented that I look like a clown with the barest amount of powder applied.  But the blush here, by contrast, is not quite so bold.  It is, however, buildable, and it is a matte shade that blends nicely over my foundation and finishing powder.  It was relatively difficult for me to mess up the blush application, which I am really happy about.

There is a highlight shade (the white one on the bottom left).  I only use this as an eyeshadow.  It is quite shimmery and is really just too much for use on my cheeks.  It makes an excellent shadow, though, and it really pops over some primer.  It is similar to some other shimmery/glittery Lorac shades in that you have to work to pick up pigment on your brush (and you kind of kick a lot of powder loose in the process), but it stays put once you apply it -- at least over primer.  (I have to use primer as I have oily eyelids.)  The gold color has very similar behavior to the highlight shade.

The remainder of the palette, I have used as eyeshadow.  It's mostly matte and the formula is similar to other non-metallic/non-shimmery Lorac shadows I've tried.  It is a little neater to pick up the matte shades with a brush, without making a mess, and they blend quite well (regardless of whether the color underneath is matte or metallic).

One thing to note is there may not be a suitable liner color in this palette.  The darkest shade has a significant reddish tint to it, which might make for a strange eye look.  But then, this is not a problem for me since I don't like to use shadow as liner in the first place.  This palette is actually much more useful to me with the shade that's there, which I will use as a shadow, as opposed to having a dark brown or black or something I will never even stick a brush in once.

Eyeliner goes on nicely over this and stays in place.  I have not gotten much in the way of fallout.  This has not irritated my eyes.  I find the larger pans are big enough to get a blush brush in there, too.

Overall, I love the shades, I love the performance of the blush, and I find this very handy in terms of its compact size (with a fairly large mirror, I might add).  Recommended!
summary: good performance, nice and compact; highlight shade is a bit glittery so I use it as eyeshadow only

reviewText: I like this LORAC palette.  I carry it in my makeup bag for quick touch ups if needed during the day.  It has everything; blush, bronzer, eye shadows and highlighter.  The eye shadows require a light touch as is true with all LORAC eye shadows.
This colors and unique

This is a beautiful palette, from the pink satin sheen of the outside, to the nicely sized mirror on the inside, right to the heart of the very well coordinated shades.
The blush is the perfect neutral pink. It's matte, but almost creamy and a little goes a long way. It gives that very sweet lit from within flush.
The highlighter is on the silver side, (I find most highlighters hint of gold), but this one is like being washed over by moonlight. Love. It also is beautiful doing double duty as a brow bone, inner corner of eye and cupids bow highlighter too.
Bronzers aren't usually my thing, but this sports a soft neutral that is great. Matte, no shimmer, and makes contouring effortless.
The eyeshadows are smooth, highly pigmented, and very blendable. Three are matte, perfectly coordinating shades of natural earth tone browns. The fourth is a coup de grace of perfect gilded gold, a little goes a long way!
