* The moisturizer really moisturizes without feeling super-greasy.  It is heavy enough to do the trick, but not so heavy that it feels like you want to wipe it off.

* The exfoliating gel feels good.  I was a bit concerned that this would be too drying for my skin, but I am happy to report that this isn't the case.

If you are looking for something that might just help your dry and aging skin, this might be for you.
Please note, no miracles will occur with the use of these products.  Your skin might just look a tad better.

I don't have a problem with crepiness, but I am beginning to see the very beginnings of something resembling it under my upper arms. Like yuck! (Aging really sucks.)

Naturally I'd be for anything that would forestall it. I was glad to try the Crepe Erase two part system (despite the name, which gives me the heebies.) The moisturizer is OK, the scrub like most average scrubs. So all I have to do is use a scrub and moisturize and it'll all be fine? Because regardless of what the company claims, after several weeks, I see zero change in my incipient underarm crepiness. If this product is supposed to make a difference, it's not doing a thing I can see.

Two stars cause the products aren't horrible, but minus three stars cause I don't see that they do at all what the manufacturer claims. You can get a similar result a lot cheaper with almost any moisturizer and sugar scrub for a LOT less. Pass.
summary: OK moisturizer and scrub, but doesn't do what the manufacturer claims

reviewText: This is the kind of product that works as a gift...from others. The price tag is high, but for the right complexion and body type, is great treatment. Designed for "body" repairs - probably not advisable for face, but maybe not a problem? This is not clear to me. 10 oz lasts a long time if used appropriately. Aroma is nice - not overly powerful, but certainly a pleasant scent. Good product, simply a high price point which might put it out of reach for most.
summary: is great treatment. Designed for "body" repairs - probably not ...

reviewText:
What I liked:

' the scent was nice and citrus-y
' a little bit  goes a long way
' it's super moisturizing
' this is a pretty decent sized tub

What I don't like:

' the price is nuts, there is no way I'd ever pay over a hundred bucks for lotion
' it's greasy, even on my super dry skin
' because it was greasy, it left spots on my duvet cover (where I sat after lotioning my legs)
' I didn't notice a bit of difference after 27 days of use

I would not buy this again unless it was twelve dollars at the drugstore because it did nothing for the parts of my body that have crepey skin (upper legs, hands, neck, elbows, knees). I don't have a lot of wrinkles yet, despite being fair skinned and having spent way too much time in the sub) but I applied it to my face as a moisturizer. It did give my facial skin a nice bit of moisture and if I had time to let it "dry" it made my skin look really pretty, but not so pretty that I'd pay this much.

I didn't find out this is a Gunthy-Renker product until after I'd already used it so I didn't have any preconceived ideas about it prior to review, however had I been thinking of purchasing it and learned that information, I would not have completed the purchase.

I saw this product, Crepe Erase, available in the Amazon Vine program and wanted to try it because my skin is starting to look old (crepey) in some areas mainly due to constant tanning when I was younger. (The product description actually states CREEPY-looking skin in one place; I assume this is a typo!)  Given the list price of this, it is not something I would likely buy myself; luckily, I had the opportunity to try it free of charge.  The 10 oz jar is quite big.  If they marketed a jar about one-third of the size (and about one-third of the cost), I think people would be more likely to try it because it would not be so cost-prohibitive.

I was not familiar with Crepe Erase, so I did some reading about it on the Internet.  Crepe Erase is made in the USA and is distributed by Guthy-Renker, a marketing company that sells products to consumers through infomercials, television ads, direct mail, telemarketing, e-mail marketing, and the Internet.  They use celebrity endorsements for their products.  Jane Seymour is the celebrity endorser of Crepe Erase.  The products marketed by Guthy-Renker are usually more expensive than similar products available at your local grocery and drug stores.  Bottom line, the question is:  Does Crepe Erase work better than other comparable products to make it worth its price?  Well

I have now used the product for almost two weeks.  While Crepe Erase works well as a moisturizer, I have not seen any noticeable difference in the youthfulness of my skin.  According to their website:  Results can vary for each individual.  Some users can notice visible results after the first application, while it can take others up to 60 days or longer.  Directions state for best results to use with Crepe Erase Exfoliating Body Polish, which I did not do because of the cost.

Bottom line, based on cost and results thus far, I do not recommend this product.  However, I will continue using it until the jar is gone and will update my review should I notice any changes in the appearance of my skin.
summary: Works well as a moisturizer, but no noticeable difference in crepey skin

reviewText:
My 60-something mother stole this from the wife, and has sworn that this is the greatest thing to reduce the wrinkles on her neck and her dry skin. She's been on this for 3 weeks, and I've never seen her happy with any sort of skin cream before. There's no detectable "greasy" feeling and no odor and doesn't wear off on the shirt collar. But if mom's happy, then that's something.

The only gripe is the price - despite that you're using a small dab, it's still a psychological thing to get over - spending $100+ on a jar. But if mom's excited about buying another one of these when this runs out, then that's a good sign.

Overall I would say this product is most effective as a moisturizer.  After a couple of weeks of use, I do think it diminishes wrinkles and creases, but like anything else, it is not a magic bullet.  I think age and amount of skin damage will play a huge part in results.  I am in my mid 50's, tend to stay out of the sun when possible, and have relatively young looking skin for my age.  I did notice improvement though anywhere I applied it to wrinkles such as by knees or elbows.  Results by the face/eyes were less dramatic, but I have minimal wrinkles there to start with.

The primary ingredients are water, shea butter, coca seed butter, coconut oil, olive fruit oil, followed by a litany of other ingredients, mostly alcohol and chemicals.  The product contains a propriety mixture named Trufirm.

Crepe Erase has a delicate fragrance.  It is there but not overpowering by any means.

The jar is fairly large (10 pounces) but pricey, over $110 as of this writing.  Application is suggested as a "pearl size" so it does go a long way.

It does appear to have some benefit, but I don't think it is going to really minimize badly creped skin.
summary: Seems To Work, Results Probably Vary Based On Skin

reviewText:
I ordered Crepe Erase Intensive Body Repair Treatment, along with the Crepe Erase Body Polish. (I've reviewed the Body Polish separately.) I really like the thick emollient feeling of the Intensive Body Repair product, and I LOVE the incredible light citrusy smell. It's super thick - thicker than body butter - kind of a cross between coconut oil in a jar and body butter... The kind of coconut oil that's hardened at room temperature, not the oil that pours. It doesn't feel quite like either of those though, and the smell is wonderful!

The Crepe Erase Intensive Body Repair Treatment goes on so smoothly. It feels a little greasy at first, but not sticky, and then is well absorbed into your skin. It left my skin feeling softer and looking healthier. It's done a really good job of softening my rough elbows, knees, and feet, which get super dry during the cold dry winter months. Crepe Erase is perfect for dry winter skin, but to be honest, it's heavier that what I'd use in the summer months because it would leave me feeling sweaty. Perhaps at night during the summer on those areas that are particularly dry - like my knees and elbows.

When  I ordered this product I didn't realize that it's a Guthy-Renker product. I make it a personal policy not to order products from infomercials because I've had problems with two products I ordered a long time ago which left me with a negative opinion of that ordering process. Since I can get if from Amazon, I would order the Intensive Body Repair Treatment again next winter. It's the richest body cream I think I've ever tried, which is great for my dry, sensitive skin.

I really liked the Crepe Erase Intensive Body Repair Treatment, and would definitely continue to use it during the winter months if it wasn't so expensive.  I didn't care for the Crepe Erase Body Polish. It didn't make my face feel clean,  and left little scratches on my skin.  I'll stay with the exfoliator I've been using since my teens, St Ives Peach Facial Scrub.

Update 8 4 2017
I STILL look for a cream as good as this and have yet to find it!!  This one is a bit outside of my budget for now,  otherwise I'd a year's supply at a time!
summary: Amazing smell! Nice rich body cream , , ,

reviewText: This cream has a good scent and moisturizes well. Be sure not to put on too much as it can appear glossy. Add the right amount and the dry appearance of skin is diminished considerable. I don't find it greasy or oily but comparable to many hand creams in effect it has on skin. It might absorb just a little slower than most. Overall an effective wrinkle reducer.

Crepe Erase actually seems to be highly effective. Initially the cream seems very thick, dense and greasy (my first thought was comparing it to Crisco), but it absorbs easily when applied to dry skin and surprisingly doesn't leave it feeling oily and weighed-down. It has a very light scent that's I would describe as lightly floral with herbaceous hints that's rather pleasant (pleasant enough that I've sniffed my better half after she's applied it to her arms, legs and feet). My wife has been using it for at least 10 days now, and it's made a noticeable difference in the areas of her skin that tend to be the most dry, particularly her arms, ankles and tops of her hands and feet.

This is an expensive cream, and honestly, whether it's worth it to you or not is going to depend on how well it works for you and your skin type. For my wife, who has considerable problems with dry skin, it's been effective when a lot of other products haven't been. This isn't going to be in the budget for a lot of working households out there, but I kind of wish that it was, because I can see it working and can tell she likes the effect that it's having. It does look like a little goes a long way, and this 10 ounce size looks like it might last her well over a month, but there's no denying that this is an expensive product, but I also can't deny that it works well.
summary: Works very well moisturizing dry skin and largely lives up to its claims.

reviewText:
I was surprised at the size of the tub.  This is a huge container unlike most creams on the market.  It has 10 oz in here.  This is good because it costs approx $100.  It is a thick cream but not much is needed.  A small amount will melt on the skin.  Unfortunately, this is not an overnight miracle so whether or not it actually will improve my (very) crepe-y neck remains to be seen.  I have taken several photos and will compare them in a week, 2 weeks and a month.  I will also update the review how long it lasts. Somebody said the cream is greasy.  I don't agree with that if a small amount is used.  I'm using it on my neck which is very dry.  Perhaps the reviewers who report too much shine don't have dry skin like me.  I don't use this on the face since I have Rosecea and very sensitive skin.  I only use it on the throat.

Update October 9, 2016. I've stopped using it because it made my rosecea worse and I gave it to my mom who seems to like it. She is 94 and convinced she has too many wrinkles; she doesn't but she likes it a lot and it seems to soften her skin.

Good:
Large size (10 oz)
OK-Aroma; I didn't mind it
Thick cream which goes on smoothly and spreads well
Only a very small amount is needed
Contains natural ingredients

Not so good:
The only negative so far has been the name.  Not very inviting!  Who wants to admit you have crepe-y skin?  Not sure what else I would have called it but not that.
I realize that folks think it's too expensive but my goodness, it's 10 ounces!!  Look at the bottles at the department store counters and see how little is in them.  I don't think this is overpriced but it might just be too expensive for many in spite of how much is in there.
summary: Smooth and creamy and easy to apply but not good for my roseacea.

reviewText:
Due to illness and medications, my skin is extremely damaged. It is beyond the damage that occurs due to aging and sun exposure, so my trial of Crepe Erase really goes beyond what the product was designed or can be expected to resolve. Still, while it's on, my skin's creasing and dryness is relieved and its appearance is improved. It is not a cure (nor is it meant to be a cure) but it is a temporary relief and remedy. The easiest way to evaluate it is to break the factors down as follows:

PROS:
--It has no strong perfume (although "fragrance" is listed at the bottom of the ingredient list. It smells more buttery than anything else.
--It goes on smoothly and spreads well (a little over 1t will cover an arm (all around) up to the shoulders).
--The effect is immediate (a visible relaxation of the skin creases) and lasts until you bathe and remove it.
--The container is pretty large and should last quite a while. I've been using it for almost two weeks daily on both arms, neck and front and have used almost a quarter of it. (The lid is 3.5" across and the jar is 2.75" high).
--It isn't sticky.
--The ingredients listed first are mostly natural. Towards the end, some sound chemical but not too many.

CONS:
--The Price (GOOD GRIEF!)
--It doesn't really absorb. It stays on the surface and leaves a sort of shine on the skin for the first few hours. (I'm not talking "youthful glow" I talking shine).
--The effect lasts no longer than until your next shower.

CAVEATS:
--The product is supposed to be used after application of another product that I don't use. I just use it at night, after showering.
--My arms are dry, bruised, and damaged by years of Cushing's Syndrome and steroid use in addition to normal aging and living in a tropical climate. I think this product is meant to treat wrinkles and dryness caused by aging and maybe excessive sun exposure. However, I think that the CONS I listed would still apply to people with more typical skin damage.
--If the price was lower (sary $50), I might have given this product 4 stars because it is more effective than any other cream or lotion I've used (including prescription strength Ammonium Lactate 12%), but the cost is so excessive and difficult to justify that I took off one star.
summary: Could have been 4 stars but for the price.

reviewText:
With ingredients like shea butter, cocoa butter, coconut oil, and olive oil, along with dimethicone how could you go wrong?  It also has its proprietary ingredient called Tru Firm.  This product has been endorsed by Jane Seymour and Dorothy Hamill.

This powerful hydrator does make the skin feel smooth and moist, sometimes too moist and greasy. Has a very pleasant flowery fragrance, which I just loved on my lovely wife. The description says that it is for your neck, chest, arms and legs.  I would assume that this is not for the face?

$113, as it is priced now. is pretty steep for this 10 oz. jar.  She is not convinced that it is worth the price or has the results it claims.
summary: Will Erase Your Bank Account for Sure

reviewText:
I just had to try this because " it was created to target hard-to-treat creepy-looking skin". I have a lot of "creepy" skin because I'm an elder hippy who spent years in the sun au naturale, before we knew the sun was so bad for us. The directions say to take a pearl sized piece and massage it into the skin for up to a minute. It would take me an hour long Bali massage to treat all of my skin.

So I've been trying it on my right hand and wrist for a few days, It does take a while to absorb, and my skin feels tacky at first, but that goes away. I find the fragrance very light. As a control, I've been using a natural goat's milk product on my left area. Crepe Erase is doing a slightly better job. I'll probably save this very expensive creme for my neck area.

I have what's called Crepe skin on my elbows. It's a dry patch of skin. That no matter how much you use lotion. It's still dry. I used a finger tip on my elbows. I rubbed in a circular position. This works very well. I applied three times a day.  This keeps my skin from that Crepe feeling. The only thing I did not like was the smell. Reminds me of a hair perm. Overall my skin is starting to look better.

I just started using this product this week so I haven't used it long enough to say if it actually has an effect in reversing sagging underarm skin or crinkly cleavage.  What I can say so far is that the rub is very thick.  A little goes a long way and it needs the appropriate amount of massaging to effectively be absorbed into the skin.  The scent is subtle and not overpowering.  It definitely is a high octane moisturizer and skin feels extremely treated (in a good manner) after applying.

Will try to update more after further use

The formula for this body repair treatment is interesting.  It's not a drippy lotion; in fact, it is almost a solid, like a tub of Crisco.  It goes on very greasy, and stays greasy for quite a while.  It is very hard to rub in.

I don't see any incredible changes in my skin just yet, but will add that this has a very strong fragrance. I'm not sure why a company thinks this is a good idea.  Besides causing a reaction on sensitive skin, it would clash with any perfume one might choose to wear.

Overall so far, this is just ok.  It might have gotten a higher rating if it was unscented and I honestly don't know if I'll continue to use this because of the smell.  It doesn't seem worth the $113 price.

edit:  I decided to bite the bullet and use this daily at bedtime.  I'm actually used to the fragrance now.  It does leave my skin very soft and moisturized when I wake up, but I don't know if that has anything to do with this product being special, or just because it's so thick.

I thought this did a good job on my over exposed forearms which have the appearance of alligator skin. They are very wrinkly, creepy, and ugly. After just one application my forearms looked far better. The skin looked supple and smooth and retained moisture all all day long. There are other comparable creams that perform as well. My only reservation is the cost. This seems a bit pricey.

This body cream is thick and rich and scent-free, so it won't clash with fragrance. All plusses.  Given its price--it's practically on par with solid gold--I have strictly limited its use to most crinkliest spots: neck, chest, back of arms, knees. It hydrates my skin well, but I cannot honestly say it reverses the effects of aging. Had I not received this product through the Amazon Vine program, I wouldn't have been willing to spent this amount of money on an "intensive body repair treatment."

Also, talk about unfortunate branding. Who wants to have a product around that blasts the word "CREPE?" It's a downer.

I like this cream. It has a bit of a stronger scent then the body lotion but it's very pleasant. It has good ingredients as well including Shea Butter, Coconut Oil, Cocoa Butter and Olive Oil.  All are good and rich ingredients for your skin.

What I don't love is the price. It seems pretty high. I do like the cream it's very hydrating and feels great on my aging skin. Recommended.
summary: Like the Scent and the Hydration

reviewText:
I have used this for about a week and think that I did notice a difference in my skin - it is smoother, tighter and firmer.
The cream felt a little bit sticky going on. It is a bit more greasy than I am used to. But I think the results was good enough.

I received this from Amazon Vine. However I am not sure I will be ordering this due to the high cost.
summary: I like it and it seems effective.

reviewText: This is certainly a thick cream! I like that because you can really control the amount you use. And you only need a small (very small!) amount at a time. If you use too much, you'll get that greasy feeling. I think the scent is pleasant; it seems a bit strong out of the jar, but as it goes on your skin, it seems to lighten up a bit and I don't find any real lingering scent. I've used it pretty much everywhere on my body and prefer it for my arms (elbows) and my feet (heels). I don't really think it's an intensive body repair treatment, as the name indicates. Especially for the price ($113.00 is the going rate on Amazon as of this review, for a 10 oz. jar). It does the job as a moisturizer and I was fortunate enough to get it as a freebie, but I don't think I would purchase it again for that price.
summary: Price is a little steep for this product...

reviewText: This is great in moderation; I use only a tiny amount, which goes a long way. If you use too much it will be obvious because you won't be able to rub it all in and you'll be left feeling greasy. A smaller amount really penetrates the skin and feels wonderful. The smell Isnt my favorite, but I wouldn't go so far as to say that it stinks--it just doesn't smell natural, but isn't necessarily bad. I'm hoping that after a few weeks of using it the results will be so impressive that I will be able to add back the star I took away for the smell; I will update the review appropriately.
summary: Feels amazing if you use just a small amount!

reviewText: I just started using this so I can't vouch for its long-term effectiveness.  But I do like how it feels.  I did not find it greasy at all.  Just a little dime-sized portion goes a long way.  You can feel your skin moisturized right away and it lasts throughout the day.  I put this on in the morning and at night.  I'm optimistic that it will bring positive results.  Minus a star for the ridiculous price.

This is a very thick cream. Very thick. A little drop goes a long way. I applied to clean and dry skin. I rubbed it into my skin with upward massage strikes until it soaked in. It didn't leave a greasy coating. My skin looks and feels moisturized. The reason for only three stars? The scent. It has a very strong chemical like perfume smell. If this were scented with essential oils or unscented, I would give it five stars. This would be very irritating to sensitive skin.

I read somewhere once that facial scrubs can actually scratch your skin. I don't feel like that's necessarily true, especially after using the Crepe Erase scrub. This product has a light fruity scent (contains fruit)  and is clear with tiny white particles. I almost didn't try this because the description sounds like it's geared towards dry skin, then it also said it was good for all skin types. It works! My skin is so soft with a brighter complexion. This is a new brand to me and one I plan to invest in further.

This facial scrub is quite amazing. It is a gentle scrub without the gritty feeling that most exfoliating or micro-bead based scrubs have. I like the way it gently polishes and exfoliates my skin, leaving it soft and smooth. I don't have crepey skin, so I can't tell if it helps. That said, it does make my skin feeling a little brighter, soft and smooth. Also, the scrub has a fresh, subtle fragrance that is quite pleasant.

All in all, this is a great facial scrub that exfoliates the skin without the gritty feel to it. It leaves my skin feeling fresh and clean. I have sensitive skin and this scrub doesn't irritate me. Great product.

I live in the desert and my 35th birthday is in a couple of weeks and  my face is beginning to show it. I have very fine lines near my eyes (baby crow's feet) and smile lines. I have only used this once and it felt good going on. Its not greasy, but doesn't feel like it dries my skin out. It has a fine graininess that works to exfoliate the dead skin surface. i am fairly sensitive to scents and thankfully the one in this scrub is very mild. My face and neck feel really soft after using it. I look forward to seeing what it does long term and have taken "before" pictures. I will update my review with an "after" picture and follow-up comments on the product.

I am a big fan of facial washes and was eager to try this product.

So far this one has been a winner. One of the things I noticed right away was that the directions and ingredients were easy to read. A lot of these skin care products are made for middle-aged and older customers, and it's frustrating when the print is too tiny to read. That's not a problem here.

The scent is subtle and pleasant. Not too flowery or sweet.

I used a small amount on my face, neck, and chest and loved the way it made my skin feel. According to the instructions, you are supposed to "gently massage with fingertips for 1 to 2 minutes" and then rinse. Again, I used only a small amount, and it was more than enough, so the 6 oz. container should last a long time.

This product offers a low-maintenance to keep my skin clean and healthy, and I highly recommend it.

i'm a huge fan of facial scrubs and now that I'm at an age where my skin is showing signs of getting older, I was so excited to try this.  This has a very pleasant scent, not quite floral but more of a fresh scent, and not too strong, just pleasant.  The scrub itself is not like using sandpaper, like some scrubs i have.  It's a gentle scrub.  i do it at night and it really makes my face and neck feel very smooth.  I have noticed that my skin is brighter.  I haven't noticed any decrease in lines yet, i don't have many wrinkles or crepey skin but it makes your skin smooth, soft and brighter.  I will continue to use this and see where it takes me.  This is a quality product.  I love it

I have been using this facial scrub about 2 1/2 weeks and really like it. I've used a lot of different scrubs and facial cleansing products, but, more than most, this one leaves my face feeling soft and moisturized. I think the lines/creases that go around my neck have faded a bit, and that's very encouraging. Some of the facial products I have used cause a sensitivity to the sun, but I haven't found that to be a problem with Crepe Erase. I like the stimulation of the scrubbing "beads" as well as the luxurious feel of the gel-like substance the beads are suspended in. The directions say to use this product daily, and I have tried it in the morning in the shower as well as in the evening at the sink - both are fine. I have been massaging it into my skin for closer to one minute than two (the directions say to rub it in gently for 1-2 minutes). My skin is not overly-sensitive, but I'm very fair, so I do have to be careful. As much as I like this product, I'm not sure I'd be willing to pay the price, but only a small amount is used each day, so a tube would probably last a couple of months. My results have been very good, but I don't see a huge difference in the condition of my facial skin. If I did, I'd be more than happy to pay full price.

I ordered the Crepe Erase Facial Scrub for use by a lady friend who has used a similar product in the past. Her impression of this scrub is that it is worth the money. A little bit applied at a time goes a long way and after one week of application she believes she has found a product she will reorder. She likes the smell and the micro-beads in the formulation. I am now tempted to order one more for myself.
summary: Crepe Erase Facial Scrub - One user likes it

reviewText: This cleanser is a thick, clear gel with some soft white bits for vey gentle exfoliation. It's pretty potent--I keep using too much. Has a light, inoffensive fragrance. I've found it nicely gentle with no irritation. Maybe a little tricky to rinse off, but I use it while showering so not a big deal.

Crepe Erase Refining Facial Scrub is a gentle exfoliant scrub that does not dry skin like other moisturizers do by wiping out the natural skin oils. This product does leave a little of the natural oils, but still will dry your skin because of the nature of the cleanser. The microbeads are just firm enough to do away with the days dirt and surface debris. In the few weeks that I have used it, I have noticed that my skin looks brighter and more radiant than previously, as promised by the TrueFirm Complex ingredient. All in all, it is a much better cleanser than the more popular commercial products. To top it off, it has a nice gentle scent that is not too fragrant and not too citrusy. Has a nice flower smell that is pleasing to the senses. Only tip is to buy a moisturizer to use after using this to maintain your skins optimum moisture.
summary: Gentle Exfoliating Facial Scrub with a pleasing scent

reviewText:
I ordered the Crepe Erase Body Cream, which I really like, but the Crepe Erase Facial Scrub just isn't for me. The scrub didn't leave me feeling like my face was fresh and clean. Instead of feeling like I'd just washed my face, it felt as though I'd used something heavy or slightly oily. Also, the micro beads didn't exfoliate as much as they actually left tiny scratches on my face.

I've been exfoliating with St. Ives Peach Facial Scrub since I was in my teens, and I know to scrub very gently.  It might be the difference between St. Ives natural, ground peach pit scrub, and Crepe Erase's plastic micro beads, which I found to be too harsh for my sensitive skin. Also, plastic micro beads aren't biodegradable, which isn't good for our waterways. (Something our older son pointed out to me.)

I've been really happy with the St. Ives facial scrub for many years, and it's what our kids prefer as well, so I'll continue to buy St Ives, even though I did really like the Crepe Erase Body Cream. (Which I'll be reviewing separately.)

I was hoping to get to try this out, but I happen to be allergic to all sorts of things.  Because of this, I always try products on my hands before I try them on my face.  Unfortunately, I broke out in hives (for 3 days) after trying this out on my hands and so I can't use it any further.

I wanted to use this product for a while before writing the review. So far my forehead, cheeks and nose feel more fresh and clean even with using just small amounts of this facial scrub. I like that it has some small granular pieces that will dissolve after some rubbing and massaging. The fragrance is very light - almost no scent. In short, this facial scrubs works well for me, and better than most others I tried in the past.
summary: My skin feels refreshed after this

reviewText:
For facial scrubs this one is pretty good.  It doesn't have a lot of tiny scrubbing particles but you can certainly feel them as you wash your face.  I used it exactly as directed and the overall process is easy.  Only a small amount is needed and it lathers just a little bit.  Rinsing all the particles off takes several splashes, but it seems to clean everything off very well.  l still had to use a moisturizer afterwards because my skin felt tight after patting dry with a towel.

It's kind of expensive, but I think it will last a long time.  As of this review it costs $21.63. I hope after many uses I will notice a smoothness in those areas that have a bit of sun damage and the skin is dryer and a little crinkled.
summary: Crepe Erase Refining Facial Scrub 6 fl. oz.

reviewText:
As one in the full bloom of middle age--and living in a desert clime--I recognize the necessity for maintaining a skin care regimen. I'm always on the lookout for effective products.

From several days of use, I give high marks to this product. It's a thorough scrub that exfoliates effectively.

The instructions suggest 1-2 minutes of usage, to refresh the skin across the face and neck. I used it in this way, applying it with a Clarisonic electronic brush for men. It worked well, and did not cause any irritation.

Several issues you may want to consider:

--part of the effectiveness of this product may be in the inclusion of microbeads. Because of their cumulative environmental impact on water systems. microbeads are being outlawed by a rising number of states. I don't know what the substitute will be, but this product may be reformulated. How it will perform then, compared to now, one just can't know.

--while the value of this product is high, so is the price. There are numerous alternatives for lower prices, and of various formulations.

--any skin care product is a very individual choice. While this works well for my skin, there's no way around the fact that others might face irritation, allergic reaction, etc.

In sum, this product works well for me. I'm constantly trying new products, and this one is in the top rung of those I've experienced. Perhaps it will work for you.
summary: Excellent Skin Scrub: High Value, High Price

reviewText: Really like the subtle but pleasant smell of this and the exfoliating grit is just right--not abrasive, not to weak to do anything. It says not to use it on the eyes, but I did, keeping them closed, and had no issues with stinging or anything. It removed all my makeup and left my skin feeling clean. There has been no allergic reaction and no redness or irritation or bumps.
summary: Really like the subtle but pleasant smell of this and the ...

reviewText:
I got this for my wife who is always looking to try new cleansing products.
The Crepe Erase scrub is really nice.  6 oz. might not sound like a lot, but you get a LOT of product in the tube and a little goes a long way.  Also, when you put it on your face (about a quarter size is plenty for the whole face), it foams up slightly so that it spreads all over easily.  The beads that comprise the scrub are large.  The product isn't packed with the scrub beads, but there are enough to do the trick.  It washes off easily, and my skin definitely looked freshly scrubbed and felt super smooth. It has a very nice smell: maybe slightly floral, slightly fruity.  Not overwhelming, but there.
summary: A lot goes a long way

reviewText: I really love this product. I have used facial scrubs in the past, but skin getting sensitive as I get older and scrubs being so rough and grainy, I've started to back off from them. Not with this product, it's very gentle to my face and does a nice job cleansing. Only a smidgeon is needed to cover my entire face, so this generous tube will likely last quite a while. I am sensitive to perfumes and other strong odors, but I really didn't pick up on anything like that with this product, another huge plus for me.

I hate to complain, I got the worst rash ever from this product. I have no idea what triggered it. I washed my face, I used my normal moisturizer, and about 15 minutes later my face felt like it was on fire. I had red blotches everywhere. It took two days to go down.

This may not happen to all users, but this is what I experienced. I do have large pores, and moderately sensitive skin. It was not heavily fragranced, I'm not sure if it was the wash with my moisturizer, or the wash alone, but it hurt.

I've tried what seems like a million facial scrub products by now, and I think this is one of best ones yet. Why? Because it's the gentlest. Some scrubs are very abrasive, especially the natural-type versions that often have ground up peach or apricot pits in them. Some feel as though you're rubbing sand into your face. This has little soft balls that are gentle yet very effective. It did a great job sloughing my skin to a lovely smooth texture and left it soft for hours afterward.

This is a really nice skin care product.

Beyond the name and price is beautiful skin.  I really loved the duo. The cream is thick and I needed just a little bit. The scrub is my favorite. Both have a wonderful effect on my skin.

Sizes are generous!  Both the body wash and the cream.

Cream smells wonderful, very lemony.

I turn bottle around in my shower so people do not see the name.
summary: If you overcome the name and price... You'll find a luxurious body treatment

reviewText:
I have mixed emotions after having used this product for about 10 days.  Here's why:
Does my skin feel softer than before?  Yes
Does my skin look any different?  No
Is the improvement enough to justify the time and cost required?  Well, herein lies my quandary.

I received this product as a sample through the Amazon Vine program. Never in a million years would I have spent that kind of money on what is essentially a "vanity" product.  Never.  Ever.  Granted, the tub of creme is massive and those 10 ounces will last long enough to take some of the sting our of the cost-per-use.  But the Exfoliating scrub is only 8 ounces and I feel like I'm using it at a disproportionate rate to the creme.  I expect I'll have to switch to a different method of exfoliant before I get to the bottom 1/3rd of the creme.  Anyway you look at it, a hundred fifty bucks to get started is a huge cash outlay, at least from my perspective.  I'd have to declare this as a capital asset on my personal financial statement had I paid full price for it.

Secondly, the directions for use require a substantial amount of time.  You are to dampen the skin, scrub with the body polish, wash the scrub off and then moisturize with the creme.  The most effective way to do this is scrub before showering and moisturize after you towel off from the shower.  If you try to just rinse the scrub off at the sink with a washcloth you invariably leave some grans of scrub on your skin.  This makes for an mess when you go to rub the creme in.  Any way you do it, you're looking at a 15-20 minute process, unless you are just targeting one or two small areas.

I used this on my elbows, knees and neck- which kind of extended to my whole arms, legs and chest.  Once you've got the scrub on your hands and targeted areas anyway, it only makes sense to do the surrounding areas too.  I was going to leave two areas untreated as a "control" for the test but I couldn't bring myself to risk being asymmetrical considering all the effort I was putting forth.  The kicker is that now I really don't know if it was the ingredients in the "Crepe Erase" that made my skin softer or if it was just the result of getting all that attention after years of neglect.

So I'll use this up but wouldn't  buy more.  I'll be fine with some gentle soap, a scrubby bath poof and some basic moisturizer.  Wouldn't it be great if we could all just be happy with "the skin we're in" without going to such desperate measures to meet somebody else's definition of beautiful?
summary: OK product but not worth the list price.

reviewText:
I just started using the Crepe Erase Full Size Body Duo, Intensive Body Repair so this review is my opinion of how the product works, smells and feels. The first step is the Exfoliating Body Polish, it has a slightly gritty feeling that melts away as you mix with water cleaning away old dry skin away. I use a rotating Japanese style soft brush to apply, it foams up and leaves my skin feeling fresh. It has a citrus scent thats mild but pleasant.
Once you finish exfoliating apply the Intensive Body Repair Treatment, it hydrates and revitalizes my skin as its worked in and leaves my skin looking alive and fresh! So far I do see my skin looking better, after all that work I should hope so. If I see an improvement over time I'll update my review. Its worth a try so I'm willing to keep treating my skin.
summary: I love the smell and the fresh look this treatment leaves my skin looking!

reviewText: I've been using the Crepe Erase Duo for three weeks now, and here's what I have learned: The exfoliating scrub is is definitely the better product of the two, the body treatment cream is super thick, and I really can't tell any noticeable difference in my skin.  As for the scrub, a little goes a long way.  I've tried to find more information about the tiny beads used in the scrub to see if they are biodegradable or not, but I have not found any answers.  So I feel a little guilty using it, but it's not too harsh and leaves skin feeling great.  The body treatment cream just isn't for me.  It's very thick and takes a while to apply evenly.  It also leaves my skin feeling too greasy. Many reviewers have commented on the pleasant scent, but I don't find it all that pleasing,  It's pretty strong for my liking- especially for skin care and treatment.  Overall, my skin feels good, but I observe no significant difference.  There are other products out there that I prefer.  I'm glad that I tried the Crepe Erase duo, though.

First point: for $140, this had better work! We were encouraged to see that this is put out by Guthy Renker, a well-known producer and marketer of high quality products over a lot of years. We first ran into the company back in the day, when they put out Tony Robbins' "Personal Power" series, and we used their teeth-whitening system as well.

From the female of the family -- I'm willing to spend good money on "anti-aging" products as long as they work (although there's really no such thing. You try and be the best you can for your age!). I was given a sample of "Crepe Erase" to review and I'm grateful, because I'd have to see a lot of 5-star reviews before I'd spend the money. Having said that, when it works, I'll dish out the dough -- I'm worth it!

I have used this daily for two months before I wrote the review, as you need time with something like this to prove that it works. I'm in my early 60s, and I can definitely see the signs of aging, and the reduction in youthful collagen that causes especially female skin to get that loose and "crepey" look.

This is a 2 step Treatment to tighten and smooth the skin. My impression: the Crepe Erase duo really do smooth thin, aging skin on the back of hands, arms, legs and neck area. The fragrance is fresh -- a light citrus. The treatment starts with an exfoliating scrub that buffs away dead skin, leaving the body smooth and clean. I only use the exfoliator every third or fourth day since it takes about that long for skin to shed a layer of cells. Skin remains buffed and smooth for several days.

The hydrating cream ("Intensive Body Repair Treatment") is great to use every day. Living in arid Arizona, I have dry skin on my lower legs that I continually battle. Crepe Erase has helped with this, and I truly think it has reduced that look of crepey skin around my knees and upper legs. I love how the body cream works all day and doesn't quit before my next shower. I discovered many of my favorite ingredients in the cream; shea and coconut butter, coconut oil, olive oil and beeswax. One excellent ingredient in the duo is apple extract -- antioxidant and astringent, possessing a natural alpha hydroxy acid that helps remove dry skin. The acid-wash action of both the body polish and the cream work well for me. I am a long-term fan of exfoliating with alpha hydroxy acid because it's an easy method and does not require undue scrubbing, which can be hard on the skin itself. With the rich, long lasting and effective ingredients in the body cream, this is a winning combo for me.

By the way, there's no paraben and mineral oil in this, which are contraindicated these days.

Being as expensive as it is, I would not recommend this to you unless I was 5-star-pleased.

First, I'm not exactly sure what crepey skin looks like, but I've got an area on the back of my leg that could be mistaken for Death Valley on a cloudy day. So I figured I was a good candidate for this intensive treatment. Next, we know that crepe often accompanies aging, reflecting a loss of collagen and skin elasticity. Wouldn't it be nice to be able to scrub away the years and smooth that skin with a jar of intensive repair cream? Never one to give up hope, I began this trial with atypical scientific fervor, using the duo only on my left leg and nothing on the right leg. After several weeks of use, I can report...no change, and no difference between the two. The body repair treatment has a thick, almost waxy consistency, so the skin does feel coated for hours after application. If you're looking for a short-term solution, like a special event, this might do the trick. If you want longer lasting results, you really have to go with laser treatment or (less expensively) try Retin-A/tretinoin or skin peels. Finally, the price. Breaking down the components, the scrub sells for under $20, the repair cream for under $100. Why pay $20 extra for the set? A mystery. You get a lot of product for your money, but after a year or so, I'm afraid it may start to get a little too nasty or rancid to use. There is nothing particularly innovative in the ingredients. Unlike most items at this price point, there is nothing luxurious about the product presentation: the containers are not particularly attractive and will occupy a lot of precious space in your bathroom. If, after reading this review, you are still so intrigued that you are willing to part with your hard-earned money, I recommend the trial size -- Crepe Erase Trial Size Body Duo, Intensive Body Repair 3.5 oz. and Exfoliating Body Polish 3 fl. oz. -- still not expensive, but with the money you save you can buy a tube of Retin-A, which will take up less room and might actually produce results.
summary: Sure cure for your crepey $100 bills

reviewText:
:: THE GOOD::
 It works. I've only been using this for a week and I've already noticed a significant difference with the skin on my neck. Now, I'm only just starting to show the signs of aging skin, so your mileage may vary, but the crepe texture I get when I stretch my neck is all but gone.

 It's pleasant to use. I like how light and gentle both creams are. The Exfoliating Body Polish uses beads versus harsher sand-like crystals in other exfoliants I've tried. The Intensive Body Repair cream is also less invasive than other products that promise skin rejuvenation.

::THE BAD::
 I find the "Duo" somewhat disproportionately sized. I'm cruising through the Exfoliating Body Polish and barely putting a dent in the Body Repair cream.

 Expensive. While this product is working for me, it is definitely prohibitively expensive to "try". And its 3oz version isn't experimentally priced either.
summary: This is a great product, if you can stomach the cost

reviewText:
I don't see how this kit is going to reduce the "crepe" effect as the name strongly suggests. It's a good exfoliator though.

Signs of aging aren't going to be smoothed away but the skin can be made healthier through exfoliation and for some the moisturizing is an excellent second step. As far as I can see, the innovation this product represents is that it's a 2-step process.

The products have a light citrus scent. They don't have SPF protection. They're not exclusively directed to people with "crepey" skin, since of course exfoliation and moisturizing are good for non-crepey skin.

My wife likes the product and reports that it's good although the cost seems high even after use.
summary: Good exfoliating product with a name that over-promises

reviewText: Lotion feels great on skin and appears to smooth, if not totally erase, crepey upperarm area.  I just ordered another round. . .

I got the Crepe Erase Ultra-Hydrating Body Lotion to help with the skin on my arms that is thinning and is no longer as resilient as it used to be. Ah, the joys of aging.

This lotion is designed to hydrate the skin and plump it it so it looks more youthful and healthy. It was designed to be used  with Crepe Erase Intensive Body Treatment but I did not buy the cream as it was quite expensive. So, the body lotion was left to do the job on its own. The lotion is light feeling when you put it on and absorbs fairly quickly. I like that quality because I don't like waiting around for something to dry before I can get dressed. I don't have a ton of time to waste that way. I applied the lotion every day in the morning for almost a month. By the end of the first week, I could see a difference in the texture of the skin on my arms. It was getting smoother and the fine wrinkles were not as apparent. I kept using it for the better part of month and I was pleased with the results.

My only complaint was the scent of the lotion. I usually try to get cosmetics and skin care products with no perfume in them as I have very sensitive skin.  As a result, I did not use this lotion on my face. That was only asking for trouble and I didn't need that. The lotion was fine using it only on my arms.

I like the product and recommend it for help with taming those signs your aging skin needs attention.
summary: Crepe Erase Ultra-Hydrating Body Lotion is a nice lotion to ease the fine wrinkles that develop as you get older. It works.

reviewText: A very rich, luxurious-feeling cream with a hideous name.  It's in the pricey range, but it is a nice big tube of lotion.  I like the scent and use it more as a general moisturizer, I'm not sure what crepes are and I don't want to google it!

I love this stuff, I use it tat night after I have used  my shower face brush. The skin on my face arms and hands is much better in a week. My hands were looking very worn, now they look nice and feel smooth.

I have been testing this Ultra-Hydrating Body Lotion for several weeks. Initially I was using it on my arms and legs, but decided to discontinue doing that since those parts of my body are rarely exposed and I wasn't seeing any benefit from the lotion. Since the lotion is rather costly, I decided that I would continue to use it only on my neck and upper chest area. The saggy skin on my neck does appear to be slightly smoother and feels moist and soft, though still saggy - the lotion doesn't purport to fix that problem! I really like the citrusy scent and thick texture of the lotion. A little goes a long way, so I will continue to use it on my neck daily to moisturize and plump up the loose skin on my neck. Like others, I find the product name, Crepe Erase, to be rather off-putting, and believe that the manufacturer should consider another name. Perhaps they could just drop the "Crepe Erase" title and use the other descriptors on the lotion tube: "TruFirm Complex, Ultra Hydrating Body Lotion".
summary: Moderately Effective, Great Scent, But Rather Costly

reviewText: Wow, this product is so smooth and the fragrance is divine! My daughter is convinced also that once applied on the skin the fragrance changes a little to a super mild and even more pleasant quality. The Crepe Erase Ultra-Hydrating Body Lotion is a high quality product. Living in South Dakota with the dry, harsh winters, we have come to appreciate good quality moisturizers.

This lotion is super thick.  It goes on as expected but then it is not greasy nor gross.  I kind of thought that all the claims were crap, but after a week of using every night on my knees, the skin looks tons better.  I was getting those super ugly lines that radiate out from around the knee.  Now I have only about two where the skin folds naturally.  Super weird, but GREAT!  There is no noticeable scent, just rich thick cream.  This lotion is just one part in a whole Crepe Erase line.  The lotion is the lightest treatment, for those just starting into the crepey years.  lol
summary: Visible difference after a week of using every night.

reviewText:
This stuff hydrates.  My skin looked firmer pretty much immediately.  Plus you don't need to use a lot.  Now if you think it will take away wrinkles that probably is unrealistic but it may make them look less visible.  I have been using it off and on the past week and can see results that are consistent and hold up.
Good product but don't have unrealistic expectations
summary: Hydrates & firmer skin. But if you think it will take away wrinkles that probably is unrealistic but it may make them look less

reviewText: Two problems with this product: the dimethicone's drying after-effect defeats the purpose, and the product name. Does anyone like the name of their favorite skin product associated with the word "crepe"? It's creepy. And crepey. Where else do you hear the word crepe? Oh yes, those crepe buntings covering coffins at funerals. Sure, our skin loses elasticity with age, but I don't want it assumed that I've got cryptkeeper skin! I feel that I have to hide this product from the public, and with good reason. The first person to see the tube on my bathroom counter came out and appeared to be examining my face, looking for something. When I asked, she replied that she didn't think my skin looked bad at all. Include on the tube a description of how the product works to eliminate the appearance of crepey skin all you want - in fine print. But please, rename it something less unappealing!

I thought this lotion was excellent in resolving dry skin patches.  It goes on creamy smooth, has just a slight pleasant fragrance, and lasts several hours.  I have a few dry patches on my face and legs, and this lotion improved my skin after just a couple of uses.  Minus a star for the price tag that I believe to be too high.
summary: Good effective lotion for dry skin patches

reviewText: Got this for my wife who loves lotion. First time use it smells good, feels good, goes on easy. It's expensive compared to a lot of lotions but it is becoming popular. So far she has no problems with it. We'll see how it goes over time.
summary: First time use it smells good, feels good

reviewText:
I really like the scent of this lotion (I'm big on scents). It's a large 7.5oz tube that has a flip top. As soon as I opened the tube (which was sealed in plastic and also had a seal inside) it reminded me of a smell from my childhood that might be Sea & Ski Suntan Lotion, so I compared the scents (yes, I still do have some Sea & Ski) and found the Sea & Ski does also have a citrusy scent, but it's much stronger than this Crepe Erase lotion.

The lotion is thick enough that it doesn't run out of the tube. If used sparingly it should last quite a while. It does make my hands feel softer and absorbs into the skin without feeling greasy. Being almost 65 I'd definitely say my skin has lost it's youthful snap; sigh. It also seems to make my hands look firmer and not as wrinkly. The scent lingers; I keep smelling my hands and they still smell like lemon.

I'm really liking the feel and smell of this lotion, but the current price of $29 for 7.5 oz. I think is too high.

Yes, the actress Jane Seymour is the product spokesperson for Crepe Erase product line by  Guthy-Renker. Seriously though I would have liked to have tried the complete product line to evaluate the efficacy:
Exfoliating Body Polish
Intensive Body Repair Treatment
Refining Facial Scrub
Restorative Facial Treatment
Ultra Hydrating Body Lotion

I used the lotion (not a cream) on my 54 year old florescent white arms for 20 days and found it to be a good moisturizer. The only turnoff is the citrus scent which conflicted with the perfume I like to wear.

fyi - Crepe Erase products do not contain sunscreen.

Winner -  not tested on animals.
summary: If it's good enough for Dr. Quinn Medicine Woman, it's good enough for me

reviewText: I am not totally sure that I love this cream.  I think I wanted it to be richer and much more emollient.  It did not have a strong scent at all...which was a really nice change.  However...as nicely un scented as it was I felt as though I still needed a richer lotion to use along this with this one.  I would never use it on bare legs in the summer because I didn't like the way it left my legs still looking kind of dry.  It absorbed really quickly but I didn't like the feel of it. I did not feel as hydrated as I wanted to.

My skin is often dry often moisturize twice daily when I'm out side a lot.  I slather myself often and I have a number of favorite lotions that work well.

The Crepe Erase Ultra-Hydrating Body Lotion is quite good and I had no set expectations.  The very first thing I noticed was a pleasant scent, stronger than most other lotions I use, but not too much. I do tend to like a scent to my lotions.

It applied very nicely, a cream thickness to it, not watery or runny. It absorbs well and hydrates my skin nicely. It's pricey for a lotion, but good for what you get. I'm in the sun a lot and this makes a difference in the appearance of my skin, which is well hydrated skin.

A little does go a long way and while I like it a lot, I pay the same for a Creighton coconut and Cocoa butter based lotion that is 33oz for the same money. Don't get me wrong, it's certainly good but maybe I'm not firmly enough in the target market for this product.

This body lotion has dimethicone, olive oil, glycerine, coconut oil, shea butter and cocoa butter and several flower and herb extracts in its composition. Given the relatively lower cost compared to many skin hydration lotions from prestige brands I find it to be a ok for the price. Skin hydration and repair is a constant process anyway, and one has to keep at it every day and also take vitamins and drink lots of water or even the best cream does nothing.

So Crepe Erase is working for me and I am using it on my arms and neck. So far so good. It works nicely in the Spring season when it's still cold enough for skin to get dry. I tried using it for my face but it burned really badly, maybe due to higher alcohol content. I don't have very sensitive skin and typically I can apply most body and hand lotions to my face. But not this one, it stings! So I am giving it 3 stars, if it was relatively less irritating on my face and around my eyes, I would rate it higher.
summary: Erases dry spots on body, but irritates facial skin.

reviewText:
I love the highly perfumed scent of this lotion- it's got a very, very strong lemon note with less prominent notes of lavender, cinnamon, and chocolate.
It's a white color, and a perfect consistency for me- it comes out of the tube easily but it isn't at all thin or watery.  It's thick enough so there's no waste squeezing it out, and it isn't so thick it doesn't spread easily.  It absorbs in quickly, and leaves skin highly scented, smooth, and soft, and it does ease crepe on my hands, knees, neck and arms.

My main issue with this product is that it does contain dimethicone, which, to me is a cheap ingredient that feels great but isn't all that great for skin when used regularly.  Some people find that dimethicone causes their skin to get drier over time with regular use, like a rebound type dryness.  I switch my lotions out a lot depending on what scent I feel like, and I rarely use them daily, so it's really not a problem for me.  This could be an issue for some, but not others.

Bottom line, it's highly perfumed- you probably won't like it if you don't like the scent of lemons.  It works as advertised but I wouldn't use it frequently, and monitor that your individual skin doesn't suffer from a rebound type dryness with it's use.
summary: Lemony, creamy, works well for me, I'd just not use it all the time because of the dimethicone in it

reviewText:
I tried to use Crepe Erase and found it so heavily perfumed, it was nauseating. I used it on my hands and didn't notice much to write about. Certainly not any better than a store brand Olay. Some may have great results but if you have any perfume sensitivities, stay clear.
The strong, alcohol/perfume lingered and every time I put my hand near my lips, they actually stung. I could never use this product on my face.
You do get a nice big tube, so there's that. This product is not for me.

I like this lotion a lot. The scent is very pleasant and not too strong. And it seems to have a lot of nice ingredients including olive oil, coconut oil and shea butter.  It also does seem to be really hydrating to my skin.

It's pricy but this is a large bottle, I'll update in a month or two about the longer term results. So far, really nice.

Rating Explanation: 3.5 stars for how it did make my skin shimmer nicely. 2.0 stars for the pricing of Crepe Erase products. 2.0 for the too-strongly-floral scent, and how it seems to dry out my hands a little.

Description: relatively large tube (but at this review it's a little over $28 a tube), thick cream-white, and a floral/citrus scent.

Testing: I applied the Crepe Erase to my right hand and my Vaseline Intensive Care to my left hand--rubbing it in circular motions as the Crepe Erase instructions indicated. Then I compared how it felt applying and what my hands looked like side-by-side. The Crepe Erase is a little more "greasy" while my regular lotion soaked into my skin more readily. Comparing my hands, there wasn't a lot of difference except that the Crepe Erase hand seemed to have a bit of a shine to it--perhaps some kind of light-reflecting ingredient.

But the weird thing is that I notice while the Crepe Erase is more emollient going on, it tends to, ironically, dry out my hands. When I first opened the product and applied it to my hands, I did notice later on my hands felt dry but I thought it was from something else I did during the day. I wasn't sure about this until I applied Crepe Erase to my right and Intensive Care to my left hand, and sure enough, the hand with Crepe Erase, 20 minutes later, is more dry feeling while the Vaseline Intensive Care hand still feel soft and supple--hmmm - I wonder about this.

I then applied the Crepe Erase to my body, arms, legs. Again it's a little greasy going on, but eventually soaks in. There was that same light-reflecting "shimmery" look--I've seen this with some other types of moisturizers so again I assume it's something in the ingredient. I do like this, even if temporary.

Company Claims: The company makes a lot of claims about how gross aging skin is and how they will make our skin look younger again. Well, aside from the fact that it'd be nice to be able just to age normally while still taking good care of our body and skin by eating right, exercise, using sunscreen, and drinking plenty of water, as for the claims of making my skin "younger looking," there is really no way to tell what this product is doing at a cellular level to change my skin below the surface other than having that documented scientifically/dermatological over time. Unless the results are dramatic enough that I can see them right in front of me. However, my thoughts are that if one really wants a change to aging skin (aside from the healthy living we should all do), one would have to do more than Crepe Erase to get there--retinoids or Botox or surgery, oh my! While there may be some slight changes, this "over the counter" cream probably isn't going to work miracles--however, until I try it over at least a month, I have to give it some benefit of the doubt. However, for the price, even with small changes, it would give me pause. I am willing to give it a go to see over the next month if it will-if I can stand the scent and the slight drying effect on my skin.

I'm not particularly fond of the scent--there is almost a rose-scented aspect to it even if it doesn't have rose in it, and that's one of my least-favorite scents. It doesn't dissipate quickly, so I'm a little put off by that highly floral scent lingering.

Research on Product:  The ingredients list shows a lot of hydrating - emollient - ingredients--like shea/cocoa butter, and oils like olive/coconut that can really moisturize your skin - a good thing there. There is dimethicone in it--that's an ingredient in the make-up primers you can put on your face before your foundation to allow the foundation to "sit" on your skin--that may be why it doesn't absorb quickly, and why it makes the skin look a bit smoother--but I also know that if you massage your skin, it will cause a slight inflammatory response that will make your skin swell a little and that in itself will smooth out some wrinkles.

In all my research, I could not find anything on TruFirm - an ingredient in Crepe Erase. For all I know it may do the job of smoothing out skin on a more permanent level, but with continued use of this product, and the other two that go with it when they arrive, I will do everything they instruct and then see if my skin shows any difference, and if I note a difference that makes the cost of these products worth it (and I'm very skeptical), then I will come back here and tell you all.

Final Observations: I am put off by the cost of these Crepe Erase products, and unless I see something dramatic over the weeks of use of this product and the body buffing and body repair, which are super expensive, I can't ever imagine spending that kind of money on a non-prescription product that has an ingredient for which no one seems to know what it is or what it does to my skin. However, if there are dramatic results, I will certainly come back here and tell you all about it.

I am skeptical but willing to give it a continued-use try.

.
summary: Did ironically dry out my skin a little . . . .

reviewText: Is it weird that I only have crepe skin on my left arm and not my right? Either way, I decided to give this a try and so far I really like it. My crepe skin isn't that bad at all, but I wanted to try this before it gets worse. I saw a difference immediately after applying it. Basically it just moisturizes your skin and plumps it up so that the skin is more full and less thirsty. This is how it pulls the crepe out. I did see results right away, but what I really love about this is the fragrance. I don't tolerate a lot of fragrances but this stuff smells so good. It isn't an overpowering scent at all and I prefer this over most perfumes. Plus you have the bonus of having nice plump and soft skin without making your skin feel greasy or sticky. I'm very happy with this product so far. And since I haven't broken out in hives, it's a definte 5-star thumbs up from me.
summary: Love this product. Love the fragrance and my soft plump skin.

reviewerName: Leah Maines, best-selling, award-winning author, actor, and editor
reviewText: This skin treatment has little fragrance so it does not interfere with my perfume, and it does not bother me when I don't feel like adding yet another scent to my skin treatment routine.  The creamy lotion is non greasy and quickly absorbs.  My skin can get pretty dry, and this cream wasn't able to fully fight the dryness.  I really didn't see any improvement with crepe skin issues either.  I'm not sure it's worth the money for my skin so I doubt I would purchase this in the future.

I'm normally a bit skeptical of lotions, but this cream truly does hydrate, and skin stays hydrated all day.  Its third ingredient is olive oil, and I have to wonder if the ancient Greek women were on to something when they'd coat themselves in olive oil to prevent sunburn. It also contains coconut oil,  shea butter and cocoa seed butter. There's a very subtle fragrance to this lotion.  It goes on smoothly and quickly penetrates the skin, leaving no greasy residue.

This creamy white lotion is lightly fragranced with citrus. Formulated with olive and coconut oil, it glides on and absorbs quickly. It made my skin feel soft and look smooth. I have an area of crepiness on my hand and wrist from driving without sun protection. It did eliminate the appearance of crepiness. My mother has crepiness on her arms due to living eight decades. While this product didn't eliminate the crepiness, it did lessen it.  The tube arrives encased in plastic which eliminates damage from potential spillage. Overall an effective product that is enjoyable to use.

I love the aroma and how gently it glides and slides on my skin.  This is a good product that as other U.S. reviewers have noted, does work well with related products.  In addition to consisting of natural products, it makes my skin feel good.

I requested this for my wife, and little did I know how much she'd love it.  It came in such a luxurious package, and even the fancy metal (as opposed to plastic) spatula impressed her.  That was just the start.  It smells great, feels smooth, and skin is left feeling plump and refreshed.  The product claims powerful hydration, and more than anything, it's a superb moisturizer--powerful hydration indeed.

The fly in the ointment is the cost.  Everyone has different budgets and priorities, but more than any other ridiculously pricey stuff she's tried, this is the one that amazed the misses, and that makes me happy.

This is one of the best skin cremes I have ever used. Yes, it is expensive. But this is one of the times I can honestly say you get what you pay for. A little goes a long way, this should last you for months, so it is well worth it. Goes on rich and luxurious, absorbs super quick into your skin. I use it immediately after I shower to lock in moisture and I can say for the few months I have been using it now, my skin looks and feels fresher and softer. I love the fragrance and the way it applies. I can highly recommend this IS Clinitcal creme to anyone with 40+ skin. Minimizes wrinkles, adds moisture back to aging skin and makes your skin glow and feel wonderful. Takes years off your face!

Ive been using this for almost 1 month now.  Many times face crmes irritate my skin so I have to stop using them. This crme did not irritate  not even the sensitive under-eye area.  It is very rich so a little goes a long way.  It absorbs fairly quickly & does not leave my skin feeling greasy as long as I use a small amount.  If you put on too much, it is kind of sticky/greasy feeling.

It has a light citrusy scent  there is no added fragrance/parfum listed so I assume that is from the ingredients  various citrus extracts and oils.

It doesnt miraculously get rid of fine lines/wrinkles but it does plump them up & make your skin look more youthful.

I have an extremely sensitive face so I was very hesitant to try this product (as I am anything new in fear of breakouts). First of all, I did not get any break outs at all. I like to tan in a booth a couple days a week during the winter and this product definitely helped put the moisture back in my face. I was also starting to get severe smile wrinkles and they certainly seemed to lighten up or go away completely depending on where. Highly recommend this product.

Only a long span of time will tell if this is the fountain of youth or not, but I'm using it sparingly. I have never reacted to anti-aging creams before but the first night I used this, my eyes oozed and squeezed shut. And if I'm not supposed to use this around the eyes, what's the point. That's where I need it most. I have since used it again, but only on my forehead. I did not have an allergic reaction that time.

Practice caution. Test it out on a sensitive area of your body first.
summary: Only a long span of time will tell if this ...

reviewText:
iS Clinical eye cream is a really nice light anti-aging eye cream. Ive been using it for just under a month and have already noticed some brightening of the area under my eyes and some plumping of the fine lines around my eyes.

I have somewhat dry combination skin and needed an eye cream that was light and would absorb - not sit on top, feeling heavy. This light eye cream has antioxidants, peptides, and hylauronic acid - all the things my dermatologist talks about getting in an eye cream. So far this cream is keeping my eye area moisturized and looking brighter.

Another thing that is a must for me with any product I use on my face, but especially around my eyes, is that it not burn or blur my eyes. I've had A LOT of problems finding something that fit the bill, but finally I've found the iS products have not caused any problems with my eyes. As someone who's had 4 eye surgeries, I won't compromise on this point. This product is dermatologist approved, and although I'd prefer ophthalmologist approved, I know these designations aren't given freely.  So I was more comfortable giving it a try.

The application process is simple. On clean skin, pump about a half a pump onto your ring fingers. Put a small amount under each eye and gently tap around the area beneath each eye. The product absorbs quickly and is perfect under makeup. Also apply at night after cleansing your face - before bedtime. I love the iS products and I love the packaging. Most products that come in a pump applicator don't allow you to get all of the product. This one does! The top comes off easily so you can get every last drop!

The results thus far have been good and with daily use I'm hoping to lose some more of the wrinkles around my eyes.

If you have mature skin and are looking for a product with peptides, antioxidants, and growth factors you might give this one a try.

This Youth Intensive Creme is light and soft with a great scent. It has great coverage and absorbs quickly into skin. It isn't heavy and doesn't leave any residue, like some other face cremes.

It did come with an applicator, but I don't use it, simply because I'm not always near a sink to rinse it after each use. I usually just use a clean fingertip instead.

Wrinkles and lines were visibly reduced almost immediately after I started using this creme. Yes, it is expensive, but a little goes a long way and it really is a great product. I recommend considering the total cost over the number of uses you expect... that helps put the cost into perspective!

I've been using this moisturizer morning and night for about a week now, and I've never found a moisturizer I like better.  I have mostly been using CeraVe on the advice of my dermatologist, and washing my face with Cetaphil, but that's IT as far as product on my face. I have eczema that flares up around my mouth, nose, and eyes, and just about any product I try makes it flare up.  The CeraVe/Cetaphil combination kept my skin clean and somewhat moisturized and didn't make my face get red and flaky, and I thought that was the best I could hope for. Every once in awhile I would try another product, hoping to find something that worked better than 'adequate', but always had problems.

Until now. After a week of use, I have noticeably fewer fine lines and less redness.  My skin feels softer and examination with my 15x mirror reveals no flakiness.  The fine line reduction is as good as I had with my one try with a Retinol product, but without the extreme redness and flakiness that showed up after three days of using Retinol. The redness I still struggle with a little, but it is much less, and considerably less blotchy and noticeable.  Even my 11 year old son noticed my face was less red.

You don't use very much - the product comes with a tiny spoon, but honestly even that little spoon holds more than you need. I barely touch my finger to the surface and then dot that around my face twice, and that is plenty. So even though this is by no means cheap, it's going to last awhile. And it's so effective that it's worth it. Very happy!
summary: Love it - Better than Retinol for my eczema

reviewText: This is a high quality product.  My wife has reaction issues with so many such products because of contaminants, etc.  Not with this one though.  It works and feels great.  Definitely recommend.

I have struggled for years with my uneven skin tone, n recently had issues with my face feeling dry & tight after having a bath. This product has rejuvenated my skin & now my skin tone is visibly evening out, after using the product for under 2 months. It is definitely workin for me. Hope is does the same for u
summary: I have struggled for years with my uneven skin tone ...

reviewText:
I have tried many facial moisturizers and creams over the years and with these types of products, the old adage about "pay for what you get" is not necessarily the truth. I've seen many dermatologists on TV say that some of the drug store age-reducing creams are just as good.

In this case, I am giving this 5 stars because I love how it feels on my face. My skin feels like it's absorbing more and it's greasy without being greasy, if that makes any sense. In other words, I can definitely sense that my face feels more moisterized and there is a little coating of product left on my face after I put it on.

Despite that bit of coating, I can easily apply either a BB cream or cream or powder foundation over it and it blends better than ever. When I put this cream on at night, my face still seems moisterized in the morning.

This product also has a nice smell; neither medicinal nor flowery.

Recommended. I will be using this product in the future since I like it so much. Hard to tell if it's making me look any younger, but I'll settle for having my skin feel better and having my makeup and foundation blend so smoothly.
summary: 5 stars for how it feels on my skin - would be hard to tell if it really makes my skin more "youthful"

reviewText: It is creamy and goes on so smooth, the scent isn't overpowering. So far I have found no difference in my facial skin and the moisture doesn't seem to last long so my wrinkles appear more prevalent after a half hour or so. I feel this product doesn't live up to its claims, I can see no tightening my my skin and the wrinkles are not disguised and look actually worse if I only use this product. My face started looking so bad that I had to start using my usual products. Sorry but for my face it si pretty much thumbs down on this particular cream.

When it comes to skin care, I wasn't born yesterday.  And that's precisely the reason I'm in the market for an intensive creme product like this, which minimizes the effects of aging. For a price of $195, this product needs to deliver.

So the first thing I noticed was the packaging. It's definitely heavy-duty and elegant, which translates into expensive.  I'm guessing that a good 25% of the product cost is in the packaging. Subtract that cost, and iS Clinical is still way up there in price. I've used it for a week now, and will need to circle back after 30 days have gone by.  So far, I can report this: the creme is rich yet gentle, with a pleasant citrusy smell. Its hydration benefits are immediately evident. Compared to the last moisturizing product I used (Clarins), my face felt moisturized throughout the day.

Next to water (the #1 ingredient in any skincare product), the next is hyaluronic acid -- a substance that is naturally present in the body. In reading up abut it, I was most impressed: hyaluronic acid is said to have powerful anti-aging properties an done gram can hold up to six liters of water. Now THAT Is amazing.  The next few ingredients listed are also impressive.

Bottom line: I do love the feel and moisturizing effects of this product.  My only concern is whether the price/value ratio is too high. Only time will tell and I will gladly update this review in another month.
summary: For women who weren't born yesterday

reviewText: Was pretty skeptical to use this cream, as many products claim to promise a noticeable difference, but fail to deliver. I was pleasantly surprised to actually see the skin on my face look firmer and younger. I can imagine that with use over time that I will see even greater results!

I like this creme a lot. It's light and doesn't feel thick or heavy on the skin. It has a light, pleasant smell, unlike a lot of creams that just smell like your grandma.
