The tiny spoon is adorable, and helps measure out the amount to use.
The cream is very liquidy, so keep the lid on tight.
It plumps the skin up nicely before heading out the door.

I can't review it yet based on results after a few weeks, but I'd imagine that overall my skin will be looking younger because of it..
summary: I like this creme a lot

reviewText:
WOW!!  First of all the presentation of this product when you first open it is striking.  It is as though it is meant to be opened by royalty.  It comes in a shiny royal blue metallic box about 3 inches high that is taped shut with clear tape on two ends so that it doesn't open by accident.  When you life the lid off of the box there sits your beautiful jar of intensive cream appearing to be sitting on a "throne".
I am so not worthy....LOL
Now as to how this lovely product performs.....
Well, that's the best part.  I am 68 years old with aging, dry skin.  I am beginning to show a few liver spots, or aging spots on my face.  Well I seem to have found the fountain of youth.  This cream really works.  I appear to have younger skin almost immediately.  There is a lot of moisture in this product for one thing because my face is so smooth and soft.  I certainly like that.  But it is also showing fewer lines.  I like that even more.  Well, I suggest you give this a try.  I can tell you that it is pricey.  That's a fact.  But it should tell you something when I tell you that I won't run out.

It smells great - to me it's smells like lemons (a more sophisticated nose could describe it better), but when it arrived the bottle was open inside its cellophane-wrapped box - the Rochas box (not the Amazon shipping material) was drenched with the Eau de Toilette and the scent was so intense that my wife had to put the box on our front porch.  Now our neighborhood smells like lemons, I suppose.  If I had spent $70 for this product I would have taken and photo and asked Amazon to send me another as a replacement.  I'm guessing this is a very rare occurrence but deduct one star for faulty packaging.
summary: Smells great but leaked all over its packaging

reviewText: This is a fun, beachy kind of fragrance.  It has a cery strong limey smell and is very fruity overall.  It reminds you of drinking margaritas on the beach. It would be a fun scent for a day outdoors, but I cant envision it for an evening out. My hisband had the same reaction. He likes it, but it is not his favorite
summary: This is a fun, beachy kind of fragrance

reviewText: I definitely have nothing like this eau de toilette in my scent arsenal. It is so lovely with a mixed citrus scent but with the depth of vetiver. I don't have a professional perfume vocabulary; I will say the fragrance is full and lively. For me the end result is just so spring-like and balanced. I am completely new to this scent yet it is an instant favorite. Generous 3.3 oz bottle with an attractive textured design.

My hair is color treated, flat, straight and getting progressively thinner with age. It looks so thin lately that it's really become an issue for me. So far, I absolutely love the results I'm getting with R+Co Dallas Thickening Shampoo. It makes my hair look and feel noticeably fuller and thicker, yet the texture still feels soft and smooth. Other thickening shampoo I've tried seem to add volume by drying out my hair too much and making it frizzy. But with R+Co Dallas Thickening Shampoo, I get the added volume I want and my hair still feels manageable, smooth and even has some added bounce after blow drying with a round brush. My thin hair doesn't look or feel drier and actually looks revitalized after using this shampoo.

R+Co Dallas Thickening Shampoo is safe for color treated hair (according to R+Co customer service) and has UV protection. My hair looks clean and shiny after working a small amount throughout my hair and rinsing well. This shampoo has moderate fragrance out of the bottle, though the scent barely lingers in my hair. I like the scent even though I'm not much of a fragrance fan- I'm not sure of the exact fragrance, but I think it hints of citrus and lavender. This shampoo is sulfate and paraben free, gluten free and vegan, though it doesn't appear to be a chemical free product based on the ingredient list. Still, I love the results and recommend this thickening shampoo for those looking for a product to help with thin, flat or fine hair. Made in the USA.
summary: Love How This Shampoo Makes My Thin Hair Look Thicker And Revitalized-It Has Fragrance But Smells Pleasant To Me

reviewText: Product did not do as advertized. Left hair limp and stiff.

I'm not seeing any real results having used it a few times.  I'm used to some results right away.  It's not a bad shampoo, but I've used better thickening shampoos.

The scent is ok, kind of understated, but pleasant enough.

The bottle is crazy small for the price.  I won't be buying this.

R+Co Dallas Thickening Shampoo washes the hair very well.  The one thing I liked about it was the pleasing smell.  The shampoo rinses well and leaves the hair fresh and clean.  It does seem to add volume which is always good.  This is a nice shampoo that is well worth adding to the shower or bath.

This shampoo is nice and creamy, makes a wonderful lather and really left my hair soft. I have very fine hair and as I have gotten older there's less of it...UGH. This shampoo does seem to work in making my hair feel thicker. Lots of shampoos like this coat the hair shaft which is fine with me if it adds volume and thickness to my otherwise thinning hair.
summary: Worked pretty well on making my hair feel like it had lots of body.

reviewText: I usually use the Bumble & Bumble thickening shampoo, but I've grown tired of it and was looking for other options. This one is fabulous! It smells so, so good. Citrusy. It suds up well and my hair feels really nice. I'm going to try the conditioner, too.

Product description states that this shampoo is good for "Thin, fine hair in need of volume." That's my hair. Thin. Fine. Limp. Unattractive. Needs one or two volumizing products just to look "normal." With this shampoo, I'm one step ahead as soon as I've shampooed. It volumizes as well as any one after-shampoo product. Leaves my hair shiny and easy to style. Lathered well. Rinsed easily. I'm going to order the conditioner and see how they work together. I am not wild about the scent. To me, it seems woodsy and masculine. But I do love the effect on my hair.

I've used StriVectin High-Potency Wrinkle Filler lotion for a few weeks now and can say that the product does have my face and neck feeling baby soft, but I do not see any visible difference in my wrinkles.  I'm 54, and have a few on my face and forehead that I would love to lessen the appearance of.

This container is 15 ml - that's one half of an ounce.  Tiny container with a huge price tag.

I also notice a build up of product on my face after I use this - almost like I put clear fingernail polish on my face and its now peeling.  Not a good feeling.

Wrinkle filler?  I wish.
summary: No Visible Difference in My Wrinkles After Several Weeks of Application

reviewText:
This filler does work around fine lines.  It softens wrinkles around the eyes and upper lip.  It does not, however, eradicate deep lines over foreheads.  Half a pump press is enough to cover forehead, eyes and mouth area. Using it twice a day for at least a week shows some softness around the eyes.

The effects last most of the day.  The skin feels slightly tightened and moisturized.

Its always difficult to review and evaluate any type of anti-aging cream or lotion because most require testing over a period of time. Plus, if you're using other cosmetic products  its always hard to know if this new product is solely responsible for any improvement.

Because of this, what I can say is whether or not something is irritating to the skin because thats important to know, especially if you have sensitive skin like I do. As to that, I can report back that this product is not irritating  which is great.

What is surprising about this product is that  I can report back after only 2 weeks of use that it is helping. I am able see an improvement, but only  to one particular part of my face - the smallish area above my upper lip.

At first I tried the product all over and it was so-so, But now If I use the product twice a day on the lines on the limited area over my upper lip it,  it actually helps. (Just remember, before you use this, clean the area by using either a lip sugar glazer and wiping it off or you use whatever else you want to use to make sure the area is very clean and any dead skin sloughed off.)

This has really helped puff up and helped the bleeding lines that sometimes show up on your upper lip when you put on lipstick or gloss and this is the first product that has done that. Mind you, the lines aren't completely gone, but there is an improvement.

On the negative side, if this product is applied too heavily (which isn't hard to do,) you can end up with it peeling/sloughing off - not a good look when you happen to look in the mirror. When applied above the lip this way, it really looks bad so just be aware of that.
summary: Where its great, where it isnt. Pros and Cons

reviewerName: German Girl with a Spanish Name
reviewText: Been using this for about a week and not really seeing a difference.  Not sure if I used too much, but gets kind of a build up and starts kinda peeling, not a good look during the day.  It stings a bit when you first put it on, but it stops after just a few minutes.
summary: not a good look during the day

reviewText: StriVectin products are the only wrinkle products that I have consistently come back to and used for the last ten years. This filler is supposed to reduce the look of lines and wrinkles. While I don't really have deep lines and wrinkles, I want to prevent the ones I have from getting any worse. There are no miracle products. Period. But I have found through trial and error what works for me and Strivectin products,  particularly their excellent retinol eye cream,  are a favorite. I recommend giving them a try. I have been rarely disappointed in this brand.

I had great results. I took close up before and after pictures and was shocked at the difference with a little more than a week of using it.  Im an almost 60-year-old New England woman with generally well-kept skin thats outdoors daily and I have average wrinkles for my age.

I used a tiny dab as instructed and applied it to outer edges of my eyes, outside edge of my forehead, and around my nose/lip area. Mostly once a day. Sometimes twice a day. As instructed, I left it on by itself before applying anything else. My experience, which I have not seen this reported anywhere else, is that my skin flaked a bit on the first few applications. It slightly stung at first. Be careful and don't get it too close to your eyes.
I was skeptical, so I read all the reviews here and googled it to see what other sources said.

The Dermatology Review has a good explanation of what this product is about.  It includes user reviews there too and its a mixed bag, some love this and have amazing results, others nothing.

I also read aboaut this on The Consumer Health Digest website.  Similar information, saying results can appear faster for some. They also add that the company,  does appear to be a very reputable company who provides good customer care

Yes, its pricey. At this rate the tube will last a few months.

StriVectin does a really good job with its products.  The main reason like them is that they include some impressive ingredients in their products, and this one does that.  It absorbs very easily into the skin. A little bit goes a long way. I don't detect any kind of fragrance at all.  It didn't leave any kind of oily residue.
summary: Another excellent product from StriVectin that uses impressive ingredients.

reviewText: I'm a little ambivalent about this product. I'm 37 with a little sun damage, fair-medium skin and freckles, I don't have any extreme lines but the ones in my forehead seemed smoothed by this lotion when I'm not making any facial expressions. It sinks in nicely and no adverse effects. I'm not totally on board because of the price point and amount of product. This is a small pump tube. A little goes a long way, but I certainly wouldn't pay more then 15 bucks for it. There's no huge improvement for the price.

StriVectin has been around a while, starting out as a stretch mark cream, and as sometimes happens, what starts out as a product for one thing becomes a product for another as customers notice that the product does something extra than what it was intended for. In this case, the stretch mark cream was claimed also to help with wrinkles.

StriVectin has NIA-114, which is a form of Niacin/Vitamin B3 that may help the skin by strengthening the barriermaking the skin thicker or whatever so it is more like it was when it was younger.

You cant compare over-the-counter facial creams to the prescription retinoids, since the strength and effectiveness just aren't going to be the same, so best you can do is find over-the-counter creams that work almost as well, or with continued daily use maybe reach similar results over a longer period of time. So to that end, it makes it difficult to review a facial creams over-time effectiveness unless you wait the 3-4 months to see the difference it may make.

When I evaluate a face cream, serum, moisturizer, etc, I consider how it makes me feel, how it feels smoothing on my face, does it irritate my skin, the cost of the product, and are the claims it makes at any level working at allas in this case of StriVectin the immediate results claim.

Ive used this lotion over the last 3 days and though I don't have a lot of wrinkles, I do have aging skin. Evaluating it over my usual considerations:
1) It feels rather dry going on. Theres no luxe feel to it, but I do feel a bit of tightening to my skin, a little. I wish it were a little more luxe feeling for the price. That oh, this feels really nice feeling. However, the tightening feeling gives me the thought that something is working on some level to tighten my skin, even if temporary.
2) It does not irritate my skin. Theres not even a tingling or warming as I find with some creams. Only that slight tightening-dry feeling.
3) The cost is rather high for .5 oz of product. This is a tiny tube for about $60. For that price, Id like to see more dramatic immediate results, and Id like to know it is really going to do something I will actually notice weeks or months ahead, as now I tend to stare in the mirror after Ive applied it and think Is there a difference? I want to see the immediate results thing promised more definitively.

There may be a slight difference in the look of my skin on the immediate results level, but nothing dramatic. What Im more interested in is the long term effectiveness of the niacin/B3 (their NIA114). There is evidence that niacin/B has positive effects on the skin. At $60 for .5 oz, however, you could purchase a prescription strength retionol product and receive a more powerful punch for a better bargain. However, if your skin cannot tolerate the Retin-A types of products, then a lotion, serum, or cream with niacin/Bs may be great for you to try.

Im really on the fence about this product. Im not excited about it, nor do I think its worthless. But, overall, its not exciting me, or making me feel great about how it feels, enough to spend $60 on that tiny tube of product. So thats a 3-star for me.

Ill continue to use it daily until the product is gone. If I see any dramatic result, of course Ill return and report that, but I likely will return to other products that have quality ingredients for less cost. And consider a prescription-strength retinol treatment should I want those more dramatic results.

Thing is, the prescription strength products may seem as if they will be too expensive, but when you compare the cost per ounce of some of these products, like StriVectin, the better bargain is the prescription strength. Over-the-counter products make fantastic claims they cant always back up by science. But, they are effective in their own way, and good for those who would rather not mess with prescription strength products, or that those products are too harsh for their skin.

Id likely not purchase this product again but I will use it until its gone.
summary: Claims may be too lofty, but it has its merits

reviewText: Jury is still out on this and I will update as I keep using it but so far I'm not that impressed.  I notice no difference in any wrinkle or line and the "filling effect" is not so much.  I know nothing really will completely fill in wrinkles but so far this has done absolutely nothing.

The BIO IONIC Boarshine Brush does indeed give you shiny manageable hair. My hair is short, so there wasn't as a noticeable difference as with my daughter's long curly hair.  This brush not only cut the drying time, but left her with smooth and shiny hair. I have uploaded Before/After pics. The "before" pic was her hair after using her regular hairbrush. The "after" picture is with the BIO IONIC Boarshine Brush.  Nice, comfortable grip. Easy to work with. Nice results!

This is a big, salon-type brush, much larger than other hair brushes I'm used to. The bristles feel a little rough, especially if you don't have thick or "big" hair. I found it works best after shampooing, when you're using it to style your hair while blow drying. It gives your hair a nice shine while keeping it free of tangles.

Again, my only critique is that the rough texture of the bristles took some getting used to. It's definitely a high quality brush that appears it will last a long time.
summary: Big, Salon-Type Brush with Rough Bristles - Best for Blow Drying

reviewText: I've used Boar bristle hair brushes for most of my life but must admit this is the best one by far, my hair is graying so its dry and kinky after washing and conditioning but once I start using this great thick Boar brush my hair gets a natural shine without looking oily or greasy, it holds its shape and looks GREAT too! I won't use anything else after being spoiled with the benefits this brush offers.  The size of this brush is excellent too, I can twist it as I brush adding some wavy to my hair too. My only problem is I keep loosing this chair brush, my girlfriend keeps walking off with it because she like it so much, guess I''ll buy another one so she can have her own. Her hair is thin blond that is about shoulder length, she also loves the shine plus the lasting control.
summary: This Boar bristle hair brush leaves my hair with a natural shine that doesn't compare to hair products, its smooth but not oily

reviewText: Boar bristles combined with nylon bristles makes this a unique brush that produced great results. Dry styling actually worked quite well. Combining a hot blower with this styling tool on hair with product in it helped smooth and shape the style. For wet styling the brush moved professionally through shoulder length hair and left no flyaways in a dry climate. The large brush has a comfortable handle and is easy to manipulate.

For the record, I didn't realize this was targeted at menopausal skin, just aging skin generally. I can't speak to the effects of menopause, but I'm 45 & definitely see the effects of aging (lines, additional dryness, loss of tone and duller texture). My skin is dry and a bit sensitive.

The texture of this cream is somewhere between cream and gel. It's quite light and absorbs quickly and fully. At first, it seemed like it couldn't possibly be hydrating enough, but after just a few days, I could tell it was just as hydrating as my other recent favorites (derma e hydrating night cream & kiehl's ultra). My skin looks pretty dewy & not at all greasy, even before washing in the am or at night. I've gotten away with skipping an application without a noticable effect on my skin (usually only a problem with lower-end creams). And the more I used it, the more it grew on me. Though plenty moisturizing, it's non-greasy, and I found my bangs stay cleaner longer with this product. If you're not an everyday shampooer & you have bangs, you'll appreciate that.

A little goes a long way, which was also a surprise for such a light-feeling cream. I feel I'm using a bit less than kiehl's or derma e, which is good because this is a bit more pricey (though still in the ballpark, not a completely different zip code like some products out there).

The feature that was odd at first is the cooling property. If you've used cooling lotion, you'll know the feel--a very, very light menthol-type sensation. I assume that's to combat nighttime hot flashes. I can't say whether it's effective there, but I'm certainly looking forward to using this in the summer, when it will be especially refreshing. Do note the cooling sensation can feel a bit sensitive around the eyes--I feel a bit sting-y for 20-30 seconds when I first apply to eyelids--but for me, this is almost always true of any cream with anti-aging ingredients. It's gone quickly and leaves no reaction on my skin. I was able to use this with a mild retinol cream at night with no sensitivity issues under my eyes, but when I tried the combination on my lids it was too much and I had to stop both for a few days (either product alone was fine), so if you have mildly sensitive skin & want to try retinol on your lids, either use a mild eye cream or save it for days you're skipping lids (I don't like to fuss with a separate eye cream if I'm already adding a second product to my routine). (For the record the retinol was also a Vichy product.)

Due to the light texture, I found it just as suitable for daytime use.
summary: Cooling, fast-absorbing gel cream is great for day, too; stings a bit on my eyelids, especially used with retinols.

reviewText:
The description I first saw of this made it sound like just a general moisturizer.  It's changed since them to focus more on post-menopausal skin.  I'm not menopausal yet let alone post.  But I do have skin that is fairly sensitive and that gets dry very easily.  So I figured this couldn't hurt.

The good news is that my skin definitely feels tighter and better moisturized than it has been lately.

The bad news is that the scent is too overpowering for me so I cannot use it regularly.

Great if you don't mind a strong scent.  If, like me that is a deal breaker for you, I'd try something else.

This was a little tough to review, being a pre-menopausal male ;-)  Usually my wife loves to try new products, but alas she still wasn't the target market, nor did I want to imply that she was.  Fortunately there are other ladies in my life who are more of the age that this is designed for (yet still young and lovely).

It's a thick dense cream, perhaps surprisingly so.  It's every bit as moisturizing as you'd expect for the price or for the aforementioned thickness.  That moisturizing doesn't take much of the product, as it's one of those "a little goes a long way affairs".  After applying, you're almost left with the feeling that you put too much on, as it's so thick and moist (almost tacky).  Definitely start with much less than you'd expect to need.  The results are refreshing and invigorating, as the skin feels soft, yet firm.  It's not devoid of scent, but it's rather mild in that regard, and it hasn't caused any issues whatsoever.

All in all, it's a nice product, but it doesn't have a value in excess of its cost, and I cannot foresee a follow up purchase.  YMMV, and it's worth a try.
summary: Rather nice, for the price.  May be worth a try.

reviewText: Another outstanding Vichy product.  This cream is silky smooth, and absorbs perfectly.  Leaves skin amazingly replenished and protected, with absolutely zero greasiness.  We're very pleased with this night cream.

I am older and have very dry skin, I don't even wear base make up anymore because the makeup settles into the flakey areas of my dry skin & accentuates those areas.
The most noticeable results from using this nightly is that the dry flakey areas of my skin on my face are gone. My skin is noticeably "normal"! Something I never thought I would have again. Also I have VERY sensitive skin, most lotions/creams burn terribly and/or cause breakouts (*something I NEVER had growing up!) this cream did not cause any problems at all. Yes, it is "moist" feeling when applied and remains so for quite some time. Just read the ingredients, the first 3 items (in descending order) are water, glycerin & apricot kernel oil!!  Of course it will stay "moist feeling" for awhile after applying it. That is a GOOD thing! It is NIGHT TIME cream! Just apply a scant amount if it bothers you but really, isn't that why you are buying it anyways, to have moist , refreshed looking/feeling skin again? It does what it says, I only took off one star because for the ingredients I really feel they could have given us this product for a bit better price regardless of their cost in developing it but it does leave my skin better than a LOT of more expensive products that I have had to throw away because of side effects in the past.
summary: It leaves my dry, post menopausal skin feeling and looking better than it has in a long time plus NO stinging,burning or side ef

reviewText:
Really feels good when you put it on your skin and then it has a hint of a tingling sensation for a few seconds.  I focus on the area around my eyes.  I am 60 and really have that weathered look around my eyes.  I also have some health issues which has hurt my complexion.  Im currently doing intermittent fasting and green smoothies.

The cream is not greasy and dries quickly.  Its called night cream but then the instructions say to put it on morning and night.  I normally do both anyway.  It has a light fragrance that doesnt overpower my nose.  Some creams I cannot use because the fragrance is too strong but this one is subtle and has a nice smell.

I think it's helping and I like that it feels thicker than most other creams, which never do a thing for my skin, The area around my eyes is now smooth and soft.  I have combination skin and I just had a horrible time with some Vitamin C serum 20 from Skinceuticals which caused blackheads in ALL of my pores so I'm cautious about where I put any cream at the moment, except around my eyes which are drier than a desert and crepey.
Wake up to baby smooth skin. It does the job. No complaints here.

I am a big fan of the Vichy Neovadiol Magistral Oil and use it every day. I love that stuff. This Replenishing Night Cream is a great addition to using the Neovadiol oil. This is a very rich and moisturizing cream that you can use at night and then use in the morning under make up. It's very hydrating and makes my skin feel great while lessening fine lines. There are a few Vichy products that I have tried that are okay, but the Neovadiol products rate very high in my book. The products are expensive but they last a long time. This moisturizer is best for women over 50. The oil however, I use everyday and so does my teenaged daughter. There are some products this company makes that are hit and miss, but this nighttime cream is very good and I recommend it along with the oil to combat wrinkles and overall dryness and aging skin.

I'm rather picky about what I put on my face since my face is very sensitive, but I have heard a lot of good things about this so I thought I would try it.  The first thing I noticed was how heavy this cream was.  I tend to like lighter creams because the heavier ones will almost always break my face out.  This cream so far has not broken me out, but I can't say I like or feel comfortable with leaving it on my skin.  The first night I made it 3 hours and then had to wash it off and the next few nights I made it farther each time and have finally made it all night.  In the morning I wash it off and m face does feel softer and I can see a few differences.  I can't say what this will do long term, but I am going to continue to use it for now.

This is a heavy cream that leaves your face feeling a bit tacky, so if you don't like your skin feeling sticky, you won't like this. I don't like having it on my face, but I went ahead and used it anyway. It has a mild fragrance that isn't too bad. I have a sensitivity to fragrances, but I can handle this one well and the fragrance dissipates fairly quickly anyway. The price is a bit on the high side but a little goes a long way and it does seem to plump up your skin nicely. After showering, the tackiness was gone and the skin was still soft and not overly dry like it normally is after I take a shower. So far it hasn't caused any acne or rashes on my face. If you don't mind going to bed with a tacky face, then it's worth a try. I'm not used to wearing much of anything on my face other than a light moisturizer, so it could just be that I'm not used to the feeling on my face.
summary: Thick and tacky after applying, but seems to work well.

reviewText: I love this night cream.  Very nice and not greasy.

Although I am not totally in love with the scent of this night cream, I have found it to be a fairly effective method of helping your face look rejuvenated and fresh.  I don't think anything can completely turn the clock back on your age, but I can see some improvement based upon using the night cream for a couple of weeks.
summary: Can't turn back the clock, but it does make a difference

reviewText:
I don't think I'm the target customer for this product, but it's hard to find a good night cream and I thought I'd give this one a try. I have to say that I'm extremely impressed. My #1 complaint about other creams are 1) too oily 2) causes break outs 3) no results. I found this this Vichy cream passed all these tests. It is fairly thick, but goes on smooth and doesn't shine at all. I could wear it out in public at high noon and I doubt anyone would notice. So far no signs of break outs or other skin irritation (I have very sensitive skin). And results! Yes, smoother, healthier looking skin. I don't look 16, but I look better than before. Only took a few days before I starting noticing a difference, too.

OVERALL: While the price is downright scary, I have to say that I have never had a better experience with night cream. I looked for every possible area to critique but I just don't have any complaints. I will also say that the little tub does last a long time. A little goes a LONG way so it can last several months easily. If you put it in that perspective, the near-$60 price tag isn't quite as shocking. I definitely recommend giving it a try.

I've been applying this cream twice a day for almost a month.  Once in the morning, and then again before bed.  It does not feel heavy at all and has a nice consistency.  I couldn't find any directions for this product on the package or on the jar which is unusual.  It has a description of the product on the package in every language going.  There are directions on the amazon page.  You dab some dots of the cream on your problem areas, spread the product upward and then massage it in.  I really haven't noticed any difference in my skin compared to all the other products that I have been using for wrinkles.  They all basically plump up your face so that wrinkles aren't as noticeable.  You can use many other products for a lot less money, more like in the low $20 range that will have the same effect, in my opinion.
summary: Less expensive products work as well

reviewText: I love how this cream makes my face feel!  It actually has more like a gel texture and refreshes my dry skin in the morning after my shower, and make for easy foundation application that looks very natural....One of the very few creams that doesn't make my face breakout. Has a fresh pleasant scent unlike other face creams I have tried.

Although I'm now officially in menopause, my face still gushes oil and I live under a layer of acne products. For this reason I can't use Vichy Neovadiol on my face, so I've been using it on the back of my hands, feet, knees, and elbows twice/day.

It is somewhere between a gel and a cream, and feels greasy at first, but absorbs pretty quickly.  I don't usually like scented lotions, but this has a nice clean, "beachy" scent.  I can't feel any cooling effect when I apply it, but it makes my skin look really nice!  I like it!

I must say that I have been consistently impressed with the Vichy products that I have used so far, and this is no exception.  I did find the gel texture a little tacky but it dries down to a soft feel without residual stickiness in a few minutes and it's a night cream so it's not like you're applying make up on top of it.  I did think that it enhanced the efficacy of the Vichy LIFTACTIV Retinol HA Advanced Concentrate that I use.  I'm almost 57 and my skin is a lot plumper and appears firmer than it did 2 years ago and I attribute it to all the Vichy products that I've been using.

I have used Vichy Neovadiol products before and this is the first time I came across the night cream product for mature skin.  As a matter of fact, this particular product is promoted for women who are postmenopausal.  I ordered product online, so I was not sure what are the active ingredients of the product at the time I ordered it.  For anyone who is not familiar with Vichy skin care line, it is important to mention that all Vichy products contain special Vichy spring water (from France).  But here is where the confusion kicks in.  This product arrived in packaging that had English and Russian labels.  It looks very exotic.  But when I looked more closely, it appears that this product is made or distributed in Scandinavian market because it shows that it is distributed by Loreal Vichy from Denmark and Norway.

The actual bottle I received looks a little bit different from the one on this picture.  My glass bottle is ribbed.  The product itself is similar to the products I used before.  Texture is light and silky while scent is mild and very pleasant.  Color of the cream is light blue and it absorbs into the skin quickly and beautifully.  I was concerned that product may not be good for my skin since I am not menopausal woman.  But when I read ingredients, it seems that there are many moisturizing ingredients.  So in my personal opinion this may help older women more, especially if they have thinning skin, but it can be used for women all ages.  I love to use it only chest area because I continue to use products in my age group on my facial and neck area.
summary: Super hydrating facial moisturizer for mature skin

reviewText:
I have sensitive skin and usually break out in a rash in my cheek area to the sides of my nose/under eye area whenever I try a new cream.  With the Vichy Neovadioal cream, I did not!  That was rather amazing.

I wouldn't really call this a cream, it has a different texture more of a cream/gel mix....kind of the consistency of an instant pudding before it thickens!

You do not need a lot of cream, and it is not real heavy on your skin, it seems to absorb well.

Rather confusing is that it's called a night cream, yet the instructions say to use at night and morning....if you do use it in the morning, there is NO sunscreen in the product.

I have seen results, my skin seems more smooth, and softer.

I took away a star for the scent, it is rather strong, a sweet floral scent, and I'd rather use unscented products on my face.  Other than that, I really like the product, hopefully they'll offer an unscented version for future purchases.

(SEE UPDATE AT END) Over time I have had the opportunity to work with many different levels of face cream products. Some have been remarkable and some have been awful. Some have been okay but nothing extravagant. This cream seemed interesting and worth a look. As a makeup artist who specializes in mature skin, I am particularly interested in finding products for skin care because it greatly improves makeup application and appearance. Not having the right skin care is one of the biggest problems I run into with older women. WHAT IS THIS NIGHT CREAM LIKE? The Vichy Neovadiol Replenishing Care Night Cream comes in a rather small glass blue jar with a silver plastic screw on cap. There is a inner liner in the jar so that means that product will not leak all over if you happen to have it in a case laying on its side from time to time. The cream itself is part way between a soft gel and a lightweight cream. Think of a hair conditioner that is not runny but can hold its own soft peaks in your palm and that is about the weight of it. The cream has a pungent fragrance to it which it seems like you either love or don't. HOW DOES THIS NIGHT CREAM PERFORM? I have used this cream for enough time to get an excellent feel for it. You don't need a whole lot- just a lentil sized dot on each cheek, chin, and forehead seem to take care of the entire face and for me I can bring it down along my neck too. The texture is surprisingly lightweight. I would compare it to Algenist Firming and Lifting cream as far as weight goes and how well it absorbs into the skin. This is nowhere near what I expected for a night cream. It feels deceptively lightweight. I put it on in the night and also the morning on a dry day and the absorption is such that I don't find it tacky or oily at all. It leaves the skin feeling moisturized without being a problem of having to wait long to put on makeup (in the morning). RESULTS? I have seen good results with this cream. -moisturizing lasts for 24 hours when using this cream at night only except on days when the heat is running a lot with no humidity -brighter complexion definitely improves the appearance of the skin with a subtle glow -lifting and firming action resembles some of the higher end creams, but perhaps not as marked as Lancome Rengerie Multi-action -wrinkes and lines seem to improve slightly but nothing remarkable as of yet. I will update over time as I continue to use this. HOW DOES THIS COMPARE WITH OTHER CREAMS? I have used many brands of face creams of this nature. Among them are: Lancome Absolue, Lancome Renergie (various styles), Algenist, Yes to Blueberries, Yes to Carrots, Clinique, Dior, Chanel, La Prairie, L'Occitane, SK-II, Ole Henriksen, L'Oreal, Olay, Peter Lamas, Lorac, Fresh, Philosophy, Origins, and Clarins, just to name some of them. I would put this on a par with performance I have gotten from Algenist, Hydroxatone, Yes to Blueberries, Lorac Aquaprime, Fresh, and Clarins. It is not quite as effective as the Lancome, Dior, and Lamas have been but it is not far behind so far in my experience. I think it is a good contender. It sure is a lot cheaper. THE BOTTOM LINE Out of the many lines of skin care products I have tried over time, I think that this night cream is one of the better ones. It does perform well in a relatively short span of time for me. Deceptively lightweight, it leaves skin moisturized, brighter, firmer, and in decent shape without oiliness or tackiness. The only thing I have a difficulty with is the pungent fragrance. The first few times I have used it, it literally turned my stomach and I thought I would not be able to use it at all. So far I have moved past it, but I do notice that my eyes tend to act a little sensitive to it even though the cream is nowhere near my eyes where I put it. It is almost like the fragrance waves get in my eyes and make them a little watery, but not so much as to stop using the cream at this point. So far, I have been able to work past that, and am enjoying this cream. It does make a difference on older skin (I have tested it on much older skin too) and if you can get past the fragrance, it is worth checking out for half the price or less than some of the top effective creams. For the fragrance, I have given this four stars. If it was not so pungent to me and hard to get past, I would rate this five stars for the price range of this cream. If you find yourself in or just past menopause, I think it would be a good cream to try out, but even if your skin is just very dry, it might also be worth trying out. Just be prepared if your eyes are sensitive or if you are sensitive to smells. This cream has potential to irritate some people. UPDATE I have changed this to five stars. As time has passed, I have learned that if I use 99% Natural Hyaluronic Acid Serum 1 fl oz (29.6 ml) Liquid on my skin BEFORE applying this cream, it really improves the performance even more. I usually do that for most creams but did not in my preliminary testing of this product. I also have obtained the Vichy Neovadiol Replenishing Care Moisturizer, 1.69 fl. oz. which I use during the day, reserving this for night time use only. I like the results even more, although you can easily use the night cream day and night if you can only afford one. The results over time have improved even more and I have to say that this is an excellent choice for mature skin. Makeup application improves greatly for mature skin after using this product. I plan to tell mature clients about it when I do their makeup, as skin care is the most important part of making your makeup look good as you get older, especially past menopause. The scent no longer seems to affect my eyes and I find myself noticing it less than when I first got it. I still wish it was less cloying, but at this point, the cream performs so well that I am raising my rating to five points. Will update further if there is anything to add. UPDATE 10-2017 I wanted to add that I use this product regularly now and am really impressed by the long term effects. The combination mentioned above is a winning team and half the price of some of the other products that I have used over time for myself and recommended to clients. If you can look past the scent of this line, it is well worth the effort. It is still great stuff! Very luxurious feeling.
summary: UPDATED-Makeup Artist For Mature Skin Perspective- How Does This Compare To Other Brands And Is It Worth Trying?

reviewText:
Vichy is a French company, subsidiary of LOral, which has been in business for about 80 years. I still haven't found out why the box is printed in something that looks like Russian. You might want to zoom in on the thumbnail pictures on the product page because the printing on the box is TINY. The ingredients are:

AQUA / WATER  GLYCERIN  PRUNUS ARMENIACA KERNEL OIL / APRICOT KERNEL OIL  ALCOHOL DENAT.  DIMETHICONE  HYDROXYPROPYL TETRAHYDROPYRANTRIOL  PROPANEDIOL PROPYLENE GLYCOL  ISONONYL ISONONANOATE  ZEA MAYS STARCH / CORN STARCH  HYDROXYETHYLPIPERAZINE ETHANE SULFONIC ACID  AMMONIUM ACRYLOYLDIMETHYLTAURATE/STEARETH-25 METHACRYLATE CROSSPOLYMER  AMMONIUM POLYACRYLDIMETHYLTAURAMIDE / AMMONIUM POLYACRYLOYLDIMETHYL TAURATE  C13-14 ISOPARAFFIN CAFFEINE  CAPRYLYL GLYCOL  CI 42090 / BLUE 1 CITRIC ACID  DEXTRIN  DIMETHICONOL  DISODIUM EDTA EPERUA FALCATA BARK EXTRACT  LAURETH-7  METHYLDIHYDROJASMONATE  PENTAERYTHRITYL TETRA-DI-T-BUTYL HYDROXYHYDROCINNAMATE  PERLITE  PHENOXYETHANOL  POLOXAMER 338  POLYACRYLAMIDE SILICA  SILICA SILYLATE  SODIUM ACRYLATES CROSSPOLYMER-2  SODIUM HYALURONATE  PARFUM / FRAGRANCE.

The cream/gel has a very light feel. I know everyones perception of fragrance is different but it smells very fresh and clean to me and the scent dissipates quickly.  I didn't find it sticky at all.  The box says at bedtime: and at awakening: which would make one think it should be used twice a day. I don't wear a foundation, so I really don't know for sure, but it seems to me it wouldnt work well under make-up. I need a moisturizer with sun-screen.

The big question: does it work? It seems to, for me. My skin is firmer and smoother and wrinkles have softened. Is it worth the cost?  I guess thats a personal choice. I haven't found anything (cheaper or more expensive) that works better so it would be worth it for me.
summary: Vichy Neovadiol Replenishing Care Night Cream,...

reviewText:
This Vichy Neovadiol Night cream is kind of a green/blue color and what I consider to be a medium consistency. It has an odd scent I find unappealing, though the scent does fade quickly upon application. This cream is paraben free. This cream sounded great to me- it's supposed to be formulated for post menopausal women, have an anti-warming effect, provide immediate hydration and make skin feel denser. The box also describes the cream as non-sticky, soothing and good for sensitive skin. This cream should have been perfect for me. I'm in the targeted age group, I use a cleanser by Vichy that's fantastic for my skin, and I have sensitive skin that gets dry. I also have a weak spot for high quality skin care products made in France like Vichy.:)

Unfortunately, on application, this cream isn't compatible with my skin. I've tried it a few times, but each time it makes my face feel prickly and itchy. It causes my skin to get small bumps within minutes (which is likely causing the prickly feeling). I don't feel an anti-warming or soothing effect, plus this cream feels tacky on my skin. I do have sensitive skin and occasionally have allergic reactions to products.  My skin is clearly sensitive to something in this product, so it's just not a cream I can use. I am giving it a neutral rating, however, because in my experience Vichy makes good products, and I have had negative reactions to products that others don't experience so I can't say it's a bad product. But I do know it's not good for my skin.
summary: Doesn't Work For Me, But May Work For You

reviewText:
I have tried other creams from this line and them very moisturizing. This one is different. First of all, if you are very sensitive to scents you ought to know it has a beautiful salty, sea smell. I only noticed when I opened the jar, not after it was on my face.

It does seem to have a positive effect on my skin, but it doesn't leave it feeling soft. It looks firmer and, paradoxically, smoother; but, it feels a little dry.

I have been absolutely thrilled with this "super serum elixer." The name sounds like something from a science fiction movie, but the effects are most definitely not fiction! After only a few applications, I actually did see (in a 10x magnifying mirror) a reduction of the appearance of those little wrinkles around my eyes. I've called them squint lines, but they are wrinkles just the same, and they have been getting deeper. Because of the quick reaction my skin had to this product, I have hope that it will continue to improve the appearance of my skin. It was completely non-irritating and feels like a very light oil. After a bit of time, my skin drank it in. The scent is very light and did not disturb me at all. This serum is so ultra-concentrated that it requires the smallest amount to get a full, light application. I would not hesitate to recommend this to a friend or family member. If you are tempted to treat yourself to a "high end" product for your skin, you would do well to try this one!

This serum is a lightweight oil that goes on easily and smoothly. You don't have to use much, which is good because it's expensive. My skin feels softer after using this in the morning and before I go to bed. It has a light, fresh scent.

I have really sensitive skin, so finding products that are compatible can be challenge.  Along with being sensitive, it's DRY.  So I've developed some dry lines on my forehead that NO amount of moisturizing has been able to fix.  I decided to give this a try.

It's like a very, very light serum and it covers a large area so you don't need a lot.  Given the price, this is a huge plus!  At first, I thought I felt a little itchy but I decided to not wash it off after 15 seconds, which I usually do the minute I think I might have a reaction.  Instead, I left it on and the "itch" went away almost immediately.  It was most likely my skin reacting POSITIVELY because I had no redness, no reaction.  My skin was probably thirsty for some help.

I have been putting this on for the past 3 days.  It WORKS.  I have seen  noticeable improvement in my fine lines and my skin feels younger & rejuvenated!  I'm really impressed and would highly recommend!
summary: Sensitive skin is HAPPY with this one!

reviewText: This serum has the consistency of a very smooth low viscosity oil.  It comes in a pump that allows you to carefully control how much you dispense.  It has a scent that is sweet and artificial to my nose --- everyone has her own feelings about scent.  The oil feels pleasant to use and stays on the surface of the skin for a prolonged period.  There is no comprehensive list of ingredients on the container, the box, or the leaflet.  But the leaflet (in very tiny print) says that this serum is "powered by the unique blend of intelligent bio-actives of Anti Aging Peptides, African Birch Bark,Red Seaweed and Pavina Pavonica."  Also contains Hyaluronic acid Camelina Oil which I suspect comprises the greater part of this serum.  After having used this I would have to say that this  product does not produce different results from my far less expensive basic hyaluronic acid serum.  But as they say, your mileage may vary.  I would have given it four stars but I dislike the scent.
summary: Expensive Hyaluronic Acid and oil serum that has a noticeable scent

reviewText:
I found this product to be frustrating, not terrible but not worth the high price.

Firstly it commits the packaging sin of having TWICE as much space in the box as the tiny little bottle takes up.  There is literally no reason for it to be in that size box, except to imply that the consumer is getting more product than they are actually getting.  Dishonest.

It has a very strong, distinctive smell which I personally did not prefer for my face.  It lingers because the serum is an oil base, so you still get whiffs of the smell long after you've applied it.

It takes a while to sink in due to the oily nature of the product.  While I think this allows for a good concentration of the hyaluronic acid component, it's a little unpleasant if you accidentally touch your face before it's absorbed.

I strongly dislike this brand's lack of a transparent disclosure of ingredients.  I want to know exactly what I'm putting on my face.  This information is severely lacking - they say that it's hyaluronic acid and oil, but that's it.  I'm sure there are other additives.
summary: Overpriced and deceptively packaged.  Lack of clarity in ingredients list.

reviewText:
I've been using this product for a couple of weeks now, and I do think I see a marked improvement in the tiny lines around my eyes and mouth.  This is a very slick and oily serum and takes a while to be absorbed into your skin, so I've been using it a night rather than as a day moisturizer under my makeup.

The directions say to keep this serum out of your eyes, so be careful about that. Otherwise, just rub it into your face and neck.

I really like this product except for the smell. I'm awfully sensitive I should say, and the odor of this product really puts me off. For that reason, I won't be ordering more. And it's a shame because it really works. :(

My wife is in her 50's and so wrinkles are a fact of every day life. She does have young looking skin for her age but the wrinkles are still there. She has been using various products for the last 20 years to moisturize and treat fine lines so needless to say, we were skeptical at best of this product.

Her report: "This serum feels somewhat greasy going on, but once on the skin for a few minutes, feels refreshing and adds moisture. Upon application, it leaves my skin feeling young and smooth. The elixir has a very appealing smell, light and slightly floral. After three weeks of use, my husband and I both agree this has reduced lines around the eyes and forehead somewhat, especially when the facial features are relaxed. I would say this is the best elixir I have tried."
summary: Really works, unlike the cheaper stuff

reviewText: Felt like baby oil. Very heavy on the skin. Broke my skin out.

I have been using this for three weeks and I have noticed softening of my wrinkles. They can be deep harsh lines and this has made them look smoother and less defined. Hopefully over longer use it will soften them even more. It smells like rose. It comes out very liquid and only a tiny bit goes a long way. It does make your skin feel greasy. I like it the most on my neck.

This does a nice job minimizing lines and wrinkles.  It goes on smoothly.  It dispenses a bit too much in one pump because it is thin so be careful to dispense where it won't drip right off your fingers.  I gave it 4 stars because it is a bit too oily.  Label states to apply moisturizer right after but you really need to give the serum some time to be absorbed--this is not always convenient for me in the morning. (Not so big a problem at night)
summary: This does a nice job minimizing lines and wrinkles

reviewText:
This is not a lotion but an opaque oil.  It is heavily scented and goes on greasy.  I find that if I put it on early enough ahead of my makeup, I can go ahead and apply makeup over it, but immediately after application my face feels oily and not a good surface to apply makeup.  Thankfully, the scent also fades, because it's really strong and would not only clash with my cologne but is overpowering so close to my nose. I love scented products but this one is a bit much even for me.  One pump is enough only for my face; if I want to include my neck and decollete I need two.

How does it work? My face feels moisturized and "plumper" after application. I don't think it does a whole lot to minimize the look of fine lines and wrinkles that are already there.  I have to trust that it's working in the long run, but short-term there's not a lot to go on.

Basically, I like how my face feels after applying this serum, but the scent is really too much for me.
summary: Overpowering scent; goes on greasy but dries to a nice moisturized feel

reviewText:
This serum is very oily. Too oily for a serum. It's very slick on the skin and goes on more like a layer rather than absorbing right in. It takes quite a while for it to absorb, and actually, I don't feel like it ever fully absorbs no matter how lightly a I apply it. My skin feels oily and slick until I wash it off... such as if I apply it in the morning, it'll stay greasy feeling all the way into the evening/night unless I wash my face sooner than that.

I don't have many wrinkles aside from a few tiny ones at the corner of my eyes, but I didn't see any improvement in those. I didn't think my skin looked better or worse in general, except for the fact that using this serum made me break out in tiny pimples on my upper lip.

I wouldn't buy this due to how oily it is and the lack of any kind of benefit from using it.

The ingredient I recognize as a wrinkle reducer is Hydrolyzed Hyaluronic Acid.  The serum is basically an oil and the pump helps to dispense a small amount and not end up with a greasy mess. The bottle and presentation is very nice, at this price point I expect this.  The bottle contains .5oz of the serum. I did not have any breakouts or issues from using the serum.

From my daughter: I usually just use jojoba oil to clean and moisturize my face, but I liked how this felt on a dry spot on my hand and I also liked how it didn't have any fragrance so I tried it on my face and really liked it. It moisturized well and gave a nice glow. It is also very light on your skin and doesnt feel heavy like some face creams.
A rich, emollient night cream perfect for the neck and chest as well as face. Takes a few minutes to sink in. Not inexpensive, but a little goes a long way.

My wife loves this nighttime cream/therapy. It helps her fight dryness, and it appears to be firming. This is no cheesy cream you find in the discount stores, but I'm not sure if it's worth the price. Well, I guess it's a small price vs. cosmetic surgery.

Super rich nighttime moisturizing cream that really works! I used this last night, and after showering this morning without doing more than washing my face with soap, my skin still feels soft and smooth the following afternoon. Cleaver dispenser top that protects the cream from contamination, too.

Wow! I've tried several skincare lines and received training is so many (I work in esthetic field). I am very positively surprised how good ingredients are and how good my skin looks and feel after using it.
Basically if you apply moisturizer and 30 minutes later your skin feels dry it means it was mostly water. Invest in a good skincare- skin the largest organ we have, selfies are 90% of the picture and skin will represent you for a long time.
I use it am and pm, it's just great, not too heavy, a little goes long way.
Now I'm curious about the whole line.

Have a healthy skin!:)

This moisturizing cream is my new favorite beauty product. I just glow after using this, I don't know how else to explain it. My face looks healthy and radiant and I notice such a difference in the way I look in pictures. I included a makeup free, unfiltered picture of myself to try to show off my skin. My face feels so soft and so smooth, and my skin feels restored. I feel like I'm writing a paragraph of cliches here, but they're true. I have sensitive skin, occasionally dry, not oily. If you're like me, do yourself a favor and treat yourself to this. I've never used Replenix before, but this has me searching for all of their skincare line. I'll be back to update on any other products that compliment this nicely. I also love the way that this dispenses. No wasted product here--just push down on the cap inside, and the perfect amount to apply is right at your fingertips. 5 stars, all around.
summary: My skin truly radiates after using this for only a few weeks.

reviewText: Obsessed with this product! Such a flattering color and the formula is so soft and provides great coverage. Love it!
summary: Such a flattering color and the formula is so soft and provides great coverage. Love it

reviewText: Lovely color and scent.  Lasts for hours.
Dries out my lips
This dries out my lips

This review is for the Julep It's Whipped Matte Lip Mousse

It is very dark, so if dark colors don't look good on you, you most likely will not approve of this.

Goes on smooth in a matte finish. Looks very good on. Easy to apply.
summary: so if dark colors don't look good on you

reviewText:
Now this is the color I'm talking about. I don't look good in red's and when I got a darker red I thought I looked terrible. I'm so glad I found this color. It's so very close to my natural lip color but it just gives them that oomph I was missing. I normally put on a clear lip gloss on my lips before leaving but now that I have this I'm sold.

This applies so smoothly. It's doesn't even feel like there's anything there when it's dry. I love the color. I feel amazing with this. I never normally spend this kind of money on my makeup but it was well worth it!

Thank you Julep.
summary: Love this color- ooh la la!

reviewText: Thankfully, this doesn't have the excessive fragrance problem of some other Mustela baby products. It's basically unscented. When I try it on my hands, I feel a slight cooling/tingling sensation, which could be nice for a baby with diaper rash. Seems like a good barrier protectant from the numbers 1 and 2 which are irritating skin. Note it's a little smooth. I don't have a good basis to say if it's better or worse than: Triple Paste Medicated Ointment for Diaper Rash, 16-Ounce, which is thicker, easy to use, very effective, and WAY WAY cheaper. I'd say it's effectiveness is kind of similar. Despite giving it 5-stars, given the cost, I'd use the triple paste.

This diaper rash cream seem to work really well on a very small rash that my daughter developed in the diaper region. It is an extremely sticky white cream, but once it is on her skin and inside the diaper, her skin warms it to where it melts and spreads to provide a good coating. It cleared up a diaper rash in about 24 hours, and though it wasn't a bad rash, it had persisted a few days prior to trying this on it.

Well, I suppose it does a decent job of taking care of my daughter's behind, but this is probably one of the most barely-doing-the-job creams I have ever used. It provides the barrier one would expect, but does very little to soothe or treat. Perhaps I am spoiled by other rash creams that offer so much more? If I am, well, there it is. This provides a barrier, but doesn't spread well or do much in the way of treating problems.

This works well for my baby's sensitive skin. It is not as thick as other brands and seems to have more of the protecting ointment as well as the zinc.

I use this at bedtime since she is in one overnight diaper all night. It does a good job of keeping her rash free.

I like this product and will continue to use it!

Our toddler grandson has been lucky as far as diaper rash woes go. We seem to have found the right combination when it comes to his diapers and wipes, and likely his diet may play a part in his mostly rash-free experience. Nevertheless, there have been occasions where he's had issues, and they have been painful and horrendous, as any amount of irritation goes for a little one. I can't emphasize enough how this Mustela cream has virtually erased these rashes, most of the time within one or two applications.

That said, we've indulged many premium brands of baby skin care, including some rash remedies that are twice the price of the Mustela. We have always purchased products which are fragrance-free, with as few "unnatural" ingredients as possible. The Mustela label claims 98% of the rash cream ingredients are of natural origin, leaving a mere 2% of ingredients in question. In this case, we are fine with that and grateful for the cream's superb effectiveness.

It's stressful for everyone when your child is suffering in pain. This stuff works wonders and has wiped out every occasional rash on my grandson. If your child suffers with more chronic rashes, I'm willing to bet this would be an effective preventative. Highly recommended!
summary: The best, most effective cream we've ever used!

reviewText: Has a relatively high level of zinc oxide and does a great job fighting diaper rash on my 2 year old's bum.  She recently started antibiotics for a little ear infection and (as per usual), broke out in a big rash on her bum.  I started using this diaper cream instead of my usual Burt's Bees zinc oxide cream.  I really like that the Burt's Bees cream is very thick - almost like an ointment - and stays put very well.  However the Burt's Bees is really heavily scented and my little one has had lots of reactions to scents and perfumes.  So I like that this Mustela does not have extra dyes or perfumes.  I wish it was just a little bit more water resistant, hence the removal of one star.  I received this sample in exchange for a review - if it's helpful to your purchase please vote helpful!  :)
summary: high level of zinc oxide, no scents (yay) but wish it was thicker

reviewText: A little less hard-paste than most so goes on easy.  And everything mistela is gentle.  No irritation with this.
summary: A little less hard-paste than most so goes on easy. And everything mistela is gentle

reviewText: Average diaper rash cream.  It is not as thick as some of the "maximum" strength lines.  It is smooth and easy to apply and has a clean scent.  It has a flip-top cap which is easy to open and closed one-handed.  We haven't been able to see any better prevention/healing of diaper rash with this cream versus any other brand we have used.

My baby has a tendency to get rashy if she's in a dirty diaper too long (which could literally mean sitting in it for ten minutes while we drive to a rest stop), so we use a lot of zinc oxide-based diaper cream to get rid of and control her diaper rash. This one just didn't do the trick for her bottom. It has a lower percentage of zinc oxide (9.9%) than Desitin Rapid Relief (13%), and I think that's the problem for my kiddo. It's just not enough zinc oxide to keep her bottom dry enough. The Mustela cream didn't prevent rashiness, either, when we applied it to a non-rashy bottom.

The "naturalness" of the cream's ingredients will appeal to some parents (we're not as concerned about that), but I wouldn't recommend this for babies that easily get diaper rash. It just isn't strong enough.
summary: Not strong enough to prevent/treat my baby's diaper rash

reviewText: My toddler has been on a long dose of antibiotics and I've been using this to keep a bad rash from the antibiotics from getting bad. I've used it pretty regularly for a week or two and it's done a good job. She hasn't gotten a really bad rash although it has been been red a few times. Overall, it performed well.  I like that the ingredient list is more natural than most of the market. I'm happy with the product.
summary: Works well at keeping a diaper rash at bay!

reviewText: Compared to Desitin, the Mustela Diaper Rash Cream is much thinner and doesn't stay on. I would use this cream as a preventative like A&D, but not to get rid of a diaper rash already there. The ingredients are hypoallergenic and don't bother my son.

My daughter has been having some GI issues so I thought this would be great as a barrier cream to help her but it appears she is allergic to the zinc and it left her red, bumpy and irritated everywhere I put it.
summary: Zinc - your child could react to it

reviewText: This diaper rash cream pretty much relieved my daughters diaper rash over night.  I love that this cream washes off of your hands easily while it also absorbs easily into my child's skin.  This does not leave that white paste like substance left from other brands.
summary: Relieves the Worst Diaper Rashes Quickly

reviewText: This diaper rash cream has a lot of things going for it. It is made of skin-healing ingredients and is completely unscented. I think it might work for skin irritations and also help to prevent diaper rash from escalating if the rash is in the early stages or is very mild. The reason I say that is that it has one glaring problem--it is not thick enough to protect the skin when diaper rash is extensive and already in full bloom. The creams that work effectively are very thick and heavy, thereby producing a strong barrier between the irritated skin and a wet diaper. This cream, while smooth and silky, absorbs into the skin much too easily (instead of laying on top of it).  I would recommend this cream for use on people who have a skin irritation, such as redness from lying in a bed, as it may help to prevent or slow down the prevention of pressure sores. Caregivers may find it helpful. However, as a diaper rash cream, it falls short.
summary: Too thin and absorbent to be effective

reviewText:
It soothes the skin without being too heavy. It is a good, thick cream for skin conditions other than diaper rash as well.

~ Kort

My review is for use of this product to get rid of acne, not for babies.
This product has a high percentage of zinc oxide, which is excellent for clearing acne and red spots.
Most individuals recommend against using diaper rash cream because the petroleum in the cream clogs pores, which mitigates the benefit of using the zinc oxide. This product does not have petroleum. It does have beeswax, though. So YMMV.
For me, it works as a red spot and acne remover. Wash and dry your face with a cleanser. Then apply a small amount on the red spot or acne. It will disappear overnight.
For that purpose, I give it five stars.

I have been using Mustela for quite some time now. Once upon a time you could only find it in boutiques and specialty stores, but now it's easier to find. I really like Mustela and have been using this diaper cream since it came out. Anytime my baby has more than a bit of redness I know that something with zinc is needed and this cream does the job perfectly.

Spreads easily ( like toothpaste!) and is not thick compared to my favorite penaten and weleda creams. However I must note that my newborn does not currently have any diaper rash so I'm using this more as a preventive cream and not to treat an actual rash. It does not have the usual smell associated with mustela products and the tube is easy to squeeze.

Mustela Vitamin Barrier Cream is my #1 go to diaper cream. I've tried everything & this is the only cream that seems to relieve the redness & irritation the best. The cream itself has a nice scent but does not cause further irritation from the fragrance. It is a little pricier than most but I think it's worth it.
summary: I've tried everything & this is the only cream that seems to relieve the redness & irritation the best. The cream itself has a n

reviewText:
I get allergic dermatitis very easily on my legs and it results in a prolonged battle back to clear skin. This is an excellent cream to help heal and then maintain intact skin. It also helps me avoid steroid creams.

So many positives here: it is scent free. While it comes out of the tube white, it works in clear. It is non-staining on my clothes and not greasy. It has no drag and glides on to skin easily. The Mustela motto seems to be "from birth on". Definitely had adult uses and it would be a shame to limit this product to infants only.
summary: Amazing on my dermatitis prone legs

reviewText:
I have to say, I got a few, little squiggly stretch marks anyway when using this cream--but I'm not one that believes in creams completely preventing stretch marks. I was very swollen at the very end of pregnancy (preeclampsia) and am pretty sure that is the reason I got stretch marks. I didn't get them with my first child, and moisturized religiously (not with this cream, though).

I didn't really like the bust serum much--it was truly a serum and less hydrating than the belly cream. Again, I didn't feel like it did anything. The belly cream smells really nice and is very emollient feeling, but sinks right in. although I'm not pregnant anymore, I'm still using it as an all over body lotion. It's great.

All in all, I really like the belly cream and would recommend it, but definitely don't think there's anything topical that is a completely foolproof method to prevent stretch marks. I have used a lot of these types of products and would prefer this Mustela cream over bio-oil any day :)
summary: Nice belly cream, but would skip the bust serum.

reviewText: 3.5 stars - I used it on my 2nd pregnancy hoping to reduce the effects of stretch marks. It helps with the itching on my skin as it stretches, however, I don't think it had much effect on the stretch marks at all. I found the scent to be too strong for me. I was really sensitive to scents earlier on in my pregnancy and this lotion used to make me nauseous. It got better as I became less sensitive to the smell in the third trimester. I would have preferred all pregnancy products to be unscented. Also had a problem with the tube design. The cap always caused the lotion splatter when opened.
summary: Moisturizing but no help for stretch marks

reviewText: A really good firming moisturizer. This keeps my skin hydrated and more pliable. This would reduce the likelihood of stretch marks but at the end of the day so would any other hydrator. This product feel good and went on nicely. It dried fast and kept my skin soft until the next shower so for that alone I recommend it. It's also free of harmful chemicals.

Whether or not one gets stretch marks during pregnancy is most likely genetics, but it doesn't hurt to apply cream every day to help prevent them - and Mustela is the only brand that my ob/gyn recommends. I like that it's light and easy to apply, and the small bottle goes a long way. That said, I still did get a few stretch marks - not too bad, all about a week before my due date. (Sounds like I"m not too unusual. The packaging says that 96% of women did not get marks after using this cream, but in small print it clarifies that there were only 26 women involved in their trial.)

But now, the bust serum: this is amazing! It's a true serum, slightly clear and liquidy. It seems to tighten even as I'm putting it on. Is it a placebo effect? Who knows? It feels good! Are my breasts still stretched out? Oh, sure, breastfeeding does a number on them. But they feel good, and at least THEY have no stretch marks!
summary: Great set and would make a perfect present for a mom-to-bed

reviewText: Wife's review- I'm 7 months pregnant with baby #2, been using this since I started to show (about 4 months). I've only been using it once daily, after showering. I'm bigger than with my first pregnancy & so far, no stretch marks. So it's doing what it's supposed to. However, with my first pregnancy, I used Palmer's cocoa butter for stretch marks and also did not have stretch marks. I'm about to run out of the Mustela, and when I do, I'll go back to the Palmer's- simply because it's over $20 less. I'm not sure the bust cream is doing anything at this point, but it is a nice moisturizer and smells good.

The clinical data looks impressive at first, but they are consumer *perception* claims, and let's face it, we all know that stretch marks and skin elasticity are highly genetic. Nevertheless, the cream and serum are developed in France under EU cosmetic regulations which are more stringent than the US. Thus, these formulas are EVEN free of paraben replacements like phenoxyethanol or caprylyl glycol, which is highly commendable. The stretch mark cream is the winning formula in this kit. The Bust Serum is really just a temporary tightener (it has lots of film formers which help give a sensation of tightening and hold) but feels really nice and is great for postpartum without implications to breastfeeding.

Stretch Marks Cream Ingredients:
AQUA/WATER/EAU, DI-C12-13 ALKYL MALATE, ETHYLHEXYL COCOATE, CETEARYL ALCOHOL, DICAPRYLYL CARBONATE, HYDROLYZED SOY PROTEIN, BUTYLENE GLYCOL, CERA ALBA/BEESWAX/CIRE DABEILLE, LAURETH-23, GALACTOARABINAN, BUTYROSPERMUM PARKII (SHEA) BUTTER, GLYCERYL STEARATE, 1,2-HEXANEDIOL, CETYL ALCOHOL, CETEARYL GLUCOSIDE, GLYCERYL CAPRYLATE, PARFUM (FRAGRANCE), XANTHAN GUM, CETYL PALMITATE, COCOGLYCERIDES, SCLEROTIUM GUM, ZINC GLUCONATE, PENTYLENE GLYCOL, HELIANTHUS ANNUUS (SUNFLOWER) SEED OIL, SOPHORA JAPONICA FRUIT EXTRACT, HYDROLYZED AVOCADO PROTEIN, MALTODEXTRIN, CITRIC ACID, LUPINUS ALBUS SEED EXTRACT, TOCOPHEROL.

Bust Serum ingredients:
AQUA /WATER/ EAU, PEG-6, BUTYLENE GLYCOL, DEXTRIN, 1,2-HEXANEDIOL, DIPHENYLSILOXY PHENYL TRIMETHICONE, ACRYLATES/C10-30 ALKYL ACRYLATE CROSSPOLYMER, PEG-40 HYDROGENATED CASTOR OIL, GLYCERYL CAPRYLATE, HYDROLYZED SOY PROTEIN, DIMETHICONE/PHENYL VINYL DIMETHICONE CROSSPOLYMER, PARFUM (FRAGRANCE), XANTHAN GUM, HELIANTHUS ANNUUS (SUNFLOWER) SEED OIL, SODIUM HYDROXIDE, GLUCOSE, SOPHORA JAPONICA FRUIT EXTRACT, CENTELLA ASIATICA EXTRACT, SORBITOL, HYDROLYZED AVOCADO PROTEIN, MALTODEXTRIN, PENTYLENE GLYCOL, CITRIC ACID, LUPINUS ALBUS SEED EXTRACT, CI 47005 (YELLOW 10), CI 16035 (RED 40), TOCOPHEROL
summary: Feel safe about using these during breastfeeding postpartum

reviewText:
Both lotions smell very nice, not over powering and won't compete with your perfume if you wear one. I chose this because my skin is super sensitive and I figured if it's safe for a pregnant woman, it's safe for any woman, right? Plus, if it will plump up your breasts, why not your face? If it'll remove stretch marks, why not crows feet?

For the bust cream:
I can't say that I've noticed the differences advertised (no "plumping") and in checking the ingredients, this scores pretty low on the toxicity scale, which is nice. It's not greasy, feels great when you put it on and I do believe that moisturizer is going to help you feel better and helps keep your skin young looking.

Bust Firming Serum:

AQUA /WATER/ EAU, PEG-6, BUTYLENE GLYCOL, DEXTRIN, 1,2-HEXANEDIOL, DIPHENYLSILOXY PHENYL TRIMETHICONE, ACRYLATES/C10-30 ALKYL ACRYLATE CROSSPOLYMER, PEG-40 HYDROGENATED CASTOR OIL, GLYCERYL CAPRYLATE, HYDROLYZED SOY PROTEIN, DIMETHICONE/PHENYL VINYL DIMETHICONE CROSSPOLYMER, PARFUM (FRAGRANCE), XANTHAN GUM, HELIANTHUS ANNUUS (SUNFLOWER) SEED OIL, SODIUM HYDROXIDE, GLUCOSE, SOPHORA JAPONICA FRUIT EXTRACT, CENTELLA ASIATICA EXTRACT, SORBITOL, HYDROLYZED AVOCADO PROTEIN, MALTODEXTRIN, PENTYLENE GLYCOL, CITRIC ACID, LUPINUS ALBUS SEED EXTRACT, CI 47005 (YELLOW 10), CI 16035 (RED 40), TOCOPHEROL

This again is a nice smelling, non-greasy moisturizer. Will it prevent stretch marks? Well, stretch marks are genetic so I would be interested in learning about a lotion, potion or cream that could actually do that! But again, using moisture on skin that is stretching quickly will make it feel better and certainly can help with the awful itchiness that can start when the belly really starts to pop out there. So I would be cautious in believing this will fend off stretch marks - science just doesn't support that. But it's a nice lotion.

Stretch Marks Prevention Cream:

AQUA/WATER/EAU, DI-C12-13 ALKYL MALATE, ETHYLHEXYL COCOATE, CETEARYL ALCOHOL, DICAPRYLYL CARBONATE, HYDROLYZED SOY PROTEIN, BUTYLENE GLYCOL, CERA ALBA/BEESWAX/CIRE DABEILLE, LAURETH-23, GALACTOARABINAN, BUTYROSPERMUM PARKII (SHEA) BUTTER, GLYCERYL STEARATE, 1,2-HEXANEDIOL, CETYL ALCOHOL, CETEARYL GLUCOSIDE, GLYCERYL CAPRYLATE, PARFUM (FRAGRANCE), XANTHAN GUM, CETYL PALMITATE, COCOGLYCERIDES, SCLEROTIUM GUM, ZINC GLUCONATE, PENTYLENE GLYCOL, HELIANTHUS ANNUUS (SUNFLOWER) SEED OIL, SOPHORA JAPONICA FRUIT EXTRACT, HYDROLYZED AVOCADO PROTEIN, MALTODEXTRIN, CITRIC ACID, LUPINUS ALBUS SEED EXTRACT, TOCOPHEROL.
summary: Don't have to be pregnant to use

reviewText:
Mustela makes a big thing about their products being natural and hypoallergenic. Since I have sensitive skin, I always try a dab of any cream on the inside of my arm (where the skin is thin) and wait for a few hours. It only took a few seconds to realize that the Stretch Marks Prevention cream was problematic for me! It made my skin red and irritated, even on the back of my hand where I rubbed the leftover portion when more came out of the tube than I expected. I immediately washed my skin but it stayed red for a while and felt like it was burning.

So what is in this prevention cream? MustelaUSA says "AQUA/WATER/EAU, DI-C12-13 ALKYL MALATE, ETHYLHEXYL COCOATE, CETEARYL ALCOHOL, DICAPRYLYL CARBONATE, HYDROLYZED SOY PROTEIN, BUTYLENE GLYCOL, CERA ALBA/BEESWAX/CIRE DABEILLE, LAURETH-23, GALACTOARABINAN, BUTYROSPERMUM PARKII (SHEA) BUTTER, GLYCERYL STEARATE, 1,2-HEXANEDIOL, CETYL ALCOHOL, CETEARYL GLUCOSIDE, GLYCERYL CAPRYLATE, PARFUM (FRAGRANCE), XANTHAN GUM, CETYL PALMITATE, COCOGLYCERIDES, SCLEROTIUM GUM, ZINC GLUCONATE, PENTYLENE GLYCOL, HELIANTHUS ANNUUS (SUNFLOWER) SEED OIL, SOPHORA JAPONICA FRUIT EXTRACT, HYDROLYZED AVOCADO PROTEIN, MALTODEXTRIN, CITRIC ACID, LUPINUS ALBUS SEED EXTRACT, TOCOPHEROL." (I apologize for the caps but I pasted this from their site.)

None of these are among my usual allergens but many of them I have not heard of.  I have had problems with some fragrances and a few fruit products. Fragrance can be anything so it is hard to judge but it is noticeable as soon as you open the tube. In EWG's Skin Deep Database, fragrance is the ingredient that keeps this product from getting a high rating, along with Laureth-23, which they say can cause irritation and organ system toxicity, and zinc gluconate, which can bioaccumulate and also has organ system toxicity.

The Mustela website claims good results based on a "Clinical trial conducted on 26 pregnant women who used this product throughout their pregnancy."  But personally I cannot recommend it.
