I did not dare to try the second product in the package after the bad experience with the first one. It also contains fragrance.

This set is made in France.
summary: The Stretch Marks Cream Made my Skin Burn.

reviewText:
The Mustela Belly and Bust Pregnancy set is great for a pregnant woman. I used the Palmers Cocoa Butter for my first pregnancy and didn't get any stretch marks on my stomach area. I didn't think to use it on my hips and upper thighs and ended up with some stretch marks there. My second pregnancy I used just regular lotion and ended up with stretch marks on my stomach. I can't say pregnancy lotions prevented my stretch marks. It could be a difference in where I gained weight each pregnancy, my age during each pregnancy, or other factors. So for my current pregnancy I was happy to be using a lotion specially for pregnant women.

The belly cream is medium thickness. In the winter I use a body lotion for very dry skin, which is thick. In the summer my skin allows me to use a regular lotion that is much thinner. The Mustela cream feels right in between those lotions consistency. It absorbs into the skin with some gently rubbing and dries pretty quickly. I try to use it at least twice a day. It has a light floral scent. Nothing obnoxious which is good for a sensitive pregnancy nose.

The bust serum is a pale peach color and has the consistency of most face serums I've used. I breast feed both my kids so my breasts are in need of firming up. Prior to my first pregnancy I read somewhere that sagging breasts actual are a result of improper bra support prior to birth. So it recommended a good bra and not going braless. I'm past that point, so I've been using the serum. It too has a light floral scent. It absorbs quickly. I have not really noticed a difference in firmness, but I'm going to keep using it.
summary: Great for a pregnant belly & bust

reviewText: I used this cream to help relieve some of the over stretched skin after pregnancy.  I got this too late to prevent any stretch marks, but I think it has definitely helped my skin retain some of the elasticity that I lost.  Drinking lots of water also helps, but skin doesn't do it on it's own....the lotion definitely helped me get my body back!
summary: Lotion helped me get by body back!

reviewText:
The Belly and Bust Pregnancy Skincare Set comes with offers 2 specially formulated products, Stretch Marks Prevention Cream (5.07 oz) and Bust Firming Serum (4.22 oz).

I love that the Stretch Marks Prevention Cream doesn't have a funny odor. It actually has a pleasant smell. If you apply more that the directed amount you are left with a residue, but if you apply a thin layer like the directions state you should use then it goes on smoothly without staining clothes or any residue. It also works well as an overall body lotion to moisturize your skin, anywhere other than your belly. I haven't noticed any stretch marks.

I really enjoy the pump on the Bust Firming Serum more than the squeeze tubes of Mustela's other products. This serum has no smell and I like the orange color. It feels like it's working from the tightness the serum leaves on my skin. A small amount goes a long way and it doesn't feel sticky. It feels quite smooth. It's reassuring to know that Mustela identifies that breasts need a different Cream than your stomach.

The cream is very light and is has a nice smell...

I can tell it's meant to moisturizer the skin and keep it from cracking... if this is used early on I can definitely see it reducing the chances of having stretch marks!

It's cool going on and not greasy...

Remember it's stretch mark prevention... not stretch mark removal...

 Avocado peptides: a patented active ingredient that promotes suppleness, eases tightness and brings elasticity to the skin.

 Arabinogalactan: patented active ingredient that activates elastin fibers and promotes collagen to prevent the formation of stretch marks.

Beeswax and shea butter: hydrates and nourishes the skin. Bust firming serum: a non-sticky, quickly absorbing serum formulated to help firm skin and tone tissue for a restructuring effect: light, delicate floral fragrance with notes of rose, bergamot and plum.

 Centella asiatica: boosts firmness and tones tissues for intense firming action.

This products incorporates a lot of great ingredients and I recommend it.

Stretch marks are mostly genetic so a cream or lotion will probably not totally prevent them, rather they can perhaps help ease their appearance when skin is properly hydrated and moisturized. I am lucky enough not to have any stretch marks from previous pregnancies but have saggy skin from my recent pregnancy a few months ago. These two creams are easily absorbed by my skin and i like using them after showers to lock in moisture and hopefully firm up those areas.
summary: really good moisturizer that works for me, for stretch marks per se i am unsure..

reviewText:
My wife has not used this on her "bust and belly" because she has flawless skin and has remained impervious to the affects of pregnancy...

We have been using this for the kids' skin.  The lotions are really great and absorb quickly.  The scent is also very pleasant.  Similar to other Mustela products, it's light and clean.
summary: Not Just For Bust and Belly...

reviewText:
My oldest daughter is pregnant and started getting stretch marks, so she wanted to try this to stop any more from developing. After having six kids, I wanted to see if the breast firming gel would work for me as gravity has done a number on my figure.

My daughter absolutely loves the stretch mark product. It goes on easy, no gross residue, and has a pleasant scent. It also stopped the development of additional stretch marks in their tracks and she seems to have experienced a lightening of the few she did develop before using this in addition to not developing any others.

To be totally honest the breast firming product, which is kind of like a gel (but with no residue) didn't do much for me but it seems to act as a very good moisturizer and also has a very pleasant scent. Perhaps if I had used this product in the set throughout all of my pregnancies I would have had better luck. As it is, I saw little to no improvement in the bust area and my daughter also came into my bathroom to use it daily and she couldn't tell a difference really either (although that may be because she doesn't need help in that area).

Overall, even if the breast product isn't a hit the stretch mark cream definitely is and is worth the price of the set itself. I've tried stretch mark creams during my pregnancies that cost much more but did much less than this product has done for my daughter. Definitely recommend if you're worried about keeping your skin in the best shape possible during pregnancy and postpartum. One of the few stretch mark creams out there that really works.
summary: Awesome Stretch Mark Cream But Breast Product Could Use Improvement

reviewText: So, I have been using this for about a week (26 weeks preggo) and I can't really tell if it's doing anything with the stretch marks, but it is helping with my irritated skin.  Since the skin is stretching, it is SUPER dry and itchy ALL THE TIME! I have started using this anytime it starts to feel itchy (so like 3-4 times a day) on my belly and chest.  It is very moisturizing and really makes the skin feel nice. It also has a subtle, but nice scent to it.  It immediately stops the itchy/dry feeling and lasts about 6 hours or so before I start to get itchy again and need to reapply.  Overall, it's good lotion, I feel like only time will tell for the stretch marks, but as for the moisturizing part, it's AWESOME!

The bust cream is particularly absurd. I bought it for my wife. The bust cream is a silicone-like, clear cream, with a slight scent that dries clear. There's a big difference between a slightly tight feel on your skin and actually firming breasts. You need several pumps (each pump is not much cream) to have enough to cover your breasts. The stretch mark cream is a thin, white cream with a stronger scent. There's nothing remotely medical about these cosmetic lotions.

I really like the Mustela brand for their Stelatopia unscented moisturizing lotion, and we've used a ton of their milky bath oil when bathing our child, but these lotions are being marketed with pseudo scientific nonsense. The firming agents are a joke, with trace quantities of avocado that have no medical action.

It's a shame when a brand builds trust with one product, just to erode it with false claims on another.

A few minutes ago, as I was preparing to sit down to write this review, my husband admitted to me that he was curious about these products and had used the breast firming cream on the loose skin under his chin.  He's impressed!  I've been using it as well - mostly in the areas of my décolletage  and we have both noticed the firming up of that skin.  It's a cool gel that goes on with little fragrance.  I use a single pump on my neck and collar area and work it in until it has fully absorbed.  You can even feel a tightening sensation.  I would recommend the "breast serum" very highly to anyone who is interested in toning up those tender skin areas under the chin.  It would also benefit those who have recently lost weight and have a little bit of extra skin to contend with every day.  I give this half of the review 5+ stars.

The Stretch Mark Prevention cream is very nice too - but I don't know how revolutionary it is.  It has a stronger fragrance than the bust cream and goes on smoothly with fast absorption.  It doesn't make your hands feel greasy.  The fragrance is a bit much when used on the top part of the body - it's easier to take if you keep in the belly, saddle and upper thigh area.  It contains agents that help promote your skin to manufacture collagen and encourages elasticity.  It also has shea butter in it to moisturize the skin.  A regular routine using high quality ingredients like these should help reduce or eliminate stretch marks.  I would give this product 4 stars on its own.

Overall, this is a great set that would make a wonderful gift to a newly expectant mother.
summary: The Bust Firming Cream works wonders for skin of all ages.  The Stretch Mark Prevention cream is very high quality.

reviewText: I used Mustela Pregnancy belly (previously called double action strecth mark cream) with my two previous pregnancies, and had no stretch marks due to pregnancy. Now that I am pregnant with my third child I have used this new version daily, and continue to have no stretch marks. This may be genetic...but I continue to use this product hoping it is helping! When not pregnant I have stretch marks on my hips and insides of my legs. I've been using the stretch mark cream on those areas this pregnancy as well and have noticed that they are diminishing in appearance and are less noticable. I've also noticed that my skin is SO soft where I have used the products. My skin also feels less itchy from the stretching skin. This is the first time I have used the bust serum and I'm a fan. I use it on my bust area, chest, and up to my neck area. It goes on smoothly and does not have a scent. These are both a must have for every pregnancy!

The lovely thing about this breast ointment is how cleanly it dries.  It also has a soft, smooth, silicone like texture that is pleasant, and it has no particular scent.  It does add a bit of comfort, but seems to do little else.

I can only rate it three stars because I found the size of the product absurd given how quickly it dries and how much you need to use.  It's a little larger than an Avon hand lotion and it has a pump (which I like).  If you have breasts of any size you will need to use about 5 pumps to cover your breasts and massage up to your neck according to the instructions.  Unless you have small breasts, you'll plow through a tube of this quickly.

The body lotion doesn't dry as quickly and is a little easier to work with.
summary: silicone like texture that is pleasant

reviewText: I have had two babies and do not have a single stretch mark to show for it. (Thank goodness) I have no idea if it was from using the MUSTELA skincare products or not, but I like them so much that I would definitely not take a chance on having stretch marks. The lotion is very creamy and smell is soft and almost like a product that you would use on a baby. The bust firming serum is a gel and I used that more on my neck than I did on my breast. The cost of this lotion initially seems a little high, but if it the end result is smooth tummy, it is worth every penny.

Mustela has been making skincare for babies and their mommies since 1950, and are committed to using natural products that are safe. Most of the ingredients they use are plant based.

This kit comes with 2 products:  one 150 ml squeeze tube of Stretch Mark Prevention Cream, and one 75 ml squeeze tube of bust firming serum.  They are both in easy to apply bottles with pop style tops.
They both have a strong fragrance that I find to be pleasant and feminine.  Quite luxurious after a hot bath.

The Stretch Marks Prevention cream is created to help prevent stretch marks during pregnancy and is made from 3 principle ingredients: Galactorabinan, Avocado Peptides, and Shea butter.  The Bust firming serum is made with  3 key ingredients which are centella asiatica, elastoregulator, and avocado peptides.  The ingredients are created by Mustela Labs, and again, are plant based, natural, and safe. There are other ingredients in both products, like water and binding properties, but the key ingredients for skin softening are as listed above.

Hypoallergenic, safe for breast feeding mothers, and created with the environment in mind, I think this set makes a great baby shower gift.  The sooner a mother to be can begin applying the stretch mark prevention cream, the better.  (Of course, lots of people get stretch marks during growth spurts, so this cream can be used for anybody, you don't have to be expecting).

The instructions on the box recommend starting the cream by the 8th month of pregnancy.

Just based on the ingredients, the reputation and longevity of the company, and the wonderful fragrance of the products, I like this set.  It would be ideal as part of a bridal shower gift basket.

As far as results, the Mustela company had clinical studies that are quite favorable.  In their studies, 26 expectant mothers used the stretch mark prevention cream and 96% of them developed no stretch marks.  Those are positive results!
summary: Lovely Fragrance - Clinical Studies Were Performed - Safe Products From Reputable Company

reviewText:
I'm an off label user; I took this set for a refill of the stretch mark cream. I use it on scars and my growth stretch marks ( grew 6" in one year at 15). It minimizes them and keeps them from getting irritated. The bust serum was new to me. I tried it out and it has a slight pulling effect. I also tried it on my dcolletage and my neck and it does seem to minimize crepe and wattle. Don't get old ladies. :)

I like these products a lot. They have a safety tab and are minimally scented. I am fond of a Mustela in general as a product line. This set is a very good value.
summary: Cream is great on existing stretch marks and scars. Bust serum gives a gentle toning/tightening.

reviewText:
This is a pleasently scented lightweight lotion for the prevention of newstretch marks and to help reduce the look of existing ones. As a new mom I'm using it for the latter purpose. The cream itself is moisturizing without stickiness or oiliness but it does take awhile to soak in and leave that nice matte feeling. I've been applying it to my stretch marks and while I feel it will be awhile before I know how well it works to fade them it is deeply moisturizing so I can definately see this going a long way towards preventing them.

The breast firming serum is the reason I'm giving this set as a whole four stars rather than five. It's thick and not nearly as pleasent to apply as the cream. It takes so long to soak in that I can only use it when I'm pretty sure I won't be nursing the baby soon. Even then I have to keep on an old shirt after I use it since I'm not comfortable getting it on the inside of my nursing bras. That said, I does seem to have a firming effect. For now I'll be saving it until my little one is older and I don't have to worry so much about timing the application of it.
summary: wonderful cream paired with an ok serum

reviewText: goes on non greasy. Does not have a heavy smell to it. Makes my skin feel very soft and supple. Definitely something I would continue to use.  Like it a lot

I got to try this BIO IONIC Long Barrel Styler Curling Iron.  Totally gave my hair a smooth appearance like a top quality iron should and curl stayed all day on my silky limp hair as my picture shows.  You really shouldn't do like me and wrap the cord around it tho, a bad habit.

This was my first time using a long barrel curling iron, but since I have hair that goes all the way to my mid back and is also very thick, the extra length seemed perfect for me.

While I let the iron heat up, I sectioned my hair with alligator clips (so necessary to make my long, thick hair easier to manage and to make sure I don't miss a strand.)  Working in sections I sprayed my hair with hairspray (currently using Living Proof Style | Lab Flex Shaping Hairspray), let it dry then wrap a small section at a time around the barrel starting a few inches away from my scalp.  I then slowly slide the iron down to the ends of my hair, while rotating, so I can curl the full strand of hair.  (A stylist taught me to curl it this way so you can spend the least amount of time on the ends, which can be more fragile and damaged.)  I then spray with a bit more hair spray and repeat until I've done my whole head, piecing through the curls gently at the end to separate them and give a more natural look and will often spray my hair with a bit more hairspray.

Using that method and this iron, I think my hair turns out great.  I also think the slightly wider curl from the 1.25 inch iron works really well with my longer hair.  My hair looks flawless for hours (people often ask if I had it done), and I still have soft waves the next day.  Granted, my hair type is slightly coarse and naturally wavy/curly, so it tends to hold curls pretty well, your results may vary.

I also enjoy the experience of using this.  There's a good range of temperatures and I find even with my coarse hair I don't have to jack it up to the highest temperature to see results.  It also heats up really quickly.  And the longer barrel definitely makes quicker work of my long hair.  I also especially love the finger grip on the end.  None of my other curling irons have that and it makes it much, much easier to maneuver, as does the swivel cord.

The one thing I will say is that since it is longer than your average curling iron it felt a bit bulky at first and took a little time to adjust to, but after doing my hair a couple of times it felt completely normal.

Would recommend!
summary: Love the longer barrel to make quicker work of curling my long, thick hair

reviewText:
Tried very many methods of using this curling iron.  None of which worked at all on my hair.

Totally scrapped my previous review and this is what worked today.

First off...no curls per se. Tried many methods that brought this iron down to a 2 star...but I kept plugging along and now voila 5 stars!
My hair is heavily highlighted, shoulder length, fine hair but thick in quantity.

Today I let my hair dry naturally.  Then used the iron, mid heat setting, for about 30 seconds per section.  Let results just stay and finger styled and scrunched after a few minutes with a styling product for that purpose.

The end result for me was fluffy, casual waves...pretty.

Happy hair today.
summary: Finally...success....each person's hair is individual...had to play around quite a bit...

reviewText:
Pros:
Heats up quickly
Large, long handle is good for maneuvering
The electrical cord is long, so it easily reaches even outlets that are further away from the bathroom counter
Has a lock option to keep you from accidentally changing the heat
The heat resistant tab/cap/handle at the end stays cool for a comfortable grip

Cons:
A bit longer than some other curling irons, so takes up more space
Tricky to get the curls to hold on long, straight hair.

General features:

It's a bit longer than my curling wands for sure. It heats up well within a minute, and stays a nice consistent heat. It's easy to change the heat to make it hotter or cooler. The temp change buttons are right on the handle, so I accidentally hit them while curling my hair, but that's okay because you're supposed to lock the heat settings by double-pressing the power button, so then you can't change the temp by accident.

How it works on hair:

My hair type is regular to fine strand thickness, regular to thick amount of hair, long and straight with layers. I tried it out using the lower end of the heat settings. The curls came out soft and shiny in large, loose barrel curls. But they flattened out rather quickly, into the barest hint of a wave. The shortest layers held the curls a bit better than the longer layers, but they still flattened out to only a bit of a wave. But this result is, I think, due more to user error than a problem with the curling iron. I've never been very good at using the larger curling irons and wands. Next time I use it, I'll try a higher heat setting on less freshly-washed hair, and then set the curls with hairspray right away. Hopefully that will work better!

Wow!!! I'm very impressed with curling iron!! It makes beautiful curls that last!! It also curls my hair so quick and easily!! The curling iron is extremely well made and I love the temperature lock feature! I've tried a lot of high end curling irons like Paul Mitchell that are horrible compared to this one! I've also tried a lot of cheaper irons and I was hoping this would be better than my beloved Tony and Guy curling iron and it is! It's really helpful that the barrel is longer for my long hair too and the 1 inch size is the way to go if you want lasting curls because they loosen up to perfect size and stay for 2-3 days! I highly recommend this curling iron!

I like how this curls my hair.  I have long hair and this curls each section with ease.  It curls fast and the curls stay in all day!  My only complaint and why I did not give it 5 stars is because of how the cord twists up and makes it hard to curl with.  I have to continually manually unwind the cord so that I can continue curling.  Other than that annoyance I love it.

I keep sunscreen in my purse year round, both for the children and for me.  Finding sunscreen for our faces is always a benefit.  I just don't feel like the quality of most sunscreens is high enough.  But La Roch Posay is going to be a better quality sunscreen.  SPF 50, or at least SPF 35, is important in Michigan even in the winter.  It seems like it is a reflective state.  Light reflects from the snow and from the water, both of which we have year round.

This product is described as being a primer.  My mistake in this was not seeing that it is tinted.  The tone of it is fine and even matches my skin tone perfectly.  However, I would never put tinted anything on my face, or on the childrens faces.  I just dont.

La Roche-Posay makes very high quality products with quality ingredients.  This is a very good product but is better for some uses than others.  If you want to use this for sun protection, its great. It gives a nice even texture and a natural but better look. The color happens to work perfectly for me too. It does not have a heavy scent.  It can also be used as a primer under makeup and that is where I think it loses something. Everyone has different skin types and likes, but for me it seemed a bit heavy/thick for a primer. It definitely cleaned up some imperfections, but I prefer something smoother with a more moisturizing feel. I am older and my skin is starting to dry so that may be part of the reason it felt dry.  It really deserves 4.5 stars
summary: This is a very good product but is better for some uses than others

reviewText:
I took this because I am very pale and need sunscreen daily. I am not impressed. I let this warm up in my bathroom for 8 hours before I tried it ( it was cold coming in from the mail). I almost could not get it out of the tube, it was so thick. It did not apply easily with a make up sponge so I used my fingers. My skin looked uniform but uniformly chalky.

I am not sure who the intended market is for this product but I ended up with an unpleasant orange tone to my skin. Unless I followed this with a lot of foundation, I could never wear it to work or out. I might take it with me on a camping vacation where no one will really see me. Overall I did not like the thick consistency nor the color tone. It would be helpful for customers to get a sense of how deep the color is of this product....perhaps a color swatch? Had I known the depth of the color I'd have never chosen this.
summary: Thick and chalky, made me look a wee bit orange

reviewText: Love this! It has a powdery feel after application but is not dry. Works great as a make-up primer!

Despite previous reviews saying that this casts an orange tint to the skin, I had really been hoping that this would work for me -- but it's definitely orange!  I'm pretty fair (I wear MAC foundation in NW 20), and this just doesn't seem to work for lighter skin tones.  If you have more color to your skin, it might work better for you.

It does go on nicely, though, and has a smooth feel to it.  The 50 SPF is also great, and was the reason that I was hoping this would work.  Using it definitely saves the extra step of applying a tinted moisturizer after sunscreen.

If La Roche-Posay came out with this in a few shades, it would be much better.  As it is, it's definitely not a universal product.

I like this but I can't really use it as it is intended.  I'm 64 years old.  This cream is so thick it settles into every little wrinkle!  I wish it were lighter weight.  The color is great for my olive complexion.  I have a lot of yellow undertones.  I will probably use this at home out by the pool.  I really need some sort of protection against the sun's rays.  I just won't be able to use it as a daily tone corrector.  I did find it to be excellent at covering the tiny brown spots on the back of my hands!  It blends in smoothly and perfectly.  It doesn't wipe off on everything you touch, either.  It really is too expensive to just use as a sunscreen or cover up for your hands.  So, I won't be getting any more of it.
summary: Great spot concealer for your hands!

reviewText: For some reason I did not know how tinted this sunscreen is and I was a bit taken aback by the slight orangish yellow cast if gave to my skin. To its credit the product does not make my acne prone skin break out and additionally it makes the pores on my nose which I often feel are huge definitely appear smaller.  This product does have good and long lasting protection from the sun and I am reassured by the fact that the manufacturer, La Roche-Posay, is recommended by many dermatologists.
summary: Tinted Sunscreen That Minimizes Pores And Does Not Cause Acne Breakouts

reviewText:
...in an instant.
Smoothing this on really makes skin look more even and pores smaller. Small pores on my nose dissappear after using foundation on top of this, but it actually looks great without foundation.
Very light scent that quickly dissipates.
Love the high SPF.

Most of us are aware that we need sunscreen/sunblock every time we expose our delicate skin to the harsh rays, but finding a product that is both effective and safe for long-term use can feel like a monumental challenge. You can read the Environmental Working Group's annual list, ponder the tradeoffs between chemical (hormone disruptor?) and mineral (looks ghastly) sunscreens, and make yourself slightly crazy in the process. Complicating the matter is that the FDA has failed to approve effective and apparently non-toxic ingredients that have been safely used in other countries for decades. La Roche-Posay produces some of the best sunscreens in the world, but, alas, you can't buy them in the United States. Amazon sells them on its UK site (look for "Anthelios XL") with the note: "Sorry, we can't deliver this item to the United States." Which brings me to this Anthelios product. It's got a walloping dose of titanium dioxide, an SPF of 50, and appropriate level of hype: "instantly conceals to reduce uneven tone for smoother, flawless looking skin." Were the copywriters serious? Did they even get a sample to try? This product is thick, like stage makeup. If you have even a hint of lines on your face, it will accentuate them and make you look mummified. After an initial horrific encounter, I used the product over a moisturizer with a lower SPF and it applied much more easily. That obstacle conquered, I went on to deal with the tone-correcting issues. Reading other reviews here, I saw references to the product being ideal for yellow or olive skin. In fact, that's a reason I chose to try this sunscreen. I have medium Mediterranean coloring and figured the color would be ideal, vs other tinted sunscreens that are way too pink. Um, well, no, I don't know whose skin tone this "corrects" but it made me look grayish and ill. So, over the Anthelios I added another layer of foundation. If you're keeping track, at that point I had three layers of stuff on my face. I was out for a walk with my family and my son looked at me and said "mom, your face is peeling off, like a mask." Clearly, my technique still needs to be refined. Living in a sunny, warm climate, I own and use many sunscreens. For example, EltaMD UV Daily Broad-Spectrum SPF 40 TINTED, 1.7 oz and Andalou Naturals Brightening SPF 30All In One Beauty Balm, Sheer Tint, 2 Ounce are good if you like a light tint (though my daughter complains about the Andalou rose scent). The boys love this product, which is a little white going on but disappears after you apply it: Burnout Ocean Tested Physical Spf30+ 3.4 OZ -- and it's top-rated by EWG too. I am going to save the Anthelios for days that I am going to be out in the sun a lot because nothing's getting past that titanium dioxide. But aesthetically speaking, I doubt it would be anyone's top choice.
summary: Keeps sun and rain away from your face

reviewText: It's almost a little misleading to call this a "tone-correcting primer."  It definitely does add a color tone and works well under makeup, but the tone leans way to the orange side.  If that's the tone your complexion needs, then it would serve as a tone corrector; however, my fair, pink complexion doesn't benefit from this color.  The consistency was fine, a little heavy but typical of other sunblockers I've used with color in them, and I liked that it is not greasy or sticky.  The coverage seems heavy at first but does smooth out, and as mentioned, does work well as a makeup primer.  It is easy to wash off at the end of the day.  It's a little early in the year to be certain of its sunblocking properties, but I have been out in the sun a little and have had no burning (and my skin burns very easily).
summary: Seems to work well, needs to be more specific about "tone correcting"

reviewText: Great product, but there's a clumpy texture to it that's more than expected from merely being a mineral product. While it works effectively as a sunblock, I'm not sure that the clumsiness is normal, or if it's a quality defect.

I was excited to try the La Roche-Posay mineral primer.  I LOVE that it has an SPF of 50 first off.  It goes on a little gritty but I am going to attribute that to the minerals in the product.  This goes on evenly and is actually the perfect shade for my medium/olive toned skin.  I would not use this as a foundation.  I am using it as a primer under my regular foundation.  This helps keep my foundation looking fresh on my skin during the day.  It does not make my skin oily.  I also love that there are antioxidants in this.  I would definitely recommend this as a combination sunscreen/primer.
summary: La Roche-Posay Daily Tone Correcting Primer with SPF 50

reviewText:
This is tinted facial sunscreen which is a great idea but at first try it is thick.  It reminds me of the old fashion cake make-up but the key to this product is to apply sparingly and rub in well. I am fair with blue eyes and the color is good for me. As with all sunscreens re-apply throughout the day.
I recommend this product but I do wish it was creamier.
summary: Great tinted sunscreen to protect your face

reviewText:
La Roche-Posay is a very, very amazing brand. l have used multiple products from them, and have rarely been disappointed. When I ordered this Tone Correcting Primer with Sunscreen, I fully expected it to be another knockout product. I was a little bummed with its consistency and was hoping it had more tint, but as a sunscreen it did not disappoint at all.

Pros:
+ La Roche-Posay knows a thing or two about sunscreen as their facial sunscreen line is a favorite of dermatologists, cancer doctors, and skin care experts around the world. Even if that is all I used this for, it does give outstanding protection as a broad spectrum sunscreen.

+ This is very gentle for sensitive skin or people with rosacea . I hate having to spend so much money on sunscreen, but when you have skin that reacts to any type of sunscreen except mineral (unless it's full of preservatives or perfumes) and burns in less than 15 minutes in the sun, it's worth it. Some people that don't have sensitive skin can have a sensitivity to titanium dioxide or zinc oxide, though, so be warned.

+ I have combination skin, and a lot of mineral sunscreens will really show off the parts of your skin that are dry because they don't contain any extra moisture. As long as I used a moisturizer beforehand, I had zero problems with this primer showing off my dry spots. If you have dry skin, be aware you may need extra moisturizer as mineral sunscreens tend to dry out skin (which is why some acne treatments will use titanium dioxide or zinc oxide to dry up pimples, so with continual use some people may find their skin becoming clearer).

+ As a makeup primer, it works amazingly well. After several days of my face getting yuck sweaty a few times...wow. My T-zone stayed matte, and my makeup looked as good 10 hours later as it did when I put it on. Be aware, though, that if you make a makeup oops and need to correct something, this stuff does NOT let you off easy. Whereas I can usually use a damp q-tip for a quick fix, I had to dip it in makeup remover to fix my boo-boos when I used this as a primer.

+ If you have pinkish or reddish skin or undertones, this is great at helping to balance out your skin tone. It provides a nice base for my usual foundation. I really wish it had a bit more tint to it so I could use it on days when I don't want to use foundation, but it doesn't give enough coverage for that. If used in combination with a tinted moisturizer, I am able to get enough light coverage to even things out perfectly.

+ There is no real scent to this. It has a bit of faint chalk-like scent, but I suspect that is from the mineral content. It reminds me of the sunscreen sticks that leave the big white stripe down your nose.

+ It doesn't clog pores, which is great for any sunscreen. The particles for titanium dioxide are too large to penetrate the dermis. I know far too many people who refuse to wear sunscreen on their faces because they a) think the 15 SPF in their face lotion is enough (it's not), and b) don't want to break out so they risk skin cancer rather than pimples.

Cons:
- Don't order this if you expect it will give you ANY real coverage. It won't. It's a tinted primer that is meant to go under your usual foundation. It has a bare hint of neutral color that leans towards the yellow side, so if you suffer from redness or pink undertones, it will help you on your way to achieving a neutral undertone. If you have a sallow skin tone and choose to use this, you may want to adjust your normal foundation color for one that has pinkish undertones in order to balance out. There's not enough pigment in this to do much more than take a slight edge off of any facial redness or to act as more than a complement your usual foundation.

- This comes out of the tube feeling thick and a bit gritty. If you don't let it warm up on your hand first it can be a bit of a pain to get it to cover evenly (or at least until it warms up on your skin). I have found that putting it in a glass of hot water while I'm in the shower makes it into the mousse-like texture that they describe. Or you can mix a bit of your face lotion with this too.

- You should reapply this every two hours if used correctly, but that's hard to do with makeup on over the top of this without taking it all off first and redoing everything. I can't hold this against them, as every sunscreen says to do this, so make sure you have other sun protection handy. Neutrogena makes a wonderful face spray sunscreen that not only is cooling but does not destroy your makeup. I used it last summer and it was amazing.

I will definitely be purchasing this again for the upcoming summer months. No other primer I've tried has worked anywhere close to as well as this one did. The meh level of tint and the unappealing texture were the reason for the star bump. If this is their first foray into what could be a full makeup line, consider me intrigued.
summary: I love La Roche-Posay for sun protection

reviewText:
I'm always looking for new, high-SPF tinted moisturizers, and I think I've found my new favorite!

The texture is a little unusual - it comes out thick, with an almost clay-like texture. I was skeptical at first. However, it applies super easily and I immediately noticed a difference in my skin. It looked clear, smooth, and even (the cream immediately took away all of my redness). I was glowing. It gives a texture that is somewhere between matte and dewy - I didn't have the powdered look of matte, but I didn't have the "was she sweating?" look that dewy sometimes gives me. And it held through the work day! Usual caveats apply about how the SPF would wear off during the day, etc, but I work in an office so I'm more concerned about my bright commute to work when it comes to SPF than I am about the harsh lights in my office (where I want to look good more than to protect).
summary: Will definitely replace my go to Shiseido

reviewText: Patience is a virtue in applying this product to the face. Best to under-estimate what you'll need because a little bit can go a long way. The warming and spreading of the product mostly happened for me after I applied it to skin and then reworked it. I also tried not to judge the color until I gave it a few moments to settle in. While it still looked yellow indoors and under the lights of the bathroom, it wasn't as noticeable in the bright sunshine. My face did feel a little dry, but the product didn't run into my eyes when my scalp began to sweat, and there was no heavy smell. I did feel that it sort of had to wear off rather than wash off, so I'm glad I used such a thin coat. That being said, I didn't burn at all, and I have very fair skin. It also didn't cause me to break out, as many of the other products do. The cost is such that I will probably use it just on my face and the back of my hands. I've used a clear La Roche-Posay sunblock before and really liked it. I think I prefer it to this tinted version so that's why this one gets 4 stars.
summary: A Little Dab Will Do You

reviewText:
Truthfully, having read a few reviews before ordering this, I was a little nervous that this would turn my face orange, but it didn't.

First a few comments:
It was extremely thick and I had a little difficulty squeezing some out of the tube
The shade is a medium shade that would not work on very fair people
There was no obvious scent - a definite plus
Spread nicely on skin and could be worn alone
Definitely more CC cream than primer

I have skin color that most cosmetic companies call "light" - not very pale, or medium. So this cream was a little bit dark on me, but only a little. This cream was very thick, and rich, and only had the slightest hint of a silicone feel. Honestly, I thought it looked great on its own. The fact that it's a mineral sunscreen is great - no irritation like you get with regular sunscreen - and it has a fabulous 50 SPF. I have very sensitive skin and was really happy that this didn't cause any itching or irritation. It is a tiny bit dark on me, so I'm sure I'll wear it way more in the summer. This is a great product.
summary: Feels great on, no overwhelming scent, but a little dark

reviewText: I have medium tone skin, so I was a big fan of this product. I was surprised at the consistency and colorthis does not go on sheer, and it would likely be too much for lighter skin tones. But it worked very well for me. I used it underneath makeup, and my makeup stayed on for longer than usual. This doesn't spread super easily, so I'd likely use it alongside a moisturizer with sunscreen, but overall, I'm happy with this!
summary: For medium skin tones, not light!

reviewText: This wasn't what I expected. It is a thick foundation-like cream that did not leave a chalky look on my fair skin that others complained about. It just looked like I was wearing a thick foundation. If my skin was worse than it is I would appreciate the coverage, but as it is I normally can get by with a BB cream and the heavier coverage was more than I wanted. I have been wearing it as a sunscreen. I have to say that for the price I prefer Eltamd UV Clear SPF 46, 48-Gram 1.7 oz. It provides a relatively sheer coverage with good sun protection. Both products are easy on my very sensitive skin. I don't expect to buy more of this.

The consistency of this mineral based product is thick. Since it comes in one tint it is not going to replace foundation that is carefully matched to skin color in a cosmetics department. For a day in the sun, not at the beach or pool this is a good product to use.  I went to a tennis event and used this and then applied my regular blush over it and the results were acceptable. My skin tone is light/medium. It did not run and burn my eyes as many sunscreens do.  The directions suggest reapplication every two hours which would really layer this on thick. It is not water proof. I removed it with a make up remover by La Roche-Posay and it all came off easily.

La Roche-Posay is a brand I have come to love as I have been extremely happy with their facial sunscreens for years. This Tone Correcting Primer with Mineral Sunscreen for Sensitive Skin (with SPF 50) is a new product. Unfortunately, I found the cream too thick to be able to apply lightly and evenly.

As for the SPF rating, I usually buy the SPF 45 and don't think this will be much different. It has always protected my sensitive skin from getting red or burning, even when I only apply it in the morning.

I am giving this 4 stars for the qualities that I am able to assess now. Since we are not in summer months with a lot of sun yet, I cannot rate it as a sunscreen and how well it protects in that function. I can only rate it as a primer and rate it's physical attributes.  I do not doubt that it will function properly as a sunscreen,  as this has always been a well rated line, including the sunscreen products, from this brand, but I can't say for sure yet, so 4 stars so far and I will update when I get to use it as a sunscreen. I have hyperpigmentation so I have to be very picky with sunscreen and I can tell within minutes if one works or not, since my skin will get darker in those areas, feel hot, and sweat, within just a few minutes of being in the sun without a good sunscreen. Some work well for hyperpigmentation and some don't work at all and allow the spots to get darker. Time will tell how this one works and I will update on that later.

So, I can only try this as a primer as of right now and for that purpose I do like this product. I like that it goes on with a very dry feel. There is no greasy feel and there is not even any lotion type or cream type feel to it. It is just a very dry mousse and that works out really nice for me. It is similar to a Cotz product that I really like as well.

The skin tone correcting factor is nice because it doesn't actually show up as a lot if color on your skin at all. It looks dark at first, but works into/onto the skin without any real traces of color. I am pale until the summer months, so I can't use darker foundations or primers. This one blends down to match your skin tone and give it a more perfected look. Now, if you use too much and get it too heavy you will see some color of course. You do not need a lot of this at all. A tiny little squeeze blends down to cover a lot of area and provides a nice thin, unnoticeable layer. I recommend trying a little bit on the back of your hand first so you see how it spreads and works in and how much area you can cover with just a little dab... that way you don't end up with too much on your face and not liking it or needed ing to remove some. It is waterproof, so it's not the easiest thing to just wipe off excess.

The waterproof factor is another feature that I like. I put it on the backs of my hands to give it a try before I had used it on my face and went about rinsing and filling the tub, rinsing my hands under water, etc. The water just beads right off and doesn't effect the primer. That is important to me because I spend a lot of time in the sun in the summer and spend a few weeks at the beach... I need to know it is not going to wear off quickly or sweat away.

This type of sunscreen/primer is nice because it allows you to have a little bit of coverage and not just bare skin and sunscreen. It's pointless to wear makeup to the beach, pool, etc because it is going to wash off in the water or sweat off. But, sometimes you just want a little bit of perfection for your skin and a more even toned look, like you would get with a foundation..  that's what this product is great for. There's no heavy makeup look of feel, no caking or cracking, and no streaking when you sweat or get your face wet. Plus, it has a strong sunscreen built in to protect you. I didn't care about sunscreen too much until several years ago when I first noticed the sun damage and hyperpigmentation.  It looks like someone threw mud on my face. It's embarrassing and I hate it. So. I've tried sooo many different sunscreen products and skin lighteners. There's not many sunscreens that actually work to protect the dark spots from getting darker.  I've even tried using sunscreen just on the spots and leaving the rest of my face bare just to try and get it to even out some, but no luck of course. I just end up with darker brown spots. Mine is a large portion of my forehead, across the tops of my eyebrows, across my top lip (like a moustache! Ugh) and smaller spots on my cheekbones. My lips even have it around the edges and it looks like I am wearing brown lip liner. Summer and sunlight is my skins number one enemy now and that really is upsetting because I spend so much time outside and at the beach. I wish now that I would have taken better precautions when I was younger. I will be 40 soon and my damage showed up about 7 years ago. To me that was rather devastating and "too young " to have that damage. So, USE YOUR SUNSCREEN PEOPLE!  And please make sure to slather it on your kids and teens, too. They may thank you one day and you will definitely be more happy while walking around WITHOUT mud splats all over your face!

UPDATE - I wanted to update now that I have used this for hours on end on the beach so many times. It was excellent at preventing sunburn and staying effective even when sweating heavily from baking in the sun. My brown spots, especially above my lip, always sweat more than the rest of my face and sooner than the rest of my face. Above my lip will start to sweat first, then everywhere else. (Sounds attractive, right?!?) It is hard to keep sunscreen above my lip due to the sweating. This one works very well in that regard and I did not even have to reapply as often as with other brands. Although it did protect against sunburn, my brown marks did of course get darker, which is always expected, unfortunately, and I did gain more splotches this year so far. Large patches across my cheekbones and some developing on my chin, too. As much as I hate them, I just keep wishing my whole face would become one big splotch just so its all one even color. Anyway, the fact that it is so long lasting and preventing sunburn is great. That's what you want in a sunscreen. I am someone who goes out on the beach at 7 am and do not come back in til 7 or 8 pm except to run in the house quick to use the bathroom or grab more water, etc. So, when I test a sunscreen, I really test it. This one does not cause any breakouts, my pores do not feel clogged or gross by the end of the day after I have applied it a few times and it dries and sets quickly without any greasiness and no shine. Good, good stuff right here and worth the price in my opinion.
summary: very nice as a waterproof primer/time will tell as sunscreen

reviewerName: Gina Pera, Adult ADHD Expert and Author
reviewText:
I love this cream! It's the only "mineral" sunblock/screen that doesn't leave me looking freshly embalmed (i.e. waxy white).

The slight bit of tint works perfectly on my fair/olive Italian skin.

I love the creamy/powdery texture that spread evenly and even provides a bit of coverage.
summary: Perfect tint and coverage for my skin color

reviewText:
I like the weight of this skin serum,put in a pump bottle that will reduce both contamination and deterioration.  It spread readily and evenly and dried rapidly.  I did not experience with stinging even when applied over skin treated with a microneedle skin roller.

The product is designed for seriously stressed skin where oxidation has occurred due to stress, smoke,and sunlight. The main active ingredient, Supplamine, is a combination of two amino acids that work together to treat advanced glycation end products (AGE products.)  . Glycation is a major cause of skin aging, and is cause by sugars attaching to collagen and elastic, creating inflammation and less resilient skin. Supplamine in vitro using skin cell cultures prevents toxic sugars from being made. It is designed to neutralize existing AGE products existing in the skin. Whether it will do the same on intact human skin is to be determined .since tissue culture is not the same as a complex human body.

I do find the price excessive for one ounce, although it can be obtained for $15 less.  Still if cost is not an object this appears to be a superior product.
summary: A superior product to reduce Advanced Glycation End Products

reviewText: For a quality product I was shocked when I couldn't open this bottle, it just turned in place never lifting the pump. MEG 21 products are all very good so felt safe using it. The inner part of the bottle lifted out so I was at least able to get some product out and able to use. It goes on easy without feeling greasy or sticky and drys fast. It has no perfumes added but does give off a faint fruit scent thats pleasant. Anti-Aging qualities are not going to show up instantly but my face has a glow it didn't have before, I look alive. Dry dead skin is ugly so having a product like this on your face helps keep your skin moist so it doesn't dry and flake off. I will update this review if I see changes, lasting changes. I hope MEG 21 fixes this poorly designed plastic bottle, use glass with a simple dropper and forget spending so much on different packaging that fails.
summary: Smooth alive looking skin that feels soft without being greasy and oily!

reviewText: There are many of these products out there that promise much and cost much. Having only just gotten a bottle of this to test out, I can't tell you what the long term effects are, but I'll try to post an update after about a month of use. For now I can say the lotion goes on light and soaks in completely leaving no weird smell, and no burning sensation, so it's already better than many I have tried. As for results . . . stay tuned.

I was excited to try this product, but sadly, was disappointed. The formula itself is very nice; a light lotion that glides on without a sticky feel. It has a merest trace of fragrance. I don't have sensitive skin on my face, but I always do a patch test elsewhere first, just in case. I applied this serum to the back of my hands, and immediately felt a burning sensation. I thought it might subside, but it continued to burn and burn until I washed it off. This is a no from me.

I've been using the MEG 21 Cell Therapy Anti-Oxidant Boost Serum for just a few days and will update after 3 weeks (to address their claim).
I am also experimenting on the back of one hand to have a more accurate comparison.

I have extremely sensitive skin that is very dry.  Being post-menopausal, I lost what little moisture I had--plus I live in a drought area with extremely low (or nil) humidity.  I am scent sensitive as well.  The skin on my face is soaks up moisture (as if it is starving...which it may be)

Out of the gate, the scent of this product is faint and borderline for my sensitivity.  The initial scent strength fades quickly, but does remain in my acceptable range.  The "scent flavor" is of the perfumy type (very light) vs. citrus or medicinal.

What I like A LOT is that this Serum spreads smoothly, dries quickly, and leaves a silky sheen without appearing (or feeling) oily/greasy.  High fives here.  I appreciate my skin feeling and appearing hydrating without a greasy covering.  30 minutes after applying both (as of this writing), my face and the back of my right hand feel slightly cooler to the touch with a lovely pleasurable soft feel.  Both FEEL moisturized--which is a plus.

I have LOTS of fine (and not-so-fine) lines on my face with its 64 years mostly due to starting with dry skin (+ age-related moisture-loss & residence weather).  I have no fantasies of losing all the lines, but am interested in giving my facial skin the help and health I can.

Other reviewers (and the description on amazon) do a complete job in the science and trials-info -- so I will not repeat here.

The bottle is small (1 oz)--under 5" high--very nicely packaged.  Simple, elegant.  The opening inner cap is a new & interesting design...twist one way and the inner-pump dispenser lifts up; twist the opposite and the dispenser retreats back into the silver outer cap (handy for travel & evaporation prevention)  Nice, light, and easy to hold and operate.

Recommended to be applied twice each day onto clean skin.  (the follow-up moisturizer is also suggested, but I have only the Serum to review)

Of course, what shoppers want to know... Does it work as advertised, is it worth the price (current on amazon: $95), and how long does it last?
I am sorry to make you wait... but, I'll be back in mid-to-late September to update.
summary: A lovely product in its feel, application and appearance.

reviewText: This MEG21 skin care anti oxidant boost is supposed to work best in conjunction with a hydrating moisturizer. MEG21 has its own face treatment and advanced formula. I have some aging spots on my face and once I apply this cell therapy I feel it work right away. 1 ounce = 30 grams can be quite expensive at $100 but I'm glad the product is made in the USA and there are some serious claims to the product working well according to the meg21 website. I have not waited the recommended 28 days to see the full difference the product claims to make but I can see some improvement in my skin with regards to reduced roughness and increased firmness.
summary: Great USA made product with solid knowledge behind it but on the expensive side

reviewText:
MEG21 is a skin care line created by a  PHD research scientist, and has some serious science to back up its claims.. The main active ingredient, supplamine, is a combination of two aminos that work together to  treat glycation.  Glycation is a major cause of skin aging, and is cause by sugars attaching to collagen and elastic, creating inflammation and less resilient skin.  Supplamine not only prevents the toxic sugars from being made, but it also works to neutralize existing toxic sugars.

So now with that background information out of the way, I can share how my experience with it has been.  I have rather sensitive skin, and many anti-aging products have caused irritation and stinging when I apply it.  This serum hasn't caused any problems for me in terms of discomfort or irritation.  The product information says it takes at least 28 days for full effects to be seen, so I will have to update this review after a few weeks use in order to evaluate that claim.  However it does leave my skin feeling well hydrated and is not sticky or unpleasant feeling.

This is only 1 ounce of product, so at close to $100, is rather expensive.  At this point it is hard to say if that price is justified, but I'm hoping I'll have positive results to report back after a month.
summary: Skin care backed by serious science

reviewText: Light, a little goes a long way. A bit of a scent when put on - not perfumey....more citrusy I would say. Is not real greasy, it seems to give you almost a polished look. Light enough that you don't really feel it weighing your face down - it actually feels kind of nice. On the expensive side and once I have used it long enough I will report back on how I think it is working. they say to use it twice a day on clean skin and to follow its use by other moisturizers of theirs.

This serum can be applied after washing and before moisturizing your face. I have not experienced any irritation or skin problems as a result of use twice daily. The product is a milky liquid that applies easily with just a few drops for each area of the face. The dispenser works well and can be easily controlled to dispense only the amount you want with each push. Moisturizer goes over the serum smoothly and I found no problem mixing the MEG 21 serum along with either a Dennis Gross or Strivectin moisturizing product.
summary: Easily applies. No significant scent. Dispenser works well. Used between washing and moisturizing.

reviewText: I have not seen any drastic changes for the better, or any changes at all after using it for about 10 days. It is an excellent moisturizer: goes in deep and gets absorbed quickly without heavy feeling. It does feel like skin food, but no visible changes of any kind. Will update after I pass a 30 days use. I have a very sensitive dry skin and there were no irritation or reactions of any kind; in fact, it has a calming effect on my skin.
summary: I have not seen any drastic changes for the better, or any changes at all after using it ...

reviewText: I have very sensitive skin, so I am cautious when I use new things on my skin. I did a test using the back of my hand, and so far so good. The serum felt good on my skin; I didn't have any stinging sensations as another reviewer mentioned. I then tried the serum on my forehead, just to make sure it was ok on my face. Again, so far so good. I will have to come back in a few weeks to give a followup to this review. I do think this product is rather expensive, so the results would have to be phenomenal to get me to buy it.
summary: and so far so good. The serum felt good on my skin

reviewText: Well, my honey was not impressed.  He's a vain, gay little fellow who has hit his 50s and is not happy about it.  My bathroom looks like the place face products have gone to die.  Sadly, he didn't feel or notice any difference with this, but I've begged him to keep trying since waking up next to a gorgon can be tough!  Anywho, we have this bathroom rule now for these prodcuts, one in, one out.  Too many bottles and vials end up falling on me when i open the cabinets.  Maybe the denser male skin is the issue, but I think this will be in the "one out" category.  SOrry.

This is a nice moisturizer for my face and it makes my complexion look a little brighter. It doesn't take much of this serum to apply an even coat on my face. The fragrance is pleasant, a nice floral scent and it doesn't stick around for long. My skin is very dry and at first it would soak this lotion right up. I feel like my skin is more moist and supple now, and the lotion isn't getting sucked into my skin quite as fast. It did sting a little bit the first few days I used it, but that sensation has been gone ever since. My complexion looks more vibrant and less worn or tired, so MEG 21 Cell Therapy seems to be doing its job for me.

I don't know that I have the exact right word for what this product does to my skin. To say it makes it youthful is too strong of a statement, but lines are greatly lessened and there is a gentle elasticity under my chin that hasn't been there for years. Healthy, I guess is the best word. My face looks healthy in a way that really pleases me. It goes on quite easily and absorbs rapidly. No greasy residue or oily sheen (which I hate).
summary: I guess is the best word. My face looks healthy in a way ...

reviewText:
I like this MEG 21 Anti-oxidant Boost serum.  It has a thick, silky consistency that goes on smoothly and absorbs rapidly into my skin.  I have combination skin and I was happy to find that it left the dry spots hydrated but didn't make the oily spots even oilier.  The serum didn't cause any irritation to my hyper-sensitive skin, and my nose only picked up the faintest of scent.  I couldn't quite identify the scent  cucumber possibly?  If you have ever used Elizabeth Ardens SuperStart, this Boost serum feels a lot like that.

Like a thousand other creams the MEG 21 advertises wrinkle and age fighting results, but what is intriguing is that the main ingredient, Supplamine, started out as a pharmaceuticals product.  Like Tretinoin (retinoic acid, Retin-A, Tazaroc) which started out as an acne cream and turned into a block-buster wrinkle cream, or Bimatoprost which started out as  eye drops for glaucoma and turned into the eyelash lengthening mega-hit, Latisse, Supplamine was first developed as a treatment in the prevention of kidney disease and blindness in diabetes patients.

Will Meg 21 turn out to be as effective as Retin-A?  Only time will tell, but Im curious enough to use it long turn and test out the effect.  I have a lot of creepy skin under my eyes, so I will take some before pictures and after a few months of use I will take some after pictures to compare.

I will update in a few months.
summary: Will this become the next Retin-A???

reviewText:
MEG 21 Cell Therapy Anti-Oxidant Boost Serum makes many claims and provides some science to bolster such things as reduces fine lines.  I am not an expert on skin care products, but can provide some personal background on my own experiences with other products along with MEG 21 Cell Therapy.

Growing up in Florida, and having a parent that had sun related melanoma, I have understood the importance of sun screen for years, and routinely use it.  Later in life, I moved to colder and drier climates and wanted a daily use unscented sunscreen moisturizer not just for sun protection but to reduce dry itchy skinI have used some form of P&Gs Olay Complete for sensitive skin since 1982 (aged 20 years).  (The name and formulation have changed a couple of times, but performance as a daily sunscreen moisturizer has remained constant).  Now in my 50s, I still use Olay Complete (with occasional forays into Total Effects Anti-Aging Moisturizer depending on price), but nothing stops the progression of time, particularly around the eyes.  Fine wrinkles are normal, and I have them.  I have tried a number of products that purport to reduce or minimize these wrinkles.

Again, not being a skin care expert, my own estimation of the range of products making claims generally fall in to a couple of categories.  Covering agents (including colored pigments, fillers, and reflecting agents), constrictors and tightening agents (various alcohols, witch hazel, astringents), relaxers (Botox!), chemical and mechanical exfoliants (Retin A, retinol, organic acids, alpha-beta hydroxyl acids, peroxides, micro beads and scrubs, laser peels), and plumbers (collagen injections, moisture retainers, and purported collagen buildersinternal and external).

With the exception of anything injected (collagen, Botox), face lifts and anything laser--I have tried all of these topical products at one point or another.  Certain products I avoid putting on my face since they seem to make my skin sensitive and irritated (notably Olay Body WashUltra Moisture, with or without the loofahnot sure why-- and the obvious mechanical scrubbing agents containing micro beads).

Cutting to the chase, I prefer scent free productsor a scent that is very light and disappears quickly. No sticky residues after application is also important.  Application cost must be under control, something can be expensive as long as you do not have to slather it on!  So, in addition to daily Olay Complete, my preference for around the eyes and over time has been limited to another Olay product, Definity, which is now called OLAY EYES ILLUMINATING EYE CREAM.  This product has some reflecting pigments which brighten darker skin under the eyes, along with a refreshing hydration agent. In the 80s Clinique had a serum product that must be similar to their current All About Eyes that I liked (?)and seemingly compared very well with the MEG 21 Cell Therapy in a couple of key characteristics.

Enough about other products, what about MEG 21?  Well, first off, product cost and printed science on the label should make it superior to all others? There are things to love.  A very light almost imperceptible scent that reminds me of the prior Clinique product  a slight pine-citrus scent that disappears quickly.  A small amount around your eyes dries quickly with no stickiness and no residue, along with a very pleasant refreshing cooling effect that lasts during the same drying.  Tired eyes will love it.

Over a couple of days of suggested twice daily use, some apparent wrinkle reduction was present under certain lighting conditionswhich perceived as tightening rather than hiding, filling, or reflection.  Now it remains to be seen if that wrinkle reduction was due to reducing glycation or other large marketing ideas about toxic sugars (which, frankly, as a chemist, I consider mumbo-jumbo).  If glycation is reduced the wrinkle reduction would be expected to be a longer lasting effect? Personally, having used sunscreen all my life, aging is normal and while progression can be slowed it cannot be reversedparticularly with the topical application of a cream?  All that aside, and most subjectively, wrinkles seem reduced when MEG-21 is present and I like the way it feels when I put it on.

Now the elephant in the room.  Application cost is low with just small dabs used around the eyes, but there is initial sticker shock at almost a hundred dollars an ounce (what is that in cost per lb? yow!)but if you are in the market for these higher end products, it is not out of the realmmany cost about the same.

I do love MEG 21 for its low scent, invisibility, quick drying, and no residue or stickinessproviding some subjective wrinkle reduction and refreshing feeling when applied.  Given an opportunity I would try some other MEG 21 products!

This lotion has a clean, subtle smell and feels really good on my skin; no stickiness or heavy residue at all. After application my skin feels clean and fresh. It comes in a great little pump bottle that keeps germs and debris from getting in and is easy to use. I've been using this for a week and loving it, but will update again after three to better review their claim!
summary: Clean and fresh with no residue

reviewText:
I like the product, very easy to apply and a huge thumbs up for the packaging and ease of use via the dispenser, another thumbs up for no strong scent that I can detect. That said, I've been applying this daily for a week and really haven't seen any significant improvement. I don't have the crow's lines, but I do have puffiness on the lower lid and I just am not noticing any improvement at all, in fact I had better results with an Olay product  that is half the price of this cream.

A very nice eye cream, and it seems from other reviews on this page folks are having better results than I am. I would have rated it four stars, but for the very high (for me) price tag. Your mileage may vary.
summary: This is a very nice eye cream and moisturizes well...but...

reviewText: I'm not the best person to review this because I haven't tried all others--I have used different creams that serve as wrinkle reducers around the eyes, but I haven't used them religiously and I don't really have significant wrinkles to begin with, so I've had trouble deciding how well the items work.  This doesn't make things worse, but I can't see that it makes things better.  It comes out as this little white creme and a little goes a long way.  It is absorbed into the skin and appears to be working.  I just can't say for sure that it has erased wrinkles.  In terms of ease of use, I find the pump okay--I  dabbed the item into a finger and applied it directly like that.

This is a nicely moisturizing product, but I cannot say that it has much of an actual brightening effect. I do not experience puffiness around my eyes, so I can't access whether it works for that purpose. Happily, there is only a very mild scent, which is produced from "fragrance," listed in the ingredients. In fact, the list of ingredients is a bit disheartening, since many of them are chemicals known to be irritants or are considered less than clean on a toxicity scale. Most commercial (and even high-end) cosmetics and skincare products include them, so clearly this is an area of personal preference. The packaging is attractive and is good in theory, but there are two problems with this type of dispenser: first, it dispenses more product than you need, so you have to be very careful in trying to dispense a half pump, so as not to waste it. Secondly, when you get close to the end, it is really hard to access the product. It is overpriced, in my opinion, and there are far better eye brightening products available from DHC for much less.
summary: Moisturizing reatment that has a lot of chemicals and seems to be overpriced for the effectiveness promised

reviewText:
My wife loves this eye cream, she says that the texture of the cream is soft and silky, and that the combination of the eye cream and eye serum works wonders for reducing her puffy eyes when she stayed up late last weekend - supposedly she used the eye cream at night and serum in the morning.

She said that her eyes felt hydrated and that the puffiness was reduced when she applied the eye cream just before she slept. The eye cream is very light and has a slight fragrance to it so it apparently absorbs into the skin around the eyes better. As for brightening of her eyes, she was not able to tell as she has not applied it long enough to tell any difference.
summary: Effective eye cream - light and silky eye cream that reduces puffiness of the eyes

reviewText: This is clearly a solid product.  However, products of this type work differently for different people.  The bottle is a cool design and the product has a decent sweet smell.  A single pump of the product is more than enough for each use and the consistency of the product is easy to work with.  The product is a great moisturizer but we (house of two home using the product) have not seen a brightening effect.

This is an eye cream that claims to both brighten and firm the under eye area.  It comes in a pump bottle which allows you to control the size of the pump to customize how much product you get out.  It has the very slightest of scents, more from the ingredients, I think, than any added fragrance.  You'll only smell it if you have a really sensitive sense of smell.

Honestly, I don't think this eye cream is worth the hefty price tag.  It does okay with moisturizing.  It sinks in nicely and my undereye does feel soft and moisturized after using.  I'm not seeing any brightening effects, however, nor anything in the way of firming.  In fairness, I was not expecting much firming, but I was really hoping for some brightening.

I keep trying products that say they will reduce under-eye puffiness, and so far none of them work, so I don't have a  lot of hope for this. BUT, on first try, it seems to maybe be working? I will update this review on further testing.

The product comes in an interesting twist-top container that reveals a pump. One pump-worth of cream is plenty (possibly too much). It goes on smoothly and quickly, but it leaves a bit of a coating that can pill into white clumps if rubbed or if you put too much on, so be careful with that. It's not a good look.

So far, I'm pleased but this better be effective at this price. Hoping for the best. I will absolutely buy more if it works!

This eye treatment has a nice consistency and a very pleasant but very mild scent.  It was easily absorbed but if it will "tighten and firm" the fragile skin around my eyes is yet to be seen, but I'm willing to give it a chance.  As an aside, the bottle in which this treatment came, was unusual and was very impressive which has zero to do with the effectiveness  of the product, but I id  like it.

I wrestled with how to rate the MEG21 Eye Treatment. The information from the company states that results should be visible in "four weeks or less." To fairly evaluate MEG21 I used it exclusively for 32 consecutive days. I stopped using my usual eye treatment, replacing it with MEG21. However, I continued the rest of my normal routine. The advertising for this product, as well as, many of the reviews speak of incredible, visible results - unfortunately, I did not have a similar experience.
From the beginning: The packaging is nice. I really like the pump dispenser, it was easy to open, did not clog and can be locked back into place. This is especially helpful for those that travel and/or those who have small children at home. (Many a cream has been playfully dispensed onto my counter and floor. I wish all products had a locking cap like this one.) The cream itself is thin, very silky to the touch, with a barely noticeable scent. It goes on smoothly and dries quickly. This product did NOT cause any type of irritation or tearing of the eyes. (I mention this because it has happened with two other eye creams in the past.) The "highlight" effect in MEG21 is almost overdone. If you have bags under your eyes, even small ones, this cream highlights those - making them even more noticeable. I used this eye treatment daily and there's been no softening of lines, tightening of the skin or reduction in puffiness. Even the over eye skin shows no improvement. I expected the over eye skin to at least reap some level of moisturizing benefit... But, I was wrong.

MEG21 has an enticing advertising pitch and a well packaged product - unfortunately that's all. This product is overpriced and failed to deliver any of the benefits for which it was intended. For these reasons I cannot, in good conscience recommend MEG21 to others.

As it seems to be with all these products, claims do not meet reality. The feel of this is very nice, smooth and creamy. The scent is mild and faintly citrus, which I like a lot. I had no reaction to this at all. The design of the bottle is cool, the way the top pops up when you turn it, and the pump works well. However, for the price and the claim that this reverses wrinkles..it's really just a nice moisturizer.
summary: Very nice, but nothing more than a moisturizer

reviewText:
This MEG 21 "bright and firm" eye treatment is an off white creamy product in a pump dispenser to apply under the eyes and surrounding areas. I'm using it twice a day after washing my face per the directions. A little goes a long way- one full pump is too much even for the areas around both eyes, so I gently depress the pump and use about a half of a pump twice a day. This treatment isn't greasy at all, though my skin feels a bit tacky after I first apply it. After a few minutes, it gets fully absorbed and I can apply my eye makeup. This eye treatment feels nice, it moisturizes well and has a firming feel, leaves my skin smooth feeling and doesn't irritate my eyes or skin. It does have a mild fragrance that's pleasant, doesn't affect my sensitive skin or allergies and dissipates quickly.

MEG 21 claims to help fine lines, crow's feet, puffiness and discoloration. My biggest issues are dark circles and fine lines from aging. MEG 21 has botanicals-such as Vitamin K rich Suma Root- that I've read may actually help dark circles. It also has ingredients that are supposed to inhibit glycation on the skin from sugar that causes wrinkles due to a negative effect on collagen and elastin. This treatment has a lot of potential, though it will take about 2-4 weeks of daily use to see benefits (according to MEG 21 customer service), and I'll need to use it longer and update my review. For now, as compared to other eye treatments, I'm really pleased with how this treatment  moisturizes and makes my skin feel smooth and firm around my eyes, plus it causes no skin or eye irritation. While I can't judge the long term benefit yet, MEG 21 eye treatment seems like an excellent product. I'm rating it 5 stars and will update as appropriate.

12/23/2016 Update: I've been using this eye treatment regularly for a few months. Nothing will ever rid me entirely of dark circles I've had since being a teen, but Meg 21 works as well or slightly better than other dark circle treatments I've tried over the years such as Hylexin. My best friend for dark circles is Amazing Cosmetics Concealer. Also, my fine lines around my eyes are barely visible, and my skin looks and feels firm. Crow's feet and puffiness weren't issues before I started and still aren't issues for me, so I can't comment on the effectiveness of Meg 21 there. Notably, I still haven't run out of this product despite making it my regular eye treatment the last few months. Nothing works equally well for everyone, but I would definitely purchase this Meg 21 treatment in the future.
summary: Nice Feeling Treatment That Doesn't Irritate My Skin/Eyes Despite Light Fragrance- Takes 2-4 Weeks To Judge Longer Term Benefits

reviewText: My only regret is that I didn't take before and after pictures so you could see the difference. I have had dark circles under my eyes for as long as I can remember. I have tried a number of products with little change. The MEG 21 Bright and Firm Eye Treatment has made a remarkable improvement in my skin tone and has brightened my skin under my eyes. I will continue to use the product because it offers great results.
summary: I will continue to use the product because it offers great results.

reviewText:
Ive been looking for an eye treatment for years that would counteract the dark circles and crepe-y skin under my eyes.  These were issues Ive battled since my teens, but nothing has ever helped.  And now, at close to forty, I see the first signs of crows feet forming.  Youd think Id give up.  But I havent.
