reviewText:
This is a great setting spray that works well with my other brand makeup, as well as Dermablend products. The smell is a typical setting spray smell but I find that it is not that strong. My other, high-end and more expensive setting spray has the same smell but much stronger. The spray is even and applies consistently all over my face. I only spray four sprays (8"-10" away from my face) and there is no product running down my face. It dries in about 2 to 21/2 minutes and leaves a little bit of a shine. My makeup lasts (foundation, concealer, contouring products, powder, blush, eyebrow liner) all day, anywhere from 10-12 hours, even in summer weather.  I apply all of my makeup (without liquid eyeliner) and spray THEN apply eyeliner. I found that the spray would liquefy my favorite brand eyeliner and so it would start streaking. Since it is waterproof and longlasting by itself, I apply the eyeliner AFTER the setting spray.

Like all setting sprays, it does contain alcohol.

This setting spray works reasonably well and last reasonably well once applied.  The problem I have is with the instructions.  You are supposed to hold this a few inches away from your face, close your eyes, and spray 4-6 times in an X and T shaped pattern.  The first time I tried that, just as instructed, I ended up with a dripping wet face and had to start all over with fresh foundation.  Since then, I've found that two sprays are sufficient without soaking my face.  Of course, this means I can do a T shape or an X shape, but not both.

It doesn't cause an adverse reaction in me, and is a fairly neutral smell.  When lightly applied, it doesn't interfere with makeup, but does help to set it, as it should.  But practice before the first time you use it on your carefully made up face, or you may be frustrated, as I was, with a wet face that does nothing to enhance your looks.
summary: Too Wet and Drippy If You Aren't Careful

reviewText: I like using this because it gives my face a nice fresh, non-powdery look. I hate when my face gets that dusty look, I can almost feel how loose and airy the make up is after I use a setting powder foundation. The spray locks it in and gets rid of the powder that might be floating around. Also if you wipe your face, the spray will help keep it from transferring. I do not use the 4-6 sprays like it suggests, i use 2-3 and my face feels pretty good with that. I use it everyday to keep my makeup looking fresh and not heavy!
I like this product because you spray it on your face and it sets your makeup.  It makes it stay solidly.
summary: I like this product because you spray it on your face ...

reviewText: Very nice. I tried this on half my face and used my current fav setting spray (Kat Von D Lock-It Makeup Setting Mist - 1oz/30ml )on the other side. By the end of the night, I could not tell a difference. I do prefer the finer mist that I get with the Kat Von D spray, but this one is pretty close in that respect as well. They are comparable in price, but this is definitely a solid setting spray. It extended the wear of my makeup (an essential with my oily skin) and took down the powdery look from my other products.
summary: Works as well as Kat Von D Setting Mist!

reviewText:
This setting spray works really well.  I had previously used Urban Decay spray and this is just as good.  It keeps my makeup looking fresh for the entire day and even into the evening.

I have also purchased the L'Oral Pro-Spray and I will eat my hat if this isn't an exact dupe of that product.  They even come in the same bottle.

Maybe setting sprays are not for me. I tried this over my regular (not dermablend) foundation, and while I found it unpleasant to spray something at my own face, I will say it did seem to make my makeup a bit smoother. Just hold your breath, because this is sort of smelly-like chemical smelly. I had to spray a cloud of perfume to cope.
While initially my makeup looked good, after a grueling day of sitting at a desk with a desk fan, my make up was coming off just as usual. I do have oily skin, so that could be a major reason why. Perhaps if it were drier this would have stayed.
I think I'll stick with the powder setting stuff for now, as I can easily reapply it at work and it doesn't smell weird.

Must say~ Best Part of this is the sprayer!!

It covers your whole face in a perfect mist!
No drips, drizzles, or concentration to one area of your face.
Four sprays thorughly covers your whole face.

I live in a year round warm climate & work outside.
So sweat is a given and setting spray is my only hope of concealer lasting past lunch.

I've used all setting sprays from NYX to Urban Decay.
All perfectly respectable products.

This Dermablend spray is in a category on its own.
It's the only one that I can feel a soft, yet tacky finish, implying it may actually last & it does.
You can only feel this by touching your face.
In no way will you notice it moving your face.

Most setting sprays I've tried seem to do more to set the finishing powder into your skin for a natural look.
While they extend the length of coverage, it's rarely all day when I'm working outside.

The Dermablend actually made my make up AND my skin look better!
The highlights & contours ebbed & flowed as I had been effortlessly airbrushed.

This is a steal at this price point!!

*QUICK TIP*
Apply mascara as last step in routine.
Spray before mascara.
Will give mascara a primer type base & help thicken your lashes.
As well, mascara won't smudge to if you spray after.

Hope this helps & as always feel free to ask any questions

Do not like this at all. Worst makeup spray I've tried and it could all be fixed by making it an aerosol. The problem is it's TOO liquidy. It leaked all over the lid and when I pulled the lid off, this stuff went everywhere. So there's shipping issues they need to fix. And then I went to spray it on my face, following the instructions, 8 inches away, and it shot giant blobs of liquid all over my face. That doesn't help my makeup; it ruins it.

I've tried a makeup spray before and it was an aerosol and sprayed over my face thinly and evenly. This does not.
summary: Do not like this at all

reviewText: I typically use L'Oreal Paris Cosmetics Infallible Pro-Spray and Makeup Extender, Setting Spray and this bottle feels exactly the same. The Dermablend version definitely looks as though it lasts all day, even through a nap. Could be the spray or the Dermablend Blurring Mousse Foundation I use underneath so I will continue using them together!
summary: Setting Spray with Foundation Lasts All Day!

reviewText: This gives you that extra little something that keeps your make up on a special on these hot humid months of summer. Just spray a couple of spritzes and it keeps everything in place a lot longer than you would expect. Dermablend makes great products and this is no exception
summary: Dermablend makes great products and this is no

reviewText: I applied my make up and sprayed this on top to set it. It dried very quickly. It felt a little on the sticky side to me. But it really did the job. The only negative is the perfume they put in there. It works but it's kinda sticky and has perfume smell.

I've tried the Evian and Vichy type of this setting spray.  This by far outdoes them.  I don't wear much makeup in the summer here in Georgia thanks to the heat, humidity and the fact I don't have to work since I'm a teacher.  I do apply powder when I go to church.  This helped set the powder but it made my mascara run a bit.  I use waterproof Great Lash.

This pink cream applies smoothly and leaves skin feeling soft. Designed to firm and enhance the  dcollet and bust, it is formulated with encapsulated caffeine, Shea butter, coconut oil, hibiscus flower and something called "adopofillin complex". the user is directed to massage in an upward motion fro 20-30 seconds from the base of the breasts to the collarbone. Recommended usage is twice a day.

I find this cream pleasant to use. It has a light somewhat soapy, herbaceous scent. I'm not crazy about the fragrance but it is mild and dissipates quickly. It does leave skin feeling smooth and soft and imparts a slight sheen. I have yet to finish the container so it is too early to tell whether it delivers on tightening and enhancing. I can't say I notice anything other than a slight sheen. But it is easy and enjoyable to use and this oft neglected area is certainly entitled to a bit of pampering.

Usually I LOL at the directions for the Bliss products, like do 50 squats after putting lotion on thighs.  It kind of reminds us old people of Carters little Liver pills.  Werent the directions to take with 8 glasses of water?

HOWEVER, this time I wasn't messing around or laughing at directions.  I have noticed that my 53 year-old skin is a little wrinkly in some places.  (We shall never speak of this again.)  It isn't that it is wrinkly but it looks dry and drinks up lotion like water in sand.  My skin sucked up this lotion while it was changing right in front of my eyes.

I am running off to see what other places I can put this.
summary: I have never seen instant results before this little jar

reviewText:
This product claims "Our active complex works to make skin firmer and more toned with use over time, while skin is tighter, smoother, and more glowing with just the first use".

Really? One use. I think not. I've now used this three day's in a row and while I love the consistency and that there is no real detectable smell and it's thick and luxurious, after one use...my skin looks exactly the same way.  I'll be back in a few weeks to report updates.

When it comes to bliss products, I'm on the fence. Some of them, like their face and body washes, are really nice. Others, like their toning and cellulite creams are gimmicky. And still others like their body lotions and face creams/lotions are hit and miss. I do love the bliss Soapy Suds and Body Butter (in grapefruit) and their Aloe Leaf + Peppermint Foot Patrol (unbelievable after a long day on your feet!!!), so I thought I would give this a try. I do have sensitive skin, and I have had some reactions to bliss products in the past, but I suppose it's due to each formulation. I always do a patch test first to see if things will go south or not. The patch test I did with this did okay, so I liberally applied this to my neck, chest, and the 'girls' as the directions tell you to.

The lotion itself is a pretty shade of light pink and it feels soooo silky smooth going on. There is a fragrance, but it is very, very light and pretty pleasant. You can definitely wear this with perfume and not have it overpower that scent. When applied it absorbs pretty quickly and doesn't leave behind a greasy feel. It also doesn't develop a sticky texture as you are applying it, like some lotions do. I'm not sure if that's from the water content in them being absorbed faster than the rest of the ingredients, but I was happy that this lotion didn't do that. I've been using this for a little over a week and am about 1/4 of the way through the jar. I'm bummed that it goes so quickly, as this lotion is pricey. It moisturizes quite well, but $45 is still a steep price to pay. This is one of those times when the product actually FEELS as expensive as it is.  One thing to watch out for - if you happen to apply this and not wash your hands afterwards, the taste of the lotion can transfer to food even if your hands are dry. I applied and went for an apple about 20 minutes later, and my first bite tasted like this lotion. Yuck. I had to brush my teeth and tongue to get the taste to go away.

As an aside, this would make a great lotion to use when doing monthly SBEs. Because it is so silky and absorbs evenly, it allows your fingers to evenly move across your skin without tugging or sticking, which is important when performing these exams. Using a good lotion is a trick my ob/gyn suggested because it makes these exams easier, and it also keeps that delicate skin moisturized, which is also important. Some cancer causes the skin to dimple, flake, itch, crack, or turn red and these are also things that can happen with dry skin. So it's VERY important to keep your chest and breast skin properly cared for.
summary: Delivers soft, silky skin but dries out your wallet

reviewText: I had never heard of this product, but the name gave me a good giggle.  Leave it to Cleavage, a spoof on "Leave it to Beaver," the main character being Beaver Cleaver during the show's 1957 - 1963 run was clever.  Baby Boomers to Millenials alike will have a giggle over the name of this product.  On a serious note, if you want to tighten up your neck and bosom area, then you want this product.  It is gentle; has no odor and glides onto your skin smoothly.  I highly recommend!

I am familiar with Bliss products both from our local spa and from using their great Body Butter. The Body Butter is the greatest for adding moisture to really dry skin, but not for getting rid of wrinkles, creases or crepiness. This Bliss fabgirl leave it to cleavage says you'll notice a difference in one day.

To see if there is a difference in only one day, I applied the cream on one half of my chest, up to the neck following their directions. The next morning, I did not see any difference, but I did feel a difference. My skin felt way smoother, silkier and tighter, but the creases were still there. So, I used it again every night and on the fourth night, when I went to apply the cream, there was a noticeable difference on the deepest creases.

I was very impressed that in only three applications, the deepest creases on my upper chest were actually less deep. Since then, I have applied it for a full week and I do see a visible difference in the really deep crease lines. They not only look less deep, but my skin feels silky smooth. I see no difference in any wrinkles or crepiness, only in the deep chest creases. The cream itself is silky light, not greasy with a slight perfume smell. I will be using this every night, as lessening deep creases is a huge nice improvement, but I have yet to find anything that helps get rid of the crepe skin in the upper chest /neck area, that I had been hoping for.

bliss Leave it to cleavage sounded like a good match for me.  I'm 40 and while I don't feel the need for much in the way of skin firming products, I figured it's never too early (and probably for me a little late) to feel better about oneself, especially one's more prominent physical assets, particularly a chest that has been through misguided support (or lack there of, for most of my teen years), breastfeeding, a surgery (a large biopsy in my teens, thankfully I was left with just the memory and only a small scar), sun exposure (I wear mostly v-necks), and time.

I have used bliss products before and found them somewhat effective and enjoyable to use (fatgirl sleep is my fix for ankle swelling after a long day).  I do have sensitive skin, but usually my face reacts and I could put anything in the rest of me without ill effect.

Leave it to cleavage is the exception, it seems.  It is lightly fragranced (smells like a lightweight powdery, Love's Baby Soft) and on the skin, the fragrance disperses quickly, becoming indiscernible from other products I use, and not enough fragrance to clash with my signature fragrance.

The feel is light and silky and it spreads easily and does not feel like a cream, and it feels more slippery than your average lotion.

Half an hour after application, my joy ended as I started to itch and my chest was vividly red.  Thankfully a quick wash and some hydrocortisone calmed things down immediately.

Not a good match for me, but hopefully bliss has something up their sleeve for folks like me who need the extra care, and who enjoy a taste of luxury in their day, but also need things extra gentle.
summary: Feels and smells fantastic but not for my sensitive skin

reviewText: I used this cream twice daily as directed and it does leave your skin silky soft with a smoother appearance. Just don't expect a breast lift from its use! It is a pink cream that absorbs quickly into the skin and leaves no residue behind. I however couldn't stand the smell, felt it was too strong, specially when it's so close to your nose.
summary: Scent may be to strong for some

reviewText: This new cleavage lotion from bliss is smooth and creamy. It feels like applying buttered sour cream. However, it was overpriced in my opinion at $45 (current MSRP).
summary: It feels like applying buttered sour cream

reviewText: Relatively mild scent that dissipates pretty quickly. It feels rich and smooth on the skin, and definitely feels like a higher end cream. However, this tub will only last about 3 weeks if used on a daily basis - it's small! It leaves a subtle sheen but doesn't seem to have changed the texture of my skin. It might be more effective if skin is more wrinkly.

This is a lightweight souffle cream, a very light pink color with a sweet, very pink scent.  The scent is very clean and pleasant.  The instructions say to apply this cream to chest up to the neckline twice a day.  I'm not sure what makes it cleavage appropriate -- I'm sure it would work just fine on other expanses of skin.  Curiously, the container explicitly states that this product is not for fat or weight loss.  I did not detect any shimmer in the product.  If there is shimmer, it's quite subtle.
summary: heavenly sweet scent in a lightweight cream.

reviewText: the consistancy of hand lotion. has a strong perfumy smell. this light pink colored cream, a little goes a very long ways. put it all the way up to your collar bone. I got it because in the summer I get really red above my breast area. I used it today on it, and i can see a slight difference and it does not burn the area. i think over time this would be really nice.

I cant say this is the most important and essential beauty product Ive ever used, but it is quite a treat nevertheless. If you start with the premise that anything called Leave it to Cleavage cant be bad, youll be in just the right mindset to enjoy the experience.

What you get is a generous sized tub of pink, floral scented, whipped textured crme, which Bliss calls a souffl. You are to apply the souffl in upward massaging strokes for 20-30 seconds twice a day. There is nothing arduous about this, the experience is quite pleasant. You know full well that you will not begin to look like a 20 year old Anita Ekberg or Sophia Lauren, but for some reason, thats quite OK. Every little bit helps.

The souffl contains encapsulated caffeine and adopofilin complex, coconut oil, shea butter, and hibiscus flower extract. There is a tiny bit of pearlescence. The promise is to firm and tone while leaving the skin smooth and lustrous. There is a temporary firming effect caused by the caffeine, the other ingredients are very good moisturizers.

Things do appear improved. I'll take it.
summary: Hope in a Jar, Cleavage Edition

reviewText:
I have always been a fan of Bliss products, and especially the FatGirl products. FatGirl Sleep is hands down my all time favorite body product and totally worth the splurge fyi. Now, this cleavage cream is nice too.

It is not a miracle product and it won't make any permanent changes, but while you're using it, you do see some improvements.

If you have had kids, breastfed, just have "aging" cleavage, or all of the above like me, this product helps the appearance and eliminates (temporarily) the crepe-y look of the skin on the breasts.

The tiny little crinkles and tissue paper look that the skin can have is smoothed out and softened. The tiny white stretch marks are less noticeable and do not look as wrinkly.

There's no residue, not sticky or tackiness. Once the cream is absorbed the skin feels satiny smooth and soft.

This is a scented product and it smells really good to me. It smells like a high end facial cream.

The jar is filled to the tippy top and you do not even need to use a whole lot, so it should last a while. I can put a moderate dab on each breast and rub it in, all around, and then also spread some up my chest to the center of my collarbone. The collarbone area there at the neck also tends to get a little wrinkly looking as we age and due to sun exposure etc.,.. this product makes that area look nicer, too. I am starting to nice the leathery skin issue in this area due to so much time in the sun. This cream really softens it up and makes it pretty much unnoticeable.

Overall I think it is a nice product. It does what it says and is one of those things that is worth the splurge to help you feel a little better about yourself and maybe look a little "improved" for special occasions etc. It is something else that I will be adding to my favorites list and use/buy regularly. Although I probably wouldn't use it every single day since no one really sees my cleavage on a daily basis, I think it is just a nice, pampering, feel good product to have and use when desired. I am a sucker for lavish scents in my beauty and body products, so this one lures me in with that as well.

This is a great facial brush. When compared to a Clarisonic I had, this one is twice as cheap and does just as good a job. I especially love that it's on the the smaller side but the facial brush is pretty large so it covers larger areas quickly. I use it both on my face, neck, and chest and noticed considerably smoother skin within just a week. Another big plus compared to the Clarisonic is that the replacement brushes are a lot cheaper.

I have been using this cleaning brush for a month and I love it.  It looks nice, the blue and flowers are so pretty, yet it is light and easy to use too.  I feel like it is really deep cleaning, not damaging my skin.  It is is to charge up and after you are done using it, it rinses clean easily too.

When sonic toothbrushes first came out, I was among the first to race out to buy one.
Later, when the first sonic skin care brush appeared on the market I broke my piggy bank in order to get one of those as well.
This offering from Michael Todd is a true sonic device, as opposed to a rotary brush.
It is truly beautiful, and will look nice as it patiently waits for you to use it.
Like most similar devices, you can take it into the shower without any fear of damage.
The only drawback, in my opinion, is that when you're using it on your face and the beeper that indicates that it's time to move to a different area goes off, make sure you aren't by your ear. It is LOUD.

I also have the full size Michael Todd device. The big difference is that it comes with an extension handle so that you can use it on your back, or anywhere else that you can't reach.
No matter which one you choose, you can't go wrong. Pores look smaller when they're cleaner, and nothing cleans better than a sonic device.
It also helps to save money on expensive facial cleansers, because when using one of these a little drop of cleanser is all you need. The sonic action activates any cleanser.

Does NOT come with USB wall adapter.

Straight out of the box the first thing I noticed was how cute The Soniclear Petite really Is. I really like the bright, vibrant colors. Plus it doesn't show water spots like many others do.
It's recommended that the unit be charged for 24 hours prior to the first use  -  Okay. With a full charge I've used it for 133minutes. Which is 13 minutes more than the stated 2 hour charge. (Also, Soniclear's nearest competitor, Clarisonic's petite unit has a mere 26 minutes on full charge.)
There's 3 speeds available: On Low the bottom indicator light is illuminated. On Medium the top indicator light is illuminated. On High both indicator lights are illuminated. Days I wear heavy make-up I use the High setting except in sensitive areas. The unit "beeps" while in use, to signal it's time to change the area of the face being cleaned. (I must admit I didn't listen for, nor wait for the alert -- I just cleaned my face.)
There's no real protocol I just had to use it and figure out what works best for me, my skin type and my personal regiment. I really like the pulsating motion much better than the customary swirling with other units. It feels good on my face (I mean really good) and I can see how well it's cleaning. I took an alcohol soaked cotton ball and wiped my face after using the Petite - amazingly there was barely anything on the cotton ball. It's easy to hold. It's not cumbersome or awkward in any way. It's pretty and looks nice on the counter. And there's an assortment of colors to choose from.

The "Base," is a different story. I do not like the white base. It looks mismatched, out-of-place, and unattractive. (IMO: The base really needs to be redesigned to match the unit.) And bending the USB cord to fit in the bottom slot is already showing a crease. In time the pressure will cause the cord to fail. The USB cord magnetically attaches to the unit and it IS colored to match. There's a clear plastic brush cap included. This helps keep the brush dust free between uses.

I really like the Petite. It does a great job cleaning, looks nice sitting out, and is nearly 1/2 the price of comparable units. I have no problem recommending the Petite to others.

*The manufacturer recommends changing brushes twice a year. Replacements are $25. This is something to consider when purchasing any electronic brush system. *Does NOT include wall adapter.

I have heard all the hype about the Clarisonic cleansing brushes, but I did not want to shell out $100+ for a tool to wash my face. When I got the opportunity to review this product, which is a less-expensive copycat of the Clarisonic, I decided to give it a try. First of all, be aware that you have to charge this for 24 hours before using. In actuality, the blinking "charge" lights went out after about 12 hours, so it was probably fine then but I gave it the full 24 to be fair. It's not intuitive how to connect the charger (it's magnetic), so I had to read the instructions. It's probably a good thing that I read them because there is a warning not to unplug the charger before disconnecting it from the brush, because the battery can discharge and then you would have to start over again. When I finally got to use this product, I was not impressed at all. The brush is very soft (a good thing) but it vibrates (as opposed to spinning) and it just made my head vibrate and feel uncomfortable. It actually felt like a mild electric shock. There is a vibrating timer on the brush that tells you to move to a new area, but based on this timing it would take about 45 minutes to wash my entire face. When I moved the brush to my nose, I felt actual pain (I broke my nose a few years ago and had a surgical repair, but have never felt pain after the initial healing until I used this brush). I tried to give it to my teenage daughter, but she has sensitive, acne-prone skin and didn't want to risk using this product. Maybe I'll use it to clean my shower.
summary: Horrible vibration feels like a milk electric shock; not for anyone with a broken nose either

reviewText: As a guy, I haven't ;used facial massagers.  However now that I'm a senior citizen, I find my facial skin sometimes feels oily and this massager definitely makes it look and feel better.  Of course the looks of ;it are exclusively feminine, but then nobody sees it except me, so that's okay.

This handy device lives up to its promises. It's small enough to fit comfortably into any hand, doesn't mind the water, and cleans thoroughly without making a mess of itself. I own a Clarisonic that I never use because digging out all the grime was disgusting, and not cleaning it was worse. Not a problem with the Soniclear Petite.

Right now, there don't seem to be a lot of heads for this model, whereas Clarisonic offers a few, plus there's a healthy after-market in replacement heads. That's an issue, though a small one, which doesn't prevent me from preferring the Soniclear to the Mia.

This is really a nice face massager, very heavy duty looking and love the colors. There are a lot of do's and do not's in the instruction booklet, some worth mentioning on here so you are aware of them before you buy. Some are just downright funny, like the first one.
1. Do not store your charger near water. Ok, the massager itself can be submerged but the charger can't. I understand that but since it can only be charged by your computer, this just cracks me up. How many people have their computer tower near water??? The charging cord is about 32" by the way. That is my only gripe with this device. The only way to charge it is on your computer. Why in the world didn't they do it for an outlet since it is a bathroom item....well, unless they didn't want it near water when it was charging which makes me wonder just how powerful it is. Since one of the rules is also to not have it near aerosol products or flames. Ok, maybe it is a good idea it has to be charged on a computer. I'm starting to get worried about what could happen in the bathroom with it!
2.  Do not use or have nearby if you have medical devices like a pacemaker.  Keep it away from cd's, tapes, credit cards, magnetic devices. Uh, oh. I just realized my credit card was laying right beside it! Since it's near my computer, so is my cd's and tapes.
3. Do not use near eyes....trust me you can't stand it and won't do it after the first time. Your eyeballs feel like they are going to pop out of there. Ok, I just had to try it once to see what happened. The pulsating motion is pretty heavy and I only used the lowest setting, there are 3 settings by the way.
4. Do not use while you are drowsy or half asleep. Well, that would be hard to do since it gives a loud beep every 20 seconds to wake you up. Oh, wait, that is to tell you to move it to another section of your face.

A man must have written these instructions and think we women need better instructions than they include in a smart watch booklet!

This comes with a brush that can be changed out. A new brush runs around $25 which I found rather disturbing and worrisome. I have been using a little cheap facial massager and the brush rotates but doesn't pulsate. This one doesn't move but just pulsates. I wish it brushed too. Supposedly those little brushes can scratch your face which I hadn't noticed before but it's possible, I guess. For $25, this one better not do any scratching. It needs to be cleaned after each use. Since I can't stand the thought of getting make up on it, I clean with the cheaper brush (since those are cheap to buy) and use this one afterwards. I couldn't figure out what the big deal was on the pulsating until I researched it. Evidently the biggest plus is it gets the blood moving and helps control wrinkles and puffiness under the eyes and even those little stray hairs. I have a problem with all of those so fully intend to keep pulsating! Wonder why they don't make a mask with eye holes you can just put over your face and pulsate everything at once. It would sure save time. Every 20 seconds a buzzer goes off and you are supposed to move it to another spot. Since the brush isn't all that big (1 1/2"), you are moving it a lot. It turns itself off after 5 or 6 moves (thinking you are done and forgot it or fell asleep maybe???). Anyway, it's a good idea to have some soap on the brush because it's supposed to also be cleaning (even though it's not rotating) and it might scratch your face without the liquid. This brush is also supposed to be antimicrobial protected against bacteria getting into it.

Upon arrival you are supposed to charge it although mine came with a little charge.  Charge it by the computer for 24 hours and it will last at least 2 hours. It beeps twice when you first put in cradle to let you know it's charging. The lights turn solid and stay lit when it's fully charged. The charge lasts me for a few days, so it's not as big a deal as I thought having to do it by the computer. There are 20 pages of information for you to read and it might be a good idea to glance through it.

It's nice and durable and I think it will last a long time.

This is a nice, multi-speed, rechargeable facial cleaner.  It does not come with extra brushes  :( , but I am happy with the one it comes with.  It is small and therefore does not take up a lot of vanity space and easy to pack.  The battery needs to be charged 24 hours before first use, and should not be left plugged in all the time.  There is no electrical plug included.  When fully charged you get about 1 1/2 to 2 hours of use, it's hard to tell because you would never use it for 2 hours straight.
My face felt so soft and clean after use.
My concern is with the price...it's quite high for my budget.
summary: My face felt so soft and clean after use... very nice rechargeable, multi-speed facial cleanser

reviewText: This is charged with a USB cord so that is very modern. It is very pretty. It does the job. It is subtle but it does the job fingers and hands cannot. It has a light when you turn it on in the bristles. And there is a light to tell it is charging. I really like that the makers made this very pretty. It is sleek in the hand -- just the right size. I really like it.
summary: Just the right size for the hand and plus it is pretty

reviewText:
My wife has been using the standard rotating facial brush for years. Thus we were hopeful when getting our hands on this option.

+ Different colors and patterns to choose from.
Not that it really matters since nobody but the owner will ever see this device

-- Instructions for battery charging are very specific and makes one think they are using really old technology for this battery.
Instructions include things like:
1. Must charge at least 24hrs before first use
2. Don't leave plugged in
3. When it's time to charge again, charge for 8 to 12 hrs. "Hours", it says!
4. After recharging for 12hrs you may get 2hrs of use before having to charge again

+ Interestingly, this uses a magnet on the end of your USB cable to connect to device and charge.

-- USB charging provided, but most bathrooms do NOT have USB for charging. It would have been nice to have been provided an AC Adapter...especially for the cost.

+ If you want to use the stand when not in use, you can place the handle down into the stand and charge at the same time.
The USB cable feeds through the bottom and hangs loose when not charging.

> Two red LEDs that are supposed to communicate to you lots of different things.
For example, wife wishes the LEDs would turn green when device is fully charged, but it only has red.

+ My wife prefers to keep this on high speed for every use. She doesn't find a use to slow it down for any reason. She's just glad it has the high speed setting.

+ My wife really, really likes the way it cleans and how it makes her skin feel afterward.

+ There are beeps to let you know when to a different zone on your face.
My wife ignores these and just works it all around for a couple of minutes. This works fine for her, though I can see how some would like the sound indicator to move to a new zone.

-- I found 3 or 4 sonic + pulsing brush competitor products, with positive reviews, in the $35 to $40 price range.
Not liking that this is twice the cost AND the other products sometimes give extra brushes...this does not give you anything extra.

> Replacement brushes average $25 and they recommend you change that every six months.
Hmmm. Probably not going to happen but once every couple of years. . .depending how the brushes hold out.

OVERALL:
Battery and price are questionable.
Otherwise, my wife is glad she switched from rotating brush to this pulsing, sonic brush.
summary: Probably a 3.5 star rating due to battery and price issues

reviewText:
You need to charge this before using it.  Which leads me to the charger.  It is a USB cord but the Soniclear does not come with a wall charger/wall wart   it really should.  But you may have extras around your house - I do.  So I used one of those to plug the USB in to an outlet.

The charger makes a magnetic connection at the front of the handle.  I actually like these connectors & have it on other devices.  This unit comes with a stand that holds the magnetic connector/charger in place, you fish the cord thru the stand & out the bottom.  I like this too because it gives me a simple place to store the Soniclear & allows it to air dry & charge at the same time.  Just takes a couple minutes to set up correctly.  After that, you just use it, clean it, wipe it dry & put back in the stand.

Yes, its pretty ;)  but how well does it clean compared to the other more famous brand?  I own 2 versions of the other brand.  This is similar but not quite as thorough IMO.  Thats not to say this one is not good  it is quite good.  My skin feels clean & exfoliated.  If the other brand is too much for your skin, this may be better.

-It has 3 speeds.  I just leave it at the high speed.
-It has a timer that beeps to let you know you should move to another area.  I don't really care for the beeping but some people may like this.
-The handle is comfortable  not too big, not too small.
-It comes with 1 brush.  I like this brush  its not too stiff or too soft.  It may be too much if you have sensitive skin.
-It is waterproof & can be used in the shower.  I would not store it in the shower  thats a recipe for ick!  Keep it on your counter so the brush can dry.  And clean the brush really well after every use.
-The brushes are antimicrobial.  This does NOT mean you don't have to clean them well.
-Has a 3 year warranty.

I have had a Clarisonic Mia 1 for year and really like it. This brush comes with 3 speeds which meant less to me than I thought it would. Flower graphics are cheerful. This cleans well at any of the speeds. I found the "time to move on" beeps annoying. Overall, functional for me.

I don't really like the charging stand. You need to snake the charging element through the stand and force the cord through a channel at the bottom. I've owned this less than a day and already the cord is fraying from the too tight channel. The stand is also a bit wobbly. I had to buy a tap/plug for this since it only comes with a USB end for charging. I think that is annoying.

Overall it works fine, it would be 5 stars except for my misgivings about the charge cord and stand.
summary: Works fine but needs a tap to plug in, not just a USB. Charging stand wobbly.

reviewText: This pretty facial cleansing brush looks like the ones that whirl cleansing cream around on your face, but several things make it different. First, it isn't just water resistant like most. It has no charging openings on the handle at all, so it's completely waterproof. This means you can use in the shower in the morning. Because of this, the charging method is different. The charging cable plugs into a USB socket instead of an electrical socket. It takes 24 hours to charge before its first use (red lights on the handle blink while it is charging and turn solid red when it is ready). The charger pod at the end of the cable clings magnetically to the flowered handle. A plastic cradle is provided for charging, but I found its design a little awkward. It was easier to charge the device without it, for me. Once charged, it will run about two hours, but it takes only about 3 to five minutes to do your face, at the most, so you can use it a long time between charges. It doesn't whirl around. It vibrates. It feels terrific and leaves your skin almost miraculously smooth and clean. The company plans to make additional accessories, and I look forward to seeing what they offer, but I'm really happy with this great cleansing brush. (It looks very pretty on the counter too. I have an ocean-themed bathroom, but these colors fit right in.)
summary: Pretty, Powerful, and Practical Facial Cleansing

reviewText: Not sure this does anything. Not powerful and has an annoying usb charger.

I love my Clarisonic Pro, but at 8 5/8 oz. - including a brush head - and measuring roughly 7 1/2" long and 3 1/4" high, it was a bit larger than desirable for travel.  The "Clarisonic Mia FIT, Sonic Facial Cleansing Brush System - 2 Speeds for Gentle and Invigorating Cleansing" was exactly what I needed.  It is about 5 3/4 oz., including a brush head, and measures roughly 2 1/2" X 2 1/2" X 2 1/2" without the brush head.  It charged the first time in less than twelve hours and the charge lasted through a two week vacation, using the Clarisonic twice a day.  I used the faster speed the entire time and felt it cleansed my skin extremely well.  While I took the charger with me, I did not need to use it and will probably leave it at home the next time I travel.  Further, my skin stayed much clearer than it has in the past.  My only regret is that this unit does not come with a carrying container, but that is not a significant negative.
summary: Compact, Portable and Powerful ...  Excellent for Travel ...

reviewText: The unit is hard to turn on.  I have some minor arthritis so I thought that might be the issue and asked two other women to try to turn it on and they found it a bit difficult too. It does fine cleaning my sensitive "T" zone, which is great.  It also requires less facial cleanser when using it.  It does not hold a decent charge, however.  I thought this was a name I could trust but I found both positive and negative results.  I am frustrated with the charging defect.
summary: It does fine cleaning my sensitive "T" zone

reviewText:
Ive been a loyal Clarisonic user for nearly 4 years.  I started with the Mia 2 and over the years have been lucky enough to own the Clarisonic Smart Profile, Opal and now the Mia FIT.  I was very excited to try this because I LOVE the brands products and am always curious whether a newer model is better than what Im already using.

In case you're new to Clarisonic or unfamiliar with their face brushes, the big selling point is that they are more effective at cleaning your skin than cleanser and hands alone and that the brushes also help with exfoliation.  Without a lab or testing methods of my own its hard to truly prove out that claim, but I can say that I used to be someone with troubled acne-prone skin and its been well managed over the past few years with a routine that includes the Clarisonic.  (Though its hard to 100% attribute it to the Clarisonic since I do, understandably have many other products in my routine and since my acne is hormonal its very likely there have been some shifts in my cycle/hormone levels over the years.)  Every Clarisonic facial brush (this one included) has left my skin feeling very clean and soft.  Having also tried other knockoff versions I can also say that Clarisonic just FEELS better  the device itself feels more premium and substantial and the brushes feel more pleasant on your skin (and represent a larger range for a variety of skin types and concerns).  And I also appreciate their longevity  my first Mia 2 is still going strong and although the charging cord for my Opal had some issues it was replaced at no cost by the manufacturer slightly before the 2 year warranty.

Already convinced that Clarisonic brand makes the best facial cleaning brushes, I was curious how this model would compare to other models I had tried.  From a functionality perspective, this seems very similar to the Mia 2.  Both have two cleaning settings  Delicate and Power/Universal, depending on the model.  According to the website, the two settings with the Mia FIT are new (and very gentle) vs. older models, but personally I cant tell the difference.  The biggest difference I can notice seems to be that the Mia Fit is more compact and sits upright on its own.  Because of this difference it feels a little different in your hand.  Of all 3 models I own, I personally think the Mia 2 feels the most natural and ergonomic in my petite hands.  However, I imagine this is largely a matter of personal preference.  If this is something you're concerned about it could be worth a trip to a beauty store where you can handle all the devices in person, like Sephora, to do research before buying.

The big advantage of the compact design is that its more space-friendly if you take your Clarisonic on the go  either traveling or to the gym.  I didn't necessarily find the size of the Mia 2 to be an impediment, but the Smart Profile is definitely bigger than I would like for travel.  I think part of what makes this more suitable for travel is the shape, being a more uniform overall size vs. curved which does tend to pack better when you're squeezing it in a toiletries bag with other items.

I also really like the new radiance brush head.  When I first got my Clarisonic I found that the brush heads were a bit more abrasive, and as such I only used them every other day or 2x a week with my dry skin.  But the brushes have become a lot more plush over time so you can use them more regularly.

Overall, Im a huge fan of this device.  I still think the Smart Profile is my favorite since it is the most multi-purpose for face and body cleaning, BUT as someone who travels a lot this gets used the most since I don't hesitate to throw it in my gym bag or suitcase.  What model you choose to go with is a largely personal decision depending on how you plan to use it.  More on the go  Mia FIT is a great fit.  Largely at home and on the face  Mia 2 is perfect.  Want to clean your face, body and feat  opt for the Smart Profile.

But no matter what you pick I think they make great products and it is hard to go wrong.
summary: Compact Clarisonic that travels well with all the cleaning power

reviewText:
I had wanted one of these for a long time and I'm so glad I went for it and got one. My skin feels different. It's soft and smooth and I don't even use it every day, just every 3-4 days. I've had it for over a month now and have used up the sample product that came with it so I'm just using face wash now and it works just as well with that. I like the radiance brush. I have some others but I keep going back to the one it came with. It seems too soft to get a good clean but once it starts running it works really well.

The whole unit itself is well made but is heavy for its size. It works in the shower under running water or at the sink. It is kind of noisy, my one complaint. It also has a series of pauses in the buzzing when it's on to try to get you to move to another section of your face. I could do without that since I focus on where I tend to breakout rather than go by section with even time for each. It runs at high or low speed but I usually use the higher speed with the radiance brush, low speed for the deep clean type brushes. It charges by sitting on a cradle. Nothing plugs into it. It's not exactly compact for travel with the charging unit but it's so convenient when at home to just set it down and it charges that I don't mind.
So light weight.  Perfect for travel.  Easy to use.
summary: Light weight.  Great for travel.  Easy to use.

reviewText: I'm really surprised how simple this is to use. It's basically one function/speed in 2 different durations. There's a shorter duration for every day use and a longer one for deep cleaning. It can either be charged by USB or with a wall adapter. To charge, it just sets on top of the base without any need to line up contacts. It also keeps nice, clean, and rust free with the contact free charging. It comes with a little bottle cleanser to start but its simple to use your own cleanser if you have a preference or run out. It's also really easy to find the replacement brush heads for this one. There's a cover to keep the brush head clean or travel with. As far as how it feels it's very gentle. I have extremely flaky and sensitive skin. It wasn't too rough for me and left my skin feeling a lot more soft with the gentle exfoliation. After using it, the brush head was easy to rinse clean for next time.
summary: Incredibly Simple to Use, Gentle Enough for My Skin

reviewText: I had an older model that I really liked for years. I thought I'd upgrade. This newer version just seems to kind of vibrate. Nothing really gets scrubbed. Maybe the brush head is too soft and I just need a coarser one. Going to experiment a bit, but I'm pretty disappointed.

Prior to the Mia FIT I was using the Mia 2.

To be honest, they are both basically the same thing.  They have very similar features - both have two speeds, both charge with a magnet style cord, both have a timer on the cleansing.  The main feature change is the style of the device, which now fits in your palm like an egg vs a paddle style design.  It's really an ergonomics thing and I do seem to prefer cleansing with the FIT - I feel like I get a better gauge of things and it's more comfortable.

If you have the Mia 2 and aren't looking to splurge there really honestly isn't anything that I honestly feel is worth upgrading over to the new device.  However if you don't have either one and are looking to get a new one, I highly recommend the FIT.  If possible, the best idea is to go to someplace like Ulta and see which feels best in your hand before giving it a go and then going from there.

I do really enjoy the cleanser that comes with the MIA and already purchased a full sized version.
summary: Great cleanser, not worth the upgrade from Mia 2

reviewText:
The Mia FIT by Clairsonic is a handy little compact device that makes your skin look & feel wonderful!  This was my first time trying a Clairsonic system, & I'm very happy with it. Here's what I love- first, & most important, my skin looks brighter & better than it's been in years. I tend to have dry skin & have had trouble with breakouts, but after using this for over a month, my breakouts have noticeably less. Other things I love about it:
- it's light & compact. Convenient to travel with & doesn't take up a lot of space on my counter.
- Easy to use. Has 2 speeds- push a button to change between the 2.
- USB plug can plug into my computer to charge. That is handy when traveling & a unique feature.
- When using it, the brush is soft & feels great on my face.

When using for the first time, the unit will need to be charged. It says charge for 18 hours at first & that was about how long it took for mine to charge completely.  The system is very easy to use. You just place it on the charger. The unit sits on the charger, & will buzz twice to let you know that it is charging. There is a little faint light on the unit that blinks red while charging, green when fully charged.

I use it in the morning on the #1 setting which is a gentler setting and  #2 setting at night because most of the time I'm removing makeup later in the evening. It makes your face feel fresh & clean.  The only drawback that I could see may be the price, although, when you think about it, if you go for 2 or 3 facials (or maybe even 1, depending on spa/salon), you could easily spend that. This system is an investment in having good skincare year round. I give this an enthusiastic 5 stars, & highly recommend it (especially if you have had issues with breakouts).
summary: Great device for better looking skin

reviewText:
I got this for my wife because she has been experiencing very bad adult acne that only seemed to be getting worse. Since she was the one who needed it, I asked her to explain the results to me so I could write the review. English is not her first language, so I wrote it the way she explained to me. I did put it against my own skin to know how it felt and I put it in a shallow dish of water to convince myself it was indeed generating ultrasonic vibrations. (My wife of 30 years died of ovarian cancer after a long depressing six year battle in 2004. My new wife is considerably younger, but even she can have medical problems.) So the rest of this is in her words except I converted it into fluent English.

I immigrated to the United States from the Philippines in 2013 when I was approaching 25 years old. I never had pimples or facial breakouts until I arrived here. It has become progressively worse this past year and was to the point I desperately needed to do something to solve severe adult acne breakouts that seem to appear at random. I suspect the source of some of my problems must be diet related so I plan to get allergy tests performed. I eat a much more diverse range of foods today that I could never have afforded in my past life.

By the time this Clarisonic Mia Fit arrived five weeks ago, I was at a crisis stage with very bad acne on my cheeks, forehead and chin. I got off to a bad start when I used the sample facial cleanser that was included. One side of my face turned a bright red like a rash. I probably incorrectly associated it with the sample cleanser and stopped using it immediately. And I lost faith in the entire system for the next three weeks. I went back to my regular routine with a new product called Garnier Skin Active scrub to unclog my pores and clear my complexion.

It wasn't really working that well, so I began to use this Clarisonic Mia Fit again and continued with the Garnier Skin Scrub. And it really started to make a visible and undeniable improvement. It has to be the result of this sonic cleanser brush.

Currently Im on a ten day trip and now I fully appreciate how portable and compact this rechargeable ultrasonic cleaner is. It takes up very little space in my carryon luggage.  Its been a week so far and the battery still performs without any noticeable decline in intensity. Thats good because I forgot to bring the charger.

The cleansing brush is very soft and feels really nice against my skin. I had strong doubts the vibration truly cleaned the pores in my skin, but now Im a firm believer. I have been using it to remove residual makeup after my first pass of soap and water to remove the majority of the makeup. It makes the job not only easier, but I can feel this Clarisonic Mia Fit has done a much more thorough job of removing all the makeup. My skin really feels smooth and far cleaner compared to what I was doing.

Obviously, Ill have to update my results as I use the sample and other cleanser products and if I determine if a large part of my problems are diet related. I think it will still take weeks to even months to really get all my skin problems solved, but at least I am confident I now have the tools to regain the good skin complexion I had four years ago.
summary: An Undeniable Improvement in My Adult Acne

reviewText:
I have a Mia 1, and I like it okay. The Mia FIT 2 I like better, though. I like its shape and fit in my hand better, and I really like the timed zones function. That it has two speeds is nice, as well. With the Mia1, I often would skip using it because even with a sensitive skin brush, it was too scouring for my skin. With the FIT, I at least can adjust it.
I don't like the cleanser that comes with either of them. I can't handle most facial cleansers, as my skin is very sensitive, and I don't like fragrances. While pleasant, the fragrance of this cleanser is too strong, and it leaves my skin feeling stripped and tight. So, while that's not a thumbs up for me, the FIT, itself is.  It cleans my skin far better than even a lightly exfoliating cloth, and without the itching that some chemical exfoliants creates.
Four stars is because I've noticed that with the FIT, the charge doesn't last as long as the Mia 1, or the FIT that I received isn't charging well. Maybe it's a fluke, though the light comes on as if it's charging. If I use it soon after, all is fine. If I wait a few hours, it's dead as if it wasn't charged at all.

As someone that has owned a Clarisonic device since the first year that they hit the market, I'm so disappointed in this incarnation.
It could possibly be that I received a demo that was not quite ready for market, because I can't imagine that Clarisonic, a company with a reputation for quality and innovative skin care, would release a subpar device.

The original Clarisonic has an elongated handle with a sculpture stand. The Smart Profile as well as the Mia are designed with an easy to grip  handle.
In order to get the footprint smaller, and perhaps to make it more gender-neutral, the Mia FIT model is more bullet shaped and rests comfortably on its own little disc charger. Not quite as comfortable to hold as you are cleansing your face, but probably not enough to be a deal-breaker.
As with all models, the Mia Fit is waterproof. A big plus to the Clarisonic line is the fact that you can take it in the shower, or rinse it under a running tap, without risking any damage to the unit. In addition, every model that I have owned or used has had a nice long battery life between charges.
Not only does this unit NOT hold a charge as well, there is also a design flaw that women in particular will find more than a little annoying. The button to turn it on must be pressed extremely hard in order to get the unit to operate. I'm not able to do it with my fingertip. It requires the bottom of your toothbrush or tweezers to press the button enough to get it to turn on. I have long and strong almond-shaped fingernails, so I'm able to use my thumb nail to turn it on, but each time one risks getting a broken nail. Yes, it is that difficult.

Over the years, I've also invested quite a bit in brush heads, so this review also needs to cover the brush heads. You might be tempted to buy replacement heads that are not from the Clarisonic company. You can find knockoffs on Amazon, eBay, Woot, and other outlets. If you are really particular about your skin, you might want to rethink getting them from these sources. Part of what you're paying for is the rounded tip on each bristle. That's also why you want to replace the heads periodically. The cheap knock-offs are just like cheap toothbrushes in that the bristles are not shaped for optimal and effective cleaning without damage.

If you've never owned a Clarisonic device before, you're going to be thrilled with how far your  cleansing lotions  or soaps will go when using  one of these. You might be used to using a dollop of cleanser, but on a Clarisonic, you will only need to use a fraction of that dollop .  You'll get the same results as the Sonic action encourages  your cleanser to froth up.
There is one more thing I need to mention that is very important. Your face is not like the kitchen sink. Scrubbing harder does not equal a cleaner surface. When it comes to a Clarisonic and your skin, a light touch is actually much more effective. The bristles and the Sonic action do the work. A light touch allows the bristles to clean each pore more effectively. If you have large pores, a clean pore will always look smaller.
And that, my friend, is why I have used and continue to use Clarisonic devices. I have large pores on my nose, and a Clarisonic is the closest thing to a miracle when it comes to making them look smaller.

 I highly recommend Clarisonic devices, perhaps just not the Mia FIT.

I was a little concerned about using this due to my sensitive skin.  I shouldn't have worried.  I've been using this for weeks now and my skin has never looked better.

Even the higher setting is gentle enough on my skin, but the difference in my skin condition is palpable!

When you first get this out of the box, you'll need to charge it before using it.  It rests on its charger easily and gives you a green light when its ready to go.

I found it easy to select the strength I wanted to use and very easy to use.

Best of all, it feels really good on my skin.  At first I worried that it might be too gentle - it doesn't feel like it's doing much.  But the difference is noticeable right away.  My skin is cleaner and the Mia FIT buffs away those horrid dry bits of winter skin.

I'm now a fan and have added this to my regular routine.  Note that it also comes with a small tube of the Skin Illuminating Cleanser and it's wonderful.  It helps make my skin look so clear and soft!  (Quick note - you can use any cleanser with it!)

I once tried a cheaper ($40) version of this type of device and was pretty unimpressed, as it did absolutely nothing. So I didn't really have high hopes for this Clarisonic, despite all the hype about it. Wrong!

This has two speeds. I tried the lower one first and could barely feel it, so I switched to the higher one. Again, could barely feel it. The whole time I was thinking, "they have got to be kidding"... until I rinsed my face. WOW! It was as smooth as silk. I couldn't believe every rough patch, every flake was gone.

I've continued to use the Mia every day, with my usual cleanser, and my skin looks terrific!  I use prescription Retin-A at night and benzoyl peroxide in the morning and this device has caused ZERO irritation.

This is one of those things that truly lives up to all the hype.

This Clarisonic Mia FIT is the second skin cleansing system Ive had (third if you count washcloth and manual brush), so it hasn't significantly changed my skin, its already in good shape. Like my other brush system, the Clarisonic is a huge time saver. Just about any system will be when compared to scrubbing with a manual brush and washcloth. In those days, I was occasionally too tired to do an adequate job with my hand brush and washcloth. My face paid the price of my laziness and I experienced breakouts long past the normal breakout age. I finally acknowledged that handwashing wasn't cutting it and began using a cleansing system for the first time. The biggest difference between that old system and this new system from Clarisonic, is that the Clarisonic brush doesnt spin. Instead, it has sonic cleaning power. The brush filaments vibrate at high speeds while I draw small circles with the Clarisonic. Even when I feel like Im moving deliberately slowly, the Clarisonic glides, directing the pace. In no more than a minute, it leaves my skin feeling absolutely glowing. Also, the Clarisonic is built differently, more compact, it fits wonderfully in the palm of my hand, providing better control over the pressure I apply. I also realized it is waterproof. Not just water resistant, water proof. No longer confined to over the sink, I can step into the steam shower and luxuriate while using the Clarisonic. Other brushes are available, but Ive had no need to check them out. The included brush was the perfect one to maintain the regime I had already established with the old system. I initially questioned what appeared to be a big difference in price, the Clarisonic costs a lot more than my old system. It didn't take long, using and comparing the Clarisonic to the my old system, to feel the price difference is warranted. If you are looking at skin care systems for yourself or to give another, definately include the Clarisonic in your considerations. From my perspective and experience, its the most advanced in design and the better performer.
summary: Most Powerful, Most Compact, Most Effective

reviewText:
** UPDATE ** 11-25-2017
Worked great, for just about 1 year.  Now the battery will no longer hold a charge at all.  Which is incredibly sad when you are paying so much for a product that works really well.  Honestly this company can't spend a few more cents for a decent battery that will hold up?  My induction rechargeable toothbrush has a better set up; it has lasted for 6 years and is still going strong.  Come on Clarisonic - I am not the only one who has brought this topic up.  There is an entire group of YouTube videos dedicated to detailing how to break into your products in the complicated process solely to swap out the cheap battery for a low cost - high quality battery.
Treat your customers with a little more respect.
===========================================

My wife likes to call this her "little genie".  The bristles are gentle on the skin, yet provide a thorough, deep pore cleansing.  The rotating head vibrates enough to be effecting, but not so fast that it feels like a grinding wheel and the entire package is easy to hold in your palm.  Great for control and being easy to reach all the areas of your face. The motor is powerful and does not get bogged down and the charge lasts a really long time. It has two speeds - one for extra gentle - but she rarely uses this speed.  Plus the entire package is waterproof.  To charge, just rest it in the cradle charger provided.

My wife like to use her preferred cleanser (not a bar of soap). Her recommendation is to keep the brush head clean and dry when not in use.  In other words, don't use it, put it down and just walk away.  Keep the head clean and make sure it dries really well between use.  She sets hers bristle down on a folded sheet of paper towel.  As others have stated, soak it in hydrogen peroxide every few weeks.

Kind of pricey, but well made and certainly worth it.

Cheers!
summary: Gentle power in the palm of your hand.

reviewText:
I was a bit apprehensive before using this. I've always just used a mild cleanser or water, and my skin has always be fairly nice, no major issues, but lately it seems like I'm getting more and more blackheads, so I was ready to try something else.

This brush is so easy to use, and it's amazing the difference it makes. My skin is glowing and it feels so smooth. Most importantly I'm seeing a decrease in blackheads.

-When following the instructions you start with your forehead, which leaves soap and water dripping into your eyes (maybe I overdid it on both?) so I now start with the bottom of my face and work my way up.
-The brush head itself is rather large, making it hard to get the area around your nose. Speaking of nose, that was the hardest part to get since it tickled a lot.
-Don't push too hard or the vibration will stop, that took a little getting used to for me
-It does take up space on my counter to charge, but the charging station is small
summary: and my skin has always be fairly nice, no major issues

reviewText:
Pros:
This device does a great job cleaning my skin.
I love that it can be used in the shower.
It's small and fits nicely in a travel bag.
The included brush head is a very soft premium brush.
The charging stand works very well - I like it better than a Mia 1/2 charger.

Cons:
I'm not crazy about the shape. When using this device, you don't want to press it too close to your face. The handle on the Mia 1 or Mia 2 gives you better control.

Care:
I rinse the head well after each use and let it air dry. The brushes last longer if you gently rinse them well after use and allow them to air dry completely - I leave the plastic cover off them until they're dry.
The directions say you can leave the head on the device for a week, but I remove the brush head when I'm not using it - leaving it on causes mold to grow underneath the head. The device stays much cleaner if you remove the brush each time.

I wasn't sure what I would think of the Clarisonic cleaning system, especially since it seemed like a pricey gimmick, but wow, this works.  Although it looks like the head might spin, it does not and instead the soft brush head vibrates.  You clean your face in a circular motion using either the Clarisonic cleanser (a small sample tube is included) or your favorite facial cleanser.  It's incredlbly easy to use -- except on my nose because the vibrations tickle like heck.  Like a sonic toothbrush, the Mia Fit indicates when it's time to advance to the next area.  Read the directions, since there is a pattern you need to follow if you want to spend the correct time on each section.  (Of course, you can always ignore the vibration alerts and proceed as you want.)  When you're done, you rinse and dry your face -- and do the same to the Mia FIT.  I couldn't believe how polish my face felt after the first time, and I thought maybe it was a fluke.  Nope.  My face looks better than I expected, with a more radiant and smoother feel, even when I use my regular wash.  I always follow with a moisturizer to keep my skin hydrated.

The FIT, um, fits well in my hand.  It's about as tall as my palm. It comes with a charger and a USB cable that plugs into a two-pronged wall charger.  The included cap has holes on the top to let the bristles air dry without being completely exposed.  It's small enough to toss in a weekend bag without your noticing the space it takes.

-- Debbie Lee Wesselmann
summary: I Didn't Think This Would Work This Well

reviewText: I struggled with giving this five stars because of the price. But in the end, I can't argue with success. I have a Beauticontrol facial stick and it retailed for $75. And it did good. I used it twice a week with my Beauticontrol cleanser and I did see results. But this blew that out of the water. On the lighter setting, I used my new favorite cleanser from Dr Denese Hydrating Cleanser 6 Oz Tube Sealed and the first time I used it, there was a noticeable glow. It's sounds gross but I saw dead skin float off when I rinsed and cleaned the head. Baby bottom soft and it didn't aggravate my rosacea. Simple to use and clean. Make sure you clean the head every time you use it and let it air dry. My first head from my first system started to smell like old water before I realized it wasn't air drying completely.

Very soft bristles feel nice on the face. Item is waterproof but the charger cannot be in the water. Gives a nice strong quick vibration to alert you when properly seated in the charger. I do wish the USB came out the side or something of the charger vs the top/bottom. that's awkward if you have limited plugs to work with in your bathroom. The charging base is small and takes up only the footprint of the device itself. The recharging is nice, but i almost wish it was just battery powered so I could keep it wherever and not have yet another thing plugged in on my bathroom sink.

I used to have an Olay version of this (waaaaaaaay cheaper). This one is softer, but also a much bigger brush. That means that I can't use it in areas like my forehead or the sides of my temple without getting my hair all soapy. that's kind of annoying. also, this will need to be part of a several step process if you also need to remove eye makeup, since you can't do that with this device. This one also does have the same "sonic" vibration that my Philips Sonicare does. It's definitely different than the Olay one.

So I compare this to the toothbrush thing (Sonicare vs your standard $5 or $10 electric toothbrush). It is nicer than the standard cheap electric version (softer, chargeable, more effective vibration). But if you don't have the disposable income sitting around for this version, the cheaper one is JUST fine and will accomplish 98% the same thing. If you want to and can splurge, go for it. But don't think you are missing out on much if you can't.

This is a 5 star item, but since the price is just so CRAZY, 3 stars when factoring that in.
summary: Very soft bristles feel nice on the face

reviewText: As someone with oily, acne-prone skin, I know the importance of exfoliation. For years I heard good things about Clarisonic, but I was always reluctant to buy one. (They aren't cheap.) Therefore, when I had the chance to review one for Vine, I jumped at the opportunity. Here's the pros: It is really compact and easy to use: just wet it, apply cleanser, and use it. It's really, really gentle, too, but it works. My nightcream went on easily and the rough patch on my cheek was all but gone. It also made my pores look temporarily smaller. The only con is that it takes awhile to charge us. The instructions say up to 18 hours, but it was ready to go in 8. That's shorter, but still long. Over all, I am pleased with this product and will continue to use it.

Clarisonic has been a part of my skin routine for over five years. My skin has never looked better. In fact when I am away and have not brought my Clarisonic, I miss it. My skin does not  feel as clean.

The Clarisonic Mia is a step up from my old Clarisonic. In this package. You will receive, the Mia, a brush head, the radiance brush, cleanser which is very nice, but you can use your own cleanser, universal  charger, and directions. With the MIA we have two speed settings, sixty seconds for sensitive skin, and eighty seconds, a power cleanse for use with make up. I was used to the sixty seconds only, and this was satisfactory, but I really like the eighty seconds.

When you are first starting, use the radiance brush head, use for sixty seconds. If skin becomes red, stop using for awhile. If there are no problems, use the MIA for two data week until you feel more comfortable using it every day. I try to use it every day. I often use it in the shower with my cleanser.

The MIA Clarisonic, is such a wonderful invention. My skin feels clean all the time, much softer and my skin looks good.

Highly Recommended. prisrob 12-06-16

I use to only find this product line in doctors offices only so glad I can just order it. This product really gets the skin clean and makes your skin tingle, just be careful this is strong stuff and you may have some dryness if you over use it. Just take your time and develop some toleranc to it. I would not recommend to some one with super sedative skin.
Works great with my skincare regime, helps get those dead skin cells off!
Won't be without this!!
Enjoyed switching to this product . Leaves your face feeling refreshed and clean .

I use "IMAGE" products because the Professional Skin Therapist I go to recommends these.  She uses these on her clients and also sells these products in her shop.  I've been very happy with the order & shipment experience going thru AMAZON.COM for these purchases.

My doctor recomended this line to me and I have slowly started to use more and more.  I love the way it makes my skin slightly tingle as it cleans.  My face feels tighter and softer, the lines seem softer and my spots have faded (not dissapeared).  I use quite a few products on this line; obviously the cleanser, the Anti-Aging Serum, Total Repair Cream, the Eye Lift Cream and the resurfacing mask,  which is my favorite thing ever!!.  I can not, however, use all of them at the same time everyday or my skin will go dry (I am guessing due to the Retinal).  I use the serum in the AM and just the Total Skin Repair at night, if I try to combine the two my face itches and is a bit uncomfortable.  I just rinse my face with water in the AM and use the cleanser in the evening.  I would absolutly recomend this line to anyone my age (40) and up, just use caution and introduce new products slowly. Reasonably smudge-proof after being worn all day the mascara itself is a good basic formula. Building length requires adding coats with sufficient time allowed for each thin application to dry before layering on the next. If carefully applied the mascara works well adding some length to lashes along with the primary purpose of adding color and structure to pale thin lashes.

The wand and tube both have a tried and true design that continues in use because it is an effective method to apply the product. The jet black color is a deeply pigmented black. The mascara was easily removed with a make-up remover wipe.  The formula wears well but there was a bit of flaking the longer it was on.

The mascara did not irritate my eyes, which has happened in the past, so that is a plus. This is more than I usually spend for mascara primarily because it is recommended that after opening it be replaced every three months (web md) to avoid possible bacteria contamination so I view it as a quickly disposable product.
summary: Julep Jet Black Length Matters Mascara

reviewText: I rather like this mascara.  It applies without fumes or irritation and lasts all day without flaking off or smearing.  It dries quickly too, so you can feel safe about applying as much as you want.  This is one of those that thickens and sort of lengthens, the more you apply it.  I find that if you go too far you just get clumpy looking eyelashes.  The lengthening effect is a little lost on me - I just don't notice much difference.  The julep brand has proven to be high quality and non-irritating.  I like how the tube is designed to pull all the excess product off the wand so that you have a clean applicator to work with every time you dip it.  This is a big frustration I have with the cheap department store varieties and it makes this line stand out in terms of quality.
summary: Nice quality mascara that goes on smoothly and dries quickly.

reviewText:
This is very gentle on my eyes.  It is beeswax based and it stays on well.  It lengthens, defines, and thickens lashes, and gives mine about the best look I ever achieve.  It is not waterproof.  It doesn't come off that easily either though unless you use makeup remover or oil.  I slept it in to test to see what it does, and it flakes around the eyes a good bit.  I didn't have major raccoon eyes, but there were flakes of mascara around my eyes.

It lasts about 12 hours on me before it starts shedding and flaking a bit.
It comes in a very plain looking tube.  It's attractive enough, but fairly basic.  It has a plastic thin, low spine rod instead of an actual brush, but I like that type, it seems to really define my lashes best.  I didn't feel or see any evidence of fibers.  If they are in there, they are small.  Usually I can feel fibers because they usually make my eyes a bit red and I can sometimes see them in the corners or around my eyes.  I didn't see that with this mascara.
I didn't find it to clump, but my lashes are very long and spindly.  It might or might not clump on thicker lashes, but for me it doesn't clump whatsoever.
The color black that I got was a deep black.  It says Jet Black and that is a very good description of it.
summary: Very easy on my eyes, non-irritating, not waterproof but long lasting - very nicely performing mascara that lasts a long time

reviewText: My favorite mascara is L'Oreal Paris Voluminous Miss Manga Rock Mascara (in the pink wand) that I buy at CVS or Walmart but it is not this waterproof version. I wanted to see if something could beat the thickness and length of my favorite and this one could not and I've tried many mascaras over the years. What I love about this Julep Length Matters Mascara is: - The brush applicator is easy to use and makes applying the mascara a cinch. - The mascara washes off easily with soap and water. - It does not irritate my eyes. - It does not clump. I know other users said it did but it did not for me. If one waits a few seconds for it to dry between applications, I find that it goes on smoothly. What I dislike: - It doesn't lengthen unless I apply 4 or 5 coats of mascara. - It doesn't give me the thick full look of the Miss Magna Rock mascara I love. - The mascara does not smudge like the Maybelline brands I have used previously but it does flake off a little during the day. - The current price of $20 is double what I pay for my favorite brand at the local drugstore. Of course if I could find that brand on Amazon at the same price they sell the waterproof version, I would purchase it here. In summary, this mascara is easy to apply, does lengthen somewhat, but doesn't give me the fullness I get from my favorite brand. It also flakes off during the day and cost too much for the product quality I am getting.
summary: This mascara is easy to apply, lengthens somewhat, but doesn't give me the fullness I get from my favorite brand & it flakes off

reviewText:
This is just an ok mascara for me. While it does make the lashes look longer, it doesn't really add any volume. I'd say it gives more of a natural look, rather than the "falsies" look I'm after.

The mascara flakes a little, but only after wearing it most of the day. I've found that's often the trade-off with non-waterproof mascaras. You have to put up with some flaking if you want easy removal.
