reviewText:
I have been using my lavender (sensitive) FOREO LUNA 2 for about a week. I didn't even need that long, really, too review it. From the first use, my skin was super soft. I was actually surprised to find my skin so soft. I couldn't stop touching my cheeks!

I have pale skin that turns red easily.  I used it on the highest level, and it did not cause any redness or pain to my sensitive skin.  I use it as a cleansing tool - place your regular cleanser all over your face and then run the Luna 2 over your face. It kind of pauses quickly when it thinks you should move to the next section. I would say that I ignore it, because I use it longer than suggested. Once done with cleansing, you rinse off the cleanser. I semi dried mine and then used it again on my dryish face for the anti aging segment of use. Use it in areas that commonly have wrinkles. I left the power turned all the way up, so I wouldn't have to keep adjusting it.

Im a longtime Clarisonic fan, though I use it weekly, rather than daily, as it can be a bit too much for my sensitive skin. The Luna 2 is a similar idea, with a significantly different set-up.

Like the Clarisonic, its a vibrating, rechargeable cleanser, but instead of a round, changeable bristle brush, this little hockey puck a built-in silicone scrub head. I don't think the wide base is quite as easy to handle as the Clarisonic handle, but it is submersible and the battery lasts far longer between charges.

The much more gentle massage is also totally suitable for daily use, so Ive got this one in the shower to use every morning, and am keeping my Clarisonic to use with deep cleaning masks and for weekend facials.

Im skeptical of the reverse side anti-aging massage as it mostly just felt like holding a vibrating cell phone to your face  not unpleasant, but hardly useful  but, all in all, the Luna 2 definitely makes my skin feel softer and cleaner than washing alone and its compact size and long-lasting battery make it an easy-to-use addition to my daily routine.

This is my first product of this type and I love it!  Both the massage and cleaning functions are awesome.  Because it does not absorb your cleanser you only need a drop or 2 to do the job.  My family has noticed a definite improvement in my skin.  I love the 'sensitive' model as I am 57 and need to be gentle to my skin.  My fine lines are less noticeable and even the crease between  my brows has lessened.  I marked it down 1 star because it randomly skips a beat or stops and restarts.  Also I sometimes have to turn it back on and then off again to get the light in the base to go out to preserve te charge.  Hopefully it lasts well because I LOVE what it does to my skin!

This is my first-ever experience with a facial cleansing device. I really didn't know what to expect, and the promises of "smoother and younger" are always something I take with a grain of salt.

That being said, the FOREO LUNA 2 (SENSITIVE version) is a great beauty tool that I'm pleased to say works very well on my 50-year-old skin.  The few issues I have with it relate to charging, packaging and price more than the product or its performance.

Here is my take on the LUNA 2 by FOREO.

-------------------------------------------------------------------

 WHAT I LIKE ABOUT THIS BEAUTY PRODUCT 

1. It's compact and highly portable. Easy to throw in an overnight bag or take on a month-long international trip.

2. Can be used with any facial cleanser. Although I would avoid things with 'grit' to them; exfoliants, as that, will just gunk up the device and would probably be way too harsh on your skin.

3. One full charge of the FOREO LUNA 2 is supposed to last up to 7 months!  I don't know about that, but if that isn't the case I will update this review later.

4. FOREO gives a 2-year limited warranty on this item with a 10-year quality guarantee.  Not sure how that works for the 10-year thing, but it sounds good and the 2-year limited seems generous for a device of this type.

5. It's waterproof. No worries if you decide it's best for you to use in the shower.

6. There's an anti-aging massage (opposite side of the cleansing bristles), which encourages collagen to fill in those fine lines around your eyes and mouth.  The pulse action is pleasant and supposedly tones the skin.  You can adjust the intensitiy.  Moisturizers with Vitamin C - used after using the LUNA 2 - were a bit more stingy than usual, but not irritating to my skin.

7. The LUNA 2 exfoliates and unclogs pores without damaging or irritating skin. The vibration of the device (which agitates the silicon bristles) has variable levels of intensity so you can easily adjust it for what works for you.

8. Its soft silicone design is comfortable to hold and feels good on your face.

9. Using this product twice a day made my skin feel much smoother.  Like it was gently buffing away dirt, oil, and dead skin cells, but also lifting them up and out to be easily rinsed off.

10. I like how the device pauses to remind the user to lift it and move to another section.  It's tough to 'over-clean' an area, thus adding to any possible irritation.

11. After using the LUNA 2 cleansing side and then the anti-aging (pulsing) side, I put on moisturizer.  It seems to help the moisturizer go deeper into my skin and my face feels more moisturized throughout the day.  **If you don't need or want the anti-aging perks, the FOREO MINI LUNA 2 is the one you want. **

12. There are different LUNA 2 products addressing combination, oily, normal and sensitive skin.  The cleansing brush on the front of each is slightly different.  The SENSITIVE one that I have doesn't go too deep.  It's gentle, yet gets the job done.

------------------------------------------

 WHAT I WISH WAS BETTER ABOUT THIS PRODUCT 

1. The price of this device may be prohibitive for many. However, I'd recommend saving up for one. It could be especially helpful if you have eczema, acne, rosacea, or similar and already spend a lot on skin care products that may or may not be working for you.  This is my new 'go-to' gift idea for my sister, daughter, and niece this year! (Shhh... don't tell 'em!)

2. Poor included directions really had me stumped out of the box. I ended up on YouTube looking at a tutorial of how to use it, after checking out the manufacturer's website.  I would have loved a booklet with photos big enough for old eyes to see (I got out my magnifying glass) with clearly written directions for use.

3. The charging cable (USB to device) is proprietary, making it something you can easily lose and have a tough time replacing. There's NO AC charging adapter for this device.  I plugged it into a backup battery with a USB port for its initial charge.

--------------------------------------

Overall, I would give this product a 4.5-star rating (if it was possible).  It's really easy to use and works wonders in terms of gently cleansing and buffing off dead skin and dirt. It's got a great battery and feels good both in the hand and on the face. Both the anti-aging toning pulses and cleansing agitation are gentle, yet effective.  My skin really looks healthier and most importantly - feels it!

The way it charges, the poor directions and the price are to be considered, but none of these things cannot be overcome if this product is for you.

NOTE:  If ordering, make sure to get the right LUNA 2 for you in terms of skin type.

WARNING:  Even with the SENSITIVE skin LUNA 2, I did experience some redness when using this product twice daily.

It's important to gauge your own skin's sensitivity, not 'rub' the LUNA 2 on your skin, and keep it moving around your face so as not to leave it in one place too long. The type of cleanser used with the product should be grit-free and water soluble for easy rinsing of the LUNA 2.

Some users may also want to cut the 2 minute cleansing time in half until they see how their skin responds.

______________________________
________________________________

Using it only once a day (in the shower in the morning) my skin is softer and smoother.  I feel like my complexion has evened out and overall looks younger and healthier. reviewText: Both my husband and myself are using this, I clean it with an alcohol rinse between uses, we were both sceptical about this little contraption but...we both feel it helps remove dead skin cells and it invigorated our skin.  He says his shave feels nice and smooth, I think my skin feels softer, we both like it but feel it's overpriced and out of reach for many people.

I have been using this for about a month now before writing this review. On first impression I wondered why this was so expensive. It seemed simple enough of a product with albeit a somewhat strange look to it. I was not familiar with this type of device.

Now that I have had some time with it, I can say that I do appreciate what it can do. It is one of those things that until you've learned the ins, outs and details of it that you might just write it off as marketing hype.

There is a Foreo following, a community of users that appreciate, refine and push the boundaries of what a good skin care regime can be.

I have not been an exfoliating user in the past. The most I have done is an occasional Olay Regenerist 2 part facial cleanser. There are quite a few bottles of partly used cleansing products on the bathroom closet shelf. I don't like the way most of them leave my skin feeling. This Foreo Face Brush has changed that.

I have found that it can turn an ordinary or sub-par cleanser into a completely new experience. Cleaners that once did barely anything or left my skin feeling greasy, now leave it feeling clean, refreshed and tone. There is a complex micro-pulse technology to the vibrations that the Luna 2 creates that makes it more than first impressions reveal. After the first couple of uses I realized there is more to it.

After using for a while and trying out different cleansers I have found that I makes just about all of them work better. I find it works best with the less abrasive ones. You can over do it. I have come to prefer a twice a week cleansing with it. That works for me. You can of course vary this. If you press more lightly and for a shorter duration, you can even use it daily. I would say my sessions tend to be on a medium scale of intensity for mid week and then the weekend session is a deep scrub.

I have only been referring to it as a cleaner so far, but the marketing for men is as a pre-shave prep. In this regard I do find most of the marketing to meet the claims. I'm not sure that razor blades last up to twice as long, but it seems they do last longer. Perhaps they aren't having to cut thru as much dirt and whatever else unseen is on our faces. I'm not sure the reason for this. I can say it does give a better feeling shave and with less irritation. I'm tending to think this is because it really works the shave gel in and gets your skin hydrated well before the shave. It and warm water really make the shaving experience so much the better. You can use less shaving cream too. I find that you can use non-arisoled creams now as it tends to whip them to an airy consistency.

I keep it in the shower on a higher up shelf. It is completely waterproof I think. I haven't had any problems with it in that respect. I find the USB rechargeable system to work very well. Everything is USB now a days and this works with my phone charger. Curiously mine only came with a cord and no charger. Not a big deal as I am changing out one bathroom vanity receptacle to feature 2 built-in USB charge ports on it. It is the one downline of the GFCI receptacle so it is shock protected. Going to add a few more around the house too.

I have tried the massage feature a few times, although I must admit that I don't really find the time for it. If you are practicing a facial skin care program and are committed to it then I image it also has merit. I would say that eating an optimized diet and perhaps adding supplements would be a critical part of that as well. Don't forget stress management too.

We are going thru an epidemic cold and flu season this year and I can say this really feels good on a stuffy face and sinus areas. I have found the time to use it for that.

Overall this really has turned out to be more than I first thought it was. I am going to give it a 5 star rating because I really don't have any negatives to say about it. It is a bit pricey. I wouldn't have purchased it unless a friend or professional had really convinced me of it. All I can truly say is that everyone is different and results can vary. I do want to be thankful for the opportunity to try and be introduced to this as I would not have known about it otherwise. I guess my message would be that if you're already looking into this then it may be worth a try. I found it to not be just a gimmick or over hyped marketing.

So far so good. This was simple to charge and easy enough to power on. It comes with a cloth bag to store it and a USB power cord. I wet my face and put liquid soap on the brisels. It has a nice massage feel, while I also feel it cleans better than just my using my hands. Not sure on the antiaging part, hopefully the cleaning aspect will help with that. I gave this a 4 star, because the included directions weren't very specific. There is a downloadable PDF that explains the product a bit more, along with the USB port being safe from water damage. The base of this will light up, which I find really cool.

Works just as well as the pink one I've tried. My face has never looked better. It's a bit larger, made for a man, but I use it too. The thing I like the most about it is that is charges!! It has a charger and I've only one complaint: it doesn't come with an adapter. You have to plug the cord into an already on-hand adapter. Thankfully I have a few, but a product such as this and as expensive as this should come with its own.

You turn it on, wash your face with the rubbery bristles--note it smells really rubbery--be sure to use soap and water or cleanser and water..you hit the button again and while you rinse and dry and shave your face if you choose, it's "on hold", then you hit the button again and use the backside on your wrinkles, a minute in each spot. I'm not sure what that does, but it doesn't hurt!
summary: My face has never looked better. It's a bit larger

reviewText:
The Foreo Luna 2 for men is easy to set-up and use.  I took the face brush out of the box, plugged in to my laptop with the included cord which attaches the brush to the computer.  Lights on the bottom of the brush came on indicating that the unit was charging.  I came back in a couple of hours and the lights had gone off, indicating that the unit was charged.  Minimal directions are provided with this unit so I went on-line to Foreo where a useful manual is available.

The Foreo Luna is advertised as an aid to shaving and it is.  I shave in the evening in the shower.  Now I use the Luna to clean and prepare my face using the side with the scrub brush to go over all areas to be shaved.  I did not know what to expect at first but was pleased with the ease of shaving after using the scrub brush and then the closeness of the shave that was a surprise for me.

The scrub brush takes less than two minutes to use and I think it is worth it to take this time to prepare my face, especially if I want a close shave.  After using the Foreo, I can go two days without shaving again.  Guys with a heavy beard most likely won't have this experience, but my guess is that they will get a closer shave.

On the other side of the scrub brush is a face massager which I tried and like  Im not sure about the benefits of the massage, but it feels good.  Readers of this review who buy this device definitely need to go online to get the directions for how to use the activating button on the scrub brush side of the device that controls the pulsing of the unit either for shaving or massaging.  So far, so good.

For me, so far so good.  The Foreo Luna does a good job preparing my face for shaving and does help me get a good, close shave.
summary: Helps me get a good, close shave.

reviewText: I cleanse my face daily, as does my husband and we both did not like how this cleanser made our faces feel. I have been using a Clairsonic Mia for the past two years and I still prefer that one over this one. And it is less than half the price of this one. I felt as though the vibration on this one was too intense, my whole head could feel the vibrations. I also felt like my skin wasn't as clean. Like another reviewer said, it's a $200 vibrating piece of silicone. I don't get it. At least with my Clarisonic there are bristles that are getting in the creases around my nose, and doing scrubbing. With the luna I did not feel like i could get the area between my nose and face well without a huge struggle. The way you go about holding this is really weird too. You hold it the same way you would hold a grilled cheese sandwich and it is hard to manuever. I wish I could find something good to say about this, but I really cannot think of anything.

As my husband has been getting more into a skin care routine I was happy to see a facial brush geared towards men. I have a similar style version of another brand but there was no way to convince him the pink brush would work for his face as well. It is easy to use and comfortable to hold. The unit has a one hour charge time, a cord does come with and the charge lasts quite awhile as he is still using his initial charge. It has variable speeds that are easy to control with simple plus and minus buttons. He does like the wash mode, the silicone bristles feel good on the skin and do not cause him irritation. He doesnt really enjoy the massage mode, so he won't be using that side. To be honest, the unit is on the pricey side for a cleansing brush but it does do as it claims and it works well.

This is way to pricey for what your getting.  This is nothing more than a fancy overpriced hand massage.  The thing is nice for what it does, but for absolute ridiculous price of 169.00 This thing is way over priced.  It is re-chargeable with a usb cord.  The Face brush works, I don't know if it is anti-aging, I think time will tell after I use it for a bit.  But the deal breaker is the pricey price tag that is a deal breaker for me.  I just don't feel it is worth the amount they are charging for this thing.
summary: Way too pricey for what your getting

reviewText: I don't know if I look any younger after using this, but my face feels great. And its a nice soothing buzz to wash my face and use this. My two nitpicks: I wish it had a charging base because I don't like loose charging cables around my bathroom and I wish you could adjust the strength of the vibration during use. Right now you press +/- then the start button.
summary: but my face feels great. And its a nice soothing buzz to wash ...

reviewText: I have used other face brushes in the past, including a top of the line Clairsonic, and this is so much better. For one thing, it really exfoliates without causing irritation. It's a breeze to charge, and I love that instead of having to replace a brush head, all I need to do it wash the silicone bristles. It's the bristles that really make all the difference. Also, this may be marketed as a men's product, but it truly is unisex. I love this.
summary: So much nicer than the Clarisonic

reviewText: I've been using this cream for a few days now and really enjoy the way it leaves my skin. I have sensitive skin and this cream left it feeling soft and nourished. It has a soft scent, almost a little hint of floral which is nice but not too strong. The cream absorbs into your skin without making it feel greasy or sticky, and I have noticed that it does seem to have evened out my skin in just a few days. Not sure it would work for severe hyper pigmentation or melasma, but it is great for mild discoloration and pigment unevenness. This cream is an excellent overall moisturizer that goes well with any other skincare products and does not feel heavy under makeup.
summary: Pamper your skin and treat mild discoloration or unevenness

reviewText:
I am more familiar with the Firmarine line; this is my first product in the White Marble set. The volume is significant. This is a thick white cream that is mildly fragrant. The scent is pleasant but hard to describe....Id say floral crossed with citrus. It does not linger on my face.

I am over 60 so hydration and moisturizers are my life; however this is just too heavy for me to wear for daytime. I tried it and it was a bit overwhelming. It is wonderful and soothing as a night cream. My skin feels fresh and looks bright in the morning. Cant recommend it as an AM moisturizer (plus no sunscreen) but its terrific for night time use.
summary: Great as a night cream, too heavy for me to wear for day. Light fragrance.

reviewText:
I am normally an Aveeno kind of gal, so this is way out of my comfort-zone, price-wise, but I was eager to try it out and see if it lived up to the high-cost hype.

First off, this is a good-size tub, which should last quite a while. A week in with twice daily use and Ive barely made a dent, so thats something. It also comes with a tiny plastic applicator, which is more sanitary than using your fingers, though I admit Im usually applying with freshly washed hands (and not sharing my cream) so, yeah, I do just normally dip in. (Partly because I forget I even have the scoop.)

This is thick, and rich, lotion but does absorb impressively well. My skin does feel very hydrated afterwards, but not greasy, which is all quite good. Not sure I saw any brightening of my skin tone, but Im already pretty pale without much redness right now.

My biggest knock, beyond the price, is that this doesnt contain sunscreen, something I think every day moisturizer should have. That protection alone is hugely anti-aging, in a very measurable way, and even in winter you should be using daily protection on your most delicate skin (face, neck and hands).

If you can afford it, this is a high quality effective, lotion. But I, personally, wouldnt buy it again, due both to cost and the lack of sunscreen.
summary: Good Moisturizer, But Lack of Sunscreen and High Price Means I Wouldn't Buy Again

reviewText:
This is a beautiful, luxurious cream. It has a very light, citrus-y fragrance and it feels so good going on. It absorbs quickly into my skin and it visibly brightens my skin all day long.

But after almost three weeks of use, day and night, I have not noticed any lightening of any dark spots/patches. I have very fair, fairly thin skin and the dark spots I have are not terribly dark to begin with so I thought they would lighten pretty quickly, but if there has been any change, it is so negligible that I don't see it.

So, for me the lightening aspect is not working, but I absolutely LOVE how my skin looks in every other way since I began using this.

Unlike so many other luxury brands that seem to be more jar than product, there is a lot of product in this jar.

The little spatula that is included is also very nice because it keeps fingers out of the jar and lessens the chances of contamination.

The Bottom Line: 5 STARS for this amazing cream. But I have to pull one star because of the lightening claim which is not happening for my skin.
summary: I LOVE this cream. Even though I do not see lightening, it noticeably and beautifully brightens my skin.

reviewText: This is a top quality product. It absorbs quickly, has excellent coverage, and does everything the product page description says it does.  When I'm using it, my skin looks clear and smooth, with an even color and a healthy luster. There is a slight citrus scent to it, very mild, when I'm applying but it does not linger. Overall, a terrific product.
summary: Lush and easy absorb hydrator with excellent coverage, a pleasant citrus scent and visible improvement with regular usage

reviewText:
This White Marble Translucence Cream from Emo Laszlo is an interesting product.  I'm not really qualified to talk about it from a value perspective because this is a type of product that I'm just not that familiar with.  It seems expensive, but without the proper context, it's hard to say.  Also being on the latter half of my 30's instead of my 50's, I'm not sure if I'm the target audience for this product.

Here is what it does do: moisturize!  Applying this to your face feels great and leave skin feeling soft and supple with a minor glow.  This tub is small but one scoop is almost enough for my face and this could probably last 2 months from daily use.  A little dab goes a long way.  Rubs in nicely and does leave your face with a greasy residue.  The scent is subtle and citrus like and I found it to be pleasant.

Overall a great moisturizer but I can't speak to it's wrinkle smoothing ability.
summary: Feels great on your face.  Deep moisturizer.

reviewText: This is a very rich cream, so a little bit goes a long way. The little scoop enclosed is a great help when removing some from the jar. I do not take too much and waste, which is important because this is an expensive cream. The scent is barely noticeable to me and does not clash with my perfumes. We will see what a difference it makes with my skin.

Because I absolutely love Erno Laszlo's Firmaline Serum, I expected to love the White Marble Translucence Cream as well. But I really don't care for it because the fragrance disagrees with my nose - and body chemistry.  It's very mild, gentle sort of a citrus scent - something I normally adore - but in this case reminds me of some sort of mild cleaning product for the house, not the face. I wish I could put my finger on it. And, here's the big problem -  the scent gets stronger on my skin. A lot of scents do this, so I would only consider the fragrance here a concern if you react with perfumes the same way I do. (If I want to wear a fragrance, it must be a pure essential oil; nearly everything else reacts with my body chemistry, as this cream does.)

If the scent isn't a problem, this is a very nice cream with a luxurious feel and ingredients that inhibit dark spots and improve moisture while freshening your face. I've no doubt it works since Laszlo's Firmarine Serum works wonders for me.
summary: Nice, but the Fragrance and My Body Chemistry Don't Play Well Together

reviewText: I'm impressed by how effective this face cream is after only a few applications.  I avoid the sun for health reasons but I am still pretty sun kissed in the face, chest and arms because we live in NW Florida.  After using this cream morning and night for two days, I was able to see a noticeable difference in the darkness of the pigment in all three areas.  I am pretty fair (Nordic ancestors), so being able to even out my complexion without any burning, itching or irritation is a bonus.

This perfecting, hydrating cream is very rich. Only two little scoops from the enclosed miniature spoon covers my face, drenching it in moisture. It takes time to see results with creams like this, however I did notice a glow about my skin after several applications. It is easy to use and spreads easily and evenly. It is absorbed quickly into the skin and leaves behind no oily or greasy film. There is no discernible scent to this cream. This a good-sized jar (1.7 ounces), and, taking into account the miniscule amount needed for an application, this jar will last a long time.

I was given a free sample of this cream in exchange for an unbiased review.

Erno Laszlo White Marble Translucence Cream is a high end brightening face cream that eliminates fine lines and crepe lines, smooths your skin and will also gradually even out your skin tone. The cream itself looks thick, but is very light and fluffy. It absorbs completely and quickly into your skin. The scent is very light citrus. I can smell lemons and oranges, which is very pleasant.

The container has a nice large opening and comes with its own small application stick with a scooped end. A little goes a long way. The directions say to apply this in the morning and evening, but I found the evening is enough. If you do apply this in the morning, you will need to add a sun protection. Due to the acids in the citrus ingredients, it leaves your skin more vulnerable to the sun. I saw instant results in two applications. Less crepe skin, fine wrinkles vanish and after a week, a more bright, even skin tone. A wonderful product for aging skin. 5 STARS.
summary: Eliminates Crepe Skin, Fine Lines, Smooths & Evens Out Skin Tone

reviewText:
My wife and I enjoy this product and we see the improvement on our mature skin because this cream works well on mature facial skin. The benefits are many. It locks in the brightening benefits of one it's ingredients, the white marble, that provides skin with a deep and lasting hydration, brightens, lightens the skin, evens out overall skin tones, and creates a protective, hydrating barrier that feels soothing. The dark spots and patches on our skin seemed to vanish after a short daily application.
For best results the use of this white translucence cream is recommended to use mornings and evenings, and this is what we did. Even after a few days of applying this cream, we saw the benefits of a younger, smoother skin.

Erno Laszlos Marble Translusent Creme is an excellent moisturizer.

The moisturizer comes in a small plastic tub with a screw top lid. The cream is opaque and salmon colored and has a very slight fragrance that smells like soap. The creme absobs instantly and leaves behind smooth and supple skin, that is not greasy or slimy. A little bit of the lotion goes a long way, so this expensive lotion will last a while.

I use this creme nightly and it keeps my combination skin nicely moisturized throughout the night.  If the lotion had SPF in it I would happily wear it throughout the day.

All in all... excellent moisturizer.

This JAPONESQUE Kumadori Fan Brush is perfect for apply loose powder. It applies it evenly and helps to cover your face in an efficient way. It's a little bigger than I was expecting but I"m enjoying it

I've been using the Japonesque fan brush to apply loose powder, and it works okay for this purpose. The bristles are a good texture for loose powder application and so far I haven't noticed any shedding. I'm not crazy about the texture of the handle, it's not very comfortable to hold or to shift in your hand. I've had good luck with Japonesque products, but this is not my favorite.

This Japonesque Kumadori Fan Brush is for the application of bronzer or loose powder. I haven't used a fan brush before, so I clicked around the Internet and found there are various ways to use them (to highlight, gently clear excess powder or makeup, apply powder to set foundation, etc.). I've used this brush to apply and distribute a light dusting of loose finishing powder to set my foundation. The brush is synthetic but soft, the handle is ultra lightweight, and the brush is adequate for a nonprofessional like me. It's also relatively inexpensive compared to a lot of fan brushes on the market. At the same time, this synthetic brush and looks and feels cheap to me and is made in China. Perhaps I expected more because I love Japonesque Velvet Foundation made in Italy, but there's just nothing special to me about this brush. At best, it's just okay and gets 3 stars from me.
summary: Works Okay, But This Fan Brush Is Nothing Special

reviewText: Fan shaped brush worked great. Quite big to store, but bristles are soft, and works exactly as promised.

I really like the JAPONESQUE Kumadori Fan Brush for the ability it gives me to apply bronzer or blush without it looking like I am heavy-handed.  This brush allows me to apply either of those cosmetics and not have an obvious transition between them and my foundation/tinted moisturizer.  Although I have not done so, I think this brush would also work well for applying loose powder.

The 2  wide brush  measured from the top, outside corners straight across  provides ample coverage of your skins surface.  The fan-shape gives you maximum control over  application of the chosen loose powder-type cosmetic.

 I like the textured handle of the JAPONESQUE Kumadori Fan Brush.  It has the look of being wrapped with a black cording.  Even if your hands are wet, the brush handles surface allows you to hold the brush securely.  The brushs ferrule is also plastic.  Synthetic brush bristles are very soft and will not irritate even the most sensitive skin.

This mid-priced fan brush is a good choice for your use when applying different types of loose powder-style cosmetics.  While I often find budget-friendly alternatives in art brushes, the fan-shaped brushes in the art/craft department are not as soft and often feature a mix of different bristle lengths that result in an uneven finished look to makeup.

The JAPONESQUE Kumadori Fan Brush is an excellent choice in the cosmetic brush category.  I recommend trying it  you may find as I did  that you really like this product.
summary: An Excellent Choice for Any Applying Loose Powder, Bronzer, or Blush for a More Natural Appearance ...

reviewText:
If you use a featherweight brush you will find this brand a good addition to your tool kit. The handle is a little flexible, the design attractive, and the quality seems good, though I have only used it a few times.

An excellent choice for super light powders where you want just a little dusting.

I don't know what some people have gotten but this brush works well.  I gave it to one of my friends to use and her exact words were "It's amazing because it's really soft and doesn't make the product you use all chalky and streaky looking."  This is from someone who is studying to be a makeup artist.  That being said Japonesque makes good items and products.  This is another that fits the bill.
summary: Good brush at a good price

reviewText: My wife reports: "I use make up brushes every day. I have brushes for every powder, shade etc., but a fan brush was the one I was missing. Almost all brushes I have are Ecotools and Lancome, both which I like very much. I was very excited to try this brush, and in short, I love it! It is large (2.5 inches/ 7cm wide), the bristles are very soft and evenly spread. I did try to pull very hard on the bristles, but not even one of them came outgreat! The wisteria (sort of a woody vine) wrapped handle is very stable in your hands and does not slip. I like how it feels, but the only concern I have is how durable it will be, since I love to submerge my brushes into liquid when I wash them. I used this brush with a pearl-like highlighter around the eye area and it works great.  It puts on a very, very, small amount of powder, evens out very well, and really helps me to compete my make up routine and helps my skin look fresh and healthy."
summary: Specialized brush, durable and wide, leaves a soft finish

reviewText: I love this brush! Honestly, I like the Kumadori Fan Brush more than the Kabuki brush for applying loose powder. First, this brush is very soft. I liked how it fit in my hand and how easy it is to grip. I liked how the bristles fan out. I used this with some loose Neutrogena powder on top of foundation to set my make up. I liked how easy this made it to apply a thin layer of powder without feeling like too much. I felt that this made the powder go on nice and easy without getting all over the place and making a mess, which is what typically happens when I use powder. In all, this brush is awesome. I highly recommend adding it to your makeup routine.
summary: I Liked The Kumadori Fan Brush Better Than A Kabuki Brush

reviewText:
Awhile back, I had a friend comment on 'streakiness' in my loose powder application and suggested I buy a good brush to remove excess.  I ended up with Ecotools line and have been happy with it - the extra softness and evenness of the fibers were well worth the xtra dollars. Similarly, I've started to explore the Japonesque line.  I've been pleased with most of their products but this one just didn't live up to expections.  I feel like this is a $2 product with a brand name lifting the price up.

The handle has a molded plastic 'Japense sword hilt hemp rope weave' that I suppose is supposed to look fancy but just doesn't. For casual application, it's fine and your hand won't slip because of the ribbings. But for extended use for a fancy event, I don't think I'd be happy with it. The brush itself isn't as soft as my ecotools, oddly enough, and that's where the 3 star review comes in. I had expected much better, even at this price point.  Although not soft, it does work well to remove the excess loose powder.

I got this makeup brush for my wife, and overall she really likes it.  She said it is very soft, so it brushes smoothly on her face.  She also liked the fan-like width, because it avoids the markings that narrow brushes can leave.  However, because of the latter, the brush doesn't hold very much foundation powder.  Therefore, she has to use a powder puff to apply the foundation first, and then use the fan brush to spread and smooth it out.  Hence the 4/5 stars.

This brush is for blending liquid makeup on your skin.  These days I am used to putting on my liquid makeup with the foam egg thing, like a Beauty Blender.  I tried this brush, and although it was okay, I think I like the egg better.

The brush is very nicely made and has a very distinct Japanese feel to it - not overdone.  The bristles are synthetic (yay - no moth problems!) and the handle is texturized so that you have a super grip.

The brush is smaller than you think looking at the pictures.

I will use this brush to actually blend my eye shadows.  It is big enough to sweep over the whole eye and blend powders to perfection.

Ultimately, GREAT for big eye shadow blending, not so great for the full face liquid blending.

I always read at least a few reviews before writing my own to see if there are any issues with products I need to address and to try to offer different information to readers like you.  I read another reviewer had a problem with bristles falling out of her brush, so I knew to lookout for it. I used my brush like her for a week and washed with mild soap and water.  I had about a dozen small bristles fall out.  You can't tell any difference in the brush now, but if that trend continues for the lifetime of the brush, there won't be any brush left!  I still gave it 3 stars for now because it is so soft to use and provides a good shape and finish to my powders.  I use it with a compact of Neutrogena pressed powder.  I'm going to come back and give an update, but at least you know for now it could be an issue.  I see there are other reviewers that don't mention a similar issue so maybe we just got some bad brushes?  However, you may not want to chance that with your hard earned money.
summary: I had bristles fall out of the brush too

reviewText:
I am not a huge makeup person, but I got this brush because I do occasionally wear foundation and was looking for a better way to spread it on my face (was using fingers). I like this brush a lot. It is very soft, and I only need to use a little foundation on my brush. It brushes very evenly, and looks very natural. Part of the reason I do not wear much makeup is because I don't like it caked on, and this brush overcomes that problem. This brush is the right tool for me, and keeps me looking great.
The only reason I gave it 4 out of 5 stars is because some of the hairs come off when I use it.
summary: Great brush for a natural look

reviewText:
Synthetic brushes are generally best for liquid/cream makeup because they don't absorb the makeup and natural brushes generally work best for dry makeup powders/blush/etc.  This buffing brush is synthetic.

Put your liquid foundation on top of the brush & gently blend in to the skin in a circular pattern.  Less is more - don't put on too much.  You can always add more later.  This brush did a good job of applying foundation evenly - it takes practice to get this right.

Besides being a beautiful brush, the handle is comfortable & easy to hold with control.  However, I prefer a hard, easy-to- clean handle.  I think this handle will fall apart over time & may even collect grunge.

A few bristles came out the first time I washed it but nothing dramatic.  The second time, no bristles came out.  It is not unusual to lose a few bristles but if they fall out every time, you eventually have a bald & useless brush.

Keep your brushes clean!  For dry-use brushes, wash them at least once a week.  For brushes you are using with wet/foundation/cream you really should wash after each use - at least a rinse under warm water.  I wash all brushes with a gentle shampoo but any unscented soap will work.  I rinse them well with warm water & let them air dry.  Not only does this help your brushes last longer & stay soft but it is really important to wash out the bacteria/dead skin/oils/makeup that build up quickly on makeup brushes - YUCK.  If you don't take care of them, you can get rashes, breakouts, etc. & your makeup will be a mess.
summary: Very Good Synthetic Bristle Brush - Liquid/Cream Makeup

reviewText: I like the unique natural handle, it is a series of concentric circles piled on top of each other.  This provides a comfortable and effective grip.  The weight is also just right.  Soft, but not as soft as my favorite facial brush.  It is also less dense. Still, it feels great on your face.

I was surprised that this brush was small, the photo gave me the impression that it was bigger. Regardless, the brush worked great when I used it with my foundation. I know this is the new Kumadori line, but the handle seemed cheaply made. Overall, it works great, but I expected better quality from Japonesque. Hairs are already falling out of the brush when I use it.

Absolutely fantastic buffing brush. Besides being a perfect smaller size (will not take up that much room in your makeup case), it fits wonderfully in your hand allowing for expert applications. The bristles are strong, yet oh so soft. Use this for my blush application and the results come out professionally every time. I cannot recommend a better brush for this purpose. Japonesque is known for they high quality products and this buffing brush is no exception.
summary: Great brush - every woman should own one!

reviewText: I got this for my daughter to test when she applies her makeup.  Currently she uses many different brushes from Bare Minerals and likes this one.  First off the quality is very nice..  The soft bristles are synthetic and the handle is just the right size.  She commented that "this brush is good and should last a very long time".  Nice brush with the oriental flare.  Well worth adding to the makeup kit..

This is a very nice brush.

I was not able to get great results using this brush with liquid makeup.  But here the fault may be mine.  When I use liquid makeup--which I rarely do--I am accustomed to using a sponge applicator.  I may not really have been able to master the technique of using a buffing brush with liquid makeup.

I use mineral-based powder makeup more often, and I was able to get excellent results using this brush to apply it.  So--though that is not what the brush was designed for--that is how I will continue to use it.  It works much better than the smaller, natural-bristle brush that I usually use.

This Japonesque Kumadori Buffing Brush is a great brush, until you wash it. The brush is a perfect size. The handle is ribbed and comfortable. The bristles are firm, yet very soft. The brush worked well with foundations, bronzers and blushes. The design has a looped end for easy drying after washing it.

The real test of a good quality brush is washing it. After using it for a week with powders, I rinsed it, gently washed it with a drop of mild shampoo, rinsed, towel blotted it, reshaped it and hung it to dry. The next morning, I applied some powder and immediately upon using it, the bristles were falling out all over the place.

I've had cheap brushes where the brush falls apart after a few washings, but this is ridiculous. A brush that cannot survive one gentle wash is a total waste of money. I am surprised that Japonesque would allow a brush this nice to be made this cheap and pass any form of quality control. If I could, I would rate this 0 Stars, as it's a total waste of money.
summary: After One Wash, The Brush Hairs Are Falling Out

reviewText:
This is a really nice brush.  Feels great and applies make up evenly. I may use it for blush instead of powder, but it works great for powder.

Now, if I can keep it away from the cats.  They are seemingly enthralled with it.

It does make a difference! This powder brush is far better than the ones you can get at the drugstore. The powder goes on smoothly and evenly. I also like to blend to give a finished look and this brush worked beautifully!

The handle is well made and easy to hold. The bristles are soft and feel lovely on my skin. I couldn't be more pleased.
summary: This powder brush is far better than the ones you can get at the drugstore

reviewText: I am just starting to use various brushes when I apply my makeup.  this brush was a good addition to my small collection.  The bristles are very soft and I would say they are from some kind of animal fur.  The handle is wrapped with some kind of twine? which makes it super easy to maintain a grip on.  My one complaint is that it makes a big mess when you use it.  the powder comes completely off and doesn't leave anything behind but it gets everywhere.  You definately will have to be careful when you use this brush.
summary: Nice and soft bristles but be careful when you use it.

reviewText:
I am no expert on makeup or makeup brushes.  In some ways, that actually makes me a good reviewer of this product.

What I learned, immediately, is that it really makes a difference what sort of makeup brush you use.  I had been using what I thought were high-quality brushes to apply mineral finishing powder.  Maybe they ARE high quality; they certainly were expensive.  But this brush simply does a much better job.  It's easier to use, and it provides a more even application.

I will leave comments on the finer points of brush construction to people who know more about such things.  What I know is that this is a brush that does a very good job with loose powder.
summary: This brush provides the most even application of loose powder of any I have used.

reviewText:
This is a lovely brush, both to see and use. Kabuki brushes are designed to use to apply loose powdered make up. This spreads the makeup evenly.
This is made in China. The handle is wrapped with thin wisteria vine, making a secure and attractive make-up utensil.

 I am frustrated that there is no clue as to what the soft brush is made of. Traditionally the brushes used animal hair, but many today have synthetic bristles. This does say natural and is very soft. It almost reminds me of rabbit hair.
The brush does work with my pressed blush but it does spread wide and with a flourish of powder. It creates a natural look as long as the powder does not get on your clothes.
Still its a lovely addition to any makeup set.

With the receipt of this brush I am adding a lovely powder brush to my inventory.  It is by far the nicest brush in my collection.
It is so soft.  There was no indication in the packaging but I suspect that it is made of fur of some kind.
The application of powder or blush with this brush is wonderful.  All product is smoothly applied and evenly applied.
I am very pleased with the outcome of the application.
The handle is wrapped in wicker or straw of some kind.
This one will last a long, long time.

I use brushes and face powder every day. This brush is better than any I have owned. It does a wonderful job at uniform application of powder without clumps or missed spots. The result is a very smooth skin appearance. I have textural flaws and this brush applies powder in a way that makes my skin look younger and firmer.

This brush has a dynamic that really propels powder so it is best to use before you dress for the day. One touch and I had face powder down to my knees! The handle is wrapped with wisteria and provided a terrific grip. There is no case included for this brush; I will add it to my existing case but you will want to think about how you will store this.

The manufacturer gives no details about the origin of the bristles other than they are "natural". I suspect sable but really do not know. I am assuming animal in nature so this is not suitable for vegans. The brush is made in China.

One lovely thing about this brush is that it completely transfers powder or blush to your skin leaving the brush virtually empty. No residual seems to remain which is nice to prevent buildup.
summary: Superior, even coverage. Wonderful textured handle.

reviewText: I thought this would be a neat thing to get for my wife.....so I did.....she writes, "This is a very soft, fluffy make-up brush with a wrapped handle (which makes it easy to find even by touch only in the make-up drawer).  Feels very soft on the skin.  I first tried it with my blush and it wasn't stiff enough for that job.  Washed the bristles (to make sure all the blush was out) then tried again with my mineral veil setting powder.  This is what this brush is designed for!  Great light application of powder foundation, {although I still prefer my Kubuki brush for this step - gives more coverage}, OR foundation setting powder (like Bare Minerals Mineral Veil).  The brush gives a feather-light finish to your made-up face and feels really soft against your skin. I recommend it highly!  Natural bristles are easy to clean periodically with a facial soap and it's made really well."  So there you have it.  I hope this helps.

Aside from being beautifully designed, this is a highly functional item for your makeup brush collection. (The only thing that would make it better would be if there was a container available to store it in for travel.)

I tried this with powdered foundation, blush, finishing powder and bronzer. What I liked best is that the powders did not clump or cling to the bristles, which made for a more even application. This would also make a great brush to use when contouring your face.

The feel is soft on your skin, unlike some brushes which actually feel itchy or scratchy. The manufacturer does not specify what the bristles are made of, and that is something that could easily be corrected. By referring to them only as "natural" one gets a feeling they don't want you to know. But if you're going to talk about "wisteria" handles, why not name the bristle type/source? Are they hiding something? It's one of the most relevant thing for many people who have allergies, etc. or who do not want certain types of materials.

The way the handles are covered gives a nice, firm grip, welcome given how slippery some handles on brushes are.

It's interesting to read the various reviews. Some folks say that powder gets everywhere, while others say it is contained. I've had both experiences and the difference is the product I am using. Some powders are very loose, while others are more firm and compact, so less will go on and less will "fall" off.

The real test of any brush is how well it wears and it's way too soon to know this. By "wear" I mean if the bristles stay intact and don't shed and if the shape remains firm and full. So far, so good.
summary: Well-designed and functional makeup (foundation, blush, bronzer) and contouring brush. Soft, easy to grip.

reviewText: If your looking for the best, then this is it. I have been using powder brushes to apply blush for roughly 60 plus years and never have I found one this soft. The brush evenly applies the blush with out clumping or dropping. The brush holds the powder until it is applied with little to no mess. The application is always smooth and even. All powder brushes should follow the standard set by JAPONESQUE. I have found a new product for my face that I love.

Synthetic brushes are generally better for liquid/cream makeup because they don't absorb the makeup as much and natural brushes generally work best for makeup powders/bronzer/etc. This powder brush has "natural" bristles.  It is domed and puts on powder evenly.  I am not a pro so I prefer a brush like this one, that puts on a smaller amount with control - I can always add more if I need to.  I've had brushes that put on makeup more heavy & make me look clownish.

Besides being a beautiful brush, the handle is comfortable & long enough to hold with control.  However, I prefer a hard, easy-to- clean handle.  I think this handle will fall apart over time & may even collect grunge.

Keep your brushes clean!  For dry-use brushes, wash them at least once a week.  For brushes you are using with wet/foundation/cream you really should wash after each use - at least a rinse under warm water.  I wash all brushes with a gentle shampoo but any unscented soap will work.  I rinse them well with warm water & let them air dry.  Not only does this help your brushes last longer & stay soft but it is really important to wash out the bacteria/dead skin/oils/makeup that build up quickly on makeup brushes - YUCK.  If you don't take care of them, you can get rashes, breakouts, etc. & your makeup will be a mess.
summary: Very Good Natural Bristle Brush - Setting Powder/Bronzer/Powder Foundation

reviewText:
I picked this brush up for my teenage daughter to use. She uses it to apply powdered foundation and really likes it. The brush is very soft but picks up the powder beautifully. It smooths the powder over her face, leaving a thin regular layer. She feels that the handle of the brush is not of equal quality to the brush itself, it seems a bit cheap to her compared to similarly priced brushes she has used.

Overall this is a very nice brush with a so-so handle.
summary: Very nice brush, handle is only okay

reviewText:
Wow I've never had such an exquisite makeup brush!  This is super soft and full with a very luxurious, amazing feeling on the skin.  This is so far above any makeup brush I've ever experienced that it justifies the higher price.  The handle is long and elegant.  But the long very full bristles are what give this a feeling that my skin loves.  And the powder glides on and spreads evenly on my face so there is a perfectly smooth application.

I have never experienced a high end makeup brush before but there is a tremendous difference in feel and application with this.  The higher price is well justified.

I love this brush. The handle is wrapped in wisteria. Wisteria is a wonderful plant. It has long chains of purple flowers that make a stunning display. The stems are vine-like, and that is the part they wrapped around the handle. It's like you are holding concentrated beauty.

The soft bristles are loosely bound in a soft clump. This is a soft brush, for powder. The box says you can use it for foundation, but it doesn't seem like the right kind of brush for a liquid. I prefer to use the stiffer, flatter brush for foundation. This brush is good for powder and contouring. It works great with a contouring kit. If you don't have a contouring kit, do an Amazon search. I only discovered they exist recently, and what a great invention.

The brush is sculpted to an aesthetically pleasing curved point. The shape gives it functionality. You can cover broad swathes of your face lightly, or you can focus on a small area with the tip. With practice, you can get good coverage and you will look beautiful.
summary: A wonderful brush, wrapped in Wisteria of all things.

reviewText:
It's a great brush with a cross between a tear drop shape, and a wedge shape, that's great for picking up powder and blending.  According to the box, it is natural fibers, though it does not say what kind.  It's very soft, and well made, with no shedding.  The handle is rather unique- it's well balanced and is wrapped with natural wisteria vine that's tucked on both ends.
It's pretty as can be, but the real star, I think, is the shape- unlike regular brushes, the bristles are cut so that they are very full about 3/4 of the way out, then they taper, with a bit of a wedge.  It picks up powder well.  It's really a joy to use for application and blending.
summary: Unique shape to the brush head, a bit of a cross between a tear drop and a wedge shape.  Works great, very nice to use

reviewText: This is a super high quality make up brush!  I love trying new make up products and this brush works wonderfully at applying face powder.  It picks it up well without depositing a ton of it in one spot on your face and blends the powder well.  It is nice and fluffy and feels soft against the skin.  I highly recommends this brush!

This is a really nice, dense brush.  This is the first Japonesque brush I've used, and, based on my experience with this brush, their reputation for quality brushes is true.

Although it's listed here as a powder brush, the box states that it can be used for foundation, setting powder, or bronzer.  I've tried it for all three, and prefer it for powder and bronzer.  The bristles feel too fluffy to make your foundation go on in an airbrushed way, which is the look I prefer.

For point of reference, I'm including a photo of this next to my MAC 187 stipple brush and my Sonia Kashuk blush brush.  The Japonesque brush is the same length, but you can see how the brush tapers in at the head.  This makes it ideal for getting powder into hard-to-reach areas on the face, and it deposits both powder and powder bronzer lightly.

This is a really nice, soft brush that also has a luxe look and feel to it!
summary: Really nice quality, and can also be used for bronzer

reviewText: Good quality brush, super soft, and blends well.  The knock from 5 to 4 stars is the lack of a protective cover for the bristles, or a mechanism which would retract the bristles into the handle.  Even a slip cover or sleeve would improve the life of this brush.
summary: Great brush, but could use some protection

reviewText:
This brush is wide with soft bristles.  Other reviewers have written about how to use the brush for both powder and blush, depending on the angle with which you hold the brush.  I like that the brush handle is short and flat, it makes the brush compact without decreasing the effectivity or fullness of the bristles.

It's relatively inexpensive for the quality of brush that you get.
summary: Wide with soft bristles, works both for applying powder and blush

reviewText:
There is no cosmetics company as underrated as Japonesque. I've owned their blush and finishing powder, and they are easily as good as many other prestige, high end brands.

Their new Kumadori line of brushes are simply superb. They're made to continue the makeup traditions of kabuki theatre, and in so doing, easily compete with many much more expensive Japonese brush lines.

The blending brush is really a do-it-all appliance. The rubberized handle is comfortable in the hand, and the dark, soft natural hair bristles are dense, but not so dense you can't use it for pretty much every powder face product you own. Hold it perpendicular to the face, and you are buffing in powder foundation. Til it to the side, and you can apply and sweep off excess finishing powder. Turn it on its edge, and you have a great contour or blush brush.

I have a lot of brushes, but this beats them all. I'm definitely making the small investment in other Japonesque brushes, because using them is such a freaking pleasure!
summary: Super high quality do-it-all brush, from a brand that needs to be better known

reviewText:
Let me join the chorus: this is a well-designed brush with an easy-to-grip handle and soft, pliable bristles that allow you to distribute product lightly or apply more pressure for serious blending. It is a large brush, not the largest I own but larger than it looks in the photo, with the bristle area about 2.5" x 1.5" so you will want to use it for applying blush and contouring. It will not work for your eyeshadow! The brush is attractive: you can see the Japanese aesthetic at work.

I have read reviews complaining that the bristles tended to fall out. I have not seen that problem, and I have tried tugging on the bristles. They're not going anywhere. I haven't tried cleaning the brush yet, but as delicate as the bristles feel, the construction seems sturdy.

The Japonesque website states that all their products are cruelty-free, but I spent some time searching for the exact materials used and could not find that information anywhere. (That question is even posed on their website FAQ...and not answered specifically!) Apparently the materials are animal "byproducts" but since the brush is made in China, you may indeed wonder about the provenance of the bristles. For that, I deduct a star and will not be likely to acquire more of these in the future. If that doesn't bother you, this is a great addition to your collection.
summary: Sturdy blending brush with soft, softer, softest bristles

reviewText: This brush is much nicer than I'd expected.  It feels like I'm putting my makeup on with rabbit fur.  It is so soft.  It feels absolutely wonderful.  It is also much bigger than I'd anticipated, making my make up application go faster & blends much more natural looking.  This is by far the nicest brush I've ever used.  As to what the brush is made of, I have no idea.  There is no indication on the box.  It just says that it's natural fibers.  I'm going to guess it is animal fur.  I described rabbit previously.  Another way to describe the feeling is, it is very much like pressing your face into your cats fur.  If you are Vegan, you will most definitely not want to buy this, for the rest of you, enjoy the luxury.

The JAPONESQUE Kumadori Blending Brush is a full sturdy blending brush for all your make up needs.

Kumadori  is A Japanese stagecraft tradition in ancient Kabuki performances. The purpose of the Kumadori is to emphasize the facial expressions rather than to hide them. The soft touch wide handle feels comfortable to hold while the ultra-soft natural brush hairs blend pigmented powders and liquids to smooth perfection.

This is by far the best brush i have ever owned and i would highly recommend the Japonseque line.
summary: A Beautiful Brush for An Amazing Blend

reviewText: This is a very well made and functional brush.  Before ordering it for review I had looked at the dimensions, but wished that I could have seen it compared to something, so that is why I have included a photo.  The brush is comfortable to hold, with no real concern over it being slippery and it is extremely soft and light. Blending is very easy with it and everything considered it makes it easy to recommend this if you are looking to spend $20-$30 on one.
summary: Nice size, great quality and works very well

reviewText: This is a beautiful blending brush and very quickly becoming my favorite.  The bristles are ultra soft and the brush just glides over your skin.  The rubber coated handle makes it easy to hold.  What I don't like about this brush is that there is no cover or case for it.  That means that if I toss it in my cosmetic bag the brushes are unprotected and are surely going to get ruined.

Oh my goodness. If it's possible for a makeup brush to feel like silk using it against your skin, Japonesque has figured out how to do it. It both applies and blends my makeup so well. It holds on to makeup and smooths it out, rather than dropping much of it like cheaper brushes do.

Some brushes irritate my skin and make it red or itchy. I don't have that problem at all with this. The bristles don't fall out and there's tons of them packed into the brush. It's a thick full brush, and nothing was skimped on. Even the handle is nice!

Mmmm,  how I do love this blending brush! It is smooth, soft, and wide. The handle is comfortable without being unwieldy. I have washed the tip ends of the brush taking care not to get the base of the fibers wet and have experienced no fall out so far. I am not a super high end brush buyer. I don't own any Shu Uemura and others that get such excellent reviews, so I can't compare. But I do own sets of Sonia Kashuk, and other drugstore brands. This Japonesque compares very favorably to every brush I own so far. I use it to smooth powder and bronzer across my cheeks and forehead. It is effective with a couple of light swipes and leaves no unsightly lines. I am very enthusiastic about the quality and design. I checked Ulta and makeup alley and other sites and found that other women are similarly impressed. I do recommend it!
summary: This brush is my favorite of all the brushes I own!

reviewText: This is supposed to be good for liquids and creams as well as powders, but as I have been using it with creams and liquids, I find that it keeps shedding hairs which get stuck and are annoying to pick off, plus picking them off damages the finish I just created. It's still very good for powders, which don't seem to pull the hairs free.
summary: Sheds too much to use with liquids or creams.

reviewText:
This is a makeup brush that is beautiful to hold and feel.  I thought the flat handle might feel strange compared to the long thin rounded brush handles I am used to, but it feels natural in my hand.  The bristles are soft and lush feeling.  The wide rectangular shape gives you a wide flat side for blending but you can also use one of the narrow ends for smaller areas you want to blend.

Good makeup brushes are not cheap, so the price of this (at least as of the date of this review) does not seem out of line for comparable brushes.

The only drawback, and it is minor, is that the size of the handle means I can't stick it in the jar where I keep my other makeup brushes because it is too short.

The cleaner is a spay, similar in function to hair spray.  The amount you get is very small for the price, roughly less than 3oz, think trial size.

Functionally, it did take the build-up off my brushes, combs too, but left them covered in perfume.  The smell is strong, very strong.  Its musky, and stays on your fingers for a while after use.  I'd be careful with it, if you're very sensitive to smells.

One problem - I received my bottle half empty, apparently emptied during shipping.  The nice box it comes in was covered in product as well, many oily stains, and so was the bottle itself.  If this company should continue to sell on Amazon, better care should be paid to packaging.
summary: Strong smell but works well, very small size

reviewText:
This doesn't just remove makeup from brushes. When I was done applying all the layers, I needed to clean off the counter top as well. Without thinking, I just sprayed some of the brush cleaner onto the counter, and that came clean rather quickly too. Granted, this is rather expensive for using on counters regularly, but if you can't find your makeup removal cloths, it will do the trick.

Spray some onto your dirty brush, and run the brush across a towel. Why is this handy? Because sometimes you need to clean your brushes to re-use them for something else, and don't have time to wait to do a full water cleaning. Also, with some of my more expensive brushes, I'm not to keen on cleaning them with soap and water, because I don't want the fibres to get damaged by anything.

All in all, in spite of the cost, I think it's worth it to have a bottle of this stuff in your arsenal.
summary: Spray some onto your dirty brush, and run the brush across a towel

reviewText:
This waterless brush cleanser works great. It is alcohol based, so it doesn't require water in order to clean the brushes. The spray bottle is small but very portable and easy to use. Just a few spritzes to saturate the brush head and then wipe it from side to side on a towel paper until it looks clean. It dries almost instantly, which is great if you want to use it immediately. The alcohol also disinfects the brush in the process. That said, I wouldn't  substitute regularly shampooing the brushes for this spray. It is great for when you're in a hurry or out traveling.

The brush cleanser does have a fairly strong scent but it is very pleasant. Though the scent seems to linger on the brushes after drying. It may bother you if you're sensitive to fragrance. All in all, this product works great. It cleans, disinfects and dries fast. It is rather expensive but very handy when you're in a hurry or traveling.

I wasn't aware of how dirty my makeup brushes really were until I used this product. I laid my brush on a paper towel, applied the remover and gently began wiping away the makeup. It took several times to get 1 brush clean, but what a difference! Dried quickly and the scent was barely noticeable. A tad pricey, but works well.

I never knew that they made brush cleaners, so this product was a very welcome surprise.  I used to eventually clean my brushes with soap and water which was a very laborious task.  When my brushes  got too dirty, I would throw them out and buy another non expensive T. J. Max brand.  Japonesque waterless brush cleaner is a keeper.  It is easy to use, smells fresh and does the job intended.  I needed to repeat the procedure three times for the large brush I use for my bronzer.  I rotated the brush's head in a circular manner as directed, till eventually no more powder came off on my paper towel.  The brush I use for my blush was not as dirty and only required two sprays to come clean.  On the expensive side, however, you no longer need to waste time on a rather mundane but necessary chore.

This little spray bottle makes quick work of cleaning my makeup brushes. It's something I know I should do, but I'm terrible about actually doing it. I'm always afraid that somehow I'll damage the brushes. With this product, it only takes one or two squirts, then a quick wipe on a paper towel or washcloth to have nice and clean brushes. The scent is minimal, and the product really does dry quickly. I was able to use the brushes again within a minute or two. If you over-saturated them, it might not dry as quickly, but a squirt or two is all that is needed to clean.

It works, and works well. If you want to clean your makeup brushes in a hurry and not have to wait for the brushes to dry, this is the product for you. I was able to clean my brushes in just a few seconds, and only had to wait a minute for them to be dry enough to use. I had to ding it for the appalling scent, however. It reeks of this strange chemical vanilla alcohol scent.  Definitely not a product for the scent sensitive.

I don't clean my makeup brushes anywhere near as often as recommended so this cleaner by Japonesque had its work cut out for it.  I used this on a variety of brands of makeup brushes (Sephora, Laura Mercier, Mac, etc.) as directed by the instructions.  In other words, I held the bottle about 6 inches away from the brush (doing it one brush at a time) and directed nozzle towards the brush head. I evenly sprayed the cleaner onto the brush head. Then, I gently rotated the brush head in a circular motion on a paper towel until all the makeup was removed.  Because my makeup brushes were more saturated with makeup than most I did it 2 times per brush and was really happy with the results.  I loved how quickly the brushes dried and how completely clean they were afterwards.  Applying makeup with them afterwards I could tell how much cleaner and crisper the color was thanks to a perfectly clean brush.  And I worried that cleaning the brushes might distort the shape but that wasn't the case at all.

I've previously used brush cleaners from the Sephora brand and I really like Japonesque as well and think the quality of this product is on par.
summary: Got my dirty, dirty brushes clean

reviewText: I have lived many years without using a product like this, but thought I would give this a try.  After spraying this on a brush, I could hardly stand the smell.  If you are going to use this product, I would suggest not doing it in a small bathroom.  You really need to be in a large well-ventilated room.  As for me, I prefer to clean my brushes with a little soap and water.  It did a good job of cleaning the brush, but considering the price and the smell, I would not recommend it.

This is a handy cleaner and I tried it on my worst brush. It was one caked and gummy with a creamy cover up. It did take several times spraying and wiping on a paper towel, but that brush is now clean and soft.
I have used alcohol before to clean brushes, but this does dry immediately and seemed to leave the bristles softer. So I guess if you cleaned your brushes before they get completely caked this might work better.

This is truly waterless!  I had my doubts, but it does an excellent job cleaning without water and the brushes are dry in mere minutes vs overnight with my usual "brush shampoo".  I found the scent to be lovely and not overpowering, unlike other reviewers, however, I have sensitive skin and the fragrance may not agree with me long term.  It is too early to tell.  The pump action is easy to use and it has a narrow spray angle so you don't waste a lot of product with overspray.

Pros:
- easy to use
- don't need water
- brushes dry almost instantly so you could switch colors immediately
- thorough cleansing, product is largely alcohol based so it will reduce/eliminate bacteria on the brushes
- 3 oz size would allow you to put it in your carry-on bag for flying so it is travel-ready

Cons:
- PRICEY!  This is a small 3 oz spray bottle and it takes a fair number of sprays for even a small brush to get completely clean so I don't imagine it will last very long
- scented; even though I like the scent my "brush shampoo" is fragrance-free which is probably better for my sensitive skin in the long run

Overall:
I like the cleanser and will use it every now and then when I'm in a hurry to clean my brushes but I'll probably use my brush shampoo more often because it is fragrance-free and more cost effective.
summary: Great, truly waterless brush cleaner but it is pricey

reviewText: I use a foundation brush, blush brush, and eye shadow brush at least once a day. The Japonesque Waterless Brush Cleanser sprays easily and cleans effectively. I did not notice the strong scent as others have said and I am usually very sensitive to strong smells. The only reason I gave it 4 stars is because unless you are in a pinch and need your brushes dry immediately I would save the money and just use soap and water.
summary: The Japonesque Waterless Brush Cleanser sprays easily and cleans effectively

reviewText: When I sprayed this on my expensive makeup brush ($30 brush) Professional Kabuki Makeup Brush With Big Angled Flat Top for Liquid, Cream Mineral, & Powder Foundation & Face Cosmetics - Best Quality Design - Carrying Case & E-Book Included I was instantly worried as my finger started to sting and I realized there was alcohol in the product. I grabbed the box and the first ingredient was Alcohol. More on that later in my review. I had not cleaned this brush in probably a good month (I know, terrible) and I use this with compact Makeup Forever powder foundation MAKE UP FOR EVER Pro Finish Multi-Use Powder Foundation 120 Neutral Ivory 0.35 oz so the foundation has been really packed down into the brush for some time. I sprayed about 10 squirts of this product and had a white dish rag I had and begun gently rubbing side to side and the makeup began to come off. I would check deep into the bristles each time until they were clean. I had to do this about 5 times for this particular brush. After the amount I soaked it with, the brush was dry as each time I would gently rub back and forth on the cloth. The alcohol in the product helped with the quickness of the drying. Next I went on to a big puffy Avon brush I had which I use for blush. This one is not nearly has caked in with product and I only had to do my 10 sprays and it was complexly clean. Next I moved on to my eye shadow brushes, some of these I had to do two or three times and again, they came clean. The heads of some of the brushes were white again. FRAGRANCE The fragrance to the product is STRONG and if you are sensitive to smell would not recommend. I personal love smells and did not mind it at all. Each of my brushes smelled wonderful. The next morning when I used my brushes I could smell the strong perfume smell of the product on them. It was lovely. ALCOHOL I had never used alcohol on my brushes before, so I went to my favorite search engine and was surprised to see many notes out there to disinfect your brushes in 99% Alcohol. Honestly, this surprises me as I thought this would dry the bristles out. Overall very happy with this product. I would NOT however use this as my sole brush cleaner and will continue to use the brush cleaner I have. These will be nice for quick touchups or when I am traveling and want to be sure they are clean.
summary: Works Well, Bristles are Soft, Strong Perfume Smell

reviewText: I was very impressed with this brush cleaner. I was able to clean my eyeshadow brushes with one spray each and my face brushes with three. Then I wiped each brush on a paper towel. Its amazing the amount of product that gets removed! Also, the smell it leaves on my brushes smells amazing!

If you're lazy... ahem, I mean busy and don't wash your brushes as often as you should (like me), this brush cleansing spray is good in a pinch. It removed nearly all of the product from my blush and eyeshadow brushes with the exception of my two workhorse brushes that apparently had a whole lot of eyeshadow built up in the bristles. Simply spray the product onto the brush, rotating the brush as you give it a few spritzes to make sure the cleanser saturates evenly, then rub the brush onto a paper towel. It's very easy to use.

The instructions say to hold the spray 6 inches from your brush, but I found that led to a LOT of product loss as the spray spritzed pretty much everything on the other side of the brush. I held it much closer and found that I needed to use fewer spritzes to get the brush bristles wet enough.

The product does have a pretty strong scent, which could be bothersome if you have allergies or very sensitive skin (as the scent lingers on the brush after cleaning). It's also rather expensive for a small can.

It definitely doesn't take the place of actually shampooing your brushes, but if you need to get them clean in a hurry, it's a good product to reach for.
summary: Good for a quick brush cleaning

reviewText: I attempted to use the JAPONESQUE Waterless Brush Cleanser on a foundation brush and it worked to get an average amount of the foundation off. As you can see in the video, it took several applications but the brush did not get 100% clean. I probably used a quarter of the 2.366 fl. ounce bottle. That product evaporates quickly so you must work fast. I could not get into the middle of the brush to get it clean, but the outside seemed cleaner but there was foundation residue left behind. It has a strange scent that is hard to explain. It is not bad smelling but it is does linger behind. It probably works better on eyeshadow, blush or any kind of dry powder makeup instead of liquid even though it states all types of cosmetics. I think I will to stick with my mild soap and water to get my brushes clean.
summary: Meh - not so great for cleaning foundation brushes

reviewText: OH MY GOODNESS!!!  My makeup brushes were a mess...I thought they were half way clean until I used the Japonesque Waterless Brush Cleanser on them and saw all the makeup residue come off onto the paper towel.
