I really liked using this in that way and it works great for that.

Overall I am pleased with this product and will definitely use it in the future.  I would recommend to those who want a nice neutral matte palette that is easy to use for both contouring and eyes.  I will definitely be checking out other bliss products in the future.
summary: Nice pigment, blends easily, this is a nice neutral matte palette for both contouring and eyes.

reviewText:
I just totally dissed the Bliss Bronzer, but this is a nice product.  The contour cream is easy to blend.  I've been using the Lancome double-ended contour stick.  This is like that with one more color.  I like the two lightest colors, and the darker one is one I'm not sure I will need (unless I can use it on my hips?).  They blend well and don't look like stripes.

The colors are soft too, you could actually use these as a shadow if you were in a hurry.  Completely natural looking.  Also, no odor or greasy feel.

Big like

This makeup combination provides the perfect blend of shades for contouring. I haven't gotten the knack of doing this yet, as this is my first time trying this. You can find videos on YouTube that show you how to use different shades on different parts of your face to create a professional look. This makeup will work really well for that. I am very fair skinned so I used just the 2 lighter colors and it looked good but I need more practice. The makeup is high quality and it's easy to apply with a brush.  So far, I like it.
summary: Easy to apply, high quality powder.

reviewText:
Very easy to apply. Doesn't stay on the brush too much when you put it on. Looks like it will last a long time. I like how the lightest shade is still dark enough that you can use it. Too often you find contour palettes with such a light shade that it's basically worthless.

I'd get this product again. It looks great and is pretty affordable. I've used a few of bliss' products and they've all been very satisfactory.

I am enjoying this set of four shades (I have the Rose palette)- the colors look vibrant and rich, and the shades are well-chosen to complement each other-- from brightening to smoldering (plum-mish hue on the darkest shade) so this compact can easily take you from day to night. You do need your own applicator, however.

There is a good amount of product in a beautiful mirrored pack, with each circle of color being a bit larger than a quarter in diameter. This is good, since I found i needed to add a few applications for concentrated color. However, I don't use a primer, and that would no doubt help. The color does stay all day, and feels creamy and smooth and sticks to my normal moisturizer--there's no powdery fly-away on application, or any creasing later.  I'm a make-up loving gal, and this Bliss eyeshadow palette is a great addition to my makeup collection.
summary: Pretty Colors; Smooth, Creamy-feeling Powder that Lasts

reviewText:
I like this suite of eye shadows from Bliss. They look well with my dark brown eyes but I think they would also look very well with hazel and perhaps green eyes, too.

There are 4 colors and all have a shimmer - not enough to call frosted, IMO. The darkest color has quite a bit of copper and is not as dark as it looks when applied, although it's still a dark brown. The next darkest color is more of a shimmery khaki color. The pink is quite pale and shimmery when applied and the lightest color is a very shimmery, pale champagne color.

These are more like a cream/powder mix and glide on easily when applied. I use a primer before applying eye shadow and I would suggest you do, too, as creamy type shadows have a tendency to settle in the crease of your eye without a primer.

It comes in a silver and white plastic case and has a mirror under the cover.

As others have mentioned, there is no applicator. I always use my own brushes when applying any make-up so this is no big deal to me but it may be to others.

I have no idea what the price will be so I cannot comment on that yet. This is pretty eye shadow that looks good and performs well. I tend to be cheap when it comes to make-up so I'll let you know when I find out the price if I will be buying it again.
summary: Looks great with brown eyes and glides on easily

reviewText: This is a nice four pack shadow in a chick looking compact. It has a mirror to use when applying but lost a star because it does not offer an applicator nor a place to store one. The shimmering powder goes on nicely and last all day. Because there is no price listed at this time on Amazon I can not address if it is a good value or not.
summary: This is a nice four pack shadow in a chick looking compact

reviewText:
I got this for my partner because it has her colors in it.  She has been very happy with the way the product work and would give it five stars except for the packaging.  The best thing, besides the color is that there is a built in mirror in the reflective material of the lid.  Both the top and bottom work as great mirrors.  The mirror in the inside is ingenious, The mirror on the outside unfortunately almost instantly collects finger prints and looks messy quickly.

The other big issue with this compact is that it does not come with an applicator.  Nor does it have a place to store one if you had an extra to put with it.  So that makes me wonder if the built in mirror that is brilliant is meant for mobile use, or if the lack of an applicator means it should be used in a stationary location where applicators would be available.  It doesn't seem to fit either perfectly.

As for the product. my partner immediately put it on and we went out to eat and she looked great as we left as well as after we returned.  The product seem great.
summary: She has been very happy with the way the product work and would give ...

reviewText: A shiny case that is mirror-like needs to be opened carefully, just slip a finger underneath the front tab and lift up.  I thought it might be depressed, but it is just a lift to open.  All parts of the case are plastic, including the interior mirror.  Each shadow is a disk of a little larger than a quarter, and I have no idea how deep the pots go, so I can't say how long they will last.  The colors are complementary, feel good when applied over an eye primer with a brush, and the shadows blend well.  There was no irritation to the eyes or skin surrounding the eyes.  There is a very bare hint of shimmer to the texture, so this is suitable for day or night wear for most folks.  It was made in TAIWAN.
summary: Better than cheaper products but not premium

reviewText: This is a very nice assortment of colors, goes on smooth and easy, and lasts all day throughout my work day. No irritation to report, so all around good set for the price.

These are good colors, they go on smoothly and softly without tugging. They just don't last the way I'm accustomed to (Smashbox and Kat Von D being my favorites). They fade noticeably and crease within a few hours of application. They ARE easy to apply however.

They also have a reddish undertone that is NOT a friend to rosy undertoned skin. This really made the pink/red tones in my face stand out.

There's good news and bad news. The good news: the bubblegum pink doesn't go on noticeably pink at all, so no rabbit eyes. It does make a nice top of the cheekbone highlighter. The shadows stay all day, in humidity--over a thin, dried coat of Smashbox primer, as I always do. The darkest color is not too red--more of a brown-maroon. No fallout or flaking.
The bad news: the two pink shades show up as sheer white frost. The taupe shade is slightly darkening, but not much and is pretty much overwhelmed by the frost. The only shade that seems to show noticeably different is the darkest one, which does make a nice liner over a thin line of brown Smashbox Always Sharp Sumatra dark brown. It is not opaque enough to use as a liner without a deep solid base under it.
I am a medium-toned white person with hazel eyes that look like green olives with a dark ring around the outside and a star of rusty orange in the middle.
summary: Pretty much just frosty sheer white....

reviewText:
I love eye shadows. I love how the colors, when applied correctly, makes my brown eyes pop out nicely. This quad of colors came out nice. I received the rose quad for review and since I am dark-haired with light complexion, this quad of colors is perfect for me. I applied it yesterday morning for church and I was amazed at how much darker the colors were, even the lighter ones. You can really see them. And I didn't have to reapply them once. After church, I had to take my kids to camp and the color stayed on, even when it was humid out.

It is not greasy. It is not cake-like. It is actually a nice set of tinted powder that stayed on. It did emphasize the fine lines in my eyes, but will add primer to my eyes to take care of the lines. (I will apply it before putting the powder on.) What I really like about this is how the colors made my dark eyes stand out. It makes me feel feminine.

The only thing I did not like was how there were no applicator brush with it. Fortunately, I had some here but for the price of this eye shadow, I think an applicator should be included as well. That is my only complaint. Other than that, I love it.

All right, I have to admit, eyeshadow is something I love to splurge on - I have quite a few palettes. I love to mix it up, love to experiment with color, to do something different every day - neutral today, smokey the next, pop of color the day after that. And it doesn't have to be one brand, or an expensive brand. It just has to work, meaning blend well, last, and be of good quality.

bliss is known for its spa products, and I do own some of their stuff along that line - moisturizes, polishes, etc. I have to admit, this is the first time I've tried their makeup. And... eh, I'm not entirely sold. Do I believe it has quality ingredients that's good for my skin? Yes. There's a faint scent to this eyeshadow that seems natural (if that makes any sense), and it's very creamy, feels well-milled, it's smooth and it does blend very well.

I received the rose 'quad', which is a very pretty, almost natural color combination (Time to un-wine, a deep brown/wine purple, Mink it over, a slightly dark taupe brown, Frost & found, a pale gold beige-ish color, and Tickle me pink, a light pink). All of these colors are frosts, so have some glitter to them. And NONE of them have the pigment on your eyes (or at least mine) that they did in the palette. Especially the Time to un-wine one, which was supposed to be an eyeliner color. I was really disappointed in that - the pink color only had a hint of pink, compared to the beige one. I would have thought these would stand out more, but when I put them on and blended a little, it came out like a frosted nude palette. So something a little different if you're looking for a nude/natural look. It's not that heavy of a frost, but definitely not a matte look.

Maybe if you try these wet, they'll be a bit more pigmented.

No breakouts, and yes, this felt good on my eye. The makeup arrives in a nice looking, thick, solid silver compact with a mirror inside (no brush/applicator, though). Sometimes it's easy to open, sometimes not.
summary: feel really nice, but yeah, pigment leaves something to be desired

reviewText:
There is a lot to like about the Bliss eye four eyes Rose quad. The collection of colors, perfect. From the crease worthy wine, to the transitional pale pink, they go beautifully together. The soft formula has very little fallout, and blends well. Even the amount of shimmer is spot on, giving dimension without age emphasizing shine.
However, it sadly lacks in the pigment department. It took awhile to build up to a more color true eye look. Even over primer, it was sheer. Now if you like sheer, and want something that takes little effort, this is your quad. If you are more on the cutting edge and want to be able to place the color you might need to look at a different color collection.
For a quick on the go look, this is a beautiful option. But, for me I want a little more pigmented bang for my buck.

Great colors for blondes, but the shadows are very frosted. They look matte in the pan, but, in fact, they are quite shimmery on the lids. It's a bit much to use four frost shadows at once. So while I like the colors, I don't like all the shine.
summary: all four colors are frost shadows

reviewText:
Ok, so I'll be honest, I didn't expect to dislike this quite so much...it looked so pretty in its package!  But I think if all eye shadows were packaged in identical plain packages, you'd guess this was a cheap drug store brand.

The 4 colors are:
"Time to un-wine" -- (darkest shade in the lower right corner) -- looks as though it'll be a deep, darker brown with win undertones.  In reality it is a much lighter reddish brown, which (like all the colors) doesn't last at all, and the reddish coloring can make your eyes look a bit tired and bloodshot.
"Mink it over" -- (lower left corner, taupe color) -- the best color of the 4, it is a decent frosty taupe, which can be used on a large area of the eyelid without being overpowering.  But like the other colors, it lacks enough pigment to last, and you need to use a lot of it to get it to show up.  It also doesn't look right with the darker "time to un-wine" shade (because that shade is too red and not dark enough).
"Frost & found" -- (light peachy shade, upper left corner) -- I can't get this color to actually show up at all on my (fair) skin -- I can only see the frostiness of it in the light.  But it doesn't provide any pigment to even out my skin tone underneath, so it tends to look like I've just used a transparent frosting powder or something.
"Tickle me pink" -- (light pink in upper right corner) -- I hoped this would be a rosy color, adding some depth, some blushy tones.  However, it is merely a super light frosty pale, pale pink -- almost white.  Like the eye shadow you give a tween girl for her first eyeshadow.  It's ok if that's what you want -- but again, like the others it's not heavily pigmented (or even medium pigmented!), so you have to use a lot of it to really get coverage.  (And I'm fair skinned, so it shouldn't take much...)

Overall, I'm just not impressed.  These shadows are just overpriced, put in a sleek box (which, FYI, doesn't include any applicator), and seem no better than Wet and Wild or Cover Girl...save your money.  They're not pigmented nearly enough to show up (even on fair skin).  The four colors don't even look particularly nice with each other...I don't understand this palette at all!  The colors only seem to coordinate in the package, but on the face they don't coordinate well at all.  The only color I kind of like is the "mink it over," but even that can't hold a candle to several of the Urban Decay Naked2 colors (that's actually the one I'd recommend for this nude type palette, it's awesome).

On a side note, the funniest part of this is the packaging (I didn't subtract a star for this, I'm just mentioning it).  It's made to look sleek and high-end, except...it's nearly impossible to open!  It snaps closed too tight, and there's no way to grip it to open it...it's a struggle every time.  I actually have to put a tab of duct tape on the edge just to get it open, because it's so badly designed...trés chic.  ;-)
summary: No pigment, colors awful together, feels like cheap shadow

reviewText:
My Holy Grail eyeshadows are those by Urban Decay, MAC, and, more recently Color Pop, and while I wouldn't say that this new Bliss eyeshadow goes on quite as densely, I was surprised by how nice these shadows are.

All four colors have a soft shimmer to them, and went on really smoothly.  As I get closer to 45, I've noticed that heavily frosted eyeshadows just accentuate the fine lines on my eyelids, but these don't at all; they're definitely nice if you want to avoid any glitter.  I always use either Urban Decay's Primer Potion or Tarte's primer under my eyeshadows, and with those primers underneath, these shadows last all day.

The Rose palette is really gorgeous, and is a nice everyday neutral palette.

The only downside is that the case it comes in is pretty bulky, and it's a little hard to open.  Just so you know, it also does not come with any applicator wands, but that doesn't bother me since I always use makeup brushes.

I've been able to try a few of these new Bliss products recently, and I really do like them!
summary: These feel buttery and smooth, and have a soft shimmer to them

reviewText:
This lovely quad contains colors that complement each other in order to make application a no-brainer.
First there is a color called Frost and Found. It's a barely there peachy pink.
Next comes Tickle me pink, which is, of course, a girly pink.
Mink it Over is a brown-taupe, Time to Unwine is between burgundy and purple, yet looks more pinkish unless you build the color up.
All have shimmer.
The case is compact and chic, but the outside shows every fingerprint. Mirrored inner lid.
As is the case with many eyeshadows, these don't have a lot of staying power (especially on oily lids) unless you use eyelid primer.

This pressed powder is easy to apply and feels light on the skin. The powder's texture is creamy, similar to the liquid foundations but has the convenience of a compact.  I'd used the powder during a heat wave in NYC and reapplied it every hour or so without any irritation. However, as other reviewers have noted, the color does have an orange tint.  I'd have to try the different colors to find one that works better for my Asian skin.
summary: Creamy texture similar to a liquid foundation but the color has an orange tint

reviewText:
I ordered BLISS EMPOWDER ME BUILDABLE POWDER FOUNDATION, NATURAL, 0.31 OZ for my daughter. BLISS is new to us, but after trying their foundation my daughter fell in love with the product. She informed me right away that she wanted the powder as well. It came as no surprise when she told me that she loved BLISS EMPOWDER ME BUILDABLE POWDER FOUNDATION as well.

Color: Natural

Product Description
From our spa to your skin youve put your trust in us to care for your skin with our legendary spa services and world famous skin care products. Now were excited to introduce the next step to achieving complexion perfection. We like to call it tinted skincare. Weve poured our innovative spa ingredients and advanced technologies into our tinted skincare products, so youll know they're good for you and your skin. Spatacular results: you have to feel it to believe it. Creamy, silky, and luxurious, empowder me uses an advanced technology resulting in a revolutionary powder foundation that looks and feels like a second skin. Encapsulated algae, cactus flower extract, chamomile and allantoin nourish and help balance skins appearance. Easily buildable and blendable, the powder feels remarkably lightweight. Apply wet or dry with a sponge or brush allowing for a range of different finishes. You are in control.

Brand Story
Youve put your trust in us to care for your skin with our spa services and skin care products. Weve poured our innovative spa ingredients into our tinted skincare products.
summary: MY DAUGHTER IS BLISSFULLY HAPPY WITH THIS PRODUCT.

reviewText:
When it comes to packaging, bliss either excels or fails miserably. This is a case where they excel. This is one of the best compacts I have ever used. First of, the mirror is actually large enough to be useful. (Most compact mirrors are too small.) I love the bit of built in plastic to separate the puff from the powder. (This needed to keep oils, dirt, etc. from the face off the compacted powder.) This truly is great design!

When it comes to the actual product, it is fairly ordinary. It's actually not that different from L'oreal or Maybelline's pressed powders/compact foundations. (While this is called foundation, it is actually pressed powder and can be used likewise.)

Still, the products is more than fine for most people's needs, and I would recommend this if only for the compact. It is worth it.

It was a little bit of trial and error using this Bliss powder foundation.
When I tried to build the foundation in order to provide a more opaque coverage, it simply turned that dreaded  orange shade...that odd color that xanyone that uses foundation is probably familiar with, especially if you have fair skin.

While everyone is different, at least for me, this is a case of Easy Does It.
A bare minimum of product applied gives me a sheer coverage that blends in with my natural skin tone.

On days when my skin looks blotchy, or I have blemishes to hide, I'll reach for a different product, but when skin is behaving, this is a nice option.
summary: A Light Touch for Sheer Color

reviewText: This is a high quality face powder. It only needs to be applied once per day and has quite a bit of staying power. I love the design of the packaging. The clear hinged cover on the top keeps the powder from flying everywhere. The complaint that I have with this product is that even though I didn't travel with it and kept it in the same place every day, the powder cracked into pieces just a few days after I got it. Other than that, it is an excellent product.
summary: I love the design of the packaging

reviewText:
This foundation is darker than most Natural colors available and is also yellower than most Natural colors. I typically use MAC Studio Fix Liquid or Powder in NC35 (powder) or NC37 (liquid) in winter, and C40 (powder) in Summer when my skin is more olive and tanned. This foundation does not really match although I would say it's closer to C40 or even C42 than any other shade. It's got a darker yellow cast to it than any other foundation in Natural shade. See pics with and without flash comparing it to MAC NC35.

I typically check for shades on findation dot com, a gem of a site that tells you the closest match in different brands based on the foundation shades you already use. However, they did not have any details for Bliss Empowder since it's a newer product.

It includes some natural ingredients like algae, cactus flower extract, chamomile that soften the skin. The finish is creamier and smoother than MAC and it provides dense coverage for a powder foundation and does not sit in fine lines. See pic of my fingers with product  over the respective shades Bliss Natural and MAC NC35.

 The case is nicely made and the mirror is very helpful. I prefer to  moisturize my face and then apply foundation with a stippling brush for light but overall smooth coverage. Since the shade was just a test sample, I will not rate it based on that.

It would remain to be seen if this gives me any breakouts like MAC can if I don't wash it off my face every night. If it works well I may try a shade that works better for me.
summary: Smooth and creamy with good coverage, shade is darker than usual "Natural" color.

reviewText: I usually use loose powder but this compact is really nice.  The powder goes on smoothly with even color on my face.  It comes with a sponge applicator and has a cover that you can see in the picture that goes between the powder and the sponge when you aren't using it.  It left my face feeling fresh and clean, not oily.  Overall, I was impressed.

I first discovered a powder foundation many years ago made by Shiseido and loved being able to apply it either wet or dry. This product by Bliss is pretty good and because the shades are not really describable in words, I'd suggest finding the most suitable for your skin tone in a store before ordering online. The Natural shade is  just as I've discovered most Bliss cosmetics, rather yellow in undertone, which I learned years ago is the most common for a majority of Caucasian skin tones. This particular formula is non-irritating and not offensive with added scents. Like the other Bliss Cosmetics, this has a plastic case that is what I would call no frills so you are not paying for a high-class cosmetic product. For dry skin, I prefer liquid foundations but I do like the portability of this for travel as well as on-the-go touch-ups.

As much as I generally love bliss products and was searching for a good foundation, sadly this is not my shade. Based on the picture I thought it night be, but what they define as 'natural' has way too much of a yellow undertone to it. Maybe for someone else, but not for me. Still as with other bliss products, no irritation to report after the trial.

My make-up regimen is a simpleface washing followed by Olivella Moisturizer, then CoverGirl Smoothers Liquid Make Up, Creamy Beige 750, 1-Ounce. The moisturizer is 100% olive oil, so it leaves my face slightly greasy but it also helps the make-up blend in very well on my face. I follow up with a very light dusting of loose mineral foundation for a nice matte finish. The only trouble is I hate using loose powderits messy. I thought this Bliss solid powder foundation (in natural) might be a good alternative. Its color seems to match many of the medium translucent and beige shades I normally wear, but I cant seem to get it to blend as well as loose powder. It appears much heavier and dry looking on my face. Im not impressed. Maybe thats how solid foundations work. If so, Ill stick with messy but lighter applications of loose powder and brushes. Ive included a color comparison photothis shade (center with mirror attached) most closely resembles the loose powder on the right called medium translucent. Im a blonde blue-eyed gal, and can use both beige and medium translucent colors.

This makeup was really nice and very effective. Contrary to what other reviewers said, I found the tone to be just perfect. I have pretty fair skin, although I do have a little bit of a tan. It covered exactly the way I wanted to when I applied it dry. And thus far it has caused no irritation or made me break out (and I tend to have pretty oily skin.) The reason I didn't give it five stars is that there was an eyelash in the case when I got it. It doesn't bother me enough that I would send it back or anything. And I understand that those things just happen but it is kind of gross.
summary: This makeup was really nice and very effective

reviewText:
I really like this powder foundation. The powder is finely milled. It goes on smooth and has a creamy texture that doesn't feel dry or cakey over time. The coverage is excellent and it feels light on the skin. No skin irritations so far.

That being said, the natural color is much darker that I expected. It also has a slight orange/yellow tinge to it. It would not go well with a pale, light skin tone. Perhaps, it may be more suitable for someone with a medium complexion. Even then, it's hard not to notice the slight orangey or yellowish cast. It is definitely not neutral looking.

The compact is sturdy and well made. It is a little larger than most compacts, and has a shiny silver finish that is one big fingerprint magnet. It is kept closed securely with a push button clasp. I like the oversized mirror inside. It is bright and practical. There is also a hinged, interior clear plastic cover that separates the powder from the provided sponge. It is a very nice compact, albeit a little large.

Overall, the powder itself is top-notch. Unfortunately, this particular natural color is way off. I wouldn't recommend it if you are looking for a more traditional, neutral kind of natural color. If you do find a different color that suits you, go for it. It is a wonderful powder foundation.
summary: Wonderful powder foundation but the natural color is too dark

reviewText: I was so excited to use this powder! The consistency is so smooth and  the coverage is really excellent! It says neutral but it suits my medium complexion really nice but that would mean that the color match  is a bit off. Other than that I love it! Even the packaging is eexcellent and totally practical! Love it!

This new bliss Empowder Me Buildable Powder Foundation ,0.31 oz. in the Natural skin shade is a natural shade I have never seen before. When applied to your skin, it is pure yellow- not a slight yellow cast, but a deep yellow, almost gold/orange yellow tone. I have never seen a skin tone in this color and I worked for a cosmetic company for years.

If I rated this powder foundation based on the color alone, I would have to give it 1 Star, but because the actual powder foundation is really nice, I will rate the parts separately.
1.) The Color- NATURAL: Pure yellow tone that I have never seen on any skin type. 1 STAR
2.) The Powder Foundation: Wonderful creamy texture, goes on smooth with either sponge or brush. Feels light on your skin. 5 STARS.
3.) The Compact: The silver plastic always looks dirty as it holds both powder and fingerprints. It has a nice clasp to open and close securely as well as a nice clear plastic cover inside to keep the powder foundation under cover and clean. The mirror is large and clear enough. 4 STARS.

Should the actual color have been a true Natural shade, instead of a non-wearable yellow, this powder foundation would have rated 4 1/2 STARS. The product is actually smooth, silky wonderful, so I have to rate it 3 STARS based on everything put together. Bliss is going to have to let the buyer actually try these shades on before buying any, as the colors are not right, at least on the one I tried. If you want a really nice powder foundation, this one is great, just make sure you try the color on your face first, so you don't end up looking like you have jaundice in a deep shade of yellow.
summary: The NATURAL Color Is A Heavy Yellow Shade

reviewText:
Wow, this ended up being way too dark from what the picture showed.  Other than that, I like the foundation.

First, I have Caucasian pale skin.  Im not Jim Gaffigan pale/pasty, but close.  I also have to watch what I put on my skin.

I really like the case.  It has a lot of product in it, but I think the price is still a little too high.  The case is cool with the extra flap that separates it from the sponge.  I like the sponge too.  Its not cheap and applies the make-up evenly.

  I like that there is moisturizer in it so it doesnt highlight wrinkles as much.  The color was natural looking, but looked absurd on me unless I went into coloring my neck and chest too.  Since Im not doing a Broadway play, that was not happening.  I looked like Ashley Judd at the Oscars the year she walked down the red carpet with color on her face and two shades lighter on her chest.

I may go down to Ulta with a coupon and see if I can get a lighter color.  I really thought it would work for me.  I looked at the picture on Amazon and I've worn "natural" before.  My skin didn't breakout the next day.
summary: Way darker that what is pictured.

reviewText: First off, mine arrived shattered, in lots of little pieces and it was all over inside the box. For $34 I expect it to come in 1 piece and when I opened it it was a cloud of dust. Also I didn't like how it covered on my nose. It made my pores look large. Also fine lines, yup you can see them if you apply a heavy coat of it but it was fine after a few times of trying to use it, still regardless my pores look noticeable. I also strongly recommend a very good moisturizer before applying as it leaves your skin feeling a little on the dry side.
summary: Came shattered and makes my pores look large

reviewText: Stippled on with a brush, it has very nice coverage alone or on top of a tinted moisturizer.  It does have an application sponge if you prefer, but you won't get the same smooth effect you will with a fat powder brush in my opinion. Lasting, product goes where you put it and stays with very good coverage. Fun packaging and a hard working beauty product!
summary: Stippled on with a brush, it has very nice coverage alone or on top of a tinted moisturizer.

reviewText:
I have sensitive skin that can react poorly to new products, but this foundation didn't irritate my skin at all.  It's a unique formulation that starts off as a powder, but that blends into a creamy finish.

At the age of almost 45, I have fine lines and occasional dry patches from my nightly use of Retin-A, so I usually stay away from powder foundations because they tend to showcase those dry areas.  This Bliss foundation, though, goes on creamy, and feels more like a liquid.

It also has some versatility with its level of coverage.  You can apply it with the included sponge for more opaque coverage, or with a foundation brush for a sheerer finish.  It can also be applied the same ways either wet or dry.

The compact this comes in is also sturdy, but does get fingerprints easily.  It seems like it would hold up well if you take your foundation on the go.

I really like this foundation, but my reason for knocking off a star is that it is extremely hard to figure out what color to get based on the information that is available about this product online.  I ordered this from the Vine program in Natural, but it's too dark for my fair skin.  Before ordering it, I had searched the Bliss website and another online retailer, as well as a few makeup sites, to see if I could suss out more info about the colors, but I couldn't easily locate the information.  Some color swatches would be really helpful, and I'd recommend trying to locate this in person before ordering it to make sure you get the correct color.
summary: Blends to a creamy finish, and doesn't sit in fine lines

reviewText: "Natural" would be the perfect color if you were an Oompa Loompa.  It has a very orange cast to it which doesn't work for my pale to fair skin tone.  I'm not sure it will work well for anyone, Ooompa Loompas excluded. The coverage is definitely buildable, the powder is finely milled, and if it were a wearable color, it would be great. The included application sponge is of average drugstore quality. The packaging is a little odd. The mirrored case gets covered with fingerprints very easily and therefore looks messy.  There is a clear plastic cover inside that hinges off of the powder that is awkward and feels flimsy.  I can't recommend this product.
summary: Perfect color if you are an Oompa Loompa

reviewText: The best thing about this product is that it's absolutely weightless!  Works well with powder for minimalist, fresh-faced look.  Offers a little sun protection while helping to give a smooth even look to the skin.  When you pop off the cap, turn the tip and squeeze gently to dispense product.  Nice so you know it won't just come loose in your bag if the top happens to come off.
summary: You truly don't feel it, non-irritating.

reviewText:
Things I love about this product --

It goes on easily and smoothly.  Although it comes out looking 'white,' (it's the sunscreen), it didn't seem to have color on my face.
It has SPF 15 sunscreen.  Why doesn't every foundation and primer have sunscreen?  This is perfect for wear to and from the office.
I am 54 and have oily skin.  Even on a humid Iowa day, at the end of the day, after using this product, I still had a relatively matte finish rather than a big oil slick, and my foundation was still in place, i.e. it hadn't slid off the way it usually does.

Things that gave me pause about this product --

It took me a while to figure out how to get it open.  I know, how hard can it be, right?  The chrome lid is a pull-off, not a twist off.  THEN, the semi-conical "spout" does twist 180 degrees from "off" to "on"  So, two steps, which is kinda weird.

The reason I can't love this product --

I have oily, blemish-prone skin.  I'd gone 4 weeks without a breakout but by the end of the first day with this primer, I had three new blemishes.  To be totally fair, I have NEVER found ANY primer that doesn't make me breakout.  It's not an irritation at all, just blemishes.  So if you don't have blemish-prone skin and have used other primers successfully, I would recommend this one, because I really did like the feel, the performance and the sunscreen.  Unfortunately, it's just not suitable for my blemish-prone skin.
summary: Love the performance and sunscreen, but, like every other primer I've tried, it gave me zits

reviewText: This product is so smooth and silky when I applied it. It also has a very light scent that I don't mind at all. The bottle packaging is a bit bulky for the amount of product it contains and takes up unnecessary space in my makeup drawer, thus the 4 star rating. Love it and definitely recommend it!

Ive heard of Bliss spas but nothing about their products and I really couldn't find out much except they are distributed by Hatchbeauty in California.

The active ingredient is titanium dioxide, which is an opacifier . It has been used for years in food, paint and sunscreen and the purified type is considered safe for human use.

First the dispenser..meh. After turning the lid to on and squeezing I couldn't get the product out without un-screwing the lid. The titanium dioxide does a good job of covering small freckles and has a matte finish. I don't know where they get the tinted part of the description.

Would I pay the current price of almost $30 for I oz? No, Im not that impressed.  Three stars for just O.K.

Living in the South, you really need a good primer to set your foundation or you will sweat it off within a few minutes of stepping out in the heat and humidity.  I have used DHC Velvet Coat, Clarins Beauty Balm and the Body Shop Vitamin C as primers.

I like that this has a SPF in it.  The consistency was thin and I did have my doubts about use.  But it went on like a regular moisturizer but it quickly smoothed over my skin.  I've used this with powder foundation and cream.  This primer kept both intact and even though I did sweat from the car to the office, there was no loss of coverage.

The one thing I didn't like is the application.  I'm used to a pump and this has a top and the opening twists.  Just an oddity to look out for.
summary: bliss Mad About Smooth Smoothing Primer

reviewText:
a primer with sunscreen that they recommend reapplying every 2 hours if out in the sun continuously between 10am and 2 pm (basically if you are sunbathing on a beach or by a pool or out golfing or playing tennis or boating etc).

It went on my face light and smooth. I have been using for a week and have not had any negatives issues or reactions. Worked well with my foundation.

Active Ingredient: Titanium Dioxide 6.90%

Inactive Ingredients: Cyclopentasiloxane, Isododecane, Glyceryl Behenate, PEG-10 Dimethicone, Polysilicone-11, Alumina, Water, Methicone, Lauryl Polyglyceryl-3 Polydimethylsiloxyethyl, Cyclopentasiloxane, Prunus Persica (Peach) Fruit Extract, Vitis Vinifera (Grape) Seed Extract, Oenothera Biennis (Evening Primrose) Root Extract, Jasminum Officinale (Jasmine) Extract, Amaranthus Caudatus Seed Extract, Ethylhexylglycerin, Phenoxyethanol.
summary: bliss Mad About Smooth Smoothing SPF 15 Mineral Primer

reviewText: I know the secret to using this. The tube it's dispensed from is a bad design, the plastic is way too thick to easily squeeze the primer from the tube. You can't just toss this into your make-up bag, it needs to sit with the cap (silver part) on standing on end. I have to leave it in my medicine cabinet so it stays upright. It's not so easy to get out but that's the only way it works for me. Once out of the tube, I love this primer. It's thin, just takes a little to cover my face. Gives a slight glow and hides any redness I may have. I rarely use foundation, but my Physicians Formula bronzer Physicians Formula Murumuru Butter Bronzer, Light, 0.38 Ounce looks wonderful applied over this primer and stays on almost all day. Good physical, not chemical, sunscreen. I'd really like SPF 30 instead, but sometimes when the SPF is amp-ed up, it makes the lotion sticky. This isn't sticky, but it does have a slight sunscreen scent, but I have to press my nose right against my skin to smell it. Bliss needs to re-think the container design. I'd give this primer 5 stars if I didn't have to fight the tube it comes in.
summary: Wonderful primer once you get it out of the horribly-designed packaging

reviewText: This product is great for my face it leaves my skin soft and smooth which makes it easy to put the rest of my makeup on.  I wish that getting this out of the tube was easy.  It is very hard to get the product out.  I took away two whole stars because I can't always get the product out to use it.
summary: Nice product if I can get it out of the packaging!

reviewText:
I'm a bit leery about primers these days. I made the mistake of using a silicone-based primer with a water-based foundation, and it was a holy mess! If you ever find that your new foundation is pilling up or only lasting a few hours before it disappears, it might be because your primer and foundation aren't soul mates. Basically you use water with water, and silicone with silicone.

How to tell? Check the ingredients list. Bliss Mad About Smoothing primer is silicone based, and works nicely with silicone primers (look for the -cone or -ane words at the top of the description. The products with the biggest concentration are listed highest up in the ingredients list.) You should also be aware that this primer contains titanium dioxide, if that's a concern for you. Some people are sensitive to it.

Here's Bliss's ingredients, taken from their website: Active Ingredient: Titanium Dioxide 6.90% Inactive Ingredients: Cyclopentasiloxane, Isododecane, Glyceryl Behenate, PEG-10 Dimethicone, Polysilicone-11, Alumina, Water, Methicone, Lauryl Polyglyceryl-3 Polydimethylsiloxyethyl, Cyclopentasiloxane, Prunus Persica (Peach) Fruit Extract, Vitis Vinifera (Grape) Seed Extract, Oenothera Biennis (Evening Primrose) Root Extract, Jasminum Officinale (Jasmine) Extract, Amaranthus Caudatus Seed Extract, Ethylhexylglycerin, Phenoxyethanol.

Now to the primer: it went on with that silky feel you get from silicon products. Spread nicely, and my silicone based foundation worked well with it. Very thin and lightweight, which works well for my skin type. I didn't have any problems with it (but be aware, my skin is very hearty and isn't at all sensitive. YMMV.)
summary: Pleasant silicone-based primer; just check ingredients if you have sensitivities

reviewText: Would love to know how this product works but can't even get it out of the bottle.  There's an arrow that you are supposed to line up with "on" for open and "off" for closed.  That didn't work.  Tried aligning the arrow with "off" in case the bottle was assembled wrong.  That didn't work either.  Went online and asked if anyone else had a problem with the bottle.  Another user with the same issue said to try turning the top only half way.  That didn't work.  My husband tried using brut force and eventually got the product to squirt out all over the counter, breaking the twist cap, or so we thought.  I tried squeezing the bottle, but no matter which way I turned the top I couldn't get the product to come out.  After thing for several more minutes, I just gave up.  Then, 2 drops oozed out on the counter.  I dabbed those on my face and the postage stamp size area did feel soft and smooth but when I tried to get more product out of the bottle, it stopped working yet again.  I give up!

I rarely wear makeup.  When I do, applying this primer underneath gives me a smoother looking face.  Worn without makeup, it's colorless, and it makes the skin on my face feel baby soft and smooth.  I have unusually sensitive skin, and this didn't cause any irritation at all.  I like that it contains sunscreen, as my face is protected when I go outside.

It does have a bit of a learning curve to dispense the lotion, and it took me a few minutes to figure it out.  Pull the silver top off, then twist the pointy top to the counter clockwise (or clockwise if you're holding the bottle upside down).

I don't think this was exactly what I was expecting, but it does do what it promises, block sun.  My main issue with it is I am having trouble with the lid, you turn it 180 degrees to the "open" arrow and nothing comes out.  I can turn it half way back and get a little to come out, I guess mine is defective.  Once it does come out it is bright white and pretty runny.  It does go on your face smooth and blends in well so the white-factor doesn't bother me much.  I have been to the pool wearing it and it protected very well, which is why I would buy this.  Overall very pleased!
summary: Lid is hard to open but it works good once you can get it out!

reviewText:
I haven't had much experience with primers since I use a moisturizer with sunscreen under my foundation and felt primer would be one too many layers on my face.

This is a white thin liquid and has spf 15 sunscreen.  I decided to use this without my usual moisturizer.  This fills in my pores and makes my foundation look extra smooth.  I tried it first with liquid foundation and found that, as with all the other sunscreens which rely on titanium dioxide I've tried, in sunlight that white opaque chemical made my foundation color look more muddy.  I prefer chemical sunscreens for this reason.

I then tried it with my powder foundation, which as the moment is Maybelline, a surprisingly great powder.  The issue was not there with the shade turning muddy.  I assume that the powder does not react to the titanium and instead floats on top of it.  With this combination my skin looks incredible and that includes in bright sunlight.

I tend to get cysts if there are certain chemicals in facial products but this caused no cysts or irritations.  I do see a huge difference in the smoothness of my skin with the powder foundation over it and will keep using this.
summary: This works well with a powder foundation

reviewText:
As far as primers go, this latest entry into the field from bliss is pretty darn nice. I tend to sweat off my makeup by mid-day thanks to facial hyperhydrosis, so finding a good primer has been a long journey. Some worked but caused major breakouts, some were fantastic with my skin but didn't work more than a few hours. DHC Velvet Coat is a favorite, so is Smashbox Photo Finish. My current primer has been benefit's POREfessional which is not only very skin friendly but last's through even humid, muggy days when it's like stepping into a sauna any time you have to go outside. So I set aside this primer to give the one from bliss a try.

First, this primer is lighter than I expected. If I have any dry spots on my face or get lazy and skip my moisturizer (also with SPF), the POREfessional or Velvet Coat is enough to prevent any problems with that dryness showing up once my makeup is finished. I purposefully skipped moisturizer one day to see how this would perform. Bad decision. This primer is light and thin, like a toning lotion. I'm used to primers that go on a bit thicker and leave your skin feeling velvety smooth and allow foundation to be easily applied. When applying foundation over this bliss primer without using moisturizer first, it took more work to get the foundation evenly blended out. For the other trial days I used moisturizer like normal and while not as smooth a 'canvas' as with the other types of primers, my foundation did apply a good deal smoother and easier.

As for staying power, I'd have to give this about a seven out of 10. Up here in the northeast we had a lovely stretch of humid weather that had everyone feeling soggy within moments of walking outside. Still, this held up pretty well on a few days of running around doing errands, going to appointments and meetings, and walking around during a local town's Second Saturday events. It doesn't stop the shine as well as my other primers do, so I need to blot and powder a couple more times than usual.

Price-wise this primer is cheaper per ounce than Velvet Coat, POREfessional, or Smashbox. I really like that it has SPF in the mix for added sun protection, and that it doesn't bother my skin. I wish it made my skin feel smoother for foundation application, but that's really just personal nitpicking. Though it's not as hardworking has my other heavier primers, I think this one will be excellent for cooler/cold weather when I don't need that heaviness. I like using Hourglass Veil Mineral Primer for that time, but oi, is it ever expensive. Hopefully this bliss primer will turn out to be a great -  and cheaper - alternative.
summary: Nice, light primer likely better suited for cooler weather

reviewText:
Even the best foundation can't seem to smooth out the pores on my nose.
I've tried a couple of primer brands, and boy, they really do help.
What sets this one apart, is that if I'm otherwise having a 'good skin day', I don't even need foundation.
It not only fills in pores to make them dissappear, but seems to even out my uneven skin tone.
My combination skin still needs a moisturizer everywhere but my nose, but on a good day, this is my new makeup hack for quick and easy best-face-forward.
Don't even need sun protection as it has SPF 15!

I absolutely love this liquid liner! The felt tip makes application so easy to apply. I couldn't believe how long it lasted too. I have oily lids and at the end of the day it still looked like I jjust applied it. I'm already planning on purchasing more. Love i!

I am a fan of the new liquid eyeliners (well, new relative to the old ones; this type has been around for a number of years). It's like using a very fine, tapering felt tip marker to easily achieve either a very thin line, perfect for tight-lining, or you can make a thicker line and even feather it out if you so desire. It works well, lasts well, doesn't smear, smudge or raccoon eye. Why the poor rating? It arrived virtually dried out, and the price is outrageous, considering it was made in China! It is higher than the Japanese brands. Worse, the Bliss company couldn't have been less helpful in rectifying this problem. Avoid - there are so many better lines out there, especially at the high price point.
summary: Highlty pigmented, but product arrived almost dried out and company refused to make good on this. Made in China.

reviewText:
My wife's response

LOVED this eyeliner!!!  It is the blackest black and glides onto the lid super smoothly and allows for a very precise line.  Bonus:  It lasted all day!  I am a bit of a makeup junkie, and have tried several  pen eyeliners.  This one tops them all!  The big question at this point is how long it will last.  These pen-style liners can dry up fairly quickly, but based on the quality so far, I expect that it will last at least as long as my others (about a month or so).  I will be sure to update if it dries up too quickly, but don't anticipate that.  Would definitely recommend to a friend!

Traditionally, I use a pencil or crayon type eyeliner. This was my first real/serious try with liquid liner. I think I tried it once when I was in college (punk rock was the rage), but it was awkward, a little messy and took longer than the pencil. But now, years later, when offered the opportunity to try this product for my honest opinion, I thought why not? I don't regret it and overall, Im pleased with bliss On the Line Liquid Liner. After a little practiceok a lotI was able to line my eyes without looking like a clown. The applicator is thin but you can make a thicker/bolder line by tilting the applicator. What I liked: (1) this eyeliner dries quickly and doesnt smear (at least not that I noticed). I didn't get raccoon eyes and had a pretty polished look. (2) This liner comes off easily. I simply use a gentle face cleanser and it comes off pretty easily. (3) This product doesnt irritate the eye. So why not 5 stars. Well, there is one drawback. (1) This liquid liner is a little pricey (0.016 fl oz for approximately $24). And while I like the product, I am a little torn. As a consumer on a budget, I am not sure if I would purchase this product, especially if I can find a comparable product at my local drug or discount store. I would have a hard time justifying the cost.
summary: Exciting product just not sure I can justify the cost.

reviewerName: Gina Pera, Adult ADHD Expert and Author
reviewText:
This is my first attempt with liquid eyeliner. I usually use a "smudgy"stick, so this will take some getting used to.

The applicator seems first rate. Very fine point. Very clear line.  I love that the liner cleans off easily, leaving no raccoon eyes.

This particular "operator", however, needs to watch more YouTube videos on how to apply liquid eyeliner when you have very thick eyelashes that naturally curve up!

Raised in the 60's loving all the wild makeup, I was always wearing eye liner...but...THIS product, THIS brush, makes the job of applying eye makeup a joy!  I remember the clunky brushes and trying to trim them to a better point lol!  Honestly, this product glides on and you can CONTROL the line for thin or thick lines....I think this will soon become the 'darling' of women's makeup bags!  Very easy to remove too.  I would definitely suggest this to anyone.

My Holy Grail liquid liner is Kat Von D's Tattoo liner, but this one is really great.  I've worn it a few times now, and it lasts all day and provides a nice black line that leans more towards a sheen than a matte in color.  The tip reminds me of the Stila pen, but I actually think I prefer this one.

The tip on this is great for applying both thick or thin lines.  I can't seem to do a cat eye for the life of me, but this does help me make a small kitten flick easily.

If your eyes water a lot from allergies, as mine do, this liner will really stay in place and not budge.

One tip if you make a mistake is to dip a Q-tip/cotton bud in a bit of makeup remover (I love Sonia Kashuk's Remove, which you can get at Target, and which is water-like in its consistency), and then clean up your mistakes or the edge of your line with it.

It's also helped me a lot to watch makeup tutorials by MakeUp Geek and Lisa Eldridge; they have great videos that show you how to use this kind of eyeliner if you've never used it before.
summary: Really nice tip makes it easy to achieve thick or fine lines -- and stays put even with allergy-prone eyes

reviewText: I have used many brands of liquid liner, gel liner, gel pot liners, gel stick liners, liquid brush liners and all other types of powder brush liners, liquid pen liners and stick liners.  This liner went on very easily and glides much smoother than other brands I have purchased.  I attempted a wing line and it did bleed out a little thicker than I would have liked.  The color is a bit darker than I expected but I did like the boldness it provided doing an all around egyption eye liner style.  I gave this product 4 stars because the first line I screwed up and when I wiped it off the products smeared into a grey smudge all over my eyelid that took a good swab of eye makeup remover to get clean.

The foundation itself goes on smoothly - it is a thin texture so it does need to be rubbed in a bit in order to avoid streakiness. But once on, it stays with only a minor 'oily' kind of feel when first applied.  It provides light SPF protection as well to protect skin during the day.  The color, was as I expected and not too orangey or pink.

The bottle has a gimmicky applicator - a 'tear dropper' type of cap in which you can squeeze droplets onto your makeup sponge or fingers.  After about five uses, though, it does start to gunk up.  Not as problematic if you use this daily and so will go through the bottle fairly quickly.  But if you don't wear makeup daily, it will fully gunk up and be rendered fairly useless over time.  I would have preferred a regular applicator and not have to pay for the silly and fairly useless gimmick.

In all, I like the coverage and feel of the 'serum foundation.'  It didn't feel chalky from the SPF ingredients and my face did feel protected.  I haven't noticed the 'glow' enhancing my wrinkles but I'll be watching for it.

This is a light foundation in a very liquid state.

Application is easy. A dropper mechanism dispenses desired amount of foundation to apply.

Found the makeup non irritating.

Generally, I choose a shade that is one of the lightest.  On the Bliss color chart Buff would seem perfect for me.
However, it appears an odd tone when dispensed, more light yellow orange.  It does blend in however.

Added sunscreen of 20 is a bonus.  Additional layers of foundation applied are not noticably heavy.

If you wear a concealer, you will still need to do so.

I am very fair-skinned and have sensitive skin. More often than not, most foundations cause skin irritation or just do not look natural; however, this is not the case with this foundation. I really like this. It is light and gentle to sensitive skin including skin conditions like Rosacea. It washes off easily with Burt's Bees sensitive skin facial cleansing towelettes.
summary: Great foundation- even for sensitive skin!

reviewText:
This is a lovely, soft, buttery foundation that comes with an applicator tip so that you can dot the foundation on your face before blending it in.  It goes on quite smoothly and doesn't settle into wrinkles. As advertised, it is more of a tinted moisturizer than a makeup. There is no perfume that I can detect, and this particular buff color seems a bit darker than the online photo. I am very pale, but this foundation blended with my skin quite well (I used it very sparingly), and lasted a good eight hours

Coverage is medium--it blends but does not conceal blemishes and moles, but overall, it does even the skin tone nicely.

All in all, this is a great foundation for mature skin because it does not cake in wrinkles. It does not cover completely, but it does leave an even, somewhat dewy finish, and it has a SPF 20 sunscreen.

I received this foundation in the shade fondue, not buff. I really was hoping for a 'exglowsion' but it didn't work for me. The foundation comes with an odd shaped dropper. It doesn't take much of the serum to cover your face. I was hoping it would be lighter coverage. This looked too cakey and sort of dry on me. I'm a fan of bliss, but the serum foundation didn't look good on me.

As other gals have indicated, the bottle is a pain to deal with. Once you get an amount you need to apply, it goes on less smoothly than anticipated. It is very liquid, but seemed prone to streaking and not blending well. After a few hours of wear, I noticed that the few lines on my face had creased with foundation making them stand out. I'd have to smooth it out every now and then to keep my eye area from looking older than it does out of the shower, NO THANK YOU! I have very smooth skin for my age and have no desire to highlight the wrinkles I do have. I think the problem is the sunscreen they used, it felt like other sunscreens I have tried that are slippery but streaky when applied, but settle into any area that the skin creases. Too bad, the color was very nice and sheer at first.

I like this for summer.  The color was about what I expected for 'nude'.  (I got the "nude" shade. While that is a bit dark for me normally, because I normally wear ivory, it is very sheer and I have a bit of a summer tan, so it works well.  It contains 20 SPF, which I really like.  Usually the highest SPF I see in makeup is 15, so this is a bit of extra protection.

It contains argan oil and evening of primrose oil.  I **LOVE** evening of primrose oil on my face- no oil has worked better for me.  I keep a 4 ounce bottle and often wear it before bedtime.  This does contain dimethicone too, so it has that silky feel.  I'm not that big a fan of dimethicone though.  It feels good, and it is rated as fairly safe, but I am just not sure skin breathes as well using products with it.  This one feels like it does, it is very light.

Though the bottle applicator is quite different from anything I've ever used for a foundation,  I like it ok.  It works like an eye dropper, but the top of the cap has a button that you can mash that dispenses it out the bottom of the dropper. It's fairly easy to control the amount I get, and its easy to get out.  It seems like it might contribute to some product waste as the bottle is used up and at the end though.

The look of this makeup is dewy.  It's good at smoothing out fine lines, and it definitely minimizes pores.  I have not tried it with the makeup base yet, though I hope to in a week or two.  I'll update my review when I do.  It lasts very well - on me it lasts several hours.  Today I was in the pool and the hot sun and it stayed up. (I didn't get my face wet though!)  A bit of sweating doesn't take it off.

Coverage is sheer but can be built up to about a medium level.  It has not seemed at all shiny- it has just a very natural low level of shine.
I don't detect much of a small at all, it's certainly not unpleasant in that way.
summary: Very natural level of shine, minimizes pores well, smooths very fine lines/crepe - contains argan & evening primrose oil

reviewText:
This review is for the color Nude. I don't like it; I wanted Buff. I don't like the modified eyedropper either or the finish on my skin. Although the bottle is very pretty with a striking chrome top and stylish lettering, the system is clunky and wasteful. The chrome top screws off to reveal an eyedropper-like tube running through the middle of the bottle. The chrome top has a button that can be depressed to pick up or release drops of foundation from the eyedropper tube (much as a standard eyedropper's rubber bulb is pressed). If it were possible to keep the tube clean and only get the foundation inside the tube, the system might work. But the tube itself gets thickly coated with foundation that impedes efficient dropping at the eyedropper's end. The entire tube quickly gets glopped up with thickened foundation.

As the foundation came out of the dropper, I saw that the color (Nude) was an odd pinky gold that looked extremely artificial when dabbed on my light skin. The oddness of the color dissipated a lot as I spread it, but it never looked right on me. The Buff probably would have been better. But the texture was unworkable for me. It would not spread smoothly even though I prepared my skin with moisturizer and primer. I tried it a second time with moisturizer, no primer, and had even more of a problem. Finally, I tried it with a lot of moisturizer and that was the best. Still, my fine lines were emphasized by the foundation, which became dry and almost powdery as it set. My older skin looked even older by the time my makeup was finished. And it had almost a chalky look. I immediately washed it off and will not use it again.
summary: Not for my dry, lightly wrinkled skin; has a chalky finish, too

reviewText:
I ordered BLISS EXGLOWSION SERUM FOUNDATION, 1 FL OZ for my teenage daughter. To say that she loves it may be an understatement. She loved the eye dropper applicator. Said it reduces waste. Its easy to apply, and a little went a long way. It is light feeling, as if you weren't wearing anything.
Color: Buff
Product Description
From our spa to your skin youve put your trust in us to care for your skin with our legendary spa services and world famous skin care products. Now were excited to introduce the next step to achieving complexion perfection. We like to call it tinted skincare. Weve poured our innovative spa ingredients and advanced technologies into our tinted skincare products, so youll know they're good for you and your skin. Spatacular results: a foundation like youve never felt before. Exglowsion serum foundation utilizes our exclusive oxygen technology to help revitalize skin for a healthy, glowing, youthful-looking appearance. With a blend of vitamins and ceramides, this product helps moisturize and enhance skins appearance, while broad spectrum spf 20 helps prevent against sunburn. Remarkably lightweight, this formula provides buildable coverage that feels velvety smooth.

Usually, I don't care about the packaging of a cosmetic-it's what inside that counts-but this is the worst packaging I have ever encountered in over 20 years of wearing make-up. Specifically, it's got a weird sort of design where you're supposed to unscrew the cap and pump out the foundation. However, in my product, the tube was bent out of shape and due to being tossed around in the mail, a ton of foundation managed to pool up in the cap. What a waste! Also, this stuff is very thick and doesn't wash off easy-probably due to the high concentration of zinc oxide and titanium dioxide. Even with repeated washings of hot soapy water, it stayed on my hands and on the bottle-and this is before I ever applied it to my face!

When I finally put it on, it was okay. It was thicker and darker than I expected although it was not nearly as dark once I applied it to my face. It is a decent, medium to full coverage foundation with a good SPF but that is all. It's nothing great and the horrible packaging is a drawback.

I got this as freebie, so I am not out any money. However, if I had paid for this, I would ask for a refund.

Be cautioned and avoid an unpleasant experience that I did. When I unscrewed the cap from the bottle of Bliss Exglowsion Serum, the product dripped directly into my lap and it actually stained my pants. Aside from the precarious application system of a tube in a top, I really like this foundation because it is lightweight, non-smelly and produces no skin sensitivity for me. The Nude color actually turns out to be likely the one I would have selected had I tried it prior to ordering. It lambs to the yellow which i often expect in makeup skin colors in lighter shades. Since I'm not a fan of heavy foundations, this is excellent for my desires and because it is not drying, my face doesn't feel taught as the day progresses. It has a minimal sunscreen of SPF20, so I still use another in addition to this, but that is not necessary for everyone. This is a really good product.

I have used Bliss products in the past. The Lemon Sage Body Butter is one of my all time favorites. When this product came up, I decided to give it a try.

Basic Info - The foundation is very thin and liquidy. It releases from a dropper. I was testing it on my hand and when I pressed the dispenser, I had a flood of fluid. Once I blended it in, though, it provided good coverage. The next morning, when I applied to my face, I was very careful to dispense only a small amount onto the foam applicator I use to apply makeup.

How did it work - Even though the liquid foundation is very thin, it provides a nice coverage level. It also allows for building of the coverage for problem spots without looking thick on your face. The product spreads evenly. Even though it is listed as providing SPF coverage, there was no suntan lotion smell, which I appreciate because I *hate* that smell.

On the negative side - I am a woman of a certain age, and have the laugh lines proving I have had a good time along the way. The Serum seemed to settle into those lines, emphasizing them. This makes me unhappy, which makes me frown, which causes more lines...it's a vicious cycle.

Though I thought I was getting Buff, I ended up with Nude, which is fine. I have a very light complexion, and my usual choices are in the Nude/Buff spectrum. The liquid blends very well into my skin.

Bottom line - I like the coverage and the weight of the product. It's thin, light, and doesn't feel like I am wearing makeup. I dislike the fact that it settles into my laugh lines and emphasizes them. As every woman knows, the bad dramatically outweighs the good when it comes to how you look. So for younger people, whose good life isn't reflected on their face yet, I would say this product would be a good fit. For those of us who have been around the block, yelling "Woo-Hoo!!" , not so much.

The foundation comes in a glass container with a dropper and is easily applied and blended into the skin.  This Exglowsion contains ceramides and vitamins which are help fight aging.  Like most good foundations, this has SPF 20.

 While it's a bit thicker than the Laroche Possy Effacer BB Blur creme/mousse foundation that I've been using, the Exglowsion doesn't feel oily nor does it feel like it clogs the skin.  I tried this foundation during a heatwave. Though it was in the mid-90s in the subway with pretty awful conditions, and the Exglowsion worked well. The foundation didn't feel too thick and it stayed on without having to be touched up. It washed off with my regular cleansing soap, it wasn't necessary to use an oil based cleanser.

 Also, the Buff color was a good match for my light Asian skin.
summary: Feels light on the skin and survived the heat wave

reviewText:
I usually wear tinted moisturizer with SPF that I sometimes mix with plain moisturizer to make it thinner and more sheer.  Since this is called a foundation, I thought it might be too heavy -- but it is so sheer and goes on so well --- much better than the tinted moisturizers I have been using  (Lancome and Laura Mercier).  And the coverage is really good, considering how lightweight this is.  I received Nude, which is a very middle of the spectrum shade.  The product is so sheer that this color works for me.  I am usually about NW25.  It feels light and non greasy.

I like that this is a physical sunscreen with 5.75% titanium dioxide and 3.70% zinc oxide. I also like that there is no fragrance whatsoever.  This really exceeded my expectations.  Very happy with this and will almost certainly repurchase.

Very lightweight, natural looking foundation. The coverage is medium but can be layered. I actually received color Nude and it was good match for my NC 25 skin. Maybe slightly to pale but it is summer now. Nothing a tad of bronzer couldn't fix. The color is neutral and I prefer yellow base, yet it wasn't bad at all.

My only concern is that I'm on the drier side and this foundation is better for oily skin. It did gibe me nice dewy look, but at the same time it was matte. I prefer more hydrating products. It wasn't sitting in the lines which is great but it was sucking my moisture out. So for drier skin I recommend good occlusive cream under.

I have a huge scar down the left side of my face (YOU CAN THANK Erlenmeyer's Laboratories for that one...be sure to check out that mess)..ANYWAY, this foundation works great in covering my scar and evening my skin tone which has a few blemish scars and a little adult acne (I am 37).  The color I received was buff and looked very nice with my summer tan.  RECOMMENDED.

I first tried this foundation on a day that was extremely humid and 94 degrees Fahrenheit.  Heat index was 104.  The product worked great, working more like my own skin, than a coverage on it. It is very lightweight and applies smoothly and effortlessly.  I got "Buff", and was surprised to see that it matched my skin tone perfectly (more on the color later).

I sprayed on my usual toner with witch hazel; let that dry, while I gave this foundation a good shake-up (holding down the button on top to allow all the foundation to re-mix).  The lid unscrews and releasing the button on top sucks foundation up into the dropper.  The foundation applies a little lighter than what you would expect, but the "whiteness" disappeared while I was lightly blending it in.

Hot and humid as it was that day (still is....) that I almost decided to not ride my bike around the campground.  But I did.  And it was a great trial for this foundation from Bliss.  It allowed my skin to breathe normally.  Sweat did not ooze or hover underneath the coverage.  Felt like I was not wearing anything.  Sweat dripping down my face did not sting my eyes.

Is the SPF 20 strong enough?  For me, yes.  I tan easily and very seldom burn--haven't burned in years and years because I usually wear something that has SPF 20 in it.

How does the color compare with what I've been using?  My usual foundation are two Bare Minerals products:  Bareskin (lighter weight for summertime and SPF 20) and Complexion Rescue (a bit richer for the colder, drier months and SPF 30).  This "Buff" color of this Bliss product compares nicely to the Bareskin Bare Natural 07 and the Complexion Rescue Suede 04.  This Bliss Buff color is a very nice balance of tint:  Not too much orange, not too much yellow, not too much pink.  I can't do too much orange, yellow or pink pigment.  Buff works well for me.

The color shown on the product page is very much the way it actually is.
summary: Glides on easily, gives decent coverage; allows my sweaty skin to breathe in hot humid weather

reviewText:
This is decent foundation.  The color/tint is probably good for me only for the summer; I will need something bluer and paler when (if?) summer actually backs off.

But my assessment of the product isn't based on anything about the color.  I just wish that--like other base-like make-up I own--there was sunscreen built into the product.  The medical common sense these days is to always wear sunscreen on exposed body parts (including, of course, your face).  So one has to put sunscreen on before putting this make-up on, which both compromises its coverage,  and makes one feel like one is wearing armor. Having to layer on extra stuff in summer just isn't fun.

UPDATE:  4 July
Thanks to the commentators who inspired me to take another look at the enclosed promotional/descriptive lit and to use a magnifying glass to read all of the tiny white print on the bottle more carefully.

Apparently there IS sunscreen in the product, according to the bottle. This is good, and the error is mine....but it was not simply an error of carelessness. The promotional literature and the info on the bottle are different, and not consistent; indeed even the color/tint listed in the lit and the color/tint listed on the bottle are different.  I think  that the lit may actually be intended for a different product.
summary: Pretty good coverage.**Note that enclosed promo literature & the (tiny) white writing on bottle may not give consistent info

reviewText: I saw no color in this spray on application at all....which might be a good thing since the makeup underneath is tinted one would not want tint added to that.  I am a bit concerned it contains butane and alcohol which are highly flammable.  Why would one want this on their face.  I realize most make up products contain some alcohol but not combine with butane.  This product has an offensive odor when sprayed although it dries quickly and the odor seems to disappear.  I do not think I will be using this on my face.  I would prefer to reapply makeup than have this sprayed onto my facial tissue.  Perhaps it would work best for 'show' makeup or the stage makeup.
summary: bliss Get set & Go Makeup setting spray

reviewText:
I really need to start checking product ingredients before I commit to reviewing the item. bliss Get Set & Go Makeup Setting Spray lists the following: Denatured alcohol comes first, Dimethyl ether is next, which may the the propellent. The third ingredient is Butane. IF that isn't enough to stop you, the rest of the list contains Water, Aloe Barbadensis Leaf Juice, Kaolin, Dimethicone, Isopentyldiol, Isododecane, Hexylene Glycol, Perfluorononyl Dimethicone, PPG-3 Benzyl Ether Myristate, Neopentyl Glycol Diheptanoate, PEG-9 Dimethicone/PEG-9 Olive Phosphate, Acrylates/Steareth-20 Methacrylate Copolymer, Caprylyl Glycol, Phenoxyethanol.

I first sprayed the Get Set & Go Makeup Setting Spray on my hand, to make sure it wasn't going to irritate my skin. I then planned to dab a bit on a spot on my face, before spraying on a face full. The smell of alcohol was so strong, I read the list of ingredients. If having alcohol as a first ingredient isn't enough, the Butane certainly was.

I do set my makeup, because I have dry skin, and I find that a quick spray makes my makeup look more natural, less dry and made up. I use a spray I make out of filtered water and essential oil. That is what I will continue to use. That works great for me. Testing the bliss was a whim, as I have found some great beauty products and make up here at Amazon. I just can't imagine spraying this on my face, even once, never mind on a frequent basis.
summary: Butane? Yes, and other interesting things.

reviewText:
I wanted to give this 2 stars when I first opened it and saw how little I received for a price list of $24! I was unimpressed. But, after applying it (despite the scent I didn't care for), I was ready to give it a chance, since it did seem to "set" my makeup.

Maybe it's not this product? But, I don't see the "tint" they are talking about. I sprayed some on my inner arm and looked with a bright light and I just don't see it - looks clear to me. Which is not a problem for me as I'd not want a tint over my makeup. It did irritate my skin a little where I applied it on my inner arm, though it didn't on my face so ? Mystery to me.

I suppose I just don't "get" these types of beauty products because I'm not a "girly girl" who spends a lot of money on certain cosmetic type products for which I can't tell whether they are doing me any good or not, and charging too much to do it. While I'll spend extra on serums and face creams and maybe my foundation, these type of products are puzzling to me.

This is my second Bliss product to try. The first was an "oxygen mist" for which the scent was wonderful and it felt great spritz on my face, but it was $38 a bottle! Way too much for my budget. That's how I feel about this Bliss product. $24 for a small can (see photo - it is a tiny can) of product is too much for my budget for something I'll likely not use enough to warrant the cost.

I tested this setting spray by first applying my makeup, spraying the Bliss, waiting a second (it dried very fast!), and then dabbing with a tissue to see how much makeup came off. Not much! I swiped a little harder and a little more came off but not much. I was impressed. I then went for a hike (this is summer as I write this) and climbed up the mountain so I'd break a sweat. I then dabbed my face again and was impressed that not much came off on the tissue. I was considering giving it 4 stars despite the ridiculous price.

Though, I will say here that I didn't care for the scent - a kind of alcohol smell that followed me around for a while. It does dissipate and for that I'm glad. It reminded me of those old hair sprays -not pleasant. (However, their Bliss oxygen mist, alternatively, smelled so good and fresh! They should use the same scent for this product!).

Then once home, I washed off the spray and makeup (washes off easily by the way) and applied the same amount of makeup, but this time I did not spray the Bliss setting spray. I let my makeup "set" and then I did the tissue test. About the same amount of makeup came off. I then spritzed my face to moisten it, to mimic sweat, and there wasn't that much difference in the tissues of spray vs not spray. I conclude that the setting spray works a little bit, but not in the way here I am completely sure about it.

Perhaps the proof is in whether the makeup stays on longer throughout your day or evening. Since I work from home, I don't wear makeup all day. I suppose it could have its merits for long travel or a long night - and I'll try it out when I travel. I'm also going to let my friends who live in a very humid climate try it out and see what they think. If they report back they love it, I'll update my review.

So with the testing of "with spray" and "without spray" there was a little bit of difference but not enough for me to be excited about at this price. Just as with the Bliss oxygen mist spray, if they'd lower the price, I'd be interested in purchasing it.
