But at $24 for this tiny can, I think I'd find a less expensive alternative if I felt the need for a setting spray.

If you live in a humid climate - I'm in the mountains and do not - and if you don't mind spending a little more on products that probably have some good ingredients in them, you may benefit from this product.
summary: I don't get it, I guess

reviewText: I always seem to have issues with my makeup staying on a busy day.  I have tried other setting sprays, but I have not found one that I really liked.  I like bliss products in general and I feel like this lives up to the name.  It didn't seem at all sticky or tacky which was my main concern.  It really feels a bit refreshing.  I feel like my makeup lasted several hours longer than normal.
summary: but I have not found one that I really liked. I like bliss products in general and I ...

reviewText:
I am puzzled that this contains butaine which aside from gasoline or pepper spray is one of the  last things I want to be spraying on my face.
I have asthma.  I took a look at the ingredients and tossed this out.  I don't have an objection to alcohol in products as I use rubbing alcohol and also many cosmetics use a moisturizing type of alcohol but butaine which is highly flammable on the face is not ok.

They could have put this in a pump spray bottle, and I suppose any type of propellant ingredient would be a problem if sprayed on the face, but lighter fluid applied to my face, when I sometimes use a hot straightening iron on my bangs, sounds like a horror movie.
summary: Butaine in the ingredient list made me toss it

reviewText:
I admit that I was a little leery to try this because of the comment about a 'tint', but I think that's just because this belongs to a line of products that do provide a tint and this is the final part that helps to set the makeup. I do have a setting spray (a primer and setting spray from Smashbox, in fact) and have used Urban Decay's as well, so I have something to compare bliss' to, and I have to say, this aerosol  spray is really nice in that once you spray it on your face, your face feels dry and your makeup is set and doesn't appear wet at all. There's no 'splatter' or worry about the spray drying (especially if you're wearing glasses). HOWEVER, there is a scent, a chemical scent, that does linger for about an hour (maybe less) which while not too bad, I definitely notice. That's why it's not five stars.
But it works, it sets the makeup and it looks good. I'm used to the price considering the other sprays I've bought. Just wish the scent was better (or non-existent).
summary: works great as a makeup setter... but ugh, the scent

reviewText: It sprayed on in a fine mist. It seemed to go on evenly. I just didn't like how it felt on my skin. It felt sticky to me. I think it added some unnatural shine to my face too.

This delivers a very fine, fine mist.  It is in a aerosol type spray, and though it is loaded with chemicals, I really thought from the quality of the spray delivery that I would love it.  It has a bit of an odor, but it is more like chemicals and alcohol than perfume.  It quickly goes away, because this product dries quickly

It does not cause cosmetics to run or change color, and powder looks more natural.

It holds makeup on well for 3-4 hours.  After 3 hours my face feels stiff and dry with this product. I can't stand it much longer myself so I remove it.  It comes off with a soap based cleanser or Olay makeup remover towelettes.  It leaves my face dry though, even in this humid, muggy weather.

I can't recommend it if needed for more than about 3 hours.  It does prolong makeup wear on hot, sweaty days for a couple of hours,  so it might work well for a photo shoot or short special event.  I would never wear it daily.
summary: Like Hairspray for your face- the stiff hold

reviewText: When I checked the ingredients on this bottle, I was shocked as denatured alcohol is the first but Butane is the third ingredients. From typing it into Google it brought up this - "Butane is regarded as one of the more harmful volatile substances to inhale. Butane gas can cause what is known as 'sudden sniffing death', which occurs as a result of cardiac arrhythmia/arrest if the person is stressed or does heavy exercise during or soon after using." On reading more websites, it's not too harmful in small quantities at normal temperatures but in higher temperatures or closed spaces it can cause much harm. I only use these type of sprays in hot and humid climates and it seems like a butane product can do most damage in those conditions. It's also pretty expensive compared to some other more natural products that I've tried. There is a rosewater based spray that is very beneficial for you Mario Badescu Facial Spray with Aloe, Herbs and Rosewater and is priced very well. It does not set the makeup like some other sprays but it's a nice spray to keep the makeup looking fresh and new. I cannot recommend this product due to its ingredients. In terms of setting makeup, it does a moderate job. For a good makeup setting spray most users recommend the UD All Nighter setting spray that does not let the makeup budge and is cheaper than this product per ounce. Many showgirls have recommended it too, and it does not seem to contain butane. It keeps makeup on even in hot and humid conditions, with this spray, the makeup tends to start fading.
summary: Contains harmful butane, too expensive. There are better products.

reviewText:
I am a minimalist when it comes to make up. I always have been. I haven't been that interested in make up till just this past year, when I tried Ipsy. I have never used a make-up setting spray before and this one seems fun to try.

I was over at the lake this past weekend and I decided to try it. I basically used just eye shadow, blush, tinted moisturizer, powder and mascara. I sprayed the make up setting spray and it seems to hold up just fine all day, even when I was in the water. When I washed my face after swimming, the make up did come off, so it didn't completely wash away in the lake. So that is a plus.

There is no odor with this spray, not that I could see. I also didn't see any tint to it (and was not expecting to see a tint). You only have to use it once and it seems to help.

The only problem I have with this is that it is rather expensive for a small bottle. I know there are people who can afford this, but for me, I would have to decide whether or not I want to spend $24 for it. It depends on how long it lasts too.

If you like make-up and live somewhere it is hot and muggy, this might be a good investment for you. I enjoyed using ti and it does seem to help keep my make-up in place.

I've tried a few makeup setting sprays over the years like All Nighter Long-Lasting Makeup Setting Spray 1.0 oz by Salamander99,JAPONESQUE Makeup Setting Spray, 3 fl. oz., and Supergoop! SPF 50 Defense Refresh Setting Mist, 0.1 fl. oz. so I was curious to try the bliss Get Set & Go Makeup Setting Spray and see how it would compare. I don't tend to use makeup setting sprays everyday, but do rely on them when I really need my makeup look to last and know it could be exposed to adverse conditions (i.e. humidity), like weddings and other events or nights out. Generally when I'm using a setting spray I'm considering whether it sprays a fine, even mist (seems to give more even coverage with less product and sets more quickly than those with large droplets), whether it actually succeeds at making my makeup last longer, and whether it causes skin irritation. Based on those needs the UD All Nighter spray has been my holy grail to date. Would the bliss compare? I was curious to see. Since the other sprays I've tried to date have been great, but not *quite* UD level I was pleased with how much I liked this spray. It does seem to spray a pretty even and relatively fine mist, makes my makeup hold steady even in the face of heat and humidity, and it doesn't irritate my skin. It also set pretty quickly and didn't feels sticky, heavy, or tacky to the touch. I do feel like the UD might hold my makeup a bit more steady and a bit longer than this does, but because I'm clearly not doing scientific tests in a lab it's hard to 100% tell when it's close. Reading other reviews, yes, the ingredients can read a little scary, but that seems to be par for the course with many of these sprays. (It's basically like hair spray for your face, but without the stickiness.) If you're seeking something more natural I'd go the route of setting your makeup with a hydrating toner like Fresh Rose Floral Toner 250ml/8.4oz or Jurlique Balancing Mist, Rosewater, 3.3 Fluid Ounce. Having used those as well you're definitely not going to get the same results as with a dedicated setting spray, but it's helpful for those days when you want something liquid to set and may not want something as unnatural or heavy duty as a dedicated setting spray. As for the size, this does seem a tad small for the price (at the time of writing you can get the UD 4.0 oz container for just a little bit more). I personally prefer a smaller size as it's easier to tuck into my makeup bag and accordingly, often buy the travel sized version of setting sprays when they're available. I have the 3.4 fl. oz version of the Super Goop! for example, but because the bottle is so long it doesn't easily fit into my makeup bag and I don't use it as often as I should. But if the price per ounce matters to you, you'll definitely want to compare when buying. As well as whether any of the additional benefits of some sprays matter to you (i.e. additional SPF, oil-control, hydration, etc.) Overall though I've been quite impressed with this!
summary: On par with UD All Nighter

reviewText:
I don't usually give just one star because it was not B A D.  So these two stars are because of these negatives:  1)  I could detect no scent and thought there would be; 2)  I thought the price was prohibitive based on the small can; 3) The ingredients really blew me away.... Butane, come on!
Maybe I shall try to learn more about the properties of Butane but even if I did, I don't think I want it on my face.

On the positive side, I used my hand as my face, using the moisturizer, foundation, blush, lipstick and eyeshadow normally used.  I did not wash the back of this hand for the 8 hours a person generally works and at the end of that period, the makeup still looked good on the back of my hand.
Yes, I know the skin is different on my hand but the makeup would be the same.

I would buy this product if the ingredients were changed but maybe if they were, then the setting wouldn't be the same.
summary: It does keep your makeup on without touchups.

reviewText:
I do not see the need for this product. It contains a bunch of chemicals you are supposed to spray on your face to "set" your makeup. It makes your makeup last for a long time. I am not sure it actually does that -- my makeup situation at the end of the day was the same as always.

Here are my layers: I like powder on top of foundation on top of moisturizer. Maybe I will dab on eye cream or serum sometimes. But I don't need need this layer of chemicals on top. It doesn't seem to do anything.

If you feel you need setting spray, there are other formulas that contain herbs and healthier ingredients than this.

This bliss Go For The Bronze Powder Bronzer is glorious!  I received the "KISS ME CARAMEL" color which is the perfect one for my complexion.  Living in Arizona, a person would think that a lovely tan is the usual thing with all that sun.  Not so....the sun is much too severe and hot during the summer, so a bronzer is the way to still look tanned.  I am very fair and have to wear a hat to protect my face, as I've already had a skin cancer removed off my nose (now wear sunscreen religiously).  I was happy to try the bronzer to add some color to my face, and I was not disappointed!  The pressed powder bronzer is packaged in a beautiful mirrored compact, and a large mirror in the inside with the words "hey sunshine" printed on it.....sweet!  No brush provided but I usually save spare brushes from other compacts, or just use one of my bigger brushes.  The bronzer went on my face easily and smoothly, and for me just the one or two swipes is all I needed to look like I had a healthy glow.  There is mica in the mixture so there is a slight sparkle or twinkle on my face and throat, not sure why it was added but it is interesting.  Because of perspiration, I've had to apply the bronzer one more time, without any streaking.  This appears to be a very fine product, pricey, but you get what you pay for....well worth it.
summary: "Bliss bronzer" is much better for your face than those damaging sun rays!

reviewText: Let me say right off that I am truly impressed with this product.  I love to have a tan, a glowing look but the Temps here in Florida this year are just way too hot to sit out and stay in the sun.  However, we all know color on our face really helps us look better. So how did this work?  Listen I only had to use a small bit of it and my face looked so much better, had nice texture and just the right amount of color. I had good comments on it for the rest of the day.  So easy to put on, no mess at all.  This is a good one and I'm happy to recommend it to you.

I have begun to pay so much more attention to my skin as of late due to the fact I am now 37 and have always been a sun worshiper (and sometimes the tanning bed too...bad girl).  I really like this bronzer because it looks very natural while covering imperfections.  The best way to sculpt your face is to use a light highlighter right under your eyes and then suck your cheeks in and put the bronzer in that divot or dimple.  Regular blush can then be used on your cheek apples.  This makeup line seems very competitive with high-end brands and I RECOMMEND it.

I was excited to try this because I have long been familiar with the bliss brand, but hadn't tried any of their makeup products yet.  Their makeup line interested me because they described it as 'tinted skincare' and who doesn't want makeup that also has complexion boosting-benefits.  I was supposed to receive 'Coco-cabana' their darker bronzer, but actually received 'Kiss Me Caramel.'

Looking at the color in the pan it struck me as being pretty accurately named.  It's a warm-toned, caramel-colored bronzer with a ever so subtle shimmer.  I used it to contour my face along with Shimmer from the Smashbox Crush on Blush palette for my highlight.  I gently swept it just under my cheek bones, along the underside of my jawline, along my hairline, and the bridges of my nose.  When used with the Shimmer it makes for a contouring look that's perfect for a day look and adds more definition for my look.  For a night look I use it after the COVER FX Contour Kit in N Medium.  For my neutral toned light/medium skin I think this shade is perfect.  However, I do have friends whose skin trends more cool and who struggle to find a bronzer that works for their skintone and for them, I'm not sure this would work.

I also liked the longevity.  It stayed all day and I only needed to touch up after work for the night out.

As for the promised skin benefits, I'm not sure I've seen them.  Which honestly isn't surprising since I use bronzer more for contouring and am only applying a small amount to small sections of my face.  That aside I'm still very happy with this bronzer.  I think it's a great choice for contouring for someone who many not want to invest in a whole kit, especially if you already have a highlighter that you like.

When I read that this bronzer gave a "natural.....glow", I did not expect it to have bright sparkles in it.  I'm not of an age to do sparkly makeup.  And actually, even when I was at that age, I didn't go in for sparkles.  Yes, I did look at the close up picture of the make up on this product page, but I just did not make the connection.  The inclusion of tiny sparkles in this bronzer is a disappointment to me.  Neither the words "natural, radiant, sun-kissed glow", not the pictures, conveyed to me that it had so much sparkle.

The color is fairly well represented on this product page.  It may be a touch lighter than I expected, but barely.

It is easily picked up by my brush, and it applies effortlessly and smoothly.

I am enjoying the other Bliss product that I have, Exglowsion Serum Foundation, but this one is not for me.
summary: The inclusion of tiny sparkles in this bronzer is a disappointment to me.

reviewText: I know this is a detail, but I so much prefer powders and bronzers in a round cake form like this Bliss Go for the Bronze powder. I also like not receiving another small useless brush which is often found in compacts. Having a wonderful set of cosmetic brushes on hand assures that I can deftly apply cosmetics with tools that are not simply add ons enclosed to market a product. The texture of this bronzer is very sweet with a little glisten to enhance the skin texture when light hits the face. As with other Bliss cosmetics, I've experienced no skin sensitivity and find no offensive scent. Of course, if a light touch is used when applying the bronzer, the color will not be as concentrated or rich as when an additional layer is applied. I'm finding that Bliss cosmetics tend to have the underlying yellow hue which I have seen in other higher-end cosmetics. The square plastic case is well designed to protect the product yet it is lightweight due to its plastic construction and shiny mirror like finish. This also has an interior mirror which is handy for an application on the go.
summary: Avoid the sun but still glow

reviewText:
Bronzer can be tough, especially in the summer months when your skin tone can change from day to day depending on how much sunscreen you put on. This bronzer does a great job giving you the shine that makes you look like you're tan, even if you aren't. It's incredibly easy to apply and will have you looking stellar in no time.

I would note that if you're looking for a day to day bronzer, this one comes in a bit dark. It definitely augments your face if you're going out on a date, but might be a little much for Target or the grocery store.

It looks like it will last a long time. You only need a little to look great. Overall, it's hard to go wrong with this bronzer.

I'm a huge Bliss Spa fan.  I've been using their heavenly Lemon + Sage Body Butter for years and recently discovered the Incredi-Peel Glycolic Pads (which easily rival Dr. Dennis Gross Alpha Beta Peel Pads for almost fifty percent less).  So I'm surprised it took them so long to release a line of color cosmetics.  Naturally, I was eager to give them a go.

Although I'm not a big user of bronzer, I'm also not very outdoorsy.  So sometimes it's nice to have a little color during the summer when everyone else has gotten a rosy glow from a day at the beach.  I've never tried the gold-standard of bronzers - Guerlain's Terracotta (which is a perpetual fixture on every magazine's annual "Best Of" list) because I wouldn't get enough use out of it to justify spending upwards of $50.  I have tried Physician's Formula (too dry and frosted) and Sephora's Sun Disk (too matte and orange), so I have those to compare this against.

This product creates an attractive, subtle glow.  It isn't too brown (which can read as dirt), nor too orange (otherwise known as the Lohan/Trump-effect), but has a natural rosy undertone that makes it flattering on my fair skin (with yellow undertones).  It goes on very smooth and almost creamy, similar to mineral foundations.  The only thing that was a bit startling is that, in lieu of frost, it actually has little bits of sparkle.  When first applied, they appear quite obvious which, for someone my age, is not particularly desirable.  However, after it settled into my skin, the sparkles were nearly invisible.  Still, I'd recommend a judicious application, because the sparkle/glitter effect looked okay on my cheekbones, nose ridge and over my forehead, but kind of weird above my lip.

Overall, I'd say this lives up to the Bliss reputation.  An easy way to create that healthy summer glow.

Being uber pale skinned,I was nervous about ordering the darker option of bliss' two bronzers, but once I received this I'm glad that choosing the lighter one wasn't a possibility. This darker shade reminds me of the Too Faced bronzer in 'Chocolate" (but without the yummy scent). When applied this bronzer looks quite natural even on my fair skin as long as I don't apply it with a heavy hand. My cheeks tends towards flushing red when the weather is warmer, so I often skip blush during the summer. I use bronzer instead as the yellow in it is often enough of a counter to the redness that my skin doesn't appear so flushed and my cheeks appear to have a natural blush. I like that the bliss 'Go For the Bronze' has a bit more yellow in it than the Too Faced and (except for the sparkle) looked even better than I expected. If you have light or medium skin, I would think this bronzer color would look even better.

I had to take a half star off for this bronzer because it has a bit too much shimmer to it for everyday, normal wear. It's great for evenings, going out, special events, and other such things, but sparkly skin isn't always the best for the workplace. Another half star off because of the texture of this powder bronzer. It could have been more finely milled for a silkier feel. You shouldn't feel the powder particles when applying them, but you can with this. The coarse feeling of the powder on your skin has you looking twice at the package to be sure this is a bliss product and not some cheap knockoff or low-end makeup brand. On the other hand, the staying power is excellent. We spent a muggy Saturday afternoon walking around a local town's sidewalk sales, and though most of my eye makeup migrated and had to be cleaned up and touched up, the bliss bronzer was still going strong by dinner. It came off easily with a little makeup removing cleansing oil. No irritation was experienced, nor was any odd smell to the product.

For a bronzer offering from a company known for great skincare products, I was expecting a higher quality product. I realize that bliss is just getting into the makeup market and has some growing pains to get through, so I won't judge them to harshly for this initial offering. Since bliss is great at the skincare game, I'd like to see them offer this and other makeup in cream form rather than powder form.
summary: Great bronzer color but a bit too much shimmer

reviewText: Great product ~~  I'm actually using it for contour as it's just dark enough on my skin.  I love it!  It goes on smoothly and easily, looks great, and stays on all day.  I love, love that it's made from natural ingredients and is only improving my skin!  Bliss is a fantastic line of skin care, so I'm thrilled to get a chance to try out some of their make up.
Ok, for me the deal breaker is that this product has glitter in it. Not just shimmer, but chunks of glitter! Not what I was looking for.

I have average skin, not pale, not dark.  I'm what the ladies and gentlemen at Sephora call "a perfect candidate" for bronzer. They showed me repeatedly what a great benefit it would be to make me look, healthy, sunny (without skin cancer danger) and even slimmer!  Yep, the trifecta of goodness.

But it doesn't. Some bronzers are okay (the Bare Escentuals light one seems okay) but the rest make me feel like my face is dirty.  Even just a light dusting feels like I'm sprinkling dirt on my face.

So I eagerly tried this, because if it makes me one pound slimmer it's a win, right?  No.  It just felt like dirt. Something about the texture, no matter how much I blended, felt like I had a sticky powder on my face.  It is heavy on the pigment and not easy to blend in the first place.  But even when I had a friend put it on me, it just stuck out as "OMG that lady must have been downwind of a factory explosion!!!!".  I don't know if it's me or Bliss (I like their other products immensely). Maybe it's me, but my friend tried it too, her with a darker complexion, Neither of us was happy.

Try to sample before buying.  Although I'm sure Amazon would accept a return.
summary: Too dark, too hard to blend

reviewText:
I have been using the LumaRx women's foil shaver for a week now and I am pleasantly surprised at how much I love it. I've owned a few shavers over the years and quickly became disenchanted with them. This one was well thought out and really does a superb job on my legs.

First, right out of the box. You receive a charge stand, the shaver, a cloth drawstring pouch, a power cord, instruction booklet, double-sided cleaning brush, and a bikini trimmer headguard. The instructions say to charge for 24 hours which I did but it turned on right out of the box and seemed fully charged. It took me a minute to find where to plug the power cord into the unit. I'm a person that always reads the instructions first, and nowhere in the instructions does it show a picture or even say anything about it. So if you are just receiving the unit, on the back of the charger stand is a very small opening. Plug the cord into that area. After charging, I unplugged the unit so that I could leave it standing for easy use.

The shaver has nice curves that feel perfect in your hand. The weight is balanced very well. I had no problems shaving my legs and found that each time I shaved with the unit, my legs felt a little better. Either I was getting better at using it or my legs were adapting to a new way of shaving. I used the unit dry for several times. Today, I used it in the shower because it can be used either way. For me, I found it a little harder to shave in the shower. It shaved well in wet as well as dry. The unit has this little strip on it that supposedly is an almond oil moisturizing strip. I thought that I would feel it in the shower but really didn't notice anything that felt moisturizing so I'm not sure about that particular addition. Perhaps it worked but I didn't feel anything.

Kudos to the developers of the LumaRx Women's Foil Shaver! It is really a wonderful product. I look forward to many years of use.

UPDATE:  I just reduced my review to 4 stars after speaking with a representative from the company that makes the shaver. First, when the battery no longer will hold a charge, the shaver is dead. You cannot replace the battery because it has been soldered to the unit. She did say if you can find an authorized service center, they may be able to replace it, but my guess is that the cost would be prohibitive. Also, I did inquire about the moisturizer strip. She said that there is enough oil in the strip to last for the lifetime of the shaver. I told her that I couldn't see or feel the oil, but she assured me that it was there. I personally think the strip is useless and just a marketing add on.
summary: Finally, a women's shaver that works as well as my razer blade!

reviewText:
The first thing to keep in mind before buying this is that an electric shaver can never be as close as a manual safety razor blade.  Some come close but the shave will always be inferior to a real blade. The real benefit of an electric razor is that it can be used practically anywhere and it does not require shaving cream or a great deal of care to prevent nicks or cuts.  If you are ok with this fact then the LumaRx Foil Shaver is a decent choice.  It is very easy to use and comfortable.  The shave is close enough for general areas such as armpits but it won't wow you with  skin that feels silky smooth.  Most women will find this to be great for daily use but when you really need a close shave a manual is always the best choice.

*** Positive Points: ***

- Easy to charge on its included charging stand
- Has a built in trimmer that is comfortable to use
- Provides a fairly consistent shave that is reasonably close
- Has a reasonable shave time of 30 minutes per charge
- Has a nice carrying pouch and brush to help clean the razor

*** Negative Points: ***

- Charge time is very long (20+ hrs)
- Shaving foil works well in most areas but is a bit large for "sensitive" areas
- The instructions mention replacing the foil every 6 months which seems a little too frequent
- Shaver must be dry before charging
- No display or indicator to let you know how much charge is left
summary: A Good Option As Long As You Know That Electric Shavers Are Not As Close As A Blade

reviewText:
I have no complaints about this razor, it works just as well as other brands I've owned. I like that this one has a stand to charge in, rather than having to have it lying on the counter. I have fair hair so it's difficult to see the hair I want to shave. But I can feel it. I was able to shave my legs as smooth as with a blade razor but with no cuts - and I didn't even have to watch where I was shaving, I was able to do it completely by touch, which means this would be a nice idea for someone who has a visual impairment.

It's really easy to clean, just pop through top off and rinse the foil. Make sure you let it dry thoroughly before putting it back so water does not drip into the electronics.
summary: Excellent - would work well for someone visually impaired

reviewText: I love that you can use this shaver in the shower. I am currently 6 months pregnant and I can easily get to the areas that need shaving without having to go over my legs two or three times. You get a very close shave. It fits easily in my hand and is very comfortable to use. I would recommend this shaver

Disposable blade vs shaver...who is the winner?  I've always used a disposable blade, even though over time doing that costs more money in blades and shaving cream.  However, I never knew which shaver to pick.  I'm glad I got to try this one. This shaver comes with a bikini trimmer guard, charging station/cord, brush to clean the shaver head coils, and a carrying/storage case.  The carrying case is nice if you plan to travel with the shaver. It is recommended to clean the shaver after every use.  Although it is easier to clean a blade, you still need to make sure it is clean so I say both are almost in that respect.

There is a little prep work you need to do before your first shave.  The battery requires charging for 24 hours for the first and each subsequent use.  The charging stand is small, only about three inches in diameter.  However, the cord going into the base has a two inch segment that is not flexible, so the device will require a minimum of five inches of counter space from the wall outlet. It just barely fits on my counter without falling into the sink.  Luckily, the shaver feels very secure on the stand, so it won't fall over easily.  The power cord is six feet in length. If placed in the bottom outlet, the plug will not block both openings.  I don't like that there is no display or indicator to let you know how much charge is left. I took off a star for that/it takes a long time to charge.  You could be in the middle of a shave and lose all your charge and have to wait a day.  That of course would not happen with a disposable blade.

To test the product for this review I used the shaver both in and out of the shower. I get great results every time: a close shave with little effort on legs, underarms, and personal area. It is a close shave.  The shaver gets all your hair quite easily in one or two passes.  The handle remains easy to grasp securely in both wet and dry conditions. The size of the shaving head is good for legs and underarms but it is a little large for use on your personal area so be careful when shaving there.  Most important to me in comparison with a disposable blade is that I had no bumpy irritation spots after using the shaver.  That is a giant plus in my book.

There is no way to replace the battery so the real test of this shaver will come later  how many years will it last before the battery dies out.  This shaver needs to last longer than what I would pay for shaving cream and disposable blades.  If it dies before its time I will update my review.  Overall, I think this is a reasonably priced shaver that works well.
summary: Reasonably priced shaver that works well

reviewText: This LumaRx Women's Foil Shave is a good size and shape for a woman...but I do not care for where they put the trimmer, I think a smaller one on the side would of been a better design. The shave was fairly good, NEVER are you going to get a close shave with an electric as you do with a regular blade shave.  This comes with a cleaning brush plus travel bag, nice if you take it along on a vacation, then you can do a fast leg shave as necessary. I tried it both in the shower and in the bathtub, it worked well enough, but, I still prefer a regular blade shave, myself.

I've used this shaver a couple of times now while in the tub. I am very pleased with how close it shave for an electric shaver....and no, you are not going to get a razor close shave with this, but it is good for what it is. I shaved both my legs and armpits with this shaver. I liked how it shaved my legs, but not so much my armpits. This shaver had a had time handling the curves of my armpits and therefore I was unable to use it for that and is why I gave it 4 stars instead of 5. I also used it to "trim" and I was also happy with the results of that. I had no bumpy irritation spots after using it. Overall, I like it and will use it when I shave most of the time.
summary: Not bad for an electric shaver

reviewText:
I am still getting used to this shaver so I'll list what I like and don't like and add to the review if familiarity changes my opinion.

What I like:

I love that I can take it into the shower and that it is cordless.  I like shaving in the shower because shavers and razors seem to grab less when my skin and hair is wet.  But sometimes I'd rather shave under my arms in front of the mirror because I can see the places I miss.  The combination of going anywhere and especially in the shower is a major plus for me.

I like the little piece for doing longer hair.  Given the things I'm not so wild about, I think it will be a long time before I try a bikini shave, but if I haven't shaved all winter and am getting ready for spring, that attachment definitely comes in handy.

What I didn't like:

This is the first "electric" shaver I have ever used -- I've been shaving with a razor my whole life.  And I think there may be a learning curve on how to hold it,  But the leading edge caught on a large skin tag under my arm and cut it.  I also manage to catch just regular skin under my arms in that leading edge and keep getting places that are almost like razor burns.  Later on they turn into sore red lines under my arms.  I am hoping that practice will teach me how to shave under my arms without tearing them up.

A shaver doesn't give me the exfoliation that a blade does so my skin doesn't feel as smooth as after I have shaved with a blade.  The convenience of this shaver will eventually overcome this but I did notice I wasn't feeling quite as smooth.  Because the weather is still cool, that isn't as much of an issue but later in the spring when I use self tanner, I'll want more exfoliation to keep the color longer.  I'll just have to exfoliate my legs other ways.

I should point out that my leg and under arm hair is fairly light in color and texture.  I waxed my legs for years and the hair never grew back as thick or dark as it had been.  And my under arm hair seems to have gotten lighter as I have aged as well.
summary: Mixed feelings will need more time to resolve

reviewText:
I've never been particularly impressed by the electric shavers I've used in the past. They never seemed to give me a close enough shave and would leave my legs feeling prickly even after multiple passes. I'm pleased to report that the LumaRx shaver gives me a close enough shave that it's nearly indistinguishable from a regular multi-blade razor shave.

This shaver is wet/dry, so you can use it in the shower (but do not submerge it in water or use it in the bath!). I personally prefer using it dry, though, but that's mostly because my bathroom can be rather cold, and the shaver is not terribly comfortable going over goosebumps. But it runs smoothly over my legs and gave a close shave after one or two passes. It was a bit uncomfortable on my armpits, but my skin there is rather sensitive and would need to get used to an electric shaver.

You should charge this shaver for 24 hours before first use and continue to charge it as the instructions say after you use it. A single charge allows for 30 minutes of shaving, which can last multiple days. The shaver opens up easily for cleaning, and you can rinse it out, which is a nice bonus for cleaning. I haven't used the trimmer attachment yet, but I'll update my review once I do.

Overall? This is a really great electric shaver. I may be converted when it comes to shaving my legs.
summary: Surprisingly close shave for an electric shaver

reviewText: This product is hard to clean. Since the body is made of cheap plastic, instead of aluminum, any shaved hair tends to stick with the surface. To clean it, I rinse it under warm running water but the hair doesn't want to fall off the plastic. I have to use a toothbrush to actually clean it. This is not acceptable. I recommend Panasonic Arc3 Electric Razor, Men's 3-Blade Cordless with Wet/Dry Convenience, ES8103S, only $10 more. Have you heard "pink tax"? Search it online. It is an idea that many products designed for women may not be as reliable as men's products.

The LumaRx Women's Foil Shave is nice and sleek and a good weight, but the slide button to turn it on is quite difficult and sticky. The shave is pretty good--it is meant for everyday use, so I think that in the summer I'll use it more! It has a guard that can also be used as a type of case for the blade, and comes with a cleaning brush and travel bag which is great. I used it in the shower without any cream or anything and it did not irritate my skin! Yay!

The LumaRx Women's Foil Shaver is a very nice option for women. It fits in your hand well, and is surprisingly not slippery. As with most electric shavers, the shave is never is close as with a razor. The shave also has a trimmer feature, although a little on the large size for a woman.
The charge time on this shaver is very long, at least twelve hours for a full charge, but it's difficult to tell because it does not have an indicator.
I nice product that could use some design tweaking, but still a very solid choice.

This is a very cute and feminine shaver for women. Very simple to set up and use, make sure you charge it for at least 12 hours and then you are ready to go. This can also be used in water but don't submerge it. It comes with a cute little travel bag as well, it cuts/trims very well and works great for me. Just what I needed!
summary: it cuts/trims very well and works great for me

reviewText:
This razor functions well without irritation or bumps for my various hair textures; ranging from fine to coarse. The various accessories (Bikini Trimmer Guard, Dual-Sided Trimmer, Brushes and Beauty Bag) make this very nice to have. However the rechargeabilty of 24 hours to get 30 minutes of use is a drag, that is about 2 uses per charge. This means I need to keep this plugged in almost all the time. (minus 1 star)

My old electric tooth brush requires a 24-hour charge too, but using it 4 minutes a day all week before I plug it in for recharging is manageable. I need to figure out the formula that works with this shaver. Despite that, it sure beats disposable razors.

Obagi is a brand you can find in most Dermatologists' offices. Sadly, the price is super high and it's not a huge amount in the tube. Here are some great points about this cream:
- it has a reverse pump so that basically the interior base rises as you pump instead of sucking air back into the tube. This could make the cream last longer and keeps it cleaner.
- the cream is a think white cream that easily spreads on skin and disappears, so there is no unsightly acne cream look to it
- it left my skin super smooth, and it could swear it smoothed a few lines
These are first impressions and it takes at least a month of use to know for sure that it's helping, but so far I'm hopeful.
summary: Left skin feeling smooth and cool

reviewText: Came in broken. The bottle was cracked and leaking and there was no tube to reach to the bottom.

If you are searching for some type of non-toxic, organic acne lotion then keep looking because the ingredient list on this could make even a hardened waste inspector blush. On the other hand, if you need serious results when it really counts then this is a good investment. Like many adults, I'm prone to a break-out now and then - this is a serious solution. No, it doesn't work instantly but it can help seriously shorten the duration.
This is doing a good job of clearing up some minor skin issues I have. Very pleased. It is also not creating issues with my allergies.
summary: This is doing a good job of clearing up some minor skin issues I ...

reviewText: My wife tried this: The CLENZIderm line from Obagi is specifically geared for acne-prone skin.  My skin has gotten better as Ive grown older, but occasionally I need a little extra help.  This product is THE product for those who break out, but because of the benzoyl peroxide, it can feel fairly harsh on the skin; you know, like its on fire. While it can be quite uncomfortable, it does its job, and thats what counts!  Can be a saving grace for those who experience frequent breakouts! PS  it got 4 stars because of the burning feeling (though par for the course with benzoyl peroxide) and the cost (ka-ching).
summary: Great for acne-prone skin, but its potent

reviewText:
The Obagi products I have tried thus far have been very good. I expected to feel the same about this product, but instead I have mixed feelings. I have gone through probably 10 tubes of La Roche-Posay Effaclar Duo, which is a 5.5% benzoyl peroxide cream. I LOVE it, but figured this Clenziderm Lotion would perform similarly because it has 5% benzoyl peroxide. I have also used PanOxyl 10% Foaming Wash, as well as several other OTC benzoyl peroxide products (usually around 2.5%).

Although it is effective at obliterating acne and keeping it at bay, this Clenziderm lotion feels very harsh to me. It has a sting after application that stays around for a good 15-20 minutes before going away. It also makes my skin red wherever I apply it (and it stays red for a while too). Now, as mentioned above, I am no stranger to benzoyl peroxides of this strength. I have also used many AHA/glycolics on my skin and have tolerated them very well. I am not someone with particularly sensitive or reactive skin. I have even used Panoxyl 10 as a face mask in the past, which was slightly irritating but it went away as soon as I washed it off (I don't know if it is "recommended" in the usage directions, so take that idea with a grain of salt ;)).

Although I like Obagi Clenziderm Lotion enough to finish it, I don't believe I would purchase another tube because of the irritation--and more so because it doesn't dethrone La Roche-Posay Effaclar Duo. I have been using Clenziderm solely as a spot treatment, and I like it for that purpose.

This treatment lotion for acne did ok, but not great on my occasional adult acne.
I was prepared to give it three stars and toss it, but instead gave it to a teen to try.
It worked better with his teenage skin. Didn't dry him to a crisp or cause further irritation.

No one product works for 100% of the people that have the issue the product addresses.
If you've been disappointed with other teen/young adult acne products, you might consider this Obagi lotion.
I'm beyond needing acne treatment, but this is a good face lotion for this old guy.  It seems to make my wrinkles less noticeable.  I recommend it for all ages.
summary: An effectiv e dkin lotion, even for us old folks

reviewText:
I don't have acne, but I do have very sensitive skin, an actual medical opinion from my dermatologist, not just me self-diagnosing. Last fall, I was bitten on one side of my face twice by some unknown insect, which set off a lot of swelling, hives, and giant oozing bite wounds. If it sounds disgusting, it was. After using a number of doctor-approved concoctions to heal the bites and my skin, what I ended up with was a case of recurring acne on one cheek that would not go away after 4 months.  OTC medications do not work for me because they completely dry out my skin and cause uncomfortable burning and skin reactions.

I decided to try this when I saw it on Vine, and these are the results:
The Pros:
1. Holy cats, this stuff worked! My skin started to clear up within 24 hours, and after a week, all bumps were gone.
2. It did not dry out my skin or cause any other reaction.  None.  I was relieved and surprised.
3. I used my regular cleanser and moisturizer in conjunction with this.

The Cons:
1. There was no pump straw in the bottle or the box.  This is a quality control issue.  I had to whack the bottle on my palm or use a Q-tip to get the lotion out.
2. It is grossly overpriced.  For the price, the delivery system should have been flawless.
3. Obagi is not supposed to sell on line, but through physicians' offices only, so I have to question the authenticity of the product's claimed manufacturer.  They may have changed their policy, but I am not aware of them having done so.
summary: Expensive, poor packaging, it works for sensitive skin

reviewText:
The off-white lotion is of better quality than similar benzoyl peroxide lotions and creams that I have used.  It is notably easier and more pleasant to apply than a thick cream.  Compared to other lotions, it disappears into the skin quickly and doesnt leave a white film, even in pores and crevices.

The plastic bottle holds 1.6 fl. oz. or 47 ml.  It has a standard threaded top to prevent leaks during shipping plus a pump top with a separate cap that makes it easy to dispense.

However, the lotion contains the same, effective, active ingredient that is found in many common brands of acne medication, including the tubes they sell at pharmacies and even at dollar stores.  It is a better carrier lotion in a nicer container, but the inexpensive 5% benzoyl peroxide acne treatments are just as effective and are a much better value.  I also would not trust a physician who tried to sell this product to me instead of simply recommending the less expensive but equally effective products.  (Price does not affect my product ratings as it is not an inherent property and can change.)

I am surprised that this product is sold by Amazon, because the Obagi Medical Products website states that (g)enuine Obagi products are available only through physicians, medical spas, and other skin care professionals and  Obagi Systems and Products are physician-dispensed and should be used only under the guidance of your skin care physician.  Obviously, neither statement is true.

The bottle that I received has what appears to be a date about 11 months from receipt, but it is not identified as an expiration date.

Active ingredient: Benzoyl peroxide 5%.
Inactive ingredients:  Benzyl benzoate, BHT, dicaprylyl ether, dimethyl isosorbide, disodium EDTA, hydroxyethyl acrylate, sodium acryloyldimethyl taurate copolymer, phenoxyethanol, polysorbate 60, propylene glycol, squalane, water.
summary: High quality but a poor value

reviewText: Compared to over the counter products that come with 1% benzoyl peroxide, the Obagi comes with 5% benzoyl peroxide.  I used the product on a blemish and it cleared up the area in much shorter time than over the counter products.  My skin did not try out and it did not become irritated. The product also did not leave a white residue on my skin.  I didn't have to use a lot of the product to obtain the results I did.  The main issue with the product is the price.  At the current price that is charged on Amazon it is very expensive and may be out of financial reach of many.  While it may be worth a try to see if the performance is worth the price for your situation, over a long period of use the price needs to come down for many people to purchase the product.

Of note: I do not have sensitive skin and Ive never had a problem with moiturizers or acne creams in the past. One application of a small amount of this on my forehead yielded an almost immediate burning sensation that intensified rapidly. Wiping it off revealed reddened skin. This might be a fluke, but I won't be using it again.

this one I tried for a week and half. That is plenty of time for me to know if A. it will dry out my combination skin an B will it clean my face. I works great!! I can say no drying me out and stops my adult acne.  I like there is no weird smell to this one. Nice and clean. Comes off cleanly too.  Not messy to work with. I would really recommend this one

This worked pretty well on my pimples. Cleared them up pretty quickly. I see other people said it stung when they used it, I only got a slight tingle. I do like that it is a lotion consistency and there is no smell! I am just not so sure on the price. It seems pretty expensive when I have used other brands and formulas for half the cost that just work as well, but this is a pretty decent size bottle you get so it will last awhile and it works, so if you are having trouble finding something that works for your pimples then I would suggest trying this out! :)

Whats the uniqueness? I sadly got two pimples a while after this came in. I had used it on another pimple and didn't see anything so great about it, but thought what the heck lets be all sciency. So my loss was your gain. After 5 days of using both this and a generic brand 5% BP there was not noticeable difference. My gf thought this product might have moisturized more but the results sure didn't show it. Also worth noting Neutrogena makes a formula which 25% BP if you really need acne taken care of. Maybe this has some ingredients that make it more effective or more worthwhile but not for my skin.

Also just because they are in dermatologists office doesnt instill much confidence the product for me. I went to dermatologist in Beverly Hills because my insurance covered it. The guy had no idea what was causing a rash on my face or why it would peal he through everything and the kitchen sink at it and said: we don't really know why this happens but lets see if it works. Also he tried 3 different products on my dark circles under my eyes and none of them worked-- I was not bothered at all by them but he insisted--because guess what he has his own very successful beauty line. I was clearly not his usual clientelle. Once he left the room and his PA said I could get literally the same products minus an ingredient or two that had no appreciable clinical effect mostly OTC. I'm sure there are ancient or homeopathic ingredients that would make a difference in some products. It just seems these doctors have no inclination to actually research it. They just find a sales angle and go with it.
summary: I'll stick with the OTC brand

reviewText:
This has a very light texture like a lotion, not a cream consistency. It has a slight smell of the benzoyl peroxide. It absorbs really fast, and after a minute or two you feel the tingling/burning sensation on your skin--for my wife it was about a 5 minute long sensation. Obviously different skin types may react differently, but it doesn't leave her skin red like some other treatments. She has tried using 10% creams in the past, but they are too strong and cause a bad skin reaction and redness. This 5% mixture is the right balance for her skin. Compared to other benzoyl peroxide acne treatments, this does not dry your skin that much, but still is effective at reducing the acne. It gave noticeable results and clearer skin after just 1 week. The downside of this cream, like others, is that it increases your sun sensitivity, so you may need to take extra precautions to protect your skin. Of all the acne treatments my wife has used (at least a half dozen brands), this is the most effective she's used yet. However, if she stopped using it for a day or two, the skin condition regressed. But she was extremely satisfied with the results. A minor caution while using benzoyl peroxide treatments, they can discolor fabrics, like pillow-cases, so use a cheap one!
Another acne treatment with similar results but that doesn't affect sun sensitivity so much is the Skinoren brand with Acidum Azelaicum 200mg (20%). But this cream is mostly available in Europe; I have not found it in the USA yet.

The active ingredient in this product is benzoyl peroxide. The same benzoyl peroxide that I've been using for 40 years. The same benzoyl peroxide that you can find on any drug store shelf for around $5-$10. So what makes this product worth $81? Nothing. This is a light lotion that goes on very smoothly, but it is SHINY. It's not greasy but it shines, shines, shines. I used it at bedtime and when I woke up, I had a face full of clogged pores. Not pimples or an inflammatory response, but something squeezable. I was so shocked and very annoyed. Wasn't about to use it again. For a great (and more affordable) acne treatment, I recommend La Roche-Posay Effaclar Duo Dual Action Acne Treatment Cream with Benzoyl Peroxide, Oil-Free, 1.35 Fl. Oz.. Not only does it contain benzoyl peroxide, but it also has micro-exfoliating lha-lipo hydroxy acid. For me, this cleared my skin of every blackhead, something no over product has ever done. At my last visit, my dermatologist even exclaimed, "You don't have a single blackhead!"

For 81 dollars, this does not seem to work much better than over the counter acne creams. It comes in a bottle that required being put together, and it doesn't come with a "straw" to get down to the bottom of the bottle. This means when you have about 1/3 left, it is difficult to get out of the bottle. The pump does squeeze a fine amount - it's not meant for full facial coverage, but for spot coverage. Having had the monthly breakout, I used two products on two different pimples (both were small). The redness faded slightly faster (a morning before) the other over-the-counter product. It did not seem like an appreciable difference given that the Obagi is 16x more expensive than the other OTC.
summary: Perhaps slightly more effective than standard OTC products, but not by much

reviewText:
My daughter gets breakouts around her chin & forehead area.  She's been using another dermatologist recommended brand and it seemed to work pretty good, but she ran out a couple months ago, so her breakouts are back.  She's been using this product for a couple days.  The benefits so far have been that it has a non-oily with a light feel to it.  It goes on great.  Although her acne isn't gone, as it's only been a couple days, it has calmed down quite a bit.  Interestingly, there hasn't been any drying or flaking like with the other product she used.  The redness & inflammation seem to be calmer.  We'll continue using it and update on how long the product takes for her acne to be completely under control.

The cost is pretty pricey, so we're assuming that the cost is backed up by providing clear skin.  We shall see!

Updates to come.
summary: After a couple days, redness & inflammation have improved!

reviewText: Obagi CLENZIderm line offers a therapeutic lotion with active ingredient Benzoyl peroxide 5% (acne treatment).  This product also has valuable squalane it is which is definitely an added plus.  I do not have acne, but occasionally I will have a pimple.  And like most people I like to get rid of the pimples fast.  Benzoyl peroxide 5% is strong enough to get rid of the people within a day or two.  This is a generous size bottle so if one is a person with a lot of acne, this product can be used daily in the morning and at night until acne are cleared.  But for people with occasionally breakout this is a go to product one can go to and use to get rid of the acne.  With daily use, this product can probably last 2-3 months because only a small amount of product is needed on the ace.  With occasional use, this one bottle can last 6 months or longer.  The other thing to mention is that this is a kind of product that I would call unisex - both men and women of any age experiencing acne breakouts can use it for a treatment of acne.  This product is strong and effective.  You will experience a little bit of tingling when applied on the skin.
summary: Powerful lotion for acne treatment with 5% Benzoyl peroxide 5% active ingredient

reviewText: This is a good product but it does dry my daughter's skin out a little more than proactive.  She has switched to using it every other day so alleviate some of the drying effects.
summary: This is a good product but it does dry my daughter's skin out ...

reviewText: As I've gotten older, I've gotten acne along my throat and my upper chest. After a couple of days of use of this product, I found it to work miracles for me. On the first night I used it, it took all the redness away from my acne. On the second night, I noticed that all the acne were a lot smaller than before. On the third night, most of the acne were either drying out or starting to go away. I don't think I've ever been so impressed with an acne product as this. Not only did it not bleach my bed sheets, or clothes, but it also didn't dry out my skin like other products. There's a slight tingling burning sensation when you first apply that goes a way after a half hour or less. But it's well worth the pain. I've also started to use this product on my 12 year old daughter with some clear signs of success on her face so far. Count me in as continued customer for this product!
summary: but it also didn't dry out my skin like other products

reviewText:
I was looking forward to using this product.  I am 52 and Caucasian, but I still breakout once a month.  I was also sick over the holiday and my skin was dry.  I was drinking a lot water and moisturizing regularly and I still had a bad reaction to the cream.

First, for $80 bucks, youd think the person boxing the product would make sure there was a straw in the box.  The top of the bottle has to be removed and replaced with a pump with straw.  I double-checked the envelop, the box, and my kitchen and bathroom floors; no straw.  I took the bottle and got some in my palm.

I was planning to put it on a few minutes before my shower and let the benzoyl peroxide kill germs in my problem areas and rinse off, as not to dry out my face.  Oh no.  It burned.  I quickly got undressed and jumped in the shower and rinsed it off.  Even after I got out of the tub, my skin was still irritated.  I had to cool it off will some cooling face cream.

This whole experience did surprise me because I have been using 10% benzoyl peroxide for years.  This was only 5%.  Very disappointed.
summary: On top of no straw, it then burned my face.

reviewText: Gose on smooth. I can wear this under makeup with no problem. It soaks into skin, isn't drying and most important of all doesn't make my skin flaky.  It isn't as drying as some medications. I wear this as a preventative measure to ensure I don't get break outs and it works great. Obagi products are sold at my dermatologist and she always says they are some of her favorites. Now I see why.

feels really nice misted over your skin. Specially on a hot day. 3.4 oz bottle tones and  refreshes you skin with a fine mist. no weird order or smell to it. does not feel sticky really does make my skin feel refreshed would definitely use this one in the summer when I want to cool off

This is a funny product, in that it works as advertised ... it is a refreshing spritz for a tired face, in a handy little bottle. But at the same time, it seems really overpriced for what is essentially a little bottle of scented water. It has a nice little citrus scent, a  happy, natural ingredients list, and definitely picks you up with a little spray. But it is hard to justify that price.

I grabbed this because I do enjoy a good toner/mist/whatever spray (lately I've been using rosewater). And bliss is known for their great spa and beauty products. This Triple Oxygen Radiance Restoring Mist sounds great, and when you get it home to try it, it's a sleek pump bottle that's easy to use, you just shake and pump to spray a fine mist that has a lovely but not overbearing citrus fragrance on your face. I've been using this for a week or two now, with and without make-up (it doesn't affect my make-up, which is nice when you're wearing it and want to feel a little more refreshed or to make your skin feel a little more 'dewy'), and while I can't say it's done wonders for it, it does help my skin feel better after I put it on.
Reason it's not five stars? The second ingredient is alcohol denat. (denatured alcohol), and while I know that the kind used in these products isn't supposed to be the 'drying' kind, there's a lot of other rather long-worded ingredients as well. When you can find something with essential oils in it (which is important, especially in the heat) and little else for a bit cheaper....

A long time ago I had a little aerosol spray of purified water next to my desk. It was intended as a refresher, and also helped with dry eyes (I wore contacts back then). It was nice. Every so often, I would use it and it was kind of like taking a little break. I haven't seen those around in a long time, but this looked kind of like it, so I decided to try it out.

It is pump, not aerosol, which is fine. In fact, maybe more than fine, as the aerosol cans never seem to hold as much as the pump versions, so perhaps it will last longer that way.

I was a bit skeptical. Okay, more than a bit. The claims like oxygenation of your skin, the fact that it contains vitamin C, but you don't ingest it, all seems a bit hokey to me. However, I gave it a fair shot and sprayed it on my face (with my eyes closed, as they recommend), and it was nice. Refreshing, like my old plain water spray, but also has a nice light natural scent that reminds me of licorice and bananas. Nothing strong - this isn't perfume by any means. Just enough scent to be pleasant. I also found that my skin felt softer afterward. I'm really not sure why, but it was true.

Overall, I like this. It is kind of like a little portable pick-me-up that would be great after coming inside from the heat, or just to break up a long day. I took off a star because it is crazy overpriced. The profit margins on this thing must be stunning. However, it does the job, and I enjoyed it.

Sean Logue, 2016

I really love this Bliss Mist. It has a citrus smell and goes on with a fine mist. It makes my skin feel soft and moisturized. I might keep this in the fridge in the summer for a nice cool spray.  There are a few glycol ingredients which I usually tend to shy away from. If it was organic/all natural, I'd give it 5 stars! I'll update as I use it over time on the radiance factor.

My wife has been feeling sort of dragged down lately and lacks sleep. I gave her this mist which has a somewhat citrus scent. She closed h jher eyes tight and sprayed her face. After a short while she said that she felt a psychological and somewhat physical lift. I did not observe any marked amount of radiance.

I took this because I am tired all the time and I need all the refreshing that I can get. When I got it I closed my eyes and sprayed my neck and face. It felt good and it has a mild citrus scent to it.

I guessed that it had water in it and that that is the first ingredient. Some of the ingredients are not familiar to me but the ones that are besides the water are licorice,  a form of chamomile, cranberry fruit extract,garlic bulb extract soy and wheat protein and gingseng root extract. If you are allergic to soy or wheat, you may not want to try it.

You are not supposed to spray it in your eyes but if you do accidentally, wash them out with water.

I do not like the price of it. That is my only negative.

If I was still working, I would pop it into my purse and use it when I feel drowsy.
summary: Nice Citrus Scent But Seems Expensive

reviewText:
I love trying anything that has to do with skin care and this is no exception. I thought with summer coming, it would be nice to have something like this to spray on my face throughout the day when I need a picker-upper. It smells good but the smell doesn't linger as long as you would think. It is a bit sticky even after I have rubbed it in on my face.

I don't notice any difference in my skin radiance. I think I do look less tired after spraying it but it really didn't make a lot of difference.

If they lower the price on this, I might be sold on buying it again. As of now, I put it on my skin before I apply make up and it does help applying make up a bit smoother.

This bliss Restoring Mist smells and feels awesome, but, as others have noted, is very pricey for something that is really an add on to your skin care. It doesn't replace your moisturizer, or really any other essential product. That said, it does feel really great on, and it is light and refreshing during the summer heat.

Update: I am still using this mist and have come to enjoy it quite a bit. I received it in May and this is the beginning of October. I used in on my bare face a lot in the hotter months, but also to 'set' my make up at any time - I apply my make up and then spritz my face with the Bliss. Though I still think it is too much for me to pay ($38), I continue to love the way it feels and the light citrus scent, so there you go. If I could find a less expensive brand that feels and smells the same, I'd be really happy! If Bliss would lower the price on this or put it on sale, I'd be even happier. But I have to give it its due for lasting me, so far, for months, with a good bit of use.
----------------------------------------

I really liked the scent and feel, and claims, of this product but find it completely over-priced - $38 for a little over 3 oz of product, of which some of that product ends up spritzing out into the air. As well, consumers, at least this one, want to feel they are getting something substantial when paying this much for a beauty product, and since this mist is just that--a mist--it feels like air and water. That's a difficult thing to pull off, to ask consumers to pay almost $40 for citrus-scented water, even if the claims of the ingredients are accurate. With creams, serums, lotions, we apply something "solid" with control, and can control how much or how little. To some point you can do this with the mist, but once you depress the plunger, out the product comes and there's no controlling that--a portion of your $38 is going into the air.

I did a search for facial mists, and found many under $20. And even brands like Clinique, which can be pricey, has a less expensive facial mist at $22.00, so why would I spend almost twice that for this product? I wouldn't.

The claim is:
Key Ingredients/Benefits
Our advanced CPR technology:
Vitamin C: Clarifies, brightens and evens skin tone with a more stable form of this powerful antioxidant.
Cruciferous Extract: Protects skin by helping to stimulate defense proteins and create a protective barrier to shield skin from aggressors.
EUK-134, Fluid 02, and Soy Protein: Revitalizes skin via this exclusive complex that converts free radicals into healthy oxygen and then carries that oxygen to cells to drive energy consumption.

All of that sounds really great, and perhaps it does do some magic to my face, but since you are to mist your face with what feels like expensive water, you feel as if that $38 bottle is going to be used up very quickly. It's not a lot of product for $38. I consider if the product really does as it claims would I want to spend that much, and I'd still consider that I'd rather spend the money on something I can apply to my skin with a little more control, without having some of it go flying into the air, wasted. Or, purchase one of the less expensive mist products.

On the positive side, I love love love the citrus scent and how refreshing it feels to my skin! I'm constantly on the look-out for scents that are citrus, or spicy-scented, and it's very difficult to find products that aren't "grandmother's powder" scented. This product feels amazing when I spritz my face - and I'd imagine in the summer I could put it in the fridge when I wanted a nice cooling sensation to wake me up and cool me off - and give me that really nice citrus scent I so love.

If they significantly lowered the price, I would purchase this product to use when I wanted a little pick-me-up for my skin. I would also use it to spritz my face after applying foundation if I wanted a little extra moisture. For as I said, the scent is nice, and it feels great on my skin for the length of time it remains until it dries.
summary: Oh that the price were a little lower!

reviewText: I have used this several times over last week and I really like it as a little refresher/pick me up when I'm feeling tired or hot or both. I honestly haven't noticed a difference appearance wise so far but it does seem to brighten me up a bit. It has a light lemon lime scent and absorbs very quickly. If you are a fan of bliss products I think you will really like this spray!

I took before and after photos to make sure I was fairly judging my level of youthful radiance before and after using this product. I can say frankly that I look no more radiant, toned, or youthful after using it than I did before.

Never mind. I don't think that's really the point of this product. I think the point is that you can, on a day when you're feeling a bit tired or your skin is a bit dry, spray this lovely stuff on your face and feel much better. The scent is pretty but not lasting, it's certainly hydrating, and your skin will feel softer. I find it refreshing, and that's worth something.

Try it to set your make up in the morning or to revive your energy if you're heading out after work, to keep moisture in after a shower, to refresh yourself when you're out in the summer heat, or to combat that afternoon slump at work. Pass it around at the beach or the pool, and think of it as a pick me up when you're hard at work. It's a much healthier alternative than another cup of coffee or a trip to the vending machines.

The main ingredients are water and alcohol - with a list of chemicals at least a couple of inches long, including fragrance, which can include just about anything... mostly harmful to health. The Restoring Mist does include some natural ingredients that are generally helpful. Maybe if they got rid of the artificial chemicals and kept the natural if might be a product worth considering. Is it refreshing? Yes, the nozzle puts out a fine mist, which can be something of a wake-up call, although I don't care for the smell. The nice little bottle is reusable. I dumped out the contents in favor of vitamin C crystals dissolved in green tea. I found it equally refreshing, without the stink. Try 1 tsp. vitamin C powder to 9 tsp. green tea. It should last about a weak before the vitamin C breaks down. If you use a clear bottle, the vitamin C will break down quicker. Try Vitamin C Crystals Ascorbic Acid 100% Pure Powder, 8 Ounces using 2 Empty Blue Glass Spray Misters - 4oz Refillable Bottle is Great for Essential Oils, Organic Beauty Products, Homemade Cleaners and Aromatherapy with a White Fine Mist Dispenser - 2 Pack of 4oz Bottles if you don't have a Restoring Mist bottle... or if you're trying to avoid plastic.

reviewText: This Triple Oxygen Radiance Restoring Mist by Bliss, doesn't really appear to be anything special. I gave it to my mother. After using it a few times, she said she did not notice any real change in her "radiance." However, she said it did feel refreshing and didn't mind the citrusy smell. I think the vote is still out whether this stuff is of any real value.

who thinks this is a silly product?  I ordered this through vine, because for one thing  it didn't cost me anything and yes, I was curious enough.  But honestly, I didn't feel (or look) any more radiant, toned or hydrated. The only things I felt were silly for spritzing my face and neck with this slightly sticky feeling, citrus smelling water and grateful that I didn't spend any money on it.

Would I recommend?  NO.

Bliss radiance restoring mist is a fantastic moisturizer for use anytime. My skin tends to dry out due to a thyroid condition. I've found that using bliss helps me look the best I can be, day and night.

Bliss features vitamin C which is proven to be beneficial for skin health. Other useful ingredients include soy protein, wheat protein, cranberry fruit extract and ginseng. I simply couldn't imagine a more nourishing, refreshing and clean-smelling mist that works as well as this.

Suffice to say that I highly recommend bliss radiance restoring mist to everyone.

reviewText:
The numerous pictures provided on the product page along with the ones others have posted provide an accurate run-down of the contents of this sample box so I had a general idea what to expect and was not disappointed. The Julep nail polish color varies. I received a gorgeous shade of blue (Nedra-It Girl) which is one I would have selected for purchase. I have a couple of bottles of their polish and this is a full-size container, not a sample, and it costs approximately 2/3 the price of the entire sample box alone, and that is over-and-above the credit toward a future purchase within the selected group.

So, for me this sample box idea is a win because even with items that may not initially be of interest, I rarely refuse a free sample since in the past I have discovered helpful items I did not know about and even switched brands after trying something new. And, I can check for skin sensitivities with a sample before purchase. So that the box is not customized is not a primary concern. .

Specific contents within the 20 samples I received include two mens cologne and a shaving cream sample but otherwise the contents are either generic, like the toothpaste, or are plainly products marketed to women. My daughter swears by her Clarasonic, and this assortment of heads really is great. If your skin is sensitive, the Sensitive brush head is gentle yet efficient. The Cashmere Cleanse Lux head is gentle, yet more efficient. The Radiance brush head is a little more intense, to get the dull, dry skin off. The Deep Pore head is the deepest cleaning. If you have large pores, this helps minimize them.
All of the brushes are super soft and non-irritating. They really help get your skin clean and healthy and get the blood flowing in your face!

This is a great brush head set which includes: Sensitive Brush Head, Deep Pore Brush Head, Radiance Brush Head, and 1 LUXE Cashmere Cleanse Brush Head for extra dry skin. My skin runs oily but I like all 4 of these brushes.

SENSITIVE: Normal to combination
DEEP PORE: Refining; flush away impurities to minimize pore size
RADIANCE: Gentle care
LUXE CASHMERE: Gentlest brush out there

This is a good combo of brushes that range from super gentle (LUXE) to more invigorating (Deep Pore). It's a good kit for beginner Clarisonic users too so that they can figure out which brush works best for them. Or, you can use it like I use it--as an "year-round" brush kit. I use the gentlest brush in the winter, and the deep pore in the summer.

I have been using Clarisonic products faithfully for many years. When I had the opportunity to try this collection of brush heads, I was delighted. As we all know, our skin condition can vary from day to day depending on weather, hydration level, sun exposure, exfoliation treatment, etc. This set provides the options we need to make the right choice for cleansing each day. Included in this set are four brush heads: Radiance, Deep Pore, Sensitive, and the exceptional Cashmere Cleanse.

Each brush head is well-made with the quality I have come to expect from Clarisonic. They vary by stiffness and density of the bristles for specific uses. The Cashmere Cleanse is the most luxurious of all, with a soft, delicate feel that makes even the most irritated skin feel soothed. As always, each brush is compatible with all types of Clarisonic handsets and fits easily in place with a satisfying click.

My only complaint, as this is with all Clarisonic brush heads, is that of storage after use. The cardboard box it comes in is not suitable for putting back a wet brush head. Some sort of plastic storage device would be very helpful, especially if you plan to use all the brush heads in active rotation.
In all, this set is a lovely way to try some of the newer brush heads, as well as bring more flexibility into your facial cleansing routine.
summary: A wonderful sampler kit of Clarisonic brushes, each perfect for rotating use depending on your daily skin condition

reviewText: This is a nice mix of brush heads in a cost savings package. They fit my Clarisonic Mia 2 just fine.
