reviewText: You can spray your hair, your body, your bed and about anything you want with this spray. It is water based and doesn't stain. Even with water based, I can pick up the sweet orange and cedar wood fragrance. If you use essential oils, the fragrance is not quite the same.  The oils are for fragrance are typically artificial while the essential oils are made from plants. The fragrance is much stronger and lasts longer than the essential oils, if you were to mix those two scents of sweet orange and cedar wood. This is light enough that it doesn't bother me at all and it is pleasing to the nose.
summary: Nice water-based scent that doesn't stain

reviewText:
The Rituals The Ritual of Ayurveda Body Mist is a 1.6 ounce body mist that comes in a glass spray bottle.  It sprays a fine mist, & it is highly fragrant so a little goes a long way.  The first time I tried it I sprayed it on my hand, because I have sensitivities to flowery scents & I wasn't sure how the cedar wood would be?  First spray will make you smile if you love orange. It has a sweet, orange smell that smells wonderful! It's fruity, & smells great. I didn't smell anything "woodsy" like you would expect a cedar wood to smell like.  I was surprised I liked this as much as I did.  It's listed as a Hair & Body Mist, & while I've never tried a mist for your hair (besides the smell of hair spray, gels, & products specifically made for hair styling), I think this is a nice body mist.

I would recommend this for those who enjoy the smell of sweet orange.

Remember- a little goes a long way, & the scent stays for awhile, so you only need a little at a time. The bottle will last awhile.

4/5 stars.

If it were strictly Sweet orange, without the cedarwood included, it would be a solid 5 stars. ;)

Though the scent of this is both rose and honey, the rose definitely dominates. In fact, I couldn't smell any honey tones at all, but my best guess is that it mainly cuts through the cloying overly floral scent of pure rose. I found this to be more potent than expected for a body spray or something designed to be sprayed on a bed, but I guess it was made to fade over time, but still leave a vague presence. For my part, I found it too intense for use on my body, but fine as something sprayed onto clothing or into a room.

While this is strong for my tastes, I did note that it doesn't have any sharp, artificial smells or any alcohol scent. It smelled pretty natural to me. I also loved the beautiful packaging and the dark glass bottle that will stop sunlight from interacting with it.

reviewText: I am suspicious of this product. I have followed Ayurvedic practices for awhile and central to Ayurveda is determining one's dosha. Is this for pittas? Vadas? Kaphas? Is it tri-doshic? Or, is the manufacturer capitalizing on the popularity of Ayurveda and using conventional perfume making ingredients with a "natural" scent? It does not smell natural at all, but like a commercial perfume. A quick look at the Rituals site reveals that the Ayurveda line is only one of six scent lines, all with an Eastern theme. One of the ingredients, cyclohexene, is on OSHA hazard lists. It does contain some natural ingredients, but since Ayurveda is about balancing your energy naturally, why spray yourself with a mist created in a chemist's lab? Be your own advocate and if you're attracted to Ayurveda, don't fall prey to slick marketing tactics supported by pretty prose and photographs. Keep it simple, keep it natural.

This mist is light and airy and smells spicy and exotic.  It is almost addictive.  I like to sink my nose into the sprayed area and take deep breaths.  It is very calming, and very relaxing.  The scent doesn't last long but this is a plus for me because I like to mist it on my yoga pillow before meditation.  The scent doesn't cling to the fabric for days on end, so I can use different scents without the pillow smelling like a bordello.

reviewText: I have been flat ironing my hair for years. Finally I recently discovered the Keratin treatment and have loved it ever since. For casual, straight looks in a hurry, the Straightening Brush was fabulous.

reviewText:
This straightening brush would work optimally for people with thin(ner) already pretty straight hair.  I got this for my daughter who has long, thick wavy blond hair...that naturally she wants to be straight instead of wavy.

reviewText:
I do hair for a variety of people.  One of the people I have worked with for a long time has hair that is thick and frizzy, but on humid or hot days, the hair is CRAZY.  It is color treated and borders on being dry, although not always.  I also do hair for another person who has straighter hair but wants to have shiny and ultra straight hair.  I got this brush to use with both of them to see if we could do some new looks with their hair.

WHAT IS THIS BRUSH LIKE?
The brush comes in a box which has a hole in one side and you push and the box slides out.  Sounds silly, but it took me a bit to figure that out since I started with the other sides of the box first.  Inside is the brush with a warranty card and a brief instruction sheet.  The brush itself is a slick handle.  On the back of the handle is an on off pad which you press.  The first setting is the 320F setting and the power button blinks when it first is turned on.  There are three other settings.  To get to them you press the power button briefly and it will change temperature.

The bristles of the brush are arranged in such a way that it will discourage tangles and work through them more easily than other brushes.  The bristles on the outside are plastic but the inside ones are ceramic.  These are all different heights, staggered so that they will handle long hair more easily.  The cord is a heavy round cord and the plug is a polarized plug (on prong is wider than the other).

HOW IS THIS BRUSH TO USE?
I found that when I turn on the brush, the power light flashes and the first temperature is 320.  It says to lock in temperature, that you have to press and hold for 2 seconds.  For me, it just stayed at the temperature and I did not have to hold it.  To move it up, I simply pressed the power button and it changed.  Then you press quickly until you either get a new temperature or you turn the unit off.  I am thinking that the setting of the temperature is so that if your hand slips while using the brush, you won't accidentally have it higher than you want and not know it.  I did not have a problem with that, however.

The brush takes about 2 minutes to heat up.  At first the power light blinks when it is turned on.  When ready to use and up to temperature, the power light turns green and you are ready to go.  The cord gives plenty of length to use freely even if you are not on top of an outlet.

The brush slides through the hair quite easily.  You pull it slowly through a section of hair- not a huge section- and then move on to the next one.  The first hair I tried it on was tangled, had not been combed all day and was frizzy as could be.  It looked wild.  The brush slid through the hair VERY easily.  I set it at 320 and it was perfect.  The hotter temps made it too straight.  320 made it so that the surface was very smooth, there was still a small wave, but it was shiny and beautiful.  Frizz was gone.  Once the entire head was done, I dampened my hands and gently squeezed the hair all over to set in some wave.  The effect was beautiful.  The hair is feathered and long but tapered with multiple layers.

The second hair I used it on had a slight wave but is pretty much straight.  It also was color treated.  350 and 400 seemed to work better for this hair.  It is medium fine, but to get a good shine and straightening, the higher temperatures worked better.  This hair was not dry or fragile but quite sturdy.  The effect was a great shine and straightening and made this person very happy.  Color was accented and the shine was really nice.

WHAT I DIDN'T LIKE
My only problem with this brush is that it was hard to hold on to.  The handle is slick and I found myself almost dropping it a few times.  I would prefer a handle that had some sort of gripping ability on it, a bit thicker than the one that is on there so it is easier to hold and manipulated through the hair.  This one is a bit too slick.  For that, I take off one star.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For frizzy or straight hair with a slight wave, this brush gave a great shine and eliminated frizz. It only takes about 2 minutes to heat up.  Depending on temperature used, the effect can still leave some body or you can go poker straight.  The settings are easy to do and seemed to be easy to keep in place.  You can lock settings so you don't accidentally change it while using.  Tangled hair seemed to be no problem for this brush as it slides right through if you go slowly.  If you can stand the slick handle, this is a great brush.  It has versatility to it and so far the people I have used it on really like how it performed on their hair.

I give this four stars because of the slick handle, but it is more like four and a half since the brush itself worked so well on the different types of hair I used it on.
summary: This Brush Performed Well On A Variety Of Hair, If Not For The Slick Handle, It Would Be Perfect!

reviewText: I really wanted to like the S2 super Smoother electric straightening brush, but was slightly disappointed.  First of all, for some reason the Amazon description says something about speeding up the drying process with a hair dryer.  This product does not dry or speed up the drying process.  It is not a hair dryer at all.  It is more like a heated brush for styling.  I love the very long 9 foot cord that swivels so it doesn't get twisted up.  That's a huge plus in styling appliances.  However, the brush is bulky and somewhat heavy so it takes some getting used to and figuring out how to hold it for best results.  It has a 1 hour shut auto shut off...great idea for this reason.... it might be difficult to figure out how to turn it off.  If you repeatedly press the power button, it will scroll through the different heat settings and the little light that shows up is hard to see.  It is very small.  It took me a few tries to figure it out and the instructions are not clear on how to turn it off.  It heats up quickly.  I got the best results if I brushed through small sections, but I have a lot of hair so this was time consuming.  The brush does not get close enough to the scalp like a flat iron does, so the results were not the same.  I was able to use the brush to curl and style the ends of my hair.  I did manage to burn my finger on one of the bristles when I tried to hold my hair while brushing it from beneath, so watch out for that.  Overall, this is a good product that will work better for some than others.  For me, I will continue to use the Straightening brush and finish with my flat iron.
summary: Not a dryer, more of a heated styling brush.

reviewText:
I really wanted to like this brush, I truly did. However, the truth is that my daughter and I both dislike it, and she has long straight hair and I have short, curly hair.

Here's why~
1. It's bulky and heavy and just seems it would be easier to use if it was much lighter.
2. The bristles are stiff and hard and the design just doesn't seem to hold the hair in place to do a good job.
3. Even though there's a lock button, I still have a hard time using the buttons and their placement isn't the best. Keep hitting them while in use.
4. It doesn't smooth our hair as it shows in the video/pics. Nothing close.

I wouldn't recommend it, sorry.
summary: A bulky product that just doesn't work like I thought it would. Disappointing.

reviewText: I am a "smooth" shampoo user and use my straightener almost every day.  So when given the opportunity to try this product, I was all for it.  Problem is, I just didn't like the results as much as using my normal 2 inch straightener.  I wanted to love this so much, but the results took longer (even on a high setting) and still didn't straighten my hair near as well.  I actually burnt my hand a little trying to push my hair into the comb because it wasn't gliding well even after I blow dried and I brushed all the tangles out of my hair.  I ended up using my straightener in the end to fix what this brush simply didn't do.. oh well :(  Boo!
summary: Didn't like as much as I thought I would...

reviewText: I like this, but it seems as though i would definitely need a good serum to go along. It has a nice long cord with a Velcro strap to wrap it up when finished. It has 4 temp settings, the highest being 430. The back of the brush doesn't get hit and your able to brush from root to ends. You need to make sure your hair is knot free. My hair is not thick, but I have a lot of it and it's between wavy and curly. It took me about 20 minutes to run the brush through my entire long head of hair. In the end it was straight but frizzy, not smooth. I will be using a good serum with it next time to see if it helps.
summary: I like this, but it seems as though i would ...

reviewText: Cuts styling time down! I have really fine, somewhat frizzy, kinky hair and have used a flat iron for years, this however is so much easier to use and works nearly as well as my flat iron and takes SO much less time and energy to use. The flat iron would take at least a good 20 minutes to use and would inevitably fry the ends of my hair, even with protective spray. This works in about 5-8 minutes and is way easier on my hair, takes away all the frizz and except just just a little flip on the ends of my hair leaves it straight and smooth. I love it and see using it all the time!
summary: I have really fine, somewhat frizzy

reviewText:
Let me start by saying that the current description for this product is wrong. "The speed dr) brush is open vented which helps channel the air from the blow dryer while the curved shape hugs the scalp getting closer to the root allowing for the removal of excess water: speeding drying time by up to 30 percent."  Um, no. It's not a blow dryer and you use it like a flat iron on DRY hair.

With that out of the way, I like it! I have long, extremely thick curly hair that I like to wear straight on occasion.  I blow dry it as straight as I can, then have to use a flat iron to get it smooth and silky. Only problem is, it also makes my hair very flat. A good look on many women, but not on me. With this brush, I can get my hair straight but also maintain some volume. It's easy to pull it through a section of hair just using one hand. As a bonus, you can use this device to make easy flips or curls at the end of your hair!

In summary, if you want super-straight, sleek hair, buy a traditional flat iron. But if you're looking for straight hair with volume, then I recommend this product.

Thus worked great to help me smooth out my hair after wearing it in a bun or ponytail. If I put my hair up for even a short time it gets kinks in it. Well this heated up quickly and slid right through my hair brushing it and straightening it all at once. My hair looked smooth and glossy afterwards and it seemed to last all afternoon. This is a really great way for a busy mom to keep up with looking put together, without stress and money and time. I love it.

This Super Smoother Electric Straightening Brush from TS2 is kind of a quicker alternative to a flat iron for straightening your hair.

I have used flat irons over the years and they do a great job of straightening my frizzy, kinky hair but it takes forever since my hair is long and fairly thick. Also, if I use a flat iron too often, it does dry my hair out.

This is like a regular hair brush that heats from 320 degrees to 430 degrees and does a remarkable job straightening my hair in a very short period of time. I do use a heat protection product on my hair prior to using heated styling tools.

Here are my tips for getting the best results with this brush:
1. Make sure your hair is completely dry.
2. Use a heat protection product on your hair prior to use.
3. Use the lowest possible temperature that gives you the desired results.
4. Brush or comb your hair completely before using this straightening brush. This may be a brush but it doesn't handle tangles well at all.
5. For the smoothest possible hair, use small sections at a time. You can definitely use large sections and it will straighten your hair but the hair won't be quite as smooth.
6. Move slowly down each strand and keep the strand in the center of the brush as much as possible.
7. Let your hair cool before pinning or clipping or brushing or applying hair spray.

One big difference between a straightening brush and a flat iron is that you can't get as close to the roots with the brush. This may be very important depending upon your hair type.

I prefer the brush but I've discovered I can use both together when I want super smooth, silky hair. I use the straightening brush with larger sections of hair and quickly straighten my whole head. Then I come back with my flat iron and smooth out the top layers of hair. The results are really excellent in almost no time.

The power button is on the handle and you use it to cycle through the various temps (320, 350, 400, 430). The selected temp is indicated by an LED. You can also lock the temp by holding the power button depressed for 2 seconds.

A word of caution - you can still burn your fingers with this so I suggest a heat resistant glove.

This has a thick, round power cord that's 9 ft. long and moves easily in any direction. It also has a velcro cord management strip for more convenient storage.

My daughter has a USpicy straightening brush, which currently retails for about $10 more than this brush. I've used hers, too, several times and there are some slight differences. Hers heats up 20 degrees hotter (450) and the brush area is a little bigger. Hers comes with a single heat resistant glove and a storage pouch. Hers has a digital temperature read out and a wider range of temps (250 to 450.) I got the same results on my hair using both products because I don't use either product at the max temperature and I already own some heat resistant gloves.

If you don't have a heat resistant glove or your hair needs a max temp of 450 degrees to achieve straightening, look at the USpicy. Otherwise this brush works just as well for $10 less and I'm really happy with it (although I really wish they had included a travel/storage pouch.)
summary: Way less time for straight hair than with a flat iron

reviewText: My teenage daughter has waist length hair, and she straightens her hair at least twice a week. Her hair isn't curly, but she likes her hair straighter than her natural hair. As long as her hair is, she has to brush it out first, before using the straightener brush. Tangles are hard to get out with the electric brush, so she gets them out with another brush first. She loves this straightener, as she says it works faster than a flat iron. So far this works great. I hope it doesn't damage her hair like flat irons can do over time. So far she loves it, it's so easy to use. Has different settings for different types of hair!

I was super skeptical about the ability of a brush to straighten. My hair is curly. I usually blow dry my hair straight and then straighten it with the straightener. However, with this, I tried it on just my dry, curly hair. I was thinking it was an unfair trial because there was no way it would do anything without me blow drying it straight first. I was shocked when it actually straightened my hair. It also didn't take nearly as long as my regular straightener. I couldn't get my hair stick straight like I can with my Chi, but I can get it pretty straight and smooth. I am very impressed.

These straightening combs are pretty amazing, my wife really likes them since they are super easy to use, and they work quite well for her.  She has another one which is quite similar to this one, although the brush part is a bit larger, and the controls are digital instead of the more analog selections here.  They both are quite similar otherwise (i.e. very quick heat up, ceramic brush elements with some rubberized bristles).

This one wasn't as nice since the edge pieces can catch the hair in some cases, not sure if that will be better over time, or just a design issue.  You can lock the heat setting in so you don't accidentally change/turn off your brush when using it.  There is also a nice built in hook and loop (i.e. velcro) fastener on the cord that lets you wrap up the (9ft) cord.
summary: These straightening combs are pretty amazing, my wife really likes them since they ...

reviewText: As a busy mom of two, I don't have hours to spend getting dressed and using various hair tools and products. This is a great tool to use if you don't have a lot of time in the mornings. I brushed through my dry hair a few times paying special attention to the shorter layers and was ready to go. It has several different heat settings for different hair types.  The only complaint I had was trying to straighten short pieces is kinda hair with the brush bristles and by the end of the day the humidity had gotten the best of it.

This cream makes my skin incredibly smooth. I LOVE it. I use it once a day so they're lasted me longer than normal. It doesn't have a scent which my sensitive skin appreciates. This feels and looks beautiful under my makeup. It definitely smooths the fine lines on my forehead. The price can be a little high for some, but this product will make your skin feel so luscious. I love also how it smooths out my pores making going without makeup less obvious and evens out my skin tone. Cindy is onto something. I look forward to incorporating more of her line in my daily skin care routine.
summary: I LOVE it. I use it once a day so ...

reviewText:
There is always a tradeoff to value versus price. For those who can afford the 'gimmick' of measured doses through capsules, it's a nice way to put the perfect amount onto your skin.  But at the same time, knowing how much waste goes into this is also a bit frustrating and I wished there was a little spatula rather than capsules.

To use, each capsule has a little tab on top to break off and then squeeze the premeasured amount onto your fingertip.  You then spread this across the areas that could use some wrinkle reduction - e.g., eyes and mouth lines.  This is for fine lines, of course - it won't remove all lines or the deeper wrinkles. But in reducing the smaller wrinkles, you will notice a difference.

This has a light and not problematic scent - you won't notice its on once it seeps into skin.  I put this on under makeup just fine.  Yes, I have noticed the small change in wrinkle appearance so it does indeed work.  But again, its purpose is to reduce, not remove, so you'll always need to be using this when you want those wrinkles less noticeable.  For me, it's a special occasion treatment due to the price.

I've been using this serum daily for 3 weeks, and honestly, I can't really tell any difference in my facial crinkles.  I have some thin lines at the corners of my eyes, some on my forehead and some slightly sun damaged skin on my cheekbones.  I was hoping this serum would fade out some of the lines and sun damage, but I swear, if it's better, it's only slightly.  I will continue to use this until I run out of it and update this review if I notice some improvement.  I thought 21 days would be long enough but I guess not.  After application my skin feels better (not as dry), but it doesn't last long and my skin gets tight and dry again causing me to apply lotion.

The delivery system (the purple squeezies) is fine but there really isn't enough in one capsule to adequately cover my face and still leave a little for my neck.  I frequently have to use two to get a full thin coating.  I like the beta or alpha hydroxy creams you can still buy at the drug store because they work and you can use as much as you want with no tiny casings to throw away.

This wrinkle cream is very moisturizing, and it acts like a primer.  I apply it in the morning, before I put on my foundation.  It glides over my skin, and makes it feel really soft.

I like the capsules.  It is the perfect amount for my face and neck.  Since they are portioned out, I don't waste any.  The lotion doesn't have a scent, so it doesn't overpower me as I apply it.  You pull the little part off the capsule, and then apply it to your skin.

If you have ever used Smashbox primer, that is exactly how this moisturizer feels when you apply it.  It glides onto your skin, and leaves it feeling smooth.  If you are looking for a wrinkle cream that does double duty as a primer, then this one is perfect for you!
summary: Leaves my skin smooth, and works perfectly as a primer for my foundation.

reviewText:
60 capsules of serum/moisturizer in a jar with screw top.

The capsules are a nice idea, but I'm not entirely sold on it. It's not that it is a hassle, but it's just an added step to my already "beauty in a hurry" attitude. It gives me a good amount of product to smooth on my face, but not so much on the throat and chest, however. The good part is there's no dipping my fingers into the cream and having too much, or contaminating the rest (though I always use clean hands and only I use my creams).

Applying the lotion is so very nice. Leaves my skin feeling soft and smooth. There's no way for me to tell what it's doing at a "cellular level" because not enough time has passed for me to know what effect this will have on my skin long-term.

But a big negative is that it's way over my budget. At 60 capsules, two a day, that is a month of product for $54 (at time of this review). So $54 a month for a serum. If I thought it was doing really great things I still couldn't pay $54 a month. I could use it once a day and that would make it more manageable, but there are also other serums on the market that aren't as expensive and give the same feeling to my face and make the same claims. Perhaps this line of Cindy Crawford products does have better quality ingredients and some "magic" to it, but I still would have a hard time paying $54 a month for any beauty product on my budget.

Money aside, if I weren't concerned with my budget, I'm not sure if I would purchase. I really do like how it makes my skin feel but I have less expensive serums that feel great too. If I see that it does wonders for my face as time goes on, I'll come back to reflect that.
summary: Silky smooth skin and just the right amount in the capsules for my face

reviewText: This is a nice light weight lotion in tiny capsules.  When I apply it, the lotion goes on smoothly and although I don't have many wrinkles, it does seem to act as a filler or pre makeup smoother.  I don't know why it is made this way.  It seems like an awful expense to place a tiny drop of lotion into all these little capsules.  The jar is nothing to speak of for such a pricey product.  I would rather just buy the lotion then have to go through popping it out of  purple bubbles.  On the positives, it doesn't smell and is lightweight.
summary: Okay, kind of pricey for the amount you get.

reviewText: This meaningful Beauty wrinkle smoothing product in small purple capsules has little to no odor which is a plus. Small capsules you twist the top off and squeeze out. At first I didn't like this feature but it has grown on me, I like getting the measured amount and they are sealed keeping them fresh. Be sure to press the small amount out of the small piece you twist off. I do find this makes my skin feel silky yet it has not changed the size or shape of my wrinkles. I have a couple smile lines and small crows feet and occasional forehead furrow if I get dehydrated. My skin had no reaction or break outs, redness or swelling. I will be happy to continue this product but not sure if I would get it again due to no changes in the actual wrinkling. It does make the skin feel very soft and silky.

These capsules are off the hook.  They are like little tiny squeezes of thick, liquid creamy silk.  The feel of the product is insane, so soft, it absorbs right away.  It smooths and relaxes the lines.  I only wish the capsules were bigger.  I can't get all the problem areas on my face without using it all up and I want to use it on my neck, too.  I love these.  This is the second product in this line that I have.  I really thought the whole melon and French doctor was a TV gimmick, but the products, thus far, are amazing.  LOVE THEM!
summary: I wish they made a capsule big enough for me to climb inside

reviewText: One tiny capsule covers my entire face. It smells nice and goes on smooth, without much residue left behind on my hand. However, after a couple weeks of use, I really don't see much difference. It's a nice moisturizer, I don't know that I'd spend this money on something that doesn't have lasting results.
summary: It smells nice and goes on smooth

reviewText: The small capsules help to measure out the right amount. Wife loves the smooth creamy easy to spread lotion. She has reported that she sees very little improvement in small wrinkles after two weeks of use but it does make her skin feel soft and smooth. She currently does not see paying this price for such small improvement but if anything seems to improve we will file an updated review.
summary: Leaves skin feeling smooth and silky. No real sign of improving small wrinkles.

reviewText: The jar contains 60 adorable purple blebs which, when popped open, can be squeezed to evoke a white silky fluid which can then be smoothed into one's face. I often find that moisturizers leave a little too much of a sheen on my skin, and would rather have a substance that leaves my skin looking healthy but dry rather than looking like I forgot to dry my face after a shower, or like I've just spread a thin, albeit clean, film of motor oil on my cheeks. The feel of this smoothing product is unlike any other product I've tried, sort of like running a thin film of silk onto my skin. The liquid leaves my face feeling well moisturized throughout the day, without the dry chapped skin that I often get in the winter, but without looking like I've used "product." Does it actually smooth out wrinkles? Well, perhaps the very fine lines around my eyes, but more than that hasn't responded to any over-the-counter product. Now if I could only keep my girlfriend from using these, I might actually get the full 60 days' use from the jar.
summary: These are great for menthey moisturize and smooth without making it look obvious that you've used any skin product

reviewText:
When this serum came in the mail, I was really hoping it would keep my skin moist in the winter.  The first thing I really liked about it was that there are little pods of serum that are more sterile than dipping your hand in a jar every night.  I found them easy to open with a pinch of my nail.  That is pretty much the only positive thing about it.

I was not happy on how it works and I don't know why or how Cindy Crawford can look so good at her age only using this product.  While it goes on fine under make-up, it really did nothing for me.  I am 52 and Caucasian.  I know there is no magical cream or serum that will erase already existing lines, but I do want to prevent lines and have existing ones less noticeable.  I used the serum twice a day for nine days and I think my skin looks older.  I am drinking plenty of water and the lines on my forehead are now more pronounced.  It just did not work for me.
summary: It made my lines more pronounced after a week.

reviewText:
I've used a couple of Cindy Crawford Meaningful Beauty products-my favorite being the ones that contain the Melon Complex and Melon Extract. I have found that nothing compares to the fabulous results I get from the Night Moisturizer with Melon Extract. This Meaningful Beauty Wrinkle Smoothing Capsules Advanced Formula, Hyaluronic Acid Targeted Treatment Serum, 60 Count are small and targeted to the deeper forehead and laugh lines.

These capsules have a twist off end, so that tiny drop goes on totally fresh. I've been using these for a few weeks and though my forehead and laugh lines are still there, the lines themselves are actually smoother and softer. The results are much quicker when using the Night Moisturizer with Melon Extract than using these capsules. The deeper lines on the forehead and around the mouth are very hard to get rid of, and so far, these capsules are not showing any dramatic results, but the lines do feel softer and smoother after a few weeks. I'm hoping long term, the results will be better, but for now, I'm happy with the softening of the lines and I feel this is a 4 STAR product.

I have very sensitive skin. Meaningful Beauty did burn when I put it on, not horribly but my face definitely felt hot. It continued for about thirty minutes. I was careful not to get it near my eyes. Does this work, well my skin felt smoother. I did not notice any difference in fine lines but my face was soft and felt hydrated. I used this only at night as it caused my face to also become red for about an hour when I applied it under my make up.

The capsules are easy to open and you only need one.  This goes on well and you do not need more than the amount in the little capsule. This is convenient and helps you with the proper amount of product. I will continue to use this at night but will not do so in the morning due to the burning sensation and red skin.
summary: Hydrates but beware if you have sensitive skin

reviewText: I have tried several different creams like this, but this one really works for me. It is scented, but if that sort of thing isn't a concern for you, you'll be fine. I have experienced no irritation or any breakouts as I do tend to do with facial creams. My skin is smoother, softer and I couldn't be more pleased. I have used it once a day for a week and I am noticing a difference. I use in morning under makeup.

Meaningful Beauty Wrinkle Smoothing Capsules contain a white, silky serum that's supposed to improve the appearance of facial expression lines. I'm in my 50's and have sensitive skin that tends to get really dry. I apply this serum all over my face and neck, but I first concentrate on problem areas on my forehead and around my eyes and mouth. This serum isn't greasy and my skin absorbs it quickly. I apply my face cream after (like I do after applying any face serum) and then apply my makeup with no issues. The biggest benefit so far is that this serum makes my skin feel really soft and smooth.

This serum adds some hydration but isn't as soothing or hydrating for my dry skin as my favorite serums. I don't notice any immediate plumping or improvement in the appearance of my fine lines. Still, this product has a pleasing feel and nice attributes- it's non irritating, has no added fragrance (hard to find) and no parabens (a controversial preservative). It also has ingredients that sound good quality like melon fruit extract, olive oil, jojoba seed extract, sunflower seed oil and more. I like this serum enough to use all 60 capsules and see if I notice any visible improvement in the long term.

I really like the capsule delivery system. I find them easy to gently twist open and squeeze to get all the product so none is wasted. The product is fresh and free of bacteria that gets into a product from dipping into a container with a finger (as most of us probably don't use a spatula). Plus, the product is pre measured and is the perfect amount for one application. I also like knowing how many applications are left-a guessing game with a serum pump. In short, I like the capsules, the serum quality and how smooth the product makes my skin feel. So far, it doesn't seem quite hydrating enough for my dry skin-but it is likely to suit those with less dry skin. I'm hoping for some longer term benefits, but can't judge them until I use all 60 capsules. I'll update as appropriate.
summary: Good Quality Serum That's Non Irritating To My Dry Sensitive Skin And Makes My Skin Feel Soft But Not As Hydrated As I Like

reviewText: This product rates on the low end of moderately toxic according to the EWG website (a 3 out of 10). It contains Cyclopetasiloxane which is classified as toxic by Canada not to mention a possible endocrine disruptor and Oryza Sativa Rice which can contain high pesticides unless it is organic.  I don't know why celebrities put their name on products without researching the ingredients.  These are probably the same capsules I used in the eighties that were under a different brand name.  I did like them back in the 80's but I'm into more natural products these days since there is more information out there.

Oh, my goodness! You won't believe it until you see it and touch it. This Meaningful Beauty wrinkles smoothing formula glides on like your skin is silk. No joke! I was extremely amazed in how my skin felt. Granted, I haven't used it for a long time yet, BUT if I notice anything different I will return to edit my review. - So, in the meantime, this capsule contents makes my skin feel wonderful! This advanced formula hyaluronic acid is to boost your skin's hydration level for a dewey appearance. And apparently, my skin must of needed hydration in the worst way because I had to use 2 of the capsules to moisturize my skin. In the winter, I should order a 10 gallon container of this stuff as my skin is severely dry.  But now it feels so smooth, and I love it! I'm so hopeful that my laugh lines, frown lines, creases below nose to mouth, and crow's feet around my eye's will have a better appearance going forward. I just cannot say enough good things about Meaningful Beauty.

This cream is so amazing I am willing to forgive the silly delivery system and inelegant jar. Simply twist off the top of the little purple "pearl" housing a dollop of cream and spread on your face. The cream is white and has no discernible odor. It absorbs immediately and leaves skin feeling smooth and moistand looking fresh and dewy. Even my 86 year ld mother loved it. Her skin is drier than the Sahara and although she has few wrinkles she does have deep laugh lines. Although there was no noticeable difference in the lines (to be fair it has only been a week) her skin looks and feels better than it has in year. So this cream is definitely a keeper.

I find the capsule system rather silly. I use Elizabeth arden ceramide capsules occasionally and they too come in capsules reportedly to prevent oxidation. Unlike those, however, these actually ar easy to open . Some of the cream makes it way out of the opening. But it doesn't spill and you don't lose any. On one hand  I suppose it is nice to have the proper amount divvied up but on the other hand faces and needs differ. Today one capsule may be sufficient but tomorrow you might need more. there are sixty capsules in the jar and the capsule form is not a deal breaker.

The jar is decidedly inelegant. Plain glass with a silver metal screw on cap, it is plain. And not in the minilalist chic way but plain in the "i got a lot of these for cheap at Big Lots" way. It is functional, easy to open but certainly no collector's item. But again the product is sufficiently impressive that I am happy to overlook the lack of packaging niceties. The labels  match the jar in lack of design. Even worse they are hard to read with small,
light gray print. In the end it is what is on the inside that counts. In this case, the cream is simply amazing.

I am 50 years old and have always had great skin, which I understand is a genetic gift. I wear no makeup and instead spend my money on simple, high quality skin care.

My routine is simple - an oil cleanser, followed by rose hip oil, a serum, eye serum, and an oil (jojoba or vitamin e) to top it off. My skin has never looked better!

Many products are made with anti-oxidant ingredients, and need to be kept away from light and air. The easiest way to do this is to use single-use ampules, which is what this product does. This packaging gives you the optimum amount per use, while also limiting the spread of bacteria from your fingers, as well the introduction of water or other products to the mix.

The ampules are easy to open. Just hold upright and twist off the top. Each capsule contains one use, so it is easy!

This is lightweight and odor-free. It just smooths right in, leaving no residue at all. My skin looks great, with temporary fading of any fine lines. I would use this again!
summary: Easy to use and my skin looks great!

reviewText:
I have read the other reviews and I don't know why some people hate the capsules. It may seem like a waste of space but if they didn't have them I am sure I would end up using more of the product than I need and that same amount would not last 60 days. I don't know if the cream needs to be in capsules to prevent oxidation. If not, then maybe a pump would be better.
When I first opened a capsule I thought it would be more liquidy and spill out. But it is a nice silly cream that is enough to cover my face and neck. It doesn't take long to absorb. I'm sure this could be used in the mornings under makeup but I prefer to put it on in the evening a couple hours before bed.
My skin definitely feels moisturized after use. Hopefully this will reduce current wrinkles and slow the new wrinkles from coming. It is hard to tell if the product is worth the price because it can take a while to work. I'm not one to buy celebrity products but Cindy Crawford is known for working with dermatologists on skin care products. I guess time will tell.

I'm nearly 50 with dry, sensitive skin. While I adore the Meaningful Beauty Creme de Serum Meaningful Beauty Crème de Serum, Night Moisturizer with Melon Extract, Peptides, and Hyaluronic Acid, 1 Fluid Ounce, I don't care for these capsules much. They're OK, and I'll use them up, but I won't reorder. The purple capsules are tough to open. I twist the end off, and some product splatters on my hands. There's still enough for your face and neck even if you lose part of it squeezing too hard. What don't I like? I feel like I'm slathering straight dimethicone all over my face. Slimy feeling -- and too much dimethicone and I don't get along too well. I end up with milia sometimes. As far as smoothing out wrinkles and laugh lines? I don't notice that at all, and even if I did, it would be only temporary. I've seen other beauty skincare lines that use these type capsules, and the manufacturers swear the enclosed capsules keep product from the light so it doesn't oxidize. I have no idea why this cream is in a capsule, but 60 of these for a somewhat high price isn't very cost-effective for me. I've reordered the Creme de Serum since I started using it 6 months ago, and I love that product so much more.
summary: I don't like the "feel" of this on my skin

reviewText:
When I gave this tube a squeeze, I was surprised at the relative thinness of the product. I was expecting a thick creme that I would have to rub between my hands until it was warm/thin enough to work through my thick, Eastern-European, too-long, wavy hair (trust me, it can be an unruly mess). So, already I was impressed. Then, I caught the light fragrance. It's a little perfume-y ... in a really good way. So, I worked a moderate amount through my hair, stacked it in a bun and pinned it there for about an hour. And, man, when I unpinned it, that gorgeous fragrance just surrounded me. Super appealing!

Now, the first time, I make the mistake of combing my hair. It gain about double the volume and looked insane. The second time I used it, I ran my fingers through my hair instead ... and, presto! Beautiful, loose, defined curls as well as volume. Therefore, you may wish to skip the comb/brush. And, soft? Oh my gosh, each curl is genuinely touchable-y soft. My boyfriend just loves touching my hair ... what a nice bonus!

Not only does this smell heavenly, but the overall look is gorgeous! Genuinely recommended!

After washing and using a small amount of conditioner I applied about a pea-sized drop, which I spread between my palms onto my shoulder length curly hair. I stuck primarily to the lower two-thirds of my hair. My hope was that it would not weigh down my hair. It is finely textured but I have lots of it. Most curl serums and primers while keeping down frizz also weigh down the curls. Some dry hard and crunchy leaving hair looking good but feeling brittle and unpleasant.

So, my expectations were low but this product actually worked quite well. Granted I used just a small amount but it had no sticky feel on my hands, it smelled great and tamed the frizz leaving soft defined curls. And, since fragrance is subjective, so while I really liked it, others may not, but it did not linger at all. I could not smell it on my hair after air drying.

Because it is thin, it was easy to distribute throughout my hair. A small amount did a good job and I expect the tube to last for quite a while. A little pricey but performed well.

This product works well as a primer, which means it is a product you would use before adding your typical styling products.  Just used on it's own, with no additional styling products and no heat, it does a good job of keeping frizzy flyaways to a minimum and doesn't get super crunchy or stiff.  There is a nice, light fragrance to the product that lasts for a while but isn't overpowering.  I have very fine hair but a whole lot of it that can get weighed down by product and I didn't find this product to be overly heavy or super greasy for my hair type.  I do also have more of a wave than any substantial curl to my hair, which means I have to load up on product and drying to keep the curl I can get to stay; this product is a good base to help protect my hair from those abuses I might put it through on the days when I want to have a bit more curl.
summary: it does a good job of keeping frizzy flyaways to a minimum and ...

reviewText: I gave this to my daughter who has long curly hair that can get a little frizzy from time to time. She has tried it a couple of times and she really likes it. Her hair is noticeably less frizzy and has a nice shine. It also adds volume and definition to her curls without crunch or crust. It is very lightweight and doesn't weigh her hair down. She uses it as a leave-in conditioner on her damp hair and also uses her usual styling products afterwards. It is a great product but pricey.

I confess I have zero curl in my fine waist length hair. What I do have is frizz, especially when it rains. We've had several weeks of straight rain here in southern WI and my hair is climbing to heaven. I applied a dime sized amount to my dry hair and wham! I not only had control, I had shine. I happen to really like the scent as well. I tried this on wet hair but it was not as effective for me. Since I am not the target user, I understand that this is designed to comb through damp hair.

Very happy with the product. Don't be afraid to use it in the manner that works for you. Will definitely buy this in the future.
summary: Off label user but truly love it! Frizz fighter!

reviewText: I have very curly hair and usually use John Frieda's Frizz Ease Secret Weapon touch-up creme. It does a great job of keeping my hair smooth and in ringlets or less defined curls depending on how much I want to put in. It costs about $6 at any grocery store or convenience store. When I have ordered this product, priced $25, I have expected a lot more from it than from a $6 alternative. My curls felt a bit more glossier and that is ALL! I used it several times just to account for weather, my hair's moods and styles, but it did not do anything more than other much better priced products. The hair stayed soft and lightweight, frizz free and defined, but there are several other products under $10 that do the same. I guess I was looking for a lot more for the price. Something truly spectacular, or just simply much better if I was going to pay four times more than my current product.
summary: It does a great job of keeping my hair smooth and in ringlets ...

reviewText: This works really well to keep my wavy hair frizz free and gives it body all day.  A little goes a long way and I have shoulder length hair so this tube will last awhile. I use this primer and then my usual mousse and texture spray.

Edit:  I gave this to my sister, who does have really curly hair, and she loves it.  "Best curl cream I ever used in my life" and "it's a knock out of the park," she says.  So I'm leaving my own review below, but raising to 5 stars.  (For me it was only a 2-star product.)
...

My hair is naturally wavy; with a little effort, I can corkscrew my damp hair into curly tendrils and let it air dry.  I don't typically get a really "curly" look but it is much more curly than my usual "comb and let it air dry" method.  I tried my corkscrew method this morning after using the Twister Curl Primer and it looks no different from the "comb and let it air dry" method.  Then, when my hair was dry, I tried using my curling iron to see if the Twister would help hold the curls a little longer.  So far so good - but then, my hair usually holds curling-iron-curls at least overnight.  Perhaps I am not the right target audience for the product, since I don't have "curly hair" - but can report that it did not make my hair greasy or crunchy.  So at least there's that.  But I wouldn't re-buy.
summary: Perhaps it's good for girls with really, really curly hair.

reviewText:
This stuff is great.  It works as a standalone curl enhancer, adding spring and definition without weight, crunch, or crust.  I've been experimenting with using it as a base with a mouse or gel.  For my hair, it seems to be a good curl-starter, and then I've been finishing it with a little bit of styling creme/pomade.  My wife, who also has curly hair is enjoying it as a standalone project.  Her hair looks amazing!

One thing: the smell is kind of strange. I wish it were odorless since it's technically a base layer for other product.  Anyway, easily overlooked as it fades once applied.

I'm really pleased with this product. I have short, thick curly hair. It helps tame the frizz and if I put it in when my hair is damp, I get nice, smooth curls. (If you want a lot of detailed definition, you may still need a product like Paul Mitchell's Round Trip on top of this---I've also had good luck with Citrseal to control frizz.)

My concern is the price. Round Trip, at its priciest, is $17 for more product, and Citrseal is $10 for a LOT more product. The R+Co Twister Curl Primer is quite runny, so you can expect to use this up pretty quickly. (I would be hesitant to let my teenager use it for this reason---her curly hair is pretty long and she'd probably go through this small tube in about ten days.)  If budget is no concern, go for it; otherwise, you might want to use this for special occasions if the cheaper products don't work well for you.

I have thinner long hair but love wearing curly hair on the first day after washing my hair.  Curl products do a great job of activating the curl for my hair and this product worked great. Not as good as a salon product that I use by Redken for curls but this works great.  My hair is soft and the curls are nice and bouncy. Not as curly as the other product I use but almost as good.

I applied a dollop and spread through my hair - Dried a little with a hair dryer but let air dry and scrunched my hair.. Happy with this product !
I was not terribly impressed.  This product did not really do anything to enhance my curls, and it certainly did not help tame the frizz.  I think I would pass on this one.
summary: Did not work well for me

reviewText:
For my type of hair, the hold was not very strong. However, it did say you could use it as a base for your other styling products. Still, at that price point, it's an expensive product.

Having said all that, I did like it. If your hair is not as curly as mine, you'll probably like it more.

It didn't really hold the curls, but I wet my hands with water and lightly touched the ends of my hair, which made them curl up nicely. It also made my hair feel quite soft, not hard as occurs with other styling products.

The scent is a light botanic scent, and the product feels light in your hands.

This product is best for people who have moderately curly or wavy hair.

I have almost curly hair, so this product worked okay, but not great.  HOWEVER, if you have super curly hair, this stuff is going to rock your hair.  It is not stiff, goes on like a cream and when your hair dries, your curls are locked in place and soft and really nice.  For my very wavy hair with a bit of curl it worked pretty well. I tucked everything up into a ponytail and left a few wavy wisps around my face - lasted all day.  So I think if you have that great natural curly hair you will love this product.  If you have wavy hair like I do, maybe pass on this, unless you have some curl.  Nice smell, fades fast.  This tube will last for quite a while you don't need to use much at all to get your hair set.
summary: Interesting product.  Great for super curly hair.

reviewText: I have wavy, medium curly hair that rests on my shoulders. In my experience, finding a hair gel designed for curls which delivers on its promise is rare. R+Co Twister Curl Primer does offer a hold that lasts all day. I use a small, dime size amount and rub it between my palms. Then I apply the product to the ends of my hair, damp from the shower but not soaking wet, staying away from my scalp. I next spray my hair with hairspray to lock it in. My curls lasted all day and the product was light, not greasy. I follow this regimen with different gels, and sometimes my hair stays intact and others, not so much. I am not giving the product five stars because at the end of the day, my hair had frizz and the curls were not as bouncy as in the morning. However, given how little product I used, it seems to be a good option.

Its a good product but i am not entirely sure its for me. I do have curly/wavy hair and i use curl creams to give me a messy yet put together, wet hair look. This product did do that but it also made my hair dry :( hence the 3 stars. I used it on my wet hair and let it air dry but it made my hair little frizzy and dry. May be like the other reviewers pointed out, your hair needs to be really curly for this cream to work. I will use this when I am out on the beach but not for an everyday look.
P.S It does smell good though.

It's in the name, but in case it's unclear, this works best as a primer as opposed to a catch-all product that results in your desired look. This clean and fresh-smelling stuff helps prevent frizz and disorder, but as far as styling or anything with hold goes, you'll need something else. Not to worry, though--it works well with other products, which you can use to set whatever style of curls or waves you want.
Nice step one product with a great, light scent--just remember you'll need more supplies to finish a look.
summary: Half the solution to wrangling curls

reviewText:
2/12/17- One more update. This is my new go to product.
No matter what else I use or alternate...Every. Time. I use this my style lasts AFTER I comb it out.
Straight. Waves. Curls. Always bounces back.
Worth every penny!

*10/25/16 Update*
Without using any additional styling product, my waves that I curl to smooth out & add definition LASTED until my next wash (3days!)
Was able to brush/comb & they bounced back!!
AND this really smells great & clean!

Org Review-So this is a primer which best I can gather is like a leave in conditioner with texture definition. I tried this on wet & dry hair. On dry hair, that already had product, refreshed my waves & gave a beachy, salt air, teased look. Now, on the wet hair with no additional product ...Whoa! Soft and defined waves. I wear my hair as "natural" as possible but after 20 plus years of various color treating, I need product! I feel like this may be what I'm looking for. Smell great! Clean not fragranced. Think I may have to get my guy to ck this out!
summary: Run your fingers through soft & wavy

reviewerName: German Girl with a Spanish Name
reviewText:
UPDATE:  It's been 8 months and this is still my go to for when I want to let my hair air dry!!  I love this stuff and will definitely continue to use it.  Only thing is, if you live in a place with high humidity it might not be that great.  I find on humid/rainy days my hair does get frizzy pretty quickly.

I have dry frizzy hair, that has some curl/wave to it.  I'm always in search of a product that will allow me to air dry my hair (I hate blow drying) and just go.  And I think this one might finally do the trick.  It gave my curls definition but no crunch like you might get from gels or mousses.  And also didn't dry into a big poofy mess like it normally does.  A+ for this product.  My only issue was that the tube wasn't sealed and leaked during shipping.
Pleasant smell. Good texture--I was able to distribute it mostly evenly throughout my hair. My hair had more volume but I cannot say it actually helped with the curling process.
summary: Good texture--I was able to distribute it mostly evenly throughout ...

reviewText:
This creamy serum works well to define curls, and makes it easy for me to achieve the intensity that my natural wavy/curly hair has.  It says that it won't make your hair crunchy, but it does make my hair crunchy, and it makes it look like I am going for the wet look.  I'm not going for that look, so I was a bit disappointed in that.

The cream is kind of sticky, and a little goes a long way. Instantly, after I put it on, my hair felt slightly sticky.  Using less is best, especially the first time you use it, so you can see what it is going to do.
summary: Creates more of a wet look with my hair.

reviewText: I don't like to spend a fortune on the hair products I use, because I've found the inexpensive stuff works just as well for me.  That being said I really do like this product and depending on how long the tube lasts I could see myself buying it. Right now my hair is color treated, below my shoulders and naturally curly. A little of this product goes a long way, I'm using maybe a nickel-sized amount on my damp hair after the shower. Then I apply the products I normally use which are mousse and a little bit of finishing spray. I found that using this product I don't have any additional frizz and the curls stay together better. Overall it's a good product that seems to work and smells nice and if this  tube ends up lasting me between 45 to 60 days, I'd be okay paying the current price.

I'm a white girl with long, extremely thick, voluminous curly hair. My curls have a silky texture and are not dry. I usually use Devacurl products to wash and style. I like trying new products every once in a while, but usually end up disappointed. Didn't really have high hopes for this primer, as the glowing reviews sounded a little fake to me.

I washed and conditioned my hair as usually. This product is supposed to be a curl "primer" to be used as a foundation for other products. However, the directions just say to apply to damp hair, and don't mention adding other products over it. I was a little unsure of what to do, so I just used the primer alone.

This went on like a leave-in conditioner, not like a gel or anything that would hold curls together. I began drying with a diffuser and really thought, "Ugh!" when it appeared all I was going to get was limp strands of curls. However! The more I dried the bigger the volume and the more defined the curls! When I was done, I can honestly say I've never seen such poppin' curls.  Soft, frizz-free and a huge head of hair.  Curly girls need to try this!

(Just a little side note: This primer is for people WITH curly hair. It's not going to give you curls if your hair is straight.)

This is very good on my daughter's curly hair.  She has thick, VERY curly hair.  This primer worked pretty well on her hair.  I used it as directed on her wet hair and then let it air dry.  It kept her curls springy and smooth.  When her hair was totally dry the curls were intact and looked great.  There was a nice scent, but not overpowering.  Overall, this worked well for us!
summary: Nice for my daughters difficult curly hair

reviewText: This is a great styling product.  I've used a lot of these and found them to leave a film on my hair that weighs it down but that's not the case with this one.  It's lightweight, has a pleasing scent and it helps bring out the natural curl in my hair as well as control the frizz.  It's become one of my favorite styling creams.  Definitely recommend it.

My partner likes my hair in ringlets, and she is amazed at what this stuff did for my curls. Well that and she applied it and put in a bunch of extra twists, but it definitely formed soft ringlets without any crunchiness. It is pretty darn good. Although she raves about it and that's all that matters.

It has a pleasant scent and comes out in a soft lotion like consistency. It dried with the same speed as always and has a strong but soft curl. Great product.
summary: Great soft curls, my partner loves it

reviewText:
I am so particular about my mascara wands. I know that the super large, full bristle mascara brushes are in vogue, but I can't use them. They just leave my eye lids messy and my lashes lackluster.
While I'm not into the injection molded wands either, (I've found many to be too 'sharp' and 'pokey'), I decided to give mad lash a try since it was the only gently curved one.
Oh my. The brush is not sharp, doesn't poke, and deposits perfectly rich black pigment over each and every lash. The curve is gentle, and the brush head itself seems to flex with my lid. Amazing.
The formula is not dry, yet not too 'wet' either. It applies easily, and dries very quicky. My lashes don't feel brittle, and it does not flake or run. I'm able to apply a touch up coat mid day or evening without clumping.
Totally worth the price. I love it!
The BEST BEST BEST!!! Im 55 and have tried at least as many mascaras. This really looks like false eyelashes if you add a bit extra.
Works but nothing fantastic.
Pretty good stuff, not waterproof , but no irritation

I received a sample tube of this in a beauty box and immediately loved it because it was the first and is the only mascara that I've ever used that doesn't flake into my eyes nor does it smear very much. In fact, the very minimal smearing is most likely from me rubbing my eyes without thinking. Doesn't clump, glob and gives me nice, thick lashes. Now if I only had a good friend to show me how to curl my eyelashes.......
summary: No flake - no clumping - stays on but comes off easily

reviewText: This is my current favorite mascara! It gives my lashes amazing volume without any clumps! I highly recommend it!
summary: This is my current favorite mascara! It gives my lashes amazing volume without ...

reviewText: This mascara makes my eyelashes look so amazing, I had a certified eyelash extension applicator (who was working on my mom) assume I had eyelash extensions.

I know my makeup. Seriously. I've been wearing it since I was 14 yrs old (40+yrs ago) and I've tried every brand on Earth- department store brands, designer brands, box store brands, drugstore brands, mail-order brands...you name it. And if I say this is the best mascara, it is. It's amazing stuff.

Ahhh I have finally found the mascara I've been looking for!! I feel like I've tried a million over the last couple years and had come to the conclusion that, no matter what you spend, they're all alike. I always thought I had pretty nice eyelashes, but I feel like my mascara always makes them look clumpy and blah. I had never heard of theBalm before when I came across it on Amazon, but I was struck by all the reviews from people who got it in their Ipsy box and ended up purchasing it. I figured it couldn't hurt to try; it's more expensive than a mascara you'd get in the drug store, but still relatively low cost compared to what you could spend.

After using it for a few days, I am in love! I think it must have something to do with the thin curved wand, but this mascara goes on so easily and actually lengthens my eyelashes and thickens them without making them clumpy. Seriously, every time I look in the mirror, I'm so happy because my eyelashes finally look how I want them to look. It comes off easily with my makeup remover and when I wake up in the morning, I don't have to use more makeup remover, like I have with mascaras in the past. I also love that the mascara is cruelty-free. So happy I discovered this!
Love Love love it

WAY better than Benefit They're Real. I received a sample of this in my December 2016 Ipsy bag. I did not think I was going to like it but it is seriously so nice! It does not clump at all and provides a perfect amount of length and volume. Once I run out of the sample size I have I will totally purchase the full size!
summary: One of the best I have ever tried!

reviewText: It is fine mascara; nothing too different about it.

The bottle this men's scent comes in is gorgeous.  It's a heavy glass, slightly smoked.  It has a thick bottom and the liquid is in a curved section.  It has a little bit of (masculine looking) black ribbon at the top.  It is a spray with a typical spray atomizer that works just fine.

My husband and I both like the scent.  It is a very, very nice scent if you like woodsy, fairly typical types of men's fragrance.  And it is a well known brand, easily recognized, almost iconic although not for its scents.

However, as nice as this is, I think it is relying more on brand name than a truly unique, yummy fragrance.  As I said, it is a very nice scent and has extraordinary packaging but I don't think it is quite good enough to justify its luxury status.

I love men's fragrances and wear Eternity for men a lot (even though I'm a woman). This spray has a nice woodsy aroma that reminds me of the now discontinued Woodland Men's Shower Gel from Bath and Body. I like this fragrance but the aroma lasts only about half a day. I would have expected it to last longer since men's products tend to have "staying power."

The black misty bottle with the black bow is super attractive.
summary: Nice woodsy men's fragrance that I like wearing but the aroma lasts only one-half day on me

reviewText:
Mr. Burberry is the first cologne I've found that tempts me away from the Chanel Platinum goste I've been wearing for years (er, decades). That's not too surprising, as I did a little online research and found quite a few similarities in the basenote/topnotes* between them. Both have a sandalwood base, and a citrus top note.

Between the two, my wife much prefers Mr. Burberry. A survey of the four kids breaks along gender lines, with the boys liking Platinum goste and the girls preferring Mr. Burberry, probably because it's a little lighter and more "floral" on top.

The black and white photos don't do justice to the color of this cologne - a lovely, pale aqua vitae blue. The bottle looks really great on the shelf.

* Mr. Burberry
Top Notes: Grapefruit, Tarragon, Cardamom
Heart Notes: Birch leaf, Nutmeg, Cedarwood
Base notes: Sandalwood, Vetiver, Guaiac wood
summary: Wife prefers this Mr. Burberry to my old Platinum goste

reviewText:
I am not good at discerning or finding right words for describing a smell. I think that after spraying it on my skin, I smell musk, wood, a hint of tobacco, and, maybe -- just maybe -- a bit of citrus. I love citrus and use Chanel Allure Homme Sport for day, but also like Lanvin or Armani -- for evening, so I cannot say that I am going to use this cologne a lot. However, I must admit that it is very solid perfume and makes a good impression.

The bottom line: this is a solid evening perfume for man. It is heavy and warm, quite long-lasting (I used just one pump of spray in the afternoon, worked out and showered afterwords, and I still smell it in the morning). It is pretty strong at first, so be careful with the amount and give it time to develop...

I was excited to try the Silk'n Flash & Go Hair Removal System.  This system is so easy to use.  You look at the instruction booklet and it will tell you based on your skin tone and hair color what settings you should use.  When you plug in the AC adapter a series of lights start flashing in a circle.  One orange and five green.  As soon as they are all flashing one right after another, the unit is ready to use.  You shave the area that you want to treat and then start the process of removing your unwanted hair.

The Silk'n Flash&Go system comes with a Silk'n Trim small pen size Trim unit which will allow you to trim areas such as your eyebrows.  The Trim unit also also comes with a shield that will allow you to determine the length of hair or if you want to get rid of it all together.  The only issue I had with the Trim unit was that sometimes it was difficult to turn off.  It runs on one AAA battery which can easily be replaced by puling the darker gray shaving head away from the base of 'pen'.

To set the energy level simply press the center of where the lights are flashing.  I wasn't sure about this step at first, as I kept clicking the bright fuchsia button on the opposite side of the unit and getting no results.  When you push the enter button, the lights will remain lite to indicate the level of energy you are using.  In addition, a small fan will begin blowing to keep the unit cool.  When you are ready to use the device, hold it against the area you want to treat and turn your eyes away from the bright light that will flash when you push the fuchsia button.  There may be a little warmth where the unit touches your skin.

I have just started using the device and am happy with the results.  The system is easy to use and is compact.  It comes with its own carrying case which makes it portable and easy to carry with you if needed.  I will continue to use the unit to see how long it will take to get the desired results.

The unit is recommended for use on underarms, arms, bikini line, and legs on women and chest and back on men.  The Silk'n Flash&Go also says that you can use it on your chin and upper lip which most units like this do not allow.

If you leave the unit plugged in, it will reset and the fan will turn itself off.
summary: Compact, great carrying case, with Trim bonus

reviewText:
This device is very similar in apperance to Veet Silk product, which I wanted to try for facial hair removal, but was unable to because Veet Silk specifically said not to use it on the face.  I was surprised to see that this device being practically identical to Veet Silk said it was OK to use on the face but be careful not to flash the bright IPL light into eyes.  Even marketing images on the box are the same on these two products.

So I tried it on the face and immediately encountered problems with the light not flashing because the safety sensor cannot be fully covered due to the curvature of the face.  For example, I was unable to make this device flash in the middle of my upper lip right under the nose.  The center part of the sensor is flush against the skin, but the ends are not, so the light won't flash.  I am looking for a device that won't leave me with a Hitler mustache.

It is easy to use on flat skin surfaces like legs, arms, legs, or cheeks, and it fits comfortably in hand.  However, I wanted this device specifically for use on my face but it does not seem to work well on all areas of that part of my body.
summary: Says OK for face but won't flash when used on the upper lip

reviewText: So I really got this to compare to Veet Infini'Silk Light-Based IPL Hair Removal System For Home Use which I also own. When just looking at them, there seems to be only minor differences. This model comes with a case and separate trimmer, it also says it is safe for use on the face while the other model specifically says not to use on face. Size wise there doesn't seem to be any significant difference. What you feel while using it is the same, the overall look is nearly the same, I only notice a color difference but am in the middle of unpacking from a move and haven't found my other one so I am going from memory. The Veet Infini'Silk had an expected 50k pulses. This model has 150k. Neither offers replacement cartridges as some others do. That out of the way, my experience with both of these in similar. I use level 4-5 but I do have sensitive skin so I worked my way up to that. Some people describe it as burning, if you feel that, please start a lower level than what you started at (the booklet tell you what your ideal max level is based on skin tone and hair). I am really pale but have some lighter hair and some darker. It's best used on darker hair - you may or may not get results on lighter hair. Personally because my lighter hair is on place like my arms, where I don't care as much as say my legs? I've just skipped using in on the lighter hair since there are a limited number of pulses (some of their other models have cartridges you can buy when the pulsing has stopped working). I've never counted the number of pulses I need because the legs can be tricky, but each underarm is going to have you using 3-5 per arm. It can take awhile to do the legs. The actual section that the light pulses through is about 1 1/4" long and 1/2" wide. That is what you will be using to target the hair with. That light window is about smack dab in the middle of the part you place against your skin. So you want to be careful to get all of the area you are targeting without overlapping. It's a bit of a learn as you go process. When I accidentally overlapped I sometimes had skin irritation. It didn't last long and really wasn't bad, but is something to be aware of. I haven't used more traditional laser hair removal. I will say that you do get better results if you shave or use a depilatory cream (Veet or Nair) and use this than if you just shave or use a depilatory cream alone. Do not use any hair removal devices that pull the hair out by the root before using this. It needs some hair below the surface in order to target it. Will you get amazing permanent results? Don't expect miracles. You will reduce hair growth, I have found that some of my hair is more stubborn than others. Right around my knees for example seem extra stubborn compared to the rest of my leg. So I made sure to target it extra carefully and still had lesser results. My underarm, however, seems to benefit more. How well you keep to a schedule with this device will also affect your results. There were times I was using it as often as was safe and other times when I slacked a little because who wants to take the time to run this device up and down their legs when they can "do it tomorrow". How well it works for you is really just a matter of do your skin tone and hair colors that you will target fall within the ideal ranges, do you use the device regularly, and honestly it seems to be a bit of luck. Some who seem to fit about the same description as me and kept to a regular schedule seem to have lesser results than me while some others who don't fit the ideal description and slacked in using it seemed to get better results than me. For me? It really limits the number of days between shaves. Before it I'd probably shave every 3 days, now I can go a week, sometimes longer depending on the area. The Silk'n Trim is a nice bonus but probably not necessary. Other similar devices sell for around $10. The case for this is the biggest difference I see between this and my prior Silk'n light based hair removal device. I have kept that one in the cardboard is arrived in, which hasn't been ideal. The case with this is much appreciated. Like the other device, you must leave it plugged in. That, for me, is the biggest negative with this device. If you don't have a convenient place to sit and use this device that is next to an outlet, you better remedy that. There is no cordless option. So would I recommend it? Basically if shaving / using a depilatory cream less often is important to you and you're willing to trade off that for a day every week or two of targeting those areas with this device? I'd say go for it. If that doesn't seem like the benefit is worth the hassle? It's not for you. After consistent use the benefits should be more obvious and may result in even greater times between your normal hair removal routine but, again that's going to vary for everyone. *UPDATE* I finally unpacked the Veet Infini'Silk and took a picture of the two side by side. This Silk'n Flash&Go is the pink one in the case while the Veet Infini'Silk is the purple in the cardboard box.
summary: Great device, but not for everyone.

reviewText: I love how compact this is. The last one I had was big and bulky and because it was so big I had a little trouble figuring out where I had left off. Get on a schedule instead. You'll see results pretty quick.

reviewText:
The Flash & Go is actually an IPL system when used over time, helps reduce unwanted hair growth. The "hair remover" is the Silk N Trim which is mostly a piece of junk, though some may find it useful for removing hair on the face. I personally do not recommend it. If you want to remove hair from the face, I would use a Twinkle razor instead.

IPL technology is best used on those with light to medium skin tones and dark hair. Those with darker skin tones and those with light skin and blonde hair, do not waste your money on this, the technology has not caught up to you yet.

To use, the hair is shaved away then the device is used to damage the hair within the pore. This is not a laser, but a pulse of light. This is not something that is used daily. There is a schedule for using this as to get all of the even and odd hairs.

This particular model is similar to the Nair version, but seems to be a little more painful (maybe more powerful?)  Unlike Nair, the Flash & Go is okay for the face. These do have a feeling like a small rubber band being snapped against the skin and sometimes a burning smell is present. This is really nothing to be alarmed about. If you have tattoos, you should not use this device on them.

IPL is not as strong as a laser and you will definitely not see results overnight. This is a product that must be used on a regular, scheduled basis to get results. Make sure to clean the light part is an anti-bacterial wipe after each use.
summary: Use on a scheduled basis to see results

reviewText: I've done professional laser treatments and have another home ipl system that I've used with success.  This is right in line with my other home system - meaning it's not quite as good as the pro laser treatments, but after several uses you can get similar results. Pain level is just what I expected (sort of like someone flicking your skin with a tiny rubber band - it stings, but it's not exactly burning - if you feel burning you may be doing it wrong and the level is probably too high)  I had some issues getting it to flash on my upper lip and chin areas since I believe the surface area wasn't quite even or flat or whatever the machine needs to determine it should flash, so that was a little bit of a let down since this machine advertises that it can do those areas while my other machine is slightly larger and can't be used on those areas. Still, for other larger, flatter surface areas like legs and underarms, there was no problem and it worked just fine.
