reviewText:
This is my second laser hair removal device. The first one I tried was the Veet Infini'Silk Pro Light-Based IPL Hair Removal System (white device and black box in the pictures). I've had good success with the Veet, so I wanted to see if this Silk'n device would be any better. It turns out they are both made by the same company (you can see they used the same images on the boxes). The devices look very different, but the actual laser window looks the same (the Veet window is a little larger). Beyond the appearance, they sound, feel, and work exactly the same. The one real difference I noticed is that the Silk'n has a glide option which makes it much faster to use on large areas, like legs, than having to pulse-move, pulse-move etc.

I haven't owned this long enough to compare the effectiveness of each laser, but it looks like they are pretty similar. If you can find one at a better price than the other, grab it. For me, I really like the glide function of the Silk'n, and I like the shape and size better too. Keep in mind that laser hair removal isn't a one-and-done process. It takes several months to see results (see the manual schedule pic), but in my opinion, it's well worth the time.
summary: Silk'n vs Veet: Which laser hair removal device is the best?

reviewText: The thing about reviewing this is I won't get to review and share the final result photographs for many months. reviewText:
I have used a couple IPL systems before, including a different Silk'n model and the Philips Lumea.  Both work well, and I was excited to try out this system that promised to be more compact for getting into tight places.  Unfortunately, it is almost identical to the Lumea, and I don't say that to be dramatic.  It is seemingly the same unit with a purple trim portion and carrying case.  Thankfully, the Lumea is a nice unit, but my hopes of a smaller detail hair removal tool were dashed.  My guess is that only very specific models have been FDA approved, limiting the diversity in home systems.

If you are new to IPL, I will try to give a brief overview.  The IPL system has emits a burst of light at a frequency that is absorbed by pigmented areas, with the goal being to heat up the base of the hair follicles enough to damage them.  With repeated use over months and years, the hair will grow back thinner and more slowly, making it much easier to keep smooth.  So, this will only work on relatively light skin and relatively dark hair.  If your skin is dark, it will absorb the light before it gets to the hair root.  That means it won't work, plus it might burn you.  The more pigmented areas of the body like the genitals or thicker hair density areas like a man's face are not advised for these home systems, but certainly they are done with more powerful systems in a clinical setting.  I think the main point of that warning is to avoid liability.  If you choose to do it anyway, start with the lower intensity light to make sure you don't burn yourself.

As with the Lumea, you can hold the button down between flashes to cause it to flash as soon as it is ready.  That makes going over large areas easier than the original Silk'n.  Since it has the same shape head, with a large border, it is awkward to use under the nose or other creases.  However, it can be done.  Even large areas are pretty quick and the pain isn't bad if you have pale skin.

For home use, this is as good as it gets right now.  It's still a bit clunky and low powered compared to professional treatments, but persistence does pay off.  Don't expect quick results and be disciplined and you'll likely be pleased.  The main alternative is doing electrolysis, but I find that challenging without causing scarring on myself.
summary: Works Well, But Identical to Lumea

reviewText:
A few years back we got a Veet device that used light to remove hair.  After receiving this device I was comparing them and noticed they were identical.  Then I noticed the Veet was actually licensing the Silk'n technology for their own machine (essentially rebranding it).  The only major difference was color, and that this version included a nice storage case (plus a separate battery powered trimmer).

In my experience these do work, but they will take some patience as well.  The light spot is small and it takes a few seconds for each flash.  You need to shave/trim before using it, and you need to have lighter pigmented skin with darker hair, that allows the light to be absorbed by just the hair and kill it, from what I understand.  Just like any other hair removal, you'll have to continue to do it to get all the different growths (hair lies dormant, and then cycles).  Good for small areas, and 50,000 flashes, the processional one has a bit larger area and can do 3x the flashes I believe, but still will need some patience.

Applying makeup of varying types is nearly an art given that there are many different kinds of makeup that achieve different effects.  This bronzer clutch adds the ability to achieve natural colors and to enhance feature definition in a way that can be remarkably natural with the right brush and a bit of patience.  The faint shimmer of the sun kissed and greater shimmer of the gold pen add a bit of special effects when used lightly, either with the other bronzers, on their own, or with other blush colors.

The clutch includes a non-magnifying mirror set in the upper lid of the clutch is large enough to actually use for applying makeup.  Included in the kit is sun kissed, which has just a touch of shimmer, sun baked and sun shadow, both of which are matte, and gold, which is shimmery.  The variety of colors enable a large array of face-enhancement, particularly when highlighting cheek bones and decreasing the effect of minor skin imperfections.  Note that a good quality blush brush kit is absolutely required to go with this clutch.

The three bronzers in the clutch palette are 0.39 ounces or 10.8 grams, which is quite a lot of bronzer.  The gold in the pen is 0.01 ounce or 0.5 grams, which is fine for effects since a minimal amount of gold is typically used.

This kit is a great addition to nearly any makeup kit, either for home or on the road.  When used with colors, the bronzer can achieve all kinds of facial effects and can enhance the beauty of nearly any woman with skin tones light enough to make use of the bronzer.  Just be sure to couple the clutch with a good brush kit!

Enjoy!

reviewText:
I am pretty impressed with this bronzer "clutch". Even though I live in the south my skin is very fair and these colors, when used in moderation, work very well for my complexion. reviewText: This is my second butter LONDON True to Form Clutch. I also own butter LONDON Just Darling Clutch Blush, Magnolia/Petal/Orchid, 5.8 oz., which I bought back in April. And I love that palette so much I was excited to get this! butter LONDON describes the included shades as follows (and they seem pretty accurate to me): - Sunkissed Bronzer (golden bronze shimmer) - Sun Baked Bronzer (matte bronze) - Sun Shadow Bronzer (matte contour) - On the Glow Pen in Gold (0.01 oz.) Looking at this in person, I thought this was a really nice selection of warm-toned bronzers. There's a good enough range of colors to necessitate having a palette (especially when sun kissed leans more shimmery), but not SO many that it seems impossible to ever make my way through (for me as tempting as Too Faced Little Black Book of Bronzers was, it falls in this camp). The formula is very velvety. It goes on evenly with a blush brush (I've been using Sephora Pro #56) and is beautifully buildable so it's easy to go as natural or bold as you want. I've been using these where the natural shadows on my face are or to create more definition, vs. all over. That said, some marketing copy I've seen refers to this as if it were a a standalone contouring palette. I'm not sure that's entirely accurate. Yes, the pen is more of a highlighter, but other sets come with both a highlight powder, that I prefer. Don't get me wrong, I LOVE this palette, but if you're looking for a true contouring palette I personally prefer Too Faced Cocoa Contour for powder and CoverFX Contour Kit for cream (that one is especially great because they have six different palettes based on the tone and darkness of your skin so you can find one that best works for you). I also love the packaging. It's sleek and feels well constructed and is much better than palettes I have that are constructed over cardboard and can get quite beat up over time. (While I love the aforementioned Too Faced Cocoa Contour, I DON'T love the cardboard.) I also love that it is customizable and you can switch other singles in and out or switch up items between two palettes (as I've already been doing) and I especially appreciate that each palette has a different shade of highlight pen, so no dupes. I've definitely had palettes where I've used up 1 color first so I love the option of switching other things in. And since you can also switch in eye shadows and blush it offers the option of creating a custom, practically full face palette that would be great for traveling. I hope they continue expanding on this concept! I'd love to see setting powders, concealers, and even lip sticks/gloss in a pan. Often I don't love full face palettes because the colors aren't something I would have chosen, but customizing solves that problem. I haven't bought any singles yet but it does look like they have quite a few options available so I'm looking forward to it. Though it is worth noting that all of the shades available in each palette don't seem to be available for purchase individually so if there is something you fall in love with and want to purchase a single of that doesn't always seem to be an option. (For some reason only Sun Baked seems to be available for purchase on its own.) In short, I think this is a really great palette. I love the range of colors and the formula and especially love the ability to customize and swap things in and out.
summary: Love the bronzers themselves and customizable palette design

reviewText: I've never tried any Butter products other than nail polish, and needless to say, I am thrilled at the quality of both the bronzer and the clutch.  First of all, the clutch can be customized with other colors, tints, and powders.  The clutch has a nice sized mirror and closes firmly.  (I say this because I've had some compacts that pop open in my makeup bag!)  Though the bronzer that is included is supposed to be a "contouring" powder, I use it as an allover bronzer and it works just fine.  The shades can be blended in any number of ways.  Get a bit of sun?  No problem.  With this compact, you can blend the shade that works for you.  I like that this gives my fair skin a more natural glow and not an orange-y tone.  Also, my skin is rather sensitive, and sometimes I have issues with harsher products.  This goes on very light and even and did not cause any irritation, so that's a huge plus.  I'm looking forward to refill.

This is by far the best bronzer I have ever used. All the other types I've used were really well pressed into the palates/compacts. So it took a lot of dabbing with a makeup brush to get the bronzer onto the brushes. And then the bronzers always went on so lightly it left little more than a subtle copper sparkle on my skin. But this bronzer is exactly what bronzers should be. It's soft and just like any other type of face makeup, easy to apply and work with.

Included in the palate are three bronze shades and then also a highlighting "pen" so you can contour and/or blend the colors giving you the exact shade or look you are going for. I'm loving how the makeup melts into my skin (I guess that's why they call their makeup butter!) and gives it a beautiful bronze glow. The color is so much richer than other bronzers I've used. It's a makeup rather than a barely-there powder you dust over your face. This is such an awesome bronzer and it gives skin an amazing summertime glow!
summary: Melts into your skin for an amazing summertime glow

reviewText: Butter London is an American company, not a British endeavor. The Bronzer Clutch contains 3 contouring bronzers that are made in the United States and a gold stick that's made in Korea. From my minimal research, it appears that the stick is a part of the clutch system and although I really like it, don't know that I would repurchase the stick on its own. Each of the colors in this collection seems to be pretty universal and can be worn individually or used by building upon one another. The highlighting stick makes for a very nice accent to lighten areas of the face. It's operated by unscrewing a little cap to access the pencil eraser sized tip for dispensing the gold highlighter.  What is ingenious about this clutch system is that by lifting from the sides, the top plastic section of the case rotates up from the base and each color can be slid out and replaced with any other color. I've seen that several refills for the system are available online and have not made a trip to the store yet to investigate further but I really like the idea of removing one of the bronzer and having the option of replacing it with a shadow duo refill. The clutch size is larger than I expected and the case is much more luxurious than I anticipated from the photos I've seen. This also contains a large mirror that extends to the edges of the interior lid so it's easy to apply the makeup using the mirror. Just remember that you will need your brushes or sponges to apply these. This is probably the nicest cosmetic I've received lately, not only for the system, but the quality of the actual cosmetics. I'm impressed.
summary: Personalize the clutch with various refills

reviewText:
This is a gorgeous palette in a beautiful case. It has a nice large mirror and the shades are very generously sized. The gold highlighter stick is an added bonus. There is one shimmer bronzer and 2 matte shades that work well with neutral to yellow skin tones.

The texture is very creamy and pigmented, it's really great quality and I was very pleased when I tried them on. The product picture does not really represent the shades very well, so I have taken some pics. This is a nice contouring palette that will last some time as there is a lot of product in here. The shades also work perfectly for a bare look natural eyeshadow and the gold highlighter for the brow bone.
summary: Beautiful palette, pigmented and creamy shades and a large mirror.

reviewText:
Let me start by saying I am a big fan of butter LONDON products and have been for a long time. Everything blends so well (I have fair skin that can look clownish easily) and never causes breakouts on my sensitive skin.

This is a GREAT bronzer. When I ordered it, I didn't realize it was really targeted to contouring, but it didn't make a difference. I've now used it as both... a light natural bronzer just dusted on my cheeks and forehead, and for more dramatic contouring.

It comes with three shades of bronzer. The one with the most gold (far left) is the only one with shimmer, in case you are trying to avoid that for daytime or winter use. The bottom stick that looks like an applicator is actually a highlighting stick. It works best on my browbones... the yellow tone doesn't quite match my undertones enough to use it on my nose, even though I'm a neutral.

Kardashian fans take note... this is not dark enough to give you tiger stripes. Which is just fine by me. It's natural and would work for probably my tone (quite fair, but not true porcelain) and darker. I'm also getting to the age of larger pores, but the built in primer keeps this VERY smooth and it didn't settle in them at all. It's also really easy to blend - one night I went a little heavy and had no problem smoothing it to something more believable.

One thing I love about the compact - it's reusable. You can slide out the colors when you are done and refill it with other butter LONDON makeup. I'm happy about this because it's a super cute compact, even though it will be a long time before I use it up.

It does come with instructions, but if you are new to contouring, I'd suggest looking it up on Pinterest instead. In my experience, every face shape should contour differently.
summary: Another butter LONDON product to love - smooth, natural-looking and sensitive!

reviewText: This is the first time I have used this polish and really like it .would buy again stays on long

I wore this color with butter LONDON's Stag Do and they went well together. This color has a shimmer/rainbow effect once it is on your nails and is just gorgeous. It is more of a sheer color, but I feel it's very summery. I would highly recommend purchasing this color.

I bought this brand of polish because of the healthier ingredients. I also bought the base and top coats by Butter London ($29.99 for both) and followed exact instructions. I used a base coat, 2 coats of polish and top coat. Less than 24 hours later, it's chipped dramatically all over. Unfortunately, I can't return these products because of Amazon's return policy of hazardous materials i.e. nail polish.
summary: Don't waste your money or time

reviewText: I just love love love Butter London polish... the quality is wonderful and the colors are so vibrant! Goes on with ease!

I give this bronzer set 4 stars because of the lack of a highlighter color. The pen type highlighter is ok for highlighted lines, like under the eye brow, or above the lip, but you cannot use it to highlight your face above your cheekbone and under the eyes. Typically a bronzer/contouring palette has a highlighter color. The lightest shade in this one is actually a bit darker than it seems and does not function as a highlighter, unless you have a very dark skintone perhaps, but it is not iridescent either - it is matte.

The first color is a nice shimmery copper bronzer, the middle color is a matte natural medium tan, and the last color is matte light tan/dark beige but of course too dark to be a highlighter as previously mentioned. Perhaps you already have a favorite highlighter color in a separate palette and this will be no issue. I like the highlighter in one of my Lancome Blush Subtil Palettes, so I just use that and the colors go very well together.

The highlighter pen is like a loose powder eyeshadow pen that applies with a pointed sponge tip. The light colored end that you see in the pic is the small area that holds the color and the sponge tip is dipped into there to pick up the color. It is a bright gold, very shiny/sparkly, but can be blended down nicely to a pale shimmer.

The palette colors and the highlighter pen color are pretty well pigmented and apply very smoothly. Not chalky or dusty. A light swipe gives a very good amount of color and you can build it up as you need. You can tell that it is quality cosmetics and not just cheap stuff with a higher end brand name slapped on. The powders are pressed nicely, and while there is a bit of fall out onto the palette when swiping lightly with a brush, it doesn't seem to actually do any damage to the cakes. Of course your mileage will vary in that aspect depending on your brushes.

Overall I do like the colors in the set. They all give a very natural looking tone, with the only exception being the shimmery bronzer perhaps since it is so metallic, but that is expected with these types of cosmetics of course. You can use the colors on the eyes as well. The fact that they are very well pigmented means the palette should have a nice lifespan, especially with the amount of color which applies with just a light swipe. This was the first time I tried face cosmetics from Butter London and now after seeing the quality, I would not hesitate to buy more. The compact is very sturdy and well made also. Not thin or clanky. Reminds me of some of my thicker Lorac palettes.

First, the compact-
This is a really nice compact that can be used for other colors as well if you like.  Other colors I've seen for around $7-15.  It has a very nice, big mirror that is well made and does not distort.  The compact opens and closes easily, and is a good size to fit in a purse.  It holds 3 of the colors and the pen.  The top can be lifted up on one side to slide the squares out or to replace one or all of them.  It has a textured pattern on the top and overall is very good quality and very attractive.

The makeup
This is a creamy powder with a lot of pigment.  When it first arrived, I tried a bit with my fingers- this is not the optimal way of using this!  I ended up with a stripe I could not blend.  However, when used with a brush, these colors are marvelously easy to blend.  It only takes a single pass of a brush to pick up pigment, and it does not make a lot of powder waste on the compact.
It comes with instructions for using it on cheeks and as a whole face bronzer.  The colors do work very well for a very natural bronzer, and it worked well for me, and I am very fair skinned.  It is easy to customize it to the color you need- if you have darker skin, you might simply use more of the darker color.

It has a little highlighter pen that is wonderful when used around the top lip, on the browbone, or on the bridge of the nose if you wish to highlight that area.  It is a very pearlized shade, and for me, I prefer just to use it on my browbone, under my eyebrows, and to line my upper lip with.

All this said, my favorite use for this is to minimize the appearance of this double chin age and weight gain has cursed me with.  This is very good makup for contouring the chin line and minimizing the neck.  Because it does blend so well, it is easy to blend it down into the neck without an obvious 'line of demarcation.'

Without fixative, it lasted me about 8 hours in an air conditioned environment.  After that, I noticed it had started to fade.
summary: Blends beautifully when used with a blush - Compact can be reused or customized- great colors for sculpting athe neck & neckline

reviewText:
I am coming off of a 2 week vacation in full sun so I am as tan as I will ever get in life. I thought this would be fun to try. Unfortunately I am still too pale for most of it. The compact has a nice large mirror. You will need your own brushes and sponges for application. The Sun Shadow color was the only one of the 3 colors I could use for contouring. The Sun Kissed/Sun Baked were too brown or orange-y for my skin. The real keeper for me us the gold highlight pen which is terrific at getting the effects I want. I love it.

I intend to swap out colors that don't work for me with others I buy from the clutch collection. That will make this a one stop shop for my daily makeup.
summary: Lovely compact, mostly too dark for me. You can customize with other colors.

reviewText:
This is really a nice collection of bronzers in a versatile set of colors.  I say that because my daughter and I are different color tones and we each found a bronzer that worked for us. She is porcelain.  I am tanner right now.  She looked fabulous in the light shade on the left.  I used a combination of two, center and left.

It's easy to go daytime sunny or evening dark with these powders.  I used a medium fluffy brush and was careful to not press down to hard.  I'm not sure I would carry this my purse as the powders are soft.

Wonderful selection.  Will buy when this runs out.

This butter LONDON Bronzer Clutch is a beautiful quality color palette that comes in a lovely 4-1/2" x 3" compact. Inside, the compact has three warm brown shades of bronzer/contour makeup, an "On The Glow" highlighting pen and a nice quality mirror. The bronzer/contour makeup is rich in color and a velvety smooth texture that reminds me of a high-end eye shadow. The frame of the compact lifts up so individual contour colors can be changed out and new ones can be added. The compact closes tightly and doesn't leak, so I can carry it in my purse just as it is, or I can carry it in my cosmetic bag.

My makeup routine has been dull for years now (concealer, powder foundation, blush, mascara and lipstick), and my fair but olive skin tone can look drab. It's really fun to switch up my routine by using this bronzer/contour palette. I don't have a contour brush, so I use a blush brush to apply and blend the colors, and it works just fine. This makeup adds such a warm glow that lifts my skin tone and adds some much needed definition and contour to my face. I'm just learning about contour makeup and am so pleased with how easy it is to apply and blend this makeup for a smooth appearance. And I love the results- this contour makeup creates the illusion of higher cheekbones and even makes my face look slimmer.

I'm still practicing how best to use this palette, so I appreciate the included tips that show how to accentuate features, achieve definition and get a natural looking glow by blending the darkest color in my cheek hollows followed by the bronze color on my cheekbones, and the lightest shade at the top. The instructions show how to use the highlighting pen for added contouring and enhancement of lips and eyes. It really just takes a little experimentation to see what looks best on me, and so far I'm really happy with how little effort it takes to achieve a really flattering look. The bronzer/contour color is made in the USA, and the gold highlighter is made in Korea. This is a gorgeous product that I definitely recommend.
summary: Beautiful Quality And Produces Gorgeous Results With Such Minimal Effort

reviewText: This wasn't what I expected when I ordered it but it ended up being so much better than I had hoped.  The colors work well with my skin tone and the size is perfect for putting in my desk or weekend bag.  It does need a good brush kit to pair with but it goes one easily and smoothly and blends nicely.  There is some shimmer which isn't typically my thing but this is just the right amount to make my skin glow without going too far.  The gold pen is a really nice touch with the colors and adds a nice dimension to the clutch.
summary: It really is a universal color set and a great addition!

reviewText:
I'm not much of a bronzer user.  I've tried several over the years with mixed results.  I've never used the gold standard - Guerlain Terra Cotta, because $50 is more than I'm willing to spend on something I'll only use occasionally.  I have tried Physicians Formula, Sephora Sun Disk and Bliss Spa. Since Butter London is a fairly new cosmetics brand that's been popping up in a lot of the better ladies mags, I was eager to give this one a try.

First off, the compact is much larger than I expected.  It measures about 4.5 inches long and 2.5 inches wide, so you get a lot of product for the money.  I did not try the contour shade, but used a combination of the bronzer and highlighter (which is a warm frosty gold) over my forehead, along my cheekbones, nose bridge and chin.  Frankly, I'm amazed at what a lovely, natural looking glow it gave me.  Not dirty looking, nor orange-y in the least.  It really mimics the look of a light tan.  I was really channeling my inner Kardashian with this stuff.

The "glow pen," a small tube that contains a golden liquid with a sponge applicator, looked more like a pale frosted yellow/gold eyeshadow than anything I would use on my face, but at my age, that sort of embellishment tends toward the ridiculous.  I imagine a touch of that on the cheekbones or brow bone of a younger woman would look very glamorous.

This is, by far, the best bronzer I've ever tried.

I was pretty certain that the color on the far right, Sun Shadow (a drab medium brown matte contour) and the On the Glow Pen (Gold, smooth and shimmery highlighter) would work for me. When I first received the package and opened the gorgeous, substantial compact with large mirror, I thought the Sun Kissed Bronzer (golden bronze shimmer) and Sun Baked Bronzer (warm brown matte contour) would not. Well, I was wrong. Every one of the wonderfully varied contour powders works on my blue undertoned, light-but-not-ivory skin. The powders apply super smoothly. They don't sit in wrinkles or emphasize age. I have used one at a time or all at the same time and either way, I get the effect I want. The Sun Shadow matte contour even works as a subtle eyeshadow. My skin looks vibrant and healthy when I wear this so I can't imagine going a day without it, whether I wear foundation beneath or not. HIGHLY recommended!
summary: Skin looks vibrant and healthy so I can't imagine going a day without it!

reviewText: I always put alot of the makeup on at first to see how it looks with a lot applied and then I end up clearing it off. This product looks great on weather you pound it on or put on a light coat. It makes your face looked kissed or smothered by the sun. The instructions were so well done I knew exactly where to put what and it was fun to play around with the gold pen, adding touches of gold around my eyes. Great little kit.

Pretty nice bronzer in warm tones + brush. A little really goes a long way with this one for someone as light as me, I used the lightest color with a large brush to get an overall sun-kissed look and used the darker colors for a little extra contouring. No  irritation.
I like this one! it's really thick for a glitter and I just wore it alone. loosk great with 4 coats.
Be sure to buy this nail lacquer from Butter London and NOT from Shop Adorn!!  Butter London is a quality product, but Shop Adorn sent me old, thick, streaky BL nail lacquer.
See description above. The London Butter nail lacquer that I purchased from their company is 100% fantastic!!  But, the London Butter nail lacquer that I purchased  from Shop Adorn was disgusting!!
summary: Shop Adorn's polish was pasty, thick and left streaks on my nail which I couldn't cover = pink-white-pink-white-... stripes. Yuck

reviewText: The butter London brand lacquer has turned me into such a polish snob. I can tell a huge difference in this brand of polish from the cheaper department store/drug store brands. I love this shade of pink, it's not hot pink but not a baby pink either.

I've read the other reviewers' comments, and all are 'correct' however, here are a few things one needs to know before purchasing. If you thought this would look like the bottle all by itself, with a standard one or two coats, you'll be disappointed.  This polish is best used with other colors, or if alone, more than two coats.

yes the polish dries rough, and somewhat matte, to fix this use their top coat and the colors will also look much more intense.
Also, I believe this polish was intended to be a topper, or an added dimension to an under coat of color, either holgraphic/opaque glimmer, or cream color.  If used on top of a pale pink, and topped with a gloss, the effect is girly to the max,,, also, depends on how many coats one uses.  top a red and you'll get more gold...  If used alone, over a standard base coat, try building up till the color intensity suits your look.  this could be three or four. While matte looks are a statement, the rougness makes using it that way less appealing.  This polish 'looks' like it would be glossy, but it's not, not by itself.  This can happen with almost any of the polishes that have actual glitter in them.

All in all this is a very versatile, flexible polish to have in your bag of nail tricks. the key is to get creative and have fun with it.
summary: A FUN POLISH TO USE WITH OR ALONE, a how to

reviewText: This Butter brand polish has added to my collection from this brand. The colours (and monikers) are great. The less toxic ingredients are an added bonus!

This polish, as with many glitter polishes, should be used over a base coat of a French pink shade. The color is slightly pink of the lacquer itself while the glitter is a light shade of gold. This item matched very well the stock photo and I am very pleased with this shade, and the butter London nail polish line

I loved the color of this nail polish when I first bought it.  However, after applying two coats it was a disastrous mess.  The ending result was thick, streaky and looked as if I applied 5 coats.  When dried it was so unattractive, it had to be removed straight away.  Not worth $14.00!

This is an awesome nail polish. It is as good as chanel nail polish but half the price. I used it with orly brand top coat and so far it has been two days and no chipping. It went on smoothly and dried fast. It is pricey but worth it.

I bought three different colors of this dreamy looking nail polish and used them as stocking stuffers (including my own!)  The sheen is lovely, but the polish chips easily, and can't be worn without a topcoat, as even two coats won't stand up to normal wear and tear for even a day.
love butter polish....this color was just a bit light for me.........has shimmer to it but is light even with 2 coats.

I really really like this eye cream! I received a small sample in a Amazon Beauty Box and started applying morning and evening. The first day I didn't notice anything but starting evening of the second day I noticed no puffiness and lines seemed less "vibrant". I finished my sample size two weeks later and totally happy with the way my eyes looked I decided to take advantage of the $20 credit and apply toward the full price.

The full price vial is the same product ( look and feel )  in the sample. My eyes ( below the eyes and upper with NO irritation ) look less puffy and my eyes look better than before taking.  Super happy with this eye product. I rub my eyes in my sleep and at 48 years old my eyes need all the extra support they can get!

I have been using this for a week. The results have been INCREDIBLE to see My ( starts of) crow's feet disappear right before My eyes!! THAT QUICK! It IS light and milky, but ABSORBS SO QUICKLY AMD THOROUGHLY!! It doesn't burn or dry and has a wonderful, actual, coconut smell. Haven't had an eye cream work this fast before!
summary: Works MIRACLES Right Before My Eyes!!!

reviewText:
I'll be honest-- On first try, I was disappointed because of the light, fluid texture (like a thin, milky lotion). See, I love thick, dense, buttery eye creams, feeling that they "work" better to hydrate. But I was surprised -- this featherlight formula proved to soften, hydrate, and make my eyes look more rested better than my beloved $200 Amore Pacific eye cream. Lightweight eye creams usually evaporate and leave my eye area dry after a few hours. Not so with this one -- my eyes are bathed in all-day nourishing moisture with a tightening/toning sensation.

To be honest, the ingredients aren't anything extraordinary by themselves-- which goes to show that this is an extremely well-made, efficacious formula that is synergistically greater than its parts. Highly recommended, and reasonably priced to boot.

Ingredients: Aqua, Coco-Caprylate, Olea Europaea Oil Unsaponifiables, Cetearyl Alcohol, Glyceryl Stearate, Potassium Palmitoyl Hydrolyzed Rice Protein, DImethicone, Cyclopentasiloxane, Polymethylsilsequioxane, Sodium Stearoyl Glutamate, Tuber Malanosporum Extract, Pullulan, Algae Extract, Hydrolyzed Hibiscus Esculentus Extract, Paullinia Cupana Extract, Potassium Azeloyl Diglycinate, HDI/Trimethylol Hexyllactone Crosspolymer, Helianthus Annuus Seed Oil, Daucus Carota Sativa Root Powder, Panthenol, Sodium Hyaluronate, Phenethyl Alcohol, Sodium Polyacrylate, Propylene Glycol, Glycerin, Tocopherol, Glyceryl Caprylate, P-Anisic Acid, Parfum, Oryza Sativa Powder, Disodium EDTA, Coumarin, Linalool, Dextrin.
summary: A light, fluid eye cream that's just as effective as thicker, richer ones

reviewText:
Under eye illuminators are all over the stores right now with Olay, L'Oreal, and others having launched their versions. It really isn't an under eye cream for the night. It's a moisturizing complex for the day time or evening time that can be worn over makeup to add a bit of pearl essence to the eyes.

In the summer I use it under eyes on bare skin after applying moisturizer and then pat a little foundation in powder form on top. In the winter, I apply it under the liquid foundation and then dab a bit on top too. I don't think it will work for those who have deep dark circles. I typically don't apply concealer so it's a little something that gives me some moisture and a little more pearl shine but I don't think it does anything major for me. It's just a little moisture as the under eye skin can be so sensitive. Given the higher price tag I'd rather spend money on an all over anti aging face cream with a bit of illumination. There are several products from the same brands for that.
summary: Gives under eye area a bit of sparkle, and moisturizes the area, but a bit expensive.

reviewText: The Iceland illuminater is a refreshing product for under eye puffiness. The application of the product is great. It's hard describe but when you apply it really does have a icy, cool effect on the under eye area.  It states it will help brighten dark circles but I have not noticed a change therefore it gets 4 stars instead of 5. As stated though I really notice that my eyes looks less tired and not puffy at all.
summary: The application of the product is great. It's hard describe but when you apply it ...

reviewText:
The manufacturer uses technical language to make promising claims. Example: "hyaluronic acid locks in critical moisture to minimize wrinkles while skyn Iceland's proprietary light infusion complex kicks into gear to help regulate skin's biological clock desynchronized by stress and to help strengthen cells so they can regenerate and renew. Truly illuminating, this detoxifying serum employs cutting-edge pink pearlescent pigment technology to reflect light and disguise imperfections so skin looks visibly brighter and more luminous on contact..."

Whew!

It is difficult to tell the difference that this eye cream makes. It seems promising, but for $35, the price is a bit steep. That is why I reduced one star. If you can fit it into your budget, you can give it a shot. First link, I did not notice a big difference. It seems that getting a good amount of sleep might have a bigger difference on the condition of your eyes.
summary: Get a goodnight sleep and save $35

reviewText: The good points -- it feels great -- nice and cool -- going on. That is a plus. But, honestly my undereye circles don't look any better. It is supposed to make your eyes look brighter and less tired. Maybe it will do this for other people -- it doesn't do this for me. I am a 48 yearr old caucasian woman who perpetually has dark circles under eyes. I think this might work with puffy eyes well. If get puffy circles under your eyes I'm thinking this might really help -- but that is a theory. I expected great things out of this. It just didn't work for me but it might work for you. I"m going to give mine to my 19 yearr old daughter. Maybe it works better on younger skin.
summary: Maybe works better on younger skin

reviewText: Many years ago a friend had a makeup party where she sold me an under eye illuminator that I absolutely loved. I don't remember the brand or product name so I haven't been able to find it since. I have been looking for something similar ever since. This ICELAND illuminator is exactly what I have been searching for. You only need to use the tiniest little bit of this stuff because a little goes a long way. I dab a little on my pinky finger and put little dots of this under my eyes. Then I use my pinky finger to smooth it under my eyes very gently so as to not pull or stretch the delicate skin under my eyes. Illuminator helps reflect the light under my eyes so they appear brighter and less tired. When I am doing a full face of makeup I put the liquid foundation on first, then illuminator, then an ever so light dusting of powder just so it sets. I usually do not wear illuminator if I am using a pressed compact alone, but I guess it could work the same way as when using the liquid. In the video I tried so show how it gives a little shimmer when the light hit where I put it on the back of my hand. I hope it's clear enough in the video. You can definitely tell in person.

This gel absorbs into the skin and leaves it smooth. Although it can feel sticky sometimes, it's not bad and you can work it into the skin with the metal attachment at the top of the tub. I don't see any huge differences on my eye area but it's good to take care of it.
summary: Brighten and soften your eye area

reviewText:
This skyn ICELAND Under-Eye Illuminator, 0.5 fl. oz. is supposed to lighten, brighten and recharge tired looking eyes, as well as minimize wrinkles with it's thirst quenching hyaluronic acid. I've been using it for a few weeks now to see if my eyes look less tired, brighter and more moisturized. The result- I don't see any difference from what my under $10.00 drug store brands (like Oil Of Olay) can do.

This skyn Under-Eye illuminator is made in Italy with their miracle ingredient- Icelandic Glacial Water. It comes in a very small 0.5 fluid ounce tube with a metal tip applicator, so it feels cool going on. The directions say to put it on either every morning or night, or both. I did it both times and I saw nothing special in the results. This under eye illuminator simply did nothing out of the ordinary for my eyes- they look exactly the same as when I use a cheaper drug store brand of under eye cream/moisturizers. It's just an average 3 STAR product.
summary: A Little Brightness, A Little Moisturizing, But, Too Little For The Price

reviewText: I got this product right before a business trip and figured trips are pretty tiring and mess up your sleep so that would be a great time to test how well this really works on "tired eyes".  And I was a bit sick so this was a great opportunity to truly battle test this product.  My typical go-to for puffy tired eyes is a bit of hemorrhoid cream.  Side to side comparison, hemorrhoid cream did a better job on depuffing eyes (did one eye with each).  This did give a but of luminescence that helped decrease the appearance of dark circles but the effect was minimal.  This did not erase the tired sick look I had but was perhaps a bit better.  Under normal use conditions (after returning home and kicking the cold), this product did seem to brighten my eyes a bit but the effect was not transformative.  I doubt I would purchase this product again.

skyn ICELAND's under-eye illuminator is to help with dark circle's under your eyes as well as combat signs of aging. It has a metal tip that helps 'cool' the eyes and it feels really nice (but other products have that, too), and has pearlescent pigment in the formula to help brighten up beneath your eyes (you can buy a lot of products that help 'brighten' or 'highlight' these days). It's not a bad product... but I'm not sold on the runny formula that makes application a bit of a problem. I wish it was a little thicker, because a lot of times it seems that I'm applying too much... and for almost $40 (at the current price), you don't want to waste this stuff.

This is very light and refreshing under the eyes.  I had no irritation from using it.  The applicator is interesting but you have to be careful not to get too much product out at one time.  I didn't see a huge difference in the area under my eyes as far as the dark circles but the puffiness and wrinkles were reduced.

Truly, there is nothing special about this under-eye product that would compel me to pay the $30 it costs. It is light and does not cause skin irritation to sensitive skin; however, aside from that I did not find the product to be effective. My recommendation is to get a good night's sleep and drink plenty of water.

This has something in it to be cool and refreshing under the eyes. Felt great.  I like this brand and have used many items from it.

I did take off one star because after opening the box, the product had no seal. There was no anti-tamper packaging on the box.  So that bugged me. And also, it has the doe-foot applicator (metal) that I don't care for. I prefer a rollerball or just a squeeze tip.  So yes, it's good but box and delivery method is not so hot.

This feels great going on, even on my fingertips when I pat it in (because it is easy to dispense too much product from the tube).  Looks very shiny and moist going on, but by the time it has dried (settled, whatever you want to call it), it still feels cool but it looks quite matte.  However, the real problem I have (and this is a problem with me and every eye cream I've ever tried), eventually it starts getting into my eyes.  I don't put it too close, but it began to burn after a little while (maybe 20 minutes). It does provide a very minor "concealer" effect - I left one eye undone and did the other eye as a test - but sadly I can't use it.  Giving it three stars since it seems like a good product otherwise.

skyn ICELAND Under-Eye Illuminator works great as intendedbrightening, lightening, and recharging tired skin under the eyes. I am not an expert on skin care products, but can provide some personal background on my own experiences with other products along with skyn ICELAND Illuminator.  Skyn makes no statements about reduction of fine lines common for skin care products used around the eyes.

Growing up in Florida, and having a parent that had sun related melanoma, I have understood the importance of sun screen for years, and routinely use it.  Now in my 50s, I still use Olay Complete (with occasional forays into Total Effects Anti-Aging Moisturizer depending on price), but nothing stops the progression of time, particularly around the eyes.  Factors beyond age, including late nights and stress only exasperate the dark circles and bags under the eyes.

Again, not being a skin care expert, my own estimation of the range of products making claims for reducing under-eye darkness generally fall in to a couple of categories.  Covering agents (including colored pigments, fillers, and reflecting agents), constrictors and tightening agents (various alcohols, witch hazel, astringents), and potentially chemical and mechanical exfoliants (Retin A, retinol, organic acids, alpha-beta hydroxyl acids, peroxides, micro beads and scrubs, laser peels). Covering agents containing typical make-up base (color pigments) and reflecting agents seem most typical for darker skin under the eyes.

I prefer scent free productsor a scent that is very light and disappears quickly. No sticky residues after application is also important.  Application cost must be under control.  So, in addition to daily Olay Complete, my preference for occasional use around the eyes and over time has been limited to another Olay product, Definity, which is now called OLAY EYES ILLUMINATING EYE CREAM.  Like skyn ICELAND, this product has some reflecting pigments which brighten darker skin under the eyes, along with a refreshing hydration agent.

For this review, I thought it would be interesting to compare skyn and Olay directly.  Skyn ICELAND has a wedged applicator tip that you are supposed to run underneath your eye.  Olay is simply dabbed and rubbed.  In actual use, the skyn applicator seems unnecessary and requiring a bit more coordination than simply using a dab on the finger (which also controls the amount a bit better).

Once applied, on clean dry skin, one dab of each, skyn ICELAND and Olay Eyes, under opposite eyes, the masking and illuminating effect is very subtle but visible!  Neither product has any perceivable pigment, relying on the micro-reflecting effect for color reduction.  Skyn ICELAND has a slight advantage in darkness reductionyou cannot expect dramatic effects with either product, but the effect is visible on my skin.  The feeling on the skin after a period of drying is bone dry for the skyn ICELAND, with more cream stickiness for the Olay.  Both products provide a refreshing period during the drying with the skyn ICELAND having the definite advantageit feels more cooling than the OLAY and seems to last slightly longer.  This refreshment lasts only a couple of minutes.  Tired eyes will love it.  There is no perceivable scent or fragrance in either product.

On the first application of skyn ICELAND I applied too much (using the applicator) and probably did not spread it out enough.  After a little while it looked like the edges of application were peeling off.  Less is definitely better.  Olay tends to have a similar effect, if you rub your eyes, over application tends to slough off in tiny little clumps.  Again, less is better!

Money wise, skyn ICELAND costs more per ounce than the Olay Illuminator.  Grocery and drug store availability may be limited.  Olay products are everywhere and while still expensive can be very cost competitive on the shelf with similar products. Since these products are typically applied sparingly and occasionally, cost of application is low so do not let the sticker price deter you from trying?

Overall, I like the skyn ICELAND  Under-Eye Illuminator.  It has advantages over the Olay Illuminating cream including a bit more color reduction, drier feeling after application, and a bit more refreshing feeling with application.  Based on the low cost of application (when dabbing rather than using the applicator tip) it is cost competitive.  If you have never tried these types of products, skyn ICELAND Under-Eye Illuminator should be a product you try. Also, given the opportunity I would try other skyn ICELAND products.

In my opinion this is a temporary fix and does not help in long term repair.  The small tube has a metal tip with an opening that allows you to apply the serum when you squeeze the tube.  However since the serum is has a watery consistency, too much tends to come out and I am always trying to squeeze it back into the tube.

The serum is light and dries quickly leaving behind a pearled sheen.  It seems to fill in those fine lines underneath my eyes and make the skin more taunt.  It works great for use during my daily makeup routine every morning, but once I wash my face the "illusion" is gone.

I thought this was going to be yet another overpriced and not-especially-effective skin cream.  Well, it is overpriced, but I have to say it's smoother than facial creams like Eucerin, it's smells great and I actually feel better after rubbing it on my temples.  So, I'd get this again, but I wouldn't pay over sixty smackers for it.

I have never used SKIN&CO brand products before this one.  SKIN&CO eye concentrate is priced similar or cheaper to other comparative brands. However, currently I'm on a tight budget, and this product is not normally something I could justify buying, especially without knowing how well it worked.  I'm so glad I had the opportunity to try it. Its definitely worth the cost.  I have tried a lot of eye products over the years. This is the best eye concentrate for reducing dark circles and reducing puffiness. It has a thick consistency similar to other eye concentrates, and it absorbs quickly.  I use it once a day.  As far as it being age defying... Lines have not re-appeared, since I ran out of Lancme Genifique my previous eye cream and started using this Roma Truffle Therapy.  I definitely will consider buying more in the future as my budget allows. I will update if anything changes about the lines.  It might take more time for the benefit of the Genifique to wear off.  SKIN&CO still beats Lancme for dark circles and puffiness.
summary: I'm so glad I had the opportunity to try it

reviewText: Now that I am nearing my mid-thirties, I am definitely more conscious of skin sensitivity and taking care of wrinkles or puffiness.  This seems to plump the eyes, and treat the delicate eye skin very softly - doesn't cause redness or irritation, which is common for me since I have sensitive skin.  Haven't seen huge difference in results yet, but I am optimistic that this eye cream will get rid of the crows feet that have started to creep in....
summary: Now that I am nearing my mid-thirties, I am ...

reviewText:
This is a nice lightweight cream that brightens the eye area.  I have not been using an eye cream but will continue to use this.  I like the texture and how it sinks in immediately.  It is non-greasy.  There is a slight perfume scent but that doesn't bother me and it's a nice scent.

The jar is small but is the same size as most eye creams and this will last a long time since such a small amount is used.  After using this for several
 nights my under eye circles look less obvious.  The tiny lines are now invisible.  This has a slight plumping effect on the skin, holding in moisture.  My lines are caused by dryness only so this takes care of that.

I'm quite impressed with this cream.  It makes a definite difference in the appearance of the skin around my eyes.

The truffle therapy line by SKIN&CO is by far my absolute favorite skincare line. I was introduced to it last year and have been buying and using the line of products ever since. They not only work well, but something about their sweet light fragrance is divine and addicting.

This was my first time trying the eye therapy and I am pleased with how it works on my skin. Unlike the face moisturizers which hydrate and soften the skin, this eye cream ever so slightly tightens and firms. So it gives you a more refreshed, awake appearance. After using this about a week, I find I don't look as tired. And like all the other products from the Truffle Therapy line, is has a light wonderful scent.

If you've tried other products from SKIN&CO's Truffle Therapy line and like how they work for you, this eye cream will likely become another favorite as well. Works nicely and smells great!
summary: Love the skincare products from the Truffle Therapy line.

reviewText:
This is an okay product.  Have not really seen a noticeable improvement, but have only been using for a few weeks.  The eye concentrate goes on smoothly and quickly and feels as though moisture is penetrating my skin.  Other reviewers have noted the fragrance, but it is not strong or unpleasant (at least not to me).

Not crazy about putting my finger in the jar since the cream gets trapped under my nails.  I need to find a better solution.  Hopefully after a longer time using the product, I can further update.

My main problem is dark circles, and I have not seen much change in that. This is a nice rich night cream for under eyes though. Soaks in well and feels nice without being greasy. TINY container - box is bigger, then the glass container is smaller, and THAT is only like halfway full. Like nesting dolls of eye cream. But a little goes a long way. I just barely get a little on my fingernail and it's enough for under both eyes.
summary: This is a nice rich night cream for under eyes though

reviewText: I have extremely sensitive eye lids, so once I find a product that works, I'm loathe to change it. I've been using Roc Retinol Correxion Eye Cream Treatment, .5 Oz. under my eyes for a few years now, and it really does work to smooth out fine lines. For upper lids, I've been using Clinique Repairwear Laser Focus Wrinkle Correcting Eye Cream - 0.17 Oz. It's pretty good for keeping the skin supple, and is non-irritating, but doesn't do anything for fine lines. This eye cream by Skin & Co comes in a very tiny jar, but it's comparable to the amount you get from other brands. This will easily last 6 months. The cream is scented. Why, I don't know. Fragrance is one of the top allergens in beauty products. The scent is not bad, but if you are sensitive to fragrance, you won't like it. The product seems a bit thick and greasy, but it absorbs quickly and the skin feels smooth and supple afterwards. This has not bothered my sensitive skin at all, but at the same time, it hasn't done much to improve the appearance of my skin. Perhaps it needs more time. So far, I neither love nor hate it.

This might be truffle, but to me it has faint coconut scent.
Most importantly, as you pat it under and around your eye area, it melts in without feeling greasy.
Anything that sits on top of the skin as opposed to melting in, tends to find its way into the outer corner of my eyes. As soon as it does that, my eyes burn and sting.
No problem with this luxurious product. In about a week, it looked like some of the fine lines softened.
A tiny bit goes a long was, making it a decent value for a premium skin product.
I also like that the 'use by' date is clearly marked.
Especially for something around the eyes, I don't want to risk using an old product.

I first have to say that I am the kind of person who's convinced that there's no 100% absolute cure for fine lines and wrinkles. Having said that, there are a few really good products that I have tried that do make the appearance of them seem next to none, and this Skin & Co Eye Concentrate is one of them. The jar is very tiny at .5 fl oz and with the $66 price tag, some might gasp, but this is definitely not the most expensive that I've seen on the market at this size. As far as performance, it only took a few days of use to notice a difference in the appearance of my skin in the under eye area. I was actually very impressed with the rapid results with other products that I've tried taking much longer.

The first thing that really stuck out for me was this brightening effect on my skin in the eye area. It gave the skin around my eyes a more vibrant, suppleness, which in turn made any fine lines appear less noticeable.  The product has a very light fragrance to it that's not bothersome for me. I actually think it's quite pleasant. As far as absorption, this aspect was just okay. Upon placing my finger gently in the application area after a few hours, I still felt a bit of the serum still present. With that being said, the serum is a very light cream that actually feels like it hydrates, so while it wasn't fully absorbed into my skin, it wasn't greasy either. I am not going to sit here and say that I have deep wrinkles under my eyes, but at my age, the fine lines are starting to show up and this cream has been working really well. After achieving the positive results that I did with this product, I will be checking into the rest of the company's line to see if they have a matching all over facial serum or moisturizer.
summary: Adds a Lovely Brightening Effect to the Under Eye Area

reviewText:
I tend to use a lot of good products on my eyes, most recently NIA 24.  My eyes are really important to me.  For me, the issues aren't so much wrinkles but bags and the feeling of my eyes.

After using this product, I kept wanting to touch my eyes, just because of how smooth and soft they feel.  It's hard not to touch them.  The skin around my eyes is just so soft and supple.

PLUS I smell good.  What's not to like about that?

It has a nice silky feel, absorbs well & did not irritate my skin but I don't see any magical results. It does have a scent - kind of a coconut/earthy scent that will be off-putting to some. I'm not sure I believe all the marketing flannel about "anti-aging" but it is very moisturizing & plumps up the skin to make it feel soft & smooth. Is it better than many less expensive creams? To me, maybe. It is a lovely moisturizer & you may feel it's worth the expense. But if you do not like scent on your face, you may not like wearing this. In order to guard against contaminating this product, I take a spoon & put a small amount of the concentrate for daily use in to a small container (like a lip balm container). That way, I won't contaminate the entire jar by putting my finger in it. Always make sure you finger is clean before applying. Beauticom 5G/5ML High Quality Clear Plastic Cosmetic Container Jars with Screw Cap Lids (Quantity: 25pcs)

It seems like the scent is either loved or hated. I am a little indifferent, but am leaning to the "love" camp. I don't think it is overpowering. The cream is light enough to go on easily. I have been using it before bed and in the morning. I don't see miracles, but also don't expect them. My eyes feel uncomfortable at night due to the cream leaking into them, but not as badly as with the majority of the eye creams I have tried.

I don't like the huge ingredient list and would prefer if it was in English, not just Italian.

Like many cosmetics, it is way over-packaged. The box is big, but the actual jar is small and the contents tiny.

It works OK, but not enough better than other products for me to buy more, especially at this price.

My wife loves this eye cream. The fragrance is subtle and pleasant.  Texture smooth and easy to apply.  She has started to use it but doesn't have concrete results yet. Price point is a little high for the size, but many high end brands (Bobbi Brown and Lancome) are charging about the same.

I could smell the perfume as soon as I grab the package out of the mailbox. When I opened up the package, a huge waft of perfume came out. It gave me an instant migraine headache. There is no way that I can use this. If you have allergies, sensitive skin or are sensitive to scents, this is not for you.

I love the way this cream feels and smells.  I know these things don't seem important but they do.  I've tried lighter formulas that had an overpowering scent and they not only didn't minimize fine lines but they sometimes made my eyes water a bit.  It will take longer for me to know if it will work on my fine lines.  What I would love to see, and so far no product has done this, is a little less puffiness around my eyes.  I'll be updating my review in a month to share my results.
summary: So Far So Great and Keeping My Fingers Crossed

reviewText:
Here are some thoughts on my overall experience with this product:

1.) The delivery system is less than ideal. Dipping one's finger into a jar repeatedly encourages contamination. A pump bottle is a better choice since it is a bit more sanitary ... likewise, for a dropper system. So, one has to keep a closer watch on this jar than one would with a dropper or pump bottle. Any change in consistency or odor and one should dispose of it promptly (especially since it is applied to the delicate eye area). So, while the jar may be cosmetically lovely in one's cabinet, it is not the best choice.

2.) The scent is pervasive. One notices it when one opens the jar and removes the seal ... it seems tolerable (similar to a very strong raw shea butter). But the scent does not dissipate. Thirty minutes later, it's still there. An hour later, when I turned my head, I could literally still smell it. I doubt that it's an added fragrance (one probably would not elect to add this scent), so it may be organic to the product itself. Nonetheless, it does wear on one. And those sensitive or allergic to fragrances may find themselves unable to use this product ... just proceed with caution.

3.) While I was able to pat it under my eyes, and it seemed to be absorbed into my skin, I later went to remove my contacts, and it just rolled up in little balls with a mere touch. So, I would advise not to touch the area after application (and to avoid side-sleep because the same happened with my pillow-cases).

Rather than trying trendy cremes with pearl dust, gold flakes, or truffles, simply try a retinoid ... they are the gold standard (and they have nearly no  scent. Bonus).
summary: Less Than Ideal Delivery System, Strong Scent, Gimmicky ...

reviewText:

After a hamstring tear and working from home, I had to go back to the office and I wear makeup but I go so used to not wearing any, that the first week was horrible to my skin and eyes (and mind). I have to go on a business trip in a few weeks and I'm definitely going to pack these.  I'm sure this trip with be morning to night meetings and I will need to get the eye makeup off and will need a gentle way of doing it.  I never heard of this brand before but I'm glad I got these.  They are definitely worth it and if you need your makeup off fast and gentle, try these

I received this product for free for my unbiased and honest opinion. I was not paid for this.
I opened this package and the smell was overwhelming. I do not wear eye make up but thought these would be nice to use to clean my face. You can use it to remove mascara and liner with no problem.  It doesn't have much of a fragrance to note.  They come out of the package feeling a bit cool to the touch.  They are sized big enough so that you have plenty of area to use to work the tough spots as needed.  The package is like others of its kind - easy to open and reseal.  These would be very refreshing on a hot summer day.

reviewText: I love these cleaning cloths! I am usually very lazy and don't always remove my eye makeup before going to bed. I've tried other cloths in the past and didn't care for the smell and they seemed too harsh. These cloths are amazing, the scent is just enough without being too strong, they're gentle on my eyes, and I give my face a once over with them too, since the cloths are so large, it seems wasteful otherwise, and it's so refreshing.

I use waterproof mascara + eyeshadow & liner on my eyes. reviewText: These simply do not work for removing eye makeup that I've been able to remove successfully with inexpensive Neutrogena face wash for many years. I never use waterproof eye makeup, and I never have trouble washing off any of my makeup at the end of the day with a simple, 30-second washing. They left my skin feeling tight, strange, un-cleansed. Imhad to always follow with my regular face wash. I had high hopes for a product I could use in a hurry or take to the gym. These did not deliver.

summary: It takes off eye makeup like a champ (even Halloween grease paint) and it smells ...

reviewText:
I like to have cleansing cloths in my bathroom for when I come home from a night out. I am almost always too tired to do a complicated makeup removal. Cleansing Cloths make it much easier and quicker. I have been using them for years, but this is my first time trying them from skyn.

I LOVE how the ICELAND Glacial cloths soothe my eyes. They are so relaxing on tired skin. I think I may even start using them after long nights at work when my eyes are sore too. reviewText:
I use thick black mascara and these cleansing cloths did the trick in getting it off with one cloth! I love the scent and the feeling of the liquid on the cloth is very smooth and cool.
