reviewText: There are better eyelid cleaners to be had for less. That being said they do refresh the eye very well. As I don't wear makeup I couldn't say how they do on that. They did fail to stop the burning from some Ben Gay that I accidentally got on my eyelid. Don't ask.

Very easy and effective to remove any kind of makeup on your eyes - it was pretty easy to remove a mascara (revlon) and an eye shade I had used.

It is good and works for your face as well

I've tried many cleansing cloths which have failed to make quick work of the waterproof eyeliner I wear - but I'm happy to announce that this product is a success. Only a couple swipes and my eye makeup comes off - no rubbing, no repeated contact. I have been using it for a week now and no adverse reactions or stinging by my sensitive eye area.  I was so happy with the cloths that I used it all over my face and neck to take off all my makeup and sunscreen/lotion I use during the day. Again, no adverse reaction.  The cloth itself is gentle and the product with which the cloth is saturated is also very mild.  The instructions say to take the cloth and rub it with itself to create a lather and then apply to the skin.
summary: Quickly takes care of my waterproof eye makeup

reviewText:
Skyn Iceland's Blemish Dots are advertised to shrink blemishes and sooth irritation. They can be worn during the day, but overnight is more practical. The Dots are supplied in a package of 4 sheets with 12 dots per sheets. There are two sizes of Dots, 11mm and 14mm, with six of each on a sheet. The Dots peel off the sheet and stick to your skin. They are clear and barely noticeable unless the light hits them at a certain angle. They stick well and stay on at night, even if you wear a sleep mask or toss and turn. I have a lot of skin allergies and sensitive skin that becomes stressed and irritated easily, but the Blemish Dots don't bother me. I only use salicylic acid as a spot treatment, as it is too drying for my skin, but the Dots didn't noticeably dry my skin or cause peeling.

The ingredient list does not indicate how much salicylic acid is on the Dots. In fact, salicylic acid isn't listed as an ingredient. Willow Bark Extract is listed as a natural source of salicylic acid. Other active ingredients are: volcanic ash (detoxifies, absorbs oil), phytosphingosine (moisturizes), grape seed extract (anti-oxidant), Canadian willowherb (anti-inflammatory), bakuchiol (natural retinol alternative), and Skyn Iceland's proprietary Icelandic Complex.

I've used the Dots on acne that had recently begun to emerge under the skin. I wore the Dots overnight, 8-12 hours. The acne has consistently improved by the morning. I believe this is due the Dots, because acne at that stage usually gets worse before it gets better. The Dots didn't reduce the acne to nothing, but the blemishes shrank. The blemishes I used this on were fairly large and completely under the skin; the Dots might do more for smaller blemishes. I found the Dots to be as effective as a benzoyl peroxide cream without drying or being harsh to my skin. And the medication goes where I want it, on the blemish, not smeared around. So, while they don't work miracles, Blemish Dots are a helpful addition to my anti-acne arsenal.

Ingredients: Acrylates Copolymer, Aqua/Eau/Water, Alcohol Denatured, Angelica Archangelica Root Water*, Vinyl Caprolactam/Vp/Dimethylaminoethyl Methacrylate Copolymer, Salix Alba (Willow) Bark Extract **, Volcanic Ash, Melaleuca Alternifolia (Tea Tree) Leaf Oil, Epilobium Angustifolium Flower/Leaf/Stem Extract (Willow Herb) , Bakuchoil, Rubus Chamaemorus (Arctic Cloudberry) Seed Oil, Simmondsia Chinensis (Jojoba) Seed Oil, Vitis Vinefera (Grape) Seed Extract, Sodium Hyaluronate, Phytosphingosine, Ceramide NP, Glycerin, Potassium Sorbate Sodium Benzoate, Citric Acid, Perfluorodecalin, Alcohol, Sodium Metabisulphite, Sucrose Palmitate, Phenoxyethanol, Xanthan Gum, PVP, Sodium Hydroxide, Butylene Glycol, Polysorbate 80.  *Component of Icelandic Glacial Water  **A Natural Source of Salicylic Acid
summary: Blemish Dots Don't Work Miracles, but They Help.

reviewText: It works but don't expect miracles. It takes a few days before you see a result. It does make your pimple smaller and if you keep it overnight and all day it eventually will make it somewhat better.  I like that I can put it on my pimple and it does not slide... so the stuff in it stays on your pimple all night which is good. I gave 4 stars (it takes time to see a difference) and its so expensive.
I love these dots, I wish I had found them years ago. I have tried other brands, but these have salicylic acid as a mild treatment. Will defiantly be repurchasing!

Big disappointment. The dots adhere to skin superbly. They stick on and stay on through sleeping or a sweaty workout. They peel off gently, too. That's all great but they don't reduce blemish size which is what they're for. The spots I treated even got worse as if there was no medicine on at all (I'm not saying they got worse because of the dots but just that the dots do not treat them). These stick on great, as I said before, and they protect the spot by covering it but they don't shrink blemishes so they were a waste of money. Better off applying a salicylic acid gel and a bandaid.
summary: The dots stick on great but don't work.

reviewText:
The Vichy Aqualia Thermal Facial Essence Water works very well as a supplement to my usual facial moisturizer.  Apparently designed to "add an extra layer of hydration" to skin, I did find that this water was effective at keeping my usually dry patches on my face moisturized.  I have combination normal/dry skin, and often when I use moisturizers, my normal patches get a bit greasy feeling while my dry patches show no significant change (aka, my skin is still dry and flaky).  After using the Essence Water for a few weeks now, I've noticed that my entire face is well moisturized without being oily in some patches and flaky on others.  It's really helped simplify my facial routine, and the results are overall positive.

The Essence Water has a consistency of water, so it would be prudent to either use a cotton pad to apply, or to put this into a spray bottle.  Why Vichy didn't put it into a spray bottle to begin with is a bit confusing to me since using one really makes application much easier.  The Essence Water has a light floral scent to it which vanishes quite quickly.  I used it with my normal moisturizer and found that the scents paired well and didn't conflict with each other.  I did try using this water by itself, but it wasn't moisturizing enough for my skin, so keep in mind that this works best as a supplement.  I would likely buy this Essence Water in the future simply because seems to work, and gives my skin that extra little boost it needs.  Overall, it was the missing piece I've been looking for in my skincare routine - it's a simple, but good light moisturizer.
summary: The Extra Little Moisturizing Boost My Skin Needed

reviewText:
Just like other Essence water products I have used I really like this water.  I apply as soon as I wake in the AM and after removing my makeup ( and before my night moisturizer ) in the PM. My face feels great and has never been cleaner and brighter. After using for three weeks my face just looks awesome and I totally attribute to  essence water products..

I have used in the spray bottle and I like this bottle better. Easier to use with a cotton swab. Love Love Love!

I have been pleasantly surprised by this product! As directed, I apply the essence water after cleansing and prior to applying moisturizer or any other products. I have extremely sensitive and eczema-prone skin this time of year, and this product really has done a remarkable job at keeping my skin hydrated. I typically apply a heavy moisturizer at night and a light moisturizer in the morning, but with this product I have found that I can do without the morning moisturizer. I have now been using this product for almost a week and I haven't had any breakouts or any adverse reactions. Overall, I am very pleased. It feels like a simple, clean, and light product and it actually does what it claims to do - it helps maintain the moisture in my skin.

Facial essence waters claim to do many things.  This one helps with hydrating your skin.  You wash your face, dry it, then apply this essence water, then apply your normal moisturizer, serum, whatever on top of it.  This is NOT a toner (a toner is usually for PH balance or skin exfoliation).

This essence water absorbs quickly & does not make my skin feel tacky/sticky/oily.  It does not ball up under my moisturizer or foundation.  It does actually seem to help with moisturizing.  I especially notice it on my neck & cheeks.  I was skiing in cold, windy weather & this helped protect my face  I did not get chapped.

It does have a fragrance (I really wish it did NOT)  I don't like fragrance in my face products.  But it is not too heavy.  I do notice it for an hour or so.  It is kind of a clean, cleanser type of scent.

Vichy Aqualia Thermal Facial Essence Water is a wonderful product for those of us who have sensitive skin. I especially like it while traveling long distances on planes. It relaxes and refreshes my skin in a gentle and soothing way.
Vichy Aqualia Thermal Facial Essence Water is a lovely addition to my beauty regime, and perhaps to yours as well! I can't describe how hydrated and soft my skin feels after using it.
summary: Marvelous Vichy Aqualia Thermal Facial Essence Water brings my skin back to life during long plane rides

reviewText:
This felt more like perfumed water, with some glycerin and moisturizers added. My face doesn't feel dry anymore after using astringent followed by the Vichy, and it isn't greasy or thick. I felt it might have been better if it were a cleanser and moisturizer but some might feel it compromises too much on either aspect - or perhaps some menthol added for a soothing effect.

Overall: 4/5 stars
summary: Neutral scent, does prevent overdrying after cleansing

reviewText: This is a good facial toner, w enough moisturizer to normalize your face and remove any tightness or after-washing stripping you might experience from a cleanser. I use this right after drying my face from cleansing, but before my base moisturizer. This Aqualia Thermal works as intended, and does make my face feel relaxed and hydrated, like a good moisture primer. It's very light, and feels just like water, w a very mild scent, which is hardly noticeable once dry, but pleasant. If you like to go nearly au natural, you could possibly skip your moisturizer and just use this. When I am putting on my regular foundation, however, I like to use an additional moisturizer as a base.  The feeling is soothing and cooling, and it's nearly like water itself.
Love.  I just apply after I wash and let it set dry and then add my foundation... love it!
summary: Love.  I just apply after I wash and let it set dry and then add my foundation... love it!

reviewText:
Excellent product!  I have reviewed two other liquid skin treatments from this same brand and I just love them!  This one prepares your skin for moisturizer.  It is not strong with alcohol or any astringent.  It feels very cooling and I think it is a luxury to use.  This is for sensitive skin, and I believe any skin type would be agreeable with this product.  It doesn't add substantial moisture, but what it adds it seals in. It balances oil and water.  I use it after a scrub or gentle cleanser (I only use harsh cleansers for tough jobs as when I have breakouts or clogged pores.)

It is a serum you can use either at night or day.  I am using it just out of the shower with a cotton pad.  I can see a bit of grit on the pad even after cleansing and drying my face.  I just love this step in my beauty regimen, and I recommend any of the Vichy products inspired by the French.
summary: Excellent product! I have reviewed two other liquid skin ...

reviewText:
I am not sure exactly how it works, but I like it.  The difference is subtle but I do notice that my serum and then moisturize smooths on more easily.  This is a very mild "moisturizing water" it doesn't have the harsh alcohol feeling (or smell) thank goodness.  It is just a refreshing feeling while cleaning your face to add a layer of moisture in preparation for the next step in your regiment.

After using for 2 weeks I have noticed that my face is not as dry at the end of the day, and that is saying something in winter in Colorado.  My skin has not had any reactions to it and it really only takes a little bit, so this bottle should last a long time.  I have had other products by Vichy and have had great results with them.  I can't wait to try their serum next.
summary: Extra layer of moisture is perfect for the winter.

reviewText:
I love Vichy Aqualia on my face. It makes my skin feel smoother and more moist right after I apply it. I have sensitive skin and I did not notice that having it on my skin presented any problems. I have not noticed any difference with my skin except right after I apply it. To me, it has no scent.

Out of the bottle, it has a consistency of water so trying to place some of it on fingertips will prove futile. You will need a cotton ball or other absorbent medium to be able to get it on your face.
summary: Refreshing product that makes skin feel smoother and more moist after applying

reviewText:
I used this product every day for 2 weeks. I was so enthused by its possibilities that I had the follow-up product - Aqualia Thermal Power Serum - in my Amazon cart. I removed it for the following reasons.

This Vichy Aqualia Thermal Hydrating Refreshing Water made it difficult to apply my favorite tinted moisturizer. It was blotchy and not blendable. It did not slide across my face which is why I like that tinted SPF moisturizer so much.

But I persisted.  Over time, flakes and redness around my mouth started to appear. It could be a reaction to the active ingredients, which are water, glycerin, and castor oil. Or any number of color dyes . Or the version of polyethylene glycol which is derived from bees wax. (I also have reactions to most bee products from a guy whose name begins with "B".) Or the copper sulfate, which in large enough quantity dissolves roots from plumbing pipes. Or the chelation agent disodium EDTA, which is probably beibg used as a preservative. Or the "parfum", which could be anything. Or the myrtrimonium bromide, which is an ammonium salt.

So I cannot say what my skin reacted to, but react it did.  I had to discontinue the product and get a prescription from my dermatologist for the redness which also tightened my skin painfully.

Yes, it sounds like plain old innocuous water. And it was indeed tested on "asian (sic) sensitive skin". But not on mine anymore. (I am neither asian nor Asian.)

But I have admittedly wonky skin. If you have wonky skin, I would not recommend this. If you have admirably normal, normal dry, or otherwise non-sensitive skin, then I would say yes, give this product a try. But know that you are getting a lot more than just water.
summary: Any Number of The Non-water Ingredients Made My Sensitive Skin Red & Flaky; Had To Consult Dermatologist

reviewText:
The Vichy Aqualia Thermal Facial Essence Water is a product that my wife was very interested in. She has slightly drier skin than mine and the midwest climate that we live in can be a bit of a challenge. She uses a regular moisturizer before her sleep but since this was mentioned as a additive, she wanted to see if it helped...

 This facial essence fluid is very much like water and so like the other commentators have recommended, it will be good to use a cotton ball to better utilize it. My wife used it on her face on the drier patches and then the regular areas. It's very easy to apply and spreads nicely. This is not without a fragrance but it's a mid one and soon dissipates.

 She mentioned that after using it for a couple of weeks, she's noticed that the dry patches are looking a little better. She also uses aveeno moisturizers so please take that also into consideration.  The bottle is on the slight pricy side but with judicious usage, you can justify the cost and use it every night or day to moisturize and clean your face.
summary: A moisturizing booster for dry & regular skin.

reviewText:
Vichy's Aqualia is basically water on steroids. It is light, hydrating, and a pleasure to use. I tend to be lax about skin care routines and rarely bother with makeup, but I am using Aqualia regularly because I absolutely adore the light, mildly floral fragrance.  This product not only smells wonderful, it doesn't set off any sinus twitching in my chemically-sensitive nose. That's a very good thing.

My oily youth has paid off - my very mature skin isn't terribly dry, so this product is perfect for me. I use it morning and night after washing my face (and sometimes in the afternoon because it's so refreshing). I just put a little on a cotton pad and rub it in. It seems to clean my skin a little more after the soap, which is pretty impressive. And it feels sooo good.

Aqualia absolutely keeps my face more hydrated than it normally would be - that's obvious on drier days. On very dry days, I put a little moisturizing cream on top of it, especially if I'm going out.

I've been testing this product in winter and I love how refreshing it is. In summer, it's going to be over-the-moon pleasurable to use! I will be purchasing more before this bottle runs out.

While not inexpensive, if you don't soak your cotton pad too heavily, this will last quite a while. (I don't recommend using cotton balls because they will make it go too fast.) If your skin is anything but very dry, I'd recommend giving Thermal Facial Essence Water a try.

If you wear makeup, this is a great light moisturizer

This Facial Essence Water is fragranced, so stop here if that's not what you like. It does contain glycerin and castor oil, so it has moisturizing ingredients in it, even though it has the texture of water. Application is difficult in this bottle, as it's not something you pour on your hands to use. It's definitely necessary to use cotton or something similar to apply. It dries nice, and the fragrance does fade after a while. It's nice under make up, and for a night time routine. It's not oily yet it manages to hydrate the skin very well against all elements. The Vichy products I have used have all been fantastic.

I have never considered myself as someone who has sensitive skin, but this product and my skin did not get along.  I followed the directions as written on the bottle and less than an hour after the first application I could feel the irritation on my skin; a little itchy and warm.  Because I thought it might be a case of "no pain, no gain" I applied it that evening and received the same results, but a bit more intense. I ended up having to wash my face again and applying a anti-inch moisturizer to allow me to sleep.  Because I don't know what was causing the reaction I won't say that this won't work for others, but I am unable to give it more than two starts as "I don't like it."

I have liked most of the Vichy products I have tried.  I like that this one is refreshing and feels good on my face while offering it moisture after cleaning.  I don't like the way many cleansers dry out my skin.  I just can't afford the dryness.  It kind of felt funny on my skin though.

This product has a very faint scent.  It is hard to figure out.  It is like fresh lake water or baby powder.  Kind of both.  I don't generally like scents but this one was faint enough not to bother me.

I love Vichy products and have yet to be disappointed. They are non-irritating on my rosacea prone skin and really have been a benefit to my skin.  The Thermal Facial Essence is the Vichy quality I expect - it's easy to apply with a cotton ball, safe and leaves my skin feeling soft and moisturized.  I put 4 stars because as a product - I am not sure why I need an extra step before my moisturizer and as a working mother with limited time, I really don't have time for it.  This is not moisturizing enough for me to skip the moisturizer (maybe in the summer....)
summary: Gentle and makes my skin soft - but what is it for?

reviewText:
I haven't seen a product like this before, so it's a little hard to compare to anything. Essentially it feels like very-slightly-thickened water, with some mild, pleasant fragrance and a faint blue tint. The application directions are a little vague, but you put it on your face after washing and before further steps, like moisturizing. I just use my hands, because I feel like a cotton ball would just absorb it all.

It definitely seems to smooth and hydrate. Moisturizer spreads more easily and seems to soak in better after using this.

Is that an important function? I'm not sure. But I do kind of like it, and Vichy has nice products overall. Worth a try, especially if you're in a dry climate, or have dry skin.

I like this tool a lot.  It heats up crazy fast.  It's easy to turn on and has two settings.  Immediately little blue lights go up the heat indicator and I can feel heat!  In less than a minute I able to use it.
Now, I mainly like to curl my hair, and I do prefer my cone curling iron for that, but I still think this is a 5 because it is also very easy to straighten hair with it, or just add some waves or a flip.  I much prefer it to the OneStyler brush types.  There are no little gaps or weird places that catch my hair on this one, and it only took me a couple of minutes to figure out how to use it to accomplish multiple tasks- there's almost no learning curve at all!  It gets really hot - to 410, and has a nice range of adjustable settings.  410 curl my hair well and the curls last.  It shines hair as it contacts the tourmaline plates.

The cord swivels and it turns itself off automatically if it is left on.  It has a luxe look and feel and doesn't take up a lot of space.
I think it is great.
The only possible downside I can think of is that it is not very wide.  If it were wider though, it would not be as good for curls and flips, so that doesn't really bother me.
It comes with 2 hairclip tools for holding sections of hair.
summary: It heats up superfast, super simple to learn how to use it for multiple tasks, has a luxe look and feel

reviewText:
Full disclosure: I have only used this straightener one time (so far) and only to straighten, not to attempt curling. If any aspect of my review changes or issues arise, I will edit more review to reflect the additional information.

EDIT: I hadn't used this straightener in a few weeks and, when I attempted to turn it on, it no longer worked. Will be throwing out and getting something different.

First, and perhaps not so important, this straighter does have a sleek look. It's lightweight and narrow, unlike some of the bulky straighteners I've owned in the past. This is a plus as it takes up less counter space and isn't an eyesore.

There is one button that controls on/off and the temperature of the device. Holding down the button turns it on/off, while double clicking allows for temperature control. Above the button there is a series of lights that change depending on the temperature and indicate that the straighter is heating vs ready to use. While, as far as I can tell, this type of control set-up does work, the different temperatures are not noted on the device. I use the same temp every time, so this doesn't affect me as much, but, if you might need to adjust the heat, you'll have to check the instructions pamphlet for temp ranges.

I have admittedly thin hair, but it is naturally curly. I had no problem straightening the majority with only one pass, but some of the more finicky bits, like my bedhead bangs, took a bit more finesse.

As a plus, this straightener did come with two hair clips to divide and twist up hair when straightening. I usually use bobby pins, which I constantly lose, so this was a nice bonus!

I have used just one straightener in my life and I didn't like how fuzzy and stiff my hair looked after using it.

So this straightener makes my hair straight but it isn't quite as fuzzy and stiff.  I think I may have to really really condition my hair to keep it shiny.  Because it is sorta straw like.  But I might have to adjust the heat down because I have baby fine hair that has a tendency towards flatness.  The reason I needed the straightner is because I have two really bovious cowlicks and I was hoping to flaten them out a bit.

The Luxe is super lightweight and the copper on the handle provides a handy guide for your fingers so that you don't end up turning the straightner off inadvertantly.

There is a little velcro fastener so that you can coil up the cord, I love it when appliances have these straps, it's a small thing but so useful and tidy.

So far this is a wonderful product.

Styling hair is not something I do well. I'm kind of a dunce at it. So this review will be for people like me who want to know the basics. Unlike most of my hair styling tools, this one had a simple, easy-to-use plug.  It was very simple to turn on and off, with an excellent operating display that shows clearly if it is turned on or not, and to allow you to change the temperature switch. To do that, you just press the power button until it gets to the one you want, after getting to hottest setting, press again and you're back to the lowest setting.  When the lights turn SOLID, you can start using it. If you want to turn it off, press and hold the Power & Temperature Switch. I don't trust myself or the iron enough to leave it plugged in though, so I just unplug it.

The Singlepass Luxe comes with a couple of clips to help section off the hair. You're supposed to use thin horizontal sections so the iron can be positioned close to the roots.  I need to work on that.

It worked well on my hair, which is in the 'fine' category.  There's a little chart in the instructions that says you should slow down as you use the iron and glide it through the direction of hair growth at a speed slower than when you brush your hair. If you have fine hair, they suggest 2-3 inches per second, medium hair, 2 inches per second, and course hair, 1 inch per second.  My hair looks good now that I've finished styling it, so I guess even though I didn't section it off perfectly into thin horizontal sections, it works for me.  I think I'll be able to do better with practice.

I wanted to do some little curls in the front. There were no instructions on how to do that. I'll need some

They did mention several times not to wind the cord around the flat iron because it will shorten the life of the iron.
summary: Worked well on my hair, which is in the 'fine' category. My hair looks good after using it, should look better with practice.

reviewText:
I've tried dozens of flat irons over the years. CHI used to be my go-to brand until their flat irons started frying my hair. Then I swore off flat irons that cost $100 or more and went with Remington's anti-frizz line, which did a good enough job without frying my hair but I then got better results with another flat iron that actually uses oil during the flat iron process, but I got tired of paying $25.00 every time I had to refill the iron and ran out of oil. I decided to give this one a try since I have a lot of hair and it's not easy to straighten, especially in Florida where I can straighten it and then have it totally frizz out on me in 2 hours throwing all the hard work away. I actually love the way this flat iron works.

While it doesn't get all of my hair in one pass it does cut down on my styling time. Not only does it straighten but it is also a great styling tool letting me do amazing waves. The iron's setting is adjustable so I can make it hot enough to get the job done without overdoing it. I also like that it doesn't have one of those huge plugs at the end so I can have more than one thing plugged into the outlet at a time.

Overall, if you're looking for a quality flat iron that also lets you style and curl this is a great choice. It does the job without frying my hair, the style holds all day and the humidity here doesn't ruin it in a couple of hours, you can adjust the heat setting, and it really does cut down the time it takes for me to style my hair. It also looks great, which to me isn't a "must" when shopping for a flat iron but is always a nice plus.
summary: Great Results and Easy to Use

reviewText:
I was SO excited to receive this because I have long been a fan of T3.  I recently replaced my T3 Featherweight dryer that lasted 4+ years and also have the Twirl 360 curling iron, which is another favorite of mine.  So I had high expectations of the performance of this flat iron.

Thankfully it delivers.  (And this is coming from someone who has been flat ironing her hair for 15+ years and has tried a range of flat irons from low end to high end over the years.)  The buttons are pretty minimalist so it took a peek at the directions to figure out what the lights mean and what the appropriate setting is for my hair, but after looking the first few times its intuitive.

For context, I have long (mid-back), thick, naturally wavy, color treated blonde hair.  My hair is also very dry year round (lingering side-effect from past accutane use) and is further prone to dryness because I have it bleached and toned at the salon.  Accordingly, whenever I heat style I try to minimize damage by using the lowest heat setting I can, going over each strand once (if possible), and wearing my styled hair for a few days with the help of dry shampoo.  This flat iron helps me very much with this.  If I blow my hair out as straight as possible before hand and work in small sections I can get by with a single pass for the most part.  If I flat iron my hair when it's been allowed to dry wavy, it does take a couple of passes to get everything perfectly straight, however.  I also do appreciate that even though my hair is thick and coarse I don't have to use the highest heat setting.

I also LOVE the experience of using this.  It is so light weight (I realize that can also make it feel a bit cheaper than other brands, but since I have so much hair I much prefer the lightness of this even if it means you sacrifice the quality look of the materials a bit).  The nice long swivel cord is handy and the plates are well designed.  They grip the hair perfectly so it doesn't slip and hair doesn't catch or get stuck.  And I find the width of this iron perfect.  I know some people recommend thicker flat irons for longer hair but I personally prefer this width because it's easier to control and makes it more versatile for doing curls.

And I will admit to loving the rose gold detailing.  It shouldn't matter but it makes for a very pretty iron that I'm proud to have out on my vanity.

Honestly, at this present moment I can't find a single thing to dislike about this straightener and given my past positive experience with the brand I'm hopeful my love for this flat iron will continue in the future.

Would recommend!
summary: Consistent with the high quality I've come to expect from T3

reviewText:
The T3 has a simple, clean look and professional features. My first impressions of this flatiron were very positive. It does a nice job styling my hair quickly and easily. My hair remains frizz-free, silky, and shiny throughout the day.

However, after using the T3 daily for a few weeks, I am having trouble getting it to turn on.

The problem . . .

The flatiron worked flawlessly for the first two weeks; however, the past few days I have had difficulty getting it to turn on. The on/off button should work with one push, but I need to press and wiggle the on/off button several times before it lights up. Once it is on, I am able to use it with no problem including changing the temperature and turning it off when finished. The problem occurs again when I attempt to turn it back on.

Once the iron is on and working . . .

The plates distribute heat evenly and have a bit of give, or float, which allows me to get a good grip on my hair. Despite the firm grip, my hair slides smoothly and doesn't catch or stick. The one inch plates are not overly large which is perfect for styling my fine but often frizzy hair.

The iron has a swivel cord, auto shutoff after one hour, and variable heat selections. It heats up fast -- in under two minutes it was ready to use. There are 5 heat settings ranging from 260 to 410 F, but no digital temperature readout. Once a setting is selected - I keep it on 3 -- it defaults back to that number when it is turned on again. No need to reset every time.

The T3 has dual voltage for international use. It's nice to have, but the downside is a much thicker cord that is a little more clunky to use than the flat, lighter weight, 110-only type cord on my other iron.

While I like this flatiron, I suspect I have a defective unit. Had I purchased this rather than received it for review, I would have returned or exchanged it as it is under warranty. Ultimately, I am disappointed that a unit at this price point does not have better quality control and was shipped with a defect.
summary: Good results styling my hair but unit has a defective on/off button

reviewText: The T3 Micro Single Pass Luxe professional flat iron design and look is clean and appealing.  I love the white color and gold accents.  I hope that the white stays white and clean looking.  The T3 has special technology that allows the flat iron to heat quickly and evenly.  I like the regular plug so that I can use the other half of the outlet while using the flat iron.  There is a little Velcro band attaches to the cord so you can wrap up the cord and you can find the Velcro fastener when you need it.  I have fine hair, but lots of it.  Using the included clips,  I sectioned off about 2" sections and used the flat iron to straighten my hair.  The iron glides through the hair without snagging.  A single pass actually does the trick.  You simply move slower if you have thicker hair.  The flat iron left my hair soft and straight, without fuzzy it up.  The controls are a little tricky to figure out so I need more practice there.  The heat range for the flat iron works for all types of hair.  So far, I am pleased with the results the flat iron gives my hair.
summary: Easy to use and leaves my hair soft and straight

reviewText:
I've been using a CHI for years when I want to straighten my curly hair. It's a very popular brand and is considered by some to be the "gold" standard of flat irons. I think I paid $100 for mine. While it's much better than cheap flat irons, what I don't like about it is you can't adjust the heat (it gets VERY hot) and it makes my hair very flat. Straight, but flat. I was eager to see how this T3 Micro Single Pass Luxe compares, especially being so expensive.

First, the packaging is luxurious. It comes in a beautiful box with a lid. Inside you find an elegant iron and two hair clips, plus an envelop containing the instructions and a heat-resistant resting pad. Of course, looks don't really matter (only performance does), but it's a pretty presentation nonetheless.

This iron comes with multiple heat setting, which is a big, big plus. Although my hair is curly, the strands are very silky--thus, easy to straighten. I don't need sky-high temps (like the CHI) to straighten my hair.

The plates are so smooth that they glide down the hair effortlessly. The first few times I had to look closely because it seemed like they weren't even touching my hair (they were).

The end result? Wow! I got straight, silky hair that wasn't flat and clinging to my head. Really different than what the CHI does. The next morning I woke up and my hair was still beautiful.

This is definitely worth the price!

This flat iron is replacing my 10 year old flat iron that I love. The one I have is twice as wide as this and gets the job done quickly. I figured with this being thinner it would take longer but that is not the case. This heats up quickly and gets very hot. I have medium thickness wavy hair and I'm able to get it all straightened in less than 10 minutes. I like the fact that it is thin so it allows me to flip the ends of my hair or even use it as a curling iron. With my previous flat iron I had to work quickly and do multiple passes to avoid getting kinks where it was obvious that I used a heat tool to style my hair. After using this I had no kinks in my hair and it was very smooth and frizz free. I've a also used it on my daughter who has thick, very curly hair and it works wonderfully for her as well.
summary: Smooth, straight hair with no kinks

reviewText: This flat iron has a lot going for it. Good simplicity of operation and results. My hair is color treated, long and naturally curly/wavy. It's fine, but I have a lot of it. This iron produced very satisfactory results, and while it wasn't fully "single pass" on every section (possibly because I like to grab large sections since I'm always in a hurry) I do love this flat iron. It's attractively made and works well, so how much more could I want? Just section off your hair with the clips and create the style you want. It's hard to believe that we really had to set our hair in giant rollers all night to get the full, smooth look created with this iron. Definitely recommended.
summary: I'd recommend this iron to anyone!

reviewText:
I can't help but wonder after glancing at the other stellar reviews: "Did I get a bad one?" I was very disappointed in this product. The packaging and the product are no where near what was expected for this high price tag iron, and its performance was poor on my hair.

The iron does heat up in about 2 minutes, but for my curly, thick locks - taking small sections - it took multiple passes with the iron to get the job done. I have used many professional quality irons; most less expensive than this one, that successfully did complete 'one pass' straightening, but this one did not.

NOTE:  One pass indicates constant heat is maintained throughout the iron while in use.

The T3's build quality isn't as expected either. The overall feel is one of lightweight plastic - cheap feeling - and again, very disappointing.

The good things I can say about this product: the swivel cord is of a good length and my hair moves smoothly across the heated plates. The one push on/off with blue LEDs to indicate when the iron is heated up are simple to view and use.

For the high asking price of this iron I was expecting the sort of performance my stylist's iron produces in the salon. I would have been happy if it had been on par with my other irons: HSI Professional Ceramic Tourmaline Ionic Flat Iron and the Remington S9110S T|Studio Thermaluxe Slim Hair Straightener which both tend to run in the thirty to forty dollar range and work 100% better than this T3.

Maybe I got a bad one?  It makes me sad that this iron didn't live up to its hype, but I cannot recommend this item to others.

I have used this iron on two different sets of hair in my household.  One, for my oldest daughter who is a religious hair straightener.  She doesn't go anywhere without straightening her hair.  Her go to brand has been the Chi Iron.  Her hair is thick and extremely curly.  When I say thick, it is a mane of curly, thick, long, hair.  This is her overall experience (below):

This is a really nice iron.  I like the design and look a lot.  It heats up fast and glides through my hair really nice.  It reminds me a lot of the Chi iron, except the plates are extended out a bit more, which is nice because I can give a little wave or curl whenever I want.  The heat is very consistent and I love that there is heat control.  My hair doesn't feel like it's getting fried.  I'll continue to use this iron daily and let you know if there is anything that I start disliking about the product.  The cord swivels a lot nicer than the Chi, so I'm hoping it will last longer.  I've gone through several Chi Iron's just for the cord alone.  Also, this iron It includes two hair clips which I use, so that is super convenient.  Overall, I love it.  It will be my goto hair straightener right now.

My other daughter also has curly hair, but her hair is thinner.  I was able to easily straighten her hair.  She tends to have dry hair and the iron made her hair look shiny and beautiful.  It's pretty amazing.  However,  even if you don't have dry hair,  always use a heat protectant before you start ironing.

Overall this is a very competitive flat iron when it comes to the higher end models.  If you have really thick hair, obviously it will take longer to straighten than if you have thinner hair.  But overall, you can achieve beautiful straight hair without the fear of burning or damaging it.  It's a well designed flat iron.

Should anything be faulty or become an issue, I will update my review accordingly.

Would recommend!
summary: Even temperature, bone straight hair or soft subtle curls.  Loving this!

reviewText:
I have long very fine damaged hair with waves.  I used this to help style my hair.  The first day I put it on - I used WAY too much.  My hair came out crunchy and stuck together.
I tried again the next day - less is definitely more.  I added only to the roots and then used a brush to comb through while blow drying.  Fuller hair, love the body.

Definitely recommend.
summary: I have long very fine damaged hair with waves

reviewText: There is a learning curve to this, it reminds me of a very similar product I used years ago (I think it was by sebastian or another higher end brand) which also has fibers in it. Basically you have to rub it with both hands and then quickly clap them (faster than in the video), the fibrous strands will then appear. I have very straight hair and found it hard to use without it making my hair look greasy. I also developed some zits on my scalp after using this even though I was EXTREMELY careful to only use it at my hair ends for styling purposes. Maybe this would be better for short hair dos that need scrunching up rather than to hold a hot iron type of curl.
summary: I found it difficult to use

reviewText:
THis is a neat product, but a steep learning curve for me.  You actually are making little fibers with your hands to apply into your hair. This gives your hair a sort of extra strength bonding to hold up any styling you want to do. For me, I wanted to just raise my roots for volume on top. It worked well, once I got the hang of it.

At first I used too much, the second time I used it after I had used some dry shampoo which just made a terrible mess together. It takes a bit of doing as once you put it into your hair, there's really no going back.  I'm sure it would hold some wild styles and shapes if you wanted.  For me, just the root lift is enough.

But figure on using a lot to get used to it.

I wear my thick, shoulder-length hair in a layered bob, and I like styling products that boost volume and give definition to the layers.  This is a good texturizing paste, though I think the whole rigmarole with clapping your hands to create fibers is kind of gimmicky.

I use a pea-sized amount then I clap my hands ten times (while rolling my eyes), and then I work the paste through my hair starting at the roots.  I like to wear my hair with a bit of wave to it, and this product does a great job of lifting and separating the waves, giving my hair the messy/tousled look that Im trying to achieve.  This product does not make my hair sticky  in fact, my hair feels clean and soft.  If I finish with just a bit of hairspray my hair will hold its shape for hours without requiring a touch-up.

Some things to keep in mind

*Use a small amount of product (you can always add more)
*Make sure the product is clear before you apply it to your hair
*Expect to experiment a little; if you're not used to working with a paste there is a learning curve
summary: A good texturizing paste despite the fussy application technique

reviewText:
Wife says: I have thick, curly, wavy and medium-length hair. And Man! this product worked!

I absolutely loved this gel, Small in size, but very effective. DO read the usage direction and it will be easy to use.

My hair stayed exactly in place the entire day, on a warm humid day, and I looked so fresh, as the gel gave my hair a look of freshness. It was very easy to come off both from the hands and the hair. Just a wash (no soap/shampoo needed) was enough.

I can't say if my hair felt drier after using this, as I am yet to use it enough number of times. So far, I've loved this product and can count on it during my travel.

This is an interesting product. It puts more texture into your hair than a pomade but a little less than a styling hair gel. Adding just a drop of this to clean hair can give it that day+ old hair texture, without the oily look. Definitely a product for shorter hair. The more hair you have the more it weighs the product down, and adding more product doesn't really work since it just makes your hair feel like you ran glue through it. But for short hair it works great.
summary: Best for those with short hair.

reviewText: When they say use a pea-sized amount, use a pea-sized amount. The problem with that is you will feel like it doesn't make much of a difference, so you're tempted to use more, but even a little bit more makes your hair stiff and sticky, although it settles down after you roll it or iron it or hot brush it or sleep on it. So the amount is critical, somewhere between this does nothing and this makes me look like Frankenstein's bride. The slapping your hands back and forth -- not sure what that does. It does sort of whip it up like you're whipping cream and the blob of cream starts to develop peaks.
summary: Use a Very Little of This

reviewText:
Calista has become a fairly well known company with hair care products. I have used their hairspray and curling irons. This product has specific uses, and must be used exactly as directed.

This product separates and defines hair without stickiness.  This can be an essential styling product, hair shaper, and texturizer for any look.  This is how I use it:

Put a pea-size amount into your hands and rub hands together. Clap hands together until you begin to see formed fibers connecting hand to hand. The more fibrous you make it, the lighter the product becomes. For fine hair clap your hands repeatedly before applying it to your hair. If your hair is heavy in weight, clap your hands only a few times, leaving the product more concentrated. Apply to dry hair, run through the root area for lift and fullness, and apply to the ends for texture. It is important to know that this product is not for staying power, you must use hairspray to keep the style.

Recommended. prisrob. 08-15-17
Smells identical to axe cedarwood bergamot body wash. That is just my opinion. Everyone's nose is different. Pretty good sized bottle though

The tobacco scent is very strong and lasts all day.  If you like the scent then you'll absolutely love this wash.  The narrow flask-shaped bottle is made of very hard plastic and quite difficult to squeeze the desired amount of product out.
summary: If you like the scent then you'll absolutely love this wash

reviewText:
This is an amusing product: An all-in-one wash that looks and smells like fine whiskey. They really nailed the scent, which is pleasant and masculine.  Although described as "tobacco," it smells nothing like a cigarette, which is a relief.

If the idea of a whiskey-themed body wash appeals to you, look no further!

Lathers up great and smells good.  Some people are describing the scent as tobacco, but I picked up more of a wet leather mixed with cedar wood.  My wife said she likes the smell of it and it is a far cry from the heavily perfumed mainstream products out there today.  This wash works great as shampoo and conditioner.  It did not dry out my hair or my skin for that matter.
summary: I like the whole whiskey bottle look to this 3 in 1 wash

reviewText: Not for your Missus or Girlfriend. This is a manly scent that really wakes you up in the shower. I use it as a body wash and love the scent and how it leaves my skin feeling clean. Its got a tobacco infused scent that reminds me of the rugged outdoors and smoking cigars.

The scent just doesn't work for me. I'd describe it like this: Take a pan of freshly prepared caramel, drizzle on a large helping of imitation vanilla, and then spritz with dollar store musk cologne. It doesn't smell very bad, but as others have noted, it does end up smelling like a cheap candle- one of those bath store candles aimed at women with a name like "Summer Mood" that doesn't actually describe any known smell in the universe.

So what you get is a container of mostly oversweet vanilla with undertones of cheap "manly" smells. If this was merely the first draft, as though these really were alcohol distillers and the first batch came out badly, then I'd say it has promise. As is I think this product is probably stuck where it is, so I'm not impressed.

The bath soap lathers just fine, but does NOT rinse well. The smell and an oily sensation clung to my body to the point that I wasn't sure when I would be done rinsing. So again, it feels cheap.

If this was something you could pick up at a dollar store, it might be a neat "masculine" gift. As it's not something I'd recommend unless you're buying it for the Axe crowd who aren't very discerning with scents to begin with. It certainly doesn't live up to its packaging.

Well... it goes like this: if you really, really want to smell like 'old men' after the shower, try the Man Made Wash because will. Seriously.

I suppose it's supposed to be a 'old fashion' but I tend to be allergic to fragrances and this is one body wash my body or skin is not super enthusiastic about. My standard for a 'good' body wash is one that does not smell at all and does not suppress the skin's natural and healthy odor. But the Man Made seems to aggressively attempt to replace that with some combination of stale tobacco, old leather and sweat which maybe make some feel good or more manly but it makes me want to go back to the shower and wash again with something else to get this odor off.

My three star rating stand for: "if it's not good for me, it doesn't mean that everyone should avoid it." Because it does the wash part. It's only the smell that makes me disagree.

Not only for men, I loved this when I first used it. It smells so much like Perlier Caribbean Vanilla and Coffee Eau de Toilette Spray that I've used off and on for several years, even down to the bottle being similar. I don't care for floral scents and girly-girl perfumes, I've always gravitated to earthy scents. This is OK, it smells like vanilla slightly. I've used it as a shampoo/conditioner as well as a body wash. My significant other (male) doesn't care for it. As far as lather, it makes enough...this doesn't dry out my hair, and I smell good for hours after showering. So why 3 stars? While I like the scent, it lingers for hours and HOURS---way over 20 hours, and after awhile it's a little cloying.
summary: It smells like rich warm vanilla, but after awhile the scent is cloying

reviewText:
You know, in moderation, I actually really kind of like how the 18.21 Man Made Wash smells. There aren't a whole lot of "manly" body washes out there. Sure, there are a lot marketed as being for men, but you have to wonder what kind of guys buy the stuff (think "Beast Aftershave" from Rocky II...a lot of the stuff just doesn't "smeel manly"). Don't get me wrong, 18.21 Man Made Wash is definitely some sweet-smelling stuff, but it's an odd (but appealing) mix of vanilla, honey and tobacco that together conjures up images of Bourbons and Burley Blends. The scent itself seems overpowering the first time you sniff it, and honestly, to me it was a bit overpowering when I was actually washing with it, but it rinses off well enough and just kinds of mellows when you're done with shower time. It's still very noticeable, but both my wife and daughter said something about me smelling good as soon as I walked out of the bathroom. I generally keep myself pretty clean, but I'm not used to that kind of reaction.

Unfortunately, actually using the wash wasn't the best experience. It didn't lather up well at all. I have very soft water, so things generally foam up pretty easily, but in this case, I had to apply it to my hair twice before it would even work up a moderate lather. Trying to get it to lather up applying it directly to your hands is a seemingly futile effort, and I ended up using a whole lot more of this than I should have, and despite the fact that I used a good bit, I still went to the bar soap to work up a decent lather for washing the dirtier areas. It might be better with a wash puff of some kind (a manly option, indeed), but overall it just didn't seem to do a great job. It did rinse off well enough, and my skin doesn't feel dried out, but it also doesn't feel particularly moisturized.

I liked it a bit better using it as a shampoo, as it did leave my hair feeling clean, soft and great-smelling (at least according to my wife and daughter). I would still use a separate conditioner, as using it alone does leave it feeling a bit dry, but my scalp doesn't feel itchy (which it generally does unless I'm using a dandruff or dry scalp shampoo).

All-in-all, the 18.21 Man Made Wash makes for a pretty good shampoo, but only a halfway decent bodywash. If it lathered up a bit better and I didn't have to use so much of it to get halfway decent results, I might like it a good bit more, but as it is, the scent is the only thing about this that's outstanding.
summary: Great scent and good as a shampoo, but only halfway-decent as a body wash.

reviewText: This wash, which is a shampoo, conditioner, and body wash, is contained in what I think is a fun bottle with the shape and color of a bottle of bourbon. I can imagine people at the health club thinking, "Hey, he needs a drink even in the shower!" But joking aside, the wash works and I felt clean and fresh after using it, and my hair looked good. My wife told me that I had a manly smell after I washed. I received it on condition that I write and honest review and can honestly say, "This wash does what it claims."
summary: This wash does what it claims

reviewText:
A body wash/shampoo/conditioner with a seriously manly scent! The sweet tobacco scent is not subtle at all, especially when you lather up in the shower, but it smells good and it fades once you rinse off - but stays with you in a subtler fashion throughout the day. I can see the scent being divisive, you either love it or hate it. I like it, and so does my wife, so it works in my household.

This is rather expensive wash, at about twice the price I would normally pay for wash, but it is a large bottle and a little does go a long way. I had no issues getting a good lather going, and I'm not sure why some other reviewers have reported low foam, as I get quite a lot of foam using a bath sponge. The one thing I don't quite like is that this wash leaves a kind of soft feeling on the skin, like a moisturizer, and I prefer not to have that feeling on the skin coming out of the shower. But all in all, I like the stuff quite a bit!

I am not particularly fascinated with the sweet tobacco fragrance of this body wash. Although the gel is both a fortified shampoo and body wash and does the dual job, but doesnt have the extra appeal to it either in terms of smell or nourishing the skin. It does not produces enough lather. I have used many brands of body washes over the year such as; Dove Men, Nivea Men, Old Spice, Irish Spring, etc. And I am perfectly happy with any of the last four products.

This is truly a manly all-in-one product with a woodsy scent. My husband loves the bottle design (looks like a pint of bourbon and the gentle formula. His shower this morning filled the bathroom with a lovely aroma that lingers on his skin. He washed and conditioned his hair and body with the fine ingredients in this Man Made Wash - which is made in the USA!
summary: This is truly a manly all-in-one product with a woodsy scent

reviewText:
In a product like body wash or any grooming product with a fragrance, there can more than just the person doing the review to please.

I will admit I was very interested in how this would smell after reading all the other reviews online, and I'm glad I selected this product to review, although, I'm nervous they may have a new customer. :(  Nervous because I usually pay between $5-10 for the regular products at the grocery store

When I first got this product, I was very intrigued by the smell. As different as it is to most other products, I figured once I had actually used it in the shower, it would change slightly, which it did, to deliver a somewhat less powerful aroma of a 'lighter weight.'

Wanting to get the wife's approval on this new product, when I first got out of the shower and got dried off, she said that she probably wouldn't want to be too close to me right out of the shower (that's just bad news right there), but she said to check with her again in an hour.

TECHNICALLY SPEAKING - my wife is actually completely right. In the structure of fragrance, there are top notes, middle notes and base notes.

Top Notes (also known as the head, and possess the highest volatility) are what you experience first.
Middle Notes (also referred as the heart, structured with medium volatility) deliver the meat of the fragrance.
Base Notes carry a much lower volatility, and can take up to two hours to be fully released. This is what gives a fragrance the ability to linger on clothes or skin.

The base notes in this body wash are about the most persistent I have ever come across -- .I can still smell this on my skin over 2.5 hours later.

Pros
#1 I love how the product is packaged to look like an exclusive bottle of whiskey.
#2 It is a unique aroma - unlike anything I have ever owned before.
#3 Quite concentrated, it requires very little to have a complete shower.

Cons
For me - none except that the Mrs hasn't quite got on the same page yet. :)

In summary, despite the higher than average price for a body wash, because of the levels of concentration and how little it takes, it is really good value.
summary: All about that BASE - Base note that is - its a fragrance thing....

reviewText:
As a Monty Python fan, I couldn't resist. Anyway...

Although I don't smoke, I confess that I love colognes that have tobacco element.
Tabac by Mäurer & Wirtz is a particular favotite.

This scented wash has that same tobacco and leather combination, like a more refined and elegant version of English Leather.
But it's the bottle that grabs you as well as the 'Manly Man' merchandising. It's pretty fun.

If you are not a fan of pink and floral foam, do a complete turnabout with this manly scented wash in a whiskey bottle clone.
summary: If you're a lumberjack and you're okay...

reviewText:
This is super thick and lathers well. The smell is awesome and it looks like a bottle of bourbon.  I don't have a lot of hair, so most shampoos are fine. Some guys with thicker hair may not it as much.  But it's great as a body wash.

My wife loves the scent.

I realize there is some marketing gimmickry going on here . . . the dark amber bottle, reminiscent of a pint of bourbon.  The "sweet tobacco" smell, with the label styled after a tax stamp.  The thick honey-like consistency.  But this shampoo/conditioner/body wash is just superb, and in the "manly toiletries" niche', it really stands out as unique.

As a side issue, I need to address the "tobacco" thing:  Tobacco, in this case, has nothing to do with the repugnant odor of burnt cigarettes - or any cigarette.  Think more of a rich sweet pipe tobacco, one of those that everyone compliments, "even though they don't smoke".  Spicy, earthy, sweet but not flowery.  I refreshed my recollection with a light hand wash just before starting this review and I just can't stop smelling the palms of my hands.  So, how well does it work? . . . .

This is a quite thick product but does not lather heavily on the body just using the hands.  If you want lots of lather, you'll need a washcloth or one of those poofy scrubby things.  I've also discovered that I can put a generous amount into my hair which will easily lather up nicely using just my hands, then work that down over the whole body as desired.  Performs great as a body wash, as a shampoo, and as a surprisingly effective conditioner - yielding a soft silkiness superior to most combination shampoo/conditioners (many of which don't condition at all).  I have longer hair for a male and can appreciate this. The fragrance lingers for a short while (will eventually dissipate so don't be afraid to use an after shave if you wish) and, if discovered by your wife/girlfriend/significant other, will likely keep them hanging around angling for another sniff.  Love it.

Made in USA.  No parabens.  No sulfates.
summary: Wow!  Nothing else like it.  Love it.

reviewText: This gel provides a goodly portion of foam once it is rubbed on the face, and it contributes to a nice, close and comfortable shave.  I have a hard time believing that shaving gel can provide much hydration or enrichment to skin when it is on the face for so brief a time.  This gel seems to have beneficial ingredients but most importantly it provides a nice shave with a razor. I am not convinced that the benefits of this gel are worth the price difference between it and cheaper brands that I normally use.

Shaving cream lathered up beautifully, I cant put my finger on the smell, but what comes to mind is a tangy peppery smell, not for the younger crowd. I'm not to crazy about the smell, but the product does work well.
summary: I'm not to crazy about the smell, but the product does work well.

reviewText: What's not to love.  Gives a nice lather and has a minty feeling.  A couple of gobs  spread well and is enough for one shaving session.  Nice smelling as well.  It won't leave your skin feel dry.

This rich shaving gel provides a luxurious lather that ensures a nice close shave. It smells lightly of lemon grass and leaves skin smooth and hydrated. It seems to minimize irritation and contains small capsules of Vitamin E. Cruelty free, it is formulated without gluten, sulfates, paraben, mineral oil or petrolatum. Made in the USA,it makes shaving a pleasure.
Works well. Nice smooth and close shave with all my razors. Smells nice too. Good lather.
The best shave cream on the market. I have thrown out every other can I have. Great lather, great scent, great shave. I can't recommend this enough.

I tend to prefer The Taylor of Old Bond Street soaps, but the V76 by Vaughan is a great for those using a safety razor.  It's clean and refreshing, lubricates sufficiently and makes for a great shave.  I recommend this this shaving gel.
Lathers up really nicely, and has a very neutral scent. I don't have that much facial hair to shave off, but it's still nice to get this lather going and to have a very smooth shave. Much appreciate.
summary: Lathers up really nicely, and has a very neutral scent.

reviewText:
While the instructions state to use gel in the shower or right after showering, I had to test it out when the hair is dry and coarse (not after it softens up).

The gel is easy to apply, no rocket science.  My husband used a shaving machine mustache trimmer and had no problem removing the gel.  After he was done, he stated the hair was softer and easier to remove.  His face felt hydrated and there was no irritation whatsoever.  Other shaving gels usually leave a sticky feeling on his face, but not this one.

The scent is pleasant if you just sniff it but it can get overwhelming when you actually leave it on for a few minutes (which you must), not sure how to describe the scent and this might bother some people only.
summary: Softened hair and left face feeling hydrated

reviewText: Ugh.  I was excited to try this product only to discover that it was loaded with tiny blue plastic "micro-beads" which are wrecking the environment!  The smell is inoffensive, mildly reminiscent of lemon-lime, and it definitely left my skin feeling clean and soft...but the environmental cost of using microbeads is simply not worth it.
summary: Clean and soft...but at what cost

reviewText:
I am not sure what all the hype is about this shaving gel.  My husband used it and although he likes the masculine scent and the close shave that he was able to get while applied, he feels it is like other types.  Not truly understanding what he meant I used it to shave my legs.  I shaved in the bathtub the way that I normally do and almost broke my neck.  The reason is because the shaving gel is clear and I didn't see when it misfired past my hand on the tub side.  Human error but scary nonetheless!

To the shave gels credit it lathers so abundantly for such a small amount.  Be careful when dispensing because it flows out so freely and at this price point it really is such a shame to lose any amount.

I wouldn't recommend this purchase because it is just too expensive and feels just like a normal shaving gel.  It was a miss for this household.

It's a good quality product, but, for the price, I wouldn't rush to buy it. It's like Edge, but it creates a thicker, "creamier" foam. I didn't detect much of a fragrance. It protected well enough. Left my face soft and smooth. This is very good for what it is, but I would find it hard to justify the price. The can is the same diameter as a can of Edge, but about 1" taller. However, it contains 5.6 ounces versus 7 ounces for Edge. Don't know why they made the can bigger.
summary: A good gel shaving cream, but pricey

reviewText: Most luxurious shave cream I have used.  Just a dime size dollup gave me a face full of very rich lather.  The smell was very masculine but not overpowering.  The finished effect on my skin was soothing.  I don't like a face full of lather for a shave - just a nice comforting barrier and V76 does that well.

Terrific shave gel, not just for men, but for women also. I used it in a sensitive area and I liked the consistency, the gel to lather, and the smell--somewhat lemony to me--and I had a decent shave minus the red bumps. You really can't ask for much more from a shave cream. No dry skin either.

Not sure what all the hoopla is about this product.  It's a very nice shave gel, but it is nothing special at all.
Ingredients:
Aqua/Water/Eau, Palmitic Acid, Triethanolamine, Isopentane, Aloe Barbadensis (Aloe Vera) Leaf Juice, Myristic Acid, Stearic Acid, Propylene Glycol Isostearate, PEG-7 Glyceryl Cocoate, Sorbitol, Isobutane, Hydroxyethylcellulose, Disodium EDTA, Hydroxypropylcellulose, Polyquaternium-7, Agar, Cellulose Gum, Sodium Hyaluronate, Tocopheryl Acetate, Phenoxyethanol, Sodium Benzoate, Parfum/Fragrance, Limonene, Linalool, Citral, Ultramarines (CI 77007),

I goes on smooth, shaves nicely, and has a faint, very pleasing scent.

But at $19 for 5.6 ounces.....it's not worth it.
Great clean smell!  Doesn't burn my skin like major brands. I have that 3 o'clock shadow and it makes shaving a lot easier

Barely-scented with a quite pleasant masculine scent, which feels a bit "classic". This gel seems to be less viscous than my favorite Nivea Men, but this is not a problem. I use a good quality shaving brush instead of fingers -- a soft brush will not work well as it would with a less dense soap leather.

The gel is made in the USA. It has a long list of chemically-sounded ingredients: Palmetic Acid, Triethanolamine, Isopentane, Myristic Acid, and so on. It's price is 5 times higher than the Nivea's at Target, so while I enjoy using it, I do not feel that it is 5 times better. At least, to me.

I can't say it's substantially different in performance to the other, cheaper foaming gels one can buy at any given store, but this shaving gel has a really nice clean scent. It's fresh and crisp like a subtle cologne. So it gets points for that. Otherwise it shaves nice enough but you're getting a similar gel to what you can buy from target for like three bucks a can.
Best beard oil on the market right now, and reasonably priced.

I've only tried a few different beard oils.  This one worked pretty well, went in fairly smooth, and helped a bit with the itchiness.  The smell is nice, but not something I prefer (although I don't hate it).  It did cut down on itchiness/scratchiness a bit, but not sure worth getting my hands all oily getting it in.
summary: This one worked pretty well, went in fairly smooth

reviewText:
great stuff. It softens up bristly whiskers nicely. Especially useful if you do decide to shave them all off - apply this, massage in, the shaving process is a lot easier.
Made less noticable difference for trimming, but the hair was nicer, so that was good.

If you have coarse facial hair, this is a great thing to use.

Generally, I only sport a beard for a month or so each year when I withdraw from society and allow my laziness to reign supreme. The Vaughn Beard oil proved to be as effective in reduction of itchiness during the early growth period as a couple of other products I have tried and is rapidly absorbed without any significant oily residue. With the fast absorption and absence of residue, staining of shirt collars is not much of a concern. Not much of the product is required to achieve full coverage, especially with closer cropped cuts.

The concentrated solution  It is easier to apply than beard balms or salves I've used and seems equally as beneficial in softening gray hairs reducing the brillo pad effect and providing a light sheen as well.  I'm not all that enthusiastic about the somewhat woodsy scent and would prefer an unscented product but the aroma is not so overpowering that I am reluctant to use it regularly during my beard phases.
summary: Yeah, but I still have to groom it.

reviewText: When my husband first started growing a beard, it became a great gift idea to get him all kinds of beard accessories. He has tried a few different oils, and has found some that he likes more than others. In general, though, beard oil seems better suited to longer beards. He keeps his trimmed to be three-quarters of an inch, and this one really acts more like a face moisturizer than a true beard oil with this short length. It is great for skin hydration with a natural smell that isn't overpowering, but would be more effective on a longer beard.

This beard oil works well. It makes a pretty dramatic difference in beard texture, similar to the change when you put hair conditioner on dry hair. It makes the hair feel silkier and the beard shape becomes less "unruly". The smell is not unpleasant, but not what I expected. It smells a bit like wood and pine with an undertone of wet earth (that's the part I wasn't wild about). But not strong, and for me, not a big deal. Nice product worth checking out if your beard needs some grooming care.

This beard oil really does soften a beard.  After a few days use it made a huge difference in my beards softness.  What I don't like about I is the scent.  It is pleasant but I don't like fragrance in my hair care or skin care products, and it is a very heavy fragrance.
summary: Great if you like the scent

reviewText:
Getting Accustomed To Fragrance/Scent

The non-greasy softness and protection provided to the special guy's No-Shave November beard and face is very much appreciated. The fragrance? Not so much; I've been informed I'll have plenty of time to get used to it since the beard will remain for the Colorado Cold Season. He likes the way his face and beard feels, so do I. Grizzly Adams will be less grizzly to the eye and hopefully to my nostrils this season.

This is a small, green plastic pump spray bottle containing 2 ounces of beard oil. The product is scented extremely lightly - barely perceptible really with light slight floral and vegetal notes. The oil itself, a mix of plant, fruit and seed oils, is clear in appearance and just slightly viscous. The product spreads easily onto the skin and the strands and leaves behind a nice finish that holds up for a couple of hours or all day depending on how many pumps you've worked into the desired area. The product caused no irritation or breakouts for me and I continue to apply it 3-4 times per week to great effect.
summary: Lightly scented and nice healthy finish

reviewText:
I am not a fan of facial hair, in part because it feels and looks so wiry. So I was very excited to get this product for my husband to try. I immediately noticed a softer feel and shinier, smoother appearance.

I deducted a star because my husband is not a huge fan of the scent. It would be ideal if this was odorless - if the guy wants a scent he can use cologne - this product doesn't need to try to do both.

In sum, I highly recommend this product if you are tired of the wiry look and feel of a beard!!
summary: Soften up that wiry, prickly facial hair!

reviewText: This is a lightly scented oil which keeps the beard soft and conditions facial hair and skin. My Godson has tried several different brands but this definitely his favorite. It's easily absorbed, hydrating, and relieves dryness, Does not leave an oily or greasy residue. Kind of has a woodsy scent to it; very light. Product contains safflower oil and saw palmetto.
summary: Softens and Conditions Beard and Skin

reviewText:
V76 will give you a beautiful glossy beard. My husband's 1/2" beard needs less than one pump of the product to look great. The first time he used it, he rubbed in three pumps of it and walked around reeking, repelling both our cats and me. But one pump - he only repels the cat who lives to groom his beard. The aroma is cedary and pleasantly mild and after an hour hardly noticeable no matter how hard I sniffed him.

The Amazon page lists saw palmetto as an active ingredient and that intrigued us since my husband takes the supplement religiously. While we doubted (and doubt) there's any correlation between men's urinary health and its presence in beard oil, we did finally figure out that it really is an ingredient in the beard oil. It's serenoa serrulata. What does it do in cometic products? Turns out it's a good anti-irritant, helps the skin maintain water balance, and works as a natural anti-inflammatory.  I think they ought to list its common name and explain what it's for. I'm more impressed by the product for having researched it.

All in all, my guy likes this a lot, though he says he still prefers using a tiny dab of his Old Spice Spiffy hair cream, mainly because the cat who loves to groom him prefers it.

Meh... not for me.
A) the smell IS ok but kinda piney in a way to me..
B) i spray some on my hands and go to wipe it in and my hands absorbed most of it lol... so i had to use alot more.
C) per friends, the ph of my skin is NOT a good mix with something in here. i know for sure that "baby lotion" (that johnson n johnsons in a pink bottle for instance) doesnt mesh well... it turns my skin smelling to pukey fish. no joke! Colognes and lotions i can use, but i haven't the foggiest what type of ingredient(s) don't work with the ph of my skin. but, fishy moldy musky pukey smell isn't for me n the ladies..
summary: the ph of my skin is NOT a good mix with something in here

reviewText: V76 beard oil by Vaughn is good oil. It has a very light scent. It is a spray on and that is why I rated it 4 instead of 5 stars. It will drip very easily if you are not careful. That being said it does condition skin and dry rough beard hair well. It was used after a thorough beard wash, which makes your beard hold onto beard oil really well and soften it.
This texture paste is incredible. Light weight. Great texture. Non greasy. Switched over from the brand I was using for years. Highly recommend.

This stuff is magic. This paste solved all my hair problems. It helps style hair while giving an extra bit of boost. It won't cover a bald spot but it will keep thinning hair from falling flat. It keeps my hair tidy. It says "mattifying" but I haven't noticed that. I think you would have to use a lot. But then you would be using this wrong. This isn't a gel or mouse.

To get the great results, you have to activate the fiber. Put a dab on your index finger and tap it with your thumb until fine strands appear. Then kind of scrunch those fibers into your hair. Define what ever pieces you want. This works as well as salon stuff and was much cheaper.

I ordered this hair paste for my 6 year old who has a very short cut with just a bit at the front that he likes to flip up so that is almost standing straight. This is definitely a paste in that it is thick and sticky. It combs through well and keeps his hair mostly in place. But he's a sweaty littlet boy, and this product doesn't quite a have an all day hold. It is as good as, if not better than, any of the other hair products we've tried though.

The scent I'd this paste is definitelymasculine, and it goes on string.  But the scent dissipates after a while. It dirsnt completely go away, but it is pleasant and not overbearing.

While it doesn't hold his hair up in the front, it does keep the back and sides neat a nd helps to make his cowlick manageable.

reviewerName: Gina Pera, Adult ADHD Expert and Author
reviewText:
Initially, I wasn't sure what to do with this paste. I already have one that I like that is completely different; it's more expensive than Elmer's Glue, but it looks, smells, and feels just like it. Doesn't quite dry like it, though, thank goodness.

My hair is fine but there's lots of it. The weight tends to flatten, so I need firmer products to add volume and "piecy-ness".

This paste is not so sticky. It evaporates quickly.

Then,I tried it one morning on my "bed head." Cowlicks galore. Nothing falling as it should.

A little spritz of water and brushing, plus judicious application of this paste, and everything falls into place.

I like the scent, but I find it doesn't linger.
summary: not a firm hold but a shaping hold for flyaway hair

reviewText:
First let's talk functionality--
This texture paste works well, but my husband had to use a lot of it. I've tried it a few times for some mild taming, and I like the way it works. It tames my fly-aways and provides gentle texture.

Next, let's talk smell--
Unfortunately, the scent is so strong in this that I could smell my husband almost a mile away! It was definitely too strong for me when I was close to him.

The scent is not unpleasant, just overpowering.

When I used a just a tiny amount on my hair, the scent was much more muted.

There are no sulfates or parabens in this product, which is something I look for.

At a $21 price point, I don't love it enough to purchase more, but we will continue using this till it's gone.

I am a woman with waist length very fine hair. In trying to combat the inevitable flatness at the crown, I had a hair stylist recommend trying paste and pomade. These types of products give me lift at the crown that no spray or gel can match.

This works as well as any I have tried. The fragrance is quite strong and lingers. To my nose it seems like a cross between caramel and sweet tobacco. It's not offensive but it will be what you smell like that day. The paste container is plastic which is a plus for some and a minus for others. I prefer glass containers but I don't travel in a way that would be a problem. If you are scent sensitive, smell this before you buy if possible.
summary: Works well on very fine hair. Strong scent.
