It's not the kind of bold fragrance suitable for clubbing, but that's by design -- it shines as an office scent. It's primarily made for you and for those whom you pull close. Overall, I'm giving Amen four out of five stars.

P.S. philosophy dresses its packaging with copy blocks written to sound contemplative and/or food-for-thoughtish. Below is the copy on Amen's box. I'm not certain how this copy connects to the scent, but I'm including it here in case it speaks to you:

philosophy: the difference between a hero and a superstar is that a hero doesn't need a crowd. many of us have lost sight of who our true heroes really are. they are the "a" men and women who defend our country, do menial chores and act as good neighbors. whether they sweep streets or lead a nation, they walk the talk. we don't need another superstar. we do need to salute our true heroes. amen.

philosophy for men Amen Men's Spray Cologne

This cologne has a citrus base but also has stronger notes that I find difficult to identify. I'm not totally enamored with the scent. I find it strong and not to my liking. I did get compliments, when I asked, so maybe it's me. It's interesting to try and review a scent that I can't share with you. As for the packaging and bottle they are pleasant and simple.  Maybe you will like it if you like citrus based scents. I've used other citrusy colognes and liked them. This one, not so much.
summary: Citrus based cologne with other strong notes.

reviewText:
Nice citrus smell, which is not too strong and pungent, this is ideal for regular business use. Something which will not make you stand out due to the perfume. The odor stays throughout the day, at least till mid afternoon. The 2 oz bottle size is travel friendly as well.
Deducted the stars rom rating primarily due to price. In the mid-40s price range I'll expect a 4 oz bottle for this quality perfume, unless this brand is an elite one.

This cologne has a very light scent that is not overpowering or cloying.  It is more of a fresh and clean scent to wear during the day.  The smell lingers so you don't have to reapply or use very much.  RECOMMENDED.

Here in Florida it's already pretty warm during the day - I mention the temperature because this fragrance seems even more poignant in the heat. In fact, it seems to get stronger the longer it is worn. Normally I wouldn't mind except this starts off strong and gains ground throughout the day. The result is a no so flattering bit of chemical cloud that permeates the room. Nice bottle, ample size but a bit obtuse. More like the stuff you would wear as a teenager - can't take this seriously.
summary: Sorry but not a serious fragrance for men

reviewText:
This was an impulse purchase.
I had been thinking about how i missed Loves Lemon fresh from the 70s, as i have a rough time with synthetic fragrances, and Loves didn't trigger respiratory issues and smelled so happy.
About an hour later this Mens cologne appeared in my vine queue. In reading that it was citrusy I decided to give it a try. I haven't found a mens cologne i could handle my husband wearing and hoped this would do the trick.
I sprayed a spritz outside to see if it was going to be overpowering or trigger any negative response.
Passed that test, so spritzed once in house and turned on ceiling fan to disperse.
Still good.
Spritzed husband when he got home. Really liked the citrus top note. Smelled of lime to me. The base notes are subtle at first and have a nice depth and complexity that compliment the citrus.
After about an hour went back and had nice lingering hug with husband, and citrus pretty much gone and remaining scent quite different and surprisingly more intense from the starting point. More musky, soapy, linen like. Not bad, but not what i hoped for.
This makes a nice home fragrance spray for tose who don't like overly floral, heavy scents. Doesnt take much!
summary: Nice, not overly aggressive scent, the citrus notes fade too quickly for me

reviewText: Scent is strongly related to memory, and "Amen" evokes no memory so strongly as pulling on a warm t-shirt straight from the dryer. I asked several people for an opinion, and everyone hemmed and hawed the way people do when asked about scents. So I suggested "laundry?", and to a man their response was "Yes!, that's it!". So, if that's the effect you want, go for it. Full disclosure: I've been ruined by my long-term love affair with Chanel's Platinum Egoiste. No competition.

The packaging is good. The spray and the bottle is well made. The spray works well. I think this is fine as long as you don't mind the overwhelming citrus floral smell. It does linger for several hours after applying but at times it does loose it's original smell. Having said, is this bad smell? - No. But is it a good cologne? - Probably not as the smell especially after few hours of applying is not as favorable as the initial burst of sweet citrus. The asking price also weighs in and makes this a rather expensive cologne spray to own.

Overall I rating this with 3 stars generously.

I'm a long time fan of Amazing Grace scent by Philosophy. I thought the men's Amen fragrance sounded promising. The scent starts off with a pleasant citrus scent. Unfortunately, the scent than takes a bad turn. It's hard to explain, but the citrus fades to a cleaning fluid smell. Yuk. Three of us all came to the same conclusion.

I love bulgari. It is a wonderful clean scent with just the right hint of manly spicy end notes. This starts off with the same citrus notes with a little heavier lime but as it transitions to the floral bouquets and spicy undertones it loses some of the depth and staying power. It quickly devolves into just hints of sweet citrus. 4 outa 4 people could not tell difference between it and Bv for first few minutes. After an hour 4 out of 4 could and preferred bulgari.  As a scent alone I'd give it  3.5 stars. For this price and this staying power and for being a total bulgari knock off id give it 0 if I could.

I LOVE THIS.  and I never feel that way about concealer.  I pretty much toss every concealer I try.  After about 50 clicks to finally get some product out, I swiped, brushed, blended all around my dark circles from the inner corner to outer corner - what a difference, even the hubs noticed.  It's smooth and creamy and reflects a lot of light.
summary: Best Under Eye Concealer I have EVER tried. Swear.

reviewText:
This is an ok concealer in a pen which delivers a drop of the concealer onto a brush.  I found this creamy and moisturizing but it has a way of highlighting the undereye area rather than being more matte.  There is a very dewy finish that never did quite dry down and become invisible.  I found that trying to spread this out to make it less obvious only caused the concealer qualities to become thinner so nothing was really concealed.

This is ok if you only have the tiniest bit of darkness you need to conceal but if you have some major issues with dark undereye shadows you will need something more opaque than this.

This (mostly) convenient under-eye concealer has a soft brush tip into which the concealer is fed for smooth application.  You twist the end until a little concealer is extracted inside the brush, apply with soft strokes, and pat with fingertips to blend.  I have fair skin -- my porcelain/ivory skin has aged to plain fair -- and the #2 concealer is the perfect color to blend into the foundation I use on my face.  Because I wear sunglasses whenever I'm outside, I have extremely fair skin under my eyes with darker areas at the base of my eye socket.  This concealer covers both the light and the dark areas, giving a more uniform look.  The silica in the product does a great job at making the skin under my eyes look younger by (supposedly) diffusing the light.

The concealer does not wash off with plain water, which means that it will last throughout the day, even with light perspiration.  I'm not wild about the way the concealer is dispensed into the brush.  One twist of the knob doesn't seem to do it, and I often have to twist, twist, twist, testing between each, without getting any.  And then, squish, out it comes.  I wish the application were more controlled AND easier to dispense.

I have one huge disappointment with this product that won't affect 99% of users so I did not deduct a star for it.  The ingredients aren't listed as yet on the product page.  Stupidly, I used it without reading the fine print list on the box, and I wondered why my eyes were watering so badly.  I looked:  it contains seven different silicones.  Because I'm sensitive to silicone, I had to stop using it despite the great results.  It also contains polymers.

For most women, this Japonesque concealer will be a wonderful addition to their cosmetics; however, those with certain sensitivities should take note.

-- Debbie Lee Wesselmann
summary: Silicone-Heavy Formulation Works Well to Enliven Under the Eye

reviewText:
To be honest I don't wear a lot of makeup on a day-to-day basis and even on those special occasions it's still not very much. My daily routine consist of a good moisturizer with SPF, a little concealer under my eyes and possibly some eyeliner, but usually just a little mascara. Obviously since I am using concealer under my eyes, the darkness that I sometimes get bothers me so that's why I was happy to try out the Japonesque Pixelated Color Eyelighter.

Instructions are pretty simple: twist until some of the cream comes up into the brush, lightly apply it underneath the eye, and then dab with your fingertip to blend. I took two photos; the first one on the left shows me with the cream only applied to my left under eye with the right eye untreated and the photo on the right shows both under eyes after using the Eyelighter.  For me I saw a noticeable difference in the way my under eye and especially the inside area looked, the darkness was not as prominent and it looked brighter. The color also matched my skin tone well.

Overall this product was extremely easy to apply, gave me results that I was happy with and if I can get approximately 30 days use of it I will feel the price is worth it.

I like how the concealer is put into the brush by turning the bottom of the pen. Unfortunately, the only gripe I have is the amount of turns required for a decent amount. I have to start with two clicks, then increase as I try to apply with what is on the brush. The first use, I overdid it and had way too much, second try, was progressive. The brush is soft and just the right size for under the eye. I am light skinned as it is, so it was lighter than my shade which I consider natural light.
summary: I like how the concealer is put into the brush by ...

reviewText: I like most Japonesque products and this is no different. The color is as expected  and the product of high quality. The only reason I did not give 5 stars is because the applicator can get clogged a little easier than I prefer but other than that it is really a good product.

This is a review for JAPONESQUE Pixelated Color Eyelighter, Shade 02. The product application color was just as expected. It was very easy to apply, all you have to do is twist the end of the almost permanent marker size looking pen-type applicator and after few clicks you will find the color coming out of the brush. Use the pen lightly & apply it underneath the eye where the black circles generally appear, and then dab with your fingertip to blend the color into those areas you need to conceal. It does work okay in concealing the areas which makes your face look dull. Overall okay product rating with 3 stars!

Highlighters and concealers are often used in the same manner to describe a cosmetic product. I have used  concealer for years. I apply it after using foundation to provide some highlighting down the bridge of my nose, in the corner of my eyes and under my eyes. It works well for me. I was delighted to try this new Japonesque Eyelighter.

There seem to be three colors and color number two works for me. I have light to fair skin. I turned the dial at the bottom of the stick to open up the  Eyelighter. It took four or five turns to start the process. Then, using the brush, I applied a small amount under my eyes. I tapped the area so that the highlighter was almost transparent. I then applied a small amount to the bridge of my nose and above my lips. The highlighter is creamy and easy to disperse. Throughout the day, the highlighter stayed put, it did not leave a white glare under my eyes, but a gentle illumination. It does exactly what it claims do to. This highlighter is at a good price, and I would recommend it to anyone.

Recommended. prisrob 06-18-16

This Japonesque Pixelated Color Eyelighter is so easy to use! The makeup is soft and glides on effortlessly, allowing you to apply it without stretching out the delicate under-eye skin. It provides even coverage and made my eyes look better than they have in years. This didn't cause any irritation to my sensitive skin. Simply wonderful.

This product works really well to cover my dark circles under my eyes.  The darkness that I have isn't dramatic, and I usually use foundation to cover them.  This product works well for me.  It is easy to apply and it lasts all day.  So far, I like it!
summary: Works well for my dark circles.

reviewText: Just a typical concealer. Nothing special.
summary: Just a typical concealer. Nothing special.

reviewText:
Pros: Shade #2 should work with most fair to light skin tones. Creamy texture spreads evenly and blends well over foundation. Nice translucent glow.
Cons: Will highlight bags, so be careful over uneven or puffy areas. Not an opaque concealer.

An eyelighter is intended to brighten the under eye area. It is generally worn over foundation and even concealer if necessary.

This product does a good job of highlighting. It is creamy, applies evenly, blends well, and dries fairly quickly. It contains a moderate amount of pigment and is more translucent than opaque. Once applied and blended into the rest of the makeup with a dry or damp sponge, it gives an attractive brightness or glow to the under eye area, the bridge of the nose, the cheekbones, or any other area it is applied.

A similar product is Touche clat - Radiant Touch by Yves Saint Laurent. A cult favorite around for years, it comes in 10 shades, and is far more expensive than this highlighting pen by Japonesque. The texture of Touche clat is more refined, more delicate and it is more pigmented. And there are more shades to choose from. If you are new to this type of product, Japonesque is a good place to start.

There is a fascinating but somewhat mysterious video attached to this product page. In the video, a pretty young woman demonstrates how to apply a full Kardashian Kabuki face of makeup. Although she applies a seeming truckload of a variety of brands of products to her face, she never applies this Pixelated Color Eyelighter. If she does, Ive missed it. She does mention two makeup brushes by Japonesque, but that seems to be it. Ive watched the video twice, mesmerized both times as she rattles off the products shes using.

I don't usually use eyelighter/concealer. It's powder, mascara and lipstick. Lately, though, I've noticed dark circles under my eyes as well as very fine crow's feet. I'm 48 years old with rosacea and some sun damage who lives in a hot and humid metro county. pPowder has usually been enough. I tried this and to my surprise, I liked it. I usually wear Shiseido Shiseido Sheer Matifying Cmpct Refill Natural - Light Ivory or a Mary Kay one (right now I use Mary Kay Beige 1 powder) as a frame of reference for my color. This shaded blended well and didn't settle in the fine lines around my outer eyes. It's not a miracle product to hide my dark circles completely. But using this in conjunction with the powder and it did a pretty darn good job. I hiked up a mountain today and to my utter, sweaty surprise, my makeup held. Granted I used powder, this eyelighter and mascara but at no time did it sweat off. I just washed my face and everything came off. Amazing.

This works for minor under eye coverage. Those looking for intense coverage will probably want to try for a different product, but minor areas that need a little touch up will be fine with this.

It's easy to apply. You'll definitely notice some results. I've been pleased with the results. I'm not sure if it's a repeat buy just yet, but it's not terrible

This product is lovely. It smells great and works well. Just a little on my towel dried  hair gives fantastic waves that stay for hours. Didn't have to do anything else to my hair. Apply and let dry. It really was that easy. Love this!

I have thick naturally wavy hair that I do not wash every day. I love the sea salt look and have tried many brands over the last ten years. This is my favorite, the smell is great and it always leaves my hair with the best natural looking waves. My go to! Highly recommended~

I have straight fine hair and was excited to try this product. The product is a lotion and the bottle top has a long straw attached to it. You unscrew the top and pull it off and there is product on the straw. I found this way of dispensing the product to be odd. The product itself smells nice, and a little goes a long way. Unfortunately, it did not give my hair beach waves. When I tried air drying my hair was frizzy and when I used the product with a hair dryer it dried out my ends. I also didn't like the residue it left on my hair after drying. Perhaps this product would work better for someone with thicker hair. I used the produce on several occasions and I cannot recommend it for those who have fine hair.

I love that messy-beachy wave look, but my hair is naturally straight.  If I let my hair air dry theres just the tiniest hint of a wave; if I want to have any kind of semi-curl Ive got to use a curling iron.

After shampooing my hair I towel it dry and just run my fingers thru it (no combing).  I rub about a dime-sized amount of this texture lotion between my palms and rub it into my hair while twirling sections around my fingers.  After my hair air dries completely I just use a small amount of the product to scrunch the hair and loosen the waves a bit.  Im surprised at the amount of wave I can get out of my straight hair!

This texture lotion isn't sticky and it doesnt leave my hair feeling stiff or crunchy unless I apply too much.  It does take some experimenting to find the right amount and technique that will work for your hair type, but the product is easy to work with.  My one complaint is the fragrance  to me this smells just like a strong mens cologne, and I really don't care for it.  Once the hair is dry the scent dissipates, so its not a deal breaker.
summary: Brings out the wave in my (mostly) straight hair

reviewText:
Pros:
Adds some nice texture and definition to wavy hair
You don't have to use a lot
The bottle has a handy pump top, which distributes the perfect mount of product

Cons:
The price
Contains silicones (but not dimethicone - these ones can probably be removed with conditioner washing)
I hate the smell
The lid/pump top is a slightly different shade then the bottle, which makes it look cheap

Lately, I've been looking for new ways to deal with my hair. I have only recently realized that my hair is wavy (not simply frizzy and unmanageable), and the result of that realization was an overhaul of my hair routine. I looked into the curly girl method, and switched to sulfate-free, silicone-free hair products. I tried out using a diffuse, conditioner washing, plopping, hair gels, mousses, etc., in an attempt to maximize my wave and minimize frizzy craziness. Basically, I'm still experimenting to figure out what works for my hair.

When I saw this product, I liked the looks of it. "Get salt-spray waves, sans dryness"? Sounds like my kind of thing! One of the biggest philosophies of the curly girl method is keeping hair moisturized, and so far the cg method hasn't let me down. I ordered it, and expectantly waited for my new hair treat to arrive in the mail. I'm not exactly sure what I was expecting it to do, but I had a vague visions of effortless waves, no frizz, and light wafts of a lovely citrus scent while gentle breezes stirred my glowing locks. Maybe my imagination was a little over the top, but the mind works in mysterious ways.

When the little bottle arrived, I went to test it out. The box was nice enough, but the bottle initially confused me. I unscrewed the lid, and thought that the wand thing inside was weird and, frankly, a total pain. It just didn't make sense to apply the product with a wand! Now, I know for a fact that other reviewers have done this, too, so please don't judge me. By the second time I used it, I figured out that if you pull the cap off instead of unscrewing it, you'll discover a nice pump top.

Now comes the reason why I never intend to get this again: the smell! When I opened the bottle for the first time, I was immediately greeted by the strong, slightly musky, and headache-inducing type of scent that I hate. To be fair, I'm a bit sensitive to fragrances. I hate most perfumes, and anything with any musk in it gives me a headache. I don't mind essential oil scents, but scents like this... ugh. Even though I know I'm sensitive to fragrance, how can anyone describe this scent as "light"? While it was in my hair, my dad could smell it from across the room!

As for the product itself, it does give me some pretty, fluffy definition in my wavy (2a) hair, but nothing that I can't achieve with the right combo of gel, mousse, and a diffuser. But I can't get over the smell and the price. For me, it's definitely not worth it.
summary: Works but can't stand the smell ...

reviewText:
My hair is naturally curly and fine, so no matter how hard I try, I can't get beach waves. BUT! Oribe's Matte Waves Lotion does an amazing job of controlling my curls, which have a tendency to fly away in humidity, and it's amazing for keeping braids smooth and in place. It also holds very nicely when I take a braid out, leaving my hair with tight waves instead of my natural curls.

And on top of that, this product smells amazing.

It's pricy, but I highly recommend it for keeping curly hair under control.

I use a very small amount of this lotion and apply on my hair evenly after the shower. This helps to hold hair without grease. I comb in such a way it will keep hair lifted to give a more volume and it does not harden. This is a good product and it is recommended.
summary: Works as a light hold texture Lotion

reviewText: Adding a touch of this to your hair gives it the texture to make amazing beach waves. Just using a tiny bit keeps hair soft and wavy. The more you use the harder and more defined the waves get. So with this texture lotion, less is more. Which is good because Oribe texture lotion isn't cheap. The matte formula looks great, so you don't end up with a shiny finish on your hair. You get the look of beach waves without it looking like you have product in your hair. Works great!
summary: Beach waves without looking like you have product in your hair.

reviewText: I LOVE this stuff!  Thanks to a reviewer, I watched the U Tube video before I used the product.  The first time I used it, I twisted my hair and pinned it up and let it air dry, I have to say it came out really adorable.  Light, non frizzy curls.  The second time I used it, I dried my bangs and applied about a dimes worth to both sides of my hair, scrunched it and let it air dry.  Again, super nice waves, although I liked the curl better when I twisted it.  In the U tube video's it shows the models curling their hair with a curling iron.  This is not needed unless you have really straight and fine hair.  I have used many products, such as this, and all of them made my hair feel 'crunchy' to the touch.  The curls/waves you get with the texture lotion are very, very soft.  A few people mentioned the price but I think it's reasonable as I only wash my hair twice a week and used such a small amount of it.  The smell is wonderful and both times I used it my waves stayed nice, soft and non frizzy for 2 straight days. I really love it and will definitely continue to use it.
summary: Nicest texture lotion I have tried.  Soft waves.

reviewText:
I like this product, though I am still trying to decide if I like it enough to pay this price point.  It really IS a small bottle, after all.  Quite small, especially for the price.

However, you really need very little of this, and this does encourage curl without creating frizz.  It's a similar look to when I air dry my hair with only argan oil, only the waves hold an extra day.  This doesn't really add any volume at all, but unlike some products on wavy hair, it doesn't fight against the volume, so I appreciate that.

One caveat would be that I find this (like most products on wavy hair) works more magic when applied to very, very damp hair, not towel dried hair (as per the instructions).
summary: A lot of power, and a very little bottle.

reviewText: The Oribe did a good job. It gave me texture on top. A little goes a long way, too much and instead of lovely beach blown it's greasy flat dirty, so use just a tiny bit. Otherwise I like the way it lifted my hair and gave it texture without a super stuff spiky hold. The scent is really nice, I tend not to like over scented products but this was fine.
summary: Nice, not sticky or too stiff

reviewText: Love this, leaves hair slightly stiff - but maybe I am using too much.  The texture is great, love the way it looks.  The bottle seems so small, so I am convinced I must be using too much or there will not be very many applications.

Review of: "ORIBE Matte Waves Texture Lotion, 3.4 oz.," by Oribe.

This is a very interesting beauty product.  My wife truly enjoys it.  The manufacturer's specifications list: "Get salt-spray waves, sans dryness. This medium-hold lotion coaxes matte-textured pieciness out of even the finest hair, adding grip to styles and a beachy allure.  How to Use:
Glide into damp hair, defining waves and natural texture as you go. Apply bronzer while you air-dry.  Benefits: - Light lotion formula encourages 'salt-spray' waves and texture. - Ideal for creating starchy matte texture and adding grip for styling (e.g. braids).  - Distributes easily throughout the hair.  - Oribe Signature Complex (Watermelon, Lychee and Edelweiss Flower Extracts) defends hair from oxidative stress, photoaging and the deterioration of natural keratin all while protecting from the drying, damaging and color-depleting effects of the elements.  - Wave Resin Complex provides texture, style retention and hold while controlling frizz.  - Yacon, a tropical plant native to Peru, delivers nourishment to the hair.
- Brazilian Nut Extract, high in fatty acids and Vitamin E, protects the hair from damage and the elements. - Tara Plant heals damaged hair by moisturizing and thickening strands.  - Color and keratin treatment safe. UV protection for hair. Vegan, cruelty-free and gluten-free."

My wife's hair is thick and long with lots of natural curls.  She states that this product is like a great conditioner and helps to manage her hair.  The product has a slight citrus scent and has the color and consistency of a light colored thick conditioner.  It is applied to the hair with the bottle length applicator attached to the cap.  The hair is left with a little sea salt texture or "crunchiness" and the bronzer helps to lighten the waves.  Wife is very pleased.  Well done.  Five stars.
summary: A Wonderful Product to Control Hair and Condition It

reviewText:
I have waist length very fine hair, straight with no wave or curl. My hair takes no curl, regardless of how much energy I put into it. I was skeptical of this but am willing to try almost anything for a bit of texture. I do not use a hair dryer so I applied this to damp hair and let air dry.

While I did not get a head full of waves, I did get some sweet texture and volume. Plus this lotion smells fantastic in my hair. I've played around with it and like the results. I've had zero luck with similar products so I am quite pleased with the outcome with this.
summary: Worked better than I thought on my super fine long hair.

reviewText: I live in Florida and have slightly curly hair so the humidity is a total pain when it comes to managing my hair when I wear it down. I have to say that I love this product.  It's light weight (I have thin hair so that is good) and it doesn't leave a residue on your hair. A lot of the matte texture products that help hold soft waves (like salt water ones) leave your hair feeling sticky and or hard to manage... THIS did NOT. it's amazing.  It gave me the perfect texture that I wanted without all hard to manage side effects.  I highly recommend it.
summary: I highly recommend it ...especially for people with wavy hair!

reviewText:
Wow! This works! I have straight colored hair that's not thin, but not exactly thick. I also love the beach wave hair look. I followed the video instructions. I took one section of hair and applied a pump of lotion on damp hair, twisted my hair and pinned it up. I mostly let my hair air dry, but shot it with the blow dryer once. The results were soft waves with no stiffness or dryness. The scent is very mild too. I  love how well this lotion works! I don't have to use any curling wands, just the lotion. Highly recommended.
PS: I also tried this on the ends of my hair without twisting my hair. It added texture.

Some things are worth every penny and this product is definitely one of them. My hair rarely EVER does what I want it to do so I'm stuck with a quality shampoo and conditioner along with a thermal spray and a quality flat iron that won't let the Florida frizz through during the day. I have LONGED for that effortless curl look but have been unable to ever achieve it, until now. I highly suggest watching the YouTube videos on how to get the best results. My locks turned out having that effortless messed yet perfect wave and I love it. I'll definitely be ordering more. Plus the scent is wonderful. Everyone's hair is different so not all results will be the same but my hair is thick and has been processed and it works great for me. Highly recommend.
summary: Finally Got the Look I Want

reviewText:
This stuff works really great, but is waaaay too expensive, imho, therefore minus one star.  As of this review a 3.4 oz. bottles costs $42.00.  I'll definitely use up this bottle but will go back to my regular hair gel afterwards.  But, if you can swing it then by all means buy it because I was very surprised to see what it made my hair do. Often times, products that say they will do blah blah blah for your hair frequently don't work like they say they will, but ORIBE did work like it said it would.

I have short hair now (so maybe my expensive bottle will last longer) and it rarely behaves like I want it too - always a battle.  I might not have used this in the correct way, but the results made me happy.  After I got out of the shower and toweled dry my hair (but still wet), I ran a small amount of the ORIBE through my hair and then blew it dry.  It felt stiffer, but I could still run my fingers through it and make it separate into a bunch of smaller sections that really looked nice!  I guess that's what is meant by "pieciness".  It was a very interesting texture that I liked a lot.
summary: ORIBE Matte Waves Texture Lotion 3.4 oz.

reviewText:
This product doesn't seem to do much for me. In the jar, it looks like a white pomade with the consistency of a cold cream and a subtle sweet scent which is pretty nice. I took a small dab and applied it to my dry hair which had been washed the day before. It didn't do much to my hair other than making it look a little less puffy. I meant the results were very minute and my family members didn't even notice anything different. On the plus side, it didn't feel greasy nor tacky. It didn't weigh my hair down or leave any residues neither.

For the price I would have expected a little more. I guess it does somewhat help add a little tameness between washes, although the results are very minute. At any rate, it doesn't seem to do much for me.
summary: Doesn't seem to do much for me

reviewText:
Well, we had two conflicting results with this product that I will note. I think using this product and the ending result depends upon the damage of your hair. I like this product. I think it smells nice and adds a nice finish to my hair or if I use it to refresh my hair it works well in that area too. It adds a bit of tameness and shine as a refresher between washing making it quite convenient for my use. My daughter has bleached her hair and uses a flat iron daily, she is in cosmo school where they do a lot of experimenting-her ends are fried. I suggested she try this to tame her ends which are fairly unhealthy-this finishing cream did pretty much nothing to her hair. It may have just soaked in her porous hair not leaving anything on the outside-I don't know, she also didn't think it smelled very good-so, two very different results.

I have to say, I really liked the packaging on this product with a classy recycled paper box and the bottle of cream is pretty. I like this cream as a finishing touch, or a refresher. My daughter, not so much. I think it does depend on the shape of your hair as to whether this will work. On my daughter's hair, we applied quite a bit of product with no real result and for me, a little bit will work on my hair. If your hair is burnt and frayed, it may not do wonders but if your hair is healthy, this may add some pick me up to your style.

I have fine curly hair that gets flat and stringy with too much conditioner, and tends to get frizzy if I brush it.  On the days I don't wash my hair, I usually dampen my hands and scrunch my hair to redefine my curls.  I tried this Oribe Finish Cream instead of damp hands, to see if it would revive my curls without weighing my hair down or making it stiff.

It smells great and looks like body butter in the container.  I used just a tiny bit rubbed between my hands and applied to my hair.  I couldn't see that it did anything, so I applied just a tiny bit more.  The best I could describe this product is similar to leave-in conditioners.  It made my hair soft and did help a little with reviving the curls, but it really didn't do enough of anything to justify another product in my cabinet.  I alsofind this product to be way overpriced for what it does...or doesn't...do.
summary: Smells great but doesn't seem to do much

reviewText: My husband loves this product so much that I had to buy him one too! IT's such a great sculpting tool and gives good hold on the hair but isn't tacky or sticky.  Such a great product.  Light weight and conditioning as well.
summary: Love this product so much my husband uses it too!

reviewText: It works somewhat well. I do like the smell but don't find myself reaching for it every time yet. After applying to clean dry hair I find it does kind of get rid of that newly washed hair feel. It is a mix between a wax and a cream consistency. I think the concept is to add back some oil to the hair to give it the day old look, feel and manageability which it does kind of do and at the same time giving a nice pleasing fragrance. I have course hair with a slight curl and it just tames some of the fresh wash frizziness which is really not much to begin with. If you have oily hair you might not notice much of a difference. If you have dry hair you may appreciate this product more. I do notice that after a day or 2 later I am really ready to wash it to get it clean as it begins to feel heavy. I think it is a great product for the dry frizzy hair type.
summary: Great for Dry Hair Types, Not Oily.

reviewText: This is stuff is a bit sticky, but works pretty well if you have shorter hair that you want to dynamically style.  So, if you wanted a mohawk or something that is standing up, this stuff is perfect.  If you have thin hair and want some texture, this works well, but not for multiple days, as they suggest.  For my longer, thick hair, it just made it kinda greasy and didn't really work well.

This is a sweet smelling pomade the consistency of cold cream. The fragrance is fine but the product makes my hair dirty looking, even when applying a little bit. It tames down the frizz but with a hair gelled wet and stiff look. I recently tried their ORIBE Body Wash which is absolutely amazing and expected the same of this product but am disappointed. I have short, fine wavy hair that frizzes terribly in the rain. Unfortunately, this is not the product for me.
summary: Sweet smelling pomade the consistency of cold cream that leaves my hair clumpy and dirty looking

reviewText: This product sucks! I'm not sure if I'm not using it right, but it did nothing for my hair! I followed the same technique as in oribe's video, but it left my hair feeling waxy, sticky, and did nothing to tame the frizz/puffiness as it claims it should. For reference, I have long fine wavy dry hair, that tends to frizz up in the bang area after I wash it. Also my bottle came with a giant indentation in the center of it, which means a lot of the product is missing. I'm returning, this was really bad, not worth the money, and I can't even say who it would work for. Maybe short hairstyles only.

A dime sized amount of this along the ends of my hair (about two inches) gives my hair a great dirty, pieced look - even if it was just washed and dried.  It works well but I am giving 3 stars because I have used drugstore brands that deliver the same results.  At $42 I don't see a wow factor above and beyond unless you are simply going for the cleaner ingredients and can't find in a cheaper brand.

A little goes a long way. I take a dime sized amount and rub my hands together to warm it up and loosen the thick cream. Then I smooth it on my dry hair. It helps contain all the frizzes. Good product, nice smell, not oily at all.

I would recommend this for anyone with frizz and/or dry hair. NOT recommended for fine hair.
summary: Use only a TINY amount and rub between hands

reviewText: My hair is long and color treated. It's also wavy/curly and can really frizz up when the humidity kicks in. I applied it to the bottom six inches or so of my hair the most heavily, and only slightly to the rest. I was quite pleased with the results. My hair was only slightly damp, so when it dried I saw the actual results. The comb slid right through my hair. It was soft, but not limp -- it really felt nice. I used a flat iron to achieve my regular style, and my hair had amazing shine. When I ran my hands through my hair, it was not full of static, but looked fresh, with no greasy look. This product is certainly pricey, but just the slightest amount goes a very long way. I can well imagine that it could last me for months! As expensive as it is, I would invest in it again, considering the price-per-application is affordable. I'd recommend ORIBE to anyone looking for a high quality product with excellent results.

My daughter and I *love* this finish cream. She has super-curly, thick, dry hair, so during school days she tames it by putting it in braids. However, the ends frizz up like crazy. As an experiment, we worked this into the ends. It did not look greasy, and it tamed them into one cute curl, which lasted all day. I also use it to tame the frizzies that pop up around my scalp. It's fine to use it on dry (as in, unwashed) hair.

Some of the other reviewers compared this to cold cream, so I was expecting more of a mayonnaise consistency. However, it's more like a wax, and it did take some effort to work it in. The fragrance is lovely, too. I'm taking a star off for the crazy price. However, a little goes a long way, so I'm hoping that that this jar will last us through the summer. LOVE!
summary: A non-greasy way to tame frizzy hair. LOVE!

reviewText: This Oribe Finish Cream is another great smelling Oribe product. It has a light whipped texture. Just a little bit is needed on hair to give it shine. I was disappointed that it didn't work better on my dry hair ends though. My hair is long, I think this might work better on shorter hair for a textured look.

This Oribe Flexible Finish Cream is just okay in doing anything for my hair.  I used a small amount of product and rubbed it in my hands to distribute it more evenly in my hair.  It helps tame my hair and make it a little piecey but I still needed to use my hairspray to get my flyaways to lay down and to also hold my styled hair.  The smell isn't horrible but the package is very old fashioned looking.  It looks like a container that you would have found a cold cream in in the 60s.  I don't hate this product but for what it does there are other, better products out there.

This product is not working as well for me and my long, straight hair. I mostly wear my hair pinned back, but my disagreeable bangs usually need some extra oopmh (especially when they've been slept on), and I was hoping this might do the trick. The product is a bit heavy and waxy out of the jar, and I didn't notice any strong odor (a plus for me), but it was a bit heavy on my bangs and dragged them down - definitely not a product made for me, especially in that price range. I can see from other reviewers this product could work very well for those with shorter hair and looking for a dramatic effect to tame that morning after hair. Your mileage may vary.

This is the first product from Oribe I've tried, and I really like it!  I'm growing out my wavy hair, and it's just past my shoulders.  This helps create definition to the ends, and it

It also doesn't have any noticeble smell, and is free from nasty petrochemicals.  I follow the Curly Girl Method of no silicones and no sulfates, and this doesn't have any of those.

I also haven't had any of the problems that other reviewers have had of it making my hair look wet, but I only apply about a half-pea-size amount to my fine hair.

If you check the Oribe Hair Care channel on YouTube, you'll also find a helpful video on how to use this.

This does the job.  While I don't have extremely frizzy hair I do have areas that wave an annoying wave or times when bed head just won't do going to work.  A little of this stuff goes a long way.  I just take out a little larger than a pea size and rub it between both palms then lightly smooth it over the problem area/s.  While it straightens it significantly it doesn't always make it completely straight.  I like that it doesn't give a greasy/dirty sheen to your hair -if you do a light coating.  It you do a heavy coating it will look matted and greasy and you'll want to wash your hair.  It is best to do a light coating then add more gradually if you need more.  My main issue is not with the product but rather the packaging.  The cream is thick almost like a cold cream in texture.  However,  I wish it was easy and more hygienic way to remove it from its holder.  If it came as a pump or dispensed easier I would find it less messy to handle.  The flimsy screw top doesn't have many threads and since you hands are already coated with the cream it can be difficult to get the lid secure after use-many times the lid has fallen to the floor and gotten dirty because I couldn't screw it on properly.  It also has a faint chemically and flowery scent that isn't too strong but may turn off those who don't like fragrance or are hypo allergic.  However, I have found that is is not noticeable 5-10 minutes after application.
Overall, I have added this cream to my beauty care regime when my hair isn't behaving.  While it doesn't completely tame the frizz it keeps a lot of it under control and certainly looks better.  I just wish it was easier to get out and had a better dispenser.
summary: While it doesn't completely tame the frizz it keeps a lot of it under control & certainly looks better.  Needs better packagin

reviewText:
I have used Baxter of California products for years and have always liked them.  This Shave Duo kit was something new to me, so I was anxious to give it a try.  The products in this kit are a pre- and post-shave tonic spray and an aftershave gel balm.  They are 4 oz. each in size, but small amounts go a long way, and they both should last a long time even with regular usage.

The tonic spray can be used both before and after shaving.  Since the balm is used after shaving I use the tonic spray only prior to my shave.  It is supposed to help open pores and condition the skin for a more comfortable shave. The instructions say it should be applied with a hot towel, but that it can be alternatively sprayed directly on your face.  Messing with a hot towel is more work than I want to put into shaving, so I simply spray it on my face.  You do have to exercise extra care that you don't get spray in your eyes.  The tonic has a nice scent, and I let it sit on my face for a minute or so before brushing on some Pre de Provence shaving soap.  Using a double-edge razor with a Derby blade I find that I get a much closer shave using the tonic that I get without it.  The razor seemed to glide over my face more smoothly.  I have had no facial irritation, although I usually don't get much irritation from shaving with the products I already use.

After shaving I use the balm and find it makes my face feel quite good.  A very small dime-sized dab of balm is all that is needed.  It has a very light citrus scent to it that should not interfere with any other aftershave or cologne one might use.

Like all Baxter of California products, this kit is expensive.  It seems like Baxter of California prices most everything they sell in the $30 price range.  But they are nice products and generally last quite a while.  The shave tonic in this kit does seem to make for a smoother shave, and the aftershave balm is soothing as advertised.  This kit would be ideal for anyone who tends to experience irritation from shaving.  Those who shave with either a single or double edged razor should find this a worthwhile complement to their shaving routine.
summary: makes for smoother, more comfortable shave; expensive

reviewText: I enjoy the scent of both products - menthol for tonic and citrus for balm.  I also like the cooling action of the tonic after the shave, but it is not feasible for me use the tonic daily as instructions suggest (before shave spray on a hot towel and apply on the face, after shave apply to cold towel and apply on the face).  I simply do not have time for this.  I tried following instructions once, and I did not notice a significant difference in closeness of shave after using tonic first or simply using Creamo Cream.  So after shave, I close my eyes, hold my breath, spray tonic on my face, and enjoy the cooling action, after which I apply the after shave balm.  The skin feels smooth.  This works for me, but, considering the price and the effort required, I do not see myself buying this kit.  Additionally, I do not like the glass bottle of the tonic.  If you drop it in the bathroom, and if it does not break into sharp shards, it is likely to chip porcelain sink or floor tile.
summary: Great smell.  Requires too much effort. No noticeable improvement in quality of shave.

reviewText:
Top quality products with masculine smells. These are products you'd be proud to find in any barbershop.

After Shave Balm: I'd say this is a lot like Nivea For Men's sensitive shave balm (which is wonderful, my daily shaver). This balm is less creamy and with more lavender. Very mild scent, gives you that "clean" feeling after a shave. Very little burning. Really this is a wonderful aftershave, highly recommended.

Shave Tonic: A curious little product. This spritzer smells strongly of eucalyptus, and goes on best wet. Someone recommended using it on a hot towel as you shave, and I think that's a perfect usage. Smells great, leaves your skin feeling excellent. I'm not sure how much it really affects your shave as I'm already very careful with mine, but sometimes a product is so nice to use that you don't even mind. Mild recommend.

Together this kit just screams luxury. My face has never felt so pampered. My only knock on these products is that they're quite expensive, and for a fraction of the price you could just get a bottle of Nivea for Men's sensitive shave balm to get 80% of the result. But if you really want to feel pampered, it's hard to argue with these quality ingredients.

Too much of a process to be enjoyed. When I shave I want to lather, shave, and rinse. With this product I had to follow the lengthy instructions which are time consuming. And then repeat. It does allow for a smooth and clean shave but I need to plan extra time if I'm going to use this on a regular basis. I prefer something basic. One step.

I love a good barbershop shave but usually splurge on one for special occasions or when the wife surprises me. This Baxter of California kit is like a barbershop shave DIY.

Shave Tonic:
The shave tonic is the prep work to a great shave, though it can be used post shave too. I applied a generous amount of shave tonic to a hot face-towel (hot water + about 20 seconds in the microwave). The shave tonic smells great (lots of eucalyptus) and feels great too thanks to the cooling sensation of menthol.

Post-shave you can apply this product to a cool towel and apply it to your face to reduce redness and irritation.

After Shave:
This is a very good aftershave. It smells terrific (nothing floral) and leaves skin feeling cool, refreshed and clean. There's no greasy feel or excessive burning.

Paired with your standard shaving routine this is a great way to get an excellent shave. While probably not practical for everyday use the shave tonic is a great way to vary up your shave and leave your skin feeling great. Recommended!

These have great ingredients and a nice herbal smell, and will be a great product set for anyone who is looking for a shaving tonic/after shave duo. The tonic is much thinner than a shaving cream, but applied with a hot towel it prepares your skin for shaving in much the same way that a warm shower (my usual pre-shave treatment) does, but has the added benefit of skin conditioning ingredients, including aloe and other botanicals and several vitamins. I wasn't sure about the aftershave balm at first because before it absorbed it felt funny on my skin, but after just a few minutes my face felt and looked pleasantly moisturized without being greasy.
summary: Great shaving duo with high quality ingredients

reviewText: I have sensitive skin and this cleanser worked well on it.  It lathers right out of the container, so it lasts a long time.  It rinses clean, but did leave my skin feeling a little bit dry, so you'll definitely moisturizer after using this cleanser.  It doesn't really have a scent at all.  Overall, It's very nice cleanser, but nothing special or unique as far as benefits I noticed to my skin.

This is a luxuriously rich facial cleanser.  It's a pump, so you actually don't need that much because it lathers considerably and spreads around your face very easily.  It does a great job - even on sensitive skin.  I haven't noticed a significant fragrance.  A 4 ounce bottle is going to last a pretty long time.  The lather is soft and creamy - a true luxurious experience.  I've used it twice a day for  over a week and my skin has never felt tight or dry.
summary: A thick and luxurious foam cleanser.

reviewText: This light foam makes my skin feel clean without feeling dry. I just had a facial peel and am happy to have this product to keep up the maintenance. It is not overly perfumy. If your face gets too dry with soap, you may want to give this a try. This is made for oily skin, so I only use it in the morning when I feel kind of greasy. if you have super dry skin, this foam may not be for you.

Foaming Cleanser - I love this foaming soap.  I loooove soap, and foaming soap is even better.  It foams and lathers very great, and you feel soooo clean.  I just cannot tell you how good this cleanser is.  It is so good and I highly recommend it, especially to those of you who are like me and love foam.  But we all need soap/cleansers, and this cleanser is even better than standard cleansers.

For those who know me, they know that I love fluff.  There is never too much fluff.  I would be cranky if I didn't have enough fluff in my life.  I love fluffy cozy mysteries, fluffy soap (such as this foaming cleanser), whipped cream, fluffy clouds, foamy cappuccinos . . . . .

My wife and I have been using Cetaphil Daily Facial Cleanser for several years and we're pretty happy with how it cleans without drying our skin. My wife does use some additional facial cleaners/products and was excited to try out the TIZO Foaming Cleanser. After using it just a few times she was hooked and very happy with how the cleanser performed. Based on her experience I decided to give the cleanser a shot and I can see why she's a fan. This is a gentle cleanser with a light, fresh scent that cleans my skin, which tends to be a bit oily, without leaving me feeling like my skin is dry. I can definitely recommend this product and it's definitely something we plan on ordering in the future.
summary: Gentle Cleanser, Works Well on Different Skin Types

reviewText:
This is the first foaming face cleanser I have tried and I really like it. Not sure if it is still around but this works like the old Dial Complete hand soaps I remember from years ago.
One pump, which foams up lightly in your hand, is applied to wet skin. After massaging in you rinse with warm water and pat dry. I love how this makes my combination skin feel - fresh, clean and soft. It has a light cucumber scent that is not overpowering.
I think it's too soon to tell if the rejuvenation claims work but I do know that my skin definitely looks better and is softer to the touch  since I have been using this.

We've all heard we shouldn't use soap on our face as it's too drying. This cleanser works nicely...one pump provides just the right amount of foam to wash your face, and it's not so strong that you can't use it a couple of times a day. Perfect for use in more humid environments, I follow with a serum and moisturizer and that combination appears to work nicely to keep my face soft. Scent is minimal and pleasant.
summary: Excellent for men: not too strong a scent and comfortable without overly drying

reviewText: So ar soo good. it is really made for oily skin. It dries my already dry skin out too much, but my partner with a more oily face absolutely loves it. Its only been 5 days of use so far so haven't seen any skin rejuvenation magic yet but it did help clean up what looked to be a breakout starting. It smells pleasant botanical smell. Skin is left feeling soft and a little tighter. All in all a nice product if you don't mind fierce oil cutting properties. It bubbles exceptionally light and fluffy so I think 4oz will stretch a little ways. Still awfully pricey if it doesnt start showing some really great results!
summary: Not for dry skin, but works as advertised

reviewText:
As advertised, this is a gentle foaming cleanser that does leave behind softer skin.  It contains some excellent ingredients that I look for in skin care products, Taurine, Niacinamide, and Cucumber Extract.  The Taurine part is an amino acid that supposedly and hopefully over time produces antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and moisturizing benefits.

The feel of the cleanser is very pleasant.  It's extremely light and airy and rinses off easily.  There was a faint but pleasant fragrance, not at all objectionable.
summary: Light and airy foaming cleanser with some ingedients that are good for your skin over time

reviewText:
This review is for TIZO Photoceutical Foaming Cleanser, 4 oz.

I use foaming cleansers to clean my face and I generally use luxury or boutique brands.  What attracts me to this product is that it is "specifically designed to help repair, protect and revitalize environmentally distressed and photo-damaged skin." Living in Central FL, I get a healthy dose of skin-damaging sun on a daily basis and my skin often exhibits signs of stress.

Here's how I use it:  I wet my face, then apply one pump of the cleanser, gently massaging it into the skin.  I then rinse with warm water and pat dry.

I noticed that this product makes my face dramatically softer and eliminates any oil, also shrinking the visible pores on my cheeks and nose.  I do tend to agree that this product helps with skin tone and texture.  It contains Taurine, Niacinamide (think B-vitamins), and Cucumber Extract.  Note that Niacinamide, also known as Nicotinamide, is generally used in beauty products to help treat acne.

The product label says this product can be used with complimentary products AM Rejuvenation and PM Restore.  I am unfamiliar with these products but I do want to give them a try.

Overall, I am impressed with this gentle foaming cleanser and how it leaves my skin.  I would recommend it to a friend.

TIZO will probably not appreciate me describing it this way, but the Photoceutical PM Restore reminds me of a cross between a lotion and Vaseline in look and texture.  It somehow manages to feel silky and glides on (making it easy to distribute evenly).  Initially, it feels heavy but absorbs quickly (less than a minute) and you only need two pumps to do your face, neck, and dcolletage. I sometimes break out when I try a new product but that has not been the case with TIZO.
summary: I'm an loyal Arbonne night cream user but just may switch to TIZO

reviewText:
I love how the TIZO PM Cream makes my skin feel. It is almost like the buttery soft leggings that are so popular right now. It goes in very smooth and leaves my face feeling soft.

Some retinol creams can cause dryness and irritation, I did not experience that with this product.

Although it is called a cream and does make my skin soft and moisturizer, the product itself isn't very creamy.

While I do like the product, the price is not sustainable for me.
summary: I love how the TIZO PM Cream makes my skin feel

reviewText:
This review is for the TIZO Photoceutical PM Restore , 1 Fl Oz

The PM Restore has had a positive effect on my skin, and has made it feel much smoother.

It has also had a moisturizing effect. It instantly absorbed into my skin.

Goes on smoothly

All in all I am very happy with how my skin now feels after using this for just a few days.
I am fascinated by how good this makes my trouble spots, lower neck and lower arms that have gotten the most sun exposure, feel. Softer, less ravaged, less dried out.
summary: Can See and Feel a Difference in Skin

reviewText: It seems to help with skin texture and notice a slight improvement in elasticity. Only problem is the consistency. Very thick and like trying to spread Vaseline so it takes a little more for coverage. All in all, except for the ease of application, it seems to be a decent skincare product.
summary: Hard to apply with thick consistency

reviewText: Wife says it is good. She is using it below her neck but above the bust line. She loves low cut shirts, and the sun damage is catching up to her. So far so good.

According to the box, it says to use one pump to face and neck.  I did that, and that was enough.  I am glad that the box said that; otherwise, I probably would have done two or three pumps and wasted it.  It goes a long way.

I love the way this product feels.  At my age, I am eager to try things that claims things such as "accelerates skin turnover & neutralized free radicals", "retinol complex antioxidants C & E Ceramides", "visibly corrects signs of aging by reducing the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles with little to no irritation", " help repair, protect, and revitalize environmentally distressed and photo-damaged skin".  Anything to help the aging process.  I will not grow old gracefully - I will fight it every step of the way.

I tried this product and I love it.  I will continue to love it, until every ounce is gone.

Each time I've used this product, my face has been red and swollen the next morning. I checked the ingredients list (Cyclopentasiloxane, Dimethicone Crosspolymer, Isononyl Isononanoate, Isododecane, Isohexadecane, Dimethicone/Vinyl Dimethicone Crosspolymer, Dimethiconol, Cyclohexasiloxane, Lauryl PEG/PPG-18/18 Methicone, Retinyl Palmitate, Retinol, Ceramide 3, Tocopherol, Tocopheryl Acetate, Tetrahexadecyl Ascorbate, Caprylyl Glycol, Glycerin, Caprylhydroxamic Acid, Capric/Caprylic Triglyceride, Propyl Gallate) and found nothing unusual in it. I've used products with one or more of these ingredients in them before without the slightest problem. Whether my problem is with the concentration of the ingredients or the combination, I don't know. Oddly, I find my skin's reaction kind of comforting in that I am certain this serumy cream has truly active ingredients! So, I am going to start using this only on my neck, which is much tougher skin. I will update my review at that time. Until then, my guess is that if you are interested in a serum with some very active ingredients, this one may be for you. If I can get my skin accustomed to it, most likely it will become a 5-star product for me.
summary: Very active ingredients in this serum!

reviewText:
I have never been one to believe that expensive beauty products are worth the cost. It has always been my assumption that you could get near similar results with drugstore brands. After trying TIZO Photoceutical PM Restore, I have to admit Im rethinking that logic. Really, how different could they be?

I am fortunate to not have much in the way of wrinkles yet despite being in my mid-40s, so I cant speak to how well this product eliminates them. What I can say is the texture and consistency is extremely appealing. Its a very lightweight formula that goes on smoothly. And it makes the face feeling silky sleek.

While the 1 ounce sizing might seem like the manufacturer is skimping, a little goes a very long way. One pump covers my entire face and neck. I will admit the current cost is still a little pricey for me, and I probably will not splurge on another just yet. But if it drops a bit more, I might because so far this one is delivering.

I love this emulsion!  It is a cross between a cream and an ointment, but it contains no oil.  As I dab and smooth this gently across my face and neck, it feels like an oil, but it is not.  Amazing to me that this can feel like an oil, without any oil.  It leaves my skin so, very smooth.  I know I should not be touching my face so often, but I can't help it--it feels so soft and pleasing and delightful.

There is no fragrance and it seems to absorb into my skin almost immediately, yet also seems to leave a protective smoothness on top of my skin.

The pump nozzle produces an amount that is perfectly portioned to cover my face and neck.  I pump onto my fingertip, then share with other fingertips, then dab around my face and neck.  Then I can use my fingers to gently smooth it to cover the entire area.

One interesting note--and I noticed this within two days:  As I get older, I develop tiny patches of dry skin, which may appear on my neck, dcolletage, arm, etc.  They do not go away easily.  This TIZO PM Restore improves these spots quickly.  I noticed it first, when one of these spots disappeared in my neck area.  Now, I've tried it in other places, just a touch of PM Restore.  It is amazing, the results.

I'm a convert, and will be giving up my other night treatment.
summary: Feels so indulgent and luxurious!  Does wonderful things to my skin.

reviewText: As I creep towards forty aging has become a bit of a concern. More specifically seeing the signs of it around my eyes and the corners mouth where small lines are trying to make themselves seen. I have sensitive, combination skin and over the years I have had some issues with moisturizers where they gel up on top of my skin or cause red patches. Due to those issues I am always trying new products in an attempt to find my holy grail. This pm moisturizer comes very close to being the answer to my search. The product looks and feels like a mix between an ointment and a makeup primer. Although it initially feels as if it will be heavy it goes on smooth and feels light on the skin, the finish being very like a primer powdery soft on the skin. It works as well on my dry zones as it does on my oily and normal zones. It is unscented, I don't mind light scents but no scent is ok with me as well. Thankfully I am not retinol sensitive so it has not caused irritation, and the rest of the ingredients are agreeing with my skin. I really love how soft it makes my skin, it is silky after I apply it in the evenings. The small lines are less visible to me in my magnified mirror and perhaps most importantly the patchiness of my skin seems to slowly be evening out. My only pause with this product is price versus budget concerns, however if continued use evens out my skin I will more than happily find a way to fit it in my budget. Overall this is as close as I have gotten to finding my perfect night time moisturizer and I'm very happy with its performance.
summary: Soft smooth skin in the evening

reviewText:
This is a good product in an elegant bottle and it glides on effortlessly with a matte silky finish and I actually like using it under my makeup as it stays put.
It makes my skin look less wrinkled as it accelerates skin turnover while the Retinol helps it feel moisturized along with antioxidants C and E.
I wouldn't purchase this as it is expensive and the bottle doesn't last long at all so I prefer jarred creams that are cheaper per ounce.
summary: Works well on wrinkles and it makes my makeup set easily and it stays put but the pump bottle doesn't have much product

reviewText:
I've used it mostly around my eyes for the last two weeks before going to bed. As another reviewer described, it has the consistency of a lotion mixed with vaseline. However, it absorbs nicely. One pump does the trick for me.

I like the fact that it has no added fragrance. That does not mean there is no smell, but it is very mild. Additionally, since companies do not have to disclose what is in their fragrances, those products that do have fragrances often contain toxins.

This restorative serum has reduced my wrinkles and the puffiness under my eyes but at 69 it hasn't given me the skin of a 30 year old. There is no miracle serum that I know of but this helps. It goes on with a little tingle that soon goes away.

i could do without the bottle. If it were my product, I'd put it in plain brown glass and pass on the savings... but maybe the pump is more fun.

I've tried a lot of the facial creams and lotions over the last few years. I'm 46 and have zero crow's feet or wrinkling on my face or neck despite a lifetime of working with horses outside. I use sunscreen & moisturizer religiously and wear sunglasses every second if I'm outside. I don't have time to waste with skin products that do not work.

Tizo flat out works and I have two more bottles in my shopping cart right now. This is the best face cream I've ever used. It comes out in a tiny dot from the dispenser and that is all you need to get full face coverage, one more dot for the neck.

 It feels a bit like petroleum jelly initially, but smooths out and absorbs almost instantly. My under eye area is smooth, far less puffy and there's no toxic fumes to irritate my eyes after putting this on. My face is very soft and smooth after ten days of use. A friend asked me this morning what I'm doing because my skin has a bit of a glow and looks "refreshed". That makes me very happy since I wasn't wearing makeup - just applied the Tizo 3 hours earlier. I love this stuff.
summary: Ten days and my skin looks amazing. No toxic scent, absorbs very quickly

reviewText:
In recent years, retinol has become the comeback kid of skincare.  All the major magazines tout its ability to generate new collagen and make skin more toned and youthful in appearance.  I've been using Skinceuticals 1% retinol serum for about two years with satisfactory results.  I'll use it nightly for a week until the redness and peeling get too much for me, then take several weeks off.  The stuff can be harsh, but it's very effective and my skin has definitely improved over time.

Because the TIZO Photoceutical PM Restore contains vitamins C and E plus ceramides in addition to the retinol, I was eager to give it a try.  After nine days use, I can report the following:

The first thing I noticed is that it's very thick and not as easy to apply as my normal night serum.  Although the instructions say one pump is sufficient to cover face, neck and dcolletage, it takes me two healthy pumps to coat all those areas.  It feels very velvety on the skin.  Texturally, it reminds me very much of Benefit's Dr. Feelgood mattifying primer and I'm guessing it would probably work nicely as a pre-foundation primer.  The first time I used it, I experienced the slightest tingling sensation which I attributed to the retinol, although there was no peeling or redness at any point while I was using it.  This makes me suspect that the concentration of retinol is relatively low.

I can't say that I see any appreciable difference in my skin tone or a reduction in fine lines, but it seems to have improved my skin's texture.  After using this at night, my face felt very soft and smooth in the morning and the feeling lasted throughout the day.

While this will probably not replace my Skinceuticals retinol treatment, I think it's a good product that offers fairly immediate results.

I liked this cream, but, I'm on the fence about the texture of it. It was more like a serum and to me it feels like a powder almost after its put on the skin. Also, I don't care for the packaging as much. The top of mine came off before I even got it out of the packaging. Otherwise, I did think that it made my skin feel softer and more supple. I would buy it again, but I probably won't change from my usual day cream.

My wife and I have both been using the TIZO Photoceutical AM Rejuvenation Day Cream each day and we both agree that this is a very good product.  It does make the skin on our face soft and healthy looking, which is just what it says it will do on the box it came in.  The box also tells me that Tizo AM is formulated with Peptides, Niacinamide, Tea Tree Oil and powerful antioxidants.

As Peptides are the first ingredient listed, I decided to find out more about them for readers of this review.  Peptides are among the most powerful and interesting skin care ingredients being used in successful anti-wrinkle products.  The article goes on to say that they are short chain amino acids which are now being used in a variety of products like the Tizo Day Cream.

Anti-wrinkle is too strong a claim for the Tizo Day Cream.  People expecting this cream to do away with their wrinkles are going to be disappointed.  Reduce  yes.  Eliminate  no.

For those readers concerned about the scent of this product, it does have a very slight and pleasant smell.  Some people will hardly notice it, but one reviewer found the smell not to the reviewers liking.  Of course, each of us is different, but I think most people will find the slight scent of Tizo acceptable.

I am guessing that few people reading this review are going to expect a miracle in a bottle, but for $60.00 they do expect a fine product that works well to promote healthy skin, and this is just what Tizo appears to do.
summary: Works well to promote healthy skin.

reviewText: The ingredients in this moisturizer make my skin feel soft, but so far as feeling more radiant, I don't notice any difference from any of the other skin products I've used in the past.  Although it makes no claim to be fragrance free, I was aware of a slight scent which I didn't particularly like.

This is a great moisturizer. It's not greasy and it even has a matting effect. It is non-comedogenic and it helps minimize pores.
I use Clarisonic which provides great exfoliation, this moisturizer gives me the finishing touches.
It blends well with makeup and it's suitable for daily use.
I'm removing one star as they claim it repairs sun damage and reduces fine lines. I haven't noticed any change in that respect.
Regardless, this is still a great moisturizer.
summary: Great moisturizer, not sure about sun damage repair

reviewText: This day cream is truly unscented, and very silky on my face, and while most creams are smoothy, this is the type of silk that I've never tried before. And it is also a nourishing cream too. And a little bit of this cream goes a long way, so only a couple of dots are needed to cover my whole face and neck.. Its absorbed fast and it can be worn under make up. The nourishing effect to the skin is basically because it provides moisture keeping the skin of the face from looking dry. In all, it's a great daily moisturizing.
summary: Silky, unscented, and nourishing face cream

reviewText: If you have ever used a primer like bareMinerals Original Prime Time Foundation Primer, this goes on a bit like that. It is thick (like really thick), viscous, and really slick. This never dried down for me. It always remained "slick" ... not oily but like polymer/silicon. I tried to used three different foundations over it (since it reads "AM," I figured it was designed to be compatible with cosmetics). I used a Tarte foundation stick ... the look was blotchy. I then tried a CC by Bare Minerals ... I had a little more success here, but it still looked odd. Finally, I gave my usual Bare Minerals powder foundation. No way. It was dark in some places, light in others. So, I have been using this on my days off since I received it (and gave up trying to layer make-up over it). I have seen no changes in my skin over; however, it bares noting that I use a pretty serious system (as prescribed/designed by my dermatologist), so those in need of a skin rescue might see great change. Additionally, take care with the dispenser. If you become careless (like I did), some of the product will get stuck in between the case and the pump dispenser. (I guess that's the cost of a "cool" looking container). Overall, for me, this isn't a must-have product. But for you, who knows! It could be! (Especially, if it compatible with whatever foundation you wear!).
summary: A Little Thick, A Little Difficult to Use with Some Cosmetics ...

reviewText:
There are very few facial creams that I can say actually work well.  Since I have the opportunity to try many different products as an Amazon reviewer, I have a lot of experience with how some of the most expensive facial creams do not even remotely live up to their claims.  But this one is actually amazing.  The look and feel of my skin has improved with only a few days use - I'm truly astounded.
I have aging skin with large pores and the lines on my face look finer and the pores are smaller.  My skin feels soft and foundation glides over my skin and looks better than it ever has.
I don't usually think that expensive creams are really worth it, but this one absolutely is.  I will be buying this again and am looking at other products made by TIZO.

Much like some of the peptide based Regenerist products from Olay, this makes my skin feel very soft and moisturized. If the skin is a bit irritated (from sun/windburn), the TIZO cream can feel like it is burning the skin. Even on normal skin, I'd feel a warm sensation. Based on its price though, I'd say this is a good product but there are probably equivalent alternatives at a more affordable price. That being said, I don't use a whole lot of it on my face, just at some key areas that tend to dry up or where wrinkles form.

Overall: 4/5 stars
summary: Expensive and works about the same as most peptide based skin creams

reviewText: This is not a moisturizer and I wouldn't call it a serum.  It doesn't offer any protection from the sun.  What it does is help smooth out those little lines.  It's actually a rather effective primer, and that's how I use it.  After I wash my face, the first thing I reach for is a facial serum.  I use three different kinds, depending on the day and which bathroom I'm in at the time.  I'm a believer is serums and they are always the first thing I feed my skin after washing.  After that, I use a good quality moisturizer with a decent SPF.  After my skin has absorbed that, I use a tiny bit of this cream.  A little goes a long way.  To me it feels like it's creating a thin layer all across my face, absorbing just enough to equalize everything - fill in the gaps, so to speak.  Afterwards, makeup goes on with similar results as when I use a primer.
summary: Doesn't replace the serum or moisturizer I use.  Acts similarly to a primer.

reviewText: Not for me.  I have sensitive skin and this product carries a lot of dimethicone.  Dimethicone is sort of filler that makes you skin look smooth by filling in pores or lines and blurring them.  I have products that carry it that do not bother me but the high content in this cream actually clogged my pores and I could not use for very long before I had to wash it all off.  My skin felt like it could not breathe.  It may cause break outs or bumps.  I think it does make you look nice if you can tolerate it but this is not for people with skin sensitivity..
summary: I have sensitive skin and this product carries a lot of dimethicone.  Clogged my skin.  It may cause break out or bumps.

reviewText:
This is a light, non-greasy cream for your skin which isn't shiny so you can wear it under your foundation.  I like it.  It isn't heavily scented.  It applies smoothly and easily.  As far as reducing fine lines, will have to get back to you on that one.  I'll take their word on that one.  I usually wear a cream at night, so it's great to have a cream for the daytime, too.

This seems like a quality cream which I'm happy with.
summary: Light, Non-Greasy Day Cream for Your Face

reviewText:
This is not what I would call a "day cream"--that implies a moisturizer for day time, vs., say a night cream--a thicker, less makeup-friendly glop. A day cream would provide, typically, moisture that won't cause makeup to smudge or cake in wrinkles, a sunscreen of 30 spf or more, and some nice skin care ingredients--antioxidants in particular, which are needed to counteract sun exposure. This is not most of those things. It is a nice serum-primer. It has antioxidants, as well as some nice repairing ingredients like ceramides and peptides (as opposed to resurfacing kinds of ingredients like retinol and AHAs and BHAs--fair enough--the first two can be an issue with sun exposure, anyway.). You would want to wear this on cleansed skin, but you might want to add a moisturizer over it before using a sunscreen. The TIZO primer and the various sunscreens are excellent.
Just don't expect this to be a day cream.
summary: More of a serum/primer than a day cream, no spf

reviewText:
This product has a smooth feeling, and is absorbed quickly; in fact, my skin actually felt just a little dry (though it wasn't) after applying it. I am thrilled at the almost undetectable scent. I am also happy that it is free of preservatives. I haven't found a difference in the little lines on my skin, but will see what happens over time. I found that a small amount of the product is enough to moisturize. and smooth my skin.  In addition to  peptides and niacinamide, the ingredients include tea tree oil, vitamins C and E, selenium, and a host of other  ingredients, with long names,  one with ""polymer" as part of the name.
