We have always wondered whether mud masks actually work (they sort of do), so we had to give this one a try.  This mud mask did leave the skin of my significant other feeling smoother and cleaner after removal of the residual clay, though the effect does not seem to last very long.  If you plan to use a mud mask to keep your skin clean and smooth, be prepared to use the masks every few days.

This particular mud mask includes volcanic ash from Jeju (also known as Cheju) island off the south coast of South Korea.  Jeju is essentially a big, dormant volcano, so the volcanic ash is readily available throughout the island.  The volcanic ash is mixed with a couple of clays and a bunch of other ingredients that are apparently intended to provide some sort of magical benefits.  Regardless of what the other ingredients do, the mask does have some cleaning benefit, so maybe the other ingredients work.  We did notice an odor from the mask, which we presume was intended to make the mask pleasing to the nose of users, though the odor may cause some users problems.

Applying the mask was a little bit challenging because the mask has to be pressed into all the curves of the face, and thinner people with well-defined cheek bones and a sharp jaw line may find that it takes a bit of time to get the mask onto the face.  Removing the mask is much easer, just peel and toss.  As might be expected, the mask leaves behind some clay and ash that needs to be removed with a good face washing.

One thing that we should have done before the first time we used the mask is to do a good face cleaning before using the mask.  Cleaning the face before plastering the face with clay and ash seemed a bit counterintuitive, but the cleaning is needed to remove oils, which the mask seems to remove only partially.  Note to self, wash face well before and after using mud mask.

We are not interested in getting into the middle of controversy, but we will point out that this mud mask includes methylparaben, which is deemed safe by the FDA in concentrations up to 25%, though the concentration in this mud mask is likely much less than 1%.  Some people seem to have highly negative opinion of parabens, and then they turn around and fill their car up with gasoline, exposing themselves to far more toxic chemicals than they are likely exposed to for an entire day.  Then these same people walk into their highly sealed houses which contain the toxic gases the come from various wood, concrete, caulk, and petroleum-based products used in modern homes.  We are exposed to dozens of toxic chemicals every day and avoiding exposure to a very small amount of paraben is likely not going to be a make or break for any particular individual.

The real benefit to this mud mask is that it is easy to store and remove.  Application is a bit challenging the first time, and hands can get a little messy during application, but application is easier than applying mud by hand directly to the face.  On the other hand, mud can easily be applied closer to the eyes and mouth out of a jar or bottle than this mask can achieve.  Our assessment is that the mud mask is great for those times when a mask out of a bottle is not possible due to time, or there is not enough time for clean up after application of mud from a jar.  For some people, that benefit will outweigh the benefits of mud from a jar.  Each person will need to decide how much time they have available for application and removal of a mud mask, and then decide whether the mask comes from a jar or from this mask that is mostly no mess.

Enjoy!
summary: A mud mask that is a bit of a challenge to apply and fairly easy to remove

reviewText:
South Korean beauty and skin care products are all the rage. But are they really worth the hype? This mud mask left me with mixed feelings. Using the patch technology so popular in administering medications, it features a two piece mask. The box contains four, each individually wrapped. I am not sure who they used as  model for these but one size most definitely does not fit all. If you have small eye, a long nose and a big mouth in an oblong face, well you are in business. Application is a bit tricky. The mud (actually volcanic ash) infused mesh fabric is covered on one side by white plastic and the other a clear plastic wrapper. Remove the white and place over the face. Then peel the clear side away, pressing into position. Once you separate the mesh for the backing, it goes pretty quickly. The mask has a light, pleasant lemony fragrance. Leave on at least ten minutes. I left it on for twenty so that it dried completely. Peeling it off was a snap. Then rinse face with warm water. There was not much residue and it rinsed off cleanly and easily. There was no tightness or dryness and I experienced no negative reaction from this product.

I must say that after a session my skin looked and felt terrific. Pores did seem minimized and my skin looked fresh, smooth and healthy. It felt
soft,moist and smooth. Frankly, I wish this stuff came in a jar. The mask itself was clunky and although I don't mind looking temporarily like one of those Gray aliens that abduct people for the sake of beauty, the mask need major alteration to fit  the contours of my face. I also wish they had an unscented version. That beings said, the ends justify the means and the results overcame my objections to the method. It is not perfect and you will most likely need to perform surgery on the mask and still some areas will remain untouched by the mud, but overall, it was effective.
I really liked this. It cleaned up my face but didn't leave my skin feeling dry, the application was very easy and the mask itself could be used on Halloween. I love it.

This is okay. Not my favorite product because of the parabens that are included in it. I try to avoid parabens and other toxic ingredients in my skin care products. Since this isn't something I will use frequently I figured I'd give it a try. It is a little tricky to put the mask on but it stays in place well and is easy to remove. It leaves the skin soft but so do many other natural products. I'm not convinced this is something I need. It's just okay.

The SmartMud No Mess Mud Masque from Patchology includes two popular clays, kaolin and bentonite, as well as mineral-rich volcanic ash sourced from Jeju Island in South Korea. Its supposed to suck up impurities, debris, oil, and dead skin while infusing your skin with minerals. The SmartMud mask is set apart from its competitors in that it is ready-made. Each box contains 4 masks in their own envelopes. Each mask has two parts, an upper and a lower. Peel off the white backing and press the mask onto your face in the appropriate position. There are holes for eyes and mouth. Then slowly and carefully peel the clear plastic from the mask and press again onto your face, to make sure its sticking where it needs to be. Repeat with the second half of the mask. Instructions are to leave the mask on for 10 minutes. It will not dry in this time, so it won't dry out your skin.

This is supposed to be a no mess mud mask. The convenience is in taking it off, not in putting it on. The mud infuses a mesh fabric that you can just peel off, leaving some mud residue on your face, which can be removed with warm water. Patchology calls the fabric a FlexMasque; it can be stretched a bit. The fit of the mask is passable, but it doesnt contact the sides of the nose well, as there isn't enough slack in the fabric to cover the sides. This is unfortunate, because the nose is commonly a site of enlarged pores. The mask also doesnt go back as far as I would like at the jawline, below the ear. The advantage to a regular jar of mud is that you can put it wherever you want: confine it to the T-zone or extend it onto your neck. The advantage to the SmartMud mask is simply that its easy to remove.

I left the mask on for about 12 minutes. I examined the state of my pores in a 10X magnifying mirror before and after. The mask left my skin feeling smoother and softer, but it removed very few oil deposits from my pores. It doesnt have much effect on blackheads, and unoxidized oil deposits that plague my pores were similarly resistant. I was able to remove them with a combination of an oil cleanser, which dissolves some oil deposits, a fine-grained scrub, and a gentle rayon wash cloth, leaving my pores clear, even at 10X, and my skin silky smooth. Since the SmartMud mask is supposed to remove toxins and pore-clogging debris, I think it would be more effective used after clearing your pores than before. The mud may pull out some debris and oil not visible to the naked eye, but thats not possible if the pores are clogged.

The mask is recommended for normal, combination, and oily skin. I did not find it drying, even though my skin loses moisture very easily. My skin is also very sensitive and has reacted badly to some masks in the past, but I had no problem with the SmartMud mask, even though it is fragranced. Im not sure why Patchology puts fragrance in this mask, as it is a potential irritant that does nothing to improve the product. The scent is almost antiseptic. It is faint, so it didn't bother me while the mask was on my face. The SmartMud mask is non-drying and suitable for sensitive skin, which is more than can be said for much of the competition. It leaves skin smoother and softer, but not as much as a good facial will do. It doesnt effectively clear oil deposits or unclog pores, so it is more suitable to use after doing that, to take advantage of the minerals and the detox properties.

Ingredients: water (aqua), kaolin, butylene glycol, bentonite, polysorbate 80, glycerin, magnesium aluminum silicate, volcanic ash, stearic acid, xanthan gum, mica, bismuth oxychloride, iron oxides, charcoal powder, hydrolyzed collagen, allantoin, panthenol, portulaca oleracea extract, morus alba leaf extract, morus alba fruit extract, phenoxyethanol, tromethamine, dipotassium glycyrrhizate, disodium edta, methylparaben, fragrance (parfum).
summary: Not Bad, but Not Much Pore-Unclogging Power.

reviewText:
I like to use mud masques as they do detox and purify your skin. I especially like them in the summer when I'm spending lots of time outside and in the garden. They are good, but can be messy.

This masque made less of a mess then my jar. It's a bit tricky to put on and clean up is about the same. I did like it although you only get four masques in the box, where a jar can last longer.

My skin looked clean and felt great.

After using this, my face felt really smooth and my pores did look smaller and smoother. This really is less messy than a regular mud mask. I just put my hair back and peeled the backing off of the bottom part of the mask and pressed it on my face. Once it was stuck, I peeled off the front cover of the mask, so it would be able to dry and so that I could better smooth the mask onto my face. Then I did the same thing with the top part of the mask.

The directions say to let it dry for about 10 minutes, and I assume the longer it dries the better the results would be. I waited a bit over 10 minutes. It was dry in some spots, but not in the places where the mask overlapped a bit and the mud was thicker. Still, I was impatient and peeled it off. It is easy to peel off if you pull up a corner and get it started. After which, I rinsed my face. It really was easy and way less mess than a regular mud mask. The results were pretty good too.

The Patchology Smartmud No Mess Mud Detox Mask is a great facial mask for when your skin needs pampering.  The mask is a bit tricky to apply, although it's no more difficult to apply than most facial masks.  The mask comes in two pieces, and each piece is sandwiched between a cellophane like plastic.  To apply each piece, you simple remove the white plastic film from the mask, push the wet mask to your face, then peel off the clear film.  Once the clear film is removed, you can adjust the mask on your face as necessary.  You then can apply the bottom mask in the same fashion.

The mask is very similar to a thick paper towel soaked in facial mud.  Because it is towel like, you can adjust where on your face the mask sits, but it also means that mask can (and will) stick to itself should you accidentally let it flop over at any given time.  Luckily, the mask pieces unstick from itself well, and again, it's completely adjustable.  The mask has a pleasant scent to it, and feels wonderfully cool on the skin.  It is suggested to leave the mask on anywhere between 10-20 minutes, although if you leave it on longer, it won't hurt.  I left it on until it was nearly all dry - about 30 minutes.  Unlike other mud masks I've used, this mask doesn't get tight or itchy as it dries.  The mask can be peeled off easily, and once peeled off, the remaining mud is easily rinsed off with warm water.

While pricey, this mask does make your skin feel amazingly soft after use.  I didn't have any issues with irritated skin, and my skin looked and felt very lovely and refreshed.  With that said - was it better or easier to use than my usual mud mask or facial mask treatments?  No particularly.  I've used both the "slather on" type masks, as well as the cloth like material masks, and while this particular mask is good, there are options available at a lesser price and similar quality.  If you have the budget, this mask would be one to consider.  It's comfortable and refreshing to wear, feels great on the skin, and will leave your skin looking and feeling soft and rejuvenated.  I would certainly get it again.
summary: A Bit Tricky to Apply, Leaves Skin Feeling Soft and Looking Refreshed

reviewText:
This one-size-fits-all mask is a bit tricky to apply.  I need bigger eye openings so I had to stretch it so I wasn't getting it in my eyes.  But the results were very good.  My pores were clean & my face felt wonderful.  Is it better than a traditional mud mask?  Well, IMO, no but it is definitely less messy & works as well.  So if you hate the mess of a mud mask but like the results of a mud mask, this may be the mask for you.

It comes in 2 pieces (4 full face masks in a box).  Take the white back off & apply to the face -carefully.  I recommend starting at the forehead, smooth it & work your way down.  Then you take off the clear plastic side - this is really tricky because the clay on your face wants to come with it.  But just be patient & know that you can smooth the clay out once that plastic part is removed.  I had some wrinkles but I managed to mostly smooth them & made good contact with my skin.  I had to work it in a bit on the nose bridge between my eyes & the corners of my nostrils.

The bottom half was easier because I didn't have to worry about my eyes.  The mouth opening is juuuuust big enough - I don't have a particularly big face or head ;)  Next time, I will cut the eye area larger before applying.  This process reminds me of using tooth whitening strips.

It's true that it is not messy.  It doesn't run down your face or into your eyes/mouth.  You don't have a big muddy mess all over your hands & bathroom.  It has a mud-saturated cloth consistency - kind of strange.  You look like a mummy.  It feels tingly while on & has a very light, cleanser-type fragrance.  You just peel it off when done - it does not hurt to peel.  You are left with just a light ashy haze on your face.  I wiped off with a baby wipe & then rinsed my face.

These would be very convenient for travel.  I like to give myself a mud mask after a long-haul flight - this patch mask would make it very easy.

According to their website, leave on for 10 minutes or 20 minutes for a deeper clean.  I went for the deeper clean.

This is made in South Korea.  The "mud" is volcanic ash from Jeju Island, South Korea.  I'm not sure that it provides any better magical cleansing but it is nice, finely textured mud.
summary: Good Mask - But Tricky to Apply - 4.5 Stars

reviewText:
My first foray into trying a sheet mask was the Patchology SmartMud No Mess Mud Detox mask.  I find "no mess" a big promise to uphold, but this mask was far less messy than my usual mud (or other wash-off) masks.  Having a more petite face, the upper portion of the mask was particularly challenging to fit just right, I found the eyebrow area and the forehead zone the most oversized and caused me to spend extra time afterwards washing excess mud out of my brows and hairline.  The feel of the mask while on was fairly comfortable.  Once the 10 minutes were up (I set a timer) I found the mask wasn't too drying and kept it on maybe 3 more minutes or so before peeling both halves off my face.  Nearly all of the mask was easy to peel right off and toss out, with the exception of the forehead region which was more stuck on.  I found my complexion looked brightened and facial skin felt more refreshed once the mask came off.

As for value, there's only 4 sheet masks in the package, so there's a high price point per mask -- however, the masks are a once a week type of splurge, so the value opinion will vary by person.  One star off for the fact that this mask has parabens, would love to see a version that is paraben-free.
summary: challenging fit for small faces, clean fresh appearance after, contains parabens

reviewText: I really love using face masks. Especially when taking a bubble bath. Makes me feel so spoiled and happy.

This four masque set claims to eliminate the messiness of traditional "mud in a jar" applications. Unfortunately, I found it tricky to peel off and apply to my face, as the mud tends to stick to the clear backing and you have to poke around to make it adhere the way it should. Yes, it's less messy in that it doesn't drip into your eyes or mouth, but making it fit the unique contours of your face requires a bit of effort.

Once I got it, I really liked the odor and the cooling sensation. I felt pampered and after I rinsed it off, my skin felt very clean.  However, the effect doesn't last and for the price, it's easy to use up a box quickly. But it's good as an occasional "treat", especially if you have very dry skin.
summary: Feels Good For Your Skin, But Pricey and Tricky to Apply

reviewText:
4.5 stars.

APPLICATION: I subtracted a half star because it's a bit tricky to pull the clear plastic side away while the mask is on your face. I suggest started at the nose for the top and the lips for the bottom. Once I got it to stick finally, it was fine. I left it on for 10 minutes. It was easy to remove and a quick rinse took care of the light mud residue.

RESULTS: I have combination, breakout prone skin, but it's not sensitive. The mask tingles slightly while on, but nothing painful. As soon as I rinsed, I could tell a difference in the feel of my skin. It was silkier and firmer. The next day, my skin glowed. It's been three days and I'm very impressed with how good my skin looks and feels. This could become my new addiction!

My wife finds that this is a very nice Mud Detox Masque though it is still not as easy to use as suggested. In fact, she prefers using her jar masks - such as her seaweed mud and honey mask as well as a brightening mask which is very easy to apply and wash off, though it is not a direct comparison as they are hydrating and brightening masque.

She likes this mud detox masque for its promise to detox and remove impurities from the face via pulling them out of the pores. After using the masque, she mentioned that her face feels cleaner without the friction of a scrub cleanser which typically open up the pores.
summary: Great masque for removing impurities without opening the pores like a scrub (tiny beads) cleanser

reviewText:
There's a well known spa close to me that I love for its mud baths. But it's pricey, and I only get a chance to go once every few years. I love what the mud does for my skin, making it soft and luxurious feeling. So the experience of even a simple mud mask is relaxing to me, and that's why I ordered this product--for the spa-like feel, and for the skin care.

I love that this mud comes in a pre-cut mask that  I can easily apply to my own face. I wasn't sure how that was going to work out in terms of surface coverage, but it really is awesome.

The mud comes preloaded on something akin to cheesecloth. It is precut for the upper and lower face. Applying it is really easy, and I was able to get full coverage over my entire face.

I could feel a slight tingle as soon as the mask touched my face. And that slight tingle continued the entire time I had the mask on. It wasn't painful or irritating. On the contrary, I drew myself a hot bath, put my head back and feet up, and let the mask do its work for a good 30 minutes (the directions indicate a minimum of 10 minutes, but it just felt so relaxing!

I'm not able to describe scent from the mud on the mask except to say that it reminds me of the spa--clean plus something else that I rather enjoy.

Removing the mask was simple. And, as it doesn't dry out completely, it was painless. It was also virtually mess free.

And best of all, I really can see improvement in minimizing my poors. My face also feels softer and smoother than before I applied the mask.

Unfortunately, the price point is beyond what I can typically afford (or at least what I'm willing to pay) on a regular basis. But I consider these a treat that id be willing to give myself from time to time.
summary: ... a well known spa close to me that I love for its mud baths

reviewText:
I can't judge what impurities are removed from my skin, as they're microscopic.  I just have to be trustful that this works.  That said, the mud makes my skin very dry, so I"m not crazy about it.  I've had mud baths in spa retreats, and never had this problem before.
I did like that it was a relatively neat treatment.  My bathroom didn't suffer at all.  Just my skin.

The masque itself is fine and left my skin feeling good, reduced blotchiness, pores a little tighter. For me it is no better in terms of efficacy than many other masques I have tried. It works well enough and the residue rinsed off fairly easily.

I am going 2 stars for this product as the application instructions just did not work for me. The masque itself was very large for my face, landing a fair amount in my hair. The white section peeled off easily for both halves of the masque. Unfortunately the clear section would not come off without removing the masque ingredients. I work with bandages, dressings and peelables all day long as a nurse so I saw it as a professional challenge. I could not get this layer off, leaving the masque behind. I ended up leaving the chest plastic on. I looked like a hockey goalie but it was the only way to test it.

This felt good on and came off easily. However it is my opinion that this method of application just didn't work. I'd rather have a jar of product and apply it myself.
summary: Just ok masque with an application fail.

reviewText: I love this mud mask!  IT's so easy to apply-just 2 pieces that you peel and set in place. NO mess at all and removes with as much ease as it it was to apply. I wasn't sure I would see anything results-wise, but my skin looked better after one application. It removed a lot of the oils that were clogging my pores and my face even felt better! I love that you get 4 applications. I recommend this if you want a good weekly mask without a lot of difficulty in application and less mess.
summary: So easy to apply and remove!

reviewText:
*** My wife graciously provided the following review ***

If you're like me, you've done facial masks before and didn't bother to read instructions. However, after getting my hair out of my face and applying both mask pieces to my face, I realized that something wasn't quite right because the mask didn't hug my face. If you use a cheap mask, you can expect to not have the mask secured to your face requiring you to lie down face up. Although resting while having a face mask on is not a bad thing, you can't multi-task.

After a few seconds of saying, "This isn't right," I experimented with peeling the clear top layer and quickly discovered that the process is peel, apply, peel, smooth. By the way, if you read the instructions, it will tell you the same exact thing I just wrote. Smoothing the mask onto the face is like paper mché. It's easy.

Once the mask is applied correctly, you'll instantly feel a cool tingly feeling. Since the mask is not going to fall off, one could  conceivably do household chores and such, but I recommend lying down and relaxing.

According to the package, the mask could be removed in 10 minutes, but can be kept on longer. Traditionally, mud masks shouldn't be kept on longer than 10 minutes due to the drying effect, but I'm a boundary pusher and wanted to see what my face was like after 30 minutes. After all, the package did say I could leave it on longer than 10 minutes.

Peeling the mask off after 30 minutes was easy peasy and left only a residual amount of "mud" which easily rinsed off. Results: My face felt exceptionally refreshed and not dry which is what you'd expect with a traditional mud mask. Additionally, I had a positive mental outlook to continue my busy day. I'm glad I took that break.

To feel even more pampered after the rinsing, I applied a luxurious spray toner, moisturizer, and sunscreen. Now I'm ready to face the world.

The 2-piece mask is somewhat tricky to apply the first time.  I never got the nose to stay adhered to my face long enough for there to be any benefit there.  The second time I was much more successful in getting the mask to bond everywhere (leave some slack in the nose area so you can press it in with your fingers). Yet, it really didn't ever feel like the mask was attached to my skin or doing any work other than firming up on top of the skin.  The mask was soothing and felt good, but I question its ability to draw anything out of my pores.

I live in a humid climate so I left the mask on for more than the 10 minute start time. Otherwise the mask just felt damp and cool the entire time--although that's nice on a hot day.

The mask does live up to some of it's promises.  Your skin won't feel dry or tight afterward. The mask leaves very little reside on the skin and is easy to clean up. My skin looked and felt good afterward. I just wonder how much detoxing went on there. And my pores don't look any tighter. So I have mixed feeling about this.

You get 4 masks in this box and with it being recommended to use once a week, the box will last about a month. I'm not sure its worth $30 for a month of masks, especially when you can get masks so much cheaper. The product is neat though in the sense that its two pieces that you just apply to your face and let sit for 10 minutes. So if you don't like dipping your hands in mud to rub onto your face this product is definitely less messy. I feel it made my skin feel smooth and clean but similar to other cheaper masks. It did fit my face, its one size fits all, but it didn't completely form to my face and I kept pushing it down into place. Lightweight product and washes off easily. I haven't noticed anything with my pores or skin glowing yet, but it did feel better than just washing with soap.

Not as messy and easier to use than the type of clay/ mud mask where you have to mix the powdered clay with water, but not as effective. Still left my skin really soft and oil free, without drying.
The only thing I really did not like is the smell of it -- it is sooo perfume-y, smells nice, but too over powering. It smells like if you just soaked a paper towel with perfume then placed it on your face. Typically, face products that have this much fragrance make me break out and this one did as well, just a little on my forehead. So if you are sensitive to fragrances in products, I would NOT recommend this mask.

This mask was mostly easy to use -- though I think it will take a little practice to get it to not stick to itself when trying to position -- and I really like how easy the application was with it being in two pieces.  Separating the backing once you have it on your face wasn't very easy and it did fold onto itself which was then not so easy to pull apart but this is something that a little practice would likely overcome.  As far as the results, I didn't notice any dramatic changes in my skin after one use, positively or negatively, but did leave my skin feeling soft and not overly dry.  I can see adding this to a weekend beauty routine easily, getting the mud benefits without a bunch of mess and hassle.  What's not to like about that?!
summary: mess and hassle-free mask once you get the hang of application

reviewText:
This is pretty neat. It comes in two layers, the top piece for the upper part of your face and the lower for the bottom. The directions were not super clear. It said to leave the mask on for 10 minutes or more. This is where it got confusing for me. Does it dry like a Biore strip? Once it's dry do you pull it off? Or does it stay a little wet and you just pull it off after the 10 minutes? Some of the mask started to dry, so I waited about 5 minutes longer and a little more of it dried but I didn't want to stay in the bathroom all night so I ended up pulling it off.

At first while it was drying I thought my face stated to get warm. I couldn't tell if it was supposed to be like that if I was having a reaction or if I should leave it. So, I braved it out. I tried not to think about how red my face would be the following day if it truly happened to be a bad reaction. Luckily, I think it was all in my head as there was nothing wrong.

Next mask I'll leave on longer to see if it's any different but my face was really soft after taking off this mask. It was a little tricky to apply and it didn't quite seem to fit around my eyes and was a little longer than my nose which got in the way of breathing. I had to push the excess up and off to the side. It didn't quite stick to the side of my nose either and there was a bit of a gap near my eyes and temples.

I like the idea of the volcanic ash. Everyone says how restorative it is. I'm so glad this doesn't smell like sulfur though.

Super easy mud mask. Applying the mask requires peeling off BOTH sides of the plastic. First I removed the white plastic side and pressed the mud lightly on center line of my face, then I peeled off the clear plastic side which allowed me to press the cloth & mud onto my face. Both sides need to be removed to get good application. There does seem to be a trick to application and I will get better with each application. Smartmud felt cooling the entire time it was on my face and was still wet after the 10 minute wait. I peeled the mud off tossed it into the trash can and only had to gently rinse to get the remaining mud off my face. I plan to use these for girls spa night next month and I am sure it will be a hit.

This is the least messy mud masque I have ever used.  It is a little tricky to apply but once you get it in place it is fine.  It says to let it dry for 10 minutes, I left it on a little longer.  It peels off easily, and I just rinsed my face with water afterwards.  My face felt soft and moisturized.  This makes using a mud masque so much easier, I will probably do it more often since I have these instead of the mud in a jar.
summary: Easiest mud masque I have ever used

reviewText: This was a very easy mask to put on and take off.  It was the least messy mask I've ever used.  I did not like that it had a fragrance because I am extremely sensitive to scents but I did not have any reaction to the smell or to  the mask itself.  It was definitely gentle on my skin and my skin looked very nice after I used it.  It doesn't feel that strong.  I felt like I needed to leave it on there for more than 10 minutes and probably more than 15.  It was still very moist when I took it off but it felt like it needed to be more dry when I removed it in order to have the impurities attach to it.  That may not be the case but that was the sense I had about it.  Nevertheless, my face looked great when I was finished and that is what is most important.  I won't give it 5 stars because of the fragrance and because my face has been softer with other masks. but it is very easy and fast to take on and off and my face looked so smooth when completed.
summary: Easy On Easy Off - Smooth Skin - Contains a Fragrance

reviewText:
This is an interesting product that requires some experimentation to figure out how to best use. For me, mixing with a little lotion to tone down it's quite-tan color, makes a good cover to give me tan legs when I want to show them. You need to make sure, however, that you allow about 15 minutes for the color to try, or it will smear on your clothing. This is a good alternative to self-tanner, though it washes off with a shower, where self-tanner lasts about two days (in my experience.)

For me, using this product on my skin works best, but others may like it on their faces as well. In any event, it gives you a tan look without exposure to harmful rays.

A little goes a long way! I love this. I have pale skin that looks even more vampiric in the summer, but I don't want to lie out in the sun. This is a great solution. It gave me a natural-looking tan instantly, and didn't cause irritation on my face or rub off on my white clothes. It lasted until the next shower. Be careful not to use too much on your face, because you really want to blend it in, but I think the name "Body Blur" is the perfect name, because that's exactly what I felt like I was doing---blurring the line between my non-tan areas and my new "tan" areas. It instantly made me look better in a summer dress. This is a product I will be sticking with!
summary: Absolutely a must-have for pale skin in summer time!

reviewText:
I really love this -- and just wish that it wasn't so expensive!  For several years, I've been using the Sally Hansen Airbrush Legs (in both the spray and lotion versions) or Jergens BB Body Cream on my legs to cover some small spider veins and to even out my skin tone.  While I love those two (especially the spray version of the Sally Hansen), this Vita Liberata version really does blow them out of the water.

The Jergens BB cream is also supposed to blur imperfections, but this one does a much better job.

It is pretty dark for those of us who have fair skin, but it looks fine for summer, and I've also found that you can tone this down by adding in a bit of lotion.

Just be sure to give this a lot of time to set.  If you don't let it dry thoroughly, it will get onto your clothes.  I need a good ten minutes for this to set, which is a lot longer than I've needed with similar products.

It's also really good, as it claims, for masking cellulite.  The light-deflecting qualities make me feel much more comfortable wearing skirts.

Also, you can use this on your face.  I use a tiny bit, and it adds a nice glow to my skin.  You can even mix a bit into your foundation, which is great since it means that you don't have to buy a darker one for summer.  I used this in both my Lancome Teint Miracle and my Laura Mercier BB cream, and it works well in both, and doesn't change the consistency of the foundation.

The smell is more like sunscreen and since it doesn't have self-tanner in it, it doesn't have that smell to it.

The ingredients are:

Aloe Barbadensis (Aloe Vera) Leaf Water*, Glycerin*, Cyclopentasiloxane, Cetearyl Alcohol, Dimethicone, Cetyl Alcohol, Glyceryl Stearate, Phenyl Trimethicone, Isohexadecane, Panthenol, Disodium EDTA, Butyrospermum Parkii (Shea) Butter, (Beurre)*, Tocopheryl Acetate, Phenoxyethanol, Ethylhexylglycerine, Synthetic Fluorophlogopite, Tin Oxide, CI 77891 (Titanium Dioxide), CI 77491 (Iron Oxide), CI 77492 (Iron Oxide), CI 77499 (Iron Oxide). *Organic.

Since aloe is the first ingredient, it's pretty moisturizing.  I also like that it has shea butter in it, and that several of the ingredients are organic (although quite a few obviously aren't).  This brand is also cruelty-free and this particular product, according to the company website, is gluten-free as well.

Happy summer!
summary: Really does add a nice sheet to your skin, but be sure to let it dry thoroughly or it will transfer onto your clothes

reviewText:
Great instant bronzer. I really had to work it into my fair skin to get an even color; but it was well worth it.  The color is gorgeous and does not rub off until you wash it off. Made my pale legs look beautiful.

Con-I would be hesitant to wear any white clothing while using this. I don't believe there are any products on the market which would  prevent stain transfer especially in the summer months when you more prone to sweating.

I love this product!  I used it without a self tanner base and it gave me a nice tan, with a radiant glow.  The radiance is a nice glow, without looking sparkly.  A little goes a long way.  I made the mistake of pushing too much out of the tube and I ended up using it on my face, neck, decollete and  arms.  It gave me a natural looking tan with radiance.  I will definitely use this when I am going out and want a nice tan, radiant look.  I will say it is a little pricey for my taste.

I love BB creams so I was really excited to try this. When I first got it, I was thinking, wow that's really dark. Then I noticed on the back the color says Latte. Does that mean they make more than one color? Did I get a dark color without thinking? I was hesitant to try this because it was so dark but I figured, hey, I want to see if it will help my legs with some color and to hide any imperfections I have. Applying it with a makeup sponge was fairly easy. It blended out really well but the color was just not me.

Not to mention the makeup was rubbing off on my clothing. The top of my white socks were covered. I actually felt more self-conscious going out with my legs covered in make-up than I did with them just super white. I have 3 BB creams at home so I didn't bother using this on my face because of the color.

I attached a photo of how the product appears.  I wanted to show you how it looked liked compared to my bare skin. As you can see I have a greenish blue visible vein and the dreaded cellulite.  I wasn't expecting a miracle product to cover these things but did want a major improvement in appearance.  This product only slightly "blurred" these things but did not give me an airbrush look.

While the color is natural and believable, the product itself did not last long before it started rubbing off on the car seat or other items I rubbed against. The color has an illiminating effect (not fake glitter explosion) but very subtle and pretty when the sun hits your skin.  The application was doable but could spread more easily if mixed with a lotion.  I went to a pool party and was afraid of getting wet, rightfully so, I dipped my foot into the hot tub and a tan line was created shortly after.  Definitely this is a product to use on a date, indoor gathering or possibly a backyard get together, as long as you will not get sweaty or wet.  This product reminds me of Salley Hansen leg makeup but this one has more natural ingredients.

I wanted to try this primarily because of the reviews I read noting how great it is when used on the face. Also, as someone who has extraordinarily sensitive skin, I appreciated that it isn't full of parabens, phthalates, etc.

When I first saw the bottle, I was a little hesitant to put it on my face because the product appeared pretty dark, and my skin is pale. (Actually, it's pasty. Okay, fine: my complexion makes Casper look like he's been hitting the tanning bed.)

So I mixed a small amount in with my face makeup and I was pretty pleased with the results: it wasn't miraculous, but it did provide more coverage without making it look like I was wearing cakey, mask-like makeup. My skin overall looked smoother, healthier, and prettier. It also turns out that my worries about it adding too much pigmentation were wholly unfounded, as it didn't; in fact, it didn't seem to add anything in the way of a tint or glow. (which is odd as I've read other people's accounts of how well this has worked for them in that regard).

A big plus in terms of this product is that my super sensitive skin that I mentioned previously? Wasn't irritated in the slightest by this product - I didn't experience any rashes, redness, or breakouts.

So it's a pretty good "blurring" product for the face, and at least for me, it doesn't cause issues for sensitive skin. All in all, I'd recommend giving this a try.
summary: Pretty Good "Blurring" Product For the Face

reviewText: Overall I think this gave me an all over instant glow that looked pretty! There was a laminator in this product that made my skin glow. I did not find that it rubbed off in my clothing and felt it washed off without problem. Perfect product when you want to give your white arms a touch of temporary color.

This skin finish gives your face, if it is not too pale to begin with, a bronzing light suntanned finish. It looks natural if you spread it to your neck and even around to your ears. You need to let it dry and keep your hands off of your face.
I have a medium, easily tanned complexion, so the 001latte finish worked well as a colour for me.
Since it does work as a bronzer it does cover small blemishes and age spots.
There is no real discernible fragrance. It is nice for those who like a bronzed complexion.

After trying several Vita Liberata tanning products, the last one I used had me raving with joy (that was the Fabulous Self Tanning Gradual Lotion - the best self tanner I've ever used.)  I should've stopped while I was ahead, because the Body Blur Instant HD was a bit of a letdown.

Don't get me wrong. It gives a decent color, particularly on the legs (my personal bete noire), although this was probably a bit dark for me. I found the application streaky, no matter what I did. And the idea of putting this on my face? Oh gawd, no!

The real problem with this is that it rubs off. I had this on my legs, hours before I went to bed, and it didn't feel tacky. In the morning I woke up to sheets with tan-colored smears, the product embeded in the fibers. I washed them immediately, but the stains remain. Well, at least I found something where this product sticks, cause it sure wasn't my legs!

I wish I could recommend this more highly, but it's a disappointment. Fortunately, the company's Fabulous Self Tanning Gradual Lotion IS available on Amazon. Drop this, and get that, you love it!
summary: Streaky, rubs off, a total letdown (but check for the Vita Liberata tanner that's fantastic!)

reviewText: While it went on easily and blended well and it made my legs look good, I wouldn't recommend this product inasmuch as it came off all over my clothes even though I did allow it to dry.

The color of this is dark for any very light-skinned person. The description doesn't specify the color (001, Latte), and it won't work for all - it's best for medium skin tones, or people with decent tans. It's shimmery and feels light going on but definitely needs to be blended in when applied.

Claims it does not contain gluten. This reviewer was left perplexed by why an external product would need to clam this.
summary: Latte color may not work for all skin colors

reviewText: I tried this on my face using my Cailyn O! Wow Brush - the brush does a very good job of blending this product out. CAILYN O Wow Make Up Brush. You need to use very little, dotting it lightly and then blending it in with the brush (or your fingers). Why I don't like it: A. I have some hyper-pigmentation from using tanning beds years ago. This product makes these areas appear even darker. It doesn't cover them or even them out, unfortunately. B. It gives me a glow, but in the sunlight, it's tiny specks of glitter.

After trying and recommending another Vita Liberata product -- Vita Liberata Phenomenal 2-3 Week Tinted Tan Mousse, Medium, 4.22 fl. oz.-- I was fully prepared to become a Body Blur fan. Who wouldn't want a product designed to "minimize blemishes, cover imperfections, and smooth skin appearance while reflecting light for a photo-ready skin finish?" And it lasts a full day, meaning that theoretically you will apply in the morning and it will look great when midnight rolls around. Before ordering this item, I watched the Vita Liberata video that shows a bikini-clad model whose skin looks about a million times more perfect than mine ever has, even without additional product. So if that is the target for Body Blur, I'm not it, but thought I'd check it out anyway because you never know. I have tried it a few times, both on my arms and (bravely) on my face. My skin color is naturally dark, and on my arms, the Body Blur sort of but not completely masked my freckles, mostly by darkening the surrounding skin to freckle color and adding a light shimmer, which I could have done without as it tended to highlight my other various skin imperfections. Applying it to my face was a mistake. Despite following directions, I ended up with splotchy colors. There are lots of bronzing and HD products that are designed for the face and do a better job. BB is not a good look unless you are trolling for sympathy or questions about what you've got on your face. Mixing it with sunscreen produces better results, but no better than tinted sunscreen which is less work (and offers many less expensive options). Advantages: very little fragrance, non-toxic ingredients. Someday, in my next career as a bikini model who never plans ahead, this may be my go-to product, but since I'm happy with the self-tanner, I will continue to use that on my arms and legs. It lasts longer and has no sheen, so even though it's not instant, I prefer it.

This Vita Liberata Luxury Tan Body Blur Instant HD Skin Finish in the color 001 Latte will give you a light brown, with a bronze tone, tan look. I have fair skin and I find it really looks great on my pale legs. The label says it covers imperfections and minimizes blemishes, but it didn't cover any skin imperfections, not even tiny spider veins. It's great for giving a very light brown color to your skin though- almost a touch of sun look.

The directions say you can use it alone, with a foundation or as a make-up preparation. I don't use any foundation and I found the color a bit too dark for my face, but great to make my legs look like they've been in the sun.  One thing that is nice is that it contains Titanium Dioxide, which is a powerful sun protectant.  I like the smooth shiny bronze tone it gives your skin too. What I don't like is the price. This tube of 3.38 fluid ounces isn't much coverage, especially if you're using it on your legs. It will last a short 24 hours, so it isn't as good compared to an actual tanner for your legs that would last a full week. I found it to be too high priced for such an average tanner.
summary: Gives You An Average Light Brown/Bronze Tan Look

reviewText:
This is a cross between a bronzer and a ultra HD liquid to minimize imperfections. I have been using some HD skin products from brands like Nars, NYX, MAC and Ulta, and this is similar as in it evens out the skin tone and adds a bit of shimmer.

I prefer to use it not as a base but to put a few drops in my foundation to give it a smoother and slightly shimmery appearance. This is a darker colored product but when blended with a foundation that gets too light in the summer, it works nicely. It is best to apply this mix of foundation and this skin finish with a brush or even better with a facial blending sponge. The price is pretty high for a small quantity of product, so I am giving it 3 stars compared to some other products I'm using from other brands that are in the $20-$30 range. If this product works even better I will come back to update my review.
summary: Makes the skin look smoother and adds a glow.

reviewText:
This is an interesting beauty product.  It reminds me of a cross between a liquid bronzer and a BB cream for your body.  For my light/medium neutral toned skin it's an effective temporary way to give skin a natural-looking good glow and to subtly neutralize skin issues like stretch marks.  I like it!  If you have serious scars, tattoos or the like to cover you'll definitely want body makeup with more coverage, but this is perfect for when you just need a little help but still want you skin to shine through.  It's also better for times when you are wearing dark clothes you can wash since it isn't self tanner and can wipe or wash off.

Didn't realize this type of product was even a thing but I love it!
summary: Fantastic for giving your body a subtle, temporary glow

reviewText: I'm not sure about this product. The consistency is like mousse. I received mine in the Latte shade, which is a little on the dark side. It has a little sheen to it. I put some on my face. I have yellow undertones, but no tan. If I had a tan I think this would look great. But with a paler complexion I can't tell if my face looks kind of like I have dirt on it or darker spots. It was easy to blend, so maybe a lighter shade would work better. The price of $45 is way too expensive.
summary: Lighter Shade Would Be Better For Me

reviewText:
I wasn't quite sure what to expect from this product, because I wasn't really clear on what it is.

It's much darker than I thought it would be, for a start (the color is named "Latte"). It's not a self-tanner, but more like the bronzing gels that were popular in the 1970s (product is a cream, though). It goes on bit streaky and muddy if your skin is dry, and has a slightly glittery sheen. It washes off easily, so I wouldn't count on it at the beach or in the rain. Or to "tan" your hands. Also, it will get all over your clothes, sheets and towels. It's not waterproof.

While it's recommended for the whole body, it's probably best used to give your face, neck and cleavage--and maybe your shoulders--a "sun-kissed" glow for a night out.
summary: Not a self-tanner, more of a bronzer

reviewText: I love this Body Blur, it took a little effort to rub it in evenly but my legs look fabulously tanned.  It gives a great natural glow, way better than self-tanner, and has not been rubbing off on my clothing.  It's a nice thick moisturizing consistency.

It works really well alone or mixed with foundation or moisturizer. It isn't too shimmery. The 001 Latte color is a little dark for my skin. Since it is summer, I am able to make it work with good blending and a little highlighter. Come winter, it won't work for me at all.

Warning: if you are fair skinned, this may not be the product for you. It applies dark. Even if you closely follow the instructions of using it sparingly and applying it in circular motions ... it is crazy dark (and a touch orange-y but this is probably because I'm nearly translucent, that's how pale I am!)

The great news is that there is no fragrance and no "weird smell." And, while it seemed to dry quickly, it still rubbed off on my clothes even after thirty minutes of waiting. So, be careful ... especially with those beautiful white summer skirts.

Now, know that the tube is not as large as I would have imagined. Therefore, it's a bit difficult to justify this exorbitant price (with the color transfer and the dark hue).

I'm going to pass on this. However, I love the idea of people using this product rather than tanning! So, three-stars for it's potential and for its good intentions (of saving people's lives!)
summary: Dark, Small-ish Tube, Rubs Off on Clothes ... BUT, Good Idea!

reviewText:
Great quality! Love this bronzer.
Pros:
- bronze color (nor orange),
- a little goes long way,
- nice scent,
- great ingredients.

Cons:
- maybe price? but considering all the pros it's ok, it will last a while.

I use mix a tiny bit with my zinc oxide sunscreen and it is perfect! Not only I don't look like a ghost, have the best protection (zinc oxide is the only thing that protects from UVA1, UVA2 and UVB) but it blurs imperfections (evens out the skin tone). It's perfect for making winter lighter foundation a summer one, when we slightly darker or use more self tanners.
It last on the skin until I remove it with soap and water (from the body) or face cleanser.

There's something about high quality skin products that is so different than the usual pharmacy stuff. The texture and finish are smoother and blend better, and the final look is more natural and feels lighter and silky. This product gives skin a smooth, healthy appearance, like an airbrushed pinup. Gorgeous, with just a hint of shimmer.
summary: Excellent, smooth finish with a hint of shimmer

reviewText: Incredible product. Finally someone is coming out with great products for blondes.
summary: Finally something that works for blondes.

reviewText:
This is a salon quality Oribe conditioner for blonde hair. Unlike traditional conditioners, this one is a spray rather than a cream/liquid. It consists of a fine purple mist that is sprayed on then rinsed out after three minutes.
It has a pleasant scent - nothing too strong or lingering.
After using a few weeks, I did not see much improvement when it comes to the claims of "repairing" damage to my color-treated hair. But it does condition well and keeps my hair from looking too brassy.
A downside for me is the application - I have used spray conditioners in the past, but these are usually the leave-in-type that I can apply (and control) once I am out of the shower. Using a spray in the shower is awkward for me and wastes too much product.
I did get better results by spraying into my hands and then distributing through my hair.
The price point is higher than other salon conditioners but it does work if you don't mind the cost.

My girl is blonde I am white haired, we are both using this, she feels her hair is looking as blonde as ever, it looks good to me, but I really can't
tell, but its her head...LOL  I like how my hair feels with the use of this, being my hair is white I've not noticed any blonde ;-) but, I have noticed my hair has not tried to yellow like a lot of white hair WILL do.  I might buy this for just my girl to use, but I won't continue with it, as it really was not made for white hair.  Shes very happy with it.
summary: ORIBE Bright Blonde Radiance and Repair

reviewText: I have a healthy head of hair even at age 83, and I've used this product on my hair.  It works well using after shampoo and conditioner and keeps my hair which is usually pretty tousled very manageable.  It works for me and I'm sure it works just as well or better for you gals.
summary: For women, but also works for us long haired guys

reviewText:
I was born blond and through the years my hair has darkened.
I have used this product and it has lightened my hair again  not to what it used to be but it is a shade that I am much happier with.
I shampoo my hair, then spray this on while I finish my shower then rinse this off in 3 minutes.
Its an easy product to use  it will not make you peroxide blond but will lighten your hair nicely.

This product left my looking beautiful and feeling great.  It gave it a lovely shine, which it usually lacks.  For reference, I have hip-length ash blonde hair, with a very, very fine texture.

I am allergic to many products, and this did not cause any irritation.  I also dislike smelly products, and there was no strong odor left on my hair.

The method of applying it, though, simply will not work for me.  This product comes in a small aerosol can.  Pressing the atomizer nozzle expels a very light mist over a small area.  So to cover my long hair, I had to pump and pump and pump, then pause to rest my hand, and then pump and pump, and then pause to rest my hand, over and over again.  It took forever and was frustrating.  It was also very difficult to tell which parts of my hair were treated and which weren't as the product leaves almost no change in feel on damp hair.

I suspect this little canister will only hold two or at most three treatments for my hair length, so if I wanted to continue using it, it would develop into a significant cost.

So, all in all, it is an excellent product, but probably only practical for those with shorter hair.  If Oribe were to come out with a better delivery system, I would love to continue using it.
summary: Love the product, not the spray can

reviewText:
I started using the ORIBE Bright Blonde Radiance and Repair Treatment when I went blonder for Spring. I was really hoping that it would help keep my blonde highlights blonde. The formula is a watery type liquid as opposed to creamy that you spray. It is purple in color like old-time violet treatments that my Mom used to use. You use this instead of your regular conditioner once a week. I was skeptical about using it instead of my conditioner since it has that watery consistency but surprisingly, it was conditioning to my hair. My hair is very coarse and it takes something moisturizing so I can even comb through after washing and I was able to after using this.

I don't dislike this product but I didn't feel like it did that much for my hair either in the conditioning department or for keeping my blonde looking blonde over other, cheaper hair products. It certainly isn't as effective as a hair mask for conditioning or even straight coconut oil which I love to use. I really couldn't tell much of a difference colorwise in my hair.
summary: Didn't Do Much for My Hair but Okay Product

reviewText: Generally speaking, I like to use fruit-scented products (either Garnier or VO5 or whatever I find on sale really), so I found this product to be a bit too "perfumey" for my taste. If you like a scented shampoo and but you *don't* want to smell like food, you will like this product. It is not a leave in conditioner. You merely mist it over your hair, leave it in for 3 minutes and then rinse it out. I don't know that I prefer a "mist" over just a gel or cream conditioner. I find it to be a little messier in my case, since I don't have great aim and tend to get more of it on the shower curtain than on my hair. It's also a little boring to stand dripping in the shower for 3 long minutes before I can rinse out. Aside from that, I think it's a good product. I didn't see a radical difference in my hair's radiance, but I've only used it a few times since the last time I dyed my hair a few days ago.
summary: Not a leave in conditioner; mist not gel.

reviewText:
While having a product that prevents a brassy shade of blonde is remarkable, I found ORIBE Bright Blonde Radiance and Repair most special because my hair didn't frizz. I have naturally curly hair with a fine texture. It looks best when I simply let it curl as it wants to. The biggest problem I have with my hair though is frizziness if I don't roll it or blow it dry in a straight style.. Most products I've tried weigh my hair down and leave it tired with a greasy look. This spray product eliminated the frizzes and kept my hair shining and curly. After using it two week, I've had numerous compliments. Someone said,  "I don't know what you are doing different, but your hair looks better."

I must say though that I'm not accustomed to paying this much money for a hair product. If it takes away my frizzy look, it is worth it.
summary: "I don't know what you are doing different, but your hair looks better."

reviewText: I have gray hair-- mostly white in the front, and it picks up yellow tints. I have used the nasty-smelling shampoo stylists love to send you to Sally Beauty for, but this is a vast improvement. You spray it on, which means you are probably concentrating it on the top/ outer hair, which has gotten more damaged and absorbed more off-colors. You can control where it goes---I don't need it on the back, and I don't need conditioning there, either. It smells like powdery vanilla honeysuckle, but I did not notice a lingering scent, unlike cheaper drugstore products. My one quibble is that it ran in my eyes and stung like the dickens for a bit---so be careful to keep your head tipped back when you use it.
summary: Great, but be careful when applying it.

reviewText: This product is a lightweight spray conditioner. I have to think that they decided on a spray because the product itself is purple (to combat brassiness) and they didn't want people to get it on their hands. I've used several of these purple products in the past and they all make my blonde highlights look brighter and more fresh. I did not like the spray application since I wash my hair in the shower and I can't see if I'm spraying my hair evenly. I ended up spraying some into my hands and running them through my hair to make sure it was distributed well.
summary: Good product, but dislike the spray application

reviewText: This comes out of the bottle purple but rinses clean and leaves my daughter's blonde hair the best she's ever had it. This is a wonderful product, easy to use and works very well. Very happy with this.

I love this - it works really well and absorbs into damp hair quickly.  I have left it on for the recommended time and rinsed out but I have also sprayed it on out of the shower and enjoyed the effect on taming and moisturizing me ends.  Also the violet tones have been fab for any brassiness.  I almost deducted a star for the application - it's a spray which is a bit annoying in the shower but then I thought about how much I hate oils that dump out and I use too much, the spray lets me apply the right amount.

I had high hopes for this Oribe product. Like other Oribe products, it has a nice scent. It was odd to have a spray conditioner to use in the shower and a little awkward to use. I followed instructions and left it in my hair for a few minutes before rinsing. The purple color of conditioner made my hair shiny and like other blond hair products, toned down brassy color. It fell short as a repair treatment though. The ends of my hair looked unruly after using the blow dryer. So, it helps with brightening color, but not with repairing hair.

You don't have to be blonde to benefit from ORIBE Bright Blonde Radiance and Repair.  It works for brunettes, too.  Since it's a spray I thought I would have trouble running a comb through my hair but I did not end up with tangles.  Not only that, it makes my hair feel soft. lightweight, and healthy.

My only beef is although the bottle has a great form factor (i.e., not cheap), it is slippery in the shower and hard to get a good grip for spraying my hair.
summary: My only beef is although the bottle has a great form factor (i

reviewText: This is my first use of a wash off spray hair conditioner and I'm finding it hard to apply evenly. I spray it around areas of my scalp then use my fingers to try to spread it around evenly. I am finding that the spray is harder to get an even application on all of my hair compared to a creme style hair conditioner. I have short hair too! I can't imagine trying to use this with shoulder length hair or long hair. Due to the uneven application I find it's effectiveness is different each day. I use this once a day which is the same as when I use creme style conditioner. I found that my creme hair conditioner (Sukin) did a better job conditioning my highlighted to blonde hair. I'll rate it 3 stars = It's Okay although that's perhaps being generous. The price is staggering to me at about three times what I am used to paying.

This Radiance and Repair product seems to work.  I really like that it's a spray on formulae as I worry sometimes with the "gloopy" stuff that I'll use too much and it will be a problem to rinse it all out.  You basically just shampoo as usual, rinse, and spritz this Oribe on your hair and leave it for about 3 minutes.  That's it - then rinse it out and towel dry as usual.

The product is blue and has almost no odor so it doesn't linger or oppose your cologne or fragrance.  I really like this because so many products today have a strong smell, this just has a very light clean aroma. I must admit that I'm put off by the price point which for my lifestyle is our of teach. But it does what it claims to do - it helps with split ends and make your hair soft and shiny.

I'm really very pleased with this treatment.  I got it because the ingredients are similar to those in a much more expensive product that I usually prefer.  It really works to brighten my hair.  They also have a great web site with some interesting and innovative products and how-to videos.  Very nice!
summary: Great new product for me that actually does brighten. I like the ingredients.  Be sure to see the videos on their web site.

reviewText: My hair has plenty of shine now. I was a little but leery of any hair product that is supposed to make my hair better, but this works. I shampooed with my regular one and then rinsed it out. Then I sprayed on my hair, actually I couldn't hear anything come out so I sprayed some in my hand next. The product is blue. Then I followed the directions and massaged it into my clean damp hair. I allowed three minutes and rinsed it out. I have never used dyes so I was mainly interested in the shine. Now my hair is happy with luster.
This with the Oribe Blonde shampoo is amazing. Keeps my hair from being brassy and builds up strength.
My hair has NEVER looked so amazing, thick and healthy!

I've used several facial oils over the past few years, from L'Occitane Anti-Aging Divine Youth Oil for a Youthful & Radiant Glow, 1 fl. oz. to Tarte Maracuja Oil - 1.7 Oz Full Size - New Formula. The only one worth using for me has been La Mer Renewal Oil, which is worth every penny (like most of their products). But I've heard wonderful things about Elemis, so was excited to try this one, especially since "superfoods" for the face seem to be the latest trendy thing. What I like: 1. Packaging. The bottle seals securely without leaking (this is huge if you travel, of course), and the dropper works well. Other oils I've had are harder to use, or leak, or don't dispense product easily - not so with this one. Works as intended. 2. Ingredients. Lots of great-sounding ingredients, no parabens or sulfates. What I don't like: 1. Doesn't absorb. I put one drop on each of three fingertips, patted my fingers together, and pressed into the eye, cheek, and neck area (same technique for any oil I'm using). This oil just seemed to sit there, and still felt oily an hour later. There was also still a visible sheen from the oil, so I'd only want to put this on at night. 2. Fragrance! I appreciate that the essential oils give a natural fragrance, but it's really strong and lasting. At least the fragrance isn't as fake-smelling as the L'Occitane oil, but it lingers and lingers... and lingers. I tried really hard to leave this on all day, but had to go wash my face just to get the smell away from my nose after a few hours. Maybe at night it wouldn't bother me as much, but if you're sensitive to fragrances, beware. If you're looking for a heavier facial oil, don't mind fragrance, and want these ingredients, specifically, this seems like a good choice with a focus on natural ingredients. But for something lighter-weight with similar benefits (and far cheaper), I'd rank the Tarte oil higher. The La Mer oil outdoes them all, though, if you can stomach the price tag.
summary: Doesn't absorb and very strong fragrance

reviewText: Love this oil.

It's difficult to review skin products since it's subjective.  I liked this oil fine, but it's really too heavy for my complexion since I have combination skin.  It leaves my skin feeling too oily, and I realize it's a facial oil, but some leave your face feeling hydrated without the oil feel.
summary: Too oily feeling for my combination skin

reviewText: So far so good. I need extra oil for my aging skin. My face looks more supple

Lee is Superfood Facial Oil helps keep my skin hydrated, glowing, and looking good. In the fall/winter my skin gets drier than the warmer months. Over the summer I was able to use the Elemis oil in the morning under my moisturizer/sunscreen. I have pale skin and need to use a product that has sunscreen in it. The oil takes a few minutes to absorb so I only used it under my moisturizer/sunscreen if I had time to let the oil sit and absorb. I could get away with using the oil at night time without an evening moisturizer. Now that it's fall I need to use a thicker evening moisturizer. So once again I only use the oil when it has time to absorb.

The oil does have a mild scent. It doesn't bothers me. The packaging is very nice. It feels like a thick sturdy expensive bottle. The dropper has a rounded tip making it feel more luxurious than a traditional dropper. Just a few drops covers my face, so this product has lasted me. If you are in the market for a new facial oil, I'd recommend trying the Elemis Superfood Facial Oil.

I admit to being fond of facial oil products. I really like using them at night and waking up to soft skin.
I found this one to be particularly nice. It's soaks right in. Kind of reminds me of Bio-Oil.
It might seem expensive, but a little drop goes a long long way. I also rub a tiny bit around my cuticles at night. I've noticed that they are less ragged and look a lot healthier.

reviewerName: Leah Maines, best-selling, award-winning author, actor, and editor
reviewText:
I first started using Elemis products several years ago when I purchase some body lotion and bath oils from the spa on a cruise ship.  The products are a bit expensive but well worth the money.  I've always been very pleased with their products.  This facial oil is fantastic.  I apply this at night on face and throat.  I don't like using it during the day because I've found my foundation doesn't seem to wear as well when I apply this under my makeup.
This product does not break out my skin.
Leaves my skin looking healthy and reduces lines.
Great for dry skin due to cold weather--it really moisturizes.
A little goes a long way.  I only need three drops to cover face and neck.

I don't like the strong scent.  It has a very strong scent that tends to linger.  If it had a milder scent, I would have given it a five star review.
summary: Strong scent but leaves skin radiant

reviewText: I got this product for my mom.  She uses several of the ELEMIS skincare line and loves ALL of them.  This ELEMIS Superfood Facial Oil is no different.  3 or 4 drops on her face is all it takes.  She loves the way it goes on easily, the way it feels and the results she gets using this and other ELEMIS items.  Small good looking bottle that sits on her makeup dresser.  Top has a squeeze baby dropper so it is easy getting the number of drops you wish to use.  She is very happy adding this to her ELEMIS line of products.
summary: Very Happy adding this to her ELEMIS line of products she uses.

reviewText:
A few drops (I usually use 5-6 drops, which is more than the 3-4 drop recommendation on the pamphlet) covers me face and neck. It smells quite strongly (my husband complains about that) but I assure him the box says it's all natural...

I don't feel this has made my skin feel more rejuvenated or healthier. The pores are just as big after a couple of weeks and wrinkles just as apparent. I tried wearing it in the morning when I wake up for work as well as right before bed (supposedly the skin does most of the repairing at night?) but all I can say is that when I do wear it out to work, it doesn't feel very heavy or greasy, and I do look more awake and have better color on my face, so whether or not it actually helps improve my skin is not as important if I use it as a "make me look more energetic and awake oil."
summary: pretty intense scent but not unpleasant

reviewText:
Pros:
Goes on easy - especially on slightly damp skin
Is all natural

reviewText:
Very nice, non-smelling oil that is easy to apply using the drop applicator.

I found that my very sensitive skin did not like the oil.  I did not break out into a rash, just didn't like how it felt.

Reading the ingredients that are all natural, I was surprised that my skin wasn't happy with this oil.  I did not rub it off, wore it all night, and did not see any rash develop.  So it didn't cause any problems with my skin.  I just didn't like how it felt.

Reading the package states so many benefits to my skin, that I might give it another try.

reviewText: I've been wary of trying facial oils because I thought oil would cause breakouts. But I've been hearing more about how beneficial facial oils are so I decided to jump in and try one. It's great! I actually love the scent, it's like an expensive perfume. And the texture is silky and doesn't feel heavy. No breakouts so far.  I love all of the superfood nutrition that my skin is absorbing with this oil. The bottle is small but you don't need a lot, only a few drops depending on how dry your skin is. It blends right in to my skin. The dropper is easy to use too. It will be easy to throw this in my makeup case for travel. I would recommend trying this if you've been on the fence about facial oils!

The first thing I noticed when I opened this was how small a bottle this was, compared to the price. Very small bottle, pretty big price, however, once I applied this, I realized just how little you need to use. I used about 2 1/2 drops and it covered my face and neck just fine. At that amount, the bottle really would last for a long time. Once on, it took a little while to absorb, but did eventually. I am not a big fan of the scent, it isn't awful, I just don't prefer it, although I rarely care about scent in the first place. After it was absorbed, my skin didn't feel oily, just hydrated, and it made my skin feel soft and smooth. I like products like this with special ingredients, and I am excited to continue use of this.
summary: (Eventually) absorbs well, leaves skin soft and smooth

reviewText:
I must confess, putting oil, even a super high quality one like this, on my face filled me with trepidation. What if I woke up with a rash or allergic reaction? But, I was concerned about nothing, as it's very gentle. Also, did not clog my pores.

The scent is perfect if you love aromatherapy...slightly herbal-floral-woodsy. I only noticed it when opening the bottle and on application. After it was on my skin I couldn't smell it anymore.

They say use four drops. I found two did the trick. So, the bottle will last a long time.

Definitely a great option if you have dry skin on your face and neck. I will use this more frequently in the winter when I also think it will protect my skin from the harsh weather.

For now, it will be a night time treatment.
summary: Overcame initial trepidation and like this.

I am already a fan of most Stila products.  But this was my first time trying this foundation product. I have their SPF moisturizer foundation and I loved that.  Stayed put and was great in FL sunshine for a Disney trip.  Was curious about this as it has that illuminator effect and I like that idea.

It feels a bit lighter than their other foundation, but I don't mind that as I like lighter make up and don't like heavy feeling things on my face.  Also don't like a heavy make-up look.  I like a natural looking make up that adds a bit of polish and glow.  This does the trick ... flawlessly.  Smooths out my skin tones (Irish scottish heritage with freckles and some uneven skin tones) doesn't hide my freckles (why would you do that?) but does add a bit of light and finish while blending some pink tones down a bit.

If you are looking for serious foundation coverage this is probably not for you.  It is not a heavy coverage type of thing, it is a evening and translucent type of light reflecting thing.  A nice glow with some light.  There is no actual sparkle in this, it is just lightens or makes the skin glow... like it is lit.  Very nice and youthful look.  You still need some SPF if you are in the sun.... as this is not an SPF product, which I also liked as if I am indoors all day I do not want nor need an SPF on my skin.  Thank you for that Stila!
summary: Beautiful lit polished effect that isn't heavy.
