StriVectin Multi-Action Restorative Cream-I have been using this cream for about five weeks and am pleased with the results. My skin feels softer and smoother. I feel as I continue to use it, I will enjoy even more positive results. I would give it 5 stars.

Cream has a very dense feel - a little bit goes a long way so just a small dab is enough once you work it in.  Does not have a greasy feel, is quickly absorbed by the skin and is very effective at moisturizing.  I really like that it also has a minimal scent.  Hard to really assess the claims of improving skin appearance past the moisturizing aspect.

I was sent a jar of this multi-active restorative cream for an honest review.

Ive been using it daily for about three weeks and can say that its a great moisturizer. My skin is of normal texture, however the skin on my eyelids is droopier than Id prefer. When I apply StriVectin, they look firmer for the duration of the daya good thing.

I love the creams emollience. Absorbs into the skin for a moist and refreshed feeling all day. Makeup is easy to apply over it, though I admit to using only brow pencil and eye shadow.

I would definitely consider this product as an everyday and always skin prep if it weren't for the price. That being said, I give it five stars because it really is a great product.

I was a bit disappointed when I received this LumaRx trimmer.  The design looks great but the plastic feels cheap and lightweight.  The trimming blade is relatively strong and it does come with a comb attachment which makes it ideal for trimming beards or mustaches but the overall construction always left me thinking that it would break.  Fortunately this has held up fairly well with moderate use but considering the price this should be better quality.
summary: Decent Trimmer But Overpriced Considering Its Build Quality

reviewText: Seems to work!  Reduces fine wrinkles on the neck pretty well. You may see some visible results in a day (we thought we saw some right after application, but that might have been wishful thinking), and certainly more visible results after a few days. Nothing to complain about.

This is a lightweight balm that is more like a highly hydrating cream. One small drop is all I needed to easily spread on my neck. It absorbs quickly and smells fantastic too. I don't think I have been using it long enough to see a big difference in my fine lines or maybe it is too hard to take before and after pictures of my neck close-up, but my neck does feel somewhat smoother after I use it, so I will keep using it.

A somewhat "perfumey" scented lotion type white balm in attractive packaging. It is supposed to help with anti aging of my neck area. First thing I have to say is that it could be a little more generously  portioned since it's for the entire neck area I need to use more of it than what I would normally disperse, for say, an eye cream. So seeing as how this product is only 1.6 oz I did not to get even a full month's use out of it when applying it everyday to the neck/throat area.

That being said I DO like the fact that it contains so many natural ingredients: sea Buckthorn, tree fern, mimosa flower extract, macadamia seed oil and padina pavonica among others. It feels good on my skin and I noticed NO sensitivities to it even though I normally do have fairly sensitive skin and rosacea.

This balm immediately helped my skin feel hydrated and moisturized. It's a little too expensive for me to buy as a regular beauty item. At almost $80 a bottle I could not afford this regimen just to keep my neck looking younger. So unless you have a pretty thick budget then this really wouldn't be a practical product for you. Four stars for a very luxurious product but minus a star for the exorbitant price and the fact that I didn't really see any results after using the entire bottle except for a smoother and  hydrated neck area.
summary: Nice product but not something I will rebuy.

reviewText:
I have been using Elemis Anti Wrinkle Day Cream for over a year now. If there is one thing I have learned, with Elemis products you will not see immediate results, but you will over time. How much time? For me, I began to see smoother skin in 3 months with their Day Cream.

As for this Elemis Pro-Collagen Neck & Decollete Balm, you need very little applied to the neck and upper chest area, and I find I get the best results if using their products at bed time. They claim you will see results in 1 month, but I never have. I've been using this for 3 weeks and so far no results, but I know I will see results in a couple months, as this is how Elemis products work.

My skin feels tighter in this month, but the lines and wrinkles are still here. I know Elemis products get rid of FINE lines and wrinkles, but do nothing for the deeper ones. I have yet to find any products that can get rid of deep wrinkles, so I'm even happy to see the fine ones less noticeable. It's even nice to have smoother, tighter skin in 3 weeks, wrinkles and all.
summary: With ELEMIS, You Need Time To Get Results

reviewText: I'm savvy enough to realize there is never going to be a wrinkle cream that truly takes off the years or erases wrinkles/lines.  However, I'm also vain enough to try anything new to just in case I'm wrong.  I have to admit that this is not a miracle cream, but I feel like when I apply this cream (I'm only using it on the neck area) that there seems to be just a touch more suppleness than prior to applying.  There are two things I don't love about the product, and the only reason I didn't give five stars.  First, the smell is rather strong.  It doesn't stink, but it reminds me of something an older female relative used to wear, and I can't quite place it, maybe something like an old Estee Lauder type of face lotion.  The other thing I don't love (but isn't keeping me from using it morning and night) is that is takes a rather long time to absorb, leaving my neck just a touch sticky, but it does eventually go away.  I think applying lightly is the key to this not being too big of a problem.
summary: Strong scent, somewhat thick and can leave skin sticky, but adds a suppleness to my neck, so I like it

reviewText: I like this item.  I am fairly young to be experiencing this issue but it never hurts to be forewarned and forearmed so they say.  It smells pleasant and I use it after every bath.  I do like to tan so it's probably for the best.
The smell is causing me headaches. If it were odorless I would like it better. On the up side, it does work.

I sure love the way this feels going on and the wonderful, deep tingle that radiates into my skin after about 30 seconds. I also love the way it moisturizes. It's true, I wake up looking smooth and well rested. I really do enjoy using this night cream, despite the slightly annoying dispenser and the need to shake it really thoroughly before every single use. I'm just not sure whether it's doing all the amazing anti-aging jazz that it claims to do. I use retinoids and Retin-A, and I know those work because there's a wealth of clinical trial data and decades of proof. But for the price of this stuff, is it a quasi-magical elixir of aging reversal? I doubt it. But it is a truly excellent night cream that I look forward to using. Does that justify the price? You be the judge.
summary: I absolutely adore this as a night cream, but is it magic?

reviewText: Loved the texture and how easily it absorbed.  Left the skin visibly luminous and supple.  Wonderful product!

I disregarded the pseudo scientific jargon in the description. I really don't expect skin creams to do all the things they claim,  I'm judging this on the basis of: does it moisturize without irritation or other negative effects?
The dispenser is actually irritating- the 2 sides do not dispense evenly, so one will run out faster. The cream itself has a heavier fragrance than I'd like. It is very moisturizing, on the verge of feeling oily. I'm surprised this is considered a day cream . I use it sparingly  at night on my slightly dry skin and I feel very moisturized.
Since it doesn't take much, it will last awhile. I'm not familiar with the company, but it seems you're paying a lot for the name and packaging. It's an effective moisturizer at too high a price.
summary: BEST FOR DRY SKIN. ANNOYING DISPENSER.

reviewText: I absolutely love ELEMIS BIOTEC Skin Energizing Night Cream - Skin Activating Night Cream.  It is nothing short of amazing, and given the price point, thats definitely a good thing.  Im in my forties, and my skin is drier and less resilient that it once was, but Im still subject to the occasional break-outs.  After using this night cream for several weeks, I can safely say its nothing short of amazing.  My skin is softer, more hydrated, and more youthful looking overall.  I tend towards sensitive skin, and a lot of skin care products cause breakouts and irritation.  However, this caused none.  ELEMIS BIOTEC Skin Energizing Night Cream - Skin Activating Night Cream simply made my skin look and feel amazing.  If you can afford the price, this product will not disappoint.

I was concerned that the unusual way this product is dispensed might prove unwieldy, but I have no problem with getting both components to come out of the bottle in the same amount at the same time.

From the first time I used the day cream, I could see results in that my skin tone looked more even and felt refreshed.
I find that this is not common for the first use of a product; creams such as this usually take a longer time to show improvement, if at all.

The one problem I have with this product is that it feels oily on my skin, and stays that way for quite some time.
The oiliness has no adverse effects, but it feels a bit unpleasant at first.
Using a little less than the amount recommended doesn't really help deal with the problem, and I don't want to use less than what will be effective.

Regardless, I will continue to use the product, because I like what I see in the mirror.
That's a big plus for someone over 60!

I am a man in my 50s, and consider myself well groomed, regularly trim hairs and nails, and don't mind paying for quality (either in terms of innovation or heirloom-like durability).

The Zwilling JA Henckels Grooming Set is well made, attractive, and somewhat functional, but at a very high purchase price and lack of ease of use (for the trimmer).

The nail clipper is well made, easy to use, and looks to be very durable.

The hair trimmer is also well made, but for me at least has proven to be impossible to use properly (without causing pain).  A regular battery operated trimmer is for me a better choice.

Very high priced, too.

Who, I wondered when I ordered this item from Vine, is the target audience for a grooming set this expensive? Hedge fund managers, self-made men who perform self-made manicures? Captains of industry who demand a precision-engineered German steel instrument for staging a hostile takeover of their unruly nose hairs? And what on earth could distinguish a nail clipper and nose hair trimmer enough to make it worth such an outlay?

Well, Im still not 100% certain who the intended audience is, but as soon as I tried this out, I knew why it costs so much. Its almost obscenely over-engineered. The sexy little instruments come nestled in an elegant black leather snap case. Slide them out one by one, savoring the cool matte finish steel. Test them out: The nail clipper is like a grown-up Transformer; the instrument is locked closed until you slide a panel down and then it springs open with Teutonic precision and the lever sides into place at the perfect angle for snipping. The blades are insanely razor sharp and meet perfectly, completely unlike their sloppy, common drugstore cousins. The nose hair trimmer spins manually, with a twist of the fingers, but its blades are so sharp they could trim a divot in a grizzly bears fur.

Using either of these instruments almost makes you feel unworthy in your dreary fleshly imperfection.

Id say this is the perfect personal grooming set for the venture capitalist who has everything, the cyborg who demands perfectly machined tolerances of less than .0005 mm in every instrument he touches, or Michelangelos David in his smooth, polished perfection.

As for me, I will continue to work on deserving this level of luxury and engineering, but I fear that as long as these instruments are tending to me, they will always be slumming, slicing away dutifully, stoically tolerating the lowly lot that has befallen them.
summary: Personal grooming for The Terminator, or Michelangelos David. You are probably unworthy

reviewText: They aren't kidding when they say these are compact and travel size! When the package arrived I couldn't imagine what was in it. This packet is maybe 3 inches in length and snaps to keep everything inside. It's cute...handy and all, but quite expensive in my opinion for what is offered.

This is a beautifully constructed grooming set. It includes a flat nail clipper with a built-in nail file, both packaged in a sturdy snapped case. It can be opened up quickly, at which point it becomes a slimline traditional nail clipper. There's enough torque here for fingernails, but you'll still want a traditional clipper for toenails or for greater precision with fingernails. I'd use this as a lightweight travel clipper. The ear/nose hair groomer is also very well engineered and can be quickly taken apart for cleaning. An electric groomer is somewhat easier to use, however, and provides greater capability in terms of removing all annoying hair. This device, again, is great for travel and is less bulky than most electric groomers, but doesn't quite provide the complete final appearance that I typically seek from the electric devices. So overall I like this as a travel bag addition or as a stocking stuffer.
summary: Very finely engineered and attractive travel set.

reviewText: Compact (deceptively so) and easy to use, and comes in a high quality travel case.  I could find no fault in either of these products.  Exactly as advertised, and easy to use.  Is the price high?  Maybe.  But, if you need a highly compact set for traveling, I recommend it.
summary: Great tools that are perfect for travel.

reviewText:
This set is no slouch.  Henckels quality of construction is evident in this set.  They are a good size and weight and come in an attractive case.  These are very giftable! The set includes a pair of slant tweezers, a nail file and nail clippers.  I have another of their sets that has scissors instead of clippers.  I prefer this set with the clippers for personal preference.  I have never been good with scissors.

The clippers are unique and require some practice.  They lay perfectly flat in the case and must be transformed to clip properly.  They even come with instructions.  I would hang onto the instructions initially until you get the hang of it.  It effort is worth it because these are the best clippers I have ever used.  I threw out all of my cheap drugstore clippers after using this one.

This is for sure a high end set.  The price is very high.  It wouldn't work for everyone's budget, but it is a quality set that will last and last.  The Henckels name stands for quality and that is definitely what you get.
summary: the best nail clippers I have ever used

reviewText:
I love Henckels quality. I grew up with a set of Henckels knives. When offered the three-piece grooming set for review, I jumped on it.

The set contains clippers that fold flat, tweezers and a sapphire file, all in a neat red leather case. Great for travel and daily outings where a little help might be needed.

That said, I found the clippers a little hard to figure out. Once I got them open and set up, I had more difficulty closing them flat again, however, Im sure Ill get this worked out in time. I am a bit hesitant to give this set the five-star rating Id like because of the clippers and the fact that they seem a bit light for thick fingernails. The quality, otherwise, is superb, so Im settling for four and one half stars.
summary: Very nice, attractive set. Love the Henckels quality

reviewText:
The clipper, nail file, and tweezers are a nice stainless steel. The slanted tweezers work well.  They grasp the hair and pull it from the root instead of just breaking it.  The nail file is wonderful.  One side is coarse and the other side is fine.  Both sides work extremely well to shape and seal nails.

The nail clipper, on the other hand, is a bit flimsy and hard to open.  It's also made of stainless steel, but it's so thin that its difficult to cut your nails. Unfortunately, the design is great but it falls short on functionality.  I find that it slips out of place.  I have long nails and I bent one of them when the nail clipper slipped out of position.  I won't be using it again.  I'll stick with my Trim nail clipper.

I wouldn't recommend this manicure set, unless you have very thin and fragile nails, especially at the current price of $99.
summary: Love the Tweezer and File, But Look Elsewhere for Nail Clipper.

reviewText: This 3-piece manicure set gives you maximum portability.  The most amazing is the nail clipper that is almost as thin as a credit card.  This is what McGyver might be using if he is cutting his nails.  It is completely flat until you slide it with your thumb and it springs up into a nail clipper.  You have to pull the top to lock, though.  It is very sharp.  The quality is superb.  Still, I think the tag is pretty steep for this set to be a tad below a hundred bucks.  Of course, it comes with a red case protective case.

This is a really nice manicure kit. It comes in a red leather pouch with a good snap. Each piece is durable and well-designed. The tweezers have good spring and are not too strong to make your fingers hurt. The file has a heavy handle making it easier to use. The clippers are low-profile and will fold flat. They are more square than most, but it works well for this. My wife loves this and it's great to stash in a purse or travel bag. It's definitely a bit pricier than other options, but it's a great gift and feels like good quality.

Everything about this set is top notch. The kit comes double packaged in a box and sleeve so it would make a nice gift. Inside is a handsome leather case with a snap closure. The nail clippers are super sharp but the style takes a little getting used to since they lay completely flat when not in use. The nail file is great. Nothing like the cheapie ones you get in other kits. The tweezers are strong and very precise. A great kit for a travel bag, purse, or household.

AMAZING QUALITY.  The precision and sharpness of these grooming tools is the best I have ever used.  Each piece is very substantial without being too heavy for comfort.  The set comes beautifully boxed in a leatherette case with a secure sleeve to hold each implement in place for safe storage or travel.  The overall size of the case is just perfect to slide in a purse, briefcase, or even a jacket pocket.  I believe that if you place the implements securely in the case after each use, they will last for years to come!  This would make an outstanding gift for that very difficult to buy for man or woman in your life.  The set makes a beautiful presentation and impression, and I know the recipient will be thrilled with the quality of the tools.
summary: The precision and sharpness of these grooming tools is the best I have ever used.

reviewText:
Henckel has maintained a stellar reputation, which is both a blessing and a curse. It's a blessing because consumers know that they are getting a certain level of quality with their purchase, but it also means that they have a reputation to live up to. This 5 piece grooming set is a worthy addition to the brand.

The stand-out piece is the collapsable nail trimmers, which have been around for a while. They collapse to an impossibly flat position, but they work as well - if not better - than any other pair I've tried. The scissors are sharp, with a blunted safety tip, and they meet neatly at the center with no gaps, so you get a clean trim. The nail file has a fine enough grain that it doesn't tear up damaged nails, with a sturdy grip section so you can maneuver. The cuticle pusher/cleaner has a nice weight, with a clean, smooth edge. The tweezers grip firmly, no slipping hairs. There isn't a fault with a single piece in this set. The case that it comes in is a little cheap feeling in the leather finish, but the clasp and seating of the pieces is top-notch.

If you are looking for a nice gift, a quality travel set or just a home set that will last a lifetime, check this set out.

Ah, the best of two worlds:  Italian leather and German precision.  The J.A. Henckels grooming kit does seem to have it all.

The compact case is smooth black Italian leather.

And the five components are made of stainless steel.  The ingenious nail clippers are designed to fold flat and are quite sharp.  The tweezers are slanted for precise use, and the nose and ear hair scissors boast a rounded safety end.  Theres a single tool for cuticles and nail cleaning.  And theres a sapphire nail file.  (Everything Ive ever read warned against using metal files as they're too rough for most nails, and I doubt that Ill ever try this one. Others may like it.)

Its attractively packaged and I assume designed for the gift market.

On a personal level, I find the nail clippers inconvenient to breakdown to store and the nail file useless.  But it would make an upscale gift for a traveler.
summary: The Upscale Way to Clip Nails....

reviewText:
I'm a guy with bad nails. I'm trying to get better and kick some bad habits (chomp, chomp). This is a perfect thing to help - it's a perfect little grooming kit, that screams quality from the beginning, and looks like something you'd want to give for a graduation present.

Pros:
- This will last you forever. I would have no worries about this holding up forever.
- The parts are all extremely high quality. The nail clippers fold flat, and are very innovative on how they come out and work. It took me a moment, but I'm impressed.

Cons:
- It's very expensive. $40 per piece, if you look at it that way.

This is really nice. I have used the entire stelatopia line for my son with eczema, so I still prefer their cleansing cream, but this is very nice, too. Cleanses without stripping and feels very nourishing. Doesn't leave the skin taught-feeling. If your baby simply has dry skin, this is an excellent product. I would still follow it up with lotion/cream after bathing, but some probably won't feel the need to. The fragrance is very nice, also. It's hard to find a bad product from Mustela.

This is a nice set of 3 colors which would serve many skin tones, with the possible exception of olive or yellow toned skin. I have fair skin and found the darkest color to be too dark, but the other two work well for shading or highlighting the cheek area. Even so, I had to use the middle color sparingly.

The product is a baked powder, not a cream, and although the package is small- and fits easily into a makeup kit- the amount of powder in the pans is generous. There is no brush or sponge included, but it does have a handy mirror for using this on the go.

Currently at $32, this is overpriced compared to other contour sets and the quality not better to warrant the higher price. 3 stars.

My product came with the directions covered up due to the Amazon sticker.  I had no idea how to use it and the directions aren't inside.  Here they are from Blissworld

Step 1
Apply medium and darker shades to the hollow of the cheeks and anywhere the sun naturally hits you.

Step 2
Apply the lighter shade as a highlight along cheekbones, the bridge of the nose and cupids bow.

There is a contour brush that you can use with it.  I used my index finger and though probably not the best tool, it worked for me.  I applied it after I applied my foundation and saw a difference.  Another time I applied it after applying my tinted moisturizer.  Also made a big difference.

I deducted a star because there were no instructions plus it didn't come with a contour brush.  For the price a brush that fits inside the compact would be appropriate.

It goes on quite dry but did not cake either which was a positive.
summary: Made a Difference, Fun To Use and Expensive

reviewText:
It is sometimes difficult to please a teen age daughter.  Clothes as a gift?  Ha!  Like a dad can choose something she would wear?  Shoes...the same.  Jewelry...believe is or not, sometimes I do ok.  Make up?  Never.  Not a chance.  But who doesn't like a challenge.  I ordered this palette from Vine...for free of course...handed it to her...she opened the box and grinned.

She loved the colors, the case, the size.

I am a Hero!  Thanks, Vine

I'm a newbie to any kind of sculpting on my face other than adding blush over my liquid makeup....that's it!  Being retired means I don't go out every day, so there is no need to add any embellishments to my daily regimen.  I do like to have fun trying new ideas, so here we are giving this bliss contour palette, a go!  8:30am: Just finished applying everything, and I think I look pretty good.  My husband was amused because I looked so different, ready for a party!  The palette of colors are quite nice, and apply evenly and smoothly on the cheek hollows, cheekbones, nose, around eyes and brow, chin, and forehead.  The darkest color is actually a tad too dark for me, so used that one sparingly on the hollows of my cheeks.  I'm not too concerned about the pans being small, as I will be using this sculpting palette very little anyway.  Overall, this seems to be a nice product for those that love to experiment on different looks.  Enjoy and have fun ladies, and as the bliss mirror says "you're so define".
summary: Lovely contour palette for having fun with sculpting your chic look!

reviewText: This is a sweet little contour palette with a mirror inside that says "you're so define" and is compact enough to fit in a small cosmetic bag in my purse. My makeup routine is so simple most days (undereye concealer, foundation, blush, mascara and lipstick) and I've never used contour makeup, so I wasn't sure what to expect as to texture, application or results. The texture of this makeup is dry, but it has a velvety smooth feel like premium eye shadow. I assume it's best applied with a contour brush, but since I don't have one I've been using a small rounded blush brush that works fine for picking up product and blending it evenly into my skin. As to results, I'm pleasantly surprised as this contour makeup is flattering as it really does redefine the structure of my face. I'm using a touch of the darkest shade (which is quite dark compared to my fair skin) blended with the medium shade in my cheek hollows and the lighter color on my cheekbones, and it creates the illusion that I have more defined, higher cheekbones. Plus, my face actually looks about 5 pounds thinner, and this makeup blends nicely for a natural look. I really like this contour pallette by Bliss and definitely recommend giving it a try.
summary: Nice Product That Creates The Illusion That I Have More Defined, Higher Cheekbones And Slims My Face Too

reviewText: While I don't usually use contouring shades except on my eyes this is a great trio of shades. The powders are soft and silky and blend easily. My only complaint would be if I am going to spend this amount on make-up it should either have a brush to apply with or at least a place in the compact to put your own.
summary: ... contouring shades except on my eyes this is a great trio of shades

reviewText:
This is a really nice contouring palette, with a few flaws.  It's smaller than I thought it would be (it's about the size of an eyeshadow palette), and I guess that's because it's meant to be used on-the-go. It contains two contour colors and a highlighter color.

The two problems with that, though, are that the latch that keeps this closed is not very strong, so it's likely to come up easily if you leave it in your purse, and the pans are so small that it's hard to get a brush into each one precisely.

The colors in this have nice color payoff and go on smoothly.  Powder contours can sometimes settle into my dry skin, but this doesn't, especially if used over a foundation primer and foundation.

My box had the directions covered by a sticker and Amazon isn't listing them here, so here they are, as copied from the Bliss website:

"For the perfect sculpted look, apply medium and darker shades to the hollow of the cheeks and anywhere the sun naturally hits you. Apply the lighter shade as a highlight along cheekbones, the bridge of the nose and cupids bow."

For a similar price point, I'd recommend contour palettes by Kat Von D or Smashbox, or even just a single pan of contour, because two different contour colors actually feels like a bit of overkill to me.
summary: Good color payoff, but for the price, there are better brands out there

reviewText:
This is a nice little contouring set. The powder goes on nicely.  The first shade is very light, but all could also be used for eyeshadow or on your face, neck.
The size is perfect to carry with you, except then you would also need to carry a brush; there is no room for one in this case. Even at home you will need a small brush. It seems most contouring is done with larger brushes that would way overwhelm the little squares in this palette.

Those who enjoy contouring (especially for evening, since it is most effective in evening light) should find this high-quality palette to be useful. It is relatively expensive, and the amounts provided are small, but they are adequate for the presumably small number of occasions for which they would be used. (Contouring in three blends is not a daytime staple.) The products are gentle on the skin, blend well, and are an excellent combination for the highlighting and shading one would desire.

I tend to wear greys, purples and browns for my eye color, but I was surprised how much I like these shades. They were a bit lighter than I'm used to as I don't were rose tones, but I was happy with the overall result and would wear these shades on weekends and for casual days. For an evening out, I'd want darker shades, but these were not too light and looked really good.
summary: A nice set of rose shades that aren't too light

reviewText: I don't use makeup on a daily basis.  This 4 color palette doesn't stand out but it has the basic neutrals that I need - cream, pink, light brown and dark brown.  The colors have quite a lot more shimmer/frost than I usually use.  They are smooth and were easy to apply.  I did have to reapply the makeup several times.

The colors in this 4 quad eye shadow palette are beautiful.  They picked colors that would work well together.  You could go with the brown, or the pink combination if you used just the two shades. You could also use all four shades if you desired. All four shades have a lot of shimmer in them.  This is not a matte palette at all.  I wished at least one of the shades would have been matte.

These are not highly pigmented, so this palette is great for beginners or people who do not want anything too extreme.  I thought the palette was ok, but there was nothing remarkable about it.
summary: Pretty colors, great for a beginner

reviewText: The ad for this product notes that the eye shadow is "richly pigmented" but I cannot say I agree with that.  I found the colors to be very light, almost translucent in character.  I don't think this particular product is worth the price and I would suggest using something from the drug store like Maybelline or L'Oreal.  Note, I did try another product from this same company, a bronzer, and it worked very well so I guess you just need to try these makeup products individually and not necessarily judge the line as a whole.

All of the fours colors featured in the pictures are just as they appear in person. Very easy to apply be itself or mixed together to achieve an more dramatic effect. Also, I liked that the color did not fly around too much to the next one. Although, it would have been nice to have an applicator come with this palette. Yet, other than not having one I am pretty happy with this kit.
This palette is small but has nice color assortment. The colors are very pigmented, and the shadows are easy to blend and soft and buttery. The shimmer isn't too glittery, just a perfect glow.
summary: Soft, shimmery, and easy to blend

reviewText: I've tried many Bliss skin care products in the past and have always liked the fact that they are lighter than most and never cause any irritation.  The Empowder Me Buildable Powder Foundation is another quality product.  The difference is the moisturizer that is added to the powder so that it can be applied smoothly and evenly.  I don't like to wear a lot of heavy makeup, so this is perfect.  I use it in the morning, and I'm good to go for the rest of the day.  Pair with your favorite concealer, and this provides all the coverage you need. The literature claims that this can be applied wet or dry, but I only have tried the dry application, and that works for me.  Bliss really touts their "spa-powered" ingredients, and I think these are what make the difference.  Alone or with your favorite liquid foundation, the Bliss powder is light, non-irritating, and goes on smoothly.

Well, I received the "Natural" color of this product, and from the picture, it looks pretty normal, but I clearly don't have what they consider natural skin tone.  I tried using it dry first and it seemed almost too powdery, did not really go on smoothly, at least not as nicely as some other powders I use.  Then I tried using it with a damp brush as one might do with a liquid foundation.  As I was putting it on, it reminded me of Trump in his early campaign, that orange-ish color that  showed up on his face when he was on TV.  I can't say I was particularly enthralled with that look on me.  I brushed it on to a thin layer and it covered well enough, but then I felt I should put another layer of a different powder/color on so as to look more like myself.

Perhaps with the right color, I would have been more pleased, but I didn't feel this product was superior to other makeup products I had, so I will stick with what I know works. (i.e. love the Laura Gellar and Lancome foundations).  I do have older skin, and I didn't feel it did a lot to make me look younger.  I would be leery of buying this without being to actually test it, as the color was not what I expected from the picture.
summary: Not what I expected, probably best if your skin is young and flawless.

reviewText: This product is pretty much everything I hate about high-end cosmetics rolled into one annoying applicator. They create a fancy "cute" delivery system when a regular tube would have been easier and better, the company makes overblown claims and creates fancy words that sound rich and effective, but boil down to basic old-time ingredients that are easily purchased for much less in other brands. Basically this is titanium dioxide with some nice added scents. Titanium dioxide has this great reflective property and opacity - they add it to light colored paints to make them opaque and reflective - giving a room a brighter look. Used as a makeup primer you can get the same effect, it reflects light to make your face look brighter and more youthful, and also adds an opaque "mask" to somewhat hide blemishes without having to add a bunch of heavy foundation over the top. It also has the added bonus of being a decent sunscreen. Many of the "mineral" makeup companies use this naturally occurring mineral. The downside to titanium dioxide is that in flash photos it fluoresces white - which can lead to some weird results (do a Google search on titanium dioxide makeup photos and you'll see a variety of movie stars showing this effect). So, why use it? Because it has a long history of human use and is considered very safe, as opposed to some of the more recent chemical-based sunscreens, and it requires much less product to achieve opacity. Next question is why should you pay more money for this particular iteration when you can purchase something similar at your local drugstore for less than a third the price? I've used Physicians Formula Mineral Wear Talc-Free Mineral Correcting Primer, Green, 0.5 Ounce for a few years and think it works well to hide redness and other minor skin issues. It goes on light, doesn't feel oily, and seems to keep my makeup in place a few hours longer. bliss Mad About goes on a little heavier and feels a little tacky when wet. Once dried it doesn't add any heaviness and feels sort of powdery, it also seems to keep my makeup in place a few hours longer. In use, I see no difference between these two products, and the Physicians Formula does a better job at reducing redness and evening out my skin tone. Third question is, if a company can't even get the bottle right, why should I trust the product? This is 1 oz. of product in a container weighing over 2 ounces, that has an applicator that won't allow you to access the all of the product unless you break the container, but that's not the worst issue I have with it -- The tube has a major manufacturing flaw - the "ON" arrow points the wrong direction, meaning when you twist the cap to "on", the container is closed. Twist to "off" and you may be able to squeeze out a thread-thin stream of product - or maybe not. If the tip gets even slightly clogged it's nearly impossible to get things going again. So, does it work? Yes, but there are other products available at less than a third the cost that are the same or better, and even at that cheap price they actually have an applicator that works!
summary: All show and no go - literally

reviewText:
A primer with a sunscreen in it sounds very nice.  I have tried quite a few primers, but this is the first one I have used that comes out looking white, like a regular lotion.  It is thick enough to spread over the face with your fingers, whereas others I have to use a brush application to apply as they are more of a gel/liquid.  This is a very smooth, slick feeling primer, and I do feel it fills in those pesky pores in my face and makes my skin look better and smoother.  It does leave the slightest white tint from the sunscreen, but with either powder or liquid foundation, that was covered over.  It has no offending odor to it either.

But yes, that cap they decided to put on it.  Who's idea was that?  Mine doesn't seem to cause a mess like others have experienced, but the primer does not come out as easy as it should.  Not a deal breaker in my book, but it wins no points.

I prefer this primer over my several Smashbox ones that don't seem to leave my face looking smoother.  I would place this on the same level as a new Lancome LaBase primer I have that also fills in pores nicely, without irritation.  Still, for the summer and when I am outside, I would choose a primer that has some sunscreen in it.
summary: The sunscreen properties make this a great option for the summer, fills in pores, very smooth feeling, easy to apply

reviewText:
A little about me first:  I am NOT someone who uses a foundation every day, or hardly ever!  If it's a special occasion (wedding, etc.), I might pull out a tinted moisturizer or light base, but that's about it.  So why would I want to try a primer?  Well, when I'm out in the sun, I do try to use a product with SPF on my face.  Also, because my skin tends towards oily, with large pores, I do prefer something that might give me a bit of coverage in those situations, especially if I'll be at a pool/beach/similar and not wearing much other makeup.

The first thing about this product is that the container is confusing!  You pull off the cap--okay, I got that.  Then, you have to twist the inner cap 180 degrees, going from where it says "off" to "on"--this is very hard to see, as the writing is embossed.  Once I did that, I was still not able to dispense the product; I thought I had done something wrong!  It took me awhile to realize that I just had to get the product started by shaking it down to the end of the tube and squeezing a bit.

Eventually, I was able to produce some product.  To my surprise, it is white; I guess I was expecting more of a tinted moisturizer.  When I first used the toner, I LOVED it!  It seemed to give my skin a luminous quality and to actually reduce the appearance of my dark undereye circles, something I can usually only control with moisturizer.  I was so happy--I quickly applied this to my entire face!  Unfortunately, I soon saw why this is meant more as a primer, not a stand-alone product.  When applied to my whole face, I thought it made my face look somewhat unnatural.  Furthermore, over the course of the day, it felt heavy on my face (this is why I don't generally wear foundation!), and it made my face oiler rather than helped to control oil.

I find if I just use a bit of this product in my eye area, it is helpful--it does improve the look of my dark circles, and it also seems to help my eye shadow to adhere/last longer.  But it feels to heavy for me to use all over, either with or without foundation, and I personally would not recommend it for this purpose.
summary: Luminous qualities, but felt heavy when applied all-over

reviewText:
I use a variety of primers, lately ones that have a bit of 'dewy' effect to them, but I do like the added sunscreen to this. bliss' Mad About Smooth Smoothing SPF 15 primer is supposed to have a 'plush' feel to it, and yes, it does. It's almost powdery on the face, giving your skin a velvet feel to it, and I didn't notice any odd scent or paleness to my skin (then again, I'm pale. It's often remarked to me, this fact).

The bottle is a little odd, you've got a bit silver cap and you have to 'twist' the nozzle from 'off' to 'on' to get the primer (a thick white liquid) out, probably to keep it from oxidizing or something. I don't have any problems with this, though yeah, a pump would be nice.  Instructions read to use a liberal amount, probably because of the sunscreen, though with other primers they say not to, but I don't notice any adverse effect with my liquid foundation or setting powder when I use them. Again, it gives a plush feel to my skin, and does help fill in the one or two areas where I have larger pores (nostril area). Makeup goes on well, and it helps to stay on all day, even in this awful hot summer. I haven't had any adverse reactions to it, my face doesn't feel like it's drowning beneath product, so I don't have any complaints about this product. All in all, think it's one of the better primers I've used, especially if you don't want the 'dewy' effect.
summary: very effective primer, makes your skin feel very smooth

reviewText:
As a makeup artist, I have the opportunity to use a wide array of makeup primers.  Everyone has different skin and each primer suits someone else differently.  I was intrigued by this primer so agreed to take it for a run.  So far, it is okay, but there are a few things I do not like about it.

WHAT IS THIS PRIMER LIKE?
Mad About Smooth primer by Bliss comes in a unique tube.  It has a very large silver cap and the inside has a pointed very large tip to it.  To rotate the top is to open the bottle so that you can squeeze a little primer on your finger.  To close, you rotate back into place and pop on the cap.  That is interesting and different.  Unfortunately, the bottle does not stay standing up at all- so it will have to lay flat in a drawer or on top of counter/vanity.

The primer itself is a little bit like highly diluted Elmer's glue in texture.  It has a smoothness to it, but it is almost tacky too.  It clearly has sunscreen in it- so much so that there is a white tint to this product.  A little does go a long way- so be sure not to over apply.

HOW DOES THIS PRIMER PERFORM?
This primer goes on the skin pretty smoothly.  It does, however seem tacky.  I have tried this over and over in recent days, but unfortunately, we are having extremely hot and humid weather so everything feels a bit off.  I have to say that I have normal to dry skin, but if it feels this way to me, I can not see anyone with oily skin using this with great success either.

APPLICATION
As for application, this is easy to apply.  It is concentrated so don't apply too much. It also has a white tint to it so that it does add a ghost like feel to the skin.  This is also a problem when it comes to photos.  If you use this under foundation, you will get flashback- you know, those photos of people you see and wonder why their face is white but the rest of them a different color..

SMOOTHNESS
This does leave the skin with a smoother feel to it due to the "cones" in it.  This is handy if you want to make the skin surface look a bit more smooth under foundation.  Alone it would not serve a purpose.

FOUNDATION
This primer has a tacky feel to it.  It just feels like Elmer's glue just before it is totally dry, but more diluted, if THAT makes sense.  When applying foundation over top of it, it does help it stick better in high humidity, but it does keep the foundation with a tacky feel too.  I am not sure if this is due to the high humidity and heat or not.  I will update after the weather changes in the autumn time.  Foundation does not seem to stay on any longer, but it does stay on.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Although this primer does leave a smooth finish as promised, and has sunscreen in it which it also promises, I think I would prefer it to be less tacky with no sunscreen in it to avoid flashback in photos.  It would be better to offer it without sunscreen to let everyone make their own choice if they want to use it or not.  The bottle is unique, but does not stand up, so it will have to lie down in a drawer or on top of a vanity.  The texture does help foundation stay on at first, but seems to stay tacky in humid hot weather.  Since we have no end of hot weather in sight, I will be updating this in the fall and testing one more time with the change of season to see if I have a different result

For now I am giving this three stars, but will update in the fall/autumn.
summary: Smoothing With Sunscreen, But Tacky Texture and Photo Flashback Can Annoy

reviewText:
Ive used primers in the past and have never seen much of an improvement.  Even with Clinique and Elizabeth Arden primers my makeup seams to evaporate from my face within a few hours.  But I have found that this Bliss primer actually does something.  When I use the Bliss primer I find that I still have makeup on my face when I get home from work (about 12 hours after application).  My face gets very oily, and I find that the Bliss also holds down the shine amazingly well.  The Bliss keeps my makeup looking matte and uniform all day.

So 5 stars for the primer itself, but I don't like the sunscreen component as much.  The cream has a very white, opaque look that gives my skin a ghostly appearance.  Once I put the makeup on my color is fine, but this Primer is not something you could use without applying a serious amount of foundation on top of it.  The dispenser design is another big miss.  When I first opened the box I found that half the contents had leaked out.  Primer covered the inside of the box and the cap.  The dispenser has a twisting top that lets you turn the dispenser On or Off, but regardless of how I have it set, primer will come out if the bottle is squeezed.

I do like this primer so I probably buy it again, but I wish they would re-think the design of the dispenser.
summary: The primer keeps my foundation looking fresh for hours, but the design of dispenser is a big miss

reviewText: I thought this would have some color to it when I ordered it. But, what I got does not. It is sort of gray in color. Once I put it on, it was invisible. The packaging emphasizes that it is a sunscreen PF 15, which is great. However, it says it is a "primer" maybe I live a tool sheltered life, but I don't know what a primer is. I put it on under my makeup and the makeup went on smooth as silk. Other than that, I'm not sure what else to do with it. I'll have to investigate it on the Internet because the packaging doesn't tell you, nor does the description here on Amazon help much. If you know, please tell me!

I've been watching loads of makeup tutorials on YouTube, and never being the girl or teen or young adult who knew what the fudge she was doing with makeup, I've decided to try to learn how to do my own makeup properly. I have rosacea, which I am maintaining with creams and lotions, so I need a product that doesn't tear up my skin, gives me protection from the sun, and looks good under makeup.

bliss Mad About Smooth Smoothing Primer SPF 15 doesn't have quite the SPF strength that I've used previously (the other brand is 46), but it doesn't irritate my skin, does still have SPF and also smooths my makeup out nicely.

The design of the bottle was strange. You remove a lid, THEN twist the top, and THEN must squeeze, quite hard, to get the product out. Be careful, or you might end up with more than you need - and I only needed a small pinkie-nail sized amount (probably less actually) to cover my whole face. It has no noticeable or "icky" odor, it applies SMOOTHly (ha ha!), and applying makeup (foundation) on top is a breeze.

I honestly don't know, though, if I could afford the price. Amazon's price right now is $32, which seems higher than I've spent for primer (though being a newb to this makeup stuff, maybe I'm wrong).

Brought to you by:
*C.S. Light*
summary: Tough bottle to crack, product works for me

reviewText: Even though the box for the actual product was mint and undamaged, when I opened the container, there was primer all over inside the lid and on the thick, spatula like applicator. So, a little was lost here. Then, trying to get it out of the container in a clean, sensible manner was not exactly easy. The delivery system here is so deeply flawed. (I really like JAPONESQUE Velvet Touch Primer. I have used it for a little over a year with spectacular results. And, the pump bottle means the product stays clean and the amount is very much controlled). Now, I was concerned when I saw the white hue and the somewhat thick quality of the product. (And, it does smell distinctly like sunscreen). Nonetheless, if one really takes one's time and works this into the skin, it will disappear and provide a nice, smooth base for foundation. (I used this with Bare Minerals Complexion Rescue Tinted Hydrating Gel Cream Broad Spectrum SPF 30 ... it ended up looking lovely). Overall, I think my Japonesque primer is more effortless and provides a better effect. So, while I will be sticking with that, I do like the sunscreen element of this product. If the container were better, I think this would be a smashing success.

I am a firm believer that you get what you pay for. Yes, the price for bliss On the Line Liquid Liner is more than you would pay at the drugstore, but the quality is much better. With Bliss, it is quick and easy to flawlessly apply eye liner. It does not smudge and it dries quickly, which makes it an easy switch for those like me, who normally use pencil liner. What I love most is that even with my watery eyes (due to contact wear and allergies), it stays put all day long, yet is easy to remove at the end of the evening. So glad I discovered this product.

Wow. This eyeliner is like none I have every used before.  The liquid-ness of it means that it dries on and stays on.  Generally, my eyeliner has worn off within a few hours.  I've worn this several times now and I can wear it all day and it will still be going strong.  It's quite dark - a true black, compared to the pencil shade of black that I'm used to. It's very easy to apply, but don't press too firmly unless you want a VERY thick line.

Overall, I really like this liner and plan to try it in other colors. Very pleased!

This is my teenager's dream eyeliner.  A rich black formula that goes on smoothly and precisely.  Perfect for executing the very hip cat eye. You even have a few seconds after application to do a little blending before the liner sets and is virtually smudge proof. I do have some concerns about using any makeup made in China and did not realize this product originated there or I probably would not have selected this item to review as part of Amazon's Vine program. My other criticism is about the cost of this eyeliner.  I'm not sure it's worth $10 more than the good quality $10-$12 eyeliner that is sold by other cosmetics companies at your neighborhood big box store.

While the product draws a very fine line, the print on the packaging is so tiny that it is almost impossible to read even with reading glasses. Using a magnifying glass I discovered three disturbing things: the item is made in China: it is not tested by dermatologists and may cause irritation: it does not carry the Cruelty-Free label.

These are very important issues and I am washing this eyeliner off right now because my eyelid is beginning to itch.
summary: Made in China and not Cruelty-Free - caused irritation

reviewText:
I like this eyeliner because I can get a nice thin line close to my eyelashes. It stays wet long enough that I can use the broken stem  of a QTip to wipe away most mistakes. (I break them in half to use the stem to clean up mascara smudges too).
Even though this Bliss eyeliner is easier to use than other liners I've tried, I still need more practice.
I like to apply thin lines, but you can can get thicker lines my angling the tip.  This is a liquid liner and doesn't have a smudgy appearance.  It washes off with soap and water and doesn't irritate my eyes.
summary: Can be used to apply thin lines and thicker lines. East to remove.  Doesn't irritate my eyes.

reviewText: I'm not a huge fan of foundation and use it sparingly, as needed and where needed. I wanted to love this particular brand but it wasn't all that great. It does go on light and if you have a foundation brush it really blends in well, but by mid day my skin was so oily and I felt like most of the foundation had evaporated. When applied properly it doesn't crease, which is always nice and there have been no skin irritations. But for this price range I guess I expected better. I have used foundation much cheaper that this and found it to work better. Maybe for the right person/right skin type it might work better. I will most likely not purchase again.

reviewerName: Meryl K. Evans, Digital Marketing Pro
reviewText:
I could not figure out how to use the dropper and the instructions said nothing about it. I don't see the point as it's messier than pouring foundation into your hand. In fact, the dropper spilled a drop on my outfit and stained it to the point it was worrisome whether it'd come out. It did. The reason it took work to get it out is because this has zinc oxide (for the sun protection). So you may want to be sure you're over the sink when applying it and not wearing your best clothes.

The color worked well for my pale skin and it made my face look even as best as it can. No product can make it look completely even. The scent was practically non-existent, which should please a lot of folks.

If you're using this for SPF protection, you'll need to reapply every two hours. Most people I know don't reapply foundation that often. So the SPF benefit isn't a great one as it'll mess up your blush. Better to use a clear lotion for SPF than foundation that is supposed to be the make up base. The button on top of the dropper isn't easy to press. Bliss needs to redesign the bottle to make it easier to apply without worrying about messes. I wouldn't count on this for sun protection unless I know I won't be gone more than two hours.
summary: Nice color and lightness, but bottle design makes it messy to use

reviewText:
I thought from the name and the description of combining skin care and foundation, that it would be more like a tinted moisturizer.  But I think sun protection is the primary skin care ingredient.  That's not a bad thing.  I remember years ago reading articles bemoaning the fact that no cosmetics companies put SPF protection into foundation.

The problem for me is that I like to wear my foundation in a very sheet layer so this doesn't give me much sun protection.  Still, a little is better than none.

Take you time when you get this because I found the bottle impossible to figure out and broke the top trying to get it open.  The little bump you see in the picture at the top is a plunger type button and I kept pushing it thinking the foundation would come out somewhere.  I couldn't figure out how to get the silver cap off and that's what I broke.  The inner cap still works but try not to mess it up like I did.

This foundation is a little more "slippery" than the tinted moisturizer I had been wearing and it took a few tries to get it on at the sheer coverage level I like.  I think using a sponge applicator to blend it would be helpful.

And finally, I think you should figure out your shade in person before ordering online.  I was expecting this to be a little darker than it is.

Nice smell. Feels very refreshing when you first spray it on and then it doesn't leave a sticky residue. It also doesn't leave any stickiness if you  get it on your hair or clothes. It's lasts a fairly long time. When you wear a little more heavier makeup, it tends to fade away a little faster. I would definitely buy this again.
summary: Love the look of the product itself. Right size for carting around also!

reviewText: My teen daughter complained of the discomfort when spraying a heavily scented, aerosol product directly into her face. Aside from that (which she was willing to bear for the sake of beauty), she didn't feel that it really did much to cause her makeup to last longer through the day. So while it's not a bad product, it's also fairly useless. Not something we would buy again.
summary: Not much effect and uncomfortable to apply

reviewText:
I have tried make up setting sprays in the past, and all of them....every single one of them has issues...the same issues in fact:
1) not easy to apply...in fact the spray is so strong it can make you blink hard even with your eyes closed and what happens to make up...when it gets moist and you blink? you got it....smeared
2) it smells strange
3) it does not set my make up at all, without it my make up stays...with it ...it stays the same....it does not prevent it from fading through the day and I did have to reapply.
4) It irritated my skin a little, made it dry
Wife was pleasantly pleased with this product. Seems to keep her makeup set but she does need to use it more than once a day. Did not see any real color with this product at all, hence the 4 starts.
summary: Seems to towkr fine. No real color noted.

reviewText: This is a toss up between three and four stars.  I gave it to my teenager to try and her exact words were it smells horrible and it doesn't spray evenly.  It does however last longer then other sprays.  She said there are better products out there.  The biggest issue for her was the smell.
summary: Ok product. Lasts a while but smell is a turnoff

reviewText: It pains me so much to rate a BLISS SPA product so poorly.  But this product was AWFUL.  I sprayed it on after my makeup.  First I noticed that it made my mascara run and then it locked in the mess.  I had to use baby wipes to get this cleaned up.  Next, rush to the car to get to work.  I looked in the rearview mirror and much to my horror my face was absolutely shiny.  OH NO.  Like mirror gloss shiny.  NOT A GOOD LOOK.  And it stayed like that all day.  Sigh.  I give this product a pass.  Not sure what happened, usually you can totally rely on this company for a kick-a$$ product.  Not this time.  :-(
summary: Pass on this one from Bliss.

reviewText: It smells nice. It dries quickly. Makes my make up set well. Being in Georgia heat, my makeup has melted off even with this on, but Georgia heat is brutal and it didn't exactly bother me that in 90+ degree weather I sweated my contour off. Whatever. It does hold up for normal day to day wear. And I did find I have to spray before I apply mascara or the spray wets my mascara and leaves black dots on my cheeks.

To my surprise this actually works.  I don't wear a ton of makeup but the little bit I do apply has more staying power with this.  I actually loved the feel of it on my face.  It's a very cooling effect in this heat.  I'm wondering at the lack of scent though.  Hairspray smells good.  Why can't this?
summary: I actually loved the feel of it on my face

reviewText:
Well, I would love to say that I brushed this product on my face and was then able to sashay off to work with no other product looking fabulous. Yes, I am overly optimistic and/or lazy. I wasn't fabulous, and I did have to apply some other stuff- tinted moisturizer, eye shadow,etc and so on. It did give me a slightly glittery look and maybe darkened my skin a bit. And keep in mind I'm the color of white paper on the regular. I imagine you could brush it on heavier but I was in fear of looking like I had dirt on my face.

The good news is that it did even out my reddish undertone on my face and made it look more normal except for the 'glow' read glittery bits. I mean no one at work asked me why I was a disco ball but I was expecting a more even natural 'glow'. But do give it a try- a more normal skin tone can only help.

I ordered this bronzer due to the lack of color I have from not sitting in the sun.  I am so pale that I am see through. However, I made the mistake of getting this color even though it is way too dark for me. Do NOT let this deter you from getting this color.

For starters the case itself is adorable and I will use the compact even after the bronzer is all gone. If you use a big brush (not a blush brush), the bronzer goes on easier and you can control the intensity better. Since I was worried that it would look like I had dark circles like doll's cheeks, I lightly applied the bronzer on my big Kabuki brush.  I made upward motions and made sure to include my temples and the top of my nose. I realized that I applied it too lightly but this made me concerned since layering with most bronzers is an awful experience. Usually, the color looks like stripes or caked on in some areas and I wanted to avoid this. I tried another layer and believe it or not, it went on smoothly and perfectly. It layers so nicely! I was able to obtain a natural looking bronze tone without it looking like makeup. I like the fact that it is very dark for my skin because most of the lighter bronze colors are too light for my taste. It lasted for most of the day and did not cause any irritation on my sensitive skin. You will not regret getting this bronzer!

This bronzer is a very decent size, although I feel like for the price the packaging could have been a lot more exciting. I also noticed that the container called this a matte bronzer which is also not true... There is glitter in this although on the face, it's very hard to tell so it doesn't matter that much. This is also pretty pigmented which is nice, but it's important to use a light hand or else it goes on strong. Personally, I would save your cash and go after a bronzer by Rimmel or Maybelline, but this is still a good bronzer
summary: Good, but not worth the price

reviewText: I found the case difficult to open, but once opened I found the product quite nice.  I have very pale skin and worried it may be too dark, but I put it on in layers.  That way I can control how dark the bronzer gets.  I live where it is very hot and dry so I perspire quite a bit when outside, but the bronzer stayed very well.  It has a nice, smooth texture.  It's very good for contouring.  If the case were easier to open, I'd buy again.
summary: The case is  my only complaint.

reviewText: This is the fourth Bliss product I've tried recently, and it's probably my favorite. I'm very fair (as a point of reference, I wear MAC foundation in NW 20 and Lancome Teint Miracle in Buff 4C), and was worried that Kiss Me Caramel would be too dark. Since it has buildable coverage, it actually works great for fair skin. Kiss Me Caramel has some slight shimmer to it, but it's definitely not too much and I feel comfortable wearing it, even as a 44-year-old. It really goes on lightly, but it adds a nice warmth to your kin. I've attached a photo of the Bliss bronzer next to some others I own to show the color difference. The bottom left is the Bliss bronzer in Kiss Me Caramel, above it is Lorac's Tantalizwer Baked Bronzer in Golden Glow, on the top right is The Balm's Bahama Mama, and on the bottom right is Too Faced's Bronzer in Aqua Bunny. As you can see, Aqua Bunny and Bahama Mama are more matte and go on darker, whereas the Bliss and Lorac bronzers have more shimmer and go on more lightly. If you're looking for an inexpensive bronzer brush, I'd recommend EcoTools Domed Bronzer Brush. It's a really nice cruelty-free brush that does a good job of depositing product right where you want it to go. The only negative about the Bliss products is that the compacts they come in are silver, and fingerprints show all over the outside casing. It makes the case look dirty. Other than that, though, this is a great product!
summary: Kiss Me Caramel has buildable coverage that makes it great for fair skin

reviewText: I've tried different types, brands and colors of bronzers.  This one by Bliss (Bliss Me Carmel) is a great shade of Carmel with a touch of rose color.  It is great for bronzing or contouring.  The downside of this bronzer is it is way to glittery for me.  I am in my mid 50s and do not like anything (actually have never like anything) with glitter in it.  Shimmer I can handle, not glitter.  This has small pieces of glitter in it which really shows up on your skin.  I can see this being more suited for a younger person or someone who actually likes glitter in their cosmetics.  Other than that it is a silky bronzer that lasts all day.  Update:  I let my coworker who is in her late 20s try this bronzer and she absolutely LOVES it.  She likes it as a bronzer and eyeshadow making this a multi use product.
summary: bliss Go For The Bronze Powder- Bliss Me Caramel

reviewText:
This is very dark bronzing powder that does not look good on normal skin complexion, and also contains a bit of glitter, which is not what I expected and not my style.

It also causes some irritation.

I won't be able to use this application and I can't recommend it.

Nice to add that extra bronze touch to your makeup routine. I only use it at night to highlight areas in need of contrast with the rest of foundations. It applies easily with a make up brush or sponge. Gives great contouring. I typically use a natural color, I'm light skinned, not fair. This worked great even after tanning.
summary: Nice to add that extra bronze touch to your makeup ...

reviewText:
This bronzer from Bliss is a creamy powder that glides on the face easily.

I actually received Kiss Me Caramel rather than Cocoa-Cabana (a mistake in Vine shipping.) I have dark skin so because of that, the Kiss Me Caramel is almost a perfect match for my skin tone - just slightly darker. It actually works out well for me as a sort of foundation on days that I don't want to wear make up.

It has quite a bit of shimmer (read sparkle) that may be too much for some people's taste but it looks nice on my darker skin. The color is buildable and you can deepen it by applying multiple layers, although it becomes even more sparkly with more layers. I prefer a single, light layer on my skin.

The thing I don't like is that this is a cream/powder rather than strictly a powder. This is probably good for women with dry skin but mine tends to oiliness and Texas is hot. I prefer a powder for the oil absorbing properties and this bronzer has none of those. For this reason, I will likely use this in our brief winter season.
summary: Sparkly bronzer that glides on easily

reviewText: I've been wanting a bronzer for a while but never got around to getting one. I love the Bliss one I received to review. The Kiss Me Caramel provides a sun kissed look without feeling like I'm wearing a lot of makeup. It's got a nice light shimmer that reflects the light.  The only thing I didn't like was that it is scented. I prefer my makeup to be unscented.
summary: Bliss Go for the Bronze Powder Bronzer - Kiss Me Caramel

reviewText: Im not entirely sure bliss Triple Oxygen Radiance Restoring Mist actually does anything for my face other than make it feel fantastic.  I already use fairly good skin care products, and I haven't noticed a discernable difference in the appearance of my skin.  My skin does look great, but I thought it looked great before I ever tried this mist.  Ive been spraying a light mist over my face after I wash it and before I apply moisturizer.  This mist feels wonderful, very cool and refreshing, and I love using it, but I doubt Id ever purchase it for myself.  Almost $40 seems like a lot for a skin care product that just feels good but doesnt seem to actually do much else.

If your skin is dry then a quick spritz might " restore radiance ". For my oily skin I did not notice any radiance boost after 2-3 mid day spritz's over the last 2 weeks. It is pleasant way to refresh your make up

Bliss is a spa line, and their triple oxygen collection was designed to "energize, hydrate and renew the look of dull, tired skin." It's formulated with CPR technology, and if you're wondering what that is, after some searching I learned that it stands for Clarify, Protect and Revitalize. Ever since Evian first started selling spray-on water -- evian Facial Spray Mineral Water Facial Spray, 10 Ounce -- water-based mists have been astonishingly popular. I myself own two different spray-ons in addition to this one. With high temps arriving, the mist feels like air conditioning in a can. I love the fragrance, but if you don't, it vanishes quickly. I am not so enamored of the long list of ingredients. Chamomile, garlic, and ginger extracts are on there -- along with dozens of chemicals whose names most of us can't pronounce. I understand the need for preservatives, but my other products seem to work just fine without ethylbisiminomethylguaiacol manganese chloride and the rest. The packaging is deluxe, as befits the price. Which brings me to...the price. Luxury brands offer similar products for half the price or less. This compact bottle contains 100 ml, which means that TSA should let you through, but you'll have to search to find a higher cost/ounce of comparable spray-ons. Verdict: like it a lot, but not a must-have. For 1/3 the price, I'd consider it, but it is just amped-up water and you could brew your own for a few pennies.

I'd be lying if I said this was not a product I liked. It's truly refreshing and smells amazing and yes, is a nice pick-me-up for the skin. However, for the life of me I can't figure out just how significantly this benefits my skin besides a nice cool mist. Take it for what it is, a cooling spritz, but I'm not ready to classify this as real skincare, which is what I'd like at the price.

My teenage daughter uses this product, and enjoys the revitalizing feel of a quick spray to the face; the application is quick and simple, and a couple of sprays is all she needs. The smell is a reasonably subtle and not too overpowering citrus, and it is not unpleasant to be around. The mist lingers just enough to prevent you wasting by overspraying. At 3 ounces, there isn't a great deal of it to go around...

The price is definitely up there, which puts this more into the "nice to have" category rather than "must have". I am sure there are comparable products available for a lot less. That is probably the biggest negative. Not sure we would pay that much for this product. Generally though, very well received by my daughter and a refreshing and non intrusive product that she enjoys.
summary: there isn't a great deal of it to go around

reviewText: I like the sensation from the misting spray and I don't find the scent as strong as other reviewers have mentioned. It feels great, but I'm not seeing any radiance coming through for me, but my radiant days are pretty much history. I do like this a lot and have been using it daily and will continue using it until it's all gone, but at the same time IMHO the product is way overpriced as opposed to what one can make with one's home grown concoctions (shout out to other reviewers for some great tips). I would rate this a solid four stars if not for the current selling price on the Amazon page. It's a nice mister and all, but it's a very expensive mister for a bit of facial please.
summary: Nice product, but over priced at the moment this review is written.

reviewText: I hate to say (or do I?) but I suspect the same results could be achieved much more inexpensively with some water and a mister (and by mister, I mean something that delivers a fine spray of H20, not a Mr.). That said, I think this stuff is kind of cool--it has a pleasant smell, nice feel, and it does make me feel refreshed. It's definitely a little pick-me-up luxury. Would I buy it (I got mine for free in exchange for an honest review)? I doubt it, but if you have cash to burn and a thirsty face, go for it.
summary: Give your thirsty mug a drink

reviewText: Very refreshing mist. I think I'll carry it with me to air and car shows this summer. It lightly moisturizes without drowning you or ruining your makeup.  Smells like oranges.  Helps with dry skin.  I'm not sure it's doing anything for my complexion though.  I'm still getting the occasional pimple. No irritation though.
summary: Smells like oranges. Helps with dry skin

reviewText:
The claims this product makes read like a snake oil salesman. "Made with cpr technology...","...provides radiance, protection, toning and hydration for a glowing, youthful-looking complexion." It's just a lot of words put together to make it sound like it really does something.

That said, it's a mister. The scent is nice. I learned from my dad when I was a teenager that when you are sprayed in the face with water, you do indeed wake up.

You could probably buy a spray bottle and fill with water and a little something to give it scent and get the same results as this.
Nice spring color
Beautiful color as a stand alone or on top of other polish to add some sparkle

This 4 Pack was a great deal for my Clarisonic face washer.  The different heads all serve a different purpose and are easily interchangeable for when your skin needs a bit more TLC.

The bulk pack price is also fantastic. Its a great savings if you're using the Clarisonic on a daily basis like I do.

Overall, I cant have a single complaint about this. All the heads worked great and, because I don't use all Of them every day, Ive gotten a ton of life out of them.

Overall a great buy!

Highly recommended.

I can be hard on my nails so when I paint them at home I always go for a good base and top coats.  I like this one because it provides a durable layer over my polish so my nails last longer (chipping or breaking less) and without distorting the color of the polish underneath.  Would recommend.

I've applied this top coat to my regular nail polish and really does increase the shine and give it that glossy Gel polish look. I do think it extended my wear time by a little bit (but not by a large amount of time...maybe it works better if you use it with a Londontown Nail Polish rather than another brand).

I did really like the shine it gave to my nails (without having to go through the hassle of curing my nails with a UV light) and it was very easy to apply.

Since I discovered gel polish and its durability it is my go to for home manicures. This top coat unlike other gel nail polish does not require a UV or LED lamp to cure although it does say it cures in the sun. I tried it both ways drying it out in sunlight and just using my nail dryer and both worked well. It is a high shine top coat that gives a nice finished look to your polish. It lasts without chipping for about a week which is similar to other gel top coats. What I did notice is that it stayed glossy longer and did not get matte like some of my other top coats have in the past, especially after a full week of doing dishes and such. Overall its a good top coat, particularly if you don' have a lamp or a looking for your nails to stay glossy throughout the life of your manicure.

There are only a few nail polishes I bought over the years that I could say last and last, unfortunately this is not one of them. It only lasted a few days and the color is just transparent so didn't add anything special or extra to my nails.  I probably would not use again.
summary: As good as many other top coats but not a stand out

reviewText: Pricey but easy to apply.  Goes on well and lasts.  VERY glossy.

Excellent top coat.

Goes on very smoothly and has a super glossy finish.  Lasted about a week which, since I use my hands a lot, was wonderful.  I'm used; to polish chipping within 3 days.

Strong scent, but not overwhelming and the scent does fade quickly.

Will happily continue to use!

This top coat does strengthen the base polish.  While my polish alone can go for four-five days before chipping, adding this to polish lengthen it to a week.  This coat goes on well and evenly.  This is a great addition to the home manicurist.

The scent of this lotion is just too strong for me. I've tried it a few times and it makes me nauseous every time. (It's usually headaches that I get from strong scents.) This scent lingers for a long time for me, and that's with washing my hands several times throughout. After a couple of times of using it, I decided to just use it on my feet. I didn't think it through very well and put it on with my hands. I quicky realized my mistake and just had to suffer through it. (The scent reminds my husband of his late grandmother's Oil of Olay.)

It does moisturize well, though.

With body creams, I do like to splurge a little.  I want a nice scent and a non greasy feeling.  Typically, I would go to Back and Body Works for this type of product but I have a love of the scents listed and I was hoping for something more natural and less fake-fragrance chemical smelling.  This fit the bell - a really love scent combined with moisturizing that you can actually see immediately.  Skin softens and looks less tight right after the first use.

This is a nice, thick, moisturizing body cream. It goes on smooth and leaves skin silky, although it does not soak in all the way and leaves a residue behind. It has what I would describe as a "tropical fruity" fragrance that tends to linger and can become clawing. It comes in a fancy-looking tub with a wood-looking cover and a plastic bottom that makes it look bigger than it's actual 7.4 fl oz. I wouldn't buy this again for the price that it's offered, but there's nothing inherently wrong with it.

I keep planning to move this to the bathroom for an after-shower body cream, but so far it hasn't made it out of my home office, where I use it as a hand cream because I enjoy the fragrance so much (the fragrance is very strong, so beware if you're not a fan of Indian rose). It has kind of an odd, slick feeling initially, but it absorbs completely and leaves my hands soft and silky, not as if they're coated with something. A small amount goes a long way, and it really does make me pause and just enjoy the moment. The jar also looks attractive on my desk.
